《清太子今天作死了吗》作者: 木兰竹
文案
胤礽转世后当了二十年的新社会青年，一朝见义勇为回到前世。
奶团子胤礽晃着小脚丫，梳理刚苏醒的前世记忆：
幼年时，伺候他的人几乎一月一换，敢劝诫他谨言慎行的仆人一定会因“对太子不敬”率先赶走；
读书时，高龄教书师傅颤悠悠跪着授课，他因怜悯赐座，教书师傅因“对太子不敬”被严厉斥责；
少年时，和一位亲切和蔼的老大臣聊了一会儿诗词歌赋，老大臣便因“对太子不敬“被赶出京城……
兄弟姐妹与自己玩闹是对太子不敬，太子妃的住所与自己隔着老远因为不能对太子不敬……
最后自己变得飞扬跋扈暴戾自负，二立二废变成了彻彻底底的疯子。
奶团子胤礽翻了个身，肚皮朝上，仿若失去了梦想的死鱼。
四十年太子没什么大不了，现代还有五六十年的太子呢。但一生都被严密监视和控制的溺爱实在是太难熬。反正阿玛心软不杀子，只要作不死就往死里作，争取早日废太子。
于是……
“陛下！太子殿下带着大阿哥把内务府总管揍啦！”
“陛下！太子殿下带着三四五阿哥出宫和宗室子弟斗殴啦！
“陛下！太子殿下带着六七八阿哥把蒙古王子的马骗走啦！”
“陛下！太子殿下带着九十等一众小阿哥做生意把京中大臣的棺材本全赚跑啦！”
“陛下！……”
康熙按着太阳穴上嘣嘣直跳的青筋，咬牙切齿道：“说吧，保成又干了什么！”
“太子殿下留书离家出走，说要混进远航船队为大清开疆扩土去啦！”
康熙猛地站起来，一脚踹翻桌子：“还不快把那个不孝子给朕追回来！！朕这次一定要重重罚他！”
*
今天胤礽作死了吗？
当然。
今天康熙废太子了吗？
下次一定！

"Has the Crown Prince of Qing Been Courting Death Today?" Author: Mulan Zhu

Synopsis

After reincarnating, Yinreng spent twenty years as a youth in the new society before a heroic act sent him back to his past life.

The toddler Yinreng dangled his little feet, sorting through the memories of his past life that had just awakened:

In his early childhood, the servants attending to him were changed almost every month; any servant who dared to advise him to be cautious in speech and action would be driven away first for "disrespecting the Crown Prince."

During his studies, an elderly tutor would tremble while kneeling to give lessons; when he showed pity and granted the tutor a seat, the tutor was severely reprimanded for "disrespecting the Crown Prince."

In his youth, he chatted about poetry and literature with a kind and amiable old minister for a while, only for that old minister to be driven out of the capital for "disrespecting the Crown Prince"...

Siblings playing with him was considered disrespecting the Crown Prince, and the Crown Princess's residence was kept far away from his because one could not be disrespectful to the Crown Prince...

In the end, he became arrogant, tyrannical, and conceited, and after being deposed and reinstated twice, he turned into a complete madman.

The toddler Yinreng rolled over, belly up, like a dead fish that had lost all its dreams.

Being a Crown Prince for forty years is no big deal; in the modern era, there are Crown Princes who wait for fifty or sixty years. But the suffocating, doting control of being under constant surveillance was truly unbearable. Anyway, Father is soft-hearted and won't kill his son; as long as I don't court death to the point of no return, I'll keep pushing the limits, striving to be deposed as Crown Prince as soon as possible.

And so...

"Your Majesty! The Crown Prince took the First Prince and beat up the Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department!"

"Your Majesty! The Crown Prince took the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Princes out of the palace to brawl with the imperial clan's children!"

"Your Majesty! The Crown Prince took the Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Princes and swindled the Mongolian Prince's horses!"

"Your Majesty! The Crown Prince took the Ninth, Tenth, and the rest of the younger princes to do business and swindled all the ministers' retirement savings in the capital!"

"Your Majesty!..."

Kangxi pressed his temples where the veins were throbbing, gritting his teeth as he said, "Speak, what has Baocheng done this time!"

"The Crown Prince left a note and ran away from home, saying he's going to sneak onto a long-distance fleet to expand the territory for the Great Qing!"

Kangxi stood up abruptly and kicked over the table: "Why aren't you chasing that unfilial son back for me!! I will definitely punish him severely this time!"

*

Has Yinreng courted death today?

Of course.

Has Kangxi deposed the Crown Prince today?

Definitely next time!

chapters.source_text:
康熙十六年。
三藩之乱只剩下吴三桂苟延残喘。清宫之中，年轻的帝王初步握住了所有的权力，连深宫中的侍从们似乎都感受到了日益浓厚的帝王威压。
即使宫内还没有新的皇后主持宫闱，宫人们也小心翼翼，一步都不敢行错。
但这一切，和乾清宫的一处小暖阁中的奶团子没有任何关系。
穿得圆滚滚的胤礽从软塌左边滚到右边，又从软塌右边滚到左边，然后鼓着小肚肚仰面朝上，仿若失去梦想的软趴趴小奶猫。
作为一个社会三好新青年，一朝见义勇为被迫从便利的现代穿越回清朝就已经够苦逼。
经过小半年持续不断的低烧虚弱，最近，他终于融合了前前世的记忆，发现自己前前世就是那个苦逼太子胤礽，这就更苦逼了。
前前世的那些记忆没有影响胤礽的性格。在奶团子胤礽看来，那些与其说是记忆，不如说是不甘的怨念。
胤礽看完记忆了事，只是对前前世自己的遭遇深深心惊。
四十年太子不算什么，他对权力地位没什么欲/望。君不见后世五六十年太子也活得潇潇洒洒？有尊贵的地位还不干事当咸鱼，这岂不是许多现代年轻人的梦想？
但康熙对孩子过分的控制和溺爱，实在让胤礽很是受不了。
现代孩子老被父母不敲门进屋都要抱怨许久，康熙……唉，不提也罢，搁谁谁都得疯。
胤礽又想起毓庆宫那逼仄的空间，对比几个兄弟亲王府那亭台楼阁大花园，更加悲从心来。
都当太子了，为什么我没有亭台楼阁没有大花园！为什么我要被关在皇宫中蜷缩在有小迷宫之称的毓庆宫内！其他兄弟都是关在大大的王府里！这不公平！
我要大房子！我要大花园！我要被圈禁在可以种田的大庄子里！最好是带温泉的那种！
这被溺爱的太子，不做也罢！
但需要从长计议。
胤礽拍了拍自己的小肚肚。
便宜康熙老爹虽然万般不好，但有一点不错的是，他对孩子心软，绝对不会杀儿子。作不死就往死里作，深知康熙底线在哪的胤礽，一定可以争取早早自废掉。
可他若是想要一个大大的温泉庄子作为圈禁地点，让自己的圈禁人生变成美好的清朝宅男生活，这就需要技术含量了。
胤礽想，他得想出一个触及皇帝老爹底线，但又不能真的让皇帝老爹厌恶，最好还让他有点心疼的作死法来废掉这个太子。
胤礽开动着开动着脑筋，就有些昏昏欲睡。
今年五月他才满三周岁，奶团子的“硬件”让他每次想用成年人的思维思考，身体就会很快疲惫，昏昏欲睡。
平时他的注意力也很容易涣散，好不容易集中注意力说点人话，很快便会忘记之前自己在说什么，不可抑制的嘀咕一些孩童的不可名状之语。
当奶团子真难。胤礽一边打瞌睡，一边又开始滚来滚去，思索能开启清朝美好宅男生活的万全法子。
胤礽表现得如此百无聊赖，暖阁中伺候的人只低眉垂首，只要胤礽没有滚下床，全当没看见，没有一个试图上前哄哄他。
康熙对这个太子看得极重，曾经敢上前亲近胤礽的人很快便会被拖走。就算没被拖走，这伺候太子的人也是一月一换做不长。
多一事不如少一事，多做才会多错。这伺候太子的活计，就是一个跳板。只要做好本分工作，熬过这一月，他们就会被分到其他地方去。
——————
胤礽滚了半晌，把自己滚饿了。
他从床上翻坐起来，翻了好几次都因为穿得太厚重起不了身。
这时候也没个人帮他扶起来，大概都在等他自己叫人。
胤礽眼中闪过一丝落寞，很想念自己在现代的家人。
坐不起来，胤礽又摊成一个大字型，懒得坐了。
咸鱼小奶猫选择躺平。
在胤礽再次躺平的时候，隔着窗户缝隙偷看了许久的俊秀青年，才掸了掸肩膀上的细雪，微笑着摇摇头，挪动脚步绕向暖阁的门扉。
康熙推开门，小小的暖阁立刻稀里哗啦跪了一地的人。
他脸上淡淡的微笑立刻隐去，挥手让屋里伺候的人退下。
总管太监顾问行替康熙除去肩上被雪润湿的大氅，副总管太监赵昌接过康熙抱着的暖手笼，并递给康熙一方绢布手绢。
康熙用绢布手绢擦干手心悟出的薄汗之后，才走到胤礽面前，把还大字平躺着的奶团子胤礽扶起来。
“阿玛来了，居然不向阿玛请安？”康熙刮了刮胤礽的鼻头，重新恢复了浅笑。
饿得脑袋不怎么好使的胤礽，在康熙臂弯中跪坐弯腰：“请、请阿玛安，哎哟！”
圆润的奶团子一头撞到康熙肋骨上。胤礽眼泪汪汪捂头，康熙哭笑不得的揉胸口。
只比康熙小两岁、康熙刚登基便伺候左右的哈哈珠子太监赵昌垂下头，肩头微微颤抖，遮掩住脸上的笑意。
看着康熙长大，并对康熙有半师之谊的顾问行要随意得多。
他当着康熙的面扬起温和的笑容：“皇上何苦逗太子殿下？太子殿下额头撞红了，心疼的还不是皇上您？”
康熙一只手揉胸口，一只手揉着奶团子的额头，没好气道：“顾太监这话倒是说朕不对了？”
“老奴不敢。”顾问行笑着从康熙怀中接过捂着头的胤礽，帮胤礽揉脑袋。
这一下撞得可狠，胤礽额头上居然冒起了一个小肿包。
康熙忍不住差点笑岔气：“顾太监，赶紧把保成头上的包给朕揉散！等会儿玛嬷见了他，还真以为朕欺负他。”
赵昌见康熙对顾问行的亲昵，和顾问行在康熙面前的随意，心中有些艳羡。
“顾太监”这种叫法是从明时沿袭下来。宫里能被叫“姓氏加太监”的，只有前明宫廷留下的老人。其他太监都是“职位加姓名”。
前明宫廷能留下供职的人大多是读书人，身兼清朝早期皇子们的汉学启蒙工作，伴随清朝早期帝王度过了称帝后最无措的年代，教导后来太监们规矩。
顾问行便是从顺治朝时便一直看护康熙长大，曾教导过康熙汉学的“前明太监”。
曾经教导康熙书法、句读的前明太监们大多已经年老离开宫廷，仅顾问行正值中年。康熙对其信重极深，视若师长。
即使赵昌算是除顾问行之外一直伴随康熙左右第二久的人，这“第一”和“第二”中也隔着天堑。
胤礽仰头看着不像个太监、倒像个饱读诗书的文弱书生的顾问行，从已经木了的小脑袋瓜里挖出了这个人的过往，然后就因为用脑过度，往后一仰，一头栽回康熙怀里。
咕噜噜。胤礽腹鸣如雷。
奶团子扒拉着康熙的袖子，有气无力道：“饿。”
顾问行向赵昌使了一个眼色，赵昌立刻去小厨房拿胤礽的食物。
胤礽不爱喝人奶，一喂人奶就吐，所吃的食物早早换成了牛奶和羊奶糊糊，随时在乾清宫小厨房备着。
“怎么饿成这样？我缺你这口吃的吗？”康熙哭笑不得的护住胤礽，连自称都“气”变了。
顾问行顺势松开手，让胤礽完全跌入了康熙怀里。
赵昌端来温度正好奶糊糊，先用银勺子试吃了一口之后，换了一个勺子，将奶糊糊递给康熙。
康熙亲自一小勺一小勺喂胤礽食物。
胤礽保持着成年人仅剩不多的理智，一口一口吸溜奶糊糊，一会儿舔舔嘴唇，一会儿用小帕子擦擦嘴角，让小脸保持干净。
这爱干净的模样真像极了小奶猫，看得康熙忍不住轻轻捏了一下胤礽的小胖脸，笑容更深了。
“饿了就叫人给你拿吃的。”康熙喂完之后，才开始训孩子，“你是太子，他们都是伺候你的人。”
胤礽捂着嘴打了个小奶嗝，慢悠悠道：“不认识。不和、不和陌生人说话。”
康熙一手扶娃一手扶额：“你这戒心是哪来的？朕绝对没有如此教过你！”
胤礽吃饱了就犯困。他趴在康熙怀里脑袋一点一点，不住打哈欠。
顾问行从软塌床头拿来一个拨浪鼓递给康熙，康熙拿着拨浪鼓在胤礽耳边“嘭嘭嘭”摇。
胤礽=_=#。
好烦。
他伸出小胖爪胡乱挥舞，试图夺走康熙在他耳边作乱的拨浪鼓。
康熙伸直手臂，把拨浪鼓摇得更响：“不准睡，等会儿要和阿玛一起去看你乌库妈妈。保成，打起精神来。”
胤礽看着康熙那张坏笑的俊脸，瘪了瘪嘴，哭是不可能哭的，他一把将康熙的袖子抓起来，放嘴里咀嚼。
康熙笑得更厉害了。
胤礽心里难过极了。
这招已经完全不管用了。
在没觉醒前前世记忆，只知道自己是现代人穿越的时候，胤礽就不想当这个太子，从小就小规模作死。
其招数不限于咬康熙的手，爬到康熙背上当考拉宝宝，试图在康熙头上作妖揪康熙的辫子……
如果不是还残存着一点点成年人的尊严，他都准备去康熙龙袍上尿一滩了。
康熙起初很震惊，试图和胤礽讲道理。
胤礽总是一副“我只是一个宝宝，我什么都不懂”的态度糊弄过去，就等着给康熙加深他顽劣不堪不孝顺的印象，早早重新确立太子。
比如大阿哥就很不错。大阿哥的母妃乌喇那拉氏也是满洲大族。
当然，恢复前前世记忆之后，胤礽就知道自己这种程度的作死没用了。
他能当太子，是因为皇帝老爹需要元后嫡子当太子。大阿哥的身份不行。
而且，前世清宫剧中四大天王之一的乌喇那拉氏惠妃，居然不是满族显赫世家，而是内务府正黄旗包衣！
对了，未来的宜妃是镶黄旗包衣，现在还没进宫当宫女；未来的德妃是正黄旗包衣，已经当了四年宫女；唯独一个荣妃马佳氏是正儿八经的满洲正黄旗，居然位列四妃之末。
自个儿这皇帝老爹究竟是多喜欢包衣啊？
他总算明白为什么老大老八等一干兄弟弄什么蒙满大臣联名推荐会被皇帝老爹揍了。在这位皇帝眼中，什么老满族老蒙族就是个屁。
康熙不知道自家宝贝儿子正在腹诽他，逗儿子逗得特别开心。
康熙在胤礽之前有多个孩子，死掉的居多。
最开始康熙还挺伤心，后来就麻木了。
麻木之后，他便不再关心孩子的事，直到胤礽出生。
这个儿子平时总是一副懒洋洋的模样，只有见了他异常活泼。这还是他第一次有父子连心的感觉。
当父亲的感觉，大约就是这样？
他曾经期望过的幼年生活，大约就是这样？
在康熙的眼中，挥舞着小肉爪的胤礽，与幼失怙恃的自己渐渐重合。
他环抱着胤礽的手臂，收的更紧了一些。
胤礽正好站起来，被康熙这么一带，身体不稳栽倒，大脑袋“哐”的一声撞康熙拿着的拨浪鼓上。
“哎哟！”胤礽一屁股坐康熙怀里，双手抱头，努力忍泪。
康熙低头一看，胤礽包上加包，忍不住哈哈大笑。
赵昌再次低头忍着肩膀颤抖，顾问行微笑叹气。
自家这位皇上，有了太子后，比年幼时候还顽皮。
等会儿太皇太后看到太子殿下头上的包，可有的唠叨了。

作者有话说:
《今天我仍不知道亲爹是朱元璋》求预收藏，男主言情，文案如下：
陈标穿越元末乱世商人家中，为了活命无法隐藏穿越者的能耐，冒充能掐会算生而知之的神棍，小小年纪便让陈家成为仅次于沈万三的富豪。
这时，他亲爹陈国瑞告诉他，儿啊，你爹我投靠了明朝洪武皇帝，是洪武皇帝的大功臣哦。
陈标即使不是学历史的也知道洪武皇帝朱元璋晚年会杀空大半个朝堂，开始谋划着出海苟命。
陈标：“爹、娘，马皇后马上要崩逝了。”
他亲娘绣花的手一顿。
陈标：“爹、娘，太子也会英年早逝。最爱的老婆和儿子一死，洪武帝立刻就会变成滥杀的疯子。”
他亲爹憨厚的笑容一僵。
陈标：“爹、娘，我们赶紧出海置办产业，等洪武帝杀空满朝文武百官的时候，咱们就逃不掉了！”
亲娘亲爹对视一眼，点头道：“好，儿子，听你的。”
陈标露出满意的笑容。
龙凤元年，朱元璋嫡长子朱标出生。
相者道，此子生而知之，贵不可言，恐老天收之，需隐姓埋名，遮掩天机至而立之年方可归位。待此子归位，定能保老朱家万世永昌。
陈标：“爹，我们什么时候出海啊！我已经在海外置办好大庄园了！”
朱元璋：“还早还早，下次一定，明年一定。”（擦汗.jpg）
——————
再次提醒，半架空清朝YY小白文，请勿考据，谢绝写作指导，一切为了爽，纯粹放飞自我的调剂文，不喜误入。
如果我还有兴趣，下一本写明朝，然后宋、唐等一路逆推上去，一个套路用到底，都是无脑历史爽文。
————————
注：本文资料来自于《清史稿》《康熙朝宦官新探》《钦定大清会典》《钦定八旗满洲氏族通谱》等。
另：清代萧奭著的《永宪录》说惠妃是明珠妹妹是错误的。且不说乌喇那拉氏和叶赫纳拉氏都不是一个姓氏，就算同为“乌喇那拉氏”，四福晋那一支是正黄旗，惠妃和通嫔都是包衣。萧奭的《永宪录》多从邸报、朝报、诏谕、奏折等抄撮而成，和我们现在考据过程没区别，估计考据错了。
chapters.translated_text:
The sixteenth year of the Kangxi Emperor's reign.

Of the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, only Wu Sangui remained, gasping his last. Within the Qing palace, the young emperor had begun to firmly grasp all power; even the attendants in the deep palace seemed to feel the increasingly heavy imperial pressure.

Even though there was no new empress to preside over the inner court, the palace servants were cautious, not daring to take a single wrong step.

Yet all of this had nothing to do with the little milk bun in a small warm chamber of the Qianqing Palace.

Yinreng, dressed until he was round as a ball, rolled from the left side of the soft couch to the right, then from the right back to the left, before puffing out his little belly and lying face up, looking like a limp little kitten that had lost its dreams.

As a model youth of society, being forced to transmigrate back to the Qing Dynasty from the convenient modern era after a heroic act was miserable enough.

After half a year of continuous low-grade fevers and weakness, he had finally integrated the memories of his previous-previous life, discovering that he was that miserable Crown Prince Yinreng, which made things even more miserable.

The memories of that previous-previous life did not affect Yinreng's personality. To the little milk bun Yinreng, those were less like memories and more like resentful grievances.

Yinreng finished viewing the memories and let it be, though he was deeply shocked by the experiences of his past self.

Being Crown Prince for forty years was nothing; he had no desire for power or status. Hadn't he seen that in later generations, princes lived carefree lives for fifty or sixty years? Having a noble status while doing nothing—wasn't this the dream of many modern young people?

But Kangxi’s excessive control and doting on his children were truly more than Yinreng could bear.

Modern children complain for a long time if their parents enter their rooms without knocking, but Kangxi... sigh, better not to mention it; anyone would go crazy.

Yinreng recalled the cramped space of the Yuqing Palace and compared it to the pavilions, towers, and large gardens of his brothers' princely mansions, and his sorrow deepened.

I’m the Crown Prince, so why don't I have pavilions, towers, or a big garden! Why must I be locked in the palace, curled up in the Yuqing Palace, which is known as a small labyrinth! The other brothers are all locked up in big princely mansions! This is unfair!

I want a big house! I want a big garden! I want to be confined to a large estate where I can farm! Preferably one with hot springs!

This doted-upon Crown Prince, I’d rather not be one!

But this required long-term planning.

Yinreng patted his little belly.

Although his cheap father Kangxi had all sorts of flaws, one thing was good: he had a soft heart for his children and would absolutely never kill his son. If he couldn't die from his own antics, he would just keep pushing the limits. Yinreng, who knew exactly where Kangxi's bottom line was, was certain he could strive to get himself deposed early.

However, if he wanted a large hot spring estate as his place of confinement to turn his life of imprisonment into a wonderful Qing Dynasty shut-in life, that required some technical skill.

Yinreng thought he had to come up with a way to act out that touched his imperial father's bottom line without truly making him disgusted—ideally, one that would make him feel a bit of heartache—to get this Crown Prince position abolished.

As Yinreng racked his brains, he began to feel drowsy.

He had only just turned three this May, and the "hardware" of a milk bun meant that every time he tried to think with an adult's mind, his body would quickly become exhausted and sleepy.

Usually, his attention span was easily scattered; even when he managed to focus enough to speak like a human, he would soon forget what he was saying and uncontrollably mutter incomprehensible childish gibberish.

Being a milk bun is really hard. While dozing off, Yinreng began to roll around again, pondering the foolproof method to start his wonderful Qing Dynasty shut-in life.

Yinreng appeared so bored, yet the people serving in the warm chamber only lowered their heads and kept their eyes down; as long as Yinreng didn't roll off the bed, they acted as if they saw nothing, and none attempted to step forward to coax him.

Kangxi valued this Crown Prince extremely highly; those who had once dared to approach Yinreng were quickly dragged away. Even if they weren't dragged away, those serving the Crown Prince were rotated every month and didn't last long.

Better to do less than more; doing more leads to more mistakes. This job of serving the Crown Prince was just a stepping stone. As long as they did their duty and survived the month, they would be assigned elsewhere.

——————

Yinreng rolled for a long time and rolled himself hungry.

He tried to sit up from the bed, but failed several times because he was dressed too heavily.

There was no one to help him up; they were probably all waiting for him to call for someone.

A trace of loneliness flashed in Yinreng's eyes; he missed his family in the modern era.

Unable to sit up, Yinreng sprawled out into a "big" shape, too lazy to try again.

The salted-fish little milk bun chose to lie flat.

Just as Yinreng lay flat again, the handsome young man who had been peeking through the window gap for a long time finally brushed the fine snow off his shoulders, smiled and shook his head, then moved his feet to circle toward the door of the warm chamber.

Kangxi pushed open the door, and the people in the small warm chamber immediately knelt in a flurry.

The faint smile on his face vanished instantly, and he waved his hand to dismiss the servants in the room.

The head eunuch, Gu Wencheng, removed the snow-dampened cloak from Kangxi's shoulders, while the deputy head eunuch, Zhao Chang, took the hand warmer Kangxi was holding and handed him a silk handkerchief.

After Kangxi wiped the thin sweat from his palms with the silk handkerchief, he walked over to Yinreng and helped the milk bun, who was still lying flat, to sit up.

"Father is here, and you don't even greet Father?" Kangxi flicked Yinreng's nose, his faint smile returning.

Yinreng, whose brain wasn't working well due to hunger, knelt and bowed in Kangxi's arms: "G-greet Father, ouch!"

The round milk bun bumped his head right into Kangxi's ribs. Yinreng covered his head with teary eyes, while Kangxi rubbed his chest, caught between laughter and tears.

Zhao Chang, the *hahazhu* eunuch who was only two years younger than Kangxi and had served by his side since he ascended the throne, lowered his head, his shoulders trembling slightly to hide his laughter.

Gu Wencheng, who had watched Kangxi grow up and held the status of a half-mentor, was much more relaxed.

He raised a gentle smile in front of Kangxi: "Why does Your Majesty tease the Crown Prince? The Crown Prince's forehead is bumped red; won't it be Your Majesty who feels the heartache later?"

Kangxi rubbed his chest with one hand and the milk bun's forehead with the other, saying huffily: "Is Eunuch Gu saying that I am in the wrong?"

"This old servant wouldn't dare." Gu Wencheng smiled and took the head-clutching Yinreng from Kangxi's arms to rub his head for him.

That bump had been quite hard; a small swelling had actually risen on Yinreng's forehead.

Kangxi couldn't help but almost choke with laughter: "Eunuch Gu, hurry and rub the bump on Baocheng's head away for me! If the Grandmother sees him later, she'll really think I bullied him."

Seeing the intimacy Kangxi showed toward Gu Wencheng and the ease with which Gu Wencheng acted in front of Kangxi, Zhao Chang felt a bit envious.

The title "Eunuch [Surname]" was a custom inherited from the Ming Dynasty. In the palace, only the old retainers left over from the former Ming court could be addressed as "Surname plus Eunuch." Other eunuchs were addressed by "Position plus Name."

Most of those who remained to serve from the former Ming court were scholars who also took on the task of the early Qing princes' Han learning enlightenment, accompanied the early Qing emperors through their most bewildered years after taking the throne, and taught the later eunuchs the rules.

Gu Wencheng was one of those "former Ming eunuchs" who had watched Kangxi grow up since the Shunzhi reign and had taught Kangxi Han learning.

Most of the former Ming eunuchs who had taught Kangxi calligraphy and reading had already aged and left the palace; only Gu Wencheng was in his prime. Kangxi trusted him deeply and regarded him as a teacher.

Even though Zhao Chang was the second longest-serving person by Kangxi's side after Gu Wencheng, there was still a chasm between "first" and "second."

Yinreng looked up at Gu Wencheng, who didn't look like a eunuch but rather like a scholarly, frail bookworm. He dug into his already numb little brain for this person's past, and then, due to overexertion, tilted his head back and fell right back into Kangxi's arms.

*Gurgle.* Yinreng's stomach growled like thunder.

The milk bun tugged at Kangxi's sleeve, weak and listless: "Hungry."

Gu Wencheng gave Zhao Chang a look, and Zhao Chang immediately went to the small kitchen to get Yinreng's food.

Yinreng didn't like breast milk and would vomit whenever he was fed it, so his food had long been changed to milk and lamb milk porridge, kept ready at all times in the Qianqing Palace's small kitchen.

"How did you get so hungry? Am I shorting you on food?" Kangxi was caught between laughter and tears as he protected Yinreng, his tone even changing out of "anger."

Gu Wencheng took the opportunity to let go, letting Yinreng fall completely into Kangxi's arms.

Zhao Chang brought the milk porridge at the perfect temperature, tasted it first with a silver spoon, then switched to a different spoon and handed it to Kangxi.

Kangxi personally fed Yinreng one small spoonful at a time.

Yinreng maintained the little bit of adult reason he had left, slurping the porridge one mouthful at a time, occasionally licking his lips or wiping the corners of his mouth with a small handkerchief to keep his little face clean.

This clean-loving appearance was just like a little kitten, making Kangxi unable to resist gently pinching Yinreng's chubby face, his smile deepening.

"If you're hungry, just call someone to get you food." After feeding him, Kangxi began to lecture the child: "You are the Crown Prince; they are all people serving you."

Yinreng covered his mouth and let out a small milk hiccup, saying slowly: "Don't know them. Don't talk to... don't talk to strangers."

Kangxi supported the child with one hand and his forehead with the other: "Where did you get this wariness? I have absolutely never taught you that!"

Yinreng felt sleepy once he was full. He lay in Kangxi's arms, his head bobbing, unable to stop yawning.

Gu Wencheng took a rattle-drum from the head of the soft couch and handed it to Kangxi, who shook it "bang, bang, bang" by Yinreng's ear.

Yinreng =_=#.

So annoying.

He stretched out his chubby paws and waved them wildly, trying to snatch the rattle-drum that was causing chaos by his ear.

Kangxi straightened his arm and shook the rattle-drum even louder: "No sleeping. We're going to see your Grandmother later with Father. Baocheng, cheer up."

Yinreng looked at Kangxi's handsome, mischievous face and pouted. Crying was impossible, so he grabbed Kangxi's sleeve and put it in his mouth to chew.

Kangxi laughed even harder.

Yinreng felt extremely sad inside.

This trick was completely ineffective now.

Before he awakened his previous-previous life's memories, when he only knew he was a modern person who had transmigrated, Yinreng didn't want to be this Crown Prince and had been engaging in small-scale self-sabotage since he was little.

His tactics included, but were not limited to, biting Kangxi's hand, climbing onto Kangxi's back like a koala baby, and trying to pull Kangxi's braid while causing trouble on his head...

If he hadn't still had a tiny bit of adult dignity left, he would have been ready to pee on Kangxi's dragon robe.

Kangxi was shocked at first and tried to reason with Yinreng.

Yinreng always used the "I'm just a baby, I don't understand anything" attitude to brush it off, waiting to deepen Kangxi's impression of him as unruly and unfilial, so he would be deposed as Crown Prince early.

For example, the First Prince was quite good. The First Prince's mother, Lady Ulanara, was also from a prominent Manchu clan.

Of course, after recovering his previous-previous life's memories, Yinreng knew that this level of self-sabotage was useless.

He could be the Crown Prince because his imperial father needed the legitimate son of the Empress to be the Crown Prince. The First Prince's status wasn't enough.

Moreover, in the Qing palace dramas of his past life, one of the "Four Heavenly Kings," Consort Hui of the Ulanara clan, was actually not from a prominent Manchu family, but a bondservant of the Plain Yellow Banner from the Imperial Household Department!

By the way, the future Consort Yi was a bondservant of the Bordered Yellow Banner and hadn't entered the palace as a maid yet; the future Consort De was a bondservant of the Plain Yellow Banner and had already been a maid for four years; only Consort Rong of the Magiya clan was a proper Manchu Plain Yellow Banner, yet she was ranked last among the four consorts.

Just how much did his imperial father love bondservants?

He finally understood why his brothers like the First and Eighth Princes were beaten by their imperial father when they tried to organize joint petitions by Mongol and Manchu officials. In the eyes of this emperor, those "old Manchu" and "old Mongol" clans were nothing.

Kangxi didn't know his precious son was bad-mouthing him in his heart; he was having a great time teasing his son.

Kangxi had many children before Yinreng, most of whom had died.

At first, Kangxi was quite sad, but later he became numb.

After becoming numb, he stopped caring about his children until Yinreng was born.

This son was usually lazy, but exceptionally lively whenever he saw him. This was the first time he had felt a father-son connection.

Was this what it felt like to be a father?

Was this what he had once hoped for in his own childhood?

In Kangxi's eyes, Yinreng, waving his little fleshy paws, gradually overlapped with his own younger self, who had lost his parents early.

He tightened his arms around Yinreng.

Yinreng happened to be standing up, and with Kangxi's pull, he lost his balance and fell, his big head hitting the rattle-drum Kangxi was holding with a "clack."

"Ouch!" Yinreng sat down in Kangxi's arms, clutching his head with both hands, trying hard to hold back tears.

Kangxi looked down and saw the bump on top of a bump on Yinreng's head, and couldn't help but roar with laughter.

Zhao Chang lowered his head again, his shoulders trembling, while Gu Wencheng sighed with a smile.

This emperor of theirs had become even naughtier than he was in his youth since having the Crown Prince.

When the Empress Dowager saw the bump on the Crown Prince's head later, there would be plenty of nagging to endure.

‎

"I Still Don't Know My Real Dad is Zhu Yuanzhang" is open for pre-collection. Male-lead romance, synopsis as follows:

Chen Biao transmigrated into a merchant family in the chaotic late Yuan Dynasty. To survive, he couldn't hide his transmigrator abilities and pretended to be a mystic who could predict the future. At a young age, he made the Chen family the second-wealthiest after Shen Wansan.

At this time, his real father, Chen Guorui, told him: "Son, your father has defected to the Hongwu Emperor of the Ming Dynasty and is a great hero to the Hongwu Emperor."

Even though Chen Biao wasn't a history student, he knew the Hongwu Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang would kill off most of the court in his later years, so he began planning to go overseas to survive.

Chen Biao: "Dad, Mom, Empress Ma is about to pass away."

His mother's embroidery hand paused.

Chen Biao: "Dad, Mom, the Crown Prince will also die young. Once his favorite wife and son die, the Hongwu Emperor will immediately turn into a murderous madman."

His father's honest smile stiffened.

Chen Biao: "Dad, Mom, let's hurry and go overseas to set up businesses. Once the Hongwu Emperor kills all the civil and military officials, we won't be able to escape!"

His parents looked at each other and nodded: "Okay, son, we'll listen to you."

Chen Biao showed a satisfied smile.

In the first year of the Longfeng era, Zhu Yuanzhang's eldest legitimate son, Zhu Biao, was born.

A fortune teller said this child was born with knowledge and was unimaginably noble, but feared heaven would take him back, so he needed to hide his identity and conceal his destiny until he reached the age of thirty before he could return to his rightful place. Once he returned, he would ensure the Zhu family's prosperity for ten thousand generations.

Chen Biao: "Dad, when are we going overseas! I've already set up a big estate abroad!"

Zhu Yuanzhang: "Still early, still early, next time for sure, next year for sure." (Sweating.jpg)

——————

A reminder again: this is a semi-fictional, lighthearted Qing Dynasty fan-fiction. Please do not treat it as historical fact. I decline any writing advice. Everything is for fun—a purely self-indulgent filler story. If you don't like it, don't enter.

If I'm still interested, the next one will be about the Ming Dynasty, then the Song, Tang, and so on, working backwards. The same formula will be used to the end—all brainless historical power fantasies.

————————

Note: The materials for this article come from "Draft History of Qing," "New Research on Eunuchs of the Kangxi Reign," "Imperially Commissioned Statutes of the Great Qing," "Imperially Commissioned Genealogies of the Eight Banners Manchu Clans," etc.

Also: The claim in "Yongxian Lu" by Xiao Shi of the Qing Dynasty that Consort Hui was Mingzhu's sister is incorrect. Not to mention that the Ulanara and Yehenara clans are not the same surname, even if they were both "Ulanara," the Fourth Consort's branch was Plain Yellow Banner, while Consort Hui and Consort Tong were both bondservants. Xiao Shi's "Yongxian Lu" was mostly compiled from court reports, edicts, and memorials, and is no different from our current research process; it is estimated that the research was wrong.

chapters.source_text:
逗了胤礽一会儿，康熙拿起一本书，开始给儿子启蒙。
胤礽仍旧摆烂，小身子一扭，用后脑勺对着康熙，装作不想听的模样。
康熙不在乎胤礽听不听。
胤礽现在还小，身体娇弱。康熙不会揠苗助长，现在只是培养胤礽读书的兴趣。
康熙自顾自的叨叨叨念完，胤礽靠在他怀里不断打瞌睡。那小嘴张的，可以塞进好几个鸡蛋。
康熙又好气又好笑，捏了捏胤礽的腮帮子：“你可是太子，这么不爱读书，怎么当太子？”
胤礽心里嘀咕。谁想当太子让他当去，但记得先给我弄个带温泉的大庄子当圈禁地点。
“好了，差不多是时候去见你乌库妈妈了。”康熙又捏了捏胤礽的腮帮子，在顾问行的帮助下，亲手给胤礽套上小斗篷和小皮靴，然后拍了拍胤礽的圆屁股，“自己走。”
康熙身为帝王居然亲自给儿子穿鞋子，这惊世骇俗的一幕让赵昌每次看到心肝儿都在颤抖。
他用眼角余光瞟了一眼顾问行。顾问行还是那副温和儒雅的文人笑容，半点动摇也没有。
赵昌立刻提起精神。学！这波澜不惊的态度，必须好好学！
皇上前阵子说要让顾太监换个位置，那乾清宫主管太监的职位就空出来了，肯定是自个儿这个副总管来做。做得不好，不说什么权势地位，那可是要掉脑袋的。
胤礽蹬了蹬小皮靴，康熙让他自己走，他非要康熙抱。
胤礽锲而不舍的伸出小短手，和抱着双臂的康熙对峙着，两人大眼瞪小眼对峙了许久。
顾问行忍不住笑着叹了口气。
皇上又在和太子顽皮了。
如今三番未定，百业待兴，皇上时常满脸愁容。在太子这里，皇上居然会时常露出仿佛孩童般的笑容。
想起皇上登基时才八岁，如今还未到二十三岁，顾问行不由有些难过。
自家这位皇上，确实是从未有过孩童的生活。怪不得太皇太后见皇上对太子过分宠溺，也睁一只眼闭一只眼。
如今三藩之乱还未完全平定，能让皇上露出笑容的事不多。太皇太后也是怜惜这个早早登上帝位的孙子。
顾问行在心里数着这一对幼稚父子俩对峙的时间，心中默数三十息后，笑着打圆场道：“太子殿下，轿子就在乾清宫外，只几步路而已。”
胤礽皱着脸，妥协的伸出小胖手：“我要向乌库妈妈告状。”
“朕怕你不成？”康熙扬起略显得意的笑容，牵起胤礽的小手。
胤礽扬起包子脸，看着康熙年轻俊秀的面容，老气横秋的叹了一口气。
恢复前前世记忆后，每次看到皇帝老爹这张脸，他都在疑惑，自己真的是穿回上上辈子了吗？
上上辈子的皇帝老爹有这么帅吗？
难道是他对年老后的皇帝老爹印象更深刻，忘记年轻时候的皇帝老爹长什么样了？
怎么可能。
再加上自胤礽记事以后，康熙对他过分的温柔和纵容，以及相处过程中露出幼稚又贪玩的一面，胤礽开始怀疑，自己该不会是穿越到某个平行世界的清朝吧？
比如某个偶像剧中的清朝？
那是不是会有什么清穿女跳出来，和老爹或者自己的兄弟来一场旷世奇恋？
“在想什么？”康熙见儿子又开始发呆，几次台阶差点踩空，被自己及时救下，不由问道，并开始思索，如果自己把手松了，让儿子摔个跟头，儿子会不会哭。
调整一下方向，让儿子摔进扫起来的雪堆里，肯定不会受伤不会疼，应该不会哭？
康熙有些跃跃欲试。
胤礽不知道自家老爹打的坏主意。他不假思索使劲摇头：“什么都没想！”
他将来是要被圈禁在有温泉的大宅子里的，才不要被老爹揍一顿后随便丢到哪个逼仄的小院落圈禁。YY老爹爱清穿女爱得死去活来的事，绝对不能让老爹知道。
“哦。”康熙拉长语调，手一松。
胤礽“啪”的一声扑进了雪堆里，摔出了一个小人型。
周围下人眼观鼻，不敢动不敢动。
顾问行长长的叹了一口气。他见皇上故意引着太子殿下偏着走，就知道皇上没安好心。
康熙把胤礽从雪堆里捞起来，一边拍掉胤礽身上的雪，一边板着脸训斥胤礽走路不看路。
摔得晕乎乎的胤礽条件反射的认错。
顾问行立刻递上热羊奶。胤礽喝了一口暖身体，然后被康熙揣怀里抱进轿子中，烤着炉火慢悠悠朝着慈宁宫晃去。
北京冬日的雪不会立刻融化，能像砂石一样掸掉，不需要担心弄湿胤礽的小衣服。喝了热羊奶，又及时烤火，胤礽没有感觉到任何寒意。
不过扑雪堆的那一下，撞红了胤礽的鼻子。
胤礽摸了摸鼻子，成年人的智商终于上线：“阿玛，你故意松手让我摔下去！你故意摔我，还训我！”
康熙见胤礽终于反应过来，心虚的移开视线：“你自己走路不看路。”
“哼！我要告状！”胤礽用鼻子喷气，就像一只愤怒的小牛犊。
康熙把愤怒的小牛犊儿子按在怀里揉，一边揉一边笑。
胤礽气得嗷嗷直叫。
随侍一旁，跟着轿子一路小跑的顾问行和赵昌听到轿子里传来康熙欢快的笑声，对视一眼，都从对方眼中看出了几分无奈。
自家皇上怎么这么喜欢逗儿子？幸亏太子殿下不爱哭，要换成其他孩子，早就哇哇大哭了。
胤礽不会哭，但他一定会告状。
至于什么举止轻佻之类的他不在乎，最好在太皇太后心中留下一个“这重孙子虽然可爱，但举止轻佻，不够稳重，不堪为帝，建议荣养当富贵闲王”的印象。
谁都知道康熙极重太皇太后的意见，从太皇太后入手，诓骗一个带温泉的大庄子可能更容易。
轿子刚一停稳，胤礽就从轿子上跳下来，努力迈动着他的小短腿，在已经清扫干净的台阶上飞奔：“乌库妈妈！乌库妈妈！阿玛欺负我！”
康熙优雅的踩着小太监的背从轿子上走下来，施施然跟在胤礽身后走。
胤礽的确已经发挥出他的极限速度，但无奈他的腿实在是太短了。康熙迈开大长腿几步就追上了他。
太皇太后一听到胤礽那充满活力的大嗓门，就不由露出了慈祥的笑容：“快扶哀家过去，哀家要看看玄烨又怎么着可怜的保成了。”
苏麻喇姑笑着扶住太皇太后的手：“皇上真是越来越活泼了。”
“活泼才好。”太皇太后感慨道，“保成也是，活泼才好。”
宫里的孩子都病恹恹的，太皇太后看着就伤心。只保成即使身体也十分娇弱，但即使在低烧时候，也能吃能喝能睡，还能爬到他汗阿玛背上顽皮，跟没事人似的，看着就好养活。
可不，保成身体已经全好透了，嗓门又这么大了。
胤礽像个（自以为的）小炮弹似的冲进了慈宁宫，见太皇太后大老远的走过来，连忙降速，在太皇太后面前一个急刹车：“请乌库妈妈安！”
胤礽还没弯下腰，就被太皇太后揽怀里：“哎呀，保成，你的额头怎么了？”
胤礽立刻道：“阿玛撞的！”
康熙笑着给太皇太后请过安后，道：“别听那小子胡说八道。他睡迷糊了一头撞孙儿胸膛上，把自己撞了个包。”
胤礽气愤道：“还有拨浪鼓！”
康熙叹气：“顾太监都已经把他的包揉散了，他一个没站稳又磕拨浪鼓上，这不，又起了一个包。”
胤礽：“……”好像是这么回事？
“阿玛、阿玛还把我摔雪堆里！”胤礽终于又想起一个可以告状的点。
康熙继续叹气：“他走路不看路，一脚踩空，一头栽进了雪堆里，吓了朕一大跳。”
胤礽：“……”我的错啰？
他仰头看向伟大的太皇太后，请求太皇太后做主。
太皇太后横了康熙一眼：“欺负孩子很有趣？”
康熙摸了摸鼻子，知道瞒不过太皇太后，但仍旧要嘴硬保持帝王的尊严：“玛嬷冤枉，孙儿绝对没有欺负他。”
“走，乌库妈妈那有果子，咱们吃果子，不给你阿玛吃。”太皇太后护着胤礽往里走。
康熙讪讪的跟在太皇太后身边：“这次真的是保成自己干的，对不对保成？”
胤礽摸了摸额头：“不对！”
推卸责任谁不会啊，我也会。
太皇太后见康熙和胤礽你一言我一语的“吵”起来，笑得更加慈祥。
吵吵闹闹的父子俩跟在太皇太后左右走进温暖的慈宁宫，就像是平常人家的祖孙三人。
——————
太皇太后坐在软塌上后，胤礽十分没规矩的主动爬到太皇太后怀里窝着。
太皇太后每当胤礽快来请安的时候，就会卸掉假指甲。
她苍老的手将胤礽护在怀里，亲昵的揉了揉胤礽头上的小揪揪，表情宠溺极了。
康熙看到这一幕，不知道是该羡慕太皇太后，还是羡慕自家傻儿子。
太皇太后对康熙管教十分严厉，倒是对重孙儿纵容的很，仿佛寻常人家的曾祖母，令康熙有些吃味。
可康熙也想抱着儿子，揉儿子头上的小揪揪。
今儿个太皇太后和康熙有正事要说。
宫里如今子嗣不丰，太皇太后肯定不会从康熙身上找原因，便想今年多进些人。
太皇太后原本试图在康熙后宫多塞些蒙古的人，但康熙抵触得厉害。她想起曾经与去世的儿子福临关于后宫的争执，心灰意冷作罢。
爱新觉罗的帝王大约不会再让后宫出现蒙古皇后，儿子是这样，孙儿也一样。
既然蒙古人当不了高位嫔妃，那么康熙选谁都一样。
看着自家孙儿也不怎么喜爱满族家世较好的女人，偏爱包衣女子。太皇太后琢磨过味，孙儿大约是不想让后宫女人家世过高，后宫影响前朝。
思及宫里已经有了一位外家势力强大、但亲母已经离世的太子，这样也好。太皇太后便顺了康熙的心意，今年进的女人都是包衣，以宫女的名义入宫。
胤礽趴在太皇太后怀里，吃饱之后终于能动一动脑子。
根据前前世的记忆，如今宫廷大小选制度还不完善，皇帝的女人要么大臣或番邦直接送来，要么是从包衣中选择家世较好的女子。
宜妃便是今年以宫女的身份入宫，德妃入宫时也是直接冲着当妃嫔来的。之后宫里还会有许多包衣妃嫔。
这类宫女和普通宫女的差别大约是家中父辈都是有品级的官员，入宫时穿着稍稍华丽一些，可以戴首饰、穿带花纹的衣服。她们即便分配到其他有封号的妃嫔宫殿里，待遇也和没名分的庶妃差不多，不需要干宫女的活。
直接以伺候人的宫女成为妃嫔几乎不可能。康熙身边甚至没有宫女伺候，只有太监。
想起自家皇帝老爹之后连同早夭的共五十多名子女……嗯，谁能想到老爹居然不让宫女伺候？老爹这是好色还是不好色呢？
胤礽正无聊的腹诽康熙时，听到太皇太后开玩笑道：“你女人的事，你自己决定。只要不像你爹，爱一个女人爱得死去活来就行。”
胤礽灵机一动。他想到了一个既能保持皇帝老爹和太皇太后对他的喜爱，又在继承皇位上疯狂减分的办法了！
神鬼之事，向来引人忌讳。
但能看到祖宗灵魂，这不是又令人忌讳，又不至于变成巫蛊之事使他被厌弃吗？！
他张口道：“乌库妈妈，玛法说，没有爱得、死去活来。”
太皇太后没反应过来：“嗯？”
康熙看向胤礽：“保成，你说什么？什么玛法？”
胤礽一字一顿，十分认真道：“玛法说，没有爱得死去活来。玛法说，故意气乌库妈妈。玛法还说，下次还当、乌库妈妈儿子，下次还气乌库妈妈。”
利用我看过的历史书，利用我历史专业的课本知识，再加上孩童外表孩童心智装傻充愣，我就不信当不好这个神棍！
太皇太后：“……”
康熙：“！！！”

作者有话说:
男主受身体影响，行为会趋同于这个年龄的孩子。（老实说，二十岁的大男孩，除去智商学识，在亲人面前和幼儿园孩子一样幼稚。）
注：古人算虚岁，但便于写文理解，文中都算实岁；古人都说半文言文半白话，为了便于理解和写文，文中都翻译成大白话。
chapters.translated_text:
After teasing Yinreng for a while, Kangxi picked up a book and began his son’s early education.

Yinreng continued to slack off, twisting his little body to face away from Kangxi with the back of his head, pretending he didn't want to listen.

Kangxi didn't care whether Yinreng was listening or not.

Yinreng was still young and physically delicate. Kangxi wouldn't force his growth; for now, he just wanted to cultivate an interest in reading.

Kangxi rambled on to himself, while Yinreng leaned against his chest, drifting in and out of sleep. His little mouth was open wide enough to fit several eggs.

Kangxi was both annoyed and amused, pinching Yinreng’s cheek: "You are the Crown Prince. If you don't like to study, how will you be a Crown Prince?"

Yinreng muttered to himself. Whoever wants to be the Crown Prince can have it, but remember to get me a large estate with a hot spring as my place of confinement first.

"Alright, it's about time to go see your Great-Grandmother." Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s cheek again, and with the help of Gu Wenxing, personally put a small cloak and little leather boots on Yinreng, then patted his round bottom, "Walk yourself."

That the Emperor would personally put shoes on his son was a shocking scene that made Zhao Chang’s heart tremble every time he witnessed it.

He glanced at Gu Wenxing from the corner of his eye. Gu Wenxing still wore that gentle, scholarly smile, completely unshaken.

Zhao Chang immediately pulled himself together. Learn! This unflappable attitude must be learned well!

The Emperor mentioned recently that he wanted to move Head Eunuch Gu to a new position, so the position of Chief Eunuch of the Qianqing Palace would be vacant. It would surely go to him, the Deputy Chief. If he didn't do well, never mind status or power, he’d lose his head.

Yinreng stomped his little leather boots. Kangxi told him to walk, but he insisted on being carried.

Yinreng persistently stretched out his short arms, standing off against Kangxi, who had his arms crossed. The two stared at each other for a long time.

Gu Wenxing couldn't help but sigh with a smile.

The Emperor is playing around with the Crown Prince again.

With the Three Feudatories rebellion still unsettled and the country waiting to be rebuilt, the Emperor often wore a worried expression. Yet, with the Crown Prince, the Emperor often displayed a childlike smile.

Remembering that the Emperor was only eight when he ascended the throne and is not yet twenty-three, Gu Wenxing couldn't help but feel a bit sad.

This Emperor of his had truly never had a childhood. No wonder the Empress Dowager turned a blind eye to the Emperor’s excessive doting on the Crown Prince.

With the Three Feudatories rebellion not yet fully quelled, there were few things that could make the Emperor smile. The Empress Dowager also pitied this grandson who had ascended the throne so early.

Gu Wenxing counted the time the childish father and son spent in their standoff. After silently counting to thirty, he smiled and mediated: "Your Highness, the sedan chair is right outside the Qianqing Palace, it's only a few steps away."

Yinreng wrinkled his face and compromised, extending his chubby hand: "I want to complain to Great-Grandmother."

"Do you think I'm afraid of you?" Kangxi wore a slightly smug smile as he took Yinreng’s small hand.

Yinreng lifted his bun-like face, looked at Kangxi’s young and handsome features, and let out an old-fashioned sigh.

After recovering his memories from two lifetimes ago, every time he saw his Emperor father’s face, he wondered: did he really transmigrate back to the life before his last?

Was his Emperor father this handsome in that life?

Or was it that his impression of his father in old age was deeper, causing him to forget what his father looked like when he was young?

How could that be?

Plus, ever since Yinreng could remember, Kangxi’s excessive tenderness and indulgence, along with the childish and playful side he showed, made Yinreng start to suspect: could he have transmigrated into some parallel-universe Qing Dynasty?

Like a Qing Dynasty from an idol drama?

Would some transmigrated girl pop out and have a legendary romance with his father or his brothers?

"What are you thinking about?" Seeing his son zoning out again and nearly tripping on the stairs—only to be saved by him in time—Kangxi couldn't help but ask, while also wondering if he let go of his hand and let his son trip, would he cry?

If he adjusted the direction so his son fell into a pile of swept snow, he wouldn't get hurt or feel pain, so he probably wouldn't cry, right?

Kangxi was eager to try.

Yinreng didn't know the bad idea his father was cooking up. He shook his head vigorously without hesitation: "I'm not thinking about anything!"

He was going to be confined to a large estate with a hot spring in the future; he didn't want to be beaten by his father and thrown into some cramped little courtyard. The idea of his father being madly in love with a transmigrated girl must absolutely not be discovered by his father.

"Oh." Kangxi drew out the tone and let go of his hand.

Yinreng fell into the snow pile with a "thud," leaving a small human-shaped imprint.

The surrounding servants looked at their noses, not daring to move.

Gu Wenxing let out a long sigh. Seeing the Emperor deliberately lead the Crown Prince to walk off-center, he knew the Emperor was up to no good.

Kangxi fished Yinreng out of the snow, patted the snow off him, and scolded him with a straight face for not looking where he was going.

Dazed from the fall, Yinreng reflexively admitted his mistake.

Gu Wenxing immediately offered warm goat milk. Yinreng took a sip to warm himself up, then was tucked into Kangxi’s arms and carried into the sedan chair, moving slowly toward the Cining Palace while warming by the brazier.

The winter snow in Beijing wouldn't melt immediately and could be brushed off like sand, so there was no need to worry about wetting Yinreng’s clothes. After drinking the warm milk and sitting by the fire, Yinreng didn't feel any chill.

However, the impact of falling into the snow pile had bruised Yinreng’s nose red.

Yinreng touched his nose, his adult intelligence finally coming online: "Father, you intentionally let go and let me fall! You tripped me on purpose and then scolded me!"

Seeing Yinreng finally react, Kangxi guiltily looked away: "You weren't looking where you were walking."

"Hmph! I'm going to complain!" Yinreng puffed air through his nose like an angry little calf.

Kangxi pressed his angry little calf of a son into his arms and rubbed him, laughing as he did so.

Yinreng was so angry he let out a howl.

Gu Wenxing and Zhao Chang, who were following the sedan chair, heard Kangxi’s joyful laughter from inside and exchanged a glance, both seeing a bit of helplessness in the other's eyes.

Why does our Emperor love teasing his son so much? Fortunately, the Crown Prince doesn't like to cry; if it were any other child, they would have been wailing by now.

Yinreng wouldn't cry, but he would definitely complain.

As for being seen as frivolous, he didn't care. It would be best to leave the Empress Dowager with the impression that "this great-grandson is cute, but frivolous and not steady enough to be Emperor, so he should just be a wealthy, idle prince."

Everyone knew Kangxi valued the Empress Dowager’s opinion highly. Starting with her might make it easier to swindle a large estate with a hot spring.

As soon as the sedan chair stopped, Yinreng jumped down and tried his best to move his short legs, sprinting across the cleared steps: "Great-Grandmother! Great-Grandmother! Father is bullying me!"

Kangxi gracefully stepped off the sedan chair using a small eunuch’s back and followed leisurely behind Yinreng.

Yinreng had indeed reached his maximum speed, but his legs were simply too short. Kangxi caught up to him in a few long strides.

Upon hearing Yinreng’s energetic, loud voice, the Empress Dowager couldn't help but show a kind smile: "Quickly help me over, I want to see how Xuan Ye has bullied poor Baocheng again."

Sumalagu smiled and held the Empress Dowager’s hand: "The Emperor is truly becoming more and more lively."

"Lively is good," the Empress Dowager sighed. "Baocheng is the same; lively is good."

The children in the palace were all sickly, which made the Empress Dowager sad. Only Baocheng, even though he was physically delicate, could eat, drink, and sleep well even when he had a low fever, and could even climb onto his father’s back to play, acting as if nothing was wrong. He looked easy to raise.

And indeed, Baocheng had fully recovered, and his voice was so loud.

Yinreng rushed into the Cining Palace like a (self-proclaimed) little cannonball. Seeing the Empress Dowager walking from afar, he quickly slowed down and came to a screeching halt in front of her: "Greetings, Great-Grandmother!"

Before Yinreng could even bow, he was scooped into the Empress Dowager’s arms: "Oh my, Baocheng, what happened to your forehead?"

Yinreng immediately said: "Father bumped me!"

Kangxi smiled and greeted the Empress Dowager, then said: "Don't listen to that boy’s nonsense. He was sleepy and bumped his head into my chest, giving himself a bump."

Yinreng said indignantly: "And the rattle!"

Kangxi sighed: "Eunuch Gu had already rubbed the bump away, but he didn't stand steady and hit the rattle. See, another bump."

Yinreng: "..." Is that how it happened?

"Father, Father also threw me into the snow pile!" Yinreng finally remembered another point to complain about.

Kangxi sighed again: "He wasn't looking where he was walking, missed a step, and fell headfirst into the snow. He gave me quite a fright."

Yinreng: "..." So it's my fault?

He looked up at the great Empress Dowager, asking her to make the decision.

The Empress Dowager shot Kangxi a look: "Is bullying a child fun?"

Kangxi touched his nose, knowing he couldn't fool the Empress Dowager, but still had to keep a stiff upper lip to maintain his imperial dignity: "Grandmother, you wrong me. I absolutely did not bully him."

"Come, Great-Grandmother has fruit. Let’s eat fruit, and we won't give any to your father." The Empress Dowager protected Yinreng and walked inside.

Kangxi followed sheepishly by the Empress Dowager’s side: "This time it really was Baocheng’s own doing, right Baocheng?"

Yinreng touched his forehead: "Wrong!"

Who doesn't know how to shift blame? I can do it too.

Seeing Kangxi and Yinreng "arguing" back and forth, the Empress Dowager smiled even more kindly.

The noisy father and son followed the Empress Dowager into the warm Cining Palace, looking just like a normal family of three generations.

——————

After the Empress Dowager sat on the soft couch, Yinreng very improperly climbed into her arms and curled up.

Whenever Yinreng was about to come for a visit, the Empress Dowager would remove her long nail guards.

Her aged hands protected Yinreng in her embrace, affectionately rubbing the little tuft of hair on his head with an extremely doting expression.

Seeing this, Kangxi didn't know whether to envy the Empress Dowager or his own silly son.

The Empress Dowager was very strict with Kangxi, but she was very indulgent with his great-grandson, just like a regular great-grandmother, which made Kangxi feel a bit jealous.

But Kangxi also wanted to hold his son and rub the little tuft of hair on his head.

Today, the Empress Dowager and Kangxi had serious matters to discuss.

With few heirs in the palace, the Empress Dowager certainly wouldn't look for the cause in Kangxi, so she wanted to bring in more people this year.

The Empress Dowager had originally tried to stuff more Mongol women into Kangxi’s harem, but Kangxi resisted strongly. Recalling the arguments she once had with her late son Fulin about the harem, she felt disheartened and gave up.

The Aisin Gioro emperors would likely never let a Mongol empress appear in the harem again; her son was like that, and her grandson was the same.

Since Mongol women couldn't be high-ranking concubines, it didn't matter who Kangxi chose.

Seeing that her grandson didn't seem to like Manchu women with good family backgrounds, preferring bondservant women, the Empress Dowager realized that her grandson probably didn't want the women in his harem to have too high a status, lest the harem influence the court.

Thinking that the palace already had a Crown Prince with a powerful maternal family—though his birth mother had passed away—this was fine. The Empress Dowager went along with Kangxi’s wishes, and the women brought in this year were all bondservants, entering the palace under the name of palace maids.

Yinreng lay in the Empress Dowager’s arms, finally able to use his brain after being full.

According to his memories from two lifetimes ago, the palace selection system was not yet perfect. The Emperor’s women were either sent directly by ministers or foreign states, or were chosen from bondservant families with decent backgrounds.

Consort Yi entered the palace this year as a palace maid, and Consort De entered with the intention of becoming a concubine. Later, there would be many bondservant concubines.

The difference between these palace maids and ordinary ones was that their fathers were ranked officials, and they dressed slightly more luxuriously when entering, wearing jewelry and patterned clothes. Even if assigned to the palaces of other titled concubines, their treatment was similar to that of untitled concubines, and they didn't need to do menial labor.

It was almost impossible to become a concubine directly from a palace maid who served others. Kangxi didn't even have palace maids serving him; only eunuchs.

Thinking of his Emperor father’s fifty-some children, including those who died young... well, who would have thought his father didn't let palace maids serve him? Was his father lustful or not?

While Yinreng was bored and slandering Kangxi, he heard the Empress Dowager joke: "Decide your own women’s affairs. Just don't be like your father, loving a woman to the point of death."

Yinreng had a flash of inspiration. He thought of a way to maintain his father and the Empress Dowager’s love for him while crazily sabotaging his inheritance of the throne!

Matters of spirits and ghosts were always taboo.

But being able to see the souls of ancestors—wouldn't that be taboo, yet not enough to be considered witchcraft that would get him cast aside?!

He opened his mouth: "Great-Grandmother, Grandfather said, no loving to the point of death."

The Empress Dowager didn't react: "Hmm?"

Kangxi looked at Yinreng: "Baocheng, what are you saying? What Grandfather?"

Yinreng said word by word, very seriously: "Grandfather said, no loving to the point of death. Grandfather said, intentionally angering Great-Grandmother. Grandfather also said, next time he will still be Great-Grandmother’s son, and next time he will still anger Great-Grandmother."

Using the history books I've read, my history major textbook knowledge, and playing the fool with a child’s appearance and mind—I don't believe I can't play this charlatan role well!

Empress Dowager: "..."

Kangxi: "!!!"

100,000

Author's Note:

Affected by his body, the protagonist’s behavior will tend to be that of a child his age. (Honestly, a twenty-year-old boy, excluding intelligence and knowledge, is just as childish as a kindergarten child in front of his relatives.)

Note: The ancients counted nominal age, but for the sake of writing and understanding, the text uses actual age; the ancients spoke in a mix of semi-classical and colloquial language, but for ease of understanding and writing, it is all translated into plain language.

chapters.source_text:
康熙一把将胤礽从太皇太后怀里提溜起来：“保成！你说什么？什么玛法？”
被康熙抓着胳肢窝的胤礽徒劳的蹬了蹬小短腿。
“玛嬷恕罪，保成年纪小，可能糊涂了。”深知自家汗阿玛是太皇太后怒气死穴的康熙，立刻把奶团子胤礽藏怀里。
太皇太后面沉如水的摆摆手：“让他继续说。保成，谁告诉你的？”
胤礽从康熙怀里探出头：“玛法说的。”
太皇太后和康熙再次满头问号。
玛法说的？
康熙把小胖墩放腿上：“保成，你知道玛法是什么意思吗？”
胤礽想了想，好像现在皇帝老爹还没教他满文。
“玛法……就是玛法，是乌库妈妈的儿子，阿玛的阿玛。”胤礽道，“玛法是这么说的。”
太皇太后和康熙对视一眼，两人眼中都出现一丝凝重。
皇室既然重巫蛊之事，自然相信鬼神之事。
无论哪个宗教都相信小孩子能看到常人看不到的东西。而且众所周知，胤礽这么小的孩子不会说谎。如果不是有人教坏胤礽，便是胤礽真的能看到什么他们看不到的东西。
如果是其他鬼魂太皇太后和康熙还会忌惮。一听这鬼魂是顺治，他们俩就难掩激动。
太皇太后问道：“保成，你什么时候看见玛法的？”
胤礽歪着脑袋想了想，道：“不知道。”
康熙皱眉：“不知道？是今年、去年，还是多久？”
胤礽皱紧眉头：“不知道。”
康熙急了：“怎么会不知道？”
太皇太后比康熙沉得住气。
她拍了拍康熙的手臂，道：“小孩子哪有什么时间观念？你问这个，保成哪可能知道？保成，你是白天见到的玛法，还是晚上见到的玛法？玛法长什么样子？”
胤礽比划：“有时候白天，有时候晚上。玛法亮，发光，看不清，晃眼睛。玛法唠叨，听不懂，不喜欢玛法。有阿玛和乌库妈妈就看不到。”
啊这……康熙和太皇太后再次面面相觑。
亮？发光？这是什么？成神成佛了吗？
他们俩在就看不到？为什么？难道汗阿玛/儿子不想看到我？
一会儿白天一会儿晚上又是怎么回事？鬼魂白天也能出来？
康熙灵机一动：“保成，你该不会是做梦看到的吧？”
胤礽抱住脑袋cos迷惑的可达鸭：“做梦？是做梦吗？”
“是托梦啊。”太皇太后也猜到了。她叹了一口气，神情满是惆怅。
康熙没好气的拍了拍胤礽的脑袋：“你怎么没和朕说过？”
胤礽理直气壮道：“你没问过！”
康熙：“……”他好想揍这小子的小屁股。
康熙捏了捏胤礽的腮帮子：“玛法给你托梦说了什么？”
胤礽保持着cos可达鸭的的姿势，迷茫道：“很多，记不清。”
皇宫两大巨头再次无语。
“那你说你记得住的。”康熙道，“刚你不是记起来了吗？”
胤礽放下手，装作努力思考了一会儿，断断续续开始编。
“玛法说，阿玛尿过床！”
康熙：“……朕没有。”
太皇太后：“不，真的有。保成继续。”
“玛法说，保成少读书。阿玛读书吐血，保成不要吐血。”
康熙：“咳咳咳……保成，书还是要读的。”
太皇太后叹气：“玄烨，福临他一直看着你呢。”
“玛法说……”胤礽顿了顿，不知道该不该借这个机会为自己多搏夺一些康熙的好感资本。
他知道今年之前，宫里存活的孩子很少；今年之后，皇帝老爹的儿子女儿就跟雨后春笋似的蹭蹭蹭往上冒，再不愁子嗣。
胤礽想把功劳揽一点在自己身上，为将来作死被圈禁后的美好环境做准备。
可他真的能演戏演成功吗？胤礽有些不自信。
前前世那个废太子的记忆也就只是记忆。胤礽跟看电视剧似的，看完后也就多知道了些事，对自身成长没帮助。
而真正塑造他灵魂的那二十年，嗯……咳咳，那被溺爱着的二十年啊，前十八年只用愁高考，学校家里两点一线；后两年在大学里教室宿舍图书馆食堂四点一线，连社团都没加过，女朋友都没谈过。
如此枯燥乏味但很温馨顺利的生活，胤礽实在是玩不转什么宫斗宅斗朝堂争斗。
这样揽功劳，会不会直接作到死，被“夭折”啊？
胤礽的犹豫被太皇太后和康熙认为是在发呆。
胤礽经常发呆走神，他们都习惯了。
对于一个不到三岁的孩子，不经常走神才奇怪。
康熙拍了拍胤礽软乎乎的小脸：“醒醒，醒醒，玛法还说了什么？”
胤礽眨了眨眼，下定了决心。
帮皇帝老爹保住儿子这个功劳，就算不重赏他，也不可能让他被“夭折”。
而且，他自己没勇气自杀，如果皇帝老爹真的要让他被“夭折”，说不定也是一件好事。
阿玛对孩子心软，肯定会帮他想一个无痛夭折的法子。
希望被“夭折”后，他能带着记忆穿越回现代。
“玛法……经常和人打架。”胤礽眨了眨眼，道，“和黑黢黢打架，玛法打架很厉害。”
康熙和太皇太后脸上的笑容消失。
打架？打什么架？都去世了还能打什么架？
“玛法说，那是女……”胤礽皱紧眉头，“女什么……的咒？”
康熙抱着胤礽的手臂收紧：“女什么？”
难道是哪个女人的巫蛊之术？
“女……什么……的龙脉？”胤礽努力皱紧眉头，把小脸皱作一团，以掩饰自己说谎的表情，“玛法说，祖宗不是女、女？占据什么气？所以女什么生气？咒……黑黝黝？”
胤礽再次抱住脑袋歪头迷惑。
康熙和太皇太后深吸一口气。
他俩总算知道为什么胤礽老在梦中看到汗阿玛/儿子了！汗阿玛/儿子这是有非常重要的讯息让小胖墩传达啊！
可是这个小胖墩就是个傻的！根本没放在心上！
如果不是今天碰巧提到了顺治，小胖墩还记不起来！
可他们又没法怪胤礽。你能指望一个两岁孩子干什么？何况还是托梦说那么多小孩子听不懂的话。
唉！
康熙绞尽脑汁解读胤礽的话：“龙脉？祖宗？难道是祖上哪个女人？”
太皇太后却想起她还是庄妃时，从皇太极口中听过的秘闻。
“是女真。”太皇太后沉声道。
康熙惊讶：“女真？！”
太皇太后给苏麻喇姑使了个眼色，苏麻喇姑把本就已经退到慈宁宫门口的宫人们赶出了宫，自己亲自在宫门口守着。
顾问行也立刻告退，和苏麻喇姑一起守在殿门口。
硕大的宫殿，只剩下他们祖孙三人。
康熙坐直了身体。他知道太皇太后将要告诉他很重要的秘闻。
“爱新觉罗并非真正的女真后裔，这件事你应该知道。”太皇太后道。
康熙点头。爱新觉罗对外宣称是女真后裔，明朝也称他们为建州女真，实际上女真是个地域概念，即东北塞外那群“野蛮部落”。
金国女真的汉化程度相当厉害。当年仿佛野人的“建州女真”，显然不可能是真正的金国女真后裔。
建州女真中各个民族的人都有。当年清朝称“金”，不过和历朝历代一样，给自己找一门显赫的祖宗。
“哀家虽不懂政事，但文皇帝曾道大清并非金国延续，清人也并非女真人，统一族名为满洲。八旗中蒙、汉、女真等，只要归服大清，皆为满洲人。”太皇太后道，“或许文皇帝察觉了些什么。”
文皇帝即皇太极，乃康熙的皇祖父。
太皇太后说自己不懂政事，只是在皇太极时期不懂。现在她当了两朝太后，当然已经很懂。
或许政治家们都喜欢阴谋论，太皇太后很快就联想到皇太极突兀的改民族名称的事。
皇太极名义上是为了民族大融合、为入住中原做汉人之主做准备，但私底下是否涉及神鬼和龙脉之时，谁又说得清？
康熙陷入沉思。
历代帝王都相信气运和龙脉一事。无论是古时的九鼎和玉玺，还是历朝历代的“认祖宗”“护龙脉”“选皇陵”，皆是借用和聚积气运。
借了别人的气运，可能就会遭到别人气运的反噬，这很正常。如果自身气运变强，便不在乎这些反噬。大清显然还不够强。
康熙想起早逝的汗阿玛，又想起自己连续早夭的孩子，握紧的拳头中，指甲几乎陷进了手心的肉里。
“保成，你在什么地方看到了黑黝黝？”康熙咬着牙问道。
胤礽努力让自己的脸皱得更难看，掩饰自己尴尬的演技。
“哥哥？弟弟？”胤礽抱着脑袋，“阿玛别担心，都被我、吸走啦！”
正咬牙切齿的康熙和正心如刀绞的太皇太后：“？？？”
胤礽拍了拍自己的小胸脯：“玛法说，太子是潜、潜龙！有龙气，能吸引黑黝黝，让我远离黑黝黝，阿玛的龙气、能保护我！但哥哥生病，弟弟生病，阿玛教导我，要友爱兄弟！保成是巴图鲁！”
康熙和太皇太后的表情都变得一片空白，彷如晴天霹雳。
胤礽还在洋洋得意：“保成还小，吸引力不够！玛法说，哥哥弟弟要出宫养。明年，哥哥弟弟就都能回来啦！阿玛的儿子，出生时身体好，就能活！玛法说的！”
太皇太后焦急道：“玄烨！福临他不是想害……”
胤礽抱头装可达鸭，打断太皇太后的话：“可是，我吸走了黑黝黝，救了哥哥弟弟，玛法不高兴。玛法还想揍我？还好玛法揍不到我。为什么玛法不高兴，我保护了兄弟呀，我是巴图鲁！”
太皇太后松了一口气。原来不是福临让保成吸引诅咒，是保成自作主张。
“玄烨，这事肯定有转圜的余地，不用着急。”太皇太后冷静道，“招大喇嘛和大萨满进宫。”
太皇太后看着懵懂无知的胤礽，为心里生出的一丝庆幸愧疚。
对太皇太后而言，重孙子都很重要。若舍了胤礽一个，让康熙以后的儿子都能活，她难免有庆幸之感。
但对于现在的玄烨……太皇太后看着康熙难看的脸色，心里深深叹了口气。
“阿玛？”胤礽表情放空，扯了扯康熙的衣袖，“你怎么不高兴？保成做了好事呀。”
“好事？”康熙把胤礽按在了膝盖上。
胤礽：“……”
胤礽：“哇！！”
……
奶团子胤礽，自穿越后两年多时间，第一次被扒了裤子揍屁股。
这一天，很值得纪念。

（众所周知，小孩子最会说谎。）

Kangxi suddenly hoisted Yinreng up from the Grand Empress Dowager’s arms: "Baocheng! What did you say? What 'Mafa'?"

Yinreng, being held by his armpits by Kangxi, kicked his short little legs in vain.

"Grandmother, please forgive him. Baocheng is young and might be confused." Knowing full well that his own father was the Grand Empress Dowager's sore spot for anger, Kangxi immediately hid the little milk bun Yinreng in his arms.

The Grand Empress Dowager waved her hand with a face as calm as water: "Let him continue. Baocheng, who told you this?"

Yinreng poked his head out from Kangxi’s arms: "Mafa said so."

The Grand Empress Dowager and Kangxi were once again filled with question marks.

Mafa said so?

Kangxi placed the little chubby boy on his lap: "Baocheng, do you know what 'Mafa' means?"

Yinreng thought about it; it seemed his Emperor Father hadn't taught him Manchu yet.

"Mafa... is just Mafa. He is Wukumama's son, and Ama's Ama," Yinreng said. "That's what Mafa said."

The Grand Empress Dowager and Kangxi exchanged a look, both of their eyes showing a trace of solemnity.

Since the imperial family placed great importance on witchcraft and sorcery, they naturally believed in ghosts and gods.

Every religion believes that young children can see things that ordinary people cannot. Moreover, it is common knowledge that a child as young as Yinreng would not lie. If no one had taught Yinreng to say this, then it meant Yinreng could truly see something they could not.

If it were any other ghost, the Grand Empress Dowager and Kangxi would be wary. But upon hearing that the ghost was Shunzhi, they could not hide their excitement.

The Grand Empress Dowager asked: "Baocheng, when did you see Mafa?"

Yinreng tilted his head and thought, then said: "I don't know."

Kangxi frowned: "You don't know? Was it this year, last year, or how long ago?"

Yinreng furrowed his brows tightly: "I don't know."

Kangxi grew anxious: "How can you not know?"

The Grand Empress Dowager was more composed than Kangxi.

She patted Kangxi’s arm and said: "How would a child have any concept of time? How could Baocheng possibly know if you ask like that? Baocheng, did you see Mafa during the day or at night? What does Mafa look like?"

Yinreng gestured: "Sometimes during the day, sometimes at night. Mafa is bright, glowing, can't see clearly, hurts my eyes. Mafa nags, I don't understand, I don't like Mafa. When Ama and Wukumama are here, I can't see him."

Ah, this... Kangxi and the Grand Empress Dowager looked at each other again.

Bright? Glowing? What is this? Has he become a god or a Buddha?

They can't see him when they are there? Why? Could it be that Father/Son doesn't want to see me?

And what's this about sometimes day and sometimes night? Can ghosts come out during the day too?

Kangxi had a sudden inspiration: "Baocheng, could it be that you saw him in a dream?"

Yinreng held his head, cosplaying a confused Psyduck: "A dream? Is it a dream?"

"It's a visitation in a dream." The Grand Empress Dowager also guessed it. She sighed, her expression full of melancholy.

Kangxi patted Yinreng’s head in annoyance: "Why didn't you tell me?"

Yinreng said righteously: "You never asked!"

Kangxi: "..." He really wanted to spank this kid's little bottom.

Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s cheeks: "What did Mafa say when he visited you in your dream?"

Yinreng maintained his Psyduck pose and said vaguely: "A lot, I can't remember clearly."

The two giants of the imperial palace were speechless again.

"Then tell me what you do remember," Kangxi said. "Didn't you just remember it?"

Yinreng put his hands down, pretended to think hard for a while, and began to make things up intermittently.

"Mafa said, Ama used to wet the bed!"

Kangxi: "...I did not."

The Grand Empress Dowager: "No, he actually did. Continue, Baocheng."

"Mafa said, Baocheng should read less. Ama read until he coughed up blood, Baocheng shouldn't cough up blood."

Kangxi: "Cough, cough, cough... Baocheng, you still have to read."

The Grand Empress Dowager sighed: "Xuan Ye, Fulin has been watching you all along."

"Mafa said..." Yinreng paused, wondering if he should take this opportunity to gain more favor from Kangxi.

He knew that before this year, few children in the palace survived; after this year, the Emperor Father's sons and daughters would sprout up like bamboo shoots after rain, and he would no longer have to worry about heirs.

Yinreng wanted to claim some credit for himself, to prepare for a comfortable environment after he was eventually deposed and imprisoned.

But could he really pull off the acting? Yinreng felt a bit unsure.

The memories of that deposed crown prince from his previous-previous life were just memories. Yinreng watched them like a TV show; after finishing, he just knew a few more things, which didn't help his own growth.

And those twenty years that truly shaped his soul, well... *cough*, those twenty years of being spoiled—the first eighteen years were just worrying about the college entrance exam, a two-point line between home and school; the last two years in college were a four-point line between classroom, dormitory, library, and cafeteria. He hadn't even joined a club or dated a girlfriend.

With such a dull, boring, yet smooth and cozy life, Yinreng really couldn't handle palace intrigue, domestic drama, or court struggles.

If he claimed credit like this, would he just end up getting himself killed or "dying young"?

Yinreng’s hesitation was interpreted by the Grand Empress Dowager and Kangxi as him being dazed.

Yinreng often dazed off, and they were used to it.

For a child under three, it would be strange if he didn't daze off often.

Kangxi patted Yinreng’s soft little face: "Wake up, wake up, what else did Mafa say?"

Yinreng blinked and made up his mind.

Helping the Emperor Father keep his sons alive—even if he wasn't rewarded heavily, it was unlikely he would be "made to die young."

Besides, he didn't have the courage to commit suicide himself. If the Emperor Father really wanted him to "die young," maybe that would be a good thing.

Ama was soft-hearted toward children; he would definitely help him find a painless way to "die young."

He hoped that after being "made to die young," he could travel back to the modern era with his memories.

"Mafa... often fights with people," Yinreng blinked and said, "Fights with the pitch-black ones, Mafa is very good at fighting."

The smiles on Kangxi and the Grand Empress Dowager’s faces vanished.

Fighting? What kind of fighting? What could he possibly be fighting after he had already passed away?

"Mafa said, that is the female..." Yinreng frowned tightly, "Female what... curse?"

Kangxi’s arms holding Yinreng tightened: "Female what?"

Could it be some woman's witchcraft?

"Female... what... dragon vein?" Yinreng tried hard to furrow his brows, scrunching his little face into a ball to hide his lying expression, "Mafa said, the ancestors are not female, female? Occupying what energy? So female what is angry? Curse... pitch-black?"

Yinreng held his head and tilted it in confusion again.

Kangxi and the Grand Empress Dowager took a deep breath.

They finally understood why Yinreng kept seeing Father/Son in his dreams! Father/Son had very important information for the little chubby boy to convey!

But this little chubby boy was a fool! He didn't take it to heart at all!

If it hadn't been for the accidental mention of Shunzhi today, the little chubby boy wouldn't even have remembered!

But they couldn't blame Yinreng. What could you expect from a two-year-old? Especially when it was a dream visitation saying so many things a child couldn't understand.

Sigh!

Kangxi racked his brains to interpret Yinreng’s words: "Dragon vein? Ancestors? Could it be some woman among the ancestors?"

The Grand Empress Dowager, however, recalled a secret she had heard from Huang Taiji when she was still Consort Zhuang.

"It is Jurchen," the Grand Empress Dowager said in a low voice.

Kangxi was surprised: "Jurchen?!"

The Grand Empress Dowager gave Sumalagu a look. Sumalagu chased away the palace servants who had already retreated to the door of the Cining Palace and stood guard at the entrance herself.

Guwenxing also immediately took his leave and stood guard at the palace gate with Sumalagu.

In the massive palace, only the three of them—grandmother, father, and son—remained.

Kangxi sat up straight. He knew the Grand Empress Dowager was about to tell him a very important secret.

"Aisin Gioro is not a true descendant of the Jurchen; you should know this," the Grand Empress Dowager said.

Kangxi nodded. Aisin Gioro claimed to be descendants of the Jurchen to the outside world, and the Ming Dynasty also called them the Jianzhou Jurchen. In reality, "Jurchen" was a geographical concept, referring to those "barbaric tribes" in the Northeast beyond the borders.

The Sinicization of the Jin Dynasty Jurchen was quite profound. The "Jianzhou Jurchen," who were like savages back then, obviously could not be the true descendants of the Jin Dynasty Jurchen.

The Jianzhou Jurchen included people from various ethnic groups. When the Qing Dynasty called itself "Jin," it was just like every other dynasty—finding a prestigious ancestor for itself.

"Although I do not understand state affairs, Emperor Wen once said that the Great Qing is not a continuation of the Jin Dynasty, and the Qing people are not Jurchen; he unified the ethnic name as Manchu. Among the Eight Banners, whether Mongol, Han, or Jurchen, as long as they submit to the Great Qing, they are all Manchu," the Grand Empress Dowager said. "Perhaps Emperor Wen sensed something."

Emperor Wen was Huang Taiji, Kangxi’s paternal grandfather.

The Grand Empress Dowager said she didn't understand state affairs, but that was only during Huang Taiji's time. Now that she had been the Empress Dowager for two reigns, she certainly understood very well.

Perhaps politicians all love conspiracy theories; the Grand Empress Dowager quickly associated this with Huang Taiji’s abrupt change of the ethnic name.

Nominally, Huang Taiji did it for ethnic integration and to prepare for entering the Central Plains to become the ruler of the Han people, but whether it involved ghosts, gods, and dragon veins behind the scenes, who could say?

Kangxi fell into deep thought.

Emperors throughout history believed in fate and dragon veins. Whether it was the Nine Tripod Cauldrons and the Imperial Seal of ancient times, or the "recognizing ancestors," "protecting dragon veins," and "choosing imperial tombs" of various dynasties, all were ways to borrow and accumulate fortune.

Borrowing someone else's fortune might lead to a backlash from that fortune; this was normal. If one's own fortune became strong enough, one wouldn't care about these backlashes. The Great Qing was clearly not strong enough yet.

Kangxi thought of his father who died young, and then of his own children who died prematurely one after another. His clenched fists were so tight that his nails almost sank into his palms.

"Baocheng, where did you see the pitch-black ones?" Kangxi asked through gritted teeth.

Yinreng tried hard to make his face look even uglier to hide his awkward acting.

"Older brothers? Younger brothers?" Yinreng held his head, "Ama don't worry, they were all sucked away by me!"

Kangxi, who was gnashing his teeth, and the Grand Empress Dowager, whose heart was aching, were: "???"

Yinreng patted his little chest: "Mafa said, the Crown Prince is a latent dragon! I have dragon energy, I can attract the pitch-black ones, let me stay away from the pitch-black ones, Ama’s dragon energy can protect me! But older brothers get sick, younger brothers get sick, Ama taught me to be brotherly! Baocheng is a Baturu!"

The expressions of Kangxi and the Grand Empress Dowager went blank, as if struck by lightning.

Yinreng was still smug: "Baocheng is still small, the attraction isn't enough! Mafa said, older brothers and younger brothers need to be raised outside the palace. Next year, they can all come back! Ama’s sons, if they are healthy when they are born, they can live! Mafa said so!"

The Grand Empress Dowager said anxiously: "Xuan Ye! Fulin, he didn't mean to harm..."

Yinreng held his head and pretended to be a Psyduck, interrupting the Grand Empress Dowager: "But, I sucked away the pitch-black ones and saved my brothers, Mafa is not happy. Mafa even wanted to hit me? Good thing Mafa couldn't hit me. Why is Mafa not happy? I protected my brothers, I am a Baturu!"

The Grand Empress Dowager breathed a sigh of relief. So it wasn't Fulin who made Baocheng attract the curse; it was Baocheng acting on his own.

"Xuan Ye, there must be a way to turn this around, don't be anxious," the Grand Empress Dowager said calmly. "Summon the Great Lama and the Great Shaman to the palace."

The Grand Empress Dowager looked at the ignorant Yinreng and felt guilty for the trace of relief she had felt in her heart.

To the Grand Empress Dowager, all her great-grandsons were important. If sacrificing Yinreng could allow Kangxi’s future sons to live, she couldn't help but feel a sense of relief.

But for the current Xuan Ye... the Grand Empress Dowager looked at Kangxi’s ugly expression and sighed deeply in her heart.

"Ama?" Yinreng’s expression went blank, and he tugged at Kangxi’s sleeve, "Why are you unhappy? Baocheng did a good deed."

"A good deed?" Kangxi pressed Yinreng onto his lap.

Yinreng: "..."

Yinreng: "Waaaah!!"

...

The little milk bun Yinreng, for the first time in the two-plus years since his transmigration, had his pants pulled down and his bottom spanked.

This day was worth remembering.

100,000

Author's note:

It is common knowledge that children do not lie.

(It is common knowledge that children are the best at lying.)
