chapters.translated_text:
The news of Uya-shi’s pregnancy quickly spread throughout the inner palace.

Empress Tong, acting on the Grand Empress Dowager’s decree, ordered the Imperial Hospital to take the pulse of every consort. While no other pregnancies were discovered, several consorts were found to be suffering from serious illnesses.

When these consorts learned why they had been saved, they all prayed for the Crown Prince’s well-being in the small Buddhist shrine.

No matter how sour she felt inside, Empress Tong had to admit that this Crown Prince was truly too kind—so kind that he didn't seem like someone from the palace at all.

Her dowry mammy once again urged Empress Tong to get closer to the Crown Prince.

Empress Tong’s attitude finally softened: "We shall see. Whatever I do, I must wait until the Empress recovers from her illness."

Or until the Empress dies of her illness.

Although Empress Niohuru had been sickly ever since her miscarriage, it seemed she wasn't quite at the point of death yet.

Upon hearing that Empress Niohuru’s condition had improved, Kangxi pondered with a dark expression for a moment before going to the Cining Palace to tell the Grand Empress Dowager: "To bring good fortune to the Empress, we should promote some consorts and release some older palace maids. The Empress’s younger sister has served her well; she may be enfeoffed as a Pin."

The Grand Empress Dowager thought to herself that the Emperor truly loathed Empress Niohuru and wished for her to die sooner.

Coincidentally, that was exactly what she was thinking as well.

The Grand Empress Dowager’s kind smile was like that of a Bodhisattva in a temple: "The Emperor is benevolent; it is only right to do so."

And so, in early May of the 17th year of Kangxi, Kangxi once again bestowed grand titles upon the inner palace.

Empress Niohuru’s younger sister was enfeoffed as Wen Pin and resided in the Changchun Palace; Uya-shi was enfeoffed as De Pin and resided in the Yonghe Palace; Borjigit-shi was enfeoffed as Xuan Pin and resided in the Xianfu Palace. The remaining low-ranking consorts were granted titles by decree without the need for formal enfeoffment, so they will not be listed here.

Upon hearing this news, Yinreng sighed and lamented for a long time.

Since Uya-shi was enfeoffed as a Pin before the Fourth Prince was born, she would definitely raise the child herself after the birth; the Fourth Prince would not have such a miserable life this time around.

Thinking of the Fourth Prince’s childhood, Yinreng couldn't help but shed a tear of sympathy for him.

Later generations often said that Tongjia-shi was the Fourth Prince’s foster mother, as if he had lived like a half-legitimate son while she was alive, and only became an invisible figure in the palace after her death, but that wasn't actually the case.

As a consort and later Imperial Noble Consort without children of her own, Tongjia-shi had basically raised the children of low-ranking consorts as well as those of high-ranking consorts during their confinement.

For instance, the Eighth Prince Yinsi and the Fifth Prince Yinqi were both entrusted to Tongjia-shi to raise before being sent to the palaces of Consort Hui and the Empress Dowager, respectively.

When Tongjia-shi’s health declined due to the early death of her daughter, she wanted to return Yinzhen to his biological mother, who had by then been promoted to Consort De, but Consort De politely refused because she was busy caring for the sickly Sixth Prince.

After Tongjia-shi passed away, the eleven-year-old Yinzhen was again politely refused by Consort De, who was busy caring for the young Yintao, and was then taken by Kangxi to be raised by his side for a period of time.

Aside from the Crown Prince, Kangxi had only raised Yinzhen for a few years, likely out of sympathy for this son.

In this life, Yinzhen never felt true maternal love.

His biological mother abandoned him to take care of the Sixth and Fourteenth Princes;

Empress Xiaoyiren raised many sons and treated them all with kindness, so the love he received was not unique to him;

The Tongjia family, which he relied on for emotional support, almost entirely chose the Eighth Prince Yinsi;

Yinzhen was the one who was always being abandoned throughout his life.

Research from later generations suggests that some of Yongzheng’s overly manic deeds clearly stemmed from severe psychological illness.

He exhausted himself for state affairs while consuming alchemical pills until he died suddenly—wasn't that just his way of trying to prove his worth?

To prove that he would be a good emperor and that those who abandoned him were blind.

Yinreng put away his sympathy for the Fourth Prince.

Forget it, psychological illness or whatever—who doesn't have it? His past life, the Eldest Brother’s past life, many of his brothers in past lives—who didn't have some sort of psychological issue? No one had the right to pity anyone else.

In short, it was all the scumbag father’s fault.

"Hmm? What are you daydreaming about?" Kangxi, who was reading history books to Yinreng, noticed his son’s eyes were a bit unfocused.

Yinreng replied reflexively: "Father is a bad father."

Kangxi: "???"

He put down the book and pulled Yinreng onto his lap, pinning him down.

Yinreng, who had snapped back to reality: "..."

He immediately became alert, putting his hands together and bowing repeatedly like a kitten that had made a mistake: "Father is the best father in the world! Father is the kindest and most amiable father in the world! Father is the most wise and martial father in the world..."

"Too late." Kangxi sneered and "smacked" Yinreng’s little bottom.

The sound of the patting through his trousers was very loud. Yinreng’s howling was quite loud, but it was all thunder and no rain; he wailed for a long time until his throat was hoarse, yet not a single tear was seen, and Kangxi still had to serve his son water.

Yinreng gulped down a cup of water, and Kangxi rubbed his forehead: "I’m reading to you, and you call me a bad father? Hmm?"

After finishing the water, Yinreng wiped his mouth with Kangxi’s sleeve, only to be pushed away in disgust: "I remembered what the Eldest Brother said and accidentally repeated it."

Sorry, Eldest Brother, please be the scapegoat. You did say it, anyway.

Kangxi was amused: "Does he hate studying that much?"

Yinreng said with an old-fashioned air: "It’s because the tutors teach so poorly. We aren't taking the imperial examinations; we only need to understand the meaning behind the stories in the classics and histories. What’s the point of memorizing those books? Besides, the annotations in those classics are written by later generations; how can we guarantee their accuracy? It would be better to think for myself; if others can compile them, I can too."

Kangxi flicked Yinreng’s forehead: "Learning more about the thoughts of the sages will only be beneficial. As for understanding, what could you possibly understand at your age? You must memorize them first."

Yinreng curled his lip. Imperial princes in the Qing palace started their studies at six; he wouldn't suffer the same pain as the Eldest Prince, who had to read, copy, and recite everything a hundred times, would he?

No, he must find a way to save himself before he starts his formal studies.

Yinreng’s eyes darted around; he was clearly up to no good. Kangxi was looking forward to seeing where Yinreng would cause trouble next.

The one in the Kunning Palace just wouldn't die, and the delay was starting to test Kangxi’s patience. Only playing with his son could make him feel slightly better.

In the Kunning Palace.

When Empress Niohuru learned that Kangxi had bestowed grand titles upon the inner palace while she was critically ill, she was so shocked and terrified that she nearly collapsed, only to be comforted by her sister, who had been enfeoffed as Wen Pin.

Empress Niohuru was a daughter cultivated by her family with a singular focus on their interests; her personality was sharp, competitive, and quite fierce.

As the second daughter, Wen Pin was caught in the age gap between her siblings. Before the Empress had her accident, she was an invisible person in the family, and her personality was nurtured to be very gentle and magnanimous—the two extremes compared to the Empress.

Wen Pin persuaded her: "Sister, as long as you are alive, you are the Empress. Whoever becomes the Emperor in the future must honor you as the Empress Dowager. What is this current grievance? As long as you endure it, the Emperor’s anger will subside, and if we keep a low profile in the palace, we will survive."

Empress Niohuru wept: "What if I survive? I have offended the Emperor and the Crown Prince; the family is likely hoping for my death so they can make room for you."

Hearing these heart-piercing words, Wen Pin didn't even raise an eyebrow.

She knew what kind of personality her sister had and was long used to it. Besides, the Niohuru family did indeed hope for her sister to die; that was the truth.

"Sister, the position of Empress you hold now is the last and only chance for our Niohuru family to touch the position of Empress. If you are gone, it is impossible for another Niohuru Empress to emerge in the inner palace," Wen Pin said calmly. "This has nothing to do with whether I can be favored in the future. The Emperor is wise; it is impossible for one inner palace to have two Empresses of the same surname. If you are counting on a woman from the Niohuru family to give birth to a prince who can replace the Crown Prince and win that Empress Dowager position..."

Wen Pin paused, a mocking look on her face: "There are many women in the palace, and the Emperor is so young and already has three healthy princes. Forgive me, sister, but I have neither the confidence nor the ability to win in this den of tigers and wolves."

Empress Niohuru’s crying stopped.

After a long while, she said in a hoarse voice: "Is there really no other way?"

Wen Pin said calmly: "Yes. No way."

Empress Niohuru sighed: "Then I must hold on, I must hold on."

Wen Pin stood up: "Then I will go watch them brew the medicine. Sister, rest for a while."

Wen Pin had complained about being sent into the palace by her family even though she had already found a suitor. But after complaining, life had to go on.

Whether it was because she couldn't bear to see her sister forced to death or to make her own life in the palace easier, she had to find a way to save her sister.

As long as her sister let go of her worries, it shouldn't be difficult to recover from the illness.

Should be.

Wen Pin watched the bubbling medicine, her eyes as still as an ancient well.

After serving the Empress her medicine and putting her to sleep, Wen Pin refused the small sedan chair and walked back to the Changchun Palace alone with one palace maid and one eunuch.

This was the only time she could get some fresh air every day.

As she walked out of the Kunning Palace, Wen Pin looked up at the sky.

The palace walls were very high, and the sky was framed into a square, as if it had been severed.

Wen Pin watched the clouds fly into the square sky, looking like a painting on paper.

But the clouds could fly off the paper with the wind, while she was already a person in the painting.

"Master Wen Pin, watch your step," the head maid said.

Yinreng: "..." Mongolian girls are truly amazing. I can’t let the Eldest Brother and Xuan Pin continue to interact.

Kangxi: "..."

He looked down at the bad son in his arms who was looking up, and then fiercely knocked on the bad son’s head.

I will definitely not lose to her!

There must be one high-ranking Mongolian consort in the palace.

As long as Yinreng was there, he was that bold. Even if Kangxi didn't speak, he dared to run.

Kangxi did not stop them.

He laughed and scolded: "Two little rascals."

Xuan Pin lowered her head, her face flushed, twisting the corners of her clothes with both hands.

Seeing Xuan Pin’s shy appearance, Kangxi felt even more restless.

Although the Grand Empress Dowager knew that the Qing Dynasty could not have a Mongolian Crown Prince, it would be good if a Mongolian consort gave birth to a prince or even a princess.

When she learned that the reason for Xuan Pin’s sudden favor was that Yinreng had instigated Kangxi to compete with Xuan Pin in archery, she hugged Yinreng and kissed him twice regardless of the rules, and opened her treasury to send Yinreng a box of gemstones to play with as marbles.

Yinreng’s eyes went straight.

However, after he sighed, he remembered that the gemstones couldn't be sold, and he couldn't spend money since he couldn't leave the palace, so he immediately lost interest.

He had the people in the palace make the gemstones into chains and sent them back to the Grand Empress Dowager, and also gave some to the Empress Dowager and Kangxi.

Kangxi was puzzled: "Why are you giving these to me?"

Yinreng joked in an old-fashioned way: "Father can reward them to the consorts in the palace. Father always says the inner treasury is empty and can't pick out good rewards. Don’t worry, your son will support you."

Kangxi: "..." He didn't know whether to be angry or moved. Why was this kid so lovable?

Kangxi actually rewarded the gemstone chains and pointed out in his oral decree that this was a filial gift from the Crown Prince to the various palace consorts.

Even Empress Niohuru, who was recuperating, was not left out.

Empress Niohuru stared at the gemstone bracelet in a daze, thinking of the Crown Prince’s kindness, thinking of her lost child, and was both regretful and sad, falling ill again.

When Kangxi learned of this, he felt even more disgusted with Empress Niohuru. The Crown Prince gave you a gift, and you fell ill? What are you doing?! Are you trying to use your life to frame the Crown Prince?

After Kangxi was completely tired of Empress Niohuru, he found an excuse to have Wen Pin close her doors and copy scriptures, forbidding her from serving Empress Niohuru again.

Wen Pin held the Buddhist scriptures and choked up silently.

Half a month later, Empress Niohuru passed away.

Kangxi, citing the fact that the Revolt of the Three Feudatories had not yet been quelled, simplified the funeral, which was slightly inferior to the old funeral rites of Empress Renxiao.

The Grand Empress Dowager wanted to cry at the mausoleum, but was persuaded back by Kangxi on the grounds that she was too old, and the funeral was presided over by the Empress Dowager.

At that time, Xuan Pin was pregnant and, along with the pregnant Consort De, was granted the grace of only needing to cry at the mausoleum for one day before returning to the palace to rest.

The three princes also returned to the palace after only one day of mourning because they were too young and physically fragile.

But Kangxi himself completed the entire funeral process, so the ministers outside the palace did not think Kangxi had neglected Empress Niohuru, only that Kangxi valued his offspring.

Afterward, Kangxi bestowed the posthumous title "Empress Xiao'an."

Peace and smoothness are called "An." The Niohuru family breathed a sigh of relief. This posthumous title was considered to have fulfilled the honor of Empress Xiao'an after her death, and the Emperor did not blame Empress Xiao'an for the miscarriage.

Those in the palace who knew the truth about Empress Niohuru’s miscarriage also sighed that the Emperor was truly magnanimous.

Only Yinreng had a strange expression, criticizing Kangxi for being petty in his heart.

Empress Xiaozhao became Empress Xiao'an, and he’s not petty?

The next day, Yin Reng and Yin Ti feasted on milk porridge and meat buns, then went to tease Yin Zhi, who was full and busy fussing with his own little feet.

Yin Zhi laughed when he saw Yin Reng, but as soon as he turned his head and saw Yin Ti, his face changed, glaring at him as if he were about to pounce and bite.

Yin Ti sneered, picked up a soft cushion, and fought a great battle with Yin Zhi, just like teasing a dog.

Yin Reng protected Yin Zhi, preventing him from pouncing too far and falling off the couch.

Yin Zhi’s wet nurse stood to the side with her hands down, letting the Crown Prince take over her job.

She had already accumulated many things in her heart to tell her mistress. The Crown Prince was truly the most sensible and kindest child she had ever seen; the Third Prince being close to the Crown Prince was definitely the right choice! Her mistress truly had a good eye!

Yin Zhi and Yin Ti were both full of energy, so they fought until they were both exhausted.

The two lay panting on the couch, looking at each other with a hint of mutual appreciation.

Who knows where a one-year-old Yin Zhi would get mutual appreciation; he was probably assimilated by Yin Ti.

Yin Reng directed the eunuchs and wet nurses to change the damp clothes for Yin Ti and Yin Zhi, and brought warm milk to soothe their throats and quench their thirst.

Little children need to drink more milk to grow tall.

The Empress Dowager came to the side hall to visit her great-grandsons and happened to see Yin Reng directing the wet nurses and eunuchs to take care of Yin Ti and Yin Zhi like a little adult; her tired face revealed a gratified smile.

"Let's go back, don't disturb them." The Empress Dowager smiled.

Sumalagu smiled: "This servant finally understands why His Majesty searches the whole palace for the Crown Prince whenever he is too tired from work or in a bad mood. Just by looking at the Crown Prince, no matter how tired or bad his mood is, he can become happy."

The Empress Dowager nodded with a smile.

After smiling, she thought of the child in Xuan Pin’s womb, not knowing if it was a boy or a girl.

As soon as Xuan Pin became pregnant, the thoughts of the Mongol nobles, which had previously subsided, became active again, and even the Empress Dowager was stammering about some things in front of her.

The Empress Dowager’s face darkened, and she sneered in her heart.

When Fulin was still alive, she was still young, Mongol power was still strong, and the Emperor had not yet fully controlled the court. Even then, even though she filled the harem with Mongol women, was it useful?

If it wasn't useful even then, what could one hope for now that this grandson, who could purge powerful officials and pacify the Three Feudatories at such a young age, had taken over?

Besides, she was already old and didn't have many years left to live.

Once she died, those Mongol nobles and Mongol concubines who dared to make the Emperor uncomfortable would all be liquidated.

How Empress Niuhuru died—others might not know, but the Empress Dowager couldn't be unaware.

The Empress Dowager had already seen clearly during the Shunzhi era. Whether it was the Mongol nobility or the Manchu nobility, no one could ever be above the Emperor. It was a pity that when she saw it clearly, Fulin had already died early from smallpox, and the mother and son didn't even have a chance to ease their relationship.

The Empress Dowager closed her eyes, restraining the sharpness in them.

"Clean up the people around the Empress Dowager more; she is a fool." The Empress Dowager said, "Also, make it clear to Xuan Pin not to have thoughts she shouldn't have, and ruin the little bit of affection Xuan Ye has finally developed for her."

Sumalagu said: "The Empress has already realized her mistake and is reflecting on it; please rest assured, Empress Dowager. As for Xuan Pin..."

Sumalagu paused and smiled bitterly: "You don't need to worry about Xuan Pin even more."

The Empress Dowager’s face turned black: "What happened to her now?"

Sumalagu sighed: "She heard from somewhere that concubines can leave the palace to live with their sons. And so, she has already started imagining the future."

The Empress Dowager exerted force, and her prayer beads snapped.

You are already imagining your husband's death?! Are you tired of living and want to die now?!

The Empress Dowager turned around expressionlessly: "I'd better spend more time with Baocheng."

Sumalagu smiled bitterly: "Yes." She also wanted to spend more time with the Crown Prince.

When the Empress Dowager returned to the side hall, Yin Ti was waving a small wooden sword in the room, practicing martial arts with "swish, swish, swish" sounds; Yin Reng had found a zither from somewhere and was plucking out off-key notes "plonk, plonk, plonk," while Yin Zhi provided "ah, ah, ah" accompaniment.

The Empress Dowager’s stern face immediately melted, her eyes becoming incredibly gentle and kind.

"Uku Mama!" Yin Reng stopped abusing the zither and opened his arms toward the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager immediately took a few steps forward and pulled Yin Reng into her arms: "Oh, my dear Baocheng, you can play the zither?"

Yin Reng said righteously: "No! Just plucking it!"

The Empress Dowager said: "It sounds good even if you just pluck it! Baoqing’s sword dance is also good, he has your Khan Ama’s momentum."

Yin Ti, who was just waving the small wooden sword randomly, lifted his head: "That's right!"

Yin Zhi tilted his head and clapped: "Ah, ah, Mama..."

Yin Reng corrected: "Uku, Mama."

Yin Zhi clapped his little hands twice more: "Ku, Ku, Mama."

Yin Reng corrected again: "U, Ku, Mama."

Yin Zhi stopped clapping and tried hard: "U! Ku! Mama!"

"Brother is so good and so smart!" Yin Reng looked up, "Uku Mama, listen! Brother can talk now!"

The Empress Dowager hurriedly pulled Yin Zhi into her arms too: "Yes, yes! Little Three is too smart."

Little Three... pfft, cough, oh no, I've been poisoned by the internet of my past life and my thoughts are impure. Yin Reng suppressed a laugh.

Yin Ti moved back a few steps.

He didn't want to be pulled into the old lady's arms; it was quite uncomfortable.

The Empress Dowager coaxed the three little ones for a while, then ran out of energy and was helped back to rest by Sumalagu.

Yin Reng sat back at the zither and plucked the string closest to him "plonk, plonk, plonk," Yin Ti threw away the wooden sword and switched to waving a small whip, and Yin Zhi continued "ah, ah, ah." The three children continued to play music and dance.

Gu Wenxing’s expectant eyes became dead silent.

Empress Dowager, didn't you notice that this zither is His Majesty’s favorite Tang Dynasty antique? His Majesty himself couldn't bear to play it.

Forget it. Since the zither could end up in the Crown Prince’s hands, His Majesty probably tacitly allowed it.

Gu Wenxing put aside his heartache for the Tang Dynasty zither and relaxed to watch the three babies perform.

This was a performance even His Majesty hadn't seen. If he wrote to His Majesty about it, His Majesty would definitely overturn his vinegar jar.

Gu Wenxing thought mischievously.

"Phew." After continuing to play music and dance for a while, Yin Reng was tired.

He took a hot bath and tucked himself into the warm quilt.

Then Yin Reng realized that today he had still forgotten to think about the things he had been worried about before.

Uh...

Yin Reng turned over. Forget it, I can't remember, it probably wasn't anything important, right?

Yin Reng "forgot in the morning" and "remembered at night" for several days in a row, until Kangxi sent word that he was already on his way back.

The concubines had long since returned, and the First Prince and Third Prince had returned to their respective mothers' sides. Only Kangxi had to put on a show and stayed for a few more days before returning.

The weather in the capital was gradually entering deep winter; although it wasn't snowing yet, the Imperial Garden was already withered everywhere, a scene of desolation that brought a trace of sorrow to the faces of the concubines strolling through the garden.

Some concubines with higher cultural literacy twisted withered leaves in their hands, reciting poems about the sadness of autumn and winter, which made Yin Reng want to recite a poem too.

But after thinking and thinking, he could only think of "Qin Yuan Chun · Snow."

Cough, forget it. He wasn't worthy.

The older brother and younger brother had returned to their mothers' sides, and they had their mothers to dote on them. Only Yin Reng was left in a small corner of the Imperial Garden, kicking his little feet and staring blankly at the withered branches and fallen leaves.

Gu Wenxing thought that if His Majesty saw this scene, he didn't know how heartbroken he would be.

Yin Reng’s eyes were unfocused, but it wasn't because of loneliness.

With no older or younger brother around to make noise, Yin Reng could finally calm down and recall some things.

"It's November, right?" Yin Reng asked.

Gu Wenxing thought the Crown Prince was missing Kangxi and hurriedly replied: "Yes, Your Highness, His Majesty will be back soon."

Yin Reng took a deep breath.

November.

He finally remembered.

This November was when he was supposed to get smallpox.

He had now survived cowpox, so he wasn't afraid even if he encountered smallpox again. But the older brother and the third brother hadn't been vaccinated yet.

The smallpox virus was an infectious disease; it wouldn't appear out of thin air, but spread through contact and droplets. He had gotten smallpox because he had come into contact with the smallpox virus in the palace.

Even if he had already had smallpox in advance, at the time point when he was supposed to get it, there would definitely be a smallpox infection event in the palace.

Yin Reng’s heart chilled, and he stretched out his hands to Gu Wenxing: "Quickly carry me to see Uku Mama, I have something very important!"

Gu Wenxing was puzzled but immediately obeyed.

He carried Yin Reng and, disregarding palace etiquette, ran all the way into the Cining Palace.

The Empress Dowager was puzzled: "What is so urgent? Is someone bullying the Crown Prince?"

Yin Reng hooked his little finger at the Empress Dowager: "Uku Mama, lower your head, lower your head, I have something I can only tell Uku Mama!"

The Empress Dowager had someone bring Yin Reng into her arms and let him whisper in her ear.

"Uku Mama, the curse has strengthened; Mafa says there may be an epidemic in the palace." Yin Reng brought out the universal scapegoat, Shunzhi.

The Empress Dowager hugged Yin Reng tightly: "Is this true?"

Yin Reng said: "I don't know. That's what Mafa said."

I can't guarantee it; why don't you go ask in front of Mafa’s spirit tablet?

The Empress Dowager held Yin Reng and frowned in thought for a while; it was better to believe it than not.

It just so happened that an Empress had just died in the palace, and it was near the end of the year, so she could use the excuse of clearing away bad luck to do a deep cleaning of the entire palace.

"Your Ama will be back tomorrow; we'll discuss it with your Ama then." The Empress Dowager said calmly.

Yin Reng nodded.

Indeed, there was no rush for this moment.

But man proposes, God disposes. On his way back, Kangxi encountered a rare winter rain and landslide that blocked the road, and the Empress Dowager also fell ill due to overwork after Kangxi left.

The matter of the curse could not be told to the concubines, even if they had already guessed it. There was actually no one to preside over the epidemic prevention in the palace.

Yin Reng was anxious, running to his older and younger brothers every day, looking at everyone as if they were carrying the smallpox virus, so anxious that blisters formed on his lips.

The Empress Dowager forced herself to stay alert and issued an imperial decree for Hui Pin and Rong Pin to send the children to the side hall of the Cining Palace.

"You do it! I know you can!" The Empress Dowager coughed and said, "Your Mafa must have taught you!"

The Empress Dowager now completely believed that Shunzhi was teaching Yin Reng in his dreams.

Through observation, she suspected that Yin Reng could talk to Shunzhi even when not in a dream.

The epidemic prevention matter just happened to confirm her guess.

Yin Reng hesitated for a moment. He was worried about exposing too much.

If he exposed too much, Kangxi would definitely have higher expectations for him in his childhood and give him more opportunities to show himself;

But when he grew older, Kangxi’s wariness of him would become deeper, and their father-son relationship would be even more precarious.

Should he play dumb and muddle through?

Yin Reng thought of the older brother who was now talking about his younger brother all day, and the third brother who was babbling, and he loosened his clenched little fists.

"Okay." Yin Reng looked up, revealing a maturity that did not match his age.

The Empress Dowager was startled, seeing the shadow of Kangxi.

No, this should be... could it be...

The Empress Dowager had a guess in her heart but didn't dare to say it out loud. She was afraid that if she said it, her fantasy would disappear.

Under the Empress Dowager’s arrangement, Yin Reng began to issue orders in her name.

Yin Reng first had the side hall of the Cining Palace disinfected with quicklime water and Chinese medicine with bactericidal effects, then he and the First Prince and Third Prince lived in one room, and the two pregnant women lived together in another.

"De Pin, Xuan Pin, I'm sorry, I've wronged you for a while." Yin Reng apologized personally, "I cannot explain the reason, please bear with this period of time."

"This concubine believes in the Crown Prince." De Pin, with her big belly, said with a firm expression, "This concubine will take good care of Xuan Pin, the Crown Prince need not worry."

Xuan Pin was in much better spirits now, almost no longer having morning sickness. She smiled and said: "I know you are capable, I will listen to you. Don't worry, my strength has returned, I won't add to your trouble. Sister De Pin, my pregnancy is shorter than yours, I should be the one taking care of you."

Yin Reng breathed a sigh of relief. If the two pregnant concubines didn't make trouble, most of the problem was solved.

After Yin Reng had the two princes and two pregnant concubines move, he immediately combed through the people serving them.

Taking pulses, checking temperatures, observing faces for pox, asking who they had been in contact with... anyone with the slightest suspicion was temporarily transferred away from the Cining Palace.

After combing through, he sent imperial physicians to wait in a small house outside the Cining Palace. The Cining Palace was sealed, and no one could enter or leave at will.

Several high-ranking concubines wanted to go to the Cining Palace to inquire about news, but they were all blocked outside the palace by people sent by the Empress Dowager.

Yin Reng’s actions made the harem panic, and even the outer court heard rumors.

But the Empress Dowager’s prestige was heavy, and under her strong pressure, no one dared to complain.

Tong Guifei had no children, and seeing that these matters revolved around the princes and pregnant concubines, she let go and stopped caring about it, staying behind closed doors to live her own life, waiting for Kangxi to return.

Hui Pin was anxious and went to consult Rong Pin.

But Rong Pin was as calm as a wooden statue, as if it wasn't her son who had been taken away.

"What is this all about! What exactly is the Empress Dowager doing!" Hui Pin was so anxious she lost her mind.

Rong Pin put down her prayer beads and said: "It's useless for you to be anxious; you might as well stay in the palace and wait for the Emperor to return."

Hui Pin said impatiently: "I know, of course I know, but..."

"Believe in the Crown Prince." Seeing Hui Pin getting worked up, Rong Pin, remembering that the First Prince had been good to the Third Prince during her time away from the palace, gave a hint, "The Empress Dowager is ill, the Empress has no such courage."

Hui Pin was stunned: "How old is the Crown Prince?"

Rong Pin said: "The Crown Prince is someone taught by the Emperor himself."

Hui Pin said nothing.

"Go back and wait for news." Rong Pin said, "The Crown Prince has an excellent relationship with the First Prince and Third Prince, no need to worry."

Hui Pin sighed: "I know."

Knowing it but still anxious! She suspected that someone was harming her son, but she didn't know any news and could only wait passively for the result, which was truly heart-wrenching.

Why didn't the Crown Prince tell the truth? Even if other concubines didn't mention it, she and Rong Pin would definitely help the Crown Prince to protect their sons.

Why did the Crown Prince have to say nothing and make everyone panic?

After Yin Reng handled the affairs of the Cining Palace, he began his next move.

First, he sealed the various palaces in the inner palace, letting healthy eunuchs deliver food, garbage, and chamber pots daily, and forbade palace servants from visiting each other privately;

Then, he used the Empress Dowager’s imperial decree to have the concubines in charge of each palace conduct a health census of the people serving them, and disinfect and fumigate the palaces;

Finally, he arranged for imperial physicians to diagnose palace servants who might have health problems, and all medical expenses were pulled from his own father’s inner treasury.

The Empress Dowager wanted to open her own treasury, but Yin Reng said: "Doing favors for the palace in Ama’s name is just right for accumulating blessings for Ama."

The Empress Dowager then gave up.

Yin Reng ordered all palace servants to face the Qianqing Palace and kowtow to thank Kangxi for his grace before taking medicine.

Thus, there were rumors in the palace that the great health census in the palace was Kangxi’s grace to the people in the palace because he was saddened by the Empress’s death.

As it spread, the news reached outside the palace. The commoners all praised Kangxi as a benevolent monarch, and Kangxi’s name for benevolence was even carried to other places by merchants and travelers.

Because Yin Reng was still young, everything was done in the name of the Empress Dowager and Kangxi. Except for the two people involved, De Pin and Xuan Pin, only Hui Pin and Rong Pin, because their sons often spent time with the Crown Prince, knew the Crown Prince relatively well and guessed some things. Therefore, all the benevolence was collected by the Empress Dowager and Kangxi.

Yin Reng hid behind the scenes, deep in merit and fame.

"Brother, what exactly are you doing? Is it about the curse?"

Oh, besides De Pin, Xuan Pin, Hui Pin, and Rong Pin, the First Prince had also come to understand some things.

Yin Reng forced himself to maintain the rationality of an adult every day, his head aching faintly, his energy and physical strength almost at the edge of exhaustion, all relying on tonics and frantic eating to continue his life.

"Brother, don't worry." Yin Reng said perfunctorily, "It will pass soon."

"Do you know how bad your complexion is right now!" Yin Ti said angrily, "You put on powder and rouge when you go out, not letting Uku Mama know. You also know Uku Mama would worry! What is more important than your body!"

"I'm fine, just tired. It will be fine after this period of time." Yin Reng comforted, "Soon, soon, it will be fine immediately."

"Fine what! Tell me, what is it!" Yin Ti lifted his hem and sat in front of Yin Reng, not allowing Yin Reng to leave, "If you don't tell me, I won't allow you to go out!"

Yin Reng persuaded him nicely: "There's really nothing, trust me, Brother."

Yin Ti said coldly: "I don't!"

Yin Reng: "..." Oh no, Brother’s stubborn temper is up.

"It's about what you think. Some things only I can do." Yin Reng had to say perfunctorily, "It will pass soon. I heard the road has been cleared, and Khan Ama will be back soon."

Yin Ti’s eyes turned red, not knowing if it was from being angered by Yin Reng: "There are so many people in the palace, there is the Empress Dowager, the Empress, the Guifei, E-niang, many concubines, the Imperial Household Department, the Imperial Hospital... why are you showing off?"

"Oh, it's really nothing. When it's over, I'll just sleep..." Before Yin Reng finished speaking, Gu Wenxing ran in stumbling.

Gu Wenxing rarely panicked, Yin Reng’s face sank, and he stepped over from Yin Ti’s side.

Yin Ti hurriedly stood up, patted his butt, and followed Yin Reng out.

"Crown Prince, Crown Prince, heaven..." Gu Wenxing saw Yin Ti also following Yin Reng out, and his words immediately retracted.

Yin Ti said urgently: "Speak! What is there that I cannot hear!"

Yin Reng glanced at Yin Ti and sighed: "Speak."

Gu Wenxing caught his breath, his voice trembling: "It’s smallpox. Smallpox has been discovered in the palace."

Yin Ti was stunned for a moment, then suddenly turned his head to look at Yin Reng.

Yin Reng had one hand behind his back, the other clenched in front of him, his chin slightly tucked, his thin lips pursed into a cold sneer: "Investigate!"

"It took so long to discover that someone had smallpox; someone must have deliberately concealed it!"

Yin Reng’s child voice sounded unnatural after being deliberately lowered, but his actions, his expression, and his tone were so much like Kangxi’s extreme anger that Gu Wenxing and Yin Ti actually broke out in a cold sweat on their backs.

And the Empress Dowager, who had rushed over regardless of her illness upon hearing the news of smallpox, saw this scene, but what came to her mind was not Kangxi.

100,000

chapters.source_text:
太皇太后屏住呼吸，不敢说话。
她害怕自己一说话，幻影就会消失。
胤礽觉察到了有人出现。
他回过头看着满脸震惊的太皇太后，知道自己泄露太过，眼眸不由躲闪了一瞬，头也微微侧开。
这种条件反射的躲闪动作，让太皇太后更加确定自己的猜测。
人多口杂，太皇太后收敛心神，扶着嬷嬷的手颤颤巍巍走到胤礽面前。
“此事交由哀家处理，太子快去休息。”太皇太后一边说一边观察胤礽的神色。
胤礽皱眉。
太皇太后现在正在病中，又没有传染病基本防护意识，他怎么能放心将此事交给太皇太后？
但如果顶撞太皇太后，等阿玛回来肯定会斥责自己，甚至会为了自己现在展现出的过于妖孽的能力而疑惑，甚至警惕。
等等，这不是一件好事吗？
自己救了人，展现出了妖孽的能力，引起了阿玛的警惕，阿玛肯定既会废太子，又会对自己愧疚补偿！
“太皇太后请回。您是宫里主心骨，应安心养病，此事交于我。”胤礽为了让自己显得更加靠谱，没有叫乌库妈妈，而是称呼得更为正式。
胤褆吓得眼睛都瞪圆了。
太子弟弟居然怼上了太皇太后？他胆子怎么这么大！
胤褆忙想替胤礽圆场求情，却见太皇太后不但没有生气，甚至眼圈都红了，好像很感动？
很、很感动？
是感动吗？怎么感觉太皇太后有点难过？
“别说了，太皇太后都伤心了。”胤褆忙道。
胤礽愣了一下，抬头看向太皇太后。
他看到太皇太后的眼神中蕴含着悲伤、怀念、愧疚，甚至还带了一点点委屈。
胤礽眉头一皱，直觉不对。
事情有点出乎他的预料了。
他的脑子急剧转动，几乎垮过了前世的大学生，直接冲着前前世的原配置太子脑子去了。
胤礽眼睛睁圆，不可置信地看向太皇太后。
而太皇太后看到他的神情变化，更加确定了。
她伸出手，死死抓住胤礽的右手：“你、你……”
太皇太后知道自己不能叫出那个名字，但她现在却抑制不住自己叫出那个名字的冲动。
胤礽看着太皇太后祈求的眼神，心头一慌，条件反射抽出手。
他一将手抽出来，太皇太后的眼泪终于控制不住，顺着眼角的皱纹溢出、滴落。
胤褆脑子懵了。
至、至于吗？！太子弟弟也没说什么吧！为什么太皇太后会哭了！
胤礽忙把自己的右手放回了太皇太后手心，并踮起脚，用另一只手擦拭太皇太后眼角的泪痕。
“此事交给我。我会保护好他们。”胤礽猜到太皇太后此刻反常的原因了。
太皇太后怕不是以为自己被鬼附身了。
被祖先鬼皇玛法顺治皇帝附身了。
都怪自己天天嚷着“玛法说”，这下自己表现得过于成熟，才被人以为鬼附身了。
不过胤礽并不慌张。这在他的计划中。
虽然有祖宗附身这种事，比他自己才华横溢危险多了，小时候会让地位稳固，长大了估计就会被砍了，就算康熙再疼他，也忌讳这些神神叨叨的事。
所以他很快就会让顺治下线，下线的机会他已经想好了。
现在趁着太皇太后认错人，他现在正好利用一下。
胤礽心中闪过“利用”这个词的时候，心里一阵不舒服，眼神也有了一瞬黯然。
前前世的黑暗记忆除了给了他适应这个时代的学识和常识之外，也让他的思维不由朝着那个冷酷疯狂的太子接近。
前前世的自己，毕竟是康熙亲自教出来的未来帝王。
帝王心术，冷酷无情，所有的人所有的事都能被算计利用。
胤礽眼中一闪而过的痛苦让太皇太后心一慌，握着胤礽的手不由松了开来。
胤礽收回手，没有继续理睬太皇太后。
他继续发号施令，命令整个后宫都动起来，将天花疫情消灭在萌芽中。
太皇太后强忍着不适站直身体。她在小小的胤礽身后，就像是一尊坚不可摧的保护神。
最了解太皇太后的苏麻喇姑眼中闪过一丝诧异。
她看着这曾祖母和玄孙二人，眼前的情景渐渐和以前的画面重合。
是太皇太后和康熙皇帝。
也是曾经的太后和顺治皇帝。
胤褆眉头紧皱。
他眼睛死死地看着胤礽，看着胤礽有条不紊的安排一切，直到所有事情安排完毕，胤礽抬脚准备去太医院问太花疫情详情时，胤褆拉住了胤礽的衣角。
胤礽疑惑回头。
胤褆声色俱厉，身体不断颤抖：“你、你是谁！我的弟弟呢？我的弟弟他怎么……”
太皇太后大惊失色：“大阿哥！”
猜到了情况的苏麻喇姑立刻上前抱住胤褆的嘴，不让胤褆再说话。
胤褆狠狠踹了苏麻喇姑一脚，一口咬到苏麻喇姑手上。
“哎哟！”苏麻喇姑松手，“赶紧把大阿哥抱进去，大阿哥被天花吓得魇住了！”
“你不是太子弟弟，把弟弟还给我……呜呜……”胤褆挣脱苏麻喇姑之后，朝着胤礽扑了过去。
两个五大三粗的嬷嬷拦住了胤褆，捂着胤褆的嘴，把胤褆抱了起来。
胤礽抬起头，神情无悲无喜，眼神幽深，仿佛眼底是一汪深渊。
胤褆吓得浑身狠狠一颤，眼泪和鼻涕泡泡同时冒了出来。
他使劲挣扎，想要继续扑向胤礽。
“太子无事。”胤礽收起冷漠，眼神回暖，带着无奈的语气轻笑道，“别担心。”
胤褆停止了挣扎。他抖得更厉害了。
“放心，此事绝对不会传出去。”太皇太后表情狠厉地扫了周围一眼。
“孩童六岁之前都有通天彻地之能，但仅限于血脉至亲，且身上阳气微弱者。”胤礽移开视线，压低声音道，“既然您已经发现，帮我给玄烨带句话。玄烨身上龙气环绕，我无法直接与他交流。胤礽之后可能身体羸弱，不堪为太子。若到了那时，给胤礽一个带温泉的大庄子当圈禁地吧。”
胤礽的声音很低，只有靠近他的太皇太后听到了。
太皇太后眼眸微闪，俯下、身压低声音道：“你、福临、额娘我……”
胤礽侧开头，闭上眼：“对不起。”
说完，他头也不回地离开。
胤礽走上慈宁宫外早就等候着的小轿子。等轿子门帘一落下，他就抱头蹲守。
啊啊啊啊啊啊好尴尬啊，尴尬得脚趾都抠出另一座慈宁宫了啊！
恢复前前世的疯太子模样的装逼很尴尬，冒充顺治就更尴尬了！
我为什么要这么做？！我的脑子是不是又抽了！
一定是我最近精力消耗过度，脑细胞消耗过度，变成智障了！
太皇太后怎么会认不出顺治，你多说多错，太皇太后肯定已经发现了！
胤礽你是个大白痴！你的脑子被僵尸吃掉啦！
胤礽抱完头之后，仗着自己体积小，爬上轿子坐垫平躺着。
他双手交叉放在腹部，表情安详。
让我死吧。我现在想离开皇宫，离开京城，离开大清，去海外闯荡。
再见了我的祖国。
胤礽处于后知后觉极端尴尬中的时候，太皇太后往后一倒，靠在苏麻喇姑身上，身体瘫软。
“福临……福临……”太皇太后喃喃道，“他的对不起是在责怪我吗？”
苏麻喇姑道：“肯定不是。皇上也想和您和好。”
太皇太后闭上眼养了一会儿神，重新站直。
“今日之事决不能泄露出去。”太皇太后道。
苏麻喇姑道：“太子殿下在慈宁宫中梳理了好几遍下人，现在留下的都是慈宁宫的老人，太皇太后请放心。”
不放心的人早就撵了出去。且刚刚太子和太皇太后说话的声音极小，大阿哥还在那里挺大声的抽泣，要听清也不容易。
太皇太后点了点头，这才让人放开胤褆。
胤褆被放下来之后嚎啕大哭：“我要太子弟弟，我要弟弟，把弟弟还给我！”
“乖，弟弟很快就回来，别担心。”太皇太后把胤褆揽怀里，“他有事要做，马上就回来。”
果然孩童敏锐，一眼就看出眼前的太子不是真正的太子。太皇太后心中叹气。
周围人不明白刚才古怪一幕是发生了什么，他们也没有听到最后胤礽和太皇太后的窃窃私语。
现在听胤褆一嚎之后，他们才恍然大悟。
大阿哥虽然年纪小，也知道天花是绝症。他一听太子去处理天花，就急得口不择言了吧。
小孩子疯言疯语正常。
太皇太后担心大阿哥又说出什么惊人之语，把大阿哥带进了自己住的地方，并让人把三阿哥也带了过来。
胤褆紧紧抱住感受到周围不安的气氛后也变得很是敏感害怕的胤祉，抿着嘴一言不发。
胤褆被太皇太后警告之后，知道现在什么该说什么不该说了。
他小小的心灵其实并没有完全明白现在发生了什么，只是模糊地感觉面前的太子弟弟发生了很大的变化，不像是他认识的太子弟弟。
胤褆又想起了诅咒的事，很担心太子弟弟回不来。
汗阿玛你在哪里？给一个讨厌的皇后守灵，比太子弟弟、比我、比宫里这么多人都重要吗？
你怎么还不回来？再不回来太子弟弟会被诅咒带走了！
“大、大哥。”刚学会一个字一个字往外蹦的胤祉，抱紧了胤褆的脖子，“二、哥，要、二、哥……”
“二哥办正事去了，很快就会回来。三弟弟别担心。”胤褆学着胤礽哄胤祉那样，轻轻拍着胤祉的背。
胤祉瘪嘴：“我、怕……要、二、哥……”
“别怕，大哥保护你。”胤褆轻轻拍着胤祉的背，咬牙道，“大哥也会保护二哥。”
“嗯。”胤祉把小脑袋埋进胤褆怀里，终于安静了。
太皇太后注视着这一切，心里又是欣慰又是难过。
福临……保成……
这些事要怎么告诉玄烨？
还有福临最后的话。
那些诅咒难道会缩减太子的寿命？还是说福临附体保成会伤害到太子的身体？
若是太子真的身体不好，就算玄烨不废太子，以后的皇子肯定也会趁机争夺太子之位。
或许那时候真的只能让那个玄烨提前圈禁保成，才能保太子一命。
带温泉的大庄子啊……太皇太后很怀念。
她和福临都喜欢泡温泉。胤礽却从未去过温泉。那时胤礽体内的果然是福临。
……
胤礽虽然为自己突然演技爆发尴尬得要死，还是咬牙把所有事情处理完了。
小小的太子在宫里奔波劳碌，没有一个人敢轻视他。
甚至因为太子的年龄实在是太小，处事又实在是太成熟老练，让看到太子如此老辣做派的人感到毛骨悚然。
人都会害怕超出常理的事。
太子现在所作所为就已经超出了常理。
他们看着太子的眼神渐渐生出了恐惧，就像是遇上了怪物一样。
胤礽不在乎他们怎么想。现在他还是太子，就没人敢传他的闲言蜚语。
胤礽安排好每一个御医的工作之后，又去探望高位嫔妃们。
佟贵妃送给胤礽一个祈福荷包：“太子保重身体。对皇上而言，没有比太子殿下的身体更重要的事。”
“佟贵妃娘娘请安心，孤的身体还行。您也要保重身体。”胤礽收下了祈福荷包，“这几日委屈佟贵妃娘娘暂时待在承乾宫中不出门了。”
佟贵妃道：“是我份内之事。”
胤礽又去了惠嫔宫中。
到了惠嫔宫中后，他的态度缓和不少，没有在承乾宫那般贵气。
“大哥很精神，没被吓到。”胤礽主动道，“惠嫔娘娘保重身体，大哥很担心你。”
惠嫔知道宫里出现了天花之后，就忍不住朝着慈宁宫方向叩谢胤礽。
居然是天花，原来是天花，怪不得太子会如此紧张。
太子已经出过天花，他自己不惧怕天花。太子如此大的动作，全是为了皇帝其他的子嗣。
太子不愧是宫中最为仁慈之人。
“大阿哥没添乱就好，没添乱妾身就安心了。”惠嫔按着胸口不断道，“慈宁宫比妾身宫里安全，妾身就不送东西给慈宁宫了。请告诉大阿哥，让他老实点。”
胤礽失笑：“大哥真的很老实，惠嫔娘娘真的不用担心。”
惠嫔满脸不信。
我自己生的儿子我还不知道他是什么德性？宫中只有太子殿下天天夸大阿哥，其他谁不知道大阿哥是个混世魔王？
当胤礽来到荣嫔宫中的时候，荣嫔一言不发就朝着胤礽磕头，把胤礽吓了一跳。
“妾会管好钟粹宫。三阿哥让太子殿下费心了。”荣嫔磕完头后站起来平静地道。
胤礽摸了摸鼻子：“不费心不费心，三阿哥是我弟弟，哥哥照顾弟弟怎么能叫费心？”
说完，胤礽落荒而逃。
荣嫔的态度让他又开始尴尬。
他这次是真的演得太过，他自己率先受不了。
还好胤礽安排完所有事之后，就听到康熙得知宫中之事，不再和仪仗一起，而是快马加鞭赶了回来，最迟明日下午就能回宫。
他心头一松，把什么前前世前世的成年人脑子全部丢掉，将过度使用的脑子恢复正常。
我，奶团子胤礽回来啦！
然后“轰”的一声，脑子里紧绷的弦断掉后，紧绷的身体也跟着垮掉，胤礽立刻浑身发热，不省人事。
胤礽昏睡过去时的心态十分轻松安详。
只要我昏过去了，那么尴尬什么的就无所谓了。我也不需要向阿玛解释什么了。
不愧是你，胤礽！太聪明啦！
掉线几天就像是掉线了好几年的康熙终于回到宫中，就得到太子将一切处理得井井有条后累得病倒的消息。

The Empress Dowager held her breath, not daring to speak.

She was afraid that if she spoke, the phantom would vanish.

Yinreng sensed that someone had appeared.

He turned his head to look at the Empress Dowager, whose face was full of shock. Knowing he had revealed too much, his eyes flickered for a moment, and he turned his head slightly away.

This reflexive dodging movement only made the Empress Dowager more certain of her guess.

With many people around and ears everywhere, the Empress Dowager composed herself and, leaning on her nanny's hand, walked tremblingly toward Yinreng.

"Leave this matter to me; the Crown Prince should go and rest." The Empress Dowager said this while observing Yinreng's expression.

Yinreng frowned.

The Empress Dowager was currently ill and lacked basic awareness of infectious disease prevention; how could he feel at ease leaving this matter to her?

But if he defied the Empress Dowager, his Ama would surely reprimand him upon his return, or even grow suspicious and wary of the overly monstrous abilities he was currently displaying.

Wait, wasn't this a good thing?

He saved people, displayed monstrous abilities, and aroused his Ama's wariness—his Ama would surely depose the Crown Prince while feeling guilty and wanting to compensate him!

"Empress Dowager, please return. You are the backbone of the palace; you should rest in peace, and leave this matter to me." To appear more reliable, Yinreng did not call her Wuku Mama, but used a more formal address.

Yinti was so shocked his eyes widened.

The Crown Prince brother actually talked back to the Empress Dowager? How could he be so bold!

Yinti hurriedly wanted to smooth things over and plead for Yinreng, but he saw that the Empress Dowager was not angry; instead, her eyes were red, as if she were deeply moved?

Deeply... deeply moved?

Is it being moved? Why does it feel like the Empress Dowager is a bit sad?

"Stop talking, the Empress Dowager is already sad," Yinti said hurriedly.

Yinreng froze for a moment and looked up at the Empress Dowager.

He saw sadness, nostalgia, guilt, and even a hint of grievance in the Empress Dowager's eyes.

Yinreng frowned, his intuition telling him something was wrong.

Things were a bit beyond his expectations.

His brain whirred rapidly, almost bypassing his previous life as a college student and going straight to the brain of the original Crown Prince from his life before that.

Yinreng's eyes widened, and he looked at the Empress Dowager in disbelief.

And when the Empress Dowager saw the change in his expression, she became even more certain.

She reached out and grabbed Yinreng's right hand tightly: "You, you..."

The Empress Dowager knew she couldn't call out that name, but she couldn't suppress the urge to do so now.

Yinreng looked at the Empress Dowager's pleading eyes, his heart panicked, and he reflexively pulled his hand away.

As soon as he pulled his hand away, the Empress Dowager's tears finally could not be controlled, spilling over and dripping down the wrinkles at the corners of her eyes.

Yinti's mind went blank.

Is, is it necessary?! The Crown Prince brother didn't even say anything! Why is the Empress Dowager crying!

Yinreng hurriedly placed his right hand back into the Empress Dowager's palm and stood on tiptoe, using his other hand to wipe the tears from the corners of her eyes.

"Leave this to me. I will protect them well." Yinreng guessed the reason for the Empress Dowager's abnormal behavior at this moment.

The Empress Dowager probably thought he was possessed by a ghost.

Possessed by the ancestor, the ghost Emperor Shunzhi.

It was all his own fault for shouting "Grandfather said" every day; now that he was acting too mature, people thought he was possessed.

However, Yinreng was not panicked. This was part of his plan.

Although being possessed by an ancestor was more dangerous than just being talented—it would secure his status when he was young, but he would probably be executed when he grew up—even if Kangxi loved him, he would be wary of such supernatural matters.

So he would soon make Shunzhi "log off," and he had already thought of the opportunity for that.

Now, while the Empress Dowager was mistaking him for someone else, he might as well take advantage of it.

When the word "take advantage" flashed through Yinreng's mind, he felt a wave of discomfort, and his eyes dimmed for a moment.

The dark memories of his life before last, besides giving him the knowledge and common sense to adapt to this era, also caused his thinking to inevitably lean toward that cold and crazy Crown Prince.

In his life before last, he was, after all, the future emperor personally raised by Kangxi.

The art of imperial governance is cold and ruthless; everyone and everything can be calculated and used.

The pain that flashed through Yinreng's eyes made the Empress Dowager panic, and she involuntarily loosened her grip on his hand.

Yinreng withdrew his hand and stopped paying attention to the Empress Dowager.

He continued to issue orders, commanding the entire inner palace to mobilize and nip the smallpox epidemic in the bud.

The Empress Dowager forced herself to stand straight despite her discomfort. Behind the small Yinreng, she looked like an indestructible guardian deity.

Sumalagu, who knew the Empress Dowager best, had a look of surprise in her eyes.

She looked at the great-grandmother and great-great-grandson, and the scene before her gradually overlapped with images from the past.

It was the Empress Dowager and Emperor Kangxi.

It was also the Empress Dowager and Emperor Shunzhi of the past.

Yinti frowned deeply.

He stared fixedly at Yinreng, watching him arrange everything methodically. Until everything was arranged and Yinreng lifted his foot to go to the Imperial Hospital to ask about the details of the smallpox epidemic, Yinti grabbed the corner of Yinreng's robe.

Yinreng turned back in confusion.

Yinti was stern, his body trembling constantly: "Who, who are you! Where is my brother? How did my brother..."

The Empress Dowager was horrified: "Eldest Prince!"

Sumalagu, who had guessed the situation, immediately stepped forward and covered Yinti's mouth, not letting him speak further.

Yinti kicked Sumalagu hard and bit her hand.

"Ouch!" Sumalagu let go, "Hurry and take the Eldest Prince inside; he's been frightened by the smallpox and is having nightmares!"

"You are not the Crown Prince brother, give my brother back to me... wuwuwu..." After breaking free from Sumalagu, Yinti lunged toward Yinreng.

Two burly nannies stopped Yinti, covered his mouth, and carried him away.

Yinreng looked up, his expression neither sad nor happy, his eyes deep, as if there were an abyss at the bottom.

Yinti trembled violently with fear, tears and snot bubbles appearing at the same time.

He struggled hard, wanting to continue lunging at Yinreng.

"The Crown Prince is fine." Yinreng put away his coldness, his eyes warming up, and he chuckled with a helpless tone, "Don't worry."

Yinti stopped struggling. He shook even harder.

"Rest assured, this matter will absolutely not spread." The Empress Dowager swept a fierce look around.

"Children under the age of six have the ability to connect with heaven and earth, but only limited to close blood relatives with weak yang energy." Yinreng looked away and lowered his voice, "Since you have already discovered it, help me pass a message to Xuan Ye. Xuan Ye is surrounded by dragon energy, and I cannot communicate with him directly. Yinreng may be physically weak later and unfit to be the Crown Prince. If that time comes, give Yinreng a large manor with hot springs as a place of confinement."

Yinreng's voice was very low, and only the Empress Dowager, who was close to him, heard it.

The Empress Dowager's eyes flickered, and she leaned down and lowered her voice: "You, Fulin, Mother I..."

Yinreng turned his head away and closed his eyes: "I'm sorry."

After saying this, he left without looking back.

Yinreng stepped into the small sedan chair that had been waiting outside the Cining Palace. As soon as the curtain fell, he hugged his head and squatted down.

Ahhhhhhh, so embarrassing, so embarrassing that my toes have dug out another Cining Palace!

Pretending to be the crazy Crown Prince from my life before last is embarrassing, but pretending to be Shunzhi is even more embarrassing!

Why did I do that?! Is my brain malfunctioning again!

It must be that I've been consuming too much energy lately, burning out my brain cells, and have become mentally disabled!

How could the Empress Dowager not recognize Shunzhi? The more you say, the more mistakes you make; the Empress Dowager must have already figured it out!

Yinreng, you big idiot! Your brain has been eaten by zombies!

After hugging his head, Yinreng relied on his small size to climb onto the sedan cushion and lie flat.

He crossed his hands over his abdomen with a serene expression.

Let me die. I want to leave the palace, leave the capital, leave the Qing Dynasty, and go overseas to explore.

Goodbye, my motherland.

While Yinreng was in the midst of extreme, belated embarrassment, the Empress Dowager fell backward, leaning on Sumalagu, her body limp.

"Fulin... Fulin..." the Empress Dowager murmured, "Is his 'sorry' blaming me?"

Sumalagu said: "Certainly not. The Emperor also wants to reconcile with you."

The Empress Dowager closed her eyes to rest for a while, then stood straight again.

"Today's events must never be leaked." The Empress Dowager said.

Sumalagu said: "His Highness the Crown Prince combed through the servants in the Cining Palace several times; those who remain are all old hands of the Cining Palace, please rest assured, Empress Dowager."

Those who couldn't be trusted had long been driven out. Besides, the voices of the Crown Prince and the Empress Dowager were very low, and the Eldest Prince was sobbing quite loudly there, so it wouldn't be easy to hear clearly.

The Empress Dowager nodded, and only then did she let people release Yinti.

After Yinti was put down, he wailed: "I want the Crown Prince brother, I want my brother, give my brother back to me!"

"Be good, brother will be back soon, don't worry." The Empress Dowager took Yinti into her arms, "He has things to do and will be back soon."

Sure enough, children are sharp; one look and he saw that the Crown Prince in front of him was not the real one. The Empress Dowager sighed in her heart.

The people around didn't understand what had happened in the strange scene just now, and they didn't hear the final whispers between Yinreng and the Empress Dowager.

Now, after hearing Yinti's wailing, they suddenly realized.

Although the Eldest Prince was young, he knew smallpox was a terminal illness. He must have spoken without thinking out of anxiety when he heard the Crown Prince was going to deal with smallpox.

It's normal for children to babble.

Worried that the Eldest Prince would say something shocking again, the Empress Dowager took him into her own living quarters and had the Third Prince brought over as well.

Yinti hugged Yinzhi tightly, who had also become very sensitive and scared after feeling the uneasy atmosphere, and kept his mouth shut.

After being warned by the Empress Dowager, Yinti knew what should and should not be said now.

His little heart didn't fully understand what was happening, just vaguely feeling that the Crown Prince brother in front of him had changed a lot, not like the Crown Prince brother he knew.

Yinti thought of the curse again and was very worried that the Crown Prince brother wouldn't come back.

Han Ama, where are you? Is guarding the tomb of a hateful Empress more important than the Crown Prince brother, than me, than so many people in the palace?

Why aren't you back yet? If you don't come back, the Crown Prince brother will be taken away by the curse!

"Big, brother." Yinzhi, who had just learned to pop out words one by one, hugged Yinti's neck tightly, "Second, brother, want, second, brother..."

"Second brother went to do important things and will be back soon. Third brother, don't worry." Yinti mimicked the way Yinreng coaxed Yinzhi, gently patting Yinzhi's back.

Yinzhi pouted: "I, afraid... want, second, brother..."

"Don't be afraid, Big Brother will protect you." Yinti gently patted Yinzhi's back, gritting his teeth, "Big Brother will also protect Second Brother."

"Mm." Yinzhi buried his little head in Yinti's arms and finally quieted down.

The Empress Dowager watched all this, feeling both comforted and sad.

Fulin... Baocheng...

How to tell Xuan Ye about these things?

And Fulin's last words.

Could those curses shorten the Crown Prince's life? Or would Fulin possessing Baocheng harm the Crown Prince's body?

If the Crown Prince really had poor health, even if Xuan Ye didn't depose him, future princes would surely seize the opportunity to fight for the position.

Perhaps at that time, it would really be necessary for Xuan Ye to confine Baocheng in advance to save the Crown Prince's life.

A large manor with hot springs... The Empress Dowager felt nostalgic.

She and Fulin both liked hot springs. Yinreng had never been to one. It really was Fulin inside Yinreng at that time.

...

Although Yinreng was dying of embarrassment for his sudden burst of acting, he gritted his teeth and finished handling everything.

The little Crown Prince ran around the palace, and no one dared to look down on him.

Even because the Crown Prince was so young and his handling of affairs was so mature and sophisticated, those who saw his seasoned style felt a chill down their spines.

People are afraid of things that go beyond common sense.

The Crown Prince's actions were already beyond common sense.

The look in their eyes as they watched the Crown Prince gradually turned to fear, as if they had encountered a monster.

Yinreng didn't care what they thought. As long as he was still the Crown Prince, no one dared to spread gossip about him.

After arranging the work for every imperial physician, Yinreng went to visit the high-ranking concubines.

Noble Consort Tong gave Yinreng a prayer pouch: "Crown Prince, take care of your health. For the Emperor, there is nothing more important than your health."

"Noble Consort Tong, please rest assured, my health is fine. You should also take care of yourself." Yinreng accepted the prayer pouch, "For these few days, I'm sorry to have to ask you to stay in the Chengqian Palace and not go out."

Noble Consort Tong said: "It is my duty."

Yinreng then went to Consort Hui's palace.

After arriving at Consort Hui's palace, his attitude softened quite a bit, lacking the regal air he had at the Chengqian Palace.

"Big Brother is in good spirits and wasn't scared." Yinreng said proactively, "Consort Hui, take care of your health; Big Brother is very worried about you."

After learning that smallpox had appeared in the palace, Consort Hui couldn't help but bow toward the Cining Palace to thank Yinreng.

It was actually smallpox, so that was it; no wonder the Crown Prince was so nervous.

The Crown Prince had already had smallpox and was not afraid of it himself. The Crown Prince's massive mobilization was all for the Emperor's other children.

The Crown Prince was truly the most benevolent person in the palace.

"As long as the Eldest Prince didn't cause trouble, I am relieved." Consort Hui pressed her chest and said repeatedly, "The Cining Palace is safer than my palace, so I won't send anything there. Please tell the Eldest Prince to behave himself."

Yinreng laughed: "Big Brother is really well-behaved, Consort Hui, you really don't need to worry."

Consort Hui looked skeptical.

Don't I know what kind of character my own son has? In the palace, only the Crown Prince praises the Eldest Prince every day; who else doesn't know that the Eldest Prince is a little demon?

When Yinreng arrived at Consort Rong's palace, Consort Rong bowed to him without saying a word, which gave Yinreng a fright.

"I will manage the Zhongcui Palace well. Thank you for your trouble regarding the Third Prince, Your Highness." Consort Rong stood up after bowing and said calmly.

Yinreng touched his nose: "No trouble, no trouble, the Third Prince is my brother; how can it be called trouble for an older brother to take care of his younger brother?"

After saying that, Yinreng fled in a panic.

Consort Rong's attitude made him feel embarrassed again.

He had really acted too much this time, and he himself couldn't stand it first.

Fortunately, after Yinreng finished arranging everything, he heard that Kangxi had learned of the palace's situation and was no longer traveling with the honor guard, but was galloping back, and would be back in the palace by tomorrow afternoon at the latest.

His heart relaxed, and he threw away all the adult brains from his previous lives, restoring his overworked brain to normal.

I, the little milk bun Yinreng, am back!

Then, with a "boom," after the tight string in his brain snapped, his tense body collapsed, and Yinreng immediately became feverish and lost consciousness.

Yinreng's state of mind when he passed out was very relaxed and serene.

As long as I'm unconscious, then embarrassment or whatever doesn't matter. I don't need to explain anything to Ama either.

You really are something, Yinreng! Too smart!

Kangxi, who had been "offline" for a few days as if it had been a few years, finally returned to the palace, only to receive news that the Crown Prince had handled everything in an orderly manner and had fallen ill from exhaustion.

100,000

chapters.title: 第 23 章 [V]
chapters.source_text:
康熙十四岁便能在所有人不看好他的情况下除掉鳌拜，可见其心机深沉，性极能忍。
即使在得知三藩叛乱时，康熙也只是沉着脸，没有显露出太大的怒气。
皇宫中人已经很久没有看到康熙如此生气过。
他面目狰狞扭曲，额头青筋暴绽，将手边一切能砸的东西全砸在了地上，还抽起墙上挂着的宝刀将桌案砍成了两半。
当康熙发泄完怒气之后，他席地坐在冰冷的宫殿地板上，按着突突直跳的太阳穴，眼神阴鹜地瞪着乾清宫门外的天空。
康熙现在很想杀人。
想杀很多人。
宫中那些患了天花的人，那些让胤礽劳累至此的人，甚至连太皇太后病倒后、明明该她们处理宫务却毫无用处的皇太后与嫔妃们，都被康熙恨上了。
虽然那不理智的恨意很快就消失了，但康熙心中的怒气怎么也消失不了。
最后，他泡了很久的热水澡，把自己泡得头昏脑涨后，才勉强恢复了冷静。
康熙将胤礽接回了乾清宫与自己同住，其他皇子仍旧留在慈宁宫。
胤礽高烧退了一日又烧了起来，醒了一会儿又很快睡去。御医们都说没有生命危险，但康熙怎么也放心不下。
吴三桂已死，政务都不是很要紧。康熙便继续罢朝，一直看护着胤礽。
胤礽见康熙回来之后，心神彻底松懈，什么事都撒手不管了。
他一醒来就哼哼唧唧往康熙怀里钻，吃饱喝足之后玩一会儿康熙腰间的玉佩又继续睡。
胤礽和其他孩子不同，病得再厉害也不哭不闹，也不排斥苦药，十分好伺候。
稍稍有一点精神，胤礽就滚来滚去爬来爬去并试图骚扰批改折子的康熙。
康熙被胤礽弄得哭笑不得，忍不住捏了捏他的小鼻子：“好好养病，别乱动。”
胤礽哼哼唧唧道：“多动动身体才容易好。阿玛陪我玩。”
康熙把折子丢到桌案上：“玩什么？”
胤礽想了想，道：“我们下象棋。”
康熙问道：“为什么是象棋不是围棋？”
胤礽道：“围棋要计算，考脑子，不想动脑子。”
康熙点了一下胤礽的额头：“象棋也要考脑子。算了，来吧，朕让着你。”
胤礽裹着小被子趴在棋盘上，下巴垫了一个软软的枕头，像只毛毛虫一样和康熙下象棋。
康熙虽然让着胤礽，胤礽也赢少输多。但无论输赢他都乐呵呵的，兴趣半点不减。
胤礽以前没这么爱下棋。康熙很快就觉察出，胤礽是发现自己的怒气和担忧，故意用下棋来安慰自己。
又下完一局棋，胤礽打着哈欠收拾棋子，被康熙一把抱到怀里。
胤礽埋在康熙硬邦邦的胸口，鼻子撞得有一点点疼，说话带了一丝鼻音：“阿玛，怎么了？”
“你养好自己的病，不用做多余的事安慰阿玛。阿玛不需要你安慰。”康熙收紧怀抱道。
胤礽抓紧康熙胸口的衣服，闷声道：“阿玛是因为我才难过，我当然要让阿玛开心。阿玛放心，我只要多吃几碗肉多喝几碗奶，很快就会好。”
“小馋猫。”康熙用下巴蹭了蹭胤礽头顶的小辫子，勉强挤出微笑，“吃吧吃吧，只要不撑着，想吃多少吃多少。”
康熙松开胤礽之后，胤礽嚣张的在康熙怀里盘了窝，舒舒服服地靠着。
他仰头道：“阿玛，你还没夸我呢。”
康熙虎着脸道：“夸你什么？夸你生病？”
胤礽不满道：“哼！我这么厉害！你怎么不夸我！”
康熙沉默了一会儿，道：“太皇太后说，你玛法上了你的身？”
胤礽睁大眼睛：“什么？”
康熙道：“这些事是不是玛法上你的身做的。”
胤礽生气了：“污蔑！这是我自己做的！我就是这么厉害！”
我就装了一小会儿而已！大部分时间我都是本色演出，哪里和玛法一样了！太皇太后你不能因为偏爱玛法就把我的功劳都分给玛法啊！
如果阿玛认为这些事都是玛法做的，那我的功劳呢？我可以换免死符和温泉庄子的功劳呢？都被玛法吞了吗！
胤礽气得啪嗒啪嗒拍打康熙的手臂：“是我的做的！功劳是我的！是我做的！什么玛法！没有玛法！”
康熙见小奶团子气得都快蹦起来了，笑着把胤礽安抚住：“好，好，是你做的。太皇太后说的是怎么回事？她不会认错你玛法。”
胤礽歪头。这他要怎么说？
康熙只当胤礽记不太清，便一步一步的引导。
胤礽能说清的地方就说清楚，说不清楚的地方就抱头冒充可达鸭表情包，让康熙这个脑洞极大的人自己脑补。
康熙根据胤礽的话，脑补出以下结果。
顺治可能真的上了一会儿胤礽的身，但大部分时候都是胤礽自己在做，顺治出谋划策，直到太皇太后叫出顺治的名字，才小小的出现了一会儿。
在那个时候，胤礽的记忆有一小段模糊。其他时候胤礽记忆都很清晰。
即使顺治是康熙的汗阿玛，康熙也不能接受顺治能上胤礽的身的事。特别是胤礽这次病得这么重，很可能和顺治上身有关。
一个不怎么疼爱他的已经死掉的阿玛，和自己一手带大的宝贝儿子，选谁还用想吗？
康熙得出初步猜测之后，立刻召见张道长和德海大师。
张道长和德海大师自从被胤礽装神弄鬼连累之后，一直住在京城。
作为唯二能看出胤礽问题的宗教人士，在康熙眼中挂上了号。康熙虽不会封他们为国师，但也给予其钱粮供养，等有需要就召见他们。
张道长和德海大师进宫的时候对视一眼，表情都很苦。
看，有需要的时候来了。
康熙见到两人后，没有直接说明胤礽的情况，而是绕弯子套话。
帝王疑心都重，问出来的话不信，套出来的话才信。
康熙就像是单纯好奇似的，询问二人是否有通灵之术。
两人是宗教人士，不是江湖骗子。
斟酌之后，张道长率先答道：“贫道未曾见过，但听闻有人曾经鬼上身。根据贫道整理消息观察，鬼只会上阳气微弱的人的身体，若非病弱，即便是有肮脏的东西上身，也会被人体内的阳气冲刷掉。”
肮脏的东西……康熙脑海中闪过顺治的画像。
咳。不知者不为罪，不责怪张道长。
德海大师沉思许久，道：“民间即便有这种事，陛下龙气加身，紫气披肩，一接触到魂灵，立刻会把魂灵冲得粉碎，不太可能见到此事。”
康熙心道，怪不得汗阿玛要等朕离开宫里才出来。
康熙又问道：“太子是潜龙，也有龙气和紫气护身吗？”
张道长和德海大师异口同声道：“理应如此。但太子年纪小，体内阳气不足，还是应该小心些。”
康熙沉默许久，挑明道：“如果太子长期被诅咒侵扰，是否会增加鬼魂上身的可能？”
大冬天的，张道长和德海大师的背瞬间汗湿。
这是我们能回答的问题吗！皇帝陛下请您不要为难我们！
看着张道长和德海大师冷汗直冒的状态，康熙叹了口气，然后神色凌厉道：“回答朕！”
张道长和德海大师腿一软，“扑通”跪下道：“太子殿下有皇帝陛下庇佑，此种可能性并不大！”
康熙视线垂下，手指指节在椅背轻轻敲打。
半晌，等张道长和德海大师腿跪疼了之后，他才道：“若不是恶灵，而是祖先魂灵呢？若是太子自己原因呢？对太子的危害有多大？”
张道长和德海大师对视一眼，两人同时想岔。
难道皇帝是惦记上了太子的神异之处，想要拿太子当祭品召唤祖先魂灵？
都说天家无父子，这也太残忍了！
不愧是蛮夷。
德海大师心中叹气，梗着脖子道：“人的阳气就那么多，阴气多一分，阳气就少一分，两者总会此消彼长，只是多少而已。此举不仅会损害太子殿下身体，也会损害祖先魂灵，断不可为！”
德海大师说完之后，对着康熙狠狠磕了几个头。
他豁出去了。
救人一命，胜造七级浮屠。他甘愿赴死！
张道长本在犹豫，但一看到德海大师慷慨的神情，眼睛一闭一睁，也下定了决心。
若连本心都无法坚持，还修什么道？
今日我助皇帝牺牲了太子，来日，我手上必会染上更多无辜鲜血。
“贫道也认为如此。”张道长伏地道，“人鬼殊途，人有人间界，鬼有鬼门关，祖先英灵可升天界。三界殊途，不和混淆，对人对灵魂都有害。民间却有祖先附体帮助后人的事迹，但顶多只是入梦。若祖先真附在后人身上，无论是祖先魂灵还是后人身体都会损耗。”
康熙任由两人跪趴在地上，许久后才冷声道：“你们真敢说。”
德海大师和张道长道：“贫僧/贫道不敢欺君。”
康熙闭上眼，声音颤抖：“好一个不敢欺君。”
他将手边茶杯狠狠砸地上。
德海大师和张道长身体猛地一颤抖，但仍旧咬牙坚持。
又是半晌，康熙恢复了冷静。
“你们起身吧。”康熙重新赐座，宫殿里唯一伺候着的赵昌将地面收拾干净，给康熙换了一杯温度刚好的热茶。
德海大师和张道长松了一口气。还好还好，皇帝这是良心发现了吗？
康熙道：“朕将在香山重修寺庙道观，交由二位主持。”
这是彻底被软禁了？德海大师和张道长立刻跪下谢恩，心里凄苦极了。
康熙再次让二人起身，又问道：“若此事已经发生，要如何护住太子和祖先魂灵？”
德海大师和张道长：“……”
两人呆住了。
已经发生？不是吧不是吧？还能有这种事？这么离奇的吗？
不过他们想起那个神奇的小太子，心中不确定了。
小孩子不会说谎，除非大人诱导。
先皇后已经崩逝，太子从小养在皇帝身边，不可能被其他人误导，那么太子绝不可能说谎。
太子还真被先帝附身过？
两人发现，要圆一个谎，就要撒更多的谎，顿时慌了。
德海大师年纪大些，经验丰富些，率先圆谎：“阳气损耗也是疾病，不需要什么偏方，让御医有病治病即可。但此事不停止，身体便会反复生病。”
张道长也想到了糊弄过去的方法：“祖灵有香火祭祀，只要回归本位，休养一段时日便可恢复。但若频繁下界，再多的香火愿力也难以维系。陛下英明神武，大清蒸蒸日上，不需祖先显灵指引。陛下可让祖先放心归去。”
康熙叹了一口气。
朕倒是想啊，但是那个汗阿玛的倔强性子，连太皇太后的话都不听，还能听朕这个儿子的话？
康熙算是明白了。顺治就是在雄心壮志刚可以施展的时候患天花去了，心有不甘，非得做点什么。
顺治倒也不是故意折腾胤礽。但那种情况下他若不出面引导胤礽，天花一起宫中一乱，即便是胤礽出过痘，也可能遭遇其他事情。
何况在顺治眼中，可能胤礽不是最重要的。
康熙所有儿子都是顺治的孙子，宫中还有太皇太后这个顺治的亲额娘，加在一起分量比胤礽重多了。
康熙越想越气，越想越悲哀，越想越怜爱胤礽。
胤礽没了额娘，就只有他这个阿玛。宫中上下所有人都有更重要的人，为了自己更重要的人都可以将胤礽牺牲掉，只有自己能保护胤礽。
保成只有朕了。康熙心中唏嘘，眼眶微红。
康熙摆摆手，让这两个虽然有本事但没什么用处的人滚了。
康熙独自坐了一会儿，道：“朕是不是该找更多的人问问？这两人根本没用。”
赵昌垂首不语。
半晌康熙自问自答道：“正因为他们二人能看出问题，又没有解决办法，朕才信他们。若他们拍着胸脯说能解决此事，那才是骗子。”
说罢，康熙感慨道：“怪不得历朝历代都是骗子入宫为祸。只有骗子，才会声称自己能通天彻地。哼，如果他们有通天彻地之能，怎么不自己当这皇帝，还要匍匐在朕脚下？”
赵昌哪敢说话，继续装哑巴。
康熙发泄完之后，心情也不知道是好是坏。
他回到暖阁，见胤礽大字摊在床榻上呼呼大睡时，严肃的表情才松动了一些。
康熙戳了戳胤礽的软肚肚：“保成，你真让朕头疼。”
胤礽：“呼……呼……呼……嗝，好吃！”
康熙无语。
这小胖子，做梦都在吃。看来身体会很快好转了。
康熙伸手去戳胤礽微张的嘴。
胤礽“啊昂”，一口咬在康熙手指上。
康熙：“……嗷！”
胤礽松嘴瞪眼：“嗷！”
赵昌头快低到胸口。
不能笑，不能笑，笑了会掉脑袋。

作者有话说:
《今天我仍不知道亲爹是朱元璋》男主言情求预收藏。
加更……我一直在加啊，上章四千五，这章四千二呢！有空我就会多写一点，能写多少就发多少，放心放心（擦汗）。
预收文案如下：
陈标穿越元末乱世商人家中，为了活命无法隐藏穿越者的能耐，冒充能掐会算生而知之的神棍，小小年纪便让陈家成为仅次于沈万三的富豪。
这时，他亲爹陈国瑞告诉他，儿啊，你爹我投靠了大明洪武皇帝，是洪武皇帝的大功臣哦。
陈标即使不是学历史的也知道洪武皇帝朱元璋晚年会杀空大半个朝堂，开始谋划着出海苟命。
陈标：“爹、娘，马皇后马上要崩逝了。”
他亲娘绣花的手一顿。
陈标：“爹、娘，太子也会英年早逝。最爱的老婆和儿子一死，洪武帝立刻就会变成滥杀的疯子。”
他亲爹憨厚的笑容一僵。
陈标：“爹、娘，我们赶紧出海置办产业，等洪武帝杀空满朝文武百官的时候，咱们就逃不掉了！”
亲娘亲爹对视一眼，点头道：“好，儿子，听你的。”
陈标露出满意的笑容。
龙凤元年，朱元璋嫡长子朱标出生。
相者道，此子生而知之，贵不可言，恐老天收之，需隐姓埋名，遮掩天机至而立之年方可归位。待此子归位，定能保老朱家万世永昌。
陈标：“爹，我们什么时候出海啊！我已经在海外置办好大庄园了！”
朱元璋：“还早还早，下次一定，明年一定。”（擦汗.jpg）
24.二更合一 [V]
康熙去见太皇太后的时候，手指头上绑着绷带。
太皇太后先吓了一跳，后来她听到康熙手指头的伤是被胤礽咬的时候，表情很是一言难尽。
康熙叹气：“朕该好好管教保成了。”
太皇太后面无表情道：“你是又趁着他睡觉，把手指伸他嘴里了？你怎么就这么不长记性！”
康熙视线飘逸。咳，没混过去。
太皇太后叹气：“玄烨啊，你多大的人了，怎么比保成还调皮？”
康熙心道，朕怎么比那个皮孩子还调皮了？
“皇玛嬷，天花之事有结果了吗？”康熙赶紧说正事，避开太皇太后的唠叨。
太皇太后皱紧眉头：“你自己看吧。”
苏麻喇姑把证词交给康熙，有些证词上面还带着血痕。
康熙翻开证词，越看脸色越阴沉。
在得知有人隐瞒宫中天花疫情时，康熙已经做好了最坏的打算。
前明势力？多尔衮余孽？白莲教？三藩？
康熙甚至都做好了血洗整个后宫的准备。
当他看到证词，松了一口气的同时，又更加愤怒了。
天花疫情被隐瞒，居然只是因为内务府的一桩陈年贪污案。
当年顺治崩于天花，所用东西理应全部被烧毁，阻止天花传播。但内务府在处理大批顺治使用过的珍贵物品时，将其偷偷贪污掉，没有完全销毁。
这些人明明知道天花有多可怕，但是财帛动人心。
他们想着，只要洗一洗就没问题，只要用布包起来卖给其他人就没问题。
那时康熙年幼，太皇太后忙着与辅政大臣们周旋，内务府管理混乱，大批量沾染着天花的物品被投运了出去。
他们当时不敢用，过了几年十几年之后，风声过去了，便拿出来用了。
其实天花脱离了宿主，不会存活这么久。但这十几年期间一直都有人得天花，互相包庇着瞒了过去，康熙并不知道。
宫中下人互相包庇的原因，自然是怕暴露偷拿宫中物品的事，怕清理疫情的时候连累自己。
出痘变成了风寒，病死可能成了意外死亡……这天花疫情就一波一波的接力了下来。
他们运气很好，天花没有大规模爆发，没有让宫中贵人们染上，所以一直没被人发现。
那些出痘后活着或者死了的人的东西，也被其他人继承了下来。
还是那句话财帛动人心。
胤礽出痘的时候，这群人恐慌了一阵子。但胤礽很快便好了，又没有其他人出痘，康熙便没有彻查宫里下人，他们再次糊弄了过去。
直到胤礽察觉诅咒即将爆发，把整个后宫全隔绝成一个个封闭的小方块，这才把那些人揪了出来。
“有孩子被感染了天花。”太皇太后叹气道，“张氏的女儿恐不行了。”
康熙现在活着的女儿有有三个——荣嫔所出的皇三女，庶妃张氏所出的皇四女，布常在兆佳氏所出的皇五女。
康熙对张氏有着几分喜欢，张氏为康熙生了两个女儿，第一个女儿三岁的时候夭折，这个女儿眼见着又活不到四岁。康熙不由有些悲伤。
太皇太后却冷哼了一声，道：“你心疼什么？她自己的额娘都不心疼！”
康熙皱眉：“怎么了？证词里没有提这件事。”
太皇太后道：“哀家让人删掉了。这些要留档的，哪能把皇家阴私写上去？保成命所有人都待在宫殿里不能外出，那张氏为了给她不成器的弟弟送钱，贿赂了管事让心腹出宫，那心腹正好是四公主的奶嬷嬷。”
康熙眉头紧皱。
太皇太后接着道：“后来保成发现了这件事，封锁了这个漏洞。但她运气就是那么差，奶嬷嬷碰巧遇到了宫里患上了天花的人。张氏那里所有人都无事，就四公主体弱感染了，唉。”
康熙闭上眼，沉默了许久才道：“若四公主熬不过去，就把她遣送回家吧。”
大清后宫礼仪规定并不严格，无宠无子的嫔妃可被遣送回家，有子太妃也能和儿子同住。
张氏罪不至死，但康熙不想再见到她。
太皇太后轻轻点头：“皇上仁慈。”
她在心中讽笑，张氏家中有个烂赌的弟弟。她这一被遣出宫，遭遇可能不比死好到哪去。
说完张氏的事之后，太皇太后又说起对其他人的处置。
宫中下人手脚不干净很正常，康熙和太皇太后都是睁一只眼闭一只眼，过分了才敲打一下。
要挨个管，他们没这精力。
没想到这一出上下勾连的贪腐，居然差点让天花在宫中蔓延，就变成了抄家灭祖才能解决的事。
“德嫔那查出几个对孩子不利的下人，和这件事有关系吗？”康熙问道。
太皇太后叹气：“没关系。她怀了龙嗣被封赏，惹了一些人眼红而已。”
德嫔在宫中被冷落四年。宫里人惯爱捧高踩低，她入宫前又是娇小姐脾气受不得气，这四年被磋磨的很惨。
如今德嫔一朝得势，曾经欺辱过她的人便惶惶不安，担心德嫔会报复他们。
人一慌张，就容易做出不理智的事。宫里几个不高不低的下人们联合起来，也能让妃嫔吃亏。
康熙淡漠道：“哪些人做的，该杀的杀了，该抄的抄了，该流放的流放。罚严重些，杀鸡儆猴。”
太皇太后点头，是这个理。
宫里许多大事的发生，背后原因可能并不是什么轰轰烈烈的阴谋，不过是一件又一件小事的累积。
比如贪墨偷窃后互相包庇，比如踩高捧低后狗急跳墙……所谓宫斗，便是一件件看似无聊的事的组合，然后造成巨大的后果。
在康熙和太皇太后平静的对话中，一条条性命、一个个家族的命运被确定。内务府三位总管大臣中的海拉逊、噶禄被罚俸，吐巴左迁，飞扬武补上吐巴的位置。
一场声势浩大的内务府整顿就此展开，宫中人人自危，连嫔妃们都噤若寒蝉，不敢出门晃悠。
两人一言一语，一直说到夕阳西斜，太皇太后才踌躇道：“福临他……”
康熙心中叹气。太皇太后果然比起保成，更在乎汗阿玛。明明保成还病着，太皇太后一开口问的只是汗阿玛。
康熙道：“朕请来了张道长和德海大师。”
他将张道长和德海大师的话告诉太皇太后，没有疏漏一点细节。
太皇太后听完之后，从这些细节判断出这一僧一道说的话是真的。
康熙皱紧眉头道：“皇玛嬷，您能劝劝汗阿玛吗？”
太皇太后叹气：“哀家什么时候劝住过他？”
康熙道：“保成病了有御医，若汗阿玛出了事，我可不知道如何是好。”
康熙改变了自称，以孙儿的身份推心置腹道。
太皇太后更关心汗阿玛，那么以汗阿玛的角度出发，更能拉拢太皇太后成为自己盟友。
太皇太后继续叹气：“你要不问问保成，他玛法有什么心事未竟？若是董鄂氏的事，就随了他的意吧。”
得知顺治并非为了董鄂氏才和她对着干之后，太皇太后对董鄂氏的怨气消去不少。
康熙道：“我想汗阿玛在乎的不是董鄂氏。保成那小子夜夜梦中都喊着玛法千古一帝。他恐怕是想看大清在我手中变得繁荣昌盛。”
太皇太后拍了拍桌子：“他就不回去了是吧？！”
那得看多少年！
康熙无奈道：“玛嬷真的没法子吗？”
太皇太后皱眉：“哀家想想、想想……唉……”
两人对坐着愁眉不展时，突然从偏殿传来孩童的叽叽喳喳笑声。
两人眉头同时一松。
康熙揉了揉眉头，无奈道：“怎么会是保成的声音？他不是在乾清宫吗！”
太皇太后站起来道：“去看看。”
两人走到慈宁宫住着大阿哥和三阿哥的偏殿，果然是胤礽来了。
胤礽这次醒来之后发现康熙不在，摸了摸自己额头感觉烧退了，立刻跑慈宁宫找大阿哥和三阿哥玩。
他已经无聊得快疯了。
每天的娱乐只有下象棋，这是小孩子该过的生活吗！
胤礽一跑进慈宁宫偏殿，大阿哥就冲过来把胤礽抱住。
胤礽哄了好久把大阿哥哄好后，三阿哥又爬过来把胤礽抱住。
慈宁宫偏殿铺了厚厚的地毯。最后三人你叠我我叠你，在地摊上玩起了游戏。
三个孩童的笑声之响亮，太皇太后和康熙都听到了。
“保成，你怎么跑这来了！”康熙抬脚进屋就开始训孩子。
“烧退了，找哥哥弟弟玩。”胤礽对康熙挥手，“我本来想来给乌库妈妈和汗阿玛请安，但乌库妈妈和汗阿玛正在谈正事，我就先来找哥哥弟弟啦。”
“谈正事你也可以进来。”康熙让人把三阿哥抱回榻上，自己将胤礽提起来。
胤禔拍拍屁股，自己站了起来：“请乌库妈妈安，请汗阿玛安。”
“来，朕来考考你的功课。”康熙抱着胤礽坐到榻上，对着胤禔点点头，“看朕离开的这几日，你功课退步没有。”
胤禔：“？？？”你又不是不知道我这段时间没上课，你故意在弟弟面前欺负人是吧？
康熙怎么会故意欺负大儿子呢？他是那么好的阿玛。好阿玛当然会关心儿子的功课。
胤礽给了胤禔一个同情的眼神。
大哥，干脆果断的认错吧。当儿子的，阻止不了老父亲欺负儿子的肮脏心思的。赶紧投降还能少受些折磨。
胤禔虽然惧怕康熙，但惧怕的同时他也很头铁。
康熙要问他功课，他就直白道：“汗阿玛知道我这几日没读书，考什么功课？”
康熙：“……”这混小子，想挨揍吧？
胤礽赶紧打圆场：“汗阿玛，三弟刚站起来走路了哦，我们教三弟走路好不好？”
康熙横了儿子一眼。
胤礽在外人面前总是叫康熙汗阿玛，让康熙有些不舒服。
自己的太子，何须在意其他人的眼神？
“汗阿玛，汗、阿玛！”胤礽拉着康熙的袖子，有节奏的呼唤康熙。
“噗。”胤禔捂住嘴，“汗阿玛，我没笑，我也没想起汗血宝马。”
康熙：“……”他就不应该让大儿子和二儿子凑一起！一个傻一个坏，专门搞坏朕的心态！
“保成！”康熙严肃道。
胤礽扬起小脸：“汗阿玛您请说，儿子竖着耳朵听着！”
“你耳朵怎么竖？你又不是兔子！”康熙捏了捏胤礽的耳朵，对面因为逃课而被罚站的胤禔露出了不赞同的眼神，看得康熙更气了，“保成！你是太子！和兄弟如此玩闹不符合规矩！即使他们是兄弟，也必须尊敬你。”
胤礽眼神死。
哦豁，噩梦的开端来了。
保成！~你是太子！~你和兄弟们走太近是没有太子威严的表现！~他们不能对你不敬！~
呵呵。胤礽在心里不爽地冷笑。
一旁的胤禔听到康熙的话之后也在心底冷笑，并露出鄙视的眼神。
呵呵，你因为弟弟更爱我吃醋就直说，汗阿玛你是不是输不起。
胤礽拍了拍康熙的手臂，语重心长道：“好好好，他们主动来找我玩，是不顾我崇高的太子地位，有损我的尊严，那我主动去找他们玩吧。我堂堂太子去找哥哥弟弟玩，哥哥弟弟不理睬我就是看不起我这个太子。汗阿玛你看如何？”
康熙：“……”朕看不如何。
“玄烨啊，你够了，别逗孩子了。”一旁看戏的太皇太后笑出了声。
她对着罚站的胤禔招了招手，把胤禔抱怀里护着：“兄弟和睦是好事，你们尽管一起玩，乌库妈妈为你们做主，别听你们汗阿玛的。”
康熙：“……”皇玛嬷，你能不能别添乱？朕不是在开玩笑，朕真的很严肃！
“汗……阿玛？”小胤祉爬过来，仰着头看着康熙。
胤礽立刻道：“小三会叫汗阿玛了！小三知道汗阿玛是汗阿玛！小三和汗阿玛父子连心！汗阿玛你感动吗！”
康熙握拳捶在胤礽头上：“不感动，一边去。”
他嫌弃地把胤礽丢给了太皇太后。
胤禔赶紧把胤礽拉到身边护着，看着胤礽的脑袋很是心疼。
汗阿玛究竟什么毛病啊！弟弟刚病愈，他居然揍弟弟！
康熙白了大儿子二儿子一眼，小心翼翼把三儿子抱起来。
“胤祉都长这么大了。”康熙笑道。
小胤祉点点头，臭味散发。
康熙：“……”
太皇太后别过脸。
胤礽和胤禔捂住鼻子。
奶嬷嬷立刻冲上来把小胤祉从康熙手中接过来。
胤礽捂着鼻子道：“小三拉臭臭了。”
胤禔捂着鼻子道：“汗阿玛一抱起来就拉了，真是父子连心。”
胤礽用身体撞了胤禔一下：“大哥求你闭嘴！别给小三惹祸！”
胤禔不在乎道：“汗阿玛是英明神武的帝王，心胸开阔无比，怎么会和还不会走路的儿子计较？就算小三把臭臭拉到汗阿玛身上，汗阿玛也不会计较。”
胤礽：“……”还是会计较的。
太皇太后：“……”大曾孙子究竟是聪明还是不聪明？算了，不管聪明还是不聪明，哀家都救不了他了。
康熙表情狰狞。
他发现了，大阿哥废话这么多，就是功课太少闲出来的！
康熙勉强保持着绷着脸的表情，把胤礽拎走了。
离开之前，他狠狠瞪了胤禔一眼。
胤禔挠挠头，疑惑地问太皇太后：“乌库妈妈，又不是我拉臭臭，为什么汗阿玛瞪我？”
太皇太后微笑道：“大约是因为大阿哥你是哥哥，皇上认为你应该管好三阿哥吧。”
胤禔瞪圆眼睛，满脸不敢置信：“我还能管得住三阿哥拉臭臭了？！汗阿玛无理取闹！”
太皇太后忍不住了，哈哈哈笑得老腰都差点闪了。
……
康熙说到做到。
宫里的人该杀的杀了该烧的烧了，疫情过去，康熙又祭拜了一次太庙，后宫全面解禁，大阿哥也回到了惠嫔身边。
他刚回去，康熙的口谕就来了，给他加了几个师傅，加个很多功课，把大阿哥最喜欢的骑射课和布库课全删了。
惠嫔捏着帕子颤抖道：“大阿哥，你又干什么了？”
为什么大阿哥刚回来，皇帝口谕就来了？！
胤禔挠了挠头：“大概是因为这段时间的课我全翘了？”
大概是因为这个。
汗阿玛总不会因为三弟弟拉臭臭的事给我增加功课吧？汗阿玛脑子又没病，不可能不知道我读再多讨厌的书，也不可能阻止三弟弟拉臭臭。
胤禔老气横秋地想。
“这样啊。”惠嫔松了一口气，“大阿哥在慈宁宫过得可好？让额娘看看，唉，瘦……”
惠嫔看着圆润了一圈的胤禔，最终没能违心的把“瘦了”两个字说完。
惠嫔尴尬道：“大阿哥肯定在慈宁宫过得很好，都胖了。”
胤禔捏了捏自己手臂上的肉肉，得意道：“那是。和太子弟弟一起住的时候，每日吃什么太子弟弟都亲自带我去选。他总是知道什么好吃什么不好吃。太子弟弟病后，我有些吃不下东西，还瘦了一些。”
惠嫔松了一口气：“那就好，那就好。大阿哥在慈宁宫可遇到什么麻烦事？”
胤禔道：“还真有。”
惠嫔心里咯噔一下，差点不小心把丝绸帕子撕开。
我只是客套一下！你怎么还真有？！
惠嫔本着对大阿哥的了解，先把下人都遣走之后才问道：“什么事？和太子有关？”
胤禔点头：“太子吸引诅咒的事，额娘也知道吧。”
惠嫔心口怦怦跳。她就知道肯定是这件事！
惠嫔勉强笑道：“天花的事，难道还和诅咒有关？”
胤禔根据自己聪明才智汇集信息之后，斩钉截铁道：“有！疫情一结束，太子弟弟就病了！病得很严重！”
惠嫔干笑道：“也不是很严重，别胡说，太子殿下这不是已经好全……”
惠嫔话未说完，胤禔就打断道：“我还没说完，额娘先听我说完，你别打断我啊，这样很不懂礼貌。”
打断别人的话很不懂礼貌，这是太子给他讲故事的时候说的。胤禔就记下了。
惠嫔脑袋上飞出一连串问号。
你说我不懂礼貌？你还记得我是你额娘吗？你这样礼貌吗！
胤禔见惠嫔（被他噎得）闭嘴，满意地点点头，继续道：“弟弟安排宫务的时候，就像被谁附身了似的。我想把弟弟唤醒，太皇太后却阻止我，还拉着弟弟哭，好像附身弟弟的人她认识……哎哟……唔？唔唔唔？”
惠嫔捂着胤禔的嘴，吓得浑身发抖：“别说了！不准再提这件事！把这件事烂在肚子里，听到了吗！”
惠嫔又气又急又怕，眼泪都涌了出来。
胤禔见惠嫔哭了，疑惑地安静了下来。
惠嫔松开了手，把胤禔抱进怀里哽咽道：“别提这件事了好不好？太子的事皇上会关心，太皇太后会关心，我们娘俩不能掺和，会死的！”
惠嫔把“死”字咬得特别重，听得胤禔起了一身鸡皮疙瘩。
胤禔小小的心灵被震住了：“为什么？”
“没有为什么。”惠嫔抱着胤禔道，“你说的事，既然太皇太后知道，那么皇上肯定也知道。他们什么都没做，那就默许了这件事。你不要揭穿，不准揭穿知道吗？你就当什么都没发生过。你只是个孩子，忘记这些事很正常，你一定要忘记！”
胤禔喃喃道：“默许吗……可弟弟病了啊……很多人都说太子是汗阿玛最重要的孩子，他不是最重要的吗？”
惠嫔心中一凛。
谁说的？大阿哥身边居心叵测的人还没有清理干净？
“保清……”惠嫔松开怀抱，揉了揉大阿哥光溜溜的小脑袋。
胤禔抬起头。惠嫔很少称呼胤禔的小名，每当惠嫔这样称呼的时候，胤禔就知道惠嫔接下来说的话很重要，他必须听。
“太子对皇上、对太皇太后很重要。但皇上所有的孩子、所有的女人全部加一起，肯定比太子重要。”惠嫔残忍道，“明白了吗？重要是相对的。”
胤禔仔细思索了惠嫔的话，身体一颤，寒意从脊梁骨蔓延开来。
他明白了。
惠嫔再次道：“不要再提这件事了。当做不知道，好不好？”
胤禔神情恍惚道：“嗯，好……”
弟弟……太子弟弟……他的生病他的痛苦，全都是汗阿玛和太皇太后默许的？
这件事，弟弟自己知道吗？
胤禔想起胤礽曾经说过的话。
“我没有额娘，只有汗阿玛和乌库妈妈。好羡慕哥哥啊，哥哥有额娘疼。”
“哥哥要对惠嫔娘娘好。惠嫔只是哥哥一个人的亲额娘，你是她唯一最重要的人。”
亲额娘。
唯一最重要的人。
弟弟那么聪明，或许什么都知道？
胤禔嘴一瘪，嚎啕大哭。
弟弟好可怜！
