chapters.translated_text:
Kangxi was able to eliminate Oboi at the age of fourteen when no one believed in him; this shows that he is deep-scheming and extremely patient.

Even when he learned of the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, Kangxi only kept a grim face without showing much anger.

It had been a long time since anyone in the imperial palace had seen Kangxi this angry.

His face was twisted and ferocious, the veins on his forehead bulging. He smashed everything within reach and even drew the precious sword hanging on the wall to hack the desk in two.

After Kangxi vented his rage, he sat on the cold palace floor, pressing his throbbing temples, his eyes glaring gloomily at the sky outside the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

Kangxi wanted to kill someone right now.

He wanted to kill many people.

Those in the palace who had contracted smallpox, those who had exhausted Yinreng to this point, and even the Empress Dowager and the concubines who were useless and failed to handle palace affairs after the Grand Empress Dowager fell ill—Kangxi hated them all.

Although that irrational hatred soon faded, the anger in Kangxi's heart would not dissipate.

Finally, he took a long hot bath, soaking himself until he was dizzy, before he barely regained his composure.

Kangxi took Yinreng back to the Palace of Heavenly Purity to live with him, while the other princes remained in the Palace of Benevolence and Tranquility.

Yinreng’s high fever would break for a day and then return; he would wake up for a moment and quickly fall back asleep. The imperial physicians all said there was no danger to his life, but Kangxi could not set his mind at ease.

Wu Sangui was dead, and the government affairs were not urgent. Kangxi continued to suspend the morning court, staying to look after Yinreng.

Seeing Kangxi return, Yinreng’s spirit completely relaxed, and he let go of everything, refusing to worry about anything.

As soon as he woke up, he would whimper and burrow into Kangxi’s arms. After being fed and satisfied, he would play with the jade pendant at Kangxi’s waist for a while before falling back asleep.

Unlike other children, Yinreng did not cry or make a fuss no matter how sick he was, nor did he reject bitter medicine; he was very easy to take care of.

Whenever he had a little energy, Yinreng would roll and crawl around, attempting to harass Kangxi while he was reviewing memorials.

Kangxi was left between laughter and tears by Yinreng, and couldn't help but pinch his little nose: "Rest well and don't move around."

Yinreng whimpered: "Moving around makes it easier to get better. Ama, play with me."

Kangxi tossed the memorial onto the desk: "Play what?"

Yinreng thought for a moment and said: "Let’s play Xiangqi (Chinese chess)."

Kangxi asked: "Why Xiangqi and not Weiqi (Go)?"

Yinreng said: "Weiqi requires calculation and taxes the brain; I don't want to use my brain."

Kangxi tapped Yinreng’s forehead: "Xiangqi also requires brainpower. Forget it, come on, I’ll let you win."

Wrapped in a small quilt, Yinreng lay prone on the chessboard, his chin resting on a soft pillow, playing Xiangqi with Kangxi like a little caterpillar.

Although Kangxi let him win, Yinreng still lost more than he won. But regardless of winning or losing, he was cheerful, his interest not diminishing in the slightest.

Yinreng hadn't been this fond of chess before. Kangxi soon realized that Yinreng had noticed his anger and worry and was intentionally using chess to comfort him.

After finishing another game, Yinreng yawned while tidying up the pieces and was scooped into Kangxi’s arms.

Yinreng buried his face in Kangxi’s hard chest, bumping his nose a little, his voice carrying a nasal tone: "Ama, what’s wrong?"

"You focus on recovering from your illness; you don't need to do extra things to comfort Ama. Ama doesn't need your comfort," Kangxi said, tightening his embrace.

Yinreng gripped the clothes on Kangxi’s chest and said muffledly: "Ama is sad because of me, so of course I have to make Ama happy. Don't worry, Ama, as long as I eat a few more bowls of meat and drink a few more bowls of milk, I’ll be better soon."

"Little glutton." Kangxi rubbed his chin against the small braid on top of Yinreng’s head and managed a smile: "Eat, eat. As long as you don't overeat, eat as much as you want."

After Kangxi let him go, Yinreng arrogantly curled up in Kangxi’s arms, leaning back comfortably.

He looked up and said: "Ama, you haven't praised me yet."

Kangxi put on a stern face: "Praise you for what? Praise you for being sick?"

Yinreng said indignantly: "Hmph! I’m so amazing! Why aren't you praising me!"

Kangxi was silent for a while and said: "The Grand Empress Dowager said that your Grandfather possessed your body?"

Yinreng opened his eyes wide: "What?"

Kangxi said: "Did Grandfather possess your body to do these things?"

Yinreng was angry: "Slander! I did this myself! I am just this amazing!"

I only pretended for a little while! Most of the time I was just being myself, how am I like Grandfather at all! Grand Empress Dowager, you can't just give all my credit to Grandfather because you favor him!

If Ama thinks these things were all done by Grandfather, then what about my credit? What about the credit I can trade for a death-exemption talisman and a hot spring manor? Did Grandfather swallow it all!

Yinreng was so angry he patted Kangxi’s arm: "It was me! The credit is mine! I did it! What Grandfather! There is no Grandfather!"

Seeing the little milk bun almost jumping with rage, Kangxi laughed and calmed him down: "Alright, alright, it was you. What is this about what the Grand Empress Dowager said? She wouldn't mistake your Grandfather."

Yinreng tilted his head. How was he supposed to explain this?

Kangxi assumed Yinreng didn't remember clearly, so he guided him step by step.

Yinreng explained what he could clearly, and for the parts he couldn't, he covered his head and pretended to be a Psyduck meme, letting Kangxi, who had a wild imagination, fill in the blanks himself.

Based on Yinreng’s words, Kangxi imagined the following result.

Shunzhi might have truly possessed Yinreng for a while, but most of the time it was Yinreng acting himself, with Shunzhi offering advice, and only appearing for a short time after the Grand Empress Dowager called out Shunzhi’s name.

At that time, Yinreng’s memory was a bit blurry for a moment. At other times, Yinreng’s memory was very clear.

Even though Shunzhi was Kangxi’s father, Kangxi could not accept that Shunzhi could possess Yinreng. Especially since Yinreng’s illness this time was likely related to the possession.

A father who didn't love him much and was already dead, versus the precious son he raised with his own hands—did he even need to choose?

After reaching his preliminary guess, Kangxi immediately summoned Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai.

Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai had been living in the capital ever since they were implicated by Yinreng’s "supernatural" antics.

As the only two religious figures who could see Yinreng’s issues, they were on Kangxi’s radar. Although Kangxi would not appoint them as Imperial Preceptors, he provided them with money and food, summoning them when needed.

When Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai entered the palace, they exchanged a look, their expressions bitter.

Look, the time of need had arrived.

After seeing them, Kangxi didn't state Yinreng’s situation directly but beat around the bush to fish for information.

Emperors are naturally suspicious; they don't believe what they ask directly, only what they can trick out of people.

Kangxi asked as if purely out of curiosity whether the two possessed any psychic abilities.

The two were religious figures, not charlatans.

After careful consideration, Daoist Zhang answered first: "This humble Daoist has never seen it, but I have heard of people being possessed by ghosts. According to my observations, ghosts only possess people with weak Yang energy. If not for illness or weakness, even if something filthy possesses the body, it would be washed away by the body’s own Yang energy."

Something filthy... Kangxi’s mind flashed with the portrait of Shunzhi.

*Cough.* Ignorance is no sin; he wouldn't blame Daoist Zhang.

Master Dehai pondered for a long time and said: "Even if such things happen among the common people, Your Majesty is protected by dragon energy and purple aura. Upon contact with a spirit, it would immediately be shattered into dust; it is unlikely to see such a thing."

Kangxi thought to himself, no wonder Father had to wait until I left the palace to appear.

Kangxi asked again: "The Crown Prince is a hidden dragon; does he also have dragon energy and purple aura for protection?"

Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai said in unison: "It should be so. But the Crown Prince is young, and his internal Yang energy is insufficient, so one should still be careful."

Kangxi was silent for a long time before clarifying: "If the Crown Prince is constantly disturbed by a curse, would it increase the possibility of ghost possession?"

Even in the middle of winter, the backs of Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai were instantly soaked with sweat.

Is this a question we can answer! Your Majesty, please don't make things difficult for us!

Seeing the cold sweat on Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai, Kangxi sighed, then said with a sharp expression: "Answer me!"

Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai’s legs went weak, and they knelt down with a thud: "The Crown Prince is protected by Your Majesty; such a possibility is not high!"

Kangxi lowered his gaze, his knuckles tapping lightly on the back of the chair.

After a long while, once Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai’s legs were aching from kneeling, he said: "What if it is not an evil spirit, but an ancestor’s spirit? What if it is the Crown Prince’s own doing? How much harm does it do to the Crown Prince?"

Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai exchanged a look, both misunderstanding.

Could it be that the Emperor is eyeing the Crown Prince’s supernatural traits and wants to use the Crown Prince as a sacrifice to summon the ancestor’s spirit?

They say there is no father-son relationship in the imperial family, but this is too cruel!

As expected of barbarians.

Master Dehai sighed in his heart and said with a stiff neck: "A person only has so much Yang energy; for every bit of Yin energy, there is a bit less Yang energy. The two will always wax and wane. This act will not only harm the Crown Prince’s body but also damage the ancestor’s spirit; it must never be done!"

After finishing, Master Dehai kowtowed heavily to Kangxi several times.

He had staked everything.

Saving a life is better than building a seven-story pagoda. He was willing to die!

Daoist Zhang was hesitant, but seeing Master Dehai’s generous spirit, he closed his eyes, opened them, and made up his mind.

If one cannot even uphold their original heart, what is the point of cultivating the Dao?

If I help the Emperor sacrifice the Crown Prince today, my hands will surely be stained with more innocent blood in the future.

"This humble Daoist also believes so," Daoist Zhang said, prostrate on the ground. "Humans and ghosts are on different paths; humans have the mortal world, ghosts have the gates of hell, and ancestral spirits can ascend to the heavens. The three realms are different and should not be confused; it is harmful to both humans and souls. There are records of ancestors possessing descendants to help them, but it is at most through dreams. If an ancestor truly possesses a descendant, both the ancestor’s soul and the descendant’s body will be depleted."

Kangxi let the two kneel on the ground, and after a long time, he said coldly: "You two really dare to speak."

Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang said: "This humble monk/Daoist dares not deceive the Emperor."

Kangxi closed his eyes, his voice trembling: "A fine 'dare not deceive the Emperor'."

He smashed the teacup beside him onto the ground.

Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang’s bodies shook violently, but they gritted their teeth and held on.

After another long while, Kangxi regained his composure.

"You may rise." Kangxi granted them seats again. Zhao Chang, the only one serving in the palace, cleaned the floor and replaced Kangxi’s tea with a cup at the perfect temperature.

Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang breathed a sigh of relief. Thank goodness, did the Emperor have a change of heart?

Kangxi said: "I will rebuild temples and Taoist shrines at Fragrant Hill, and you two will be in charge."

Is this complete house arrest? Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang immediately knelt to thank him, feeling extremely miserable inside.

Kangxi let them rise again and asked: "If this has already happened, how can I protect the Crown Prince and the ancestor’s spirit?"

Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang: "..."

The two were stunned.

Already happened? No way, no way? Can such a thing happen? Is it this bizarre?

However, remembering that magical little Crown Prince, they were no longer certain.

Children don't lie unless adults lead them.

The late Empress had passed away, and the Crown Prince had been raised by the Emperor since childhood; it was impossible for others to mislead him, so the Crown Prince could never lie.

Was the Crown Prince really possessed by the late Emperor?

The two realized that to cover one lie, they would have to tell more, and they panicked.

Master Dehai, being older and more experienced, was the first to spin a lie: "The depletion of Yang energy is also a disease; no special remedies are needed. Just let the imperial physicians treat the illness. But if this doesn't stop, the body will repeatedly fall ill."

Daoist Zhang also thought of a way to gloss over it: "Ancestral spirits have incense and offerings; as long as they return to their proper place, they can recover after resting for a period. But if they descend to the world frequently, no amount of incense and willpower can sustain it. Your Majesty is wise and martial, and the Great Qing is flourishing; there is no need for ancestors to manifest and guide us. Your Majesty can let the ancestors rest assured and return."

Kangxi sighed.

I wish I could, but with Father’s stubborn nature, he doesn't even listen to the Grand Empress Dowager, let alone me, his son?

Kangxi finally understood. Shunzhi had contracted smallpox just when his ambitions were about to be realized; he was unwilling and had to do something.

Shunzhi wasn't intentionally tormenting Yinreng. But in that situation, if he hadn't stepped in to guide Yinreng, once the smallpox broke out and the palace fell into chaos, even if Yinreng had been inoculated, he might have encountered other dangers.

Moreover, in Shunzhi’s eyes, Yinreng might not be the most important.

All of Kangxi’s sons were Shunzhi’s grandsons, and the Grand Empress Dowager was Shunzhi’s own mother; together, they carried more weight than Yinreng.

The more Kangxi thought, the angrier he became, the more sorrowful he felt, and the more he cherished Yinreng.

Yinreng had no mother and only had him as an Ama. Everyone in the palace had people more important to them, and for the sake of those people, they could sacrifice Yinreng; only he could protect Yinreng.

Baocheng only has me left. Kangxi sighed in his heart, his eyes reddening.

Kangxi waved his hand, telling these two capable but useless men to get out.

Kangxi sat alone for a while and said: "Should I find more people to ask? These two are completely useless."

Zhao Chang lowered his head and remained silent.

After a while, Kangxi answered himself: "It is precisely because they can see the problem but have no solution that I believe them. If they had patted their chests and claimed they could solve it, they would be charlatans."

After saying this, Kangxi lamented: "No wonder charlatans have plagued every dynasty. Only charlatans would claim they can communicate with heaven and earth. Hmph, if they had the power to communicate with heaven and earth, why wouldn't they be the Emperor themselves instead of groveling at my feet?"

Zhao Chang dared not speak and continued to play dumb.

After Kangxi vented, he didn't know if his mood was better or worse.

He returned to the warm chamber and saw Yinreng sprawled out on the bed, sleeping soundly; his stern expression softened a little.

Kangxi poked Yinreng’s soft belly: "Baocheng, you really give me a headache."

Yinreng: "Hoo... hoo... hoo... *hiccup*, delicious!"

Kangxi was speechless.

This little fatty, even dreaming about eating. It seems his body will recover quickly.

Kangxi reached out to poke Yinreng’s slightly open mouth.

Yinreng "Ah-ang," bit down on Kangxi’s finger.

Kangxi: "...Ouch!"

Yinreng let go and glared: "Ouch!"

Zhao Chang’s head was almost touching his chest.

Can't laugh, can't laugh, laughing will cost me my head.

100,000

24. Two Chapters Combined [V]

When Kangxi went to see the Grand Empress Dowager, his finger was wrapped in a bandage.

The Grand Empress Dowager was startled at first, but when she heard that the injury on Kangxi’s finger was caused by Yinreng biting him, her expression was indescribable.

Kangxi sighed: "I should discipline Baocheng properly."

The Grand Empress Dowager said expressionlessly: "Did you stick your finger in his mouth while he was sleeping again? Why can't you learn your lesson!"

Kangxi’s gaze drifted. *Cough*, didn't get away with it.

The Grand Empress Dowager sighed: "Xuanye, how old are you? Why are you more mischievous than Baocheng?"

Kangxi thought, how am I more mischievous than that brat?

"Imperial Grandmother, is there a result regarding the smallpox?" Kangxi quickly brought up the serious matter, avoiding the Grand Empress Dowager’s nagging.

The Grand Empress Dowager frowned tightly: "See for yourself."

Sumalagu handed the testimonies to Kangxi; some of them were even stained with blood.

Kangxi opened the testimonies, his face growing gloomier as he read.

When he learned that someone had hidden the smallpox outbreak in the palace, Kangxi had already prepared for the worst.

Remnants of the former Ming? Remnants of Dorgon? The White Lotus Sect? The Three Feudatories?

Kangxi was even prepared to wash the entire inner palace in blood.

When he saw the testimonies, he felt a sense of relief, but also became even more furious.

The smallpox outbreak was hidden simply because of an old corruption case in the Imperial Household Department.

Back when Shunzhi died of smallpox, all the items he used should have been burned to prevent the spread. However, when the Imperial Household Department processed the large batch of precious items Shunzhi had used, they secretly embezzled them instead of destroying them completely.

These people knew how terrifying smallpox was, but greed clouded their hearts.

They thought that as long as they washed them, it would be fine, and as long as they wrapped them in cloth and sold them to others, it would be fine.

At that time, Kangxi was young, and the Grand Empress Dowager was busy dealing with the regents; the management of the Imperial Household Department was chaotic, and large quantities of items contaminated with smallpox were shipped out.

They didn't dare to use them at the time, but after a few years or a decade, when the wind died down, they took them out to use.

Actually, smallpox cannot survive that long away from a host. But during those dozen years, there were always people contracting smallpox, and they covered for each other, so Kangxi didn't know.

The reason the palace servants covered for each other was, naturally, because they were afraid of being exposed for stealing palace items and feared being implicated when the epidemic was cleared.

Smallpox became a common cold, deaths from illness became accidental deaths... and the smallpox epidemic was passed on in waves.

They were very lucky; the smallpox did not break out on a large scale and did not infect the nobles in the palace, so it was never discovered.

The belongings of those who had lived or died after contracting smallpox were also inherited by others.

As the saying goes, wealth moves the hearts of men.

When Yinreng contracted smallpox, this group of people panicked for a while. But Yinreng recovered quickly, and since no one else caught it, Kangxi did not conduct a thorough investigation of the palace servants, allowing them to muddle through once again.

It wasn't until Yinreng realized the curse was about to erupt and isolated the entire inner palace into small, sealed-off blocks that these people were finally ferreted out.

"A child has been infected with smallpox," the Empress Dowager sighed. "It seems Concubine Zhang's daughter won't make it."

Kangxi currently has three living daughters: the third princess born to Concubine Rong, the fourth princess born to Concubine Zhang, and the fifth princess born to Lady Zhao Jia, a Changzai.

Kangxi had a certain fondness for Concubine Zhang. She had borne him two daughters; the first died in infancy at the age of three, and now this one clearly wouldn't live to see her fourth birthday. Kangxi couldn't help but feel a sense of sorrow.

The Empress Dowager, however, let out a cold snort and said, "Why are you feeling heartbroken? Even her own mother doesn't care!"

Kangxi frowned: "What happened? The testimony didn't mention this."

The Empress Dowager said: "I had it removed. These records are to be archived; how could we write down the shameful secrets of the Imperial family? Baocheng ordered everyone to stay in their palaces and not go out, but that Zhang woman, in order to send money to her good-for-nothing brother, bribed the steward to let her confidante leave the palace. That confidante happened to be the Fourth Princess's wet nurse."

Kangxi’s brow furrowed tightly.

The Empress Dowager continued: "Later, Baocheng discovered this and plugged the loophole. But her luck was just that bad; the wet nurse happened to run into someone in the palace who had contracted smallpox. Everyone else in Concubine Zhang’s quarters was fine, but the Fourth Princess, being frail, was infected. Alas."

Kangxi closed his eyes, remaining silent for a long time before saying: "If the Fourth Princess doesn't pull through, send her back home."

The etiquette rules of the Qing inner palace were not strictly enforced; concubines without favor or children could be sent home, and those with children could live with their sons as Dowager Consorts.

Concubine Zhang’s crimes were not enough to warrant death, but Kangxi did not want to see her again.

The Empress Dowager nodded gently: "Your Majesty is benevolent."

In her heart, she sneered; Zhang had a gambling-addicted brother at home. Once she was sent out of the palace, her fate might be no better than death.

After finishing the matter of Concubine Zhang, the Empress Dowager began discussing the disposal of others.

It was normal for palace servants to have "sticky fingers," and both Kangxi and the Empress Dowager usually turned a blind eye, only reprimanding them when they went too far.

They didn't have the energy to manage every single one of them.

They hadn't expected that this chain of corruption, linking those above and below, would almost cause smallpox to spread throughout the palace, turning it into a situation that could only be resolved by ransacking homes and exterminating families.

"A few servants detrimental to the children were discovered at Concubine De's place; does it have anything to do with this?" Kangxi asked.

The Empress Dowager sighed: "It has nothing to do with it. She was rewarded for carrying the Imperial heir, which just made some people jealous."

Concubine De had been neglected in the palace for four years. Palace people were accustomed to fawning over the high and trampling the low, and since she had the temper of a pampered young lady before entering the palace, she had been treated very harshly during those four years.

Now that Concubine De had gained power, those who had once bullied her were filled with anxiety, fearing she would take revenge on them.

When people panic, they are prone to irrational actions. A few low-to-mid-level servants in the palace could join forces to make life difficult for a concubine.

Kangxi said indifferently: "For those who did it, execute those who should be executed, ransack the homes of those who should be ransacked, and exile those who should be exiled. Punish them severely to serve as a warning to others."

The Empress Dowager nodded; that was the right principle.

The occurrence of many major events in the palace might not be caused by some grand, earth-shattering conspiracy, but merely the accumulation of one small thing after another.

For example, covering for each other after embezzlement and theft, or acting like a cornered dog after trampling on others... so-called palace intrigue is just a combination of seemingly boring events that lead to massive consequences.

In the calm conversation between Kangxi and the Empress Dowager, the fates of individual lives and families were sealed. Among the three chief ministers of the Imperial Household Department, Hailaxun and Galu had their salaries docked, Tuba was demoted, and Feiyangwu filled Tuba's position.

A massive rectification of the Imperial Household Department began, leaving everyone in the palace feeling insecure; even the concubines were as silent as cicadas in winter, not daring to wander about.

The two spoke back and forth until the sun began to set, when the Empress Dowager hesitated and said: "Fulin, he..."

Kangxi sighed inwardly. The Empress Dowager truly cared more about his Imperial Father than Baocheng. Even though Baocheng was still ill, the first thing the Empress Dowager asked about was the Imperial Father.

Kangxi said: "I have invited Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai."

He told the Empress Dowager what Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai had said, without omitting a single detail.

After listening, the Empress Dowager judged from these details that what the monk and the Daoist said was true.

Kangxi frowned tightly and said: "Imperial Grandmother, can you persuade the Imperial Father?"

The Empress Dowager sighed: "When have I ever been able to persuade him?"

Kangxi said: "Baocheng has imperial physicians for his illness, but if something happens to the Imperial Father, I wouldn't know what to do."

Kangxi changed his form of address, speaking from the heart as a grandson.

If the Empress Dowager cared more about the Imperial Father, then approaching her from the perspective of the Imperial Father would be more effective in winning her over as an ally.

The Empress Dowager continued to sigh: "Why don't you ask Baocheng what unfinished business his grandfather has? If it’s about Lady Donggo, then just let him have his way."

Having learned that Shunzhi was not acting against her solely because of Lady Donggo, the Empress Dowager’s resentment toward her had dissipated quite a bit.

Kangxi said: "I don't think the Imperial Father cares about Lady Donggo. That boy Baocheng calls out 'Grandfather, the Emperor of the Ages' in his dreams every night. I fear he wants to see the Qing Dynasty become prosperous and flourishing in my hands."

The Empress Dowager slapped the table: "So he’s not coming back, is he?!"

That would take many years!

Kangxi said helplessly: "Grandmother, is there really no way?"

The Empress Dowager frowned: "Let me think, let me think... sigh..."

Just as the two sat opposite each other, looking troubled, the chirping laughter of children suddenly came from the side hall.

Both of their brows relaxed at the same time.

Kangxi rubbed his temples and said helplessly: "How can it be Baocheng's voice? Isn't he at the Qianqing Palace!"

The Empress Dowager stood up and said: "Let's go see."

The two walked to the side hall of the Cining Palace where the First Prince and the Third Prince were staying, and sure enough, it was Yinreng.

When Yinreng woke up this time and found Kangxi missing, he touched his forehead, felt that his fever had gone down, and immediately ran to the Cining Palace to play with the First and Third Princes.

He was bored out of his mind.

His only daily entertainment was playing chess; was this the life a child should lead!

As soon as Yinreng ran into the side hall of the Cining Palace, the First Prince rushed over and hugged him.

After Yinreng coaxed the First Prince for a long time, the Third Prince crawled over and hugged Yinreng as well.

The side hall of the Cining Palace was covered with thick carpets. In the end, the three of them piled on top of each other and started playing games on the floor.

The laughter of the three children was so loud that both the Empress Dowager and Kangxi heard it.

"Baocheng, why did you run here!" Kangxi stepped into the room and began to lecture the child.

"The fever is gone, so I came to find my brother and younger brother to play," Yinreng waved at Kangxi. "I originally wanted to pay my respects to Wuku Mama and the Imperial Father, but since you were discussing important matters, I came to find my brothers first."

"You can come in even if we are discussing important matters." Kangxi had someone carry the Third Prince back to the couch and lifted Yinreng up himself.

Yinzhi patted his bottom and stood up on his own: "Greetings to Wuku Mama, greetings to Imperial Father."

"Come, let me test your studies." Kangxi sat on the couch holding Yinreng and nodded at Yinzhi. "Let’s see if your studies have regressed in the few days I was away."

Yinzhi: "???" You know full well I haven't been attending classes during this time; are you deliberately bullying me in front of my younger brother?

How could Kangxi deliberately bully his eldest son? He was such a good father. A good father would, of course, care about his son's studies.

Yinreng gave Yinzhi a sympathetic look.

Big Brother, just admit your mistake decisively. As a son, you can't stop an old father's dirty desire to bully his son. Surrender quickly and you might suffer less.

Although Yinzhi feared Kangxi, he was also quite stubborn.

Since Kangxi wanted to quiz him, he said bluntly: "Imperial Father knows I haven't been studying these past few days, so what studies are you testing?"

Kangxi: "..." This brat, does he want a beating?

Yinreng hurriedly smoothed things over: "Imperial Father, Third Brother just started walking, shall we teach him how to walk?"

Kangxi shot his son a glare.

Yinreng always called Kangxi "Imperial Father" in front of others, which made Kangxi feel a bit uncomfortable.

As his Crown Prince, why should he care about the eyes of others?

"Imperial Father, Imperial, Father!" Yinreng tugged on Kangxi's sleeve, calling him rhythmically.

"Pfft." Yinzhi covered his mouth. "Imperial Father, I didn't laugh, and I didn't think of the 'Sweat-Blood Horse' either."

Kangxi: "..." He shouldn't have let the eldest and second sons get together! One is silly and the other is bad; they are specifically designed to ruin his mood!

"Baocheng!" Kangxi said sternly.

Yinreng raised his little face: "Imperial Father, please speak, your son is listening with his ears perked up!"

"How can you perk up your ears? You're not a rabbit!" Kangxi pinched Yinreng's ear. Yinzhi, who was standing in the corner as punishment for skipping class, showed a look of disapproval, which made Kangxi even angrier. "Baocheng! You are the Crown Prince! Playing like this with your brothers is not in accordance with the rules! Even if they are your brothers, they must respect you."

Yinreng’s eyes went dead.

Oh, the beginning of the nightmare has arrived.

Baocheng!~ You are the Crown Prince!~ Getting too close to your brothers is a sign of lacking the dignity of a Crown Prince!~ They cannot be disrespectful to you!~

Heh. Yinreng sneered unhappily in his heart.

Yinzhi, standing to the side, also sneered in his heart after hearing Kangxi's words, and showed a look of disdain.

Heh, just say you're jealous because your younger brother loves me more; Imperial Father, are you a sore loser?

Yinreng patted Kangxi's arm and said earnestly: "Alright, alright. If they take the initiative to play with me, it’s because they disregard my noble status as Crown Prince and damage my dignity. Then I will take the initiative to find them to play. If I, the dignified Crown Prince, go to find my brothers to play and they ignore me, then they are looking down on me as the Crown Prince. Imperial Father, what do you think of that?"

Kangxi: "..." I don't think much of it.

"Xuanye, that's enough, stop teasing the children." The Empress Dowager, who was watching the show, laughed out loud.

She beckoned to Yinzhi, who was standing in the corner, and pulled him into her arms to protect him: "Harmony between brothers is a good thing. You go ahead and play together; Wuku Mama will back you up, don't listen to your Imperial Father."

Kangxi: "..." Imperial Grandmother, can you stop causing trouble? I'm not joking, I'm being very serious!

"Imperial... Father?" Little Yinzhi crawled over, looking up at Kangxi.

Yinreng immediately said: "Little Three can call Imperial Father now! Little Three knows Imperial Father is Imperial Father! Little Three and Imperial Father share a father-son bond! Imperial Father, are you moved?"

Kangxi made a fist and tapped Yinreng on the head: "Not moved, move aside."

He tossed Yinreng to the Empress Dowager with disdain.

Yinzhi hurriedly pulled Yinreng to his side to protect him, looking at Yinreng’s head with great distress.

What is wrong with Imperial Father! The younger brother just recovered from an illness, and he actually hit him!

Kangxi rolled his eyes at his eldest and second sons and carefully picked up his third son.

"Yinzhi has grown so big." Kangxi laughed.

Little Yinzhi nodded, and a foul smell wafted out.

Kangxi: "..."

The Empress Dowager turned her face away.

Yinreng and Yinzhi covered their noses.

The wet nurse immediately rushed over to take little Yinzhi from Kangxi's hands.

Yinreng covered his nose and said: "Little Three pooped."

Yinzhi covered his nose and said: "He pooped as soon as Imperial Father picked him up; it really is a father-son bond."

Yinreng bumped into Yinzhi with his body: "Big Brother, I beg you, shut up! Don't bring trouble to Little Three!"

Yinzhi didn't care: "Imperial Father is a wise and martial emperor with an incredibly broad mind; why would he hold a grudge against a son who can't even walk yet? Even if Little Three pooped on Imperial Father, Imperial Father wouldn't hold it against him."

Yinreng: "..." He would still hold it against him.

Empress Dowager: "..." Is my eldest great-grandson smart or not? Forget it, whether he's smart or not, I can't save him anymore.

Kangxi’s expression turned ferocious.

He realized that the First Prince had so much nonsense to say because he had too little homework and was too idle!

Kangxi barely managed to keep a straight face as he hauled Yinreng away.

Before leaving, he glared fiercely at Yinzhi.

Yinzhi scratched his head and asked the Empress Dowager in confusion: "Wuku Mama, it wasn't me who pooped, why did Imperial Father glare at me?"

The Empress Dowager smiled: "Perhaps it’s because you are the older brother, and the Emperor believes you should be looking after the Third Prince."

Yinzhi’s eyes widened in disbelief: "I’m supposed to control when the Third Prince poops?! Imperial Father is being unreasonable!"

The Empress Dowager couldn't help it and laughed so hard her old waist almost gave out.

...

Kangxi did what he said he would.

Those in the palace who should be executed were executed, those who should be burned were burned, and once the epidemic passed, Kangxi performed another sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. The inner palace was fully unsealed, and the First Prince returned to Concubine Hui’s side.

As soon as he returned, Kangxi’s imperial decree arrived, adding several tutors and a great deal of homework, while deleting the riding, archery, and Boku classes that the First Prince loved most.

Concubine Hui trembled as she clutched her handkerchief: "First Prince, what did you do again?"

Why did the Emperor’s decree arrive the moment the First Prince returned?!

Yinzhi scratched his head: "Probably because I skipped all my classes during this time?"

That was probably it.

Imperial Father wouldn't increase my homework because of the Third Brother’s pooping incident, right? Imperial Father isn't crazy; he must know that no matter how many books I read, I can't stop the Third Brother from pooping.

Yinzhi thought with an old-fashioned air.

"I see." Concubine Hui let out a sigh of relief. "Did you have a good time at the Cining Palace? Let Mother see, sigh, you’ve lost..."

Concubine Hui looked at the rounder Yinzhi and ultimately couldn't bring herself to finish the word "weight."

Concubine Hui said awkwardly: "The First Prince must have had a very good time at the Cining Palace; you’ve even gained weight."

Yinzhi pinched the flesh on his arm and said proudly: "That’s right. When I lived with the Crown Prince, he personally took me to choose what to eat every day. He always knows what’s delicious and what isn't. After the Crown Prince got sick, I couldn't eat much, so I lost a little weight."

Concubine Hui breathed a sigh of relief: "That’s good, that’s good. Did you encounter any trouble at the Cining Palace?"

Yinzhi said: "Actually, I did."

Concubine Hui’s heart skipped a beat, and she almost accidentally tore her silk handkerchief.

I was just being polite! How can you actually have trouble?!

Based on her understanding of the First Prince, Concubine Hui dismissed all the servants before asking: "What happened? Does it have to do with the Crown Prince?"

Yinzhi nodded: "Mother, you know about the Crown Prince attracting the curse, right?"

Concubine Hui’s heart pounded. She knew it had to be this!

Concubine Hui managed a smile: "The smallpox matter, could it really be related to a curse?"

Yinzhi, having gathered information with his own intelligence, said firmly: "Yes! As soon as the epidemic ended, the Crown Prince got sick! He was very ill!"

Concubine Hui laughed dryly: "It wasn't that serious, don't talk nonsense. Isn't the Crown Prince already fully..."

Before Concubine Hui could finish, Yinzhi interrupted: "I haven't finished yet, Mother, listen to me first, don't interrupt me, it’s very impolite."

Interrupting others is impolite; this was what the Crown Prince told him when telling stories. Yinzhi had remembered it.

A series of question marks flew over Concubine Hui’s head.

You say I’m impolite? Do you still remember that I am your mother? Is this polite of you!

Seeing Concubine Hui close her mouth (choked by him), Yinzhi nodded with satisfaction and continued: "When the Crown Prince was arranging palace affairs, it was like he was possessed by someone. I wanted to wake him up, but the Empress Dowager stopped me and held the Crown Prince while crying, as if she knew the person possessing him... ouch... hmm? Mmm-hmm?"

Concubine Hui covered Yinzhi’s mouth, trembling with fear: "Stop talking! You are not allowed to mention this again! Bury this in your heart, do you hear me!"

Concubine Hui was angry, anxious, and terrified, and tears welled up in her eyes.

Seeing Concubine Hui cry, Yinzhi quieted down in confusion.

Concubine Hui let go and pulled Yinzhi into her arms, sobbing: "Don't mention this again, okay? The Emperor will care about the Crown Prince's affairs, and the Empress Dowager will care; we cannot get involved, we will die!"

Concubine Hui emphasized the word "die" so heavily that it gave Yinzhi goosebumps.

Yinzhi’s small heart was shaken: "Why?"

"There is no why." Concubine Hui hugged Yinzhi and said, "Since the Empress Dowager knows what you said, the Emperor must know too. They haven't done anything, which means they tacitly approved of it. You must not expose it, you are not allowed to expose it, do you understand? Just pretend nothing happened. You are just a child, it’s normal to forget these things, you must forget!"

Yinzhi murmured: "Tacitly approved... but the Crown Prince was sick... many people say the Crown Prince is the Imperial Father’s most important child, isn't he the most important?"

Concubine Hui’s heart went cold.

Who said that? Have the people with ulterior motives around the First Prince not been cleared out yet?

"Baoqing..." Concubine Hui loosened her embrace and rubbed the First Prince’s smooth little head.

Yinzhi looked up. Concubine Hui rarely called Yinzhi by his childhood name; whenever she did, Yinzhi knew that what she was about to say was very important and he had to listen.

"The Crown Prince is very important to the Emperor and the Empress Dowager. But all the Emperor’s children and all his women combined are definitely more important than the Crown Prince," Concubine Hui said cruelly. "Do you understand? Importance is relative."

Yinzhi thought carefully about Concubine Hui’s words, his body trembling as a chill spread from his spine.

He understood.

Concubine Hui said again: "Don't mention this again. Pretend you don't know, okay?"

Yinzhi said in a daze: "Yes, okay..."

Younger brother... Crown Prince... his illness and his suffering, were they all tacitly approved by the Imperial Father and the Empress Dowager?

Does the Crown Prince himself know about this?

Yinzhi remembered what Yinreng had once said.

"I don't have a mother, only the Imperial Father and Wuku Mama. I envy you, brother; you have a mother who loves you."

"Brother, be good to Concubine Hui. She is your only biological mother, and you are the only person most important to her."

Biological mother.

The only person most important.

The Crown Prince is so smart, perhaps he knows everything?

Yinzhi’s mouth puckered, and he burst into loud sobs.

The Crown Prince is so pitiful!

100,000

chapters.source_text:
胤礽疯狂打喷嚏。
康熙吓得叫了一排御医给胤礽看病，每个御医都说胤礽没事，最后只给胤礽开了些补药。
胤礽撇头，坚决不喝。
没病喝什么药，我宁可多吃点肉。
太医院院使道：“药食同源，太子殿下若不想吃补药，吃药膳也是可以的。”
胤礽扬起小脑袋，表情超级乖巧：“对吧对吧？可以不用喝药。阿玛，我不要喝药。”
康熙使劲挼了一下胤礽的小脑袋，叹了口气同意了。
“朕真是太娇纵你了。就再娇纵你几年，等你出阁读书时，看朕怎么收拾你。”康熙笑骂道。
胤礽被康熙挼得晃了晃小脑袋，心道，到时候我一定能想出不被你折腾的方法。
胤礽还未等到出阁读书这件麻烦事，先等到了另一件让他很不舒服的事。
天花疫情过去后不久，康熙十七年也过去了。
康熙一边过新年，一边一拍脑门。
哎！我家太子还没有东宫呢！所有朝代的太子都有东宫，我家太子不能没有。
于是，他让人修缮奉慈殿，改名为毓庆宫，作为太子东宫。
文武百官都说这是康熙的恩宠，是天大的喜事。
胤礽听闻这个消息后，眼泪都要委屈出来了。
这喜事给你们，你们要不？
毓庆宫在哪？在神霄殿和奉先殿中间的夹缝中。
那四四方方的小院子，墙挨着墙，还不如京城寻常富贵人家的四合院大。
宫殿之中就更惨了。本来毓庆宫就很狭小，还被真真假假的小门隔断成很多小房间。
胤礽上辈子就在京城上学，跟着老师混进故宫没有开放的地方帮过忙，也踏足过毓庆宫。
他去的毓庆宫还是经乾隆、嘉庆两朝增建过的，都感觉很窒息。
康熙时期，这里甚至只有一间宫殿。
现代时人们都戏称毓庆宫为小迷宫，胤礽还只觉得好玩。待现在恢复前前世记忆，胤礽差点把枕头哭湿。
额娘啊！这是人住的地方吗！
想想明朝时期的太子东宫是如今的撷芳殿加端敬殿、端本宫那么大一块，里面配备齐全，甚至还有东宫官吏上班的地方。
而我呢？我这算哪门子的太子东宫！
胤礽想起兄弟家的亭台楼阁，再想想自己的破烂房子小迷宫，气得直蹬腿。
康熙只以为胤礽不愿意离开他，便严肃地教育胤礽：“你小时候和朕一起住，长大了还和朕一起住吗？你是太子，当有自己的东宫。”
胤礽含着一泡眼泪：“阿玛，我去过奉慈殿。”
康熙：“嗯？”
胤礽QAQ：“那里非常非常非常小。”
康熙：“呃……”
胤礽o(╥_╥)o：“伯伯和我说过。裕亲王府可大可漂亮，好多花花草草假山小溪。”
康熙：“裕亲王府的确……”
胤礽(╥╯^╰╥)：“呜哇！！！我不要当太子，我要当亲王！我要宽敞的大房子！我要漂亮的花花草草！我要可以爬的假山和可以踩水的小溪！太子好惨啊！”
康熙认为胤礽说得很有道理。
于是，康熙抬起巴掌把胤礽揍了一顿。
再有道理，胤礽也不该嚎不当太子。
这次康熙揍得有点狠，把胤礽的小屁屁揍肿了。
揍完之后，康熙嘴上说着“太子要简朴”“太子当以身作则”“能住就行别挑剔”“那里至少离朕近”之类的屁话，然后落荒而逃。
再不逃，他都快被小奶团子给嚎服了。
胤礽趴在榻上哼哼唧唧养屁股。
在他的强烈抗议下，他的瓷的玉的镶嵌宝石的枕头变成了舒舒服服的棉花枕头。否则他这么趴着，下巴肯定得膈出很深的印子。
时值新年，刚功课加码不久的胤禔也放了假。
他来找胤礽来玩时，便看到胤礽趴在软绵绵的棉花枕头上垂泪。
棉花枕头很大。胤礽趴在棉花枕头上的时候，一张小脸全陷了进去，把棉花枕头变成了一个“凹”形，就像是胤禔早上吃的带馅儿的糕点。
胤禔坐到胤礽身旁，摸了摸胤礽头上的小揪揪：“怎么了？”
胤礽吸着鼻子道：“被汗阿玛揍了。”
胤禔皱眉问道：“揍屁股了？屁股肿了？”
胤礽瞥了胤禔一眼。大哥，你可以不说这么大声，好丢脸啊。
胤禔戳了一下胤礽的屁股，胤礽“嗷”的一声，差点蹦起来。
胤禔眉头皱得更紧了：“打得好狠。”
胤礽有气无力道：“嗯。”
两个小孩沉默了一会儿，胤禔蹬掉鞋子爬到榻上和胤礽并排趴着。
胤礽往旁边挪动，分给胤禔半个大枕头。
“怎么惹汗阿玛生气了？”胤禔小声问道。
“还不是毓庆宫的事。”胤礽闷闷道。他把和康熙的“争论”告诉了胤禔。
胤禔无语：“很明显，汗阿玛恼羞成怒。”
胤礽使劲捶打枕头：“就是！”可恶的阿玛！连小孩子都知道你是恼羞成怒！
胤禔伸手揉了揉胤礽的小脑袋：“毓庆宫……有那么狭小吗？”
胤礽瘪嘴：“哥哥可以去看看，就是神霄殿和奉先殿中间的奉慈殿。离乾清宫很近很近。”
胤禔知道那里，但还没过去玩过。
那里是供奉祖先的地方，平时没有庆典的时候香火也不断，胤禔很不喜欢那里的味道。
胤禔又问道：“亲王府……亲王府很好吗？”
“嗯。”胤礽把自己前前世和前世见过的亲王府模样告诉了胤禔。
亲王府占地非常广，大多糅杂了皇家园林和江南园林的风格，辉煌大气，亭台楼阁，假山河流，几步一景。
亲王除了有亲王府，还会在城郊有许多庄子。
他们可以打猎，可以下田地自己掰菜，可以到水中钓鱼游泳。
亲王还能随便在京城中玩。
古玩、酒楼、戏楼……大街小巷，他们想去哪里就去哪里。
胤礽的语言功底很强，将亲王府和宫外的繁华说得绘声绘色，胤禔眼中不由生出向往。
“爷将来也能有亲王府！”胤禔斩钉截铁道。
胤礽道：“哥哥当然有。哥哥十六七岁就会出宫建府。你是我哥哥，最低也是个郡王。郡王府和亲王府也就差一些装饰规格。哥哥还能自己督造王府，想选什么样的房子和园子就选什么样的房子和园子，呜。”
胤礽说完后，更加委屈了。
我怎么这么苦！
兄弟们都有大院子住，都可以天天在京城里逛街，就我只能被关在这狭小的宫墙内看四方天。这太子谁爱当谁当去！我不想干啦！
胤禔又揉了揉胤礽。除了这样，他也不知道该如何安慰胤礽是好了。
“每朝每代的太子东宫都那么小吗？”胤禔好奇道。
胤礽把脸埋在棉花枕头里使劲摇了摇头：“前明的东宫在前庭附近。就是撷芳殿和端敬殿、端本宫那一片，很大，靠近宫墙，可以随时出去。”
胤禔疑惑：“那为什么汗阿玛不把那一片给你？”
胤礽沉默了一会儿，苦笑道：“因为这里近吧。大哥，别问了。这不好回答。你小声点，他们听到我俩说的话，立刻就会告诉汗阿玛。”
胤禔也沉默了一会儿，才小声道：“我在额娘宫里可以随便说话，你在这里不可以吗？”
胤礽：“嗯。”
胤禔问道：“你什么时候可以随便说话？也是十六七岁长大后吗？”
胤礽把脸死死埋在枕头上：“我可是太子，一辈子都会在宫里。”
一辈子在宫里，和你不能随便说话有关系吗？
胤禔心中生出小小的疑惑。
但他现在已经在惠嫔的哭泣下学会了不立刻把疑惑说出来。
他没有再提东宫的事。
胤礽继续给胤禔讲宫外的故事。从京城内讲到京城外，从华夏内讲到华夏外。
胤禔还是不断插嘴打断胤礽的故事，胤礽让他“懂礼貌”，他一点都不“懂”。
爷是哥哥，不需要对弟弟懂礼貌。
胤礽说得口干舌燥，喝了一点水润喉后便困了。
胤禔拍了拍胤礽的后脑勺，让胤礽好好休息。
胤禔走出乾清宫暖阁时，抬头看了一眼飘洒的雪花，板着脸对伺候的小太监道：“先不回宫，去奉慈殿。”
雪天路滑，胤禔被小太监抱着走到未来毓庆宫会出现的位置。
康熙虽然早早定下了将奉慈殿改成毓庆宫的事，但现在还未出正月，匠人们还未开始施工。
正月需要祭祖，奉慈殿两旁的神霄殿和奉先殿都飘出了浓厚的香火味道。
胤禔捂了一下鼻子，抬脚走进了稍显破败的奉慈殿中。
奉慈殿的确很小。
它处在两个大宫殿的之间，和惠嫔所住的延禧宫仅隔着两面墙一个夹道，宽度越是延禧宫的一半，长度倒是差不多。
也就是说，这里的面积只有延禧宫的一半吧？
胤禔使劲迈着步子，用他的小短腿衡量奉慈殿的面积。
胤禔懂事以后，在宫外住了一段时日。
大臣的府邸面积很广，里面还有小花园。
他回到延禧宫之后，还嫌弃延禧宫面积小，光秃秃，还不如大臣家，一度认为自家额娘很不受宠。
现在他已经知道了，后宫的一宫之主，已经是顶顶厉害的妃嫔了。
太子弟弟呢？他一直听到周围人说太子弟弟是这全大清第二尊贵的人，哪怕太皇太后、皇太后、皇后都不如太子。
太子是国之储君，是未来的皇帝。
可胤禔亲眼见到的呢？
就这？就这？就这还不到延禧宫一半面积的狭小东宫？就这每到祭祀的时候连呼吸都不能顺畅的太子东宫？
胤禔站在雪地里。
他穿得很厚，怀里还揣着暖炉，但他却感到很冷。
很冷很冷。
“回延禧宫。”胤禔板着的脸，和在天花之役中发号施令的胤礽有些像。
和他的汗阿玛康熙也有些像。
兄弟、父子，大约都是相似的。
胤禔离开奉慈殿的时候，趴在小太监的肩膀上回望了一眼。
从祥旭门中望过去，能将奉慈殿的全景一览无遗。
纵观之后，这一片地方显得更为狭小阴暗。
天空中的雪花大片大片的飘落，将破败的奉慈殿牢牢盖住。
胤禔眼一花，好似看到了自家小小的奶团子弟弟站在了这小小的、被雪覆盖的破旧四方天中，就好像被笼子罩住了一眼。
胤禔立刻趴在小太监肩膀上，不敢再看。
回到延禧宫后，惠嫔见胤禔神情恹恹，疑惑道：“你不是去找太子玩了吗？”
太子脾气那么好，不太可能和自家儿子吵架啊。
胤禔点头，环视了一圈周围。
惠嫔欣慰地屏退了周围人：“太子遇到什么委屈了吗？”
自家孩子每日傻乐傻乐，也只有看到太子遇到委屈时，自己才会露出委屈的神色。
胤禔再次点头：“弟弟被汗阿玛揍了，揍得很惨，都爬不起来了。”
惠嫔惊讶地睁圆眼睛：“怎么会？！”
以万岁爷对太子的溺爱，还能把太子揍得起不了床？！太子才多大一点，万岁爷不怕把孩子揍出问题吗！
惠嫔心中叹气。若是她看到万岁爷揍自家儿子揍狠了，肯定会跪着求情阻止。以万岁爷的性格，气头过去冷静下来，便不会和孩子计较。
太子没有额娘，估计被揍的时候连个阻止的人都没有，才会这么惨吧。
太子还不到五岁啊！
胤禔又道：“弟弟因为不想要毓庆宫被揍了。我去毓庆宫看了看，很小，很窄，还不到咱们这一半。这里只有我、额娘和一些低位嫔妃，以后我还会搬出去，低位嫔妃也不占地方。弟弟……弟弟以后要在那里成家吧？那得多挤啊。”
惠嫔干笑道：“这你不用担心，皇上总不至于亏待太子。太子可是国之储君。”
胤禔道：“前明太子东宫在后宫外，撷芳殿和端敬殿、端本宫那很大一片地。弟弟却只有那么小一片地。弟弟真的是大清的储君吗？”
惠嫔沉默。
听胤禔这么一说，她也觉得毓庆宫这地方是不是太寒碜了一点。
奉慈殿就在延禧宫前面，长什么样她还不知道吗？
她之前想，奉慈殿肯定会被拆了重建，皇帝再怎么也不会亏待他亲手带大的太子。
可现在她又想，就奉慈殿那么点大地方，就算翻新，能翻出花来？
见惠嫔沉默，胤禔换了一个话题：“额娘，我听弟弟说了亲王府和宫墙外的事。以后额娘可以和我一起住对不对？亲王府可比延禧宫好多了。”
胤禔已经知道，太子的事只要他汗阿玛不想解决，没有人能救得了太子。他不再为难惠嫔，只是稍稍吐露心声。
孩子总会长大的。宫中的孩子尤其如此。
惠嫔无奈道：“那得等我成了太嫔才行。”
胤禔道：“那额娘一定要好好吃饭，不要生病，儿子等着把你接出宫。”
胤禔靠着惠嫔，将从胤礽那里听到的宫外的事结结巴巴不太连贯地告诉惠嫔。
满人并不太注重男女大防，惠嫔还是个孩子的时候，偶尔会被父兄带出门玩。
已经褪色的记忆在胤禔提到熟悉的事物时重新上了鲜活的颜色，惠嫔时不时补充一些自己曾经见过的、玩过的事。
胤禔仰头看着惠嫔。他端庄优雅的额娘此刻露出了仿佛小女儿般的活泼表情，连平静无波的眼神都泛起了光亮，就像是蕴含着许多小星星。
额娘这样真漂亮。
额娘也是想出宫住大房子大花园的。
“额娘，我一定努力！我一定会当上亲王，买许多大庄子大花园给额娘住。”胤禔拍着胸脯道，“额娘努力活，我一定能把你接出宫！”
“在外面可别提这件事，犯忌讳。”惠嫔笑着把儿子揽怀里，压低声音道，“好，额娘一定努力活。”
惠嫔不想让儿子当太子、当皇帝了。
连康熙亲手带大的太子都那么凄惨，她那疑心病慎重的万岁爷，能对自家儿子好？
还是出宫好啊。出宫到亲王府里当个儿孙环绕的老封君，养养花草逛逛街，也不比被拘在宫里殚精竭虑的老太后差。
……
康熙揍完儿子之后便后悔了。
他去找自己的知心表妹佟贵妃抱怨，胤礽真是太不乖了。自己给胤礽专门建造东宫，这多大的荣誉啊，胤礽居然不领情，还嚷着不当太子。
这时候，有太监回报，大阿哥去见了太子之后就去了奉慈殿，然后捂着鼻子被香火熏走了。
康熙：“……”
佟贵妃捏着帕子捂着嘴笑道：“表哥，要不换个地方？那地方确实……”
康熙：“……”他怎么没想到儿子会被香火熏这一点？
康熙揉了揉额头：“没有比那里更近的还空着的地方了。”
佟贵妃无奈道：“太子东宫……其实可以不用离乾清宫太近。”
康熙沉默不语。
佟贵妃笑着道：“表哥担心太子太小无法照顾自己，可以先建好东宫，等太子成婚之后再搬过去住。我想太子在成婚前，也更愿意和表哥一起住。”
康熙终于露出笑容：“那倒是。”
他叹了口气：“罢了，朕再想想。”
“表哥要不回去看看太子吧？太子还那么小，刚病愈又被揍……”佟贵妃担忧道。
康熙尴尬道：“朕没揍他，朕只拍了他屁股几下。”
佟贵妃不赞同道：“太子还小。表哥你的力气多大，你自己不知道吗？”
康熙知道。康熙怎么不知道。他可是能拉十一力弓的人！
康熙摸了摸鼻子，灰溜溜地走了。
康熙离开之后，佟贵妃深深叹了一口气。
男人带孩子，就是养得糙，可怜小太子了。
自从宫中天花之事后，佟贵妃对太子的嫉妒和醋意淡了，对赫舍里皇后的嫉妒和醋意更深了。
这么好的孩子啊，怎么就不是我儿子呢？要是我儿子，我一定将他宠上天去，哪会被皇帝揍？
“可娘娘，如果仁孝皇后上天有灵，看着太子这样……”老嬷嬷道。
佟贵妃再次深深叹了一口气。
看来宫里的女人不仅要孩子，还得自己也活着才行，才不会让自己的孩子被欺负了去。
‎

chapters.translated_text:
Yinreng sneezed uncontrollably.

Kangxi was so frightened that he summoned a line of imperial physicians to examine Yinreng. Every physician claimed Yinreng was fine, and in the end, they only prescribed some tonics.

Yinreng turned his head away, firmly refusing to drink them.

Why drink medicine when I’m not sick? I’d rather eat more meat.

The head of the Imperial Hospital said, "Medicine and food share the same origin. If Your Highness the Crown Prince does not wish to take tonics, medicinal meals are also acceptable."

Yinreng lifted his little head, his expression super well-behaved: "Right, right? I don't have to drink medicine. Ama, I don't want to drink medicine."

Kangxi ruffled Yinreng’s little head vigorously and sighed in agreement.

"I really spoil you too much. I'll spoil you for a few more years. When you move to the study hall, just wait and see how I deal with you," Kangxi said with a laugh.

Yinreng’s head wobbled from Kangxi’s ruffling, and he thought to himself, by then, I’ll definitely come up with a way to avoid being tormented by you.

Before Yinreng could even wait for the trouble of moving to the study hall, he encountered another matter that made him very uncomfortable.

Not long after the smallpox epidemic passed, the seventeenth year of Kangxi also came to an end.

As Kangxi celebrated the New Year, he suddenly slapped his forehead.

Oh! My Crown Prince doesn't have an Eastern Palace yet! Crown Princes of all dynasties have an Eastern Palace; my Crown Prince cannot be without one.

Thus, he ordered the renovation of the Fengci Hall, renaming it the Yuqing Palace, to serve as the Crown Prince's Eastern Palace.

All the civil and military officials praised this as Kangxi’s favor, a joyous event of the highest order.

When Yinreng heard the news, he was so aggrieved he almost burst into tears.

If this is such a joyous event, you take it, do you want it?

Where is the Yuqing Palace? It’s in the narrow gap between the Shenxiao Hall and the Fengxian Hall.

That square little courtyard, with walls pressed against walls, wasn't even as large as the courtyard houses of ordinary wealthy families in the capital.

The palace buildings were even worse. The Yuqing Palace was already cramped, and it was further partitioned into many tiny rooms by real and fake doors.

In his previous life, Yinreng had gone to school in the capital and had even helped out in the restricted areas of the Forbidden City with his teachers, stepping foot into the Yuqing Palace.

The Yuqing Palace he visited had been expanded during the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, and even then, it felt suffocating.

During Kangxi’s reign, there was only one palace building here.

In modern times, people jokingly called the Yuqing Palace a "little maze," and Yinreng had only thought it was fun. Now that he had recovered his memories from his life before the last, Yinreng almost soaked his pillow with tears.

Mother! Is this a place for humans to live!

Think about the Eastern Palace of the Ming Dynasty—it was as large as the current Xiefang Hall, Duanjing Hall, and Duanben Palace combined, fully equipped, and even had offices for Eastern Palace officials.

And me? What kind of Crown Prince's Eastern Palace is this!

Yinreng thought of his brothers' pavilions and gardens, then thought of his own dilapidated little maze, and kicked his legs in anger.

Kangxi only thought Yinreng didn't want to leave him, so he sternly lectured him: "You lived with me when you were little, do you want to live with me when you grow up? You are the Crown Prince; you should have your own Eastern Palace."

Yinreng, with tears welling up, said: "Ama, I’ve been to the Fengci Hall."

Kangxi: "Hmm?"

Yinreng QAQ: "It is very, very, very small."

Kangxi: "Uh..."

Yinreng o(╥_╥)o: "Uncle told me. The Prince Yu Mansion is so big and beautiful, with so many flowers, plants, rockeries, and little streams."

Kangxi: "The Prince Yu Mansion is indeed..."

Yinreng (╥╯^╰╥): "Waaa!!! I don't want to be the Crown Prince, I want to be a Prince! I want a spacious house! I want beautiful flowers and plants! I want rockeries to climb and streams to splash in! Being the Crown Prince is so miserable!"

Kangxi thought Yinreng’s words made a lot of sense.

Consequently, Kangxi raised his hand and gave Yinreng a spanking.

No matter how much sense he made, Yinreng shouldn't be howling about not wanting to be the Crown Prince.

This time, Kangxi hit a bit hard, swelling up Yinreng’s little bottom.

After the spanking, Kangxi muttered some nonsense about "the Crown Prince must be frugal," "the Crown Prince must lead by example," "it’s fine as long as you can live there, don't be picky," and "at least it's close to me," then fled the scene.

If he didn't flee, he would have been worn down by the little milk bun's howling.

Yinreng lay on the couch, whimpering and nursing his bottom.

Under his strong protest, his porcelain, jade, and gem-encrusted pillows were replaced with comfortable cotton ones. Otherwise, lying like this, his chin would surely have left deep indentations.

It was New Year, and Yinzhi, who had just had his studies increased, was also on break.

When he came to play with Yinreng, he saw Yinreng lying on the soft cotton pillow, shedding tears.

The cotton pillow was large. When Yinreng lay on it, his little face sank into it, turning the pillow into a "concave" shape, just like the filled pastries Yinzhi ate in the morning.

Yinzhi sat beside Yinreng and touched the little tuft of hair on Yinreng’s head: "What’s wrong?"

Yinreng sniffled and said: "I was beaten by Han Ama."

Yinzhi frowned and asked: "Did he hit your bottom? Is it swollen?"

Yinreng glanced at Yinzhi. Big Brother, you don't have to say it so loudly, it's so embarrassing.

Yinzhi poked Yinreng’s bottom, and Yinreng let out an "Ouch," almost jumping up.

Yinzhi’s brow furrowed even tighter: "That was a hard hit."

Yinreng said weakly: "Yeah."

The two children were silent for a while, then Yinzhi kicked off his shoes and climbed onto the couch to lie side-by-side with Yinreng.

Yinreng moved to the side, sharing half of the large pillow with Yinzhi.

"Why did you make Han Ama angry?" Yinzhi asked in a low voice.

"It’s about the Yuqing Palace," Yinreng said gloomily. He told Yinzhi about the "argument" with Kangxi.

Yinzhi was speechless: "Obviously, Han Ama was embarrassed and angry."

Yinreng pounded the pillow hard: "Exactly!" That hateful Ama! Even a child knows you were just embarrassed and angry!

Yinzhi reached out and rubbed Yinreng’s little head: "Is the Yuqing Palace... really that small?"

Yinreng pouted: "Brother, you can go see it. It’s the Fengci Hall between the Shenxiao Hall and the Fengxian Hall. It’s very, very close to the Qianqing Palace."

Yinzhi knew the place, but hadn't been there to play.

It was a place for worshipping ancestors, and even when there were no ceremonies, the incense smoke was constant. Yinzhi didn't like the smell there.

Yinzhi asked again: "Is the Prince's Mansion... is the Prince's Mansion very nice?"

"Yeah." Yinreng told Yinzhi what the Prince's mansions he had seen in his life before the last and his previous life looked like.

The Prince's mansions occupied a vast area, mostly blending the styles of imperial gardens and Jiangnan gardens, magnificent and grand, with pavilions, towers, rockeries, and rivers—a new scene every few steps.

Besides the mansion, Princes also had many estates in the suburbs.

They could hunt, go into the fields to pick vegetables, and fish or swim in the water.

Princes could also play freely in the capital.

Antique shops, restaurants, theaters... in the streets and alleys, they could go wherever they wanted.

Yinreng had a strong command of language and described the Prince's mansion and the prosperity outside the palace so vividly that Yinzhi couldn't help but feel a sense of longing.

"I will have a Prince's mansion in the future too!" Yinzhi said decisively.

Yinreng said: "Of course Brother will. Brother will move out of the palace and build a mansion at sixteen or seventeen. You are my brother, at the very least you'll be a Junwang (Prince of the Second Rank). A Junwang mansion is only slightly different in decoration specifications from a Prince's mansion. Brother can even supervise the construction of the mansion yourself, choosing whatever house and garden you want, woo."

After Yinreng finished speaking, he felt even more aggrieved.

Why am I so miserable!

My brothers all have big courtyards to live in, and they can go shopping in the capital every day, while I can only be locked within these narrow palace walls looking at a square patch of sky. Whoever wants to be this Crown Prince can have it! I don't want to do it anymore!

Yinzhi rubbed Yinreng again. Besides this, he didn't know how else to comfort him.

"Is the Eastern Palace of every dynasty's Crown Prince that small?" Yinzhi asked curiously.

Yinreng buried his face in the cotton pillow and shook his head vigorously: "The Eastern Palace of the former Ming was near the front court. It was the area with the Xiefang Hall, Duanjing Hall, and Duanben Palace. It was very large and close to the palace wall, so one could go out at any time."

Yinzhi was puzzled: "Then why didn't Han Ama give you that area?"

Yinreng was silent for a while, then smiled bitterly: "Because it’s close here, I guess. Brother, don't ask anymore. It’s hard to answer. Keep your voice down; if they hear what we’re saying, they’ll tell Han Ama immediately."

Yinzhi was also silent for a while before whispering: "I can speak freely in my mother's palace, can't you do that here?"

Yinreng: "Yeah."

Yinzhi asked: "When can you speak freely? Is it also when you grow up at sixteen or seventeen?"

Yinreng buried his face firmly in the pillow: "I am the Crown Prince; I will be in the palace for my whole life."

Does being in the palace for your whole life have anything to do with not being able to speak freely?

A small doubt arose in Yinzhi’s heart.

But he had already learned from Concubine Hui’s tears not to voice his doubts immediately.

He didn't mention the Eastern Palace again.

Yinreng continued to tell Yinzhi stories about the outside of the palace. From inside the capital to outside, from within China to beyond.

Yinzhi still kept interrupting Yinreng’s stories, and Yinreng told him to "be polite," but he wasn't "polite" at all.

I am the older brother, I don't need to be polite to my younger brother.

Yinreng’s mouth was dry from talking, and after drinking some water to moisten his throat, he felt sleepy.

Yinzhi patted the back of Yinreng’s head, telling him to get some good rest.

When Yinzhi walked out of the Qianqing Palace’s warm chamber, he looked up at the falling snowflakes and said with a straight face to the little eunuch serving him: "We aren't going back to the palace yet, go to the Fengci Hall."

The road was slippery with snow, and Yinzhi was carried by the little eunuch to the spot where the future Yuqing Palace would be.

Although Kangxi had long decided to convert the Fengci Hall into the Yuqing Palace, it was not yet the end of the first lunar month, and the craftsmen had not yet begun construction.

Ancestor worship was required during the first lunar month, and the Shenxiao Hall and Fengxian Hall on either side of the Fengci Hall were emitting thick scents of incense.

Yinzhi covered his nose and stepped into the slightly dilapidated Fengci Hall.

The Fengci Hall was indeed very small.

It was situated between two large palace halls, separated from the Yanxi Palace, where Concubine Hui lived, by only two walls and a narrow alley. Its width was half that of the Yanxi Palace, though its length was about the same.

In other words, the area here was only half that of the Yanxi Palace?

Yinzhi took large strides, using his short legs to measure the area of the Fengci Hall.

After Yinzhi became sensible, he had lived outside the palace for a period of time.

The mansions of high officials were very large and even had small gardens inside.

After returning to the Yanxi Palace, he had complained that the Yanxi Palace was small and bare, not as good as the officials' homes, and once thought his mother was not favored.

Now he knew that the mistress of a palace in the inner court was already a top-tier consort.

What about the Crown Prince brother? He had always heard people around him say that the Crown Prince was the second most noble person in the entire Qing Dynasty, even more so than the Empress Dowager, the Empress, or the Consort Dowager.

The Crown Prince was the heir to the nation, the future emperor.

But what had Yinzhi seen with his own eyes?

This? Just this? This cramped Eastern Palace that was less than half the size of the Yanxi Palace? This Crown Prince’s Eastern Palace where one couldn't even breathe properly during sacrifices?

Yinzhi stood in the snow.

He was dressed warmly and had a hand warmer in his arms, but he felt very cold.

Very, very cold.

"Return to the Yanxi Palace." Yinzhi’s straight face looked somewhat like Yinreng’s when he was giving orders during the smallpox epidemic.

It also looked somewhat like his Han Ama, Kangxi.

Brothers and father-son, they were all quite similar.

As Yinzhi left the Fengci Hall, he looked back over the little eunuch’s shoulder.

Looking from the Xiangxu Gate, one could see the entire view of the Fengci Hall.

Looking at it as a whole, this area seemed even more cramped and gloomy.

The snowflakes in the sky fell in large flakes, firmly covering the dilapidated Fengci Hall.

Yinzhi’s eyes blurred, and he seemed to see his little milk bun brother standing in this tiny, snow-covered, dilapidated square patch of sky, as if he were trapped in a cage.

Yinzhi immediately buried his face in the little eunuch’s shoulder, not daring to look again.

After returning to the Yanxi Palace, Concubine Hui saw Yinzhi’s listless expression and asked in confusion: "Didn't you go to find the Crown Prince to play?"

The Crown Prince had such a good temper, it was unlikely he would quarrel with her son.

Yinzhi nodded and looked around at the people nearby.

Concubine Hui, feeling relieved, dismissed the people around them: "Did the Crown Prince encounter some grievance?"

Her own child was happy and silly every day, and only when he saw the Crown Prince in trouble would he show a look of grievance.

Yinzhi nodded again: "Brother was beaten by Han Ama, beaten very badly, he couldn't even get up."

Concubine Hui opened her eyes wide in surprise: "How could that be?!"

With the Emperor’s doting on the Crown Prince, how could he beat him until he couldn't get out of bed?! How old is the Crown Prince? Isn't the Emperor afraid of causing the child harm!

Concubine Hui sighed in her heart. If she saw the Emperor beating her own son too hard, she would definitely kneel and beg for mercy to stop him. Given the Emperor’s personality, once his anger passed and he calmed down, he wouldn't hold it against the child.

The Crown Prince had no mother; he probably didn't even have anyone to stop the beating, which is why it was so miserable.

The Crown Prince wasn't even five years old yet!

Yinzhi added: "Brother was beaten because he didn't want the Yuqing Palace. I went to see the Yuqing Palace, it’s very small, very narrow, not even half the size of ours. There’s only me, Mother, and some low-ranking concubines here, and I’ll move out later, so the low-ranking concubines don't take up much space. Brother... Brother will have to start a family there in the future, right? That must be so crowded."

Concubine Hui smiled dryly: "You don't need to worry about that; the Emperor wouldn't treat the Crown Prince poorly. The Crown Prince is the heir to the nation."

Yinzhi said: "The former Ming Crown Prince’s Eastern Palace was outside the inner court, in that large area of the Xiefang Hall, Duanjing Hall, and Duanben Palace. But Brother only has such a small piece of land. Is Brother really the heir to the Qing Dynasty?"

Concubine Hui was silent.

Hearing Yinzhi say this, she also felt that the Yuqing Palace was a bit too shabby.

The Fengci Hall was right in front of the Yanxi Palace; didn't she know what it looked like?

She had previously thought that the Fengci Hall would definitely be demolished and rebuilt, and no matter what, the Emperor wouldn't treat the Crown Prince he raised himself poorly.

But now she thought, with such a small space as the Fengci Hall, even if it were renovated, could it really be anything special?

Seeing Concubine Hui silent, Yinzhi changed the subject: "Mother, I heard from Brother about the Prince's mansion and things outside the palace walls. In the future, Mother can live with me, right? A Prince's mansion is much better than the Yanxi Palace."

Yinzhi already knew that as long as his Han Ama didn't want to solve the Crown Prince's problems, no one could save him. He didn't want to make things difficult for Concubine Hui, just slightly revealed his heart.

Children always grow up. This is especially true for children in the palace.

Concubine Hui said helplessly: "That will have to wait until I become a Dowager Concubine."

Yinzhi said: "Then Mother must eat well, don't get sick, your son will wait to take you out of the palace."

Yinzhi leaned against Concubine Hui, stuttering and incoherently telling her about the things outside the palace he had heard from Yinreng.

The Manchus didn't pay much attention to the separation of men and women; when Concubine Hui was a child, she was occasionally taken out to play by her father and brothers.

Faded memories regained their vivid colors when Yinzhi mentioned familiar things, and Concubine Hui occasionally added some things she had seen and played with herself.

Yinzhi looked up at Concubine Hui. His dignified and elegant mother now showed a lively expression like a young girl, and even her calm, waveless eyes shone with light, as if they contained many little stars.

Mother looks so beautiful like this.

Mother also wants to live in a big house with a big garden outside the palace.

"Mother, I will definitely work hard! I will definitely become a Prince and buy many big estates and big gardens for Mother to live in," Yinzhi said, patting his chest. "Mother, try to live long, I will definitely be able to take you out of the palace!"

"Don't mention this outside, it’s a taboo." Concubine Hui smiled and pulled her son into her arms, lowering her voice. "Okay, Mother will definitely try to live long."

Concubine Hui didn't want her son to be the Crown Prince or the Emperor anymore.

If even the Crown Prince raised by Kangxi himself was so miserable, could her suspicious and cautious Emperor treat her own son well?

It’s better to be out of the palace. Being an old matriarch in a Prince's mansion, surrounded by children and grandchildren, raising flowers and plants, and going shopping, wouldn't be any worse than being an old Empress Dowager trapped in the palace, racking her brains.

...

Kangxi regretted it after beating his son.

He went to complain to his confidante cousin, Noble Consort Tong, that Yinreng was really not well-behaved. He had specially built an Eastern Palace for Yinreng, what a great honor, yet Yinreng didn't appreciate it and even clamored about not wanting to be the Crown Prince.

At this time, a eunuch reported that the First Prince had gone to see the Crown Prince and then went to the Fengci Hall, only to be driven away by the smell of incense while covering his nose.

Kangxi: "..."

Noble Consort Tong held her handkerchief to her mouth and laughed: "Cousin, why not change the location? That place is indeed..."

Kangxi: "..." How did he not think about his son being driven away by the incense?

Kangxi rubbed his forehead: "There is no other empty place closer than that."

Noble Consort Tong said helplessly: "The Crown Prince's Eastern Palace... actually doesn't have to be too close to the Qianqing Palace."

Kangxi remained silent.

Noble Consort Tong smiled and said: "Cousin is worried that the Crown Prince is too young to take care of himself, so you can build the Eastern Palace first and let him move in after he gets married. I think the Crown Prince would prefer to live with you before he gets married."

Kangxi finally smiled: "That’s true."

He sighed: "Fine, I’ll think about it again."

"Why doesn't Cousin go back to see the Crown Prince? The Crown Prince is still so young, just recovered from illness and was beaten..." Noble Consort Tong said with concern.

Kangxi said awkwardly: "I didn't beat him, I only patted his bottom a few times."

Noble Consort Tong disapproved: "The Crown Prince is still young. How much strength do you have, Cousin, don't you know?"

Kangxi knew. How could Kangxi not know? He was someone who could pull an eleven-strength bow!

Kangxi touched his nose and slunk away.

After Kangxi left, Noble Consort Tong sighed deeply.

Men raising children are just rough; poor little Crown Prince.

Ever since the smallpox incident in the palace, Noble Consort Tong’s jealousy and envy toward the Crown Prince had faded, while her jealousy and envy toward Empress Hesheli had deepened.

Such a good child, why isn't he my son? If he were my son, I would definitely spoil him to the heavens, how could he be beaten by the Emperor?

"But Your Ladyship, if Empress Renxiao has a spirit in heaven, watching the Crown Prince like this..." the old nanny said.

Noble Consort Tong sighed deeply again.

It seems that women in the palace not only need children, but they must also stay alive themselves so that their children won't be bullied.

100,000

Author's Note:

Five thousand words today! Counts as a double update!

Covering my mouth in shock, such a heartwarming story, why are there readers saying it's abusive and that they cried? Are we reading the same story...

Note: The Zhai Palace was the Shenxiao Hall before the Yongzheng reign, a place for worshipping deceased empress dowagers; the Nansansuo was built during the Qianlong reign.

chapters.title: 第 26 章 [V]
chapters.source_text:
康熙回到乾清宫暖阁的时候，胤礽正在睡觉。
小孩子趴着睡觉很容易流口水。胤礽头歪到一旁，口水打湿了一块枕头，小嘴巴一会儿动一下，看上去就像是做梦还在啃肉骨头的小狗崽。
康熙让赵昌拿来纸笔，看一眼熟睡的胤礽，低头勾一笔画，画了个趴着睡的年画宝宝。
康熙皱着眉看了许久自己白描的儿子，怎么看都觉得画上的人比起儿子差远了。
赵昌向来擅长揣摩圣意，立刻小声道：“那些西洋画师或许更擅长写实的肖像画。”
康熙叹气：“可朕想亲自给保成画。”
总不能让那些西洋画师趁着胤礽睡觉的时候偷偷画画吧？他可不想把宝贝儿子睡觉的窘态给别人看。大清的太子要脸的。
赵昌想不出法子了。
总不能提议让万岁爷自己去学西洋画吧？
康熙不信邪。他让人拿来了许多画具，粗的细的笔一大堆，挨个尝试。
胤礽一觉睡醒的时候，康熙已经丢掉了一地的画。
“阿……哈……阿玛。”胤礽脸埋在枕头上擦了擦，蹭掉了嘴边的口水，打着哈欠和康熙打招呼。
康熙忙把刚画完的画给胤礽看：“像不像？”
胤礽沉默。
像个屁。
胤礽露出鄙视的表情：“阿玛画画真烂，不像我，像小狗！”
赵昌忍笑。这天底下也只有太子爷敢这么说皇帝，皇帝还不生气。
“你本来就像小狗，赏你了。”康熙拿出印章美滋滋的盖上，还题字表明这就是胤礽，谁也不准反对。
胤礽气得直哼哼。
康熙让人把画拿去装裱，捏住胤礽哼哼的小鼻子道：“怎么老喜欢哼哼？你是小猪猪吗？”
“阿玛，我是小猪猪，你是什么？”胤礽使劲甩脑袋，把康熙捏着他鼻子的手甩掉。
康熙按住乱动的胤礽：“朕是养小猪猪的人啊。屁屁还疼吗？以后不准乱说话。”
胤礽继续哼哼：“太子就是惨！”
康熙高高举起手掌。
胤礽继续哼哼：“就是惨！”
康熙放下了手掌，无奈道：“好了，朕会给你换个大房子，行了吧？反正你成婚之前也不会去住东宫，要求怎么这么多？”
胤礽心道，你要求不高，你来住试试？
我住狭小的毓庆宫，我的宫人们住撷芳殿，我去睡个觉得从后宫走到前庭，我不要脸吗？
胤礽这辈子是不可能有后宫了。他接受的教育不允许，害怕上辈子妈妈会在梦中打烂他的屁股。
到时候只和太子妃一起住，其实毓庆宫也不是特别挤？
还是好惨嗷嗷嗷！
胤礽不满道：“要花园。”
康熙敷衍：“嗯嗯嗯。”
胤礽不满道：“要大房子。”
康熙敷衍：“好好好。”
胤礽瞪圆眼睛。什么都同意吗？
“那、那要温泉也行吗？”胤礽搓搓小手。
“嗯……嗯？！”康熙捏住胤礽搓搓的小手，“宫里哪来的温泉？你又是从哪知道温泉的？”
康熙问完之后，叹气道：“肯定是你玛法对不对？”
胤礽：“嘿嘿嘿。”趁着玛法还能当背锅侠，多背几口锅，孙儿谢谢您了！
康熙笑道：“宫里没可能给你挖温泉。你喜欢温泉，明年过冬我们去温泉行宫。”
若不是三藩之乱，这两年冬天康熙也不会住在宫中。
他夏秋避暑，冬春避寒，在宫里待的时间满打满算不超过三个月。
所以康熙给胤礽选东宫的时候就随便选了一个近的地方。他不住宫里，胤礽以后自然也不会住宫里。
不过儿子既然想要大房子，宫里也不是没有旧宫殿拆了给他造大房子。
花园也是。宫里只有一处后花园还是太少了，可以再建几个。
现在三藩之乱已解，康熙口袋稍稍宽裕，可以想这些享受的事。
胤礽见好就收。
“阿玛一言九鼎！”他利索的爬起来，不装了。
康熙哭笑不得：“屁股不疼了？”
胤礽道：“疼！但是起床还是没问题哒！”
只是肉巴掌打穿得厚厚的肉屁股，这伤能有多严重？
康熙捏着胤礽的脸颊往两边扯：“既然起床没问题，过几日与阿玛一起出门。你老嚷嚷出宫，阿玛带你出宫逛逛。”
“阿玛是最好的阿玛！”胤礽立刻扑上去抱住康熙的脖子，康熙立刻接住胤礽的屁股。
胤礽跟蚱蜢似地窜了起来：“哎哟嗷嗷嗷！”
康熙看着在床上滚来滚去的胤礽，非常无良的哈哈大笑。
“我要和乌库妈妈告状！”
“哈哈哈你去啊。”
父子俩笑闹成一团，赵昌笑眯眯地退出了暖阁，留天家父子俩自己玩。
万岁爷揍了太子殿下后，自己居然偷偷抹眼泪，把赵昌吓得不行。
主子爷和小主子重归于好，他们这群当下人的才放心。
胤礽与康熙和好之后，立刻去慈宁宫告状。
太皇太后拿着玉如意，象征性地在康熙手掌心敲了敲，就当给胤礽出气了。
康熙看着插着腰仰着头满脸得意的胤礽，又有些手痒。
太皇太后看着牛气哄哄的胤礽，则“心肝儿”的叫个不停，喜欢得不得了，又拿了一匣子珠宝给胤礽当弹珠。
胤礽赶紧拒绝。
“长者赐不可辞。”康熙代胤礽收下。
胤礽腹诽。是啊，长者赐不可辞。你前脚送我东西，后脚骂我骄奢淫逸，这算钓鱼执法吗？
胤礽琢磨着，怎么把这一匣子的珠宝送出去。
现在他可聪明了。这些珠宝不能吃不能用，他就算把自己打扮成珠宝展示架也穿戴不了那么多东西，不如拿去送人，绝对不接受阿玛的钓鱼执法。
“好。”胤礽老实地收下，“孙儿会亲手设计首饰送给乌库妈妈，不送给阿玛，哎哟。”
胤礽的脑门遭遇康熙的袭击。
太皇太后笑得前俯后仰：“好，好，不送给他，他是个坏阿玛。”
“对。”胤礽点头，“哎哟。”
他的脑门再次遭遇康熙的袭击。
太皇太后笑得快背过气了。苏麻喇姑一边笑一边给太皇太后顺气。
康熙低头，胤礽抬头。幼稚的父子俩大眼瞪大眼。
太皇太后笑着把这父子俩赶走，然后抹着笑出来的眼泪对苏麻喇姑道：“希望他们一辈子都这么好。”
苏麻喇姑微笑道：“肯定会。”
太皇太后点头：“希望。”
天家父子啊……希望玄烨和保成永远都不会变。
……
康熙说带胤礽出宫，并不是直接出宫游玩。
他先带着胤礽去宫门上参加了一场阅兵式。
三藩之乱大局初定，康熙牵着胤礽御午门宣捷，顺带对重臣们再次炫耀儿子。
胤礽第一次和索额图、明珠两位将会互相斗争很多年的重臣说上话。
索额图看着胤礽的表情慈祥极了，但是胤礽选择明珠。
“汗阿玛，明珠大学士真好看！他是不是大清第四美男子？”胤礽仰头问道。
正板着脸装严肃的康熙的严肃表情差点没装下去。
他好奇道：“为什么是第四？”
胤礽掰着手指头道：“保成和汗阿玛并列第一，哥哥第三，小三太小看不出相貌，不排进来。”
康熙的严肃表情没憋住，笑着把胤礽提起来抱怀里：“并列第一？朕对这个排位很不满。”
胤礽歪头：“那……我第一，汗阿玛委屈一下，第二？哎哟。”
胤礽抱头。
“臭小子！你究竟对你相貌多自恋！”康熙笑骂道，“就你这一团小胖子模样，还敢说自己是大清第一美男？你问问明珠，朕和你谁长得更好看？”
康熙和胤礽同时看向明珠。
帅大叔明珠的笑容差点没崩住。
你们父子俩瞎胡闹，别拉臣子入坑好不好？我敢说吗？
见明珠不敢说话，胤礽恶作剧道：“汗阿玛，明珠大人不说话，是不是认为他的容貌才是第一？”
明珠：“……”
康熙：“哈哈哈哈，没错，他就是这么认为。怎么？气不气？我们罚他。”
明珠：“？？？”
万岁爷，奴才还是不是您的心腹重臣？您拿奴才开玩笑逗儿子开心真的好吗？
明珠只能苦笑着磕头说不敢。
索额图傻愣愣地待在一旁，不知道为何自己居然会被太子冷待。
总不能是因为脸吧？
他的长相也很端正啊！他们家能出皇后，长相可能不端正吗！难道太子不是看见他后更觉得亲切吗？
不过皇帝居然抱着太子见大臣，完全不顾规矩和礼仪，可见皇帝对太子的宠溺程度。
索额图稍稍松了一口气。
宫中除太子外已经有两位皇子，还有数名怀孕的妃嫔，索额图压力很大。
“别逗明珠大学士了，明珠大学士快哭了。”胤礽附在康熙耳边悄悄道。
康熙笑着点了点胤礽的额头：“是谁在逗他？”
胤礽理直气壮道：“不是我！我说的都是实话。”
“实话……”康熙打量明珠的脸。
明珠：“……”万岁爷，您还想干什么？
“他的确长得不错。他儿子长得更好看。你喜欢好看的人，朕让他儿子给你当侍卫好不好？”康熙灵机一动。
胤礽笑眯眯道：“好。”
索额图：“！！！”
明珠：“！！！”
两人同时如遭晴天霹雳。
康熙看着他俩震惊万分的模样，心情更舒畅了。
看，他和儿子父子连心心有灵犀，一下子就把这两老狐狸一起欺负了。
康熙见好就收，开始认真给胤礽介绍索额图。
索额图虽然不合他意，但作为赫舍里唯一能用的人，康熙愿意为了胤礽给索额图一些权势，在朝中培养太子势力。
胤礽却表现得对索额图淡淡。
索额图很难过。他不知道为什么太子会讨厌自己。
就算不谈交好太子会给赫舍里家带来的利益，他一看太子就喜欢，哪怕他只是太子的叔外祖父，他看着太子就像自家孙儿一样喜欢。太子却更亲近明珠。
为什么啊！索额图想不通。
明珠更想不通。
但这么小的孩子，还一直养在皇帝身边，不可能有什么阴谋诡计。
四岁的小孩子能有什么坏心思？这难道是皇帝的意思？
康熙也好奇。他在胤礽面前说过索额图许多好话，但胤礽却更亲近明珠。总不会是胤礽看明珠长得好看吧？
康熙直接问出了这个问题：“保成，为什么你好像更喜欢明珠大人？”
胤礽想也不想道：“因为明珠大人长得好看。”
康熙拍了一下胤礽的头顶：“还有呢。朕不信只有这个。”
胤礽眨了眨眼睛。这是要考我对政务的理解？不说行不行？
康熙严肃地用眼神回答。不行！朕教了你这么多，朕知道你能耐！你玛法也教了你那么多！快说！
胤礽无奈。他就知道，天花之事后，他就不能混下去了。不展露应有的聪明才智，阿玛肯定会怀疑。
阿玛可怕的帝王疑心病吧。
胤礽把背挺直，语气不再那么活泼，连自称都换了一个：“孤听汗阿玛常提朝堂之事。明珠大学士力主撤三藩、保住有实绩的河道总督靳辅，可见才干之深。相反索额图大学士在朝堂中事事与汗阿玛作对，更自诩太子外戚，飞扬跋扈。”
索额图在康熙十九年就会被汗阿玛训斥让他收敛，索额图却在汗阿玛最需要用人的时候撂挑子不干。至康熙二十二年，汗阿玛忍无可忍，革了索额图的爵位。
如今是康熙十八年。汗阿玛肯定已经对索额图很不满。
胤礽看着索额图受伤和惧怕的神情，心有不忍，表情更加冷漠。
他不让索额图在自己手中吃个大亏，索额图定会走上老路。
何况，胤礽作为三观良好的新青年，实在是看不过索额图的飞扬跋扈。
索额图立刻跪下请罪。
这没明珠什么事，但明珠也跟着跪下来。
大冬天的，明珠背后都被汗湿了。
他可不认为自己被太子夸奖是什么好事。这只能证明，皇帝是借太子之口敲打他们。
明珠知道自己和索额图是康熙竖在朝堂中相互制衡。康熙借太子之口对索额图如此不客气，绝对也是暗中对他不满了。
康熙仍旧笑着，表情不见丝毫动摇。
他揉了揉胤礽头顶的小帽子：“你倒是懂得多。”
胤礽收起成熟的神情，钻康熙怀里得意道：“那是汗阿玛说得多。汗阿玛啰嗦、唠叨……哎哟！怎么又打我！”
“朕又没用力，怎么能叫打你？”康熙抱着胤礽站起来，对跪着的人道，“你们都听到了？用太子的话自勉吧。”
康熙抱着胤礽离开去找裕亲王。他要和胤礽先去裕亲王府中换衣服，才微服上街。
胤礽趴在康熙肩膀上，对着索额图喊道：“索额图大学士，你不能因为孤批评你你就撂挑子不干啊！现在朝中正是用人之时，你要知耻后勇，好好做事，争取将功赎罪……唉？汗阿玛你干嘛又打我！”
康熙笑声爽朗，门外候着的人都能听到：“就你话多！索额图是朝中元老，难道还需要你来教？走吧，去找你伯父。”
其实正琢磨着写折子辞官的索额图：“……”
非常了解死对头，所以知道索额图绝对琢磨着辞官的明珠：“……”
明珠侧过头：“听见没，不准上折子辞官。”
索额图：“闭嘴！”
明珠：“呵呵。”
……
裕亲王福全见康熙抱着胤礽过来，一路上还在和孩子争吵着什么，表情很是惊讶。
胤礽年岁尚小，不经常出现在人前。
福全经常入宫奏事，也鲜少见到胤礽，更何况康熙不会在人前露出如此亲和的一面。
因此他虽然知道康熙很宠太子，但亲眼见到之后，他还是大为震撼。
看康熙和太子两人相处，比他和家中小儿子还黏糊得多。
福全正在心中琢磨该用什么样的态度对待这个明显被康熙宠在心尖尖上的小太子时，胤礽伸长脖子挥舞着双手向他打招呼：“伯伯！伯伯……哎哟！阿玛你干什么！”
“咳，顺手。”康熙收起捶了胤礽小脑袋的手。
胤礽继续挥舞双手：“伯伯救我！阿玛要把我的小脑袋捶出小包包了！”
康熙又抬起手。
福全干咳一声，从康熙手中抢过胤礽：“皇上，孩子还小。”
他总算明白今日去和太皇太后请安时，太皇太后嘱咐的事是什么意思了。
太皇太后嘱咐，皇上和太子一起玩闹时总显得太过顽皮，让他一定要好好保护太子。
福全一头雾水。顽皮？你说的是我那极小的时候就智多近妖的三弟弟吗？
现在他一看，果然顽皮。
小孩子的脑袋脆弱，是你能拿来当木鱼敲的吗？
福全：不赞同的眼神.jpg。
福全是个脾气很软和的老实人。因康熙自幼登基，和福全很早就有君臣之别，所以福全几乎没在康熙面前有过兄长的样子。
但福全若难得拿出一次兄长模样，康熙还是会给一点面子。
因为他知道，老实人不赞同了，那是真的很不赞同了。
胤礽扑到福全怀里之后，十分自来熟地在福全怀里找了舒舒服服的位置握着，小短手吊着福全的脖子，转过头对着康熙做鬼脸。
康熙立刻捏拳头，露出威胁的神色。
福全立刻用大手把胤礽的小脑袋罩住：“皇上，现在可是立刻去裕亲王府？”
“去吧去吧。你怎么和太皇太后一样，都宠着太子。”康熙抱怨。
福全等康熙上马车之后，才抱着胤礽上马车，没回答康熙的话。
他看着一上马车立刻把太子抢回去的康熙，腹诽道，也不知道是谁最宠太子。
胤礽抬头，甜甜笑。
福全：“……”
有、有一点点可爱。我家孩子怎么没有这么乖巧可爱？
难道皇帝比女人养孩子养得还好？福全收起自己大逆不道的想法。
“常宁已经在裕亲王府候着，也想一起去。”福全道。
康熙脸上的笑容淡了一点：“那就一起去吧。”
胤礽脸上的笑容没保持住，赶紧转头把脸埋进康熙怀里蹭了蹭，遮掩住自己的不高兴。
恭亲王常宁站在满洲勋贵那边。
他们家是反太子的主力军，也是胤礽二废的导火索之一。
大清入关之前并非君主□□，而是八王议政，勋贵共治，连皇位继承也是八王议政共同推举。
谁都想自己手中权力多一分，是以他们推举出来的皇帝，定是自己好控制的。
当初顺治继承皇位，而不是既长又嫡还有军功的豪格继承皇位，便是皇室对满洲勋贵的妥协。
之后豪格被构陷下狱惨遭冤死，给顺治心里留下了极大的阴影。
顺治那短暂的执政一生，一直致力于中央集权、削减满洲权贵的权力，废止了宗室管理各部事务的旧例。
至康熙朝，康熙直接立太子，也是为了避免宗室和满洲勋贵再次干涉皇位的可能。
因此想要恢复八王议政的宗室与其附庸的满洲勋贵，对太子很是不满。他们才是想把太子拉下马的主力军。胤禩不过是其推到前台的棋子。
所以明知康熙忌讳、雍正忌讳，他们还把胤禩往死里逼，胤禩只能被动受着。
上了贼船哪那么容易下来？
太子一废之后，宗室和勋贵们百般挑衅，试探康熙保护太子的底线。
最后他们试探成功。哪怕太子鞭打他们之事得到了康熙的同意，康熙转脸不认人，将此事作为太子罪证之一。
胤礽趴在康熙怀里蹭了蹭。唉，又是一出钓鱼执法呢。
不过，常宁那一脉出头当废太子那把刀，被康熙用完之后结局也不怎么好。常宁的儿子直接降两等袭爵，之后便只是个闲散宗室，再起不能。
什么？站在太子这边的人都死得特别惨，还有被凌迟的。构陷太子的人只是贬职？
哦，那没事了，还是我最惨。
这个太子，我绝对要想办法丢掉。
胤礽打了个哈欠。
“困了？那要不回宫？”康熙逗弄胤礽道。
胤礽立刻摇头：“我是养精蓄锐！”
康熙笑着揉了揉胤礽的小脑袋：“逛个街还养精蓄锐？”
胤礽心道，我这是要去碰瓷常宁叔叔，所以养精蓄锐。
对待兄弟，哪怕前前世曾经互为仇敌，胤礽知道他们相互争斗只是两败俱伤，何况对方还是个孩子，他愿意重新培养感情。
但那些宗室不一样。
反正我都不要太子之位了，不趁着我还小阿玛还宠我，把前前世的账讨回来，我就愧对在新社会遭受的二十年的现代教育。
八王议政也是康熙的死穴。康熙对分薄皇权的太子尚且不能忍，你们那群宗室他能忍？
他们也就是仗着康熙晚年和儿子们斗了个精疲力尽心力交瘁，杀了太多的人，为了时局稳定无法再对宗室动手。
如果我提前把这件事揭露，还年轻气盛的康熙会不会动手？
‎
作者有话说:
五千怎么不是双更了，就是双更……今天六千（捂着肝），算二点五更！
之后会用到的热知识提醒：
1、虽然明珠不姓明，索额图不姓索，但当时他们的称呼都是明大人明相、索大人索中堂，没人称呼他们的满洲姓氏；
2、顺康雍三朝都致力于消弭朝堂上满汉隔阂，顺治时大臣们们奴才、臣混用；康熙时满洲大臣对“共主”皇帝都称臣；雍正时专门下旨，不准大臣上奏时用“奴才”，统一称“臣”，奏折中一般只有内务府之事才称“奴才。
到了乾隆，乾隆是个“大满洲主义者”，尊崇满洲旧制，将雍正时政策全部推翻，命令“满洲文臣称奴才、汉族文臣称臣、武官无论满汉皆称奴才”，这就是之后大家在清宫文所看到的“惯例”。
因本文在康熙朝，所以不遵循乾隆的命令。
