chapters.translated_text:
When Kangxi returned to the warm pavilion of the Qianqing Palace, Yinreng was sleeping.

Small children often drool when sleeping on their stomachs. Yinreng’s head was tilted to one side, his drool dampening a patch of the pillow. His little mouth moved every now and then, looking just like a puppy dreaming of gnawing on a meaty bone.

Kangxi asked Zhao Chang to bring him paper and a brush. He glanced at the sleeping Yinreng, then lowered his head to sketch, drawing a New Year picture-style baby sleeping on its stomach.

Kangxi frowned as he looked at the line drawing of his son for a long time; no matter how he looked at it, the person in the drawing was far inferior to his actual son.

Zhao Chang, who was always adept at guessing the Emperor’s intentions, immediately whispered, "Perhaps those Western painters are better at realistic portraiture."

Kangxi sighed, "But I want to paint Baocheng myself."

He couldn't exactly ask those Western painters to sneak in and paint while Yinreng was sleeping, could he? He didn't want others to see his precious son’s undignified sleeping posture. The Crown Prince of the Great Qing had his pride.

Zhao Chang couldn't think of a solution.

He couldn't very well suggest that the Emperor go learn Western painting himself, could he?

Kangxi refused to give up. He had many painting tools brought over—a pile of brushes of all sizes—and tried them one by one.

By the time Yinreng woke up, Kangxi had already discarded a floor full of paintings.

"A... ha... Ama." Yinreng rubbed his face against the pillow to wipe away the drool from the corner of his mouth, yawning as he greeted Kangxi.

Kangxi hurriedly showed Yinreng the painting he had just finished: "Does it look like you?"

Yinreng was silent.

It looked like crap.

Yinreng wore an expression of disdain: "Ama, your painting is terrible. It doesn't look like me, it looks like a puppy!"

Zhao Chang held back a laugh. In this world, only the Crown Prince dared to say such things to the Emperor, and the Emperor wouldn't even get angry.

"You look like a puppy anyway, consider it a reward." Kangxi took out his seal and stamped it happily, even adding an inscription stating that this was indeed Yinreng, and no one was allowed to object.

Yinreng huffed in anger.

Kangxi had someone take the painting to be mounted, then pinched Yinreng’s huffing little nose: "Why do you always like to huff? Are you a little piggy?"

"Ama, if I'm a little piggy, what are you?" Yinreng shook his head vigorously, shaking off Kangxi’s hand from his nose.

Kangxi held down the squirming Yinreng: "I am the one who raises the little piggy. Does your bottom still hurt? No more talking nonsense from now on."

Yinreng continued to huff: "Being the Crown Prince is just miserable!"

Kangxi raised his hand high.

Yinreng continued to huff: "It's just miserable!"

Kangxi lowered his hand and said helplessly, "Fine, I'll get you a bigger house, alright? You won't be living in the Eastern Palace until you get married anyway, why are you so demanding?"

Yinreng thought to himself, if you don't think the requirements are high, why don't you try living here?

I live in the cramped Yuqing Palace, my servants live in the Xiefang Hall, and to go to sleep, I have to walk from the inner palace to the front courtyard. Do I not have any dignity?

It was impossible for Yinreng to have an inner harem in this life. The education he received wouldn't allow it, and he was terrified that his mother from his past life would beat his bottom in his dreams.

If he only lived with the Crown Princess, wouldn't the Yuqing Palace actually not be that crowded?

It’s still so miserable, waaaaah!

Yinreng said discontentedly: "I want a garden."

Kangxi brushed him off: "Mm-hmm."

Yinreng said discontentedly: "I want a big house."

Kangxi brushed him off: "Yes, yes, yes."

Yinreng’s eyes widened. He was agreeing to everything?

"Then, then can I have a hot spring too?" Yinreng rubbed his little hands together.

"Mm... hmm?!" Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s rubbing hands, "Where would a hot spring come from in the palace? And where did you even hear about hot springs?"

After asking, Kangxi sighed: "It must have been your grandfather, right?"

Yinreng: "Hehehe." As long as Grandfather can still be the scapegoat, let him take a few more, thank you, Grandfather!

Kangxi laughed: "It's impossible to dig a hot spring for you in the palace. If you like hot springs, we'll go to the hot spring palace next winter."

If not for the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, Kangxi wouldn't have stayed in the palace for the last two winters.

He spent his summers and autumns avoiding the heat and his winters and springs avoiding the cold; the time he spent in the palace added up to no more than three months.

That was why when Kangxi chose the Eastern Palace for Yinreng, he just picked a nearby place. He didn't live in the palace, so naturally, Yinreng wouldn't live in the palace in the future either.

However, since his son wanted a big house, it wasn't impossible to tear down an old palace to build him one.

The same went for the garden. Having only one back garden in the palace was too few; he could build a few more.

Now that the Revolt of the Three Feudatories was resolved, Kangxi’s pockets were a little looser, and he could think about such luxuries.

Yinreng knew when to stop.

"Ama’s word is law!" He climbed up nimbly, dropping the act.

Kangxi was amused: "Does your bottom not hurt anymore?"

Yinreng said: "It hurts! But getting out of bed is no problem!"

It was just a fleshy palm hitting a thickly padded fleshy bottom; how serious could the injury be?

Kangxi pulled at Yinreng’s cheeks: "Since getting out of bed is no problem, we'll go out in a few days. You’ve been clamoring to leave the palace, so I’ll take you out for a stroll."

"Ama is the best Ama!" Yinreng immediately pounced and hugged Kangxi’s neck, and Kangxi immediately caught Yinreng’s bottom.

Yinreng jumped up like a grasshopper: "Ouch, ouch, ouch!"

Kangxi watched Yinreng rolling around on the bed and laughed heartily, quite unscrupulously.

"I'm going to tell on you to Uku Mama!"

"Hahaha, go ahead."

The father and son laughed and played together. Zhao Chang smiled and retreated from the warm pavilion, leaving the imperial father and son to play by themselves.

After the Emperor beat the Crown Prince, he had secretly wiped away tears himself, which had terrified Zhao Chang.

Now that the master and the little master had reconciled, the servants could finally rest easy.

After reconciling with Kangxi, Yinreng immediately went to the Cining Palace to complain.

The Empress Dowager took a jade ruyi and tapped it symbolically on Kangxi’s palm, considering it as venting Yinreng’s frustration.

Kangxi looked at Yinreng, who was standing with his hands on his hips, head held high and looking smug, and his hands felt itchy again.

The Empress Dowager, seeing the cocky Yinreng, kept calling him "my heart" and loved him dearly, even giving him a box of jewelry to use as marbles.

Yinreng hurriedly refused.

"One must not refuse a gift from an elder." Kangxi accepted it on Yinreng’s behalf.

Yinreng grumbled inwardly. Right, one must not refuse a gift from an elder. You give me things one moment and scold me for being extravagant the next; is this some kind of entrapment?

Yinreng pondered how to get rid of this box of jewelry.

He was smart now. These jewels couldn't be eaten or used, and even if he dressed himself up as a jewelry display stand, he couldn't wear that much stuff. It was better to give them away; he would absolutely not fall for Ama’s entrapment.

"Okay." Yinreng accepted it honestly, "Grandson will design jewelry himself to give to Uku Mama, not to Ama, ouch."

Yinreng’s forehead suffered an attack from Kangxi.

The Empress Dowager laughed until she was leaning back and forth: "Good, good, don't give it to him, he’s a bad Ama."

"Right." Yinreng nodded, "Ouch."

His forehead suffered another attack from Kangxi.

The Empress Dowager was laughing so hard she could barely breathe. Sumalagu laughed while patting the Empress Dowager’s back to help her breathe.

Kangxi lowered his head, Yinreng raised his. The childish father and son stared at each other.

The Empress Dowager laughed and shooed the father and son away, then wiped the tears of laughter from her eyes and said to Sumalagu: "I hope they stay this close forever."

Sumalagu smiled: "They surely will."

The Empress Dowager nodded: "I hope so."

Imperial father and son... I hope Xuan Ye and Baocheng never change.

...

When Kangxi said he would take Yinreng out of the palace, it wasn't just for a casual outing.

He first took Yinreng to the palace gate to attend a military parade.

With the general situation of the Revolt of the Three Feudatories settled, Kangxi held Yinreng’s hand at the Meridian Gate to announce the victory, taking the opportunity to show off his son to the high officials again.

It was the first time Yinreng spoke to Songgotu and Mingju, two high officials who would struggle against each other for many years.

Songgotu looked at Yinreng with an extremely kind expression, but Yinreng chose Mingju.

"Han Ama, Grand Secretary Mingju is so handsome! Is he the fourth most handsome man in the Great Qing?" Yinreng asked, looking up.

Kangxi, who was trying to keep a straight face and look serious, almost lost his composure.

He asked curiously: "Why the fourth?"

Yinreng counted on his fingers: "Baocheng and Han Ama are tied for first, Brother is third, Little Three is too small to see his features, so he doesn't count."

Kangxi couldn't hold back his serious expression, laughing as he picked Yinreng up into his arms: "Tied for first? I am very dissatisfied with this ranking."

Yinreng tilted his head: "Then... I’m first, Han Ama can be aggrieved and be second? Ouch."

Yinreng held his head.

"You brat! How narcissistic are you about your looks!" Kangxi scolded with a smile, "With your little chubby face, you dare to say you’re the most handsome man in the Great Qing? Ask Mingju, who looks better, me or you?"

Kangxi and Yinreng looked at Mingju at the same time.

The handsome uncle Mingju almost lost his smile.

You father and son are messing around, don't drag a minister into it, okay? Do I dare to answer?

Seeing Mingju didn't dare to speak, Yinreng played a prank: "Han Ama, Grand Secretary Mingju isn't speaking, does he think his appearance is the best?"

Mingju: "..."

Kangxi: "Hahahaha, that's right, that's exactly what he thinks. What? Are you angry? Let's punish him."

Mingju: "???"

Your Majesty, am I still your trusted high official? Is it really okay for you to use me as a joke to amuse your son?

Mingju could only kowtow with a bitter smile and say he didn't dare.

Songgotu stood blankly to the side, not knowing why he was being treated coldly by the Crown Prince.

It couldn't be because of his face, could it?

His features were quite upright! His family could produce an Empress, how could his features not be upright? Could it be that the Crown Prince didn't feel more intimate after seeing him?

However, the Emperor actually held the Crown Prince to meet the ministers, completely disregarding rules and etiquette, which showed the extent of the Emperor’s doting on the Crown Prince.

Songgotu breathed a slight sigh of relief.

There were already two princes in the palace besides the Crown Prince, and several pregnant concubines, so Songgotu was under a lot of pressure.

"Don't tease Grand Secretary Mingju, he’s about to cry." Yinreng whispered in Kangxi’s ear.

Kangxi smiled and tapped Yinreng’s forehead: "Who is the one teasing him?"

Yinreng said righteously: "Not me! Everything I said is the truth."

"The truth..." Kangxi examined Mingju’s face.

Mingju: "..." Your Majesty, what else do you want to do?

"He does look quite good. His son looks even better. You like good-looking people, how about I have his son be your guard?" Kangxi had a sudden inspiration.

Yinreng smiled: "Okay."

Songgotu: "!!!"

Mingju: "!!!"

Both of them felt as if they had been struck by lightning.

Kangxi looked at their shocked expressions, feeling even more refreshed.

Look, he and his son were of one heart and one mind; they had bullied these two old foxes together in an instant.

Kangxi knew when to stop and began to seriously introduce Songgotu to Yinreng.

Although Songgotu didn't suit his wishes, as the only person from the Heseri clan he could use, Kangxi was willing to give Songgotu some power for Yinreng’s sake to cultivate the Crown Prince’s faction in the court.

Yinreng, however, acted indifferent toward Songgotu.

Songgotu was very sad. He didn't know why the Crown Prince disliked him.

Even without talking about the benefits of being close to the Crown Prince for the Heseri family, he liked the Crown Prince the moment he saw him. Even if he was only the Crown Prince’s great-uncle, he looked at the Crown Prince as if he were his own grandson. Yet the Crown Prince was closer to Mingju.

Why! Songgotu couldn't figure it out.

Mingju couldn't figure it out either.

But such a small child, who had been raised by the Emperor’s side, couldn't possibly have any ulterior motives.

What kind of bad intentions could a four-year-old have? Could this be the Emperor’s intention?

Kangxi was also curious. He had said many good things about Songgotu in front of Yinreng, but Yinreng was still closer to Mingju. It couldn't be because Yinreng thought Mingju looked good, could it?

Kangxi asked this question directly: "Baocheng, why do you seem to like Grand Secretary Mingju more?"

Yinreng said without thinking: "Because Grand Secretary Mingju looks good."

Kangxi patted the top of Yinreng’s head: "Anything else? I don't believe it's just that."

Yinreng blinked. Was he testing his understanding of state affairs? Would it be okay not to say?

Kangxi answered with a serious look in his eyes. No! I’ve taught you so much, I know you’re capable! Your grandfather has also taught you so much! Speak!

Yinreng was helpless. He knew that after the smallpox incident, he couldn't just coast along anymore. If he didn't show the intelligence he should have, Ama would definitely be suspicious.

Ama’s terrifying imperial paranoia.

Yinreng straightened his back, his tone no longer as lively, and he even changed how he referred to himself: "Gu has often heard Han Ama mention court affairs. Grand Secretary Mingju strongly advocates for the withdrawal of the Three Feudatories and protecting Governor-General Jin Fu, who has real achievements, which shows his deep talent. In contrast, Grand Secretary Songgotu opposes Han Ama in everything in the court and even prides himself on being the Crown Prince’s maternal relative, acting in an arrogant and domineering manner."

Songgotu would be reprimanded by Han Ama in the 19th year of Kangxi to restrain himself, but Songgotu would quit when Han Ama needed people the most. By the 22nd year of Kangxi, Han Ama would lose patience and strip Songgotu of his titles.

It was now the 18th year of Kangxi. Han Ama must already be very dissatisfied with Songgotu.

Yinreng looked at Songgotu’s hurt and fearful expression, feeling a bit of pity, but his expression became even colder.

If he didn't let Songgotu suffer a big loss at his hands, Songgotu would definitely follow the old path.

Besides, as a modern youth with good values, Yinreng really couldn't stand Songgotu’s arrogance.

Songgotu immediately knelt down to plead guilty.

This had nothing to do with Mingju, but Mingju knelt down as well.

In the middle of winter, Mingju’s back was soaked with sweat.

He didn't think being praised by the Crown Prince was a good thing. This only proved that the Emperor was using the Crown Prince’s mouth to beat them into submission.

Mingju knew that he and Songgotu were set up by Kangxi in the court to check and balance each other. Kangxi being so impolite to Songgotu through the Crown Prince’s mouth definitely meant he was secretly dissatisfied with him too.

Kangxi was still smiling, his expression not wavering in the slightest.

He rubbed the little hat on top of Yinreng’s head: "You certainly know a lot."

Yinreng put away his mature expression and burrowed into Kangxi’s arms, smugly saying: "That’s because Han Ama talks a lot. Han Ama is long-winded, nagging... ouch! Why are you hitting me again!"

"I didn't even use any force, how can you call that hitting you?" Kangxi picked up Yinreng and stood up, saying to those kneeling, "You all heard it? Use the Crown Prince’s words to encourage yourselves."

Kangxi carried Yinreng away to find Prince Yu. He wanted to go to Prince Yu’s mansion with Yinreng to change clothes before going out in disguise.

Yinreng lay on Kangxi’s shoulder and shouted at Songgotu: "Grand Secretary Songgotu, you can't just quit because Gu criticized you! The court is in need of people right now, you must be ashamed and brave, work hard, and strive to make up for your mistakes... eh? Han Ama, why are you hitting me again!"

Kangxi’s laughter was hearty, and those waiting outside could hear it: "You talk too much! Songgotu is a veteran of the court, does he need you to teach him? Let’s go, let’s go find your uncle."

Songgotu, who was actually pondering writing a memorial to resign: "..."

Mingju, who knew his rival very well and therefore knew Songgotu was definitely thinking about resigning: "..."

Mingju turned his head: "Did you hear? You’re not allowed to submit a memorial to resign."

Songgotu: "Shut up!"

Mingju: "Heh."

...

Prince Yu Fuquan was very surprised to see Kangxi carrying Yinreng over, still arguing with the child about something along the way.

Yinreng was still young and didn't often appear in public.

Fuquan often entered the palace to report matters, but he rarely saw Yinreng, let alone Kangxi showing such an affectionate side in public.

Therefore, although he knew Kangxi doted on the Crown Prince, he was still greatly shocked after seeing it with his own eyes.

Watching Kangxi and the Crown Prince together, they were even more clingy than he was with his own youngest son.

Just as Fuquan was wondering what attitude he should take toward this little Crown Prince who was clearly the apple of Kangxi’s eye, Yinreng stretched his neck and waved his hands to greet him: "Uncle! Uncle... ouch! Ama, what are you doing!"

"Ahem, just a habit." Kangxi put away the hand that had tapped Yinreng’s little head.

Yinreng continued to wave his hands: "Uncle, save me! Ama is going to tap a bump on my little head!"

Kangxi raised his hand again.

Fuquan coughed and snatched Yinreng from Kangxi’s hands: "Your Majesty, the child is still young."

He finally understood what the Empress Dowager meant when she gave him instructions when he went to pay his respects that day.

The Empress Dowager had instructed that the Emperor and the Crown Prince always seemed too mischievous when playing together, and he must protect the Crown Prince well.

Fuquan was confused. Mischievous? Are you talking about my third brother who was as intelligent as a demon from a very young age?

Now that he saw it, he was indeed mischievous.

A child’s head is fragile, is it something you can use as a wooden fish to tap?

Fuquan: Disapproving look.jpg.

Fuquan was a very soft-tempered and honest man. Because Kangxi ascended the throne at a young age, there was a distinction between monarch and subject between him and Fuquan very early on, so Fuquan almost never acted like an older brother in front of Kangxi.

But if Fuquan rarely took on the appearance of an older brother, Kangxi would still give him some face.

Because he knew that if an honest man disapproved, he really disapproved.

After Yinreng pounced into Fuquan’s arms, he very naturally found a comfortable position, his short arms hanging around Fuquan’s neck, and turned his head to make a face at Kangxi.

Kangxi immediately clenched his fist, showing a threatening expression.

Fuquan immediately covered Yinreng’s little head with his large hand: "Your Majesty, are we going to Prince Yu’s mansion now?"

"Let’s go, let’s go. Why are you just like the Empress Dowager, doting on the Crown Prince." Kangxi complained.

Fuquan waited until Kangxi got into the carriage before holding Yinreng into the carriage, not answering Kangxi’s words.

He looked at Kangxi, who had snatched the Crown Prince back as soon as he got into the carriage, and thought to himself, I wonder who is the one who dotes on the Crown Prince the most.

Yinreng looked up and smiled sweetly.

Fuquan: "..."

It’s, it’s a little bit cute. Why aren't my children this well-behaved and cute?

Could it be that the Emperor is better at raising children than women? Fuquan put away his treasonous thoughts.

"Changning is already waiting at Prince Yu’s mansion, and he wants to go too." Fuquan said.

The smile on Kangxi’s face faded a little: "Then let him come along."

The smile on Yinreng’s face didn't last, so he hurriedly turned his head and buried his face in Kangxi’s arms, rubbing against him to hide his unhappiness.

Prince Gong Changning stood on the side of the Manchu nobility.

His family was the main force against the Crown Prince and one of the catalysts for Yinreng’s second deposition.

Before the Qing Dynasty entered the pass, it was not an absolute monarchy, but a rule by the Eight Princes, with the nobility governing together, and even the succession to the throne was jointly recommended by the Eight Princes.

Everyone wanted more power in their hands, so the emperor they recommended had to be someone they could control.

When Shunzhi inherited the throne instead of Hooge, who was older, the legitimate heir, and had military merits, it was a compromise by the royal family to the Manchu nobility.

Later, Hooge was framed and died in prison, leaving a great shadow in Shunzhi’s heart.

Shunzhi’s short reign was dedicated to centralizing power, reducing the power of the Manchu nobility, and abolishing the old practice of the imperial clan managing various government affairs.

By the time of Kangxi, Kangxi directly appointed a Crown Prince, also to avoid the possibility of the imperial clan and Manchu nobility interfering with the throne again.

Therefore, the imperial clan and their vassal Manchu nobility, who wanted to restore the rule of the Eight Princes, were very dissatisfied with the Crown Prince. They were the main force trying to pull the Crown Prince down. Yinreng was just a pawn they pushed to the front.

That was why, even knowing Kangxi and Yongzheng were wary of it, they still pushed Yinreng to the brink, and Yinreng could only passively endure it.

Once you’re on a pirate ship, is it that easy to get off?

After the first deposition of the Crown Prince, the imperial clan and nobility provoked him in every way, testing Kangxi’s bottom line for protecting the Crown Prince.

In the end, they succeeded in their test. Even though the Crown Prince’s whipping of them had been approved by Kangxi, Kangxi turned around and denied it, using it as one of the Crown Prince’s crimes.

Yinreng rubbed against Kangxi’s arms. Sigh, another case of entrapment.

However, the faction of Changning that stepped out to be the knife to depose the Crown Prince didn't end well after Kangxi was done using them. Changning’s son had his title reduced by two ranks, and after that, he was just an idle member of the imperial clan, never to rise again.

What? The people who stood on the Crown Prince’s side all died miserably, some even being sliced to death? And the people who framed the Crown Prince were only demoted?

Oh, that’s fine then, I’m still the most miserable one.

This Crown Prince position, I must find a way to get rid of it.

Yinreng yawned.

"Sleepy? Then should we go back to the palace?" Kangxi teased Yinreng.

Yinreng immediately shook his head: "I am conserving my energy!"

Kangxi smiled and rubbed Yinreng’s little head: "Conserving energy for a stroll?"

Yinreng thought to himself, I’m conserving energy to go and provoke Uncle Changning.

Toward his brothers, even if they had been enemies in his past-past life, Yinreng knew that their fighting only led to mutual destruction, and besides, the other party was still a child, so he was willing to rebuild their relationship.

But those imperial clansmen were different.

Anyway, I don't want the Crown Prince position anymore, if I don't take advantage of the fact that I’m still young and Ama still dotes on me to settle the scores from my past-past life, I would be letting down the twenty years of modern education I received in the new society.

The rule of the Eight Princes was also Kangxi’s Achilles’ heel. Kangxi couldn't even tolerate a Crown Prince who shared his imperial power, could he tolerate you group of imperial clansmen?

They were just relying on the fact that Kangxi was exhausted from fighting with his sons in his later years and had killed too many people, making him unable to take action against the imperial clan for the sake of stability.

If I reveal this matter in advance, would the young and vigorous Kangxi take action?

100,000

Author's Note:

Why isn't five thousand a double update, it is a double update... Six thousand today (clutching my liver), counting as a 2.5 update!

Trivia reminders for later:

1. Although Mingju’s surname is not Ming, and Songgotu’s surname is not Song, they were addressed as Grand Secretary Ming or Lord Ming, and Grand Secretary Song or Lord Song at the time; no one used their Manchu surnames.

2. The Shunzhi, Kangxi, and Yongzheng reigns all worked to eliminate the Manchu-Han divide in the court. During Shunzhi’s reign, ministers used "slave" and "subject" interchangeably; during Kangxi’s reign, Manchu officials called themselves "subject" to the "common master" Emperor; during Yongzheng’s reign, he specifically issued an edict forbidding ministers from using "slave" in their memorials, standardizing it to "subject," with "slave" generally only used for matters concerning the Imperial Household Department.

By the time of Qianlong, Qianlong was a "Great Manchuist" who revered old Manchu systems, overturned all of Yongzheng’s policies, and ordered that "Manchu civil officials call themselves slaves, Han civil officials call themselves subjects, and military officers call themselves slaves regardless of whether they are Manchu or Han." This is the "convention" everyone sees in Qing palace novels.

Since this story is set in the Kangxi reign, it does not follow Qianlong’s orders.

chapters.title: 第 27 章 [V]
chapters.source_text:
常宁小康熙三岁，现在还只是个二十二岁的愣头青，表情控制很不到位。
他见到康熙还算恭敬，看向太子的时候就有些眉毛不是眉毛，眼睛不是眼睛，把阴阳怪气发挥到了极致。
胤礽仗着自己年纪小，做出一副担忧的表情，心直口快道：“叔父是生病了吗？叔父要注意身体呀，生病了要喝苦苦的药，可难受。”
福全本来想在康熙训斥常宁之前训斥常宁，好替常宁挡一挡。胤礽这童言稚语一出，他皱着眉闭上嘴。
这么可爱这么善良的小侄子，你阴阳怪气个屁！活该你倒霉！
康熙本就生气，听胤礽情真意切关心常宁，就更气了。
他要保护胤礽纯真善良无邪的小心灵，不会告诉胤礽常宁讨厌他，自然阴阳怪气了回去：“恭亲王大概是被冷风吹久了，脸抽了，找御医在脸上扎几针就好了。”
胤礽乖巧道：“这就是御医说的中风吗？”
福全忍笑，常宁表情更扭曲了。
康熙气定神闲道：“差不多吧。再吹一会儿风就真中风了。”
胤礽皱起眉头，上前几步拉着常宁袖口道：“叔父赶紧请御医……哎哟！”
常宁抬起被胤礽拉着袖子的手，从胤礽手中把袖子扯回来，本想对康熙行礼服个软。
他试探出康熙对太子的态度，也试探出太子如传闻那样是个善良的小傻子，连别人对其好歹都分不出来。目的既然已经达到，常宁自然见好就收，不继续撩拨康熙的怒气。
常宁抬起手时，手肘和袖子轻轻拂过胤礽的身体。
胤礽皱着眉头大呼一声，往后一倒，身体摇晃了一下后很快重新站直。
他揉着常宁袖子接触到的地方，小脸皱成一团，好像痛到了的样子。
不过三个大人还没反应过来发生了什么，胤礽眉头就松了开来，哒哒哒跑回了康熙身边。
康熙牵着胤礽的手，皱眉头道：“他打你？”
胤礽睁大他水汪汪的眼睛：“没有啊，只是不小心碰到啦。”
不小心？
康熙看向也皱起眉头的常宁，不悦道：“保成，疼吗？”
胤礽笑道：“不疼了。阿玛，赶紧给叔父找御医呀。叔父去看御医，我们去逛街！”
康熙一把将胤礽提起来，伸手揉了揉胤礽的肚肚。
胤礽不安地扭动了一下：“不痛了真的不痛了，保成穿得可厚。去逛街去逛街。”
“嗯。”康熙看着自家单纯过头的傻儿子，怒气不由上涌。
康熙当然知道常宁不至于蠢到当着他的面揍他的宝贝儿子。
常宁只是在胤礽拉着他的袖口关心他的身体的时候，很不耐烦的把袖子抽出来，动作太大打到了胤礽。
胤礽每当对待家人时便心胸极其开阔，脑袋也会变得善良到蠢。他知道常宁不是故意的，便不会哭闹委屈。
自家蠢儿子是个喝苦药扎针灸都不会哭的乖宝宝，除了被自己气哭揍哭委屈哭，其他时候很少看到他哭泣。
康熙想到这，不由有些心虚。
“常宁，你干什么？”福全生气了。
他知道常宁对康熙立太子很不满，但把不满发泄在小孩子身上也太下作了。
再说了，康熙还在这呢！当着康熙欺负他的儿子，你是在京城待腻了想去给汗阿玛守陵吗？！
“我什么干什么？”常宁看胤礽那一番动作疑惑了一下，怀疑自己是不是真的不小心打到了胤礽。
他回忆自己手上的触感，确定自己只是轻轻擦了一下，绝对没有打到胤礽。
胤礽东倒西歪，肯定是自己没站稳。
“他自己没站稳，怪我干什么？难道你怀疑我故意打他？”常宁用怀疑的目光看向胤礽，“他没站稳就算了，为什么揉肚子？搞得好像我打到他似的。”
“常宁！你什么意思？！太子故意构陷你不成！”康熙被常宁怀疑的目光激怒了。
胤礽只要面无表情并睁大表情，就是一个最标准不过的傻宝宝疑惑表情：“阿玛，什么构陷？你们在说什么？”
“皇上，太子难得出一次宫，别为常宁置气。他的混劲，您还不知道？”福全见胤礽茫然的表情，心里的怒气也迅速增加。
但先帝只剩下四位皇子，福全是个老好人，不忍心看弟弟被康熙罚，便打圆场道：“你不是不舒服吗？快不快滚去看御医！”
常宁还想再辩解几句，但他了解康熙，看出康熙现在怒气在爆发边缘，忙打了个千，利索地溜了。
他是康熙亲弟弟，还有太皇太后护着。只要康熙怒气没当场发作，他就会无事。
这种事他做过许多次了，非常熟练。
见常宁惹了胤礽后熟练地溜走，康熙的气没处发，只能踢了一脚铺路的鹅卵石。
胤礽继续努力把眼睛睁大，并在眼睛睁大的同时使劲皱起他可爱的小眉毛：“阿玛？你生气了？怎么了？”
“没什么。”康熙把怒气压下，“准备马车，我们换衣服上街。”
胤礽皱着眉头点点头。
康熙一手抱娃，一手揉了揉娃皱紧的眉头：“眉头松开，别皱，像个小老头。”
胤礽双手捂住眉头：“保成不是小老头。阿玛才经常皱眉，阿玛是大老……哎哟。”
胤礽瘪嘴：“阿玛你能不能别老敲我的脑袋，敲笨了怎么办？”
“你已经够笨了。”连常宁在欺负你你都笨到感觉不到！康熙被胤礽蠢乐了。
福全看着傻乎乎的胤礽，板着的脸也不由露出无奈和纵容的笑容。
虽然太子太单纯很不好，但有这么一个可爱善良的傻晚辈，谁会忍住不去宠？
太子还小，现在傻一点也没关系。
福全慈祥道：“马车已经准备好了，换完衣服咱们立刻出发。皇上，咱们先去哪？”
康熙道：“看庙会。”
他专门选这个日子，就是带太子来看都城隍庙会。
都城隍庙庙会正月最热闹的庙会。都城隍庙庙会开市之日汇集了世界各地的奇珍异宝，不止琳琅满目的珠宝，甚至各个朝代的古董都应有尽有。
康熙正好给太子炫耀一下自己鉴宝的眼力，收获儿子满满的崇拜。
换好衣服后，康熙抱着胤礽和福全上了同一架马车，三人气氛都有些沉默。
常宁的事给这愉快的出宫之旅蒙上一层阴影，康熙余怒未消，福全也在心中叹气。
胤礽的眉头又皱紧了。
他拉了拉康熙的袖子，小声道：“阿玛，我是不是惹叔父不高兴了？”
康熙板着脸道：“没有。你为何要这么说？”
胤礽道：“叔父见到我时脸色不好看，我以为叔父生病。但叔父离开的时候脸色又好看了。病哪能好得这么快？叔父不是生病，是不喜欢保成吗？”
康熙狠狠揉了一下胤礽的小脑袋。
儿子不蠢，只是一时没有想到从未在私下场合见到的叔父会讨厌他。
胤礽声音越来越低，快被马车晃动的声音淹没：“叔父之前说的话，是说我构陷他吗？我只是没站稳，不是构陷……”
“别说了。”康熙把胤礽揽怀里，“他脑子有病。”
福全也板着脸道：“没错，是他脑子有病。以后别理睬他。如果单独遇到他，就赶紧立刻离开，去找皇上或者来找我，在宫里就去找太皇太后，不用给他打招呼。”
胤礽就像是霜打的小白菜一样蔫哒哒。
他瘪着嘴想要说什么，嘴唇动了动，又安静的闭上嘴什么都没说，看得两位长辈心疼极了。
福全这个老好人的怒气都快突破警戒值了。
之前的事全是常宁一个人在无理取闹，先是给太子甩脸色，太子拉着他袖子关心他的时候，他嫌弃地抽出袖子差点把太子推倒。
太子自己晃了晃便站直了，皱着眉头揉了揉肚子连疼都没喊，还继续关心他。
太子做错了什么？错在没意识到常宁讨厌他吗？
太子聪慧。之前没意识到，现在想明白了，看把孩子委屈的！
于公说，太子是国之储君，除了太皇太后和皇上，就连皇太后都不能给太子委屈，说严重了就是不忠；
于私说，太子是常宁亲侄子，常宁欺负兄长唯一的嫡子，这是不慈。
即便不提这些大道理，太子还未满四岁，常宁欺负一个未满四岁的小孩子，还污蔑太子构陷他，简直不是人干的事！
“对不起。”胤礽低下头，嘴瘪的能挂上小葫芦，“阿玛，我哪里做错了，叔父才那么讨厌我？叔父是除了太皇太后和阿玛之外，我最亲的亲人。他那么讨厌我，肯定是我哪里做错了吧？”
康熙捏住太子瘪起的嘴唇：“你没错。朕都说了，是他脑子有病！朕九五之尊，金口玉言，说他有病就是有病，明白了吗？别遇到点事就从自己身上找原因。你是太子！给朕霸道点！”
胤礽挥舞着小短手像只螃蟹一样“呜呜呜”了许久，康熙才松开手。
胤礽捂着嘴，埋怨道：“痛！阿玛坏，坏阿玛。什么叫遇到点事？我就只有三个叔叔伯伯！这很重要！”
福全听到胤礽这句话心里暖洋洋的同时，也更气了。
太子是个好孩子，这么小的年纪就一直念着亲伯伯亲叔叔，说他们是除了太皇太后和皇帝之外与他最亲近的人。
这样的太子继承大统后，至少能保他们两代后代富贵无忧。常宁还有什么不满？难道常宁还奢望恢复八王议政，甚至像多尔衮那样当摄政王，和皇帝分持大权吗？
常宁就是欠守陵了吧？！
小孩子忘性大。胤礽被康熙逗弄了一会儿，又听福全绘声绘色讲述了庙会盛景之后，便把疑似犯病的常宁抛到了脑后。
出门在外时胤礽试图保持成熟稳重的好孩子样，但被康熙逗着逗着就固态萌发，要阿玛抱要和阿玛闹。
福全在康熙的默许下，也加入了和胤礽玩闹的行列。
胤礽左手一个阿玛，右手一个伯伯，小腿一缩，吊在他们中荡秋千。
康熙被御医提醒过，忙把胤礽放下来，叮嘱他不准荡秋千。
“这样你的小胳膊会脱臼！”康熙点着胤礽的脑壳道。
胤礽：“嗷！”
他刚刚答应，一会儿又荡了起来。
康熙继续点他的光脑壳。
福全笑得合不拢嘴。
他从未见过自幼登基的弟弟如此生活化的一面，比他当初刚当阿玛还要焦头烂额。
他的孩子有女人带，自己不过是逗弄一下。看弟弟和保成相处，显然弟弟说自己亲自带孩子，居然不是说着玩。
福全脑海中浮现出大逆不道的比较——弟弟带孩子，和他后院的女人带孩子时的表现差不多了，那叫一个熟练。
福全不由也起了玩乐的性子。
“保成，要不要骑脖子？”福全笑呵呵道，“庙会人多，骑伯伯脖子上好不好？”
胤礽转头看向康熙。
康熙笑骂道：“你还想骑我脖子上不成？！”
胤礽居然大无畏地点头。
福全的笑容僵住了。
他万万没想到，太子居然……算了，太子还小，太子什么都不懂。
福全刚想伸出手把太子抱起来，阻止太子大逆不道的行为。康熙居然率先把胤礽抱起来。
“只能在宫外这样，不能告诉其他人，包括你乌库妈妈，知道吗？”康熙把儿子扛肩膀上。
胤礽两只小短腿吊在康熙胸口，小短手稳稳抱住康熙的脑袋，整个脑子“轰”的一响，懵了。
他只是开个玩笑，万万没想到阿玛居然真的同意了？
这还是我那个死要面子的阿玛吗？阿玛你还记得你是封建帝王吗？我上上辈子的时候你没有那么宠孩子啊！胤礽在心底咆哮。
不过我上上辈子的时候，阿玛好像没这么帅。胤礽陷入沉思。
这辈子阿玛许多表现都和上辈子截然不同，少了帝王的威严和持重，多了许多亲切随和。
胤礽抱住康熙的脑袋，在康熙的帽子上蹭了蹭自己软乎乎的小脸。
他刚因为“陷害”常宁而生出的源自于前前世的黑暗情绪，被这个骑脖子打散。
“阿玛好高呀。”胤礽两只暖呼呼的小手捂住康熙被寒风吹得冰凉的脸，“保成给阿玛挡风。”
感到脸上软绵绵的暖意，康熙笑得异常开心：“走！和阿玛一起逛庙会！看到什么喜欢的就说，阿玛全买给你！”
康熙顶着儿子大步跨进人群，福全忙提腿跟上。
一溜的侍卫太监有的隐藏在人群中，有的装作奴仆跟在三人身后，他们脸上的表情都有些绷不住了。
皇上把太子顶肩膀上？
太子骑皇上的脖子上？
他们眼花了吗？
天家父子居然做出了和普通父子一样的行为？
庙会太过热闹，总有人贩子浑水摸鱼，还要预防拥挤和踩踏。许多健壮的父亲为了保护幼子，都将幼子顶在了肩膀上。
康熙并不是这人山人海中唯一一个这样做的父亲。他融入了许多普普通通的父亲中，和儿子好奇地逛来逛去。
胤礽一会儿收回手暖暖，然后继续给康熙遮风暖脸。他趴在康熙脑袋上轻言细语和康熙说话，身体放松，一动不动，尽可能给康熙减轻负担，比其他在父亲脖子上乱动的孩子乖巧多了。
福全看着这年轻的父子俩在人群中穿梭，不由有些眼热。
天家的孩子，谁没有指望过一份普通家庭的父爱？
但他们懂事之后便知道，这份奢望永远不可能实现。
福全分府另住之后，想过和孩子亲近。但他院中也和康熙后宫一样子嗣稀少，后院女人把唯一活着的孩子看得很紧，就跟母老虎护崽子似的，根本不准他抱出去随便玩。
福全琢磨着，要不要和后院的女人再商量商量。培养父子亲情也很重要啊。
“三爷，你也累了，让我抱抱保成。”自己的孩子抱不着，福全盯上了大侄子。
康熙回头：“想要啊？”
福全使劲点头。
康熙板着脸道：“不给。”
说完，他顶着胤礽迈开大长腿，和福全拉开了距离。
福全：“？？？”
等等，这还是他那喜怒不显于色的皇帝弟弟吗？我弟弟有这么幼稚吗？
不过弟弟好像也才二十多岁？活泼点似乎也正常？
福全摸了摸自己的秃脑门，感觉头有点疼。
他是不是冷风吹多了，吹出幻觉了。
为了确定自己是不是被冷风吹出幻觉，福全再次问道：“给我抱一会儿，就一会儿。”
康熙继续加快脚步：“不给不给，一边去。”
“就一会儿，我们换着来。”
“一边去，没听到吗？”
“我也想让侄子给我捂脸。”
“你想屁。”……
两兄弟你一言我一语，仿佛寻常娇纵弟弟和宽厚老大哥斗嘴。
胤礽趴在康熙脑袋上，嘴都快咧到极限了。
阿玛和伯伯斗嘴好好玩啊，没想到阿玛和伯伯感情居然这么好？
上辈子是这样吗？胤礽想起上辈子裕亲王和康熙相处时公事公办的君臣模样。
这是时间改变了人心，还是这两辈子根本不是同一世界？
胤礽闭上眼，又蹭了蹭康熙的脑袋。
不管了，享受这一刻才重要。
康熙感到脑袋上胤礽蹭来蹭去的触感，很遗憾今天戴了帽子。
等以后不戴帽子的季节，朕再带保成来逛庙会吧。康熙决定，趁着孩子还小，可以顶脖子上，多享受一下这寻常人家的父子亲情。
胤礽这是第一次出宫。
上上辈子留下的记忆多是黑暗的，这种逛街的小细节不会占用宝贵的灵魂容量。
上辈子胤礽倒是经常逛街逛庙会，每次都觉得很无聊，只想回家躺着。
逛街哪有打游戏看视频好玩？
这辈子没了丰富多彩的娱乐生活，连庙会都变得新奇有趣起来了。
胤礽骑在康熙脖子上，能看得很远很远。
他指挥着康熙去看人耍大刀喷火球砸石板，买了许多小玩具准备回宫送人，又馋了一串冰糖葫芦。
吃冰糖葫芦的时候，康熙终于把胤礽放到了地上，免得胤礽把糖蹭到了他头上。
胤礽吃完冰糖葫芦之后，康熙终于耐不住福全的请求，让福全享受了被胤礽骑脖子的待遇。
福全扛起了胤礽之后，才知道康熙有多开心。
孩童甜甜暖暖的气息包裹着他，除了重了点，比什么围脖都好使。
对经常骑马射箭的福全来说，胤礽这点重量不算什么。他可以扛着侄子走完整个庙会！
“三爷，经常带保成来我家玩啊。”福全把胤礽放下时，念念不舍道。
“嗯嗯嗯，好好好。”康熙把胤礽护怀里。
儿子太可爱也有坏处，总有人想和朕抢保成！
逛累之后，康熙几人去了庙会街上一家大酒楼。
这类高档酒楼都给达官贵人们随时备着雅间。福全的侍从亮出了裕亲王府的身份，他们立刻被掌柜的亲自引往楼上最好的房间。
在上楼的时候，胤礽伸长脖子观望了一眼楼下正在弹曲说书的大厅，眼尖地看到了一个因为长得太好看、神情太忧郁，而在楼下众人中显得格格不入卓尔不群鹤立鸡群的大帅哥。
胤礽眼睛一亮，脚步一顿，使劲拉扯康熙的袖子：“阿玛阿玛！我看到一个比我们俩还帅的人！我们俩大清第一美男的地位不保！”
福全：“？？？”什么大清第一美男？皇帝弟弟私下给太子侄子说了什么奇怪的话？弟弟还有多少惊喜是我这个哥哥不知道的？
康熙五分好奇五分不满地顺着胤礽的粗短手指看向大厅，也一眼看到了大厅中那个硬生生把周围众人衬托成布景板的家伙。
康熙已经到了嘴边的“绝不可能有谁比你阿玛还要帅”的话，被他无奈地咽了下去。
他回头道：“赵昌，把那家伙给我叫上来！”
扮做侍卫贴着八字胡的赵昌笑道：“是，三爷。”
他没有问叫谁上来。
都大清第一帅哥了，还能是谁？
福全瞥了一眼，不由失笑。
这真是赶了巧了，居然能在这里遇上，还被小太子一眼瞧中了。
胤礽虽然已经猜到那人是谁，还是装作好奇地问道：“阿玛阿玛，那个人你认识吗？”
康熙点头：“那就是明珠的儿子，今天刚成为你侍卫的人。”
胤礽夸张道：“哇哦！是大清第四美男明珠大人的儿子！”
福全疑惑：“大清……第四美男？”
胤礽摇头晃脑道：“我和阿玛并列第一，哥哥第三。不过现在我和阿玛要并列第二了。”
福全失笑。
这大侄子真的太逗了。小孩子都这么好玩吗？
福全决定，今天回去就算拼着和福晋侧福晋庶福晋们吵架，也要把儿子偷出来玩！

Changning is three years younger than Kangxi, and at twenty-two, he is still a greenhorn whose facial expressions are poorly controlled.

He is reasonably respectful when seeing Kangxi, but when he looks at the Crown Prince, his eyebrows and eyes seem to be at odds with each other, taking his cynical, passive-aggressive attitude to the extreme.

Relying on his young age, Yinreng puts on a worried expression and says bluntly, "Uncle, are you sick? You must take care of your health. If you're sick, you have to drink bitter medicine, which is so unpleasant."

Fuquan had intended to reprimand Changning before Kangxi could, hoping to shield him, but after hearing Yinreng’s innocent, childish words, he frowns and keeps his mouth shut.

Such a cute and kind little nephew, and you’re being passive-aggressive for no reason! You deserve your bad luck!

Kangxi was already angry, and hearing Yinreng’s sincere concern for Changning only made him angrier.

He wants to protect Yinreng’s pure, kind, and innocent heart, so he won't tell him that Changning hates him. Naturally, he retorts with his own passive-aggression: "Prince Gong has likely been blown by the cold wind for too long, causing his face to twitch. Just find an imperial physician to stick a few needles in it, and he'll be fine."

Yinreng says obediently, "Is that what the imperial physician calls a stroke?"

Fuquan suppresses a laugh, and Changning’s expression becomes even more twisted.

Kangxi says calmly and composedly, "Something like that. Keep blowing in the wind, and you'll really have a stroke."

Yinreng frowns, steps forward, and tugs at Changning’s sleeve, saying, "Uncle, hurry and call for an imperial physician... Ouch!"

Changning lifts the hand whose sleeve Yinreng is pulling, yanks it back from Yinreng’s grip, intending to bow to Kangxi and concede.

He has tested Kangxi’s attitude toward the Crown Prince and also confirmed that the Crown Prince is, as rumored, a kind little fool who can't even tell if someone is being good or bad to him. Since his goal is achieved, Changning naturally knows when to stop and doesn't continue to provoke Kangxi’s anger.

As Changning lifts his hand, his elbow and sleeve brush lightly against Yinreng’s body.

Yinreng lets out a cry with a frown, falls backward, and after swaying for a moment, quickly stands straight again.

He rubs the spot where Changning’s sleeve made contact, his little face scrunched up as if he were in pain.

However, before the three adults can react to what happened, Yinreng’s brow relaxes, and he trots back to Kangxi’s side.

Kangxi takes Yinreng’s hand and frowns, asking, "Did he hit you?"

Yinreng opens his watery eyes wide: "No, he just bumped into me by accident."

By accident?

Kangxi looks at Changning, who is also frowning, and asks displeasedly, "Baocheng, does it hurt?"

Yinreng smiles: "It doesn't hurt anymore. Father, hurry and find an imperial physician for Uncle. Once Uncle sees the physician, we can go shopping!"

Kangxi lifts Yinreng up and reaches out to rub his little tummy.

Yinreng squirms uncomfortably: "It doesn't hurt, it really doesn't hurt. Baocheng is wearing thick clothes. Let's go shopping, let's go shopping."

"Hmm." Kangxi looks at his overly simple-minded son, and his anger rises again.

Of course, Kangxi knows Changning isn't stupid enough to beat his precious son in front of him.

Changning was just impatient when Yinreng was tugging his sleeve to show concern, so he yanked his sleeve away, and the force of the movement hit Yinreng.

Whenever Yinreng deals with family, he is incredibly broad-minded, and his brain becomes kind to the point of foolishness. He knows Changning didn't mean it, so he won't cry or feel aggrieved.

His own silly son is a well-behaved baby who won't even cry when drinking bitter medicine or getting acupuncture; he rarely cries unless he's been made to by his father's anger or discipline.

Thinking of this, Kangxi feels a bit guilty.

"Changning, what are you doing?" Fuquan is angry.

He knows Changning is very dissatisfied with Kangxi appointing a Crown Prince, but taking that dissatisfaction out on a small child is too low.

Besides, Kangxi is still here! Bullying his son in front of him—are you tired of staying in the capital and want to go guard the late Emperor's mausoleum?!

"What do you mean, what am I doing?" Changning looks at Yinreng’s actions and feels puzzled, wondering if he really did accidentally hit him.

He recalls the sensation on his hand and is certain he only brushed against him lightly; he definitely didn't hit Yinreng.

Yinreng stumbling around must have been because he didn't stand steady.

"He didn't stand steady himself, so why blame me? Are you suspecting I hit him on purpose?" Changning looks at Yinreng with suspicious eyes. "It's one thing that he didn't stand steady, but why rub his stomach? Making it look like I hit him."

"Changning! What do you mean?! Are you saying the Crown Prince is framing you?!" Kangxi is infuriated by Changning’s suspicious gaze.

As long as Yinreng keeps his face blank and opens his eyes wide, he has the standard, silly, confused baby expression: "Father, what is framing? What are you talking about?"

"Your Majesty, it's rare for the Crown Prince to leave the palace; don't get angry at Changning. You know how reckless he is," Fuquan says. Seeing Yinreng’s blank expression, his own anger also rises rapidly.

But since the late Emperor only has four sons left, and Fuquan is a good-natured man, he can't bear to see his brother punished by Kangxi, so he mediates: "Aren't you feeling well? Get out of here and see an imperial physician!"

Changning wants to argue a few more words, but he knows Kangxi and sees that his anger is on the verge of exploding, so he quickly bows and slips away nimbly.

He is Kangxi’s own brother and has the Empress Dowager protecting him. As long as Kangxi doesn't explode on the spot, he will be fine.

He has done this many times and is very practiced at it.

Seeing Changning slip away after provoking Yinreng, Kangxi has nowhere to vent his anger and can only kick a pebble on the path.

Yinreng continues to try to open his eyes wide, and while doing so, he scrunches up his cute little eyebrows: "Father? Are you angry? What's wrong?"

"Nothing." Kangxi suppresses his anger. "Prepare the carriage; we'll change our clothes and go into the city."

Yinreng nods with a frown.

Kangxi holds the child in one hand and uses the other to rub his tightly furrowed brow: "Unclench your brow, don't frown, you look like a little old man."

Yinreng covers his brow with both hands: "Baocheng is not a little old man. Father is the one who always frowns, Father is a big old... ouch."

Yinreng pouts: "Father, can you stop tapping my head? What if you tap me until I'm stupid?"

"You're already stupid enough." You're too stupid to even feel when Changning is bullying you! Kangxi is amused by Yinreng’s foolishness.

Fuquan looks at the silly Yinreng, and his stern face can't help but reveal a helpless and indulgent smile.

Although it's not good for the Crown Prince to be too simple, who could resist pampering such a cute and kind little junior?

The Crown Prince is still young; it doesn't matter if he's a bit silly for now.

Fuquan says kindly: "The carriage is ready; we'll leave as soon as we change. Your Majesty, where shall we go first?"

Kangxi says: "To see the temple fair."

He specifically chose this day to bring the Crown Prince to see the City God Temple Fair.

The City God Temple Fair is the liveliest fair in the first lunar month. On the day it opens, it gathers rare treasures from all over the world, not just dazzling jewelry, but even antiques from various dynasties.

Kangxi happens to want to show off his eye for antiques to the Crown Prince and reap his son’s full admiration.

After changing clothes, Kangxi holds Yinreng and boards the same carriage as Fuquan; the atmosphere among the three is somewhat silent.

The incident with Changning has cast a shadow over this pleasant trip out of the palace; Kangxi’s lingering anger hasn't dissipated, and Fuquan is also sighing in his heart.

Yinreng’s brow furrows again.

He tugs at Kangxi’s sleeve and whispers: "Father, did I make Uncle unhappy?"

Kangxi says with a straight face: "No. Why would you say that?"

Yinreng says: "Uncle’s face didn't look good when he saw me, so I thought he was sick. But when Uncle left, his face looked better. How could an illness get better so quickly? Is it that Uncle isn't sick, but just doesn't like Baocheng?"

Kangxi rubs Yinreng’s little head hard.

His son isn't stupid; he just hadn't realized that an uncle he had never met in private could hate him.

Yinreng’s voice grows lower, almost drowned out by the sound of the carriage: "What Uncle said earlier, was he saying I framed him? I just didn't stand steady, I didn't frame him..."

"Stop talking." Kangxi pulls Yinreng into his arms. "There is something wrong with his brain."

Fuquan also says with a straight face: "That's right, there is something wrong with his brain. Don't pay attention to him in the future. If you meet him alone, leave immediately and go find the Emperor or come find me; if you're in the palace, go find the Empress Dowager. You don't need to greet him."

Yinreng looks like a wilted cabbage.

He pouts as if wanting to say something, his lips move, but he closes them quietly and says nothing, which makes both elders feel extremely heartbroken.

The anger of Fuquan, this good-natured man, is about to break its warning threshold.

The whole incident was Changning being unreasonable; first, he gave the Crown Prince a cold look, and when the Crown Prince held his sleeve to show concern, he disdainfully yanked it away, almost pushing the Crown Prince over.

The Crown Prince swayed, stood straight, frowned, rubbed his stomach without even crying out in pain, and continued to show concern for him.

What did the Crown Prince do wrong? Was his fault not realizing that Changning hated him?

The Crown Prince is intelligent. He didn't realize it before, but now that he has figured it out, look at how aggrieved the child is!

Officially speaking, the Crown Prince is the heir to the nation; except for the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, even the Empress Dowager cannot make the Crown Prince feel aggrieved—to put it seriously, that is disloyalty.

Personally speaking, the Crown Prince is Changning’s own nephew; for Changning to bully his brother’s only legitimate son is unkind.

Even without mentioning these grand principles, the Crown Prince is not yet four years old; for Changning to bully a child under four and slander him for framing him is simply not the act of a human being!

"I'm sorry." Yinreng lowers his head, his mouth pouting so much a small gourd could hang from it. "Father, what did I do wrong that Uncle hates me so much? Uncle is the relative I am closest to, besides the Empress Dowager and Father. If he hates me so much, I must have done something wrong, right?"

Kangxi pinches the Crown Prince’s pouting lips: "You did nothing wrong. I already said, there is something wrong with his brain! I am the Son of Heaven, my words are law; if I say he has a problem, he has a problem, do you understand? Don't look for reasons within yourself every time something happens. You are the Crown Prince! Be more domineering for me!"

Yinreng waves his short arms like a crab and makes "woo woo" sounds for a long time before Kangxi lets go.

Yinreng covers his mouth and complains: "It hurts! Father is bad, bad Father. What do you mean 'every time something happens'? I only have three uncles! This is very important!"

Hearing this, Fuquan feels warm inside, but also even angrier.

The Crown Prince is a good child; at such a young age, he always thinks of his uncles, saying they are the people he is closest to besides the Empress Dowager and the Emperor.

After such a Crown Prince ascends the throne, he could at least ensure their descendants' wealth and peace for two generations. What else is Changning dissatisfied with? Could it be that Changning still hopes to restore the Eight Princes' Joint Governance, or even become a regent like Dorgon and share power with the Emperor?

Changning really needs to go guard the mausoleum, doesn't he?!

Children have short memories. After being teased by Kangxi for a while, and hearing Fuquan describe the magnificent sights of the temple fair, Yinreng puts the potentially mentally ill Changning to the back of his mind.

When out and about, Yinreng tries to maintain the look of a mature and steady good child, but after being teased by Kangxi, his true nature emerges, and he wants his father to hold him and play with him.

With Kangxi’s tacit approval, Fuquan also joins in the fun with Yinreng.

Yinreng has his father on his left and his uncle on his right, tucks his legs, and swings between them like a swing.

Kangxi, having been warned by the imperial physician, quickly puts Yinreng down and warns him not to swing.

"Your little arms will get dislocated like that!" Kangxi points at Yinreng’s head.

Yinreng: "Ow!"

He just promised, but a moment later, he starts swinging again.

Kangxi continues to poke his shiny little head.

Fuquan laughs until he can't close his mouth.

He has never seen his brother, who ascended the throne at a young age, in such a domestic light; he looks even more flustered than he did when he first became a father.

His own children are taken care of by women, and he only teases them occasionally. Seeing his brother with Baocheng, it’s clear that when his brother said he would raise the child himself, he wasn't just joking.

A blasphemous comparison pops into Fuquan’s mind—his brother’s way of raising a child is about the same as the women in his own backyard; it’s that practiced.

Fuquan can't help but feel playful too.

"Baocheng, do you want to ride on my shoulders?" Fuquan says with a smile. "The temple fair is crowded; how about riding on Uncle’s shoulders?"

Yinreng turns to look at Kangxi.

Kangxi scolds with a smile: "Do you want to ride on my shoulders instead?!"

Yinreng nods fearlessly.

Fuquan’s smile freezes.

He never expected that the Crown Prince would... never mind, the Crown Prince is still young, he doesn't understand anything.

Just as Fuquan is about to reach out to pick up the Crown Prince and stop his rebellious behavior, Kangxi actually picks up Yinreng first.

"Only outside the palace, you can't tell anyone else, including your grandmother, understand?" Kangxi hoists his son onto his shoulders.

Yinreng’s two short legs hang over Kangxi’s chest, his short arms firmly hugging Kangxi’s head, and his mind goes "boom"—he’s stunned.

He was just joking; he never expected his father to actually agree?

Is this still my face-conscious father? Father, do you remember you are a feudal emperor? You weren't this doting in my past life! Yinreng roars in his heart.

But in my past life, Father didn't seem this handsome. Yinreng falls into deep thought.

In this life, many of Father’s behaviors are completely different from his past life, with less imperial majesty and gravity, and more kindness and ease.

Yinreng hugs Kangxi’s head and rubs his soft little face against Kangxi’s hat.

The dark emotions from his past life that had emerged because of "framing" Changning are scattered by this shoulder ride.

"Father is so tall." Yinreng covers Kangxi’s face, which is cold from the winter wind, with his two warm little hands. "Baocheng will block the wind for Father."

Feeling the soft warmth on his face, Kangxi laughs exceptionally happily: "Let's go! Let's go to the temple fair with Father! If you see anything you like, just say it, and Father will buy it all for you!"

Kangxi strides into the crowd with his son, and Fuquan hurriedly follows.

The line of guards and eunuchs, some hidden in the crowd and some disguised as servants following behind, can barely keep their expressions straight.

The Emperor has the Crown Prince on his shoulders?

The Crown Prince is riding on the Emperor’s shoulders?

Are their eyes deceiving them?

The royal father and son are actually behaving like ordinary father and son?

The temple fair is too crowded, and there are always human traffickers taking advantage of the chaos, not to mention the need to prevent crowding and trampling. Many strong fathers, in order to protect their young children, have them on their shoulders.

Kangxi is not the only father in this sea of people doing this. He blends in with many ordinary fathers, curiously walking around with his son.

Yinreng occasionally pulls his hands back to warm them, then continues to shield Kangxi’s face from the wind. He lies on Kangxi’s head, whispering to him, his body relaxed and still, trying to lighten the burden for Kangxi as much as possible, much better behaved than other children who fidget on their fathers' shoulders.

Fuquan watches the young father and son weaving through the crowd and feels a bit envious.

Which child of the royal family hasn't hoped for a bit of ordinary fatherly love?

But once they grow up, they know that this luxury can never be realized.

After Fuquan moved out to his own residence, he thought about being close to his children. But his household, like Kangxi’s harem, has few children, and the women in the backyard guard the only living child tightly, like mother tigers protecting their cubs, and wouldn't let him take the child out to play.

Fuquan wonders if he should discuss it with the women in his backyard again. Cultivating father-son affection is also very important.

"Third Brother, you're tired too, let me hold Baocheng." Unable to hold his own child, Fuquan sets his sights on his nephew.

Kangxi looks back: "You want him?"

Fuquan nods vigorously.

Kangxi says with a straight face: "No."

After saying that, he strides away with Yinreng on his shoulders, putting distance between himself and Fuquan.

Fuquan: "???"

Wait, is this still his emperor brother who never shows his emotions? Is my brother this childish?

But his brother is only in his twenties, right? Being lively seems normal?

Fuquan touches his bald head, feeling a bit of a headache.

Did he get blown by the cold wind too much and start hallucinating?

To confirm if he was hallucinating, Fuquan asks again: "Let me hold him for a while, just for a while."

Kangxi continues to speed up: "No, no, go away."

"Just for a while, we can take turns."

"Go away, didn't you hear me?"

"I also want my nephew to warm my face."

"In your dreams."...

The two brothers exchange words, like an ordinary spoiled younger brother and a broad-minded older brother bickering.

Yinreng lies on Kangxi’s head, his mouth stretched to the limit.

Father and Uncle bickering is so fun; I didn't expect Father and Uncle to have such a good relationship?

Was it like this in my past life? Yinreng recalls the formal, official relationship between Prince Yu and Kangxi in his past life.

Has time changed people, or are these two lives not in the same world at all?

Yinreng closes his eyes and rubs against Kangxi’s head again.

Never mind, enjoying this moment is what matters.

Kangxi feels the sensation of Yinreng rubbing against his head and regrets wearing a hat today.

When the season comes when I don't need a hat, I'll bring Baocheng to the temple fair again. Kangxi decides that while the child is still small and can ride on his shoulders, he will enjoy this ordinary father-son affection as much as possible.

This is Yinreng’s first time out of the palace.

The memories left from his past life are mostly dark, and such small details of shopping wouldn't occupy precious soul capacity.

In his past life, Yinreng often went shopping at temple fairs, but always found it boring and just wanted to go home and lie down.

How could shopping be more fun than playing games or watching videos?

In this life, without a rich and colorful entertainment life, even the temple fair has become novel and interesting.

Riding on Kangxi’s shoulders, Yinreng can see very, very far.

He directs Kangxi to watch people juggling big swords, breathing fire, and smashing stone slabs, buys many small toys to take back to the palace as gifts, and craves a stick of candied hawthorns.

When eating the candied hawthorns, Kangxi finally puts Yinreng on the ground to avoid getting sugar on his head.

After Yinreng finishes the candied hawthorns, Kangxi finally can't resist Fuquan’s request and lets Fuquan enjoy the experience of having Yinreng ride on his shoulders.

Only after Fuquan hoists Yinreng up does he realize how happy Kangxi was.

The child’s sweet, warm scent envelops him, and besides being a bit heavy, it’s better than any scarf.

For Fuquan, who often rides horses and shoots arrows, Yinreng’s weight is nothing. He could carry his nephew through the entire temple fair!

"Third Brother, bring Baocheng to my house to play often." Fuquan says reluctantly when putting Yinreng down.

"Yes, yes, yes, okay, okay." Kangxi pulls Yinreng into his arms.

There are disadvantages to the son being too cute; everyone wants to compete with me for Baocheng!

After getting tired of walking, Kangxi and the others go to a large restaurant on the temple fair street.

Such high-end restaurants always have private rooms ready for dignitaries. Fuquan’s servant reveals the identity of the Prince Yu Mansion, and they are immediately led by the manager himself to the best room upstairs.

While going upstairs, Yinreng stretches his neck to look at the hall downstairs where music is being played and stories told, and his sharp eyes spot a handsome man who, because he is too good-looking and has such a melancholy expression, stands out from the crowd like a crane in a flock of chickens.

Yinreng’s eyes light up, his steps pause, and he tugs hard on Kangxi’s sleeve: "Father, Father! I saw someone even more handsome than us! Our status as the number one handsome men of the Qing Dynasty is in jeopardy!"

Fuquan: "???" What number one handsome men of the Qing Dynasty? What strange things has the Emperor brother been telling the Crown Prince nephew in private? How many more surprises does my brother have that I don't know about?

Kangxi, half-curious and half-displeased, follows Yinreng’s thick, short finger to look at the hall, and also spots the guy who makes everyone around him look like background scenery.

Kangxi swallows the "It is absolutely impossible for anyone to be more handsome than your father" that was already on his lips.

He turns back and says: "Zhao Chang, call that guy up for me!"

Zhao Chang, disguised as a guard with a mustache, smiles: "Yes, Third Brother."

He doesn't ask who to call up.

Since he’s the number one handsome man of the Qing Dynasty, who else could it be?

Fuquan glances and can't help but laugh.

This is a real coincidence, to meet him here, and to be spotted by the little Crown Prince at a glance.

Although Yinreng has already guessed who that person is, he still asks curiously: "Father, Father, do you know that person?"

Kangxi nods: "That is Mingzhu’s son, the one who just became your guard today."

Yinreng says exaggeratedly: "Wow! It’s the son of the number four handsome man of the Qing Dynasty, Lord Mingzhu!"

Fuquan is puzzled: "Number four... handsome man of the Qing Dynasty?"

Yinreng shakes his head: "Father and I are tied for first, Brother is third. But now Father and I have to tie for second."

Fuquan laughs.

This nephew is really too funny. Are all children this fun?

Fuquan decides that when he goes back today, even if he has to fight with his wife, concubines, and secondary wives, he will steal his son out to play!

‎

chapters.source_text:
纳兰性德看到赵昌时，脸上忧郁的表情立刻变成了严肃坚毅的普通宫廷侍卫表情，吓得友人顾贞观差点一口茶水喷出来。
纳兰性德自结发妻子亡故之后，脸上时常带着忧郁，看碎了京城一地女儿心，连男的都暗地里称呼他为“第一痴心人”。
顾贞观与纳兰性德相知相交这么多年，也未曾见过纳兰性德这等充满男子汉气息的表情。
哪怕纳兰性德面对明相的时候也没有过！
“三爷让纳兰侍卫您上去一述。”赵昌笑眯眯道。
三爷……
纳兰性德浑身汗毛都竖了起来，感伤的脑袋就像是灌进了寒风瞬间清醒，还打了个激灵。
他回头看了友人顾贞观一眼，顾贞观立刻了然，拱手告辞。
能让明相之子这么紧张的人，肯定是朝中达官贵人，说不定还是宗亲。顾贞观不过是一落魄举人，不能同行。
但顾贞观还未离开，另一个侍从走了过来，又传了一个命令。
“你是顾贞观？”侍从问道，“‘人生若只如初见，何事秋风悲画扇’是纳兰侍卫写给你的？”
顾贞观：“……小的是顾贞观。”
赵昌惊讶：“那首词是写给你的？”
纳兰性德苦笑：“不、不会三爷也读到了我的词？”
赵昌笑道：“小少爷很喜欢纳兰侍卫的词。那就一起上去吧。”
赵昌给纳兰性德卖了个好。
赵昌了解康熙和太子。一听这侍从问的话，就猜到好奇顾贞观的人定是太子爷，便把这个消息委婉告诉纳兰性德。
纳兰性德倒吸一口气。
不会太子爷也来了？他想道今日康熙和太子在城楼宣捷，向赵昌点点头：“谢谢。”
赵昌笑了笑：“那就赶紧上去吧，二爷三爷还在上面等着呢。”
二爷……裕亲王也来了？
纳兰性德拉了一下友人，叮嘱道：“你可千万别失礼，失礼了我也保不住你。”
顾贞观立刻点头：“我知道。”
两人结伴走上楼。胤礽翘着小脚，正在摇头晃脑给福全和康熙讲纳兰性德的民间爱情故事。
待纳兰性德进门时，康熙对纳兰性德招了招手：“过来坐下，我有问题要问你。”
纳兰性德知道康熙微服私访，只拱手行礼，顺从坐下。
胤礽对着顾贞观招招手：“你坐那里吧，别紧张，我阿玛不吃人，哎哟。”
康熙顺手给了胤礽脑袋一下。
胤礽捂着脑袋嘟嘴：“坏阿玛，再敲真的傻了。”
“我看你现在就很傻。”康熙揉了揉胤礽头顶的小揪揪。
进屋之后炭火充足，胤礽取下了小帽子，康熙又可以揉胤礽的小揪揪了。
“三爷，有何事吩咐？”纳兰性德问道。
康熙笑道：“民间传闻，‘人生若只如初见’这首词，是你写给爱而不得的心仪女子的？”
纳兰性德：“？”
心仪女子顾贞观：“？”
康熙接着笑道：“听闻你的心仪女子是什么表妹，我后院的女人？”
纳兰性德：“！”
吃瓜群众顾贞观：“！”
康熙拍着纳兰性德的肩膀，忍着笑叹气道：“你这就见外了。说吧，你心仪表妹是谁，我给你做主。你结发妻子周年祭早就过去了，明珠天天叹息给你找续弦的事。早知你的意中人在我后院，我早把人给你送来了。”
东林党顾宪成五世孙顾贞观：“……”你们满人玩得好野，后院女人可以随便送人吗？
他想了想前明时的记载。好像达官贵人互相赠送媵妾的事不但不少见，还是雅事？
哦，那没事了。
纳兰性德脸上坚毅严肃的表情崩裂了：“绝对没有此事！我的表妹姓爱新觉罗啊三爷！”
纳兰性德的亲娘乃是英亲王爱新觉罗·阿济格之女。即使阿济格因罪被除了宗籍，但他娘也是正儿八经的爱新觉罗氏，他如果有表姐妹，那也是姓爱新觉罗。
爱新觉罗怎么入宫？！
康熙：“哈哈哈哈哈哈！”
福全也忍俊不禁。
胤礽茫然歪头。
康熙继续逗弄纳兰性德：“舅家的女儿不可能，这不是还有姨家的女儿吗？”
纳兰性德的表情都要扭曲了：“三爷，绝对没有！”
康熙继续道：“明珠姐妹生的女儿也是可以的。”
纳兰性德都快哭出来了：“三爷，我家有哪些亲戚，您还不知道吗？别逗弄下官了。下官那首词真的是写给友人的。”
这谁传的谣言？谣言都传到宫中女子身上去了！
难道是纳兰家的政敌？
是不是你，索额图！（索额图：阿嚏！）
胤礽晃了晃脑袋又晃了晃脚丫：“真的没有吗？”
纳兰性德：“没有，真的没有！”
胤礽道：“民间还有个传闻，你是写给府中丫鬟哒。但是因为身份地位悬殊，你不能娶她？”
纳兰性德：“下官不是，下官没有。”
府中女子……就算有，不能娶，能纳啊。纳兰性德就算被传为大清第一痴情人，他也是封建男子，暖床丫头又不是没有。他府中现在都还有一个带孩子的侍妾呢！
胤礽叹气：“真相这么无聊吗？只是写给友人？我还求阿玛做媒呢。”
纳兰性德：“……”原来是太子殿下传的谣言。
“保成，谁告诉你这些……荒谬的事？”康熙都想拍案大笑了。
这件事他一定要分享给明珠。逗完明珠的儿子，还要逗明珠一次。
说吧，你儿子看上了朕后宫哪个女人，朕直接把那女人赐还回娘家，再给你儿子赐婚哈哈哈哈。
康熙已经能想象到明珠那扭曲的神色了。
胤礽道：“很多人啊。传得最广的就是这两个版本。他们都说，顾贞观是幌子，纳兰侍卫那首诗是写给初恋心上人。”
“很多人……哈哈哈哈，容若啊，你看看你的形象。”康熙笑得直不起腰。
福全笑着叹气：“是容若能传出的事。”
纳兰性德：“？”什么是我能传出的事？我和结发妻子伉俪情深世人皆知，这些荒谬的谣言怎么可能是真的？！
而且就算要传我的旖旎事迹，传我和名妓都比什么宫中女子府中下人靠谱吧？！
纳兰性德快裂开了。
“原来是假的。”胤礽再次满脸遗憾的叹气。现代传了那么久的缠绵悱恻的爱情故事，真相如此无聊。
你们这群文人，一个个把友情、君臣当闺怨写，真是够了。
胤礽把视线投向顾贞观：“纳兰侍卫写的词真的是给你的？你不是挡箭牌？”
顾贞观略微一琢磨，就明白了挡箭牌是什么意思。
他立刻拱手道：“容若那首词的确是为小的所写。小的亲眼见到容若酒后将此词吟出，绝非为了哪个女子。”
“嗷。”胤礽非常老气横秋地怂了怂肩膀，“阿玛，我饿了。”
“别想糊弄过去。你可是和我打赌了，你输了就要给我学狗叫。”康熙可不会放过胤礽，哪怕现在还有外人在。
现在在面前的只是他的儿子，又不是大清太子，可以不需要面子。
“哼。”胤礽脚一荡，从椅子上跳下来。
他双手竖起在头顶当耳朵，手指一勾一勾，就像是耳朵卷动。
“汪，汪，汪汪汪。”胤礽学小狗叫的时候，还跳了两下，表演得十分到位，“汪汪汪！”
“哈哈哈，好，过来，赏！”康熙笑着伸出手，胤礽跑过去，被他一把抱在怀里坐着。
顾贞观不知道这两人身份，表情还算正常。
纳兰性德是真的裂开了。
皇上！太子！你们干什么啊！
福全还在呵呵呵傻笑，丝毫不认为有什么不对。
“纳兰侍卫别在意，我这是彩衣娱亲。”胤礽见纳兰性德那一副摇摇欲坠的身子，贴心道。
“是、是这样吗？是这样啊……”纳兰性德喘了几口气，强装镇定。
“彩衣娱亲？这个描述很确切。”康熙又揉了揉胤礽的脑袋，“赏你一个摸摸头。”
胤礽眼睛竖了起来▼_▼。
敷衍！
康熙继续摸，使劲摸，直到店小二来上菜，康熙才放过胤礽。
胤礽回到自己的位置上，康熙亲自用公筷给他夹菜。他挥舞着小筷子小勺子吃得虎虎生威，半点不需要人操心，完全不用别人喂饭。
纳兰性德一直悄悄偷瞟胤礽。
虽然刚才被皇帝太子父子俩逗弄了一番，但太子似乎真的比传闻中更乖巧更懂事，也更招皇帝喜欢。
他想起难产去世的妻子，想起那个被他迁怒后从未去看过的孩子，心里黯然。
纳兰性德突然想起，仁孝皇后也是难产去世。皇上却将太子带在身边，视若珍宝，和他对待孩子的态度是天壤之别。
看到乖巧懂事的太子，想起养在母亲膝下儿子，纳兰性德难免愧疚。他想，回去要不要和儿子增进一下感情。但一看到儿子他就想到难产去世的妻子，心情十分复杂。
干完饭的胤礽捂着嘴把嗝憋了下去。
在宫里可以无所顾忌，在宫外还是得注意礼仪。
他憋嗝的时候，看到了纳兰性德眼中那浓浓的悲伤。
胤礽擦了擦嘴，扬起头道：“纳兰侍卫在难过吗？”
纳兰性德立刻回过神，笑道：“没有。”
胤礽道：“那就是难过了。”
胤礽放下擦嘴的帕子，挺直小身板道：“刚才我只是和阿玛开玩笑。你的那些传闻都传到宫……我家里了，若是假的应该澄清；若是真的，我阿玛是个大好人，会很乐意促成这件雅事。明珠大人一直为纳兰侍卫忧虑，若纳兰侍卫能振作起来，明珠大人会很高兴。”
纳兰性德背后又起了一身冷汗。
都传到宫里了？他可是乾清宫侍卫，和后宫的女人传旖旎消息，这不是陷害吗？！
现在用开玩笑的方式把这件事说明白揭过去，的确比正经地澄清更有效。
纳兰性德冰雪聪明，立刻明白了胤礽的话。
康熙笑道：“我说要让你跟着他，他就对你上心了。拼着学狗叫，也要替你把这件事说明白。”
胤礽无奈道：“阿玛你别胡说，明明是你想欺负我，我可没说要学狗叫。我说的是学猫叫。”
纳兰性德：“……谢谢小少爷。”学狗叫和学猫叫有什么不同吗？为什么小少爷要强调这一点？
“你紧张什么？你家的事三爷还不清楚吗？他就是纯逗你。”福全也道。不过他在心底补充，皇上不是逗你，而是用你逗儿子。
纳兰性德忙道：“下官知道。”
他这时候还没意识到，康熙让他跟着胤礽是什么意思。
胤礽打断了纳兰性德的哀思之后，继续干饭。
干饭人，干饭魂，干饭就是人上人。好不容易出一次宫，他得多吃一口。
宫中御厨的手艺不是不好，但为了照顾贵人们的健康和口味，不会放浓烈的调味料。
胤礽还是个孩子，小厨房给他单独做的食物就跟猫食一样少油少盐，几乎不放香辛料。
虽然胤礽可以跟着康熙蹭饭，但康熙也不会由着他吃重油重盐的食物，更不准他吃香辛料重的食物。
更可恶的是，康熙自己喜欢重口味的烧烤油炸美食。他一边吃，一边逗弄胤礽，就爱看胤礽馋嘴的模样。
宫外的酒楼则需要用味道浓烈独特的菜肴吸引客人的味觉，胤礽吃得非常满意。
康熙这次也由着胤礽吃喜欢的食物，没有唠叨。
胤礽吃得肚圆后，满足地叹了一口气。
康熙又把沉了不少的胤礽抱怀里，亲自给胤礽擦嘴擦脸。
纳兰性德也放下筷子。
他恍然发现，今日居然不知不觉吃了不少。
自从发妻亡故后，家中唯一懂纳兰性德心中苦闷的人离开，他便用饭少，喝酒多，食不知味，身体逐渐清减。
难得的饱腹感，让纳兰性德生出一种暖洋洋的满足。
他又不由悄悄瞟了康熙怀里的胤礽一眼。
显然，是胤礽的吃相太过幸福，让他也不由吃多了。
怪不得皇帝如此宠着太子。这样让人看着就会感到幸福的孩子，谁不宠着？
胤礽将脸擦干净之后，把视线投向一直沉默着的顾贞观。
这一桌都是满洲贵人，顾贞观只是一个汉族举人，除了胤礽之前问了他一句话之后，其他人都无意识的忽视他。
顾贞观自己也很乖觉，默默低头吃饭，连吃饭都只夹面前的菜，一点声音都没有发出来，极力缩小自己的存在感。
见胤礽对顾贞观感兴趣，康熙没有阻拦。
小孩子好奇心本就重，胤礽多接触些人是好事。
何况康熙也有些好奇，能让纳兰容若写出传世诗词的友人，究竟有几斤几两。
胤礽的想法和康熙一样。
他问道：“纳兰侍卫，你这位友人可有不错的诗词？”
顾贞观身体微微颤抖了一下。
纳兰性德沉思了一会儿，道：“有。他有一句词，下官自愧不如。或许究其一生，下官都难写出比那一句更好的词。”
康熙好奇道：“居然连你都自愧不如？哪句？”
顾贞观看向纳兰性德。
纳兰性德给了顾贞观一个安抚的眼神。
如果皇上看上了这首词，或许能让友人一偿夙愿。
纳兰性德闭上眼，沉酿了一会儿情绪，开口道：“我亦飘零久！十年来，深恩负尽，死生师友。”
顾贞观垂下头，身体微躬，就像是被什么重担压垮了肩。
康熙眼眸微微颤抖。
福全端起茶杯的手一顿。
胤礽眨了眨眼，叹了口气：“原来《金缕衣》是你写的啊，你就是那个为了友人蹉跎二十年的顾贞观。”
胤礽想起了顾贞观是谁。
《金缕衣·我亦飘零久》。
许多人都说，纳兰性德的诗词是清初一座不能逾越的高峰，有一个和纳兰性德同时代的人，却用一首词甚至一句词，超越了这座高峰。
那就是“我亦飘零久！十年来，深恩负尽，死生师友”。
纳兰性德的诗词绚丽，仿若后唐李煜般婉约悲伤。
顾贞观这首送给友人的词所承载的承诺和伤痛，比纳兰性德的诗词更显厚重。
纳兰性德原本只是将顾贞观当做寻常趋炎附势的门客。当读到这首词时，他才将顾贞观引为知己好友，愿意为顾贞观营救挚友，也才写出《木兰花·拟古决绝词柬友》。
纳兰性德在这首词中以班婕妤和杨贵妃被负心男子抛弃的幽怨故事委婉告诉友人，他想要忠贞不二的“爱”。
文人的友谊，就是这么黏糊。
康熙疑惑：“你知道？”
朕都不知道，保成怎么知道？哦，肯定又是保成那个话痨玛法，呵。
康熙举起茶杯掩饰嘴角下垂。
胤礽想起顾贞观之后，便想帮一帮这个人。
就算没有他，以纳兰明珠之能，顶多再过两三年，顾贞观的友人吴兆骞就能回来。
现在他多说一句话，让吴兆骞少受两三年的罪，说不定吴兆骞不会那么早去世，顾贞观也不会在吴兆骞去世之后黯然神伤，致仕隐居。
顾贞观才华不错，可以用。
胤礽属于太子的脑子上线了一会儿，道：“顺治十四年，因源自前明的南北党争延续，而发生的科举舞弊案。”
顾贞观猛地抬起头，又立刻将头低了下去。
纳兰性德惊讶地看向胤礽，连规矩都忘记了。
福全挠了挠头。好像有这回事？
康熙眼眸闪了闪，轻笑道：“南北党争啊。”
呃，那场科举舞弊案朕知道，南北党争是什么？康熙装得很镇定，看上去好像胤礽所说的话是他教的一样。
胤礽也以为康熙知道。
这些史书上不是写着嘛，自家酷爱读书的阿玛怎么会不知道。
他却忘记了，书上可不会写什么南北党争。这是后世人经过大量的资料和唯物史观的客观评价之后总结出来的。
没有纵观大局的眼光视野，没有高屋建瓴的思想指导，古人不可能看到这一点——在古人看来，“君子结党不是结党”。
过于相信康熙的胤礽，将他以为很浅显的源于前明的南北党争之事一一道出，并阐述了顺治朝对两拨人的处置。
他没有猜测顺治如此处置的原因，但事实上便是这期科举舞弊案先是南党遭殃，后来北党也遭到了清算。
“吴兆骞确实有才，但先帝给了他机会，他没抓住，先帝总不能给他单独加试。”胤礽只评价了这么一句，显得顺治好像一切尽在掌握中。
谁让他老嚷嚷顺治千古一帝，总要帮背锅侠玛法粉饰一下。
福全使劲点头，看似一副十分聪明的模样：“对，对。就和殿试时那些吓得不敢下笔的人一样，即使有才又如何？做不出来就是做不出来。先帝让那次中举的举子们复试，通过的免罪，没通过的便是作弊，这是最能堵悠悠众口的处置。”
康熙笑道：“你这首词写给吴兆骞？”
顾贞观扑通一声跪下，伏地道：“是。”
康熙感慨：“快二十年了吧。你一直未放弃？”
顾贞观老泪纵横：“是。”
康熙叹气：“河粱生别之诗，山阳死友之传，得此而三。罢了，这事朕知晓了。”
朕……朕？
顾贞观身体瘫软。
康熙又道：“你有如此心性，很好。”
顾贞观激动叩首，不能言语。
“好了好了，别磕头了。我好不容易出来玩一趟，别把气氛弄得这么悲伤。”胤礽像熊孩子一样嚷嚷，“阿玛阿玛，我吃饱了，我们去逛街！我要继续玩。”
“你就知道玩！”康熙见自家宝贝太子才展现出英明聪慧不到半刻钟，便又固态萌发，狠狠搓了一下胤礽的小脑袋，“让阿玛歇歇，喝口茶再去。你们俩随侍。”
康熙既然已经暴露了身份，就懒得再装下去。
福全只会和他抢儿子，还是再带两个人陪同更好玩。
这两人擅长诗词，估摸也擅长金石古玩，他能和这两人有共同语言。
福全只会说，“这个贵，买了！”，实在是个大老粗。
“遵命。”纳兰性德激动抱拳，“还不快谢谢三爷！谢谢小公子！”
顾贞观使劲磕头，把额头都嗑红了：“谢谢三爷，谢谢小公子！”
他偷偷擦了擦眼泪，但眼泪怎么都无法完全止住。
二十年了，二十年了，挚友终于有救了！
胤礽看着一个大男人跪在地上哭得不能自已，担心顾贞观扰了康熙的兴致，好不容易得偿夙愿，却又横生枝节。
他从康熙腿上跳下来，掏出小手绢递给顾贞观：“别哭了。伤了身体，怎么开开心心迎接友人回来？”
康熙无奈摇头。
自己这儿子啊，唉，还是过于善良了，得改。
福全眼更红了。
善良的儿子在宫里不容易长大，但在亲王府里不会啊。唉，这儿子怎么不是我的？
纳兰性德却抿了抿嘴，内心动摇。
叶赫那拉氏站在传统满洲勋贵这一边，心底对太子并不友善，纳兰性德自然跟随家中的政治立场。
但纳兰性德本人却和汉族文人走得近，深受汉族文化熏陶，所以对太子并不抵触。
现在看到如此善良聪慧的太子，又想到那些和自己格格不入的满洲勋贵，纳兰性德内心难免动摇。
人皆说纳兰性德心如死灰是因为结发妻子。
但纳兰性德知道，他虽然深爱妻子，但并不会因为妻子而郁结于心，引父母家人担忧。
他既然深知挚爱离世的痛苦，又怎会将痛苦带给家人？
他的郁结于心，是即使想着家人也无法缓解的事，是家人给他带来的郁结于心。
顺治和康熙两朝帝王都修习汉学。纳兰明珠深知帝心，本身又很有才华，对大儿子的教导几乎按照传统汉家世家子弟来，把纳兰性德教导成了一个真正的读书人。
一个真正的读书人，忠君报国，修身齐家治国平天下，却和叶赫那拉家真正的政治目的背道而驰。

季子平安否？便归来，平生万事，那堪回首！行路悠悠谁慰藉，母老家贫子幼。记不起，从前杯酒。魑魅搏人应见惯，总输他，覆雨翻云手，冰与雪，周旋久。
泪痕莫滴牛衣透，数天涯，依然骨肉，几家能够？比似红颜多命薄，更不如今还有。只绝塞，苦寒难受。廿载包胥承一诺，盼乌头马角终相救。置此札，君怀袖。
