chapters.translated_text:
When Nalan Xingde saw Zhao Chang, the melancholic expression on his face instantly transformed into the serious and resolute look of an ordinary imperial guard, nearly causing his friend Gu Zhenguan to spit out his tea.

Ever since his wife passed away, Nalan Xingde had often worn a look of melancholy, breaking the hearts of countless young women in the capital; even men secretly referred to him as the "Number One Infatuated Man."

Gu Zhenguan had known Nalan Xingde for many years, yet he had never seen him display such a masculine and imposing expression.

Not even when Nalan Xingde stood before Minister Ming!

"The Third Master asks you to come up for a word, Guard Nalan," Zhao Chang said with a smile.

The Third Master...

Nalan Xingde felt his hair stand on end. His sentimental mind, as if doused by a cold wind, instantly sobered up, and he couldn't help but shiver.

He looked back at his friend Gu Zhenguan, who immediately understood and bowed to take his leave.

Anyone who could make the son of Minister Ming so nervous must be a high-ranking official or noble, perhaps even a member of the imperial clan. Gu Zhenguan was merely a down-and-out scholar and could not accompany him.

But before Gu Zhenguan could leave, another attendant walked over and delivered another order.

"Are you Gu Zhenguan?" the attendant asked. "Was the line, 'If life were only as it was when we first met, why would the autumn wind grieve the painted fan?' written by Guard Nalan to you?"

Gu Zhenguan: "...This humble one is Gu Zhenguan."

Zhao Chang was surprised: "That poem was written for you?"

Nalan Xingde gave a wry smile: "D-don't tell me the Third Master has also read my poetry?"

Zhao Chang laughed: "The Little Young Master likes Guard Nalan's poems very much. Come up together, then."

Zhao Chang was doing Nalan Xingde a favor.

Zhao Chang understood Kangxi and the Crown Prince. Upon hearing the attendant’s question, he guessed that the person curious about Gu Zhenguan must be the Crown Prince, so he subtly passed this information to Nalan Xingde.

Nalan Xingde gasped.

Could it be that the Crown Prince had come too? He thought of how Kangxi and the Crown Prince were announcing their victory from the city gate tower earlier, and nodded to Zhao Chang: "Thank you."

Zhao Chang smiled: "Then hurry up, the Second Master and Third Master are still waiting upstairs."

The Second Master... Prince Yu had come as well?

Nalan Xingde pulled his friend aside and warned: "You must not be disrespectful. If you are, even I won't be able to protect you."

Gu Zhenguan nodded immediately: "I understand."

The two walked upstairs together. Yinreng was dangling his little feet, shaking his head as he told Fuquan and Kangxi the folk love stories about Nalan Xingde.

When Nalan Xingde entered the room, Kangxi beckoned him over: "Come and sit, I have questions for you."

Nalan Xingde knew Kangxi was traveling incognito, so he simply bowed and sat down obediently.

Yinreng beckoned to Gu Zhenguan: "You sit there. Don't be nervous, my Ama doesn't eat people. Ouch."

Kangxi had casually tapped Yinreng on the head.

Yinreng covered his head and pouted: "Bad Ama, if you tap me again, I'll really become stupid."

"I think you're quite silly as it is." Kangxi ruffled the little tuft of hair on Yinreng's head.

The room was warm with charcoal fire, and Yinreng had taken off his little hat, allowing Kangxi to rub his hair tuft again.

"Third Master, what are your instructions?" Nalan Xingde asked.

Kangxi laughed: "There is a rumor among the people that the poem 'If life were only as it was when we first met' was written for a woman you loved but could not have?"

Nalan Xingde: "?"

The "beloved woman" Gu Zhenguan: "?"

Kangxi continued with a smile: "I heard your beloved is some cousin, a woman from my own backyard?"

Nalan Xingde: "!"

The gossip-loving Gu Zhenguan: "!"

Kangxi patted Nalan Xingde's shoulder, suppressing a laugh as he sighed: "You're being too distant. Tell me, who is this cousin you love? I will decide the matter for you. The first anniversary of your wife's death has long passed, and Mingzhu sighs every day about finding you a new wife. Had I known your beloved was in my backyard, I would have sent her to you long ago."

Gu Zhenguan, the fifth-generation descendant of the Donglin Party's Gu Xiancheng: "..." You Manchus play quite wildly; can women in the backyard be given away so casually?

He thought about the records from the previous Ming Dynasty. It seemed that high-ranking officials gifting concubines to each other was not only common but considered an elegant affair?

Oh, never mind then.

The resolute and serious expression on Nalan Xingde's face crumbled: "There is absolutely no such thing! My cousin's surname is Aisin Gioro, Third Master!"

Nalan Xingde's mother was the daughter of Prince Ying, Aisin Gioro Ajige. Even though Ajige had been stripped of his clan status due to crimes, his mother was still a legitimate Aisin Gioro. If he had any female cousins, they would also be surnamed Aisin Gioro.

How could an Aisin Gioro enter the palace?!

Kangxi: "Hahahaha!"

Fuquan also couldn't help but laugh.

Yinreng tilted his head in confusion.

Kangxi continued to tease Nalan Xingde: "If it's not a daughter from your uncle's side, what about a daughter from your aunt's side?"

Nalan Xingde's expression was almost twisted: "Third Master, there is absolutely no such thing!"

Kangxi continued: "Daughters born to Mingzhu's sisters would also work."

Nalan Xingde was on the verge of tears: "Third Master, don't you know which relatives I have? Please stop teasing this official. That poem was truly written for a friend."

Who started this rumor? The rumors had even spread to the women in the palace!

Could it be Nalan's political rival?

Is it you, Songgotu! (Songgotu: *Achoo!*)

Yinreng shook his head and then his feet: "Is there really nothing?"

Nalan Xingde: "Nothing, there really isn't!"

Yinreng said: "There is another rumor among the people that you wrote it for a maid in your household. But because of the disparity in status, you couldn't marry her?"

Nalan Xingde: "This official did not, this official has no such thing."

Women in the household... even if there were, if he couldn't marry them, he could take them as concubines. Even if Nalan Xingde was rumored to be the most infatuated man in the Qing Dynasty, he was still a feudal man; it wasn't as if he didn't have bed-warming maids. He even had a concubine with a child in his household right now!

Yinreng sighed: "Is the truth so boring? Just written for a friend? I even asked Ama to play matchmaker."

Nalan Xingde: "..." So it was the Crown Prince who started the rumor.

"Baocheng, who told you these... absurd things?" Kangxi wanted to slap the table and laugh.

He must share this with Mingzhu. After teasing Mingzhu's son, he would tease Mingzhu himself.

Tell me, which woman in my harem does your son fancy? I'll grant her back to her maiden family and then bestow a marriage upon your son, hahaha.

Kangxi could already imagine Mingzhu's twisted expression.

Yinreng said: "Many people. These two versions are the most widespread. They all say that Gu Zhenguan is just a cover, and that Guard Nalan's poem was written for his first love."

"Many people... hahahaha, Rongruo, look at your image." Kangxi laughed so hard he couldn't straighten his back.

Fuquan smiled and sighed: "It's exactly the kind of thing that would be spread about Rongruo."

Nalan Xingde: "?" What is the kind of thing that would be spread about me? Everyone knows how deeply I loved my wife; how could these absurd rumors be true?!

And even if they were to spread romantic stories about me, wouldn't rumors about me and a famous courtesan be more plausible than palace women or household servants?!

Nalan Xingde was about to break down.

"So it's fake." Yinreng sighed again with a face full of regret. The lingering, heart-wrenching love story that had been passed down for so long in modern times—the truth was so boring.

You scholars, writing about friendship and monarch-subject relations as if they were boudoir grievances, it's really enough.

Yinreng turned his gaze to Gu Zhenguan: "Was the poem written by Guard Nalan really for you? You aren't a shield?"

Gu Zhenguan pondered for a moment and understood what "shield" meant.

He immediately bowed and said: "That poem by Rongruo was indeed written for this humble one. I personally saw Rongruo recite this poem after drinking; it was absolutely not for any woman."

"Oh." Yinreng shrugged his shoulders in a very old-fashioned way, "Ama, I'm hungry."

"Don't try to brush it off. You made a bet with me; if you lost, you have to bark like a dog for me." Kangxi wouldn't let Yinreng off the hook, even with outsiders present.

The person in front of him was just his son, not the Crown Prince of the Qing Dynasty, so he didn't need to worry about face.

"Hmph." Yinreng swung his feet and jumped off the chair.

He put his hands on his head like ears, his fingers curling and uncurling.

"Woof, woof, woof-woof-woof." When Yinreng barked like a puppy, he even jumped twice, performing it very well, "Woof-woof-woof!"

"Hahaha, good, come here, reward!" Kangxi laughed and reached out his hand. Yinreng ran over and was pulled into his arms.

Gu Zhenguan didn't know the identities of these two, so his expression remained normal.

Nalan Xingde was truly breaking down.

Your Majesty! Crown Prince! What are you doing!

Fuquan was still chuckling, not thinking there was anything wrong at all.

"Don't mind it, Guard Nalan, this is just me 'wearing colorful clothes to amuse my parents'," Yinreng said considerately, seeing Nalan Xingde's crumbling state.

"I-is that so? Is that so..." Nalan Xingde took a few breaths, pretending to be calm.

"Wearing colorful clothes to amuse parents? That's an accurate description." Kangxi rubbed Yinreng's head again, "I'll reward you with a head-pat."

Yinreng's eyes narrowed ▼_▼.

Perfunctory!

Kangxi continued to rub, rubbing hard, until the waiter came to serve the dishes, at which point Kangxi finally let Yinreng go.

Yinreng returned to his seat, and Kangxi personally used serving chopsticks to put food in his bowl. He wielded his small chopsticks and spoon, eating with great vigor, needing no help at all.

Nalan Xingde kept stealing glances at Yinreng.

Although he had just been teased by the Emperor and the Crown Prince, the Crown Prince seemed even more well-behaved and sensible than the rumors suggested, and even more favored by the Emperor.

He thought of his wife who died in childbirth, and the child he had never visited after venting his anger on him, feeling desolate.

Nalan Xingde suddenly remembered that Empress Renxiao had also died in childbirth. Yet the Emperor kept the Crown Prince by his side, treating him like a treasure—a world of difference from how he treated his own child.

Seeing the well-behaved Crown Prince and thinking of his son raised by his mother, Nalan Xingde couldn't help but feel guilty. He thought about whether he should improve his relationship with his son when he returned. But whenever he saw his son, he thought of his wife, and his feelings were very complex.

Having finished his meal, Yinreng covered his mouth and suppressed a burp.

In the palace, he could be carefree, but outside, he still had to pay attention to etiquette.

As he suppressed the burp, he saw the deep sadness in Nalan Xingde's eyes.

Yinreng wiped his mouth and raised his head: "Is Guard Nalan sad?"

Nalan Xingde immediately came to his senses and smiled: "No."

Yinreng said: "Then it is sadness."

Yinreng put down his napkin and straightened his little body: "I was just joking with Ama earlier. Those rumors about you have even reached the palace... my home. If they are fake, they should be clarified; if they are true, my Ama is a very kind person and would be happy to facilitate this elegant affair. Minister Ming has always been worried about you, Guard Nalan; if you can pull yourself together, Minister Ming will be very happy."

Nalan Xingde broke out in a cold sweat again.

It had even reached the palace? He was a guard at the Qianqing Palace; having romantic rumors with women in the harem—wasn't this framing him?!

Using a joking manner to clarify and move past this was indeed more effective than a serious clarification.

Nalan Xingde was quick-witted and immediately understood Yinreng's words.

Kangxi laughed: "I said that if I let you follow him, he would take you to heart. He even risked barking like a dog just to clarify this for you."

Yinreng said helplessly: "Ama, don't talk nonsense. It was clearly you who wanted to bully me; I never said I would bark like a dog. I said I would meow like a cat."

Nalan Xingde: "...Thank you, Little Young Master." Was there any difference between barking like a dog and meowing like a cat? Why did the Little Young Master emphasize this?

"What are you nervous about? Doesn't the Third Master know about your family affairs? He was just teasing you." Fuquan also said. Though he added in his heart, the Emperor wasn't teasing you; he was using you to tease his son.

Nalan Xingde hurriedly said: "This official understands."

At this moment, he still hadn't realized what Kangxi meant by letting him follow Yinreng.

After Yinreng interrupted Nalan Xingde's mourning, he continued to eat.

A foodie's soul, eating is the path to being a superior person. Since he had finally managed to get out of the palace, he had to eat a bit more.

The imperial chefs' skills weren't bad, but to take care of the nobles' health and palates, they wouldn't use strong seasonings.

Yinreng was still a child, and the food made for him in the small kitchen was like cat food—low oil, low salt, and almost no spices.

Although Yinreng could mooch off Kangxi's meals, Kangxi wouldn't let him eat food high in oil and salt, and certainly wouldn't allow him to eat heavily spiced food.

Even more hateful was that Kangxi himself liked heavy-flavored grilled and fried foods. He would eat while teasing Yinreng, just to watch Yinreng's greedy look.

The restaurants outside needed strong and unique flavors to attract customers, and Yinreng was very satisfied.

This time, Kangxi let Yinreng eat the food he liked without nagging.

After Yinreng's belly was full, he sighed with satisfaction.

Kangxi pulled the now-heavier Yinreng into his arms and personally wiped his mouth and face.

Nalan Xingde also put down his chopsticks.

He realized with a start that he had eaten quite a lot without even noticing.

Ever since his wife passed away, the only person in his home who understood his inner turmoil was gone, so he ate little, drank much, and lost his appetite, gradually becoming thin.

The rare feeling of fullness gave Nalan Xingde a warm sense of satisfaction.

He couldn't help but steal another glance at Yinreng in Kangxi's arms.

Clearly, it was Yinreng's happy way of eating that had made him eat more too.

No wonder the Emperor doted on the Crown Prince so much. Who wouldn't dote on a child who made people feel happy just by watching him?

After Yinreng wiped his face clean, he turned his gaze to Gu Zhenguan, who had been silent all along.

This table was full of Manchu nobles, and Gu Zhenguan was just a Han scholar. Except for the one question Yinreng had asked him earlier, everyone else had subconsciously ignored him.

Gu Zhenguan was very sensible; he silently lowered his head to eat, only picking at the dishes in front of him, not making a sound, trying his best to minimize his presence.

Seeing that Yinreng was interested in Gu Zhenguan, Kangxi didn't stop him.

Children were naturally curious, and it was good for Yinreng to interact with more people.

Besides, Kangxi was also a bit curious about how much talent the friend who could make Nalan Rongruo write such enduring poetry really had.

Yinreng's thoughts were the same as Kangxi's.

He asked: "Guard Nalan, does this friend of yours have any good poems?"

Gu Zhenguan's body trembled slightly.

Nalan Xingde pondered for a while and said: "Yes. He has a line of poetry that this official feels ashamed to compare with. Perhaps in my entire life, I will never be able to write a better line."

Kangxi asked curiously: "Even you feel ashamed? Which line?"

Gu Zhenguan looked at Nalan Xingde.

Nalan Xingde gave Gu Zhenguan a reassuring look.

If the Emperor took a liking to this poem, perhaps it could help his friend fulfill his long-cherished wish.

Nalan Xingde closed his eyes, brewed his emotions for a moment, and said: "I have also been drifting for a long time! In these ten years, I have failed my deep gratitude, and lost my teacher and friend in life and death."

Gu Zhenguan lowered his head, his body slightly hunched, as if crushed by some heavy burden.

Kangxi's eyes trembled slightly.

Fuquan's hand holding the teacup paused.

Yinreng blinked and sighed: "So you are the one who wrote 'Jinlü Yi', you are Gu Zhenguan who wasted twenty years for a friend."

Yinreng remembered who Gu Zhenguan was.

"Jinlü Qu: I have also been drifting for a long time."

Many people said that Nalan Xingde's poetry was an insurmountable peak in the early Qing Dynasty, yet someone contemporary to him had surpassed this peak with a single poem, or even a single line.

That was "I have also been drifting for a long time! In these ten years, I have failed my deep gratitude, and lost my teacher and friend in life and death."

Nalan Xingde's poetry was gorgeous, as graceful and sorrowful as Li Yu of the Southern Tang.

The promise and pain carried by this poem Gu Zhenguan wrote for his friend were even heavier than Nalan Xingde's poetry.

Nalan Xingde had originally treated Gu Zhenguan as an ordinary sycophantic guest. It was only when he read this poem that he regarded Gu Zhenguan as a soulmate, willing to rescue his friend for him, and thus wrote "Mulan Hua: Imitating Ancient Farewell Poem to a Friend."

In this poem, Nalan Xingde used the stories of Ban Jieyu and Yang Guifei being abandoned by heartless men to subtly tell his friend that he wanted a loyal "love."

The friendship of scholars is just this sticky.

Kangxi was puzzled: "You know this?"

Even I don't know this, how does Baocheng know? Oh, it must be that chatterbox grandfather of his again, heh.

Kangxi raised his teacup to hide the corners of his mouth drooping.

After remembering who Gu Zhenguan was, Yinreng wanted to help this person.

Even without him, with Nalan Mingzhu's ability, Gu Zhenguan's friend Wu Zhaoqian would return in at most two or three years.

Now, if he said one more word, Wu Zhaoqian might suffer two or three years less; perhaps Wu Zhaoqian wouldn't die so early, and Gu Zhenguan wouldn't be so desolate after Wu Zhaoqian's death, retiring into seclusion.

Gu Zhenguan had good talent and could be used.

Yinreng's Crown Prince brain came online for a moment and said: "In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, the imperial examination fraud case occurred due to the continuation of the North-South party strife from the previous Ming Dynasty."

Gu Zhenguan suddenly raised his head, then immediately lowered it again.

Nalan Xingde looked at Yinreng in surprise, forgetting even the rules.

Fuquan scratched his head. Did that happen?

Kangxi's eyes flickered, and he chuckled: "North-South party strife, huh."

Uh, I know about that imperial examination fraud case, but what is North-South party strife? Kangxi pretended to be very calm, looking as if what Yinreng said was something he had taught him.

Yinreng also thought Kangxi knew.

It was written in history books, how could his Ama, who loved reading, not know?

He forgot that history books wouldn't write about "North-South party strife." This was a conclusion reached by later generations after a large amount of data and objective evaluation from a materialist historical perspective.

Without a broad perspective and high-level ideological guidance, the ancients could not see this—in their view, "a gentleman forming a party is not forming a party."

Yinreng, who trusted Kangxi too much, recounted the matter of the North-South party strife originating from the previous Ming Dynasty, which he thought was very simple, and explained the Shunzhi court's handling of the two groups.

He didn't guess the reason for Shunzhi's handling, but in fact, this imperial examination fraud case first saw the Southern Party suffer, and later the Northern Party was also liquidated.

"Wu Zhaoqian is indeed talented, but the late Emperor gave him a chance, and he didn't grasp it; the late Emperor couldn't just give him a separate exam." Yinreng only commented on this, making it seem like Shunzhi had everything under control.

Since he always touted Shunzhi as the Emperor of the Ages, he had to whitewash his grandfather, the scapegoat.

Fuquan nodded vigorously, looking very smart: "Right, right. Just like those people at the palace examination who were too scared to write; even if they have talent, so what? If you can't do it, you can't do it. The late Emperor had the successful candidates retake the exam; those who passed were pardoned, and those who didn't were cheating. This is the best way to silence the public."

Kangxi smiled: "You wrote this poem for Wu Zhaoqian?"

Gu Zhenguan knelt down with a thud and prostrated: "Yes."

Kangxi sighed with emotion: "It's been almost twenty years, hasn't it? You never gave up?"

Gu Zhenguan's tears flowed: "Yes."

Kangxi sighed: "The poem of parting at the river bridge, the story of a friend dying at Shanyang—this makes three. Enough, I know about this matter now."

I... I?

Gu Zhenguan's body went limp.

Kangxi added: "You have such a disposition, very good."

Gu Zhenguan kowtowed excitedly, unable to speak.

"Alright, alright, stop kowtowing. I finally came out to play, don't make the atmosphere so sad." Yinreng shouted like a brat, "Ama, Ama, I'm full, let's go shopping! I want to keep playing."

"You only know how to play!" Seeing his precious Crown Prince show wisdom for less than half a quarter of an hour before reverting to his old self, Kangxi rubbed Yinreng's little head hard, "Let Ama rest, drink some tea before going. You two, attend us."

Since Kangxi had already revealed his identity, he couldn't be bothered to keep pretending.

Fuquan would only fight him for his son; it was more fun to have two more people accompanying them.

These two were good at poetry and likely good at antiques and calligraphy, so he could have a common language with them.

Fuquan would only say, "This is expensive, buy it!", he was really a brute.

"As you command." Nalan Xingde clasped his fists excitedly, "Why don't you thank the Third Master! Thank the Little Young Master!"

Gu Zhenguan kowtowed hard, making his forehead red: "Thank you, Third Master, thank you, Little Young Master!"

He secretly wiped away his tears, but they wouldn't stop.

Twenty years, twenty years, his best friend was finally saved!

Yinreng watched the grown man kneeling on the ground crying uncontrollably, worried that Gu Zhenguan would ruin Kangxi's mood, having finally fulfilled his wish only to have complications arise.

He jumped off Kangxi's lap and took out a small handkerchief to hand to Gu Zhenguan: "Don't cry. If you hurt your body, how will you happily welcome your friend back?"

Kangxi shook his head helplessly.

This son of his, sigh, he's still too kind, he needs to change.

Fuquan's eyes were even redder.

A kind son doesn't grow up easily in the palace, but he would in a Prince's mansion. Sigh, why isn't this son mine?

Nalan Xingde pursed his lips, his heart wavering.

The Yehenara clan stood on the side of the traditional Manchu nobility and was not friendly to the Crown Prince; Nalan Xingde naturally followed his family's political stance.

But Nalan Xingde himself was close to Han scholars and deeply influenced by Han culture, so he was not resistant to the Crown Prince.

Now seeing such a kind and intelligent Crown Prince, and thinking of those Manchu nobles who were incompatible with him, Nalan Xingde's heart couldn't help but waver.

People all said Nalan Xingde's heart was dead because of his wife.

But Nalan Xingde knew that although he loved his wife deeply, he wouldn't be depressed because of her, causing his parents and family to worry.

Since he knew the pain of losing a loved one, how could he bring that pain to his family?

His inner turmoil was something that couldn't be relieved even when thinking of his family; it was the turmoil his family brought upon him.

Both the Shunzhi and Kangxi emperors studied Han learning. Nalan Mingzhu knew the Emperor's heart well and was talented himself, so he taught his eldest son almost according to the traditional Han family standards, raising Nalan Xingde into a true scholar.

A true scholar, loyal to the monarch and patriotic, cultivating himself, regulating his family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world, yet this ran counter to the true political goals of the Yehenara family.

100,000

chapters.title: 第 29 章 [V]
chapters.source_text:
康熙歇息了一会儿后，继续逛庙会。
康熙和纳兰性德、顾贞观聊得很尽兴。
不一会儿，胤礽的眼神就开始飘。
他听得懂那些诗词歌赋的话题，但不想听。于是他装出一副“大人的话题小孩子并不想参与”的表情，甩掉他阿玛的手，和福全走一起。
福全立刻把胤礽抱怀里，把他皇帝弟弟抛一边，胆子大极了。
康熙看着一大一小疯玩的人，无奈地笑着摇摇头，任他们去了。
康熙听了胤礽所说的“南北党争”的事，非常好奇。
他再好奇也不好意思揪着胤礽打听。
我这个当阿玛的不要面子吗？
所以康熙只能自己琢磨这件事。
纳兰性德虽然也不知道什么南北党争的事，但他门客中文人众多，南边的北边的都有。这些文人日常相处的时候总会带出一些地域偏见出来。纳兰性德感情细腻，对那些人的感情冲突记得很明白。
康熙询问的时候，他便这些事一一细说给康熙听，和康熙一起琢磨这些表面冲突背后是否有更深刻的含义。
顾贞观作为东林党人的后代，从小耳濡目染，对文人那些弯弯道道了解得很清楚。每当康熙拿不准主意的时候，就问顾贞观。
顾贞观不断擦汗。
如果可以的话，他并不想回答。
君子之争怎么变成了朋党之争？
学问争论怎么变成了利益争夺？
那些光风霁月的道德模范，背地里又有怎样的阴暗勾当？
地方豪强世家与朝中大员勾结，他们立在前面的标杆人物，是怎么从小开始养望？
顾贞观身为文人，即使自己是真的道德模范，也不愿意揭开文人那层光鲜的外皮。
若这事传出去，他就无法立足了。
可面前是皇帝啊。皇帝询问，他能不回答吗？
他倒是可以以死明志，但好不容易才有了救回友人的希望，他不能连累友人。
康熙：你挚友在我手中.jpg。
还好有胤礽这个神仙宝宝，解救顾贞观于水火之中。
胤礽头戴刚买的虎耳帽，脖子上挂着几串鲜艳的绒布花，左手拿着小小的木风车，右手拎着一个兔子灯笼，跑到康熙面前阻止康熙继续折腾顾贞观。
他跑到康熙面前后，先看看左手的木风车，然后看看右手的兔子灯笼，发现没手去拉康熙的衣角，脑子不知怎么的一抽，用木风车戳了戳康熙。
当胤礽跑过来的时候，康熙便停止聊天，微笑着低头看向胤礽。
胤礽用木风车戳。
康熙岿然不动。
胤礽迷惑地眨了眨眼，又用兔子灯笼戳了戳康熙。
康熙微笑不语。
胤礽用木风车和兔子灯笼轮流戳康熙，被康熙一把提起来大眼瞪小眼。
康熙哭笑不得：“保成，你干什么？”
胤礽：“我有话要和阿玛说。”
康熙：“然后？”
胤礽迷糊皱眉：“我要说什么来着？”戳着戳着就忘了。
康熙：“……蠢儿子，嫌弃你。”
福全立刻伸手：“嫌弃的话给我给我，三爷，乖侄子给我抱抱。”
康熙瞥了福全一眼：“你已经抱得够久了。”
他让纳兰性德把胤礽手中的小东西拿好，让胤礽双手抱着他的脖子，在他怀中坐好。
“想起来了吗？”康熙笑着问道。
胤礽眼睛一亮：“想起来了！”
康熙道：“说。”
胤礽幽幽叹了一口气后才道：“阿玛，别欺负顾贞观了。你再问下去，他就会变成文人的叛徒，被口诛笔伐，说不定全家都会被逼死。”
顾贞观：“……”太子殿下，您不用说得这么直白！
康熙皱眉：“有这么严重？”
胤礽点头：“小人不容易被逼死。君子会。”
康熙叹气：“有道理。罢了，我多找几个人问问。你说于成龙如何？我之前认为他是个难得的清官……”
康熙讽刺地笑了笑：“大清的俸禄可不低，倒也不至于抛妻别子，身无别物。”
顾贞观：“！！！”皇帝陛下，您真的是想逼死我！
胤礽拽了拽康熙的毛绒绒领口：“阿玛，人无完人，论迹不论心，论心无好人。被阿玛和玛法一直挂在嘴边的于成龙大人政绩斐然，生活简朴，这是事实。”
“你说得对。”康熙情绪来得快去得也快。
他何尝不知道这个道理？
汉官仕途本就艰难，若没有一些特立独行的“养望”之举，如何被他人所知？
从顺治朝到今朝，两代皇帝都在整顿吏治，整顿吏治的举动都十分艰难。
康熙需要树立一个清官典型，于成龙能吃得下当清官典型这个苦，他们便可以一拍即合。
“你这时候怎么变聪明了？”康熙揉了揉胤礽刚买的虎耳朵帽子。
胤礽给了康熙一个鄙视的小眼神：“儿子说的话，不是阿玛经常说的吗？阿玛是在自夸？”
康熙“哈哈”大笑，丢开纳兰性德和顾贞观，继续和儿子玩了。
福全跟在后面，表情十分落寞。
他才和太子侄儿没玩一会儿，皇帝弟弟怎么就又把太子侄儿抢走了呢？
纳兰性德和顾贞观交换了一个眼神，眼神中是对太子此举的惊艳。
从古至今神童不少，许多文人三岁能作诗，五岁写出锦绣文章。
更别说当朝皇帝也是个“神童”，八岁登基时便已经初具明君之相。
太子已经近五岁，聪慧过人并不令人惊诧。太子令人惊诧的地方是他童言稚语中对人心的把握。
这种人情世故需要经验积累，也需要天赋，有些人学一辈子都学不会。
国有如此太子，只要太子不夭折，定可以保证国两代安康。
顾贞观是汉人。汉人本就认可太子，顾贞观自然只会欣喜。
纳兰性德心中就纠结焦虑了。
他认可太子，可家里站在太子对立面上。思绪两相拉扯，让纳兰性德不由头疼得厉害。
胤礽和康熙笑闹的时候，眼神瞟到正在皱着眉头揉太阳穴的纳兰性德，拍了拍康熙的脸，指向纳兰性德。
康熙会错意：“怎么？被容若病美人之态迷了眼？”
病美人纳兰性德：“……”皇上您够了！
胤礽震惊：“阿玛，你难道不是该关心纳兰侍卫的身体吗！”
康熙：“……”
康熙把胤礽的小脑袋按进怀里，神色如常道：“怎么？风吹多了头疼？你是侍卫，身体这么弱怎么行？”
头埋在康熙怀里的胤礽闷声道：“阿玛，阿玛，是关心爱护，不是唠叨斥责。”
康熙把胤礽的脑袋按得更严实了一点，胤礽没声音了。
纳兰性德失笑：“三爷，下官只是喝酒后吹了风，不碍事。”
胤礽把小脑袋从康熙怀里拔、出来，头顶两虎耳朵因为他动作幅度太大使劲晃了晃。
“少喝酒，喝酒伤身。”胤礽老气横秋地晃脑袋，虎耳朵跟着他的晃脑袋的动作继续晃啊晃，“身体健康是实现一切理想的本钱，没有身体健康就没有一切。”
这绝对是胤礽他玛法的抱怨。康熙失笑。
顺治不就是壮志未酬身先死吗？
纳兰性德愣了愣，然后笑道：“小少爷说得对。”
胤礽对纳兰性德招了招手，纳兰性德在康熙的眼神示意下，把脑袋凑了过来。
胤礽努力探出身体，伸出两只温暖的小肉手，捂住纳兰性德的太阳穴。
“揉揉，呼呼，痛痛飞走。”沾沾纳兰性德文气，然后回去蹭给天天为读书头疼的大阿哥。胤礽美滋滋地想。
纳兰性德感受到脸上的柔软和温暖，表情微愣。
“咳。”康熙嫉妒了。
儿子太过温柔怎么办？虽然很骄傲，但并不想儿子对其他人这么温柔。
纳兰性德回过神，忙向胤礽道谢。
胤礽笑了笑，又给吃醋的康熙揉了揉。
康熙高兴了。福全对胤礽伸出手，伯伯也要，伯伯也想！
康熙：“不，你不想。”
他迈动大长腿，抱着儿子快步离开。
福全跟在康熙身后一路小跑：“就一下。”
康熙：“不给。”
落后几步的纳兰性德摸了摸自己的太阳穴。
顾贞观感慨：“太子殿下真是……”
顾贞观想了许久，不知道该如何评价这位大清太子。
只能说，谁看到这位大清太子，都会萌生“这是我家儿子多好啊”的感受吧。
福全：是的，没错，想抱回家.jpg。
……
在宫门落钥前，康熙带着满载而归的胤礽回宫。
康熙白日玩了一天，晚上就只能秉烛处理宫务。
胤礽便让内侍们拎着大包小包，找胤禔困觉。
胤禔知道胤礽今日会出宫，心里有点酸。
他也想出宫。
但这点酸意在胤礽包袱款款来找他抵足而眠的时候就消失了。
我弟弟果然爱我！
胤禔和胤礽坐在宽大的软塌上分东西。
“这个绒花给额娘。这个给太皇太后。”
“哥哥，皇太后呢？”
“啊，我忘了还有皇太后了。”
“哪个给弟弟？”
“这个。”
“哥哥，就只给弟弟一个泥人不太好。”
“他那么小，给他他也玩不了。算了，再给他一个布老虎。”
胤禔和胤礽你一言我一语，把一大包东西分成几小堆，宫里的高位嫔妃都有份。
胤礽会以他和大阿哥的名义，把这些东西送给宫中众人。
胤礽说，虽然这些东西是我逛街买的，但是大哥分的，所以算我和大哥两人送的。
胤禔认为很有道理。
“明天我们一起戴这个！”胤禔拿起虎头帽子。
这个帽子比胤礽逛街时戴的虎耳帽子更夸张，完全是一个虎头玩偶。
戴上帽子之后，他们的脸从大张的虎口处露出，就像是老虎口中吐出了一个胖娃娃。
“好。”胤礽道，“不知道汗阿玛有没有虎皮袄子，我俩一人一件，就可以扮大老虎。”
胤禔道：“明天去问问汗阿玛。”
他们分完东西之后，缩进同一个被窝里继续聊天。
胤礽先把索额图和明珠的事告诉胤禔。
胤禔感慨：“你家穷亲戚怎么比我还麻烦？至少我家穷亲戚地位不高，不会给我添太大的麻烦。”
胤礽又把常宁“面瘫”的事向胤禔告状。
胤禔冷笑：“仗着自己是长辈为老不尊的家伙，明天我们一起和太皇太后告状！”
当胤礽说起纳兰性德和顾贞观时。
胤禔对纳兰性德不感兴趣。他对顾贞观这个为了友人奔波二十年的人很感兴趣。
“那些什么诗词我听不懂，但讲义气的人，不错。”胤禔还想和胤礽说些什么，胤礽不知不觉呼呼呼睡着了。
胤礽在宫外累了一天，刚才和胤禔聊天的时候就强撑着。
胤禔把奶团子弟弟往怀里拢了拢，下巴垫着奶团子弟弟的头顶发了会儿呆。
胤禔从胤礽或开心或抱怨的分享中，发现了一些让他很困惑的事。
连太子弟弟都知道索额图在败坏自己的名声，汗阿玛为何不阻止索额图？任由索额图败坏太子弟弟的名声？
太子弟弟从未得罪过恭亲王，为何恭亲王对太子弟弟如此厌恶？为何一个亲王对太子如此不敬，汗阿玛却连斥责都没有？
胤禔再次想起身边那些说太子弟弟是大清最尊贵的皇子、是国之储君、是未来皇帝的人。
那些人已经消失了。
额娘说那些人是故意嘴碎，挑拨他对太子弟弟的嫉妒。
嫉妒？
胤禔又把呼呼大睡的奶团子拥紧了一点。
他一点都不嫉妒太子弟弟，只是不理解太子弟弟现在的处境，又因为不理解太子弟弟现在的处境而感到害怕。
或许是大人会考虑许多小孩子不会考虑的事。
如果是他遇到有人欺负太子弟弟，他会直接上拳头。
汗阿玛却会当做什么都没发生。
胤礽：“呼……呼……”
胤禔蹭了蹭怀里比暖炉还温暖的团子弟弟。
额娘说，这些事没那么简单，等自己长大之后就知道了。
长大还有多久？胤禔想着想着，也不由睡着了。
第二日，胤禔先吩咐人把胤礽带回来的东西分送出去，然后指挥小太监们给还在打瞌睡的胤礽洗漱。
胤禔每日天刚亮就要起床读书，已经养成了良好的作息习惯。
但胤礽不行。胤礽只想睡觉。
胤禔一边给胤礽套虎头帽子，一边道：“说好的去给太皇太后请安，顺便告状，你难道想等午膳时再去？”
胤礽打着哈欠抱怨：“可以等午膳后才去啊。”
胤禔道：“不行！我再过几日又得上课，难得的玩耍时间怎么能浪费在睡觉上！”
胤礽小脑袋一点一点，很想说你上课但我不上课。
胤禔一边抱怨一边给胤礽喂饭，胤礽打着瞌睡还能顺利地把饭吃完，并且胸前的小围裙上一滴食物残渣都没有。
胤禔揉了揉胤礽的虎脑袋，夸奖胤礽真乖，然后指挥太监把胤礽抱起来，一起去慈宁宫告状。
惠嫔笑着看胤禔折腾半睡半醒的太子。待两小出门后，惠嫔感慨道：“大阿哥越来越有哥哥的模样了。”
嬷嬷笑道：“大阿哥在太子殿下面前特别成熟。”
惠嫔感慨道：“希望他们俩一直这样。”
惠嫔已经没了让大阿哥争位的心。那么大阿哥和太子关系亲密，就最好不过。
当然，和自家儿子关系亲密的太子能登基，就更好了。
“收拾收拾，今日去宜嫔那逛逛。”惠嫔也换了一身衣服，不乘坐小轿子，娉娉婷婷走着去串门。
她答应大阿哥了，一定要好好养身体，争取活过康熙。
每日串门，便是她散步锻炼身体的时候。
……
胤禔带着胤礽去慈宁宫告状的时候，常宁已经在慈宁宫了。
他知道自己得罪了康熙，忙来慈宁宫搬救兵。
他在太皇太后这里哭一下闹一下，只要不是什么特别大的事，太皇太后都会宠着他。
顺治子嗣稀少，现在还活着的只有福全、康熙、常宁、隆禧。隆禧又是从小到大就病恹恹的，眼见着活不长，常宁便是太皇太后最小的孙子。
太皇太后老了，对孙子特别在意，自然总护着常宁。
不过涉及太子之事，太皇太后可不会偏帮常宁，定是要问个清楚的。
常宁正用春秋笔法告诉太皇太后自己昨日得罪康熙只是误会，胤禔就拉着胤礽气势汹汹地冲了进来。
“你还敢来！你是想恶人先告状？！”胤禔把还在打哈欠的胤礽护在身后，指着常宁道，“不要以为你是叔叔，我就会怕你！”
胤礽被胤禔突然怒气爆发吓得哈欠都断了。
他睁开半眯半醒的眼睛，眼中水雾弥漫。
常宁正想生气，太皇太后却焦急地跑过来，左手揽住胤禔，右手护住胤礽。
“怎么了？大阿哥，慢慢说，乌库妈妈为你们做主。”太皇太后见胤礽居然哭了，立刻怒气攻心。
自家两个曾孙何时如此委屈如此生气过，定是发生了很大的事！
常宁茫然。
等等，他们还什么都没说，怎么就给我定罪了？！
太皇太后你以前不是这样的！
胤礽和胤禔你一言我一语的开始告状。
胤礽：“汗阿玛说叔叔面瘫中风。”
胤禔：“他就是故意甩脸子！我弟弟怎么惹着他了！汗阿玛给他台阶他还不肯下！”
胤礽：“我自己没站稳，没摔。”
胤禔：“什么长辈啊！连小孩子都推！他要脸吗！要是摔伤了他怎么赔！”
胤礽：“就不小心碰了一下，不痛。”
胤禔：“我弟弟这么小这么脆弱，就算他只是不小心打到了也应该道歉！他居然说我弟弟构陷他！他配我弟弟构陷他？！”
常宁怒了：“大阿哥你说什么？！”
胤禔梗着脖子道：“我说什么？我说实话！你自己做了什么还不敢认？”
常宁脸色阴沉：“你别忘了，我是你叔叔！”
“我知道你是我叔叔，所以我才更生气！你作为叔叔不爱护侄子，欺负侄子还告侄子的状！你怎么当叔叔的！”如果不是太皇太后拦着，胤禔都要气得扑上去咬常宁了。
弟弟在外面受了欺负，汗阿玛不给弟弟做主，胤禔找太皇太后做主。
可常宁居然想恶人先告状？这还得了？
“常宁，够了！”太皇太后怒道。
常宁委屈了：“皇玛嬷，我什么性子皇玛嬷还不知道吗？我怎么会故意欺负小孩子？”
太皇太后道：“你什么浑性子我还不知道？！”
常宁：“……”您说得好有道理，但这次我真的是无辜的。
太皇太后冷声道：“你回去反省反省，这几日别出门了。否则皇上生气，哀家必不护着你！”
常宁：“……是。”
太皇太后这样说，已经是护着常宁了。
毕竟她也不能因为常宁对太子甩脸色而惩罚常宁。若这事传出去，常宁本就是个混不吝的性子，众人不会说他什么，但太子的威望会大打折扣。
连皇帝的亲兄弟都不尊重太子，这个太子的地位如何稳固？
太皇太后知道，康熙强忍着不发作，绝对也是因为这个考虑。
但康熙虽然能忍，忍了一时不代表会忍一辈子。康熙定会找其他借口惩罚常宁。
常宁这时候居然还敢进宫和大阿哥吵架，真是欠守陵吗？！
“好了好了，别伤心了，乌库妈妈让他滚。”太皇太后护着两个孩子，让人拿来好吃的好玩的哄孩子。
胤礽揉了揉眼睛，强撑着困意道：“不伤心。谢谢乌库妈妈，谢谢哥哥。”
胤禔抿着嘴，一言不发。
让常宁滚？这不是护着常宁吗？太皇太后你甚至连骂常宁一句都不肯！
可恶！究竟为什么！宫里人还有没有和我一样想护着弟弟的人了！
“太皇太后！德嫔发作了！”
太皇太后正哄孩子的时候，外面有人来报。
太皇太后立刻欣喜道：“德嫔要生了？快，快备轿子。”
胤礽立刻道：“我也去。”
哇哦，那个有名的四弟弟终于要出生了吗？
迟了两三个月出生，四弟弟不再是早产儿，希望他能拉得动四力半以上的弓，噗嗤。
看着胤礽欣喜的表情，胤禔突然福至心灵。
大人们靠不住，那我多拉拢几个弟弟，大家合心合力，不知能不能护得住傻乎乎的太子弟弟？
“我也去！”胤禔立刻道。
三弟那么亲近太子弟弟，其他弟弟一定也一样。
不会有人不喜欢太子弟弟，除了肮脏的大人！
“好，好，一起去。”太皇太后笑道。
她最担心的就是宫中众位皇子们兄弟阋墙。虽然皇子们还小，但这么小就能表现出对兄弟姐妹的期盼，以后感情一定也会很好。
这都是太子这榜样当得好。太皇太后心中叹息，更气常宁了。
那个混蛋孙子再这么作死下去，迟早会被皇帝送去守陵！

chapters.translated_text:
After resting for a while, Kangxi continued to stroll through the temple fair.

Kangxi had a very enjoyable conversation with Nalan Xingde and Gu Zhenguan.

Before long, Yinreng’s eyes began to wander.

He could understand the topics of poetry and literature, but he didn't want to listen. So, he put on an expression that said, "A child doesn't want to participate in adult topics," shook off his father's hand, and walked alongside Fuquan.

Fuquan immediately scooped Yinreng into his arms, casting his emperor brother aside; he was incredibly bold.

Watching the big one and the little one playing wildly, Kangxi shook his head with a helpless smile and let them be.

Kangxi was very curious after hearing what Yinreng had said about the "North-South Party Strife."

However, no matter how curious he was, he felt too embarrassed to press Yinreng for details.

Don't I, as a father, have any face to maintain?

So, Kangxi could only ponder this matter on his own.

Although Nalan Xingde didn't know about the North-South Party Strife either, his circle of guests included many scholars, both from the south and the north. These scholars would always reveal some regional prejudices in their daily interactions. Nalan Xingde was sensitive and remembered the emotional conflicts of those people very clearly.

When Kangxi asked, he explained these matters to him one by one, pondering with Kangxi whether there were deeper meanings behind these superficial conflicts.

As a descendant of the Donglin faction, Gu Zhenguan had been influenced since childhood and understood the intricacies of the literati very well. Whenever Kangxi was unsure, he would ask Gu Zhenguan.

Gu Zhenguan kept wiping away sweat.

If he could, he wouldn't want to answer.

How did the disputes of gentlemen turn into the strife of factions?

How did scholarly debates turn into struggles for profit?

What kind of dark dealings were those moral models, who appeared so bright and upright, hiding behind the scenes?

With local powerful families colluding with high-ranking court officials, how did the figures they put forward as benchmarks build their reputations from a young age?

As a scholar, even if Gu Zhenguan was a true moral model himself, he was unwilling to peel back the polished exterior of the literati.

If this were to get out, he would have no place to stand.

But the person in front of him was the Emperor. When the Emperor asks, can he refuse to answer?

He could choose to die to prove his integrity, but he had finally found hope in saving his friend, and he couldn't implicate him.

Kangxi: Your close friend is in my hands.jpg.

Fortunately, there was Yinreng, the divine baby, who rescued Gu Zhenguan from the fire and water.

Wearing the tiger-ear hat he had just bought, with several strings of bright velvet flowers hanging around his neck, holding a small wooden windmill in his left hand and a rabbit lantern in his right, Yinreng ran up to Kangxi to stop him from continuing to torment Gu Zhenguan.

After running up to Kangxi, he looked at the wooden windmill in his left hand, then at the rabbit lantern in his right, realizing he had no hands left to tug at Kangxi’s sleeve. For some reason, his mind went blank, and he poked Kangxi with the wooden windmill.

When Yinreng ran over, Kangxi stopped chatting and looked down at Yinreng with a smile.

Yinreng poked him with the wooden windmill.

Kangxi remained unmoved.

Yinreng blinked in confusion and poked Kangxi with the rabbit lantern instead.

Kangxi smiled without a word.

Yinreng poked Kangxi alternately with the wooden windmill and the rabbit lantern, until Kangxi picked him up, and they stared at each other with wide eyes.

Kangxi was amused and exasperated: "Baocheng, what are you doing?"

Yinreng: "I have something to tell Father."

Kangxi: "And?"

Yinreng frowned in confusion: "What was I going to say?" He had forgotten while poking him.

Kangxi: "...Silly son, I’m disappointed in you."

Fuquan immediately reached out: "If you're disappointed, give him to me, give him to me! Third brother, let your uncle hold the cute nephew."

Kangxi glanced at Fuquan: "You’ve held him long enough."

He had Nalan Xingde take the small items from Yinreng’s hands, then had Yinreng wrap his arms around his neck and sit comfortably in his arms.

"Did you remember?" Kangxi asked with a smile.

Yinreng’s eyes lit up: "I remembered!"

Kangxi said: "Speak."

Yinreng sighed deeply before saying: "Father, stop bullying Gu Zhenguan. If you keep asking, he will become a traitor to the literati, be attacked by everyone, and perhaps his whole family will be forced to their deaths."

Gu Zhenguan: "..." Your Highness the Crown Prince, you don't have to be so blunt!

Kangxi frowned: "Is it that serious?"

Yinreng nodded: "Villains aren't easily forced to death. Gentlemen are."

Kangxi sighed: "That makes sense. Fine, I’ll ask a few more people. What do you think of Yu Chenglong? I previously thought he was a rare incorruptible official..."

Kangxi gave a sarcastic smile: "The Great Qing’s salaries aren't low; there's no need to abandon one's wife and children and have nothing else to one's name."

Gu Zhenguan: "!!!" Your Majesty, you really are trying to force me to my death!

Yinreng tugged at Kangxi’s fluffy collar: "Father, no one is perfect. If you judge by actions, not by heart, you won't find a single good person. Master Yu Chenglong, whom you and Grandfather always praise, has outstanding political achievements and lives a simple life; that is a fact."

"You're right." Kangxi’s moods came and went quickly.

How could he not know this truth?

The official career for Han officials is difficult; without some unconventional acts to "build a reputation," how would they be noticed?

From the Shunzhi reign to the present, two generations of emperors have been rectifying the administration, and the efforts to do so have been extremely difficult.

Kangxi needed to establish a model of an incorruptible official, and Yu Chenglong could endure the hardship of being that model, so they hit it off.

"How did you get so smart all of a sudden?" Kangxi rubbed the tiger-ear hat Yinreng had just bought.

Yinreng gave Kangxi a disdainful look: "Aren't the words my son just said things Father often says? Is Father praising himself?"

Kangxi laughed heartily, left Nalan Xingde and Gu Zhenguan behind, and continued to play with his son.

Fuquan followed behind, looking very dejected.

He hadn't played with his nephew the Crown Prince for long; how could his emperor brother snatch him away again?

Nalan Xingde and Gu Zhenguan exchanged a look, their eyes filled with amazement at the Crown Prince’s actions.

There have been many child prodigies since ancient times; many scholars could write poetry at three and brilliant essays at five.

Not to mention that the current Emperor was also a "child prodigy," already showing the signs of an enlightened ruler when he ascended the throne at eight.

The Crown Prince was nearly five; his extraordinary intelligence was not surprising. What was surprising was his grasp of human nature hidden within his childish words.

This kind of worldly wisdom requires experience and talent; some people never learn it in a lifetime.

With such a Crown Prince, as long as he doesn't die young, the country is guaranteed two generations of peace and prosperity.

Gu Zhenguan was a Han Chinese. The Han people already accepted the Crown Prince, so naturally, Gu Zhenguan could only be happy.

Nalan Xingde, however, felt conflicted and anxious.

He approved of the Crown Prince, but his family stood on the opposite side. The tug-of-war in his mind made Nalan Xingde’s head ache severely.

While Yinreng and Kangxi were laughing and playing, he caught sight of Nalan Xingde, who was frowning and rubbing his temples. He patted Kangxi’s face and pointed at Nalan Xingde.

Kangxi misunderstood: "What? Are you dazzled by Rongruo’s 'sickly beauty' state?"

The sickly beauty Nalan Xingde: "..." Your Majesty, that’s enough!

Yinreng was shocked: "Father, shouldn't you be concerned about Guard Nalan’s health!"

Kangxi: "..."

Kangxi pressed Yinreng’s little head into his chest and said with a normal expression: "What? A headache from too much wind? You’re a guard, how can you be so weak?"

Yinreng, with his head buried in Kangxi’s chest, said muffledly: "Father, Father, it’s about care and concern, not nagging and scolding."

Kangxi pressed Yinreng’s head a little tighter, and Yinreng went silent.

Nalan Xingde laughed: "Third Master, this official just caught a draft after drinking; it’s nothing."

Yinreng pulled his little head out of Kangxi’s chest, the two tiger ears on top of his head shaking vigorously due to his movements.

"Drink less, drinking hurts the body." Yinreng shook his head like an old man, the tiger ears continuing to sway with his movements, "Good health is the capital for achieving all ideals; without health, there is nothing."

This was definitely a complaint from Yinreng’s grandfather. Kangxi chuckled.

Wasn't Shunzhi the one who died before his ambitions were realized?

Nalan Xingde was stunned, then smiled: "The little young master is right."

Yinreng beckoned to Nalan Xingde, and under Kangxi’s signal, Nalan Xingde leaned his head over.

Yinreng tried his best to lean out, stretching out his two warm, fleshy little hands to cover Nalan Xingde’s temples.

"Rub, rub, blow, blow, let the pain fly away." I'll soak up some of Nalan Xingde’s scholarly aura, and then go rub it onto the eldest brother who gets a headache from studying every day. Yinreng thought happily.

Nalan Xingde felt the softness and warmth on his face, his expression slightly stunned.

"Ahem." Kangxi was jealous.

What to do if my son is too gentle? Although I’m proud, I don't want my son to be this gentle with others.

Nalan Xingde came back to his senses and hurriedly thanked Yinreng.

Yinreng smiled and rubbed the jealous Kangxi’s temples as well.

Kangxi was happy. Fuquan reached out to Yinreng: Uncle wants some too, Uncle wants some too!

Kangxi: "No, you don't."

He strode away with his long legs, holding his son.

Fuquan trotted behind Kangxi: "Just a little bit."

Kangxi: "No."

Nalan Xingde, trailing a few steps behind, touched his own temples.

Gu Zhenguan sighed: "His Highness the Crown Prince is truly..."

Gu Zhenguan thought for a long time, not knowing how to evaluate this Crown Prince of the Great Qing.

One could only say that anyone who sees this Crown Prince of the Great Qing would surely think, "How wonderful it would be if he were my son."

Fuquan: Yes, that's right, I want to take him home.jpg.

...

Before the palace gates were locked, Kangxi returned to the palace with Yinreng, who was loaded with gifts.

Kangxi had played all day, so he had to process palace affairs by candlelight at night.

Yinreng had the attendants carry the bags and went to find Yinzhi to sleep.

Yinzhi knew Yinreng was going out of the palace today and felt a bit sour.

He wanted to go out too.

But this sourness disappeared when Yinreng came to him with his bags, ready to sleep in the same bed.

My brother really loves me!

Yinzhi and Yinreng sat on the large, soft couch to divide the items.

"This velvet flower is for Mother. This one is for the Empress Dowager."

"Brother, what about the Empress Dowager?"

"Ah, I forgot about the Empress Dowager."

"Which one is for the younger brother?"

"This one."

"Brother, it’s not good to only give the younger brother a clay figurine."

"He’s so small, he can't play with it anyway. Forget it, give him a cloth tiger too."

Yinzhi and Yinreng talked back and forth, dividing the large bag of items into several small piles; all the high-ranking concubines in the palace had a share.

Yinreng would give these things to everyone in the palace in his and the eldest brother’s name.

Yinreng said that although he bought these things while shopping, the eldest brother divided them, so they counted as gifts from both of them.

Yinzhi thought that made perfect sense.

"Tomorrow we’ll wear these together!" Yinzhi picked up the tiger-head hat.

This hat was even more exaggerated than the tiger-ear hat Yinreng wore while shopping; it was a full tiger-head doll.

After putting on the hat, their faces appeared from the tiger’s wide-open mouth, looking like a chubby baby spat out by a tiger.

"Okay," Yinreng said, "I wonder if Father has tiger-skin coats; if we each had one, we could pretend to be big tigers."

Yinzhi said: "Let’s ask Father tomorrow."

After they finished dividing the items, they curled up in the same quilt and continued chatting.

Yinreng first told Yinzhi about Songgotu and Mingju.

Yinzhi sighed: "Why are your poor relatives even more troublesome than mine? At least my poor relatives don't have high status and won't cause me too much trouble."

Yinreng then complained to Yinzhi about Changning’s "poker face."

Yinzhi sneered: "A guy who relies on being an elder to act disrespectfully; tomorrow we’ll go complain to the Empress Dowager together!"

When Yinreng mentioned Nalan Xingde and Gu Zhenguan.

Yinzhi wasn't interested in Nalan Xingde. He was very interested in Gu Zhenguan, who had been running around for his friend for twenty years.

"I don't understand those poems, but someone who is loyal is not bad." Yinzhi wanted to say more to Yinreng, but Yinreng had fallen fast asleep before he knew it.

Yinreng had been tired all day outside the palace and had been forcing himself to stay awake while chatting with Yinzhi.

Yinzhi pulled his little milk-bun brother closer into his arms and rested his chin on the top of his head, lost in thought for a while.

From Yinreng’s happy or complaining shares, Yinzhi discovered some things that puzzled him.

Even the Crown Prince brother knows that Songgotu is ruining his reputation, so why doesn't Father stop Songgotu? Why let Songgotu ruin the Crown Prince brother’s reputation?

The Crown Prince brother has never offended Prince Gong, so why does Prince Gong dislike him so much? Why is a Prince so disrespectful to the Crown Prince, yet Father doesn't even scold him?

Yinzhi remembered again those people around him who said the Crown Prince brother was the most noble prince of the Great Qing, the heir to the country, and the future emperor.

Those people had already disappeared.

Mother said those people were intentionally gossiping to provoke his jealousy of the Crown Prince brother.

Jealousy?

Yinzhi hugged the fast-asleep milk-bun even tighter.

He wasn't jealous of the Crown Prince brother at all; he just didn't understand the Crown Prince brother’s current situation, and he felt afraid because he didn't understand it.

Perhaps adults consider many things that children don't.

If he encountered someone bullying the Crown Prince brother, he would use his fists directly.

But Father would act as if nothing had happened.

Yinreng: "Hoo... hoo..."

Yinzhi rubbed against the milk-bun brother who was warmer than a heater.

Mother said these things aren't that simple, and he would understand when he grew up.

How long until he grows up? Yinzhi thought, and he couldn't help but fall asleep too.

The next day, Yinzhi first ordered people to send out the things Yinreng brought back, then directed the little eunuchs to wash and dress Yinreng, who was still dozing off.

Yinzhi had to get up to study at dawn every day and had developed good habits.

But Yinreng couldn't. Yinreng just wanted to sleep.

While putting the tiger-head hat on Yinreng, Yinzhi said: "We agreed to pay our respects to the Empress Dowager and complain, do you want to wait until lunch?"

Yinreng yawned and complained: "We can wait until after lunch."

Yinzhi said: "No! I have to go to class in a few days; how can I waste rare playtime on sleeping!"

Yinreng’s little head bobbed, wanting to say that you have class but I don't.

Yinzhi fed Yinreng while complaining; Yinreng could finish his meal smoothly while dozing, and there wasn't a single scrap of food on his little apron.

Yinzhi rubbed Yinreng’s tiger head, praised him for being good, and then ordered the eunuchs to carry Yinreng so they could go to the Cining Palace to complain.

Consort Hui watched with a smile as Yinzhi fussed over the half-asleep Crown Prince. After the two left, she sighed: "The eldest prince is becoming more and more like a big brother."

The nanny laughed: "The eldest prince is especially mature in front of His Highness the Crown Prince."

Consort Hui sighed: "I hope they stay like this forever."

Consort Hui no longer had the heart to let the eldest prince fight for the throne. If the eldest prince and the Crown Prince were close, that would be for the best.

Of course, it would be even better if the Crown Prince, who was close to her son, could ascend the throne.

"Clean up, let’s go visit Consort Yi today." Consort Hui also changed her clothes and, instead of taking a small sedan chair, walked gracefully to visit.

She had promised the eldest prince that she would take good care of her health and try to outlive Kangxi.

Visiting every day was her way of walking and exercising.

...

When Yinzhi brought Yinreng to the Cining Palace to complain, Changning was already there.

He knew he had offended Kangxi and hurried to the Cining Palace to bring in reinforcements.

He would cry and make a scene in front of the Empress Dowager, and as long as it wasn't anything too major, she would indulge him.

Shunzhi had few heirs, and only Fuquan, Kangxi, Changning, and Longxi were still alive. Longxi had been sickly since childhood and didn't look like he would live long, so Changning was the Empress Dowager’s youngest grandson.

The Empress Dowager was old and cared especially for her grandsons, so she naturally always protected Changning.

However, when it came to the Crown Prince, the Empress Dowager wouldn't favor Changning; she would definitely get to the bottom of it.

Changning was just using flowery language to tell the Empress Dowager that offending Kangxi yesterday was just a misunderstanding, when Yinzhi dragged Yinreng in, looking aggressive.

"You still dare to come! Are you trying to accuse the victim first?!" Yinzhi protected the still-yawning Yinreng behind him and pointed at Changning: "Don't think that just because you're an uncle, I’ll be afraid of you!"

Yinreng was so startled by Yinzhi’s sudden outburst that his yawn was cut short.

He opened his half-awake eyes, which were filled with mist.

Changning was about to get angry, but the Empress Dowager ran over anxiously, holding Yinzhi with her left hand and protecting Yinreng with her right.

"What’s wrong? Eldest Prince, tell me slowly, Grandmother will stand up for you." Seeing that Yinreng was actually crying, the Empress Dowager was immediately furious.

When had her two great-grandsons ever been so wronged and so angry? Something major must have happened!

Changning was bewildered.

Wait, they haven't said anything yet, how did you convict me?!

Empress Dowager, you weren't like this before!

Yinreng and Yinzhi started complaining one after another.

Yinreng: "Father said Uncle has a poker face and a stroke."

Yinzhi: "He was intentionally giving us a cold shoulder! How did my brother provoke him! Father gave him a way out, and he still refused to take it!"

Yinreng: "I didn't stand steady, I didn't fall."

Yinzhi: "What kind of elder is he! Even pushing a child! Does he have any shame! If he had been injured, how would he compensate!"

Yinreng: "I just bumped into him by accident, it doesn't hurt."

Yinzhi: "My brother is so small and fragile; even if he just hit him by accident, he should apologize! He actually said my brother framed him! Is he worthy of my brother framing him?!"

Changning was furious: "Eldest Prince, what are you saying?!"

Yinzhi stiffened his neck and said: "What am I saying? I’m telling the truth! You did it yourself and don't dare to admit it?"

Changning’s face was gloomy: "Don't forget, I am your uncle!"

"I know you’re my uncle, that’s why I’m even angrier! As an uncle, you don't care for your nephew, you bully him and then complain about him! What kind of uncle are you!" If the Empress Dowager hadn't stopped him, Yinzhi would have been so angry he would have pounced on Changning to bite him.

His brother was bullied outside, and Father wouldn't stand up for him, so Yinzhi went to the Empress Dowager.

But Changning actually wanted to accuse the victim first? How could this be allowed?

"Changning, that’s enough!" The Empress Dowager said angrily.

Changning felt wronged: "Imperial Grandmother, don't you know my temperament? How could I intentionally bully a child?"

The Empress Dowager said: "Don't I know what kind of reckless temperament you have?!"

Changning: "..." What you said makes perfect sense, but this time I really am innocent.

The Empress Dowager said coldly: "Go back and reflect; don't go out for the next few days. Otherwise, if the Emperor gets angry, I certainly won't protect you!"

Changning: "...Yes."

The Empress Dowager saying this was already protecting Changning.

After all, she couldn't punish Changning just because he gave the Crown Prince a cold shoulder. If this got out, Changning was already known for his reckless nature, so people wouldn't say much about him, but the Crown Prince’s prestige would be greatly damaged.

If even the Emperor’s own brother didn't respect the Crown Prince, how could the Crown Prince’s position be stable?

The Empress Dowager knew that Kangxi was holding back his anger for this very reason.

But although Kangxi could endure it, enduring it for a moment didn't mean he would endure it for a lifetime. Kangxi would definitely find other excuses to punish Changning.

Changning actually dared to enter the palace and argue with the Eldest Prince at this time; was he really asking to be sent to guard the tombs?!

"Alright, alright, don't be sad, Grandmother will tell him to get out." The Empress Dowager protected the two children and had people bring delicious food and toys to coax them.

Yinreng rubbed his eyes and forced himself to stay awake: "Not sad. Thank you, Grandmother, thank you, Brother."

Yinzhi pursed his lips and said nothing.

Tell Changning to get out? Isn't that protecting him? Empress Dowager, you won't even scold Changning!

Damn it! Why! Is there anyone else in the palace who wants to protect my brother like I do!

"Empress Dowager! Consort De is in labor!"

While the Empress Dowager was coaxing the children, someone came to report from outside.

The Empress Dowager immediately said happily: "Consort De is giving birth? Quick, quick, prepare the sedan chair."

Yinreng immediately said: "I want to go too."

Wow, is that famous fourth brother finally going to be born?

Born two or three months late, the fourth brother won't be a premature baby anymore; I hope he can pull a bow of more than four and a half strength, pfft.

Looking at Yinreng’s happy expression, Yinzhi suddenly had a flash of inspiration.

Adults can't be relied upon, so I’ll win over a few more brothers; if everyone works together, I wonder if we can protect the silly Crown Prince brother?

"I want to go too!" Yinzhi said immediately.

The third brother is so close to the Crown Prince brother, the other brothers must be the same.

No one would dislike the Crown Prince brother, except for the dirty adults!

"Okay, okay, let’s go together." The Empress Dowager smiled.

What she worried about most was the princes in the palace fighting among themselves. Although they were still young, being able to show such anticipation for their siblings at such a young age meant they would definitely have a good relationship in the future.

This was all because the Crown Prince set a good example. The Empress Dowager sighed in her heart and was even angrier at Changning.

If that bastard grandson keeps acting like this, he will be sent by the Emperor to guard the tombs sooner or later!

100,000

chapters.title: 第 30 章 [V]
chapters.source_text:
对大部分女性而言，头胎都有些艰难。
德嫔这一胎虽然安稳，也得折腾一段时间。
太皇太后在偏殿里等着，胤礽靠着胤禔打瞌睡，胤禔就有些无聊了。
他现在的年龄正好是坐不住的时候。
胤禔的屁股在凳子上磨啊磨，就跟被强迫按凳子上的猴子似的。
太皇太后看着有趣，也不主动问他胤禔无聊不无聊，就等着胤禔自己说。
胤禔快忍不住的时候，胤礽揉了揉眼睛，给胤禔解围。
“哥哥，我困，陪我去旁边睡一会儿好不好？”胤礽带着鼻音的困顿声音软绵绵黏糊糊。
胤禔立刻从凳子上跳下来，牵着胤礽问道：“有可供我们休息的地方吗？”
太皇太后使了一个眼色，苏麻喇姑立刻从准备赏给德嫔的绫罗绸缎中拿了几匹出来，给胤礽在偏殿小暖阁铺床。
那小暖阁本是给德嫔还未出生的小皇子小公主准备的地方，还未有人睡过，太子先去休息也没关系。
胤禔和胤礽来到小暖阁之后，胤礽让小太监拿出一叠扑克牌，打着哈欠道：“哥哥，我们打牌吧。”
胤禔点了一下胤礽的脑门：“你困就去睡，不用强撑着陪我。”
胤礽又让小太监拿出一本书：“那我给你讲故事吧？这次讲《孙子三十六计》，哥哥你最喜欢的兵法。”
“这个好！”胤禔眼睛一亮，然后握拳放嘴边干咳一声，“都说了不用了，快睡。”
“我这个时候也该起了。”胤礽揉了揉眼睛，又用胤禔的袖子擦了擦脸。
胤禔嫌弃地把胤礽护怀里，指挥小太监打了一盆水给胤礽洗脸醒瞌睡。
胤礽皮肤薄，洗脸之后还要擦一些护肤的油脂。
小太监立刻又拿出一盒羊脂膏。
胤禔一边帮胤礽擦脸，一边好奇道：“这个小太监是谁？看着眼生，做事倒挺周全。”
胤礽看了那小太监一眼，道：“他叫梁九功，是汗阿玛身边的人。”
“伺候你的人都是汗阿玛身边的人。”胤禔淡淡道，“他做事这么周全，我帮你问汗阿玛把他要过来。你身边的人老换也不是个事，根本不体贴。”
只有一直在身边伺候的老人才能和主子爷们养成默契，主子爷一个眼神就知道该做什么不该做什么。
就胤礽身边那些一月一换的侍从，胤礽不开口他们绝对不会动弹。
凡事都要主子爷先开口才做事的侍从，能伺候好人？胤禔不满很久了。
“没关系，汗阿玛有自己的考量。”胤礽忙拉了拉胤禔的衣角，示意他别说这个。
胤禔眼神一暗，嘴角勾起笑容道：“也是。汗阿玛肯定还没给你选到好的，选到好的就不会给你换了。”
“嗯。”胤礽摸了摸脸，又摸了摸胤禔的脸，“哥哥，你的脸也干了，我给你擦。”
胤禔低下头，让胤礽给他擦脸。
两孩子的童言稚语没有引起太监们的注意。
他们虽然会把孩子们的话传递给康熙，也不是什么话都会传，只会传一些比较重要的话。
只有梁九功嘴唇抿了抿，似乎意识到了什么。
胤禔的眼刀子很快就扫了过来，梁九功立刻垂下头，不敢深想。
他现在只是一个刚入宫一两年的小太监，装糊涂才能活下去。太子的事，自有位置更高的太监报上去。
胤礽将一切看在眼里，心里叹气。
梁九功能成为赵昌的继承人，爬到乾清宫太监总管的位置，果然有两把刷子。
上上辈子梁九功没跟过胤礽。
这辈子胤礽在和康熙胡闹的时候，听见旁边一个十几岁的小太监名字叫梁九功，本能的因为好奇多看了几眼。
梁九功当乾清宫太监总管的时候，正好是九龙夺嫡时。他在清朝文学作品中出场率极高。
上上辈子，梁九功和赵昌一样，只忠于康熙。
梁九功于康熙五十一年卷入九龙夺嫡中，康熙将其拘禁起来后，还多次下旨为他请御医，试图救其一命。
可惜，这样只忠于先帝的心腹太监，是注定会给康熙“殉葬”的。
赵昌被杀，梁九功自缢。只有站队的魏珠免于一死，比雍正命长，被乾隆从拘禁中放出来，给乾隆当了太监总管。
说起魏珠，他这时候还没出生呢。
胤礽感慨之后，就在人群中多看了梁九功几眼。
就这么多看的几眼，康熙便把梁九功送给胤礽用了。
胤礽心里那个囧啊，颇觉得有点对不起梁九功。
上上辈子康熙指着梁九功骂自己身边的人，说选人要选得和梁九功一样好用。
现在梁九功直接跟着自己了？
梁九功确实聪明伶俐，让人挑不出错。所以别人一月一换，他都在自己身边待了好几个月了。
不会吧不会吧，梁九功的乾清宫太监总管位置不会被自己蝴蝶了吧？
伺候太子的内侍之后都会被康熙砍了，还会砍好几轮。梁九功不会提前凉了吧？
我只是在人群中多看了他几眼而已！
老天保佑梁九功，让他早日回到阿玛身边，别被我带累死了。胤礽在心里叹气。
但有一说一，梁九功真的太好用了。
除了越来越忙，现在只偶尔来照顾自己的顾太监，梁九功是唯一一个不需要胤礽说话，便把事情打理得井井有条的人。
也可能梁九功干一行爱一行，不像其他内侍多一事不如少一事吧。
“你们不用陪在这里，退暖阁外面去。”胤礽吩咐道，“梁九功，你留下伺候。”
他身边只留梁九功一人伺候，康熙问起他的事时，梁九功就有机会面圣。
对胤礽好的人，胤礽都会下意识的帮一帮。
“是。”胤礽身边伺候的人虽然不伶俐，但很听话。
胤禔也遣走伺候的人，只留下一个最得用的太监。
胤礽翻开书本，开始给胤禔讲故事。
书本中是文言文，胤礽讲出来的是大白话。
胤禔就爱听胤礽讲的大白话故事。他又不去考科举，听那些文文绉绉的话干什么？
胤礽的大白话故事绘声绘色，一小段文字他能编出很大一串，还能举出许多类似的故事来佐证。
别说胤禔听得津津有味，梁九功和胤禔身边的太监也不由听得入了迷。
胤礽这讲故事的功力，去当说书人一定是头牌。
太皇太后操心胤礽和胤禔，过来看了一眼。
在门口听到胤礽讲故事之后，太皇太后不由驻足，竖着耳朵听了许久。
然后她笑着摇摇头，回到了偏殿中，不去打扰太子给大阿哥讲故事。
有长辈在，两个孩子恐怕不会自在。
德嫔这一胎，折腾了大半日都没生出来。
不过德嫔早就厚着脸皮向惠嫔、荣嫔这两位生过孩子的妃嫔请教过，一直咬牙不哭不闹，就等着把力气留到孩子快出生的时候。所以她这一胎出生的时候很顺利。
在把孩子憋出来之前，德嫔还挣扎着爬起来喝了一碗肉粥。
太皇太后得知这件事之后，都忍不住笑了。
胤礽、胤禔和太皇太后一起在偏殿用了一顿午膳，又小眯了一会儿，德嫔终于把孩子生了出来。
德嫔生了一个十分健康的小阿哥，一出生就哭声震天，据说比大阿哥出生时还虎。
胤禔歪头。
虎？
老虎挺威猛的，这一定是个好词。
“我看他和我也挺像。”胤禔背着手看着红红胖胖的四弟，违心道，“我喜欢他，以后我教他骑马射箭。”
弟弟要从小培养，才能联合起来一起对抗汗阿玛。
胤礽笑道：“哥哥教他骑马射箭，我教他读书写字。”
德嫔大概是生孩子之前吃得太好，生完孩子也没晕。她清醒着听着嬷嬷回报的大阿哥和太子说的话，疲惫的脸上露出了笑容，终于放心沉沉睡去。
太皇太后很开心，大赏德嫔身边的人。
胤礽当即打开他阿玛的库房，替他阿玛赏赐德嫔。
而孩子他爹康熙呢？
康熙正在补觉。
他熬夜批改折子，早晨又强撑着和大臣们商议事情。德嫔生孩子的时候，他正睡得舒坦，谁也不敢打扰他。
康熙的孩子们出生的时候他基本没去看过，就事后给个赏赐。能让康熙守着出生的孩子，除了皇后生的，便是康熙当时正好闲着。
所以康熙没来，宫中嫔妃也不在意，没人认为德嫔这一胎不受康熙重视。
何况无论皇子重视不重视，只要能活下来，都是妃嫔们的希望。
……
康熙睡到晚上才起来，起来之后问了一句太子在哪，把太子拎来陪他吃了晚上加餐后，才问德嫔所生的孩子的事。
康熙听闻德嫔生了一个大胖小子很高兴：“赏！”
胤礽无奈：“大半夜的，就别去打扰德嫔和弟弟了。我白日用阿玛的名义赏了些东西，阿玛看看还要添些什么，明日添。”
康熙尴尬地摸了摸鼻子。
哦，对啊，现在已经是晚上了。
康熙看了一眼胤礽帮他赏赐的清单，不多不少都是常例。
“你太小心了，多给点也没关系。”康熙笑着加了一批东西。
胤礽给了他阿玛一个白眼：“我加什么啊？太子给生孩子的嫔妃加赏赐？阿玛你不觉得不对劲吗？”
康熙：“……好像是有一点。”
旁边伺候的太监听得心惊胆战。
太子真是……什么话都敢说。皇帝不生气，他们听着也觉得汗毛倒竖啊。
康熙为了调整作息，晚上不困也抱着儿子睡了。
听着儿子均匀的呼吸声，康熙很快就再次进入梦乡。
第二日，他处理完政务之后，拎着儿子去看望了德嫔。
德嫔要坐月子，康熙只在门口问候了几句，就带着儿子去玩小儿子。
才第二天，四阿哥的皮肤就展开了不少，看着有一点点可爱了。
康熙赞叹：“这小子真的比保清还虎头虎脑！”
胤礽表情复杂的点点头。
他有点担心这辈子的四弟未来的画风了。
众所周知，未来的雍正皇帝本性并不是个闷葫芦，而是一个性格极端且超级话痨的人。
很多人说，雍正这极端和话痨，是在九龙夺嫡的时候憋坏了。
胤禛自孝懿仁皇后去世之后，就没有个真心对待他的人。
文学作品中说胤禛小时候因为九阿哥胤禟剃了他养的狗的狗毛，剪了胤禟的小辫子，才得到“戒急用忍”四个字，当然没这回事。
因为那时候孝懿仁皇后已经去世，不受德妃待见的胤禛，不可能去招惹宠妃之子。
胤禛为了自保，一直强忍着自己的脾气，几乎不和兄弟们起冲突。实在憋不住了，才吼几句。
一直隐忍的人突然暴躁，不会让人反思自己的行为是不是过分，而是会让人生出“之前你都没生气，现在生什么气？你是不是有病？”的想法。
连康熙也认为这孩子喜怒不定，给了胤禛“戒急用忍”四个字。
胤礽想想就觉得好笑，笑着笑着又觉得好悲哀。
胤禛从此以后就变成了闷葫芦，成了隐形人，在他继位之前，所有皇子都没把他放在眼中。
所以胤禛继位之后，所有人仍旧没把他当一回事，德妃都不信他有本事当皇帝，支持胤禩的人也才会继续蹦跶。
胤礽戳了戳还未取名的四阿哥胖乎乎的小脸。
四阿哥攥紧了小拳头，翘着脚丫呼呼大睡，好像随时都会出拳似的。
这辈子的胤禛不再先天体弱。拥有了亲额娘的爱，还有大哥和我的照顾，他会变成什么样子？
胤礽想起前前世的小霸王十四。
嗯，以胤禛本性里的小暴脾气，恐怕比十四还霸道。
胤礽脑海里浮现出胤禛攥紧拳头要扑上去揍人，他左腿挂着十三，右腿挂着十四，两个弟弟都含着眼泪劝，四哥算了算了，不至于不至于。
嗯，胤礽等不及看到这一幕了。
“怎么高兴成这样？朕叫你你都不应？”康熙酸溜溜道。胤礽每次都有了哥哥弟弟便不顾阿玛了。
“大哥说四弟弟像他。”胤礽笑眯眯道，“阿玛，等四弟弟长大之后，一定很有意思。”
康熙表情一僵。
别说了别说了，脑袋已经开始疼了。
一个大儿子已经让朕天天怀疑人生，再来一个大儿子翻版，朕怕不是会被他们气死！
康熙脑海里浮现出两张大阿哥背着手仰着头写满怀疑二字的脸。
“真的吗？我不信。”
“汗阿玛你就是嫉妒我。”
“汗阿玛放心忙，弟弟是我的。”
“就这就这？汗阿玛你还不如我。”
独唱变成了二重奏，在康熙脑海中三百六十度轮番播放。
康熙捂住胸口。
呼吸已经困难了！
“不至于，你好好看着四阿哥，别让他和保清学！”康熙严肃道。
他不阻止儿子亲近四阿哥了！四阿哥一定要变成保成第二，不能变成保清第二！
“汗阿玛，为什么不让弟弟和我学？”康熙身后响起一个洪亮的声音，“我这么优秀。”
康熙抹了一把脸，回头看着先呛了他一句后，才行礼的胤禔。
“你怎么来了？”康熙板着脸道。
胤禔举着手中的小弓箭小木刀：“我来给小四送东西。太子弟弟说，爱好要从小培养。”
康熙：“……”他这时候应该夸奖胤禔爱护弟弟，但他就是夸不出口。
这时候，四阿哥正好睁开了眼睛。
他的视线还不清楚，本能地转悠着眼珠子四处瞅瞅。
胤禔立刻把没开刃的小木刀塞进了四阿哥怀里。
四阿哥条件反射抱住小木刀。
“看，弟弟很喜欢！”胤禔得意道，“他果然和我很像！”
康熙：“……”别说了别说了，已经在想办法把你和小儿子隔开了。
胤礽忍笑：“弟弟还小，需要充足睡眠。大哥，咱们还是去找三弟弟玩吧？”
“好。”胤禔把带来的武器小玩具交给四阿哥的奶嬷嬷，牵着胤礽的手告辞，“汗阿玛再见。哦，再见是后会有期的意思。”
康熙虎着脸道：“朕让你们走了吗？！”
胤禔疑惑：“汗阿玛，催您去前庭的太监已经等很久了，您要翘班？翘班是不去做该做的事的意思。”
康熙：“……你哪来那么多奇奇怪怪的词？”
胤礽举起没被胤禔牵着的那只手：“汗阿玛，我教的。”
康熙：“……”你玛法究竟教了你什么奇怪的东西？！我两个儿子都被教坏了！
“去吧去吧。”康熙无奈摆手。
他能怎么办？是不去工作还是不让儿子们一起玩？
康熙离开前，深深看了四儿子一眼。
你一定不能像保清！
又过了一天，康熙给皇四子取名为“胤禛”。
禛，以至诚感动神灵而得福佑也。
孩子容易夭折，所以出生后若非特别受重视，不会立刻取名。
皇四子才出生几天就有了名字，宫中人看着永和宫的方向，心中酸极了。
只有胤禔提出了异议：“禛？这个字怎么读？慎？”
“不是，是同真音。”胤礽道。
胤禔道：“我还以为汗阿玛非常不满小四像我，所以给他取名为慎，希望他以后小心谨慎，变成和我完全不同的人。”
胤礽无语：“大哥，你也知道你一点都不小心谨慎……汗阿玛不至于这样，你想多了。”
胤禔皱眉：“真的？我怎么觉得我想的才是真相。”
胤礽使劲摇头：“不至于不至于。”
胤禔抬脚：“我去问问！”
胤礽赶紧抱住胤禔的腰：“别去别去，是不是你都会挨揍。”
已经会走路的胤祉看了看两个哥哥，也学着胤礽扑上去，抱住胤禔一条腿：“别去，挨揍！”
胤禔身上挂着两弟弟，还坚持一步一步往前挪动：“不行，不问清楚，我心里不舒坦！”
于是胤礽和胤祉阻拦无效。胤禔明明那么惧怕康熙，却抖着腿也要头铁地问出这个找死的问题。
康熙那个表情，让胤礽回味了许久。
因为康熙表情太复杂，胤礽都有点怀疑，大哥不会误打误撞说对了吧？
应该不至于。阿玛没有那么孩子气。
而且大哥人这么好，胤禛像大哥怎么了？挺好啊。
“滚！”康熙咬牙切齿的砸过去一个茶杯。
他砸的时候故意偏了一下，就只砸在自己面前，不会伤到孩子。
胤禔这才感到害怕，连滚带爬地溜了。
康熙手指头按着突突突直跳的太阳穴，想罚胤禔又找不到借口。
最终，他只能以赏赐的名义欺负胤禔，给胤禔送了许多名家字帖。
胤禔的字好棒棒，赶紧多写点给汗阿玛看，汗阿玛最喜欢看胤禔写的字了。——口谕是这么说的。
胤禔欲哭无泪：“额娘，汗阿玛这绝对是在罚我。”
惠嫔差点又被胤禔气哭了：“你既然知道，为何要去气、皇上？”
胤禔挺起胸脯：“我就是想到了问题，没答案心里难受。”
惠嫔：“……”我该拿我儿子怎么办？！回炉重造还来得及吗？！
“你以后……少去看四阿哥。”惠嫔虚弱道。
胤禔笑道：“不，我应该更频繁的去看四阿哥。”
惠嫔愣了一下，然后她轻轻地叹了一口气：“说得是。大阿哥，你真的长大了啊。”
胤禔点头：“要快点长大。”才能保护弟弟。
他想起太子弟弟私底下悄悄对他说，“梁九功很好，所以不能让他留在我身边”的话，阻止他向汗阿玛帮太子弟弟索要梁九功。
他以前头疼太子弟弟太傻，现在心疼太子弟弟太聪明。
“额娘，我过得真是太好了。”胤禔拱进惠嫔怀里，喃喃道。
惠嫔温柔地拍了拍胤禔的背：“怎么突然说这个？”
胤禔道：“太子弟弟身边没有一个他熟悉的人。他若不说话，连个看他口渴了主动倒水给他喝的人都没有。”
惠嫔抿了抿嘴，轻轻地叹了一口气：“皇上自有他的考量。你长大了就知道了。”
“嗯。”胤禔蹭了蹭他的额娘。
他难过了迷惑了，可以依靠额娘。
太子弟弟呢？
……
“阿玛，我有个问题。”胤礽趴在康熙怀里，坏笑着扬起头。
“不准问。”康熙把胤礽的脑袋按下去。
胤礽在康熙怀里滚来滚去：“就要问，就要问。大哥不会猜对了吧？哈哈哈哈，阿玛你好幼稚啊……哎哟！”
康熙恼羞成怒：“闭嘴！”
“哈哈哈，我要把这件事告诉乌库妈妈。”
“不准说！”
“哈哈哈《起居录》会记载吗？”
“他们敢！”
康熙把胆敢嘲笑自己的小团子抱起来使劲揉搓：“你怎么也会和保清越来越像了？就不该让你和保清走得太近！”
胤礽做鬼脸：“略略略，为什么不是大哥越来越像我？”
康熙：“……”
他突然发现，居然无法反驳。
儿子在外人面前可乖可甜，在自己面前上蹿下跳比保清皮多了。
该不会真的是儿子把保清带得更坏了？康熙开始怀疑自己的教育。
‎
