纳兰性德和曹寅心里都特别遗憾。
曹寅至今没孩子，抱着小太子的时候……咳，他很大逆不道的拥有了一丝丝作为父亲的开心。
纳兰性德因小太子活泼可爱，终于开始接纳亡妻的孩子，也开始悉心教导庶长子。两个孩子都还小，虽然纳兰性德以前对他们较为冷淡，小孩子不记仇，很快就与纳兰性德亲近起来。可纳兰性德还是觉得孩子还是别人家好，挺馋小太子，很想多与小太子亲近，再回去摸摸自家孩子，把小太子的聪明劲分享给自己的孩子们。
现在大阿哥剥夺了他们接过这个差事后唯一的开心，还瞪了他们一眼，好像他们是坏人似的。
胤禔低头凑矮墩墩弟弟耳边道：“他们看着你的眼神很不对，像是想把你抢回家！你小心点！”
“我是太子，他们不敢。”胤礽小声道。
胤禔“哼”了一声：“不敢是一回事，想是另一回事。想也不行。”
说完，他又瞪了纳兰性德和曹寅一眼。
胤禔的嗓门和曹寅有的一拼。他自以为的窃窃私语，纳兰性德和曹寅都听见了。
他们俩嘴角扯了扯，除了装作没听见，还能怎么办？总不能跪下请罪辩解说他们绝对没有不好的心思？
那就此地无银三百两了。
纳兰性德和曹寅心好累。
噶布喇和常泰翘首以盼，大老远就看到了一大一小两只团子携手哒哒哒走来。
在阳光下，穿得珠光宝气的一大一小两只团子耀眼夺目，闪花了噶布喇和常泰的眼睛。
两位大男人揉了揉被珠宝闪花的眼睛，揉出了几滴眼泪，眼睛才舒服一些。
“臣请太子、大阿哥安。”噶布喇扶着常泰的手晃悠悠站起来。
“外祖父请不要如此见外。外祖父正病着，若勉强病体，是孤这个做外孙的不是了。”太子板起脸，特别有气势。
“太子弟弟说得对。”胤禔打量了一下噶布喇和常泰，“噶布喇大人，你还是躺着吧。我们只是来蹭顿饭。有吃的吗？容若和子清说你们家没饭给我们吃。”
噶布喇和常泰齐齐把视线射向纳兰性德和曹寅。
纳兰性德和曹寅使劲摇头。
我不是，我没有，听我解释！
噶布喇是国公爷；常泰虽然因为侍疾暂时休假在家，身上可是有领侍卫内大臣的官职。
领侍卫内大臣名义上就是宫中所有侍卫的顶头上司，也就是纳兰性德和曹寅的顶头上司。
大阿哥你当着我们顶头上司的面告刁状真的好吗？！纳兰性德和曹寅心里苦极了。
常泰看着两人有苦难言的表情，忍不住笑着摇摇头。
以他对这两人的了解，大阿哥这话可能不属实。
倒不是他认为大阿哥骗他，只是话的理解估计不对。这两人应该只是说，来不及准备比较好的午膳吧。
常泰用开玩笑的语气将此事揭过：“阿玛养病，府中食物较为清淡，恐不符合太子和大阿哥的口味。容若和子清既然知道如此，合该买些吃食上门，免得我们怠慢了太子和大阿哥。还好庄子近日送了些新鲜东西来，否则我还真会差遣你们俩去酒楼买些饭菜回来。”
纳兰性德和曹寅拱手附和，松了一口气的同时，心里有些诧异。
在他们心中，赫舍里家都是很嚣张跋扈的。
常泰虽是领侍卫大臣，却因常在一等公府中为噶布喇侍疾，而甚少出现在人前，与他们没有多少交流。
可常泰既然身为太子的亲舅舅，理应也是极为傲气的人。
今日一见，他们却发现常泰年纪虽不大，脾气却极为敦和，还会开玩笑，实在是让两人不得不诧异。
他们再小心翼翼用眼角余光环视了一圈国公府其他人。
索额图的府中下人们都带着一股趾高气昂的劲儿。噶布喇的府中下人们却透着一股谨言慎行的味道，很是古怪。
胤礽仰起头，看着即使脸上浮粉也难掩病态的噶布喇。
噶布喇回应了一个小心翼翼、但又带着期盼的微笑。
噶布喇也不知道自己的期盼什么，只是看着小小的太子，心中就忍不住涌出热流。
“外祖父，好好养身体。”胤礽伸出小手，抓住噶布喇如枯枝般的手指。
孩童暖暖的肉肉的小手，触感极为奇特。
噶布喇那一瞬间差点忍不住落了泪：“好，臣一定好好养身体，一定。”
胤礽笑了笑，道：“孤饿了，有东西先垫垫肚子吗？”
噶布喇看向常泰，常泰连忙吩咐人张罗。
这些事本该噶布喇和常泰的福晋来做。但纳兰性德和曹寅也在，女眷不好出面，常泰便总揽了一切。
常泰现在没什么在外做事的机会，噶布喇便用府中事教导常泰。常泰仿佛府中大管家，做起事来井井有条。
一等公府再低调，生活也不可能多简朴。厨房中山珍海味应有尽有。
不过常泰记着孩童脾胃弱，一些东西吃不了。
他跑到后宅，询问了额娘和福晋的意见，让厨房张罗一些鲜美但性平和的食物，又端了一些糕点出去，让两个孩子垫肚子。
噶布喇让人搬来了太师椅，躺在椅子上和胤礽、胤禔聊天。
他关心了太子和大阿哥一些生活上的琐事后，说起了京中适合孩子们玩乐的地方。
噶布喇身体还行的时候虽不能入宫当值，但在宫外走走却是没问题的。
因此他可能比那些时时需要当差的朝中重臣们更了解这四九城的一切。
噶布喇的语调很慢，时不时还会夹杂一两声咳嗽。但他文学功底不错，说话不算字字连珠，也诙谐有趣。
胤禔和胤礽听得津津有味，不知不觉松懈下来。
胤礽本想端着一点，免得让伺候的人向康熙回报自己太过亲近亲外祖父一家。
可孩童身体对慈祥长辈的眷念，让他渐渐忘记了这个念头。
胤礽趴在了太师椅上，仰着的小脑袋随着噶布喇的话一点一点，时不时侧过头和胤禔说些孩童间的童言稚语。
胤禔一手护着奶团子弟弟，一只手胡乱挥舞，听到激动处好像要跟谁干架似的。
噶布喇看着习惯性的依偎在一起的两兄弟，嘴角笑容更加慈祥。
索额图曾来找他，说朝中有人支持大阿哥，他们应当做好准备。
噶布喇委婉劝说，皇子之事，皇帝自有决断。身为太子外戚，他们理应谨言慎行，不该多生是非。
他那弟弟才高气盛，听不得容忍退让的话，拂袖不欢而散。
噶布喇本担心自己死后，没人劝得住索额图，索额图恐怕会被皇帝斥责，殃及小太子。
前几日索额图又来找他，一张老脸露出了仿佛年轻时犯错后找他帮忙的哭唧唧表情，看得噶布喇眼睛直疼。
“太子说讨厌我。”索额图QAQ，“兄长，我是不是真的做得很不好？”
噶布喇：“……你以后好好改，太子会喜欢你。”
索额图攥紧了他的老拳，信心十足的离开了。
很快，他就听到索额图约束下人，把弟弟儿子都揍了个遍的传闻。
噶布喇嘴角直抽。
这矫枉过正了吧？算了，总比不矫正好。
噶布喇很好奇太子和索额图说了什么，才让倔强劲十头牛都拉不回来的弟弟转变了性子。
胤禔听噶布喇委婉提问，也好奇道：“弟弟，你怎么劝的索额图？赶紧和哥说说，哥要去劝明珠，让他别再挑拨离间。”
纳兰明珠他儿子纳兰性德：“……”
曹寅和噶布喇同时用同情的眼神看了纳兰性德一眼。
大阿哥年岁尚小，口无遮拦，你们家选择投资大阿哥，真是辛苦了。
估计明珠已经被大阿哥卖了无数次了吧。
“我就说，如果他再不好好帮汗阿玛干活，再给汗阿玛惹事，我就不认他这个亲戚。”胤礽道，“你这样说可能对明珠没用，他本来也不算你多近的亲戚。”
胤禔抱着手臂，憨憨的脸上露出睿智的表情：“有道理。像你一样走亲情感化的路子，对明珠没用。明天爷在额娘的娘家试试，对他们应该有用。至于明珠……”
胤禔终于想起他旁边还有纳兰明珠的儿子伺候着。
“容若，你知道明珠有什么弱点吗？”胤禔睁大他睿智的眼睛，向纳兰性德求助。
纳兰性德：“……臣、臣不知。”
胤禔道：“你真没用。”
纳兰性德：“……”我怎么会知道阿玛的缺点啊！
噶布喇忍着笑道：“明珠的确有弱点。”
纳兰性德猛地转头看向噶布喇。
国公爷！你要干什么！
胤禔兴奋道：“噶布喇大人快说！”
噶布喇道：“明珠惧内。大阿哥现在能和太子自由出宫，可往明珠府上一去，将自己的烦恼告诉明珠的福晋。明珠福晋乃是爱新觉罗，虽其父已经除宗，心也肯定向着爱新觉罗的。”
明珠的福晋乃是多尔衮胞兄阿济格之女。
阿济格因罪贬为庶人赐死，但其子嗣后来被顺治允许再入宗室。
明珠福晋的两个侄子被康熙封为奉恩辅国公。虽是入八分公中最次一等，直系亲属继承也能世袭罔替，不用担心后代地位。
经历过顺治朝的大起大落，明珠的福晋虽不管后宅外的事，但皇子都跑来告状了，她一定能劝住明珠。
纳兰性德以一首“一生一代一双人，争教两处销魂”的《画堂春》，成为后世人眼中的情圣。其实纳兰性德并不情圣。他娶妻时已经有了庶长子，妻子死后还有挚爱名妓小妾为他生了遗腹子。
他的阿玛纳兰明珠，才是真的“一生一代一双人”，从族谱、墓碑和子嗣所有记载，他都只有一位福晋，没有任何妾室。
这在古代太难得，生活在乾隆和道光年间的爱新觉罗·昭梿在《啸亭杂录》给这位同族祖宗编了很多骇人听闻的故事，说明珠福晋被残害的侍妾父亲乱刀砍死。
这肯定是假的。明珠府上要是出这么大的事，明珠福晋还是宗室女，康熙朝肯定会有记载。但这也可以证明，明珠和其福晋伉俪情深到同时代男人都很不理解的程度。
若能让明珠福晋劝说，明珠肯定会听。
当然，这一切很难。首先，他们得找一个皇子亲自去找明珠的福晋告状。
会有皇子这么不要脸吗？
而且皇子怎么去见明珠的福晋？
噶布喇看着年幼的大阿哥和小太子。
嗯，现在这艰难的条件都凑齐了。
纳兰性德神情恍惚。
还、还能这样？
他仔细想了想，倒吸一口气。
真、真的还能这样！
额娘基本不管事，但在大事上，阿玛不仅爱额娘入骨，也视额娘为最重要的幕僚，肯定会考虑额娘的意见。
纳兰性德难忍心中坑爹的冲动。
他因为家中的政治野心与自身理想不符合，终日苦闷难安。如果阿玛能放弃野心……就算不放弃野心，好歹多考虑考虑他的政治理想……
纳兰性德忍了忍，再忍了忍，终究忍不住了。
“大阿哥若想来臣的家中做客，臣的额娘定会欢喜万分。”纳兰性德委婉道，“这些日子阿玛随陛下出行，府中只有额娘。额娘喜欢热闹，很欢迎大阿哥和太子来访。”
曹寅瞳孔地震。
兄弟，你要干什么？！你是不是对你爹有什么大意见？？我就没见过像你这样坑爹的！！你想挑起你额娘和你阿玛的家庭斗争吗！！
胤禔道：“好。那我明日先不去……算了，还是先去外祖父家敲打敲打，然后再去你家。弟弟，你也去索额图家看看他们有没有改好。哥帮你撑腰，他们敢不停你的话，哥就带人揍他们。”
胤礽点头：“好，咱们说定了！哥，你一定要给我撑腰！”
火拐了个弯烧到了自家弟弟头上，噶布喇居然还在煽风点火。
“是该去瞧瞧。索额图说他整治家里小有成效，臣看着不太像，还是得太子和大阿哥亲眼瞧瞧才成。”噶布喇淡然道，“若他做得不好，请大阿哥多敲打敲打他。”
常泰一来通知吃饭，就听到噶布喇在坑弟弟。
他苦笑地打断自家阿玛的坑弟行为，道：“太子，大阿哥，午膳已经准备好了，要先用膳吗？”
“走走走，吃饭去，饿死爷了。”胤禔一抹嘴上的糕点残渣，牵着胤礽就开跑。
“大阿哥，您小心些！小心脚下。”常泰看着跌跌撞撞被胤禔拉着跑的胤礽，心脏都快猝停了，十分担心太子会被大阿哥拉摔倒。
“你们也去吧，我就不去了。”噶布喇疲惫的眯上双眼，“今日之事，请逐字逐句告知皇上。”
太子和大阿哥身边伺候的人，都兼有皇帝耳目之责。噶布喇不说，他们也会如实上报。
噶布喇只是表明自己忠心无二的态度。
待所有人离开之后，噶布喇让人把自己搬回了屋中床上。
噶布喇靠在软垫上，回忆着今日小太子模样，右手按住了双眼，眼泪从指缝中悄然流出。
真的太好了。这个孩子比自己想象中的还要聪慧可爱。
女儿啊，你的儿子真的非常非常好，你泉下有知，也该安心了。
饭桌上。
胤禔可不懂什么食不言。
他一边吃一边往胤礽的碗里塞自己认为好吃的东西。胤礽也来者不拒，吃不下了就把自己碗里的菜倒进常泰碗里。
常泰：“……”有、有受宠若惊到。
常泰明明还很年轻，此刻慈祥得仿佛溺爱孙子的老爷爷：“太子和大阿哥都能自己吃饭，太厉害了。”
纳兰性德点头：“我弟弟现在还得人追着喂饭。”
胤礽想起了纳兰性德弟弟的模样。
纳兰揆叙，坚定的反太子一党，宗室勋贵上蹿下跳推举小八的主力军，被气疯了的雍正把墓碑推了的家伙。
不过满朝宗室勋贵基本都站在自己对立面。算了，懒得想了，忽视吧。
胤礽又吃了一大口肉，幸福地眯起了眼睛。
“你怎么这么喜欢吃肉？汗阿玛缺你这口肉吃吗？”胤禔疑惑道，“别光顾着吃肉，额娘说，也得多吃菜。来，乖，吃一口。”
胤礽皱着眉头小口小口吃菜：“汗阿玛说，养生，吃饭八分饱，肉菜对半吃。”
胤禔道：“好惨。下次饿着了来找哥，额娘那有小厨房，随时想吃什么吃什么。”
胤礽使劲点头。
常泰委婉劝说道：“皇上说得有道理，吃撑了容易得病。”
胤禔瞪了常泰一眼：“我弟弟吃不饱才会得病。我就不信汗阿玛饿了的时候不会吃东西。但弟弟饿了可不好随意要东西吃。”
常泰：“……”他居然被一个孩子说服了？！
常泰因为被胤禔说服，整顿饭后半截都有些神思恍惚。
直到胤禔嚷着让常泰带他们放风筝，他才回过神。
三藩之乱未全部平定，宫中管理较为严格。风筝这种可以传递消息的玩具，胤禔和胤礽还未曾玩过。
胤禔仰头看到空中有东西在飞，大为好奇。
听那玩意儿叫风筝之后，胤禔立刻嚷着要玩。
国公府的女眷们常爱带着孩子们玩风筝，家中自然常备各种不同风格的风筝。
胤禔骑在曹寅脖子上使劲拽着风筝线，当风筝飞高之后，他就把风筝线塞到胤礽手中，自己重新放另一个风筝。
常泰惊讶不已。
大阿哥对太子也太好了一些。就是他对常海，也没这么好过。
“大哥，你先玩，我想去见见外祖母和舅母。”胤礽玩了一会儿风筝，对胤禔道，“你玩腻了就来后宅找我。”
他和胤禔都小，可以出入后宅。
胤禔道：“好，你快去，我再玩一会儿。”
女眷住的地方，纳兰性德和曹寅是不能去的。
但胤礽身边有梁九功，胤禔身边也有太监，仍旧有人随行。
胤礽牵着常泰的手走了几步，仰头道：“我累了，舅舅抱。”
常泰心脏猛地一颤，手脚五促道：“好、好。”
他立刻把胤礽抱了起来：“这样抱可以吗？不舒服就和臣说。”
胤礽非常不客气地指挥常泰如何抱他。
他坐在常泰怀里，双手吊着常泰的脖子，小声问道：“舅舅，外祖父生病，为何不告诉我？”
康熙朝将会有三位皇后。
如今的孝安皇后、上上辈子的孝昭皇后的弟弟阿灵阿生病时，康熙嘘寒问暖，亲自探望。
胤礽即使已经被圈禁，也从别人口中听过阿灵阿有多得康熙看重。
康熙在边塞巡视时，对阿灵阿的病情每日奏闻、亲自占卜，让固伦公主做饭，寻西洋名医诊治。
阿灵阿死后，皇太后和宫中嫔妃皆遣人赐茶奠酒，派皇四子、皇五子、皇七子、皇十七子护灵送灵。
自家人呢？
不说自家人已经被自己连累后。便是在自己荣宠甚重时病逝的外祖父噶布喇，病着的时候也没有如此待遇。
胤礽仔细想了想，倒也不是康熙对外祖父不满。只是外祖父病重了也只说自己常年体弱，不是大事。直到快死了的时候才奏报康熙，康熙遣了侍卫带御医去看望。
康熙遣侍卫去看望的当日，外祖父便去世了。
外祖父真是低调到了生命的最后一刻。他上上辈子甚至从未见过外祖父的音容笑貌。
“阿玛一直体弱多病，不是什么大事，哪能为这点习以为常的事打扰太子？”常泰温柔道，“太子不用担心，阿玛虽然体弱，但精神不错，病很快就能好。”
你骗我。
外祖父缠绵病榻，后年就将去世了。
胤礽收紧手臂，又问道：“我为何从未听过舅舅的事？汗阿玛总提索额图。”
常泰道：“索额图是赫舍里家最能干的人，皇上日理万机，自然只记得得用之人。”
常泰大着胆子揉了揉已经摘掉宝石帽子的胤礽头上可爱的小揪揪。
“待阿玛病好了，臣会奏请外出练兵，挣好多好多功劳回来，太子也能事事听到臣的消息了。”
赫舍里家一代有一个重臣，能在朝中帮持太子便够了。
这一代是索额图，下一代便是他。
常泰熟读兵书，擅长绘制阵图地图，对新式火器研究很深，自信一定能在军中崭露头角。
他和阿玛商量过了。
纵观史书，利用外戚的名义为非作歹者令人厌恶。若学卫青霍去病者，以微末功劳逐渐晋升，或许在皇帝眼中会顺眼许多。
常泰说起此事时，眼中带着星星点点的光。
这一条道路危险艰难，稍稍不留神可能就马革裹尸。
可男儿志在千里。常泰对自己充满信心，他也想试试不躺在家中荫蔽下，用自己的本事，能不能拼出一个真正的前程。
“太子放心，臣定能做到。”常泰斩钉截铁道。
胤礽仰着小脸看着常泰眼眸中点点星光，小声道：“嗯。”
是啊，你做到了。
一征噶尔丹，你从领鸟枪骑兵一路立功成为了将军；
二征噶尔丹，你受命成为清军右翼统帅；
三征噶尔丹，你名列从政大臣第六位，却很快没了动静。
而后，你便无声无息的死了。
你的儿子由噶礼悄悄抚养，而后被噶礼亲生额娘告发，发配边疆；
你的爵位直到雍正五年，才被雍正怜惜，令常海之子伦布继承；
你的事迹被隐瞒删除，清史上没有你的传记，连《八旗满洲氏族通谱》上也对你一笔带过。
后世史学家通过康熙、雍正朝的谕旨、书信研究，才得以窥见你曾经辉煌功劳的些许残留。
胤礽把脑袋埋在常泰怀里，努力睁大着眼睛，眼中没有一滴泪水流出。
常泰还在温言细语地说着自己擅长的、喜欢的事，踌躇满志地告诉怀中的小太子，自己一定会成为让小太子骄傲的舅舅。

36.二更合一 [V]
胤礽被常泰抱到后宅时，老福晋、常泰的福晋和小赫舍里已经摆好了糕点瓜果候着。
常泰的福晋看着小赫舍里，眼神有些复杂。
小赫舍里如今不到十岁，就算强做出一副成熟的模样，也显得一团孩气。
老福晋看着小赫舍里的眼神中也带着犹豫和痛苦。
小赫舍里心思敏感，见额娘和嫂子这副模样，也不免愁绪爬上心理。
“老身请太子安。”老福晋被常泰的福晋扶起来请安，院子中其他女眷也一一请安。
胤礽一只手勾着常泰的脖子，另一只手挥挥：“请起，不必过多礼节。”
待众人起身后，胤礽仍旧坐在常泰怀里。
常泰受宠若惊的护好胤礽，两只手把胤礽环住。
胤礽大咧咧坐在常泰怀里，两只手扶着常泰的手臂，就像是坐在太师椅上似的，特别霸气。
老福晋看见这一幕，心中愁绪被太子可爱的举止戳散，脸上笑容怎么都止不住，完全无法维持优雅的姿态。
“外祖母要抱抱孤吗？”胤礽对老福晋伸出手。
老福晋嘴里说着不敢，手却控制不住已经伸了过来。
常泰的福晋和常泰交换了一个好笑的眼神。
老福晋的身体和噶布喇一样不太好。胤礽和老福晋抱抱，让老福晋摸了摸他头上的小揪揪后，又回到了常泰怀里。
常泰昂首挺胸，神情可自豪了。
常泰的福晋忍笑。她琢磨着，回去可要好好笑话笑话常泰。
胤礽把视线投向老福晋身旁的小女孩：“这是舅舅的女儿？”
常泰忙道：“不，不，这是阿玛的女儿。”
常泰没说小赫舍里是胤礽的小姨。
且不说小赫舍里是庶出的女儿，和常泰、仁孝皇后等嫡子嫡女地位不一样。太子未主动说谁谁谁是他亲戚，其他人不能自称太子的长辈。
“哦。”胤礽一琢磨，想到了这个小女孩的身份。
平妃，他额娘的庶出妹妹，明年年底入宫。
平妃在宫中并不受宠，只因姓赫舍里，得了康熙几分照顾，昭封为妃，死后补了册封封号，算是被宫里养着。
见小赫舍里年龄，胤礽明白康熙为什么不喜欢平妃，甚至有些膈应了。
宫里有好几对姐妹花，康熙并不介意那些家族的“政治投资”。
但小赫舍里的年龄也太小了。赫舍里家族送个孩子进宫，还大言不惭说照顾太子，康熙能喜欢才奇怪。
胤礽疑惑。以他今日见外祖父言行，不像是会送年幼的女儿入宫的人。
他难道不清楚康熙的心思吗？
“这孩子，便是佟家相看的姑娘。”梁九功不愧是历史中留下名字的大太监，凑胤礽耳边，小声告诉胤礽，老福晋把这个姑娘领出来的缘由，“国公爷家似乎不太愿意。”
胤礽眼睛睁大。
什么？！隆科多原本相中的媳妇是平妃吗！！
转念一想，这很合理。
隆科多是佟贵妃的亲弟弟，小赫舍里是仁孝皇后的庶出妹妹。满人嫁娶的时候对女儿这一方不太注重嫡庶，又有太子在，两人从地位上的确十分般配。
至于这年龄差，满人家的姑娘十一二岁嫁人的不罕见。现在定下，准备个一两年，便可以入门了。
从地位到年龄，小赫舍里居然正好和隆科多配上。
意识到这一点之后，胤礽头皮发麻，头上的小揪揪都快炸开了。
之前因为前前世的感伤，都被这个重磅消息炸没了。
我亲小姨，给隆科多当媳妇？
那个著名的隆科多？
就算李四儿不再是隆科多岳父的小妾，隆科多肯定也会和李四儿勾搭在一起。
不如说，这不更适合隆科多抢人家小妾了吗？！
“不合适。”胤礽扯了扯常泰的衣袖，“佟贵妃不错，但隆科多脾气很不好，她会被欺负。”
常泰道：“额娘打听了一下隆科多的风评，也不看好这门婚事。只是……”
老福晋听太子都说隆科多风评不好，心里下定了决心。
她笑着道：“只是相看，还没定呢。有老爷在，借着姑娘还小，想在家中多留几年的话，佟家应该也不会有什么意见。今日让她来，只是给太子见见家里人。”
胤礽头皮更加发麻了。
他总算明白小赫舍里明年十二月会入宫了。
上上辈子的康熙十九年九月，索额图在康熙敲打后请求解任，外祖父缠绵病榻眼见着熬不过，佟家的权势则依托佟贵妃正值上升期。
虽宫中有太子在，但太子年幼，且不可能为一个庶出的小姨得罪宫中的佟贵妃。
对已经遭遇康熙不满的索额图等人而言，向康熙后宫送一个赫舍里的女人，是自救的方法之一；对外祖父这一家而言，在赫舍里家式微之后，不想让女儿嫁给隆科多被磋磨死，只有入宫这一条路。
现在赫舍里家的局势还没恶化到这个程度。老福晋没有说谎，她只是让小赫舍里出来见见太子。
当然，若是小赫舍里得了太子眼缘，她也有多留小赫舍里几年，然后入宫为妃帮衬太子的想法。
对赫舍里家而言，一个太子比一个庶女重要得多。外祖母不可能为了一个庶女的前程算计我。胤礽刚生出这个念头，小拳头就不由捏紧。
他恍然想，自己这疑心病真可怕。
都是上上辈子的汗阿玛的错。
“隆科多不是良配，你们尽管大胆的拒了。”胤礽道，“若佟家问起，便说家中已经有一位太子，若太子亲小姨和宫中正得宠贵妃的亲弟弟联姻，恐怕会被怀疑太子和贵妃连手把持后宫。”
老福晋脸色一慌：“太子爷，这、这……”
“孤今日说的话，会奏给汗阿玛，外祖父放心。”太子正色道，“赫舍里家已经如烈火烹油，每一步都需要小心谨慎。佟家也一样。即使佟贵妃无子，孝康皇玛嬷乃是佟佳氏。贵妃与太子关系太近，实属一步坏棋。”
其他皇子与勋贵互相拉拢便罢了，但太子位置特殊。老福晋一琢磨，立刻明白道：“太子说的是。老身会亲自去佟家去一趟，把其中利益关系好好阐明。”
胤礽展眉：“外祖母当如此。家族联姻，都是为了各自的利益。从利益出发，佟家才会理解，两家便不会结怨。”
老福晋立刻站起来俯身道：“太子英明，老身着相了！”
常泰的福晋立刻拉着小赫舍里站起来，也对胤礽俯身。
胤礽挥了挥手，道：“没事，坐下吧。赫舍里对孤很重要，帮你们也是帮孤自己。外祖父应该也看到了，纵观史书，在英明神武的皇帝手下当外戚，懂事听话远比功高显赫重要。进退有度，方为外戚存活之道。”
胤礽顿了顿，道：“孤的额娘乃赫舍里氏出生，你们难免对孤多几分看重。孤今日来，便是将话说明白了。希望赫舍里只忠于汗阿玛，只把汗阿玛放在心中第一位。这对赫舍里很重要，对孤也很重要。舅舅肯定能理解孤说什么，对吧？”
常泰一愣，然后立刻道：“是，太子！”
胤礽笑道：“见到外祖父之前，孤很不安。若外祖父是和索额图那样才高志大，却倔脾气听不得劝的人，孤可不知如何是好。今日看来，外祖父比索额图清醒许多。”
胤礽又看向小赫舍里。
小赫舍里紧张的捏住帕子。
“只要孤地位稳固，赫舍里家已经不需要显赫的姻亲，反倒是越低调越好。”胤礽冷淡道，“若孤地位不稳固，赫舍里家上蹿下跳会更招汗阿玛厌恶。”

Soon, Kangxi was surrounded by a group of burly men, all of whom were heaping praise upon Yinreng, as if they were blind and couldn't see that Yinreng had missed all three of his shots.

Yinreng lifted his little face and scanned the circle of burly men around him.

Good heavens, they were all people who would want to crush him to death in the future.

However, Yinreng counted on his fingers: the imperial clansmen were either watching coldly or wishing him dead, the Manchu nobles were either neutral or wishing him dead, and only the Han officials were praising him with genuine sincerity.

Well, that’s that then; most of the people who could go hunting with Kangxi were his enemies.

Actually, they couldn't exactly be called enemies of "Yinreng," but rather "enemies of the Crown Prince whom Kangxi had unilaterally appointed."

Sigh, what does it mean to be an enemy of the whole world? Yinreng immediately performed a tactical lean-back, hitting the back of his head against Kangxi’s breastplate, which made him tear up in pain.

"Silly Baocheng." Kangxi was busy focusing on dealing with the flattery of those around him and almost broke his composure laughing at his son.

Yinreng clutched his head, pouted, and glared at Kangxi: "Ama, you bumped my head. Shouldn't you reflect on that?"

Kangxi thought about it seriously and said, "What should I reflect on? Reflect on why I didn't make your head hard enough?"

Yinreng: "..." It sounds as if I were born by you alone.

Empress Renxiao was a thorn in the heart of the Crown Prince from his previous life, and even after two lifetimes, Yinreng wouldn't bring it up to joke about lightly.

He could only pout and rub his head pitifully.

Surrounded by a group of murderous, burly men, how could a five-year-old child like Yinreng remain so calm and even joke with the Emperor?

The burly men immediately let their presence be felt.

Let's probe him further! I don't believe an Emperor, a grown man, can really raise a child!

Yinreng sensed their radiating hormones (?) and calmly swept his gaze over the surrounding clansmen.

As Yinreng scanned the clansmen, Kangxi’s smile faded, and he also swept his gaze over them.

By coincidence, father and son made the same expression and movement at the same time. The two gazes, one large and one small, swept from left to right, then from right to left, sending a chill through the hearts of the burly clansmen.

Even though Kangxi was only in his twenties, he already possessed immense authority. When Kangxi got angry, they instinctively cowered; otherwise, they wouldn't have resorted to such petty sabotage.

And how old was the Crown Prince?

Five years old!

A five-year-old child was not only unafraid of them but was also glaring at them? That cold, icy look was almost identical to the Emperor's—wasn't he a bit too monstrous?

Kangxi noticed that the looks they were casting at the Crown Prince were wrong and quickly looked down.

Yinreng: [Frowning and glaring.jpg]

Kangxi couldn't help but gasp, almost unable to resist picking Yinreng up on horseback to kiss, hug, and lift him high.

How can the son I raised be so cute?!

Fuquan, the only one among the clansmen who held affection for the Crown Prince, touched his chest.

Hmm, today Prince Yu has also been charmed by the Crown Prince.

So cute, so sour, I also want a son who is this well-behaved and cute, yet knows how to glare at bad guys!

"What's wrong? Your eyeballs are about to pop out." Kangxi lifted the Crown Prince a bit and teased him in his ear.

Yinreng: [Glaring.jpg]

"Ama, my expression is about the same as yours. My eyeballs are popping out, what about you?" Yinreng refused to be outdone.

Kangxi immediately said sternly, "What nonsense are you talking about? My expression is not the same as yours. Why are you glaring at them? They are praising you."

Yinreng continued to glare: "Ama, does your son look that stupid? A group of wolves in grandma's clothing praising me?"

Kangxi endured, endured.

As an Emperor, I am a professional at holding back laughter. Even if I'm teased to the point of being unable to handle it by my son, I will absolutely not laugh.

"But, Ama, I haven't met them before, why do they all hate me?" Yinreng wouldn't let Kangxi keep laughing. "Except for Uncle Fuquan, they all hate me."

Yinreng hinted frantically.

Ama! They hate me!

But I haven't provoked them, how could they hate me!

They hate me on the surface, but they are actually opposing you!

They hate me, which is a slap in your face!

Although "Let the Bullets Fly" hadn't appeared yet, Yinreng suggested applying for World Heritage status for "Let the Bullets Fly" a few hundred years in advance.

Kangxi, as expected, couldn't laugh anymore.

It wasn't that he hadn't realized this point. But it was the first time someone had pointed it out so bluntly.

Kangxi didn't appoint the Crown Prince out of deep affection for his wife, nor did he value the legitimate son that much—when his first legitimate son died, Kangxi didn't even return to the palace.

Now, Kangxi’s love for the Crown Prince was cultivated while he raised his son himself, through all the messy diapers and feedings.

Kangxi appointed the Crown Prince to weaken the control of the clansmen and nobles over the imperial succession.

He knew from the start that these guys wouldn't give up. It was just that the other side pretended too well, and the Revolt of the Three Feudatories happened, so Kangxi "forgot" about this for a while.

Even his son could keenly sense this; the malice of these guys really wasn't hidden at all.

They didn't even hide it in front of me!

Kangxi shielded his son a little tighter.

Yinreng complained: "Ama, relax, relax, you're pressing against your son. Ah, son doesn't want to ride the big horse with you, son wants to go back to his own little horse."

"What little horse? You haven't practiced riding and shooting, can you ride it?" Kangxi looked at his son with disdain.

"Hmph, then I want someone else to take me." Yinreng looked up and said, "Ama wants to hunt big game, son wants to catch little bunnies, we are not going the same way."

Kangxi: "..." Wanted to spank his son's little bottom.

However, Yinreng was right. Kangxi came to the hunting grounds to show off his high martial prowess, and he had the ability to show off.

He firmly believed that he could still kill in all directions while carrying his son, but he was afraid of scaring him.

Oh, he hadn't even scared his son yet, and his son was already complaining that he was riding too fast, bumping and pressing against him.

"You are so pampered, you'll have plenty to cry about when you learn riding and shooting later." Kangxi laughed and scolded, "Who do you want to follow? Prince Yu?"

Yinreng raised his fleshy paws: "Mingzhu or Xingde!"

The last two sentences were not whispered between Kangxi and Yinreng; they were said out loud.

After Yinreng finished speaking, Kangxi regretted saying it so loudly.

Mingzhu was also following in the crowd of clansmen.

However, he hid himself in the crowd, neither too close nor too far from Kangxi, deliberately reducing his presence.

Only Songgotu tried hard to push forward, but the clansmen wouldn't give him space, so he could only crane his neck and peer inside.

With those two shouts from Kangxi and Yinreng, Prince Yu Fuquan went from happy to crestfallen, and Mingzhu almost fell off his horse.

Songgotu? Songgotu was once again doubting his life.

Yinreng immediately added: "Ama wants to hunt big tigers and bears, Uncle will protect Ama, Uncle is so amazing!"

Fuquan’s crestfallen face perked up.

That's right, this Prince is just that amazing! Leave the matter of protecting the Emperor to me!

"I will reluctantly let the super handsome Lord Mingzhu and Xingde protect me, ouch." Yinreng’s head received a loving flick from Kangxi.

Everyone looked at Mingzhu one after another.

Nalan Xingde was still in the group of guards, quite far away, so they couldn't see him.

They looked Nalan Mingzhu up and down.

Well, they had to admit, Mingzhu was indeed handsome.

If Mingzhu weren't handsome, the arrogant and overbearing Aisin Gioro Ajige wouldn't have "snatched a bride" for his daughter back then.

That handsome uncle with the outstanding temperament, Nalan Mingzhu, looked a bit distorted.

The Crown Prince was only five years old; he hadn't reached the age to covet beauty.

So who was the one whispering about Mingzhu’s beauty in the Crown Prince’s ear every day?

Case closed, it’s you! Your most noble Majesty, the Emperor of the Great Qing!

The clansmen gasped several times.

Kangxi’s reputation was ruined.

"Alright, alright, I knew you were thinking about it." Kangxi, who didn't yet know his reputation was ruined, said helplessly, "Mingzhu has to follow me, I'll let Rongruo protect you."

Someone immediately spurred their horse away to find Nalan Xingde.

Nalan Xingde followed the Emperor’s attendant and rode to Kangxi, only to have a cute little milk bun stuffed into his arms by Kangxi.

"My Crown Prince will be taken care of by you for a while. Whatever he wants to do, as long as it's not dangerous, accompany him to do it." Kangxi said generously, "Take good care of the Crown Prince, and there will be rewards."

Nalan Xingde held the Crown Prince, feeling extremely nervous: "Yes, Your Majesty!"

Wh-what do I do? I haven't taken care of a child before!

Mingzhu’s expression was about to collapse.

Our Yehenara family doesn't want to be tied to the Crown Prince!

Songgotu finally managed to squeeze in front of Kangxi with difficulty: "Your Majesty..."

"Shut up." Kangxi interrupted.

Songgotu: "..."

Yinreng straightened his arms and waved his little short hands: "Ama, be careful! Uncle, I leave Ama in your care!"

Fuquan laughed: "Alright, alright."

"Alright my foot, your riding and shooting are worse than mine." Kangxi whipped his horse’s rump and gave Fuquan a proud back.

"That’s not necessarily true." Fuquan rubbed his nose, muttered under his breath, and also whipped his horse’s rump, following Kangxi away.

Some of the clansmen continued to follow Kangxi, while others went hunting nearby. The massive crowd began to disperse, and no one bothered the Crown Prince.

When Kangxi wasn't being muddled, they acted with great discretion. Like Changning, they would only be sarcastic and didn't dare to do anything overstepping.

Speaking of Changning...

Changning actually stayed behind alone and said to the Crown Prince: "Does the little Prince want Uncle to take you to play?"

Nalan Xingde immediately hugged the Crown Prince tightly, on full alert.

Yinreng smiled: "Prince Gong, Ama has already gone far away. Is it really okay for you to stay here and tease your nephew instead of accompanying Ama?"

Changning’s face darkened.

He carefully scrutinized the little Crown Prince, who seemed like a different person the moment he left Kangxi, then turned his horse and left.

Nalan Xingde breathed a sigh of relief.

"Th-the Crown Prince is so amazing, you scared Prince Gong away?" A boisterous voice sounded beside Yinreng and Nalan Xingde.

Yinreng turned his head and saw a beautiful man, even more delicate than Nalan Xingde, staring with bright eyes, patting his chest and sighing.

Nalan Xingde was helpless: "Cao Ziqing, keep your voice down! Your Highness, this is Cao Yin, Cao Ziqing."

Nalan Xingde didn't introduce him further. He believed that the person the Emperor left behind to protect the Crown Prince with him must have already been introduced to the Crown Prince.

Yinreng certainly knew Cao Yin.

The future Jiangning Textile Commissioner, the grandfather of Cao Xueqin, the author of "Dream of the Red Chamber."

Yinreng just didn't expect Cao Yin to be so beautiful when he was young.

That's right, beautiful... oh my Ama, did you choose the Imperial Guard based on looks?

Uh, wait, the Imperial Guard is the Emperor’s ceremonial escort, the face of the Emperor’s travels, so they must definitely be chosen for looks and physique.

So amazing, let me take another look!

Seeing the Crown Prince examining him, Cao Yin hurriedly bowed: "Did this servant scare the Crown Prince?"

Yinreng shook his head: "Guard Cao, there is such a big gap between your voice and your looks."

Cao Yin: "..."

Nalan Xingde suppressed a laugh: "Yes, that's right, His Majesty says the same thing."

Such a fine face, how did it end up with such a loud voice? Kangxi had been lamenting this for a long time.

Cao Yin smiled and said: "That’s natural, this servant can't change it. Where does the Crown Prince want to play? When it comes to playing, this servant is very good at it!"

Yinreng swept a glance at the guards Kangxi left for him.

This group of guards was led by Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin. Or rather, led by Cao Yin.

The future Jiangning Textile Commissioner was now also the Emperor’s confidant. Kangxi specifically left Cao Yin behind to protect Yinreng.

And Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde were friends; them taking care of a child together wouldn't lead to any disagreements.

"I want to see a small river." Yinreng said, "There are no rivers in the palace."

Cao Yin said: "Alright, let's go over there. The river water is shallow, and there are no dangerous animals nearby. The Crown Prince can play on the grass, and maybe even catch some rabbits or birds."

In the Emperor’s hunting grounds, which area had what kind of game was all pre-determined.

If dangerous game were encountered in a safe area, those in charge of the hunting ground would lose their heads.

Cao Yin knew the situation of the hunting ground like the back of his hand and immediately found a place suitable for Yinreng to play.

That place happened to be where Kangxi would pass by on his return journey after hunting dangerous game, so Kangxi wouldn't have to take a detour to pick up the little milk bun Crown Prince.

Cao Yin could become Kangxi’s confidant and borrow money from Kangxi at will, not just because of his beautiful face and loud voice, nor even because his mother was Kangxi’s wet nurse—Kangxi had many wet nurses, but only the Cao family gained power. This wet nurse only strengthened their relationship when Kangxi promoted the Cao family.

Compared to the noble Nalan Xingde, Cao Yin was more tactful and extremely considerate.

For most people, reading the room requires familiarity.

It wasn't that the people around Yinreng weren't considerate, but they had to wait for Yinreng to speak before they knew what he needed; it really wasn't because they were neglecting him.

But people like Liang Jiugong and Cao Yin had a talent for reading the room that was almost like Observation Haki; they could be thoughtful even with a stranger.

Yinreng guaranteed he hadn't given any hints, yet Cao Yin had already done everything he wanted.

A blanket was spread on the grass, a bonfire stood beside it, rabbits and pheasants were roasting by the fire, and little eunuchs were boiling wild vegetable and fish soup under Cao Yin’s direction.

Nalan Xingde was "directed" by Cao Yin to pick wild flowers and grass to weave flower baskets for Yinreng.

Although Nalan Xingde was a noble young master, because he loved to associate with Han literati, he learned skills that were incompatible with the Manchu noble sons.

Such as elegant handicraft.

Nalan Xingde could actually weave grass crickets with long leaves, would you believe it!

Yinreng danced with joy: "Weave one for older brother, weave two for younger brother! I want one too!"

Nalan Xingde smiled: "Alright."

"This servant wants one too." After Cao Yin finished arranging things, he leaned over and smiled cheekily.

"Here." Yinreng took off the flower wreath from his neck and put it on Cao Yin’s head.

Cao Yin touched the wreath on his head, laughing and crying: "Does this count as me wearing flowers?"

"Guard Nalan, here." Yinreng stood on tiptoe and tucked a small orchid into Nalan Xingde’s collar.

Yinreng looked at Nalan Xingde’s shaved forehead and felt extremely regretful.

Even if Nalan Xingde’s good looks were such that even a shaved forehead was handsome, it was still a pity that flowers couldn't be tucked into his temples.

"Alright, we are all wearing flowers." Cao Yin said with a smile, "Thank you for the reward, Crown Prince."

"This isn't a reward, it's just playing." Yinreng said seriously, "Guard Cao, don't be so tense. I'm just a child; it makes me tired to look at you like that."

Cao Yin: "..." Did I do something wrong?

The well-loved Cao Yin was hearing such words for the first time.

Yinreng smiled: "Guard Nalan has the temperament of a high-minded literati, and those who associate with him are, without exception, imbued with that literati pride. I have often heard that Guard Cao is well-read, but due to your status as a bondservant, you cannot prove yourself through the imperial examinations like Guard Nalan."

Yinreng had a good impression of Cao Yin, even if the Cao family eventually leaned towards Yinreng, or rather, towards the Manchu clan forces.

But by then, he had already been deposed, Cao Yin was seriously ill, Cao Yin’s eldest son was in poor health, and the whole Cao family was falling apart; it was normal for the Cao family to plan for themselves.

Cao Yin’s eldest daughter was married by Kangxi to Narsu, so where else could they stand if not on the side of the clansmen?

Yongzheng was so petty, yet he only investigated the Cao family’s deficits, and after confiscating their property, he allowed the Cao family to return to the capital, not only preserving their lives but also issuing an edict forbidding others from intimidating or blackmailing the Cao family.

It shows that the Cao family’s allegiance was just following the crowd; in reality, they didn't rely on anyone.

Also, the Cao family’s adopted son was indeed too useless. Even Kangxi didn't want to bother with him, let alone Yongzheng.

Cao Yin was stunned and smiled respectfully: "Your Highness’s words make this servant feel flattered."

"Ama intends for you to take care of me, so you should have some confidence in yourself." Yinreng waved his hand, "There are many people around me who are respectful and meticulous; I don't lack one more. It's rare to have a chance to come out and play, so be normal, don't always do Liang Jiugong’s work. Liang Jiugong!"

Liang Jiugong appeared from behind Yinreng.

He glanced at Cao Yin from the corner of his eye.

Hmph.

"You take over the work in Guard Cao’s hands. Guard Cao, you stay here and play with me." Yinreng ordered.

Cao Yin was Kangxi’s guard; even if he was a bondservant, Yinreng wouldn't order him around too much.

Besides, he was really curious about the Cao family.

The prototype of "Dream of the Red Chamber." The "Flower Burial Poem" was taken from Cao Yin’s flower burial poetry.

Wait, doesn't that mean Cao Yin is basically Daiyu?

Yinreng’s gaze lingered on Cao Yin’s beautiful face for a few turns, then he retracted it, suppressing a laugh.

No, can't think about it anymore, I'll die laughing.

Liang Jiugong took Yinreng’s order and took over Cao Yin’s work.

Cao Yin had no choice but to sit side-by-side with Nalan Xingde, accompanying this little ancestor, Yinreng.

Nalan Xingde, with his back to Yinreng, made faces at Cao Yin.

Look, I told you the Crown Prince is extremely intelligent. You wanted to coax him like an ordinary child, and you got schooled, didn't you?

Cao Yin made faces back.

Schooled? I was clearly being praised.

However, the Crown Prince is truly terrifyingly intelligent. How does His Majesty raise his children?

Nalan Xingde at least had two children, although he hadn't raised them himself. Cao Yin had difficulty having children and didn't have any yet. Seeing such an intelligent child, he couldn't help but feel envious.

"Has Guard Cao been to Jiangnan?" Yinreng asked while staring at the grass cricket Nalan Xingde was weaving.

Cao Yin said: "I have. But this servant grew up in Fengrun, Zhili."

"Then tell me about Zhili." Yinreng asked.

Cao Yin thought Yinreng was just curious about things outside the capital, so he picked some interesting, delicious, and fun things to tell Yinreng.

Yinreng listened while guiding Cao Yin to bring the topic to foreigners.

When foreign missionaries entered the capital, they would first stop in Zhili after arriving in the north.

The northern section of the Grand Canal belonged to Zhili. Foreign missionaries entering the Qing territory from Guangzhou would travel north to Suzhou and Hangzhou, mostly entering the capital via the Grand Canal.

Zhili was the area of Tianjin in later generations. Tianjin Port was the gateway to the sea for the capital, very prosperous, with many foreign merchants hawking their wares.

Later, whether it was closing the country or being forced to open ports, the Tianjin port belonging to Zhili always had a presence.

Tianjin was currently under a sea ban. But the sea ban in the Kangxi era wasn't strict; it was just to guard against the Zheng family.

Tianjin’s overseas trade was mostly towards the Korean Peninsula and the Japanese islands. Kangxi was well aware of the "smuggling" and once said that for the sake of the people’s livelihood, he deliberately turned a blind eye to the sea ban.

After Taiwan was pacified in the 23rd year of Kangxi, the sea ban would be lifted. Although Kangxi didn't explicitly open the Tianjin port, the trade between the Qing and countries like Japan in the Tianjin port became more prosperous, and it was effectively already open.

This life was Yinreng’s third lifetime.

He would toss and turn because of the pain of his previous life, and he would also be full of youthful spirit like in his life before that.

Anyway, before Kangxi got old, he couldn't die no matter how much he messed around, so why not be a bit more carefree?

The Qing Dynasty would definitely be overthrown. No matter how hard Yinreng tried, the "systemic problems" were real in the Qing Dynasty.

Feudal society was bound to disintegrate, and the decaying soil was bound to bloom with the inextinguishable flowers of flame he had seen in his previous life.

Yinreng couldn't manage things hundreds of years later, but he could influence things slightly now, letting the current soil be covered with vegetation.

This way, when the Qing Dynasty was overthrown, this vegetation would turn into nutrients in the decaying soil, allowing the flowers he hoped for to bloom sooner.

Which transmigrator didn't have some ambition? Fallen flowers are not heartless things; they turn into spring mud to protect the flowers. Even if they end up at the same goal, as long as they are transmigrators with ideals and beliefs, who wouldn't want to leave something for China and let China take fewer detours?

Yinreng was curious about foreign merchants; Cao Yin originally thought Yinreng was just curious about the novel little gadgets of foreign merchants.

But the questions Yinreng asked became increasingly tricky, starting to ask about overseas colonies, political systems, royal structures, regime changes...

Cao Yin was sweating profusely: "This servant, this servant doesn't know about these things."

"You were still young when you left Zhili, so it's normal not to know. But you will eventually take over your father’s position, so you need to collect more of these things for Ama." Yinreng said, borrowing Kangxi’s name, "Those novel gadgets, with our craftsmen and technology, our Great Qing can also build them; Ama doesn't care for them. Do you understand?"

A chill ran down Cao Yin’s back: "This servant..."

"Alright, you don't understand." Yinreng shook his head like an old man, "I'll make it clearer. Ama wants to become an Emperor through the ages."

He pointed to the sky: "Above, there is the First Emperor who first unified China, whose virtue surpasses the Three Sovereigns and whose achievements cover the Five Emperors! No matter how later emperors toss and turn, they are only on this land unified by the First Emperor. In order to become an Emperor through the ages, Ama... ouch."

Yinreng clutched his head and looked down in confusion.

A small fruit was spinning on the ground.

Yinreng clutched his head and turned around in confusion.

Kangxi withdrew his hand from throwing the fruit, standing in the bushes, not knowing how long he had been listening.

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin immediately knelt to pay their respects, and other guards and palace attendants also knelt down in a messy fashion.

Only Yinreng clutched his head, condemning Kangxi with his eyes.

"Son’s head hasn't practiced Iron Head Kung Fu!" Yinreng was angry.

What is wrong with you! Why do you always hit my head! A child’s head is very fragile, I really will become stupid! Throwing dates at me won't work either!

Kangxi sneered, picked up his son, patted his bottom, and leaned into Yinreng’s ear, gritting his teeth and whispering: "Don't say what your grandfather taught you in front of outsiders! Do you hear me!"

What Emperor through the ages whose virtue surpasses the Three Sovereigns and whose achievements cover the Five Emperors, I haven't even thought about that! Except for Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Zhenzong of Song, which emperor dares to say that about himself! Do you think I am that shameless guy, Emperor Zhenzong of Song?!

Emperor Zhenzong of Song shamelessly went to Mount Tai to perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices, lowering the prestige of the Mount Tai sacrifices, causing later emperors to no longer perform them after visiting Mount Tai, only holding sacrificial ceremonies, for fear that someone would say, "You are just like that Emperor Zhenzong of Song."

Ama, you can't pin a label on your son just because you want to but haven't achieved it!

Son is already exhausted managing the vast Great Qing!

Or do you want me to be like Emperor Zhenzong of Song, bragging indiscriminately?! I can't afford to lose that face!!

33. Two chapters combined [V]

Time rewinds to the moment Kangxi spurred his horse away.

At this moment, the Eight Banners were still a legion of tough men who were considered half-crippled if they couldn't draw a bow of over ten strength. Don't look at Kangxi as if he looks like a pretty boy who could eat soft rice in later generations; his martial prowess could also rank among the tough men of the Eight Banners.

When emperors of previous dynasties hunted fierce beasts, they needed to have the beasts' teeth and claws pulled out, letting the beasts cooperate with the emperor in acting with their lives.

Kangxi didn't need to.

Bears, wolves, leopards, tigers—as long as they dared to appear, Kangxi could lead the tough men of the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Eight Banners to scatter their ashes.

Kangxi used to love this kind of bloody and exciting beast-hunting action.

Today, after shooting a few foxes and small deer, his hunting mood was getting thinner and thinner.

What is my son doing?

Did he encounter any danger?

Will he be scared if he encounters danger?

Will he call for Ama to save me if he is scared?

Bumping is bumping, pressing is pressing. My son must be proficient in riding and shooting in the future, so he should exercise now.

But will he be scared to have nightmares if he sees too bloody a scene?

It’s also not bad if he cries and hugs me when he has nightmares.

A battle between heaven and man was raging in Kangxi’s mind.

Fuquan asked: "Is Your Majesty worried about the Crown Prince?"

Kangxi looked at Fuquan in shock.

Brother! Since when were you so observant!

Fuquan laughed: "I am also worried about the Crown Prince."

Kangxi’s shocked expression turned into speechlessness.

He understood what his older brother meant. Fuquan meant that he wanted to take the Crown Prince to play, so he found an excuse to ask, not knowing he had stumbled upon the truth.

Kangxi said in a deep voice: "Where is the Crown Prince now?"

A little eunuch rode forward and told Kangxi the Crown Prince’s location and what he was doing.

Kangxi laughed and said to Mingzhu: "Your son can even weave flower wreaths and grass crickets? He is worthy of being the number one talent of our Great Qing."

Mingzhu: "...Thank you, Your Majesty?"

Should he thank him at this time? Was this a compliment? The old fox Mingzhu couldn't figure it out.

"You guys continue, I'll go see the Crown Prince." Kangxi dispersed the people around him, forbidding them from disturbing the Crown Prince. He only took Fuquan, Mingzhu, Songgotu, and a few confidants to find his son.

Changning was also driven away.

The other clansmen and nobles looked at Changning with intriguing eyes, which made Changning very angry.

When they were close to the place, Kangxi dismounted and walked on tiptoe along the trees.

Although the others didn't understand what Kangxi was doing, they followed suit, like old hunters hunting in the forest.

After Kangxi walked to a dense bush, he reached out his hand.

Zhao Chang immediately placed a magnificent, straight-barreled telescope into Kangxi’s hands.

Kangxi picked up the telescope. Heh heh, let Us see what Our son is up to!

The others: "???"

Only Fuquan understood Kangxi’s actions; he whispered, "Are there any more telescopes?"

After Kangxi nodded, Zhao Chang handed another telescope to Fuquan: "This is the only one the servant has left."

The others: "..." Regret. What are the Emperor and Prince Yu looking at?

Fuquan adjusted the focus of the telescope and said cheerfully, "That kid Cao Yin knows how to handle things; he’s already got a rabbit roasting."

Kangxi nodded: "Although he is occasionally boisterous, he is quite thorough in his work."

Fuquan added, "I didn't expect Rongruo to be so good with children. Mingzhu, why don't you let Rongruo give you a few more grandsons?"

Mingzhu: "..." He didn't know how to answer such nonsense.

Is it that I don't want Rongruo to have grandsons?

Besides, my Rongruo can't have grandsons!

Kangxi suddenly remembered something: "By the way, I once said I would let Rongruo serve as a guard for Baocheng, but I forgot during the busy New Year period. Baocheng is the same, he didn't even remind Me."

Mingzhu: "!!!" Your Majesty, please don't remember! I thought this matter had already been brushed aside, just a joke you made!

Songgotu looked dazed, as if he had suffered an unbearable blow in life.

With not many people following, Fuquan’s tone toward Kangxi was quite casual: "This is where Your Majesty is in the wrong. The Crown Prince is well-behaved and sensible; how could he take the initiative to ask you for things? He accepts what you give him voluntarily, but if you forget, he must think you have some unspeakable difficulty and, for the sake of your face, he certainly wouldn't ask."

Kangxi: "...What unspeakable difficulty could I have? But Baocheng is indeed too sensible."

Fuquan sighed: "Right? Such a sensible child is the easiest to be overlooked. If he doesn't cry or make a fuss, how can others know what he wants? If I had such a good child, I would be dying to pile all the best things in the Prince's mansion in front of him for him to choose. Sigh, of course, Your Majesty certainly cannot do that. The Crown Prince is the heir; he must set an example of frugality."

Kangxi: "...Yes, must set an example."

Kangxi looked at Fuquan silently.

Fuquan returned a questioning look.

Kangxi withdrew his gaze, feeling stifled.

In that moment, he felt as if he were seeing a larger version of Baoqing blabbering away.

Or rather, he felt as if he were seeing what Baoqing would look like when grown up.

How had he not noticed before that his eldest brother was quite adept at hitting a nerve?

Fuquan had no idea that Kangxi was associating him with the eldest prince back in the palace who was missing his younger brother. He was still nagging and sighing: "Your Majesty, the Crown Prince is so sensible and young, he probably doesn't know how to order servants around. It’s fortunate that you have always lent capable people to the Crown Prince to use; otherwise, if the Crown Prince were wronged, he wouldn't even know it himself, and would only think it was his own fault for not speaking up in time."

Songgotu finally found a topic he could interject into: "Prince Yu need not worry. The people in the Imperial Palace are all clever; as long as they serve for a long time, they can read the situation and know what the Crown Prince needs without the Crown Prince having to speak up."

Kangxi: "...Yes, that's right."

Come to think of it, after serving the Crown Prince for a long time, Liang Jiugong had once tactfully reported that the people serving the Crown Prince were not quick-handed because the Crown Prince disliked troubling others and rarely spoke.

Only when Gu Wenxing came to take the Crown Prince did those people have some order in their work because there was someone directing them.

Kangxi’s reaction at the time was to replace everyone again.

Kangxi began to feel guilty and shifted his anger. You, Liang Jiugong, I thought you were a clever person, but your report was unclear, causing the Crown Prince to be wronged!

However, Liang Jiugong had served the Crown Prince well, so he would not be punished for the time being.

Should I cultivate some long-term attendants for Baocheng? Otherwise, with Baocheng’s personality—a silent gourd who becomes mute the moment he leaves Me—the servants might really not serve him well.

Kangxi recalled when Yinreng was young, he would occasionally go hungry because he was too lazy to call for service.

It was only later, when Yinreng became fluent in speaking, that this stopped happening.

Kangxi’s heart was shaken severely, and he finally began to reflect on himself.

"The Crown Prince is too sensible; it is indeed easy for people to overlook him." Kangxi frowned, feeling extremely heartbroken.

He was busy with state affairs and not as meticulous as a woman in raising children. If Yinreng didn't say anything, there were some things he wouldn't think of.

But Yinreng was young and had a very considerate and sensible nature. Seeing him busy, he rarely made requests. Things that Kangxi didn't think of were just ignored like that.

"Last time when we went out shopping, I bought the Crown Prince a tiger-head hat, and the Crown Prince grinned the whole way." The more Fuquan spoke, the more he felt this was the case: "Your Majesty, no matter how frugal you are, you shouldn't be frugal with a child."

Kangxi said heavily: "That is correct."

The others, listening to the brothers Kangxi and Fuquan talk, all showed expressions of shock, as if to say, "What (muted) are you two talking about?"

Everyone in the capital knew that Kangxi doted on the Crown Prince excessively.

Whenever any tribute entered the palace, Kangxi would open the treasury and let the Crown Prince pick whatever he wanted.

News had also come out of the palace. When Kangxi was not in the palace, the Crown Prince would open Kangxi’s private treasury to bestow gifts in Kangxi’s name.

Not to mention daily food and clothing expenses; the Crown Prince had never once touched his own allowance. Regardless of whether Kangxi was in the palace or not, Kangxi’s allowance was sent directly to the Crown Prince to use, just as if Kangxi were present.

The Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager also frequently subsidized the Crown Prince from their own private treasuries, prioritizing the Crown Prince for everything delicious, useful, or fun.

Of course, the Crown Prince was indeed well-behaved, sensible, and frugal.

The private treasuries of the palace’s three giants were open to the Crown Prince, yet the Crown Prince did not care for those luxurious things.

Whenever he received a reward, the Crown Prince would always change the appearance of the gift and send it back as a token of filial piety.

But no matter what, the Crown Prince did not look like he was being abused, as Kangxi and Prince Yu described.

Kangxi and Fuquan, one after the other, made it sound as if Yinreng were a transparent person in the palace—yes, that kind of transparent child in a family with many children who is neither old nor young and particularly sensible.

The people around could only widen their eyes, using their gazes to express the inner cry of "I understand, but I am also deeply shocked."

Kangxi and Fuquan, while chattering away, quietly moved closer to where Yinreng was.

After getting close enough to hear Yinreng, Nalan Xingde, and Cao Yin talking, the two stopped their chatter and focused their ears to eavesdrop.

Zhao Chang quietly directed people to notify the guards, telling them not to make a sound or disturb Kangxi’s eavesdropping if they saw them.

Other trusted ministers of Kangxi followed suit, crouching down and curiously eavesdropping on the little Crown Prince.

When Yinreng pinned flowers on the two guards, the ministers secretly glanced at Kangxi.

Kangxi’s reputation suffered another blow.

When Yinreng asked about the affairs of Zhili, the ministers smiled knowingly.

The Crown Prince was indeed still a child, liking novel things.

When Yinreng shifted the topic to foreigners, inquiring about foreign regimes, royal families, and armies, asking questions that made Cao Yin break out in a cold sweat, the ministers also broke out in a cold sweat.

Is the Crown Prince really just a child?! They had never even thought of these things! How on earth did the Emperor raise this child!

Later, Yinreng pointed to the sky, his small body displaying boundless dominance: "My Khan Ama wants to be the Emperor of the Ages."

The ministers understood.

Surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors! So the Emperor’s ambition was this great! That’s why the Crown Prince, at such a young age...

Before they could finish their reflections, Kangxi casually fished a large jujube he had brought to quench his thirst from his waist and threw it accurately onto Yinreng’s little head.

The ministers: "..."

They looked at the Emperor of the Great Qing with condemning eyes.

You can't just hit a child’s head!

Listening to the Crown Prince’s complaints, this wasn't the first time you’ve hit him!

Kangxi pulled Yinreng into his arms and covered his mouth, and Fuquan started nagging again: "Your Majesty, how can you hit the Crown Prince’s head? A child’s head is very fragile! If you break it, won't your heart ache!"

Yinreng struggled hard to lift his head from Kangxi’s arms: "Right! What if my brain gets broken!"

"Fine, I won't hit your head next time, next time I'll spank your little bottom." After reflecting, Kangxi patted Yinreng’s bottom and threatened, "Stop talking nonsense, why do you say everything that comes to mind!"

Yinreng argued: "Guard Cao and Guard Nalan are not outsiders!"

He paused and added: "Or are they not insiders either?"

The crowd looked at the Emperor of the Great Qing with condemning eyes again.

The nonsense a child speaks is all taught by adults! What does a child know!

Kangxi’s reputation...

Forget it, let's stop thinking.

Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s cheeks and rubbed his head.

Kangxi’s trusted ministers watched the poor little Crown Prince being kneaded like dough by Kangxi without crying or making a fuss, and suddenly they believed Fuquan’s nonsense a little bit.

Is the little Crown Prince really too well-behaved? Is he really being bullied by wicked servants?

"Isn't Khan Ama hunting?" After being rubbed by Kangxi, Yinreng held his red, glowing cheeks and glared at Kangxi.

Yinreng’s posture of holding his face was too cute, and Kangxi couldn't help but rub it again: "I came specifically to see if you kid were up to no good."

Yinreng pointed at the rabbit that was almost roasted: "Did Khan Ama know we were roasting a rabbit and come over on purpose to eat our rabbit? Hmph, gluttonous Khan Ama."

Kangxi wanted to knock Yinreng’s head again.

However, having been scolded by so many people, he was worried about actually causing problems with Yinreng’s head, so he changed it to pinching Yinreng’s little nose: "Do I lack this one rabbit of yours?!"

Yinreng said: "Then... not eating?"

The aroma of the roasted rabbit wafted over, and Kangxi, who was in the prime of life and had just finished strenuous exercise, had his stomach growl.

Kangxi: "...Your stomach growled really loudly."

Yinreng despised: "Khan Ama, forced sophistry will only make you more... woo woo woo."

Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s two little lips, which were moving up and down, like pinching a duck’s beak: "Bring the roasted rabbit to Me!"

The guards and eunuchs immediately arranged for more barbecue.

A group of the country’s most important ministers sat on the ground, took out their beloved little daggers, and waited to eat meat.

This scene seemed very vulgar to the Han ministers, but Yinreng quite liked it.

"Come, I'll feed you." Kangxi took on the heavy responsibility of feeding the little Crown Prince.

Yinreng tilted his head, satisfying Kangxi’s hobby of feeding him.

It was just that when Kangxi accidentally dirtied his face, Yinreng would glare fiercely at Kangxi.

Kangxi would laugh out loud when glared at by his son, rubbing more oil onto Yinreng’s face.

Before one rabbit was finished, Yinreng had become a big oily face.

Fuquan couldn't watch anymore; he protected the Crown Prince and had the eunuchs wipe Yinreng’s face.

Kangxi continued to laugh out loud.

Yinreng glared at Kangxi while wiping his face. The current Kangxi was like a fool who only knew how to laugh.

The other trusted ministers couldn't help but smile.

If one set aside those political considerations, this little Crown Prince, even at a young age, already had the initial luster of a crown prince of the country.

He is worthy of being a Crown Prince raised personally by the Emperor.

Also, the little Crown Prince is really too cute! Why aren't my children/grandchildren this cute?

Even Mingzhu, who was struggling internally, couldn't help but reveal a kind smile.

"Rongruo." Kangxi had eaten three rabbits before barely feeling full, and while gnawing on a fruit, he said, "Come here."

Nalan Xingde immediately stepped forward.

"You will follow the Crown Prince for the time being." Kangxi tossed a token to Nalan Xingde, granting him permission to walk within the Forbidden City.

In the early Qing Dynasty, the rules of the inner palace were not strict. When there was an order from the Emperor, guards could even enter the inner palace.

Nalan Xingde was already a guard of the Qianqing Palace. With this token, as long as he was accompanied by the Crown Prince, Nalan Xingde could move unimpeded everywhere except for the East and West Six Palaces and the Cining Palace.

Kangxi thought for a moment and added: "If the Crown Prince wants to leave the palace, you can also take him out directly."

Yinreng jumped up: "Really! Khan Ama, why are you suddenly so good!"

Kangxi said: "You always hang out with Baoqing. Baoqing has to attend classes, where would he have so much time to accompany you? If you like to leave the palace, then go; consider it experiencing the lives of the people."

As the Crown Prince, it was necessary to understand the real lives of the people. Before Kangxi personally took over the government, he often went outside the palace to play. Now, even though he was busy with state affairs, he would still travel through the capital in disguise every once in a while.

Kangxi heard that Yinreng’s questions to Cao Yin today were very logical; although he complained that Shunzhi had snatched half of the work of teaching Yinreng, he had to sigh that Shunzhi was indeed worthy of being a person with the ambition of an "Emperor of the Ages," as the preparations were very thorough.

It was a pity that just as the preparations were finished, the person passed away.

A sigh.

After Kangxi accepted that Shunzhi was teaching Yinreng, he immediately thought about squeezing Shunzhi to the maximum.

Besides himself, was there anyone more suitable to teach Yinreng than Shunzhi?

Shunzhi was definitely more useful than any imperial tutor.

It is said that after a child reaches the age of six, they lose their ability to communicate with the heavens and earth, so Kangxi guessed that there wasn't much time left for Shunzhi to manifest.

Naturally, he had to take advantage of the time while Shunzhi was still around to let him teach Yinreng more.

Regarding matters of national economy and people’s livelihood, other ministers, even if they knew it in their hearts, would not speak too clearly to the Crown Prince without restraint. It was better to let Shunzhi teach him.

With Yinreng leaving the palace frequently, Shunzhi would definitely explain things outside the palace to him.

Kangxi thought for a moment and felt a bit uneasy about Nalan Xingde.

Although Nalan Xingde’s martial arts were good, he had been sickly in recent years; although he looked fine now, Kangxi was still worried.

He tossed another token to Cao Yin: "You are thorough in your work; protect the Crown Prince well."

Cao Yin immediately knelt to receive the order.

Kangxi then summoned Liang Jiugong and officially appointed him as Yinreng’s personal eunuch. When the Crown Prince left the palace, Liang Jiugong would attend to the Crown Prince’s side.

"Should we let Liang Jiugong learn a few moves from Eunuch Gu?" Yinreng had already given up on saving Liang Jiugong.

Ever since he took one more look at Liang Jiugong in the crowd, Liang Jiugong’s future had run away like a wild horse, further and further from his predetermined fate.

He could only try his best to be good to Liang Jiugong and teach him more skills.

If he had the chance to go to sea in the future, eunuchs could also make contributions.

"He should learn some." The head eunuchs around Kangxi all knew how to ride, shoot, and wrestle; the head eunuch around Yinreng naturally had to learn some skills too.

Liang Jiugong was extremely excited and kowtowed repeatedly to thank him.

Serving the Crown Prince was dangerous, but wealth was sought in danger. He had gone from a low-level eunuch to a capable person by the Crown Prince’s side; this span was something many people in the palace envied.

After Kangxi finished his instructions, he pointed to the important ministers around him: "You can go to their homes to play as you please, but you must return before the palace gates are locked, understand? Don't be greedy for play."

Yinreng threw himself into Kangxi’s arms and rubbed against him hard: "Got it! I’m very well-behaved! Khan Ama is the best Ama in the world! Baocheng loves you!"

"What nonsense are you talking, aren't you ashamed?" Kangxi smiled so wide that eight teeth were exposed, "In front of outsiders, pay attention to some etiquette."

The people around saw Kangxi telling Yinreng to pay attention to etiquette while picking him up and rubbing his cheeks against him, and they all wanted to hold their foreheads.

The Emperor’s hypocrisy was already a terminal illness; it couldn't be cured.

"You must come to Uncle’s place to play more often." Fuquan said with a kind smile, "Even if Uncle isn't home, come play; your Aunt really wants to see you."

Yinreng nestled in Kangxi’s arms and said: "Okay, I will definitely come to bother Uncle."

Kangxi looked at Songgotu, who was full of anticipation but dared not speak, and his heart softened: "You should also go to the Hesheli mansion to take a look."

Songgotu’s nose soured, and he almost couldn't hold back his tears.

He nodded vigorously: "Crown Prince, Crown Prince, please come to this old minister’s home to take a look, okay?" Woo woo woo.

Even Mingzhu, Songgotu’s old rival, couldn't help but look away, feeling sympathy for Songgotu, who was being shunned by the Crown Prince.

Yinreng said seriously: "Has the family style of Lord Song’s house been corrected? Are your younger brothers still neglecting their duties? Will they ruin the reputation of my Niang’s family? The reputation of the maternal relatives affects my Niang’s reputation; if you don't correct it, Gu will never acknowledge you as a relative!"

Kangxi: "..." He felt many stinging gazes.

This pot... should I carry it?

Songgotu immediately knelt and kowtowed, choking with sobs: "This old minister will change, this old minister is changing, this old minister will absolutely not insult the reputation of Empress Renxiao."

These words were too serious and scared Songgotu.

Their family had been acting arrogantly and domineeringly, relying on their status as the Empress’s maternal relatives and the merit of helping to overthrow Oboi. Now that the Crown Prince said such things, it must be Kangxi using the Crown Prince’s mouth to reprimand them.

If he didn't change, the Hesheli family would still be the Empress’s maternal family, but he, Songgotu, would no longer be a member of the Empress’s maternal family.

There was nothing more serious than this.

Yinreng glanced at the other important ministers: "You are the same. If Gu sees you doing improper things when I go out of the palace, I will immediately report it to Khan Ama. Now that the Great Qing is in a troubled autumn, Khan Ama trusts you, but you make things difficult for Khan Ama; Gu will definitely not spare you lightly."

Yinreng puffed out his chest: "Gu wants to protect Khan Ama!"

The ministers immediately knelt and kowtowed.

Kangxi smiled extremely proudly: "That’s right, if you encounter any unfair things, just come and tell Me. I will appoint you as a little Censor."

The ministers: "..." Your Majesty! You can't! You can't indulge the Crown Prince like this!

Fuquan stroked his beard and said: "It should be so."

The ministers: "..." It should be so your head! Prince Yu, can you shut up!

Nalan Rongruo and Cao Yin looked at each other, their pupils trembling slightly.

Although the Crown Prince is young, he seems very good at causing trouble?!!

This is definitely not a good job!!!

...

The Jingshan hunt ended, and the precocious Yinreng and the impulsive Kangxi stirred up the situation in the capital, causing undercurrents and unrest.

The playboys in the capital were reprimanded by their families, and there was wailing everywhere.

Mingzhu was overwhelmed because his eldest son became a guard by the Crown Prince’s side, and the imperial clan and nobles were all making sarcastic remarks, accusing him of secretly defecting to the Crown Prince.

Songgotu was even more overwhelmed than Mingzhu. He urged his family to keep a low profile, only to find that his family had been led by him to be arrogant and domineering, and now that it was difficult to correct immediately, he realized that it was hard to change deep-seated habits.

Only Fuquan returned to his mansion happily, telling his wife the good news that the Crown Prince would definitely visit soon.

Kangxi became busy again, leaving the Forbidden City to wander around, preparing for the complete pacification of the remnants of the Three Feudatories.

Yinreng jumped onto Yinzhi’s back and said loudly: "Brother! I got the token to leave the palace! Khan Ama is not here, will you accompany me out of the palace!"

Yinzhi immediately threw his pen: "Then what are you waiting for!"

100,000

34. Two updates in one [V]

With Kangxi not in the palace, the two bear children, under the doting of the Grand Empress Dowager, were like the monkey king in a monkey mountain, with no one able to control them at all.

After Nalan Xingde was thrown to Yinreng, he had to report to the Qianqing Palace every day to take care of the children.

Today, as soon as he started his shift, he heard the bad news.

"The Eldest Prince also wants to leave the palace? Does the Emperor agree?" Nalan Xingde tactfully refused.

Yinreng held up the token: "I agree!"

Yinzhi crossed his arms: "The Grand Empress Dowager agrees."

Nalan Xingde: "...This minister will go find Cao Yin, the Crown Prince and the Eldest Prince please wait a moment."

Nalan Xingde really didn't want to take the Eldest Prince out of the palace. Just the Crown Prince alone was enough to give him a headache so severe he couldn't even be sentimental. Adding an Eldest Prince with a "great reputation," could the little bun on the back of his head still be safe?

He didn't want to become a monk, but he was being forced to become one!

But what could he do?

The Emperor was away, the Grand Empress Dowager was indulgent, what could he do?

Nalan Xingde wanted to recite a poem to express his inner distress, but found that in the process of accompanying the bear children, his inspiration had temporarily dried up.

Nalan Xingde: Sad.

Cao Yin was also quite sad.

He looked at his fellow sufferer and said kindly: "After the Eldest Prince leaves the palace, you must not run around. The streets are a bit chaotic; if you get kidnapped by human traffickers..."

"Alright, alright, I know, no need to nag, hurry up and leave the palace!" Yinzhi waved his sleeve, very impatient.

It was already quite late; after leaving the palace, they would go for lunch first, and after lunch, they wouldn't be able to play for long before having to return. This person was actually nagging and wasting time!

Cao Yin’s heart skipped a beat, and his chest hurt a little.

The Eldest Prince was indeed not easy to deal with, not listening to people at all. He could only keep a close eye on the Eldest Prince.

Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde exchanged a sorrowful look.

While Kangxi in the distance sneezed several times, having a bad premonition and looking toward the capital from afar, Yinzhi and Yinreng had already boarded the carriage to leave the palace.

They had changed into the clothes of ordinary wealthy families, and their first stop was the most famous restaurant in the city.

Yinzhi often accompanied Yinreng to play with his two younger brothers. To prevent bumping into his brothers, Yinzhi was accustomed to not wearing jewelry or jade pendants.

Now he was hung with so much that he looked like a jewelry rack, which made him particularly unhappy.

Yinzhi pulled at the gold and gemstone safety lock on his neck, adjusted the gold-inlaid jade belt at his waist, and tugged at the palace tassels with gemstones and gold beads at the hem of his clothes, his face getting uglier: "I am impatient with these things."

Just now, Yinreng had hugged Yinzhi out of habit and was poked by the gold and silver jewelry all over Yinzhi, leaving red marks on his face.

"Eldest Prince, dressing more richly makes it safer to go out." Cao Yin advised, "If you are too simple, not to mention that human traffickers might target you, others might also offend the Eldest Prince out of ignorance."

Yinzhi frowned tightly: "Who would offend me? Isn't that just right? I’ll help Khan Ama rectify the atmosphere!"

Cao Yin: "..." How was he supposed to answer that?

"Big Brother, hold hands." Yinreng grabbed Yinzhi’s hand, "It’s okay, I’m also a little jewelry person. We are the two jewelry brothers."

Yinzhi looked at the gemstone headband and gemstone hat on Yinreng’s head, and his expression turned from cloudy to sunny: "Okay. Come sit next to me, the carriage is bumpy, be careful not to fall."

"Mm-hmm." Yinreng sat obediently next to Yinzhi, his two short legs not reaching the bottom of the carriage, dangling as the carriage rattled.

Yinzhi couldn't sit still. After sitting in the carriage for a while, he began to look for faults with Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin.

Yinzhi had now (forced) read many books, and he heard that Nalan Xingde was touted as the greatest talent of the Great Qing, so he wanted to test whether Nalan Xingde was really capable.

With Yinzhi’s limited reading, it was obviously impossible to test Nalan Xingde.

Yinzhi nodded reservedly: "You’re okay, better than Mingzhu."

Nalan Xingde: "..." He didn't even dare to thank him for these words.

Yinreng reminded: "Big Brother, don't belittle his father in front of his son; he doesn't dare to answer. If he answers and it gets spread out, it’s unfilial."

Yinzhi misunderstood; he glared at Cao Yin: "What?! You want to spread my words?! You want to snitch?!"

Cao Yin, who was shot for no reason: "???"

Nalan Xingde couldn't help but laugh, his shoulders trembling.

Cao Yin sighed: "No, no, I won't. The Crown Prince means that Big Brother should be careful when speaking outside later; there are many people and many mouths."

"Oh." Yinzhi said coldly.

Cao Yin: "..." Although the Eldest Prince didn't say anything, why did he feel it was so infuriating?!

Cao Yin decided that he would never badmouth the little Crown Prince again. He had only just come into contact with the Eldest Prince and deeply felt how well-behaved and sensible the little Crown Prince was.

Seeing that Yinzhi didn't think much of Cao Yin, Yinreng squeezed Yinzhi’s hand and said: "Big Brother, you should also test Cao Ziqing. Ziqing’s knowledge is also very profound. Their ancestors can be traced back to the Cao family of the Three Kingdoms."

"Really?" Yinzhi was a bit interested, "Is it the Cao Mengde Cao family of 'I love other people's wives'?"

Cao Yin: "???"

Nalan Xingde: "???"

Their group had only just set off, and the little question marks on Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde’s heads were almost drowning the carriage.

Eldest Prince, who taught you this?! It couldn't be the master who taught you to read, right?!

Yinreng said awkwardly: "Um... um, that’s it."

Sorry, I reflect. When I tell stories to Big Brother, I often slip up.

Yinzhi asked curiously: "Cao Yin, do you also love other people's wives?"

Cao Yin: "I..."

Nalan Xingde’s shoulders started trembling again.

Yinshi said seriously and sternly, "Our Great Qing doesn't have that many rules, but if you want a wife, you should seek to marry a widow; don't go around forcibly seizing women. Like Cao Mengde, who would send men to snatch away the mothers and wives of his soldiers to be paired off and bear children the moment the soldiers marched out—that is not acceptable."

Cao Yin gave a wry smile: "I do not have a penchant for other men's wives, I really don't."

Yinshi looked a bit regretful: "So you didn't inherit that trait from Cao Mengde."

Cao Yin: "..." What, what exactly was I supposed to inherit?! When people hear the name Cao, don't they usually think of their literary talent??

Yinshi continued: "Cao Mengde... so what is the use of benevolence and virtue? Take Uncle Liu (Liu Bei), he was benevolent and virtuous enough, right? In the official histories compiled by the Wei and Jin dynasties, he is the only one who never slaughtered a city. Cao Mengde could be called wicked to the core. But what about later generations? Uncle Liu was benevolent his whole life without any major stains, so it must be hypocrisy; Cao Mengde slaughtered cities, slept with other men's wives, and forced women whose husbands were still alive to remarry frequently for the sake of population growth, changing husbands as soon as they gave birth..."

Yinshi paused and sighed: "It's one thing to call Cao Mengde a hero, but now people are starting to praise him for being 'authentic' and 'not hypocritical.' As long as you succeed, countless people will speak well of you. History is written by the victors, nothing more. So regardless of the means, as long as you win, it's fine."

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin were extremely surprised.

They had originally thought the First Prince was just an ignorant child, but they didn't expect him to be capable of such insights.

Yinzhi felt proud.

That's right! The one who taught the First Prince is none other than yours truly!

I don't want to be the Crown Prince; I want to change careers and become a tutor to the princes!

Which transmigrator doesn't have some grand ambitions? Changing the future starts with the children!

"The First Prince's words are very true," Nalan Xingde said. "If Cao Mengde had failed, his stains would likely have been reviled for ten thousand generations. It is precisely because he succeeded that his stains have become minor flaws that can be overlooked on the road to success."

Cao Yin rubbed his nose.

All the Caos in the world can be traced back to the same family a few hundred years ago, so he decided not to touch that topic.

Yinshi asked again: "The Great Qing is the same now. In your opinion..."

"Ahem." Yinzhi gave a crisp cough, interrupting Yinshi's words. "Brother, don't ask them this. These things should be asked of Khan Ama; let Ama think about them."

Yinshi nodded: "Right. That's true, if we think it all through, what would Khan Ama have to think about?"

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin wiped the cold sweat from their foreheads.

Although they didn't know what question Yinshi had been about to ask, both Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin felt as if they had escaped a disaster.

Cao Yin immediately changed the subject, talking about delicious food and fun things outside the palace to divert Yinshi's attention.

But Yinshi didn't give Cao Yin any face.

The delicious and fun things Cao Yin talked about weren't as interesting as what his own Crown Prince brother said.

Since his Crown Prince brother said he should test Cao Yin, he had to test him.

Thus, Yinshi continued as the examiner, and Cao Yin answered the questions with a look of helplessness.

Although Cao Yin was not yet "learned enough to fill five carts" at his age, he could still be considered a leader among the youth.

Yinshi was very satisfied with the test and changed his address to calling Cao Yin "Cao Ziqing."

He even reminded Cao Yin, "Ziqing, are you really sure you don't have a penchant for other men's wives?"

Cao Yin: "...No, I really don't!"

He was a bit worried; with the First Prince blabbering away like this, his reputation would be ruined!

Nalan Xingde was just watching Cao Yin's predicament when Yinshi's gaze turned to him.

Nalan Xingde immediately sat up straight, sensing that something was about to go wrong.

Yinshi said: "Nalan Xingde, was that poem of yours, 'If life could always be like the first time we met,' really not written for a woman in the palace? There are even rumors that you wrote it for my mother."

Nalan Xingde wanted to jump out of the carriage on the spot.

"That's not true! Who said that?!" I'm going to go kill them! How can they spread such rumors!

Yinshi said: "It was Khan Ama. When Khan Ama mentioned this interesting story to my mother and was joking with her, he listed everyone related to the Nara clan, including my mother."

Nalan Xingde: "...That didn't happen. I really wrote that poem for a friend."

"Oh, then you let that guy named..." Yinshi looked at Yinzhi.

Yinzhi said: "Gu Zhenguan."

Yinshi said: "Next time, have that Gu Zhenguan come over too. I want to test him. Even I think the poem is good; it's a shame it wasn't written for my mother."

Nalan Xingde was already speechless.

Cao Yin asked curiously: "Doesn't this slander reflect poorly on the Concubine's reputation?"

"Why poorly? It's great. Nalan Xingde admires my mother, what does that have to do with my mother who entered the palace so early?" Yinshi said as if it were a matter of course. "It just shows my mother has a good reputation. Even Khan Ama doesn't mind."

Yinzhi: "..." Actually, it's because it didn't happen that Ama could joke with Concubine Hui so casually.

Nalan Xingde: "..." Just let me die.

Cao Yin: "..." Compared to Rongruo, my reputation damage doesn't seem that serious anymore.

People only find comfort through comparison.

Fortunately, Yinzhi was quick-witted and pulled Yinshi's runaway thoughts back in time.

He hadn't expected Yinshi's curiosity to be so off-base.

If Ama and Concubine Hui found out about this, the eldest brother's backside would definitely be in for a beating.

This time, it would definitely not be a punishment that could be avoided by writing a few big characters.

However, Yinzhi didn't expect that while he had a slip of the tongue, Ama was also prone to them.

Ama actually gossiped with Concubine Hui about Nalan Xingde and even let his son listen in? This father of his was really unreliable.

Yinshi had probably heard too many stories and was particularly interested in gossip.

Since Yinzhi wouldn't let him wreak havoc on Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin anymore, he started asking about the gossip of other people in the capital.

Especially the gossip about the inner chambers; that was simply too interesting.

It is said that one can see a person's true nature by looking at their inner chambers. No matter how glamorous they are on the outside, if their inner chambers are a mess, that person is definitely no good.

Nalan Xingde breathed a sigh of relief.

His father and mother were a devoted couple, and his inner chambers were very peaceful, which was rare among the powerful in the capital. This gossip wouldn't reach his house.

Cao Yin also breathed a sigh of relief.

The Cao family was far from the capital, so this gossip had nothing to do with them.

Neither of them knew about the inner affairs of the powerful in the capital, nor did they want to know.

Since Yinshi was curious, they could only talk about the marital relationships of the powerful in the capital.

When they mentioned that the Tong family and the Hesheli family also had intentions of intermarriage, Yinzhi, who was feeling drowsy from the gossip, felt his eyelids jump.

"The Hesheli family?" Yinzhi looked at Cao Yin, who had brought this up.

Cao Yin immediately said: "It's just a side branch of the Hesheli."

Although it was a side branch, it wasn't that far removed. Otherwise, how could they be a match for Concubine Tong's own younger brother, Longkodo?

The only Hesheli clan that could intermarry with the rising Tongjia clan nowadays was the one from Soni's line.

The Hesheli woman who married Longkodo was that poor original wife who, in later generations, was "treated like a human pig."

Yinzhi remembered this, and darkness churned in his heart.

Everyone said this was the evil deed of Li Si'er, but if a clear-headed person thought about it, how could a woman in the inner chambers influence Longkodo's behavior?

Li Si'er's evil was just following Longkodo's preferences, doing what Longkodo dared not do himself.

The fate of the Hesheli woman was known even to the Crown Prince, who had already been placed under house arrest.

How could he not know?

Just like Nersu breaking into the Hesheli house to whip the servants after Songgotu's death, Longkodo killing his own original wife was also for political purposes.

But that Hesheli woman knew this clearly, yet refused to die.

She kept gritting her teeth and living, living through all the humiliation, living until everyone saw her miserable state, using her tragedy to impeach Longkodo.

She could not commit suicide; she had to die at the hands of Longkodo and Li Si'er.

Yongzheng killed Longkodo for political purposes as well. But when Longkodo fell, everyone pushed him, and many officials who had nothing to do with him wanted him dead, citing the crime of "treating his original wife like a human pig."

The Hesheli woman's son, Yuexing'a, was also protected in Longkodo's case because of this specific charge.

A wise woman, who had already seen her husband's end when he was at the height of his power, used everything she had to take revenge on her husband and protect her son.

"Brother, what's wrong? Do you not like the Hesheli woman who is going to marry, or do you not like Longkodo? Tell me, brother will help you beat them up!" Seeing Yinzhi clench his fists, Yinshi immediately said.

Yinzhi shook his head and said: "I'm fine, it's nothing, it has nothing to do with them. Brother, I remembered that my maternal grandfather is seriously ill. Will you accompany me to see him?"

Yinshi's eyes widened: "What? Is Songgotu dying?"
