41. Three Chapters in One (10,000 Nutrient Solution Bonus) [V]

On the 15th day of the seventh month of the 18th year of Kangxi, Prince Chun, Longxi, passed away. His posthumous title was "Jing."

The Empress Dowager was deeply saddened and tried several times to attend the funeral in person, but was dissuaded by Kangxi.

Kangxi also wanted to attend the funeral, but was dissuaded by the Empress Dowager. The Empress Dowager kept Kangxi in the Cining Palace.

Yinreng, who had been moved from the Qianqing Palace to the Cining Palace by Kangxi, peeked out quietly.

Wuku Mama and Ama, you dissuade me, I dissuade you—it's quite interesting.

Kangxi was feeling sorrowful when he saw Yinreng peeking at the door. He gasped: "Baocheng! Aren't you supposed to be lying down and recovering from your illness!"

Seeing that Kangxi had discovered him, Yinreng turned and ran.

Kangxi waved his imperial hand, and several strong eunuchs rushed out from the corner, carrying Yinreng back before him.

"Bao... cheng!" Kangxi slapped the armrest of his chair hard.

Yinreng leaned in, held Kangxi's hand, and blew on it. After one puff, he looked up at Kangxi: "Blow, blow, the pain flies away, Ama won't hurt anymore."

Kangxi kept a straight face: "Do you think that if you try to please me, I won't punish you!"

Yinreng blew on Kangxi's hand again: "It's not to please you, I'm just worried that Ama's hand hurts."

The Empress Dowager, who had been grieving, couldn't help but laugh as she watched the interaction between her grandson and great-grandson.

"Come to Wuku Mama. Wuku Mama will protect you, he won't dare to punish you." The Empress Dowager beckoned to Yinreng, "Are you not sleepy anymore?"

Yinreng threw himself into the Empress Dowager's arms and rubbed against her: "Not sleepy anymore, I've slept enough."

The Empress Dowager let Yinreng lean against her and sit properly: "As long as you're not sleepy."

Although the Empress Dowager was smiling, she felt very worried inside.

The imperial physicians had tactfully stated that the Crown Prince was so young yet had already worried and exhausted himself so many times; in the long run, it would be bad for his health.

The Western doctors were even more blunt, saying that fainting from exhaustion during childhood would lower his immune system and likely lead to a weak and sickly constitution in adulthood.

The Empress Dowager rubbed the little bun on top of Yinreng's head, helped him undo the loose bun, and braided it into a small pigtail: "Are you hungry? Wuku Mama has prepared lots of delicious food."

Yinreng shook his head and said to Kangxi: "Is Ama worried? I want to go pay my respects to Uncle..."

"You are not allowed to go!" Kangxi scolded with a dark face. "I told you to rest properly. If you don't listen again, you won't be allowed to play with Baoqing and the others!"

Yinreng pouted: "Hmph, bad Ama. Baocheng wants to see Uncle off."

"It's enough that Baocheng has the heart." The Empress Dowager gently patted Yinreng's back. "Your Majesty, there is much to do today. You should rest and go tomorrow."

Kangxi: "..." Just a moment ago, you told me not to go, but as soon as Baocheng says he wants to go, you agree to let me go?

"Baocheng, stay here and keep Wuku Mama company, alright?" the Empress Dowager said kindly.

Yinreng nodded: "Okay. Baocheng will keep Wuku Mama company. Wuku Mama, don't be sad."

The Empress Dowager hugged Yinreng, calling him her heart and soul, her dear grandson.

Kangxi: "..." I am the Empress Dowager's grandson; Baocheng is your great-grandson.

Kangxi's face couldn't stay dark anymore.

He stood up, walked over to the Empress Dowager and Yinreng, and lifted Yinreng, who was acting spoiled in the Empress Dowager's arms.

Yinreng was held under the armpits by Kangxi and lifted to eye level.

He tilted his head, kicked his short legs, and flapped his two little arms: "Wua! Fly, fly!"

Kangxi, who had been preparing to tell Yinreng to rest well, finally couldn't help but be amused by Yinreng.

He lifted Yinreng high: "Alright, fly, fly."

After flying the little chubby boy twice, Kangxi hugged his son back into his own arms.

The Empress Dowager looked at Kangxi with an indescribable expression.

The Emperor's possessiveness over the Crown Prince is a bit too much. I also want to hold the soft, warm, and fragrant Baocheng.

After being stirred up by Yinreng, the sadness of the Empress Dowager and Kangxi faded quite a bit.

Longxi had been bedridden for a long time, and they had long been mentally prepared, so it was easy for the sadness to dissipate.

Kangxi's heavy heart now wasn't because of Longxi, but because of Yinreng—or rather, the "great upheaval of the earth dragon" in the capital predicted by Shunzhi.

As an autocratic emperor, it wouldn't be difficult for Kangxi to make earthquake preparations in advance under the guise of an ancestor's dream or a prediction from the Imperial Observatory.

But is this prophecy true?

If the earthquake didn't come, his prestige as an emperor wouldn't be lowered; he could just execute a few scapegoats for "misinterpreting the divination." After the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, the national treasury was empty, and he would feel pained by the waste of resources, but the loss would be controllable and at most cause some panic, which he could suppress.

Kangxi hoped even more that the earthquake wouldn't come.

If the earthquake did come, the already strained treasury would be hit even harder. Even with preparations, it would only reduce losses and alleviate the chaos; there was actually little Kangxi could do.

Compared to the losses, the bit of prestige gained from a "successful divination" was unimportant.

There were fifteen days left until the end of the seventh month. Every moment of these fifteen days, Kangxi was in agony.

Kangxi hugged Yinreng, buried his head in his son's shoulder, and took a deep breath.

Hmm, his mood felt much lighter after "inhaling" his son.

Yinreng was already used to Kangxi's "cat-inhaling" behavior. His use to Kangxi was probably the same as a kitten's—every time he was in a bad mood, he would "inhale" the cat to restore his health points.

Kangxi didn't tell Yinreng about the anxiety in his heart.

He put on a calm front in front of Yinreng, acting as if "it's just an earthquake, a small matter, Ama has everything under control." No matter how panicked he was, he couldn't let his son find out.

Yinreng had already fainted once; what if he got anxious and fainted again?

In Kangxi's eyes, every time Yinreng fainted, his lifespan was reduced by one; this was more unbearable to him than waiting for the earthquake.

The next day, a worried Kangxi attended Longxi's funeral in person and then suspended the morning court for three days on the grounds of excessive grief.

During the suspension, Kangxi summoned his trusted ministers and told them about his ancestor's dream.

"The Imperial Observatory's divination results are consistent with the ancestor's dream," Kangxi said sternly.

He took the "ancestor's dream" upon himself; this would not only increase his prestige but also protect Yinreng.

Although the miracle of the "ancestor's dream" could temporarily make Yinreng's position as Crown Prince more stable, ministers who opposed the Crown Prince would definitely use this to "praise him to death," deliberately building up Yinreng's momentum to create a rift between him and his son.

Furthermore, they might ask Yinreng to "divine" everything, and if Yinreng made a mistake, they would label him a sinner who harmed the country and the people.

Now, it was Kangxi himself who received the ancestor's dream. Kangxi wanted to see if anyone dared to put him on the fire to roast.

The ministers looked at each other, wanting to say that divination was unreliable, but they didn't dare.

But they also didn't dare to take the responsibility of warning the entire capital based on a dream and a divination, which would cause widespread panic.

The people in the court were all very shrewd. If the warning was successful, the credit would all go to the Emperor; if it failed, they would definitely be pushed out as scapegoats.

Songgotu and Changtai were also among the summoned ministers.

Although Changtai was mostly idle at home, he held the position of Minister of the Imperial Guard, nominally in charge of the palace guards. Preparations for the earthquake warning also needed to be made within the palace. His presence in the Qianqing Palace did not attract the attention of others.

Kangxi had strict control over those around him. People in the capital could not fully grasp his whereabouts. Several times he and the Crown Prince traveled together, and others thought only the Crown Prince went to Gabula's mansion.

Even if someone in the capital discovered this, they would only think Kangxi was worried about Gabula's illness, a sign of him valuing his father-in-law; no one would think Kangxi valued a young man in his early twenties so much.

Changtai had never shown his abilities outside; even Songgotu didn't know how much talent his eldest nephew had, let alone outsiders.

After Kangxi proposed the ancestor's warning, the ministers were all deep in thought, and Songgotu's face also showed a grave expression.

Songgotu was arrogant but cautious in his actions, which was why he opposed the withdrawal of the Three Feudatories.

Compared to guessing the Emperor's intentions, Songgotu had such a high status partly because of the Heseri surname, but mostly because of his talent.

Regarding the withdrawal of the Three Feudatories, Mingju jumped the highest to guess the Emperor's intentions; but during the rebellion, Songgotu, while shouting to kill Mingju, organized the suppression of the rebellion in an orderly manner, contributing more than Mingju.

Songgotu was exactly the kind of person Kangxi found most difficult to swallow—talented and capable, but too arrogant. He trusted his own judgment more than following the Emperor's wishes, so he often went against the Emperor on many things.

This time was the same; as soon as Songgotu thought about the difficulty and consequences of an earthquake warning, he wanted to stand up and oppose it.

If the Emperor was afraid of death, he should just deal with it within the palace. For people outside the palace, even if they died, it was their own responsibility. There was no need for the Emperor to let the Qing court take that responsibility for a warning.

Just as Songgotu lifted his foot, Changtai had already taken two quick steps, stepped out of the line, and knelt down: "Your Majesty, I have something to report."

Kangxi saw that his trusted ministers were all full of melancholy, and even Nalan Mingju, who was best at guessing the Emperor's intentions, didn't dare to speak; he was feeling frustrated.

Changtai, who usually didn't say a word, was the first to step out. Kangxi pondered for a moment, tapped his finger on the armrest of the dragon chair, and said: "Proceed."

Changtai knelt on the ground and spoke eloquently.

Earthquake prediction had already become a field of study overseas. People had researched where earthquakes were likely to occur, what signs might appear before an earthquake, how to protect oneself during an earthquake, and how to avoid secondary disasters after an earthquake.

When Yinreng was secretly teaching Changtai through Gabula, he guided Changtai to study overseas knowledge about earthquakes.

Yinreng had long known that there would be a major earthquake in the capital this year. Besides playing the "god" to tell Kangxi, how could he not make preparations in other aspects?

Gabula and Changtai didn't care that Yinreng was just a child; while convinced of Yinreng's miraculous nature, they didn't dig into the root of it. They only pledged their loyalty to Yinreng and helped him do things he couldn't do at the moment.

Helping Kangxi deal with the earthquake in the capital was the first major task Yinreng gave to Gabula and Changtai. Changtai had put a lot of effort into this.

"According to Western research and the folk experience of the Qing Dynasty, there will definitely be strange phenomena before an earthquake. If Your Majesty says it is an ancestor's warning, the common people and low-level officials might not take it seriously and refuse to carry it out properly. I suggest sending officials to collect reports of strange animal behavior near the capital to warn the public..."

Changtai didn't say whether he "believed" or "didn't believe"; he directly began to explain specific measures in a clear and logical way.

After the dual guidance of Gabula and Yinreng, he knew that Kangxi proposing this in front of the ministers was not a question of "to do or not to do," but a search for a way to solve the problem.

How to reduce panic while also mitigating the losses from the earthquake? This was what Kangxi cared about.

Everything else was nonsense in Kangxi's heart; arguments based on nonsense were just behaviors that consumed Kangxi's patience and increased his anger.

"Use the ancestor's warning and the Imperial Observatory's divination as a lead, supplemented by folk experience, and let the people verify for themselves whether there are earthquake signs around them. They don't need to be told what to do; they will move on their own..."

"Grain and money cannot be crushed; they can be moved from the national treasury to local warehouses under heavy guard. If an earthquake comes, disaster relief can be carried out at the fastest speed; if it doesn't come, it can also be transported to the front lines, reducing the transport time for front-line supplies..."

"Brick and tile houses in the palace and the capital might crush people and livestock. Livestock can be moved to grass sheds or tied outside, which doesn't take much effort; send more low-level officials to patrol and beat the night watch, and usually, they can shout about fire prevention at night. If they feel an earthquake is coming, they can immediately beat gongs to let people escape, which can also prevent crowd chaos..."

After Changtai finished his suggestions in an orderly manner, he said shyly: "I have been nursing my illness at home and love to study overseas works when I have nothing to do. Places like Portugal often have earthquakes. Several missionaries I have been in contact with have experienced earthquakes and told me a lot."

The missionaries Changtai mentioned were the "Western divine doctors" sent by Kangxi to Gabula's mansion to provide long-term medical care.

Under Yinreng's hint, Changtai asked the Western doctors to teach him Western languages, and as they talked, they drifted to earthquakes. The Western doctors gave Changtai many natural science books related to earthquakes.

This happened shortly after the Western doctors arrived. In addition to giving Changtai natural science books related to earthquakes, the Western doctors also gave other books. When Kangxi came to Changtai to vent his emotional baggage, he often studied these natural science books with Changtai.

As soon as Changtai mentioned it, Kangxi remembered these things.

At that time, he and Changtai were drinking and talking about relying on Western books to find mineral deposits in the West to feed the Qing Dynasty.

Now, there hadn't been an opportunity to look for minerals, but the knowledge about earthquakes had come in handy.

Kangxi and Changtai exchanged a look of mutual understanding, their hearts fluttering like a deer.

This metaphor was correct. Kangxi's mood now was like being in love—both secretly happy and proud.

When everyone else was worried, he and a minister not only had a tacit understanding, but they also happened to have discovered the solution to this matter together in advance.

Those self-important ministers were still racking their brains, while they could tacitly provide solutions one by one, catching those old foxes off guard.

Was there anything more exciting than this?

Kangxi finally understood why the letters from emperors in history to their trusted ministers were so mushy, why they ate and lived with their ministers, and why they cried more bitterly after a minister died than when an empress died.

Kangxi had initially felt the taste of having a partner and confidant helping him.

He wanted to get drunk with Changtai again right now and sleep side-by-side!

"Grant a seat." Kangxi and Changtai began to act.

Kangxi pretended to know nothing and asked Changtai why he knew these things.

Changtai also pretended that Kangxi knew nothing and pushed everything onto the teachings of the seriously ill Gabula and even the Songgotu beside him.

Songgotu was full of confusion and bewilderment, almost writing on his face: "Who am I, where am I, I really don't know anything."

Mingju, who knew Songgotu very well, muttered in his heart: Is Songgotu's confused look faked or real? Is Songgotu taking a roundabout route, starting to push his nephew out to occupy the high ground of the court?

Kangxi followed Changtai's words, summoned the Westerners who had studied earthquakes, and brought over a pile of Western books.

"I'll trouble you all to rest in the Qianqing Palace for the next few days." Kangxi kept all his trusted ministers and studied with them.

Other ministers had missionaries as translators, but Kangxi and Changtai were alone, whispering directly without a translator, which made people extremely envious.

They wondered if they should also learn a foreign language.

Although they looked down on those foreigners, it could please the Emperor.

Mingju, who was respected by the court as "most considerate of the Emperor's heart," had already made up his mind. The Heseri family had shamelessly pushed out someone who liked Western learning to cater to the Emperor's interests, so their family had to have one too.

His eldest son, Nalan Xingde... forget it, Rongruo should stick to his Sinology. His second son was still young, so he had to do it himself? Mingju sighed in his heart, truly, life is boundless, and learning is also boundless.

It was one thing for Changtai to be the first to stand up and support Kangxi, but he also put forward practical suggestions, and Kangxi's trusted ministers couldn't sit still.

They should have been haggling over "whether to do it," but Changtai, this young man who didn't follow the rules, had directly pushed the matter a big step forward, turning it into "how to do it."

While cursing Changtai for not knowing the rules in their hearts, they racked their brains to find ways.

Since the first step had been skipped, the matter was like an arrow on the bowstring and had to be fired. They had to strive to do more and grab more credit.

Seeing the group of ministers arguing like fighting cocks about how to do things, Kangxi said in English: "You are amazing, well done. If you hadn't stood up, they wouldn't know how long they would have argued."

The missionaries below: "..."

W-we don't understand the Emperor's English! Don't understand, don't understand.

Changtai smiled and replied in English: "I didn't intend to make things difficult for the ministers; it's just that the Emperor gave the order to solve this matter, so I just tried my best to solve it."

Kangxi snorted coldly: "Don't they know? They know, yet they still argue."

Changtai said: "Your Majesty, don't be angry. The colleagues are arguing back and forth, but in the end, they still have to do the work; it's just wasting more time. Their arguing only consumes their own energy and doesn't hinder Your Majesty's important business."

Kangxi couldn't help but laugh: "Well said!"

Kangxi's trusted old ministers glanced at the pair of monarch and subject on the throne with the corners of their eyes, feeling a bit sour.

What are the Emperor and Changtai talking about? Why can the Emperor still be amused by such a serious matter as an earthquake?

No way, no way, is the Heseri family going to produce a favored minister? How did this Changtai pop up without a sound? Why was there no news before?

The ministers didn't dare to pierce Kangxi with their eyes, so they turned their focus to Songgotu.

"Congratulations, Lord Song, the Heseri family is going to produce another important minister," Mingju said sarcastically.

Although Songgotu was panicked inside, he remained calm on the surface: "Same to you. It's not as good as Lord Ming's son, who has already become the Crown Prince's confidant."

Come on, let's hurt each other!

Mingju and Songgotu glared at each other.

Kangxi looked at the small actions of the ministers below like a teacher standing on a podium in later generations, seeing the small expressions the students thought were hidden clearly.

This time, Kangxi switched to Russian, lest these missionaries understand and spread rumors: "Changtai, Mingju and Songgotu are glaring at each other again. Guess what they might be saying?"

Changtai smiled bitterly: "What else? Lord Ming is probably congratulating the Heseri family on pushing out a new person in the court, and Lord Song is congratulating Lord Ming's son, Rongruo, for being so liked by the Crown Prince."

Kangxi nodded: "I think so too."

While continuing to study earthquake-related knowledge, they whispered and gossiped about the ministers in Russian.

The missionaries: "..."

Your Majesty, actually, some of us understand Russian!

Many years later, historians found that when organizing the notes of Qing Dynasty missionaries, several missionaries recorded this.

"The Emperor of the Qing Dynasty and his favored minister Changtai were on the throne, whispering in English or Russian. Other ministers did not know that this pair of young monarch and subject were mocking their private affairs. That wise Emperor of the Qing Dynasty always appeared very serious; it was the first time I saw him like an ordinary young man, mocking the pedantry of the elderly with a young man of the same age. Seeing this scene, I believe that the high and mighty Emperor also has true friends."

Kangxi and Changtai didn't know that their great friendship would be sung for centuries in literary works, and even develop into many lace-like ambiguous stories like those between Emperor Wu of Han and Wei Qing.

Now, Changtai's head was dull and painful, his ears were buzzing, and he used the foreign language he had just learned to answer Kangxi's overly sharp and harsh evaluations of the ministers in a stumbling and stuttering manner.

If these words were spread, he would probably become the enemy of all ministers, including his uncle Songgotu.

But the Emperor asked, and he couldn't not answer.

How to follow the Emperor's wishes without negatively evaluating the ministers had already exhausted Changtai's efforts.

What's even more terrible is that he also had to translate what he wanted to say using scarce foreign vocabulary.

After being kicked off the bed by Kangxi while sleeping side-by-side and getting a bump on his head, Changtai once again deeply felt what it meant to "accompany the Emperor is like accompanying a tiger."

My poor Crown Prince nephew, not only has to be kicked off the bed by the Emperor, but also has to deal with the Emperor's endless complaints that would offend people if spread out.

My Crown Prince nephew is not even six years old!

Changtai felt extremely uncomfortable in his heart.

The Crown Prince nephew that Changtai loved was also telling his brothers about the earthquake.

"The earth we live on is a sphere."

"Second Brother, how many times have I said it, I don't believe it."

"Big Brother, shut up, wait until I finish."

"But I don't believe what you say, unless one day you take me to see the ocean. I want to see if I see the top of the mast first."

"Today we are not talking about this, we are talking about earthquakes. An earthquake is the earth dragon turning over."

"Earth dragon? A very big earthworm?"

Yinreng: "..." He was very curious, how had Big Brother's teachers not been angered to death by him yet?

Yinreng ignored Yinzhi's question and continued to explain common knowledge about earthquakes.

Yinzhi couldn't understand those principles and would only argue with him endlessly; it was more important to talk about protection during and after the disaster.

Children are prone to illness and death when frightened at a young age. If he tells his brothers these things in advance, they might suffer less fright and be spared the pain of illness.

Yinzhen didn't understand, but he waved his puppy doll and "ah-ah-ah" rhythmically to keep time with what Yinreng was saying, saying more than Yinzhi, who kept arguing.

Although Yinzhi was young, he listened with great interest, and the questions he asked were more nutritious than Yinzhi's arguing.

Yinreng hugged his third younger brother and rubbed against him.

As expected of the third brother who would be learned in the future! He showed his extraordinary talent at such a young age!

Yinzhi would not only have deep attainments in Sinology, majoring in the "Gujin Tushu Jicheng," but also have deep attainments in Western learning.

He had profound attainments in music, arithmetic, geometry, and calendar calculation, and was personally taught by Kangxi. If he were in modern society, he might not be a mathematician, but he could at least be a math enthusiast.

The big milk bun Yinreng hugged the little milk bun Yinzhi, rubbing and kissing him, looking at his third brother as if he were looking at a golden baby that could be invested in.

A brother who likes mathematics will definitely be able to help him do many things in the future.

Yinreng had dreams he wanted to realize in this era, but he couldn't realize them with his own hands.

If he did too much, it would be "seizing power." By then, the father-son relationship between him and Kangxi would slide toward the abyss of his previous life.

It might be the best way for him to offer advice from behind, while his brothers do the work and gain merit in front, and think well of him in their hearts.

Yinzhi saw the Crown Prince brother hugging the third brother, his eyes felt a bit hot, so he hugged Yinreng and Yinzhi together, letting Yinreng hold Yinzhi in his arms.

Yinreng was full of question marks.

Big Brother, when did you get so strong?

Yinzhi beckoned to Yinzhen: "Come here, Fourth Brother, come here!"

Although he didn't quite understand what Yinzhi said, seeing his brothers sitting in a stack, Yinzhen spontaneously threw away the puppy doll and crawled into Yinzhi's arms on all fours and sat down.

Yinzhi struggled to stretch out his hand and handed the puppy doll to Yinzhen's hand.

Yinzhen hugged the puppy doll and rested his little head on top of the puppy doll's head.

When the Empress Dowager came to the side hall to see her great-grandchildren, she saw such a scene of brotherly love.

Yinzhi was leaning on the soft cushion at the head of the couch, holding Yinreng in his arms; Yinreng was holding Yinzhi in his arms, Yinzhi was holding Yinzhen in his arms, and Yinzhen was holding a puppy doll.

Yinreng continued to chatter and popularize science about earthquakes to his brothers, Yinzhi argued, Yinzhi asked questions from time to time, and Yinzhen responded with "ah-ah-ah."

The Empress Dowager clutched her chest.

How can my great-grandchildren be so well-behaved and interesting? I have been in the palace for so many years and have seen so many children, but this is the first time I have seen brothers with such a close relationship.

Even outside the palace, this scene is quite rare, isn't it?

The Empress Dowager has people around her who are skilled in calligraphy and painting.

She immediately had someone paint this scene and sent it to Kangxi, who was still working overtime at the Qianqing Palace.

As soon as Kangxi saw the picture, he spat out the tea he was drinking.

What is my son doing! No, I have to go see!

Kangxi found an excuse to leave temporarily and hurried to the Cining Palace. He didn't even have time to greet the Empress Dowager before heading straight to the side hall.

Yinreng was already sleepy by now.

Yinzhi was dozing off while holding Yinreng, Yinreng was dozing off while holding Yinzhi, Yinzhi was already asleep while holding Yinzhen, and Yinzhen was drooling all over the head of his puppy doll.

Kangxi couldn't help but gasp.

What was drawn in the picture sent by the Empress Dowager was true.

The reality was even cuter than the painting.

Kangxi didn't let anyone announce his arrival; he left the Cining Palace with a light step.

Seeing this scene, Kangxi's drained energy was fully restored, and he could continue to work overtime!

……

In the blink of an eye, it was the twenty-second of the seventh lunar month.

The first seven days after the passing of Prince Chun, Longxi, had passed. Although the mourning hall was still set up in his residence, the impact on the capital and the imperial court was almost non-existent.

The major issue currently being discussed in the court was Kangxi's "ancestral dream" and the divination by the Imperial Board of Astronomy.

There would be an earthquake in the capital before August.

This news was shocking. Many people did not believe it.

Kangxi did not directly order preparations for an earthquake; he only had people search for old farmers, hunters, and miners in the capital to patrol for any anomalies.

In an instant, reports of anomalies poured in—dried-up wells suddenly filling with water, wells with water running dry, insects moving to the surface as if there were a rainstorm, mountains collapsing here, and ravines rumbling there... within a day or two, hundreds of strange phenomena were reported.

Most of these phenomena were fake or normal events unrelated to earthquakes; earthquake precursors would not appear this far in advance.

Kangxi knew this clearly.

He just spread the news of these anomalies and then went around saying they were fake, telling everyone not to panic.

The imperial court said not to panic, but the public panicked.

No one knew the scope of the earthquake, and with strict household registration, they were reluctant to leave their houses, fields, and livestock.

Rumors said the earthquake would happen before August, and it was less than ten days away. Everyone felt they could endure just these few days.

Thus, without needing Kangxi to do anything, the people of the capital spontaneously began to move their property and set up sheds in open spaces to live in.

It was the seventh lunar month, and although the weather was cooling down, it happened to be an "autumn tiger" heatwave, so it was hot, and the common people didn't feel cold sleeping outdoors.

Ordinary people preferred to believe it was true. The wealthy families and officials in the city who had originally ignored it finally felt a bit panicked.

Subsequently, using the excuse of "preparing logistics for the suppression of the Three Feudatories," Kangxi took inventory of the national treasury and remaining grain in local areas, distributed them to smaller local granaries, and sent garrison troops to guard them.

This made them even more panicked.

The less Kangxi said these preparations were for an earthquake, the more they believed the court was absolutely certain an earthquake would occur.

The court wasn't saying anything, surely to avoid panic!

They quietly inquired about news from the palace, and hearing that tents were already being set up there, they hurriedly followed suit.

Some set up tents in their courtyards or gardens, while others simply went to their villas in the suburbs to stay temporarily.

The suburban villas had more flat land and fields, making them safer than the city.

Officials also quietly moved their families out of the city, keeping only a few strong servants in their courtyards to guard against the earthquake.

Some officials in unimportant positions and more arrogant nobles and clansmen took leave or skipped work to hide out for the last few days of the seventh month.

At this time, the behavior of Gabula's family seemed particularly strange.

Not only did they not leave the city, but Changtai, who had only been serving at home due to illness while holding the post of Minister of the Imperial Guard, took over the defense of the capital. Within a day or two, he intensified the reorganization of the troops, strengthened patrols in the capital, and urgently trained people in earthquake first aid.

Even Gabula’s youngest son, only in his teens, became a guard and went to guard the palace gates.

The massive Duke’s mansion was left with only the severely ill Gabula.

Some mocked Changtai and Changhai for being unfilial. The Hesheli family, contrary to the high-profile Changtai in court, remained low-key and silent, not arguing with anyone.

Some rumored that there might be a rift between Gabula and Songgotu, and that Gabula was dissatisfied with Songgotu becoming too powerful in the Hesheli family and wanted to seize his power. That was why Songgotu's faction in the court didn't speak up for Changhai and Changtai.

"Big brother! They are all talking nonsense! Why won't you let me defend myself!" Songgotu jumped with anger at Gabula's bedside.

After Songgotu finished jumping, Gabula had someone hand him tea.

"The earthquake in the capital is imminent, and the Emperor is already annoyed. Anyone who makes a fuss about things other than the earthquake right now will end up on the Emperor's blacklist and will definitely be dealt with later," Gabula said slowly while coughing. "Don't worry about Changtai and Changhai. Once the earthquake is over, they will resign from their temporary positions and return home to serve me. The rumors will then collapse on their own."

Songgotu gulped down a cup of tea, chewing the tea leaves in his anger, before he barely calmed down.

Songgotu said indignantly: "My two nephews are so capable, why did you lock them at home? Does big brother really fear me!"

Gabula and Songgotu's remaining three younger brothers, Ke'erkun, Xinyu, and Fabao, all shrank their heads and hid to the side, not daring to even look up.

Third brother, what nonsense are you talking about! Do you want to anger big brother to death!

Gabula was not angry.

He said faintly: "How many times have I told you? Can you never remember my words? I once said that the relatives of the Emperor should not be arrogant, and I told you to be cautious in your words and actions, but you never listen. Since you want to make your mark in the court, I can only let Changtai keep a low profile to avoid the Hesheli family being too conspicuous."

Songgotu: "...Big brother said that? Alright, big brother said that."

Songgotu sat on the edge of the bed: "I feel wronged! The Hesheli family is wronged!"

"What are you wronged about? The Crown Prince is the one who is wronged," Gabula said. "Do you know how much he has done for the Hesheli family, exhausting his efforts?"

Songgotu was puzzled: "The Crown Prince is still so young, what can he do?"

Gabula didn't mention that the Crown Prince was born with knowledge: "The Crown Prince is precocious and is personally raised by the Emperor; he understands everything you don't! He deliberately distanced himself from you, got close to me, a dying man, and quietly taught Changtai how to get along with the Emperor. If you insist on your own way and refuse to back down, the Crown Prince will be in a difficult position in the palace."

Gabula became more agitated as he spoke: "Since ancient times, Crown Princes only inherit the throne, they don't usurp it! The Crown Prince and his relatives can only be more respectful to be favored by the Emperor. Have you read the history books into a dog's brain?"

Songgotu: "...I have been very low-key recently."

"I know, that's why I'm telling you one more time. Otherwise, I can only find a way out for the Hesheli family and my two children, and I won't be able to look after you," Gabula said gloomily. "But my two children are the Crown Prince's own uncles. If something happens to the Hesheli family, they will be the first to be made an example of, and you will be behind them! Changtai will definitely be sacrificed; only Changhai might escape by deliberately betraying Changtai."

Songgotu felt a chill down his spine: "Big brother, do you know what you are saying?!"

Gabula said coldly: "I know, Changtai knows, Changhai doesn't know yet. When it really comes to that point, we save who we can. If you don't prepare for this, why are you an official in the court? Accompanying the Emperor is like accompanying a tiger. Today you are Minister Song, tomorrow you might become a prisoner. The Emperor's favor is like thunder and dew. The Emperor's heart is fickle; have you been an official for so long and still don't understand?"

Songgotu was speechless.

The other three younger brothers huddled in the shadows, trembling.

Their sickly big brother actually scolded their most arrogant third brother into silence; how terrifying!

Although they didn't understand, the bruises they got from being beaten in turns by Songgotu and the First Prince's guards were already aching.

After Songgotu fell out of favor with the Crown Prince, he had been reflecting.

Now hearing that the Crown Prince didn't dislike him, but was protecting him, he was very happy even after being scolded by his big brother, and he beat his younger brothers and sons even harder—but that is a story for another time.

When the anxiety and panic in the capital were increasingly suffocating and everyone could barely breathe, at the Si hour (9:00 AM – 11:00 AM) on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month of the 18th year of Kangxi, the mountains collapsed and the earth cracked.

Yinreng was held tightly in Kangxi's arms, listening to the rumbling of the earth, and sighed softly.

The earthquake is here; it's time to let Shunzhi exit the stage.

42. Three chapters in one (Overlord vote addition) [V]

Si hour, which is from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

People in the Qing Dynasty worked at sunrise and rested at sunset. At this time, most people had already left their homes to work. Coupled with the fact that their nerves had been tense for the past few days, as soon as the earthquake started, people reacted and ran to open spaces.

When the capital was preparing for the earthquake, the people in the palace were also prepared.

They had set up tents in the open space outside the houses, slept in the tents at night, and the concubines mostly stayed outdoors during the day.

As time went on, it was inevitable that they would have complaints.

Fortunately, there was a time limit of "within the seventh month," which kept them from slacking off due to complaints.

The closer it got to the end of the month, the tighter their nerves became, and the more they became suspicious of every sound.

Yinreng knew the earthquake was coming in a few days. Although he didn't remember the exact time, it should be between morning and noon.

That day, as soon as he got up, he filled his stomach quickly, then hugged Kangxi's thigh and wouldn't let go, saying the black energy was surging and it was so scary.

Kangxi immediately picked up Yinreng, organized personnel to move outdoors, and had the ministers stay at their posts to prevent any sudden changes.

The concubines covered their faces with veils, and the guards entered the palace with swords, ready for battle.

Kangxi took out the Western watch presented by the missionaries. Time passed second by second, and the ticking of the second hand hit his heart like a monk's bell.

"Father, I'm scared." Yinreng buried his head hard into Kangxi's arms, "It hurts a little."

The dragon throne had been moved to the large square in front of the Qianqing Palace. Kangxi sat on the throne, holding the child in one hand and the watch in the other, his expression tense.

"Where does it hurt?" Kangxi immediately called for the imperial physician.

"Where... does it hurt?" Yinreng raised his head blankly, "I can't say."

It was a coincidence that when Yinreng started crying out in pain, a rumbling sound suddenly came.

This sound came from the ground first, and then it seemed to come from all directions, like thousands of troops and horses, like the roar of cannons, like a rushing torrent.

After the loud noise, people felt the ground shaking, making it difficult to stand.

Kangxi loosened his hand, and the exquisite pocket watch fell to the ground.

He hugged Yinreng tightly with both hands, pressing Yinreng's head into his arms.

Dust and smoke rose from the Qianqing Palace, and as the ground shook, the palace swayed, and the glazed tiles and roof decorations fell down with a clatter, looking as if it were about to collapse.

Some palace maids and eunuchs were shaken to the ground. Some screamed, some wailed. The situation became chaotic, and even the guards panicked.

Kangxi held Yinreng tightly, sitting upright on the dragon throne, motionless, his expression unchanged.

Changtai, who was serving beside the dragon throne, took a step across to block in front of Kangxi, turned his back to Kangxi, raised the ceremonial long-handled axe, and slammed it into the ground: "Form ranks!"

The lower end of the ceremonial axe was a long metal rod, decorated with an unsharpened axe head. The lower end of the rod was inserted into the soil in the cracked floor tiles, and Changtai stood firm by relying on the axe.

With Changtai as an example, the guards pulled out their weapons one after another, inserted them into the overturned and cracked floor tiles to fix their bodies, and then, following Changtai's command, executed the plan they had practiced for a long time, moving towards Kangxi, surrounding him with the dragon throne as the center, with their backs to Kangxi.

Kangxi looked at his brother-in-law's imposing figure in front of him, his expression moved slightly.

Yinreng stretched out his hands to hug Kangxi's neck, whispering repeatedly: "Don't be afraid, don't be afraid, Father, don't be afraid, Baocheng will protect you. Ouch, it hurts so much."

Kangxi's expression moved significantly.

He rubbed his son in his arms hard: "Your father is not afraid, but you are trembling with fear. We are in a very safe place, and your father is protecting you, what are you afraid of? Don't be afraid. Bear with it, and I will have the imperial physician check you after the earthquake."

Changtai heard the conversation between Kangxi and Yinreng and was extremely panicked.

Where does the Crown Prince hurt? Did he fall? Or was the Emperor too nervous and scared and pinched the Crown Prince? Where is the imperial physician? Can't they crawl over to check on the Crown Prince during the earthquake?

Useless!

The earthquake continued.

Palace walls and palaces kept collapsing, cracks appeared on the ground, and water vapor and smoke even emerged from some cracks.

Dust kept rising, forming dark clouds and fog in the sky.

Kangxi looked up at the clear sky that had been bright just a moment ago, now disturbed by black energy. The sun shone through the gaps in the black energy, revealing broken golden light at the edges, as if a black dragon and a golden dragon were fighting.

Hallucinations caused by tension, panic, smoke, and light made Kangxi believe that at that moment, he saw the black energy curse from within the Qing Dynasty's dragon vein that Yinreng had emphasized many times.

The black energy transformed into a new, hideous dragon head, breaking out of the Qing Dynasty's golden dragon vein and biting it.

In an instant, the hallucination disappeared, and the two hideous dragons turned into loose dark clouds and broken golden light.

The rumbling of the earthquake also disappeared.

Who won? Who lost?

Kangxi was dazed. He was still sitting on the dragon throne, and the Qing Dynasty still existed; it must be that the Qing Dynasty's dragon vein had won.

A few drops of coolness fell on Kangxi's face.

Gu Wencheng, who was lying on the ground, crawled up and grabbed the huge canopy that had fallen to the ground, setting it upright. The shadow of the canopy covered Kangxi sitting on the dragon throne, blocking the falling raindrops.

"Your Majesty, it's raining, be careful not to catch a cold." As expected of a eunuch who had served two dynasties, Gu Wencheng had already calmed down and began to perform his duties as a eunuch.

Zhao Chang, who was a step behind, smashed his own useless, still-trembling legs in frustration.

Let you be afraid! Let you be afraid! Such a good opportunity to perform in front of the Emperor, it flew away!

Other eunuchs and guards were also frustrated.

But they were still terrified. Gu Wencheng, who was standing behind Kangxi holding the canopy, had a calm and respectful expression as usual; Changtai, who was standing in front of Kangxi, held the axe in one hand and pressed his hand on the big knife at his waist, his expression solemn and calm.

They looked down at their own trembling legs and hands; opportunities are for those who are prepared. It really is frustrating to compare people, it's incomparable.

Fortunately, Gu Wencheng was already a trusted head eunuch of Kangxi, and Changtai was the Minister of the Imperial Guard and Kangxi's brother-in-law, who was already highly valued by Kangxi. It wasn't some person they looked down upon using this opportunity to climb up, which made them feel a little better.

"It's over." Kangxi sighed softly, "No, it's just the beginning."

Disaster relief after the earthquake is the truly headache-inducing thing.

The pattering raindrops hit hard, finally waking up the palace staff who were still in a panic.

Under the orders of Gu Wencheng and Changtai, they quickly restored order according to the previous drills.

Kangxi wanted to summon an imperial physician to check on Yinreng, but Yinreng said calmly: "No need."

He looked at Kangxi with eyes that were complex and somewhat gratified, giving Kangxi goosebumps.

Yinreng lowered his voice and said: "Put me down. His soul is unstable and has fallen into a deep sleep. I will appear temporarily to help him resist the curse for a while."

Kangxi's heart panicked and his hands shook, and he hurriedly put Yinreng on the ground.

Yinreng frowned: "Don't panic."

He reached out and held Kangxi's finger.

Kangxi's body tensed.

I... I... I...

"Go into the tent, I have something to tell you." Yinreng's expression was neither sad nor happy, but carried a heart-wrenching sense of vicissitudes.

A child's eyes are lively and clear; a young person's eyes are vibrant and passionate; as they get older, some people's eyes become more turbid, while others' eyes become more bright and soul-stirring, like aged spirits.

Yinreng's originally childish eyes were still clear, but they had settled too many things, looking like the eyes of an old man who had experienced much pain and suffering, seemingly detached but actually containing strong unwillingness and resentment.

Even Kangxi could not show such eyes now.

Under the gaze of such eyes, Kangxi was nothing more than a young man who had not yet reached the age of thirty.

Expressions, words, and body movements can be acted out, but the accumulation of time, years, and suffering lingering on the body cannot be acted out.

After Kangxi panicked, he immediately arranged a small tent, took Yinreng's hand and walked in, not allowing anyone else to enter.

Kangxi had already arranged the response to the earthquake. Now, if the ministers were not stupid or hadn't been killed by the earthquake, they had already begun to execute according to the established plan. What Kangxi needed to do now was to comfort the palace staff, and after the chaos in the city calmed down, go to the Temple of Heaven to pray.

This was not urgent, so there was time to be alone with Shunzhi in Yinreng's body.

After Kangxi calmed down, he felt a bit lost.

He was not highly regarded when Shunzhi was alive, and he was still young when Shunzhi died.

In this life, he had never had the guidance and care of a father.

Now that he was an adult and had children, his father had awakened in the body of his most beloved child.

He didn't know how to face this father who had passed away early.

Yinreng had now completely "activated" the memories of his previous life and the life before that.

Any transmigration would have a golden finger; his golden finger was probably that if he concentrated, he could "search" through trivial matters in his memory like flipping through a book.

The guidance of Kangxi in his first life and the knowledge he absorbed as a fan of Ming and Qing culture in his second life were all revived at this moment.

His head ached faintly, and his physical strength was gradually disappearing, but if he could hold on for a day, it should be fine.

Yinreng found that he was a very restless person.

He kept shouting about finding a big villa with hot springs to be a salted fish until he died, but in his heart, he was never willing to return for a lifetime and leave nothing behind.

In his first life, he was the Crown Prince. When he died, he only recalled family affection and just wanted to return to his childhood when he was still loved by his father. He never thought about the throne or power, being cowardly and spineless to the extreme.

In his second life, he was an ordinary person, but he pointed out the country every day, wishing he could travel with a data disk now, let China unify the earth, being ignorant and arrogant, never thinking that he would be burned to death by shrewd ancients.

Well, in his second life, he was just a keyboard warrior. If he really traveled, he would definitely not be able to give up air conditioning and the internet.

Now that he had really traveled, the two ideals were entangled and churning in his heart, which was extremely contradictory.

But he was just a child now, and Kangxi still doted on him. The first dream could be realized as long as he kept hiding behind the scenes, pretending to be sick and weak. If he didn't take this opportunity to add bricks and tiles to the second dream, the vast number of transmigrators would definitely despise him.

Yinreng couldn't help but smile.

Pretending to be his grandfather to fool his father is really exciting; I'll only play this once.

Kangxi looked at the smile on Yinreng's face, which was mischievous but did not belong to a child, and couldn't help but be stunned.

"After today, I should go. Now I will tell you what I can teach you; how much you can learn depends on yourself." Yinreng directed Kangxi to call someone to move the box of materials he had organized into the tent and began to teach his father.

"Refreshing" is just one word, don't mention it.

Yinreng unfolded a history book and a map of the Qing Dynasty and began to talk from the previous Ming Dynasty.

Yinreng had listened to Kangxi handle government affairs for a long time and finally discovered that Kangxi knew nothing about the party strife of the Han people and was confused about the changes in Confucian culture. Any history and culture enthusiast of later generations was better than him.

Yinreng suddenly realized that the amount of information modern people receive in the information explosion is incomparable to that of the ancients.

Especially under the guidance of scientific thought, they look at problems comprehensively and from a high vantage point. The ancients were like blind men touching an elephant, only able to barely piece together the full picture of events based on experience.

Now, he was going to give Kangxi a lesson to make up for Kangxi's lack of historical perspective and overall view.

Yinreng talked from the initial form of Confucianism to "outer Confucianism and inner Legalism" and "outer king and inner sage"; from the original thoughts of Confucius to what changes successive emperors made to Confucius' thoughts to consolidate their rule; from the coexistence of noble families to what policies successive emperors made to weaken the noble families...

Kangxi's eyes became brighter as he listened.

Kangxi was a purely gifted emperor.

Many people thought that Kangxi's political thought was taught by Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang, who could not yet be called "Xiaozhuang," but knowing Xiaozhuang's experience, she didn't have this ability.

Xiaozhuang entered Huang Taiji's harem very early and had no chance to learn political thought. She might be smart, but she was not wise, and her insights into national politics were very shallow; she was just relatively good at power struggles.

Kangxi's thought on being a monarch was all self-taught from reading books and thinking for himself.

He had teachers, but the teachers were not emperors and could not teach him how an emperor should act.

An emperor needs to have an overall view of the whole situation and needs to learn from the horizontal and vertical experience of history; these can only be explored by Kangxi himself.

Perhaps decades later, Kangxi would form his own view of the monarch, but now, he was still struggling to explore.

Yinreng's explanation easily cleared away the confusion in Kangxi's heart.

Kangxi's confusion in studying history books and classics was finally cleared up after Yinreng's guidance.

Kangxi asked Yinreng to pause temporarily, then rearranged everything so that he could listen to the "Father's" teachings for a longer time.

Kangxi summoned Gu Wenxing and Zhao Chang, who had some grasp of the situation, to take shorthand notes of what Yinreng said. He himself also held paper and brush, taking notes as he listened. Changtai stood guard at the tent entrance with a saber held crosswise.

Liang Jiugong was also called into the tent to serve tea, water, and pastries, replace paper, and grind ink, tending to the three who were taking notes.

Yinreng first outlined the broad strokes of historical, political, and cultural shifts, as well as the true causes behind the decline of various dynasties apart from foolish rulers, before zeroing in on the "factional strife" that brought about the fall of the Ming dynasty.

Situations in the imperial court changed in the blink of an eye; the only constant was interest.

The root of "factional strife" was also interest—a mutated form of the struggles among aristocratic clans.

In the past, the north was affluent, and northern aristocratic clans held absolute dominance. After the Southern Song, the political center shifted south. Coupled with rice replacing wheat and millet as the main high-yield crop, the south grew wealthier than the north, and southern aristocratic clans began to seek higher political status.

Factional strife never strayed from its core: every bloody clash in the court was waged on behalf of the regional interests each faction represented.

A spark of inspiration flashed in Kangxi's mind: "An upright official is not truly clean; it's all for the sake of family and regional interests?"

Yinreng nodded. "Ming officials had pitifully low stipends. If they relied solely on their salaries, none could afford to eat, let alone support a family. If they were to starve to death, why remain officials? For ideals? Perhaps some were, but most bustled about for profit. Behind a single 'clean official,' there might stand several local magnates backing him."

Yinreng recalled the matter of Jin Fu being falsely accused over Yellow River conservancy a few years later.

"Take Yellow River conservancy, for instance. Once flood management yields remarkable results, the official in charge is bound to be impeached. Because when the river stops flooding, their common goal disappears, and people on both banks will no longer tolerate having their own interests harmed for the river's sake."

The reason Jin Fu was falsely accused and stripped of his post by a group of Han "clean officials" was that his river conservancy involved surveying the land on both banks and forcing powerful local magnates to cough up the land they had seized along the riverbeds.

Those upright officials who impeached him, such as Yu Chenglong and Guo Xiu, were backed by powerful local clans of Shandong in the north.

They might have done many good deeds for the Great Qing, and their personal conduct might have been upright, but for the sake of their clans, mentors, friends, and fellow countrymen, they too would resort to false accusations.

This was the "class limitation" taught in junior high school politics textbooks.

Kangxi recalled a question that had puzzled him when reading history: "When Yue Fei of the Southern Song was recalled by twelve golden plaques, was that also intertwined with the struggles among southern magnates for their interests?"

Yinreng said with gratification, "Exactly."

Kangxi immediately beamed with pride, like a child who had just received praise from his father.

In Kangxi's eyes right now, he was indeed a child being commended by his Imperial Father.

"Whether it was military expenditures for northern campaigns to reclaim lost territory or reconstruction costs after reclaiming it, the burden would fall upon the south. This was good for the country, but brought no benefit to the south. When the prestige of the emperor and the imperial court was not strong enough, Yue Fei's death was inevitable. Zhao Gou lacked the resolve to burn his boats and back Yue Fei by braving southern unrest. As for the two emperors who were captured in the north, they were actually beside the point."

Yinreng explained.

"Since ancient times, the saying 'the people can carry a boat or capsize it' has never referred to commoners, but to aristocratic clans. The entire Huaxia nation's economy and talents were in the hands of powerful clans. When the emperor was not unyielding enough and the imperial court was not strong enough, they could only live by their whims."

"The Ming dynasty originally established a policy of balancing the aristocratic clans with the hereditary nobility. But after the Tumu Crisis, the nobility faction collapsed, and the civil official faction representing local clans took control of state affairs..."

Yinreng laid out the ancestral homes and master-disciple lineages of the Donglin faction. In a daze, Kangxi seemed to see a massive web enveloping the entire court of the former Ming.

Yet before Yinreng pointed it out, he had never noticed it.

Thinking of his own court, Kangxi broke into a cold sweat.

"What the Great Qing has done is essentially no different from the former Ming; it has merely replaced the hereditary nobility with Manchu nobility. But the nobility cannot be allowed to grow too powerful either. How to use clans to counterbalance nobility, and nobility to counterbalance clans—that is what you must ponder."

Yinreng only laid out the situation without providing solutions.

Kangxi already had an established imperial mindset, and his thoughts differed from Yinreng's.

Shunzhi, as a feudal monarch, also thought differently from a modern-day college student like him. Saying too much would give the game away.

Yinreng merely presented the facts to guide Kangxi's thinking.

After covering the former Ming, Yinreng moved on to unraveling the Great Qing's current contradictions.

The Manchu-Han contradiction was primary, yet not all that important.

Times were progressing. Unlike previous dynasties that had only internal conflicts and at most looked toward the north,

the Great Qing was now surrounded by wolves and in the midst of epochal change. The power of aristocratic clans was waning, while the importance of ordinary commoners was skyrocketing.

If the Great Qing had simply acted like past dynasties—ruling peacefully after passing Shanhaiguan—nothing would have gone wrong, but Dorgon...

Yinreng's mouth twitched slightly as he asked, "Was my Edict of Self-Reproach drafted under Imperial Mother's orders, or was it the work of the Manchu and Mongol nobility?"

Yinreng put himself in Shunzhi's shoes: if Shunzhi truly had a spirit in the afterlife, he would definitely be enraged enough to pick a fight with the Grand Empress Dowager.

That posthumous *Edict of Self-Reproach* had wiped out all of Shunzhi's lifelong efforts and every political highlight of his reign, leaving a severe negative impact on future Qing emperors.

As the first emperor after entering Shanhaiguan, the so-called ancestral system could originally have been reshaped starting from him, and he indeed had been changing it slowly. Even if pressured to waver between Manchus and Hans, his policies had still leaned toward ethnic integration.

Yet the *Edict of Self-Reproach* declared that everything he had done was wrong, that he had gone against Nurhaci and Hong Taiji's policies of prioritizing Manchus and uniting Manchus and Mongols by favoring the Han, and it forbade future emperors from violating ancestral ways.

This left a fatal hidden danger for later emperors, tying their hands and feet and leaving them too frightened to carry out sweeping reforms.

Kangxi said awkwardly, "Th-This... the Grand Empress Dowager had no choice either. The Eight Banners nobility and imperial clan were too powerful..."

He could not go on.

Without the Grand Empress Dowager's tacit consent, even if the imperial clan and nobility harbored such thoughts, the *Edict of Self-Reproach* could never have been issued.

The Grand Empress Dowager had always reproached Shunzhi, wishing he would adhere to ancestral customs and detesting the Han. It was a fact that she had used Shunzhi's death to vent her anger.

"I was not wrong." After a moment of silence, Yinreng said, "If the Great Qing is to restart the process of ethnic integration, it needs scapegoats. Dorgon and other clan members, Oboi and other Manchu nobles—all can be cast aside for the future of the Great Qing."

Kangxi said immediately, "Yes! Rest assured, Imperial Father, your son will certainly clear Imperial Father's name!"

*That Edict of Self-Reproach—I'll revoke it! Even the Grand Empress Dowager won't stop me!*

*Imperial Father was so furious he climbed out of his coffin; surely the Grand Empress Dowager must feel very guilty.*

"Imperial Father, Empress Xiaoxian..." Kangxi remembered Shunzhi's "true love."

Yinreng's eyelids twitched. Unable to put on a deeply mournful expression, he silently apologized to Shunzhi and Empress Xiaoxian in his heart: "What was Xiaoxian's surname?"

Kangxi: "Donggo..."

Yinreng asked, "Do you remember the surnames and family backgrounds of all the consorts in my harem?"

Kangxi had to oversee the arrangements for the dowagers and consorts, so of course he knew.

He ran through the family backgrounds and surnames of Shunzhi's imperial consorts in his mind, and his eyes suddenly went wide—looking very much like Yinreng the chubby baby when startled.

"Donggo... especially Empress Xiaoxian's branch, which was brimming with talent," Kangxi murmured. "Among the high-ranking consorts in Imperial Father's harem, Empress Xiaoxian was the only one from a prominent Manchu clan. Among all consorts in the harem, those with Manchu surnames were also exceedingly rare. The only one with a distinguished background and capable father and brothers was Empress Xiaoxian..."

*So that's how it was... That's how it was...*

*Why did Imperial Father favor Empress Xiaoxian above all?*

*Imperial Father was elevating the inner court to suppress the outer court.*

*Why was Fourth Brother Imperial Father's 'first' son?*

*Fourth Brother was the first child born to a consort from the Manchu-Mongol nobility.*

Kangxi felt a bit aggrieved: "The Tunggiya... the Tung clan was quite capable too."

*Actually, my mother's clan was quite decent as well. Truly.*

Although in Shunzhi's reign, the Tung clan was merely part of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Military, their—their abilities were still commendable.

"Tong Tulai's family was indeed capable; capable enough to drive Li Chengdong into rebellion, truly remarkable," Yinreng remarked dryly. "Has he changed all his descendants' names to Manchu by now?"

Li Chengdong was the one who had followed Dodo in perpetrating the Jiading Ten-Day Massacre and the Yangzhou Massacre. Later, after falling out with Tong Yangjia of Tong Tulai's clan, he defected to the Southern Ming, leading to Tong Yangjia dying in battle.

Kangxi: "..."

Kangxi: "Ahem. My maternal family's ancestors... might also have been Jurchens."

It was possible, truly possible.

Yinreng said, "Jurchens who had been Sinicized for hundreds of years?"

Kangxi: "..." *Imperial Father, that's enough QAQ.*

"It doesn't actually matter," Yinreng said. "Use them if they are useful, discard them if they are not. When the Qing entered Shanhaiguan, the Han who surrendered fought other Han the most fiercely; they were the sharpest, most savage blades. If you point your sword at the world, they will also serve you on the front lines."

Kangxi: "..." He wanted to say he wasn't mentally prepared to point his sword at the world yet, but dared not say it in front of Imperial Father.

"Don't listen to your Grandma. She understands nothing," Yinreng emphasized.

The sound of a cane striking the ground echoed at the tent entrance.

Yinreng looked up. *Oh boy. Speaking ill of someone behind their back, caught red-handed by the person herself.*

Kangxi: "..." *How did the Grand Empress Dowager barge in?!*

Seeing Changtai being pinned down, anger flared in his heart.

The Grand Empress Dowager immediately explained, "This humble one could not find the Emperor and feared the Emperor had been taken hostage in the chaos."

She shot a glance at the people behind her, and two stout eunuchs immediately released Changtai.

Changtai spat out the rag from his mouth and knelt before Kangxi to plead guilty.

"It's fine. Continue standing guard." Kangxi naturally would not blame Changtai.

When the Grand Empress Dowager barged in, Changtai couldn't very well cut her down. His face was black and blue, showing he had only blocked them without daring to fight back.

To prevent anyone from overhearing his conversation with "Shunzhi," the tent had several layers of curtains and was very spacious inside, like a military council tent. Having been engrossed in his conversation with "Shunzhi," he hadn't noticed the commotion outside.

Yinreng cast a cold glance at the Grand Empress Dowager, sending a tremor through her heart.

She took a few steps forward: "This humble one... I..."

Yinreng ignored her.

He tapped his fingers on the table and continued lecturing.

The Grand Empress Dowager stood awkwardly for a moment, then went straight to a stool, dismissed everyone else, and quietly gazed at Yinreng in a daze.

Since Kangxi had assumed personal rule, the Grand Empress Dowager had never interfered in state affairs.

This was her first time "listening to governance," but from her eyes and expression, Kangxi could tell she wasn't absorbing a single word.

Seeing the yearning look on the elderly Grand Empress Dowager's face, Kangxi sighed, ignored her as well, and let her continue listening.

Another commotion broke out at the entrance.

This time, it was Fuquan and the Eldest Prince raising a ruckus with their loud voices, with Changning's sarcastic tone fanning the flames from time to time, heavily implying that Kangxi was about to collapse and Changtai, the Crown Prince's uncle, was up to no good.

Kangxi stood up in anger. "I will drive them away!"

Yinreng said, "Let Fuquan, the Eldest Prince, and... that whoever-he-is in."

The Grand Empress Dowager reminded him softly, "That child is named Changning, born to Secondary Consort Chen."

Yinreng nodded. "Let them all in. Keep the others outside."
