44. Three Updates in One (King-level Ticket Bonus) [V]

Kangxi was just about to tell Yinzhi to hurry back to study, saying that even if he couldn't attend class for now, he should study on his own and not disturb Yinzhi's rest every day. Yinzhi actually brought up a serious matter, which shocked Kangxi.

Kangxi listened to Yinzhi finish the serious matter clearly and logically, praising Yinzhi on the surface, but feeling very suspicious inside.

He didn't believe this idea was something Yinzhi could come up with. Even if Yinzhi had listened to Shunzhi's teachings and taken notes, didn't he know how many strings and tendons were in Yinzhi's little head?

Kangxi glanced at Yinzhi.

Yinzhi ⊙_⊙: Innocent.

Just as Kangxi was about to withdraw his probing gaze, Yinzhi, like a startled hedgehog, immediately blocked in front of Yinzhi, bristling with all his quills to confront Kangxi.

Kangxi: "..." Heh.

Yinzhi (︶︹︺).

Sigh, big brother is a terrible teammate! Father was clearly already fooled by me!

Kangxi smiled without smiling, not immediately exposing Yinzhi and Yinzhi: "You go think of a plan and write it into a memorial for me."

Yinzhi was shocked: "Imperial Father, how old is your son? You want your son to write a memorial?" Is there something wrong with your brain!

Yinzhi had grown up. He didn't say the last sentence, only expressed it with his expression.

Kangxi saw the last sentence Yinzhi didn't finish and was actually a bit gratified.

At least his eldest son didn't say it directly; he had already tried very hard. The old father thought with a sour heart.

"You can ask Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin to help you," Kangxi said. "The three of you think of a way together."

"Oh." Yinzhi breathed a sigh of relief.

Kangxi and Yinzhi stared at each other.

Yinzhi was puzzled: "Imperial Father, why are you staring at me?"

Kangxi said irritably: "Didn't I tell you to go find Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin to help you write the memorial? Why are you still standing there?"

Yinzhi said: "Son wants to go later."

Kangxi said: "No, you don't."

Yinzhi was driven away by Kangxi.

Outside the tent, the pouting Yinzhi jumped a few times, but in the end, he didn't dare to curse, so he had to leave sheepishly.

The guards kept their eyes on their noses and their noses on their hearts, already accustomed to this.

After moving into tents at the Temple of Heaven, those guarding the side were naturally guards with swords.

The guards used to be on duty at the Qianqing Palace, but they wouldn't enter the inside of the Qianqing Palace and rarely saw the Crown Prince and the First Prince.

After a few days of contact, they realized that not only was the Emperor's doting on the Crown Prince real, but the relationship between the Crown Prince and the other princes was also truly good.

Especially the First Prince and the Crown Prince, who were so close that even the Emperor was jealous.

Although they always felt this relationship was strange, they were also moved that there could be such sincere family affection in the imperial palace.

They heard that the Crown Prince was unbelievably kind and sensible, praised by almost everyone in the harem, and almost perfect except for his weak health. Perhaps it was because the Crown Prince was too excellent that they all liked him so much.

"Rongruo, I heard you are very close to the Crown Prince. What kind of person is the Crown Prince?" a guard asked Nalan Xingde, who was on duty.

Nalan Xingde said: "As a subject, I dare not speak lightly of the heir apparent."

The guard said: "Just asking about his personality. I heard he is especially kind?"

A smile of kindness, as if for his own child, appeared on Nalan Xingde's face: "The Crown Prince is indeed very kind and intelligent, rare in the world."

The guard: "..." You just said you didn't dare to speak lightly of the heir apparent, and now you're praising him?

Does your father know you're praising the Crown Prince?

Does Mingzhu know? Mingzhu knew plenty.

Mingzhu's wife, Jue Luo-shi, persuaded Mingzhu that since ancient times, no noble family had ever put all their eggs in one basket. Since the Emperor allowed Rongruo to contact the Crown Prince, let Rongruo follow the Crown Prince. That way, even if Mingzhu courted death, their family wouldn't fall.

Mingzhu: "???" Why is it me courting death and not that unfilial son Nalan Xingde?!

Mingzhu was very dissatisfied, but he had to admit that Jue Luo-shi was right.

What if they jumped around like this and the Crown Prince still ascended the throne? Better to have someone support the Crown Prince. So he stopped restraining Nalan Xingde.

Nalan Xingde was in a great mood. After he was in a good mood, and because he needed to accompany the Crown Prince and the First Prince at all times, he hadn't been drunk for a long time. Furthermore, he had to exercise diligently every day, fearing he wouldn't protect the two princes well. So now his body was healthier than ever, strong enough to hold one prince in each arm and walk like the wind.

Mingzhu was extremely gratified and began to arrange for Nalan Xingde to take a second wife, and then had a big fight with his eldest son—but that is a story for another time.

The other guards looked at Nalan Xingde's glowing face and were very envious.

Even if the people in the harem were well-behaved, there were times when they were gossipy. The guards often heard their whispers that they thought were quiet.

Many palace servants said that the Crown Prince was a blessed person; whoever he liked would be healthy and have good luck. Coupled with the fact that the Crown Prince had easily survived the smallpox epidemic when he was very young, many people believed the Crown Prince was a lucky little fairy boy sent from heaven.

It just so happened that Kangxi had an ancestor dream and could predict the great earthquake in the capital, so he must also be a deity.

It was very reasonable for the deity Emperor's Crown Prince to also be a deity boy.

The guards heard these words more and more, and became increasingly curious about the Crown Prince.

They originally thought this was an image created by the Emperor for the Crown Prince. Nalan Xingde also said so, could the Crown Prince really have some kind of "lucky baby" effect?

Except for bondservants like Cao Yin who were valued by the Emperor, the guards were basically Manchu and Mongol nobles, and the positions of their families were mostly... no, not mostly, almost all contrary to the "Crown Prince."

So they basically didn't hear any good words about the Crown Prince at home. If the Crown Prince's reputation improved by one point, the sighs and angry shouts of their elders would increase by one point.

The young people originally followed the teachings of their elders and had no good impression of the Crown Prince.

But the Crown Prince's reputation was getting better and better, and a "little traitor" Nalan Xingde appeared among the guards, so they became curious.

Perhaps young people always have a rebellious phase. In feudal noble families where they almost never split up, the old men pressed down on their heads for a lifetime, making their rebellious phase even longer; the more talented they were, the more intense their rebellious phase became.

They began to think independently and began to try to walk a different path from their elders.

The symbol of the "Crown Prince" was the fuse.

"The Crown Prince is indeed intelligent," said a guard who had briefly protected the Crown Prince during the Jingshan hunt. "The Emperor has taught the Crown Prince very well."

He vividly described the day the Crown Prince said Kangxi wanted to be an "Emperor of the Ages," and was glared at by Nalan Xingde.

"Don't parrot things randomly, be cautious in speech and action," Nalan Xingde reminded.

The guard touched his nose, not caring: "It's not a secret. There were so many people present at the time, what should have been spread has already been spread."

Many guards from noble backgrounds in the palace were careless in their dealings and didn't have much "political thinking." Many were still playboys here to "build their resumes." That was why E'lundai could lead the Qianqing Palace guards to play archery during an outing later.

E'lundai was a lawless scoundrel, and the fact that those Qianqing Palace guards could play with E'lundai showed how unprofessional some of the noble guards in the Qianqing Palace were.

Mentioning the Jingshan hunt, the unprofessional guards gathered around to inquire about gossip, while the serious and upright guards were squeezed to the side.

The serious and upright guards looked at each other, sighed, and took the initiative to take on the heavy responsibility of patrolling for the unprofessional guards.

They were already used to this kind of thing. It was like this in the palace, and you expected this group to change after leaving the palace? So the number of people patrolling in the Qianqing Palace was always over the limit, a group of serious guards leading a group of playboys "pretending" to build their resumes, and the unprofessional guards often skipped work.

Nalan Xingde also wanted to leave, but because he was also a noble son, he was pulled by his self-proclaimed "fox friends and dog buddies" who wouldn't let him go.

Nalan Xingde: "..." Thanks, even if you are fox friends and dog buddies, you have to choose like-minded foxes and dogs; I don't want you few.

The First Prince descended like a divine soldier and saved him.

"Rongruo, come with me. Where is Ziqing?" Yinzhi frowned with his hands behind his back. "What are you talking about? Why did this master hear the word 'Crown Prince'? Are you speaking ill of the Crown Prince?"

The unprofessional guards hurriedly shook their heads: "No, no, we are praising the Crown Prince!"

Yinzhi smiled and said: "My little brother can stand praise, you praised well!"

Unprofessional guards: "..." Alright, it's clear that the First Prince really likes the Crown Prince.

What were the family members saying about the First Prince and the Crown Prince fighting for the throne? Fighting for a fart? Would they dare to say these things in front of the First Prince?

No wonder the elders had given up on the First Prince and were staring at the Third Prince, who was walking unsteadily, and the Fourth Prince, who couldn't even talk yet.

"First Prince, this subject is on duty, may I ask what is the matter?" Nalan Xingde asked.

Yinzhi said: "Imperial Father asked you and Cao Ziqing to help me write a memorial, thinking about how to unite the young people among the nobles who hate those old immortals who don't do serious work and only know how to sow discord between me and my brother, to do something serious together. The old immortals occupy positions and don't do good things, staring at other people's family affairs all day, worse than gossiping women; the work can only be done by young people."

Yinzhi showed his straightforward (in a derogatory sense) and brain-clogging side in front of outsiders for the first time.

Nalan Xingde was already used to it, his expression as usual: "This subject will go find Cao Yin immediately, First Prince, please wait a moment."

The other unprofessional guards looked messy in the wind.

First Prince, you, you, you...

"First Prince, it's not good to scold people," a guard said weakly.

Yinzhi raised his eyebrows: "Where did this master scold anyone?"

The guard said: "Old immortals..."

Yinzhi said: "Saying they are old but in good health, is this scolding? Isn't this a compliment?"

Is that what "old immortal" means? We get it!

Pfft! How is that possible! Is that how your teacher taught you, First Prince?!

The guard said again: "You also said they are occupying positions and not doing their jobs..."

Yinzhi said: "This master didn't say it, you said it."

The guard immediately said: "Your words meant exactly that!"

Yinzhi looked at the guard quietly: "You say it means that, so it means that? On what basis do you say it means that? Are you very dissatisfied with your elders, holding back words to scold them in your heart, so you deliberately misinterpreted this master's meaning to scold people?"

The guard: "..." Although he was indeed very dissatisfied with his elders, he didn't!

The guards were shocked.

The First Prince is still a child, and his tongue is so sharp? Where did the First Prince learn this set of sophistry?

Who is the First Prince's teacher?! We dare not offend the First Prince, but we can go block the door of the teacher who taught the First Prince this sophistry! (Yinzhi: Achoo!)

Yinzhi waved his sleeves and said magnanimously: "Forget it, this master is magnanimous and won't argue with you. But you should be careful when you speak in the future, don't misunderstand randomly, it will offend people. By the way, are you interested in participating in what I said?"

Although the unprofessional guards were all playboys who didn't do their jobs, they didn't dare to do things that would bring disaster to their families; they had that much common sense.

They hesitated and said: "This subject and others don't have..."

Yinzhi said: "It's not a big deal, just finding some people to compile some books, tell some stories, and then spread them out. You can come and listen first, then decide whether to do it or not. Of course, whether to reveal it to your elders, you decide for yourselves."

Yinzhi smiled: "Whichever family's elders find out, this master will spread the reputation of that family's 'good baby' as a useless coward."

Unprofessional guards: "...Now you are scolding people, First Prince!"

Yinzhi was puzzled: "Who did this master scold? Has anyone among you already done this?"

The unprofessional guards shook their heads vigorously.

Yinzhi said: "Since none of you have done this, why say this master is scolding people?"

Unprofessional guards: "..." Can words be interpreted like this!

The unprofessional guards began to suffer.

Why did they have the feeling of being intellectually crushed by a child! Although they were often pointed at by their families and called stupid, how old is the First Prince! Are all royal children this monstrous!

Is this the legendary "wisdom close to a demon"!

If the First Prince is like this, wouldn't His Highness the Crown Prince be even more terrifying! (Yinreng: Achoo.)

Nalan Xingde quickly found Cao Yin.

In this short "quick" interval, Yinzhi had already "subdued" a group of guards who were more curious than cats and lacked any sense of propriety, and they all gathered for an unauthorized meeting under his imperial decree.

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin: "..." What on earth has the First Prince done!

When Kangxi finished playing with his son and stepped out of the tent, refreshed and ready to continue working, he discovered that nearly half of the guards surrounding the tent were missing.

Kangxi’s anger began to brew.

This group of playboys was skipping work collectively again?! It would be one thing if things were normal, but now that the capital had been hit by a massive earthquake and everything was in chaos, how dare they!

The guard captain reported: "The First Prince said he had an oral decree and took them away."

The guard captain mimicked the First Prince's words for Kangxi—perhaps because the capable officials among them all had excellent memories, he repeated the First Prince's words almost word for word.

Kangxi's facial expressions changed wildly, much like the clouds in the sky being buffeted by a strong wind.

Zhao Chang watched Kangxi’s rapidly changing complexion and prepared himself to take small, quick steps to fetch the imperial physician.

But who was Kangxi? He was the Emperor of Endurance, the one who had endured Oboi, endured the Three Feudatories, and endured many other things.

After a few deep breaths, his expression returned to normal, though his blood pressure was still fluctuating, making him feel a bit dizzy.

"It was My oral decree." Kangxi gritted his teeth and took the blame for the First Prince.

What else could he do? Say that the First Prince had falsely spread an imperial decree and taken away his guards? If that got out, it would probably turn into a story about the seven or eight-year-old First Prince plotting a coup!

Kangxi walked away without looking back.

As he left, he thought indignantly that if Yinzhi didn't do this job well, he would punish... punish Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin! (Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin: Achoo!)

Inside the tent, Yinreng recalled the words Kangxi said before leaving.

Kangxi had guessed that the ideas Yinzhi came up with were taught by Yinreng, and asked Yinreng why he didn't tell him directly.

Yinreng used "laziness" as an excuse, but it didn't fool Kangxi.

Kangxi asked: "Did your grandfather say something to you?"

Yinreng said: "It’s not Grandfather's fault."

Kangxi said: "Alright, so it was Grandfather who said something to you."

Yinreng: "..." I'm sorry, Imperial Grandfather, this really isn't my fault; it's Father’s own overactive imagination.

Kangxi did not discuss this issue further with Yinreng. He simply pulled Yinreng into his arms and emphasized that whatever benefits other crown princes had, Yinreng would have, and whatever bad experiences other crown princes suffered, Yinreng would not.

They were a father and son unlike any other in history; they were much closer.

Yinreng nodded and said, "That's right, but I'm just lazy; I don't want to take responsibility, and I don't want to work."

Kangxi was speechless: "You are still young, it's normal not to want to move right now. But you must claim your own merits; don't give them to others. Yinzhi and the others are young now, and you have a good relationship. But people grow up, and as they grow, hearts change, do you understand? This is cruel, but you are the Crown Prince, and you must learn to be on guard."

Yinreng remembered Kangxi's words, sighed deeply, rolled over twice, and actually sat up.

Yinreng stretched, proudly patting his waist, which had lost quite a bit of fat.

You’re the best, Yinreng! Through rolling around as exercise, you managed to crawl out of the sickbed in such a short time!

Yinreng felt happy, forgetting all the dark emotions that had been churning in his heart due to Kangxi's words.

"Liang Jiugong, help me get up!" Yinreng waved his little hands at Liang Jiugong.

When Yinreng sat up, Liang Jiugong had already hurried over.

"Your Highness, you still need to lie down and rest more," Liang Jiugong said, supporting Yinreng.

Yinreng shook his head: "I need to move more. A balance of work and rest is the only way to get healthy. If I keep lying down, my body will only get weaker. Take me for a walk outside, and bring a few extra sets of clothes."

When a person is weak, they sweat profusely. He estimated that after walking a few steps, his inner garments would be soaked through with cold sweat.

Liang Jiugong hesitated for a moment, then gritted his teeth and agreed: "Alright. But Your Highness, please don't push yourself."

Having accompanied Yinreng for so long, he had developed immense respect for this young but exceptionally intelligent Crown Prince and was sincerely willing to follow his orders.

He had also seen with his own eyes how Yinreng, in order to recover quickly, would force himself to eat despite the discomfort, and if he accidentally vomited, he would immediately rinse his mouth and slowly continue eating.

The Emperor knew it too. The Emperor often wiped away tears in secret. Liang Jiugong had seen that as well.

Going out for a walk was indeed better for the body. But even for an adult, let alone a child, exercising while extremely weak was agonizingly painful.

Since the Crown Prince said he could endure it, Liang Jiugong could only hold back his tears and accompany him out.

A treasonous thought sprouted in Liang Jiugong's heart.

Such a good child as the Crown Prince, why did Heaven make him suffer all this?

What curse, what possession—why should such a small child have to bear it? Could he be...

Is he... a sacrifice?

Liang Jiugong buried those two words deep in his heart, not daring to think about them again.

"A walk after a meal, chases away all illness." Yinreng happily put on his little cloth shoes, but alas, his legs went weak on the first step.

Try again!

Just like when he first learned to walk, Yinreng wobbled like a little penguin, taking difficult steps forward one by one.

Liang Jiugong and the other eunuchs and nannies followed by his side, carefully protecting him.

Yinreng only took two or three steps before he started panting heavily.

He sat down on the carpet with a thud: "Oh my, I overestimated my stamina. It seems I won't be able to walk out of the tent today."

Yinreng waved his arms and kicked his short legs a few times, and after catching his breath, he held onto Liang Jiugong's hand to stand up and continue his efforts.

"Crown Prince Brother..." The tent flap cracked open, and Yinzi’s little head poked out, looking like he was about to cry.

"Third Brother? What's wrong? Did someone bully you?" Yinreng reached out to Yinzi.

Yinzi immediately lunged over; fortunately, Liang Jiugong was behind Yinreng to support him, otherwise, Yinreng would have been knocked to the ground.

"Oh my, my little brother, Brother is weak right now and can't catch you." Yinreng smiled and rubbed Yinzi’s smooth forehead.

Yinzi sobbed: "I-I'm sorry."

"It's okay." Yinreng hugged Yinzi and nuzzled him: "A brother and brother hugging is a sign that you like me, no need to apologize. Brother is not feeling well and couldn't catch you, so I should be the one apologizing. I'm sorry, little brother. When Brother is better, I will definitely take you out to play properly."

Yinzi tightened his short arms: "Okay. Wuwuwu, Crown Prince Brother, I heard people saying you were sick and going to die, wuwuwuwu."

A hint of ferocity flashed across Liang Jiugong's expression.

My Crown Prince is such a good person! How could there still be people behind his back wagging their tongues and cursing him!

"I've been a bit weak these past few days and haven't gone out, so they were probably just worried about me." Yinreng sighed inwardly.

What kind of idiots were they, gossiping so loudly that even little Third Brother could overhear? They would definitely be beaten to death by Father.

"Dead means I'll never see you again. Yinzi won't be able to play with Brother anymore, wuwuwu, Brother don't die." Yinzi began to wail loudly.

While Yinzi was crying, the nanny rushed over: "Oh my, Third Prince! Why did you run so fast, this servant..."

"Stop her, take her away." Yinreng’s expression changed in a second, and he said coldly.

How old was Yinzi? Not even three! How could he run around like that? How could he run so fast that adults couldn't catch him?

When the princes came with Kangxi to the Temple of Heaven to set up tents, because the space was limited, there was no separation between the inner and outer courts, and guards and eunuchs were mixed together.

Most of the palace maids were left in the inner palace; only the older nannies came out, and some eunuchs were left in the palace. Every consort's staff was somewhat insufficient.

The princess born to Consort Rong had fallen ill from the earthquake, and Consort Rong was taking care of her daughter day and night, making it difficult to spare much attention for Yinzi.

However, Consort Rong had not neglected Yinzi. She took care of her daughter herself and put all the staff she could command around Yinzi, doing even the tea and water chores herself, leaving only one eunuch to boil water and decoct medicine.

Consort Rong had also entrusted other consorts who came along to look after Yinzi, sending him to them when she was busy.

Consort Rong had made all the preparations, yet Yinzi was still able to shake off his attendants and run around?

Yinreng hugged his brother tightly, the aura of his former self instantly returning, wishing he could personally whip that old nanny to death.

He closed his eyes, suppressing his violent emotions.

Honestly. After overdrawing his mental energy to impersonate Shunzhi, he was being influenced more and more by his previous life.

Perhaps being influenced was a good thing. In this era, if he wanted to be a well-integrated member of the feudal ruling class, he would inevitably encounter many things that seemed cruel to future generations. Getting used to it early would prevent him from making wrong decisions out of pity later.

However, Yinreng also forced himself to restrain his emotions.

He had to use his twenty years of experience to constrain his fifty years of experience, letting that college student Yinreng become his true self.

Otherwise, he might lose himself.

"Send her back to Consort Rong and let her handle it." Yinreng suppressed his urge to use vigilante justice and made a rational command: "Send someone to see if Father is free; if he is, tell him about this. If not, wait until he is."

Liang Jiugong accepted the order and sent people to do as Yinreng instructed, while he remained by Yinreng's side.

Yinreng lived with Kangxi, so there were many people serving in their tent, and many people who could get things done.

Before, when Yinreng said to notify Kangxi, Liang Jiugong would always go himself.

Now, unless it was something very important that couldn't be delegated, Liang Jiugong would only report to Kangxi in person; otherwise, he stayed by Yinreng's side and didn't leave easily.

Yinzi looked blankly at the nanny being dragged away with her mouth covered, and rubbed his tears and snot on Yinreng's clothes: "Did Yinzi do something wrong?"

"Little brother didn't do anything wrong; she did. I'll tell you slowly later, let me change my clothes first." Yinreng looked down at his clothes, ruined by Yinzi's tears and snot, and his mouth twitched.

A dirty little doll. This scene must be remembered to mock the adult Third Brother later.

By the time Yinreng changed his clothes, the eunuchs and nannies had already helped Yinzi wash his face.

Yinreng asked Yinzi how he heard people speaking ill of him and how he managed to shake off his attendants, while also inviting Yinzi to help him with his rehabilitation.

Yinzi was at the age of a child just starting kindergarten; he could run and jump, spoke quite clearly, and could understand the meaning of others' words.

After Yinreng made the invitation, Yinzi immediately patted his little chest and said: "I'll help Brother! I'm very capable!"

"Of course, my little brother is extremely capable." Yinreng held Yinzi's hand, and as Yinzi took careful steps forward, he followed, wobbling step by step.

A little penguin leading a big penguin, circling the large tent, both with extremely serious expressions.

Liang Jiugong smiled until his eyes squinted.

My Crown Prince is just so capable and cute!

After Consort Rong received the news, her already exhausted body went dark, and she fainted directly.

The imperial physician hurried over to press her philtrum and revived her.

Consort Rong wanted to find Yinzi, but the person Kangxi sent had already arrived.

"Consort Rong, please rest and take care of your health. The Third Prince is having a great time with His Highness the Crown Prince, so there is no need to worry," the eunuch said.

Consort Rong immediately climbed up and knelt on the bed, kowtowing toward the tent where the Crown Prince and Kangxi lived: "Thank you, Crown Prince, thank you, Your Highness."

Although Consort Rong had a son and a daughter and held a high position, she was no longer favored.

People in the palace were accustomed to stepping on the low and fawning over the high. It was fine when they were in the inner palace, as she was the head of her own palace and could manage the people in Zhongcui Palace.

After leaving Zhongcui Palace, the other consorts here, even those of lower rank, were more favored than Consort Rong, so she was treated with neglect.

Knowing that life outside the palace would be difficult, Consort Rong had sent all the people she could use to take care of Yinzi, while she herself took one eunuch to care for her sick daughter.

Yet, even so, Yinzi was able to shake off the nannies and eunuchs and run away?

If Yinzi hadn't remembered to go find the Crown Prince, her son...

With the Temple of Heaven guards standing three layers deep, Yinzi certainly wouldn't have been lost and would have been found and brought back quickly.

But she would still be heartbroken if he had tripped or fallen.

"This was not Consort Rong's fault; the Emperor asks you to set your mind at ease," the eunuch added.

He sighed inwardly; if Consort Yi weren't pregnant, she would probably be the one in trouble.

Consort Rong had told the Empress Dowager about sending the Third Prince to other consorts for care, and the Empress Dowager had personally arranged it.

When the Third Prince ran off, he happened to be with Consort Yi.

However, Consort Yi was actually wronged as well.

Her belly was already very large, and she was already feeling unwell and shaken by the earthquake; she wasn't used to the living conditions and had no experience in taking care of children.

So Consort Yi had just sent more people to accompany Yinzi and let him play near her tent.

The consorts' tents were side-by-side, and she didn't pay much attention when Yinzi occasionally wandered off, thinking others would help keep an eye on him.

Who knew that with so many people watching Yinzi, he could still run all the way to the Crown Prince's tent without the people behind him catching up?

Simply put, it was a problem of chaotic management with everyone crowded into tents at the Temple of Heaven.

The Empress Dowager was too old, the Empress was unable to manage things, and Kangxi himself was busy with government affairs; so, of course, the consorts and palace servants who followed were left unmanaged.

Kangxi only now realized this problem.

He rearranged the living quarters for the consorts and their children, no longer letting them manage their own children separately, but instead centralizing the children's management, assigning unified staff to take care of them together.

Yinreng sighed: "Father, let my brothers live with me; we can take care of each other. They often come to find me to play, unlike the sisters who stay indoors and are easier to manage. The First Brother and I can command the servants and look after the younger brothers well."

Kangxi said: "You are still recovering!"

Yinreng smiled: "We can recover together. First Brother and Third Brother can also take care of me and Fourth Brother."

"They are still so small, how can they take care of you?" Kangxi hesitated. "Fine, let them live together; I will take care of you all."

When it came to experience in raising children, Kangxi was confident he surpassed all the consorts in the palace; perhaps only the Empress Dowager was slightly better than him.

"Good." That was exactly what Yinreng meant.

Let the brothers get closer to Father so that in the future, Father wouldn't always think of using his sons as whetstones.

The blade suffers, but doesn't the whetstone suffer too?

People are not blades, nor are they stones. Human hearts are made of flesh; they bleed, they hurt, and they die.

Yinreng remembered the madness when Yinzhi had once asked to kill the Crown Prince.

Was Yinzhi truly stupid?

Everyone received the same imperial education. Even if he were stupid, at thirty or forty years old, would he not know what words would make him completely lose Kangxi's favor?

Yinzhi must have known he was a whetstone.

The First Prince of his previous life was extremely arrogant and conceited, looking down on him as the Crown Prince. Yinzhi believed that as the eldest son, he was qualified to compete with him.

Didn't Father give him so much power and let so many court officials defect to him to challenge the Crown Prince because he recognized his ability and was wavering in his choice of heir?

It wasn't until the first deposition of the Crown Prince that Yinzhi saw clearly: he was never a candidate for the throne, but the stone used to sharpen the heir.

Anyone could become the Crown Prince, except for him, the whetstone.

Because when the blade of the Crown Prince was worn out, the whetstone would certainly be worn out too.

And if the blade of the Crown Prince was not worn out and successfully ascended the throne, the whetstone would surely be smashed.

Yinzhi's future was already doomed.

They were all a group of cowardly princes. They could only hate each other and target each other even more crazily.

As a whetstone, Yinzhi could only hate the blade that tortured him as much as he tortured it.

What else could he do?

Yinreng thought of Old Thirteen again.

Was the Old Thirteen who was re-employed in the Yongzheng era already cold-blooded? Or was Old Thirteen's early death partly due to the depression caused by watching the tragedy of the brothers continue in the Kangxi era?

"Little brother, why are you hugging so tight?" Yinzhi, who was able to sleep with Yinreng again, was very happy. "Do you miss your brother that much?"

The three of them had successfully squeezed Kangxi into the next tent to sleep; if Yinzhi had a tail, it would be held high.

Yinreng joked: "That's right. Look, Third Brother almost got lost, what if I got lost? I have to hug First Brother tight, First Brother will protect me!"

Yinzi also hugged Yinzhi tightly: "First Brother protect me!"

Yinzhi sneered: "Little Third, you used to fight with me all the time. Now you want me to protect you?"

Yinzi: "...Then, I won't let you protect me."

Yinzi let go and turned his back to Yinzhi.

Yinzhi laughed out loud and turned Yinzi back around to hug him.

One little brother in each arm, Yinzhi was a winner in life!

"A-ang!" A high-pitched, displeased cry came from the cradle in front of the three princes.

Baby Yinzhen: So noisy! Can't a person get some sleep!

"Quiet, quiet, don't wake up Fourth Brother." Yinreng quickly lowered his voice.

Yinzhi: "Aow, aow, aow, alright, alright."

Babies are truly terrifying!

Kangxi was worried about the children and peeked into the tent in the middle of the night to see them sleeping.

A candle was kept burning all night in the tent so that the palace servants wouldn't step on anything while adjusting the princes' blankets.

Kangxi saw Yinreng and Yinzi curled up obediently on either side of Yinzhi, and then saw Yinzhi sleeping in an extremely arrogant "spread-eagle" position.

He gasped.

Kangxi wanted to pick up the First Prince and lie down there himself.

Shouldn't the children be surrounding him and relying on him to sleep! Yinzhi, aren't you being too arrogant! That was supposed to be my spot!

Kangxi crept in stealthily, scooped up the soundly sleeping Yinreng from the blankets, and ran.

The next morning, Yinreng was woken up by Kangxi getting up, and he stared blankly at Kangxi's face.

"Father?" Yinreng was extremely confused.

That's not right, didn't I sleep with First Brother and Third Brother yesterday?

Kangxi said calmly: "You sleepwalked and came to find Me yesterday."

Yinreng: "Huh?"

Father, I'm not a real child, you can't fool me!

Kangxi had someone carry Yinreng back and stuffed him into the arms of Yinzhi, who was still fast asleep.

Yinzhi reflexively hugged Yinreng and continued to sleep soundly.

Yinreng was still full of question marks.

Liang Jiugong and Zhao Chang, who had witnessed this, exchanged a terrified look that said, "Are we going to be silenced?"

Stealing your son in the middle of the night?! Is this something an Emperor can do?!

Actually, if it weren't the Emperor, who else could do it?!

Liang Jiugong and Zhao Chang were still shaken by the shock from last night.

Fortunately, Kangxi himself felt it was embarrassing, so he only stole Yinreng once, and then used the excuse that "Yinzhi's sleeping posture is too bad, and Yinreng isn't sleeping well while recovering, so he should sleep with Me," to take Yinreng away and only return him during the day.

Liang Jiugong and Zhao Chang exchanged another terrified look.

Your Majesty! Don't you think this is even more embarrassing!

Yinreng sighed.

What should one do with a father who is too clingy?

He hoped to move back to the palace soon so that there would be no crowding, Father wouldn't be afraid of people eavesdropping, and he could go back to the inner palace to sleep with his consorts, so he wouldn't keep using him as a body pillow.

As for the heavy arm Kangxi kept pinning him down with, Yinreng still preferred cuddling and sleeping with his brothers.

45. Three Chapters in One (30k Nutrient Liquid Extra) [V]

When Yinzhi called the playboy guards for a meeting again, he brought his three younger brothers along.

Every one of these playboys wanted to do something big but lacked the ability, and wanted to rebel against their families but lacked the guts.

The First Prince gave them a non-dangerous opportunity, so they followed him happily.

When their families asked, they just said they were supporting the First Prince in his work.

Supporting the First Prince—wasn't that just following the family's line?

No problem there!

But this time, they arrived full of enthusiasm, only to find that their "secret base" had turned into a children's playroom.

You had to take off your shoes and socks and wash your feet before entering?

The carpet felt quite comfortable to step on.

Why was there a pile of cloth dolls and soft cushions?

These building blocks and little cars looked quite fun.

Damn! Who are these little dolls?!

Yinzhi sat on a tiger-skin chair, acting like a mountain king.

In front of him, the Third Prince Yinzi, who was not yet three but walked the steadiest, was holding the hand of the rehabilitating little Crown Prince Yinreng, while the Fourth Prince Yinzhen crawled behind the little Crown Prince; the three of them strolled around the tent, and when they got tired, they just sat on the ground and rolled around playing with toys.

After a moment of stunned silence, the guards offered their greetings in a disorganized fashion. Nalan Xingde stepped forward, knelt on one knee, and asked, "Your Highness the Crown Prince, are you feeling any better?"

Yinreng wiped the cold sweat from his forehead with a handkerchief and smiled, "I'm better, I can get up from the bed now. Don't worry about me; the more I move around, the faster my body will fully recover."

Cao Yin also knelt on one knee before Yinreng, his eyes slightly red, "It is truly wonderful to see that Your Highness is unharmed."

Cao Yin was a *booi* trusted by Kangxi; he knew things that Nalan Xingde did not.

If there hadn't been others present, Cao Yin would have picked the Crown Prince up in his arms and wept.

When he and Nalan Xingde followed the Crown Prince to wander around the city, he had done such things that defied etiquette more than once.

"It's alright, it's alright, I've made you worry." Yinreng reached out his hand, and as Cao Yin lowered his head, Yinreng gently rubbed his shaved forehead, "Rest assured, I am very resilient; my body will recover in no time."

Cao Yin let out a whimper while kneeling on one knee before Yinreng, looking just like a large dog, which left the other guards full of question marks.

Guard Cao, is that really necessary!

Although this group of noble scions didn't think much of Cao Yin, a mere *booi*, he was still an Imperial Guard!

After patting Cao Yin's forehead, Yinreng patted the arm of Nalan Xingde, who was also kneeling before him, "I am truly fine, do not worry."

Nalan Xingde barely managed to control the mix of surprise and worry in his heart, forcing himself to remain calm, "Yes."

"Alright, alright, how could anything happen to my younger brother? You all are overthinking it." The "mountain king" Yinzhi waved his hand, "Let's continue our discussion, ignore them, let them play by themselves."

The guards: "..." Eldest Prince, the person in front of you is the Crown Prince! The Crown Prince's status is higher than yours! The Crown Prince is crawling on the floor, and you are sitting on a chair—are you the Em... (sound muted)?

"Right, no need to mind us." Yinreng said gently, "Big Brother, please continue."

Yinzhi nodded and then scolded, "Why are you all so surprised? Khan Ama is busy, and as his older brother, I have to look after my younger brother in my spare time—what's wrong with that? Don't you have siblings at home? Have you never been looked after by an older brother, or looked after a younger brother yourselves?"

Nalan Xingde had already stood up from the floor and chuckled, "I have."

The other guards looked at each other.

It seemed... it wasn't like they hadn't done that before, right? It was just unexpected that being an older brother in the Imperial Palace was similar to how it was in their own homes.

Since both the Eldest Prince and the Crown Prince had spoken, they could only sit stiffly on the cushioned chairs and continue their discussion.

While discussing, their attention couldn't help but drift toward the Crown Prince, who was walking and crawling on the floor from time to time.

The Crown Prince's body was indeed very weak—so weak that his walking was less steady than the Third Prince's, and his stamina was shorter than the Fourth Prince's, who could only crawl.

Yet, they couldn't bring themselves to look down on the Crown Prince in the slightest.

They had been sick too. Not to mention how miserable it was when they were ill, even on normal days, if their families didn't force them to train and exercise, they were too lazy to move. The Crown Prince was still just a child, yet he possessed such great perseverance.

How could a young child, who was struggling to survive, had no gloom on his face, and could still take care of his younger brothers and make them happy even when he was at his most uncomfortable, not evoke love and pity in any normal person?

It was understandable that Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin would be so uncomposed.

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin had also been watching Yinreng quietly.

As they watched, Cao Yin's eyes turned red again, and Nalan Xingde clenched his fists.

Such a good child as the Crown Prince, yet there were rumors outside saying bad things about him—saying the Crown Prince was aloof and didn't get along with the other princes; saying that when the Crown Prince was ill, his temperament changed drastically, becoming hysterical, crying, and beating the servants; saying that the Crown Prince was so ill he had no appetite, requiring many chickens and ducks for every meal, eating only the flavor and not the meat, throwing away the delicacies and forbidding others from eating them...

They slandered a five-year-old child just as they would a political rival in the court. If it weren't for people like Gu Zhenguan, who often walked among the common folk and sensed the signs of this, and reported it to the Emperor, they might have truly succeeded amidst the chaos following the earthquake.

Just then, as Yinreng needed to eat small, frequent meals, Liang Jiugong brought over Yinreng's nutritional meal.

Yinzi curiously took a bite, then struggled to swallow it, "It's so awful! Crown Prince Brother, why do you eat this!"

"How awful is it?" Yinzhi jumped down from his "mountain king" tiger-skin chair and took a bite too, "It really is awful. What kind of ghost taste is this? You eat this?! Your appetite is already bad, and you eat this?! Won't your appetite get even worse!"

Yinreng comforted him, "You get used to it. Before, I couldn't swallow anything, so the Imperial Kitchen ground nutritious meats and vegetables into a paste to make soup, which is easier to eat. They can't add spices to mask the fishy smell, the oil and salt can't be heavy, and they have to add some medicinal herbs. For the Imperial Kitchen to make it like this is already quite good."

Yinzhi said unhappily, "They can think of other ways!"

Yinreng continued to soothe him with a smile, "I can already get out of bed and walk; I'll be able to eat other things soon. When that time comes, Big Brother can treat me to something delicious."

Yinzi hugged Yinreng's waist and unhappily rubbed his face against it, "Yinzi will give all his delicious cakes to Crown Prince Brother too."

"Thank you, Third Brother." Yinreng rubbed the back of Yinzi's head.

"Alright, brother will take you to eat a big feast." Yinzhi took a few more bites, scolding as he ate, "It's really awful! It's disgusting!"

"Don't say 'disgusting' (dead), it's unlucky." Yinreng was caught between laughter and tears, "If it's not good, why are you still eating it?"

Yinzhi said, "I just want to taste more of exactly how awful it is, to see how many times it takes to get used to it."

"Alright, alright, Brother, go do your proper work, don't worry about me." Yinreng pushed Yinzhi away.

Yinreng had no strength at all right now; how could he possibly push Yinzhi?

Yet Yinzhi acted as if he were being pushed, shouting, "Don't push, don't push, I can walk myself!"

A warm feeling couldn't help but rise in the hearts of the watching guards.

The Crown Prince was good, the Eldest Prince was good, the Third Prince was good—aside from the Fourth Prince, who was just crawling around making "ah-ah" sounds without showing his personality yet, the princes were all very good and cute.

How did the Emperor raise his children? How did he manage to raise them so well?

And, this thing that looked so awful at first glance—was this the "delicacies that outsiders couldn't imagine being extravagant and wasteful" that the outside world spoke of?

The guards wanted to go home and tell their elders that the princes had deep affection for each other and the Crown Prince was a very good person, so they should stop playing those little tricks.

But then they thought, if their elders learned of these things, they might come up with even more disgusting schemes. It was better to keep them in the dark, letting them continue to be self-righteous in their picking and choosing regarding the princes.

Although the guards hadn't done anything, they felt a sense of satisfaction, as if they had successfully tricked their own elders.

Yinzhi continued to discuss with them the plan to compile a massive work integrating ancient myths, changing the "narrow ethnic divisions" into the "great unification of the Yan and Huang clans."

Although the guards didn't understand why Yinzhi wanted to do this, it sounded fun, so they all played along, though their enthusiasm was somewhat misplaced.

They didn't have a deep understanding of Chinese mythology and were just throwing out random ideas based on their feelings.

Yinzhi was also young, and as they talked, they ended up bragging and telling stories. No one mentioned how to divide the work or how to execute it.

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin were originally sent by Kangxi to help Yinzhi, but because they didn't quite understand the reason for Yinzhi's actions and thought he was just messing around, they let Yinzhi do as he pleased and did not lead the meeting.

Yinreng felt a headache coming on.

He clapped his hands, "Interrupting for a moment."

Yinzhi immediately shut his mouth.

The other guards also fell silent.

Wait, why was the Crown Prince's aura so strong?

"You lot, you can't even offer a single useful opinion." Yinzhi didn't forget to shift the blame and help cover for Yinreng at this moment, "Little Brother, you come and teach them!"

He ordered the eunuchs to pick up Yinreng and place him in his arms, and the two little princes also cried out, wanting to join.

Thus, on the wide tiger-skin chair, the Eldest Prince Yinzhi sat in the middle, with the little Crown Prince Yinreng on his lap, and the Third and Fourth Princes sitting and lying on either side of him.

The chair was indeed large enough.

Yinzhi’s appearance, with one in his arms and one on his lap, would have been quite the romantic scene if the subjects were beauties instead of his younger brothers.

In any case, Yinzhi's expression was extremely proud.

The guards watched this scene, barely able to hold back a benevolent, fatherly smile.

"I will start from the beginning, explaining why this needs to be done." Yinreng held a cup of hot goat milk to moisten his throat, gathered a bit of strength, and slowly began to explain why he wanted to compile the myths and legends.

Before that, he needed to guide the thinking of this group of noble scions, making them join this cause sincerely and be of use to him.

If they couldn't understand the significance of this matter and didn't want to do it from the bottom of their hearts, the effect of the propaganda would be much smaller.

If they didn't believe in it themselves, how could they convince others to believe it through their propaganda?

This matter was important, and since Kangxi had already discovered that this was done by Yinreng "directing" Yinzhi, there was no need for Yinreng to hide it too much.

He would just pull all his brothers into it; they could split the credit equally later.

Yinreng first had the eunuchs serve tea to the guards, and only after the guards had calmed down from their previous aimless chatter did he speak softly.

"Aside from Rongruo and Ziqing, all of you have reputations as 'playboys' in the capital; I have heard of this in the palace as well."

The guards' expressions immediately turned very ugly.

Yinreng looked at Nalan Xingde, "Although Rongruo cannot be counted as a playboy, his reputation among the nobles in the capital is even worse than that of a playboy. In the eyes of many nobles, being able to read, write poetry, and compose lyrics is not considered the work of a serious person."

Nalan Xingde gave a bitter smile. The other guards' expressions eased slightly.

Yinreng glanced at Cao Yin again. Cao Yin was a *booi*, so it wasn't appropriate to list him among the nobles.

Cao Yin smiled and winked at Yinreng, signaling that he didn't need to worry about him.

Yinreng pondered for a moment and said, "As for Ziqing, there is even less need to say. In the past, among the Han people, aside from military generals with their own armies, those most trusted by the Emperor were entered into the Upper Three Banners as *booi*, while others entered the Han Army Banners or the Lower Five Banners. Then there were those from the Upper Three Banners who, after being heavily used, were entered into the *booi* to handle affairs for the Emperor. Now, rumors outside make it sound as if the Upper Three Banner *booi* are the slaves of all the Bannermen. Are they worthy of saying that?"

Yinreng swept his gaze across the guards, making their faces burn.

They always felt that when Yinreng said "Are they worthy?", he was actually saying "Are you worthy?".

They usually didn't treat Cao Yin very well.

Cao Yin's fist, resting on his lap, tightened, and his smile faded.

Nalan Xingde, sitting beside him, gently patted Cao Yin's fist, winking and nodding at him.

Cao Yin returned a "don't mess around" look to Nalan Xingde.

Yinreng's eyes were almost blinded by the two of them exchanging glances.

No wonder his Ama often complained that when Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde were on duty together, they were always exchanging glances behind his back; he even said his Ama used the idiom incorrectly.

If this wasn't "exchanging glances," what was?!

The friendship between ancient scholars was truly sticky.

Yinreng recalled the poems Cao Yin would write about Nalan Xingde in the future.

Hmm, ten years after Nalan Xingde passed away, Cao Yin wrote a poem to cherish his memory, starting with "The man from Lengjia Mountain has a beautiful appearance," and then following with "Every household competes to sing the *Yinshui* lyrics, but who has ever known Nalan's heart?" If one didn't know these two were friends...

Forget it, the *Man Jiang Hong* that Nalan Xingde wrote for Cao Yin wasn't any better.

Because Nalan Xingde boasted about Cao Yin too much, some people even said Nalan Xingde was fawning over Kangxi's high-ranking officials, without even looking at what Nalan Xingde's status was. This was just friends chatting and boasting to support each other; Nalan Xingde was also just an ordinary young man.

In the lyrics Nalan Xingde wrote for other friends, one was high-minded, another was talented—all filled with the subtlety of a scholar. When Cao Yin asked him to write a poem to boast about himself and his ancestors, what kind of nonsense did Nalan Xingde write? He started by wildly boasting, then said the Emperor's calligraphy at your house is great, I'm envious, I want it.

I wonder if Cao Yin, upon seeing that rare, opulent, "fawning" poem that Nalan Xingde wrote, wanted to take down the plaque with the Emperor's calligraphy and hit his mischievous friend with it.

Perhaps he really did hit him.

Kangxi had Nalan Xingde manage the horses and Cao Yin manage the hunting dogs, so the two mocked each other as "Horse Cao" and "Dog Warden." Later, the mocking went too far and they agreed to fight, which amused Kangxi so much that he told the story to Yinreng as a joke.

The Nalan Xingde in Cao Yin's eyes was indeed truly different from the Nalan Xingde known to the public through the *Yinshui Ci*.

While Yinreng was distracted by gossip, the guards were breaking out in a cold sweat.

Appropriate silence was more stressful than a constant, machine-gun-like chatter.

Kangxi often did this, saying only half of what he meant, keeping the officials in suspense, and only continuing after they were sweating from anxiety.

The Crown Prince was truly worthy of being a Crown Prince taught personally by the Emperor; his rhythm of speaking was exactly the same.

Yinreng finished his distraction and continued, "All of your confusion and the incompatibility with your elders are due to one reason: the times have changed."

The guards all looked up in unison, their gazes shooting toward Yinreng.

Yinreng tapped his fingers on the table; his fleshy fingers didn't wear thumb rings, so they made no sound.

Yinzhi immediately slammed his palm onto the table with a "thwack" to provide sound effects for Yinreng.

Yinreng suppressed the slight twitch at the corner of his mouth and continued speaking.

"All these contradictions are because the times have changed. Your elders, and my elders, originally herded in the green mountains and black waters. Their hearts are still in those poor mountains and treacherous waters; after entering the Central Plains, they couldn't adjust their mindset, still thinking they are free-roaming herdsmen, looking at everything in the Central Plains as if they were outsiders or even enemies."

"But you are different. Since you can remember, you have been people of the Central Plains, growing up on this fertile land. In your hearts, the vast territory of the Great Qing is your hometown, not that small patch of mountains and water; all the prosperous culture of the Central Plains is the cultural foundation you have been exposed to since childhood, not the Later Jin, which didn't even have a written language before entering the pass."

"The times have changed; you are not savages or mercenaries from outside the pass; you are the nobles of the Great Qing, the aristocracy, the future great families."

"Your horizons are broader than your elders', your knowledge is more profound than your elders', and your ambitions are, compared to theirs, like those of a sparrow to a swan."

Yinreng's expression was very weary, his speech pausing and stopping.

The guards' expressions, however, became increasingly excited, their eyes growing brighter, as if they had been enlightened and suddenly saw the light.

"Everyone's thoughts are forged by their experiences. They grew up in narrow places and can only have narrow thoughts; you were born into wealth and grew up in a vast world, and what you see, think, and imagine is different from them. This ideological contradiction is irreconcilable."

"That is why you sink, why you are playboys, why you are rebellious. Because no matter how you struggle, those old people whose eyes are covered by the past will only sneer at all your opinions."

Yinreng took a deep breath and said, "Do not eavesdrop at the door. I am not Khan Ama; I really will punish you severely."

Elundai sheepishly entered and bowed, "Your Highness the Crown Prince, I am wronged; I am here on the Emperor's orders to convey an imperial decree."

That's right, the jerk Elundai had been reinstated again.

Kangxi truly loved his maternal clan.

"Speak." Yinreng said unceremoniously, "Besides 'have you eaten, have you drunk, don't be too tired,' what else is there?"

Elundai said very frankly, "Nothing else. Your Highness, can I sit here and listen too?"

Yinreng rubbed his forehead, "If you want to listen, then listen."

Elundai immediately kicked off his boots happily, rinsed his feet with the hot water brought by the eunuch, squeezed past a guard, and sat down next to Nalan Xingde.

Nalan Xingde: "..." He started to feel uncomfortable all over.

Elundai rubbed his hands together, "Your Highness, please continue, please continue! I think what Your Highness said is particularly good! Those old fogies are just useless!"

The guards: "..."

With the capital's most famous "father-pitting" playboy Elundai joining the secret chat, Yinreng started to get a headache.

Forget it, if there's a headache, it's Ama's headache; I'll just stir up trouble and not worry about the consequences.

Five-year-old Yinreng continued to fan the flames.

His words weren't entirely deception; they were partially facts.

The Eight Banners system originally stemmed from the pitifully small manpower and extremely scarce strategic resources of the Later Jin.

They had few people, so organizing them into Eight Banners was enough.

Therefore, when Nurhaci first set up the Eight Banners, he never thought he could enter the Central Plains, let alone what he would do after entering.

This guy, who hated all Han people and scholars, probably thought that if he were lucky enough to enter the Central Plains, he would just organize everyone into the Eight Banners.

By the Shunzhi reign, the Great Qing officially became the master of the Chinese land, but those old Manchu nobles couldn't adjust their mindset.

They still treated the Central Plains within the pass as "someone else's land" they had snatched, and the people of the Central Plains as "outsiders and enemies." So they had to build high walls, consolidate the Eight Banners system—which should have been disbanded after entering the pass—and isolate themselves from the vast world.

This matter should have been completed by Shunzhi. Since Shunzhi passed away early, this burden fell on Kangxi.

If Kangxi didn't complete this, it would be very difficult for the Great Qing to change later.

Actually, in the original history, although Kangxi was conservative, he did make changes; Yongzheng took up Kangxi's mantle, and even though his foreign wars were a complete mess, his internal reforms were quite good.

By the time of Qianlong, he started to restore the old ways. The efforts made by Yongzheng were completely overturned by him; he almost dug up Yongzheng's grave.

Qianlong was a decent emperor in his early years, but later he was terrified by the successive revolutions abroad and only wanted to close his eyes and dream his beautiful dream of ten thousand generations.

From Qianlong onwards, the education of princes in the palace no longer involved foreign knowledge.

Later generations couldn't understand: you, Qianlong, were afraid of foreign ideologies and technologies spreading into the Great Qing, so restricting the common people and foreigners from contact was understandable, but why forbid the princes from learning it?

Kangxi and Yongzheng were also vigilant, but their vigilance was that both they and the princes were experts on foreign affairs, with a clear understanding of world maps and political landscapes. Kangxi even had multiple foreign emperors as pen pals; Yongzheng also collected many foreign affairs for Qianlong to read.

Qianlong read them, got scared, waved his hand, closed his eyes, and pretended these things didn't exist, locking up all the materials.

Two years into the Opium War, Qianlong's grandson, Daoguang, was still foolishly asking where England was, never having even seen a world map.

This is truly sleeping through one's own dream; it's incredible.

Yinreng took a deep breath.

Change! It must be changed!

Start by abolishing the Eight Banners "Heavenly People" system!

All systems start to rot from the inside; I will unite all the young people who are dissatisfied with the elders' nagging and give those old Manchu and Mongol nobles a vicious backstab!

"You have probably already heard what they are going to do to the Bannermen. Bannermen can only receive a pitiful fixed salary and are forbidden from farming, industry, or trade. Does that sound good to you? Does getting money for nothing feel very aristocratic?"

"But you calculate it: how many people will the Bannermen increase to in a few generations? How many people can receive the grain salary? The Han people are landlords and wealthy merchants, wearing gold and silver and eating until they are stuffed, while the Bannermen have to fence themselves in, forbidden from this and that—on what grounds?"

Elundai pounded the table hard: "Exactly! On what grounds!"

Yinreng was startled by Elundai, glanced at him, and then continued speaking.

"Do you really want your descendants to shrink into this small patch of the capital? Even if officials have money, opportunities will only be given to the most talented one among the direct descendants. You are all playboys despised by your families; you should have already experienced the unfairness of resource allocation, right? Even your own Ama won't help you, but will help your cousins or even distant cousins."

"Exactly! It's too much!" Elundai said indignantly.

Yinreng: "..." Who is unfair? You, Elundai, have never encountered unfairness.

He took a deep breath and maintained his original pace: "I can understand them. They say they look down on others, but in reality, they fear others. They clearly should integrate into this vast land; this land is already entirely our land. Yet they think that if they step out, they will lose that little bit of land they have in their hands."

"The Bannermen are all locked in this capital, making it seem as if we possess the four seas, while the four seas still belong to the people of the previous dynasty and have nothing to do with us."

Elundai pounded the table again, blowing his beard and staring: "Well said! A bunch of cowards!"

The guards looked at Elundai one after another.

Yinreng: "They say they don't want to become Han people. But what are Han people? Do they really understand? Elundai, you shout the loudest, what are the original Han people?"

Elundai smiled: "I can answer that. Han people are just the people under the rule of the Han Dynasty established by Liu Bang."

Yinreng nodded: "After the Han Dynasty, the Three Kingdoms, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties were a period of great chaos; the people longed for a unified country and had no sense of identity with the fleeting regimes that followed, so they still called themselves Han people. From south to north, from east to west, as long as you recognize the Han Dynasty, you are a Han person. Han people are a cultural concept, which is why their inclusiveness is so strong."

"If you don't like the concept of 'Han people,' then just change it, seek something further back; this is why I asked you to compile the mythological classics."

"The Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the Yan and Huang Huaxia. Was Zhou an outsider to Shang? Was Qin an outsider to the other six states? But as long as they take root in this land, how can they be considered outsiders? Even the Yuan Dynasty—can they be considered outsiders? They once submitted to the emperors of many dynasties; they were subjects, they were not outsiders!"

"Tracing back through history, the place where we started our rise was Youzhou of the Han, the Yan land of the Zhou; from ancient times to the present, it has been the orthodox Huaxia."

"We must continue to search, search from the ancient era, from the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, or even earlier. If the nobles of the Great Qing are unwilling to be crowned with the title of Han Dynasty subjects, then re-establish the cultural orthodoxy. Huaxia people, Yan-Huang people—our ancestors were originally the same."

Yinreng caught his breath and said, "Give those stubborn old fogies who stick to their old ways a way to step down, and force them to break the shell that covers us."

"Whatever other great families in past dynasties could enjoy, you can all enjoy; whatever they could achieve, you can also achieve. What Khan Ama wants is for the Great Qing to become a new, brilliant dynasty in the history of the Huaxia nation, a dynasty even more brilliant than any in the past. You should also be the heroic ministers of this brilliant dynasty whose names are recorded in history, not cowering within the high walls of the capital, shrinking and hiding for the sake of so-called Manchu orthodoxy."

"Besides, the so-called Manchu nation has existed for less than fifty years, established by Emperor Taizong; it actually has little to do with any traditional ancestors." Yinreng drank a mouthful of goat milk and licked the white foam on his lips, "Our history is not that short."

Now even Elundai didn't dare to cheer.

All the guards present were stunned, terrified, and uncertain.

Yinzhi hugged Yinreng and rubbed against him, lowering his head to secretly drink a mouthful of goat milk from Yinreng's cup.

"Ahem, did you understand?" Yinzhi, whose chin was pushed by Yinreng, summarized, "This matter is very important to the Great Qing. Whether the Great Qing can truly become the master of this land, instead of shrinking in the capital and watching the people of the previous dynasty govern themselves, depends on you."

"Don't think that just because we send officials, we can govern the people. Think about it: if you send someone to a place where they are unfamiliar with the people and the place, can you manage it? Don't joke." Yinzhi said, "The meeting ends here for today; my younger brother is tired. You decide for yourselves: if you want to participate in this matter and leave your names in history, come back tomorrow. Those who don't come just need to keep their mouths shut."

Yinzhi swept his gaze over everyone: "I have remembered all your names. Whoever's family leaks news about today's meeting first, that person is their Ama and Niang's 'good baby,' a child who hasn't been weaned yet. My words are a compliment, not a scolding."

The guards: "..."

Eldest Prince, you are ruthless!

Elundai scratched his head: "Should I not have barged in halfway?"

He felt a bit of regret.

Yinreng rolled his eyes at Elundai: "You're already here."

Elundai laughed heartily: "That's true, I'm already here. I'll go back to report first!"

Yinreng was speechless. You came to deliver an imperial decree and even made the Emperor wait for you? The Emperor didn't execute you; it's truly true love.

Kangxi was thinking the same thing.

After Elundai was reinstated, he sent him to deliver an imperial decree; why had Elundai disappeared?

Kangxi was busy, suppressing his urge to find someone to urge him, waiting for Elundai to return.

He waited and waited, and by the time he had finished his own work, Elundai finally returned, swinging his arms and legs.

Kangxi immediately picked up a whip and lashed out at Elundai: "I told you to deliver an imperial decree; why did it take you so long? Did you go off to mess around again? I vouched for you to Tong Guogang, saying you were capable of doing proper work. Is this how you repay me?!"

If Yinreng were here, he would definitely sigh; his habit of using a whip in his previous life was entirely learned from Kangxi.

Elundai scrambled around, protecting his head: "The Crown Prince spoke so well that I was mesmerized and lost track of time!"

Kangxi dropped the whip: "What did the Crown Prince say?"

Elundai said: "I can't say. If word gets out that I'm my father's obedient little baby, a child who hasn't been weaned yet, I'd rather just die."

Kangxi: "..."

These words definitely didn't come from Baocheng.

These words definitely came from Baoqing!

Kangxi took a deep breath and told Elundai to get lost immediately.

Elundai scrambled away, leaving Kangxi with the back of a hooligan.

Kangxi clutched his chest. If it weren't for pitying Tong Guogang, he wouldn't have to endure such aggravation.

"Go and see what Baocheng and Baoqing are doing." Kangxi slammed his hand on the table.

Kangxi had a very ominous premonition about a topic that could keep a scoundrel and rascal like Elundai listening obediently for so long.

...

Kangxi found the children.

Kangxi listened to the reports from others.

Kangxi was lost in thought.

Kangxi... Kangxi didn't know what to say.

Could you say it was wrong? It was actually quite right. If this matter could be accomplished, it would certainly be a great help to his subsequent reforms.

But how did Yinreng... become so good at speaking?

Kangxi recalled that the late Emperor Shunzhi had likely been whispering in his son's dreams for years; perhaps the fact that his son could speak so early was all thanks to Emperor Shunzhi.

Kangxi realized.

Unknowingly, his Khan-father had already snatched away the enlightenment of his precious son from him, and now his son was completely in the image of Emperor Shunzhi. (Yinreng: That really wasn't necessary...)

"Khan-father, if this matter is done well, the older and younger brothers will all have merit!" Yinreng's eyes sparkled, his short hands cupped together like a little milk kitten bowing, "The names of the third and fourth younger brothers must also be printed in the 'Compendium of Ancient and Modern Mythology'."

Kangxi wanted to say something but stopped, only able to pick up Yinreng and pat him: "Alright."

He had persuaded him for so long not to trust his brothers too much. Yinreng was now willing to work, but he still insisted on sharing the credit with others.

The First Prince was one thing, but even the Third Prince, who hadn't started his education, and the Fourth Prince, who could barely talk or walk, were being given credit by him.

Well, so be it. What else could he do?

The official recording the meeting had already listed the attendees, with the Third and Fourth Princes' names listed right there, and both were even seated in the main seats.

Kangxi was curious about what kind of image future generations would imagine when they read this part of history.

They would never guess that "seated in the main seats" meant Yinzhi was curled up on a tiger-skin chair holding his three younger brothers while dozing off, while Yinreng was the only one there chattering away.

Kangxi suspected that the Fourth Prince, Yinzhen, had been "ah-ing" non-stop since childhood because he was influenced by the little chatterbox Yinreng.

Kangxi rubbed Yinreng again. Yinreng yawned, lay down in Kangxi's arms, and let him rub away; he wanted to sleep.

Before falling asleep, Yinreng asked: "Father, Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin are really flirting with each other!"

Kangxi chuckled: "You saw that?"

Yinreng smiled: "Rongruo was even touching Ziqing's hand under the table."

Kangxi laughed so hard he couldn't straighten up: "They still do such little things?"

Yinreng nodded: "Father, they have such a good relationship. I want friends like that too."

Kangxi thought for a moment and said: "I will recruit a few hahazhu (playmates) for you."

Yinreng shook his head: "Those aren't friends. My friends must at least be princes from other countries. Without equal status, one cannot become true friends."

Cao Yin had introduced many friends to Nalan Xingde, and some even became sworn brothers. But their poetry exchanges were always overly polite. Those people needed to rely on Nalan Xingde's power, so there was always something impure in their friendship.

Unlike Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde, they didn't need to use poetry or paintings to socialize; they could just chat, talk nonsense, brag, mock each other, and laugh at each other, and spend a happy day.

Kangxi said: "Alright. I also want to write to the monarchs of other countries, you can join me."

Yinreng hugged Kangxi's arm and rubbed against it.

He knew Kangxi had such thoughts. Although the "previous, previous life" was a long time away, we can start early in this lifetime.

...

Yinreng took the lead with his brothers, but the subsequent troublesome matters still had to be handled by Kangxi himself.

He let Yinzhi do it just to see how far Yinzhi could go.

In the end, he concluded that Yinzhi could probably only go as far as making people die of anger; as a deputy to Yinreng, one playing the bad cop and the other the good cop, it worked very well.

My Baocheng is the most capable! Worthy of being my Crown Prince!

Even with Shunzhi's guidance, the credit must definitely be mine!

Kangxi also attended the third meeting.

The guards didn't run away, and they were stunned when they saw Kangxi appear.

They were glad they hadn't run. Following the Crown Prince was indeed the right path! The elders at home didn't know a damn thing!

Yinreng smiled: "You don't need to be too surprised. My Khan-father is also a young man, just like you."

Kangxi smiled without a word, only gently pinching Yinreng's bottom.

The guards suddenly realized.

So that whole speech from the Crown Prince about the younger generation and the older generation was instructed by the young Emperor himself!

We knew it. The Crown Prince is only five, what could he possibly understand?

If he understood so much, wouldn't it make us all look like real losers!

100,000
