I wonder which is more painful, starving to death or death by a thousand cuts.

Yinreng tightened his arms again.

Songgotu keenly felt Yinreng’s unhappiness, and he said in a low voice: "Is Your Highness tired? Shall I take you back to the Emperor?"

Yinreng shook his head: "Since I'm already here, they are all staring at me."

Songgotu glanced at the colleagues who were curiously looking at the fluffy Crown Prince and pressed Yinreng’s head into his arms.

Fuquan almost couldn't help but laugh out loud.

Songgotu’s action reminded him of Kangxi.

"Where is Changtai?" Songgotu knew that Changtai was more familiar with Yinreng and wanted to hand Yinreng to Changtai so that Yinreng could be more relaxed. But he looked around for a long time and didn't see him.

"He was called away by the Emperor," a minister said sourly. "When the eunuch came, he even called him 'Imperial Brother-in-law'."

Yinreng revealed his head from Songgotu’s arms: "Imperial Brother-in-law? How did Uncle make Father angry?"

Songgotu was puzzled: "Angry?"

Yinreng nodded: "Uncle told Father that he wanted to make a name for himself through his own ability, and Father agreed. So Father only calls Uncle 'Imperial Brother-in-law' when he is angry."

Yinreng paused and said helplessly: "To call Uncle 'Imperial Brother-in-law' in public, Father must be very angry. What did Uncle do? From so far away, it’s unlikely Uncle made Father angry."

The ministers looked at each other.

"Is that so?! They thought this was a sign of the Emperor’s favor for Changtai, but it turned out the Emperor was angry!"

They remembered Changtai’s helpless and bitter smile.

So Changtai’s bitter smile wasn't because he didn't want to show off, but because he knew the Emperor was angry?

The Emperor’s heart is hard to fathom!

Songgotu was also shocked.

He had followed the young Emperor sitting above from the beginning to the present, and prided himself on accurately guessing the imperial will, but both his older brother and the Crown Prince said he didn't understand the Emperor’s heart.

It turned out he really didn't understand!

He couldn't even figure out why calling him "Imperial Brother-in-law" meant he was angry, and he couldn't figure out why being angry meant calling him "Imperial Brother-in-law"!

Isn't this very intimate!

Songgotu looked at his old friend Mingju.

Mingju: "???" Why are you looking at me?

Songgotu humbly asked for advice: "I didn't understand this, Mingju, do you understand?"

Mingju: "???" Why are you asking me!

Yinreng asked: "Is the friend Great-Uncle wants to introduce to me Lord Mingju? Have you and Lord Mingju become friends?"

Mingju: "..."

The ministers: "..."

Songgotu looked at Mingju’s extremely ugly expression and nodded: "Yes, that’s right."

Songgotu’s categorical statement was like dropping a cannonball into the hearts of the ministers, shocking everyone.

This incident was passed to Kangxi’s ears by a little eunuch who was eavesdropping nearby.

Kangxi looked at Changtai, whom he was punishing with wine, and laughed: "What’s going on with Songgotu? When did he become friends with Mingju? How come I didn't know?!"

Changtai pressed his throbbing temples and drank the third pot of wine.

Kangxi saw his small movements, knew he didn't want to come up to drink, and immediately sent someone to drag him over.

"Don't want to drink? Then you'll be punished with wine!"

Changtai finished the third pot, and there were three more to go.

Kangxi said he had already prepared a sedan chair and an imperial physician, and would send someone to carry Changtai back once he was drunk.

Changtai smiled bitterly; it seemed he couldn't avoid getting drunk.

"Uncle is disgusting Mingju," Changtai rubbed his temples, his consciousness still clear. "When facing Mingju, he likes to hurt others even if it doesn't benefit himself. If it were a fight, he would like to use his own head to hit Mingju’s head."

Kangxi laughed so hard he couldn't straighten up: "Very vivid, very lively. Changtai, do you want to try taking the imperial examination? I think you have talent."

Changtai said: "Okay, I will resign immediately and study behind closed doors."

"Get out, don't even think about it, I’m short of people now." Kangxi had someone take the wine pot away and bring the hangover soup.

He was just joking with Changtai and didn't really want Changtai to make a fool of himself at the New Year’s banquet.

Changtai said: "Your Majesty, you must find someone to replace me. I am in a hurry to go back to serve the sick. Changhai is clumsy, and I can't rest easy."

Kangxi waved his hand and said perfunctorily: "I know, I know, I know you are filial, I will definitely find you an assistant after the New Year."

Changtai held his forehead. "Finding an assistant means you won't let me go?"

"Fine, I'll find an excuse then."

"The palace is being renovated everywhere, and there is dust everywhere, which is not good for Baocheng’s recovery. During the first month, I want to send Baocheng to your house to recover." Kangxi began to talk about business.

Changtai thought for a while and said: "I really want the Crown Prince to live in my house, but my father and mother are both ill. Although I don't believe in these things, the Crown Prince’s health is important, and one cannot be too careful. My residence is really not the first choice for the Crown Prince to recover."

Kangxi sighed: "I know. But I don't trust other places. I can't send him to Songgotu’s house, can I? I’m afraid Songgotu will teach Baocheng bad things."

Changtai said: "With the Crown Prince’s intelligence, Songgotu can't teach him bad things. However, I don't recommend the Crown Prince going to my uncle’s house. My cousins are a bit stupid, and they have finally learned to behave themselves. If the Crown Prince goes, they will think they have a backer and will probably revert to their old ways. Why doesn't Your Majesty choose Prince Yu?"

Kangxi said: "Prince Yu’s heirs have died one after another; that place is unlucky."

Changtai was speechless. "Your Majesty, your words are too piercing."

Kangxi drank half a cup of wine and continued to sigh: "Looking for a trusted bondservant, their status is too low, and I don't like it; other clansmen are not good to the Crown Prince; trusted ministers, the younger generation of the Tong family has too many scoundrels, your family has sick people, and you can't go to Mingju’s house."

Changtai said: "Actually, going to Mingju’s house is not bad. Nalan Xingde is very good to the Crown Prince, and Mingju’s wife is a clansman. Although Mingju tends to favor the clan and the nobility, his wife and son are good to the Crown Prince. If Your Majesty is worried, just let the First Prince accompany the Crown Prince. The First Prince acts uprightly and can take good care of the Crown Prince."

Kangxi said in disbelief, "Baoking conducts himself uprightly?"

Changtai nodded. "The Eldest Prince conducts himself uprightly."

Kangxi asked very seriously, "In what way does he conduct himself uprightly?"

Changtai explained, "The Eldest Prince hates evil like a mortal enemy."

Kangxi pressed further, "...And how exactly does he hate evil like a mortal enemy?"

Changtai blinked and remained silent.

Kangxi pressed a hand to his forehead. "Let Zhen think on it some more. Come, drink!"

Changtai said gloomily, "Your Majesty, you just said this subject didn't need to drink anymore."

Kangxi slapped the table. "You don't have to drink penalty cups, but this is a toast of respect!"

Changtai: "..." *I will endure!*

Although Changtai wasn't carried out on a stretcher, it was pretty close.

Getting drunk at the New Year's banquet turned Changtai into the laughingstock of the court.

But soon, everyone's attention shifted away from Changtai.

Kangxi issued an imperial edict: because the reconstruction within the palace was not yet complete and the Crown Prince was young, it was inconvenient for him to spend the New Year in the palace; thus, he was temporarily sent to Nalan Mingzhu's residence to recuperate.

Moreover, the Eldest Prince and the Third Prince went along with him; only the Fourth and Fifth Princes, being too young, remained in the palace.

All at once, Mingzhu's prominence was unmatched, making him the single most envied man in the capital.

Songgotu cried until his collar was soaked through.

*Your Majesty! Why didn't you let the Crown Prince spend the first month at this old subject's manor! Have I not done enough?!*

*This old subject will go back right now to beat my brother and beat my son!*

After receiving the decree, Mingzhu was completely dumbfounded.

Looking at his eldest son, Nalan Xingde, who was the Crown Prince's trusted confidant, he asked, "Rongruo, do you know why this is?"

Suppressing a smile, Nalan Xingde said, "Rest assured, Ama, there is no special reason. His Majesty truly just wants the Crown Prince's health to recover quickly by changing his environment. It's just like how the Eldest Prince and the Third Prince were sent out of the palace to be raised back then."

Mingzhu asked, "Then why our house?"

Nalan Xingde replied, "His Majesty doesn't fully trust the imperial clansmen. Prince Yu has sick family members, Prince Gong is somewhat unreliable in his dealings, E-niang is of the Gūwalgiya clan, and I am the Crown Prince's confidant—naturally, he chose our home."

Nalan Xingde emphasized, "Ama, don't overthink it. The Crown Prince and the Eldest Prince are coming to stay at your son's place; it actually has nothing to do with you."

Mingzhu: "..." His hands itched—itched terribly—to beat his son!

Lady Gūwalgiya gave a dry cough.

Mingzhu sheepishly withdrew his hand. "Fine, fine. You are now the confidant of both the Emperor and the Crown Prince, far more capable than your Ama. Hmph!"

Nalan Xingde said, "The deep love between E-niang and Ama, and the absence of messy affairs in our inner courtyard, is also one of the reasons His Majesty chose our household."

Mingzhu stroked his fine beard. "That is true. Rongruo, when are you going to remarry? Right now, you only have an untitled concubine by your side. Let Ama find you... Hey, don't run!"

Nalan Xingde took off running, with Mingzhu chasing hard behind him.

Lady Gūwalgiya pressed a hand to her forehead and smiled softly.

Ah, this father and son.

48. Three-in-One Chapter [V]

Nalan Mingzhu and Lady Gūwalgiya were rare anomalies in this era. Almost all of Nalan Xingde's longing for romantic love came from his parents.

"One lifetime, one generation, one pair of souls"—Nalan Xingde wrote this into his poetry, moving countless women in future generations. Yet he merely tossed it casually into his verses; he never lived up to it himself.

When Nalan Xingde's wife entered the household, his concubine Lady Yan had already borne him an eldest son born out of wedlock. In the eight years between Lady Lu's death and his own passing, he not only fathered a posthumous son with Shen Wan, but also four daughters born of his wives and concubines.

Of course, ancient men often separated the soul from the flesh. Remembering his deceased wife did not prevent Nalan Xingde from living a suave, unrestrained life.

Therefore, someone like Nalan Mingzhu, who achieved true unity of soul and flesh, was simply incomprehensible in this era.

Because it was so incomprehensible, an imperial clansman who had been dismissed from office in later generations got bored and wrote a gossip book called *Xiaoting Zalu*, which thoroughly smeared Lady Gūwalgiya. The rumors about Mingzhu fearing his wife and Lady Gūwalgiya being savage and tyrannical originated from this very book.

In his past life, Yinreng had read many stories related to the Qing dynasty, and he had read this book as well.

The wild history account claimed that Lady Gūwalgiya gouged out a concubine's eyes, and the concubine's father crept up to her bedside at night to hack her to death, ultimately causing Mingzhu to be dismissed by Kangxi—a tale that had left a tremendous shock on his young mind.

Moreover, *Xiaoting Zalu* didn't even name her "Lady Gūwalgiya," but fabricated that Mingzhu's wife was "Lady Hesheli." Yinreng had good reason to believe that fellow wrote it to slander the Hesheli clan, and by extension, him.

Nalan Mingzhu married Lady Gūwalgiya in the eighth year of Shunzhi. Her father, Prince Ying of the First Rank Ajige, had failed in an uprising in the seventh year of Shunzhi and was executed in the tenth month of the eighth year. Nalan Mingzhu had married Lady Gūwalgiya just moments before Ajige's execution, thereby shielding and protecting her.

With such a tragic family background, it was impossible for Lady Gūwalgiya to be arrogant and domineering.

That act of romantic impulse dealt a heavy blow to Nalan Mingzhu's official career.

He had become a second-rank imperial bodyguard at the age of sixteen, achieving early success. Yet after marrying Lady Gūwalgiya, he remained stuck in that same position for thirteen whole years, receiving not a single promotion throughout the entire Shunzhi reign, until he was finally elevated to Supervisor of the Imperial Household Department in the third year of Kangxi.

By then, he was already twenty-nine years old.

As an ancient man, Nalan Mingzhu willingly delayed his official career to save his beloved, harboring neither resentment nor regret throughout those years. He lived in perfect harmony with Lady Gūwalgiya and never took a single concubine.

Lady Gūwalgiya passed away more than a decade before Nalan Mingzhu. During those dozen-odd years after his wife's death, Mingzhu never took a concubine or fathered another child either.

What profound and fathomless devotion! Which of those ancient men who penned moving poems mourning their dead wives could hold a candle to him?!

Nalan Xingde as a devoted romantic? Fake.

Nalan Mingzhu as a devoted romantic? Truer than true!

After Yinreng, dressed up like a little white bear, shared this gossip with Yinzhi and Yinzhi, the two elder brothers didn't quite grasp it, but the wet nurses, eunuchs, and palace maids riding in the carriage with the three princes wept until their eyes were swollen red.

*To think Chancellor Ming was this kind of man!*

*We must spread the beautiful love story of Chancellor Ming and his wife to the world!*

Yinzhi immediately clapped his hands. "This sounds fun! I'll hire an opera troupe to perform it. Don't tell anyone yet—I want to give Chancellor Ming a surprise!"

Having satisfied his craving for storytelling, Yinreng began trying to salvage the situation. "Don't do that. Chancellor Ming doesn't like people gossiping about his private affairs."

Yinzhi retorted, "What does whether he likes it or not have to do with me? I like it."

Yinreng said, "We're going to live at his house. What if he spits in our food?"

Yinzhi's eyes widened. "He can do that?!"

Yinreng replied, "Who knows? Even if he spit in it, we wouldn't be able to tell."

Yinzhi said, "Then we won't use his name; we'll adapt it into characters from a past dynasty."

When in doubt, shift it to previous dynasties.

Yinreng asked curiously, "Eldest Brother, why did you suddenly think of writing an opera?"

Yinzhi rubbed his nose sheepishly. "Imperial Father promised me that for E-niang's birthday this year, I could hire a small opera troupe to stage a play for her. In her spare time, E-niang loves reading romance stories. She will definitely love the story of Mingzhu's family."

Yinreng said, "Why didn't you say so earlier! This younger brother supports you!"

*Sorry, Lord Mingzhu, but my brother comes first.*

Yinzhi felt even more embarrassed. "It's my E-niang's affair, how could I trouble you with it?"

"How could it be trouble?" Yinreng said, looking pitiful. "Eldest Brother, I don't have an E-niang, so I can't celebrate a birthday for her. Won't you please include me?"

Yinzhi immediately said, "Deal!" He hadn't told Yinreng earlier precisely because he worried Yinreng would feel sad remembering Empress Renxiao.

The fluffy little white bear Yinreng hugged Yinzhi's arm. "Thank you, Brother."

Yinzhi pulled the little white bear brother into his arms, bubbling over with joy.

"Me too! I want to join too!" Yinzhi hadn't understood, but since the Crown Prince Brother was participating, Yinzhi had to participate too!

Yinzhi wriggled fiercely until he burrowed right onto the fluffy little white bear's tummy.

Yinreng patted Yinzhi's little head with his bear paw. "Alright, we'll help Eldest Brother together. Third Brother, go back and ask about Concubine Rong's birthday, and we'll prepare a gift for Concubine Rong as well."

Yinreng was still young; aside from Noble Consort Tong, the highest rank among the other women was merely "Concubine," which did not qualify them to receive gifts from the Crown Prince.

However, if the princes had good relationships with one another, giving birthday gifts to each other's mothers was perfectly normal and did not depend on status.

Yinzhi nodded. "Okay. When is Crown Prince Brother's birthday? This younger brother will prepare a gift for you."

"Crown Prince Brother doesn't celebrate birthdays," Yinreng said with a gentle smile.

Yinzhi asked in confusion, "Why?"

Yinzhi gave a dry cough to cut off Yinzhi's questioning. "You'll understand when you grow up! Alright, we're almost there. You must keep this secret for me, absolutely don't let it slip! Also, help me spy on the details of how Mingzhu and Great-Aunt interact, so I can write them into the script."

Everyone in the carriage immediately agreed.

*The deeply touching love between Mingzhu and Lady Mingzhu must be passed down through the generations!*

The entire carriage had formed a united front, while Mingzhu remained completely oblivious.

He only noticed that the people from the palace were unusually warm toward him—especially the women, whose eyes practically sparkled like stars when looking at him.

Mingzhu was instantly on high alert.

*What are you doing! You are people from the Emperor's palace! Is someone trying to frame me!*

Mingzhu promptly ducked behind Lady Gūwalgiya.

*Wife, protect me!*

"I don't understand the affairs of the inner courtyard very well, so I'll leave them to you, Madam." Mingzhu frantically dropped hints to Lady Gūwalgiya that there were bad people among this group.

Lady Gūwalgiya glanced across the palace staff and smiled gently. "Leave it to me, Duanfan, rest assured."

Yinzhi asked in confusion, "Duanfan? Carrying rice? Is it time to eat? Does eating require Madam to carry the rice?"

Lady Gūwalgiya held the noble title of First-Rank Lady, so others could respectfully address her as Madam.

Although Yinreng and Yinzhi privately called her Great-Aunt, they still needed to address her more formally face-to-face.

Lady Gūwalgiya chuckled. "Duanfan means a model of upright conduct; it is his courtesy name."

Mingzhu's face darkened completely.

Yinzhi had visited his home several times before, and every single time, he managed to turn Mingzhu's face black with anger.

By now, Mingzhu had completely abandoned any thought of backing Yinzhi to contend with the Crown Prince for the throne. The imperial clan and prominent nobility felt the same.

Right now the Crown Prince was young and there weren't many princes, so they weren't in a hurry. Once the Crown Prince came of age and the Emperor began to grow wary of him, the other princes would have grown up as well, and they could take their time picking.

The Eldest Prince had been swiftly crossed off their candidate list.

This blockhead Eldest Prince was unworthy of being championed by them as an heir to the throne!

Mingzhu shifted his gaze to the Third Prince, Yinzhi.

The Eldest Prince wouldn't do, but perhaps the Third Prince might...

"Carry rice! Carry rice! Yinzhi is hungry! Carry rice!" Yinzhi swayed Yinreng's little bear paw.

Among the three children, Yinzhi wore snug, warm clothing and didn't fear the cold at all; Yinzhi was dressed in bright red, styled like a chubby New Year painting baby; only the frail Yinreng went the fluffy route, turned into a little white bear.

Yinzhi adored his little white bear Crown Prince Brother so much that he wouldn't even hold his dolls—he only wanted to hug his Crown Prince Brother.

"Little Third, you mustn't be so impolite. Duanfan is Lord Mingzhu's courtesy name, which is like a childhood name. Just like Crown Prince Brother's Baocheng and Eldest Brother's Baoking," the little white bear Yinreng scolded with a straight face. "It hurts to have one's name mocked. Little Third must apologize to Lord Mingzhu."

"Oh," Yinzhi said dispiritedly. "Lord Mingzhu, apologize."

Yinreng patted Yinzhi's head with his bear paw. "It's not 'Lord Mingzhu apologize,' it's 'Lord Mingzhu, I apologize.'"

Parroting again, Yinzhi said, "Lord Mingzhu, I apologize."

"It's fine, it's fine. The Third Prince is only a child, what does he know?" Lady Gūwalgiya stepped in first to forgive Yinzhi on Mingzhu's behalf.

Looking at the little white bear Yinreng, her face brimmed with warmth. "Who made this outfit for Your Highness the Crown Prince? It's truly lovely."

Mingzhu bristled his mustache.

*Where is it lovely? It completely lacks the dignity befitting a Crown Prince!*

Yinreng smiled and said, "The Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager made it. But the idea came from Eldest Brother and Imperial Father. They said since I had to dress warmly and fluffily anyway, I might as well dress up as a fluffy animal."

Mingzhu no longer dared to bristle his mustache.

It was Kangxi's idea, sewn by the hands of the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager themselves—even if he were lent a hundred gallbladders, he wouldn't dare blow his mustache at that.

Mingzhu frowned, looking at the little white bear Crown Prince.

The little white bear smiled and waved at Mingzhu.

Mingzhu: "..."

He could no longer keep up his stern face, so he made an excuse and fled in disarray.

Lady Gūwalgiya carefully scooped up the little white bear Yinreng, gently bouncing him to gauge his weight. Comparing it to her second son who was the same age, she let out a deep sigh.

His Highness the Crown Prince had lost so much weight.

She said to Yinreng, "Duanfan actually likes you very much; he's just shy."

Yinreng smiled. "I know. No one dislikes me." *Provided one disregards the identity of Crown Prince, that is.*

Yinzhi put his hands on his hips. "That's right! Whoever dislikes you, I'll beat them up!"

Yinzhi raised a tiny fist. "Beat!"

"Alright, alright. We are temporary guests in someone else's home, so behave yourselves. Let's go tidy up the rooms together," Yinreng said.

Yinzhi quickly said, "The two of us will sleep together."

Yinzhi wrapped his arms around Yinreng's waist. "I sleep with Crown Prince Brother!"

"All together, all together." His brothers were so clingy—it was truly a sweet burden, Yinreng thought cheerfully.

When princes came to stay at an official's residence, they naturally had the final say in how to arrange their rooms.

Lady Gūwalgiya had originally prepared three courtyards for the three children. Hearing that they wanted to stay together, she reorganized things and brought out a large huanghuali wooden bed from her dowry, spacious enough for the three children to roll around side by side.

Yinreng grew tired after directing things for a short while and was carried aside by a wet nurse to rest.

Full of energy, Yinzhi and Yinzhi continued directing the servants to hang their favorite toys all over the room, making it garish and exceedingly hideous.

Lady Gūwalgiya smiled and let them boss everyone around wildly. Once their fuss was done, she stepped in to make minor adjustments, neatly turning the chaotic room into an orderly space.

Yinzhi and Yinzhi looked at Lady Gūwalgiya with starry eyes. "Great-Aunt is amazing!"

Taken aback for a moment by the form of address, Lady Gūwalgiya then crouched down, pulling the two children into her embrace with a soft laugh.

A child of five or six peered in from the doorway. Taking in the scene, his eyes darted around, and he darted toward the side wing.

The servants noticed this and leaned in to whisper into Lady Gūwalgiya's ear.

Lady Gūwalgiya said helplessly, "That boy Rongde... Sigh, come, let's go take a look."

"Who is Rongde?" Yinzhi asked.

Lady Gūwalgiya replied, "My second son, Nalan Kuixu, courtesy name Rongde. He is the same age as His Highness the Crown Prince."

Because Nalan Kuixu was young and frail, Lady Gūwalgiya had always kept him secluded in the inner courtyard away from guests, so neither Yinzhi nor Yinreng had ever seen him.

Yinzhi said, "The same age as Crown Prince Brother? That's great, we can play together."

Lady Gūwalgiya smiled. "The child is unruly; I fear he might collide with and offend the Crown Prince."

It was merely a polite turn of phrase, yet Yinzhi immediately blurted out, "What? He wants to collide into my brother! My brother is so delicate, how could he withstand a bump from him! That brat is looking for a beating!"

With that, Yinzhi dashed off toward where Yinreng was napping. Yinzhi pumped his short little legs vigorously, wobbling along behind Yinzhi. "Me too! I'll protect Brother!"

Lady Gūwalgiya's smile froze.

She wanted to explain that by "collide," she hadn't meant literally bumping into His Highness the Crown Prince.

Rubbing the corners of her brow, Lady Gūwalgiya sighed softly. Ah well, the Eldest Prince simply had this kind of temper; why bother taking it to heart?

When Yinzhi and Yinzhi ran next door, Yinreng was already awake.

He sat there looking bewildered, being hugged and nuzzled by a skinny child.

"What are you? A big doggie?" the skinny child asked.

Yinreng said, "No, I am a bear."

The skinny child asked, "What is a bear?"

Yinreng said, "A bear is a very scary creature that eats people. Awoo!"

The skinny child was startled by Yinreng, yet he still refused to let go. "But you're not scary at all."

Yinreng said, "That's because I'm still small. When I grow up, I'll eat people. Awoo!"

The skinny child's eyes welled with tears from the fright, yet the arms hugging Yinreng didn't budge an inch.

Yinzhi charged in like a little firecracker. "Brother! Eldest Brother has come to protect you! You're not allowed to bump into my brother... Huh, who's the skinny kid next to you?"

Terrified, the skinny child buried his face straight into the fur on Yinreng's chest. "Doggie, protect me!"

Yinreng said, "I told you I'm not a doggie, I'm a bear. Ah, Eldest Brother, don't get excited, don't get excited. Who else in the Nalan residence could be our age? It must be Rongruo's younger brother."

*The hardcore Eighth Prince partisan whose tombstone Yongzheng defaced with graffiti: "Tomb of the Disloyal, Unfilial, Treacherous, and Fawning Kuixu." Pfft, Old Fourth was truly hilarious.*

Realizing this skinny child was Nalan Kuixu, a flicker of darkness churned at the bottom of Yinreng's heart.

After Yinreng's first deposition in his life before last, Nalan Kuixu and Alingga had spread malicious rumors and fabricated countless bizarre accusations against him, smearing his reputation among the common folk to ensure he would never be reinstated.

In the film and television works of later generations, those grotesque, pathetic, and laughable depictions of him as a clown mostly stemmed from the handiwork of these two men.

True to the Nalan family name, Nalan Kuixu possessed remarkable literary skill, crafting stories with vivid life; in modern society, he would undoubtedly have been a best-selling author.

When Yinreng's gaze darkened as he stared down at Nalan Kuixu, the frail boy sensed the hostility and immediately hugged Yinreng even tighter out of fear.

Yinreng: "..."

The darkness faded, and his bright nature returned. Allowing Nalan Kuixu to cling to him, Yinreng let out a deep sigh.

*Yinreng, you are a fine youth born under the red flag and raised in New China; you cannot bully a child over things that haven't happened in this life.*

Genuine five- or six-year-olds possessed an extraordinary intuition, just like cats and dogs.

The moment Yinreng's hostility toward Nalan Kuixu dissipated, the child began nuzzling the fluff in his arms again, clearly treating Yinreng like a giant plush toy.

"Shoo, shoo, you're not allowed to hug my brother." Yinzhi tried to push Nalan Kuixu away.

Being the youngest child in the manor, Nalan Kuixu was somewhat tyrannical by nature. "Won't let go, won't let go! The doggie is mine!"

"I already told you, I'm a bear—the kind that eats people," Yinreng drawled lazily.

"Brother!" Yinzhi rushed up as well, clutching Yinreng tightly and refusing to let go. "Who is he!"

Yinreng said, "He is Nalan Rongruo's younger brother... Ow, stop tugging, stop tugging, I'm not a ragdoll!"

All three children draped themselves over Yinreng, trying to monopolize him.

When Lady Gūwalgiya walked through the door and saw this scene, she called out in alarm, "Rongde! Come here!"

Nalan Kuixu shuddered, and tears began gathering in his eyes.

Used to raising younger brothers, Yinreng couldn't bear to see little children cry.

He immediately patted Nalan Kuixu's face with his bear paw. "Good boy, don't cry, don't cry. You can play with my bear paw."

Sniffling, Nalan Kuixu grabbed the bear paw, squeezed it, and beamed through his tears.

Yinreng chuckled, using his other bear paw to rub Nalan Kuixu's head. "Alright, Eldest Brother, Third Brother, stop fooling around."

"Oh." Yinzhi released Yinreng and slung an arm casually around him. "Why is Rongruo's brother so tiny?"

Yinzhi sprawled on Yinreng's tummy, whimpering softly. He still didn't want an unfamiliar person sharing his fluffy brother.

Yinreng said, "In the future, you'll have younger brothers with an even bigger age gap than Rongruo and Kuixu."

Yinzhi was shocked. "Is Imperial Father that good at siring children? Then how many brothers will I have!"

Yinreng said, "Twenty or thirty?"

Yinzhi's face turned black. "I refuse to have that many brothers."

Just one Third Brother was already fighting tooth and nail with him over their Crown Prince Brother; the thought of twenty or thirty younger brothers gave him a massive headache.

Yinreng said, "Counting sisters too, Imperial Father will definitely have that many."

Yinzhi made a face of disgust and horror. "Ugh, even pigs don't... Mmph."

Yinreng smacked a bear paw directly onto Yinzhi's face. "Shut your mouth, Eldest Brother! Think before you speak; if Imperial Father punishes you, this younger brother won't be able to save you."

Yinzhi tilted his head up. "Won't save!"

Yinzhi smacked a hand onto Yinzhi's head. "Shut up!"

Yinzhi: "Ouch." He stretched his little arms out, hugging Yinreng even tighter.

Mimicking him, Nalan Kuixu tightened his grip as well.

Lady Gūwalgiya stood dumbly to the side, watching as Yinreng smoothly harmonized the dynamics between the brothers and the newly arrived Nalan Kuixu. The three children were happily clustered around Yinreng, whispering together and chattering about things adults couldn't comprehend.

When had their pampered little tyrant at home ever listened to anyone like this?

Nalan Kuixu rubbed against him. *Big doggie—no, big bear—I like you.*

Lady Gūwalgiya tried to lead Nalan Kuixu away, but his tears threatened to fall again.

Yinreng said, "Let him stay here so we can play together; we're the same age anyway."

Nalan Kuixu nodded his little head repeatedly. *Yes, yes, I want to stay here.*

Back when Lady Gūwalgiya gave birth to Nalan Xingde, she had been young, and with her family suffering catastrophe, grief had taken a toll on her health, leaving her body severely weakened so that she bore no children for many years.

Only after nursing her health for over a decade did she have her second son.

There were no peers of his age in the manor, and being physically delicate, he couldn't go outside to play with other children.

Now that Nalan Kuixu had met such warm and adorable peers, he clung eagerly and refused to leave.

Lady Gūwalgiya had a terrible headache. Even if the Crown Prince said it was fine, she couldn't simply leave Nalan Kuixu here unattended.

Lady Gūwalgiya tried coaxing him a few more times, but Nalan Kuixu buried his head tightly into the white bear Yinreng's fur, refusing to utter a single word in reply.

Lady Gūwalgiya had no choice but to attend to other arrangements first, planning to properly reason with Nalan Kuixu in the evening.

Once Lady Gūwalgiya left, Yinzhi said perceptively, "She doesn't want her son getting close to us."

Yinreng smiled. "We are princes. Even if all three of us are good children, others will still worry about us bullying him using our status."

"Hmph." Yinzhi was displeased. "This lord wants her son to play with us; could she even refuse?"

Yinreng said, "Naturally she couldn't."

He rubbed Nalan Kuixu's head again. "Stop pretending. Seeing your eyes darting around, I know you're a precocious child. At five or six in the Nalan family, your schooling must have already begun, right? What are you plotting?"

Yinzhi immediately turned a wary eye toward Nalan Kuixu.

Nalan Kuixu froze, not expecting to be seen through.

He had never been exposed like this at home; even his Ama was kept in the dark by him.

"You..." Nalan Kuixu said sheepishly, "I'm not pretending, the bear really is cute."

He had originally just wanted to see what the Crown Prince who caused disputes between his Ama and eldest brother looked like, but the moment he saw the bear, he couldn't bring himself to let go.

"Thank you," Yinreng said. "Do you want to play with us? If you do, I'll let Mingzhu know. If not, we won't stop you from leaving."

Nalan Kuixu said immediately, "I do! There's no one to play with me at home."

"Poor thing, just like my Crown Prince Brother used to be." Yinzhi's heart softened slightly.

Yinreng said, "Eldest Brother, there was someone playing with me."

Yinzhi rolled his eyes at Yinreng. "Who?"

Yinreng replied, "Imperial Father..."

Yinzhi was speechless. "Was Imperial Father playing with you, or was Imperial Father playing *with* you like a toy? I remember crystal clear how he treated Little Fourth!"

Yinreng looked up at the sky.

*Well, yes, him playing with me like a toy could still be called playing together—just like how beating someone's fist with my face could technically be called a mutual brawl.*

Nalan Kuixu played the pity card: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, may I play with you? I'm very well-behaved."

He was determined to observe up close the Crown Prince who made his eldest brother and Ama quarrel!

"Alright," Yinreng agreed nonchalantly.

With the three brothers coming to stay at Nalan Mingzhu's home, keeping them separated from Nalan Kuixu was impossible anyway.

When he heard that his second son had secretly snuck over to see the Crown Prince, clung to him without letting go, and even fought over him with the Eldest and Third Princes, Mingzhu clutched his chest, nearly blacking out and keeling over.

It was bad enough that his eldest son had been swayed by the Crown Prince, but his second son was still so young—why was he clinging to the Crown Prince as well!

Nalan Xingde clasped his hands behind his back and tilted his head, acting cute despite his age. "This only proves that His Highness the Crown Prince is wonderful. Otherwise, could it be said that there's a problem with your parenting, Ama?"

Mingzhu was so furious he almost hurled the book in his hand at Nalan Xingde.

Lady Gūwalgiya sighed and said, "Master, if you don't like it, I will separate the Crown Prince and Rongde. Don't be angry."

Nalan Mingzhu said aggrievedly, "It's not a matter of whether I like it or not..."

Nalan Xingde said, "Father just doesn't understand. But Father, do you really not understand? You have seen the Crown Prince so many times; do you really not like him?"

Nalan Mingzhu fell silent.

Jue Luo-shi patted Nalan Mingzhu’s shoulder and said, "From the bottom of my heart, I also like the Crown Prince. Rongde is just a child; he doesn't consider too many things and only follows his instincts, so it is normal for him to like the Crown Prince. When he grows up, if you slowly teach him that he cannot like the Crown Prince, he will stop liking him for the sake of the family."

Jue Luo-shi did not think Nalan Mingzhu’s agitation was correct.

However, Nalan Mingzhu had wasted over a decade during the Shunzhi reign and had a deep, intense craving for power.

Nalan Mingzhu’s targeting of the Crown Prince was not because he truly disliked the Crown Prince or wanted to betray Kangxi. It was because he deeply understood how powerful the imperial clan and the nobility were; if he did not follow this group, he would be abandoned and cast aside.

There was already Songgotu in the imperial court supporting the Crown Prince; if he did not oppose the Crown Prince, the Nalan family could not become the leader of another faction in the court.

He did not want to become anyone's vassal.

But now Songgotu had retreated, and Kangxi seemed to no longer intentionally cultivate opposing factions to balance power in the court. Even his eldest son had clearly defected to the young Crown Prince. Mingzhu was caught in a dilemma.

Mingzhu had just received new information: Changning, the leader pushed by the imperial clan to oppose the Crown Prince, had also backed down, stating bluntly that his relationship with the Crown Prince was good, that the Crown Prince was excellent, and forbidding others from speaking ill of him.

Previously, someone had said in front of Changning that the Crown Prince was sickly and wouldn't live long, and had been whipped by Changning for it.

The noble youths serving as imperial guards in the palace also praised the Crown Prince incessantly, and even that scoundrel Tong Guogang’s son, Elundai, was shouting that he was convinced by the Crown Prince.

If the Crown Prince had been an adult, Mingzhu would have already started stirring up trouble, claiming the Crown Prince had too much prestige and harbored rebellious intentions.

But the Crown Prince was still so young, and Mingzhu found himself completely unable to find a way to counter him.

He couldn't exactly run to Kangxi and say that a five or six-year-old Crown Prince had too much prestige and threatened the throne, could he?

If Songgotu were still jumping around now, he could have pushed all of this onto him, falsely accusing the Heseri family of building momentum for the Crown Prince.

Songgotu, aside from completing the work given by Kangxi, was now obsessed with going home to beat his sons and younger brothers, closing his doors to guests. The Heseri family’s new favorite, Changtai, was a complete loner and a bore. Unless Kangxi asked him to speak, he could stand in the court like a wooden stake from beginning to end.

Mingzhu tried to find people to impeach him.

Duties not completed? "I request to investigate myself, and if there is a problem, I will resign."

Embezzled public funds? "I request to investigate myself, and if there is a problem, I will resign."

Acting too arrogant? "I request to investigate myself, and if there is a problem, I will resign."

Frequently entering and exiting the palace, contrary to etiquette? "Good, I think so too!"

Kangxi: "Resign my foot, you think what! Don't even think about escaping, get back to work for me!"

Changtai cupped his hands, showing a dejected expression in front of all the civil and military officials.

All the officials understood: Changtai was anxious to go home to serve his critically ill father, but there was too much work in the court, and the Emperor would not allow it.

If he made any more trouble, the Emperor would get annoyed.

Mingzhu rolled his eyes in anger.

What kind of person was this Changtai! He had never seen anyone like him! You call him cautious, he openly opposes Kangxi; you call him incautious, he finishes his work and immediately goes home to care for his old father, refuses all invitations, and even throws gifts sent by others directly at the door, telling people to pick them up themselves.

Mingzhu had accumulated a lot of frustration in his heart, and today, upon hearing that his second son also liked the Crown Prince, it finally exploded.

For the first time, he had the illusion that he was a clown on a stage.

The Emperor and the Crown Prince shared a deep father-son bond, and the Crown Prince was perfect in every way except for his weak health. He insisted on trying to replace the Crown Prince, yet the more he jumped around, the more annoying he became, and even his own family began to misunderstand him.

What exactly was he working so hard for?

"The Crown Prince is still young. Father doesn't need to make a choice so early. At the very least, wait until the Crown Prince comes of age; it won't be too late for Father to consider it then," Nalan Xingde said. "Who knows, perhaps as Father said, once the Crown Prince grows up, because he is too perfect, the Emperor will no longer be able to tolerate him."

Jue Luo-shi sighed: "That would be so pitiful for the Crown Prince."

Nalan Xingde also looked somber.

Mingzhu looked at his sentimental wife and son and immediately coughed: "Don't be so pessimistic. The Crown Prince is so intelligent, he will surely find the right way to get along with the Emperor. The Emperor is not cold-hearted; the child he raised himself won't be so easily... Rongruo! What is that expression on your face!"

Nalan Xingde turned and ran: "I'm going to see the Crown Prince, the First Prince, and the Third Prince!"

"You come back here!" Mingzhu was so angry he threw the book in his hand.

As soon as he threw it, he immediately lifted his robes and ran over to pick it up, patting it with heartache.

He hadn't finished reading this book yet!

Jue Luo-shi couldn't help but laugh.

When Nalan Xingde found the Crown Prince and the others, the Crown Prince was asleep again, and Yinzhi was playing with building blocks quietly with Yinzhi and Nalan Kuixu.

The blocks were made at Yinreng's request.

He provided the blueprints, making miniature versions of labor tools and new weapons to cultivate his brothers' interests in advance.

When Nalan Xingde entered, Yinzhi quickly made a shushing gesture.

Nalan Xingde looked worriedly at the little Crown Prince, who was curled up like a fluffy ball and sleeping soundly.

"Little brother doesn't cough much anymore, he just gets tired easily," Yinzhi whispered. "He sleeps longer than we do, and when he's well-rested, he's in high spirits. The imperial physician said not to worry too much."

Nalan Xingde breathed a sigh of relief.

He rubbed his younger brother's little head: "Are you happy?"

Nalan Kuixu’s eyes were bright.

These toys were all very fun. It was his first time playing with such fun toys with peers!

Nalan Xingde looked at the blocks on the floor and also became interested: "Can I play with you all?"

Yinzhi said generously: "Come, join in. Today I must build a big house for my little brother!"

When Yinreng woke up, not only was Nalan Xingde sitting on the floor, but Mingzhu had also joined the ranks of building block players at some point.

Yinreng was speechless.

Lord Mingzhu, even if the blocks are fun, don't you want your dignity as a Prime Minister? Rongruo’s overly free-spirited nature is like yours; shouldn't you reflect on that?

Mingzhu saw Yinreng’s speechless expression and said awkwardly: "Your Highness the Crown Prince is awake? Are you hungry? I have food prepared in the kitchen at all times."

Yinreng nodded: "I'm hungry. But I have to write a letter to Khan Ama first."

Yinzhi said grumpily: "Just send someone to pass a message, why write a letter? So troublesome?"

Yinreng said: "Ama wants to see the letters we write."

Yinzhi rolled his eyes: "He just wants to torture us!"

Mingzhu: "..." Giving up on supporting the First Prince was truly the right decision!

While Mingzhu had people prepare food, Yinreng pulled his older and younger brothers to write to Kangxi.

He spoke, and Yinzhi acted as the scribe.

Yinzhi could now write almost all common characters, and his handwriting was quite good. But as he wrote, the elegant characters grew larger and larger, as if he were venting his anger by drawing circles.

In the palace, Kangxi opened the letter. Even though Yinzhi didn't say a word, he could see Yinzhi’s impatience in the handwriting.

We didn't even go far!

Aren't you annoyed by a letter every day!

Khan Ama, are you intentionally torturing us!

Ahhhhh, I don't want to write anymore! Flipping the table!

Kangxi’s mouth twitched.

It's just one letter a day, it's practically practice for your calligraphy. Are you really making such a fuss!

Kangxi put down his magnifying glass.

When reading at night by candlelight, Kangxi was accustomed to using a magnifying glass to enlarge the text to protect his eyes.

Now, with Yinzhi’s large handwriting, he didn't even need the magnifying glass.

Yinreng told Kangxi about his plan to put the love story of Mingzhu and Jue Luo-shi on the stage with Yinzhi.

Yinreng found a very good excuse.

Due to the brutality during the Qing conquest, Han civilians had demonized all Manchus, and it was only recently, after life had stabilized, that things had improved slightly.

Nalan Xingde, with his talent, had his "Cemao Ci" and "Yinshui Ci" sung in every household, changing the Han people's impression that Manchus were vulgar and untalented.

The loyal and unwavering love between Nalan Mingzhu and Jue Luo-shi also fit the public's yearning for love and family; if adapted into a play, it would be no worse than the famous plays of the Yuan and Ming dynasties.

Of course, on the surface, we would still say it's an old story from a previous dynasty. But those who know, know; the truth would soon spread through every street and alley.

The Nalan family, as Kangxi’s Manchu image ambassadors, was very suitable.

Kangxi chuckled, stroking his chin.

Although he knew Yinreng was covering for his eldest son’s mischief, this matter might actually be quite useful.

Kangxi turned the page; it was Yinzhi’s turn to speak.

Yinzhi, prompted by Yinreng, knew that one had to hold up a big banner to get things done. He said he would try this new way of spreading plays first. If it worked, he would write the newly compiled myths into new plays and let the troupes perform them all over the Qing Dynasty. Wouldn't that make it easy to spread the myths of their ancestors?

Kangxi’s smiling expression froze.

He rubbed his eyes in disbelief, re-read Yinzhi’s letter from the beginning, and called for the eunuch who delivered the letter: "Was this idea really Yinzhi’s?"

The eunuch said: "It was the First Prince’s idea."

He recounted the process of how the First Prince came up with this idea.

Yinzhi had actually just slipped up while bragging, not even realizing what he had said.

Yinreng had quickly called a halt, carefully asked about Yinzhi’s thoughts, and then pulled Nalan Xingde over to ask about the situation with the troupes, perfecting the matter.

So the idea was indeed proposed by the First Prince, and the Crown Prince merely perfected it.

Kangxi pinched the bridge of his nose, his eyes glistening.

You’ve grown up, my eldest son.

"Take a jade ruyi to Concubine Hui," Kangxi said with satisfaction.

Although he knew the First Prince’s newfound intelligence was thanks to his precious son, he couldn't reward the Crown Prince for the First Prince’s actions; he had to reward Concubine Hui, who gave birth to the First Prince.

Concubine Hui had also worked hard for a long time because of the First Prince.

When Concubine Hui received the jade ruyi, she was puzzled as to why she had been rewarded so suddenly.

When she learned it was because of the First Prince, Concubine Hui hugged the jade ruyi and wept, crying even harder than when she was promoted to Concubine.

Amazing, my son! You actually earned a reward for your mother!

Wait, that’s not right. I know my son so well; he doesn't seem like the type who could earn me a reward!

After Concubine Hui finished crying, she inquired about what had happened.

When she heard that it was because of something in the letter written by the three princes that made Kangxi happy, she immediately patted her chest and said: "It’s the Crown Prince."

She knew it. Her own silly son wouldn't know how to please the Emperor; it must have been the Crown Prince pulling her silly son to do a good deed.

Yinzhi didn't tell others when he helped the Crown Prince, only Concubine Hui.

So Concubine Hui knew that Yinzhi had been given a lot of credit by the Crown Prince and was now starting to come into contact with government affairs and noble guards.

Every day, Concubine Hui would quietly recite the Longevity Sutra ten times for the Crown Prince in the Buddhist hall, feeling deeply grateful to him.

She stroked the jade ruyi, unable to put it down.

This was the first reward her son had ever earned for her.

After Concubine Hui received the reward, all the concubines in the palace were extremely jealous.

Concubine Rong thought about how her son was also by the Crown Prince’s side and smiled, no longer jealous;

Concubine De looked at her own big, chubby son who couldn't even speak yet and spent his days grumbling, and thinking of the Crown Prince’s affection for the Fourth Prince, she wasn't jealous either;

Concubine Yi thought of the Fifth Prince, who was still being raised by Noble Consort Tong, and put all her effort into nourishing her body, preparing to compete for favor, and prayed that the Crown Prince would look after her son more;

Other concubines with princesses thought of the Crown Prince’s kindness and hoped he would be even better to their daughters; those without children, like Noble Consort Tong, simply had an extra bowl of unsweetened yogurt.

Hmm, unsweetened yogurt is delicious.

...

After arriving at the Nalan mansion, Yinreng felt much more relaxed, and his body also became more agile.

Even though the people around him would still report his affairs to Kangxi, it wasn't every half hour like in the palace.

The messengers couldn't possibly tell Kangxi everything he did and said every day. A daily report meant that Kangxi wouldn't know what he did for most of the day.

This made Yinreng feel as if even his breathing had become easy.

The imperial physician came to the Nalan mansion every day to take Yinreng’s pulse, and his face showed more and more smiles.

The Emperor was right; changing the environment really did improve the Crown Prince’s health.

When Kangxi received the results of Yinreng’s daily pulse check, he was thinking about something else.

"It is indeed as Khan Ama said, Baocheng cannot stay in the palace for long," Kangxi said, feeling very pained.

He even suspected whether his Fourth Brother, Prince Rong, whom he had once deeply envied, had also attracted a curse, which was why he survived smallpox, why Changning survived, and why Longxi was able to live in a sickly state until last year.

Only the child the Emperor loved deeply, the child he truly wanted to inherit the throne, could attract a curse.

Only such a sacrifice could be considered precious.

Kangxi walked out of the Qianqing Palace, his hands behind his back, looking up at the sky.

The sky in the first month was still gray, and it was likely that another heavy snow would fall.

Is heaven’s will hard to defy? But it’s just a curse, how can it be called heaven!

"Summon troupes from all over to the capital to prepare for the Empress Dowager’s birthday next year," Kangxi gathered the officials and posted notices nationwide. "After the earthquake, we need a grand celebration to boost morale, and the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories has also been initially quelled. The Empress Dowager’s birthday next year will be celebrated grandly."

Officials: "Yes!"

The imperial edict was written, copied by the Grand Secretaries, and sent by fast horse to all provinces of the Qing Dynasty, and the provincial officials then conveyed the decree to the famous local troupes.

Thus, the Four Great Anhui Troupes, which would only appear in the 55th year of the Qianlong reign, appeared early in the Kangxi reign.

There were more troupes entering the capital this time, and a wider variety of plays.

49. First and Second Update [V]

Yinreng changed into a little tiger doll outfit, and Yinzhi and Kuixu held him from left and right, refusing to let go.

Mingzhu was already used to this scene.

If Yinzhi hadn't forbidden it, Kuixu would probably have wanted to squeeze into the Crown Prince’s bed and sleep with him every day.

But even without sleeping together every day, when the Crown Prince took his afternoon nap and the First and Third Princes were playing energetically, the equally sickly Kuixu would always consciously climb onto Yinreng’s bed to serve as a body pillow.

Yinreng shot a glance at Kuixu.

Nonsense! It was clearly this kid who used me as a body pillow!

Yinreng was unusually soft-hearted toward children. Kuixu looked delicate and cute, so Yinreng couldn't bear to scold him and had to let him be his body pillow.

With the Crown Prince being so soft-hearted, Mingzhu was so worried he pulled out several of his beautiful whiskers.

He also began to worry about the Crown Prince’s future without realizing it.

Originally, the only person in the Nalan mansion worried about the Crown Prince’s future was the big traitor Nalan Xingde. The Crown Prince had only been at the Nalan mansion for a few days, and Jue Luo-shi was also sighing from time to time.

Jue Luo-shi’s family were losers in the imperial power struggle, and she knew how terrifying the deceit and treachery of the royal family were.

Although the Crown Prince was more precocious than ordinary children, and his speech and insights sometimes made even adults feel ashamed, this overly kind heart was more of a burden than his weak body.

After Jue Luo-shi was saved by Mingzhu, and because Mingzhu had wasted decades for her, she now took Mingzhu’s ideals as her heaven. Even if she had her own thoughts, she only acted according to Mingzhu’s ideals, putting the Nalan family’s interests first.

Her persuading Mingzhu to agree to Xingde’s choice was also based on giving the Nalan family another path for the future.

Therefore, Jue Luo-shi pitied the Crown Prince, but she only sighed secretly behind Mingzhu’s back, lost in thought, and wiped the corners of her eyes. When she saw Mingzhu, she became the gentle and strong wife of the Prime Minister again, supporting everything Mingzhu did.

When Jue Luo-shi was still the carefree Fifth Princess of Prince Ying’s mansion, Mingzhu, who was just a little guard, would secretly look at her.

This habit hadn't changed even when Mingzhu had silver strands at his temples and wrinkles had crawled onto the corners of Jue Luo-shi’s eyes.

The smiling fox, who could stir up wind and rain outside, would peek through door cracks, hide in corners, and dodge behind trees, secretly watching Jue Luo-shi wipe away tears, anxious and scratching his head.

He had come into contact with the Crown Prince a few more times behind his back, and the more he interacted, the more he understood why his wife would cry in secret, and his heart began to lean toward the Crown Prince.

The Crown Prince was indeed a good child. Not to mention in the royal family, among all the children he had ever seen, the Crown Prince could rank first, and the second couldn't even compare to him.

Such a good child coming to the royal family was like a fairy boy stepping into a filthy world; every quarter of an hour, every hour he lived, was a quarter of an hour, an hour of torture.

If the Crown Prince had been born into an ordinary family, he would surely be loved by everyone.

But he was the Crown Prince, and most people didn't look at "Yinreng" as a person, but at the identity of "Crown Prince." From the moment he was born, countless enemies wanted him dead.

Now that the Emperor doted on him and protected him, he could still be carefree. But as he grew up, he would eventually face all the cruelty.

Perhaps even the Emperor would suspect him, guard against him, and hurt him.

When that time came, how would this good child with a soft heart face the bloody reality?

Mingzhu thought too much and couldn't help but start sighing.

Nalan Xingde was a child taught by Nalan Mingzhu himself; Nalan Xingde’s talent, free-spiritedness, and sentimentality naturally had a share of Nalan Mingzhu’s contribution.

Nalan Mingzhu, who was over forty, seemed to have returned to his youth at this moment, with more softness and more worries.

"Lord Mingzhu." The little Crown Prince was dressed warmly and softly, and his smile was also warm and soft, making even those who had hostility toward him lose their guard temporarily upon seeing his smile.

Mingzhu had already decided to wait until the Crown Prince grew up before thinking about who to support or oppose, and his smile toward the little Crown Prince became a bit more sincere: "Has the Crown Prince been living well at my house? If you are bored, you can let Rongruo take you out to play; the Emperor has agreed."

Yinreng said: "Thank you, Lord Mingzhu. My health hasn't fully recovered, so I won't go out for now. I would like to borrow a few books from you, Lord Mingzhu."

Mingzhu nodded and took Yinreng to his library.

Yinzhi and Kuixu, who were clinging to Yinreng, immediately let go of him and ran off to find Yinzhi to play as soon as they heard they were going to the library.

When Yinreng wasn't reading, they liked Yinreng the most; once Yinreng started reading, they put the importance of Yinzhi, who could take them out to play, at the forefront.

Mingzhu blew his beard and stared.

How could his, Nalan Mingzhu’s, son not love reading! When the Crown Prince returns to the palace, he must teach his youngest son well!

Mingzhu loved collecting books.

After Mingzhu died, Kuixu, in order to make the Nalan family rise again and become the Ninth Prince’s money bag, handed over most of the Nalan family’s wealth for the Ninth Prince to squander.

Unlike the fictional image in movies and novels, the money that supported the Ninth Prince’s name as the God of Wealth came from two sources: first, relying on extortion and bribery in the officialdom, similar to Heshen in later generations; and second, from the offerings of the Nalan family. It shows the depth of the Nalan family’s wealth.

In this era, you needed money to have books to read. Mingzhu was obsessed with collecting books and built the Xueyan Studio. Ordinary Manchus spent their money on gold, jewelry, fine horses, and treasures, while Mingzhu spent thousands of gold just for a volume of books he hadn't seen before. Even if it was just a version he hadn't seen, it was fine.

After Yinreng came to the Nalan mansion, he would read with Mingzhu or Xingde when he had nothing to do.

After going a few more times, the barrier between Mingzhu and Yinreng gradually disappeared, and they got along like a normal grandfather and grandson. Mingzhu would even hold Yinreng on his lap and teach him the allusions in the books word by word.

Mingzhu held the position of Crown Prince’s Tutor; although it was only a nominal position, it could be said that he had the responsibility of teaching the Crown Prince.

The more he taught, the more he liked Yinreng. Yinreng also admired Mingzhu more and more.

The three Nalan brothers were all talented people with high literary attainments. As their father, Mingzhu’s literary cultivation naturally couldn't be poor. Most of the important imperial classics of the Kangxi reign were edited by Mingzhu as the Chief Editor.

When Mingzhu taught Yinreng, his words were brilliant, and he could cite allusions with ease; if Yinreng were a real child, he would probably be fascinated.

Yinreng’s favor for Mingzhu deepened, and one day he hinted to Mingzhu: "Lord Mingzhu, what do you think is the most important thing for Khan Ama to do after quelling the Three Feudatories and the rebellion?"

Mingzhu thought for a while and said: "Mongolia, Tsarist Russia?"

Yinreng shook his head, and he said seriously, word by word: "It is to rectify the administration."

Mingzhu’s expression froze slightly.

Yinreng said: "The Manchu nobility still hasn't shaken off the small-mindedness they had when they first entered the pass. When they arrived in the vast land of the Central Plains, they still thought about grabbing as much as they could, and only what they held in their own hands was solid, just like nomadic tribes raiding the borders."

Mingzhu frowned deeply.

Yinreng continued: "The Qing Dynasty is already the orthodox ruler of China. What Khan Ama wants is long-term peace and stability, the submission of the people’s hearts, and to be an emperor for the ages. The Manchu nobility followed the Qing into the Central Plains, and in the end, they must remove the title of 'Manchu' from their heads and become the true nobility of the Chinese land. If you cannot change your mindset, how can you follow Khan Ama to build achievements?"

Mingzhu was shocked in his heart: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, you..."

Yinreng waved his hand and said: "I didn't intend to tell you this. You group of people are old, and your horizons are narrow. Khan Ama is still young, and he values young people more. The generation that grew up after entering the pass is more suitable for the young Qing Dynasty than you are. It’s just that after talking to you, I think it’s a pity."

Yinreng put his little short hands behind his back; today he was wearing a dog hat and dog clothes, and there was even a dog tail sewn on his butt that was useless except for decoration.

"The Crown Prince’s Tutor is only in his prime, exactly the time to be useful," Yinreng said with a straight face. "Someone is impeaching you; have you almost sold off all the official positions?"

Mingzhu immediately knelt down: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, there is absolutely no such thing!"

"Whether there is such a thing or not, you know it in your heart. There are few useful Manchu civil officials in this court, and Han civil officials have to endure extortion and blackmail to hold onto their positions. The late Emperor’s bias toward Manchu officials who extorted and blackmailed, leading to the suicide of frontier officials, gave you a lot of courage."

Yinreng sighed and shook his head.

"But you don't think about it, did the late Emperor not want to kill? He didn't want to, he couldn't. Many things that cannot be accumulated will eventually lead to disaster for someone. You are, Songgotu is, and others are the same. But you are rare and capable ministers under Khan Ama; if it weren't for you, the ratio of Manchu and Han officials in the court would be unbalanced, and how could Khan Ama complete his ideal of the Qing Dynasty truly becoming the orthodox ruler of China?"

Mingzhu’s back was soaked with cold sweat. He suddenly realized that he didn't understand the Crown Prince at all.

The Crown Prince was by no means as weak and kind as he appeared!

No, the kindness was real. It was just that the Crown Prince was more intelligent than he had imagined.

Mingzhu looked up: "Please, Your Highness the Crown Prince, give me your instructions!"

Yinreng said: "That depends on what your ideal is. Do you want to be a powerful minister? Do you want to accumulate wealth? Or do you want to leave your name in history and become a famous minister and general engraved on the monument of China?"

chapters.title: 第 32 章 [V] (6)
chapters.source_text:
明珠道：“臣当然想要名垂青史！”
胤礽笑道：“不，你现在没想过。容若想，你真的没有想。但你现在可以想。因为你当不了权臣。汗阿玛不会容忍任何权臣出现，权王也不行。汗阿玛一定会将权力全部集中在他的手心，无论是什么权力。”
明珠神色大骇。
“孤本不打算提点你。但你真的很有才华，真的太可惜。”胤礽叹息。
康熙朝最有才华的朝臣是谁？
说来说去，文臣中有名者如流星雨划过天空无数，谁也比不过康熙朝早期的明珠和索额图。
明珠眼光极准，推举的官员几乎都是能臣。他在打三藩、平台湾、御沙俄等国土问题上，是坚决的主战派和激进派。胤礽要逼着他阿玛剑指全球，明珠这种人必不可少。
索额图虽然没多少国家领土观念，好像懒惰的青蛙一样戳一下才动一下，无论是擒拿鳌拜还是之后在三藩等中获得的功劳，都是“被逼”去的。但只要他接下什么工作，就能把工作做到完美。统筹大局稳定后方调遣军备，全靠索额图指挥。
若用游戏术语，明珠开了透视挂，索额图开了全图挂。
两人若不互相拖后腿，而是一起使力，康熙几乎所向披靡。
胤礽实在是舍不得这样的人才啊。
没有了明珠和索额图，康熙要从零开始培养征战全球的人才，那得多难啊。
一个皇帝有雄心壮志的时期就那么一二十年，当康熙年岁步入五十之后，就算主观意愿还想勤政，客观情况也不会允许，怠政懒政不可避免。
胤礽希望康熙成为真正的千古一帝，时间很赶。等康熙年老之后，他就不能再作死，而是苟着找机会请辞太子之位了。
“好了，别跪了。你再不给孤读书，外面的人就要进来……唉，大哥，你怎么在这？什么时候来的？”胤礽吓了一跳。
胤禔不知道从哪钻出来：“明珠跪下的时候我就来了。”
胤禔揉了揉胤礽的狗头：“小心些，外面太监张望很久了。你来这里好不容易松一口气，又被送回皇宫怎么办？”
胤礽抱住胤禔蹭蹭：“好。”哎，一思考起剑指全球的事，他就忍不住想作死。
没事没事，他现在还是个孩子，阿玛不会多想。等阿玛多想的时候，他请辞太子之位好了。
给大清多立下些功劳，到时候请辞之后用功劳换温泉大庄子。
胤礽为自己的作死找了个借口，不承认自己就是不安分。
胤禔又拍了拍胤礽的狗头，对明珠道：“不要辜负太子冒着危险对你的提点。”
什么危险？明珠皱眉思索，想起胤礽和胤禔提起的太监，倒吸了一口气。
他早该明白的，太子身边的人肯定会事无巨细地将太子的事告诉皇上。太子有许多神异传闻，又过于早慧，或许皇上对太子护得更紧。
这是皇上对太子的看重。可听大阿哥和太子的意思，这看重似乎过于令人窒息。
“老臣明白。”明珠立刻道，“臣定不会辜负太子。”
胤礽蹭了几下胤禔后，对明珠笑道：“辜不辜负我没什么关系，不要辜负提拔重用你的汗阿玛。你和别人不同，汗阿玛是你的伯乐。你想要的荣华富贵，也只系于汗阿玛一人身上。擦亮眼睛看看，那些宗亲和老贵族，真的能对汗阿玛造成威胁吗？”
明珠再次出了一身冷汗。
胤禔冷哼：“皇玛法势弱时，他们也没能对皇玛法造成什么麻烦，不过是在皇玛法驾崩后伪造遗诏恶心一下皇玛法。汗阿玛虽然对太子弟弟不好，但也算个厉害的皇帝，他们敢反？”
明珠立刻再次跪下磕头，吓得不行。
造反这种事，大阿哥怎么能挂在嘴上说？！
胤禔白了跪下磕头不敢说话的明珠一眼：“他们总以为自己领着兵就能威胁到汗阿玛，但他们敢喊一句谋反试试？英亲王当年那么厉害，皇玛法不是说杀就杀。他们还以为那些兵是自己的私兵？时代不同了。”
胤礽拉了拉胤禔的袖子：“大哥，英亲王是明珠大人岳父。”
胤禔道：“那明珠不是更该明白这件事？他怎么还这么蠢？他真的值得你提点？”
胤礽道：“明珠大人只是老了。时代变了，他没跟上时代。”
胤禔叹气：“这群老臣真麻烦。”
胤礽看明珠快脑溢血了，忙转移话题：“大哥，你来找我，有什么事吗？”
胤禔拍了拍脑袋：“哦，有事，我差点忘了。顾贞观他们来了，他们对咱们说的戏文很有兴趣，你也来，咱们一起写戏文。”
胤礽再次怜惜地看了明珠一眼：“好。”
明珠大人松了一口气，总算送走了两个快把他吓死的皇子。
他这时候还不知道，自己将要遭遇什么。
文人雅士喜欢的娱乐中，听戏一定能排前三。
当他们当不了官，手头拮据时，经常帮戏班子写戏。偶尔比较洒脱的文人，还会登台扮演唱戏，也算是一件雅事。
顾贞观等人都来自南方，南方戏文文化在这个时代更加兴盛。他们在市井间随便抓个人，都能掐着嗓子唱几句。
顾贞观的品行被康熙看重，渐渐被重用。
清朝任命官员，并不严格按照科举。举人或者非科举人士比比皆是，和明朝非翰林不做大官的情况不同。
康熙看重顾贞观，顾贞观便青云直上。
年后，顾贞观便要走老于成龙所走过的路，去外地当官。如果顾贞观在任上有政绩，之后仕途便一路通畅了。
离开之前，顾贞观来纳兰府和纳兰性德小聚，顺带把自己离京后仍会住在自己家中养病的友人吴兆骞托付给纳兰性德。
纳兰性德跟随太子之后，公务繁忙，和友人们聚会变少。
今日大家齐聚一堂，真准备好好喝一坛，以酒会友。
结果胤禔带着弟弟们前来参加会议。一众文人面面相觑，立刻把酒换成了清茶。
当着皇子的面喝酒，失态了可就是大问题，就算没失态，如果皇子不小心偷喝了酒，身体出了问题，他们就要掉脑袋了。
三位皇子还是小孩，除了熟悉胤礽的顾贞观打起了精神，其他人都没把他们当贵人看待，不认为自己表现良好就能获得什么。
要投靠某位皇子，也要等皇子出宫建府后。现在这几个小孩能懂什么？
“我要写这样一出戏。”胤禔开门见山，把自己和胤礽已经总结好的故事梗概拿出来，“这出戏要推向市井，戏词尽可能的通俗一些。”
“市井？通俗？”有文人皱起眉头。
胤禔脾气不好，看着就要发作，被胤礽一个狗爪子摸摸忍了下来。
胤礽笑道：“诸位认为，诗词文章戏文是什么？”
文人们看着一团孩气的小太子，一时半会儿不知道怎么说。
他们不是不明白，只是在斟酌说辞，怎么让小孩子听懂。
胤礽扫视了文人们一眼，纳兰性德和顾贞观立刻正襟危坐：“是表达。”
文人们看向小太子。
“说出的话和写出的话，都是为了表达，为了让其他人明白自己的意思。曲高和寡也想要知音，阳春白雪也希望有欣赏的人。各位没有异议吧？”
胤礽再次扫视了文人们一眼，这次文人们看着小太子的眼神多了几分认真。
“昔日白居易和杜甫写诗时会念给不识字的人听，他们便是很明白这一点，知道自己写的诗能被市井传唱。因此每次创作之前，你们该明白创作的目的。”
“写给达官贵人的诗词文章，写给友人知音的诗词文章，抒发自己情感希望被人所理解的诗词文章，还有教化世人的诗词文章。这些文章的措辞表达，肯定各不相同。”
胤礽用狗爪爪拍了一下桌子，很没有气势，但仍旧扣住了众人的心弦。
“你们都是读书人，你们看的经史子集，多是用对话形式表现，并无多少高深之语。是先贤们不会说那些骈俪的话吗？不，是先贤们希望用最通俗的字词，就像和你们面对面说话一样，将自己的思想传给你们。”
“戏文是什么？你们自娱自乐时，戏文编得再高深都是你们的自由；大阿哥要编出能教化市井的戏文，那就得尽量通俗易懂，明白吗？”胤礽笑道，“不会有人给不识字的孩童启蒙时，用晦涩难懂的古文典籍吧？”
文人们面面相觑。
他们不明白一个孩童的任性，怎么还和教化黎民扯上关系了。
只有参与了神话编写的纳兰性德和顾贞观立刻意识到了一些事，忙道：“臣等定会竭尽全力。”
他们向友人们使眼色。
赶紧答应啊！
吴兆骞被顾贞观提点过，立刻道：“草民愿为太子殿下、大皇子殿下、三皇子殿下执笔教化黎民。”
其他文人见有人带头，也马上附和。
他们依附纳兰府，本就有想借纳兰府权势走青云路之意。虽他们不信任几个小皇子能给他们好处，但纳兰性德和顾贞观能啊。
“如此甚好。”胤礽退下，让胤禔继续说。
胤禔风风火火提出自己的要求，特别是中心思想，绝对不可更改。
那男子定要是深情无悔，那女子定要是坚韧不拔，两人必定要琴瑟和鸣，是爱人也是知己，不可有其他女子男子插足。
对了，这么美满的爱情一定要加一些外人的诽谤，说那女子善妒，和男子的真实关系一定很不好。
文人们疑惑：“为何？”
胤禔道：“叫你们写就写，哪那么多问题！”
胤礽安抚胤禔：“外界的不理解，不正证明他们的伉俪情深有多可贵吗？”

怪不得康熙和鄂伦岱这么合拍，如果顺治没早死，康熙有顺治罩着……嗯，不敢想。
这么多人都加入进来，戏文编写立刻加速。
戏文写好，一堆纨绔子弟钱财一凑，让几个戏班子停了演出专门排这出戏。
当胤礽身体大好，可以回宫的时候，戏排演好了。
康熙抱着胤礽，裕亲王福全和恭亲王常宁也各带一个皇子，去了戏台子上听新出的戏。
这戏一开幕，便是一个老生在墓碑上撒酒。
“一生一代一双人，争教两处销魂。相思相望不相亲，天为谁春？”
凄厉唱词一起，康熙不由拍桌，大喊一声“好”，从篮子里抓起一把铜钱，洒向台上。
唐代诗人骆宾王在《代女道士王灵妃赠道士李荣》中曾有一句传世诗句，曰“相怜相念倍相亲，一生一代一双人”。
这首《画堂春》开篇用了骆宾王的传世诗句为开篇，如李清照用欧阳修的“庭院深深深几许”开篇一样，致敬前人，引出另一首传世诗词。
光是这首词，这场戏就看得值了！
老生唱完，舞台上布置一换，从男女主人公年少时写起。
女子是前朝王府的郡主，天真烂漫；男子只是一个小侍卫，只痴痴望着女子的背影。
他努力奋进，只愿能入王府的眼，迎娶心上人。
直到王府谋逆，全家被贬为庶人，金枝玉叶的郡主将要迎来凋零结局时，悍然不顾家人反对，前来求娶。
之后便是男子仕途受阻，女子因家人和丈夫的遭遇以泪洗面，两人相互安慰携手共渡难关，你读书来我研墨，期间是苦也是甜。
康熙一边笑一边揉眼睛，也不知道是被感动了还是笑过头了，又抓了一把铜钱撒下去：“好！”
胤礽嘴角抽抽。
他看着戏台上那洒满的铜钱碎银布花，这打赏简直太疯狂了。
谁说追星是现代人的专属？古时人追起星来，这疯狂也不见得比不过现代人啊。
福全和常宁也是老戏迷了，两人还不知道故事写的是谁，只听得如痴如醉，兴致来了还要跟着唱几句。
胤禔看过多次排演，本以为会没意思。哪知道有了周围人叫好，这戏文听得多了一分新鲜。
胤礽看着自家大哥小小年纪也跟着大人摇头晃脑，嘴中称好，大把大把铜钱往下撒，已经颇具纨绔子弟雏形，不由心中大痛，狠狠拧了一把康熙的手背。
康熙想用扇子敲胤礽的脑袋，落到一半，想起儿子的脑袋不能敲，改敲儿子的肩膀：“拧我作甚？”
胤礽道：“阿玛，你悠着点，别教坏大哥。”
康熙失笑：“你小小年纪，怎么这么古板严肃？来。”
康熙塞了一把铜钱到胤礽手中：“撒。”
胤礽：“……我不。”
康熙把胤礽抱起来放到戏楼栏杆处：“快，不然不放你下来。”
胤礽嘴一瘪，这个阿玛不能要了，就知道教坏小孩子。
他无奈钱一撒，力道太小，没撒到头上，撒到楼下一个老头子的头上。
老头子摸了摸脑袋，抬头看到一可怜兮兮被不靠谱的大人抱在栏杆上的小孩，不由吹胡子瞪眼，怒视康熙。
康熙注意到那老头子，脸一黑：“他怎么在这？！”
胤礽好奇：“他是谁啊。”
康熙咬牙切齿：“顾、炎、武！”
名字有点熟。胤礽思考了许久，小拳头往掌心一捶：“哦，是他啊，前朝遗民顾炎武。”
康熙重重喷气：“哼！”
顾炎武是谁？前朝遗民四个字足以概括。
顾炎武和顾贞观先祖东林先生顾宪成，虽都出自江东顾氏望族，但大约也就是一个省里都姓顾的那一点关系。
顾炎武与顾宪成不仅不是一个时代，也分属不同学问流派，见面肯定是要打出狗脑子来。
比起顾宪成，顾炎武才更被后人所知，被后人评价为明末清初四大启蒙思想家之一。
改朝换代，时局渐渐平稳，普通老百姓们已经逐渐习惯在新的朝代生活，再掀起乱局已经很难。
这时候，有的前朝老人不阻止后人融入这个新的朝代，让子孙后代能继续生活下去，自己则坚决不出仕，守着前朝遗民的身份度过一辈子。
顾炎武便是其一。
康熙深深敬仰其学问、也深深敬佩其品行，越是尊敬，就越对其不爽。
可这不爽后，他又更敬佩顾炎武。
两股滋味交杂，让康熙看戏的心情都没了。
胤礽倒是兴奋不已：“阿玛！我要去找他玩！”
康熙白了儿子一眼：“别想了，他不会出仕。”
“我没想让他出仕，我就想请教些问题。”胤礽扭来扭去，从怀里挣脱，跳到地上，“哥哥陪我去！”
胤禔道：“好。人多，你牵稳我的手。”
康熙给两儿子一人一个爆栗。胤礽那个爆栗砸在半空中，落在了胤礽的背上。
“你这么小一点，能保护得了谁？”康熙没好气道，“朕带你们去。”
胤礽问道：“三弟弟去吗？”
胤祉打哈欠：“不去，睡觉。”
说完，他翻个身，在手足无措的常宁怀里继续睡觉。
对胤祉这么小的孩子而言，戏文一点意思都没有，就算有人吵闹也很催眠。
福全问道：“臣也一起去吗？”
康熙想了想，把大儿子的手塞回福全手中：“不用，你带着老大在上面，我和保成去。”
胤禔不满：“为什么？我也要去。”
康熙道：“你脾气暴躁，我怕你冲撞了老人家。”
胤禔闷哼了一声，同意了。
他有自知之明。如果那个老人敢对弟弟不敬，他不但要冲撞，还要使出全身的力气撞过去。
康熙整理了一下衣衫，然后看着一眼今天是黄色小鸡的儿子，有些犹豫。
这么去见顾炎武，会不会被顾炎武说不成体统？
“阿玛，快走。”小鸡仔胤礽催促康熙，“你不去我一个人去啦。”
“不准。”康熙抱起小鸡仔儿子，硬着头皮下楼。
他把顾炎武叫不进宫。勉强顾炎武，那家伙肯定会去撞柱子。这个倔老头不是朝堂那些沽名钓誉的御史，虽然活得很滋润，不寻死，但真的不怕死。
康熙要脸，对方不来就他，他也不乐意去做什么三顾茅庐的事，何况顾炎武已经老了，他也用不上几年，没必要屈尊降贵。
但既然碰巧遇到了，康熙很想去顾炎武面前炫耀儿子。
我儿子，大清太子，可优秀了！你赶紧夸！
比起黑暗的前明，我大清有如此太子，肯定有更光明的未来，后悔吧倔老头！
顾炎武不认识康熙。
他看到楼上的小鸡仔来了，以为小鸡仔是来道歉的，摆摆手道：“不碍事，但不要把孩子抱那么高，危险。”
“老先生，可单独一叙。”小鸡仔胤礽从康熙怀里跳下来，小翅膀搭在顾炎武膝盖上，凑顾炎武耳边小声道，“偷偷告诉你，其实我是太子哦。”
顾炎武治学严肃，对普通小孩子则极慈祥。
小鸡仔胤礽哒哒哒跑过来时，他就佝偻着身子，配合胤礽把头垂下。
听到这句话，顾炎武眼眸微动，他抬头看了康熙一眼。
康熙有些紧张，板着脸给了顾炎武一个不屑的眼神。
顾炎武失笑：“好。”

51.三更合一 [V]
顾炎武此人在前明遗民中，经历也算与众不同。
他上半生为了南明朝廷辗转，中年多牢狱之灾，晚年多次拒绝朝廷征召。
但他并未完全与大清朝廷隔绝开。
许多受了顾炎武影响的人都在朝中当官，顾炎武的外甥徐乾学是康熙年间探花，如今正依附纳兰家，以后会官至刑部尚书。
顾炎武入京后，与朝中许多汉臣都有来往。
顾炎武的行为准则很清晰。他希望用自己的学问影响如今的大清朝堂，但又不愿意出仕。
康熙朝中如今研读经义的人莫不以顾炎武为师，康熙早闻顾炎武大名。
顾炎武不认识康熙，康熙不但看过顾炎武的画像，还在微服私访时偷偷观察过顾炎武。
哦，康熙偷偷观察顾炎武的时候，明珠跟在康熙身边。
所以康熙做出这等行为，一定是明珠的错。
这间戏楼背后的人是皇宫，为康熙收集消息的据点之一。
康熙想要单独的房间，戏楼再热闹都能有。
他们所在的雅间仍能看到、听到楼下的人唱戏，干瘦老头顾炎武神情自在，眼神还不断往戏台子上瞟，仿佛比起康熙，戏文更吸引他。
康熙气得就想拂袖离开。
胤礽拉了拉康熙的袖子，展开双翅哒哒哒走到顾炎武身边：“仰头和你说话好麻烦，抱抱。”
顾炎武愣了一下。
他低头和天真无邪的小太子对视，脸上终于多了一点无措。
胤礽可不管顾炎武的呆愣，抬起小短腿就往顾炎武膝盖上爬。
顾炎武僵硬地任由胤礽爬上他的膝盖，靠在他怀里，还长长舒了一口气，不敢置信看向康熙。
康熙忍着笑道：“保成被我娇纵得厉害，老先生请见谅。”
胤礽把顾炎武两条胳膊拉过来护住自己，仰头道：“不需要见谅。不会有人不喜欢保成，对不对？”
顾炎武：“……”这孩子穿得稀奇古怪，怎么没办法说出拒绝他的话？
康熙放松下来，道：“保成，你不是有话要和老先生说吗？”
康熙装出一副不想和顾炎武说话的模样，是儿子非要来他才来。
胤礽看着康熙开始演戏，十分无语。
阿玛你明明非常想和老先生说话，为什么要拉我当掩护？你确定我能和老先生谈论经义？
哦，你还真教过我。头疼。
胤礽叹了口气，道：“顾先生，圣人是不是无人能敌啊？”
顾炎武做好了心理准备，但没想到胤礽居然会问这个：“当然。”
胤礽扳着手指头道：“可是圣人的弟子不能比圣人强，圣人弟子的弟子不能比圣人弟子强……一代都比一代弱，否则就是不敬圣人，那文人不是越来越没用？”
顾炎武：“……”
康熙若有所思。
胤礽又道：“你有儿子的话，希望儿子不如你，孙子不如儿子吗？”
顾炎武叹气：“自然不希望。”
“荀子《劝学》中言，‘青，取之于蓝，而青于蓝；冰，水为之，而寒于水。’孔子也言，‘三人行必有我师焉。’可见圣人们也是不希望的。”胤礽晃悠了两下小短腿，“现在我们熟知的经义，真的是圣人本义吗？”
顾炎武道：“谁知道呢。”
胤礽道：“顾先生开朴学之先河，重新考据经义，是否也是想到了这个问题？”
顾炎武笑而不语。
胤礽仰着头看着天花板：“顾先生，我知你和大清有血海深仇。昆山屠杀，是你心中永远不可愈合的伤疤。”
康熙表情微动。
傻孩子，你说什么呢！你还在他怀里呢！你不怕他直接捅你一刀吗！
顾炎武仍旧笑着，仿佛他怀里的不是大清的太子，面前的不是大清的皇帝。
“可你现在仍旧出现在京城，仍旧愿意为在朝中当官的汉臣们解惑。”胤礽道，“因为顾先生看到改朝换代之事已经不可避免，黎民百姓迎来了短暂的喘息。若大清能像华夏大地上其他王朝一样，哪怕它的建立充满了血腥，对黎民百姓而言，也是一件好事。”
“兴，百姓苦；亡，百姓苦。前明覆灭已不可逆转，往前看才是对百姓好的事。所以顾先生为南明殚精竭虑，却拒绝为叛乱的三藩出力。满汉融合，让大清皇帝成为整个华夏的皇帝，让华夏的血脉和文脉在大清身上延续下去，是你现在正在做的事。”
“为此，你深深厌恶大清，仍旧在为大清培养人才。”
胤礽从顾炎武膝盖上跳下来，两只鸡翅膀合拢，对着顾炎武作揖：“先生高义。”
康熙瞳孔地震。
是、是这样吗？！原来顾炎武是这么想的吗？！
康熙换位思考，如果自己一家都死在清军屠刀下，他能为大清培养人才吗？
滚！不死不休！
他闭上眼，深深叹了一口气，走到儿子身旁，也作揖道：“先生高义。”
胤礽震惊，他用眼角余光瞥康熙。这还是他阿玛吗？他阿玛会做这样的事？！
康熙保持着作揖的姿势岿然不动。
顾炎武脸上如面具般的微笑终于松动。
他收起笑容，看着面前对自己作揖的大清最尊贵父子二人，久久没有动作。
康熙和胤礽保持着作揖的动作，也久久没有动。
“唉。”顾炎武道，“皇上，太子，你们可知，我恨不得大清宗室全部死绝。”
康熙先横跨一步，把胤礽护在身后后，才道：“若我换做先生，也一样。”
康熙并非从行伍中成长起来的帝王，他是和平时期之帝王。
至少现在，他真的有一颗仁心。
胤礽没说错，时代变了。
顾炎武又沉默了许久，道：“你会成为一个好皇帝吗？”
康熙道：“朕在此承诺，定会成为一个好皇帝。”
顾炎武想扯出一个笑容。
刚才他能一直笑着，现在却笑不出来。
他本就很苍老了，现在却连精神气都没了，好似已经变成了一个完完全全半只脚踏入了棺材的老人，岁月和苦难已经完全压垮了他的脊梁。
但康熙知道，胤礽知道，这只是错觉。
眼前的病弱老头直到死亡前的一刻，仍旧在著书立作，教书育人。
胤礽更知道，后世在清朝能排得上号的汉人名臣，几乎都研读过他的著作，接受过他的思想熏陶。
他一生未为清朝出仕，但他的徒子徒孙撑起了整个大清文人仅剩的脊梁，直到大清覆灭。
他深恨清朝，清朝的长治久安却有他不可磨灭的功劳。
清初其他启蒙思想家，都不像顾炎武一样行事“矛盾”。他与所有人都截然不同。
顾炎武仰起头，眼泪横着眼尾的皱纹，没有落下。
他无声哭泣，康熙一手护着孩子，一只手在身前攥紧，眼眶也有些红。
人非草木，孰能无情。即使是皇帝，也有被某人某事感动的时候。
胤礽牵着康熙的衣角，心里难受极了。
他有些后悔，自己是不是不该来见顾炎武。
可他想来见顾炎武。
见这封建末期时代唯一一个一只脚踏足了半圣的大儒，一个真正继承了孔孟之道的大儒。
一个让清朝帝王深深感到挫败，却在《清史稿》中为其单独列传的大儒。
顾炎武，人的名，树的影。
“我和阿玛……我和父亲不会强逼顾先生出仕，只希望顾先生的著作能第一时间给我和父亲一份。无论什么著作。”胤礽从康熙身后探出鸡冠头小脑袋。
顾炎武没有擦眼泪。
他的眼泪很快就干了，就像是没有流过泪一样。
顾炎武看到胤礽探出的鸡冠头小脑袋后，脸上终于重新浮现笑容。
他对胤礽招招手。
胤礽松开康熙的衣角，从康熙护着他的手臂下钻了出去，扑到顾炎武的膝盖前，像接受祖父教导的孩童一样仰头看着顾炎武。
康熙没拦住胤礽，攥紧拳头深深叹了一口气。
“好。”顾炎武揉了揉胤礽的鸡冠头，“都给你。”
胤礽认真道：“还有啊，顾先生的外甥是个贪官，你知道吗？”胤礽以为顾炎武的外甥蒙蔽了顾炎武。
顾炎武笑道：“知道。这个官场就是如此，不贪不能合群。你父亲没教过你？”
胤礽像小猪一样哼哼。先生居然知道！
康熙握紧拳头，放嘴边干咳一声：“吏治……吏治朕会想办法。”
顾炎武讽刺道：“你管得住那群满洲人吗？他们骨子里还带着从关外带来的野蛮，根本没想过成为这片土地真正的官员。”
胤礽“呀”了一声，道：“顾先生和我说的话一模一样！我和父亲说过！父亲还揍我！”
顾炎武赶紧护住胤礽，瞪了康熙一眼。
康熙：“……”顾先生您睁大眼睛看看，你面前的也是个满洲小孩，也是满洲人！别把我当坏人，把他当好人！我是他爹！要坏坏一窝！
顾炎武轻轻拍了拍胤礽的脑袋，就像是掸掉胤礽头上的灰尘：“预言地震的是不是你？”
康熙震惊：“顾先生怎么知道！”
顾炎武道：“要得到什么，就要付出什么。他重病，你没病。”
康熙：“……”真是简单粗暴的判断。
顾炎武注视着胤礽。
他在猜测出胤礽的存在之后，几欲呕血，心神大恸。
儒信天人合一。正统王朝立世，自开国皇帝之后，总会有一两代仿若有神人相助的帝王出现。这是上天承认这个王朝的证明。
有这样的帝王出现的王朝，大多会延续至少百年。
清朝居然也是吗！
上天已经承认了暴清吗！
顾炎武很想对天嘶吼，悠悠苍天何其不公。
可他理智上明白，天地不仁，以万物为刍狗。天地没有感情，万物都和祭祀用的草狗一样，天地不会特别对待任何人任何事，只是按照一定规律行事。
纵观历史改朝换代，屠城屠百姓称王称帝者不知多少。上天不会为这些事惩罚帝王和王朝，只有黎民百姓在哀嚎。
神灵和天地都不会庇佑百姓，能庇佑百姓的只有人自己。所以他不能倒下，不能隐居，他必须为黎民苍生留下些什么。
大明气数已尽，大清气数正是旺盛时。他无法逆天改命，只能孤身入局，影响这个残暴的王朝。
顾炎武自进京之后就看到了这件事。
地震之后，顾炎武完全失去了那仅剩不多的反清复明的希望。
他看着眼前被神灵钟爱的孩子。若他能成为皇帝，或许百姓会过得很好。
就算是昆山、就算是扬州、就算是嘉定，也一定会恢复繁华。
顾炎武突然想起，那些地方其实已经慢慢恢复繁华了。
许多人都已经忘记大明了。他们已经认可自己是大清的人了。
何其可悲，何其可悲。
遗民犹有一人存，遗民只有一人存啊。
顾炎武重新把胤礽抱到膝上，和胤礽说起自己的一些思想和见解。
被无视的康熙摸了摸鼻子，拖了把椅子坐在顾炎武身旁，让赵昌问店家拿来了笔墨纸砚，一边偷听一边做笔记。
顾炎武说的话很通俗直白，力图让孩子也能听懂。
胤礽不但能听懂，还能提问和说出自己的见解。
他们一老一小说了很久，说得口干舌燥，说到戏终人散，华灯初上。
顾炎武一生的心血不可能在几个时辰说完，但他只会与胤礽说这几个时辰。
这几个时辰，他为黎民苍生，暂时为太子师、为帝王师。
走出这扇门，他又是大明遗民顾炎武，是那个和清朝有血海深仇的孤独老头。
顾炎武在《日知录》中道，“易姓改号，谓之亡国；仁义充塞而至于率兽食人，人将相食，谓之亡天下……保国者，其君其臣、肉食者谋之；保天下者，匹夫之贱，与有责焉耳矣！”
他大半辈子都在为了“保国”而奔走，现在他的所作所为，则是为了“保天下”。
他进入京城，与文臣结交，让子孙门生出仕，便是试图把大清这个“仁义充塞而至于率兽食人”的王朝影响成一个人能活下去的王朝。
为了“保天下”，他背弃了自己的本心，背弃了血海深仇。
顾炎武嗓子哑了。
他没有喝康熙亲自递过来的水，只用口水勉强润了润嗓子和喉咙，继续教导胤礽。
他最后说的是许多儒生不擅长、甚至鄙夷的治财学问。
顾炎武善于治财。
他家财被豪强占尽，被其追杀满地逃窜，他还被关进监狱里，出来时身无长物。可他每到一处，便自垦田地，置房置产，离开时便将这些资产交给门人，弃掉财产。等到了下一处，继续赚钱置产。
像他这种经历的人，几乎全都贫困潦倒，他却几乎没有生活困顿的时候。
顾炎武在京城当官的外甥徐乾学等人为疏通朝中关节，向顾炎武借了数千白银，顾炎武都懒得去讨要，可见他多有钱。
顾炎武若能出仕，康熙把户部给顾炎武，顾炎武估计能让国库的银子翻一倍。
可惜，可惜，顾炎武不可能出仕，永远都不可能出仕。
康熙遗憾，更加厌恶多尔衮和多铎。
敢情坐皇帝位置的不是你们，你们就可以乱来了吗？我的千古一帝汗阿玛的话，你们都当耳边风！
康熙想了想自家汗阿玛那时候的岁数，脸有点黑。
好吧，不当耳边风才不可能。就跟鳌拜能听我的话似的。
顾炎武勉强熬了熬，终于把自己想说的大致说完了。
只是大致，只是梗概。剩下的，胤礽可以看书自己学。
顾炎武不会敝帚自珍。他的著作本就会公开给所有人看，皇帝和太子想看自然也能看。
康熙再次奉茶，顾炎武再次拒绝了康熙的茶。
他把胤礽还给了康熙，然后摇摇晃晃，深一脚浅一脚走出门。
康熙吩咐人偷偷跟着顾炎武，保护顾炎武安全回家。
胤礽抱着康熙的脖子，父子俩沉默地回宫。
晚上，康熙没有去后宫。
他抱着儿子，长吁短叹。
这个大清，还能有第二个顾炎武吗？很难了吧。
胤礽蹭了蹭康熙：“阿玛，你努力，你可以成为第二个顾炎武！”
康熙：“？？？”
他捏了捏儿子的脸：“是你好好努力！”
胤礽翻身，背对着康熙：“我不要。我还小。阿玛，你听过一句话吗？”
康熙把胤礽翻过来，正对着自己：“敢用后脑勺对着阿玛，你很嚣张啊。说，什么话？”
胤礽一字一顿道：“慧、极、必、伤。”
康熙抱紧了儿子：“谁说的？不准再说这种话。快睡觉，你还想不想睡了？”
胤礽：“哦。”
太监将蜡烛吹灭。
半晌，黑暗中响起康熙的声音：“这话究竟是谁说的？”
胤礽：“当然是皇玛法。还有半句是情深不寿。”是金庸。
康熙：“哦。”肯定是玉林通琇那个假和尚说的。
没事了，这话一定不是真的。康熙自我安慰。
……
顾炎武见到康熙和胤礽之后，收拾了行李，第二日就离京归家了。
他回到昆山，做回了田家翁，安心著书。
康熙让当地官员好好照顾他。这一声招呼，让康熙知道顾家家产被昆山豪强叶家占据，叶家还追杀顾炎武的事。
他叹了口气，叫来了与昆山叶家同宗的叶方蔼，让叶方蔼回家一趟处理此事。
叶方蔼是个清官，还多次举荐顾炎武。叶家却是霸占了顾家家产，还追杀顾炎武的昆山豪强。
康熙又想起顺治在乾清宫前帐篷中对他的教导。
当一个官员清廉时，还得看看他背后的家族、他的师门、他当地的豪强，才能看到他是否是个好官。
康熙收集了其他有名的前明遗民的著作，他看完之后，叹气道：“国外也有类似的思想。”
胤礽知道康熙说的是什么思想。
他们开始怀疑君主制度的正确性，开始试图探索一种更适合华夏的制度。
康熙很忧虑，甚至有了焚书的想法。
胤礽笑道：“这不是好事吗？”
康熙难得敲了敲胤礽脑袋：“怎么能叫好事？”
胤礽捂着脑袋道：“一种思想形成现实，至少要过两三百年，那时候咱们大清肯定差不多没啦。”
康熙：“……别胡说。”
胤礽攀上康熙的膝盖坐着：“阿玛，咱俩还说那些虚的干什么。大清有阿玛教导祖孙三代，大概能兴盛一两百年，之后肯定会走下坡路，两三百年差不多了。后一百年肯定还是半死不活的状态。”
康熙想揍儿子。事实或许是如此，但自家人哪能这么没志气！
“两三百年啊，也不错了。”康熙其实也很没志气。短命的王朝多得是，何况大清“先天不足”。
事实也是如此。
如果大清没有变成半殖民地续命，外部矛盾强压着内部矛盾不爆发，大清早没了。
半殖民地半封建社会对华夏是百年浩劫，对大清而言却是续命的良药。
“等这个思想成熟，咱们大清差不多也没了。这样正好后面没皇帝。”胤礽笑嘻嘻道，“我们得不到的东西，也不能让别人得到。从大清之后，这片大地没皇帝啦！”
康熙：“……”还能这么想？保成你的脑袋怎么长的！
胤礽吊着康熙的脖子晃了晃：“儿孙事自有儿孙自己担心，我和阿玛只需要在青史留名就好啦。咱们允许这些思想，当时代变革的时候，我们会不会变成圣人？身为皇帝，却反思皇权的弊端，嘿嘿，这不是圣人是什么？”
康熙失笑：“这不是坑后代吗？”
胤礽摇头：“坑不了。咱们华夏有了几千年的皇帝，除非真到了不得不改的时候，否则皇帝是绝对不可能消失的。到了那个时候，我们现在做什么事都无法阻挡。”
康熙叹息：“就不能有让咱们爱新觉罗家永远当皇帝的法子吗？”
胤礽道：“有啊，隔壁倭国就是。”
康熙想起倭国那个天皇，俊脸一黑：“那还是算了。”
康熙越想越烦恼。烦恼的同时，他又觉得自己为两三百年后的事烦恼很傻，就更烦恼了。
皇帝烦恼了就想折腾人，明珠等人就遭殃了。
康熙将明珠、索额图、佟国纲等人叫到一起去听戏，并问他们感想如何。
明珠：“和臣没关系！”只要我不承认，就很我没关系！
明珠看到完整的戏时，都已经傻了。
这一出在纳兰府、在他眼皮子底下写的戏，居然是以他为主人公？
里面的诗词曲居然还是他儿子写的？
纳兰性德！家法伺候！
现在明珠每日出门上朝办公，都会有人用或敬佩或探究的眼神看他，甚至还有相熟的人过来拍着他肩膀似笑非笑，“你和夫人情深意切我们都明白了，谁敢说你们坏话你告诉我，我帮你弹劾他”。
明珠嘴角抽搐。
不，那处戏和我没关系！一点关系都没有！那是前朝旧事，和我大清朝的纳兰明珠有什么关系！
佟国纲幽怨地瞥了明珠一眼：“挺好看。”
这戏文虽然暴露了明珠一些令人发笑的习惯，比如喜欢偷偷跟着自家夫人暗自烦恼，比如在人前人模狗样人后却伤春悲秋比他儿子容若还矫情，比如由于太喜欢书每看到一没看过的书就会兴奋得拉着夫人叭叭叭说半天……
这些小习惯其实没什么，就是知道原型是明珠之后，就特别震惊，让人忍不住惊呼“明珠你居然是这样的人”。
但这戏文总体上是夸奖明珠，是夸奖啊！
而我呢？被写成了大渣男大反派，我面子往哪搁？这些事我从来没做过啊！我从来没有说过明珠和他夫人的坏话！
可佟国纲不能辩解。他只能昂首挺胸做出清者自清不屑解释的姿态，如果勉强辩解，反倒更引人主意。
谁干的！我要揍死他！
是不是你！鄂伦岱！
鄂伦岱：是的，就是我，怎么滴！
佟国纲捂着胸口，恨不得再去康熙面前嚎一声“请诛此子”！
索额图挠挠头：“陛下，戏文中明珠的死对头不会是臣吧？肯定不是臣。臣虽然不屑拿他家宅内事说三道四，但如果有人说他坏话，我肯定只会跟着笑，不会为他辩解。”
康熙白了索额图一眼：“你倒是很有自知之明。”
索额图笑道：“戏文中把臣美化成这模样，臣有些不好意思了。这些戏谁写的？”
康熙似笑非笑：“朕主持编写的。”
索额图笑容裂开。
明珠身形摇摇欲坠。
佟国纲已经坠了。他跪在地上半晌不能语。
康熙让人把佟国纲扶起来：“朕知道你冤枉，这素材是你儿子提供的。”
佟国纲一口气没提起来，眼前一黑，差点晕倒。
他就知道！
康熙用扇子敲了敲桌子，让三人坐下：“朕准备用戏文宣传一些事，明珠的故事只是一个尝试。民间都妖魔化满洲人，明珠和夫人伉俪情深，很适合作为宣传。至于什么对手和仇人，不过是为了戏曲冲突需要，你们不用在意。”
索额图和佟国纲在心里呐喊，皇上你不在意，你写你自己啊！
但他们不敢喊出声，只能含泪道：“是，皇上，我们不在意。”
明珠突然淡定了。
虽然被人叨叨私事很不爽，但他至少是个正面人物啊。比起被迫和他惺惺相惜的索额图和名声被亲儿子抹黑的佟国纲，那真是好太多。
有对比才有幸福感，明珠佛了。
回家就揍儿子！拿你阿玛额娘的事写成戏文，你怎么不写你自己！
“这出戏就算这么过去了，接下来的事，你们好好上心。”康熙这次不仅要笑话他们，还要让他们干活。
那群小年轻在民间随便做做事还行，各地戏班子进京之后的统筹安排，还得让这些老成持重的朝中中流砥柱来做事。
康熙本想把这些事交给汉臣，但现在他想试探一下满臣的态度。
索额图立刻领命，丝毫没有犹豫，和以前每次康熙下命令他都要叽叽歪歪半天完全不一样，让康熙分外欣慰；
佟国纲犹豫了一会儿，也很快领命。佟家深受汉文化熏陶，虽然一直想朝着满洲勋贵靠拢，但佟国纲不傻，知道皇帝的信任才是佟家的生存之道，不会阻拦康熙的命令；
而最能察觉圣心体恤圣意的明珠却愣在当场，半天没有反应。
康熙平静地看着明珠，没有出声提醒。
索额图和佟国纲疑惑地用眼角余光瞟着明珠，不知道明珠为何这个时候哑了。
半晌，明珠才回过神。
他想起了太子对他的提点。太子果然是最了解皇上的人。
还是说，太子当日的提点，其实是皇上的授意。
勋贵搞事和宗室搞事不一样。宗室是自信自己手中有兵，康熙不敢对他们做什么；勋贵们本身地位只是皇帝的臣子，他们搞事则是自信手段隐蔽，康熙不会察觉。
他们暗地里积攒反对太子的力量，对皇子们像去市集摊子上选东西一样挑挑拣拣，这一切都隐藏在他们忠心耿耿的表情下，自信康熙对此不知情。
如果康熙一早就知道他们心中的弯弯道道，知道他们反对太子的原因是想要削弱帝权呢？
反对太子和削弱帝权截然不同，前者可能皇上睁一只眼闭一只眼，后者是真的会掉脑袋的事。
明珠深吸一口气，跪地磕头：“陛下请将这件事交给臣。臣愿卸下一切职位，以这件事优先！”
索额图和佟国纲十分惊讶。
明珠这反应他们看不懂啊！为什么明珠会突然这么激动？！难道发生了什么他们不知道的事吗？？
康熙手中的扇子轻轻敲着桌面，一下、两下、三下，就像是撞钟一样在三人心中撞响。
康熙也在疑惑，明珠为何态度这么激动。
明珠是猜测朕知道了什么对他极其不利的事？那件事是什么？
君臣相处很多时候都要进行心理博弈。明珠以为康熙知道，康熙不知道也要装作自己知道。
他略一思考后，道：“那就辛苦你了。”
明珠肩膀一下子垮了，他心想，果然如此，皇帝已经对他动了杀心。
皇上圣明，他的一切小动作小心思都在皇上的慧眼下无所遁形。在皇上看来，自己这种被他亲手提拔起来的人做这等事，不仅是对皇帝的背叛，还有对恩人的背叛。若不是儿子和太子亲近，恐怕……
纳兰家必须和勋贵宗室切割了。
明珠狠狠磕头：“谢陛下宽恕！”
索额图和佟国纲还愣在那。
怎么了怎么了，发生什么事了？皇帝和明珠在他们眼前交换了什么心有灵犀的交易吗？
索额图看佟国纲：你看懂了吗？
佟国纲看索额图：我看不懂，但我大受震撼，有点心悸。
“起来吧，你能明白就好。太子说你有大才，朕再给你一次机会。”康熙观察明珠表情。
明珠神情恍惚了一下，如释重负。
太子……是太子帮我求情了。
太子明知我想做什么，还帮我求情，这孩子怎么这么傻？
明珠哽咽：“是臣愧对皇上，愧对太子。臣一定会把握住这个机会！”
现在已经没有让纳兰家左右摇摆的余地了！
果然和朕那个好儿子有关。康熙满意地用扇子砸了一下手心。
好了，回家问儿子就行。
不知道儿子对明珠说了什么，让明珠吓成这样。
胤礽的一些行为脱离了康熙的控制，康熙慌张了一瞬之后，很快欣慰就占据了上风。
厉害了，我的儿！回去好好夸你！你居然还瞒着阿玛，是想给阿玛一个惊喜吗！
康熙抛下一位陷入自我脑补、两位正在迷糊的重臣，兴高采烈回到宫里，把早上睡懒觉、吃完午膳下午还要睡懒觉的小懒猪提起来：“保成，你和明珠说了什么？他快被吓死了？”
胤礽迷迷糊糊道：“什么吓死？”
康熙从太监手中拿过湿帕子给胤礽擦脸，把今日之事告诉胤礽。
胤礽打了个激灵。
明珠误我！你居然在阿玛面前自爆了！我就不该提点你！
算了，躺平吧。
胤礽懒得挣扎，打了个哈欠，挂在康熙脖子上蹭蹭：“明珠先想支持大哥，大哥气到他之后，他又对我两个弟弟挑挑拣拣。我说你再这样，阿玛会杀了你。”
康熙脸色一沉。
胤礽懒洋洋道：“别生气啊，阿玛你要为这种事生气，会天天都生气，气出病来。满朝满蒙勋贵都不想让阿玛自己决定太子人选，阿玛立我的时候不早就知道了吗？”
康熙张开嘴，半晌发不出声音。
是的，他早就知道。
他知道立太子的目的，他知道太子是靶子，他知道保成成为太子之后将面临的恶意，这一切他都知道。
可他现在不想让保成知道。
保成知道了，会这么想他这个阿玛？会认为他的父爱不纯粹吗？
可保成实在是太聪明了，还有一个顺治在他耳边叨叨，他没瞒住。
“阿玛会保护你。”最终康熙只是抱紧怀里哈欠不断的儿子，语气沉重道。
胤礽又打了一个哈欠：“嗯，哈，阿玛，我可以睡觉了吗？”
“还睡！”康熙捏了捏胤礽的鼻子。
胤礽揉了揉脸：“我也不知道为什么，回到宫里就犯困。”
大概是因为宫里太无聊了吧。
大哥又被逼着上学，三弟弟和四弟弟回到自己额娘身边，他每日待在弟弟们身旁的时间不好太久，而且要等大哥放学一起去。真是太无聊了。
康熙却会错了意。
他的心又沉了起来。
胤礽才回宫不久，诅咒又开始消耗他的体力了吗？
“保成，今年要不要去你额娘墓前拜祭？”康熙决定大修宫中风水，让胤礽再出宫住几日。
胤礽立刻眼睛瞪圆：“要去！”
康熙揉了揉胤礽的脑袋，失笑。
还好还好，儿子精神还是很好的。
