52.三更合一 [V]
胤礽每年生辰都是在仁孝皇后的灵牌前度过。
大清以孝治国，胤礽出生时仁孝皇后难产，注定他一辈子都不可能举办寿辰。
前前世的胤礽非常讨厌这个日子。从懂事起到死亡那一天，每到这一日，就会有人不断在他耳边提醒他，你额娘是因为你而死。
康熙斥责他“生而克母”后，每年这一日，胤礽都会夜不能寐，产生幻觉，仿佛仁孝皇后的鬼魂来责骂他，说后悔怀他生他。
那时候的自己应该已经半疯了。
胤礽难得的出了一会儿神，然后去找胤禔玩，告诉胤禔这个好消息。
他要出宫祭奠仁孝皇后，肯定会带上大哥。
胤禔得知这个即将离开京城的好消息后，却没有像每次出宫时那样开心地大笑。
他揉了揉胤礽的头，把胤礽揽进怀里抱抱：“嗯，大哥陪你去。”
胤礽一瞬间感觉，这辈子其实阿玛什么的无所谓了，只要有这个大哥就……啊！
正在抱抱蹭蹭的大阿哥和小太子，被他们并不老的老父亲一把扯开：“这么大的人了，还这么黏糊干什么。”
胤禔鼻子喷着气，就像是一只愤怒的小牛犊：“汗阿玛，我和弟弟年纪都不大，都是小孩！”
“哦，是吗？”康熙刚有强烈的直觉，必须把这两家伙分开。等把胤礽抱到怀里的时候，康熙才松了一口气。
胤禔气得跺脚，想把胤礽抢回来，又不敢上前抢。
惠嫔捏着帕子站在后面，笑容都僵了。
无论看了多少次儿子和皇上抢太子的情形，她都无法习惯。
两个哥哥要出京去巩华城，自己却因为年幼不能随行，胤祉气得跑去同样不能出宫的胤禛抱怨了许久。
胤禛终于能说单字。胤祉对着他抱怨，他就重复胤祉的话。
胤礽扒着门框偷看，心想四弟弟现在好像一个坏掉的复读机。
德嫔在胤礽身后偷看，和胤礽交换了一个“我儿子/四弟弟好可爱”的默契眼神。
历史中德嫔现在肚子里应该已经揣上了六阿哥了。
但戴佳式肚子里原本的七阿哥都显怀了，德嫔居然还没怀上。
胤礽担心，这六阿哥怕是被他蝴蝶掉了。
胤礽正担心着，听闻宫中安嫔怀孕了。
安嫔……谁啊？胤礽想了想，才记起来这个安嫔，居然还有个了不得的家世。
安嫔李氏，汉军正蓝旗人，大明第一个降清的大明将领李永芳的孙女。
因这个家世，安嫔虽然不受宠，也在康熙十六年大封后宫时位列嫔位之首，居启祥宫。
之后安嫔无子无宠，再未晋升，在宫中蹉跎几十年。但因其家世显赫，于康熙四十年左右，她被送回娘家供养。
康熙虽然多情，但对宫中女子大多都不错，也愿意给臣子恩典，多次送无子无宠的嫔妃回娘家。
安嫔李氏、敬嫔完颜氏、姓博尔济吉特氏的扎鲁特格格等都被康熙送回过，其他没有记载的庶妃宫女，也在康熙给宫中老人恩典的时候放回去不少。
对康熙而言，既能减轻宫中花销，还能得一个仁善的名声，何乐不为？
现在安嫔居然怀孕了，哪怕孩子夭折，也肯定不会被送回娘家了。
对于妃嫔而言，在宫中蹉跎二三十年后回到娘家好，还是终老宫中好，谁也不能说得清？但安嫔现在肯定是欢喜的。
宫中又多了一个怀孕的嫔妃，太皇太后和康熙却没有多少欢喜。
自从胤礽说自己吸引诅咒之后，宫里孩子一个个的生，每个孩子都很健康，这显然是胤礽的功劳。
宫里每一个出生的孩子，都提醒他们胤礽正处于怎样的折磨中。
康熙又找了僧道二人，想从他们口中询问有没有终止或者转移胤礽所受诅咒的办法。
但僧道二人，废物！
康熙气冲冲在祖庙转了几圈，让先祖们赶紧想办法。
但先祖除了朕那下凡过一次的汗阿玛之外，废物！
康熙心里堵得慌，他以为此刻正饱受折磨的胤礽，却越来越开心。
离五月越来越近，他马上要离开京城，去巩华城看额娘啦！
五月，莺飞草长，碧草连天。京城天气逐渐炎热，火气十足的胤禔已经换上了轻薄的夏装，胤礽仍旧穿了好几层单衣。
康熙亲自把儿子送上马车，离开前捏了捏儿子的脸颊。
经过这几月的休养，胤礽的脸蛋重新圆润，虽比不过之前胖墩墩，那肉肉的下巴也分外招人疼。
“好好听大哥的话。”康熙道。
胤礽怀疑道：“汗阿玛，您确定？”
康熙沉默了一会儿，道：“让你大哥好好听你的话。”
胤礽点头。这才差不多。
康熙对纳兰性德和曹寅道：“你们跟好太子，任何人让你们离开太子的命令都不准听。”
纳兰性德和曹寅跪下道：“臣/奴才遵旨！”
康熙仍旧不放心。他挨个嘱咐和胤礽同行的人，听得胤礽分外无奈。
巩华城说是离开了京城，其实就在京郊。
按照现代地图，巩华城就在北京昌平区沙河镇，城中不但有行宫，还有大小庙宇二十多座，还有专门为皇宫和清军制作毡子的擀毡局。
康熙悼念亡妻，去过几十次巩华城，对巩华城大小建筑了如指掌。胤礽让康熙给他画好地图，标注好游玩顺序，做了旅游指南，把行程安排得满满的。
他催促康熙：“汗阿玛，再不出发，今天的行程就完不成了。”
康熙气得把胤礽按膝盖上拍屁股。
阿玛这么担心你！你只想着玩！你是去看你额娘，不是去玩！
康熙拍屁股的力道很轻，胤礽在康熙膝盖上托腮道：“额娘肯定也想看我到处开心的玩耍，而不是在她面前哭。”
康熙拍儿子的屁股一顿。
他突然想起，亡妻的忌日正是儿子的生日。
宫中每个皇子公主生辰时都有小小的庆祝仪式，都会有大把大把的赏赐。
唯独胤礽在生日前后那几天，只能茹着素守着小小的牌位发呆。
儿子从出生起，连一碗长寿面都未吃过。
他居然现在才意识到这件事。
“好吧，好好玩。”康熙道，“朕和跟着你的人说说你这个歪理，免得你在你额娘面前笑得太开心，被人弹劾不孝顺。”
胤礽托腮回望：“汗阿玛真好。”
“这时候就知道阿玛的好了。”康熙把太子放下来，再次挨个叮嘱。
出行的人都面露无奈。只是去个京郊而已，皇上您不必这么紧张。
康熙还有政务未处理，被太监小心翼翼催促几次之后，即使还有满腹叮嘱的话没说完，也只能不情不愿地让车队上路。
胤禔把弟弟揽到怀里护着：“太颠簸就抓紧我。唉，汗阿玛真唠叨。”
胤礽笑道：“我们俩这么小，汗阿玛不放心很正常。大哥，我想看窗外。”
“看吧，一起看。”胤禔做出小大人的模样。
两个孩子扒着床帘缝，小心翼翼偷看车厢外的情形。
京城除皇城之外，还有内外城之分。内城是八旗子弟和王公贵族所住的地方。胤礽胤禔出宫游玩时，只在内城玩耍。
车队悠悠驶过内城城门，进入了外城，繁华的北京城逐步在两个孩子眼前徐徐展开。
清初因满汉隔阂，汉人都被赶到外城居住，各地的会馆也都在外城。原本明北京城的繁华，都转移到了外城。
在外城，沿街可看到各地来的人接踵比肩。行商叫卖，文人骚客边走边呼朋唤友，甚至还有八旗子弟混入其中醉醺醺路过。
非年非节，外城的热闹居然和内城集市时差不多了。
“比我们玩的地方热闹。”胤禔道，“下次来这里玩。”
“汗阿玛恐怕不会同意我们到外城玩。”胤礽道，“不过可以求着阿玛微服私访带我们去。”
“指望汗阿玛，还不如指望伯父叔父。”胤禔不屑道。
胤礽道：“汗阿玛不同意，他们也不敢带我们出去啊……哎哟。”
马车急刹车，胤礽半个身体探出了车窗，被胤禔赶紧拉了回来。
胤禔怒道：“怎么回事？！”
梁九功连忙来报：“有一辆马车坏在了途中，挡住了我们的路。”
胤禔立刻警觉：“难道是刺客！”
胤礽拍了拍胤禔勒紧他的手臂：“哥，少看些话本。在北京城里，怎么会遇到刺客。我们在马车上等着吧。”
梁九功也立刻道：“是外地来京赴任的八旗官员，不是刺客。”
胤禔一听不是刺客，立刻屁股坐不住了。
胤礽按了半天没按住，被胤禔拉下了马车，借着看前面马车的借口，去呼吸一下外面的新鲜空气。
这条街挺繁华，打扫得很干净，没什么异味。
胤禔一下马车就被路旁的小吃吸引住了。胤礽抱着他的腰，死活不准他吃。
胤礽有上上辈子的记忆，知道要在城里寻找美食，只能去经常有达官贵人光顾的酒楼，否则可能就会拉得生不如死。
古代可没有什么食品安全卫生，全是“古法”制作。酒楼里怕贵人们吃坏肚子，还算干净。路边摊中能看出食材的糖果之类还能舔一舔，其他就不行了。
胤禔就要杠：“话本里说，路边摊才有美食。”
胤礽叹气：“哥，你平时吃的精盐你知道有多贵吗？”
胤禔没懂胤礽为什么突然问这个：“啊？”
胤礽开始给胤禔掰着指头算，精盐、辛香料、提现的高汤……不说食材，宫中一份菜肴的调味料的价格，就够城中贫苦人家吃一年。
胤禔的眼睛开始打圈圈。
胤礽道：“再加上食材，那就更别提了。你以为他们会给你上好的肉？新鲜的菜？”
胤禔心里已经信了胤礽，但还是要保持作为大哥的尊严，坚持要尝一尝。
胤礽叹了口气，挥手让侍卫从旁边闻起来非常香的馄饨摊上，给胤禔拿了一碗馄饨。
这个馄饨摊人非常多，每个人吃馄饨的表情都如痴如醉，好像吃了什么山珍海味，这才把胤禔吸引了。
但馄饨一端来，胤禔就没了胃口。
装馄饨的木碗看着有些脏，里面的汤水浑浊，馄饨皮居然还是灰色。
胤礽忍着笑：“吃吗？”
胤禔咬牙：“吃！”
他梗着脖子咬了一口，然后“呕”，差点吐出来。
这是怎样可怕的味道？馄饨的面皮夹杂着麦麸十分粗糙，汤里除了咸味还有涩味和苦味，油腻的汤水更有一种不可言说的腥臊味。
胤禔忙用清水漱口，不敢置信道：“这么可怕的味道，为什么他们吃得津津有味？”
胤礽道：“馄饨皮只有麦麸没有泥土，汤中咸味和油味很足，可能馅里也真的有肉，这对普通老百姓而言，就是一顿良心美食了。”
胤禔愣住：“这、这样吗？”
胤礽点头，他叹息道：“对于老百姓而言，有混杂着麦麸的面粉大米、有一点油水、有足够的粗盐吃，就是很幸福的日子。如果人人都有这样的食物吃，就可以称得上前所未有的盛世了。”
胤礽想家了，想真正的家。
在那个真正的家乡中，才能真正做到“美味都在路边摊”。因为普通老百姓也有能力购买新鲜的食材和足够的调味料，用勤劳的双手和智慧的大脑烹饪出和大餐馆不同的味道。
“还去看吗？”胤礽问道。
胤禔兴致缺缺：“不去了。看来外城也没什么好玩的。”
胤礽无奈：“只是一个路边摊而已，还不能代表外城。外城也有富贵人去的地方。外城外地和外国的商人云集，无论是店铺里卖的东西还是酒楼里卖的食物，都比内城种类多。特别是各省会馆附近，你能在外城吃到全国各地正宗的美食。”
胤禔问道：“真的？”
胤礽道：“我骗你作甚？回头我们求求阿玛，让汉臣带我们去逛逛，他们对外城熟。”
胤禔被胤礽一哄，终于开心了。
他随手把这碗馄饨赏给路边一个衣衫褴褛的人。那个人立刻对着胤禔使劲磕头，搞得胤禔怪不好意思，想赏给他一贯钱，被胤礽拦住。
胤礽附在胤禔耳边悄悄道：“你赐给他食物，他吃了就是自己的。你赏给他太多钱，咱们前脚一离开，他后脚就会被人敲闷棍。”
说完，胤礽吩咐小太监，等车队离开之后，再偷偷给那老乞丐几个铜钱，算是为胤禔积善积德。
胤禔叹气：“京城里都有乞丐，外面恐怕更……罢了，那是汗阿玛要操心的事。”
胤礽笑了笑，没说话。
三藩之乱之后还有噶尔丹，康熙朝早期可没有什么精力去顾什么民生。
不过噶尔丹之乱本可以不用延续那么久，一征噶尔丹的时候就应该结束。不知道自己能不能做什么。
胤礽突然想起，一征噶尔丹的时候汗阿玛病了，自己和老三去探病，被斥责不够悲痛送回了京城。
那一年自己才十六岁。
后来一废二废的时候，汗阿玛说那时候自己就表现得不孝不悌，忍了自己几十年。
那一年自己才十六岁啊。
哈。
“不舒服？”胤禔突然把胤礽抱起来，“回马车上去。”
“啊，哥，别抱，我自己能走。”胤礽回过神，忙道。
胤禔道：“我是你大哥，我抱着你走怎么了？”
胤礽哭笑不得：“你就比我大两岁，你抱不动……哎哟。”
“你哥我的力气可大了，能抱得动。”胤禔不仅把胤礽抱起来，还颠了颠。
就是他在颠胤礽的时候，胤礽脚落地了。
侍卫赶紧把两个皇子一起抱起来送回马车上去。
这一番折腾，前面车辆也终于挪开了。
入京的是镶黄旗沙济富察氏，汉姓李，名倪满。
他们知道挡住了太子和大皇子的车架之后，倪满吓得肝胆俱裂。
富察氏有两支，先祖为旺吉努一支在朝堂上显赫无比，先祖为莽色都朱乎的一支则因皇太极时期的皇位争斗而凋零。他正是莽色都朱乎那一支。
他这一支富察氏几乎只有他一个独苗苗人才，虽然族人也只有小猫两三只了，好歹他也是全族的希望。难道就要因为这个意外而仕途终止吗？
倪满想去太子和大阿哥那里磕头请罪，却被侍卫拦在一旁，不准靠近。
他站在附近，听到了太子和大阿哥所有对话，心里震撼极了。
这就是大清朝的太子吗？这也过于聪慧了吧？
聪慧就罢了，为什么太子会对民生如此了解？咱们的万岁爷究竟是怎么教导的太子？
车架移动后，胤礽这才看到了那个冷汗涟涟的官员，打开车窗探出脑袋，安抚道：“这是意外，你不必担心。汗阿玛不会因为这点小事斥责你，他心胸可宽广了。”
胤禔也探出脑袋，大声道：“真的吗？我不信！汗阿玛不是最小气了吗？”
“闭嘴吧大哥！”胤礽赶紧捂住胤禔的嘴，把胤禔拖回了马车。
听到胤禔的话的众人：“……”
请给我们一双没有听到大阿哥的话的耳朵，谢谢！
大阿哥害我！！
皇宫中，康熙自然很快得到了太子和大阿哥的车架被一辆坏掉的马车堵住的事。
“倪满？”这个人是康熙亲自圈点进京的人，他自然有印象，“他……运气可真差。”
顿了顿，康熙补充道：“他们那一支运气都很差。”
现在在大清朝廷中，旺吉努那一支富察氏很显赫。但在历史中，莽色都朱乎那一支富察氏才为清廷立下了大功劳，导致莽色都朱乎的近亲几乎全部被大明屠戮。
莽色都朱乎的小女儿衮代嫁给努尔哈赤。她所生的大贝勒莽古尔泰死后被人告发谋逆，一家人都除了宗。衮代也被移出皇陵，抛尸荒野。
这谋逆是真是假康熙不好评价，反正为了收拢八旗军权，削弱贝勒们的权利，皇太极和顺治必须这么做。这一家只是被牵连了。所以这一族中有能用的人，康熙仍旧会重用。
虽然倪满纯粹无妄之灾，康熙为了自家宝贝儿子的面子，仍旧准备小惩一下。
传话的侍卫立刻把太子和大阿哥给倪满说的话告诉了康熙。
康熙听到太子所说的话时，微笑道：“太子仁善，罢了，就不罚他了。”
康熙又听到大阿哥所说的话，微笑立刻变成了狰狞：“胤禔这个混账！”
朕究竟是造了什么孽，才生了这么个气死人的儿子！！！
康熙捂着胸口，惩罚倪满的心思没了，现在只想快马加鞭亲自冲出京城把大儿子揍一顿。
倪满回到京城租赁的院子，忐忑不安地等来了康熙安抚的旨意，松了一口气。
他对妻子和儿女道：“若没有太子当众说的那句话，我可能就要受罚了。”
倪满的夫人也叹气：“怎么运气就这么差，车轴断在了半路。”
倪满的女儿闺名为“彤”，现在正举着一幅图，不悦地看着她的父亲，图中俨然是车轴构造。
倪满侧目，不去理睬女儿。
李彤气得小脸胀红。
“好了好了，阿玛知道了，彤彤早就发现车轴松了，是阿玛不好，急着赶路，以为可以支撑到回家。”倪满把女儿抱起来，反省道。
李彤点头，被忽视的气消了。
她拉了拉倪满的胡须，道：“那个穿黄色衣服的小哥哥好好看。”
倪满立刻严肃道：“那是当今太子，不能说好看。”
李彤愣了愣，呆呆道：“那……不好看？”
倪满黑线：“也不能说不好看……唉，是不是该教你些礼仪了？”
“阿嚏！”马车里的胤礽连打三个喷嚏。
胤禔立刻道：“肯定是汗阿玛念叨咱们。”
胤礽揉了揉鼻子：“有可能。”
阿玛要念叨也念叨大哥啊，我又没说你坏话。
“哇哇哇，出城啦！”胤禔惊喜大叫，把脑袋又伸出去一些。
这一看，他脸就黑了，忙把脑袋缩回来。
胤礽问道：“怎么了？”
胤禔蔫哒哒道：“你自己看。”
胤礽拉开帘子，无奈耸肩。
去年京城大地震，虽灾后重建快一年了，但封建时代的赈灾效率也就这样，灾民们还是沿着京城一线搭棚子住着。
康熙听常泰的意见以工代赈，先从京城里开始修缮，所以京城中有许多吃饱饭的机会，那些灾民们便不肯走了。
他们白日进城做工，晚上回棚子睡觉。京城重建需要人手，官员们不会驱赶他们。
胤礽道：“你不是早听教书的师傅说过这些事，怎么突然生闷气？”
胤禔闷声道：“看了心情不好。”
胤礽拍了拍胤禔的肩膀：“你这话可不能被其他人听到了，否则肯定会有人借着让你心情好的名义，把这群人全部赶走，那这群人就没活路了，你也会被人说残暴。”
胤禔往胤礽身上一倒：“好复杂，不想思考。”
胤礽失笑。
他笑完之后，再次拉开帘子，看往车窗外。
巍峨的北京城城墙越来越远，面黄肌瘦表情麻木的灾民们依附在城墙下，随着车队的远离缩小成虫蚁。
阳光落下，虫蚁被隐藏在城墙的阴影下，很快便看不见了。
这个时代啊。
胤礽突然觉得，自己纠结于前世亲情的可怜模样很是矫情。
这么一想，他心中的黑暗淡去了不少，前前世的怨念都被冲散了。
只是冲散前前世怨念的是更强烈更沉重的感情，让他胤礽的心情更不好了。
这些感情只有胤礽独自品味，这个时代的任何人都无法听胤礽述说，都无法理解胤礽的痛苦。
他只能自己勉强将感情封锁，把注意力转移到沿路景色上。
胤礽描述着路途中的景象，偶尔还引用一两句诗句。
胤禔还是个小孩子，很快就被景色吸引，重新恢复兴致勃勃。
两人一路笑闹，到巩华城的时候已经过了午膳时间。
他们在马车上用了许多点心肉干，现在并不觉得饿，先去殡宫前上香。
胤礽目视着殡宫深处，那里停放着他额娘的梓宫。
胤禔静静地陪着胤礽，见胤礽久久不动弹，才小声道：“弟弟，你想哭就哭吧，哥哥陪着你。”
胤礽摇摇头。
他对额娘的思念，上上辈子的几十年已经耗尽，现在想起来，只是怅然。
他上上辈子想过念过也恨过，在死亡之前更深深地怕过。
胤礽不敢死，怕在地底下见到仁孝皇后，仁孝皇后也说出和康熙同样的话。
生而克母。
胤礽闭上眼。
上上辈子的太子生涯就这样过去吧，好不好？
胤礽脑海里又浮现胤禔赏赐馄饨的路边乞丐，想起城墙下缩在阴影中的“蝼蚁”。
翻腾的不甘被更深的不甘压下，胤礽拍了拍自己的心脏处，咧嘴笑了笑，道：“大哥，别担心，我没事。”
“好，好，你没事。”胤禔把胤礽抱怀里，轻轻拍了拍，“不哭也好，免得皇额娘担心。”
胤礽蹭了蹭胤禔：“嗯。额娘看到大哥陪着我，肯定不担心。”
当晚，胤礽做了一个梦。
他那两辈子都无缘见面的额娘露出了脸，脸居然和他在现代社会的母亲一样，搞得胤礽十分混乱，不知道是该道歉自己让仁孝皇后难产，还是该道歉见义勇为的时候英年早逝。
听着他胡乱的道歉，他的母亲只露出一个无奈的笑，然后给了他一个虚无缥缈的拥抱。
没有温度，没有触感，但能让人的心立刻静下来的拥抱。
胤礽似乎还听到耳边有人说，过去了就过去了，人要往前看。
往前看，是做一个嚣张的穿越者的意思吗？
胤礽醒来时，盘着小短腿陷入沉思。
额娘是这个意思吗？她是不是认为我穿越一辈子束手束脚，不像她儿子？
如果两辈子的额娘是同一个，那么咱额娘脾气风风火火，可喜欢冒险可喜欢说“为了梦想无所畏惧”了。
嗯，额娘天天鸡娃。
胤禔问道：“弟弟，你愣在那里干什么？今天不是要去逛庙子吗？”
“哦，来啦来啦！”胤礽赶紧起床。
算了，等玩够了再想吧。
皇宫中，康熙听到胤礽在殡宫前呆立了许久，然后扑胤禔怀里无声大哭（胤礽：并没有……），也愣了许久，忍不住落下来泪来。
康熙又听到胤礽哭过之后，性格活泼不少，和胤禔一起调皮捣蛋，去找驻军的麻烦，揪出几个吃空饷的人，无奈扶额：“他们俩没受伤吧？这种事告知朕就行，哪还需要他们亲自出面？”
报告的侍卫道：“大阿哥先冲上去，太子便也挥舞着小皮鞭冲上去了。”
显然，侍卫是站在太子这一边的。
因为大阿哥实在是太令人头疼了。大阿哥居然挨个找侍卫打架切磋？！我们能和八岁的小孩切磋吗！！
康熙笑不出来了。
他开始让人整理折子，准备熬夜批改奏折，早点去巩华城陪伴两个儿子，免得宝贝儿子被大儿子带坏。
寝食难安的惠嫔也得到了儿子的消息——康熙可不能自己一个头疼，总要找个人和自己一起吐槽。
惠嫔一边听来人的叙述，一边脑袋越来越歪。
如果这个时代有问号，那么惠嫔的脑袋上一定会有很多小问号。
我儿子……究竟有什么毛病？
惠嫔开始反思，自己生胤禔的时候，是否吃错了什么东西。
“太子殿下……辛苦了。”惠嫔心好累。她想，如果没有太子护着看着拦着，她儿子会变成什么鬼样子。
惠嫔决定，自己要成为坚定不移的太子党。除了太子，谁还能制得住护得住自己那才八岁便如脱缰烈马般的儿子？
如果太子出事，她儿子那傻样肯定是当不了太子。其他皇子当太子，儿子肯定不能活。
惠嫔听完儿子的消息后，又去了小佛堂，为太子念诵祈祷平安经文。
康熙听到惠嫔的反应之后，心气顺了。
看，不是朕一个人在烦恼！
康熙又把这个“好消息”分享给太皇太后。
太皇太后可不烦恼，养孩子是康熙的事。太皇太后笑得前俯后仰，直呼大阿哥和小太子都是她的开心果。
康熙悄悄撇嘴。
自从太皇太后看到顺治降临，彻底不管事之后，就变成了乐子人，专注于看孙儿康熙的笑话。
“朕想把五阿哥送于皇额娘处抚养。”康熙不能让太皇太后继续乐下去。
太皇太后微愣：“为何？佟贵妃养得不好？”
康熙道：“她又要养孩子，又要照顾怀孕的嫔妃，还要处理宫中大小琐事，更憔悴了。”
chapters.translated_text:
Mingzhu said, "Of course, this servant wishes to leave a name in history!"

Yinreng laughed, "No, you haven't thought about it until now. Rongruo thinks about it, but you truly haven't. But you can think about it now. Because you cannot be a powerful minister. Imperial Father will not tolerate the emergence of any powerful minister, not even a powerful prince. Imperial Father will certainly concentrate all power in his own hands, regardless of what kind of power it is."

Mingzhu’s expression was one of great shock.

"I originally didn't intend to give you a hint. But you are truly talented, it would be such a pity." Yinreng sighed.

Who was the most talented minister in the Kangxi era?

When all is said and done, the number of famous civil officials is like a meteor shower across the sky, yet none could compare to Mingzhu and Songgotu in the early Kangxi era.

Mingzhu had an extremely sharp eye; the officials he recommended were almost all capable. Regarding national issues such as suppressing the Three Feudatories, taking Taiwan, and resisting Tsarist Russia, he was a staunch hawk and a radical. If Yinreng wants to force his Imperial Father to point his sword at the world, people like Mingzhu are indispensable.

Although Songgotu didn't have much of a concept of national territory and was like a lazy frog that only moved when poked, whether it was capturing Oboi or his later contributions regarding the Three Feudatories, he was "forced" into it. But as long as he accepted a job, he could do it perfectly. Coordinating the overall situation, stabilizing the rear, and deploying military supplies all relied on Songgotu's command.

In gaming terms, Mingzhu had a wallhack, and Songgotu had a maphack.

If the two didn't hold each other back but instead exerted effort together, Kangxi was almost invincible.

Yinreng truly couldn't bear to lose such talent.

Without Mingzhu and Songgotu, how difficult would it be for Kangxi to cultivate talent for global conquest from scratch?

An emperor’s period of ambition only lasts about ten or twenty years. Once Kangxi entered his fifties, even if his subjective desire was to be diligent, objective circumstances would not allow it; slackness and negligence would be inevitable.

Yinreng hoped Kangxi would become a true emperor for the ages, but time was tight. Once Kangxi grew old, he could no longer court death, but would have to lie low and find an opportunity to resign from the position of Crown Prince.

"Alright, stop kneeling. If you don't go back to reading, the people outside will come in... Sigh, Big Brother, why are you here? When did you arrive?" Yinreng was startled.

Yinzhi didn't know where he had popped out from: "I came when Mingzhu knelt down."

Yinzhi rubbed Yinreng’s head: "Be careful, the eunuchs outside have been peering in for a long time. You finally managed to catch a breath coming here; what if you get sent back to the palace?"

Yinreng hugged Yinzhi and rubbed against him: "Okay." Sigh, whenever he starts thinking about pointing his sword at the world, he can't help but want to court death.

It’s fine, it’s fine, he’s still just a child, Father won't overthink it. When Father starts overthinking, he’ll just resign from the Crown Prince position.

Let’s make more contributions to the Great Qing; when the time comes to resign, he’ll trade those merits for a large hot spring estate.

Yinreng found an excuse for his death-courting behavior, refusing to admit that he simply couldn't sit still.

Yinzhi patted Yinreng’s head again and said to Mingzhu: "Do not let down the Crown Prince’s hint, which he gave at great personal risk."

What risk? Mingzhu frowned in thought, remembering the eunuchs Yinreng and Yinzhi had mentioned, and he gasped.

He should have understood sooner; the people around the Crown Prince would certainly report every detail of the Crown Prince’s affairs to the Emperor. The Crown Prince had many miraculous rumors surrounding him and was overly precocious; perhaps the Emperor protected the Crown Prince even more tightly.

Yinreng patted the table with his little paw—it lacked any imposing aura, yet it still struck a chord with everyone.

Agree quickly!

The man must be deeply affectionate and have no regrets; the woman must be resilient and unyielding; the two must be in perfect harmony, being both lovers and soulmates, and no other man or woman could interfere.

The Tang Dynasty poet Luo Binwang once had a famous line in "On Behalf of the Taoist Nun Wang Lingfei to the Taoist Li Rong": "Cherishing and missing, twice as close; a pair for a lifetime."

This "Hua Tang Chun" used Luo Binwang's famous line as an opening, just as Li Qingzhao used Ouyang Xiu's "The courtyard is deep, how deep is it?" to pay tribute to predecessors and introduce another classic poem.

Just for this poem alone, this play was worth watching!

After the old actor finished singing, the stage setting changed, starting from the youth of the male and female protagonists.

The woman was a princess of a former dynasty's prince's mansion, innocent and lively; the man was just a small guard, gazing foolishly at the woman's back.

He worked hard, hoping to catch the eye of the mansion and marry his beloved.

Until the mansion plotted rebellion, the whole family was demoted to commoners, and the golden-leafed princess was about to face a withering end, he defiantly ignored his family's opposition and came to propose marriage.

Afterward, the man's career was hindered, and the woman wept because of her family's and husband's plight. The two comforted each other and weathered the difficulties together; you read, I grind the ink—there was bitterness and sweetness in between.

Kangxi laughed while rubbing his eyes, not knowing if he was moved or had laughed too much, and grabbed another handful of copper coins to scatter: "Good!"

Yinreng's mouth twitched.

He looked at the copper coins, silver fragments, and cloth flowers scattered all over the stage; this tipping was simply too crazy.

Who said chasing stars is exclusive to modern people? When ancient people chase stars, this madness isn't necessarily less than that of modern people.

Fuquan and Changning were also old theater fans. The two didn't know who the story was about, only listening with fascination, and when the mood struck, they would follow along and sing a few lines.

Yinzhi had seen the rehearsals many times and thought it would be boring. Who knew that with the people around cheering, listening to the play felt a bit fresher.

Yinreng watched his big brother, at such a young age, also shaking his head along with the adults, calling it good, and scattering handfuls of copper coins, already showing the prototype of a playboy. He couldn't help but feel a sharp pain in his heart and pinched the back of Kangxi's hand hard.

Kangxi wanted to knock Yinreng's head with his fan, but halfway there, remembering that his son's head couldn't be knocked, he changed it to knocking his son's shoulder: "Why pinch me?"

Yinreng said: "Father, take it easy, don't teach the big brother bad habits."

Kangxi laughed: "You're so young, why are you so old-fashioned and serious? Come."

Kangxi stuffed a handful of copper coins into Yinreng's hand: "Scatter."

Yinreng: "...I won't."

Kangxi picked up Yinreng and placed him on the theater railing: "Quick, or I won't let you down."

Yinreng's mouth pouted; this father is beyond saving, he only knows how to teach children bad things.

He helplessly scattered the money, but the force was too small; it didn't land on the stage but on the head of an old man downstairs.

The old man touched his head, looked up and saw a child being held on the railing by an unreliable adult, and couldn't help but blow his beard and stare, glaring at Kangxi.

Kangxi noticed the old man, his face darkened: "Why is he here?!"

Yinreng was curious: "Who is he?"

Kangxi gritted his teeth: "Gu, Yan, Wu!"

The name sounded familiar. Yinreng thought for a long time, then pounded his small fist into his palm: "Oh, it's him, the remnant of the former dynasty, Gu Yanwu."

Kangxi snorted heavily: "Hmph!"

Who is Gu Yanwu? The four words "remnant of the former dynasty" are enough to summarize him.

Gu Yanwu and Gu Zhenguan's ancestor, Master Donglin Gu Xiancheng, although both came from the prominent Gu family of Jiangdong, were probably just related by the fact that they both had the surname Gu in the same province.

Gu Yanwu and Gu Xiancheng were not only from different eras but also belonged to different schools of thought; if they met, they would definitely fight until their dog brains came out.

Compared to Gu Xiancheng, Gu Yanwu was better known to later generations, evaluated as one of the four great enlightenment thinkers of the late Ming and early Qing dynasties.

With the change of dynasties, the situation gradually stabilized, and ordinary people had gradually become accustomed to living in the new dynasty; it was difficult to stir up chaos again.

At this time, some old people of the former dynasty did not stop their descendants from integrating into this new dynasty, allowing their offspring to continue living, while they themselves resolutely refused to serve as officials, spending their lives as remnants of the former dynasty.

Gu Yanwu was one of them.

Kangxi deeply admired his scholarship and also deeply admired his character; the more he respected him, the more annoyed he was by him.

But after this annoyance, he admired Gu Yanwu even more.

The two feelings mixed, making Kangxi lose the mood to watch the play.

Yinreng was excited: "Father! I want to go play with him!"

Kangxi rolled his eyes at his son: "Don't even think about it, he won't serve as an official."

"I didn't want him to serve as an official, I just wanted to ask some questions." Yinreng twisted and turned, broke free from his arms, and jumped to the ground, "Brother, come with me!"

Yinzhi said: "Good. There are many people, hold my hand tightly."

Kangxi gave both sons a flick on the forehead. The one for Yinreng landed in mid-air and hit Yinreng's back.

"You're so small, who can you protect?" Kangxi said irritably, "I'll take you there."

Yinreng asked: "Is Third Brother going?"

Yinzhi yawned: "No, sleeping."

After saying that, he turned over and continued to sleep in Changning's arms, who was at a loss.

For a child as young as Yinzhi, the play was meaningless, and even if people were noisy, it was very hypnotic.

Fuquan asked: "Should I go too?"

Kangxi thought for a moment and stuffed the eldest son's hand back into Fuquan's hand: "No need, you stay upstairs with the eldest, Baocheng and I will go."

Yinzhi was dissatisfied: "Why? I want to go too."

Kangxi said: "You have a bad temper, I'm afraid you'll offend the old man."

Yinzhi snorted and agreed.

He had self-awareness. If that old man dared to be disrespectful to his brother, he would not only offend him, but also use all his strength to crash into him.

Kangxi tidied his clothes and then looked at his son, who was a yellow chick today, feeling a bit hesitant.

If he went to see Gu Yanwu like this, would he be criticized by Gu Yanwu for being improper?

"Father, let's go." The chick Yinreng urged Kangxi, "If you don't go, I'm going alone."

"Not allowed." Kangxi picked up the chick son and bit the bullet as he went downstairs.

He couldn't call Gu Yanwu into the palace. If he forced Gu Yanwu, that guy would definitely go and hit a pillar. This stubborn old man wasn't like those fame-seeking censors in the court; although he lived comfortably and didn't seek death, he really wasn't afraid of death.

Kangxi cared about his face; if the other party wouldn't come to him, he wasn't willing to do any "three visits to the thatched cottage" thing. Besides, Gu Yanwu was already old, and he wouldn't be of use for many years, so there was no need to lower himself.

But since they happened to meet, Kangxi really wanted to show off his son in front of Gu Yanwu.

My son, the Crown Prince of the Great Qing, is so excellent! Hurry up and praise him!

Compared to the dark former Ming, my Great Qing has such a Crown Prince, it must have a brighter future; regret it, you stubborn old man!

Gu Yanwu didn't recognize Kangxi.

He saw the chick upstairs coming and thought the chick was coming to apologize, so he waved his hand and said: "It doesn't matter, but don't hold the child so high, it's dangerous."

"Old sir, can we have a private talk?" The chick Yinreng jumped down from Kangxi's arms, put his little wings on Gu Yanwu's knees, and whispered in Gu Yanwu's ear, "Secretly tell you, actually I am the Crown Prince."

Gu Yanwu was serious in his studies but extremely kind to ordinary children.

When the chick Yinreng ran over, he hunched his body and cooperated by lowering his head.

Hearing this, Gu Yanwu's eyes moved, and he looked up at Kangxi.

Kangxi was a bit nervous and gave Gu Yanwu a disdainful look with a straight face.

Gu Yanwu laughed: "Good."

51. Three chapters in one [V]

Gu Yanwu's experience among the remnants of the former Ming can be considered unique.

He spent the first half of his life moving around for the Southern Ming court, suffered many imprisonments in his middle age, and refused the court's summons many times in his later years.

But he was not completely isolated from the Great Qing court.

Many people influenced by Gu Yanwu were officials in the court; Gu Yanwu's nephew, Xu Qianxue, was a top scholar during the Kangxi era and is now attached to the Nalan family, and will later become the Minister of Justice.

After Gu Yanwu arrived in the capital, he had dealings with many Han officials in the court.

Gu Yanwu's code of conduct was very clear. He hoped to use his scholarship to influence the current Great Qing court, but he was unwilling to serve as an official.

Those who study the classics in the Kangxi court now all take Gu Yanwu as their teacher, and Kangxi had long heard of Gu Yanwu's great name.

Gu Yanwu didn't recognize Kangxi, but Kangxi had not only seen Gu Yanwu's portrait but had also secretly observed Gu Yanwu during his incognito visits.

Oh, when Kangxi secretly observed Gu Yanwu, Mingzhu was by Kangxi's side.

So Kangxi doing such a thing must be Mingzhu's fault.

The person behind this theater was the Imperial Palace, one of the strongholds for Kangxi to collect information.

Kangxi wanted a private room, and no matter how busy the theater was, he could have one.

The private room they were in could still see and hear the people singing downstairs; the thin old man Gu Yanwu looked relaxed, and his eyes kept glancing at the stage, as if the play was more attractive to him than Kangxi.

Kangxi was so angry he wanted to flick his sleeves and leave.

Yinreng pulled Kangxi's sleeve, spread his wings, and walked to Gu Yanwu's side: "It's troublesome to talk to you while looking up, hug me."

Gu Yanwu was stunned for a moment.

He looked down and met the eyes of the innocent little Crown Prince, and finally, there was a bit of helplessness on his face.

Yinreng didn't care about Gu Yanwu's daze; he lifted his short legs and climbed onto Gu Yanwu's knees.

Gu Yanwu stiffly let Yinreng climb onto his knees and lean into his arms, and he even let out a long sigh, looking at Kangxi in disbelief.

Kangxi held back a laugh: "Baocheng has been spoiled by me, please forgive me, old sir."

Yinreng pulled Gu Yanwu's two arms to protect himself and looked up: "No need to forgive. No one can dislike Baocheng, right?"

Gu Yanwu: "..." This child is dressed strangely, how can I not say words of refusal to him?

Kangxi relaxed and said: "Baocheng, don't you have something to say to the old sir?"

Kangxi pretended to be unwilling to talk to Gu Yanwu; it was his son who insisted on coming, so he came.

Yinreng watched Kangxi start acting and was speechless.

Father, you clearly want to talk to the old sir very much, why use me as a cover? Are you sure I can discuss the classics with the old sir?

Oh, you really have taught me. Headache.

Yinreng sighed and said: "Mr. Gu, is the sage invincible?"

Gu Yanwu was prepared, but he didn't expect Yinreng to ask this: "Of course."

Yinreng counted on his fingers: "But the sage's disciples cannot be stronger than the sage, the sage's disciples' disciples cannot be stronger than the sage's disciples... each generation is weaker than the last, otherwise it is disrespectful to the sage. Then aren't scholars becoming more and more useless?"

Gu Yanwu: "..."

Kangxi was thoughtful.

Yinreng added: "If you have a son, do you hope your son is not as good as you, and your grandson is not as good as your son?"

Gu Yanwu sighed: "Naturally not."

"Xunzi said in 'Exhortation to Learning', 'Blue comes from the indigo plant but is bluer than the indigo plant; ice is made from water but is colder than water.' Confucius also said, 'In a group of three, there must be my teacher.' It can be seen that the sages also do not hope for this." Yinreng swung his short legs, "Is the classic we know now really the original meaning of the sage?"

Gu Yanwu said: "Who knows."

Yinreng said: "Mr. Gu pioneered 'Puxue' (evidential research) and re-examined the classics; did you also think of this problem?"

Gu Yanwu smiled without saying a word.

Yinreng looked up at the ceiling: "Mr. Gu, I know you have a deep blood feud with the Great Qing. The Kunshan Massacre is a scar in your heart that will never heal."

Kangxi's expression moved slightly.

Silly child, what are you saying! You are still in his arms! Aren't you afraid he will stab you directly!

Gu Yanwu still smiled, as if what was in his arms was not the Crown Prince of the Great Qing, and the person in front of him was not the Emperor of the Great Qing.

"But you still appear in the capital now, and you are still willing to solve puzzles for the Han officials who are officials in the court." Yinreng said, "Because Mr. Gu sees that the change of dynasties is inevitable, and the common people have ushered in a brief respite. If the Great Qing can be like other dynasties on the land of China, even if its establishment was full of bloodshed, it is a good thing for the common people."

"'When it rises, the people suffer; when it falls, the people suffer.' The fall of the former Ming is irreversible; looking forward is the good thing for the people. So Mr. Gu exhausted his efforts for the Southern Ming, but refused to contribute to the rebellious Three Feudatories. Manchu-Han integration, making the Great Qing Emperor the emperor of the entire China, and letting the blood and culture of China continue in the Great Qing is what you are doing now."

"For this, you deeply loathe the Great Qing, yet you are still cultivating talent for the Great Qing."

Yinreng jumped down from Gu Yanwu's knees, put his two chicken wings together, and bowed to Gu Yanwu: "Sir, your righteousness is high."

Kangxi's pupils shook.

Is, is it like this?! So that's what Gu Yanwu thinks?!

Kangxi put himself in his shoes; if his whole family died under the swords of the Qing army, could he cultivate talent for the Great Qing?

Get lost! It would be an irreconcilable feud!

He closed his eyes, sighed deeply, walked to his son's side, and also bowed: "Sir, your righteousness is high."

Yinreng was shocked; he glanced at Kangxi from the corner of his eye. Is this still his father? His father would do such a thing?!

Kangxi remained in a bowing posture, motionless.

The mask-like smile on Gu Yanwu's face finally loosened.

He put away his smile, looked at the most noble father and son of the Great Qing bowing to him, and did not move for a long time.

Kangxi and Yinreng maintained the bowing posture and did not move for a long time either.

"Sigh." Gu Yanwu said, "Emperor, Crown Prince, do you know, I wish all the Qing imperial clan would die."

Kangxi first took a step across to protect Yinreng behind him before saying: "If I were in your place, sir, I would be the same."

Kangxi was not an emperor who grew up in the military; he was an emperor of a peaceful era.

At least for now, he really had a benevolent heart.

Yinreng was not wrong; the times had changed.

Gu Yanwu was silent for a long time again and said: "Will you become a good emperor?"

Kangxi said: "I promise here that I will definitely become a good emperor."

Gu Yanwu wanted to force a smile.

Just now he could keep smiling, but now he couldn't smile.

He was already very old, but now he didn't even have any spirit, as if he had become an old man who had completely stepped half a foot into the coffin; time and suffering had completely crushed his spine.

But Kangxi knew, Yinreng knew, this was just an illusion.

The sickly old man in front of him was still writing books and teaching people until the moment of his death.

Yinreng knew even better that the Han officials who could rank in the Qing Dynasty in later generations had almost all studied his works and been influenced by his thoughts.

He never served as an official for the Qing Dynasty in his life, but his disciples and grandchildren supported the only remaining spine of the Qing Dynasty scholars until the Qing Dynasty fell.

He deeply hated the Qing Dynasty, but the long-term stability of the Qing Dynasty had his indelible contribution.

Other enlightenment thinkers in the early Qing Dynasty were not as "contradictory" in their actions as Gu Yanwu. He was completely different from everyone else.

Gu Yanwu looked up, tears crossing the wrinkles at the corners of his eyes, but they didn't fall.

He cried silently; Kangxi protected the child with one hand and clenched his other hand in front of him, his eyes also a little red.

People are not made of grass or wood, who can be without emotion? Even an emperor has times when he is moved by someone or something.

Yinreng held Kangxi's sleeve, feeling very uncomfortable in his heart.

He regretted a little; should he not have come to see Gu Yanwu?

But he wanted to come to see Gu Yanwu.

To see the only great Confucian in the late feudal era who had stepped half a foot into the realm of a semi-sage, a great Confucian who truly inherited the way of Confucius and Mencius.

A great Confucian who made the Qing emperors feel deeply frustrated, but was given a separate biography in the "Draft History of Qing".

Gu Yanwu, a man's name, a tree's shadow.

"My father and I... my father and I will not force Mr. Gu to serve as an official, we only hope that Mr. Gu's works can be given to my father and me as soon as possible. No matter what works." Yinreng poked his little chicken-crest head out from behind Kangxi.

Gu Yanwu did not wipe his tears.

His tears dried quickly, as if he had never shed them.

After Gu Yanwu saw Yinreng's little chicken-crest head, a smile finally appeared on his face again.

He beckoned to Yinreng.

Yinreng let go of Kangxi's sleeve, drilled out from under the arm Kangxi was using to protect him, and threw himself in front of Gu Yanwu's knees, looking up at Gu Yanwu like a child receiving guidance from his grandfather.

Kangxi didn't stop Yinreng, clenched his fists, and sighed deeply.

"Good." Gu Yanwu rubbed Yinreng's chicken-crest hair, "I'll give them all to you."

Yinreng said seriously: "Also, Mr. Gu, your nephew is a corrupt official, did you know?" Yinreng thought Gu Yanwu's nephew had deceived Gu Yanwu.

Gu Yanwu smiled: "I know. This officialdom is just like this; if you're not corrupt, you can't fit in. Didn't your father teach you?"

Yinreng snorted like a little pig. The teacher actually knew!

Kangxi clenched his fists and coughed dryly at his mouth: "Official administration... I will find a way to deal with the official administration."

Gu Yanwu said sarcastically: "Can you control those Manchus? They still carry the barbarism brought from outside the pass in their bones; they never thought about becoming real officials of this land."

Yinreng let out an "ah" and said: "Mr. Gu said exactly the same thing as me! I told my father! And my father beat me!"

Gu Yanwu hurriedly protected Yinreng and glared at Kangxi.

Kangxi: "..." Mr. Gu, open your eyes and look, the one in front of you is also a Manchu child, also a Manchu! Don't treat me as a bad person and him as a good person! I am his father! If we're bad, we're bad together!

Gu Yanwu gently patted Yinreng's head, as if dusting off the dust on Yinreng's head: "Was it you who predicted the earthquake?"

Kangxi was shocked: "How did Mr. Gu know!"

Gu Yanwu said: "To get something, you have to pay something. He is seriously ill, you are not."

Kangxi: "..." What a simple and crude judgment.

Gu Yanwu stared at Yinreng.

After he guessed the existence of Yinreng, he almost vomited blood, his heart and mind in great pain.

Confucianism believes in the unity of heaven and man. When an orthodox dynasty is established, after the founding emperor, there will always be one or two generations of emperors who seem to have the help of gods. This is proof that heaven recognizes this dynasty.

A dynasty with such an emperor will mostly last for at least a hundred years.

Is the Qing Dynasty actually one of them too!

Has heaven already recognized the violent Qing!

Gu Yanwu really wanted to roar at the sky, why is the heaven so unfair.

But he understood rationally that heaven and earth are not benevolent, treating all things as straw dogs. Heaven and earth have no feelings; all things are like the straw dogs used in sacrifices. Heaven and earth will not treat anyone or anything specially, but just act according to certain laws.

Throughout history, as dynasties rose and fell, countless rulers and emperors slaughtered cities and massacred the common people to claim their thrones. Heaven does not punish these emperors or their dynasties for such acts; only the common folk are left to wail in agony.

Neither gods nor the heavens will protect the people; the only ones who can protect the people are the people themselves. Therefore, he cannot fall, he cannot retreat into seclusion; he must leave something behind for the sake of the common masses.

The vitality of the Great Ming has been exhausted, while the Great Qing is in its prime. He cannot defy the heavens to change fate, so he can only enter the game alone to influence this brutal dynasty.

Gu Yanwu saw this clearly from the moment he entered the capital.

After the earthquake, Gu Yanwu completely lost the last remaining sliver of hope for overthrowing the Qing and restoring the Ming.

He looked at the child before him, who was favored by the gods. If he could become emperor, perhaps the people would live well.

Even places like Kunshan, Yangzhou, and Jiading would surely regain their prosperity.

Gu Yanwu suddenly remembered that those places had, in fact, already slowly begun to recover their prosperity.

Many people had already forgotten the Great Ming. They had already accepted themselves as subjects of the Great Qing.

How pathetic, how truly pathetic.

"The remnants still have one person left; the remnants have only one person left."

Gu Yanwu took Yinreng back onto his lap and began to speak to him about his own thoughts and insights.

Kangxi, having been ignored, rubbed his nose, pulled up a chair to sit beside Gu Yanwu, and had Zhao Chang fetch brush, ink, paper, and an inkstone, taking notes while eavesdropping.

Gu Yanwu’s words were plain and straightforward, striving to make them understandable even to a child.

Yinreng could not only understand them but could also ask questions and offer his own insights.

The old man and the young boy talked for a long time, until their throats were dry, until the play ended and the crowds dispersed, and the evening lanterns were lit.

It was impossible to convey the life’s work of Gu Yanwu in a few hours, but he would only share these few hours with Yinreng.

For these few hours, for the sake of the common people, he served temporarily as a teacher to the Crown Prince, as a teacher to an emperor.

Once he stepped out of this door, he would once again be Gu Yanwu, a remnant of the Ming, a lonely old man with a blood feud against the Qing Dynasty.

In his *Rizhilu* (Record of Daily Knowledge), Gu Yanwu wrote, "Changing the surname and title of the state is called the fall of a nation; when benevolence and righteousness are so blocked that beasts are led to eat men, and men begin to eat each other, that is called the fall of the world... Protecting the nation is the duty of the ruler, his ministers, and those who eat the meat of the state; protecting the world is a duty in which even the lowliest commoner has a share!"

He had spent most of his life running about to "protect the nation," but now, his actions were for the sake of "protecting the world."

By entering the capital, befriending civil officials, and allowing his descendants and students to take office, he was attempting to influence the Great Qing—a dynasty where "benevolence and righteousness are blocked to the point of beasts eating men"—into a dynasty where people could survive.

For the sake of "protecting the world," he betrayed his own heart and his own deep-seated blood feud.

Gu Yanwu’s voice grew hoarse.

He did not drink the water Kangxi personally offered, but merely moistened his throat and mouth with his own saliva, continuing to instruct Yinreng.

Finally, he spoke of the study of managing wealth, a subject many Confucian scholars were not adept at, or even despised.

Gu Yanwu was skilled in managing wealth.

His family wealth had been seized by powerful local bullies, and he had been hunted and forced to flee everywhere; he had even been thrown into prison, leaving with nothing. Yet, wherever he went, he would reclaim land, buy property, and when he left, he would hand these assets over to his followers, abandoning the wealth. Upon arriving at the next place, he would continue to earn money and acquire property.

Almost everyone with his experiences ended up in poverty, yet he rarely faced financial hardship.

When his nephew Xu Qianxue and others, who were officials in the capital, borrowed thousands of taels of silver from Gu Yanwu to grease the wheels of the court, Gu Yanwu couldn't even be bothered to ask for it back, which shows just how wealthy he was.

If Gu Yanwu could be persuaded to take office, and Kangxi gave him the Ministry of Revenue, Gu Yanwu could probably double the silver in the national treasury.

Alas, alas, it was impossible for Gu Yanwu to take office; it would never be possible.

Kangxi felt regret, and even more loathing for Dorgon and Dodo.

Just because you weren't the ones sitting on the throne, did that mean you could do whatever you wanted? You treated the words of my ancestor, the Emperor of the Ages, as wind in your ears!

Kangxi thought about his ancestor’s age at that time, and his face darkened slightly.

Well, it was impossible for them not to treat it as wind. It was just like how Oboi would never listen to me.

Gu Yanwu pushed himself to endure, finally finishing the gist of what he wanted to say.

Just the gist, just the outline. For the rest, Yinreng could read books and learn on his own.

Gu Yanwu would not hoard his knowledge. His works were meant to be made public for everyone to see; if the Emperor and the Crown Prince wanted to read them, they naturally could.

Kangxi offered tea again, and Gu Yanwu refused it again.

He returned Yinreng to Kangxi, then walked out the door, swaying, his steps heavy and uneven.

Kangxi ordered people to secretly follow Gu Yanwu to ensure he returned home safely.

Yinreng held onto Kangxi’s neck, and the father and son returned to the palace in silence.

That night, Kangxi did not go to the inner palace.

He held his son, sighing repeatedly.

In this Great Qing, could there ever be a second Gu Yanwu? It would be very difficult.

Yinreng rubbed against Kangxi: "Father, you work hard, you can become the second Gu Yanwu!"

Kangxi: "???"

He pinched his son’s cheek: "You are the one who needs to work hard!"

Yinreng turned over, his back to Kangxi: "I don't want to. I'm still young. Father, have you heard a saying?"

Kangxi turned Yinreng back around to face him: "You’re quite arrogant, daring to turn your back on your father. Speak, what saying?"

Yinreng said, word by word: "Extreme wisdom brings harm."

Kangxi held his son tighter: "Who said that? You are not allowed to say such things. Go to sleep, do you still want to sleep or not?"

Yinreng: "Oh."

The eunuch blew out the candles.

After a long while, Kangxi’s voice sounded in the darkness: "Who exactly said that?"

Yinreng: "Of course it was the Imperial Grandfather. The second half of the sentence is 'deep affection does not last long'." (It was Jin Yong.)

Kangxi: "Oh." It must have been that fake monk Yulin Tongxiu who said it.

It’s fine, that saying must not be true. Kangxi consoled himself.

...

After meeting Kangxi and Yinreng, Gu Yanwu packed his luggage and left the capital for home the next day.

He returned to Kunshan, became a farmer again, and focused on his writing.

Kangxi ordered the local officials to take good care of him. This order made Kangxi aware that the Gu family’s property had been seized by the powerful Ye family of Kunshan, and that the Ye family had even hunted Gu Yanwu.

He sighed and summoned Ye Fang'ai, who was of the same clan as the Ye family of Kunshan, and ordered him to return home to handle the matter.

Ye Fang'ai was an honest official and had recommended Gu Yanwu many times. Yet the Ye family were the local bullies who had seized the Gu family’s property and hunted Gu Yanwu.

Kangxi remembered the lessons Shunzhi had given him in the tent in front of the Qianqing Palace.

When an official is honest, one must also look at the family behind him, his teachers, and the local bullies in his hometown to see if he is truly a good official.

Kangxi collected the works of other famous Ming remnants. After reading them, he sighed: "There are similar ideas abroad."

Yinreng knew what kind of ideas Kangxi was talking about.

They were beginning to doubt the correctness of the monarchical system and were beginning to try to explore a system more suitable for China.

Kangxi was very worried, even having thoughts of burning the books.

Yinreng laughed: "Isn't this a good thing?"

Kangxi rarely tapped Yinreng on the head: "How can you call that a good thing?"

Yinreng covered his head and said: "For an idea to become reality, it takes at least two or three hundred years. By then, our Great Qing will definitely be gone."

Kangxi: "...Don't talk nonsense."

Yinreng climbed onto Kangxi’s lap: "Father, why are we talking about such abstract things? With your guidance, the Great Qing can probably prosper for one or two hundred years, but after that, it will definitely go downhill; two or three hundred years is about right. The last hundred years will definitely be in a half-dead state."

Kangxi wanted to spank his son. The facts might be so, but how could his own family be so lacking in ambition!

"Two or three hundred years, that's not bad." Kangxi was actually quite lacking in ambition himself. There were plenty of short-lived dynasties, not to mention the Great Qing was "congenitally deficient."

The facts were indeed so.

If the Great Qing hadn't become a semi-colony to extend its life, with external conflicts suppressing internal ones from erupting, the Great Qing would have been gone long ago.

A semi-colonial, semi-feudal society was a century-long catastrophe for China, but for the Great Qing, it was a life-extending medicine.

"By the time these ideas mature, our Great Qing will be gone anyway. That’s perfect, no more emperors afterward." Yinreng said with a grin, "What we can't have, we can't let others have either. After the Great Qing, there won't be any emperors on this land!"

Kangxi: "..." You can think like that? Baocheng, how is your head wired!

Yinreng hung onto Kangxi’s neck and swayed: "The affairs of descendants are for the descendants to worry about; Father and I just need to leave our names in history. We allow these ideas; when the era changes, will we become saints? Being an emperor, yet reflecting on the flaws of imperial power—hehe, if that’s not a saint, what is?"

Kangxi laughed: "Isn't this setting up our descendants?"

Yinreng shook his head: "Can't set them up. Our China has had emperors for thousands of years; unless it truly reaches a point where it must change, the emperor will absolutely not disappear. By that time, nothing we do now will be able to stop it."

Kangxi sighed: "Can't there be a way for our Aisin Gioro family to be emperors forever?"

Yinreng said: "There is, the neighboring Wa country (Japan) is one."

Kangxi remembered the Emperor of Wa and his handsome face darkened: "Let's forget about that."

The more Kangxi thought, the more annoyed he became. At the same time, he felt foolish for worrying about things two or three hundred years in the future, which made him even more annoyed.

When the Emperor was annoyed, he wanted to torment people, and Mingju and the others suffered.

Kangxi called Mingju, Songgotu, Tong Guogang, and others together to watch a play and asked them for their thoughts.

Mingju: "It has nothing to do with me!" As long as I don't admit it, it has nothing to do with me!

When Mingju saw the complete play, he was stunned.

This play, written in the Nalan mansion, right under his nose, actually had him as the protagonist?

And the poems and songs in it were actually written by his son?

Nalan Xingde! Family discipline awaits!

Now, every time Mingju went out to attend court and work, people would look at him with admiration or curiosity, and even acquaintances would come over, pat him on the shoulder, and say with a strange smile, "We all understand the deep affection between you and your wife. If anyone dares to speak ill of you, tell me, and I will help you impeach them."

Mingju’s mouth twitched.

No, that play has nothing to do with me! Nothing at all! That is a story from the previous dynasty; what does it have to do with Nalan Mingju of the Great Qing!

Tong Guogang glanced at Mingju with resentment: "It’s quite good."

Although this play exposed some of Mingju’s laughable habits—like liking to secretly follow his wife and worry, like acting dignified in front of people but being more sentimental and dramatic than his son Rongruo behind their backs, like being so fond of books that whenever he saw one he hadn't read, he would get excited and chatter on to his wife for ages...

These little habits were nothing, but knowing the prototype was Mingju made it particularly shocking, making people want to exclaim, "Mingju, you are actually this kind of person!"

But the play was generally praising Mingju, praising him!

And what about me? I was written as a big scumbag and a big villain. Where do I put my face? I never did these things! I never spoke ill of Mingju and his wife!

But Tong Guogang could not defend himself. He could only hold his head high and adopt an attitude of "the innocent need no explanation"; if he tried to defend himself, it would only draw more attention.

Who did this! I want to beat him to death!

Was it you! Erlendai!

Erlendai: Yes, it was me, so what!

Tong Guogang clutched his chest, wishing he could go before Kangxi and howl, "Please execute this son!"

Songgotu scratched his head: "Your Majesty, the rival of Mingju in the play wouldn't be me, would it? It definitely isn't me. Although I disdain gossiping about his domestic affairs, if someone spoke ill of him, I would definitely just laugh along, not defend him."

Kangxi rolled his eyes at Songgotu: "You certainly have self-awareness."

Songgotu laughed: "The play beautifies me so much, I’m a bit embarrassed. Who wrote these plays?"

Kangxi smiled enigmatically: "I presided over the writing."

Songgotu’s smile cracked.

Mingju’s figure swayed, about to collapse.

Tong Guogang had already collapsed. He knelt on the ground, unable to speak for a long time.

Kangxi had someone help Tong Guogang up: "I know you were wronged; this material was provided by your son."

Tong Guogang couldn't catch his breath, his vision went black, and he almost fainted.

He knew it!

Kangxi tapped the table with his fan, telling the three to sit down: "I intend to use plays to promote some things; Mingju’s story is just an attempt. The common people demonize the Manchus, and the deep affection between Mingju and his wife is very suitable for promotion. As for the rivals and enemies, that’s just for the sake of dramatic conflict; you don't need to mind."

Songgotu and Tong Guogang shouted in their hearts: Your Majesty, if you don't mind, write about yourself!

But they didn't dare to shout it out, and could only say with tears: "Yes, Your Majesty, we don't mind."

Mingju suddenly calmed down.

Although it was annoying to have his private affairs gossiped about, he was at least a positive character. Compared to Songgotu, who was forced to sympathize with him, and Tong Guogang, whose reputation was smeared by his own son, it was much better.

Happiness comes from comparison; Mingju was at peace.

When I get home, I’m beating my son! Using your father and mother’s affairs to write a play, why didn't you write about yourself!

"This play is over; for the next matters, you must pay close attention." Kangxi didn't just want to make fun of them this time; he wanted them to work.

It was fine for those young people to do things among the commoners, but the overall coordination of the theater troupes coming to the capital had to be handled by these steady and reliable pillars of the court.

Kangxi originally wanted to hand these matters to Han officials, but now he wanted to test the attitude of the Manchu officials.

Songgotu immediately accepted the order without the slightest hesitation, unlike the past when he would grumble for a long time before every order Kangxi gave, which made Kangxi particularly gratified.

Tong Guogang hesitated for a moment, but also quickly accepted the order. The Tong family was deeply influenced by Han culture, and although they always wanted to lean toward the Manchu nobility, Tong Guogang was not stupid; he knew that the Emperor’s trust was the way for the Tong family to survive, so he would not block Kangxi’s orders.

But Mingju, who was best at sensing the Holy Will and showing empathy, was stunned on the spot and didn't react for a long time.

Kangxi looked at Mingju calmly, without prompting him.

Songgotu and Tong Guogang glanced at Mingju with the corners of their eyes, confused as to why Mingju had gone mute at this moment.

After a long while, Mingju finally came to his senses.

He remembered the Crown Prince’s hint to him. The Crown Prince was indeed the one who understood the Emperor best.

Or was it that the Crown Prince’s hint that day was actually the Emperor’s instruction?

When the nobility caused trouble, it was different from when the imperial clan caused trouble. The imperial clan was confident they had troops in their hands, and Kangxi dared not do anything to them; the nobility’s status was merely that of the Emperor’s subjects, and when they caused trouble, they were confident their methods were hidden and Kangxi would not notice.

They secretly accumulated power to oppose the Crown Prince and picked and chose among the princes as if they were choosing goods at a market stall; all of this was hidden behind their loyal expressions, confident that Kangxi was unaware.

What if Kangxi had known about their twists and turns all along, and knew that the reason they opposed the Crown Prince was to weaken imperial power?

Opposing the Crown Prince and weakening imperial power were completely different; the former might be something the Emperor would turn a blind eye to, but the latter was something that would truly cost heads.

Mingju took a deep breath, knelt, and kowtowed: "Your Majesty, please entrust this matter to me. I am willing to step down from all positions and make this my priority!"

Songgotu and Tong Guogang were very surprised.

They couldn't understand Mingju’s reaction! Why was Mingju suddenly so excited?! Had something happened that they didn't know about??

The fan in Kangxi’s hand tapped the table gently—once, twice, three times—ringing in the hearts of the three like a bell.

Kangxi was also wondering why Mingju’s attitude was so excited.

Did Mingju guess that I knew something extremely disadvantageous to him? What was that thing?

The interaction between monarch and subject often involves psychological games. Mingju thought Kangxi knew, and even if Kangxi didn't know, he had to pretend he did.

After a moment of thought, he said: "Then I will trouble you."

Mingju’s shoulders slumped; he thought, just as expected, the Emperor had already moved to kill him.

The Emperor is wise; all his little actions and thoughts were invisible under the Emperor’s keen eyes. In the Emperor’s eyes, someone like him, whom he had personally promoted, doing such things was not only a betrayal of the Emperor but also a betrayal of his benefactor. If it weren't for his son being close to the Crown Prince, I’m afraid...

The Nalan family must cut ties with the nobility and the imperial clan.

Mingju kowtowed heavily: "Thank you, Your Majesty, for your mercy!"

Songgotu and Tong Guogang were still stunned.

What happened, what happened? Did the Emperor and Mingju exchange some telepathic deal right in front of them?

Songgotu looked at Tong Guogang: Did you understand?

Tong Guogang looked at Songgotu: I don't understand, but I am greatly shocked, and a bit heart-palpitating.

"Get up, as long as you understand. The Crown Prince said you have great talent, so I will give you another chance." Kangxi observed Mingju’s expression.

Mingju’s expression was dazed for a moment, then relieved.

The Crown Prince... it was the Crown Prince who pleaded for me.

The Crown Prince knew what I wanted to do, yet he still pleaded for me; how can this child be so foolish?

Mingju choked up: "I have failed the Emperor and the Crown Prince. I will definitely seize this opportunity!"

There was no room left for the Nalan family to waver!

It really did have to do with my good son. Kangxi tapped his palm with his fan, satisfied.

Good, I’ll just ask my son when I get home.

I don't know what my son said to Mingju to scare him like this.

Some of Yinreng’s actions were beyond Kangxi’s control, but after a moment of panic, gratification quickly took the upper hand.

You’re amazing, my son! I’ll praise you well when I get back! You were actually hiding it from Father; were you trying to give Father a surprise!

Kangxi left behind one minister lost in his own imagination and two others who were confused, and returned to the palace in high spirits. He picked up the little lazy pig who was sleeping in, had finished lunch, and was about to sleep in the afternoon: "Baocheng, what did you say to Mingju? He was almost scared to death?"

Yinreng said groggily: "Scared to death?"

Kangxi took a wet towel from the eunuch to wipe Yinreng’s face and told him about today’s events.

Yinreng shuddered.

Mingju, you’ve ruined me! You actually exposed yourself in front of Father! I shouldn't have hinted at you!

Forget it, just lie flat.

Yinreng couldn't be bothered to struggle, yawned, and hung onto Kangxi’s neck, rubbing against him: "Mingju first wanted to support the eldest brother, but after the eldest brother angered him, he started picking and choosing among my two younger brothers. I told him if you keep doing this, Father will kill you."

Kangxi’s face sank.

Yinreng said lazily: "Don't be angry, Father. If you get angry over such things, you’ll be angry every day and get sick. The Manchu and Mongol nobility don't want you to decide the Crown Prince candidate yourself; didn't you know that when you named me?"

Kangxi opened his mouth, unable to make a sound for a long time.

Yes, he had known all along.

He knew the purpose of naming a Crown Prince, he knew the Crown Prince was a target, he knew the malice Baocheng would face after becoming Crown Prince; he knew all of this.

But he didn't want Baocheng to know now.

If Baocheng knew, what would he think of his father? Would he think his father’s love was impure?

But Baocheng was just too smart, and with Shunzhi whispering in his ear, he hadn't been able to hide it.

"Father will protect you." In the end, Kangxi only held his son, who was yawning constantly, tighter, and said in a heavy tone.

Yinreng yawned again: "Hmm, ah, Father, can I go to sleep now?"

"Still sleeping!" Kangxi pinched Yinreng’s nose.

Yinreng rubbed his face: "I don't know why, but I feel sleepy as soon as I return to the palace."

Probably because the palace is too boring.

The eldest brother is forced to go to school again, and the third and fourth brothers have returned to their mothers' sides. He can't stay by his brothers' sides for too long every day, and he has to wait for the eldest brother to finish school to go together. It’s really too boring.

Kangxi, however, misunderstood.

His heart sank again.

Yinreng had only been back in the palace for a short while; was the curse already starting to drain his energy?

"Baocheng, do you want to go pay respects at your mother’s tomb this year?" Kangxi decided to renovate the palace’s feng shui and let Yinreng live outside the palace for a few more days.

Yinreng’s eyes widened immediately: "I want to go!"

Kangxi rubbed Yinreng’s head and laughed.

Good, good, his son’s spirit was still very good.

100,000
