53. Three Chapters Combined [V]

For the past few days, Yinreng had been dreaming of Empress Renxiao and his mother from his previous life.

Later, his dad also entered his dreams.

When Yinreng saw his dad, he was stunned for a long time before bursting into tears.

Because of the memories from his first life, the fatherly love he craved always revolved around the two Kangxis, and he had actually forgotten this dear dad of his.

Why was he chasing after Kangxi's fatherly love? Didn't he have a dad who was incredibly good to him?

At this moment, Yinreng realized that a piece of his memories from his previous life seemed to be missing; the darkness and bloodshed of his life before that acted like a thick veil, covering his happy memories of his previous life.

That pathetic, miserable, and detestable Crown Prince was just from the life before last; this is already my third life.

In my previous life, I was a child raised with doting, had close friends, air conditioning, toilets, the internet, and was a happy, decadent youth who drank soda, ate junk food, played games, and cursed.

Dad, Mom, I want to go home.

Whoever wants to be this Crown Prince can have it; I just want to go home and be a normal youth of the new era.

Even being a 996-working-hour programmer would be better than being this Crown Prince, who is constantly worried and afraid!

His parents rubbed his head, giving him comfort and praise.

Child, you've done a great job. You are worthy of being our son.

After waking up, Yinreng wiped away his tears, feeling much lighter.

He ran to the side of Empress Renxiao's coffin, squatted down, rested his chin on his hands, and whispered, "Mother, did you also reincarnate as my mother in my previous life? If so, I'm sorry for passing away young and making you sad. But I was acting out of righteousness, so you must be proud of me, right?"

Yinreng wanted to cry, but he laughed out loud instead.

If his mother from his previous life was the reincarnation of his mother here, then not only did his mother not hate him, but she also... ahem, found a better man as a husband.

Who is Kangxi? We aren't close!

Hahahaha, Mother did a great job!

Yinreng wiped away the tears of laughter, his eyes filled with madness and obsession.

"Good, Mother and I have continued our bond, and it has nothing to do with him, nothing at all, hahaha."

Yinreng squatted on the ground, wiping his tears, laughing until he felt like vomiting.

Yinreng was now like someone with schizophrenia, split into three personalities.

The first personality was trapped in darkness, deeply envious and jealous of the second;

The second personality missed home like crazy and didn't want to accept the darkness of the first;

The third personality was caught between the two, unable to detach from their negative emotions.

Perhaps the environment was too gloomy, perhaps his parents in his dreams made him fragile, or perhaps his mother's coffin was right before his eyes, but Yinreng released all his negative emotions.

While he was laughing and crying as if he had gone mad, several people stood outside the funeral palace.

A few days after Yinreng and Yinzhi's formal memorial ceremony, Gao Shiqi said to Chen Tingjing, who had come with him, that the little Crown Prince laughing in front of Empress Renxiao's coffin was unfilial, and wanted to persuade his colleague to join him in admonishing the little Crown Prince.

Chen Tingjing would not make a decision based on Gao Shiqi's one-sided words. He observed the little Crown Prince with Gao Shiqi for several days.

Every morning, the little Crown Prince would come to the funeral palace and tell Empress Renxiao that he was going to play with the First Prince, telling his mother not to worry about him;

After returning from playing, the little Crown Prince would arrive punctually at Empress Renxiao's coffin and laughingly tell her what he had played and eaten, and how happy he was.

Sometimes, the little Crown Prince would imitate things from the outside world, like small animals, flowers, or people, just like a child playing in front of a kind mother.

"I have my older brother taking care of me, and I'm having a great time every day. Mother, don't worry about me."

The little Crown Prince patted his chest, his face blooming with smiles.

Chen Tingjing turned and asked his colleague, "Are you sure this is unfilial?"

Gao Shiqi: "...Although it's understandable, laughing is still not appropriate."

Chen Tingjing said, "During the formal memorial, the Crown Prince's expression was very solemn and sad, without any errors in etiquette or demeanor. When he speaks privately to his mother, must he only cry and complain? Do you have deceased friends or relatives? Do you only cry in front of them?"

Gao Shiqi: "..."

Chen Tingjing pointed at the funeral palace with dissatisfaction, "Would a normal person see this scene and think the Crown Prince is unfilial?"

Chen Tingjing pointed to his own chest, "I only feel that the Crown Prince is very filial and very sensible—so sensible that it makes one's heart ache."

Gao Shiqi looked ashamed.

He had gained the Emperor's favor through poetry, and the Emperor trusted and doted on him, but did not give him a position with real power. There were also rumors in the outside world that he was just a sycophant of Kangxi. He desperately wanted to find an opportunity to prove himself.

From ancient times to the present, the fastest way for a civil official to become famous is through remonstrance, especially remonstrating with the Emperor.

Gao Shiqi dared not remonstrate directly with the Emperor. Settling for the next best thing, remonstrating with the Crown Prince was the best path.

Also, from ancient times to the present, chasing after the Crown Prince's words and actions to remonstrate was something officials loved to do. Gao Shiqi was allowed to accompany the Crown Prince on trips, and with Kangxi hinting that he could interact with and teach the Crown Prince things, he became a bit impatient.

Chen Tingjing had a neutral impression of Gao Shiqi and said bluntly, "I know you don't have a good relationship with Songgotu, but the Crown Prince doesn't either. Whose family doesn't have troublesome relatives? You shouldn't be prejudiced against the Crown Prince because of Songgotu; the Crown Prince was raised by the Emperor himself."

Although Chen Tingjing's words were meant as advice, they sounded quite unpleasant to Gao Shiqi.

Gao Shiqi flushed red and argued, "That is a malicious accusation!"

Chen Tingjing bowed lazily, "As fellow Han officials, I'm just giving you a reminder. If you don't want to hear it, I won't say it."

Gao Shiqi, embarrassed and angry, flicked his sleeves and left.

Accepting favors from Songgotu and being scolded by him as a house slave was the most painful thing in his life. But he absolutely refused to admit that he was taking his anger out on the Crown Prince because of this.

Chen Tingjing watched Gao Shiqi leave, brushed his sleeves, and felt a sense of relief.

It seemed Gao Shiqi was just impatient and didn't truly have a prejudice against the Crown Prince because of Songgotu.

There were very few Han officials who could influence Kangxi, and even if he didn't recognize Gao Shiqi's talent for practical affairs, he hoped Han officials wouldn't get involved in the factional struggles of the Manchu officials, causing the Han officials who had finally gained some importance in this dynasty to suffer setbacks.

If there were no Han officials in the court, who could protect the safety of the Han people?

After noticing the Crown Prince's situation, Chen Tingjing, in order to prevent others from misunderstanding the Crown Prince like Gao Shiqi did, stood guard at the door every day when the Crown Prince went to visit Empress Renxiao, recording things truthfully so he could testify for the Crown Prince when Kangxi asked.

He was also present when Yinreng had his emotional breakdown.

Chen Tingjing was extremely shocked to hear the child's sharp crying and laughter.

He immediately stepped into the funeral palace, but the First Prince, Yinzhi, stepped across the door, blocking his path with his small body.

Yinzhi stood with his hands behind his back and shook his head at Chen Tingjing.

Chen Tingjing stood quietly behind Yinzhi, watching as Yinreng, after his emotional outburst, curled up into a ball on the ground, leaning against Empress Renxiao's coffin, motionless.

Only then did Yinzhi walk into the funeral palace and gently pat Yinreng on the shoulder.

Yinreng tilted to one side; he had actually fallen asleep.

Yinzhi sighed and carried Yinreng on his back.

"Let me..." Chen Tingjing said hurriedly, but was interrupted by Yinzhi before he could finish.

Yinzhi shook his head, "My younger brother looks strong, but he is actually extremely fragile. If I'm not here to accompany him at this time, I'm afraid he'll be startled awake."

Yinzhi was only two years older than Yinreng, but his steps were steady as he carried him.

Chen Tingjing marveled at Yinzhi's strength and was also surprised by the bond between these two royal brothers.

He walked beside Yinzhi, escorting him as he carried Yinreng to the small sedan chair heading to the temporary palace, then immediately turned to find the accompanying imperial physician.

After the imperial physician examined Yinreng, he stroked his beard and smiled, "Although this emotional outburst consumed some of the Crown Prince's energy, the knot in his heart has been untied quite a bit, which is beneficial and harmless to the Crown Prince's health."

The accompanying officials breathed a sigh of relief and hurriedly reported this to Kangxi.

Nalan Xingde stayed by Yinreng's side, while Cao Yin went to report it in person.

Before Cao Yin left, Chen Tingjing hoped to accompany him.

Cao Yin hesitated for a moment before agreeing.

Cao Yin reported the Crown Prince's whereabouts in great detail, and Chen Tingjing told Kangxi everything he had seen and heard truthfully, including the First Prince carrying the Crown Prince away and the misunderstanding Gao Shiqi and others had about the Crown Prince.

Although Gao Shiqi gave Chen Tingjing the cold shoulder after being stung by his words, the matter of Chen Tingjing coming to "complain" had been discussed with Gao Shiqi.

Gao Shiqi's attempt to remonstrate with the Crown Prince would definitely be reported by the eunuchs. So it was better to let Chen Tingjing, also a Han official, report it and put in a good word for Gao Shiqi.

Kangxi was stunned for a long time, then swept everything on his desk onto the floor.

He stood up with his hands behind his back, paced around the desk like a headless fly, and looked up, "Baocheng is precocious; he understands the idle gossip and malicious words of others, and he remembers them all! I thought that with me protecting him, he wouldn't be wronged. But in places I couldn't see, how much grievance has he suffered! Otherwise, why would he be in such pain!"

Kangxi was so angry he was incoherent, even changing his self-reference.

Cao Yin and Chen Tingjing stood with their heads bowed, not daring to answer.

Kangxi continued to roar incoherently, like an enraged tiger.

He started from every instance of grievance he remembered from Yinreng's childhood, from everyone who had whispered in Yinreng's ear that Empress Renxiao's death was caused by him, from every member of the imperial clan who mocked Yinreng for being born and killing his mother...

Kangxi had endured for too long, endured until he thought it didn't matter, and was almost brainwashed by these people.

Until Yinreng fainted in front of Empress Renxiao's coffin.

Kangxi remembered his own childhood; after his mother passed away, he had already become Emperor and was much older than Yinreng.

Whenever he was frustrated by the court officials, especially Oboi, he would run to his mother's spirit tablet and cry.

When he encountered happy things, such as his wedding or the capture of Oboi, he would also report the good news with a smile in front of her spirit tablet.

How similar he and Yinreng were in this regard!

"Prepare the carriage, we are going to Gonghua City!"

After Kangxi finished roaring, he drank the warm tea handed to him by Zhao Chang and said in a deep voice.

Memorials could be reviewed anywhere, but if his son was sad, he couldn't be without his father!

Cao Yin had long guessed this would happen and had asked Nalan Xingde to prepare for the Emperor's arrival before leaving. Hearing that Kangxi wanted to leave the palace overnight, he hurriedly knelt to persuade him otherwise.

Chen Tingjing also immediately knelt to persuade Kangxi, saying that there were still many government affairs to be handled today, and the Crown Prince had already fallen asleep, so if he wanted to go, he should go tomorrow.

Kangxi was furious and wanted to rush out regardless. A thin, hunched old man walked into the Imperial Study, step by step, leaning on a cane.

He didn't kneel, didn't offer greetings, and just looked at Kangxi silently.

Kangxi's furious expression was like being splashed with a bucket of ice water. He was stunned for a moment, then straightened his clothes and walked back to his seat to sit down.

Zhao Chang, with a few young eunuchs, instantly cleaned up the Imperial Study.

"Grant a seat to Grand Tutor Du." Kangxi's voice was very soft, as if he were afraid of startling the old man in front of him.

Du Lide sat down with his cane and said, "It was the Empress Dowager who asked this old servant to come."

Kangxi glared at Cao Yin.

Cao Yin gave Kangxi an "I'm very innocent" look.

Your Majesty, it was you who ordered me to give the Empress Dowager a report on the little Crown Prince's daily news.

Clearly, as soon as the Empress Dowager heard about Yinreng's situation today, she knew Kangxi would definitely skip work and slip away, and no one could stop him—not even her.

Thus, the Empress Dowager invited someone who happened to be in the palace and could stop Kangxi: the Imperial Tutor, Du Lide.

Du Lide, as a Han official, was the teacher of both the Shunzhi and Kangxi Emperors.

Du Lide had wanted to retire due to old age many times, but Kangxi begged him to stay and help him. It was Du Lide who helped Kangxi through the lowest points of dealing with Oboi and pacifying the Three Feudatories.

Kangxi's reliance on Du Lide was almost equal to that of a relative or elder. The increase in the number of Han officials gaining importance in the court was largely due to Du Lide.

Du Lide was rarely this impolite, and whenever he was, Kangxi would feel intimidated.

"I should not intervene in the Emperor's family affairs, but the Crown Prince's affairs are also state affairs, so let me listen," Du Lide said with a sigh, at the Empress Dowager's request.

Han officials should not intervene in the internal strife of the Manchu royal family, as this would deal a fatal blow to the already fragile Han official system. The matter of succession was a taboo in every dynasty, let alone in the Manchu court, which did not trust the Han people.

But Kangxi was raised by Du Lide, and he had a complex sense of closeness to him. He had also seen and taught the little Crown Prince, and he liked this child very much, recognizing his character and talent.

Seeing Kangxi lose his composure for the sake of the Crown Prince, whether for Kangxi's sake or the Crown Prince's, he broke the rules slightly at an age when he already had one foot in the grave.

Just guiding the Emperor on handling family relationships shouldn't count as interfering in succession, Du Lide comforted himself.

With a look from Kangxi, Cao Yin immediately withdrew.

Seeing that Chen Tingjing was still stunned, he hurriedly tugged on his sleeve.

Seeing Cao Yin's signal, Chen Tingjing also immediately took his leave.

After leaving the Qianqing Palace, Chen Tingjing thanked Cao Yin.

Cao Yin waved his hand, "There's nothing to thank me for. We are all working for the Emperor. You definitely couldn't tell others about the Crown Prince's affairs."

Chen Tingjing said, "I understand." He wasn't stupid.

Chen Tingjing stayed at home temporarily, waiting to accompany Kangxi when he set off for Gonghua City the next day.

After returning home, he was filled with emotion and couldn't help but write a poem, expressing his feelings about the filial and fraternal love between the Crown Prince and the First Prince, and reflecting on his own relatives and parents.

This poem became important historical material for studying the early temperaments of the Crown Prince and the First Prince; that is a story for another time.

Returning to Du Lide taking the initiative to find Kangxi and listen to his troubles regarding the Crown Prince, Kangxi was extremely moved.

He knew his teacher was very cautious. Yet, he had broken the rules for him; his teacher was indeed (crossed out) true love (crossed out) loyal to him.

Kangxi pulled up a chair and sat face-to-face with Du Lide, beginning to pour out his worries, and as he spoke, it turned into bragging about his son.

Du Lide lazily raised his eyes, thinking that the Emperor's appearance was very similar to a friend of his who only had one son.

But the Crown Prince was not the Emperor's first son, nor his only son. The Emperor truly liked the Crown Prince immensely.

However, the Crown Prince was worthy of the Emperor's affection.

Du Lide sighed in his heart, trying to find Kangxi's actual worries from his bragging.

As he listened, his eyes widened, and his body, which was somewhat cold in mid-May due to old age and illness, actually broke out in a sweat.

He wanted to tell the Emperor to stop talking, but his lips trembled, and in the end, he gritted his teeth and continued to listen.

Du Lide had an intuition that whether he could change the plight of the Han people under Manchu rule might hinge on the Crown Prince.

Kangxi trusted Du Lide very much. Du Lide knew plenty of secrets; one more about the Crown Prince didn't matter.

He hadn't told Du Lide before out of respect and care for his teacher. Since his teacher didn't want to enter the whirlpool of succession, he didn't want him to worry about his student's family affairs when he was about to retire.

But Du Lide had a soft heart and jumped in himself, so Kangxi couldn't be blamed for being "cruel."

Kangxi spoke to his heart's content.

These things had been weighing on his heart, and he dared not tell anyone.

The Empress Dowager was already old, and her vision wasn't broad enough; even if Fuquan and Changning knew a little, they were members of the imperial clan, and Kangxi kept his guard up, not to mention that these two weren't of much use.

Only Du Lide.

He was a Han person, posed no threat to the succession of the Manchu royal family, and he was almost dead, soon to take all his secrets to the grave. Kangxi didn't need to worry about him leaking them.

And he was very smart and could help Kangxi solve his puzzles.

Kangxi felt refreshed and relieved. Du Lide was so overwhelmed he almost fainted, relying entirely on willpower to hold on.

Kangxi didn't want to scare Du Lide to death and hurriedly asked if he needed an imperial physician.

Du Lide waved his hand, drank a few sips of hot tea, rubbed his chest, and caught his breath.

Kangxi looked at Du Lide, who had regained his composure so quickly, with a very regretful expression.

Du Lide glanced at Kangxi; how could he not know that Kangxi wanted to see him make a fool of himself?

The Emperor had grown up from a mischievous child. Kangxi was now a young man, much more steady than before, but in front of those close to him, he still couldn't hide his inner mischievousness.

"I suggest building an Eastern Palace for the Crown Prince outside the palace," Du Lide said.

Kangxi immediately said, "No! He is still so young!"

Du Lide sighed, "He will grow up. Will Your Majesty feel at ease with the Crown Prince living alone outside?"

Kangxi remained silent.

Du Lide said, "The Crown Prince is frail and has many secrets. If he faints while alone before he is married, it will indeed be dangerous."

Kangxi said, "Then why did Grand Tutor Du ask me to prepare an Eastern Palace outside the palace?"

Du Lide said something cruel, "The Crown Prince is indeed perfect, but given his health, is it really good for him to inherit the throne?"

Kangxi looked flustered, but he couldn't bring himself to scold Du Lide.

Du Lide said, "The late Emperor also warned Your Majesty, and you understand this in your heart. When the Crown Prince bore the curse, this matter was already unchangeable. If you don't build an Eastern Palace, then build a temporary palace; it has hot springs, forests, and vast fields, to be used for the Crown Prince to recuperate in the future."

Kangxi understood the implication of Du Lide's words.

Du Lide's implication was also what Shunzhi had warned him about.

If the Crown Prince was too frail to inherit the throne, or if he needed to abdicate quickly to the Imperial Grandson after inheriting it, the place for his retirement and recuperation should be determined by Kangxi first. Otherwise, even if it were the Crown Prince's own child, they might not be very devoted to the Crown Prince due to fear of the Retired Emperor.

Kangxi said sullenly, "Why is the Grand Tutor just like Han-ama, always thinking of the worst? The Crown Prince's health will definitely improve. He only falls asleep when reciting, and he is full of energy at other times."

Du Lide's eyelid twitched.

Falling asleep when reciting—wasn't the child doing that on purpose?

Probably not; deep sleep couldn't be faked.

Du Lide pondered for a while and said, "Does the Crown Prince consume his physical energy rapidly whenever he concentrates and uses his brain?"

Kangxi nodded, "If he were willing to be serious, he could handle things on his own now. I often treat him as an advisor."

Du Lide gasped, "Your Majesty! If the Crown Prince's health never improves, shouldn't you reflect on yourself!"

Kangxi, having let it slip, lowered his head.

Well, I am reflecting; I have been reflecting for a long time.

Du Lide rubbed his chest, took the tea handed by Zhao Chang, drank another sip, and rubbed his chest again.

How did it sound to him that his disciple, who was almost thirty, was not as mature and reliable as the little Crown Prince?!

"Everything should be prepared for the worst first. The Crown Prince is purely filial and kind; solving his worries is what Your Majesty should consider first," Du Lide said sternly. "The late Emperor warned you, why haven't you done it yet?"

Kangxi: "..."

Kangxi lowered his head and reflected.

Could he say that thinking about these things was too painful and he was temporarily avoiding it?

That would be so embarrassing to say.

Although the Kangxi from Yinreng's life before last made Yinreng disrespectful to his teachers, the Kangxi of both eras was very respectful to his teachers when he was young, and he was quite obedient when being lectured.

Du Lide’s expression softened slightly as he said, "Your servant understands Your Majesty's feelings. The Crown Prince is still so young and was raised by your own hands; thinking of any pain the Crown Prince might suffer makes you feel extremely uncomfortable, and it is inevitable that you would have thoughts of wanting to shield him."

Kangxi said, "I will immediately select a location in the suburbs of the capital to build an auxiliary palace for the Crown Prince to live in, and I will bestow it upon him when he marries."

Du Lide nodded: "If Your Majesty wants to protect the Crown Prince and cannot bear for him to leave the palace, you could simply select another area within the palace to serve as the Crown Prince's Eastern Palace, and then let the other princes live there together. To the outside world, you can claim it is for the Crown Prince to instruct his younger brothers and strengthen their fraternal bonds."

In other words, an Eastern Palace in name, but a residence for the princes in reality?

Kangxi had already discussed with Du Lide that in order to isolate the influence of the maternal clans on the princes, once they are old enough to study, they should move out of the concubines' palaces and live together; this would also strengthen the bonds between the princes.

Concentrating the Eastern Palace and the princes' residences together would indeed be very convenient for the Crown Prince, who wants to visit his younger brothers every day.

Kangxi felt a pang of jealousy.

Du Lide looked at Kangxi’s expression and was speechless: "The Crown Prince has a good relationship with his brothers; could it be that Your Majesty is actually feeling jealous?"

Kangxi immediately said, "Grand Tutor, what are you saying? How could I think that? I am only worried that those little rascals will disturb the Crown Prince's rest."

Du Lide sighed: "Allowing the Crown Prince to have a better relationship with the other princes—if I may say something treasonous..."

Kangxi waved his hand: "Grand Tutor, no need to say it; I understand."

Du Lide had laid his cards on the table, and Kangxi reciprocated by stopping Du Lide from saying anything more excessive.

Du Lide said: "The Crown Prince has received divine instruction from the late Emperor; his teaching of the other princes is far more useful than us ministers teaching them. Your Majesty has to handle state affairs and lacks the energy to teach each prince one by one; isn't handing them over to the Crown Prince just right?"

Kangxi remembered the eldest son who had been "taught" by the Crown Prince and sighed softly: "The Crown Prince is indeed very good at teaching others."

Du Lide said: "If the Crown Prince can successfully inherit the throne, given his generosity toward his brothers and his prestige in their hearts, he will surely be able to keep the brothers united."

Kangxi’s expression turned somber: "Just like Zhu Biao, the Crown Prince of the former Ming Dynasty?"

Upon hearing the words "former Ming," Du Lide’s expression darkened for a moment: "Yes."

Kangxi said: "The matter of Zhu Biao must never be repeated. Does Grand Tutor Du have a solution?"

Du Lide said: "I do, but is Your Majesty willing to let go?"

Kangxi was stunned and fell silent once again.

Du Lide did not speak further either, but closed his eyes to rest for a while.

Kangxi murmured: "I don't know."

He and Du Lide both understood what the solution was.

After the Crown Prince marries and the legitimate grandson grows up, Kangxi would first abdicate to the Crown Prince while protecting him and teaching the Grand Prince; when the Crown Prince’s energy wanes, the Crown Prince would then abdicate to the Grand Prince, and Kangxi would continue to serve as the Grand Emeritus Emperor to mentor the Grand Prince.

But Kangxi did not know if he could live that long, nor did he know if he would become as power-hungry in his old age as the emperors in history books.

Du Lide said: "Think about future matters in the future. Even if you are prepared now, you cannot keep up with the changes of Heaven. Who knows, perhaps the Crown Prince’s health will improve?"

Kangxi nodded vigorously: "The Crown Prince’s health will definitely improve! As long as the curse weakens, the Crown Prince’s health will improve!"

Du Lide laughed: "Then Your Majesty must study harder. I hear Your Majesty intends to set your sights on the globe and become an emperor for the ages?"

Kangxi: "..." How does even the Grand Tutor know about this?

Kangxi remembered that Du Lide disliked the scourge of war, so he said: "It is just the idle talk of a child."

Du Lide said calmly: "There is nothing wrong with that. If Your Majesty can achieve it, there is no harm in doing so."

Kangxi was surprised: "The Grand Tutor actually agrees?"

Du Lide said: "If a man has no far-reaching plans, he will have immediate worries. Most of Mongolia has submitted to the Great Qing, and the rest are just minor troubles. With no strong enemies eyeing the borders of the Great Qing, I fear we will become complacent. I have also learned about the situation in the outside world; for instance, that Taiwan was once occupied by Westerners. With their ambitions, we will have a war sooner or later."

This was not Du Lide’s true inner voice.

To gain a firm foothold in the imperial court, Du Lide had to do things that catered to the Emperor's preferences. For example, when Kangxi and the Crown Prince showed interest in foreign countries, he immediately had his disciples and grand-disciples study foreign history; even though he was old and nearing retirement, he was still studying Western affairs.

The more he learned, the more alarmed he became, yet he also believed this was an opportunity.

If Kangxi was not satisfied with just the Central Plains, the limited talent of the Manchus would never be enough; he would inevitably have to use Han talent, even if it meant expanding the Han Banners.

The scourge of war is indeed terrifying, and vanity only brings disaster to the common people. But the Eight Banners were barbarians to begin with; rather than hoping they would sheathe their blades, it is better to have them point their blades outward.

The Manchu Qing court does not base its nation on morality; whether it is supporting war through war or supporting the nation through war, as long as they are fighting in wealthy places, the barbarians are already quite skilled at it. That is how they treated the Great Ming.

In order to prevent them from slaughtering the people of the Central Plains, Du Lide could not care about the lives of others.

He was not a saint or a Confucian scholar. He did not cultivate morality and did not fear retribution. Having seen the tragic state of the Central Plains under the ravages of the Qing, he was merely a vicious villain and a hypocrite willing to become one of these wolves and tigers to slightly influence the direction in which they moved.

To achieve his goals, Du Lide could be more ruthless than anyone else; even if his Han colleagues were in his way, he would crush them without mercy.

Du Lide narrowed his eyes, concealing the sharp glint within them.

Although he was old and decrepit, his eyes were still as bright and ambitious as they were in his youth.

Beneath his skin of a Confucian scholar who practiced self-restraint and propriety lay a heart full of dirty, bloody schemes.

"Your Majesty wants to balance the relationship between the Manchus and the Han, but the wealth is in the hands of the Han. If the Manchus do not covet and seize it, how can they become the new nobility? Power and wealth—the world is driven by profit; for most ordinary people, power is also for the sake of wealth," Du Lide said slowly. "If the Manchus covet and seize it, the foundation of Your Majesty’s throne will become unstable. Then, we just need to find a different source of wealth growth."

Kangxi assumed a posture of humble instruction.

Du Lide paused and continued: "Moreover, the Eight Banners were never a system for governing the people, but a system for governing the military. The Eight Banners are not ordinary commoners, but military households. If Your Majesty wishes to abolish the Eight Banners, you need an army stronger than them, and a strong army can only be forged through war; if Your Majesty does not wish to abolish the Eight Banners, you must find a place for them to sharpen their blades, otherwise, the Eight Banners, who exist only for war and not for the people, will surely wither away if not sharpened."

"Supporting war through war, supporting the army through war, supporting the people through war—this must absolutely not be applied to your own subjects. Be an external king and an internal saint; the Great Qing was founded on bloodshed. To consolidate your rule, Your Majesty must be a benevolent saint to the people within the Great Qing."

Du Lide took a few deep breaths; his emotions seemed too intense for his aged body to bear.

Kangxi hurriedly stood up to personally soothe Du Lide’s chest and serve him tea.

Du Lide had lacked energy in his old age and had not instructed him in such detail for a long time.

"Grand Tutor, please rest first; we can slowly discuss these matters later," Kangxi said.

Du Lide shook his head: "We cannot be slow. Once it is confirmed that Your Majesty has the ambition to contend for world hegemony... oh, that phrase also came from the Crown Prince. 'World hegemony'—those four characters are very vivid."

Kangxi: "..." What else has the Crown Prince said that I don't know about?!

Du Lide continued: "Once it is confirmed that Your Majesty has the heart to contend for world hegemony and wishes to become a Martial Emperor rather than a ruler who merely maintains the status quo, I have much to teach you. But I am old; I have lived through this year, but I may not necessarily open my eyes next year. Even without waiting for next year, I might become senile by next month or even tomorrow. Therefore, I request to establish a separate team to explain the ways of a Martial Emperor to Your Majesty."

His eyes were piercing: "The fierce generals who entered the pass with the Eight Banners have not all died of old age yet; Your Majesty still has people to consult, and if you don't consult them now, it will be too late."

Kangxi closed his eyes, pondered for a moment, then opened them and said: "Granted. I will begin working on this immediately."

Du Lide nodded slightly, then his head tilted to the side, his eyes closed, and he actually fell asleep.

Kangxi said helplessly: "How is it that the Grand Tutor has this habit, just like Baocheng?"

Zhao Chang replied in a low voice: "It must be a lack of energy."

Kangxi sighed.

Yes, it is all a lack of energy.

My Baocheng.

Kangxi kept thinking about his precious son until the next day.

And having vented his frustrations, the now quite cheerful Yinreng decided to follow the hopes of his parents from his dream and began to seriously court disaster.

Since I didn't die even after that miserable first life, why not be a bit more carefree and act like the arrogant transmigrator from those old-school 'poisonous' transmigration novels?

By being rebellious and unconventional, I won't be executed, and I might even avoid being this damn Crown Prince.

Yinreng touched his chest; the obsession from his first life was deep, like a child throwing a tantrum.

I don't care what your father is like in this life; I just don't want to be the Crown Prince!

I won't do it!

Yinreng sighed, coaxing the obsession from his first life as if he had a split personality. Fine, I won't do it, I won't do it; I don't want to be trapped in the imperial palace anyway.

The world is so big; I want to go see it with my big brother! Wouldn't it be better to leave the throne to the younger brothers?

Yinreng was as happy as a little bird that had suddenly realized it had wings.

Seeing that Yinreng had returned to his silly, happy self—and was even more lively and silly than before—Yinshi breathed a sigh of relief.

To keep Yinreng in this silly, happy state, he even patted his chest and promised to be an accomplice in Yinreng’s schemes to pit Kangxi against himself.

"Father Emperor’s actions are still too slow; how can one be an emperor for the ages while being so hesitant? Even if the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories isn't settled, you can't just do nothing else," Yinreng shouted, waving his arms. "Can't the reorganization of the Eight Banners be done at the same time? Why not set up Western-style factories and produce the things the foreigners sell us at high prices ourselves, and then sell them back to the foreigners?"

Yinshi nodded vigorously: "Exactly! Father Emperor is just useless! The palace has cut back on expenses and tightened its belt several times; is this money something you can just save? If you don't have money, go earn it! Even a child understands this! Hasn't Father played the 'Great King' game?"

Yinreng said: "We are young and our words carry little weight; Father Emperor definitely won't listen to us. We need to find people to help us submit memorials."

Yinshi suggested: "That group of imperial guards is not bad. But I’m afraid they don't have the guts."

Yinreng and Yinshi looked at each other, then simultaneously extended their hands for a high-five and shouted in unison: "Elundai!"

Nalan Xingde was nearby protecting the two children visiting the Temple of Literature and heard every word of their slander against the Emperor.

He thought he was already used to it, but when these two children called out the name "Elundai," he finally couldn't hold it together.

No! No matter who you team up with, you cannot go to Elundai!

When Elundai was someone else's son, everyone watched with amusement as he angered his father; but if Elundai corrupted his own children, it wouldn't be amusement—it would be a stroke. If the Emperor knew that the two princes had gotten close to Elundai, he would definitely be angered to the point of illness.

Nalan Xingde hurriedly said: "If the Crown Prince and the First Prince have need, your servant can submit a memorial!"

Yinshi and Yinreng glanced at Nalan Xingde and then looked away: "Fine, we'll add you. Where is Elundai? Did he follow us too?"

Nalan Xingde clutched his chest in a 'Xizi' pose. Can you two stop obsessing over Elundai?

Nalan Xingde said tactfully: "Your servant alone will suffice. I can also pull in Ziqing."

Even if he had to drag Cao Yin onto the thief... the princes' ship, he could not let the princes go find Elundai.

Yinshi and Yinreng nodded in perfect unison: "Good, add Cao Ziqing. Is Elundai in Gonghua City?"

Nalan Xingde: "..."

Yinshi frowned: "Guard Nalan, we are asking you a question!"

Nalan Xingde could not hide it and said sorrowfully: "He is."

Yinshi said: "Hurry up and go find Elundai. We will wait here."

Yinreng suppressed a laugh and told Liang Jiugong to go call for him.

Liang Jiugong sighed in his heart and walked away with heavy steps.

Even Liang Jiugong had heard of the name Elundai.

This capital city would probably be turned upside down by his Crown Prince and the Crown Prince’s brother.

Fortunately, the sky belongs to His Majesty, so it shouldn't be too much of a problem.

100,000

54. Three Chapters in One [V]

Elundai arrived.

Elundai arrived with his signature hearty smile.

Nalan Xingde’s head had already started to ache.

"Crown Prince, First Prince! What fun thing do you have for me!" Elundai gave a casual bow, considering his duty done.

Nalan Xingde couldn't help but kick Elundai: "Mind your manners!"

Elundai rubbed his nose: "Rongruo, you are so pedantic."

Nalan Xingde did not argue with Elundai: "Shall we go to the drill ground and practice later?"

Elundai: "...No thanks."

He honestly performed the bow again.

Nalan Xingde was a man of culture, a man of culture with very high combat ability.

When Nalan Xingde was born, Nalan Mingzhu was still in a period of political frustration. He pinned all his hopes on Nalan Xingde, and Nalan Xingde received the most comprehensive elite education.

From Manchu horsemanship and archery to Han poetry and classics, Nalan Xingde lived up to Mingzhu's expectations and achieved excellence in every aspect.

Nalan Xingde’s literary talent needs no elaboration; his martial arts skills are often overlooked by later generations, who assume he was a weak scholar.

Nalan Xingde was always a member of Kangxi’s imperial guard; almost wherever Kangxi went on inspection tours, Nalan Xingde was sure to accompany him.

This accompaniment was not because Kangxi viewed Nalan Xingde as a literary companion like Gao Shiqi; Nalan Xingde truly held the position of a bodyguard.

In Nalan Xingde’s letters to friends, one can see that he rarely discussed poetry with his close friends, but rather spent more time discussing horsemanship and archery.

In the 21st year of Kangxi, Kangxi prepared to take military action against Tsarist Russia and sent people to investigate the border situation between Russia and the Qing. Nalan Xingde was the one who took on this secret military mission and was ordered to go on a diplomatic mission to Suolong. He spent four months and successfully completed the task.

When Nalan Xingde passed away in the 24th year of Kangxi, the report of the great victory at Suolong had just arrived. Kangxi ordered people to report the victory to Nalan Xingde’s tomb with tears and honored him with the ceremony for a fallen hero. From this, it can be seen that Nalan Xingde not only made a great contribution in this military mission, but his premature death was also likely related to the injuries he sustained during it.

This was not the only secret military mission Nalan Xingde carried out.

According to the poems written by Nalan Xingde’s friends and colleagues in mourning, they mentioned multiple times that he had been to the Northwest and compared him to "Huo Qubing," yet there is no record of this in official history.

Yinreng was still young at that time and did not know about important military operations. But he had heard Kangxi mention many times that he had sent Nalan Xingde to carry out secret military missions. Since they were secret, they naturally would not be recorded.

Kangxi had also laughed, saying that Nalan Xingde’s identity as a talented poet and scholar was a perfect cover. When someone questioned him, Nalan Xingde could speak in verse and write a beautiful poem on the spot, making him look not like a soldier on a mission, but like a scholar traveling the mountains and rivers in search of inspiration.

Kangxi clearly wanted to cultivate Nalan Xingde into a military talent, which is why he gave him so many difficult tasks. Unfortunately, the Nalan family’s political ideals ran counter to Nalan Xingde’s future. As long as the Nalan family refused to become Kangxi’s loyal subjects, Nalan Xingde’s ideal of becoming a true "Huo Qubing" could never be realized.

He could only be left with a body full of injuries, trapped at home, and die of depression.

Such a Nalan Xingde, a Nalan Xingde who could lead missions to scout intelligence on the northern border—his combat ability can be imagined.

And what about Elundai?

He was also carefully taught by Tong Guogang when he was a child and experienced several years of elite education as the eldest legitimate son. After falling out with Tong Guogang, he became an idle hoodlum, usually bullying others and looking arrogant, but in reality, his skills had become mediocre due to his laziness over the past two years.

He could still rely on playing dirty to fight Longkodo, but when encountering a master like Nalan Xingde, even if Nalan Xingde let him use both hands, one kick would send him crawling on the ground, unable to get up.

You ask why Elundai was so self-aware? That is, of course, because Elundai couldn't stand Nalan Xingde always hanging out with Han scholars and had gone to cause trouble for him.

After causing trouble, Elundai bowed to Nalan Xingde: "Master, you are the master! You can play with whoever you want!"

The little interaction between Elundai and Nalan Xingde made Yinreng gossip a lot in his heart.

He immediately whispered to Yinshi, telling him the gossip and sharing it with his dear big brother.

Yinshi’s eyes lit up, and his gaze darted back and forth between Nalan Xingde and Elundai.

Elundai felt a chill: "First Prince?"

Yinshi coughed dryly and pretended to be serious: "I was wondering, which of you is stronger? Do you want to have a match?"

Elundai spread his hands in a rogue-like manner: "First Prince, you are trying to see me die."

Yinshi: "..." When encountering such a shameless person, all the fun disappears.

Yinshi waved his hand, told Elundai to sit down, and said: "Do you know that Father Emperor is dissatisfied with the idle Eight Banners youths?"

Elundai spread his hands again in a rogue-like manner: "When has the Emperor ever been satisfied with the idle Eight Banners youths?"

Yinshi: "..."

Yinreng covered his mouth with both hands, his cheeks puffed out and his little shoulders shaking, struggling hard to suppress his laughter.

The First Prince, the bully of the palace, had met Elundai, the bully of the capital, and had actually lost slightly.

Yinshi poked his younger brother, the Crown Prince, who dared to mock him, with his elbow, frowned, and said: "Father Emperor is dissatisfied with you all, so he is preparing to build a school and force you to go inside to attend classes, so you don't cause trouble."

Elundai was stunned: "No way? Is the Emperor that cruel?"

Nalan Xingde couldn't help it. Although he hadn't heard this news and it was nine-tenths likely that the First Prince was bluffing Elundai, he also thought Elundai’s words were very unreasonable.

"Learning more things is a gift from the Emperor; how can you call it cruel?" Nalan Xingde said. "You spend your days hanging out on the streets achieving nothing; aren't you ashamed?"

"I'm just playing, why should I be ashamed?" Elundai remained unmoved.

Yinshi threatened: "Father Emperor is making you go to school; do you think you can escape?"

Elundai said helplessly: "First Prince, just tell me what you want me to do."

Yinshi: "..." This guy is impervious to reason!

Yinreng patted Yinshi’s arm, telling his big brother, who wanted to roll up his sleeves and beat someone, to calm down: "Father Emperor is indeed preparing to establish a government school for the Eight Banners youths in the capital."

But that was a matter for the 24th year of Kangxi, and it only trained the three divisions of the Imperial Household Department, i.e., the bondservants.

Elundai grinned, showing his teeth: "And then?"

Yinreng said: "The things taught in the government school are just Han poetry, books, and etiquette; my big brother and I have no patience for the Eight Banners youths to learn these."

The uninhibited curve of Elundai’s mouth finally dropped.

He frowned and thought for a while, then said: "The trend of the Manchu Eight Banners learning Han culture is unstoppable."

Yinreng said: "In this world, culture is not just the Han lineage. We Manchus are called barbarians; before entering the pass, we were blank slates with nothing. They look down on blank slates for having no substance, but it is precisely because they are blank slates that they can encompass all things. The Eight Banners government school must be established, and it must be established grandly. The content of the learning cannot be decided by the Han people."

Yinshi nodded like a chicken pecking at rice: "Do you have the patience to read a book a hundred times, memorize it a hundred times, and copy it a hundred times? If you are willing to learn like that, then you don't have to join us."

Elundai raised both hands, resolute: "I'll join!"

He had long heard how strict the Crown Prince’s studies were in the palace. The Eight Banners youths are going to learn like that too? This is asking me, Elundai, to die!

Nalan Xingde’s mouth twitched.

The Crown Prince is too clever; he really has Elundai’s mind completely figured out.

After Yinreng persuaded Elundai, he leaned on Yinshi, closed his eyes to rest, and left the rest to Yinshi.

The thing Yinreng was dragging Yinshi to do was to have the Eight Banners youths themselves apply to establish a school exclusively for them, different from the Imperial Academy, using the excuse that "Manchus shouldn't just learn the Han way," and pushing for new education under the guise of Manchu-Han conflict without resistance.

The new school is divided into liberal arts and martial arts, with the same basic subjects: literature, history, geography, arithmetic, engineering, and politics.

The difference is that the textbooks and specific content for each subject are divided into different versions for civil officials and military generals.

Taking geography as an example, the liberal arts study how to develop local agricultural, animal husbandry, forestry, and fishery production according to local conditions, while the martial arts study examples of deploying troops and formations according to different terrain and weather.

In fact, the basic knowledge is the same, just the examples given are different.

Yinshi forgot his words as he spoke.

He looked down at his dozing younger brother, frowned, and couldn't bear to wake him up, so he furrowed his brows and racked his brains to think of what else his brother had said.

Liang Jiugong was worthy of being the most popular eunuch in the mid-Kangxi period; he immediately handed over a small booklet.

Yinshi flipped through it; Liang Jiugong had already organized the subjects for the new-style education that Yinreng and Yinshi had mentioned.

Yinshi beamed with joy, then glared at his personal eunuch.

Look at Liang Jiugong! Learn from him!

Yinshi’s eunuch immediately became alert. He really had to learn. The First Prince was going to participate in state affairs so early, and he only knew how to serve people; he was afraid he wouldn't be able to keep up with the First Prince’s pace.

"Let me see, let me see." Elundai was impatient to continue listening and reached out to Yinshi for the booklet.

It just so happened that Yinshi was also too lazy to explain, so he threw the booklet to Elundai.

Nalan Xingde also leaned over to read it together. He was actually listening with great interest and deeply agreed.

Are the Crown Prince and the First Prince not planning to mess around this time?

However, every time the Crown Prince and the First Prince messed around, it was effective, making one wonder if they were actually messing around at all.

"You didn't know beforehand?" Elundai was curious. He thought this kind of thing must have been thought up by this insidious guy Nalan Xingde, who was full of ink.

Nalan Xingde said truthfully: "Not very clearly."

Elundai opened the booklet, and the two studied it together.

Although Elundai was a bit of a rogue now, the foundation of the elite education he received in his early years remained, and he soon realized the terrifying nature of this education.

He had no patience for the classics and histories, but if the classics and histories were broken down and added to practical examples, he actually developed an interest in learning.

Although the Eight Banners youths were playboys, they had all received basic education—when everyone was a child, no one had the conditions to be a playboy, so they definitely had to study hard.

The Eight Banners government school that Yinreng created was actually "vocational re-education," teaching things that were extremely utilitarian. After graduating from this school and becoming an official, one would immediately know what needed to be done. Unlike many scholars who came out of the imperial examinations, who were completely clueless once they put down their books, relying entirely on the old clerks in their mansions for all administrative affairs.

There was also a "Martial Arts" course in the Eight Banners government school.

The martial arts course was compulsory for both liberal and martial arts students, but it also had different levels of courses depending on the different focuses of the liberal and martial arts students.

Although it is said that "civil and martial arts are different," the subject divisions in martial arts classes are not strictly enforced. Students can choose their own courses according to their needs.

Other civil and martial arts courses are the same. In addition to their compulsory courses, students can also take elective courses based on their interests, and they will receive elective credits after passing the exams.

School graduation is different from the imperial examination; it is not decided by a single exam. Instead, following the training guidelines of Han academies, there are exams every month, every semester, and every academic year, divided into different credits. Only after accumulating enough credits and passing the graduation exam can one graduate. Based on the weighted sum of credits and graduation exam scores, students are graded and granted official positions.

Clearly, Yinreng wants to institutionalize the traditional "Baitang'a promotion" system of the Eight Banners.

The so-called "Baitang'a promotion" is similar to the previous imperial system of hereditary protection and the recommendation system.

"Baitang'a" is a transliteration from Manchu, meaning "talent."

After the sons of the Manchu and Mongol Eight Banners turn eighteen, their names must be registered to become "Baitang'a." Based on recommendations and assessments, the outstanding ones are assigned official positions, and the most excellent ones enter the palace directly to become servants. After a five-year term, those who perform well can be directly appointed to official positions.

Every dynasty has had such special promotion channels for the children of nobles and prominent families. The Qing Dynasty expanded this to the entire Manchu and Mongol Eight Banners, effectively broadening this special promotion channel.

However, the recommendation system always has one drawback: it relies on "people," and those with connections get the positions.

Changing the recommendation system to a different kind of assessment is fairer for the Eight Banners' children.

Elundai and Nalan Xingde both belong to the Eight Banners' children who "have people in the family and people in the court," but they both believe this system is better.

No one can guarantee that their family will prosper forever, nor can they guarantee that the people doing the recommending and assessing won't be their political enemies. Clearly, exams will be slightly fairer. As long as they are willing to learn, even if their descendants fall on hard times temporarily, they can rely on their own efforts to regain glory.

Moreover, these things are very practical; as long as one wants to be an official or a general, they will learn these things sooner or later.

The elite education both received already included these. Instead of looking for teachers everywhere themselves, it's better to let the Emperor gather the talents and teach them together.

"Good!" Elundai slapped his thigh hard, "This is what we Eight Banners children should be learning!"

Nalan Xingde's eyes flickered. Although he didn't think the official school was perfect, he had to admit that most Eight Banners children were flighty and impatient, and learning these practical things would be more useful.

"This is not the only promotion path for the Eight Banners children." Yinreng, having rested his eyes for a while, opened them and said, "The imperial examination will still be open to the Eight Banners children. If any Eight Banners child wants to make a name for themselves, they can aim to be the top of the three lists: the official school, the civil service exam, and the military exam."

Nalan Xingde felt his scalp tingle, his breathing hitched, and he couldn't help but feel his blood surge and his heart race.

He adjusted the sword at his waist to calm himself down a little: "Can children who are already officials also enroll?"

Elundai glanced at Nalan Xingde, laughing to himself, not expecting Nalan Xingde to have such ambition.

But Nalan Xingde also had the talent to match his ambition.

And what about me? Elundai clenched his fists; for the first time since his mother passed away, his blood seemed to be reigniting.

He certainly couldn't be the top of all three lists, but what about passing one or two of them?

If he picked up his martial arts again, perhaps passing the military exam wouldn't be difficult?

Elundai blinked, loosened his fists, and returned to his usual unrestrained smile: "It must be very difficult to get the Emperor to change the content of the official school."

Yinreng said: "That's why we must request the establishment of the official school before Khan Ama promotes it, so we can keep the initiative in our own hands. Most of the officials in the court who can teach the classics and histories are Han officials. Although I don't want to admit it, the foundation of the Manchus is much shallower than that of the Han. The useful Manchu officials in the court are already stretched thin, and it's impossible to have powerful Manchu officials to teach you."

Yinzhi quickly added: "Do you want the teachers in the official school to be nothing but pedantic scholars shaking their heads?"

Elundai thought about it and shuddered: "Absolutely not!"

Nalan Xingde sighed and rubbed his forehead.

Many of his close friends were Kangxi's imperial scholars, or rather, Kangxi used him to manage and monitor that group of imperial scholars. He had a good impression of those scholars, but he really didn't think they could teach the Manchu and Mongol Eight Banners children well.

It was highly likely that the teachers wouldn't teach wholeheartedly, the students would continue to play, and the official school would be abandoned.

"We have to play a game with the Emperor." Elundai touched his messy stubble, "Exciting!"

Nalan Xingde rolled his eyes at Elundai. He knew this guy couldn't say anything decent.

"If we write this into a memorial and explain it to the Emperor in detail, the Emperor might consider our opinions; there's no need to use such an extreme method," Nalan Xingde suggested.

Yinreng and Yinzhi said in unison: "That wouldn't be any fun, would it?"

Elundai instantly understood what the two children were thinking and nodded like a chicken pecking at rice: "Exactly! That wouldn't be any fun!"

One adult and two children exchanged a look of mutual understanding; at that moment, they felt like soulmates.

Nalan Xingde stepped aside calmly, using his body to block the eye contact between the adult and the two children: "If the Emperor knows this idea came from the Crown Prince and the First Prince, he might get angry."

Yinzhi waved his hand dismissively: "When we return to the palace, after you submit the memorial, my brother and I will run to the Cining Palace. I don't believe Khan Ama can catch us. The Empress Dowager will definitely support us. She has always been impatient with those Han affairs."

Kangxi walked over angrily: "No need to return to the palace, I'll beat you two unfilial sons right now!"

"Ah!!!!!" Yinzhi screamed, grabbed Yinreng's arm with one hand, and started running: "Rongruo! Elundai! Stop Khan Ama!"

Nalan Rongruo: "Your Majesty! Please calm down!"

Elundai: "Your Majesty, this is a good thing, don't be angry, don't be angry."

Both were kicked aside by Kangxi, clearing the way.

Kangxi lifted his robes and started playing "hawk catching the chickens" with the two children in the back room of the Confucian Temple.

"Why is Khan Ama here!" Yinzhi screamed while running, "Khan Ama, how can you be so elusive! You're cheating! Brother, this way, hide here!"

Yinzhi stuffed Yinreng under the table and crawled in himself.

Kangxi kicked the corner of the table, and the heavy wooden table shook: "Get out here!"

Yinzhi protected Yinreng: "No! You say you won't hit me and my brother first, then we'll come out!"

Kangxi was so angry he laughed: "Don't even think about it, move the table for me!"

The eunuchs and guards looked at each other in dismay.

Kangxi said angrily: "Are you not listening to what I say?!"

The eunuchs and guards moved the table sluggishly, while Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin, who had followed Kangxi in, exchanged frantic glances.

Nalan Xingde: Ziqing, think of a way! The First Prince doesn't matter, but the Crown Prince just fainted once!

Cao Yin: What way can I think of? This isn't the palace, we can't go find the Empress Dowager...

Nalan Xingde: Hurry!

Cao Yin: Hurry my foot! You think of something too!

The two were exchanging glances, extremely anxious.

There was simply no one here who could persuade Kangxi!

Elundai watched coldly from the side as the guards and eunuchs moved the table, then suddenly lunged forward, grabbed one little prince in each hand, and ran for it, actually jumping out of the window in front of so many people.

Kangxi: "!!!"

Kangxi was so angry his hair stood on end... uh, let's not trouble that little braid. In short, Kangxi roared very angrily: "Elundai! I will kill you! I will wipe out your entire clan!"

Elundai shouted while running: "Your Majesty, don't forget you are my cousin. My entire clan includes you!"

Kangxi: "??!!"

At this moment, the word "damn" couldn't help but appear in everyone's mind.

Elundai, in terms of courage, there is no one in this Great Qing more courageous than you. You are simply our new generation of Baturu!

Elundai carried the two cousins and quickly scrambled up the wall, then pushed them toward the tree by the wall: "Climb quickly!"

Kangxi watched as Yinreng climbed onto the tree branch shakily, his heart nearly breaking with fear. He wanted to shout, but was afraid of scaring Yinreng and making him fall.

Zhao Chang hurriedly directed the eunuchs to get mattresses and straw, and the guards, under the command of Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde, lined up in several rows under the tree, ready to catch the children.

Yinzhi was very bold and often climbed trees in the palace, so he quickly climbed to a safe position and sat down.

Yinreng looked well-behaved, but in his previous life, he was skilled in both civil and martial arts, and in his past life, he often climbed trees to catch birds and went into rivers to catch fish; climbing a tree was a piece of cake.

The two children sat obediently on the tree, dangling their feet, and Elundai also climbed onto the branch next to them, protecting the two children with one hand, and dangling his feet along with them like a tough guy.

He even broke off three tender branches and gave one to the Crown Prince and one to the First Prince.

The one adult and two children had little branches in their mouths, dangling their big and small feet, watching the people below busy themselves.

Kangxi first clutched his chest, then clutched his head.

His chest hurt, and his head hurt too.

He regretted it so much now. When Tong Guogang said "please execute this son," why didn't he just take the opportunity to chop off Elundai!

"Come down!" Kangxi finally calmed down after his chest and head hurt severely.

Yinreng: "Khan Ama, you first promise not to beat me and my brother."

Elundai: "Don't beat me either."

Yinzhi: "Write a note! Write a note!"

Damn it... Kangxi took a deep breath, and Zhao Chang and Liang Jiugong helped him soothe his breath.

Your Majesty, Emperor, Your Imperial Highness, don't be angry, don't be angry, if you ruin your health, no one can replace you.

The accompanying officials looked up, especially the Han officials who had no chance to interact with the princes and Elundai, and were dumbfounded.

How are the children in the palace just like their own naughty kids? They also climb trees to avoid their father's beating?

"Come, down!" Kangxi gritted his teeth, "Don't force me to say it a third time!"

Yinreng stretched out his hands: "But Khan Ama, I can't get down."

Yinzhi looked down and shook: "Oh my, how did I climb so high?"

Elundai scratched his head: "Seems like it's a bit too high."

Kangxi's vision flickered black and white, and he almost fainted from holding his breath.

"Bring the ladder, bring the ladder!"

"Where is the straw? Where are the mattresses? Why haven't they come yet?"

"Crown Prince, First Prince, please don't move around!"

"Don't be afraid, hold on tight to the branches."

The scene under the tree was in chaos.

Elundai patted his chest and said: "It's fine! There's no wind, we are very safe!"

Just as Elundai finished speaking, a gentle breeze blew, as if greeting him.

The leaves rustled, getting more cheerful as they moved. The shadows of the trees danced, gradually evolving from shy dancing to a wild frenzy, as if a group of naughty ghosts were having a carnival under the tree.

Kangxi didn't know what a carnival was; he only knew his heart was about to stop.

Elundai was still scratching his head: "Ah, why did it start blowing so hard? A bit tricky."

Nalan Xingde said angrily: "Shut up! You are not allowed to speak!"

Cao Yin gritted his teeth and said: "Please, just shut your crow's mouth!"

Elundai felt wronged. How am I a crow's mouth? It sounds like I summoned this wind. If I had that ability, I would have summoned a gale to blow Tong Guogang off the roof.

"Khan Ama, don't worry, this little wind can't scare me and my brother." Yinreng hung from the little branch, dangling his little feet again, looking extremely cute, "Right, brother?"

Yinzhi was a little scared at first, but hearing Yinreng say this, he immediately puffed out his chest: "Of course! Brother, come closer, I'll protect you."

Elundai watched Yinzhi and Yinreng huddled together, Yinreng showing no fear, and Yinzhi a bit panicked but still holding his brother, and a nostalgic smile couldn't help but appear on his face.

He and Kuadai were like this too.

Although Kuadai was so sensible and obedient that he was a bit pedantic and dull, whenever he did something bad, he would always follow behind him like a little tail, saying he wanted to take half the responsibility for him.

And no matter what happened, he would always protect Kuadai tightly.

When their mother passed away early, Kuadai was still young. Elundai protected this brother with all his might at home, just like protecting his own child.

Thinking of Kuadai and his mother who passed away early, a flash of disgust and ruthlessness crossed Elundai's brows.

His conflict with Tong Guogang stemmed from the affairs in Tong Guogang's backyard.

After Tong Guogang's wife passed away, he did not remarry, and the affairs of the backyard were handed over to the favored concubine who had the only son.

Elundai watched as the concubine, who had been humble and submissive while his mother was alive, suddenly became the mistress of their backyard, even putting on the airs of a legitimate mother in front of him. It was so disgusting he wanted to vomit, and he even deeply hated Fahai, with whom he had previously had a decent relationship.

Just a lowly concubine, just the son of a concubine, why should you be on equal footing with me!

Tong Guogang, the concubine, and Fahai were a happy family of three, while Elundai and Kuadai, without their mother, seemed like outsiders in their own home.

This wasn't because Tong Guogang ignored his legitimate sons, but reality was just that cruel.

Most feudal heads of families wouldn't raise their children personally; their communication with their children, apart from education, was based on details of daily life learned from the children's mothers.

Children without a mother would inevitably be ignored by their father to some extent. This is what the world calls "having a stepmother means having a stepfather."

Elundai was originally the most valued legitimate eldest son in the family, receiving all the love, but suddenly became an outsider. Fahai, the son of a concubine, became more important in Tong Guogang's eyes because he had a mother who could whisper in Tong Guogang's ear.

Not to mention Kuadai, who was the same age as Fahai, who was even more like an invisible person.

There is always a reason for someone to go from an excellent heir to a rebellious, dissolute scoundrel.

When Elundai's excellence was no longer praised by Tong Guogang, what other way did he have to cross the high walls of the backyard to compete for his biological father's attention? What other way could he use to cross the high walls of the backyard to help his brother compete for his biological father's attention?

Look, he became the most eye-catching person in the family, and Kuadai began to be valued by Tong Guogang, receiving personal instruction from him.

Because his biological father was very worried that Kuadai would be corrupted by his own unfilial son, hahahahaha.

Elundai looked at the Crown Prince and suddenly felt he was a bit agreeable.

He was actually very jealous of the Crown Prince. Both were legitimate sons who lost their mothers, so why could the Crown Prince grow up under Kangxi's care, while he had to use all his strength to compete for his father's attention, eventually ending up in a state of fire and water with his father, wishing the other would die?

But now, looking at the Crown Prince's unusual calmness and excellence, and noticing his sickly body, he suddenly realized that the Crown Prince's life might not be as comfortable as he thought.

The Emperor was often not in the palace, and even when he was, he would linger in the harem. The Crown Prince was always left alone.

He still had a younger brother, but the Crown Prince's older brother was the son of another woman.

How did a little child continuously gain the Emperor's favor, and how did he coax his half-brother into acting as if they were full brothers? Behind the Crown Prince's extraordinary excellence, how much effort and pain was there?

Elundai couldn't imagine it, but he empathized with the Crown Prince.

"Crown Prince, First Prince, I was lying to them." Elundai whispered, "At this height, if I hold you and jump down, I can definitely land without a scratch."

The First Prince opened his eyes wide, but the little Crown Prince smiled with his eyes curved like crescent moons.

"Cousin, I know." Yinreng shook his little head, the little branch in the corner of his mouth swaying mischievously, "If you weren't sure, you wouldn't have carried us up the tree. You are very capable."

At this age, the traces of Elundai as the excellent legitimate eldest son of the Tong family had not yet disappeared. He was not yet the Elundai who had been a scoundrel his whole life and had completely become a waste.

After all, he was not yet twenty, just having left the period of a green youth.

"Am I capable? I am the famous little scoundrel of the Tong family." Elundai spat out the little branch in his mouth, "A waste famous for knowing nothing but eating, drinking, whoring, and gambling."

Yinreng said: "Cousin is the legitimate eldest son of the Tong family's main branch. If Cousin didn't receive good education, then there must be something wrong within the Tong family."

Yinzhi said: "I know about eating and drinking, but what are whoring and gambling? Are they fun? I often hear people talk about them."

Yinreng said nervously: "Not fun, those are bad things. If you get involved, Khan Ama will really break your butt! Not only will you get your butt beaten, you'll also be punished by having to copy books and be locked in a dark room!"

Yinzhi shrank his neck: "I was just asking, I don't want to do them."

Yinreng said seriously: "I'll explain it to you when we go back."

Elundai wanted to laugh.

He thought the First Prince was protecting the Crown Prince, but why did it seem like the Crown Prince was the older brother?

Elundai thought of his own brother, who was not yet ten but more mature than him.

Sigh.

He remembered his brother going to persuade Longkodo with his cousins, getting caught in the crossfire of Longkodo's fists and kicks, and his face turning black again.

Although Manchus started practicing archery and riding at six or seven, if it were the previous Emperor's time, Kuadai might have been on the battlefield killing enemies at this age, but that was the previous Emperor's time! Longkodo, how can you be so shameless!

Elundai prided himself on being a scoundrel, but he never fought with Fahai, only provoked Tong Guogang.

"Cousin, you should tell my brother later that these are not good things and he shouldn't learn them." Yinreng said, "I know you don't like these either."

"Actually... well, I don't like them." Elundai touched his nose.

He was just looking for excitement and liked to see Tong Guogang jumping with anger. If you asked if he liked them, he definitely couldn't say so.

Yinreng's eyes curved like crescent moons again: "Thank you, Cousin. You are the best."

Elundai patted Yinreng, feeling even more favorably toward him.

Why was this child's smile and little mouth so sweet? He didn't look like a child in the palace at all. Even among the Eight Banners children he had seen, there wasn't such a lovable child.

Kuadai was certainly very good, but Kuadai often had a straight face and didn't like to smile.

Kangxi was jumping with anxiety under the tree, while Elundai, the Crown Prince, and the First Prince were chatting and laughing on the tree, looking extremely relaxed.

Kangxi clutched his chest and held his forehead, his chest and head hurting even more.

No way, no way, the eldest son is one thing, but how can my well-behaved and lovely precious son also get along with Elundai, this big scoundrel!

"Your Majesty, are you not angry anymore? If you're not angry, can I carry the Crown Prince and the First Prince down?" Elundai saw the wind getting stronger and was afraid the two children would catch a cold, so he shouted down to the tree.

Kangxi had already passed the point of anger and was very calm.

He said in a deep voice: "Wait for the guards to bring the ladder."

Yinreng said: "Khan Ama, the ladder is also dangerous. Why not tie a basket with a rope and put me and my brother in the basket to lower us down."

Kangxi took a deep breath and said calmly: "Find a basket."

A basket was easier to find than a ladder.

Yinzhi went into the basket first to scout the way for his brother and was caught by Kangxi before he even landed.

Yinzhi stiffened, not used to being held by Kangxi.

Yinreng leaned out of the basket: "Ama, hold me!"

Kangxi was speechless.

He handed Yinzhi to Nalan Xingde to hold, and stood on tiptoe to lift Yinreng out of the basket in mid-air: "Why are you so naughty!"

Yinreng hugged Kangxi's neck and said with a grin: "I just wanted to play with Ama."

Kangxi gave Yinreng's head two taps, but couldn't bear to hit him hard.

Yinreng said: "Ama, don't punish Cousin. Cousin was afraid that you would be too angry and beat me and my brother, and then it would be you who would be sad."

"He put you two in danger, I must punish him." Kangxi said seriously.

Yinreng shook his head: "Ama, you underestimate Cousin. How could Cousin be as weak as he says? At this height, he can protect me and my brother."

Just as Yinreng finished speaking, Elundai jumped down from the tree by himself and landed steadily.

Kangxi glared at Elundai: "Go to prison and reflect on your actions!"

Yinreng said loudly: "Don't forget to give Cousin brush, ink, paper, and inkstone so he can write the memorial!"

Kangxi patted Yinreng's butt lightly and glared at Elundai again: "If you can't write a good proposal, don't be a guard anymore."

Elundai knelt down, performed a salute, and was honestly taken away.

Kangxi put Yinreng down and looked at his two sons: "Now, how should I punish you two?"

Yinzhi pulled Yinreng and wanted to run again, but was caught by the back of his collar by Kangxi.

Kangxi grinned.

Want to run?! Don't think you can use the same trick on me twice!
