Kuadai finished the test paper. Yinreng couldn't be bothered to correct it, so he had Liang Jiugong collect it and take it back to the palace for the Eldest Prince to correct himself.

Yinti, who was reciting a book, sneezed violently, spraying the teacher who was sitting there with spit.

Teacher: "..." He suspected the Eldest Prince did it on purpose.

Yinti rubbed his nose, wiped the saliva from the corner of his mouth, and muttered in a low voice: "It must be Father scolding me again. I hope Father isn't bullying my younger brother."

Teacher: "..." His ears were deaf at this moment. Yes, deaf.

The younger brother Yinti was muttering about had already gone to the outer city to play with E'lundai.

Nalan Xingde had serious work to do, so Cao Yin brought several guards to protect Yinti.

E'lundai originally didn't think much of Cao Yin, this bondservant. After a few collaborations, E'lundai lost his prejudice against this loud-voiced bondservant guard who, although beautiful, was first-class ruthless in his actions. The two could now be considered drinking buddies.

E'lundai asked Kuadai: "You really aren't coming out to play with me?"

Kuadai shook his head: "I have to recite my books. Father will test me when he returns."

E'lundai said: "Father won't mind if he knows you went out with the Crown Prince and the Third Prince."

Kuadai still shook his head: "I have a dull personality and don't know how to play with others. I’d better stay home and study."

"Suit yourself," E'lundai said.

When E'lundai left, he saw a small, furry head in the corner of the wall.

His footsteps paused, and a mischievous smile appeared on his face.

Cao Yin held his sword and said helplessly: "What are you going to do?"

E'lundai made a shushing gesture to Cao Yin and then pounced toward the corner of the wall.

Fahai, who was peeking from the corner, was lifted up by E'lundai like a chicken.

Fahai struggled hard: "What, what are you doing! Big Brother, let me go!"

E'lundai smiled maliciously: "What are you doing sneaking around in the corner? Could it be that you want to do something to the Crown Prince?"

Fahai was almost scared to tears by E'lundai: "I didn't! I was just passing by!"

E'lundai said: "If you were just passing by, why were you hiding?"

Fahai said: "I didn't want to be seen by you!"

E'lundai said regretfully: "I thought you were hiding from the Crown Prince and the Third Prince."

Fahai pouted. He didn't know that the two children who were dressed less luxuriously than him were the Crown Prince and the Third Prince!

If he had known, he would have hidden even more.

The late First Madam was a Gioro, a distant branch of the imperial clan. Although the First Madam’s family had fallen and no one held a title or official position, just by the surname "Gioro," if a prince came to the Tong mansion, he would definitely be coming to find the two children born to the Gioro.

Fahai knew that the grievances his mother was suffering now also came from the imperial palace.

No matter how unfilial E'lundai was, and no matter how much his father hated E'lundai, the imperial palace would always favor E'lundai because E'lundai was the child born to the Gioro and was closer to the imperial family.

Fahai studied hard, hoping to pass the imperial examination and win some dignity for his mother.

If he became a pillar of the Emperor’s court while his big brother and third brother were playboys, then no matter how much the Emperor favored the children born to the Gioro, he would still confer a title on his mother, right?

Looking at Fahai’s hostile gaze, Yinreng was confused.

It couldn't be that this Fahai was the reincarnation of his future political rival, the teacher of the Thirteenth and Fourteenth Princes, right? Otherwise, why would he glare at him?

Little Yinzhi put his hands on his hips and stood in front of Yinreng: "Why are you glaring at my Crown Prince brother!"

Fahai: "...I didn't. My eyes are just this big."

E'lundai shook Fahai: "Tong Guogang said he couldn't control his subjects because the Emperor favored children born to imperial clan women."

Fahai trembled: "No! Don't harm Father!"

E'lundai sneered: "He dares to say it, but doesn't dare to admit it?"

Yinreng waved his hand: "Alright, I can't manage your family’s affairs. But seeing that you like this younger brother, you specifically caught him to introduce him to me for what?"

E'lundai said with a straight face: "I don't like him."

Yinreng said: "If you didn't like him, you wouldn't have brought him to see me. Tell me, what do you want to do? We’ve climbed trees together and been punished together; we’re good buddies. If you have something to say, just say it, don't be wishy-washy."

E'lundai said helplessly: "Crown Prince, I am your cousin."

Yinreng said: "Let’s keep our own counts. By the way, shouldn't I also call him cousin?"

Little Yinzhi kept his hands on his hips and said foolishly: "So small? Cousin?"

Yinreng said: "That’s right, our generation is low."

Little Yinzhi said unhappily: "Father, useless!"

Yinreng hurriedly covered Little Yinzhi’s mouth, nervously saying: "Where did you learn that!"

Little Yinzhi shook his head and escaped from Yinreng’s hand: "Big Brother!"

Yinreng said with a dark face: "Don't learn from your big brother! You mustn't speak ill of Father, do you know that!"

Little Yinzhi nodded, half-understanding.

Cao Yin looked at the sky, wanting to whistle.

He could already imagine how ugly the face of that young but majestic Emperor would be when he reported today’s events to him.

E'lundai said: "Alright, I’ll be direct. He wants to take Nalan Rongruo as his teacher. But Tong Guogang doesn't want to have contact with the Nalan family."

Yinreng said: "Such a small matter, you can just tell Rongruo yourself; it’s not like you aren't familiar with him."

E'lundai said: "Tong Guogang doesn't allow it, and if I tell Rongruo, he won't be able to agree easily."

Fahai wanted to shout "I don't need your help," but the words couldn't come out.

He really admired Nalan Xingde so much and wanted to take him as his teacher, wuwuwu.

Damn it! Why am I so spineless! I must refuse!

Wuwuwu, my mouth, speak! Hurry up and speak!

Yinreng smiled: "With me speaking, Rongruo won't be in a difficult position? You are actually considerate of Rongruo’s difficulties."

E'lundai immediately said: "I’ve always been very good to the brothers among the guards."

Cao Yin rolled his eyes at the sky again. Who is your brother?

Yinreng said: "Small matter, I’ll agree on Rongruo’s behalf first."

E'lundai let go and said maliciously to Fahai: "Get lost."

Fahai pouted: "Why help me?"

Before E'lundai could spit out any more harsh words, Yinreng interrupted: "You are his younger brother, it’s just a small matter, he’ll help you if he can. But that’s not the point; the point is that Commander Tong doesn't want you to take Rongruo as your teacher, and he wants to cause trouble for Commander Tong."

Fahai was dumbfounded.

E'lundai said with a malicious smile: "It’s too late to refuse now. The Crown Prince is the heir, and his words are as golden as the Emperor’s. Since the Crown Prince said he would agree on Rongruo’s behalf to take you as a student, you are already Rongruo’s student, hahahaha. Just wait to be beaten by Tong Guogang."

Fahai took a deep breath and ran away crying "waa."

He was almost ten years old, already a grown-up, and hadn't cried like a child for several years.

Fahai decided he would hate E'lundai for the rest of his life!

Yinreng touched his nose: "Your brother cried."

E'lundai said: "Fun, I’ll do it again next time."

Little Yinzhi tilted his head. Although he didn't understand, it did seem fun.

Cao Yin sighed. So even though he and E'lundai had become drinking buddies, he still hated E'lundai very much. Bullying even children, what a character!

After getting into the carriage, Cao Yin went to the front to act as the driver. Other guards and eunuchs followed, some disguised as servants, others as passersby. E'lundai sat in the carriage, introducing the delicious and fun things in the outer city to Yinreng and Little Yinzhi.

Having just made his younger brother cry, E'lundai seemed completely unaffected, still wearing that lazy, cynical smile.

"I’ve already sent someone to notify my brothers." After leaving the Tong mansion, E'lundai couldn't expose the Crown Prince’s identity, so he naturally couldn't call himself a subject anymore. "They will bring you to play in a while, and we’ll surround you in the middle, you can play however you want."

Yinreng said huffily: "You Eight Banners children are so famous and conspicuous; if my brother and I walk among you, who wouldn't know we are princes? Besides princes, what other children have this status?"

E'lundai was dumbfounded: "Ah, that’s right. But I’ve already called them."

Yinreng said: "Aren't there many opera troupes coming to the capital recently? At lunch, we’ll go to the theater, find a troupe with good action plays, and eat while listening to the opera with your friends, and by the way, discuss the matter Father entrusted."

Little Yinzhi tilted his head again: "Father?"

Yinreng said: "It means Father. We’ll go to the outer city and pretend to be Han children; we’ll encounter fewer troubles."

E'lundai said firmly: "Manchus have fewer troubles."

Yinreng said: "I might go talk to some Han people."

E'lundai understood: "Oh, pretending to be Han children, so we’ll encounter more troubles."

Little Yinzhi: "..." Even though he was still young, he could hear that what his Crown Prince brother wanted to do was definitely not a good thing!

Yinreng added: "Brother, remember to call me Big Brother or Second Brother, don't call me Crown Prince Brother."

Little Yinzhi nodded.

When they got off the carriage, E'lundai’s group of drinking buddies were already waiting; they were almost all guards Yinreng was familiar with.

E'lundai told them, and they immediately scattered, pretending to play their own games, but in reality, they cooperated with the guards protecting Yinreng to share the responsibility of guarding.

Everyone was a guard; although they were a bit messy, they had all learned what guards should do.

Cao Yin was always surprised whenever he saw E'lundai commanding this group of playboys. E'lundai was unlearned and was chased and beaten by Commander Tong every day, yet he had quite a good reputation among the equally unlearned Eight Banners playboys.

When it came to playing, E'lundai was an expert.

From appreciating antiques and calligraphy to bird watching, cockfighting, and playing with crickets, both vulgar and elegant, E'lundai knew everything like the back of his hand.

Children just like excitement. Little Yinzhi watched the cockfighting feathers fly and clapped and laughed happily, saying he wanted to play cockfighting when he returned to the palace.

Yinreng said: "Don't play it when you return to the palace, Father will definitely beat you."

Little Yinzhi hadn't been beaten by Kangxi yet, so he didn't believe it.

Yinreng patted Little Yinzhi’s head: "You really will get beaten."

Cockfighting and playing with crickets involved gambling, and E'lundai’s hands were itchy, so he gambled a few times and lost everything.

When in Rome, do as the Romans do; Yinreng and Little Yinzhi also gambled a few times with small silver pieces and won everything.

The two princes generously rewarded the money they won to the penniless E'lundai.

E'lundai had no mother’s subsidy, and the meager salary he got as a guard and the meager pocket money given by his family were not enough for him to have a good time. Whenever he wanted to play something, E'lundai would always steal things from home to sell. Once, he accidentally stole something bestowed by the Emperor, and Tong Guogang was so angry that he said the classic line, "Please execute his son."

Getting the money rewarded by the princes, E'lundai beamed and turned around to throw half of the reward money to a guard who had come out with them.

Yinreng was puzzled.

E'lundai said: "He is shorter on money than I am."

Yinreng said: "You don't even have money yourself, yet you’re being generous?"

E'lundai said: "I have to look after the brothers who hang out with me."

Yinreng touched his nose. E'lundai’s overwhelming sense of chivalry; no wonder the playboys all respected him.

Yinreng suddenly asked: "Would you betray the brothers who trust you for the sake of your family?"

E'lundai sneered: "The Tong family? Are they worthy?"

Yinreng said: "I must warn you, the Tong family is my grandmother's family, so they are very worthy."

Cao Yin held back his laughter.

E'lundai was famously argumentative and eloquent, yet he had been rendered speechless by the little Crown Prince multiple times.

Satisfying!

E'lundai said helplessly: "Fine, cousin, you're right. Why did you suddenly ask this?"

Yinreng pinched his own chubby chin and said with ill intent: "Nothing, just suddenly curious. If you betrayed a good brother for the sake of your family's interests, causing his family to be ruined, what would you do?"

E'lundai said without hesitation: "I wouldn't."

Yinreng urged: "Just imagine, imagine. Hurry up and say it!"

E'lundai scratched his head: "I can't imagine such a thing at all. You say I'm just a useless playboy; when would there ever be a need for me to deceive others to seize benefits for the family? Tong Guogang is still alive and kicking, and Fahai and Kuadai are more reliable than me. Besides, I have self-awareness; I can't do things that involve deceiving brothers."

Yinreng thought to himself, it is precisely because everyone knows you are not that kind of person that you are the one who must do it.

Just think about what E'lundai did in the Eighth Prince's faction. Passing notes to officials to nominate Yinsi, running to the Jiangnan region to spread rumors about the Crown Prince to prevent his restoration... Not only were these foolish acts that made Kangxi's anger rise continuously, but they were also done with such fanfare that no one even needed to investigate who was behind them.

If anyone else had done this, the clansmen and nobles who nominated Yinsi as a puppet would have definitely thought this person had malicious intentions—what later generations call "feigning loyalty while rebelling." Because he was the big hoodlum E'lundai, no one else noticed that anything was wrong.

Oh E'lundai, E'lundai, the pillar of the Eighth Prince's faction, Niohuru Aling'a, was only one year older than your brother Kuadai; he grew up playing with you and treated you like a biological brother.

When you deceived him, did your heart ache? When you couldn't protect his son and had to personally deliver the decree to kill him, were you not in agony?

After you collapsed and destroyed yourself in pain, did you know that your brother piled all his hatred onto the only beneficiary chosen by the Tong family and sought revenge for you regardless of the cost?

The "Nine Lords' Struggle for the Throne" not only caused suffering for himself and his brothers but also plunged countless officials into an abyss of misery.

E'lundai's case is still considered mild. Those who were falsely accused of being in the Crown Prince's faction just for drinking together, who were sliced to death, nailed to walls to bleed out, and had their bones ground to dust after death...

Yinreng shook his head and sighed, tsk tsk. The memories of his second life finally served as a powerful buffer; he could actually recall all these memories without changing his expression.

In any case, the Nine Lords' Struggle for the Throne will never happen in this lifetime. He is going to send all his brothers out to seize territory. The Nine Lords' Struggle? It's just because they have too much idle time!

E'lundai said keenly: "I always feel like there's more to your words. Do you think I will do things against my nature for the family in the future?"

Yinreng said: "Of course. You are the eldest son of the main branch. If you don't take on the dirty and tiring work, do you have the heart to let Kuadai do those scheming and treacherous things?"

E'lundai touched the stubble on his chin: "Kuadai is impossible; you don't know how dull and stupid he is. Fahai is pretty good; let him do it."

Yinreng said: "Fahai has high integrity, but his temperament is stubborn. It's fine to let him study, but fighting for power and profit? He would be led into a ditch one hundred percent of the time."

E'lundai felt a headache: "The way you put it, only I can do it? Can't I go find my uncle?"

Yinreng said: "Your uncle isn't your own father. If you don't pay something, will he help you?"

E'lundai raised his hands: "Master, you are the master, my great master, stop scaring me. Hurry up and tell me, what do you want me to do? I'm not good with fear."

Yinreng smiled: "My father said, let you roll back to the official school to study hard and become a new person."

E'lundai's mouth twitched: "I knew I would definitely be sent to the official school. Anything else? If it's just this, you didn't need to scare me."

Yinreng said: "The point isn't rolling back to the official school, it's studying hard and becoming a new person."

E'lundai: "...So you scared me for half a day just to tell me to hurry up and study well?"

Yinreng said: "Otherwise?"

E'lundai rolled his eyes, completely disregarding that the child in front of him was the Crown Prince of the dynasty.

Cao Yin held back for a long time and couldn't help but laugh: "E'lundai, even the Second Young Master can't help but worry about you."

E'lundai spread his hands: "Completely unnecessary."

Yinreng said: "I don't want to care about you; it was Father who told me to persuade you more. My father has broken his heart for you."

Little Yinzi tugged at Yinreng: "Brother, how broken is his heart?"

Yinreng thought for a moment and said: "Probably something like, if he doesn't work hard, he'll be transferred to work in the study?"

Little Yinzi didn't understand, but he still raised his arms and shouted: "Copy books! Copy books!"

E'lundai shrank his chin and showed a shocked expression: "Cousin isn't afraid I'll smash the study?"

Yinreng smiled enigmatically: "You can try." Although he was lying to tease E'lundai, he now had significant weight in front of Kangxi, and the Kangxi of this life was also a playful character; he might actually agree to let E'lundai work in the study.

Yinreng couldn't help but laugh at the thought of E'lundai mixed in with a group of great scholars.

Cao Yin fanned the flames: "Good, good, very suitable for E'lundai, he should go and be influenced by the great scholars... Ouch!"

E'lundai kicked Cao Yin on the leg: "Get lost!"

Little Yinzi liked this good-looking guard Cao Yin very much, so he quickly stepped forward and kicked E'lundai on the ankle: "Not allowed to bully Guard Cao."

E'lundai widened his eyes in shock. He was actually kicked in pain by such a small child!

"Third Pri... Third Young Master's strength is a bit big." E'lundai flexed his ankle.

Cao Yin patted the dust mark E'lundai left on his leg: "Third Young Master's strength is indeed very big. The Master even said that Third Young Master's strength is even greater than the Eldest Young Master's."

Yinreng pulled Little Yinzi back to his side, shaking his head and saying: "That's not quite true. That father of mine, when evaluating his sons' martial arts, always likes to compare them to the Eldest Brother. Probably because the Eldest Brother is the oldest. Only a fool would believe him."

Even though their ages were very different, Kangxi always said this son was stronger than the eldest, that son was better at archery than the eldest, and another son was more handsome at riding than the eldest...

When Kangxi praised people, it was mostly when the little princes were just starting to learn riding and archery. At that time, if they really fought, the eldest brother could give them both hands, and they still wouldn't be able to break his defense.

"Father just wants to encourage my brothers. The Eldest Brother is very powerful, which is why he says the younger brothers are stronger than him." Yinreng patted Little Yinzi's head and sighed, "But everyone admires Father, and the comparisons that come out of Father's mouth will definitely hurt the person being compared. Although the Eldest Brother is the eldest, Father should also take care of his feelings. Isn't it bad to compare with outsiders? Why hurt your own sons?"

E'lundai's eyes flickered, and he grinned: "Probably because talking about others is boring, and only talking about family can make us have the heart to compare and compete."

Yinreng shook his head: "Brother, next time Father says such things, you must keep a straight face and sternly refuse Father's praise, telling Father that you are not allowed to compare with the Eldest Brother; if you win, the Eldest Brother will be sad, and if you lose, you will be sad, hurting the brotherhood."

Little Yinzi nodded: "Okay! I'll remember!"

Cao Yin looked at Yinreng with extremely kind eyes. He wanted to stay by Yinreng's side every day to soak up some good fortune, hoping to give birth to a child as sensible as Yinreng.

He must also remember these words well and report them to the Emperor word for word.

Cao Yin thought somewhat treasonously that the Emperor sometimes didn't handle things as thoroughly as the Crown Prince. The three princes now have such a good relationship; if you insist on saying one is better than the other, isn't that sowing discord between them?

E'lundai's hands felt itchy: "Second Young Master, can I touch your head?"

Yinreng took off his little hat: "Rub it."

E'lundai laughed loudly, lifted Yinreng up, held him in his arms, and rubbed vigorously: "If only you were my child."

Yinreng's head wobbled from E'lundai's rubbing: "You are my cousin, how am I not your child?"

E'lundai picked up Yinreng and hoisted him onto his shoulder: "Right."

Cao Yin remembered Yinreng's words to keep an eye on the Third Prince, that whatever Yinreng had, the Third Prince should also have. He immediately picked up Little Yinzi and put him on his shoulder.

Little Yinzi was stunned for a moment, then hugged Cao Yin's head and laughed hard: "So high!"

Yinreng asked: "Cousin, do you have enough strength?"

E'lundai patted the little short legs Yinreng had dangling in front of his chest: "Don't underestimate me. My martial arts may be rusty, but my strength isn't."

Cao Yin rolled his eyes: "You still know your martial arts are rusty."

With the two guards carrying the two children, the guards and eunuchs behind them looked on with extreme envy.

The intimacy E'lundai and Cao Yin had with the princes could almost guarantee the wealth of their next generation, right?

On the tea house by the street, three old men poked their heads out of the window.

If Cao Yin looked up at this moment, he would definitely be startled.

E'lundai wouldn't be startled. He had been a guard for so long that even if he saw them every day, he wouldn't recognize the faces of many Han officials.

These three old men were Wuying Hall Grand Secretary Huang Xigun, Fujian Governor and Minister of War Yao Qisheng, and Shi Lang, who had served as Fujian Naval Admiral but was now idle at home.

Yao Qisheng had traveled all the way from Fujian to Beijing because he was impeached by Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanwen and had come to defend himself.

Since he was already here, Yao Qisheng naturally immediately submitted a post to visit the Wuying Hall Grand Secretary Huang Xigun, who was also from Jinjiang, Fujian, and pulled in Shi Lang, who had always hoped to conquer Taiwan, the three of them conspiring to persuade Kangxi to conquer Taiwan immediately after finishing with the Three Feudatories.

As the three old men were drinking tea, Huang Xigun heard E'lundai's signature hearty laugh and subconsciously poked his head out to look.

Yao Qisheng and Shi Lang followed suit and poked their heads out: "Who is it? Do you know him?"

Huang Xigun said: "E'lundai, Tong Guogang's son."

Yao Qisheng and Shi Lang nodded together: "Oh, oh, oh." Yes, pretending to be very familiar.

Huang Xigun rubbed his eyes: "No way..."

Poke, poke, continue to poke.

Yao Qisheng handed over a telescope: "Can't see clearly? Here, try this."

As the Governor of Fujian, isn't it normal for him to carry a telescope with him?

Huang Xigun picked up the telescope and gasped: "Hiss!!!"

Yao Qisheng asked: "What? Scared by the telescope and bit your tongue? You wouldn't be that weak, would you?"

Huang Xigun returned the telescope to Yao Qisheng and glared at him fiercely, not knowing whether he should reveal the true identity of the child playing with E'lundai.

Although Shi Lang was old, his eyesight was excellent. He frowned and said: "Is that... Guard Cao Yin?"

The frontier official Yao Qisheng was confused: "Guard Cao? Who is that?"

Shi Lang said: "An Imperial Guard of the Qianqing Palace. Although he is a Booi, his mother was the Emperor's wet nurse, and he grew up in the Imperial Palace, deeply trusted by the Emperor. I once saw him when he was delivering an imperial decree."

Yao Qisheng: "And then?"

Shi Lang felt a bit uncertain and looked up at Huang Xigun.

Huang Xigun sighed and decided to tell the truth: "Those two children are from the palace."

Yao Qisheng's body suddenly lunged out the window, half of his body poking out.

Two children?! From the palace?!

There are only three children in the palace who can come out, and if you arrange them, the probability of the Crown Prince appearing is as high as two-thirds!

Although Yao Qisheng didn't know the three princes, he took one look at the ages of the two children and guessed their identities: "The Third Prince and... and..."

Huang Xigun nodded: "And the Crown Prince."

As a Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, although he didn't dare to talk to the princes, the little Crown Prince lived in the Qianqing Palace, and Kangxi's high officials had all seen the cute little Crown Prince bouncing around.

Sometimes when Kangxi gathered high officials to discuss matters in the Qianqing Palace, they would see the little Crown Prince's happy figure flash past the door or window, which was incompatible with their serious and formal discussion atmosphere.

In recent years, Kangxi had become increasingly doting on the little Crown Prince. He suppressed the requests from officials for the Crown Prince to study in the pavilion, and often held the little Crown Prince with him when discussing matters or listening to lectures, letting the little Crown Prince study with him.

Officials had many complaints, but Kangxi told the officials with complaints to shut up, and then the officials had no more complaints.

Thinking of this, Huang Xigun, who had once had complaints, felt particularly aggrieved.

If it were a previous dynasty, even if the Emperor rejected the officials' opinions, he would at least find a reason. But this barbarian Emperor just told them to shut up, and they didn't dare not to.

Of course, if it were other matters, they would definitely argue based on reason. But when it involved the Crown Prince, even someone as headstrong as Xu Yuanwen, who had just impeached the old man Yao Qisheng next to him, could only obediently hold it in.

Do you see the little Crown Prince on the Emperor's lap? This is the Emperor's reverse scale; don't touch it, don't touch it.

"Pretend we didn't see it?" Yao Qisheng asked.

Huang Xigun said: "Of course! Don't think about 'bumping into' the Crown Prince; the Emperor protects the Crown Prince very tightly."

Yao Qisheng was full of regret.

Yao Qisheng had many lifelong ideals, one of which was conquering Taiwan. If he gained the Crown Prince's support, would it...

"Sigh, this old man is obsessed." Yao Qisheng pulled back his upper body and patted his head, "The Crown Prince is so young, what can he manage?"

Shi Lang also nodded. If the Crown Prince were already an adult and had entered the court to deal with political affairs, that would be one thing, but he was so small, it was useless.

Huang Xigun thought to himself, that might not be the case.

When he lectured to Kangxi, although the little Crown Prince only whispered to Kangxi and never communicated with them, he knew that the little Crown Prince was definitely a prodigy from Kangxi's expressions of satisfaction, contemplation, or extreme headache.

There were also rumors in the palace that when the Crown Prince was only four or five years old, after Kangxi left the palace, he took the Empress Dowager's order to exercise his talents by managing the inner palace.

Huang Xigun observed the attitude of the palace eunuchs toward the Crown Prince; the love and respect were one thing, but the faint fear and the reverence as if seeing a god were very intriguing.

Du Lide, the spiritual leader of the Han officials in the palace, went against his stance of not contacting the princes and frequently contacted the Crown Prince, even supporting the Emperor's various exceptions in treating the Crown Prince, which made the Han officials perk up.

As long as Du Lide had not left the center of the court, his inclination was the direction for the Han officials to move forward. Whether it was the difference between North and South or the difference between civil and military, once Du Lide spoke, everyone would step aside.

This teacher of two emperors had single-handedly brought about a situation where more than half of the Han officials in the court were his students, and all Han officials knew that following Du Lide was absolutely correct.

"Grand Tutor Du once instructed all Han officials in the court that they must be respectful when seeing the Crown Prince, but they must never be close." Huang Xigun said, "Grand Tutor Du once said that the Crown Prince is very important to the Han officials. So in order for the Crown Prince to succeed to the throne smoothly, unless assigned by the Emperor, Han officials must never contact the Crown Prince without authorization."

Yao Qisheng, who was not in the capital, had also heard of the great name of Grand Tutor Du Lide. He said in surprise: "Grand Tutor Du would actually get involved in the dispute over the succession?"

Huang Xigun nodded: "He even specifically warned the leaders of the literary circles in the North and South. If the Crown Prince is in office, one must never get involved in the dispute over the succession, and one must not even publicly express support for the Crown Prince. He pointed out to us that we only need to tell the Emperor that everything is based on the Emperor's will and only be loyal to the Emperor."

Yao Qisheng stroked his beard and said: "If you don't want to support other princes and only want the Crown Prince to succeed, then officials should indeed not contact the Crown Prince and should be completely 'Imperial Party'."

Although forming cliques for private interests is not allowed, where there are people, there will be groups, and there will be factions. The Crown Prince's status comes from the Emperor and is the legitimate heir. So as long as the Emperor still loves the Crown Prince, supporting the Emperor is supporting the Crown Prince. If you want to be in the Crown Prince's party, you should be a die-hard Imperial Party.

As the heir, the Crown Prince has already shared the imperial power. If you want the Emperor not to be wary of the Crown Prince, the officials who want the Crown Prince to succeed must never surround the Crown Prince and let the Emperor think this is the Crown Prince's own power. This is the crystallization of the Han people's wisdom in the court for thousands of years.

After Du Lide became old, to prevent his late-life reputation from being ruined, he had already closed his doors to guests and became a silent clay bodhisattva in the court—in Du Lide's view, the last thing he did in the court was to establish a "perfect Han official" image in the Emperor's heart.

He was almost dead, and before he died, there must be no stain that would lower his favor in the Emperor's heart.

All clear-headed Han officials knew what Du Lide was doing now. And Du Lide had actually made a move, which surprised them extremely.

The little Crown Prince who made Du Lide use his last breath to manage the Han officials in the court made them even more curious.

Huang Xigun was also very old. He also wanted to retire.

Before retiring, Huang Xigun wanted to contact the little Crown Prince to see what abilities the little Crown Prince had that made Du Lide break his own rules.

But it was definitely not now, not by taking Yao Qisheng, who held heavy troops, to contact the little Crown Prince.

After listening to Huang Xigun's explanation, Yao Qisheng peered down again, scratching his head like a monkey.

Oh my, curiosity is aroused.

Shi Lang didn't have much of a reaction. He only wanted to be reinstated now and couldn't think about too many things.

When the three old men were poking their heads, Yinreng had already noticed them.

The tea house on the roadside was not too high, and three old men's heads suddenly poked out of the window. How could Yinreng, who was riding on E'lundai's neck, not notice?

His eyes weren't blind.

Yinreng was not familiar with Yao Qisheng and Shi Lang, but he recognized Huang Xigun at a glance.

Yinreng originally wanted to greet Huang Xigun, but Kangxi was not by his side today, so it was not easy for him to contact Kangxi's high officials, so he let it go.

Yinreng rubbed his little hands, then rubbed his face with his little hands.

Oh my, oh my, so curious. Huang Xigun, like Du Lide, basically closed his doors to guests and waited to retire. The old man who could come out to drink tea with Huang Xigun must be very famous.

Yinreng's heart felt as if a little kitten was grinding its claws.

If Father were here today, I could have dragged Father to "bump into" them. Yinreng decided that when he returned to the palace, he would tell Kangxi about today's events and let Kangxi find out what Huang Xigun was doing.

Yinreng had actually almost guessed the identities of the other two.

Huang Xigun was from Jinjiang, Fujian, and the only thing that would make him break his rules before retiring was naturally his hometown.

The various sufferings in Fujian were all because Taiwan had not been pacified. It just so happened that Fujian Governor Yao Qisheng had come to Beijing to report on his duties, so one of the two unknown old men must be Yao Qisheng.

The identity of the other unknown old man who looked very down-and-out was also ready to come out: he must be the former Fujian Naval Admiral Shi Lang, who had been dismissed by Oboi and others.

Shi Lang was the only naval talent in the Qing Dynasty today, and he was also the person who was most vigilant against foreign colonialists besides him. Yinreng had long kept this person in his heart.

After Shi Lang was dismissed by Oboi and others, his life was very miserable, and he relied entirely on his wife to work in a workshop in the capital to make a living.

When Yinreng was young, he heard Kangxi explain Taiwan and the navy, so he indirectly made Kangxi take care of Shi Lang's life. Kangxi bestowed a small villa on Shi Lang to live in; after he got in touch with his maternal grandfather's family, he let Changtai secretly take care of Shi Lang. Shi Lang's life had been pretty good in the past few years, at least he didn't have to rely on his wife to work for a living.

Shi Lang thought he had no connection and could not have any connection with the Crown Prince, but he didn't know that Yinreng had already quietly taken care of him when his own prospects were unclear and he was seeking a foothold by pretending to be a ghost.

Yinreng hugged E'lundai's head and turned to Cao Yin: "Guard Cao, remember to tell my father that there were three old men poking their heads out of the tea house to look at me just now, and one of them was Wuying Hall Grand Secretary Huang Xigun."

Cao Yin had also noticed it, but he didn't recognize who the three people were and was just about to send someone to investigate later.

Hearing the Crown Prince say this, he smiled and said: "Yes. Second Young Master has such good eyesight; I didn't even see it."

Yinreng exposed him: "You must have seen it, you just didn't recognize who it was."

Little Yinzi asked curiously: "Huang... Who is Huang Gungun?"

Huang Gungun... Cao Yin and E'lundai held back their laughter.

Yinreng kept a straight face and scared Little Yinzi: "Huang Xigun is a lecturer for the imperial lectures, the person who makes our father read, recite, and copy books."

"Wow!" Little Yinzi opened his eyes wide and leaned back, gasping, "So powerful, so scary!"

Cao Yin and E'lundai couldn't help but laugh.

Although Huang Xigun was indeed the person who accompanied the Emperor to study, who would dare to make the Emperor read, recite, and copy books 120 times? The Emperor wasn't the First Prince.

Wait, there really was someone who had done this!

Du Lide is watching you.jpg.

"Should we go up and find them?" E'lundai asked.

Yinreng shook his head: "Discuss poetry and books with them? Cousin, run!"

"Okay!" E'lundai carried the little Crown Prince and darted away at high speed.

"Hey, hey! Wait! Don't run so fast! It's dangerous!" Cao Yin was a step late and followed E'lundai in fear.

Little Yinzi waved his arms hard: "Flying! Flying!"

"Ah, Third Pri... Third Young Master, don't let go! Be careful not to fall!"

Yinreng hugged E'lundai's head, his soft little face pressed against E'lundai's head, laughing loudly. The milky laughter and E'lundai's wild laughter formed a symphony of laughter that gave Cao Yin behind them a headache.

Well, Cao Yin didn't know what a symphony was yet; let's call it the "Great Laughter Breaking Array Song" (...).

After they were tired of playing, they went to the theater to watch a play and eat, while discussing serious matters.

When the playboys learned that Kangxi was going to set up an official school, they all held their heads and showed extremely painful expressions.

"I don't want to go back to study."

"Who has the patience to read the words of the sages? Just kill me."

"Please let me rot in the mud; I don't need anyone to save me."

"I am rotten wood, I am rotten wood, I am rotten wood!"

Yinreng was so happy that his stomach hurt from laughing.

If this group of people were in later generations, they would definitely be members of the "sand sculpture" netizens, and might even become internet meme packages.

"Don't think about it, unless you can convince your families to give up on you." After Yinreng laughed enough, he said with a little straight face, "The official school is under militarized management; you are finished."

E'lundai was scared: "What is militarized management?"

Yinreng counted on his fingers and spouted nonsense, talking about morning runs, taking responsibility for one's own life, and folding quilts into small squares...

With a "thump," E'lundai was the first to smash his big face onto the table.

"Thump, thump, thump," there were many sounds one after another, as the playboys smashed their faces onto the table one after another.

The smile on Cao Yin's face disappeared.

He was deeply trusted and loved by the Emperor, so he would probably also be an exception to enter this official school, which was only eligible for Eight Banners children.

Is what the Crown Prince said true? This is a bit too much, right?

"You can at least choose what you learn now. If you don't hurry up, just wait to recite the Four Books and Five Classics." Yinreng hugged his arms, shook his head, and threatened, "Zhi hu zhe ye (classical particles)."

The playboys raised their heads, their young faces all wrinkled like 50 or 60-year-old men.

When did the cute, chubby-faced little Crown Prince become a scary little monster?

Please give us back our soft, kind little Crown Prince!

"Don't waste time." The chubby-faced little monster Crown Prince patted the table lightly, "My father is gathering your elders to revise the content of the official school. If you don't come up with a memorial that my father approves of before your elders set the learning content, this right to speak will fall to your elders."

The chubby-faced little monster Crown Prince scanned the crowd, his little mouth grinned, revealing his white little milk teeth: "As elders, they definitely hope that the suffering they experienced will be experienced by you twice over."

Gasps sounded in the room one after another.

Cao Yin held his forehead and said: "It's too noisy here; let's change places. The official school is not just our business; we need to unite more people."

E'lundai kept a straight face and said: "You are responsible for calling those young talents too. I think they definitely don't want to learn the 'Zhi hu zhe ye' they've already learned again."

Cao Yin sighed: "Of course."

He touched the little booklet the Crown Prince gave him in his sleeve.

Everything was as the Crown Prince expected; next, he just needed to bring out the details of the teaching content formulated by the Emperor and the Crown Prince.

Cao Yin's heart beat very fast. The Crown Prince was too monstrous, which made him feel a little uncomfortable.

He even suspected how much of the content written in this booklet was formulated by the Emperor? Could it be that it was all thought up by the Crown Prince alone?

Cao Yin looked at Yinreng.

Yinreng tilted his head and blinked at Cao Yin.

Cao Yin: "..." Well. The discomfort disappeared. My little Crown Prince is really too cute! Isn't it good to be smart? The Crown Prince should be this smart!

Cao Yin was not wrong; these contents were indeed formulated by Yinreng and reviewed by Kangxi.

Yinreng said a lot about the reasons for holding this official school, but there was one point he kept deep in his heart, which neither Kangxi nor Yinti knew.

The Eight Banners are rotten? Officials' retraining? These are not the real reasons.

Yinreng used many deep-seated reasons to cover up the fact that "holding an official school" itself was his goal.

It doesn't matter who enters the school; what Yinreng wants to do is just to run a new-style school in Beijing.

If he said he wanted to run a new-style school, he would definitely be opposed by everyone. Even if Kangxi acted more and more radically under his influence, he would definitely not support him.

Therefore, Yinreng stirred up the conflict between the Manchus and the Han, utilizing the Eight Banners' instinctive distrust of the Han people, as well as the stubborn Manchu nobility's disgust for Kangxi's promotion of Han studies, to make the emergence of "modern schools" a logical progression.

The Manchu and Mongol Eight Banners did not have much of their own culture or scholarship. They opposed Han studies, yet they did not know what else to teach their descendants.

If Yinreng provided them with a mature educational system completely different from the current Han academies and the imperial examination, they would use it as a weapon to oppose traditional Han studies and take the initiative to charge into battle for Yinreng.

The matter of modern government schools was the first time Yinreng had taken the initiative in the imperial court after his memories from both lives were fully restored.

In order to plan this, he almost slept for more than fifteen hours every day, turning into a real little lazy cat.

Once the young Eight Banners disciples in the capital all united to submit a petition, the subsequent work fell to Kangxi.

Yinreng was curious about what kind of modern government schools his father in this life could run, and whether he could cultivate pragmatic talents who were loyal only to the emperor.

Yinreng was also curious about what measures the Han officials would take after learning about these new government schools.

Yinreng was not worried that only holding government schools for the Eight Banners would cause the Han people to fall behind.

As the saying goes, "Once you have mastered literary and martial arts, you sell them to the emperor's house."

Most scholars study for the sake of becoming officials. Therefore, they learn whatever the imperial court needs and whatever the imperial examination requires.

For example, in the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, the imperial examination gradually turned into the eight-legged essay. Scholars became increasingly pedantic, knowing only how to write eight-legged essays.

Therefore, as long as the Eight Banners' government schools were established and pragmatic new learning and Western studies flourished in the court, Han scholars would definitely rack their brains to self-study and learn better than those Eight Banners disciples in the government schools.

When they started to learn these new subjects, they would realize how important they were. After realizing their importance, people of insight would certainly open new schools in their localities.

Do not underestimate the sharpness of the Han people. As long as you open a window for them and let them see the true appearance of the world, their ability to act will be violently unimaginable.

Yinreng only needed to provoke the people at the very top of the Qing Dynasty's pyramid, making them pursue new learning in order to oppose traditional Han studies, and that would be enough.

Yinreng returned home satisfied with his younger brother.

After hearing Cao Yin's report, Kangxi's attention was indeed drawn to the three prying old men: Huang Xigun, Yao Qisheng, and Shi Lang.

He laughed: "These three are colluding; they must be plotting something."

Taiwan will definitely be fought. After the battle, Taiwan will become the starting point for the Qing Dynasty to step out of the Central Plains and move toward the world.

The active movements of these three people perfectly matched Kangxi's expectations.

"Elundai..." After finishing the serious business, Kangxi sighed softly again, "Tong Guogang is truly incapable of managing his household affairs."

Although the inner household is a woman's business, a man cannot just wash his hands of it.

Kangxi, as the emperor, is busy with a thousand tasks a day, yet he still finds the energy to balance his harem.

"The Tong family's inner household is not very good," Kangxi added, "The men of the Tong family are all worrying when it comes to private matters."

The inner households of the two brothers, Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei, were both in chaos. Tong Guogang's wife, the Jue-luo clan, had laid a good foundation before she passed away, so despite Elundai's rowdiness, Tong Guogang's household was actually cleaner than the seemingly calm household of Tong Guowei.

Tong Guowei's sons followed suit; some were not even married yet, and their backyards were already in chaos, causing Noble Consort Tong to send verbal instructions back to discipline them time and again.

Poor Noble Consort Tong had become much more haggard.

"Elundai looks a bit chaotic, but his nature isn't bad; he even knows to find a teacher for his younger half-brother," Kangxi said. "Rongruo, I'll act as a lobbyist for the Tong family. When you have time, teach Fahai. Your family's traditions are good; you can let your mother teach Fahai about some inner household matters."

Nalan Xingde gave a wry smile: "I obey the decree."

Kangxi rubbed his forehead.

Sigh, the Hesheli family has calmed down, and now the Tong family is giving him a headache again. Relatives of the emperor are truly restless.

Speaking of the emperor's relatives...

"Changtai resigned to go home and nurse his father-in-law, but he didn't even send me a memorial to tell me about his father-in-law's condition," Kangxi complained. "Forget it, since he won't say, I'll go see for myself."

Thus, Changtai, who was squatting in the cow shed completing the "cowpox experiment" ordered by Yinreng, unknowingly welcomed Kangxi and the little Crown Prince who had snuck out of the palace.

Covered in straw and mud, Changtai was squatting on the ground observing the cow with pox, while Kangxi, holding Yinreng, poked his head out from the corner of the wall to observe Changtai, who was supposed to be nursing his father but was instead in the cow shed.

"What is your uncle doing?" Kangxi whispered.

Yinreng said: "Wanting to drink fresh milk?" Of course, it was to observe cowpox. But the cowpox inoculation experiment didn't need to observe cowpox! Uncle, what are you doing!

Kangxi gathered his breath in his dantian, stepped out from the corner, and roared: "Changtai! What are you doing!"

Changtai was startled: "Ah?!"

The cow was also startled.

It lifted its hind leg, and the current Imperial Uncle and future brave general, Changtai, was kicked to the ground by the cow.

57. First and Second Update [V]

Choosing the path of a military general, Changtai had naturally thought about the scene of being seriously injured.

Perhaps it would be a dark night with clouds obscuring the bright moon.

He would hold a broadsword, ambushing the enemy camp in the rustling light snow. The snow would melt on the back of his blade, and the snow and blood would drip from the blade onto the white snowy ground, like beautiful red plum blossoms blooming in the snow.

Perhaps it would be in a mountain forest filled with thick fog.

He would draw his bow and shoot arrows, while the opponent's arrows would also rain down. Every arrow decorated with carved feathers would take an enemy's life, but the enemy's arrowheads would also sink into his body.

Perhaps it would be when the two armies were engaged in battle.

On the vast battlefield, countless soldiers would be divided into two sides. At the sound of a command, he would ride his steed into the enemy formation, the long sword in his hand flashing with cold light, and the blood rain it brought up would make it impossible to tell whether it was spurting from his own body or someone else's.

Changtai was both a warrior and a scholar. While nursing his father, after his father fell asleep, he would often sit on the steps in front of his father's door, looking up at the sky, imagining himself fighting on the battlefield, being seriously injured, or even dying in battle.

Changtai had thought of many, many things, but he never expected that his first serious injury would be in such a situation.

When the imperial physician spat out the cruel and merciless words "bone fracture," the culprit, Emperor Kangxi, not only felt no guilt but also laughed out loud while pounding the table.

Changtai was expressionless, his eyes unfocused.

This was the biggest blow he had encountered in his life since he was born.

Yinreng couldn't bear to watch anymore. He tugged at the sleeve of Kangxi, who was laughing until tears were streaming down his face: "Father, stop laughing. If you keep laughing, Uncle is going to cry."

Kangxi laughed even harder: "Good, let me see how he cries!"

Changtai glanced at Kangxi, his expression indifferent, and he calmly shifted his gaze away, continuing to stare blankly.

Kangxi laughed until he was out of breath, wiping his tears while swaying over to Changtai: "That cow is really hateful! How dare it kick and injure you! I will order someone to slice that cow into a thousand pieces right now to go with your wine!"

Changtai: "..."

He wanted to commit regicide.

Although it was just a thought, he really wanted to commit regicide right now.

Kangxi added with a laugh: "But the main thing is still your fault. Why were you squatting in the cow shed watching the cow? A gentleman does not stand under a dangerous wall, understand? You need to reflect on yourself properly."

Changtai: "..."

He wasn't just thinking about it anymore; his fists were already clenched.

Kangxi was still laughing unscrupulously: "You, are you really wanting to drink milk directly?"

Changtai: "Your Majesty, if you keep laughing at me, I'm going to throw the incense burner by the bed at you."

Kangxi immediately put his hands under Yinreng's armpits and lifted his son up to block in front of him: "Go ahead and throw."

Yinreng was passively spreading his arms with a blank expression, his short legs kicking helplessly.

Changtai took a deep breath, and another deep breath. He closed his eyes and turned his head away, refusing to look at Kangxi.

Kangxi retracted his arms and rubbed his son in his arms: "Hahahahaha."

The young Changhai leaned against the door frame and saw this scene, then quietly returned to the bedridden Gabula, reporting what he had seen and heard with a pout.

Changhai had tears in his eyes: "The Emperor is laughing so wildly, and Big Brother looks so pitiful."

Gabula coughed while saying: "This is a sign that the Emperor and your Big Brother have a good relationship."

Changhai said: "Big Brother definitely doesn't want to have such a good relationship with the Emperor."

Gabula sighed.

That is certainly true. When you have a good relationship with the Emperor, it becomes easy to blur the boundaries between monarch and subject.

Just like the allusion of sharing a peach in history books. When you eat a very sweet peach, you immediately give it to the Emperor. When you have a good relationship with the Emperor, the Emperor will say you are eager to share everything good with him; when the Emperor dislikes you, he will say that you dare to give him something you have already eaten, which is an insult to him.

Killing with kindness and overstepping one's bounds always go hand in hand. After the Emperor leaves, he must warn Changtai again.

Gabula coughed a few more times.

Long-term illness makes one a doctor. Gabula vaguely sensed that he probably wouldn't live past this winter. He had to take advantage of the time he could still speak to warn Changtai and Songgotu more. Lest after he died, the two of them would have no reins on their necks and be blinded by the Emperor's favor.

The little Crown Prince might be able to remind them, but the little Crown Prince was already tired enough; they couldn't always rely on him.

Changhai was still chattering and complaining that the Emperor was so naughty, even naughtier than him.

Gabula smiled.

Indeed, the Emperor's naughty side in private was truly surprising. If the Emperor had treated his daughter with this attitude, her life shouldn't have been too difficult when she was alive.

Gabula lay back on the bed. Changhai replaced the injured Changtai to serve his sick father.

Poor Changhai grew up overnight and took on the affairs of the household. The reason for all this was that Changtai was kicked by a cow.

Who knows who spread this matter—it was most likely Emperor Kangxi himself. In just a few days, Changtai became the laughingstock... the talk of the capital.

When the Emperor went to visit Changtai, Changtai was observing the family's cow, and the little Crown Prince's voice startled the cow, causing Changtai to be kicked.

The inexplicably scapegoated little Crown Prince Yinreng: "???"

Yinreng said resentfully: "Father, do you have no shame?"

Emperor Kangxi, who was spreading gossip about Changtai being kicked by a cow while pushing the blame onto his son, coughed and changed the subject: "I didn't expect Changtai to gain experience in preventing smallpox by raising cows. If cowpox inoculation can really prevent smallpox, giving Changtai a separate first-class duke title would be well-deserved."

Yinreng said resentfully: "Father, is half of this separate first-class duke title to compensate Uncle for his bone fracture?"

Kangxi couldn't keep up the act; he continued to laugh until his sides ached.

For the past few days, he couldn't stop laughing whenever he thought of or mentioned this matter; it was just too funny.

His brother-in-law's personality was very serious, cautious, and earnest. Sometimes Kangxi even disliked Changtai for being so stubborn and dull in his adherence to etiquette, making him very uninteresting.

That was why it was even funnier that Changtai had made such a fool of himself.

Whenever Kangxi thought of Changtai's incredulous expression when he was injured, he felt incredibly good.

"Yes, that is indeed the case," Kangxi said very honestly.

Yinreng shrugged and sighed.

Is being an emperor so great! Can an emperor not only feel no guilt after causing a subject to be injured and make a fool of himself, but also add fuel to the fire?!

Yes, being an emperor is indeed great.

Yinreng climbed onto Kangxi's lap, and Kangxi leaned back a little to make Yinreng sit more comfortably.

"Cowpox," Yinreng said, "If it's useful, let's inoculate the brothers and sisters in the palace first, okay?"

Kangxi rubbed Yinreng's head: "Of course. Sigh, if only back then..."

Kangxi thought of Emperor Shunzhi.

People could still be inoculated now, but they were inoculated with human pox, which was still relatively dangerous and very rare. If it were replaced with cowpox, not only would the danger be greatly reduced, but the cost of inoculation would also drop sharply. Even ordinary people with their own cows could try to inoculate themselves if they weren't afraid of the danger.

"Father, such a great merit as promoting cowpox will surely lead the common people to build a merit monument for you," Yinreng said. "Congratulations to Father for taking a huge step toward becoming an emperor for the ages."

Kangxi proudly rubbed his son's soft cheeks.

That's right. He wouldn't steal Changtai's credit, but the credit of his subject and brother-in-law was naturally also the credit of him, the emperor.

The two merits of preventing earthquakes and promoting cowpox were enough to push his reputation among the people to its peak. Everything he did next would be much easier.

Those nobles and imperial clansmen who coveted his imperial power would also have to weigh their options.

Next, he only needed to pacify the Three Feudatories and Taiwan, sweep away domestic affairs, and then he could stretch his limbs and compete for world hegemony with other countries in the world.

An emperor of China, no matter how good he is, can only be on par with the enlightened monarchs of past dynasties. As Kangxi looked at the world map and gradually clarified the distribution of forces in various countries, his ambition could not help but grow larger and larger.

Those countries were originally far inferior to the Qing Dynasty and China. Just because they had colonies, their wealth had gradually caught up with the Qing Dynasty.

They had endless gold and silver, countless food, and inexhaustible populations.

The Qing Dynasty is not a Han regime to begin with, and it has its own national conditions. What they can do, the Qing Dynasty can also do.

Kangxi looked at the memorial Changtai had submitted while recovering from his bone fracture, his eyes glowing with the burning flames of ambition.

Yinreng sat on Kangxi's lap, holding Kangxi's teacup with both hands, looking up to drink tea and looking down to exhale.

No young emperor with both talent and ambition could refuse the temptation of a world map.

Father, work hard to become the world hegemon and an emperor for the ages; don't let down the honor of being "Saint."

While the Eight Banners nobles and imperial clansmen in the capital were laughing at the unlucky Changtai, an imperial decree from Kangxi made them unable to laugh anymore.

Inoculate cowpox to prevent smallpox?

Is this why Changtai was squatting in the cow shed and kicked by a cow?

I don't believe it! How can humans be the same as livestock!

Memorials impeaching Changtai flew into the Qianqing Palace like snowflakes, and no one even cared about Yao Qisheng, who was being impeached.

Yao Qisheng scratched his remaining few hairs, feeling a bit at a loss.

He had wanted to take the opportunity of self-defense to reiterate the importance of a full-scale war on Taiwan. Now that all the officials in the court were talking about cowpox, his talk about Taiwan seemed out of place?

Although it was out of place, Yao Qisheng still submitted the memorial.

Taking advantage of the fact that all the officials were attracted by cowpox, Kangxi hurriedly reinstated Shi Lang and let him rebuild the Fujian navy.

He summoned Shi Lang and showed him the world map.

"The Qing Dynasty can go wherever the foreigners can go," Kangxi tapped the world map hanging on the wall. "If their navy dares to come and snatch the Qing Dynasty's territory, we will not only drive them away like Zheng Chenggong did, but we will also go to their territory to take a look and let them see the national prestige of the Qing Dynasty."

"It is impolite not to return a favor!"

Shi Lang looked up at the ambitious young emperor and knelt down, kowtowing heavily: "I will definitely build the strongest navy for Your Majesty that looks down upon the world!"

Shi Lang's greatest wish was originally just to defeat the Zheng family and recover Taiwan.

Now the young Qing emperor told him that the Zheng family was just a whetstone for the Qing navy, and Taiwan was just the starting point for the Qing navy.

The true opponent of the Qing navy was the whole world.

England dares to call itself the empire on which the sun never sets, and Spain, Portugal, and France dare to call themselves maritime hegemons. The Qing Dynasty is more powerful than them; how can there be no Qing flag on this world map?!

Yao Qisheng stood in the corner. He wanted to say something. For example, do not be overly ambitious, or do not snatch other people's land and wealth.

But in the end, he said nothing.

The Qing Dynasty is not the Ming Dynasty, not the Song Dynasty, and even more radical than the Tang Dynasty.

It is ambitious, like the Han Dynasty that swept the Western Regions, and even more like the Qin Dynasty that destroyed the six states.

Once it discovers broader fields and richer wealth, it will not stop its pace of conquest.

Since its founding, the Qing Dynasty has been a plunderer and a conqueror.

Yao Qisheng lowered his head.

Long-term Confucian education told him that such external expansion and plunder by the Qing Dynasty were wrong. But the increasingly strong heartbeat in his aging body told him, no, that's not what you think.

Yao Qisheng tucked his hands, which were hanging at his sides, into his sleeves, his clenched fists trembling slightly.

"Your Majesty, if you want to send the navy out, the coastal ports should be rebuilt," Yao Qisheng suddenly raised his head, the smile on his weathered, furrowed face somewhat distorted. "Listening to Your Majesty, our military power must be effectively converted into commercial tax revenue, otherwise the blood of the Qing navy will have been shed in vain."

Kangxi stood with his hands behind his back, looking up at the world map and nodding.

As long as all this is converted into what the northern nomadic tribes once did, it can be understood.

Fight first, and after winning, demand annual tribute and offerings, open border markets to promote trade, collect taxes on Qing territory but pay no taxes when selling things on the other side's land... In the five thousand years of Yan and Huang, our ancestors have experienced many things. Just flip through the history books, and you can find examples to learn from.

Kangxi closed the door of the study and told the two ministers who had a clear understanding of the importance of the navy about the world situation.

In the eyes of the two old ministers, the door to the world slowly opened, and the world scene settled in their hearts.

They were already old and might not have many days left to live after finishing the Taiwan battle. So they were very nervous, not knowing if they could see the magnificent sight of the Qing Dynasty's giant ships sailing to all parts of the world in their lifetime.

Perhaps they should focus on cultivating naval talents and entrust their hopes to future generations.

Fortunately, Shi Lang had many capable sons, and Yao Qisheng also had an eldest son, Yao Yi, who inherited his mother's immense strength.

After leaving the study, Yao Qisheng pondered about writing a letter to his wife immediately, telling her not to supervise the other children's studies for the imperial examination anymore; they wouldn't achieve anything, so she should hurry and teach them martial arts.

Yao Qisheng's wife, the He clan, was strong enough to walk leisurely while carrying a stone mortar, which Yao Qisheng found astonishing, so he hurriedly asked to marry her.

Yao Qisheng himself was a weak old man; if his wife hadn't protected him on the battlefield, he didn't know how many times he would have died.

Because Yao Qisheng knew that as a Han person, it was difficult to gain the complete trust of the imperial court in the circle of military generals. So, except for the eldest son who inherited his mother's talent, the other sons were forced to study.

But Yao Qisheng himself was only a Juren, and his sons really didn't have much talent for studying, not even managing to become Xiucai.

Forget it, let them throw away the pen and join the army.

After Kangxi summoned Yao Qisheng and Shi Lang, he called for Songgotu and Mingzhu.

Although these two old companions of Kangxi had caused Kangxi great trouble by forming cliques for personal gain, in terms of ability, if they cooperated, they would be invincible.

Fortunately, Songgotu was now well-behaved, and Mingzhu was also more low-key, so Kangxi was willing to give them another chance.

Kangxi tapped the world map: "See that! Don't use your minds for infighting; this is what you should be considering."

Songgotu stared at the world map foolishly for a long time, then said in disbelief: "Why is the Qing Dynasty's territory so small?!"

Mingzhu looked at the foolish Songgotu speechlessly.

No way, no way? Changtai is known as the first person in the court to know about world affairs, and he has repeatedly claimed that he was taught by you. You haven't even seen a world map?

Mingzhu suddenly felt some sympathy for Changtai.

Changtai kept praising Songgotu outside, trying to create the illusion that the uncle and nephew were working together, but unfortunately, this Songgotu, humph, is incompetent!

Kangxi was also speechless: "Your father-in-law's study has a world map. Your father-in-law has studied it; haven't you?"

Songgotu: "...I thought Big Brother was lying to me."

Kangxi opened his mouth, actually not knowing what to say.

He asked again: "There are so many foreign language books in your father-in-law's study; haven't you read them?"

Songgotu: "Who has the patience to read those ghost symbols."

Kangxi began to doubt life. Is Songgotu really an important minister of the country? Is he really capable?

Songgotu is indeed very capable, but he is also very conservative and does not like to learn new things.

Although Mingzhu had gathered his forces and no longer fought for power with Songgotu in the court, he would definitely be the first to jump up if something could make Songgotu miserable.

"Your Majesty, you should hire some teachers for Lord Song. He doesn't even understand foreign languages and doesn't recognize the map; it will be difficult in the future..." Mingzhu glanced at Songgotu with a half-smile, "I have already started learning."

Kangxi nodded solemnly: "That makes sense. Even the First Prince can speak English, and you are not as good as the First Prince."

Songgotu hadn't reacted yet, but Mingzhu's heart skipped a beat.

What?! The First Prince can speak English?? I'm still memorizing words!! Am I not as good as the First Prince!!

Mingzhu's mind conjured up the image of the First Prince standing proudly with his hands behind his back. Then this figure began to split, and accompanied by the First Prince's loud voice, it kept spinning in Mingzhu's mind.

Mingzhu quietly covered his chest, his figure trembling slightly.

Just recalling the First Prince made Mingzhu almost vomit blood. He absolutely could not lose to the First Prince!

Songgotu rolled his eyes at Mingzhu: "Learn then. If Mingzhu can learn it, I definitely have no problem."

Mingzhu straightened his body: "Heh."

Seeing the two important ministers fighting with eye daggers again, Kangxi also felt "heh" in his heart.

Forget it, as long as they don't form cliques, don't seize power, and don't delay serious business, it doesn't matter if they don't get along.

After Songgotu and Mingzhu fought to a draw with eye daggers, they looked up at the world map again.

He frowned and said: "After seeing the situation of various countries on the map, I realized that Tsarist Russia has repeatedly violated our borders. Could its hidden purpose be here?"

Songgotu reached out and tapped lightly on the area around Sakhalin Island.

In terms of overall control, Mingzhu was not as sharp as Songgotu. Mingzhu was good at understanding people and discovering talent.

However, as soon as Songgotu pointed it out, Mingzhu immediately realized Tsarist Russia's intention.

"Tsarist Russia wants to go to sea." Mingzhu gasped, "Could they be wanting to build a port here?!"

Kangxi was stunned for a moment. Is, is that so? Is that it?

Kangxi was busy with many things, and the matter of Tsarist Russia had to be put aside; he hadn't thought about it there yet. Although he knew that Tsarist Russia was eyeing the Qing Dynasty, he only thought that Tsarist Russia was like the Netherlands, which had once occupied Taiwan, and just wanted to plot more land.

He revealed a profound expression: "You finally discovered it."

Songgotu sighed: "Your Majesty must have seen it long ago, which is why you insisted on letting Sabusu resist the enemy despite all opposition. My vision is indeed narrow. If I hadn't seen the world map and listened to Your Majesty's explanation of the world situation, it would be like a blind man touching an elephant or looking at a leopard through a tube; it would be difficult to detect the true intentions of foreign countries."

Mingzhu also nodded: "After seeing the world map, I realized that Tsarist Russia's environment is so harsh that it doesn't even have an ice-free port for sailing. Their multiple large-scale actions and multi-point attacks on the Qing border were actually to cover up their true intentions."

Although Songgotu hated Mingzhu, he still recognized Mingzhu's talent, otherwise he wouldn't have regarded Mingzhu as a great enemy.

He agreed: "The Qing Dynasty has the Three Feudatories and Taiwan in the south, and the Mongol tribes are restless in the north. If Tsarist Russia agrees to negotiate when the Qing Dynasty is tense in other places, giving up most of the land and only keeping this line..."

Suoetu circled the lower reaches of the Heilongjiang River, near its mouth.

"If we didn't know their true intentions, we would certainly agree."

Suoetu was in a heavy mood, even feeling somewhat annoyed.

Suoetu was responsible for the logistical deployment of military campaigns across various regions, so if a ceasefire was called on the Heilongjiang River, Kangxi would undoubtedly send him to negotiate. If he failed to discover Tsarist Russia's true intentions, wouldn't he be tricked by them?

Mingzhu also thought of this. However, he did not feel any Schadenfreude. Because the probability of him and Suoetu being sent to negotiate was a 60-40 split, and he could just as easily be the one who got tricked.

"If Tsarist Russia builds a port here, they will certainly train a navy here as well. With Tsarist Russia stationing troops on the Qing border, there will surely be no peace here in the future," Suoetu said, gnashing his teeth. "Since they want a port, they must want to follow the path of external plunder taken by countries like England. Who's to say they don't also harbor the intention of heading south along our coastline to plunder?"

The Eight Banners army was formidable, making it difficult for Tsarist Russia to advance by land. But the Qing navy was very weak; if they launched plundering raids from the coast, the Qing would be in serious trouble.

Mingzhu nodded: "A grand national strategy is measured in centuries. Even if they don't come in this generation, the moment the Qing's national strength weakens just a fraction, they will bare their fangs."

Suoetu said: "They border various European countries to the west. Perhaps when they bare their fangs, it won't be just one nation, but multiple nations coming together to plunder interests from our Qing. Tsarist Russia, which understands the Qing best, is the vanguard."

Mingzhu asked: "If we implement a ban on maritime trade..."

Suoetu shook his head: "Unless we cover the Qing with a giant dome, they will certainly manage to plant people to gather our intelligence. To say nothing else, when those missionaries who outwardly show utmost respect to the Qing see their home countries come into conflict with the Qing, would they stand on the Qing's side? They might not even need missionaries; they could simply spend some money to get the information they want from the Qing people."

Mingzhu sighed, and then his expression turned fierce: "Then we can only fight outward! Fight them until they dare not come over! If they can plunder, why can't we of the Qing?"

The two high-ranking officials bantered back and forth, completely clarifying the situation between the Qing and Tsarist Russia.

Kangxi's expression was calm, his eyes as deep as an abyss, as if all the deductions and judgments made by Suoetu and Mingzhu were entirely within his expectations.

That's right. How could an emperor who opened his eyes to see the world earlier than his subjects not know Tsarist Russia's true intentions, and the sinister motives spanning a hundred or several hundred years that might be hidden behind those intentions?

Kangxi understood it all by heart, Kangxi was full of confidence, Kangxi...

Kangxi was a little confused.

While putting on an expression that said, "Zhen understands, Zhen understands very well, Zhen cannot possibly understand any better," he was inwardly pondering why he had overlooked this matter.

Could it be that Zhen is not as smart as Suoetu and Mingzhu?！！

No!!! Zhen does not accept this!!!
