60. Third and fourth updates (Overlord ticket bonus update) [V]

Kangxi did not think he was being reckless.

He believed he had passed the age of recklessness; everything he did was well-planned, and he had foreseen the consequences.

Kangxi had wanted to abolish the queue order ever since he learned the cause and effect of the curse several years ago.

The queue order was the reason why there were still resistance uprisings everywhere in the Great Qing. The more the people resisted, the more the Manchus feared, and the more they wanted to enforce the queue order. Kangxi had originally thought the same. But after learning of Shunzhi's ideals and seeing the world situation clearly, Kangxi's thinking changed.

Since the Manchus were also descendants of Yan and Huang, and he was going to promote the unification of Yan and Huang, then hair and such no longer mattered.

His territory would welcome envoys from countries all over the world; people of different skin colors, different eye colors, and different attire would become his subjects. If he forced everyone from all over the world who integrated into the Great Qing to shave their hair and change their clothes, would he have enough troops to suppress them? Would those people oppose the Great Qing because they hated these troublesome matters?

Both publicly and privately, Kangxi had sufficient reasons to act against the queue order.

It just so happened that the queue order appeared when Dorgon was regent.

It was Dorgon who gave the order, and Dodo who executed it; by the time Shunzhi personally took power, they had already entered the pass. Therefore, Kangxi could distance his father and himself completely from this matter, pretending to be an innocent white lotus in front of court officials and the people.

To be a qualified emperor, one must be thick-skinned; when it's time to shift the blame, one must shift it. As long as he shifted the blame, Kangxi's move against the "queue order" would not be considered a violation of ancestral rules.

Thus, another problem was solved.

Next came the opposition from the Eight Banners nobility and the imperial clan.

Kangxi needed to wait for a good opportunity, one where even if the Eight Banners nobility and the imperial clan opposed him, it would be useless and would not endanger his throne.

While it seemed that the Revolt of the Three Feudatories had left the imperial army fighting outside and Kangxi's central military strength empty, in reality, this was the perfect time for Kangxi to act.

The imperial clansmen and nobles who held military power in the court were all on the battlefield, and their families were in the capital; they would have reservations about rebelling.

The army suppressing the Three Feudatories included not only the Eight Banners but also Ming dynasty defectors; this group would absolutely support Kangxi's reform of the "queue order" and help him keep the Eight Banners army in check.

Furthermore, if the Eight Banners army showed any flaws, the Three Feudatories would surely make a comeback, dragging the Eight Banners army onto the battlefield.

The Eight Banners army fighting outside would likely not mutiny, but what about the capital?

The remaining defense forces in the capital were already in the hands of people Kangxi trusted. Before Kangxi made this decision, military affairs inside and outside the capital were controlled by the Tong and Heseri families; Changtai, whose bone fracture had not yet healed, was appointed as the Commander of the Nine Gates, taking office while injured to guard the capital.

Kangxi had also long since gained high prestige among the young Eight Banners disciples by sharing tasks with them and helping them resist their elders.

To these young Eight Banners disciples who grew up inside the pass, they scoffed at the things the older generation of Manchus worried about, believing that since the Great Qing had already been established, those feelings of inferiority and resistance were just looking for trouble.

Moreover, the young Eight Banners disciples thought their hairstyles were ugly, and it was very inconvenient to shave their heads all the time; razors often cut their scalps, which was particularly troublesome. If only they didn't have to shave.

Elundai, who was entrusted with an important task by Kangxi at this moment, grinned with a mouthful of white teeth and gathered the children of conservative nobles and the imperial clan: "You wouldn't betray the Emperor, would you?"

A group of playboys around him rolled up their sleeves and prepared for action.

The colleagues shook their heads one after another. Don't dare, wouldn't, don't talk nonsense!

As for the situation in the palace, Kangxi also believed it was very stable.

Next was the common people.

Kangxi's reputation among the people had already been rising steadily due to his prediction of earthquakes and the promotion of cowpox. The people almost regarded Kangxi as a reincarnated deity, and many had secretly set up longevity tablets for him.

Regarding the shaving of hair, the common people actually still felt a bit uncomfortable about it.

Compared to culture or tradition, the uneducated common people didn't have those thoughts. What they thought was that it was really too inconvenient.

In later generations, men would find it troublesome to shave their beards every day, and a slightly dull razor would cut their faces.

In this era, how sharp a knife could you find? Especially for ordinary people, a knife at home might be used for a lifetime and still have rust on it. Cutting the head might lead to death from tetanus.

In the early Qing dynasty, the queue had to be a "money-rat tail" that could pass through a copper coin. When the common people's hands shook, they all ended up looking like monks, and they could only use mud paste to stick two strands of hair on.

Therefore, the part shaved in the Great Qing's "queue order" decreased year by year, and the queue left behind increased year by year. In the end, the bald scalp was no longer the symbol of the Manchus; the thick, shiny long queue was. In the late Qing dynasty, many people just shaved their temples and a small circle on their foreheads and braided their hair to finish it.

Kangxi wanted to change the "queue order," which saved the common people so much trouble and time; naturally, they raised both hands in welcome.

Look, didn't Kangxi consider everything very thoroughly? Wasn't everything under his control?

Then the question arises, why did Kangxi suddenly issue the decree now?

Yinreng hugged his older and younger brothers and wailed: "That's because low risk is still risk! Khan Ama could have waited for the official schools to cultivate new talents and take away the military power of the older generation before slowly planning it! That group of imperial clansmen and Eight Banners nobles are all old and won't live for many more years!"

Kangxi hugged his arms and watched his son cry, his eyes drifting a bit.

Well, that was true. His temper suddenly flared up, his blood suddenly boiled, and after thinking that it wouldn't be a big problem to do this now, he issued the decree.

Besides the curse, there was one thing that made Kangxi feel like he had a fishbone stuck in his throat, becoming the fuse for his decree.

In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui had already died, the rebel army of the Three Feudatories had collapsed, and the Great Qing should have been able to achieve victory in suppressing the Three Feudatories in one fell swoop.

But now it was already the nineteenth year of Kangxi, and the Eight Banners army was still hovering on the edge of Yunnan; the two armies had actually entered a stalemate.

Kangxi had originally thought it was because the remnants of the Three Feudatories were resisting too strongly. Later, he received secret reports from Han generals one after another that the Manchu generals were just hovering and not fighting after the Three Feudatories no longer posed a threat, eating rations for nothing, watching the war situation, and not actively fighting the remnants of the Three Feudatories at all.

Kangxi quietly asked Prince Kang Jeshu, whom he had promoted himself and who was currently stationed in Fujian. When Yao Qisheng came to the capital to defend himself, he brought Jeshu's letter.

Jeshu told Kangxi that this was indeed the case, and it was an old problem of the Eight Banners.

The Eight Banners banner lords and generals treated the Eight Banners as their private soldiers. Once the Revolt of the Three Feudatories was basically over, the Manchu Eight Banners generals refused to fight hard anymore to avoid increasing casualties under their own banners.

Furthermore, if the Revolt of the Three Feudatories ended, they didn't know if there would be any large-scale wars to eat rations from, so they and their soldiers naturally wanted to delay time and cheat more rations; if the war situation remained in a stalemate, Kangxi would also increase rewards.

The young emperor only came into contact with war for the first time during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories and sent out the Eight Banners army for the first time.

He held the letter and sat silently in the study for a long time, so long that his son crawled into his arms and started snoring, before he carried his son to sleep.

If Yinreng hadn't insisted on crawling into his arms to sleep, Kangxi suspected he would have sat quietly for the whole night.

This letter made the "Eight Banners drawbacks" that Shunzhi told Kangxi about when he possessed Yinreng appear even more intuitively in front of Kangxi.

Before entering the pass, the Great Qing's Eight Banners system was actually equivalent to a tribal system. The Eight Banners banner lords each ran their own affairs, and the banner people were the private property of the banner lords. The emperor was just the "leader" of the banner lords.

Starting from Huang Taiji, the emperors of the Great Qing had been weakening the power of the Eight Banners, such as expanding the banner people and military power under their own control, or letting their own descendants take over the Eight Banners.

But these were all treating the symptoms, not the root cause.

Even if the Eight Banners were in the hands of his sons, could the emperor fully trust his sons? Could the emperors who succeeded later fully trust their brothers?

Wasn't the previous succession of the Great Qing controlled by the imperial clan because the Eight Banners army was in their hands?

The military must be reformed, and the Eight Banners must be abolished.

The emperor is the only ruler of all armies and people. There cannot be two masters in heaven; things like "banner lords" should not exist at all.

During the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, Kangxi had already felt the deep powerlessness brought to him by the Eight Banners system.

But now he could not abolish the Eight Banners. Because if he abolished the Eight Banners, the Eight Banners army might really mutiny.

He could only weaken them.

The method for solving the "Manchu generals delaying and watching, wasting time and rations" in the letter from Prince Kang Jeshu gave Kangxi inspiration.

Jeshu asked Kangxi to appoint the "Four Han Generals of Hexi" as generals and let them be the vanguard, which could quickly break Kunming.

However, Jeshu also told Kangxi that it was best to wait until next year to let the "Four Han Generals of Hexi" be the generals; otherwise, the Eight Banners banner lords hadn't eaten enough rations and might cause bigger trouble to continue eating rations, making the war situation worse.

The timeline of the twentieth year of Kangxi could be considered a step back for both Kangxi and the Eight Banners banner lords.

Kangxi decided to adopt Jeshu's strategy.

Could this strategy also be used in the subsequent weakening of the Eight Banners?

If he could pull the Manchu Eight Banners to suppress the Han officials, then pulling the Han officials to suppress the Manchu Eight Banners would be about the same, right?

As long as he had no Manchu-Han prejudice in his heart and didn't think of himself as the emperor of the Manchus, but only as the "supreme emperor," this choice was not difficult to make.

The so-called Manchu-Han dispute was the same as the regional North-South factionalism, civil-military factionalism, and new-old factionalism of the previous dynasties; they were all about forming cliques for power, so they could all become chess pieces in the emperor's hands to balance the court and concentrate imperial power.

Changing the "queue order" was Kangxi's probe to win over the Han generals.

After listening to Kangxi's explanation, Yinreng continued to wail: "But Ama, you could have waited until the Revolt of the Three Feudatories ended, punished them for delaying the war opportunity logically, and then collected the military power of the Eight Banners!"

Kangxi put down his arms and looked at the sky with his hands behind his back.

Yes, no matter how many considerations he had in his heart, the reason for doing this now was just the curse and the delay of the war opportunity; his anger burned his hot blood, making him stubborn.

"I didn't expect you to be such a coward." Kangxi comforted his precious son who was crying and hiccuping, "I'm not even afraid, what are you afraid of? Do they dare to attack?"

As soon as Kangxi finished speaking, Nalan Xingde, dressed in iron armor, walked in with a fierce momentum to report: "Your Majesty! The camp outside the capital is in chaos!"

Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng: "..."

Before long, Elundai, who had a very strong aura today, also hurried over: "Your Majesty! Prince An Yolo has brought the imperial clan to seek an audience. They refuse to take off their armor and weapons!"

Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng: "..."

Yinreng wiped away his tears and said seriously: "I will take my younger brothers to the Cining Palace. Please, Khan Ama, temporarily grant me the power to manage the affairs of the harem!"

Kangxi looked at Yinreng, whose eyes were as swollen as peaches, and gritted his teeth: "Zhao Chang! Give my precious sword to the Crown Prince! If anyone in the harem does not listen to the Crown Prince's orders, no matter who it is, the Crown Prince can use this sword to execute them!"

Yinreng knelt down to receive the sword, calling himself a subject for the first time: "The subject obeys the decree!"

"Cao Yin." Kangxi said again.

Cao Yin walked out from the shadows, knelt down and said: "The servant is here!"

Kangxi said: "You take a team of guards to follow the Crown Prince and obey the Crown Prince's orders."

Cao Yin said: "The servant obeys the decree!"

"Yinreng, your great-grandmother, grandmother, and concubine mothers, as well as all your brothers and sisters, are all entrusted to you." Kangxi helped Yinreng up, "I believe in you. Zhao Chang, put on my armor!"

Yinreng said loudly: "The subject will definitely protect the family. The subject is in the palace, waiting for Khan Ama's triumphant return!"

Kangxi smiled and patted Yinreng's head.

Then the father and son turned around almost at the same time and left separately.

On the sedan chair to the Cining Palace, the terrified Yinzhi pulled Yinreng's sleeve: "Brother, will it really, really start fighting?"

Yinreng did not answer. He asked: "Big brother, will you protect me and the younger brothers?"

Yinzhi immediately said: "Of course!"

Yinreng nodded: "Then big brother, take your bow and arrows, and I'll let you shoot when I tell you to."

Yinzhi patted his chest and said: "Leave it to me!"

Yinreng said: "With big brother here, I'm not afraid anymore. Even if someone in the harem defects to the imperial clan, they are just eunuchs and palace maids without armor or weapons."

Yinzhi, having been solemnly entrusted by Yinreng, lost much of his timidity and spoke fluently: "That's right! I want to show them the power of the future Great Qing Baturu!"

Yinreng said to Yinzhi, who was still trembling: "Little Three, you are also a big brother. You take the four younger brothers and hide well. Except for me, big brother, and Khan Ama, don't come out no matter who calls you; even if the Empress Dowager, the Empress, or the concubine mothers in the palace call you, don't come out. Can you do it?"

Yinzhi nodded hard: "I can!"

"Well, Yinzhi is also a brave and good big brother." Yinreng smiled and patted Yinzhi's head, then said to Yinzhi, "Big brother, I originally wanted to let you hide too, but I'm a little scared by myself."

Yinzhi said with a straight face: "Don't be afraid, I'll stay with you."

Yinreng hugged Yinzhi and rubbed against him, then hugged his younger brothers one by one.

The Fifth Prince was in the Cining Palace. The two younger brothers who were just born were unaware and still sleeping with snot bubbles.

Yinzhen held his cloth dog tightly; the child's instinct sensed the tense atmosphere, and he pouted, his golden beans about to fall.

When Yinreng hugged Yinzhen, Yinzhen rarely threw away the cloth dog and hugged Yinreng tightly: "Brother, scared."

"Don't be afraid, brother will protect you, the cloth dog... the cloth wolf will also protect you."

Yinreng put the cloth dog back into Yinzhen's arms: "How about I tell you a story after brother solves the problem? This time we'll tell the story of a foreign magician."

Yinzhi said: "Foreign magician? Is it fun? You might as well tell it now."

Yinreng rolled his eyes at Yinzhi: "Not in the mood. We'll talk about it after things are over."

Yinzhi sighed: "After things are over? That doesn't know how long. I can't stay for a moment today."

Yinreng was speechless. Just a moment ago, big brother was still scared, and now his heart had flown to the story.

I hope big brother won't be scared when he sees blood later.

No, I should hope that no bloodshed occurs later.

Yinreng kept Yinzhi by his side, of course, not because he was afraid.

Although Yinzhi was not old, his martial arts value was already quite good; at least the eunuchs in the palace who hadn't practiced wouldn't be able to beat him with weapons.

But Yinzhi had never seen blood, so he couldn't be Yinreng's bodyguard. Yinreng kept Yinzhi to let him kill for him.

When there was real chaos in the palace, guards killing people was not as shocking as a prince killing people himself.

Only when a prince kills someone himself will those who cause chaos know that the prince is not a soft persimmon and will not let them be manipulated.

Yinreng's own hands and feet were soft, and it was difficult to kill; even if he reincarnated his state of mind into the first life, it was inevitable that he would feel resistance in his heart when killing now.

Adding the two together, if he did it himself, it would definitely not be clean.

To use a prince's killing to deter others, it must be clean and neat. Yinreng hoped Yinzhi could do it.

If Yinzhi couldn't do it, he would eventually have to bite the bullet and do it himself.

When they arrived at the Cining Palace, the eunuchs had already passed on Yinreng's order to move all concubines with rank and offspring to the side hall of the Cining Palace.

The two concubines who had just given birth this year were in a small separate room, while the other concubines lived on a large kang, which inevitably led to some complaints.

Following Yinreng's request, the Empress Dowager sat among the concubines, closing her eyes and chanting scriptures.

The concubines didn't dare to complain anymore and followed along, chanting scriptures to pray for peace.

The Empress Dowager breathed a sigh of relief. She could still bluff people with a straight face! As expected of the Crown Prince! He actually discovered her strengths!

The Empress Dowager went to manage the concubines, while the Empress Dowager guarded the children. The Cining Palace had a secret room; Yinzhi took the four younger brothers and hid inside, while the princesses stayed by the Empress Dowager's side.

The older princesses who already understood some things showed a trace of sadness, but soon cheered up under the encouragement of the Empress Dowager and picked up weapons, saying they would protect their younger brothers.

The Empress Dowager was extremely gratified. Baocheng letting the princesses take classes to learn men's archery and killing skills was indeed correct. Even if the princesses' martial arts weren't good, with such courage, they wouldn't have a hard time on the grassland.

Yinreng and Yinzhi stayed in the main hall of the Cining Palace, using sundries to seal all doors except the main gate.

Cao Yin sent people to climb onto the roof of the Cining Palace to observe the outer walls of the Cining Palace and guard the situation around the Cining Palace.

Yinreng sent most of the palace servants to one place and forbade them from walking around at will.

While stuffing beef jerky into his mouth, Yinzhi said unclearly: "No one should come to the Cining Palace, right? Coming to the Cining Palace at this time is equivalent to treason."

Yinreng raised his eyelids: "Big brother, don't be a crow's mouth."

Yinzhi's cheeks bulged as he said: "Don't talk nonsense, your big brother is not a crow's mouth."

A eunuch came over with a teacup, and just as Yinzhi was about to take the tea, he was pulled by Yinreng.

"Big brother, shoot." Yinreng whispered.

The meat in Yinzhi's mouth wasn't swallowed, and the wooden bow that had been slung over his arm was already fully drawn, and a feathered arrow flew out with a "swish".

Before the eunuch who was serving the tea could react, Yinzhi's arrow grazed his shoulder, drawing a line of blood.

He let go in pain, and when the tea tray fell to the ground, two more arrows followed, one hitting his chest and one hitting his stomach.

When Yinreng reminded him, Yinzhi actually fired three arrows in the blink of an eye, and only the first one missed!

The guards rushed up and pinned the eunuch down.

No one paid attention to the eunuch's words of "the servant is wronged" and dragged him away directly, leaving a trail of blood.

Yinzhi slung the bow and arrow back over his arm and held his chest: "Ouch, you scared me to death! This is my first time shooting at a person! Brother, how did you find out he had a problem?"

Yinreng pointed to his head: "I remember the faces of the palace servants I allow to walk in the Cining Palace."

Cao Yin, who was guarding the door, hurried in to plead guilty for his negligence.

The guards didn't know the people in the Cining Palace. They gave the eunuchs and palace maids who could walk around separate uniforms, but just now someone reported that one person had diarrhea and, fearing punishment, changed his uniform without permission and let his companion serve.

Yinreng frowned.

There was no way to know if this companion had bad intentions, but...

Yinreng hid his compassion and let Cao Yin continue to patrol.

Cao Yin added a word: "If the Crown Prince finds something wrong, you can let the guards hold the sword on your behalf."

Yinreng shook his head: "If it weren't for big brother and me taking action, we wouldn't be able to suppress the people in the palace and the back hall."

Yinreng pointed to the location of the women in the palace: "Now the people there already know that the First Prince has killed someone, so they should be very quiet."

Cao Yin was stunned for a moment, took a deep breath, and bowed his head: "Yes!"

Yinzhi was curious: "Why is it quiet inside?"

Yinreng was helpless: "Because even with Khan Ama's sword, the guards dare not kill the women in the palace. But as princes, we can kill."

Yinzhi gasped: "Wow!"

Yinreng held his forehead. Wow your head.

In the back hall, the concubines who were restless even while chanting scriptures became quiet when they heard about the First Prince killing someone.

"The First Prince is really brave." A concubine said to Concubine Hui.

Concubine Hui showed a perfect smile, but she was screaming in collapse in her heart.

How old is my son! How could he kill someone?! Baoqing, are you scared? Are you uncomfortable?

Who dared to harm my son and force him to take action!

In the main hall, a guard came to report that a group of clan wives came to seek an audience.

Yinreng couldn't help but laugh: "The imperial clansmen went to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, but they let the women come to the Cining Palace? If I don't let them in, can they break in?"

The guard said: "They said they were worried that someone would kidnap the Empress Dowager, and they really wanted to break in."

Yinreng sighed, stood up, and straightened the sword at his waist: "I'll go out and see."

Yinzhi immediately said: "I'll go too!"

Yinreng shook his head: "If we kill people this time, we will definitely offend the imperial clan to death."

Yinzhi said: "Then I should go even more. If we offend them, we offend them together. And with your small arms and legs, who can you cut?"

Yinreng was speechless. Well, that's true.

He also found a small bow and arrow, carried it on his back, and went to the Cining Gate with Yinzhi.

Outside, the clan wives were shouting loudly, but when they saw the Crown Prince and the First Prince leading a group of guards out, they were suddenly dumbfounded.

Yinreng had someone move a chair to the middle of the Cining Gate, sat on the chair, and placed the sword given by Kangxi across his legs.

Yinzhi stood on one side of Yinreng, his bow and arrow already strung, ready to be pulled at any time.

Yinreng scanned the aggressive clan wives: "Coming without a summons, what kind of rule is this? Or is it that you no longer recognize the Empress Dowager, the Empress, and me, the Crown Prince? Then can I consider you as traitors?"

Even though they were clearly just two children in front of them, the momentum of the clan wives stalled, and the words they had originally set could not be spoken.

They had originally wanted to rely on their large numbers, thinking the guards wouldn't dare to take action, and come to the Cining Palace to complain to the Empress Dowager, hoping the Empress Dowager would persuade the Emperor to take back his order.

This Crown Prince sitting there with a sword made them look like they were forcing the palace.

Wronged! We didn't think that way!

100,000

61. First and second updates [V]

The Cining Gate opened wide.

Yinreng sat in the middle of the city gate, confronting the dark mass of clan wives.

The noblewomen were caught in a dilemma, unable to retreat or advance.

Before they could speak, Yinreng spoke again.

"Did you come here without summons and storm the gates of Cining Palace? You only need to answer: yes or no."

Yinreng’s voice, still a high-pitched, childish tone that hadn't yet broken, feigned a deep gravity. Under normal circumstances, it would have been cute enough to make people laugh. But now, no one could manage a smile.

The noblewomen looked at one another, not daring to answer.

Yinreng tossed the sword that had been resting across his lap to Cao Yin and nodded at him.

Cao Yin led a group of imperial guards to stand before the noblewomen.

The leader of the noblewomen asked in terror, "What are you doing?"

Yinreng sneered, "Did you come here without summons and storm the gates of Cining Palace?"

The leader’s lips trembled, unwilling to answer.

Cao Yin drew the blade, "This is a precious sword bestowed by the Emperor, granting His Highness the Crown Prince the authority to execute first and report later. Please answer His Highness's question."

Cao Yin curled his lip, "A group of noblewomen like you, failing to kneel upon seeing the Crown Prince and the First Prince—are you truly planning a rebellion?"

Cao Yin was a bondservant and the son of Kangxi’s wet nurse; he was loyal only to the Emperor.

Usually, his status as a bondservant was looked down upon by the banners of the Upper Three, but now, that very status was the most terrifying thing to them.

The noblewomen all knew that these imperial bondservants were merely the Emperor’s hounds, and they feared offending neither the nobility nor the clans.

Yinzhi tightened his grip on his bow and said with displeasure, "Why waste words with them? They came without summons, stormed the Cining Palace gates, and failed to bow to us—any one of these is a capital offense. Just kill them all."

As soon as Yinzhi spoke, the noblewomen’s legs went weak, and they collapsed to their knees in a flurry.

Many who had been confused by the whole affair and had merely followed the princes' and dukes' wives to fit in were so frightened they kowtowed repeatedly, crying out that they were "wronged."

The guards, following Yinreng’s orders, questioned the kneeling noblewomen one by one.

There was only one question, and the answer could only be "yes or no."

Once a noblewoman answered, eunuchs and palace maids would step forward, bind their hands with silk ribbons, and lead them into the Great Buddha Hall in the rear of Cining Palace to be held.

Because the Empress Dowager was a devout Buddhist, the main hall of the rear of Cining Palace, originally intended for living quarters, housed a large Buddha statue, while the Empress Dowager resided in the side chambers.

Now, prayer mats were laid out one after another before the statue, and the noblewomen were brought in one by one to kneel on them.

Before them stood the magnificent Buddha, the walls depicted fierce Arhats, and the hall was filled with the lingering smoke of incense. The noblewomen, already harboring guilty consciences, were terrified to the point of bloodlessness in such an environment, as if the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Arhats were about to leap out from the statues and murals.

The eunuchs and maids only bound the noblewomen’s hands loosely, without force.

They pressed their palms together and chanted before the Buddha to soothe their inner fear.

As the noblewomen who entered earlier began to chant, those who entered later—seeing the environment and the atmosphere—became pale with fright, even if they hadn't been scared before. They began to tremble like hairless quails, also starting to chant in shaky voices.

The guards began by questioning the lower-ranking noblewomen, until finally, only the wives of the princes and dukes remained before Yinreng.

Their expressions had initially been one of unbothered arrogance. But as those around them were taken away one by one, they finally began to panic.

However, the wives of the princes and dukes were all in the same social circle; if anyone bowed, they could no longer blend into this group. They were panicked, but none dared to be the first to yield.

The guards stopped making arrests. Yinreng took the sword back from Cao Yin and laid it across his lap again.

Noblewomen from every prince and duke’s household in the capital had come, including not just the primary wives, but also the senior wives and secondary wives—all the heads of their respective households.

Yinreng first cast his gaze toward the wife of Prince Kang, of the lineage of the original Prince Heshuo Li, Dai Shan: "Prince Kang is loyal to Khan Ama; I do not believe the women of his household would force their way into the palace. I will give you a chance to defend yourselves."

The expressions of the women from Prince Kang’s household shifted, and the other noblewomen cast subtle glances at them.

Yinreng noted their expressions one by one, categorizing them into different groups based on their reactions.

Prince Kang’s successor wife, Borjigit, was still young and didn't know how to react, so she could only look blankly at the senior wife, the Khorchin Borjigit.

Remembering this person’s surname, Yinreng asked his next question in Mongolian.

The senior wife of Prince Kang kowtowed tremblingly and said, "This subject is of the Khorchin Borjigit clan. Hearing that members of the clan were coming to Cining Palace, I was worried about the safety of the Empress Dowager and the Empress, and feared others might offend them, so I came without summons. If these people dared to coerce the Empress Dowager and the Empress, I would risk my life to protect them."

Having said this, she kowtowed again.

Among the noblewomen, the primary wives of Prince Shuncheng Lejin and Prince Duoluo Ping Luodu were also Khorchin Borjigit; hearing the senior wife’s words, they were immediately struck with alarm.

The primary wife of Prince Zhuang Boguoduo was a Chahar Borjigit, whose relationship to the Khorchin Borjigit was akin to that of a southern branch to a northern branch. She also understood Mongolian, and her complexion turned very poor.

The senior wife of Prince Kang had used this excuse to clear her name; if they, who were also Borjigit, didn't provide the same reason, wouldn't it imply they were unfaithful to the Empress Dowager and the Empress?

Their status within the clan relied entirely on the Empress Dowager and the Empress. If they offended them, even if the men in their families seized power, would their lives be any easier?

"I believe Prince Kang," Yinreng said, trusting the words of the senior wife.

Although many of Prince Kang’s descendants died young, they were generally men who could fight on the battlefield. Even if one of their daughters married Nalan Mingzhu’s third son, the couple spent their time traveling, composing poetry, and painting, staying out of politics.

The Prince Kang family were rare, honest people among the nobility who were loyal to the Emperor and talented. Aside from Aisin Gioro Zhao Lian, who wrote the "Xiaoting Xulu" (a collection of gossip about the nobility), no one in their family had ever been convicted or stripped of their titles. This showed just how honest they were.

Yinreng had the eunuchs help the senior wife and the successor wife of Prince Kang up and send them to the Empress Dowager.

Hearing this order, the noblewomen of Mongolian descent felt their resolve waver even more.

Since His Highness the Crown Prince dared to send them to accompany the Empress Dowager, did it not mean that the Empress Dowager and the Empress were safe and sound, and that the Emperor’s actions were permitted by them?

Even after marrying into the imperial clan, the women of Mongolian origin could not help but lean toward their homeland.

To put it bluntly, what did the Manchu imperial family have to do with them? What did the change in the tonsure decree have to do with Mongolia? If the Han people had opportunities, Mongolia was closer to the Great Qing than the Han were, and perhaps they would gain even more.

Recently, people from Mongolia often complained that the Manchu nobility was increasingly suppressing and wary of them. If the Emperor weakened the Manchu nobility, it might be good for Mongolia, not bad.

Seeing the wavering expressions of the noblewomen with Mongolian features, Yinreng said, "Are there any others who, like the senior wife of Prince Kang, came only because they were worried about the Empress Dowager and the Empress?"

Before the two Khorchin noblewomen could speak, the primary wife of Prince Zhuang, the Chahar Borjigit, lunged forward a few steps and kowtowed, "This subject also came because I was worried about the Empress Dowager and the Empress! I am willing to swear to Eternal Heaven! I have absolutely no disloyal intentions toward the Emperor!"

After she finished speaking, she immediately swore the most vicious oath.

The other noblewomen gasped, looking at the primary wife of Prince Zhuang with strange expressions.

*You woman, isn't that too sycophantic! Do you have any self-respect as a Prince's wife left?*

The primary wife of Prince Zhuang sneered inwardly.

Self-respect? What is self-respect? Prince Zhuang’s household still had no sons, and the Prince and all the other nobles and their wives had stepped on her, calling her a hen that couldn't lay eggs, calling her jealous, and calling her a sinner of the Prince Zhuang lineage.

But she was never favored to begin with. Prince Zhuang’s household had many secondary wives and concubines, yet hadn't they only given birth to daughters? What fault was it of hers?! The one who couldn't produce a son was clearly Prince Zhuang Boguoduo himself!

Boguoduo was a Prince, but he was neither scholarly nor martial, and had always been mediocre.

This time, he was one of the most active agitators, as if he thought he could seize total power if the Beile council system were restored.

The primary wife of Prince Zhuang did not want to see Boguoduo get his way. She already had a miserable life in the Prince’s mansion, relying entirely on her Mongolian family to support her just to catch her breath. If Boguoduo succeeded, could she even survive?

Seeing that the Crown Prince was wise and the Empress Dowager and Empress were safe, it would be better to defect to the Crown Prince and the Empress Dowager; her life would be much easier.

After swearing her vicious oath, the primary wife of Prince Zhuang was also allowed to go to the Empress Dowager.

With two Mongolian-born princely wives defecting to the Crown Prince, the remaining noblewomen felt even more anxious.

At this moment, another princely wife slowly crawled out of the crowd and kowtowed to the Crown Prince: "This subject, the successor wife of Prince An, Hesheli, came only to protect His Highness the Crown Prince."

After speaking, she took a jeweled dagger from her bosom: "This dagger was bestowed by the Filial and Benevolent Empress."

The noblewomen: "???!!!"

*This one is the real traitor!!*

Yinreng chuckled, "Aunt, you were so quiet, you scared me. If you had come to force the palace, I would have had to hold the Empress's spirit tablet and cry. Quickly, help Aunt up."

After the successor wife of Prince An was helped up, she bowed slowly once more.

She did not enter Cining Palace, but walked to the side of the guard in front of Yinreng, holding the dagger and facing the noblewomen.

The noblewomen: "???!!!"

*Hesheli, what are you doing?! Are you threatening us?!*

In particular, the senior wife of Prince Ping, Tonggiya, was so hateful she nearly ground her teeth to dust.

Yinreng glanced at Tonggiya and thought, "Oh?"

This senior wife, Tonggiya, was the daughter of Tong Yangxing, a distant cousin of Tong Guolai’s family. She and her son, the Beile Noni, had been reported by her aunt and mother-in-law, the Gioro clan, for abusing Noni’s primary wife, a Khorchin Borjigit.

Yolo couldn't stand the sight of Noni’s wife’s misery and had both the senior wife Tonggiya and Beile Noni locked in the Clan Court, stripping Noni of his Beile title and leaving him a commoner of the imperial clan. The senior wife Tonggiya had hated Prince An, Yolo, to the bone ever since.

By the way, ten years after Yolo died, Noni joined the "Half-Court Tong" faction of that time to accuse Yolo of unfair dealings.

The new Prince An was born to the successor wife Hesheli. Just as Kangxi began to loathe the Crown Prince and suppress his influence in the military, Yolo’s posthumous title was revoked, and his descendants were demoted to the rank of Prince of the Third Rank.

Later, because Yolo’s granddaughter married the Eighth Prince Yinzhen, the Prince An lineage, seeing the Crown Prince was no longer useful, threw their support behind the Eighth Prince, only to be punished by Yongzheng later.

The miserable history of the Prince An lineage being repeatedly beaten is a story for another time. But as for this Tonggiya woman who abused her daughter-in-law and ended up in the Clan Court—hmm, could it be that abusing daughters-in-law, favoring concubines over wives, and domestic chaos were a Tong family tradition?

While Yinreng was gossiping in his mind, his eyes remained fixed on the senior wife Tonggiya, until she snapped out of her rage, terrified into a cold sweat.

She suddenly remembered that as a distant relative of the late Empress Dowager Cihe, she should be supporting the Emperor.

But the men in her family were all standing in opposition to the Emperor and the Crown Prince... The senior wife Tonggiya suddenly remembered that this Crown Prince was born to the Hesheli clan, not the Tonggiya clan, so causing him trouble would be a good thing.

Having been locked in the Clan Court for abusing a high-born daughter-in-law, the senior wife Tonggiya was not very bright to begin with. She overthought things, and her actions were slow. By the time she came to her senses, the Mongolian-born noblewomen had already sided with the Crown Prince, claiming they were only worried about the Empress Dowager’s safety and hadn't come to force the palace.

Her own daughter-in-law, the primary wife of Prince Ping, had already "surrendered."

The primary wife of Prince Ping was stunned after her "surrender"; she had stood up, but her mother-in-law Tonggiya was still stubbornly kneeling.

Seeing her eldest daughter-in-law making decisions on her own, the senior wife Tonggiya lost her temper and began to berate her.

Her third daughter-in-law, who had also been Khorchin Borjigit and was the reason she was locked in the Clan Court, was of the same clan as the eldest daughter-in-law. With old grudges and new ones flaring up, the already paranoid and elderly Tonggiya lost all reason and actually lunged forward to attack the primary wife of Prince Ping.

Yinreng immediately slapped the armrest of his chair with his sword, warning the irrational senior wife Tonggiya.

Consumed by rage, the senior wife Tonggiya turned and began to berate Yinreng, claiming that as a relative of the Empress Dowager, Yinreng’s treatment of her was unfilial.

Yinreng: "???"

*Let alone that you, the daughter of Tong Yangxing, are only a distant relative of Empress Dowager Cihe, even if Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei were standing before me, they wouldn't dare point at my nose and curse! You’re quite brave, aren't you?*

The senior wife Tonggiya, who had brought sixty maids as a dowry when she married—startling even Hong Taiji and causing multiple generals to be punished—was indeed very brave. She actually jumped up from the ground to chase the primary wife of Prince Ping.

The arrow in the First Prince Yinzhi’s hand was fully drawn, and with a slight tremor of his hand, he accidentally shot an arrow into the senior wife Tonggiya’s leg.

Yinzhi: "..." *Oops, that's bad.*

He looked at Yinreng: "My hand slipped."

Yinreng: "...It’s fine."

He stood up, walked to the senior wife Tonggiya, who had finally regained her senses after the pain, drew his sword, and slashed her other leg.

The senior wife Tonggiya screamed repeatedly, a sound that made the other noblewomen’s hearts shatter with fear.

Yinreng suppressed his discomfort and sheathed his sword: "Take her to the Qianqing Palace and tell the clansmen that the noblewomen trespassed in Cining Palace. I tried to persuade them with kind words, but she dared to strike and curse me. The First Prince and I injured her in self-defense. Ask the clan ministers on my behalf how this woman should be dealt with."

Cao Yin accepted the order, had the guards assemble a stretcher from bed boards, tied the senior wife Tonggiya to it, and carried her away.

Yinreng sat back in his chair and swept his gaze across the noblewomen: "Continue."

The noblewomen were bewildered.

*Continue? Continue what? Is it to admit guilt or to admit death?*

The wife of Prince Ping, who hadn't left yet, immediately knelt and kowtowed until her forehead bled, repeatedly arguing that the Prince Ping household had no disloyal intentions and that the senior wife was just senile.

Yinreng ignored the pathetic woman and continued to watch the remaining princely and ducal wives who were still kneeling and hadn't declared their stance with a calm gaze.

The First Prince and the Crown Prince had actually injured someone right in front of them; the group of noblewomen finally knew fear.

They confessed one after another, were bound by the eunuchs, and sent to the Buddha Hall.

The women already in the Buddha Hall, seeing the princely and ducal wives being bound and brought in, lost all hope. One by one, they kowtowed toward the door, hoping the Crown Prince and the Empress Dowager would show mercy.

The guards and eunuchs shut the doors of the Buddha Hall, locking the noblewomen’s cries within the solemn hall.

With the doors closed, the hall became dim, and combined with the noblewomen’s wails, even though they were physically unharmed, they began to hallucinate that they were in hell.

A few older noblewomen couldn't hold on and fainted; the younger ones didn't dare look at the Buddha statue and curled up in corners, as if it would provide more security.

The handling of the noblewomen reached the Empress Dowager. The successor wife of Prince An, Hesheli, told the Empress Dowager everything that had happened behind the Cining Gate.

The noblewomen sent to the Empress Dowager’s side were pale, thinking the Crown Prince was truly heartless.

The Empress Dowager, however, spat and frowned: "The Crown Prince is still too benevolent! This group that dared to storm the gates should have been beaten to death! Especially that Tonggiya woman, daring to insult the Crown Prince! Cao Yin is also useless! To make the Crown Prince draw his sword in self-defense! He should have just taken his sword and chopped that woman’s head off!"

The noblewomen: "..."

*Alright, they understood now; the Empress Dowager was indeed on the side of the Emperor and the Crown Prince. Their plan to come and cry to the Empress Dowager to pressure the Emperor was a mistake from the start.*

Sumalagu comforted her: "After all, they are the elders of the clan, and the Crown Prince has already shown them the utmost face and tolerance. If this spreads, no one will say the Crown Prince is in the wrong."

"Who dares to say my great-grandson is in the wrong?!" the Empress Dowager raged. "I want to see how the clansmen will defend themselves for this incident of the noblewomen storming the gates!"

The noblewomen around the Empress Dowager trembled.

*They thought this was the end, but was it only just beginning?*

At the Cining Gate, Yinreng finally finished dealing with the noblewomen and couldn't help but collapse.

It wasn't from fear, but from exhaustion. Every time Yinreng used his brain intensely, his body would become weak.

Yinzhi noticed Yinreng’s discomfort and hurriedly dropped his bow and arrows to support him: "What is it? Did seeing blood make you go soft?"

Yinreng said weakly, "Not soft. Tired. Hungry, sleepy, and tired. It’s always like this when I use my brain."

Yinzhi remembered Yinreng’s old ailment, patted his head, and said, "Then sleep for a while; I’ll protect you."

Yinreng shook his head: "I can't sleep yet; who knows if more people will come."

He yawned, stood up, and stumbled toward Cining Palace, only to be picked up by Cao Yin.

Cao Yin smiled bitterly: "Your Highness should give this servant more work to do. Today, I was almost useless."

As a bondservant, he was supposed to do the dirty work for his masters. But both times blood was shed, it was the Crown Prince and the First Prince who did it themselves.

Although the Crown Prince signaled him not to intervene, and Cao Yin had to obey, he felt terrible inside.

"If you had acted, not only might they have rioted, but you would also face retaliation in the future. That’s why my brother and I had to do it." Yinreng leaned on Cao Yin’s shoulder, yawning continuously, "Don't worry, my brother and I will explain everything to Khan Ama. Ha... ah."

Yinzhi looked up at the yawning Yinreng, deeply worried: "Stop talking, just sleep. Give me the sword, I’ll stand guard. The noblewomen have been dealt with, no need to show any more face to the rest. Whoever dares to come, I’ll cut them down."

"Mm, hoo..." Yinreng tried to hold on... hold on... but couldn't, falling into a soft, limp ball in Cao Yin’s arms.

Cao Yin felt both heartache and a desire to smile kindly; his expression was extremely distorted.

The other guards’ expressions were just as distorted as Cao Yin’s.

They saw and remembered the little Crown Prince’s protection of them. It was hard to imagine such a kind child surviving the cruel struggle for the throne. But such a kind child also made it hard not to pray for him to live a long life.

...

In the Qianqing Palace, the clansmen’s attempt to force the palace had also ended, in a process so bizarre it left Kangxi both laughing and crying.

It was said that when Prince An Yolo entered in armor and with a sword, Kangxi also donned armor and drew his sword, setting the stage.

Just as the two sides were in a standoff, and a clash seemed inevitable, the fifty-five-year-old Prince An Yolo suddenly turned and rammed into several clansmen beside him with his armored bull-rush, knocking them to the ground before they could react.

Prince An Yolo shouted: "Your Majesty! Quickly, seize them!"

Before Kangxi could recover, Changtai, who had been notified in advance by another Hesheli woman married into the clan and had rushed into the palace to protect the Emperor, had already charged out.

Yolo and Changtai, one old and one young, worked together, beating the clansmen until they were scurrying for cover.

The other guards finally reacted and joined the fray.

There were few among the clansmen who could actually fight, and those few had been knocked down by Yolo at the very beginning. Thus, in less than two quarters of an hour, the chaos in front of the Qianqing Palace was over.

Prince An Yolo fell to the ground, weeping, and pleaded guilty to Kangxi: "I couldn't stop them, so I had to use this desperate measure to make them lower their guard and capture them before the Emperor. Please punish me for the crime of disturbing the imperial presence!"

The bound clansmen cursed loudly, wishing they could tear Yolo to pieces.

Kangxi waved his hand, and Changtai immediately sent people to stuff the mouths of the clansmen with rags.

Prince An Yolo wept again: "They sent noblewomen to disturb the peace of Cining Palace. Although my old wife mixed in with a dagger to protect the Crown Prince, I don't know the situation there. Please, Your Majesty, send people to Cining Palace immediately to protect the Empress Dowager and the Crown Prince!"

Kangxi slapped the dragon throne and stood up with a "whoosh." Before he could speak, Liang Jiugong led a few guards and eunuchs, carrying the gagged Tonggiya, and requested an audience at the entrance of the Qianqing Palace.

Kangxi hurriedly let them in to ask about the situation at Cining Palace.

When he heard that the First Prince had shot a treacherous eunuch and the Crown Prince had sat at the Cining Gate to calmly capture all the noblewomen, Kangxi laughed loudly and praised them;

When he heard that the wife of Prince Ping had confessed and yielded, but the senior wife Tonggiya had attacked and cursed her and tried to charge at the Crown Prince, only to be injured in both legs by the Crown Prince and the First Prince, Kangxi’s face turned as dark as water.

He stepped forward, walked to Tonggiya, and suddenly drew the long sword from his waist, decapitating her in one stroke!

Blood sprayed, the floor of the Qianqing Palace was stained red, and the struggling clansmen froze, falling into dead silence.

100,000

62. Third and Fourth Updates (Bonus for 60,000 nutrient solution) [V]

No one expected Kangxi to take such an action.

As everyone knows, Kangxi lost both parents at a young age and held his maternal clan in high regard. Although Tong Yangxing was not of the direct line of Kangxi’s maternal clan, he still received a great deal of favor from Kangxi.

This was not the first time Old Fujin Tongjia had lost her mind.

Old Fujin Tongjia and her precious youngest son, Noni, had mistreated his legal wife. The legal wife’s mother was Noni’s paternal aunt, Heshuo Gege Jue-luo, and her father was of the Khorchin Borjigit clan, the same clan as the Grand Empress Dowager; both were still alive.

Tongjia’s husband, Luoluohun, died early, and Tongjia ruled the household with an iron fist. She acted without propriety, even failing to wear mourning clothes after her mother-in-law, Nara, passed away.

Having caught them in the act, Jue-luo immediately reported them to Yuele, who was in charge of the Imperial Clan Court, on the grounds of their unfilial behavior.

These crimes were enough to get them into serious trouble, and at the time, Yuele even submitted a memorial hoping for Noni to be executed.

Yet, Kangxi, who was only in his teens at the time, was already extremely protective of the Tongjia clan. Noni was merely stripped of his title, and the unfilial and unkind Tongjia was released without punishment.

Even when the imperial clansmen of the Jue-luo clan joined forces with the Grand Empress Dowager’s maternal Khorchin Borjigit clan, they could do nothing about the unfilial and unkind Tongjia. From then on, Old Fujin Tongjia became even more arrogant and domineering, with no one able to keep her in check.

After this incident, the imperial clansmen and nobles understood just how biased Kangxi was toward his maternal clan. The influence of the maternal Tongjia clan was unparalleled, vaguely possessing the power of a "Tong Half-Court."

Now, Kangxi had actually personally chopped off the head of Old Fujin Tongjia, whom he had previously favored?!

The bound imperial clansmen and the nobles who had arrived late to observe the situation were all dumbfounded, standing like wooden chickens, not knowing how to react.

At this moment, a thick-skinned boy said "Tsk," breaking the deathly silence of the Qianqing Palace.

E'lundai, who was bruised and battered after a fight with the imperial clansmen due to his poor combat skills, knelt on the ground and shouted loudly: "My Tong family has hundreds, if not thousands, of clansmen. If everyone dares to call themselves the Emperor’s elder, then the Emperor has far too many elders."

Kangxi, who was in a fit of rage and holding a dripping blade: "???"

Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei among the nobles: "???"

E'lundai bared his teeth and said: "I am the Emperor’s own cousin, and even I wouldn't dare to act so arrogantly by claiming to be the Emperor's relative."

Kangxi looked down at his blood-dripping sword. Are you sure?

Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei: "..." Are you sure?

"For such an arrogant person, there is no need for the Emperor to dirty his hands. Next time, just tell me, and I will do it." E'lundai’s expression was ferocious. "Whoever dares to ruin the Tong family's reputation, I will kill them."

Kangxi silently shook the blood off his blade and sheathed it: "Oh, okay."

As soon as E'lundai popped up, Kangxi’s belly full of anger suddenly vanished.

He had originally been venting his anger on the Tong family—Kangxi knew he had favored the Tong family too much, thinking they would reciprocate. Who knew that after he let Tongjia off once, she would dare to scold and chase after his two sons, causing even someone as kind as Yinreng to panic and strike her with a blade.

The Tong family has failed me!

Once E'lundai said those few words, Kangxi was no longer angry.

It was true; there were hundreds or thousands of people in the Tongjia clan, and it was impossible for all of them to be sensible. He only needed to look after his direct maternal relatives; he shouldn't have been so biased toward the other collateral branches anyway.

Besides, this wasn't the first time he had been disappointed by people from the Tong family, so there was really no need to be this angry.

Kangxi scanned the late-arriving nobles with their dark and uncertain expressions and said indifferently: "This matter is concluded. Lock the offending clansmen in the Imperial Clan Court prison. The rest of you, my ministers, may return; we shall discuss other matters tomorrow."

The late-arriving nobles kowtowed in obedience; how could they dare to say anything more?

The guards began to clean up the blood in the Qianqing Palace. E'lundai was granted leave by Kangxi to go home and recover from his injuries. Changtai took some clothes and stayed temporarily in the side hall of the Qianqing Palace to guard the palace.

Kangxi took a bath and changed his clothes before going to the Cining Palace to see his sons.

When he arrived at the Cining Palace, he found his sons sleeping in a pile with the eldest prince, Yinzhi, at the center. His precious son, Yinreng, was being held in Yinzhi's arms, serving as Yinzhi's body pillow.

Kangxi gasped, his worry for his sons leaking out like a punctured water skin.

The Grand Empress Dowager smiled and said: "The eldest prince and the Crown Prince were truly exhausted today. Both children are such good boys."

Kangxi glared at the eldest prince, Yinzhi, who was sleeping sprawled out and looking very arrogant, with one arm around Yinreng and the other resting on Yinzi's stomach, and gritted his teeth: "Yes, good boys indeed!"

The Grand Empress Dowager said: "Shall we let them continue sleeping?"

Kangxi said: "Fine."

Having said that, he dragged Yinreng out from the crook of Yinzhi's arm.

The Grand Empress Dowager’s smile stiffened.

Sigh, this grandson of mine... how should I put it? Sometimes he is exceptionally childish.

Despite Kangxi’s rough movements, Yinreng remained fast asleep, but Yinzhi was woken up.

He opened his eyes, glanced at Kangxi, turned over in a daze, replaced his body pillow with Yinzi, and continued to sleep soundly.

Kangxi: "..." He really wanted to wake Yinzhi up.

The Grand Empress Dowager hurriedly intervened: "Let the children continue to sleep."

Kangxi snorted coldly, first putting Yinreng back on the bed, then adjusting the sleeping positions of his other sons and tucking them in, before going to the main hall of the Cining Palace to talk with the Grand Empress Dowager.

The Grand Empress Dowager was even more speechless.

Since you intended to let the Crown Prince continue sleeping here, why did you bother dragging him out of the First Prince's arms in the first place?

After the childish Kangxi felt a bit sour and performed some futile actions, he proceeded to interrogate the clan wives one by one, filled with deep discomfort.

The clan wives had already been interrogated once by the Empress Dowager, and now, contrary to all reason, they were being personally questioned by the Emperor, leaving them so terrified they nearly fainted.

Kangxi had their testimonies recorded and ordered the clan wives to return home, where they were to be temporarily confined to their respective residences, forbidden from leaving, and left to await further handling.

Kangxi then inquired about the situation of his concubines and offered them comfort.

As the situation in the palace had not yet been fully clarified, Kangxi's concubines were to stay temporarily in the side halls of the Cining Palace for the night.

Upon hearing that Kangxi had personally executed an elder of her clan, Imperial Noble Consort Tong was so frightened that her face turned pale and she nearly fainted.

Kangxi comforted her and spoke of the merits Olondai had earned that day, attempting to use Olondai's achievements to cheer her up.

In Kangxi's eyes, his mother was the sister of Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei, and the sons of Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei were all his own cousins.

But in the eyes of the Imperial Noble Consort, it was not like that. Even within a clan, the eldest and second branches would compare themselves to one another; a cousin from the eldest branch always felt like an outsider, and she had always hoped for her own brothers to excel.

Yet Kangxi did not understand this.

Or perhaps, as an Emperor, Kangxi stood too high and saw too far to concern himself with the conflicts between the eldest and second branches, nor did he wish for such conflicts to appear before his eyes.

Imperial Noble Consort Tong knew Kangxi well, so she could only force a smile and say that she felt comforted.

Kangxi left, satisfied, while the Imperial Noble Consort buried her head in her quilt, biting her lip to keep from sobbing aloud.

The next day, already exhausted from the heavy palace duties and her inability to conceive, the Imperial Noble Consort developed a high fever after a sleepless night and was bedridden.

Kangxi hurriedly had the inner palace tidied up and ordered the Imperial Noble Consort to be carried back to the Chengqian Palace to recuperate. The other concubines stayed at the Cining Palace for a few more days before returning to their own quarters.

The Imperial Noble Consort was quite ill, and not daring to tell Kangxi that her illness was caused by the fact that Olondai was capable while her own brothers were not, she simply claimed she had been made ill by the arrogance of the Tong family relatives, who acted high and mighty because they were imperial in-laws and caused trouble for Kangxi.

Whatever the Imperial Noble Consort said, Kangxi believed.

He ordered the name of the Old Princess Consort Tonggiashi to be struck from both the Gioro and Tonggiashi genealogies, her corpse burned, and her ashes scattered; he further issued an edict stripping her eldest son, Prince Ping Luokeduo, of his title, and removed all three sons born to the Tonggiashi—including Luokeduo—from the clan, with the title of Prince Ping to be inherited by Aisin Gioro Keqi, the eldest son of Luokeduo’s third uncle.

After Kangxi finished handling these matters, he came to comfort his beloved consort. "Look! I've vented your anger for you! Do you feel better now?"

Gritting her teeth, the Imperial Noble Consort forced a smile: "Thank you, Your Majesty, I feel much better. My illness will surely improve soon."

Kangxi left the Chengqian Palace in high spirits. The Imperial Noble Consort buried her head and wept once more.

By using the excuse of the Imperial Noble Consort's illness to punish the Old Princess Consort Tonggiashi and her children, Kangxi had made the Imperial Noble Consort take the blame for the Crown Prince and the First Prince. Not only was the branch of Tong Guowei now completely at odds with the rest of the clan, but the branch of Tong Yangxing would surely also have a rift with Tong Guowei's family.

Although Tong Guogang and Tong Guowei were noble imperial in-laws and appeared prestigious, neither of them had ever achieved any real, tangible merits.

Within the vast Tong clan, only Tong Guoyao, the grandson of Tong Yangxing, was a military talent with actual battle achievements, and he was currently occupied with suppressing the Revolt of the Three Feudatories. Therefore, Noble Consort Tong’s branch had always maintained a mutually supportive relationship with the descendants of Tong Yangxing.

For the descendants of Tong Yangxing to be suppressed was equivalent to severing one of the Tong family’s arms within the military.

Noble Consort Tong could not stop weeping, yet she dared not remain ill for long, fearing that the Kangxi Emperor might discern her true intentions and grow dissatisfied with her and the Tong family. She had no choice but to grit her teeth and force herself to take her medicine and eat, hoping to recover as quickly as possible, though her heart was filled with unspeakable bitterness.

While Noble Consort Tong suffered, Tong Guowei was also in great agony.

In a large family, the senior and junior branches are always prone to competing with one another. The *Classic of Poetry* says, "Brothers may quarrel within the walls, but they will oppose insult from without." When there were no external threats, Tong Guowei would think of ways to get the upper hand over Tong Guogang, aiming to make the second branch the primary line of the Tong family.

Tong Guowei’s literary and martial accomplishments were far inferior to Tong Guogang’s, but because he had a favored daughter, his status in the Tong family had finally risen to be vaguely higher than Tong Guogang’s.

Tong Guogang had few heirs; his eldest son was a scoundrel, and his two younger sons had not yet come of age. Tong Guowei, however, was very prolific and had a brilliant, exceptionally skilled "qilin son" named Longkodo, and his descendants were also stronger than Tong Guogang’s.

Tong Guowei had assumed that his position as the true head of the Tong family was secure.

Who could have known that the Emperor would actually appoint the infant son of the late Empress as Crown Prince, while his own daughter had yet to bear a child? Longkodo had been impeached for his private life, causing his official career to fluctuate, while Elundai had caught the eye of the Emperor by clinging to the Crown Prince, and had even achieved merit this time.

Not only that, but Tong Guogang’s concubine-born son, Fahai, had become a student of Nalan Xingde, a man highly favored by both the Kangxi Emperor and the Crown Prince, while his second legitimate son, Kuadai, had been chosen as a study companion for the First Prince. Tong Guogang was suddenly riding high, and the senior branch seemed poised to overshadow the second branch once again.

Tong Guowei had only enjoyed the prestige of being the Tong family’s true power-holder for a few years; how could he stand to watch Tong Guogang’s status rise above his own again?

On one hand, he scoured the land for folk remedies to send into the palace, urging Noble Consort Tong to conceive a child quickly; on the other, he continued to seek a wife of distinguished lineage for his "qilin son," Longkodo.

Originally, Tong Guowei had set his sights on the younger half-sister of Empress Renxiao, but she was still too young, and the Hesheli family was overly cautious, refusing to marry into the family of a favored imperial concubine, so the matter had to be dropped.

Later, Longkodo caused a scandal by "indulging in brothels and refusing to marry," which made families who had previously been interested in an alliance with him adopt a wait-and-see attitude, forcing Tong Guowei to temporarily shelve Longkodo's marriage plans.

At this time, Tong Guowei's wife, Lady Hesheli, wanted to favor her own kin and have Longkodo marry her brother's daughter. Tong Guowei had originally been tempted, but now, he was no longer satisfied.

Although they were both of the Heseri clan, his wife’s branch was merely a distant relative of Soni, and there was no one capable in her family who could provide any support to Longkodo.

After much deliberation, he hooked up with the Niohuru clan, the family of the late Empress Xiao'an.

Tong Guowei already had marriage ties with the Niohuru clan; one of his daughters was married to Yanzhu, the son of Ebilun and the half-brother of Empress Xiao'an.

Consort Wen of the Niohuru clan was not particularly favored in the palace and happened to need the support of Noble Consort Tong. Thus, through the mediation of Lady Yanzhu, the Niohuru clan strengthened their ties with Tong Guowei by betrothing their youngest legitimate daughter, who was only nine years old, to Longkodo.

This youngest legitimate daughter of the Niohuru clan was the youngest daughter of Ebilun’s second wife, the Bayara clan. Manchu women married early; they could be wed at the nominal age of eleven or twelve. This youngest daughter would be ready for marriage after a year or two of preparation at home, making her age just right.

Longkeduo saw that Elundai was actually starting to show promise, and he began to feel anxious himself. Therefore, he behaved very honestly this time; he didn't even visit brothels, and not only did he fraternize with the men of the Niuhulu clan, but he also entrusted others to send many gifts to his young fiancée.

The Niohuru family was very satisfied with Longkodo, and even Concubine Wen entrusted Imperial Noble Consort Tong to send some gifts to Longkodo as a gesture of goodwill.

A happy event brings a refreshed spirit; seeing her younger brother finally pull himself together, Imperial Noble Consort Tong’s illness recovered immediately.

With Imperial Noble Consort Tong recovered, Kangxi’s mood naturally improved as well. Hearing from her that Longkodo had matured, he promoted Longkodo to a second-class imperial guard, encouraging him to work hard and learn well from Elundai.

Consort Tong and Longkodo: "???"

Elundai grinned, revealing a mouthful of white teeth.

Alright, Consort Tong started having heart palpitations again.

What gave her even more heart palpitations was that Kangxi, seeing she had recovered, handed the palace affairs back to her and urged her to be cautious and diligent, advising her to oversee everything personally to prevent resentful clan factions from taking advantage of the situation.

Consort Tong, holding a ginseng slice in her mouth, tearfully continued her role as the chief housekeeper of Kangxi's harem.

When Yinreng learned of this, he shed a few sympathetic tears for Consort Tong.

But he was only a small Crown Prince; even knowing Consort Tong was pitiful, he couldn't go to Kangxi and ask him to distribute the palace duties to other concubines.

Although he meant well, persuading Kangxi not to let Consort Tong hold all the power would only make people mistakenly think he was dissatisfied with her. Thus, Yinreng could only rummage through Kangxi's treasury to find some treasures to give to Consort Tong under the guise of celebrating Longkodo's engagement.

"These are all Imperial Father's things! Consort Tong, don't refuse!" Yinreng said. "Since you're managing his household for him, I'll help you empty his treasury!"

Consort Tong clutched her chest: "Alright."

Oh my, how can the little Crown Prince be so gentle and thoughtful? If only my cousin were half as gentle and thoughtful as the little Crown Prince, would I have to cry under my quilt every day?

Consort Tong patted Yinreng's head several times, praying that she, too, could give birth to a child as lovable as Yinreng.

Boy or girl, it didn't matter, as long as it was a child. She was truly too lonely.

After Kangxi learned of this, he picked up Yinreng and lectured him: "Do I need you to help me curry favor with the Consort?"

Yinreng shrank his neck and said: "The Consort is so busy she's become skin and bones, and you don't even give her a reward. Bad Father, you scumbag."

Kangxi immediately pressed Yinreng onto his knee and spanked his bottom. Although he didn't use much force, Yinreng still had to sleep on his stomach for the night.

The weather was hot, Yinreng was wearing too little, and Kangxi had a heavy hand, so it was only natural that his bottom got swollen.

When Consort Tong learned of this, the good mood the little Crown Prince had put her in vanished completely.

The little Crown Prince had merely taken some things to give to her, and Emperor Cousin had clearly stated that the Emperor's private treasury was the Crown Prince's treasury, allowing the Prince to draw from it at will—how could he beat the Crown Prince?

Is Emperor Cousin expressing his dissatisfaction with me?!

For the first time, Consort Tong roared aggressively at Kangxi when he came to Chengqian Palace.

Kangxi rubbed his nose. Hmm, he made an excuse about having government affairs to handle and slipped away.

Consort Tong clutched her liver, so angry it ached.

It wasn't entirely an excuse; Kangxi did indeed have many government affairs.

The issues with the clan members who attempted to usurp the throne had to be dealt with, the fence-sitting nobles had to be managed, the follow-up effects of the two imperial edicts announced to the world had to be handled, and the situation at the front lines of the Revolt of the Three Feudatories needed even more urgent attention.

Since the clan members in the capital were now almost all silent as cicadas in winter, Kangxi could resolve the issue of Manchu generals at the front avoiding battle ahead of schedule.

The following month, Prince Shuncheng Aisin Gioro Lergiyen submitted a memorial impeaching himself, stating that he had exhausted the troops and wasted supplies, missing the opportunity for victory, and requested to be relieved of his position as the Great General who Pacifies the South.

Kangxi granted the request. He ordered Zhao Liangdong, one of the four Han generals of Hexi and the Regional Commander of Ningxia, to be the Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou, leading troops into Yunnan.

Less than half a month after Zhao Liangdong led his troops toward Yunnan, he reached the walls of Kunming.

Gushan Beizi Aisin Gioro Zhangtai repeatedly blocked Zhao Liangdong from advancing further, saying that the Eight Banners' sons were precious and could not suffer heavy casualties; later, he tried to have other armies replace Zhao Liangdong.

Zhao Liangdong produced Kangxi's secret edict, ignored Aisin Gioro Zhangtai's orders, and led the troops to attack the city directly.

After Zhao Liangdong produced the imperial edict, the other Han generals only followed his orders; seeing this, some Eight Banners generals, recalling the strange changes in the capital, hurriedly followed suit in the attack.

Zhao Liangdong, a mere Han general, had actually seized the actual command of the Qing army at the front. This terrified the Qing clan members.

What terrified them even more was that after Zhao Liangdong besieged Kunming for only a few days, the city walls were breached, and Wu Shifan surrendered and committed suicide in public.

After entering the city, the clan generals demanded the "Qing tradition" of looting, as the Wu family had operated in Kunming for many years and possessed countless treasures.

However, Zhao Liangdong produced another imperial edict, ordering the entire army to maintain discipline, not to harass the people, and to seal the Wu family's treasures to await rewards based on merit.

Zhao Liangdong was already a rare disciplined commander among the generals. Even among the Han generals, only his troops never looted. Now that he held actual control of the front-line army and had Kangxi's imperial edict in hand, he naturally wouldn't let the Qing army run wild.

After sighing, Aisin Gioro Zhangtai actually supported Zhao Liangdong, helping him pacify the clan and Manchu generals.

When Kunming fell, the common people had expected to be slaughtered and looted, but they didn't expect that the things they feared would not happen.

They took the initiative to come forward to offer gifts to reward the army and denounced the Wu family's atrocities in Yunnan, seemingly viewing the Qing army as their saviors.

The Qing army was flattered.

The Manchu generals, in particular, thought these people were pretending to reward the army while actually wanting to assassinate them, and they remained suspicious for a long time.

Zhao Liangdong was speechless: "The world belongs to the Qing now, and you are suppressing a rebellion, so isn't it normal for the common people to stand on your side? You aren't the Later Jin army that invaded the pass to seize territory in the past."

Manchu generals: "..."

Ah, right.

100,000
