71.一更二更 [V]
胤礽本来也想骑高头大马。但高头大马不想让胤礽骑它。
皇宫里人见人爱的团宠小太子，被马儿嫌弃了。
嫌弃就嫌弃，胤礽骑了一匹小马驹，照样哒哒哒跑得飞快。
胤禔安慰胤礽：“你比我小两岁，等你长我这么大，肯定也能骑大马。到时候我们兄弟俩再来比赛。”
胤礽道：“好……兔子！”
胤礽说话的时候，胤禔手中弓箭已经离弦，把兔子钉在了地上。
侍卫赶紧跑去把兔子拎了过来。
胤禔嫌弃：“这么小只？皮灰蒙蒙的，难看，回去送给三弟算了。”
福全选的路线，猎物特别多。胤禔很快又射了四只兔子，每只兔子都很难看，胤禔全给弟弟们分了。
胤禔有点生气：“就没有好看一点的兔子吗！”
一箭不发的胤礽道：“反正都会被我们吃掉，好不好看无所谓。”
胤禔道：“我想给你做一顶兔皮帽。”
胤礽道：“等会儿不是有豹子可以猎吗？”
胤禔道：“豹子皮只能做一套衣服。”
胤禔倔脾气上来，胤礽劝都劝不动。他非要去给胤礽猎一只最好看的兔子。
福全赶紧吩咐侍卫去找管理猎场的人，让他们在这边多放些兔子。
皇家猎场的猎物大部分都是开始狩猎的时候从圈养的地方放出来的，不然这帮大老爷们进山翻地三尺也不一定能找到一只兔子。
京郊附近猎场的大型猎物也全是圈养的。只有去到例如木兰猎场这种和许多天然林、天然草原连通的大型猎场，才有可能有野生大型动物误入。
不过许多骑兵气势汹汹地闯进林子里，就算有野生大型动物也会逃得飞快，基本没有危险。
胤禔知道猎场的兔子大部分都是圈养的。他高声嚷嚷，就是让猎场的人多选几只皮毛好看的兔子出来，别老拿不好看的兔子敷衍他。
他嚷嚷完之后，只过了半个时辰，就猎到了好几只一根杂毛都没有的纯色兔子。
给胤礽做完一套帽子手套之后还有剩，胤禔就准备给惠妃也做一点东西。
福全问：“你不自己留？”
胤禔道：“我不怕冷，不用穿毛皮。”
胤礽小声道：“伯伯其实是想问，送给汗阿玛的兔子呢？”
胤禔疑惑：“汗阿玛难道连兔子都打不到？”
福全：“……”这孩子，又开始糟心了。
胤礽道：“打得到。但哥哥第一次来打猎，还是得送点猎物给汗阿玛。”
胤禔看了一眼侍卫马屁股上挂着的众多猎物，道：“嗯，那堆都送给汗阿玛。”
质不行，量来凑。反正汗阿玛也不会在意兔子皮毛的颜色。他根本不用兔子皮。
“行吧。”胤礽对福全像小动物一样拱拱手，“伯伯……”
福全失笑：“我知道，我会帮大阿哥说好话。”
胤礽讨好笑：“谢谢伯伯。”
胤禔见弟弟可爱的模样，也忍不住笑了：“你要不要骑大马？哥带你。”
胤礽道：“等大哥猎到豹子再带我骑。”
福全都说可以猎到豹子，那么这次围场肯定有准备豹子。
胤礽那模糊不清的童年记忆中，似乎有一次和福全一同围猎时，猎到过豹子。
大概又是他闭着眼睛乱射几支箭，然后侍卫们举起豹子“太子威武！太子殿下猎到了豹子！”这种猎法吧。
不知道真英武的大哥，能不能凭自己的功夫猎到豹子。
他们正聊着，密林间传来豹子的咆哮声。
胤禔眼睛一亮，兴奋地策马向前。
侍卫们比胤禔速度更快，挡在了胤禔前面。即使是被圈养后没了野性的豹子，如果小皇子们太过惊慌害怕，也可能会遭遇危险。
胤禔没有冒进。他待侍卫们把豹子围好之后才射出箭矢，每一支箭矢都正中目标。
胤禔“啧”了一声：“还不如人机灵。”
胤禔这句话一说出口，听言的侍卫们忍不住抖了抖。
他们突然想起来，胤禔在宗室逼宫的时候，手头那把弓箭可是收割过人命的。
“还有一只，你来。”胤禔把射箭的好位置让给了胤礽。
胤礽努力拉满小弓箭，五支箭射过去，有三支箭射中了目标。
胤禔高兴极了：“真厉害！等弟弟你再养养身体，肯定比汗阿玛还强！”
胤礽：“……”这、这倒不至于。
前世阿玛夸儿子武力值高的时候老喜欢用大哥当对比物，这一世大哥夸弟弟怎么用阿玛当参照物了？
胤礽射中了猎物，胤禔比自己射中了豹子还高兴。
福全惊诧地发现，胤禔居然这么能说，夸奖胤礽的话连句重复的都没有，真心诚意极了。
谁说大阿哥不会说话来着？那也得看说话的对象是谁。
豹子狩猎完毕，胤禔让人收拾好猎物，带着弟弟去河边先打一顿牙祭。
伺候的人很快取来调料，就地将猎物粗粗腌制，先给一位亲王两位皇子烤只小兔子垫垫肚子。
胤禔诗兴大发，对着胤礽吟了几首不怎么押韵的诗。
胤礽使劲夸赞，把胤禔刚夸赞他的话换了词还了回去，听得胤禔眉开眼笑。
福全坐在一旁，看着两兄弟你夸我我夸你，心里有点酸。
不过他已经习惯了。
他多次带着两位皇子玩耍，对这两兄弟互夸起来就拿别人当布景板的事真的已经习惯了。
所以为什么他们兄弟几人关系没这么好？这一定都是……咳咳。
不知道是不是烤兔子的香味太浓，引了几个人过来。
胤礽扫了一眼，不认识。
那几个人自我介绍，胤礽绞尽脑汁想了想，还是不认识。
这估计就是宗室或者勋贵中某些不重要的人吧。
既然不是什么重要的人，胤礽就懒得把心思分在他们身上，托腮看着火焰上的兔子，全心全意虔诚地等候美味的兔子肉烤熟。
那几个人和裕亲王、太子、大阿哥见过礼之后，听闻大部分猎物都是大阿哥猎到的，表情崇敬极了，直夸大阿哥勇猛。
伸手不打笑脸人，虽然大阿哥不太耐烦自己和太子弟弟一起吃烧烤看风景的时候有人来打扰，但被夸了他还是很高兴，便邀请他们一起来吃兔子。
那几人就开始和大阿哥聊打猎的事。
福全听他们从打猎聊到八旗的武力值，再聊到勇武才是八旗子弟该有的本事，一家里的继承人，还是得选一个身体健康的。
他嘴边浮现讥笑。
看来自己明哲保身老好人的形象很出名，这群人跑来和大阿哥套近乎，都不避开他，料定了他不会去向皇帝告状。
胤礽往大阿哥那边看了一眼，然后继续守着兔子。
还好还好，这群人的挑拨离间很委婉，大哥估计听不懂。听不懂就行，要是听懂了，他怕大哥暴怒之下做出不理智的行为，被这几个当出头鸟的傻子害得受罚。
好不容易和大哥一起开开心心狩个猎，大哥也能从繁重的功课中喘口气。如果因为几个傻子导致功课翻倍，大哥就太倒霉了。
胤礽小鼻子嗅嗅，高声打断那群人越说越嗨的挑拨离间：“大哥，兔子是不是烤好了？”
胤禔道：“我来看看。”
他走到兔子前，装模作样的用铁叉子插了插兔肉，然后看向旁边烤兔子的下人。
下人道：“还要再烤一会儿。”
胤礽装可怜：“我饿了。”
胤禔从怀里掏出一块用帕子包好的绿豆糕：“先吃一块垫垫肚子。”
胤礽犹豫：“我今日的糕点份额已经吃光了。”
“这不是你的份额，是我的。”胤禔道，“快吃。”
胤礽点头：“好。”
看着弟弟美美地吃着最爱的绿豆糕，胤禔脸上浮现开心的笑容。
康熙听御医的话，严格控制胤礽的饮食，不让胤礽多吃糕点，好让胤礽正餐多吃一些。所以胤礽一天只有一块糕点可以吃。
当然，胤礽不能吃糕点，可以吃肉干、奶糊、水果等零食果腹。
康熙不可能亏待胤礽，但胤禔看着胤礽馋糕糕，总觉得康熙在亏待胤礽，所以老会偷偷藏几块胤礽爱吃的糕点在身上，弟弟饿了就投喂弟弟。
后来小胤祉、小胤禛等阿哥饿了之后，也第一时间找大哥，从大哥怀里摸零食来吃。
胤禔成了行走的零食袋子。
康熙知晓这件事之后，思及这有助于儿子们维系兄弟情分，便睁一只眼闭一只眼，假装不知道。
胤礽只比胤禔小两岁，但胤禔一向把胤礽当脆弱的奶娃娃对待。
胤礽吃完糕点之后，胤禔便给胤礽擦嘴，又拿来下人们已经温好的牛奶让胤礽润喉。
见胤禔对胤礽如此细心体贴，刚正拐弯抹角说胤礽坏话的人面面相觑。
他们疑惑，大阿哥是没听出他们的挑拨离间；还是听出来了，故意用照顾太子的事来堵他们的嘴？
他们想再次试探一下。
一人开玩笑似的道：“太子殿下，您要保重身体啊，出门在外连水都不能喝，多麻烦。”
胤礽还没开口，胤禔皱眉道：“谁说他不能喝水？能喝牛奶为什么要喝水？”
胤礽舔了舔嘴角的奶胡子，忙道：“大哥，不能这么说，你忘记何不食肉糜的典故了吗？”
胤禔愣了一下，道：“啊对，抱歉，我忘记不是什么家庭都能把牛奶当水喝了。”
某人：“……”
胤禔补充道：“不是我们皇宫奢侈，我们自己有养奶牛，西方培养的那种奶水特别多的奶牛，所以牛奶够喝。”
某人：“……”他并不是想说这个。
他想再接再厉：“我们家也有养牛。只是大多时候我们直接喝冰的，只有体弱的人才会喝温水。”
chapters.translated_text:
Yinreng realized at this moment that being a crown prince without real power was truly wonderful; he only needed to cheer Kangxi on from the sidelines while he himself slacked off and fished in troubled waters.

Seeing that Kangxi hadn't finished dealing with the matter of his hairstyle, still had to observe the new official schools, and had to summon his ministers to discuss attacking the island of Taiwan across the sea to build the Qing Dynasty's first offshore military base... Haha, no wonder in history, none of Kangxi's concubines were pregnant this year. Kangxi was so busy he couldn't even touch the ground; how could he have time for the harem?

The only remaining time he had was spent accompanying Imperial Noble Consort Tong.

Ever since Empress Xiao'an had a miscarriage due to taking the wrong medicine in the palace, the concubines had hidden away all the so-called folk remedies sent by their maiden families, not daring to take them anymore.

After Imperial Noble Consort Tong received the folk remedy sent by Tong Guowei, she hesitated for a long time. Seeing that Kangxi had been almost exclusively favoring her lately, she temporarily tucked the remedy away at the bottom of a chest, wanting to try once more to see if she could conceive naturally.

When people hold onto hope, both their spirit and body gradually improve, and Kangxi was more inclined to visit Imperial Noble Consort Tong; this was a virtuous cycle.

Yinreng sighed with his hands behind his back, then continued happily to find his eldest brother to play.

His eldest brother had recently been learning musical instruments, and Yinreng followed along for a while, laying the groundwork for his future identity as a musical prodigy.

In the third month, Kangxi's mausoleum was finally completed. The Crown Prince led the First Prince and a group of ministers to escort the coffins of the two empresses into the underground palace of the mausoleum.

This was the first time Yinreng had shouldered such a significant ceremony on his own.

Dressed in heavy crown prince ceremonial robes, he kept his small face stern and completed every step of the ceremony perfectly, leaving the ministers and noblewomen in awe.

Some ministers remarked that this marked the Crown Prince's official debut on the political stage of the Qing Dynasty.

Only Prince Yu Fuquan and Prince Gong Changning smiled smugly in their hearts. You have no idea that this Crown Prince has already begun participating in state affairs. Our Emperor has been acting so aggressively lately, and much of the credit should go to our little Crown Prince.

Oh, actually, it shouldn't go to the little Crown Prince, but to Emperor Shunzhi, who had once possessed the little Crown Prince.

Sigh.

Fuquan and Changning asked worriedly, "Can you still hold up?"

Yinreng's small face was flushed red with exhaustion, and sweat had soaked every inch of skin on his face, yet he still nodded with a smile: "No problem."

Yinzhi tugged at his own imperial prince ceremonial robes: "Really? I feel like I have a problem, and you don't? If you can't hold up, tell me. I'll fake a faint, and then you can naturally use the excuse of taking care of me to rest."

Fuquan and Changning: "..." Eldest Prince, I admire you!

This kind of pure brotherly love made Fuquan and Changning, who were also brothers, extremely envious.

Although Yinreng wouldn't do that, he still said: "Okay, thank you, brother. If I can't hold up, I will definitely tell you."

The two children held hands and looked at each other warmly. Fuquan and Changning coughed, let the children drink a little more water, and continued with the rest of the ceremony.

After completing the ceremony, the two children did not return to the palace but went to the West Garden.

Kangxi finally couldn't stand staying in the palace, a place surrounded by walls and stones on all sides, and ran to the West Garden to work.

Because the Three Feudatories had been pacified, he held a banquet for his ministers at Yingtai in the West Garden, and officials above the rank of Vice Director in the capital could attend the banquet and receive silk rewards.

After the banquet, Kangxi stayed in the West Garden and didn't leave. After the Crown Prince and the First Prince sent the two empresses to be buried in the underground palace, they also returned directly to the West Garden.

The West Garden not only had mountains and water but also experimental fields set up by the Emperor and Empress to encourage farming and weaving.

As soon as the two princes arrived at the West Garden, Kangxi, as if showing off, took the two princes down to the fields to farm.

When Empress Renxiao was still alive, Kangxi and she would come to the Fengze Garden north of Yingtai every year to farm and weave. Kangxi would farm, and Empress Renxiao would raise silkworms, finding quite a bit of the joy of an ordinary couple outside the palace.

After Kangxi began his personal rule, he was busy with affairs and was saddened by the sight, so he hadn't come for several years.

When Yinreng saw Kangxi personally tilling the land and showing off to him, he curled his lip, rolled up his trouser legs, and went into the field too, working in a professional manner, even more skillfully than Kangxi.

Kangxi was puzzled: "How do you even know how to farm?"

Yinzhi looked, rolled up his trouser legs, and followed him into the field: "There's no difference between pulling weeds in the fields and pulling weeds in the Imperial Garden; I know how to do it too."

Yinreng almost gave Yinzhi a thumbs up.

Kangxi was amused and annoyed: "Can these be the same?"

Yinzhi pulled a few weeds: "Look, they are."

Kangxi: "..." As long as his eldest son opens his mouth, it makes one want to beat him up.

If his eldest son weren't a prince, he would probably be beaten up by many people in the future.

Seeing that his sons disdained his farming skills, Kangxi, with a very mischievous heart, assigned each of them a small plot of land and said they would compete to see who could finish weeding first.

All three father and sons were pampered and competitive. In the end, all three were howling in pain while soaking in the bath.

It hurts, it hurts, it hurts! My whole body is falling apart!

The eunuchs were all trying hard to suppress their laughter.

They had to hold it in; if they laughed out loud, it would be a matter of losing their heads!

After the bath, the two princes lay flat on chairs like corpses, while Kangxi, rubbing his sore arms, still had to continue dealing with state affairs.

Kangxi would look at the memorials for two seconds, then glance at his two sons lying there.

He saw his two sons squirming on the lounge chairs, stretching their necks to suck on milk that had been chilled, using straws made of wheat stalks, looking very satisfied.

Kangxi said with displeasure: "Who came up with the idea of using wheat stalks as straws!"

Flattery! Isn't this teaching my sons bad habits!

Zhao Chang said: "It was the Crown Prince and the First Prince who figured it out themselves."

Kangxi: "..."

Case closed; it was his own sons who didn't put their intelligence into proper matters and only knew how to think of devious ways.

"Father, it's very nice here. Can I not go back to the palace and just live here from now on?" Yinreng suddenly asked.

Kangxi laughed: "Now you know it's nice here at Father's place? Who was the one shouting before that they didn't want to be the Crown Prince?"

Yinzhi muttered to himself. It is indeed nice at Father's place, but it's not the Crown Prince brother's place.

In a few years, when he moves out of the palace to build his own mansion, he can live in a place like this every day. If the Crown Prince brother wants to live here, you definitely won't allow it.

Kangxi indeed wouldn't allow it.

How could such a young Crown Prince live alone outside the palace? Kangxi only promised to bring the Crown Prince here more often.

Yinzhi muttered even more intensely. Being a Crown Prince is really boring for my brother.

Yinreng never thought Kangxi would agree; he just wanted to get permission to leave the palace and come here whenever he wanted.

Yinreng had his eye on the experimental fields and silkworm farm here and wanted to do something here.

He was idle anyway, and besides being a strategist for Kangxi, he needed to do other things. For example, cultivating good seeds, reforming farming and weaving machines, and breeding high-yield livestock could all be done in Fengze Garden.

Yinreng detailed his request; he had read many Western books, which contained many good things to improve the national economy and people's livelihood, and he wanted to experiment with them himself.

Kangxi knew his son couldn't sit still. He had read many Western books himself and knew that researching these things couldn't be considered "strange skills and ingenious devices" or "neglecting one's proper work." Moreover, Yinreng's health would be better if he were often outside the palace, so Kangxi agreed, only requiring Yinreng to return to the palace on time.

"Hmm, when I make something good, I'll release it in Father's name! Father, protect me from being targeted by the green-eyed monsters!" Yinreng said.

Kangxi was puzzled: "What is 'green-eyed monster'?"

Yinreng said: "It's people who can't stand to see me doing well!"

A list of names immediately flashed through Kangxi's imperial mind, and he nodded: "Okay."

Yinzhi buried his face in the chair, hiding his displeased expression.

He had a lot to say, but he didn't dare to reveal it.

Yinzhi had already begun studying history books. He specifically looked up many records of crown princes in various dynasties.

Hearing Yinreng say this, he immediately thought, my brother isn't afraid of being envied by others; he's afraid that if his talent is too prominent, he'll be feared by Father.

Yinzhi said in a muffled voice: "If you have any ideas, tell me. After I move out of the palace to build my mansion, it will be much more convenient than Father's way of doing things."

Yinreng immediately rolled over and pressed down on Yinzhi: "Thank you, eldest brother, you're the best. Come, let me press you."

"Hmph." Yinzhi rolled over and flipped Yinreng off.

Yinreng counterattacked, the "Crown Prince Mountain" pressing down.

Yinzhi braced his hands on the chair and arched his butt, pushing the "Crown Prince Mountain" off.

The two children didn't get up, just rolled and arched back and forth on the wide lounge chair, looking like two caterpillars fighting.

Kangxi watched with great interest, not even noticing that the ink from his brush had dripped onto the memorial.

Zhao Chang was so anxious he was scratching his head, not knowing whether he should remind the Emperor.

...

After Yinreng got permission to use Fengze Garden at will, he stayed there every day and really started to tinker with things.

Yinzi and Yinzhen, who could finally run and jump, were brought along by Yinreng and often came to Fengze Garden to play.

Kangxi was extremely helpless. He only allowed Yinreng to go to Fengze Garden, but Yinreng brought all his younger brothers along.

Now he had been persuaded by Yinreng to give Yinzhi, who was studying, one day off every six days. On that day off, Yinzhi would also follow his younger brothers to tend to the crops and take care of the silkworms.

Kangxi complained about this to the Empress Dowager. The Empress Dowager looked at Kangxi's smug expression and gave him an eye roll.

The princes are personally farming and weaving at such a young age, knowing the hardships of the people; these are all good seeds for a wise monarch and virtuous king. You should be proud, what are you complaining about?

Time approached the fifth month, which was again the anniversary of Empress Renxiao's death.

Just as Yinreng was preparing for the bathing, fasting, and sacrificial rites, he received the news that he was to have a birthday banquet.

Yinreng was dumbfounded: "Ah? Me? There must be a mistake, right?"

In his previous life, after he grew up, he would receive gifts and rewards on his birthday, but he never had a grand birthday banquet.

Kangxi said: "The sacrifice for your mother is on the third day of the fifth month, so your birthday is moved to the fourth day of the fifth month. If I never celebrate it for you, your mother would probably be sad too."

Yinreng was still standing there, foolishly stunned.

He thought he had misheard.

He thought he was hallucinating.

He even thought he had been under house arrest for so long that everything now was just a dream before death.

Would Father say "If I don't celebrate your birthday, your mother would be sad," instead of "Your mother died giving birth to you, you must be sad every year at this time"?

Kangxi didn't notice Yinreng's dullness and continued: "I wanted to set it on the second day of the fifth month. You were born in the early hours of the third, so the evening of the second would also work. But the next day is the sacrifice for your mother, so you probably wouldn't be in the mood for fun."

When Kangxi made this decision, no ministers objected.

Anyway, Kangxi had done many shocking things last year and this year; letting the Crown Prince celebrate his birthday a day late was nothing major.

Using filial piety as an excuse, the ministers all thought it was quite good.

"What's wrong?" After Kangxi finished speaking, he realized Yinreng was stunned.

He amusedly poked Yinreng, who swayed like a roly-poly toy, his eyes still unfocused.

Kangxi felt a bit of heartache: "It's just celebrating your birthday, are you so surprised that you've gone silly?"

Yinreng came back to his senses and immediately shook his head: "Father, let's forget it. You don't even hold a 'Thousand Autumns' banquet, why should I hold a birthday banquet?"

Kangxi said: "It won't be a grand one, just the people in the palace eating a good meal together, and giving your brothers and sisters a day off..."

"Okay!" Yinreng said immediately.

Kangxi laughed loudly, lifted Yinreng up, and shook him: "You, as long as there's a benefit for your brothers and sisters, you agree, don't you?"

Yinreng deliberately flattered him: "No, no, I only agreed because it won't be a grand one. Thank you, Father, you are the best Father in the world, your son loves you!"

"Shameless." Kangxi held Yinreng in his arms, his arm skillfully cushioning Yinreng's bottom.

Even though Yinreng was seven years old this year, Kangxi still held his son very easily.

Kangxi sighed: "You're growing into a big child, Father can barely hold you anymore."

Yinreng hugged Kangxi's neck and rubbed against his shoulder: "In Father's presence, I will always be a little child. When Father can't hold me, I'll hold Father's hand. Father, please don't ever throw me away."

He only wanted this Father, not the Father from his previous life.

Yinreng was both happy and scared. He really worried that all of this was a dream before he died, and he also worried that the current Father would become that terrible Emperor Kangxi from his first life when he got older.

If only he could never grow up. If he never grew up, Father would always trust and cherish him, and would not fear, loathe, or hate him to death.

Kangxi laughed: "Throw you away? You're a little piglet I've raised with such difficulty, how could I let someone else take advantage of that?"

Yinreng deliberately made pig-snorting sounds to amuse Kangxi.

Kangxi and Yinreng played for a while, then gave Yinreng another surprise.

He had only started learning poetry last year, and he gave his first proud work to Yinreng.

Yinreng recited it, shaking his head: "A hundred-year-old paulownia tree grows long, a thousand-year-old pine fills the branches. Ten thousand peaks welcome auspicious energy, billions celebrate the spiritual mushroom. Good poem! Good poem!"

Kangxi was a little nervous: "Is it really good?"

Yinreng encouraged Kangxi: "Father, you've only been learning for a year. Isn't this already good enough?"

Although after his father had been learning poetry for decades, his level was still just like this, without the slightest improvement. Yinreng said quietly in his heart.

Emperor Kangxi, who prided himself on having first-class literary and martial skills, was really not good at writing poetry. No wonder Qianlong said he was like his grandfather; in this regard, Qianlong and Kangxi were indeed very similar. Fourth brother's poetic talent was much, much better.

Kangxi was persuaded by his son.

So he took his proud work to Gao Shiqi: "My son said I write poetry really well, what do you think, my dear minister?"

Gao Shiqi: "...Your Majesty has achieved such results after only one year of learning poetry; it is truly a natural gift."

Gao Shiqi secretly wiped his sweat. That's right, the Emperor has only been learning poetry for a year. When I had been learning for a year, what I wrote wasn't very good either.

Kangxi was extremely proud and went to find Yinreng again, wanting to write a piece of calligraphy for him personally.

It just so happened that Yinzhi came after school to play with Yinreng. Kangxi stood at the door, pricking up his ears to eavesdrop.

Kangxi knew that eavesdropping on his eldest son would likely make him angry nine times out of ten, but he still couldn't control his urge to eavesdrop.

Yinzhi: "Who wrote this? You? Not bad."

Yinreng: "It's not me, it's a birthday poem Father wrote for me?"

Yinzhi: "What? Father? Just this? Isn't it embarrassing?"

Yinreng: "Father has only been learning for a year, and he's already written it very well."

Yinzhi: "Heh, oh, not as good as me."

Yinreng: "Wait until next year for your birthday, and I'll have Father write one for you."

Yinzhi: "Ugly, reject."

Yinreng: "...Eldest brother, please don't use the simplified words I taught you so casually!"

Yinzhi: "It's written too ugly, I refuse."

Kangxi: "..."

He took a deep breath and turned to leave.

Kangxi was worried that if he pushed the door open and went in now, he would want to beat Yinzhi up.

He decided that from now on, he would only write birthday poems for his precious son! And write them secretly! And throw them away after writing, not allowed to be saved!

(Emperor Kangxi: Ah, yes, yes, you're right.)

Kangxi wanted to give his son the very best; how could he possibly agree to scale it back?

Kangxi and Yinreng began a tug-of-war, each citing classics to insist on their own viewpoints, even bringing the matter to the Imperial Lectures for the officials to debate.

The lecturers at the Imperial Lectures: "..." Fine, the Crown Prince's ceremonial guard is indeed related to ritual, we can discuss it.

Kangxi and the little Crown Prince looked at each other helplessly.

Kangxi: These people only know how to spout nonsense.

The Crown Prince: We might as well draw lots.

Gabula, who was already seriously ill, was almost choked by Songgotu's words.

Gabula sighed deeply.

Why was his health so poor? If only he could live a little longer and help the Crown Prince for a while more.

He had thought that since he was led in directly by Zhao Chang, who was guarding the door, there would definitely be no one in the study.

Yinreng hurriedly tidied his clothes and messy short hair, bowed to Kangxi obediently, and exchanged greetings with Yu Chenglong.

Seeing the uncontrollable smile on Kangxi's face, Yu Chenglong immediately understood that he had become a tool for the mean-spirited Emperor to bully his son.

He sighed helplessly in his heart.

When he saw the Emperor last time, why didn't he notice the Emperor was so playful? Was it because the Three Feudatories had been settled and he held absolute power that the Emperor was showing his true nature?

Yu Chenglong had sons and grandsons. If his son dared to bully his grandson like this, he would have already grabbed the sole of his shoe and slapped his son's face.

But the person in front of him was the Emperor, not his son, so he could only pretend he hadn't noticed anything and look sympathetically at the little Crown Prince, who was full of suppressed anger but still had to squeeze out a stiff smile.

"Yu Chenglong wants to test your studies, don't embarrass me." Kangxi ruffled the short hair Yinreng had just tidied.

Yinreng silently smoothed his messy hair and said gloomily: "Yes, Imperial Father."

Yinreng bowed to Yu Chenglong: "Please, Minister Yu."

Yu Chenglong: "..." I never said I wanted to test the Crown Prince's studies! Your Majesty, don't talk nonsense!

But since the Emperor had spoken, his word was law, and others could only cooperate. Yu Chenglong helplessly asked about the books Yinreng was currently reading and then randomly picked a few passages.

Kangxi wanted to show off his son, and Yinreng couldn't let Kangxi lose face, so he could only concentrate and activate his "memory cheat."

Thus, Yu Chenglong asked for a long time, and Yinreng's answers were word-perfect, even correcting a few errors for Yu Chenglong, whose memory wasn't as good as it used to be.

Yu Chenglong gasped: "The Crown Prince has actually memorized all the books?"

Yinreng nodded, saying modestly: "I have memorized some."

Kangxi ruffled the hair Yinreng had just tidied again: "So Minister Yu knows why I don't let him study in the Pavilion? As the Crown Prince, memorizing the classics is enough. If he has the interest later, he can continue to study them. Now, while I still have the energy, I should teach him more knowledge that cannot be learned from books."

Yu Chenglong sighed: "The Emperor is right. But you shouldn't let the Crown Prince go farming."

Kangxi laughed: "Farming is his hobby; I don't teach him this. Ordinary children play around in their spare time; he doesn't like luxurious things, nor does he like riding horses through the streets, he only loves farming, and I am also very helpless."

Yinreng silently tidied his hair. No, farming is not a hobby; I quite like playing around, and farming is not an interest; I really want to achieve something, but unfortunately, liberal arts student, useless!

Yu Chenglong had nothing more to say.

Not to mention princes, even children from ordinary noble families inevitably have some luxurious hobbies.

The Crown Prince lived a simple life, and his only hobby was farming; what could he say other than praise? Could he say that the Crown Prince farming himself was beneath his status?

If they dared to impeach him for this, history books would definitely record them, letting future generations call them pedantic.

"Congratulations, Your Majesty." Yu Chenglong could only bow and bend his waist.

Kangxi nodded slightly. The plan to show off his son today had been preliminarily achieved.

"Grant a seat." Kangxi granted Yu Chenglong a seat again and then took Yinreng onto his lap: "Look at this memorial."

The person who submitted the memorial was also named Yu Chenglong, and he was impeaching the Director-General of River Affairs, Jin Fu.

Yinreng looked up at the elderly Yu Chenglong and then at Kangxi, who was waiting for his question: "Is it this Minister Yu?"

He knew it wasn't, but since Kangxi was waiting for him to ask, he asked.

Kangxi smiled and shook his head: "It is a younger Yu Chenglong. You can call the person who submitted this Yu Zhenjia. You can call the Minister Yu in front of you Yu Beiming."

Yinreng asked: "Are they family?"

Kangxi smiled and shook his head again: "No. It's a coincidence, isn't it? Both of them are honest officials and capable administrators. When Yu Beiming came to see me, Yu Zhenjia's impeachment memorial happened to arrive, so I had him look at it together."

Yu Chenglong bowed and said: "This official is not good at managing water affairs and cannot resolve the Emperor's doubts. But Yu Zhenjia is honest and upright as an official and would not impeach someone for private gain."

Kangxi said: "Haven't you read many books on managing water disasters? Look at his impeachment memorial and tell me your thoughts."

Yinreng was speechless.

He asked with his eyes: Can the son not look or think about it? The son wants to go back to sleep.

Kangxi answered with his eyes: No, hurry up and talk properly.

Yinreng sighed in his heart. Father hasn't shown off his son enough yet.

He roughly read the memorial and said: "Not impeaching for private gain does not mean the impeachment is correct. Managing the Yellow River requires starting from reality, carefully investigating the geography and hydrology along the banks, before making a decision. If Yu Zhenjia has already explored the banks of the Yellow River before proposing such suggestions, then Imperial Father can listen to him. But he has never walked along the Yellow River and is merely assuming that water management is universal based on his experience managing other rivers; whatever suggestions he makes can be ignored."

Yinreng didn't continue talking about Yu Zhenjia; he picked up another memorial that also impeached Jin Fu: "Although Yu Zhenjia didn't start from reality, he was at least well-intentioned; the others impeaching Jin Fu for corruption are unreasonable."

Kangxi asked: "Have you heard rumors about Jin Fu and know that he is not corrupt?"

Yinreng said: "It is impossible not to be corrupt when managing river works. Even in the Imperial Household Department, every time money passes through someone's hands, they deduct a few coins. When funds for river management are allocated, they are deducted layer by layer; historically, if three-tenths of the funds are actually used for water management, one can be called an honest official."

The smile on Kangxi's lips faded.

Yu Chenglong looked up in astonishment, ignoring etiquette to look at Yinreng.

"Jin Fu was able to achieve results, and after achieving results, he was impeached for embezzling five-tenths of the funds." Yinreng sighed, "He should have indeed used five-tenths of the funds on the river, so being impeached was inevitable."

69. First and Second Updates [V]

The most impartial and harsh evaluation in this world is the final judgment after death.

In later television dramas, in order to highlight the two Yu Chenglongs, their deeds were even merged into one person, and Jin Fu, who was hostile to them, became a representative of corrupt officials who embezzled river funds.

But this was only in film and television works.

People in later generations, as long as they had seriously attended junior high and high school geography classes, could speak eloquently about "river management experience." This knowledge, which later generations looked down upon, was experience and lessons summarized bit by bit in ancient times by many people walking along the banks of great rivers, step by step, wearing out countless pairs of shoes.

Jin Fu was such a person. After his death, he protected the Yellow River from major breaches for nearly thirty years, and the people along the banks built temples and erected monuments for him, honoring him as the "River God."

Since Jin Fu's death, no other river management expert appeared in the Kangxi era. Those who impeached Jin Fu at most made repairs on the framework Jin Fu had already built.

Even so, Jin Fu's achievements laid the foundation for the Kang-Qian Golden Age.

Yet such a person suffered constant hardships throughout his life, was continuously impeached for corruption, and was even uglified as a corrupt official by television screenwriters who didn't read history or think.

Sad and lamentable.

Fortunately, even with such uglification, his achievements in history books would not be erased, and the common people still offered incense in his River God temples.

"Their bodies and names may vanish, but the river flows on forever."

Yinreng had already made up his mind to use his meager wisdom to make this era better, so he stopped thinking about whether being too sharp would make Kangxi wary. Therefore, Yinreng had been subtly influencing Kangxi for several years, trying to make the life of Jin Fu, a capable river management official, have fewer setbacks.

At worst, he would just be a think tank for Kangxi, and when Kangxi gave him real power, he would pretend to be sick.

But come to think of it, in his first life, he didn't seem to have any real power either, just working for Kangxi all the time.

Yinreng composed himself and continued to describe the Yellow River.

Kangxi's attitude toward Yellow River management also followed the principle of seeking truth from facts. He had once sent imperial guards to walk through the entire Yellow River basin and map it out.

After knowing that Yinreng could already recite most of the Four Books and Five Classics, Kangxi stopped teaching Yinreng Confucian book knowledge and changed to teaching him various administrative knowledge.

The Yellow River was the top priority, and its harm to the Great Qing was even more serious than the Three Feudatories. Yinreng had naturally seen the map of the Yellow River basin.

Yinreng quietly let Yin Ti suggest that the map of the Yellow River basin be made into a sand table and handed over to Jin Fu for improvement.

Jin Fu was a man who knew how to manage rivers but not how to speak. He was too straightforward, and his thinking was even more like that of an engineering student; every time he debated, he couldn't win against those who impeached him, and he relied entirely on Kangxi to protect him.

With the sand table, Jin Fu suddenly had an epiphany. He no longer debated with people in fields he wasn't good at, but pointed at the sand table, describing the terrain and hydrology of every bend of the Yellow River in detail, and then asked the people who impeached him if they knew it. If you don't know, stop talking nonsense, go and do a field survey first.

Kangxi was also convinced by Jin Fu. Originally, the military pledge Jin Fu made this year was due to expire, and he was about to face the disaster of being dismissed from office and continuing to manage the river while under indictment.

The Rebellion of the Three Feudatories had been settled early, and Kangxi had made a lot of money from confiscating property, so he gave Jin Fu an order in advance, giving him a five-year extension. Jin Fu was still the Director-General of River Affairs and did not end up with a criminal record despite his achievements.

Yinreng calculated the time; in his first life, Jin Fu fulfilled his promise to Kangxi in the 23rd year of Kangxi. In this life, Kangxi's support for him was greater, so the progress of river management should only be faster, not slower.

Kangxi had people bring the Yellow River sand table. He held Yinreng and let him introduce Jin Fu's river management methods to Yu Chenglong.

Jin Fu's method of managing the river was based on the "binding water to attack sand" method created by Pan Jixun of the Ming Dynasty, and the "embedding dredging in construction" method he innovated, which was very difficult for people at the time to understand.

People in this era were accustomed to finding answers in old books; if something couldn't be found in old books, it would be attacked as unorthodox and impeached by many.

Yinreng, however, was Jin Fu's confidant.

As mentioned before, anyone who had seriously studied geography in later generations knew the situation of the Yellow River basin. Yinreng had a memory cheat; although the maps of the soil, vegetation, and river course of the Yellow River basin in his mind were from several hundred years later, the general climate and soil were similar.

Based on his memory, Yinreng checked for gaps and filled them for Jin Fu, and then let Changtai tell Jin Fu.

Forgot to mention, the person sent by Kangxi to walk the entire Yellow River course in this life was Changtai. Kangxi had this bad habit; he would work anyone he liked to death. He himself was a workaholic when he was young, so he wished everyone around him was a workaholic.

Yu Chenglong indeed had no concept of water management. After Yinreng pointed out the sand table of the Yellow River course to him one by one with his small chubby fingers, he actually understood it and even had the illusion that "I can do it too."

"Director-General Jin is amazing." Yu Chenglong exclaimed, "Your Majesty, you must protect Director-General Jin!"

Kangxi sighed: "It's difficult."

Yu Chenglong was astonished again. Why did the Emperor know Jin Fu's brilliance but still say it was difficult to protect him?

Kangxi said: "Baocheng, you continue to talk to Minister Yu."

Yinreng nodded.

He had been worried that his brilliance would make Kangxi vigilant. He didn't expect Kangxi to have thought of these things long ago, so he could speak boldly and confidently.

Yinreng said: "First of all, in order to manage the river, Jin Fu took out at least five-tenths of the funds for river works. This greatly violated the rules of the river officialdom, so he will definitely be continuously impeached."

Speaking of this, Yinreng chuckled: "Before at the Yong'an Embankment, everyone said it would cost more than 500,000 taels, but Jin Fu built the Yong'an Embankment with only 70,000 taels, which already offended many people."

Although he was an honest official, Yu Chenglong was not stupid. He understood what the officialdom of the Great Qing was like.

Even if he was an honest official and had no surplus wealth in his own home, it didn't mean he hadn't spent money to clear the way. Otherwise, with his official position, his legal income alone would be enough to make him wealthy.

After hearing this, Yu Chenglong sighed deeply.

"Secondly..." Yinreng pointed his small chubby finger at the lower reaches of the Yellow River, "Is river management really good for everyone? Look at this vast stretch of land; it is all fertile soil left behind after the Yellow River changed course, and it has already been occupied by local powerful families in the lower reaches of the Yellow River."

Yinreng stopped at the right moment.

Yu Chenglong had risen rapidly through the ranks during the Kangxi reign; he could not be unaware of the composition of the officials in the imperial court.

Jin Fu’s approach to river management was not like his predecessors, who only repaired breaches as they occurred. He viewed the Yellow River as a whole, managing it "from beginning to end." While dredging the upper reaches of the river, he also surveyed the hidden fields in the lower reaches to secure funds for repairing the riverbanks, which greatly infringed upon the interests of the local powerful clans in the lower Yellow River region.

The "pure officials" Kangxi relied on in the court, such as the censor Guo Xiu and others, all had families who were powerful clans in the lower Yellow River region. They might be upright and incorruptible themselves, and they might be impartial, but if the interests of their hometowns and families were involved, they would never tolerate Jin Fu continuing his river management work.

Yu Chenglong let out a deep sigh: "Jin Fu is too impatient."

Kangxi nodded: "I have hinted at this to him before, but he says that as long as the Yellow River is not tamed, the people on both banks cannot sleep soundly for a single day, and the Qing treasury will continue to waste vast amounts of money and grain on the river channel."

Yinreng interjected: "If the Yellow River were already tamed and the Qing treasury no longer had to spend vast amounts of money on it, those who line their pockets by relying on river management would starve to death. If he, Jin Fu, doesn't die, then who will? Ouch, Ama, why did you hit me?"

Kangxi said: "Don't be so blunt. As the Crown Prince, you must learn to be reserved and profound; you cannot be so straightforward and impetuous."

Yinreng immediately put on an inscrutable expression: "Yes, Ama."

Kangxi looked at Yinreng’s inscrutable expression and barely managed to hold back his laughter: "Very good, very good, that is exactly the expression."

Hearing the logic Yinreng had laid out, Yu Chenglong, who was worried about the country and the people, was feeling depressed, but seeing the royal father and son already playing around, he was momentarily speechless.

He dared not interrupt the playfulness between Kangxi and the Crown Prince. Only after the noble royal father and son had quieted down did he say: "Your servant is willing to write to Yu Zhenjia to explain the stakes involved. With a capable river manager like Jin Fu, a day of peace and prosperity will surely come."

Yinreng shrugged: "Impossible. Never mind the Yellow River; all rivers will have floods when they encounter heavy rain, and they will surely breach their banks once the rainfall is heavy enough. As long as there are no major gaps and river transport can function during non-flood periods, then it is already considered well-managed."

What was he thinking? When the rain gets heavy, the rivers, lakes, and seas in modern society breach their banks just the same.

Yu Chenglong looked blank, clearly not understanding why a well-managed river would still breach its banks.

Kangxi had someone bring over three basins of water and poured them simultaneously from the upper, middle, and lower reaches of the Yellow River model.

Yu Chenglong watched helplessly as the water overflowed the embankments. It felt as if all the strength had been drained from his body. He stared blankly at the water covering the sand table, as if he were seeing the Yellow River breaching its banks and corpses strewn for ten thousand miles.

Kangxi looked at the sand table covered by water, his own mood far from calm.

Originally, Kangxi, like Yu Chenglong, had believed that the scourge of the Yellow River could be eradicated if only a capable person were found.

After having the sand table, Kangxi often studied books on water management from past dynasties with his sons and even sought out people with water management experience from abroad to consult.

Several years ago, Kangxi had gathered capable people from both China and abroad to form an advisory group. Among these advisors were talents in water management.

Through sand table simulations, Kangxi knew that water disasters could not be perfectly solved anywhere. Water disasters were a type of natural calamity; the imperial court had to constantly pour money into it—dredging waterways, repairing embankments, and plugging breaches.

In the final analysis, the Qing Dynasty still lacked money and grain. If the Qing could be like England and other countries, moving the world's wealth for the use of one place, what would there be to worry about regarding the Yellow River?

Repair it, repair it as much as you want—I have plenty of money and grain!

Every time Kangxi looked at the world map, he would fantasize: if he had money, he would build more canals and more roads, so that the decrees of Beijing could reach every corner of the Qing Dynasty without obstruction, and so that the Qing army could appear in any part of the land within a day or two.

If such a vision could be realized, why worry about the stability of the Qing rule?

After Yu Chenglong, who had been forced to stuff his head with water management experience and felt lightheaded, left, Kangxi patted Yinreng on the head: "Once Taiwan is taken, the money in the treasury must be prioritized for the Qing navy."

With no outsiders left, Yinreng covered his hair, which had been ruffled by Kangxi again, and began to reason with his own Ama—the son was grown up and needed privacy.

Kangxi first explained that he hadn't intentionally brought people to watch him bathe. He was just worried about Yinreng, who had been swaying with fatigue, and had stayed to watch over him a bit longer. Seeing that Yinreng was fine, he had left; this was concern.

Then, Kangxi expressed deep incomprehension regarding Yinreng’s request for privacy.

As the Emperor, even when he slept with his concubines, there were people guarding inside and outside the room, and people served him when he bathed or used the toilet. What kind of privacy rights did the Crown Prince need? Besides, the Crown Prince was still a child; children have no privacy.

Kangxi teased Yinreng, asking if such a small child could actually be shy. At Yinreng’s age, he should be running around with his bottom bare.

Yinreng tried to argue: "...That’s different. The people serving are different from outsiders."

Kangxi laughed: "Yu Chenglong is not an outsider; don't be so formal with him."

Yinreng: "..." Forget it, he understood. Debating these topics with a feudal monarch and feudal patriarch like Kangxi was completely meaningless.

Yinreng stopped discussing this topic, but Kangxi told the story as a joke to the Empress Dowager, the Grand Empress Dowager, and a crowd of concubines.

Even Yinzhi did not understand why Yinreng would be so embarrassed and angry. Yinzhi said that Yinreng should have invited Kangxi and Yu Chenglong to bathe together.

Yinreng opened his mouth, closed it, opened it again, closed it again, and then closed his eyes, thinking, "Ah, yes, yes, you're right."

He once again felt how out of place he was in this era.

What made Yinreng even more depressed was that after Kangxi realized he didn't faint as easily anymore, he intensified his efforts to make him study and participate in government affairs.

In Kangxi’s view, fainting was like running—if you could run one lap around the training ground today, you could run one and a half laps tomorrow. As long as Yinreng was pushed to his limit every time, his next limit would come later.

Kangxi had pushed himself this way, so he believed his son could do it too.

Yinreng had known this would happen, so his mood didn't fluctuate much.

In his first life, he had been pushed even harder. In this life, compared to his older brother’s studies, he was actually being pampered by Kangxi; as long as he finished his lessons every day, he had plenty of time to squander.

If his older brother finished his lessons early, Kangxi would surely say, "Good, keep up the effort," and then add a pile of extra work.

In his first life, the princes only had a few days of vacation a year, not even resting during the New Year. They had to leave to study around 4:00 AM before dawn and could only rest after dark. This life continued until they moved out of the palace to establish their own residences.

Children raised with such cramming education, no matter how stupid, would still have some skills.

Unfortunately, after the Qianlong Emperor, for some reason, education for children was relaxed—perhaps because there were too few heirs.

Kangxi had many sons, so he could afford to be reckless; if one son was exhausted to death, there were others.

Kangxi and Yinreng reached a silent understanding. Yinreng’s daily workload increased significantly, and Yinzhi was not happy when he saw this.

He was certainly not jealous of Yinreng. He remembered that his Crown Prince brother often fell ill from overwork, and his Ama’s so-called method of "fainting from overwork this time means you can work harder next time" was almost like fighting poison with poison.

Even though imperial physicians checked Yinreng’s pulse every day to ensure his health, Yinzhi still thought this was not good.

If one’s health is poor, one should rest; how could there be a saying that if your health is poor, you should work harder?

But Yinzhi was anxious and couldn't change Kangxi’s opinion. He could only bury his head in studying and practicing martial arts, hoping to share his Crown Prince brother’s workload sooner.

Seeing that his eldest son was also starting to work hard, Kangxi began teaching both children together, hoping to smooth out the eldest son’s rough edges and make him more mature, so he wouldn't keep angering his poor Ama.

Kangxi didn't think much of it, but other officials started to overthink.

Even though these officials knew Kangxi didn't mean anything by it, everyone knew that when it came to the issue of succession, the most feared thing was "treating everyone equally."

"Treating everyone equally" meant that the non-heir and the heir were placed on the same footing. Then, did the original heir still have any significance?

Although Kangxi favored the Crown Prince the most, he also treated the First Prince equally, so it was inevitable that the people below would start having active thoughts.

The fact that the imperial clansmen were raided after their failed attempt to force the palace showed the clansmen how stable Kangxi’s position was and how strong his character had become. With a strong ruler and weak officials, ambitious ministers did not like such a monarch. Likewise, the more excellent the Crown Prince Kangxi personally selected and raised became, the less they liked him.

The Crown Prince held the title of "legitimate," but didn't the First Prince hold the title of "eldest"? If they supported the First Prince and made him compete with the Crown Prince in the court, perhaps they could get the Emperor to depose both of his capable older sons, and then they could support a weak prince.

Kangxi had almost crippled the imperial clan through the palace-forcing incident, but precisely because he had almost crippled them, they jumped even more violently.

Among the Manchu nobility, there were those who transferred their resentment toward Kangxi for changing Manchu customs and promoting Han officials onto the Crown Prince. They hit it off with the desperate imperial clansmen.

Even among the Han officials, there were those who attached themselves to them.

Although intelligent Han officials knew that if the Crown Prince succeeded to the throne, the general environment for Han officials and the Han people would be better, not everyone had foresight. Even if some knew this, they still wanted to seek the merit of supporting a new emperor for their own private gain.

If the Han people were all clear-headed, how would the Qing have had the opportunity to enter the pass?

Thus, a display of deep affection between Kangxi and his son, and brotherly love from the First Prince, actually caused the court, which had just calmed down, to have undercurrents moving again. Without the First Prince’s knowledge, he had become the banner of the opposition to the Crown Prince, and many forces had gathered under that banner.

Nalan Mingzhu, as one of the first "partisans of the First Prince," was naturally invited.

After hesitating, he chose to protect himself and stay neutral.

"I have already been reprimanded by the Emperor. If I join you, it will make you too conspicuous and expose you under the Emperor’s nose," Mingzhu said with a silver tongue. "It would be better for me to pretend to be a loyal minister to the Emperor, or even stand on the Crown Prince’s side, and then defect at the critical moment to deal a fatal blow to the Crown Prince."

Even though the Yehenara and Ulanara clans were not even distant relatives, if one had to say, they shared the same ancestor. Mingzhu and Songgotu were at daggers drawn, so no one believed he would stand on the Crown Prince’s side. Therefore, when Mingzhu said he wanted to be a double agent, those people immediately believed him.

After Mingzhu sent this group away, he sat behind closed doors and pondered for a long time.

In the end, he did not report this matter.

This group had not yet organized, so reporting would be useless; even if they did organize, if they hadn't committed any crimes, the Emperor probably wouldn't care about this matter and might even use it as a whetstone for the Crown Prince.

Besides, did the Emperor really not know about these things? Do not underestimate the Emperor’s control over the court.

Mingzhu thought of the little Crown Prince who had lived in his house for a while and couldn't help but sigh.

When he was still on the side opposing the Crown Prince, he had made detailed plans to topple him.

When the Crown Prince was young, they had no hope of toppling him; when the Crown Prince grew up, they could show their fangs. Given the Emperor’s character, he would deliberately give them power to let them become the Crown Prince’s whetstone; as long as the Emperor tolerated their existence, there was a high possibility the Crown Prince would be deposed.

A person is not a knife. Being honed like this is a great test for both body and mind. With the Crown Prince’s naturally noble status, it was very difficult to withstand such a test.

Moreover, as long as they kept whispering bad things about the Crown Prince in the Emperor’s ear, and the Emperor tolerated them saying these bad things, he would eventually be influenced by these malicious words.

"Three people make a tiger"—there were many examples in ancient times that proved this.

Now the Crown Prince was still young, and the Emperor trusted him; as the Crown Prince grew older and the Emperor grew older, suspicion would surely grow.

Mingzhu was very clear about this.

Now that he saw things developing in the direction he had planned, he couldn't bear it.

After all, Kangxi was not the Hongwu Emperor who pampered the Crown Prince unconditionally, and the Crown Prince was not that flawless eldest son, Zhu Biao.

Their Qing imperial clansmen and nobility were even less like the imperial clansmen and nobility of the former Ming.

The court was about to become chaotic.

Just as Mingzhu was thinking, he heard Nalan Xingde knocking on the door of the study.

"Ama, the Crown Prince heard you were learning the Russian language and asked me to bring these to you." Nalan Xingde brought in a pile of books.

Mingzhu looked at the pile of books, feeling both a headache and amusement: "Does the Emperor know?"

Nalan Xingde smiled: "These books were selected by the Crown Prince and the Emperor together; how could the Emperor not know? The Emperor said that in a few days, he will take the Crown Prince to the border to inspect the situation of Russian encroachment, and he will definitely bring Ama along. Ama, you might be able to make a great contribution again."

The Fifth Prince couldn't even speak Chinese; what books would he study?

The Empress Dowager thought and thought but couldn't find a solution, so she had to ask the Grand Empress Dowager for help.

Besides arranging a few more people who knew Chinese for the Empress Dowager, the Grand Empress Dowager didn't know what else to do.

How could the Fifth Prince not speak clearly? The Grand Empress Dowager couldn't understand it.

Yinreng came to check in on his younger brothers on time every day and heard the doubts of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager.

He scratched his head. Little Five in this life is a bit miserable; why has the Empress Dowager also started "chicken parenting" (intense parenting)?

In his previous life, the Fifth Prince hadn't studied Chinese until he was nine. When other princes were nine, they couldn't speak Mongolian very well, so the Fifth Prince had almost no close brothers, and he wasn't very close to Consort Yi, with whom he couldn't communicate. He spent his days accompanying the Empress Dowager in chanting sutras and praying to Buddha, developing a kind and honest temperament at a young age.

Now that the Fifth Prince was only one year old, why was the Empress Dowager already worried about his language problem?

He was very close to the other princes, and since the Fifth Prince couldn't communicate, the Empress Dowager was afraid he wouldn't fit in. She had suffered enough from not fitting in herself and didn't want the Fifth Prince to experience it too.

Later research showed that it is much easier for humans to learn a language through songs than by speaking alone. Many people who learn foreign languages later in life learn foreign songs first.

The Fifth Prince clapped his hands and echoed with "Ah, ah, ah, ah."

Little Yinzhen stuffed the cloth puppy in his arms to Little Yinzhi, encouraging his third brother and singing along with him.

Little Yinzhi was moved and kissed Little Yinzhen on the forehead—he had learned this from Yinreng—and plucked up the courage to continue singing.

"Little Five, come, let’s sing together." Yinreng repeated the melody, "It’s very simple, let’s do it together."

"Twinkle..."

"Twinkle..."

"Star!"

Little Yinzhi and Little Yinzhen didn't find it troublesome and continued to sing with the Fifth Prince.

The Empress Dowager’s fingers were twisting restlessly, and she actually started singing along.

The Grand Empress Dowager was stunned, then smiled and patted the Empress Dowager’s arm, actually singing along with the children.

The Grand Empress Dowager followed along with the nursery rhyme, and the Empress Dowager breathed a sigh of relief, singing even louder.

Yinreng smiled: "The melody only has these few lines, but the lyrics are actually more complex."

"Crown Prince brother..." Little Yinzhi looked at Yinreng expectantly.

"Hmph." Little Yinzhen turned his head and stopped looking at Yinreng.

Little Yinzhi and little Yinzhen hugged the picture albums tightly to their chests, their eyes shining like the little stars in the song: "Thank you, Brother!"

Yinreng said: "How could Father Emperor not know? I've used Father Emperor's piano several times already."

Kangxi was speechless: "...You call that playing the piano? Weren't you just smashing the piano with your fists?"

Yinreng defended himself: "I was practicing! Who can play well right from the start?"

Kangxi didn't believe that Yinreng banging away on the piano keys was practicing: "Who taught you this song?"

Kangxi: "No wonder it only has a few repeating notes. I should find you some teachers."

Little star, what are you? You light the traveler's path, shining like a diamond, accompanying me until the sun rises again, yet I still do not know what you are.

Kangxi: "...Did I say something wrong?"

71. First update, second update [V]

Yinreng originally wanted to ride a tall horse too. But the tall horse didn't want to let Yinreng ride it.

The little Crown Prince, the beloved pet of everyone in the palace, was rejected by the horse.

Rejected is rejected, Yinreng rode a small pony and still ran fast, clip-clop, clip-clop.

Yinzhi comforted Yinreng: "You are two years younger than me, when you grow as big as me, you will definitely be able to ride a big horse too. By then, we brothers can have a race."

Yinreng said: "Okay... rabbit!"

While Yinreng was speaking, the bow and arrow in Yinzhi's hand had already left the string, pinning the rabbit to the ground.

The guard hurried over to pick up the rabbit.

Yinzhi was disgusted: "So small? And the fur is gray and ugly, forget it, just give it to the Third Brother when we go back."

The route Fuquan chose had a lot of prey. Yinzhi soon shot four more rabbits, all of which were ugly, and Yinzhi gave them all to his younger brothers.

Yinzhi was a bit angry: "Aren't there any better-looking rabbits!"

Yinreng, who hadn't fired a single arrow, said: "We're going to eat them anyway, it doesn't matter if they look good or not."

Yinzhi said: "I want to make you a rabbit fur hat."

Yinreng said: "Aren't there leopards to hunt later?"

Yinzhi said: "Leopard fur can only make one set of clothes."

Yinzhi's stubborn temper came up, and Yinreng couldn't persuade him at all. He insisted on hunting the best-looking rabbit for Yinreng.

Fuquan hurriedly ordered the guards to find the people managing the hunting grounds and have them release more rabbits here.

Most of the prey in the royal hunting grounds were released from captivity when the hunt began; otherwise, this bunch of big men could dig three feet into the ground and might not find a single rabbit.

The large prey in the hunting grounds near the capital were also all captive. Only in large hunting grounds like Mulan, which were connected to many natural forests and grasslands, was it possible for wild large animals to wander in by mistake.

However, many cavalrymen would charge into the forest aggressively, so even if there were wild large animals, they would run away very quickly, and there was basically no danger.

Yinzhi knew that most of the rabbits in the hunting grounds were captive. He was shouting loudly just to make the hunting ground staff pick out a few rabbits with nice fur and stop fobbing him off with ugly ones.

After he finished shouting, only half an hour later, he hunted several pure-colored rabbits without a single stray hair.

After making a set of hat and gloves for Yinreng, there was still some left, so Yinzhi prepared to make something for Consort Hui as well.

Fuquan asked: "Aren't you keeping any for yourself?"

Yinzhi said: "I'm not afraid of the cold, I don't need to wear fur."

Yinreng whispered: "Uncle is actually asking, what about the rabbit for Father Emperor?"

Yinzhi was confused: "Can't Father Emperor even shoot a rabbit?"

Fuquan: "..." This child, he's starting to be exasperating again.

Yinreng said: "He can. But Big Brother is hunting for the first time, you still have to give some prey to Father Emperor."

Yinzhi glanced at the many prey hanging on the guards' horses and said: "Hmm, give that pile to Father Emperor."

If the quality isn't there, make up for it with quantity. Anyway, Father Emperor wouldn't care about the color of the rabbit fur. He doesn't even use rabbit fur.

"Fine." Yinreng bowed to Fuquan like a little animal, "Uncle..."

Fuquan laughed: "I know, I will put in a good word for the First Prince."

Yinreng smiled ingratiatingly: "Thank you, Uncle."

Seeing his younger brother's cute appearance, Yinzhi couldn't help but smile: "Do you want to ride a big horse? Brother will take you."

Yinreng said: "Wait until Big Brother hunts a leopard, then take me."

Since Fuquan said they could hunt a leopard, then there must be leopards prepared in the enclosure this time.

In Yinreng's vague childhood memories, it seemed that once when he was hunting with Fuquan, they had hunted a leopard.

It was probably another case of him closing his eyes and shooting a few arrows randomly, and then the guards would lift the leopard and shout, "The Crown Prince is mighty! His Highness the Crown Prince has hunted a leopard!"

I wonder if my truly heroic Big Brother can hunt a leopard with his own skills.

As they were talking, a leopard's roar came from the dense forest.

Yinzhi's eyes lit up, and he rode forward excitedly.

The guards were faster than Yinzhi and blocked his path. Even if they were captive leopards that had lost their wild nature, if the young princes were too panicked and scared, they could still be in danger.

Yinzhi didn't act rashly. He waited until the guards had surrounded the leopard before shooting his arrows, each one hitting the target.

Yinzhi "tsk"ed: "Still not as smart as a person."

As soon as Yinzhi said this, the guards who heard him couldn't help but shiver.

They suddenly remembered that when Yinzhi was forcing the palace during the clan dispute, the bow and arrow in his hand had claimed lives.

"There's one more, you go." Yinzhi gave the good shooting position to Yinreng.

Yinreng tried his best to pull his small bow to the full, shooting five arrows, three of which hit the target.

Yinzhi was overjoyed: "Truly amazing! When you build up your body more, you'll definitely be stronger than Father Emperor!"

Yinreng: "..." That, that's not quite necessary.

In his past life, when Father praised his son for his martial prowess, he always liked to use Big Brother as a comparison. Why is Big Brother using Father as a reference when praising his younger brother in this life?

Yinreng hit the prey, and Yinzhi was happier than if he had hit the leopard himself.

Fuquan was surprised to find that Yinzhi was actually so eloquent; the words he used to praise Yinreng didn't repeat once, and they were extremely sincere.

Who said the First Prince couldn't talk? It depends on who he's talking to.

After the leopard hunt was over, Yinzhi had people clean up the prey and took his brother to the riverside to have a snack first.

The attendants quickly brought seasonings, roughly marinated the prey on the spot, and first roasted a small rabbit for the prince and two princes to pad their stomachs.

Yinzhi was struck by poetic inspiration and recited a few unrhymed poems to Yinreng.

Yinreng praised him vigorously, returning the words Yinzhi had just used to praise him, making Yinzhi beam with joy.

Fuquan sat to the side, watching the two brothers praise each other, feeling a bit sour.

But he was already used to it.

He had taken the two princes out to play many times and was really used to these two brothers using others as background scenery when they praised each other.

So why didn't his own brothers have such a good relationship? This must be... *cough cough*.

I don't know if the smell of the roasted rabbit was too strong, but it attracted a few people.

Yinreng glanced at them; he didn't recognize them.

Those people introduced themselves, and Yinreng racked his brains to think, but he still didn't recognize them.

These were probably some unimportant people among the clansmen or nobles.

Since they weren't important, Yinreng was too lazy to spare any thought for them, resting his chin on his hand and watching the rabbit over the flames, waiting devoutly for the delicious rabbit meat to be roasted.

After those people paid their respects to Prince Yu, the Crown Prince, and the First Prince, and heard that most of the prey had been hunted by the First Prince, their expressions were extremely reverent, and they kept praising the First Prince for his bravery.

You don't hit a smiling face. Although the First Prince was a bit impatient that someone had come to disturb him and his Crown Prince brother while they were having a barbecue and enjoying the scenery, he was still very happy to be praised, so he invited them to eat rabbit together.

Those people started chatting with the First Prince about hunting.

Fuquan listened to them talk from hunting to the martial prowess of the Eight Banners, and then to how bravery is the skill that Eight Banners children should have, and that for an heir to a family, one must choose someone with a healthy body.

A sneer appeared on his lips.

It seems that his reputation as a "good old man" who protects himself is well-known; these people came to cozy up to the First Prince without even avoiding him, betting that he wouldn't go to report them to the Emperor.

Yinreng glanced at the First Prince's side and then continued to guard the rabbit.

Good, good, these people's sowing of discord is very subtle; Big Brother probably doesn't understand. It's fine if he doesn't understand; if he did, he was afraid that Big Brother would do something irrational in a fit of rage and get punished because of these few fools acting as vanguards.

It was hard enough to have a happy hunt with Big Brother, and Big Brother could also take a breather from his heavy schoolwork. If his schoolwork doubled because of a few fools, Big Brother would be too unlucky.

Yinreng sniffed with his little nose and loudly interrupted the group, who were getting more and more excited with their sowing of discord: "Big Brother, is the rabbit roasted yet?"

Yinzhi said: "Let me see."

He walked to the rabbit, pretended to poke the rabbit meat with an iron fork, and then looked at the servant roasting the rabbit nearby.

The servant said: "It needs to be roasted for a while longer."

Yinreng acted pitiful: "I'm hungry."

Yinzhi took a piece of mung bean cake wrapped in a handkerchief from his pocket: "Eat a piece to pad your stomach first."

Yinreng hesitated: "I've already eaten my quota of pastries for today."

"This isn't your quota, it's mine." Yinzhi said, "Eat it."

Yinreng nodded: "Okay."

Watching his younger brother happily eating his favorite mung bean cake, a happy smile appeared on Yinzhi's face.

Kangxi listened to the imperial physician and strictly controlled Yinreng's diet, not letting him eat too many pastries so that he would eat more during regular meals. So Yinreng only had one pastry to eat a day.

Of course, Yinreng couldn't eat pastries, but he could eat snacks like beef jerky, milk paste, and fruit to fill his stomach.

Kangxi wouldn't mistreat Yinreng, but Yinzhi always felt that Kangxi was mistreating Yinreng when he saw him craving pastries, so he would often secretly hide a few of the pastries Yinreng liked on his person and feed them to his brother when he was hungry.

Later, when little Yinzhi, little Yinzhen, and other princes were hungry, they would also find Big Brother first and fish snacks out of his pocket to eat.

Yinzhi became a walking snack bag.

After Kangxi found out about this, thinking that it helped his sons maintain brotherly bonds, he turned a blind eye and pretended not to know.

Yinreng was only two years younger than Yinzhi, but Yinzhi had always treated Yinreng like a fragile baby.

After Yinreng finished the pastry, Yinzhi wiped his mouth and brought him some warm milk that the servants had prepared to soothe his throat.

Seeing Yinzhi being so careful and considerate to Yinreng, the people who had just been subtly bad-mouthing Yinreng looked at each other in dismay.

They wondered: did the First Prince not understand their sowing of discord, or did he understand and deliberately use taking care of the Crown Prince to shut their mouths?

They wanted to test him again.

One person said jokingly: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, you must take care of your health; it's so troublesome to not even be able to drink water when you're out."

Before Yinreng could speak, Yinzhi frowned and said: "Who said he can't drink water? Why drink water when you can drink milk?"

Yinreng licked the milk mustache on the corner of his mouth and hurriedly said: "Big Brother, you can't say that; have you forgotten the allusion of 'why not eat minced meat'?"

Yinzhi was stunned for a moment and said: "Ah, right, sorry, I forgot that not every family can drink milk like water."

Someone: "..."

Yinzhi added: "It's not that our palace is extravagant; we raise our own cows, the kind of cows that produce a lot of milk that Westerners cultivate, so there's enough milk to drink."

Someone: "..." That's not what he wanted to say.

He wanted to press on: "Our family also raises cows. It's just that most of the time we drink it cold; only those who are weak drink warm water."

chapters.source_text:
胤禔道：“那你们家真不讲究。能喝温热的为什么要喝冰的？出门在外的时候没条件就罢了，有条件还是要对自己好一些。”
胤禔揉了揉胤礽的脑袋，揉完之后替胤礽把头发理整齐：“别听他胡说，天气变凉了，喝什么凉水凉牛奶？我们家又不是出不起柴火钱。”
某人：“……”所以为什么大阿哥说的话落脚点总在皇宫很富我们很穷上？我并不是嫉妒你家富裕好吗？！
福全忍不住了，他笑着道：“你们家养孩子养得真糙，我家孩子哪敢给他喝冰的。”
他家那个病恹恹的儿子詹升，在经常和大阿哥、太子一起玩耍之后，身体越来越好。现在他眼巴巴地瞅着康熙教他怎么养儿子，太子怎么过日子他儿子就跟着怎么过日子。
胤禔道：“你该不会从小没有热水热牛奶喝？那你身体可真强壮，是个从军的好苗子。你有没有想去军中效力的想法啊？”
胤礽插嘴道：“他这个年龄，或许应该正在官学中上课吧。”
胤禔来了兴致：“你在大学上学？”
那人头皮发麻，直觉有点不对劲了：“在……”
胤禔立刻冒出一连串提问：“读了什么书啊？上次考试成绩如何？排名如何？你们现在放假了？作业做完了吗？”
那人：“……”心、心梗。
胤禔又对那人身后的人道：“你们呢？考试成绩如何？作业做完了吗？
来挑拨离间的一群愣头青们纷纷呆滞石化。
胤礽道：“大哥，显然他们成绩很差，作业也没有做完，不然现在肯定炫耀了。”
胤禔抱着手臂，皱眉道：“一群学渣？”
福全问道：“大阿哥，什么是学渣？”
胤禔道：“顾名思义，渣就是渣滓。”
福全捻胡须：“懂了。”
你们，一群渣渣。
愣头青们被胤禔万箭穿心，一句话也说不出来。
“其实、其实我成绩不算差。”一个人忍不住了，“作业也做了大半。”
“对对对，我能进年纪前百。”
“呵呵，我综合成绩年纪前五十。”
“我前十说话了吗？”
“呸，你倒数第十吧？”
“作业当然早就做完了。我阿玛每天回来检查功课。”
“给我抄！”
“闭嘴！裕亲王、太子和大阿哥在这里，你还敢说抄作业！”
“别说上学了，别说了，啊，要开学了。”
“上学度日如年，假期怎么一眨眼就结束了？”
愣头青们就像是有应激创伤一样，纷纷抱头说起了学校、考试和作业的事。
胤禔和胤礽十分好奇，询问他们上课和考试的细节。
这群愣头青们立刻大吐苦水，说大学有多可怕。
不过说着说着，他们还挺自豪。以前他们什么都不懂，现在他们上知天文下知地理，当个官绝对不会被底下人糊弄住。
“最近大学里来了个叫陈潢的汉人教我们治水。那堂课真有趣。”
“是啊，把河道做成沙盘，然后学生们分组拿着有限的资源，尽可能延缓河水决堤漫延，真是紧张感拉满。”
“我才知道，原来入海口不是乱疏通的。有些海面比江面高，会海水倒灌。”
“等我有机会去地方上任，先在山上多植树。”
“种果树呗，然后河运卖出去。”……
愣头青们纷纷就授课内容聊了起来。这些教材差不多太子都过目过，大阿哥也学过，自然很容易就加入了他们的话题。
于是他们聊得十分开心。当发现太子几乎无所不知之后，他们还向太子请教问题。
有些愣头青表面上是个纨绔子弟，实际上连狩猎挑拨离间都带着假期作业。他立刻把假期作业拿出来，向太子请教。
没带家庭作业的也加入进来一起讨论作业题，回去之后就能做。
于是一个挑拨离间大会，就这么变成了假期作业辅导大会。
老师：太子胤礽；助教：大阿哥胤禔。
裕亲王福全？他是背景板。
愣头青们纷纷疾呼：“太子殿下，您怎么什么都知道！”
大阿哥胤禔没好气道：“他当然什么都知道。你们根本不知道我汗阿玛的教导有多严苛。我和三弟弟他们在毓庆宫上课，每日天亮就要起床，读六日休一日。他是汗阿玛单独带着教导，汗阿玛起床他就起床，汗阿玛去哪读书他就跟着去，还要去丰泽园种地养蚕……”
胤禔抱怨了一大堆，胤礽弱弱解释：“大哥，其实还好啦，汗阿玛吃得消，我肯定也吃得消。还有，去丰泽园种地养蚕是我的爱好，不是功课。”
“汗阿玛多大的人？你多小的人？他吃得消你就吃得消？”胤禔叉腰，“你累的时候该嚷嚷就得嚷嚷，你什么都不说，汗阿玛就心安理得的压榨你！会哭的孩子才有糕糕吃，懂吗？不要太懂事！”
胤礽垂着头停训。
他知道胤禔都叉腰了，他敢辩驳，胤禔会不高兴。
愣头青们见大阿哥把太子训得抬不起头，幻视了自己在家被大哥、阿玛训斥的情形。
他们纷纷劝说，大阿哥算了算了，太子只是太懂事，不好意思和皇上争执，别气了别气了，兔子好了，我们吃兔子！
于是一群人转战兔子附近，和乐融融吃起了兔子。
吃完兔子之后，他们继续铺开作业本，在太子和大阿哥的教导下做作业。
“我们也可以加入吗？”有个侍卫忍不住了。
胤禔不在乎地摆摆手：“一起吧。”
年轻的侍卫们高兴地加入了太子、大阿哥的作业辅导班。
不知道是哪个混蛋（胤礽：阿嚏！）提出了辅导班的意见，他们这群侍卫在不当值的时候，也得去大学上课。
于是一群年轻小伙子们都围绕在两个小孩子周围，听两个小孩子授课。
梁九功做事非常激灵。他让人拿了一块大木板，上面糊了一层白泥，烘干后让胤礽和胤禔用炭笔在白泥上写字。
胤礽这才意识到，这个时代似乎还没有黑板。
他把这件事记在心上。等围猎结束后，他就给梁九功提议，让梁九功把黑板弄出来，后来黑板的发明人就是梁九功了。
康熙在景山猎场的另一处猎了一只虎，也坐在河边一边烤山羊一边等候儿子那边的消息。
重新获得信任的明珠和索额图陪伴在康熙身边，常宁闷头不语拿刷子给烤羊刷调料。
他的皇帝兄长说要吃亲手烤的羊，结果刷了几下调料就嫌烦，把调料刷子丢给了他。
常宁心里苦，但不敢说。
他以前以为康熙再怎么着也不会杀弟弟，所以随便作死。现在康熙抄了一圈宗室的家，常宁怂了。
不砍脑袋，但是可以圈禁抄家对不对？
“来了。”康熙见一个小太监匆匆跑过来，冷笑道，“朕要看看，他们会背着朕给朕的大阿哥说什么。”
明珠和索额图竖起耳朵偷听，常宁刷调料的手也慢下来。
小太监从头开始述说那群愣头青来之后说的话，康熙的表情越来越难看。
在康熙耳中，这些人不仅是挑拨离间，还是在咒太子体弱，甚至于咒太子早死。
不过很快，康熙的表情难看不起来了。
你们家喝不起牛奶吗？
你们家用不起柴火吗？
哦，抱歉，我不知道你们家这么穷。
不愧是朕的大儿子！把气朕的功力用一半，就足以让其他人哑口无言！
而后，胤禔一连串“学了什么考得如何作业做完了吗”灵魂提问，让索额图和明珠两个猫狗不合的人都忍不住交换了一个“大阿哥真狠”的眼神。
康熙更是笑得直不起腰：“好，好，他们就是功课太少。”
常宁忍不住道：“后来，他们就在太子和大阿哥的教导下，开始假期补课做作业了？！”
小太监点头：“侍卫们也加入了进来。还有许多年轻的勋贵子弟往太子和大阿哥那里跑，估计是听说太子和大阿哥正在讲解作业题。”
康熙笑得喘不过气，康熙的心腹重臣们目瞪口呆。
他们想过无数个此事后续走向，唯独没有想过还能这样！

派人出去打探大阿哥和太子关系的勋贵宗亲们也得到了这个消息。
那群傻小子居然完全忘记了长辈们交给他们的使命，向太子和大阿哥请教作业去了。
这……他们原来这么爱学习的吗？
“可能他们不是爱学习，只是聚众抄作业。”
“那还等什么？！赶紧去逮这群小兔崽子！怎么能抄作业！”
于是一群人乌压压地冲了过去，去逮自家小兔崽子，看他们是认真学习还是在抄作业。
剩下年纪较大的没有孩子上学的勋贵宗亲们十分无语。
你们就只关心抄作业吗？！你们难道不关心太子和大阿哥的关系吗？？
他们再无语，太子和大阿哥初次围猎事件，还是在紧张刺激的学习中结束了。
康熙给大阿哥和太子赏赐了许多东西，作为对他们初次挫败勋贵、宗亲阴谋的奖励。
大阿哥这才知道有人要推举他当太子。
胤禔倒吸一口气：“这群人有病吗？”
胤礽点头：“病得不轻。”
胤禔道：“我当太子？！让我在宫里住一辈子？！”
胤礽：“啊……”
胤禔气得脸都青了：“我十五岁就能出宫建府了，你十五岁能干什么？”
胤礽弱弱道：“能……能有一间大一点的房子？”
胤禔翻白眼。
胤礽安慰（？）胤禔道：“哥，其实当太子也没什么不好的。哪天我病得当不了太子了，大哥就当太子好不好？大哥当太子，肯定比汗阿玛疼我。”
“我当不了。”胤禔直白道，“如果汗阿玛不让你当太子，肯定是汗阿玛的错。我会站在你这边。汗阿玛肯定会连我一起揍。”
胤礽愣了愣，他干笑道：“那、那我还是继续当太子吧。大哥不要和汗阿玛对着干。”
胤礽有些头大。以他大哥认死理的性格，这事还真有可能发生。
到时候就是汗阿玛准备废太子，大哥揣着毒药去赌咒，汗阿玛要提着宝剑砍死大哥了。
大哥揽了十四的角色，不一定有十四的好运气。十四是宠妃的小儿子，惠妃能救下大哥的狗命就已经不错了。
胤禔揉了揉胤礽的脑袋：“别想太多。你身体不好就别劳心劳力，有什么事告诉大哥，大哥帮你做，你就动动口。”
胤礽扑在胤禔怀里撒娇：“大哥最好了！”
“当然。”胤禔拍拍胤礽的背，小声抱怨，“汗阿玛既然知道这些事，为什么不动手把这些人处理了？”
胤礽也凑胤禔耳边小声道：“汗阿玛大概是想用那些人磨砺我们。”
胤禔冷笑：“呵。要是我们不堪磨砺，被挑拨成功了呢？我几岁你几岁？我们这种年纪，不正该是被长辈保护的时候？”
胤礽小声为康熙辩解：“阿玛比较着急。他和玛法都是很小的时候便继位了。不过我看阿玛至少能活七十岁，他想太多。”
胤禔又拍了拍胤礽的背，眼中有了些许计较。
他年纪长大之后，能理解一些康熙的做法，也知道康熙是真的疼爱太子弟弟。
但这种疼爱，胤禔仍旧不能理解。
他知道老鹰会把小鹰推下悬崖，就为了让小鹰学会飞翔。但他相信老鹰将小鹰推下悬崖的时候，一定有另一只老鹰在悬崖底部盘旋，如果小鹰飞不起来就把小鹰接住，下次接着训练。
汗阿玛的后手他却没看见。
或许汗阿玛有后手，只是他知道得不够多，所以没发现？
胤禔将疑问记在心中，等待以后解惑。
经过这么多年，兄弟俩已经知道如何说话不会被身边的人听见后报告康熙。
他俩的窃窃私语，康熙并不知道。
康熙只知道两儿子又黏黏糊糊许久，有点吃醋。
不过当儿子们把猎回来的猎物送给他时。他就不吃醋了。
看，小儿子送给我一头豹子，大儿子送给我很多只兔子！
常宁不由吐槽：“皇上，大阿哥猎的豹子可没送给你。”
康熙道：“那是大阿哥懂事，知道太子要送豹子，他就不能送豹子。”
常宁道：“皇上，您确定？”
康熙把常宁打了出去。
常宁摸摸被康熙揍过的脑袋，冷哼一声。
看样子皇上知道在大阿哥心中，他不是第一位。不过大阿哥这么耿直，反倒是让皇上比对其他皇子多上了几分心思。
这难道是贱得慌？
常宁摸摸胡须，讥笑着离开。
皇上也不过如此嘛，连儿子都管不住。
不过康熙倒是冤枉胤禔了。胤禔的确是因为太子送了豹子，他才不送。
胤礽替胤禔澄清了这件事，并告诉康熙，虽然大哥不送康熙整只豹子，但会把豹子肉腌制好了送给康熙。
康熙满意了。大儿子心中果然有我。
然后，胤禔不但送给他豹子肉，还亲自抱过来一坛豹鞭酒：“汗阿玛，政务太忙，也要注意身体。今年宫里居然没有弟弟妹妹出生，您要努力啊。”
胤禔前半句让康熙很感动，后半句……
康熙让人专门制作的用来揍儿子的“能抽疼但不会让儿子受伤”小鞭子，终于派上了用场。
得亏胤礽抱着康熙大腿不放，才让胤禔成功跑到太皇太后宫里求救，否则就算是特制版小鞭子，胤禔都会被康熙抽得下不了床。
后来此事以胤禔被康熙罚了抄一百遍《孝经》作为惩罚结束。
胤礽哭笑不得：“大哥，你为什么要这么刺激汗阿玛？”
胤禔摸了摸脸上被康熙抽出来的红印子：“我不知道汗阿玛会生气啊。我这不是关心他的身体吗？”
胤礽悄悄道：“男人很忌讳别人说自己不行。”
胤禔愣了一下，头发都炸了起来：“什么？！汗阿玛揍我是因为他不行吗？！我还以为他只是太累了，没想到他居然不行了！”
胤礽赶紧捂住胤禔的嘴：“闭嘴啊，你真的想汗阿玛揍死你吗！汗阿玛当然是太累了，没空去后宫转悠！不是不行！但是你送虎鞭酒，就好像汗阿玛不行似的，他才生气！”
胤禔冷静下来：“哦，这样啊。他误会我了。”
胤礽点头：“对对对，汗阿玛误会你了。”
胤禔嚷嚷得太大声，康熙当然很快知道了这件事。
他下巴搁在立在桌上交叉握住的双手，表情深沉无比：“我究竟是造了什么孽，才生出胤禔这个儿子？”
皇帝陛下气得说我了，明珠只能苦笑不敢说话。
“胤禔不像我，也不像惠妃，难道是返祖？”康熙再次道。
明珠更不敢说话了。无论大阿哥像爱新觉罗家哪个祖先，他也不敢说话啊。
康熙叹了口气：“罢了。儿子就是债，生都生出来了，只能将就着养着，又不能丢了。听说有人邀请你加入大阿哥党？”
明珠忐忑道：“确有此事。”皇上问这个，他猜到皇上要做什么了。
康熙果然如明珠所料，道：“那你就加入吧。把他们的消息告诉朕。”
明珠叹气：“是，皇上。”
康熙笑道：“好了，别愁眉苦脸，朕不会害你。朕找了个人帮你。”
明珠拱手：“皇上，何人为臣内应？”
康熙神秘地笑道：“等你去参加他们第一次聚会就知道了。”
明珠忐忑地参加了大阿哥党在京中第一次聚会。
这个聚会在北京外城的一座酒楼中。那酒楼新开不久，名为“四川酒楼”，背后之人是四川会所，卖的全是辛辣食物，什么火锅串串麻辣烫，刚开的时候口碑极差，现在一座难求。
满洲人口味比较重，许多武将不太爱那些精细的食物，很快就成了四川酒楼的常客。
明珠最终还是加入了大阿哥党，没有人怀疑明珠居心叵测，谁让明珠是第一任大阿哥党首领？
明珠这次来参加聚会时仍旧简称自己表面上只会忠于皇上，给他们当皇上身边的暗线。大阿哥党们都说明珠老奸巨猾，这就是安插在皇上和太子身边的一把尖刀。
今天他们吃的是鸳鸯锅。火锅很好吃，但明珠食不知味。
他左瞅瞅右看看，愣是看不出哪个也是皇上的内奸。
直到有个人推门而入：“抱歉，来迟了。”
明珠的筷子落在了桌面上。
索额图扫了明珠一眼：“呵，有我在，他有什么用？他已经因为支持大阿哥被皇上骂过，你们让他加入，难道不担心他暴露你们？”
明珠：“……”
他冷笑讽刺：“哎哟，太子的叔外祖父怎么来我们大阿哥党聚会？你该不是奸细吧？”
索额图回敬道：“要说奸细，你不更像奸细吗？谁不知道你们纳兰家投靠了太子，纳兰性德可是太子身边第一红人。”
两人顿时剑拔弩张。
现场众人立刻拉架。
“明相，索相，大家以后都在同一条船上，消消气消消气。”
“给我一个面子，以前你们俩关系不好是因为政见不合，现在政见一致了，大家和睦相处。”
“明相，坐好，坐好，索相是真心加入我们的。”
“索相别生气，来，吃菜，吃菜，明相表面上不会帮咱们，他是皇上那边的暗线。”
暗线？
索额图看向明珠。
明珠冷笑地与他对视。
两人心中明了。
得了，他们知道皇上的神秘微笑是什么意思了。的确，这个人他们一看就知道绝对不是大阿哥党，绝对是皇上的奸细。
皇上！您居然让我和明珠/索额图共事！您是真的想让我们做正事，还是想看我们俩的乐子啊！
乐子人康熙抹了一把脸，把上弯的嘴角压下去：“朕当然是相信你们啊，爱卿们！”
索额图和明珠心中憋气不已。
作为被康熙带着去擒拿鳌拜的侍卫，他们俩当然是知道年轻的康熙有多么皮。
没想到康熙儿女都一大堆了，性子居然丝毫没有变化？！
索额图和明珠暂时偃旗息鼓之后，勋贵宗室们吃着火锅聊着天，会议气氛重新热络起来。
索额图作为坚定不移的太子党，此次加入大阿哥党，也没有任何人觉得索额图是来当奸细的。
因为他们对索额图非常了解，知道这个人有多自傲自负，是绝对不屑于做这种事。
何况索额图近些年的不好过，他们都看在眼里。
索额图作为太子党第一人，曾经在朝中呼风唤雨，嚣张跋扈不可一世。
但太子之亲近亲外祖一家，多次直言对索额图不喜。太子的亲舅舅常泰更是接替索额图成为康熙身边第一红人。
索额图逐渐低调，闭门不出。就这样康熙还不放过他，居然解除了索额图所有子嗣的职位，让他们去新官学读书。
这索额图能忍？
别说索额图，他们都不能忍。
索额图转而支持大阿哥，这实在是太正常了。
再说了，索额图是庶子，本就和赫舍里家的嫡子们中间隔着一层。他想为自己拼一个前程，多正常？
于是，所有大阿哥党都举酒欢迎索额图弃暗投明。
索额图心中冷笑。弃暗投明？是弃明投暗吧？
一群傻子。
吃完火锅，明珠和索额图抖抖衣服上的火锅气味，在酒楼前互瞪一眼，拂袖离去。
其他大阿哥党们苦笑不已。
“明相和索相真的是因为政见不合才关系不好吗？”
“屁，他们俩还是皇上近卫的时候就天天吵架打架。”
“我们大阿哥党真强大，连明相和索相这俩天生不和的人都能共事。”
“谁让皇上太过分，把我们逼急了呢。”
大阿哥党们纷纷点头赞同。
如果不是皇上把他们逼急了，他们怎么会如此急躁地想对皇上亲手带大的太子动手？
这个皇上太强大，他们不敢动。所以他们绝对不能让一个被皇上亲手带大的孩子成为未来的皇帝。
皇宫中，店小二绘声绘色地给康熙描绘宗室勋贵吃火锅时的情形，康熙一边笑一边挼胤礽的脑袋，把胤礽挼得脑袋都快冒烟了。
胤礽抱住脑袋道：“阿玛，您怎么能让明珠和索额图做内奸的事？他们俩性格不适合啊。”
康熙笑道：“正因为他们性格不适合，所以不会有人猜到他们俩是内奸。而且他们性格太过不合，很适合给彼此打掩护。”
胤礽叹气：“总觉得明珠大人和叔外祖父有些可怜。”
康熙道：“可怜什么？他们说不定乐在其中。你以为他们的本性是现在表现出来的那样吗？”
康熙回忆起他们仨都还年轻时的往事，道：“他们俩其实挺爱玩，也挺爱演。”
“好吧，希望……唔，希望大阿哥党们能安然无恙。”胤礽继续叹气，“还好他们没把大哥也拉进去。”
康熙想了一下大儿子加入大阿哥党的场面，再次笑得喘不过气：“保、保清啊，哈哈哈，不错不错，等他再长大一点，就让他加入。”
胤礽无奈：“阿玛，还是算了吧。以大哥的性子，如果他们吃火锅时谁说我的坏话，他能把沸腾的火锅扣那人头上去。”
康熙继续大笑：“那不是更好吗？”
胤礽抱着头使劲叹气。
为什么他的阿玛会这么皮？把成熟睿智的阿玛还给我！
算了，他还是要这个皮皮阿玛吧。阿玛要变回前世那样，他就太苦了。
大阿哥党之事暂时如此处理。太子还未长大，这群人就会蛰伏不出。待大阿哥出宫建府时，他们才会动作起来。
明珠和索额图施施然加入其中，成了大阿哥党的核心人物，并没有任何人发现他俩有问题。
就是他俩每次会议都会互相讽刺攻讦说对方是奸细，让劝架的人头疼不已。
胤禔终于在抄了第二十遍《孝经》后，被解除了禁足——台湾打下来了，康熙很高兴，胤禔的惩罚自然就免了。
胤礽的第一世，康熙二十一年七月决定攻台，二十二年十一月收复了台湾。
这一世康熙二十年二月正式决定攻台，十二月底收复了台湾，耗费的时间少了许多。这和康熙支持力度更大、也和施琅等人比胤礽第一世年轻了一岁有关。
对于武将而言，身体一年一个状态。何况这一世的施琅有常泰暗中照顾，生活状况好了许多，身体也就更加健康。
台湾一收复，康熙就准备派常泰去台湾担任大清第一任台湾总督，并着手建造大清第一个海军基地。
康熙目前最信任常泰，大清军队走出国门的第一步，自然要交给常泰来做。
但常泰刚接到圣旨，噶布喇却病重了。
康熙亲自带中外名医视疾，并将太子留在国公府中居住。
但噶布喇这次病情来得太过凶猛，中外名医皆摇头，让赫舍里家准备后事。
胤礽将小脸埋在噶布喇枯槁如老树的掌心，哽咽不止。
噶布喇本来应在今年九月病逝。他多熬了三个月，还是没熬过康熙二十年的冬季。
“太子……”今日噶布喇突然有了精神，苍白蜡黄的脸泛起了红晕，口齿也变得清楚了，“保成……”
胤礽抬头，眼睛红肿：“姥爷第一次叫保成的名字。”
噶布喇笑了笑。
同样眼睛红肿的常泰给噶布喇背后垫了软垫，扶噶布喇坐起身。
噶布喇抬起手，轻轻揉了揉胤礽的脑袋：“保成，如果赫舍里家拖累了你，不要保护赫舍里家。”
胤礽吸了吸鼻子：“我不。”
噶布喇笑道：“只要你好，赫舍里家以后出了能人，总能继续辉煌。所以你要看护好你自己，知道吗？”
胤礽不说话。
噶布喇又对常泰和常海道：“这话也是对你们说的。时时刻刻以太子为先，知道吗？若太子的局势不好了，你们就跟着一起请求废太子，千万不要谋求复立太子。”
常泰和常海低声道：“是。”
噶布喇这些话，以前和他们说过，现在只是以遗言的形势再强调一次。
噶布喇又叹息道：“可惜小女还没有找到合适的人家。”
胤礽道：“外祖父，交给我，我一定给小姨找一个好人家。”
噶布喇笑道：“好孩子，那就交给你了。这算是我对你的请求吧。”
胤礽再次瘪嘴不语。
噶布喇没有再说话，他只是一次又一次的揉着胤礽毛绒绒的小脑袋。
今日之前，他从未如此放肆过。
噶布喇总是恪守君臣的界限，总是非常恭敬，从未将胤礽当亲外孙一样对待。
但现在，他就像是寻常人家的外祖父，和最疼爱的外孙无比亲昵。
胤礽被噶布喇揉着揉着，眼泪大颗大颗地从眼眶砸落，很快就打湿了整张小脸。
他咬着嘴唇，坚强地不让自己哭出声，只有眼泪怎么都忍不住。
这辈子好不容易有机会亲近的至亲，却很快就要与他分别。胤礽脑子中一阵一阵的天旋地转，连思想和理性都快被眩晕搅碎。
“好孩子，别哭，外祖父只是去见你额娘，把保成是个好孩子的消息告诉你额娘。”噶布喇轻笑道，声音越来越低，“你额娘一定……很想知道你的事，外祖父不能让她……久等……”
噶布喇说完了最后一个字，咽下了最后一口气，手掌轻柔地从胤礽头顶滑落。
胤礽赶紧抓住噶布喇滑落的手掌，双手将噶布喇的手掌放在自己的头顶。
胤礽举着噶布喇的手掌，低着头哽咽得无法出声。
常泰和常海扑通跪下，趴在地上泣不成声。
康熙二十年十二月中旬，领侍卫内大臣公噶布喇病逝。
康熙领太子、大阿哥亲临祭奠，后又命人加祭三次，并下旨令噶布喇长子常泰袭一等公。
之后，康熙命人为其立碑墓道，谥号靖齐。
恭己鲜言曰靖，执心克庄曰齐。
一等公噶布喇虽然一生没有什么成就，康熙为其所定谥号，也算肯定了他的品德。
