Changtai and Kangxi each held a long pole with a cloth bundle dipped in ink, walking into the large circle drawn for the charcoal painting.

A hit with the pole counted as one point; the first to reach ten points would win. Stepping out of the circle would result in an immediate loss.

Yinreng pulled out a bamboo whistle and blew it with all his might. Changtai and Kangxi charged at each other simultaneously.

Every move Changtai made had been refined in the military camps of Taiwan—they were true killing blows. Kangxi, having been taught by master instructors and possessing great natural talent, was surprisingly able to hold his own against Changtai for a short time.

Yinzhi exclaimed in surprise, "Father Emperor's skills are not bad at all."

The third, fourth, and fifth princes also nodded in succession, "I didn't expect Father Emperor to be so formidable."

Yinreng was speechless, "In your minds, is Father Emperor considered weak?"

Kangxi had been pricking up his ears, hoping to hear his sons' admiring cheers, but he hadn't expected to hear these remarks. Aside from his beloved little Crown Prince, did his other sons have problems with their upbringing?

While Kangxi was distracted, Changtai seized the opportunity to strike directly at Kangxi's face. Kangxi jumped back a step by reflex.

"Your Majesty, you have lost." Changtai retracted his long pole.

Kangxi looked down and realized he had already jumped outside the circle.

He gritted his teeth and said, "Were you forcing me out of the circle the whole time just now?"

Changtai raised an eyebrow, "Isn't that a matter of course? Your Majesty, don't forget to give the horse to the First Prince."

Kangxi tossed the long pole to a eunuch, "Fine, fine, you all conspired to swindle my horse. How did you become so formidable after just one trip to Taiwan? You didn't actually go to the battlefield to fight, did you? Even if you went, weren't you just training the navy?"

Changtai replied, "The pirates came ashore a few times. Your Majesty, why don't you change your clothes first, and we can chat while having a drink later?"

Kangxi said, "Alright."

He left Tang Zhen with the princes and walked off with his arm around Changtai.

Kangxi was extremely curious about Taiwan, the navy, and the pirates, and couldn't wait to have a long talk with Changtai. He was prepared to push aside today's government affairs to have a good jar of wine with him.

Since Changtai left the capital, Kangxi hadn't been able to find a suitable person to drink and boast with.

Tang Zhen stood there blankly, not knowing what he should do.

The Emperor and Lord Chang just left him here and walked off with their arms around each other?

"Mr. Tang, don't be so restrained; let's play together." Yinreng was also quite frustrated by Kangxi's "hands-off" style. He knew, of course, that Kangxi was implicitly leaving him to clean up the mess, but he was still speechless. "Mr. Tang, have you been to many places?"

Tang Zhen recalled his experiences of being displaced across the Great Qing and nodded gently, "Many places."

Yinreng smiled, "Let's play 'Travels of the Great Qing' together. While we play, would you mind introducing the local customs and traditions you know to us?"

Tang Zhen didn't know what "Travels of the Great Qing" was, but since the Crown Prince had invited him, he naturally agreed.

When Yinreng brought out "Travels of the Great Qing," Tang Zhen was somewhat amazed, "This game... is truly ingenious. One can learn about local customs and traditions while playing; it is very suitable for children's enlightenment."

Yinzhi puffed out his little chest, "It was a school entrance gift from Crown Prince Brother!"

Little Yinzhen immediately said, "I will have one too when I start school!"

Little Yinqi nodded.

Tang Zhen looked at the Crown Prince and exclaimed, "His Highness the Crown Prince is truly brilliant."

Yinreng handed the rulebook to Tang Zhen, "Enough with the compliments, it's just a game. Let's play first."

Perhaps great scholars who leave their names in history inevitably possess the ability to remember things after one glance. Even though Tang Zhen was already getting on in years, his memory hadn't faded. After reading the rulebook a few times, he grasped the key points, and after one round, he was already adept and entered "teaching mode."

Tang Zhen aimed to be an Imperial Tutor. Among the works he would leave to future generations, the sections on how to educate the Crown Prince were the most extensive.

He had already imagined countless times in his mind how to educate the Crown Prince and the other princes, and now, for the first time, he was putting those abstract thoughts into practice. After practicing, he realized there were many parts of his manuscript that needed revision.

Tang Zhen had imagined the Crown Prince and the princes to be very clever, but this Crown Prince was excessively clever, and the First Prince was... ahem, too fond of contradicting people.

Whenever the First Prince encountered something he couldn't believe, he would stubbornly choose to continue not believing it, forcing Tang Zhen to produce evidence.

Yinreng looked at Tang Zhen's awkwardness, a smile appearing on his face that said, "Ah, it's great to know I'm not the only one being countered by Big Brother."

In this era, there were no cameras, tape recorders, or video recorders. Unless he took his brother to see it in person, how could he prove it to him?

Speaking of cameras, was the world's first camera about to appear? What were the technical principles of primitive cameras?

Yinreng took a deep breath and gave up on thinking.

Hehe, as if he would know. To develop the technology of the Great Qing, he'd better count on his uncle to bring back talent from abroad.

Although the First Prince was a bit of a contrarian... no, the First Prince was the contrarian himself, the princes were quite satisfied with Tang Zhen's company.

To travel ten thousand miles and read ten thousand books—this was what it meant for a scholar to broaden their horizons. Tang Zhen had achieved both.

Although the princes' tutors were all highly learned, most of them had been reading behind closed doors since they were old enough to understand things, then took the imperial examinations, and entered the government as officials. They had no opportunity to travel, and their insights into various parts of China came only from books.

Tang Zhen's appearance perfectly complemented the princes' knowledge. Even the contrarian First Prince showed reluctance to see Tang Zhen go.

Yinzhi sighed, "Regarding the other tutors, I find it hard to come up with new points to refute." Because there was nothing fresh left to hear.

Tang Zhen was caught between laughter and tears.

Seeing his younger brothers having a good time, Yinreng called for people to arrange lunch, ate with Tang Zhen, and rested for a while before continuing to play.

When he saw that Tang Zhen was running low on energy, he stopped his brothers and had Liang Jiugong bring over an unfamiliar civil official.

"Although Mr. Tang is my uncle's subordinate, my uncle has been kept in the palace by Father Emperor, and Mr. Tang is likely unfamiliar with the people in his residence, which might make him feel restrained. I heard from my uncle that Mr. Tang has not returned home for a long time, so I took the liberty of finding a Shujishi (Hanlin Bachelor) from Sichuan in the Hanlin Academy. Mr. Tang might prefer to stay with a fellow countryman."

After introducing the Shujishi to Tang Zhen, Yinreng took out a letter and had his older and younger brothers sign their names, "Since Mr. Tang has come to the capital, he must want to visit the great scholars here. With the letters of introduction from my brothers and me, Mr. Tang can visit any residence he wishes. Among the Manchu officials, Mr. Tang might want to visit Rongruo, but Rongruo is currently guarding the frontier, so it's not a good time."

Tang Zhen took the letter Yinreng handed him, his hands trembling slightly, "Your Highness the Crown Prince, this, how can this be!"

"Father Emperor entrusted Mr. Tang to me, which is an implicit agreement for me to make the arrangements." Yinreng said with a reassuring smile, "Don't worry, my name is not on it; it's a joint letter from my brothers. Those who see it will know it is Father Emperor's intention and will not associate it with forming cliques."

Yinzhi interjected, "Don't be so blunt; you'll scare people."

Yinreng said, "Father Emperor calls Mr. Tang 'Sir,' so he surely wants Mr. Tang to stay out of the political whirlpool. Mr. Tang has been by my uncle's side, so he will know about these things sooner or later. When Mr. Tang visits his friends, he should also ask them for advice on the political situation to avoid being trapped."

Those Han officials were not Tang Zhen's friends, but upon seeing this letter, they would all become his friends.

Tang Zhen immediately said solemnly, "Thank you, Your Highness the Crown Prince!"

Yinzhi said, "If you want to visit someone, hmm, Chen Tingjing is not bad."

Yinzhi immediately said, "Find Chen Menglei! Chen Menglei is very learned!"

Little Yinzhen racked his brains to think of any Han official's name that had left a deep impression on him. Since his brothers had all spoken, he couldn't be the odd one out.

He hesitated for a moment and said, "Tutor Li Guangdi speaks very well; you can learn from him."

Little Yinqi looked blank. Sorry, he still hadn't remembered the names of the tutors teaching the princes.

Yinreng said, "Although Li Guangdi and Chen Menglei are from the same hometown, they don't get along very well. Xu Qianxue, Xu Yuanwen, and Xu Bingyi are the nephews of Mr. Gu Yanwu. You can discuss Mr. Gu's ideas with them. Xu Qianxue is the most learned, but Xu Yuanwen and Xu Bingyi have better character..."

Yinreng commented on the Han officials in the court one by one, not only for Tang Zhen to hear but also for his brothers.

These words were hinted at by Kangxi.

As the princes started school one by one, it was inevitable that they would develop relationships with their tutors. Although Kangxi didn't teach the princes the art of statecraft, he didn't want his sons to be deceived.

Kangxi didn't have time to teach his sons these things, so after writing to Du Lide, he let Yinreng teach the princes about court affairs on his behalf.

Tang Zhen kept the Crown Prince's pointers in his heart. When he left the Changchun Garden, his back was soaked with sweat.

He glanced at the fellow countryman he would be staying with. The man had taken off his official hat, and his hair was wet in strands—even more sweat than he had.

The two looked at each other and couldn't help but laugh out loud, their initial awkwardness fading significantly.

They exchanged greetings and discovered that both were descendants of famous figures.

Tang Zhen was a descendant of Tang Yu, a great Confucian scholar of the early Ming Dynasty and an Imperial Tutor. The Shujishi's surname was Su, from Meishan, a member of the "Three Sus" clan of the Northern Song Dynasty.

Both had illustrious ancestors, and their mutual compliments felt much more genuine.

The Shujishi, Su Ze, sighed, "I had long heard that the Crown Prince was incredibly brilliant. Seeing him today, I realize the rumors were not exaggerated at all."

Tang Zhen joked, "It's just that after the Crown Prince's evaluations of the officials leaked, I wonder how those lords will face him."

Su Ze said, "With the Emperor's wisdom, perhaps the Emperor is using the Crown Prince's mouth to warn them."

Speaking of this, Su Ze suppressed a laugh, "Of the three Xu brothers, the eldest is the most learned but his character is not as good as his younger brothers'. Xu Qianxue will probably have trouble sleeping and eating."

Tang Zhen said, "But among the people the Crown Prince evaluated, why wasn't Lord Gao Shiqi mentioned? After I entered the capital, I heard rumors that Lord Gao Shiqi is the Emperor's most favored official."

Su Ze sneered, "The Crown Prince only named the princes' tutors. How could Gao Shiqi be worthy of being a tutor to the princes?"

Tang Zhen understood. That Gao Shiqi was likely a sycophant.

Su Ze had just passed the imperial examinations. Because of his good ranking and his background as a Su from Meishan, he was immediately "captured" by a high-ranking official in the court to be a son-in-law. That official was a Han general who had a good relationship with Zhao Liangdong, who was currently enjoying his time as a university teacher.

With his father-in-law's backing, Su Ze had a large mansion in the capital. He was very generous and gave Tang Zhen a small courtyard with a garden, allowing him to bring friends over to play at will.

Su Ze laughed, "I can also take advantage of Mr. Tang's letter to get to know more high-ranking officials in the court."

Tang Zhen chuckled. As expected of a descendant of the Su family, he really knew how to speak. With Su Ze saying this, the awkwardness of being a guest in his home vanished.

Tang Zhen stayed behind closed doors at Su Ze's house for two days, exchanging knowledge and discussing matters of the capital with him, before he began to visit his "friends."

The Han officials in the capital had already received the news and were waiting anxiously at home, worried that they would not be on the list of people Tang Zhen would visit.

That was a letter of recommendation written by the Crown Prince and signed by the princes. The names in the letter were likely the people closest to the Emperor's heart! If they weren't on it... if they weren't... if...

The Han officials felt their scalps tingling.

Kangxi and Changtai were drinking wine, and Kangxi patted the little Crown Prince's head, laughing, "Every time there's an imperial examination, Han officials from various provinces start fighting over each other. If I don't give them something to worry about, they'll give me trouble."

Changtai poured a glass of red wine for Kangxi.

For the sake of Kangxi's health, Yinreng had changed Kangxi's preference to red wine in advance and kept a close eye on him, not allowing him to overindulge.

Kangxi really wanted to overindulge.

Thus, low-alcohol wine was brewed in the palace, so Kangxi's indulgence was no longer called overindulgence.

"I wonder if Mr. Tang can handle such pressure." Changtai was a bit worried.

Kangxi said, "If he cannot handle such pressure, how can I trust him to assist you? What do you say, Baocheng?"

Yinreng said, "Mr. Tang spent the first half of his life displaced, failing at everything he did, yet his ambition remained unchanged. After being appreciated by my uncle and meeting the Emperor, he was neither humble nor arrogant, and did not lose his composure out of joy. He has experienced both extreme sorrow and extreme joy; this little bit of pressure is surely nothing to him."

Kangxi put his arm around his son and said to Changtai, "Look, you are not as insightful as your nephew."

Changtai retorted, "Isn't that a matter of course? The Crown Prince was taught by the Emperor himself. Is there anyone in this world more insightful than the Emperor?"

Kangxi said shamelessly, "No."

Changtai: "..." Although his flattery was somewhat sincere, seeing Kangxi accept it so completely still felt a bit stifling.

"Xu Qianxue is a bit out of line now. Greed is nothing; there are few in this court who are not greedy. Even if he isn't greedy himself, his family won't be clean. But he wants to become the leader of the Han officials..." Kangxi ate a piece of cold-dressed pig ear, wiped the oil from the corner of his mouth, and sneered, "He should weigh whether he has the ability. If it were his uncle, Mr. Gu, I would hand over the position of leader of the Han officials with both hands."

Yinreng held a plate of pig head meat and said while eating, "There is only one Mr. Gu in this world. Both were displaced, but Mr. Tang would fail at business, while Mr. Gu could start from scratch and become a millionaire anywhere. They cannot be compared."

The pigs in the Qing Dynasty already had a complete castration and breeding process, and the Qing royal family became very fond of pork after entering the pass.

Yinreng naturally loved it too.

Piggy is so cute, piggy is also so delicious, I love piggy.

When his uncle takes the Great Qing Navy to tour the world, he must catch more foreign pig breeds and develop that kind of pig that can get fat in just a few months.

Although that kind of pig isn't particularly delicious, for the common people, having meat to eat is a more magnificent sage's rule than a prosperous age. Why worry about the texture?

Eggs, milk, and meat are the foundation for a nation's progress. Let's get the vegetable basket project going!

After hearing Yinreng's words, Kangxi put down his chopsticks.

His chest hurt, and the cold-dressed pig ear no longer tasted good.

"Don't focus on what you've lost, look at what you already have." Yinreng poured chicken soup for the soul for Kangxi, "Come, come, Father, eat your vegetables. You already have many talented people under your command."

Yinreng said he should eat vegetables, so he only picked vegetables for him.

Kangxi gently tapped Yinreng's hand with his chopsticks, "Your father is not a rabbit."

"A balanced diet of meat and vegetables is good for the body." Yinreng said earnestly, "Eating only meat makes it easy to get sick. Father, you must set a good example for me, otherwise, I will only eat meat too."

Kangxi was amused by Yinreng's self-binding attack.

He immediately picked a bowl of vegetables for Yinreng, forcing him to finish them, before he himself ate the small bowl of vegetables Yinreng had picked for him.

When the father and son finished their vegetables, they looked straight at Changtai.

Changtai: "?"

Kangxi and Yinreng simultaneously waved their chopsticks rapidly, filling Changtai's bowl with vegetables and even pressing them down.

Changtai: "..."

Thanks, I was truly infantilized by this father and son of the imperial family.

Changtai's return to the capital made the Manchu and Mongol nobles who opposed the Crown Prince very uncomfortable.

Now that Songgotu had defected, Changtai was the number one supporter of the Crown Prince. Seeing Changtai so favored, how could they remain indifferent?

Although it was not yet time for the succession struggle, taking Changtai down early would count as preparatory work.

Thus, the First Prince's party, without the participation of the First Prince himself, held an emergency meeting to discuss how to impeach Changtai.

Mingju and Songgotu were busy with the issue of Tsarist Russia in the Northeast. When they received news of the meeting, they cursed simultaneously.

I am so busy I can't even touch the ground, yet you are causing trouble. Are you that idle! If you're that idle, go to Aihun City and move bricks to repair the city!

What people hate most is being disturbed when doing serious work. Mingju and Songgotu were full of anger, and without consulting each other, they made a unanimous decision: if they didn't get a few of the First Prince's party members dismissed and sent home to chew on their own fingers this time, they wouldn't be surnamed Yehenara/Hesheli!

Mingju and Songgotu brought their full fury to the meeting.

The attendees were also very angry. Seeing Mingju and Songgotu's anger, which was more real and visible than their own, they couldn't help but sigh that Mingju and Songgotu were indeed the backbone of the First Prince's party.

"Changtai sent people to visit Han officials everywhere as soon as he entered the capital. Isn't this forming cliques?" Songgotu slammed the table hard, "A capital offense!"

Mingju said sarcastically, "He actually stayed at Changchun Garden without leaving after entering the capital. Being so undisciplined, he is worthy of being the Great Qing's number one sycophant. Is there anything left to discuss regarding the reasons for impeachment?"

Songgotu continued to slam the table, "And the Eight Banners are armies on horseback; what's with this navy! The Zheng family is gone, what's the use of a navy! The overseas lands are so desolate, there's no need for us to go out. He is inciting the Emperor to be bellicose! A treacherous official!"

Mingju suggested, "Building such a large naval base, he must have embezzled a lot. Can't you find evidence of his corruption?"

The First Prince's party members were enlightened by Songgotu and Mingju!

They would write the memorial to impeach him right now!

88. Third and Fourth Update (Overlord Vote Bonus) [V]

Just as Changtai was instructing the First Prince on how to use the sword, he learned that he had been impeached by the First Prince's party.

Changtai: "...Oh."

Yinzhi: "...Damn."

Yinzhi shook his hand, which had been numbed by Changtai's wooden sword, and said unhappily, "Uncle, does this group of First Prince's party members really want to nominate me as Emperor, or do they want to kill me? I think they just want to kill me."

Changtai rolled up Yinzhi's sleeve, poured medicinal oil on Yinzhi's arm, and rubbed it vigorously. Yinzhi winced in pain.

"Endure it. Only by dispersing the bruising now will it not hurt tomorrow." Changtai held down Yinzhi, who wanted to run away, "Of course, they don't have good intentions. In the past, the imperial clan nominated young princes. You are older than the Crown Prince, so you are not their final choice."

Yinzhi complained, "Yes, it's so obvious. They just want the Crown Prince Brother and me to fight until both are injured, then nominate a stupid younger brother to take the throne."

Changtai said, "The status of the eldest son and the legitimate son in the Emperor's heart is different from that of the other princes. If you two fight and something happens, it will be a great blow to the Emperor's spirit. They seem to be setting traps for you, but in reality, they want to hurt the Emperor. The Emperor is too wise and martial, which puts a lot of pressure on them."

After Changtai dispersed the bruising on Yinzhi's arm, he wiped the medicinal oil off with hot water, applied a cooling medicinal oil, and then wrapped Yinzhi's arm with white cotton cloth.

Yinzhi showed a look of relief, "That feels good. It's truly painful during the massage, but it's truly comfortable afterward."

Changtai smiled, "The First Prince is very formidable. Shi Lang said that many children of military families cannot endure this kind of hardship."

Yinzhi waved his bandaged arm and said, "What's the difference between children of military families and me? No difference."

As the two were talking, Yinreng brought a group of younger brothers over with food boxes. Yinzhi immediately hid his tired expression, walked toward Yinreng, and showed off to Yinreng and his younger brothers how formidable he was.

No matter how Yinzhi boasted, Yinreng could always find words to agree, praising Yinzhi until he was beaming with joy.

Seeing this scene of brotherly love, Changtai also felt warm inside.

What he worried about most was the Crown Prince being too lonely, isolated, and suppressed in the palace. With the First Prince accompanying him, Changtai felt much more at ease.

Yinreng had been instilling in Changtai the idea that "the Crown Prince's status is stable only if the Emperor says so," so Changtai looked at the princes only as playmates for his own nephew. He was willing to be good to whoever was good to the Crown Prince.

If the princes were truly willing to treat him as an uncle, even though these princes couldn't compare to his own nephew, Changtai would certainly treat them better than other strange children.

"I want to learn, Uncle, I want to learn too!" Little Yinzhen jumped high, pestering Changtai.

Changtai said, "When the Fourth Prince grows up, I will definitely teach him."

Little Yinzhen wanted to pinky-promise with Changtai: "It's a deal!"

"Yes, it's a deal." After Changtai pinky-promised with little Yinzhen, a eunuch came to find Changtai, saying the Emperor had summoned him.

"Uncle won't be in trouble, will he?" Yinzhi asked worriedly.

In the past few days, Changtai had accompanied the princes to play and taught them martial arts, winning the favor and respect of the little princes. Now, their call of "Uncle" was deep and sincere.

Yinreng was a bit worried. Changtai's relationship with the princes was too close. It was fine now, but when the princes grew up... ah, don't overthink it. Uncle was staying in Taiwan, so far away, and his younger brothers were still young; they would forget after a few days of separation.

"Are you worried about Uncle being impeached?" Yinzhi asked.

Yinreng smiled reluctantly and said, "Yes." Actually, he wasn't very worried.

Yinzhi frowned, "So annoying. I really want to take a whip and give that group of people a lash each."

Yinreng said, "There will be an opportunity."

Ahem, in his previous life, they had whipped many officials and imperial clansmen, not just him. When Father punished the imperial clan and officials, he would even have them hold the whips.

When Changtai walked into Kangxi's study, Kangxi had smashed something again.

Seeing him enter, Kangxi waved his hand impatiently, telling him not to perform the greeting.

Changtai frowned, first picking up the things on the floor that weren't broken and putting them away, then signaling the eunuchs to come and clean up the broken things, before saying, "If Your Majesty is angry, you can go to the training ground to vent. It's not worth it to hurt yourself by smashing things."

He paused, then added, "If you break things, you have to use the Emperor's own money to replace them; it's not worth it if you don't even manage to hurt anyone."

Kangxi was so angry he slapped the table: "I was wondering where Baocheng got that stingy nature of his; so it turns out he learned it from you!"

Changtai immediately retorted, "I certainly didn't, don't wrong me. Isn't it because His Highness the Crown Prince constantly hears you complaining about the lack of money in the national treasury and the inner palace that he is occasionally a bit stingy?"

Kangxi said angrily, "If I say it's your fault, then it's your fault!"

Changtai refused to take the blame: "Your Majesty, shifting responsibility onto your subjects is not the behavior of an enlightened monarch."

Kangxi threw a memorial at Changtai's face, which Changtai nimbly caught: "Look at this memorial; it calls you the greatest treacherous official in the Qing Dynasty. If you don't voluntarily admit to the mistake of corrupting the Crown Prince, I will punish you!"

"No, it's all the Emperor's fault. His Highness the Crown Prince was raised and taught by you personally; it has nothing to do with me." While continuing to bicker with Kangxi, Changtai opened the memorial.

As he read, Changtai laughed: "Is this memorial targeting me or the Emperor? With their writing style, it sounds as if I wasn't teaching the princes at the Changchun Garden, but serving in the Emperor's bedchamber."

"Go, go, go, you've made me sick enough to bring up yesterday's dinner." Kangxi had been furious—it must be mentioned that Kangxi's hair was finally long enough to stand on end with rage—but after what Changtai said, he suddenly couldn't stay angry.

Kangxi couldn't help but laugh too: "They really dare to say anything. Am I being too benevolent?"

Changtai said, "There are only so many members of the imperial clan and Manchu nobility. The court must ensure a certain number of Manchu officials, so last time you only executed the ringleaders, sparing their families and children, and letting the officials keep their posts. They probably want to continue testing your bottom line."

Changtai glanced at the memorial again: "However, the person who submitted this surely doesn't know they've been used as a pawn by their accomplices to test the Emperor's bottom line."

Impeach him if they must, but to get carried away and drag the Emperor's reputation into it—truly foolish beyond measure.

"There's also this one." Kangxi handed Changtai another memorial.

After opening it, Changtai laughed again: "The Qing Dynasty rules through martial strength and has never feared anyone. It's one thing for Han officials to say this, but for a Manchu official to talk about 'impoverishing the state through military force,' and even suggest that we should be benevolent and tolerant toward pirates raiding our borders, and that the Qing should just close its gates and not compete for sea routes—if I hadn't seen that the person who submitted this had a Manchu name, I would have thought it was some pedantic Confucian scholar."

Kangxi said, "During the late Ming and the weak Song dynasties, factional struggles ignored right and wrong and only cared about stances. This group is about the same."

Changtai joked, "On the surface, this looks like the Crown Prince's faction versus the First Prince's faction, but in reality, is it the Imperial Clan/Nobility faction versus the Emperor's faction? Speaking of which, the First Prince is currently furious; I'm really worried he might lose his temper and charge at that group of his own supporters."

Kangxi got a headache as soon as he heard about his eldest son: "After he starts participating in government, that bad temper of his... sigh, just have him stand next to Baocheng. If he gets impulsive, Baocheng can hold him back."

Kangxi threw another pile of memorials at Changtai, all of them impeaching him.

Changtai sighed, understanding why Kangxi had called him over. Kangxi was just looking for cheap labor.

He asked for brush, ink, paper, and an inkstone, and listed the names of those impeaching him into a table—a tool Yinreng had taught him to use. After he went to Taiwan, he pretended he had discovered it himself and submitted a memorial to Kangxi, who then had the Six Ministries start using tables as well.

After writing down their names and positions, Changtai organized their native places, promotion histories, and teacher-student and marital relationships.

The eunuchs cut the tables Changtai made into strips, and Kangxi and Changtai rearranged them based on their personal information and pinned them to a blackboard on the wall.

The blackboard and chalk were new inventions Liang Jiugong came up with after being inspired by Yinreng; now, the university and the Imperial Academy were already using them. Teachers had even self-taught the unique skill of flicking chalk.

"Almost all the nobles and clansmen who made great contributions during the conquest are involved." Kangxi's face grew darker, "Good, very good. Am I being abandoned by everyone?"

Changtai said, "Even in the same family, there are different ideals and stances. Speaking of which, is my uncle still in the First Prince's faction?"

Only then did Kangxi remember he had sent two spies to go undercover.

He hurriedly summoned Mingju and Songgotu. With great tacit understanding, Mingju and Songgotu exaggerated how arrogant that group was, then began to talk about how busy they were and had no time to attend meetings.

The first half of their sentence was a cover; the second half was what they truly wanted to say.

Seeing that both men had lost weight and had dark circles under their eyes, Kangxi couldn't help but pity his old officials and granted them leave.

Consequently, at the next day's morning court, Kangxi scolded everyone who had impeached Changtai and, as a warning to others, stripped Mingju and Songgotu of most of their positions, ordering them to focus on handling the Russian border incursions to atone for their crimes.

Mingju and Songgotu wept with gratitude, kowtowed to admit their guilt, and declared they would never fail the Emperor.

Changtai, who had attended court this time, barely managed to keep his mouth from twitching. He thought to himself that compared to his uncle and Mingju, he still had a long way to go.

With the two most senior officials of the First Prince's faction stripped of power, Kangxi naturally wouldn't let the others off the hook.

The most vocal officials were exiled to Ningguta, and the rest were demoted or stripped of rank. The court finally quieted down, stopped daydreaming, and focused on working to resist Russia and train the navy.

Changtai was thoroughly blacklisted by the entire First Prince's faction, and many hated him to the bone. If he showed even the slightest flaw, countless bloodthirsty sharks would surely pounce.

It would be a lie to say Changtai wasn't afraid. But then he thought, as the Crown Prince's own uncle, he would likely be treated this way regardless of what he did, so he felt relieved.

This impeachment incident exposed most of the First Prince's faction's connections in the court, and Kangxi added all these people to his "little black book."

The First Prince's faction went into temporary hibernation. All officials were putting their best efforts into performing well, and the efficiency of the Qing court increased significantly.

Perhaps the situation in the court could also affect morale on the frontier. In the late autumn of the 18th year of Kangxi, Third-Class Earl and Deliberative Minister E'erduo Fiyanggu, along with the Generals of Heilongjiang and Ningguta, broke through the city of Yaksa and annihilated the Russian garrison.

By the time the Russian Regent Sophia sent envoys requesting the Qing to lift the siege and expressing a willingness to negotiate and redefine the borders, General Sabusu of Heilongjiang was already leading a group to rebuild the city of Yaksa and start farming the land.

Fiyanggu spoke Russian, but he pretended he didn't understand and agreed to let the Russians bring their own translators.

The Russian envoy was still arrogant despite being defeated, but the missionary translator made it sound as if the Russian envoy was about to kowtow and submit. Fiyanggu's mouth twitched wildly as he listened, and he immediately submitted a memorial, sent by fast horse to Kangxi.

Kangxi opened the memorial; the first sentence was a greeting, and the second was, "Learning Russian is absolutely necessary; I suggest all frontier generals learn it."

Kangxi was torn between laughter and tears: "This Fiyanggu, what did he encounter to have such a realization?"

After reading Fiyanggu's memorial and learning what he had faced, Kangxi took a deep breath and wrote the words "Request Granted."

Originally, Kangxi had intended to send another member of the E'erduo clan, E'erduo Pengchun, to Heilongjiang.

Although Pengchun and Fiyanggu shared the same clan name, they were not from the same family. Pengchun's E'erduo clan were descendants of the Qing founding hero Heheli, while Fiyanggu's E'erduo clan was the one famous for the Empress Xiaoxian of the Shunzhi era.

E'erduo Fiyanggu was the younger brother of Empress Xiaoxian.

Fiyanggu was a natural-born fierce general, exceptionally burly, with super-high combat power, and was also a wise and strategic general with long-term vision.

Because the Empress Dowager and Kangxi had previously vented their anger toward Empress Xiaoxian on him, he had been sidelined for a time. But gold always shines; Fiyanggu stood out during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories and was ranked among the Deliberative Ministers.

Originally, after becoming a Deliberative Minister, Fiyanggu would have been cold-shouldered by Kangxi again until the expedition against Galdan, which was his true opportunity to show his talent.

In this life, because Kangxi saw the "Shunzhi possession" and understood his father's hidden difficulties back then, he no longer held any ill will toward Empress Xiaoxian, and Fiyanggu's career path became much smoother.

Fiyanggu was also a talented, well-rounded man who was very good at seizing opportunities. He had learned several foreign languages early on, and was particularly proficient in Russian.

When Kangxi took Yinreng to inspect Aihun City, Fiyanggu was successfully left behind. Pengchun, who lacked language talent and didn't know Russian, returned to the capital early. The opportunity to lead the expedition against Russia naturally fell into his hands.

Fiyanggu was much more capable than Pengchun, and being young and vigorous, he didn't even consider whether the Russians would surrender or yield, directly pushing through all the Russian strongholds in one go.

If it hadn't been for the weather getting colder, he would have wanted to push a few more miles to see if he could find the towns where the Russians gathered.

You think only you Russians know how to burn, kill, and loot? Our Qing Dynasty has only been wearing the skin of civilized people for a few decades; if you dare come here to rob us, why can't we go there to rob you?

Come on, let's hurt each other and see who steals more.

Fiyanggu was extremely unhappy when he saw the peace-seeking letter sent by the Russian Regent.

He had only just begun to build his merits; how could they ask for peace? Are borders negotiated? Aren't they fought for? Whether to stop the war or not is up to us in the Qing; what are you blabbering about? Do you think you're special?

Therefore, Fiyanggu's memorial to Kangxi naturally carried his own subjective emotions, denouncing the rudeness of the Russian envoy and the deception of the missionary translator, arguing that the Russians should be taught a lesson.

Kangxi naturally granted it.

Currently, the Qing borders were peaceful everywhere except for Russia, and Kangxi could afford the military expenses.

Besides, even if there were no war, the soldiers had to be fed; it was better to send the Eight Banners troops to Heilongjiang in turns for training, lest they become a bunch of pampered young masters. When a real hard battle came, they wouldn't even be able to lift their swords.

The Eight Banners troops were also happy.

Only by fighting could they earn military merits; although fighting meant death, they knew nothing else. If they didn't rely on war to make money, how could they support their families?

After Zhao Liangdong and Yuele, two university instructors, discussed it, they submitted a memorial to Kangxi requesting to take the students out for some exercise.

Learning without practice is just a show; it was time for these Eight Banners noble youths to go to the battlefield. The bitter cold of Heilongjiang was the perfect place to temper their bodies and minds.

Kangxi naturally granted this as well.

"I wonder when Ziqing, Rongruo, and Elundai will be back." Yinzhi said, "That kid Kuadai carries Elundai's family letters with him and reads them many times a day, crying every time; it's so annoying."

After returning to the palace, Yinzhi went back to Consort Rong for the New Year, and the other young princes also stayed in their own mothers' palaces due to the cold weather. Only Yinzhi was kicked out of the palace by Consort Hui and continued to live in the Prince's Quarters.

Kangxi had been frequently summoning concubines recently, and Yinreng found him annoying, so with Kangxi's tacit approval, he also moved into the Prince's Quarters for the time being.

Yinreng said, "Looking at Elundai's letters, he has completely forgotten to return home. I didn't expect Elundai to be quite fierce in battle."

Yinzhi said, "I heard he's not very smart, just fierce."

Yinreng said, "If he's not smart, as long as he's obedient, it's fine. The three of them have already led a cavalry unit on their own; Ziqing is in charge of logistics, Rongruo acts as the strategist, and Elundai leads the troops in execution. They each perform their duties and cooperate perfectly. Sabusu and Fiyanggu praise them every time they submit a memorial."

Yinzhi was fiercely envious: "Ah, how great, I want to go and build merits too. Uncle also returned to Taiwan; it's so frustrating. The fifteenth day of the first lunar month hasn't even arrived yet; why did he run so fast?"

Yinreng thought to himself, Father uses Uncle as an emotional trash can every day; why wouldn't he run? If he didn't run, Uncle would be depressed soon.

Look at what Father says to Uncle every day? Before, it was just bad-mouthing the court officials, which Uncle was used to; now Father has actually started complaining about the concubines in the harem. Could Uncle listen to these things?

"Boring." Yinzhi lay flat, "Master Tang has also left. Without Master Tang playing games with us, the games aren't fun anymore."

Yinreng pushed Yinzhi, who was hogging his recliner: "You're just craving Master Tang's stories."

In order to teach the contrarian First Prince well, Tang Zhen's storytelling skills had improved by leaps and bounds; he could definitely make a fortune as a storyteller.

Yinreng believed that Tang Zhen's previous poverty was because he had chosen the wrong profession.

Since Tang Zhen had worked so hard, it was only natural for the princes to call him "Master."

"Yes, I'm just craving Master Tang's stories." Yinzhi said, "Aren't there any other people who are as knowledgeable and good at storytelling as Master Tang? Those old masters who teach us only know how to hold books and drone on, saying we have to thoroughly understand the classics. It's annoying, boring, I want to change masters."

"Just endure it. Father is also still studying the classics. We can only stop studying when he stops." Yinreng said, "Let's not talk about these annoying things; I'll tell you a piece of good news quietly."

Yinzhi sat up, putting his hand to his ear: "Tell me."

Yinreng whispered, "I heard the Empress Dowager and Father say they are going to Wutai Mountain. We should be able to accompany them."

Yinzhi's eyes widened immediately: "Really?!"

Yinreng smiled: "Really. Based on my understanding of Father, he will definitely go down the mountain in disguise to play when the time comes."

Yinzhi rubbed his hands excitedly: "I can finally go out with Father?"

Yinreng said, "Yes, Father said you are almost engaged and should be brought out for the officials to see, otherwise you won't be able to marry a good wife."

Yinzhi: "..."

Yinzhi lay back down: "I don't know why, but I'm suddenly not excited anymore."

Yinreng lay on Yinzhi's stomach, laughing so hard he couldn't get up: "Are you shy?"

Yinzhi said weakly: "It's not shyness, it's just that I find it troublesome."

Yinreng was curious: "What's troublesome? Father is the one arranging the marriage."

Yinzhi sighed: "Look at Father's harem. Women, trouble."

Yinreng held his forehead. Father's harem, indeed, seemed a bit too noisy recently.

Imperial Noble Consort Tong and Consort De were pregnant, so two favored concubines had suddenly lost their combat effectiveness. Plus, Kangxi had spent very little time in the palace this year, and every time he returned, the concubines vied for his favor, the gunpowder smell so thick that even the intuitive Yinzhi could smell it.

Kangxi himself enjoyed it. Yinzhi, who hated trouble, watched from the side and felt a bit annoyed.

"As long as you don't take too many women into your backyard and are a bit more doting on your primary wife, you won't have these troubles." Yinreng thought of the relationship between Yinzhi and his primary wife and said, "Father will definitely choose a woman you like for you, don't worry."

"Blind marriage, not everyone has the good luck of Elundai." Yinzhi thought of Elundai, his tone a bit sour.

Prince Kang's family had descendants training in Heilongjiang. Prince Kang's daughter would frequently correspond and exchange gifts with Elundai under the guise of sending things to her brother.

Elundai sent Prince Kang's daughter pebbles from Heilongjiang, dried flowers symbolizing victory from Yaksa, and preserved fruits made from unknown delicious berries in the dense forest—all worthless trinkets.

Prince Kang's daughter sent Elundai not-so-exquisite embroidery, poems that made one's teeth ache, and paintings of very ordinary scenery from around the capital...

Yinreng and Yinzhi, under Kangxi's instruction, also frequently corresponded with the Heilongjiang guard trio. Elundai, this guy, was very shameless and would show off his romance to his two grand-nephews every time they corresponded.

Yinzhi thought Elundai was simply sick.

Could a normal person show off their romance to their grand-nephews?!

What was even more hateful was that Elundai also told Yinzhi, "Eldest Prince, I heard you're almost at the age of engagement. I'll share some good luck with you. No need to thank me; this is what a grand-uncle should do."

Yinzhi: "???"

Is this something a human would do?!

Yinzhi now wished he could grow up immediately, then ride a fast horse to Heilongjiang and beat Elundai up!

"Let him be smug, let him be smug! When he comes back, see how I deal with him!" Yinzhi was so angry his nose was snorting.

Yinreng really wanted to ask how his eldest brother could deal with their grand-uncle. To avoid making his brother angrier, he held back.

Yinreng changed the subject: "Imperial Noble Consort Tong and Consort De are about to give birth; the Fourth Prince has been in a bad mood recently."

Consort De was close to labor, her energy was low, and she inevitably neglected the Fourth Prince.

In the past, the Fourth Prince didn't feel it when he played with his brothers every day, but now that he was alone in the Yonghe Palace, he started to feel unhappy.

"It seems someone is whispering in the Fourth Prince's ear, saying that since Consort De has a new child, she won't treat him as well as before. That the Fourth Prince is the older brother and must let his younger brother have everything." Yinreng sighed.

Yinzhi rolled his eyes: "Ah, is this the legendary harem intrigue?"

89. First and Second Update [V]

There are only three reasons why someone is whispering in the Fourth Prince's ear.

First, some concubines dislike Consort De and are sowing discord between mother and son to harm others without benefiting themselves;

Second, the imperial clan and nobility are starting to choose young princes now, so they are subtly making the Fourth Prince feel insecure, relying on the servants around him so they can influence his words and actions through these servants;

Third, that person thinks they are being kind and is simply loose-lipped.

Yinreng asked Yinzhi: "Which possibility is higher?"

Yinzhi rolled his eyes again: "No matter which one it is, that treacherous slave should be beaten to death."

Yinreng sighed: "It's the New Year, talking about death is really unlucky. If we bring it up, Father might even think we're making a fuss. After all, Consort De is about to give birth and her energy is low, so it's a fact that she won't be as good to the Fourth Prince as before. Teaching the Fourth Prince to yield to his younger siblings isn't a mistake either."

Yinzhi said: "I don't care if it's a mistake or not, beat them all to death!"

Yinreng was choked by Yinzhi.

He realized he was still out of place in the feudal era. With Yinreng's values, even if the other party said something bad, it wouldn't rise to the level of "beating to death."

But in this era, if one held onto modern values, life wouldn't be easy.

Yinreng suppressed the discomfort in his heart and said: "We don't have the authority to punish the people around the Fourth Prince. After Consort De gives birth and can spare the energy to take care of him, let the Fourth Prince complain to her."

Yinzhi was unhappy: "Just let the Fourth Prince listen to the treacherous slave's nonsense for now?"

Yinreng smiled: "Of course not."

Yinreng went directly to Kangxi: "Father, someone told the Fourth Brother that Consort De won't treat him as well as before now that she has a new child, and the Fourth Brother is very sad. I want to take the Fourth Brother to my side and teach him how to be a filial son so that Consort De won't abandon him."

Kangxi: "?"

Although Kangxi felt it was strange, as if his precious son was bad-mouthing someone, he still let his eldest son and precious son help him take care of his fourth son.

Kangxi saw that Consort De had become very tired as she approached labor, and had originally planned to let the Fourth Prince stay with the Empress Dowager and the Empress for a while to keep the Fifth Prince company, and return to Yonghe Palace after Consort De finished her confinement.

Now that his eldest son and precious son wanted to raise their brother, he trusted Yinreng and agreed.

Moreover, the fun-loving Kangxi also wanted to see how his foolish son and bad son would teach the fourth son.

Yinzhi and Yinreng went to Consort De's palace together, greeted her, and informed her of their intention.

Consort De hurriedly called out little Yinzhen and had people pack his luggage.

"Fourth Prince, Mother can't take good care of you for a while, you must listen to your brothers. I'll come pick you up after I finish my confinement." Consort De gently straightened little Yinzhen's clothes.

Consort De had already heard from Kangxi that little Yinzhen might be temporarily handed over to the Empress Dowager and the Empress to raise, and would be sent back after she finished her confinement.

Although the Emperor's word was law, pregnant people couldn't help but be sensitive. Consort De was very worried that since her son was so likable, what if the Empress Dowager and the Empress asked the Emperor to raise the Fourth Prince themselves?

Rationally, Consort De knew this possibility was very low, but she couldn't help but let her imagination run wild.

Having the Crown Prince and the First Prince raise her son was different.

Consort De trusted the Crown Prince and knew that her son would absolutely not be bullied there; and the Crown Prince couldn't raise his brother forever, so the Fourth Prince would definitely be able to return to her side.

Little Yinzhen nodded quietly, hugged Consort De gently, and left with his Crown Prince brother and eldest brother.

When they arrived at the Prince's Quarters, Yinreng and Yinzhi looked at the silent little Yinzhen and exchanged a glance.

Yinreng: Brother is so pitiful.

Yinzhi: Beat the treacherous slave to death!

Yinreng took a deep breath, dismissed the servants, and gave Yinzhi a gesture.

Yinzhi immediately picked up little Yinzhen and threw him onto the warm, soft couch.

Little Yinzhen was like a little turtle, belly up, blankly paddling his short limbs.

His eldest brother and Crown Prince second brother pounced on him and launched a fierce attack on little Yinzhen's ticklish spots.

Little Yinzhen's expression immediately twisted as he arched back and forth in his brothers' arms, trying to escape: "Hahahaha, hahahaha, so ticklish, brother stop, hahahaha, can't breathe!"

The eunuchs and nannies standing at the door pricked up their ears, and one nanny complained in a low voice: "How can the Crown Prince and the First Prince bully their younger brother?"

Liang Jiugong glanced at her lightly and noted the nanny's appearance.

"Are you happy now?" Yinreng let go of little Yinzhen, who was already limp from laughing, and straightened the clothes of little Yinzhen, who had been ravaged by his brothers.

Little Yinzhen rubbed his mouth, which was sore from laughing, and sniffed: "Brother is a bully."

Yinzhi crossed his arms and said: "It's only natural for older brothers to bully younger brothers."

Little Yinzhen muttered: "Then why doesn't Eldest Brother bully Crown Prince brother?"

Yinzhi sneered: "It's natural for older brothers to bully younger brothers, but I can also choose not to."

Little Yinzhen: "..."

He turned around and went into self-isolation.

Yinzhi didn't indulge little Yinzhen. He picked him up and faced him: "Stupid brother."

Little Yinzhen pouted: "Yinzhen is not stupid."

Yinzhi said: "Stupid. You are a prince; whichever treacherous slave makes you unhappy, you can punish them, there's no need to think too much."

Yinreng quickly grabbed Yinzhi, who was teaching his younger brother the wrong things: "Don't do that. Thinking is still necessary. If you can't think it through and feel embarrassed to trouble Consort De, just come and ask us."

Little Yinzhen sniffled and gave a small nod.

He reached out his hands, pouting as he sniffled: "Crown Prince brother, hug."

Yinreng took little Yinzhen into his arms. Having just been tickled and let out some steam, little Yinzhen gripped Yinreng’s clothes tightly and finally couldn't help but cry.

For adults, "unintentional words" that are neither painful nor itchy, or words meant to teach a child to be sensible and filial, can be a source of immense pain and trauma for a young child.

After hearing that Consort De would love another child more, little Yinzhen had been unable to lift his spirits.

The princes all seemed to be precocious; little Yinzhen understood in his heart that these words might be true, but he dared not reveal his sadness to anyone else, so he could only bottle it up.

Everyone said the Fourth Prince had become mature and steady, and even Kangxi was very pleased. Only Yinreng held him and asked if he had anything on his mind.

As soon as little Yinzhen told Yinreng his worries, his Crown Prince brother, like a hero, rescued him from his oppressive environment.

"They said, Niangniang has to take care of the younger brother or sister and doesn't want me... Niangniang wants to send me to the Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager." Little Yinzhen cried until he hiccuped, "Does Niangniang not like me anymore? Niangniang often says I'm too naughty. Am I too naughty, so Niangniang doesn't want me?"

As little Yinzhen cried, he began to admit his faults.

He said he shouldn't have disobeyed Consort De and run around, hiding so the servants couldn't catch him;

He said he shouldn't have used his little wooden sword to hack at the shrub bonsai that Consort De carefully tended, and kicked the cut leaves everywhere;

He said he shouldn't have secretly hidden pastries in his pillow, causing tooth decay, and then cried incessantly in Consort De's arms...

Yinzhi wore an expression of "I'm shocked." Are these things considered wrong? Aren't these just normal things?

He had once angered his own mother, Consort Hui, so much that she kicked him out of Yanhxi Palace during the New Year and told him to go back to the Prince's quarters to live alone, and Yinzhi never thought he had done anything wrong. What little Yinzhen did was perfectly normal.

Yinreng gently patted little Yinzhen's back, not interrupting his constant apologies.

Yinzhi fetched hot water from the side room himself, mixed it into warm water, and wrung out a towel for Yinreng.

When little Yinzhen was tired of talking, Yinreng took the wet towel from Yinzhi and wiped little Yinzhen's tears and snot: "Consort De won't send you to the Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager. After a woman gives birth, she needs to observe the postpartum confinement."

After Yinreng explained what postpartum confinement was, he said: "You are young, and Khan Ama is worried that the people in Yonghe Palace won't be able to take good care of you without Consort De's supervision, so he plans to send you to play with little Five for a few months. After Consort De finishes her confinement, you will return to Yonghe Palace."

Little Yinzhen said with swollen eyelids: "Really? It's not that Niangniang doesn't want me?"

Yinreng said: "Do you know how hard it was for your Niangniang to give birth to you? She likes you so much, how could she not like you?"

After Yinreng finished washing little Yinzhen's face, Yinzhi threw him a set of new clothes, telling Yinreng to change out of the clothes that were a mess from little Yinzhen's tears and snot.

Yinzhi took little Yinzhen away to change his clothes.

The eunuch then entered the room to replace the hot drinks and pastries, then exited again.

After changing clothes, little Yinzhen's emotions calmed down.

He held a fresh fruit sent from the hot spring villa, nibbling on it bit by bit, his swollen eyes glancing shyly at his two brothers.

"After you finish the fruit, brother will teach you about women giving birth," Yinreng said.

Yinzhi widened his eyes, frowned, tucked his chin in, and took a deep breath: "Why do I have to learn this!"

Yinreng took out a stack of cards and said: "First, once you know these things, you will understand Niangniang's hardship and be more filial; second, in the future, you will have wives and children. Knowing some things early is good for family harmony. Do you think giving birth is just a woman's business?"

Yinzhi said: "It is just a woman's business."

"Shut up, Big Brother," Yinreng said. "Women are very tired when they are pregnant and can't do many things. Think about it, if your Fujin is pregnant in the future and there's no one to manage the backyard, and someone harms your Fujin and child, you wouldn't even know how it happened. Or are you saying you trust that your future secondary wives, concubines, and maids will sincerely hope for your Fujin and child's well-being?"

Yinzhi immediately kicked off his shoes and climbed onto the daybed, sitting cross-legged very impolitely: "Then hurry up! Get on with it!"

Yinreng stuffed little Yinzhen between Yinzhi's crossed legs, cleared his throat, and began to explain using the illustrated cards.

The drawings on the cards were cute and cartoonish, the human proportions were incorrect, and the organs were very abstract.

Yinzhi and Yinreng were both young; Yinreng just wanted to tell them some basic female physiological knowledge, and he would leave the specifics for when they were married.

However, even just cartoon pictures were shocking enough for two little boys.

Yinzhi and little Yinzhen pressed their hands against their cheeks, trembling: "A-a big cut has to be made, a lot of blood flows, and the baby crawls out of the stomach?! Is it that scary!!!"

Yinreng said: "Otherwise? How did you think babies were born?"

Yinzhi said: "Just like how I poop?"

Yinreng said: "Can you poop something as big as a baby?!"

Yinzhi said: "What if the opening for giving birth is bigger?"

Yinreng said with a dark face: "Obviously, it's not big. You are already being taught about adulthood, so I'll just tell you straight."

Yinreng whispered into Yinzhi's ear, and Yinzhi's face turned paler and paler.

He looked down at himself.

The first time that happens, women bleed, so how big could the place where babies are born be?

Little Yinzhen was bewildered. He didn't quite understand what his brothers were saying, but he at least understood that giving birth was very, very scary.

"Having many children and many blessings, for a woman, is trading her life," Yinreng sighed.

As long as noble ladies in ancient times gave birth to two or three sons and their status was guaranteed, they would immediately find low-status, beautiful concubines for their husbands.

Generous and virtuous?

No, they were just trying to survive.

Many Qing dynasty palace intrigue novels in later generations say the First Prince didn't care about his Fujin's life in his pursuit of a son; that is just a fictional setting that doesn't understand the ancients.

There were no contraceptive methods in ancient times. The so-called contraceptive medicine was actually abortion medicine, and even then, it wasn't certain the pregnancy would be terminated.

There are many records in history of empresses dowager and princesses who kept male favorites and constantly had abortions; most of the pampered concubines in ancient palace records who died young died from constant childbirth or miscarriage.

Without modern condoms and birth control pills, exclusive favor meant constant childbirth.

As royal wives, the Fujins dared not have abortions and could only keep giving birth until they couldn't anymore or until they died.

Even if they secretly drank medicine, it wasn't necessarily effective.

Yinreng once saw a modern writer describe his mother. His mother had a breakdown due to frequent pregnancies.

That mother tried many methods: drinking medicine, vigorous exercise, and even lying on ice in winter to freeze herself, but she couldn't stop herself from getting pregnant, and couldn't even manage a miscarriage.

Later, that mother became half-mad and half-silly from poisoning while experimenting with contraceptive and abortion folk remedies.

After the First Prince Yinzhi married his Fujin, even if it was to pursue a son as the novels say, he could have slept with other women while his Fujin was pregnant or menstruating. According to Manchu tradition, having a son by a concubine first was nothing. As long as his legitimate son came before the Crown Prince's, it was fine.

But Yinzhi had no other children while the First Fujin was alive; his concubines' children were born five years after the First Fujin died.

Given Yinzhi's vitality, he likely spent three full years in mourning for his First Fujin before touching other women.

Afterwards, the mothers of Yinzhi's children were evenly distributed, and it wasn't until his later years that one concubine, Guo, gave birth continuously. It is estimated that by then, the only concubine he had left was that one, Guo.

Not only the First Prince Yinzhi, but the Thirteenth Prince Yinxiang was the same.

The Thirteenth Fujin and Yinxiang originally had an average relationship. Later, when Yinxiang was cold-shouldered and disliked by Kangxi, the Thirteenth Fujin and Yinxiang's feelings warmed up through mutual support. Yinxiang pampered his Fujin, leading to the Thirteenth Fujin giving birth frequently, and her health collapsed early.

Further back, there was Empress Ma of Zhu Yuanzhang. Zhu Yuanzhang's first few sons were all born to Empress Ma, with little age difference. The reason for Empress Ma's early death was also that frequent childbirth ruined her health.

Women in ancient times were so pitiful; even a husband's exclusive favor was a death warrant. After dying young, they could only be labeled as "beautiful but ill-fated."

It is very difficult for women to practice contraception themselves; it would be slightly easier if men cooperated.

Trying not to have intercourse during the fertile period, and using natural condoms like animal intestines during intercourse, although not 100% effective, could give the women in the house a chance to recover their health after childbirth.

Yinreng had already written down the methods for male contraception. If Yinzhi still had deep feelings for his First Fujin as he did in his first life, he would give the contraceptive methods to Yinzhi to protect his sister-in-law's life as much as possible.

To have a loved one by one's side for a lifetime, Big Brother would be very happy, right?

Now everyone was still young, so Yinreng didn't mention contraception, only telling his older and younger brothers how dangerous pregnancy and childbirth were for women and how much harm it did to their bodies.

"Consort De doesn't dislike you; she really has no energy left," Yinreng said. "Do you understand? Little Four?"

Little Yinzhen huddled in Yinzhi's arms, trembling: "So, so scary? Will Niangniang be okay? Niangniang will be okay, right!"

Yinreng said: "Little Four can tell stories to the baby in Consort De's belly, teaching your future younger brother or sister to be good and not to trouble Consort De when they are born. Little Four can also help Consort De manage the others in Yonghe Palace. If you see someone slacking off, tell someone to send them to the Bureau of Punishments. If someone tries to drive a wedge between you and Consort De, you can lock them up first. After Consort De finishes her confinement, she can deal with them."

Little Yinzhen nodded vigorously: "I, I want to protect Niangniang!"

Yinreng smiled and touched little Yinzhen's head: "Consort De has protected Fourth Brother for so long, now it's Fourth Brother's turn to protect Consort De, right?"

Little Yinzhen immediately puffed out his chest: "I want to protect Niangniang!"

Yinreng said: "You can definitely do it. You stay with brother tonight, and tomorrow you ask to return to Yonghe Palace yourself, okay? You tell Khan Ama you want to protect Consort De and won't leave Yonghe Palace. You are already a big kid and can take good care of yourself, right?"

Little Yinzhen immediately said: "I can!"

Yinreng said: "Fourth Brother can go to pay respects to the Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager every day, playing with little Five while asking the Grand Empress Dowager how to manage palace affairs. The Grand Empress Dowager will definitely teach you."

The Grand Empress Dowager will probably send an old nanny to Fourth Brother. With someone sent by the Grand Empress Dowager, there's no need to worry about anyone in Yonghe Palace doing bad things while Consort De is indisposed, Yinreng thought to himself.

Yinreng and Yinzhi spent the night with little Yinzhen.

That night, both Yinzhi and little Yinzhen had nightmares, and Yinreng was kicked awake multiple times in the middle of the night by his older and younger brothers rolling around the bed.

The next day, Yinreng couldn't take it anymore. After sending little Yinzhen back to Yonghe Palace, he returned to the Qianqing Palace to catch up on sleep, avoiding Yinzhi, who had many questions after seeing the physiological science cards.

Before sleeping, Kangxi picked up his precious son, who was already fighting off sleep: "How do you even know about women's childbirth?"

Yinreng's head bobbed, and he yawned repeatedly: "Because... ha... I wanted to know... why Niangniang passed away... ha, sleepy, Ama let go, I want to sleep."

Kangxi tucked Yinreng into the quilt and went to sit alone in front of Empress Renxiao's portrait for half a day.

When Kangxi left, Zhao Chang secretly glanced at Kangxi's face.

Kangxi's eyes were very red, and his eyelids were a bit swollen.

Zhao Chang lowered his head, feeling a bit sad himself for some reason.

The news that the Crown Prince taught the Fourth Prince about the difficulties of female childbirth, causing the Fourth Prince to mature overnight, refuse to leave Yonghe Palace, stay by Consort De's side to take care of her, learn to help manage palace affairs at a young age, and tell stories to the baby in Consort De's belly, was leaked by Consort De.

Consort De showed off her son while subtly thanking the Crown Prince, making a name for him.

The palace concubines envied Consort De for having a filial son while also having a better impression of the Crown Prince.

Kangxi also quietly released the news that the Crown Prince studied women's childbirth because he wanted to know the reason for Empress Renxiao's death.

The Crown Prince was purely filial, so filial it was almost pitiful.

The palace concubines, whether they had met the Crown Prince or not, couldn't help but shed a few tears for the little Crown Prince.

When the Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager learned of this, they also sighed endlessly.

They took the little Crown Prince into their arms, calling him "good grandson" this and "good grandson" that, even messing up the generations.

Kangxi, the Grand Empress Dowager's actual grandson, touched his nose awkwardly on the side, pretending he didn't exist.

What made the concubines sigh even more was that the First Prince Yinzhi, who had angered Consort Hui into losing her mind and kicking him out of Yanhxi Palace during the New Year, actually knew how to be filial now.

Consort Hui said that the First Prince had been so filial lately that it gave her goosebumps, while chanting Buddha and sighing about the Crown Prince's goodness.

"If the Crown Prince hadn't persuaded the First Prince, the First Prince would have angered me to death sooner or later!" Consort Hui patted her chest, "I can't control him; the only people he listens to, besides the Emperor, the Empress Dowager, and the Grand Empress Dowager, is the Crown Prince."

The Empress Dowager and the Grand Empress Dowager shook their heads vigorously upon hearing this.

No, no, no, this great-grandson/grandson never listens to us.

Kangxi rubbed his temples, wanting to add that Yinzhi rarely listened to him either, unless suppressed by force.

The Crown Prince is still the best. The Crown Prince supported the harmony of the harem; whether it was raising princes and princesses or mediating conflicts between concubines and their children, it all depended on the Crown Prince.

When Kangxi was about to take the Crown Prince to Mount Wutai again, the concubines all sighed with regret.

Life in the palace without the little Crown Prince is really hard to endure.

Never mind, the Emperor is leaving too, so the palace won't be that hard to endure after all.

"Khan Ama, you will go on an incognito inspection, right? You will, right? If you don't, my brother and I can go on an incognito inspection, right!" Yinzhi kept pestering him.

Kangxi pressed his forehead. Just after leaving the palace gate, he already had the idea of throwing his eldest son back into the palace.
