101.三更四更（霸王票加更） [V]
第二日，赵良栋派人整理赛场，立好靶子，清理好赛道，规划好观战席。
这些都是胤礽曾经给赵良栋和岳乐出的主意，让赵良栋和岳乐折腾京中的勋贵子弟。
侍卫一看这个场地就开始恍惚，仿佛回到了期中期末考试赛场。
曹寅摩拳擦掌：“让草原人感受我们期中期末考试的痛苦吧！”
侍卫们“嗷嗷嗷”，震得蒙古人有点怕。
“他们在嚎什么？”
“不知道，就……气势很强。”
“不愧是野人女真，真可怕。”
“闭嘴吧！”
在醒悟到现在不是自己考试，而是草原人考试之后，侍卫和八旗青年军官们都露出了嗜血扭曲的狞笑。
胤礽在心里为他们配音：让世界感受我们的痛苦吧！
还有什么比看到别人经历他们经历过的苦更开心？请加倍！
侍卫和八旗军官们气势如虹，看得蒙古王公们猛男心颤。
他们琢磨，最近自己好像没有做过对不起大清的事吧？呃，好像有？就是、就是最近训练不努力，军队武力值太低，打不过叛乱的准噶尔部。
蒙古王公们这次带了许多金银珠宝和马匹牛羊来木兰围场，就是想请求大清出兵揍准噶尔部。
漠西蒙古准噶尔部的首领噶尔丹自立为汗，不再向大清称臣。因为隔得较远，目前还相安无事，大清没出手收拾准噶尔。
但对于漠西蒙古其他部和漠南蒙古诸部落而言，那事情可就大了。
他们天天被揍被抢，只能寄希望于大清出兵。
康熙知道他们的小心思，在心底骂了许多次废物。
这群草原人都自诩黄金血脉，结果现在废物得连自己的草原都保不住，还要大清百忙之中抽空帮他们揍人。
你们草原部落能不能自己给力点，把叛乱的准噶尔揍垮啊！朕把支持准噶尔的沙俄都撵走了，你们怎么还打不过准噶尔？！
接二连三的胜仗，让康熙豪情万丈，确实有主动出手征伐准噶尔的打算。但他可不想这群蒙古人只送些马匹牛羊金银就算了事。
大清出手，草原部落怎么也要出些更实质上的利益，别就想用财物打发，搞得大清跟雇佣兵似的。
大清和蒙古诸王公商量正事之前，先让皇子和蒙古王公子嗣来一场友好切磋比赛。这气氛，让草原贵族子弟们心里有点慌。
“咱们只是玩玩，对吧？背后没有其他含义吧？”
“如果输了，父亲会不会揍人？应该不会？”
“只要赢，就不怕有事。”
“对，我们还赢不了两个孩子吗？”
草原幼鹰们窃窃私语，拍了拍裸露的胸膛，认为稳了。
没错，只要赢了，这比赛背后有再深的含义都没用！
昨日，胤禔和胤礽已经骑着马在草原上跑了一会儿，让马匹习惯这里的土地。
今日，胤禔率先出战。
他坐在最爱的踏雪马上，紧张的心情被风一吹，渐渐沉淀。
胤禔想，或许他天生就属于马背。只要骑在马背上，他的胆气就足得仿佛可以捞起太子弟弟就跑，丢下汗阿玛，和太子弟弟一起去海外逍遥。
胤礽拍了拍踏雪的马头，踏雪亲昵的蹭了蹭胤礽的手背：“踏雪好好努力，帮大哥赢得胜利。”
踏雪仰头嘶鸣。
胤礽退后几步，仰头看向胤禔：“大哥，弟弟祝你旗开得胜。”
胤禔灿烂笑道：“交给哥，哥什么时候让你失望过？”
胤礽点头，回到观战席上。
胤祉紧张地拳头都攥紧了。
“要不要去更好的观战席上观看比赛？”胤礽问道。
胤祉眨眨眼睛：“更好的观战席？”
胤礽笑着让人牵出马。
赛道是环形，赛道中央的场地就是最好的观战席。
康熙也来到了马背上，和蒙古王公一起在马背上观战。
纳兰性德拿起信号枪，朝天鸣放。胤禔的马就像是离弦的箭一样冲了出去。
而其他贵族子弟的马犹豫了一下，才跑出去。
康熙疑惑：“怎么？你们的马连枪声都没听过？它们居然会害怕？”
蒙古王公有些尴尬：“这些马还没上过战场。”
康熙道：“朕的大阿哥也没上过战场，但训练的时候，总该让马匹习惯枪声。”
胤礽微笑：“你们的马不习惯枪声起步慢了，等会儿输了不会说孤的大哥胜之不武吧？”
蒙古王公们立刻道：“怎么会？这是他们训练不到家！”
胤礽道：“希望如此。”
他们聊天的时候，胤禔已经来到了第一处关卡。
赛马可不是只跑得快就行，中间肯定有障碍和比试。
关卡中有跨越栏杆、坑洞、水池上的独木桥；有下马拾取东西之后上马继续比赛；有尽可能的用大刀砍掉沿路的靶子……
这些关卡都模拟了战争时，骑兵可能遇到的现实难题。
蒙古王公们脸色有点难看了。
大阿哥和他的马显然很熟悉这些关卡，每次过关都一气呵成，几乎没有停顿。
相比之下，他们的子弟们就有些抓瞎，甚至出现了严重的失误——有几个人从马背上摔下来，似乎还不小心摔伤了。
胤礽道：“这些关卡顺序都是你们决定，大清只负责安装。而且昨日我们给了你们时间提前熟悉关卡，孤的大哥可是没有提前熟悉过场地。你们若是输了，不会怨大哥以前做过类似的训练吧？”
蒙古王公们苦笑：“不会不会，这都是模拟现实中的困境，我们在草原上跑马的时候也会遇到类似的困难。”
胤礽点头：“那就好。想你们也不是输不起。孤和大哥不过是深宫里的皇子，很少见过真正的草原，跑马也是围绕着狭小的校场，你们的草原幼鹰怎么都应该比孤和大哥强。”
蒙古王公们直说不敢不敢，脑门上汗珠不断往外冒。
康熙努力板着脸，心里高兴极了。
看到自家坏儿子去“坏”别人，他别提多舒坦。
蒙古王公们虽然被胤禔的一马当先打了个措手不及，但他们不认为自己的孩子会输。
说白了，这些障碍都是模拟现实障碍，他们的孩子天天在真实的草原上跑马，还能比偶尔骑马在狭小的校场上跑一圈的小皇子差？
赛道后半段全是边骑马边砍靶子，砍靶子有额外得分。在马上砍杀需要很强的技巧，深宫的皇子哪有这个经验和力气？
他们正想着，胤禔已经冲到了最后的打靶区。
胤禔手中提着的是一柄长柄马刀。刀身很薄、刀刃很锋利，是胤礽让工匠们打造的新式钢刀。
胤礽虽是个废物文科生，但看小说的时候，勉强记得铁加碳，再用高炉高温，还要吹进什么气体，就能得到大量的钢。
他把自己零散的记忆告诉康熙，康熙召集工匠试验。
胤礽根本没报什么希望，但工匠们还真搞出来了批量炼钢。
虽然那钢铁比不过什么几十叠百叠钢，但普通士兵也用不到那等手工打造的好刀啊。
他们能人手一把钢刀，至少比铁强。
胤禔手中的宝刀是工匠们用批量生产的钢铁再锻造后，得到的大清目前最高工艺的宝刀。
别看刀身薄，就着骑马的惯性力道，刀刃轻轻滑过靶子，靶子立刻被斩断，马匹前行完全没有停顿。
蒙古王公们猛男张嘴，瞠目结舌。
不会吧不会吧？他们的草原幼鹰们不会输吧？
这时候，草原幼鹰们也来到了打靶区。
为首的一人狠狠一刀砍向靶子，没收住惯性，刀呲溜一身荡到了马身上。
可怜的骏马哀鸣一声，把那草原幼鹰甩了出去。
赵良栋一挥手，立刻有人冲进去把那只草原幼鹰抬出来治疗。
康熙黑线：“你们不是经常狩猎吗？怎么在马上用刀都不会用？”
蒙古王公们尴尬道：“我们在马上多用弓箭。”
康熙深呼吸了几下，语气温柔地询问道：“你们难道骑在马上就只用弓箭打猎，没有进行过其他训练？等战斗的时候，你们除了弓箭，其他都不用吗？”
蒙古王公们：“……”他们要怎么说？自家子嗣这么金贵，怎么会让他们上战场？
康熙温柔劝说：“就算你们舍不得孩子上战场，也得训练他们在马上的功夫，以防万一啊。溺子如杀子，你们的孩子……唉……”
胤祉忍不住了：“皇父，还不如让儿子去。”
蒙古王公们：“……”这就有点尴尬了。
胤礽想了想，笑着道：“你还小，赢了输了都是他们尴尬。等哥哥们比完之后，咱们私下玩耍的时候你和他们切磋。那时候就别要彩头了，就只当玩耍。”
胤祉嘟着嘴道：“好，听太子哥哥的。”
胤礽问康熙道：“皇父看这样可好？”
康熙点头：“可。带三阿哥出来，就是让他多认识些人，你安排便是。”
胤礽在马背上行礼道：“儿子遵旨。”
胤祉看看胤礽，又看看康熙，心里觉得有些古怪。
太子哥哥就像是变了个人似的，一言一行都合乎规矩得过分，对着汗阿玛的表情和动作也谦逊恭顺得过分。
胤祉捏紧了缰绳，没来由的感到了些许难过。
他不知道自己为什么难过。等大哥比赛结束，问问大哥吧。
赛场上，比赛已经进入了尾声。
胤禔从出发时便与其他人拉开了差距，之后差距越来越大，后面的人看着胤禔的马屁股，神情越来越绝望。
他们发了疯似地抽打马匹，想要跑得更快一点。
赛马这种事，不是鞭子抽得狠了，马就跑得更快。
急躁的情绪升起来之后，他们的失误更多了，不断有人从马背上滚落。
康熙的脸都看黑了。
大家都是马背上的民族。大清入关之后，皇子都在校场上训练，只偶尔去景山猎场训练。
你们蒙古人天天在草原上跑，就算输，也不该输这么多啊。
蒙古八旗也是大清的兵，康熙开始怀疑蒙古八旗的战斗力了。
胤礽却一点都不意外。
从小在马背上玩耍，和赛马这种竞技比赛是两回事。就像是多年的老司机不会开赛车一样。
他们兄弟从开始骑马起，跑的就是这样的赛道，经历的就是这样的训练，寒暑不断。一群不过骑着马玩耍的草原幼鹰们，哪可能比得过他们？
胤禔不出意外，夺得了第一。
他冲过终点之后，勒马停在终点线前面，微微抬起下巴，冷漠地望着那些还未到终点的人，就像是真正的雄鹰俯瞰一群毛都没长齐的叽叽喳喳小弱鸟。
当那些草原幼鹰们来到终点线的时候，接受了胤禔不屑的目光洗礼，黝黑的脸庞几乎都失去了血色，牙关都咬紧了。
胤禔等所有没有失误的草原幼鹰们来到终点线之后，才策马转身离开。
他一句话都没说，只留给这群人一个背影。但这群人却总觉得被嘲讽和侮辱了。
“一场赛马比试，居然有一成的人受伤。”康熙叹气：“还比吗？”
胤礽道：“皇父，还是明日比吧。他们看上去很累，儿子不想胜之不武。”
蒙古王公：“……”他们已经不想听到“胜之不武”这四个字了！
草原幼鹰们蔫哒哒的回来。
有一只幼鹰嘟囔，皇子们只是占了习惯这种比赛模式的便利，被自家老子狠狠两鞭子抽在地上直打滚。
“输了就输了！别找借口！”
蒙古王公贵族气得脸更黑了。他们可不想再听太子问一次“是不是胜之不武”！！
还不够丢脸吗！
蒙古王公这次是真的丢脸丢狠了，也气狠了。
他们看着大皇子领着两个弟弟去收马收刀，三皇子蹲在受伤的马身旁长吁短叹，恨不得找个地缝钻进去。
三位皇子带来了大批赏赐，他们没有一个人得到，倒是把自己的马和武器输出去了！
胤祉蹲在地上叹气：“唉，多好的马啊，还能治好吗？”
胤禔拍了拍胤祉的脑袋，道：“交给赵师傅，能治好的就治，治不好就给你做成马肉火锅。弟弟，你带够了火锅调料吗？”
胤禔直接喊弟弟，或者其他皇子直接喊哥哥，哥哥弟弟前面没带数字排序，都是喊的胤礽。
胤礽道：“那哪能少得了火锅调料？放心，绝对带够了。”
他搞出火锅之后，拉着康熙入股，用仁孝皇后的嫁妆铺子开了火锅店，现在店铺成了康熙的探子窝点。
开分店的时候，胤礽让胤禔和胤祉入股，只拿分红不管理，作为送给哥哥弟弟们的入学礼物之一。
以后弟弟们入学，胤礽也会给弟弟们店铺分红，以免他们将来缺钱，被人引入歧途。
现在胤礽的分红只是小打小闹，等大清公司开起来，皇子们就真的不缺钱了。
常泰已经带着他的海军下南洋做生意；施琅明明年纪已经不小，还焕发了事业第二春，跑东洋去了。
常泰牢记胤礽的话，当地有什么好的工匠医生都绑回来。他绑回来的神医，还误打误撞救了姚启圣的命。
现在姚启圣在上奏请求致仕，说致仕之后也去船队上玩玩。康熙还没考虑清楚，让姚启圣进京来大学任教，还是让姚启圣上船玩。
赵良栋拍了拍马屁股，严肃的脸庞难得露出欣喜的笑容：“是好马，没骨折就能救。大阿哥……”
胤禔摆手：“我知道赵师傅你想说什么。我用不上这么多马，这些马都送到大学去，作为弟弟说的那个叫什么来着，哦，奖学金，谁期末考试考得好就给谁。不过我和弟弟会去观战。我的马，可不能让人作弊获得。”
胤祉小声道：“我也好想要新的马。”
他的马太温顺了，跑得不是很快。
胤礽揉了揉胤祉的脑袋，道：“咱们的马还是问汗阿玛要吧。汗阿玛那里的马更好。”
胤祉点头：“好。哥哥帮我挑。”
胤礽道：“没问题。”
康熙大步走过来，笑骂道：“这里的马还不够，你们居然惦记上朕的宝马了？”
胤礽行礼后道：“儿子和弟弟肯定是完成汗阿玛的考验之后，才敢要汗阿玛的马。”
胤禔撇头，在心里嘀咕康熙小气。
康熙看出了胤禔在心里嘀咕他，欣慰极了。
他的大儿子，居然知道在外人面前只心里嘀咕，没有给他抬杠，给足了他这个汗阿玛面子。
这绝对是太子教导得好！
“明日射箭，他们可就要拿出真本事了。”康熙道，“保成，你量力而行。”
胤禔忍不住了：“汗阿玛您什么意思？儿子难道赢的不是他们的真本事吗？！”
康熙：“……”他才刚欣慰！
胤礽劝道：“汗阿玛只是给蒙古诸部一个面子，假装他们没有使出全部力气，不是质疑大哥的胜利。不过明日，他们估计会派出真正的战士冒充王公子弟，不敢只让真正的贵族子弟来了。”
胤禔翻白眼：“冒充？那不是欺君吗？”
胤礽道：“我们本也没说和谁比试。”
胤禔嗤笑：“好啊，最好把他们的蒙古勇士派来，到时候输了更有意思。比射箭的准头，弟弟不可能输。”
见胤礽三言两语就把胤禔的思路带偏，康熙松了一口气。他还真担心胤禔会脑子一热，让他下不了台。
康熙有些怕了胤禔的憨脑子和直肠子了。
“是的，明日他们肯定会派出真正的战士。”康熙道，“保成，你别太努力，让他们赢也没关系。”
胤礽点头：“儿子知道。”
第二日，胤礽看了一眼参赛的人中，多出来的体格完全不同的几人，露出一个了然的微笑。
胤礽面容精致白皙，就像是精雕细琢的白玉人。
草原幼鹰们打量着这位大清国的太子殿下，怎么看，这位大清皇太子的骑射功夫也不像会有多厉害。
比赛靶子有固定靶子、移动靶子，还有加入了赛马元素的靶子——参加比赛的人上马奔驰到靶子区，计算经过靶子区的时间和所射的靶子综合评分，和胤禔后半段赛马砍靶子的比赛规则差不多。
胤礽在手上缠上了绷带，带上了扳指，俯身压了压筋。
哨声开始，固定靶场比赛开始，胤礽第一个出场比赛。
他拉起弯弓，眼睛微微眯起。
在他的视野中，微小的靶子好像一点一点的放大，空中也似乎出现了弓箭划过的痕迹。
这些只是幻觉，是胤礽精神力太过集中之后出现的幻觉。
手松开，一支羽箭呼啸着离开弓弦，呼啸飞过虚空，稳稳扎入了靶心正中央。
胤礽再抽出一支箭，弯弓搭箭，接二连三，羽箭接连不断脱手而出。
他的动作和表情都十分轻松写意，仿佛不是做射箭这等需要力气的事，而是在吟诗，在作画，在饲弄花草，端的是优雅无比。
可他的每一支箭都狠辣地正中红心，箭矢牢牢扎在靶子上，入木三分。
胤礽射空了箭筒里的十支箭，收起弯弓，慢吞吞解开缠绕在手掌上的绷带，取下大拇指上的扳指，转身离开射箭的位置。
其他人静静地看着他，居然不知不觉看出了一身冷汗。
“该你了。”
侍卫提醒下一个人。
那只草原幼鹰回过神，嘴唇翕动，半晌说不出话。
他低头看了一眼自己的双手，居然在颤抖。
草原人精通骑射，神箭手不知有多少。那群草原贵族子弟是不怎么厉害，但草原上绝对有非常厉害的人，他们也见惯了厉害的人。
轮射箭的准头，草原上也有人能做到和胤礽一样好。但没有任何一个人，会像这位大清太子一样，给他们这么强大的压力。
或许是太子第一个上场比赛就十支箭全中靶心，这样的“及格”成绩让人压力极大。第二个射箭的人失去了冷静，第一支箭居然落在了靶外。

102.一更二更 [V]
胤禔收回了看向射箭场内的视线，不屑道：“本皇子都说了让弟弟最后上场，他们非要弟弟第一个上场。看，弓都拿不稳了。”
胤祉使劲点头：“以太子哥哥的射箭成绩作为及格成绩，这群人真是，哼。”
听到两个儿子的话，康熙努力把上弯的嘴角压下，干咳一声道：“草原神弓手这么多，总会有比得过保成的人。”
胤禔：“不可能，别想，皇父你想什么？皇父你不识数吗？”
胤祉惊讶地看向康熙。什么！原来汗阿玛不识数？！
康熙：“……”他只是谦虚一下。
“保清！”康熙沉声威胁胤禔。
胤禔想起胤礽千叮嘱万嘱咐，让他在外面要给康熙面子。
他立刻改口道：“皇父难道是认为他们会自带靶子？或者那箭会拐弯，能一口气连射几个靶子？皇父英明！儿子都没想到！”
胤祉恍然大悟：“原来如此！”
康熙：“……”
曹寅看不下去了，小声道：“皇上，大阿哥已经很努力了。”大阿哥真的不是阴阳怪气您啊皇上！
康熙：“……朕是说，可能平手。”
胤禔：“哦。”
胤祉：“哦哦哦。”
康熙把视线投向站在射箭场外，正在和身旁侍卫说话的胤礽。
嗯，这时候，他只能看着自家宝贝儿子洗洗眼睛洗洗脑子，免得被大阿哥气死。
说起来，三阿哥虽然不是故意的，但是好像也微妙的朝着会气死老父亲的方向成长。
胤祉究竟是如何每一句接话，都能火上浇油，让他怒气更盛的？！
接下来确实有射箭技术和心理素质都不错的人，也在固定靶场上拿到了全满分的成绩。
但让蒙古王公脸上无光的是，这些人都是他们派进去的真正草原勇士，自己的孩子无一例外全部成绩惨淡。
这还只是第一轮。
接下来还有移动靶子，和移动着射靶子。
胤礽每轮都是第一个出场，每次都是每一箭都正中靶心。
限制他成绩的，只是他携带的箭矢数量。
如果前面的射靶子只是让众人震撼胤礽的射箭技术，在骑马射箭的时候，胤礽让他们看到了这具小小身体中所蕴含的杀伤力。
对骑兵而言，弓箭和轻弩其实才是最主要的杀伤工具，其他马刀、长柄武器之类，都是辅助。
真到了需要骑兵短兵相接的时候，已经是骑兵陷入了劣势。
对于那些年轻的草原贵族子弟而言，骑马射箭是他们唯一自信的地方——之前他们自信的地方很多，但已经被大皇子和太子碾碎了。
打猎是草原贵族子弟每日的玩乐，论骑马射箭的准头，他们相当有自信。
但胤礽策马射箭时，他们就像是看到了什么极其超乎常理的可怕的事，马都停了下来。
如果说固定靶子和移动靶子还能全中，坐在马上射箭，准确率能有五成，已经是草原人可以将其供奉起来的神箭手。
胤礽却仍旧是那一副轻描淡写的表情，箭矢随意出手，每一支箭都扎入了靶子上，好像那靶子中心有什么吸引箭矢的东西，让箭矢自己飞了过去。
甚至胤礽都没怎么瞄准，箭矢上弦，弓弦拉开，箭矢射出，一气呵成，无论是骏马行进的速度还是他射箭的速度，都极具节奏感，仿佛演奏着一支节拍分明的乐曲。
这违反常理的行为，让胤礽显得不像是一个真人。
连见多识广的蒙古贵族，都忍不住起了一身的毛毛汗。
胤礽能射出这违反常理的箭，就是因为他那违反常理的“金手指”——过于强大的精神集中力。

Reforming the queue-cutting edict—a trivial matter unrelated to the interests of the Banner people—was enough to make that group of clansmen and nobles stage a farce of forcing the Emperor’s hand. If he touched the Eight Banners, they would go insane!

"I know, I know," Kangxi said cheerfully. "Am I, your father, the kind of reckless person?"

"Shouldn't be?" Yinreng said uncertainly.

If it were the Kangxi from his first life, Yinreng wouldn't be worried at all.

But in this life... Father, you have already done something reckless once. As the saying goes, once there is a first, there is a second. Your son is truly worried!

Yinreng was filled with worry, praying every day that Kangxi would take it easy and not force the Eight Banners into rebellion so quickly. At the very least, he should wait until he and his big brother grew up and became Kangxi's right-hand men before pushing the Eight Banners to revolt.

By then, his uncle should have already trained a navy with considerable combat effectiveness. With their combined sea and land forces, those Eight Banner lords who only knew how to ride horses would be unable to hold their ground.

Fortunately, the two consorts in the palace finally gave birth, diverting Kangxi's attention and preventing him from bringing up the Eight Banner reform again.

Consort De gave birth to a daughter prematurely, and the girl's health was considered okay; Imperial Noble Consort Tong's daughter was born at full term and was also in decent health, but she had a facial deformity—she had a cleft lip.

In modern society, a cleft lip could be fixed with a minor surgery; in ancient times, a facial deformity was far more serious than the Seventh Prince's limp, and such children were almost always abandoned.

Kangxi was in great pain.

"Cousin, so we really are close relatives, aren't we?" Kangxi hugged Yinreng tightly, as if this would calm his mood a little.

Yinreng didn't know how to comfort Kangxi.

Of course, cousins were close relatives; blood ties would not change because of surnames.

Yinreng knew that even though Kangxi increasingly loathed Tong Guowei, he still held some affection for Imperial Noble Consort Tong. Kangxi had truly looked forward to this hard-won child between him and his cousin.

Many cousins in the world could marry and have healthy children, so why weren't he and his cousin the lucky ones? Kangxi was hit hard.

"Father, let's raise the younger sister in the palace; we will provide for her for her entire life. As long as public opinion is managed well, a facial deformity can be described as a 'natural anomaly.' We can say the sister was born with a unique appearance, suspected to be a fairy descending to earth, so she is living in the palace as a nun for spiritual cultivation. Outsiders won't say anything," Yinreng comforted him.

Kangxi patted Yinreng's back, remained silent for a long while, and sighed deeply: "You are truly good to your younger brothers and sisters."

Yinreng retorted: "Am I not good to my older brother?"

Kangxi was finally amused by Yinreng: "Good, you are indeed very good to Baoqing."

Yinreng nodded vigorously. No one could question the bond between him and his big brother!

"Let's do it that way." At that moment, Kangxi had already considered killing his daughter.

But when Yinreng made the suggestion, Kangxi's heart softened. He thought helplessly that with a Crown Prince who was overly kind to his siblings, it was very difficult for him to be ruthless.

The fact that the daughter was born with a cleft lip could not be hidden from Imperial Noble Consort Tong. Kangxi told her how he would handle their daughter.

"It was the Crown Prince's idea," Kangxi said. "However, cousin, don't have any more children in the future."

Imperial Noble Consort Tong was stunned upon learning of her daughter's facial deformity. When Kangxi told her he would spare the child's life, she closed her eyes, tears streaming down her face.

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong laughed: "You really dare to say that. The Tong family must have a daughter in the palace, right?"

The younger Tong-shi said, "This is Father's intention. For the sake of the Tong family's reputation, a Tong daughter entering the palace is a necessary contribution to the family. However, just as Your Highness said, by the Emperor's rules, as long as you are alive, there is no need to worry about other Tong daughters entering the palace."

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong asked, "Do you want to enter the palace?"

The younger Tong-shi did not speak.

How was she supposed to answer? If she said she wanted to, that would be wishing for the Imperial Noble Consort Tong to die.

But if she said she didn't, the Imperial Noble Consort Tong would know it was a lie the moment she heard it.

Being a second wife to someone else—how could that be better than entering the palace? Even without children or favor, the Emperor would treat her well for the sake of the Tong family. If the Tong family found her useful, they would treat her birth mother well too.

Her birth mother said that Lady Hesheli is now respected by Father precisely because of the Imperial Noble Consort Tong. As long as she could enter the palace, her birth mother's treatment at home would improve accordingly.

Marrying someone else wouldn't work. Only by entering the palace as a concubine could a woman of the Tong family change her own fate and that of her birth mother.

In the end, the younger Tong-shi only said, "Even if I'm not favored after entering the palace, as long as I am honest and follow the palace rules, the Emperor surely won't treat me the way Father treats Mother."

A faint smile appeared on the younger Tong-shi's face, which was even younger than the Imperial Noble Consort's: "Your Highness, you have always grown up in the palace without a care, which is why you think about love or lack thereof. I only seek a small, safe place to exist."

The younger Tong-shi crossed her hands and gently gripped her arms, as if hugging herself for warmth in the snow.

"If Your Highness is determined to defy Father and marry me off, please choose a frail civil official for me, okay? Even if he dies early, it doesn't matter. This younger sister is truly so afraid. Although marrying someone else means I won't be able to protect my mother, I still want to live."

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong braced herself against the bed and sat up with difficulty.

She looked straight at this younger sister of hers, who usually lacked any presence; she hadn't expected the younger Tong-shi to say such things.

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong watched the younger Tong-shi for a while, then her arm supporting her body went limp, and she fell heavily back onto the bed.

She gasped and said, "Father may be violent, but he knows his limits when he strikes; he won't abuse people."

The younger Tong-shi chuckled lightly: "He certainly wouldn't to the main wife. The main wife has sons and has you, an Imperial Noble Consort. She is also from a branch of the Hesheli clan; as long as the Crown Prince is still there, Father will always be wary of the Hesheli family's face. But my mother is just a concubine. A concubine is no different from a house servant."

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong closed her eyes and said, "I understand. You may go."

The younger Tong-shi stood up, knelt on the ground, and kowtowed: "After Your Highness spoke so much to me, I already understand that it is definitely impossible for me to enter the palace. Even if there are other Tong women who can enter, it will definitely not be me. I only ask for Your Highness's pity."

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong said indifferently, "I have no hobby of humiliating my own sister. You may go."

The younger Tong-shi kowtowed twice fiercely, leaving bloodstains on her forehead: "Thank you, Your Highness."

After the younger Tong-shi left, the Imperial Noble Consort Tong stared blankly at the bed curtains, not speaking for a long time.

Even when the eunuch beside her left directly, she didn't speak.

In the Imperial Study, Kangxi held a scroll in one hand, listening to the eunuch describe, word for word, what had happened in the Imperial Noble Consort's room, his expression indifferent.

Yinreng looked up at Kangxi, then quickly lowered his head, staring at his toes in deep thought.

"I saw Tong Guowei and his wife had several children and thought they were a loving couple. Their legitimate sons don't help their own biological mother?" Kangxi said.

E'lundai said, "Ah, are you asking me, Your Highness?"

Kangxi's face darkened: "Otherwise? Am I asking Baocheng?"

Yinreng looked up again and said, "If a son helps his mother, he would be considered unfilial, right? At most, they would kneel on the ground and get beaten together."

E'lundai said, "Yes, yes, yes, that's exactly how it is."

Kangxi said, "So, did Longkodo and the others get beaten together?"

E'lundai said, "I don't know about that. My family and Tong Guowei's family separated long ago; we don't live together, and I don't know about their private family matters. However, Tong Guowei hasn't caused any deaths, so he should just have a bit of a bad temper, not anything too excessive."

Yinreng lowered his head again to look at his toes.

Kangxi rolled up the book in his hand and tapped Yinreng's head lightly: "Say what you want to say."

Yinreng scratched his head and said, "In the common folk, when a father looks down on and insults the mother but values the son, there is a high probability that the son will also be like the father, viewing the mother as a servant."

Kangxi tossed the book in his hand gently onto the table: "E'lundai, if you dare to treat the Heshuo Gege of Prince Kang's family badly, I will have Prince Kang beat his way to your door."

E'lundai immediately said, "Even if my family had someone like Tong Guogang, we don't have the hobby of hitting women. How weak must one be to find a sense of existence by bullying women? If you want to fight, go to the battlefield; that's what a real man does. If you can't go to the battlefield, you should find other men to fight."

Kangxi and Yinreng exchanged a look, both with darkened faces.

E'lundai's words were always strange.

"Don't keep staring at your father; keep a closer eye on Tong Guowei. If he does anything wrong, submit a memorial to impeach him, understand?" Kangxi said irritably.

E'lundai sighed: "That would be better left to Tong Guogang to watch his younger brother. I can't watch him; looking at him makes my eyes hurt."

"Get out!" Kangxi grabbed a brush and threw it at E'lundai.

E'lundai picked up the brush, put it back on the desk, and then withdrew, looking completely unbothered.

Kangxi frowned, wanting very much to kick him in the backside.

After E'lundai left, Yinreng sighed: "I lost the bet with Big Brother; I have to think of a new game for him."

Kangxi pinched Yinreng's cheek: "Is that all you're sighing about?"

Yinreng said, "Otherwise? It's enough for Ama to worry about the Tong family's affairs; it doesn't have much to do with me."

Kangxi rolled up his sleeves, pretending to beat Yinreng.

The father and son chased each other around the Imperial Study, circling the desk and pillars; finally, Yinreng climbed onto the rafters and made faces at Kangxi.

Kangxi put his hands on his hips: "Get down!"

Yinreng said, "I won't!"

Kangxi sneered and clenched his fists: "Not coming down? If you don't come down, when you eventually do, you'll be waiting for a beating."

Yinreng said, "I'll get beaten if I come down now anyway!"

Kangxi said, "If you don't come down, you won't get to decorate the Eastern Palace yourself."

Yinreng obediently slid down the pillar and was pinched and rubbed by Kangxi, kneaded like a clay doll.

After bullying his son enough, Kangxi called for a table of fruit and pastries, eating with Yinreng while sighing: "Hearing about Tong Guowei's affairs, I thought about my own daughters in the future... sigh."

Kangxi couldn't manage the private family affairs of his ministers, nor did he have the energy to, but thinking of his own daughters, he couldn't help but feel a bit despondent.

Yinreng's brows twitched.

He had several sisters who passed away young after being sent to marry into Mongolia. But unlike other emperors, Kangxi sent people to investigate the causes of his daughters' deaths in detail. If the princess's early death was due to her husband, even years or decades later, Kangxi would seek revenge for his daughter.

Later generations always said Kangxi was a "central air conditioner," very considerate to the women in his harem. Even after scolding the mother of the Eighth Prince, Consort Liang, he didn't skimp on her funeral honors after she died.

Abolishing the practice of concubines being buried with the Emperor and allowing concubines who had sons to leave the palace to live with them were all manifestations of Kangxi's warmth.

Kangxi was good to his own women and had a genuine sense of pity and protection for his daughters. In this era, for an emperor to do these things, he could already be considered a good man.

"The princesses of the Great Qing have their own princess residences after being sent to Mongolia; as long as she can stand on her own, she won't be bullied by her husband," Yinreng said. "If Ama is worried, you can increase their studies."

Kangxi laughed: "Good, I'll increase their studies and say it was your suggestion."

Yinreng patted his chest and said, "Let the sisters' anger over the heavy workload be directed at me!"

Kangxi laughed and rubbed Yinreng's head again, sighing: "Relatives by marriage, relatives by marriage—once they have that 'outside' label, they really are outsiders, all with their own little schemes."

Yinreng said, "Ama, don't even mention relatives by marriage; there are plenty of blood relatives who break each other's heads fighting for benefits."

Kangxi joked: "What about you? Will you fight with Ama for the throne?"

Yinreng looked disgusted: "Ama, do you really think the throne is that great?"

Kangxi asked back: "Is it not?"

Yinreng said, "Ama, do you think it's more satisfying to lead troops overseas to conquer land and just enjoy life without worrying about governance, or to sit on the dragon throne and rack your brains? Since I was old enough to understand, I haven't seen a day where Ama didn't frown over state affairs."

Yinreng extended his index finger to press the center of his brows: "Just like this, Ama is still young, but you already have 'Chuan' wrinkles. What's so good about being an emperor?"

Kangxi was momentarily at a loss for how to refute his son.

Yinreng said, "Ama should try hard to exercise and live to be a hundred, so that I can go out and roam more. It would be best if Ama lives until the grandchildren are adults, so that after Ama passes the throne to me, I can be emperor for a year and then pass it to Ama's grandson."

Kangxi: "..."

Kangxi's hands itched; he wanted to beat his son.

Seeing that Kangxi really wanted to beat him this time, Yinreng jumped up and bolted out the door of the Imperial Study, his legs moving like wheels of fire, and he disappeared in a flash.

Kangxi clenched his fists, gnashing his teeth.

It's not good for a son to be too smart. When they're too smart, they want to slack off, even finding the throne troublesome.

Yinreng lost the bet and borrowed a group of people from the Imperial Household Department to make "Sanguosha" (Three Kingdoms Kill) cards for the First Prince.

When the "Sanguosha" cards were finished, the group of princes played so obsessively that they almost neglected their studies and were given a good beating by Kangxi.

Kangxi was so angry his liver hurt; he confiscated their cards and only allowed them to play during holidays.

With nothing to do, Yinreng could only return to strolling in the Imperial Garden, taking the opportunity to detour to the construction site of the Eastern Palace to see his new house.

During this time, he met the Imperial Noble Consort Tong, whose health was gradually recovering.

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong was more dignified and mature than before. Kangxi and the Empress Dowager both said that after experiencing hardships, the Imperial Noble Consort had finally grown from a little girl into a mature woman.

Yinreng looked up at the Imperial Noble Consort Tong, whose every word and action met the standards of noble grace and decorum, and looked at her dull eyes, but felt that the Imperial Noble Consort Tong before him seemed like an empty shell.

The Imperial Noble Consort Tong's body had recovered, but her soul seemed to have died.

The woman in front of him was just a walking corpse.

Yinreng thought that the Imperial Noble Consort Tong was holding on to her life now probably because she knew Tong Guowei was hoping for her death, so she refused to close her eyes no matter what.

She was now like a ghost with an obsession.

Yinreng really wanted to persuade the Imperial Noble Consort Tong that even if one's father was a beast, and even without children, one could still live for oneself.

But he had no standing to persuade the Imperial Noble Consort Tong.

His persuasion would be of no use to a woman of this era.

Even modern women who are "brother-obsessed" are hard to change despite higher education; the Imperial Noble Consort Tong was just a pitiful and tragic ancient woman, unable to break free from the shackles upon her.

For the Imperial Noble Consort Tong to simply use "staying alive" as a silent resistance against her father was already difficult enough.

Besides Tong Guowei, Kangxi was also responsible for the Imperial Noble Consort Tong's "death."

When Tong Guowei's words and actions shattered Kangxi's filter regarding his maternal family, Kangxi's feelings for the Imperial Noble Consort Tong also faded.

Seeing the Imperial Noble Consort Tong, Kangxi would think of Tong Guowei's hateful face and could no longer be as close to her as before.

However, he still gave the Imperial Noble Consort Tong the same respect as always, only he no longer let her raise other princes and rarely stayed overnight at her palace.

Yinreng couldn't stand it and whispered a few words in Kangxi's ear.

After consulting with the Empress Dowager, Kangxi sent the daughter of Prince Gong, Changning, who had been raised by the Empress Dowager, to the Imperial Noble Consort Tong's palace, officially adopting her as a daughter and registering her under the Imperial Noble Consort Tong's name.

Kangxi had few heirs before and thought he would have difficulty having healthy daughters, so he had raised Prince Gong Changning's daughter by a concubine beside the Empress Dowager, intending to adopt her to be sent to Mongolia.

Later, when Kangxi had his own biological daughters, he didn't send this little Gege back to Prince Gong's mansion, but instead let her attend classes with the princesses.

Now, Prince Gong's little Gege officially changed her jade record to become the Imperial Noble Consort Tong's daughter. Because the imperial daughters younger than her had already been titled, Kangxi also conferred the title of Heshuo Chunxi Princess on this adopted daughter in advance.

After receiving Kangxi's decree, the Imperial Noble Consort Tong was stunned for a long time, and finally, a little light returned to her eyes.

She hugged the eleven-year-old girl and said, "Mother will protect you well from now on."

Hearing the "Mother" that the Imperial Noble Consort Tong called herself, Chunxi's eyes flickered slightly, and she buried her head in the Imperial Noble Consort's arms.

She had entered the palace since she was young. Prince Gong's concubine had no qualifications to enter the palace, so she had never seen her mother.

This was the first time someone had hugged her and said, "Mother will protect you."

Mother... Chunxi recited in her heart for a long time before she timidly said it out loud: "Mo... Mother."

"Yes." The Imperial Noble Consort Tong burst into tears.

Yinreng peeked quietly at the entrance of Chengqian Palace, then grabbed the arm of Yinzhi, who wanted to stick half his body out to watch, and dragged his older brother away.

"Let the Imperial Noble Consort and Chunxi have some time alone, Big Brother, don't go and ruin the atmosphere," Yinreng said. "Third Brother! Hold onto Big Brother!"

Yinzhi held onto Yinzhi's other arm and said, "You got it, Crown Prince Brother!"

Yinzhi grumbled and complained as he was dragged away from Chengqian Palace by his two younger brothers.

Kangxi watched this scene from afar and asked, "What are the three of them doing?"

Zhao Chang said, "The Crown Prince and the Third Prince probably don't want the First Prince to disturb the Imperial Noble Consort?"

Kangxi's face darkened: "Why would the First Prince want to disturb the Imperial Noble Consort?!"

Zhao Chang looked at Kangxi with great pity. How would this servant know? Besides the Crown Prince, who could figure out what the First Prince was thinking?

After asking, Kangxi realized that no one could answer this question except the Crown Prince.

And even the Crown Prince couldn't guess what his eldest son was thinking at every moment.

Kangxi was impotently furious: "The First Prince is just idle! I should find him something to do!"

Kangxi pondered for a moment and took the First Prince, the Crown Prince, and the Third Prince to hunt outside the Gubeikou of the Great Wall to see the Mongols who had been a bit restless lately, and to take the opportunity to observe the young Mongol descendants.

After being depressed by the Tong Guowei affair, Kangxi was very worried about his daughters' future marriage prospects and wanted his sons to mingle with the young Mongol nobility in advance so they could choose good husbands for the princesses later.

Upon learning that he could travel with his brothers this time, the Third Prince Yinzhi was as happy as a little hen, circling Yinzhi and Yinreng, chirping "Brother, Brother" incessantly, making Yinzhi and Yinreng's eyes swim.

Yinzhi dragged the little hen Yinzhi to the training ground to test his martial arts: "Don't embarrass me and your Crown Prince Brother when the time comes!"

Yinzhi was full of confidence: "I won't! I'm very strong."

So he and Yinzhi competed in archery, with Yinreng acting as the referee.

Little Yinzhen and little Yinqi sat beside the training ground with their chins in their hands, watching obediently, their little faces looking extremely sour.

Little Yinzhen pouted: "I want to grow up quickly; I will definitely be better than Big Brother and Third Brother in the future!"

Little Yinqi nodded: "Fourth Brother will definitely be very strong!"

Little Yinzhen said, "You have to work hard too! Big Brother and Third Brother have two people; we must also join forces to defeat them!"

Little Yinqi's brows knitted together, and he stuttered: "I... I will work hard." *Sob*, I have no confidence.

Yinreng, on the side, looked deeply at his two little brothers.

Oh my, the princes are already starting to form cliques; I hope Ama can handle it.

Speaking of which, by the time they return from the hunt, the Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth brothers should be able to talk and crawl, entering the cutest and most fun stage of their lives—they could serve as large, intelligent toys, right?

Yinreng pinched his delicate little chin, which was no longer fleshy after his growth spurt, and his bright eyes revealed a mischievous light.

At the end of the sixth lunar month of the 22nd year of Kangxi, Kangxi took the Crown Prince, the First Prince, and the Third Prince outside the Gubeikou of the Great Wall.

From then on, every autumn, Kangxi would take the princes to the Mulan Hunting Grounds to hunt, in order to connect with and intimidate the Mongol nobility.

For this tour, Kangxi brought along Songgotu and Mingju, who had been dismissed due to the "First Prince's faction using the First Prince to amass wealth" incident, but did not bring the two Tong brothers he had trusted and relied on.

What surprised the courtiers even more was that a few days before heading to Mulan for the hunt, Kangxi scolded Tong Guowei with a reason similar to "you stepped in with your left foot first."

Kangxi cursed Tong Guowei for being old and dim-witted, saying he should vacate his position for the young, and stripped Tong Guowei of all his real power, forcing him to retire early.

After being punished by Kangxi, Tong Guowei had no idea why he had been punished.

He hadn't done anything wrong, had he?

E'lundai, who was furious because he couldn't go to the Mulan Hunting Grounds due to being implicated by Tong Guowei, told Tong Guowei sarcastically that the reason he was scolded by the Emperor was that the Imperial Noble Consort was not yet dead, and he wanted to send a new daughter into the palace, which was clearly cursing the Imperial Noble Consort to die, annoying the Emperor.

Tong Guowei sneered: "The Emperor pities Empress Xiao'an and lets Consort Wen live in the palace to serve Empress Xiao'an; there is already a precedent. I was merely letting the Imperial Noble Consort's sister enter the palace more often to keep her company; it's impossible to have committed a taboo!"

E'lundai grinned, showing his gums: "Oh, then maybe I was mistaken; Uncle, keep up the good work."

With his hands behind his back, he walked with a swagger to find the future brothers-in-law of Prince Kang to build relationships.

After the Mid-Autumn Festival, he was going to marry his wife. He missed his wife so much now and hoped the brothers-in-law would give him some face and let him meet Shujin a few more times.

Tong Guowei flicked his sleeves and left to complain to Tong Guogang.

Tong Guogang looked at Tong Guowei lazily, sprawled out on a recliner with his clothes open, scratching his belly like a street thug or a loafer.

Tong Guowei talked until his mouth was dry, but Tong Guogang just scratched his belly comfortably and didn't reply a single word.

Tong Guowei was once again so angry he flicked his sleeves and left, finally feeling a bit panicked in his heart.

He hurriedly released Hesheli-shi and told her to go find the Imperial Noble Consort Tong.

After entering the palace, Hesheli-shi didn't see the Imperial Noble Consort Tong, but only saw the Imperial Noble Consort's newly adopted daughter, Princess Chunxi.

"Grandmother, have some tea." Princess Chunxi's smile was extremely sweet.

...

"If we aren't in the palace, will the Imperial Noble Consort be bullied by Tong Guowei again?" Yinzhi raised his whip on horseback. "I don't care about the Imperial Noble Consort, I just can't stand Tong Guowei being so arrogant and domineering toward people in the palace."

Yinzhi nodded vigorously: "People in the palace cannot be bullied by outsiders!"

Yinreng smiled: "Don't worry, the Imperial Noble Consort has Chunxi by her side; Chunxi will protect the Imperial Noble Consort well."

Yinzhi was skeptical: "Is Chunxi very strong?"

Yinreng said: "Chunxi is the best student among the princesses. Her talent is no less than ours."

Yinzhi wrinkled his face: "Heh, I don't believe it!"

Yinreng said: "When we return to the palace, you can compare with her. Our sisters have many who are very capable. If we cultivate them well, Mongolia will be nothing to fear."

Yinzhi thought of his own sister and said: "Sister Rongxian is also very capable."

Yinreng said: "There are queen regents in the West, and there are precedents for women in power in Mongolia. Our sisters may very well become the actual queens of Mongolia in the future."

Yinzhi beamed and smiled: "That would be nice."

Yinzhi nodded vigorously.

Since he still had to handle official business on the way to the hunting expedition, Kangxi asked from inside the carriage, "What are the three of them doing?"

Cao Yin, who was driving Kangxi's carriage, poked his head in and said, "The Crown Prince, the First Prince, and the Third Prince are discussing how to make the princesses actual rulers of Mongolia."

Kangxi: "..."

He began to worry about this trip to Mulan.

100. First and Second Chapter [V]

Had it been in the past, Kangxi would have already reprimanded his sons for spouting nonsense.

Having witnessed the affairs within Tong Guowei's household, however, Kangxi felt a bit more softness and heartache for his daughters.

Women of the inner palace were not allowed to interfere in politics, but those were other people's women. Kangxi practiced double standards; once his own daughter married into someone else's family, let alone interfering in politics, as long as she had the ability, Kangxi would cheer her on even if she took power.

When Qing dynasty princesses married out, it was not like the peace-by-marriage (heqin) of past Han dynasty courts.

What was heqin? The northern grassland nations of the Han dynasty courts only nominally respected the Han court, while the real power over military, political, and financial affairs remained entirely in their own hands.

Princesses marrying far away were doing well just to preserve themselves; wanting to hold power was practically impossible. They basically only served a pacifying role—to put it bluntly, they were high-status gifts.

A cruel fact hidden beneath historical texts was that most of the princesses sent for heqin prior to the Qing dynasty were concubines or secondary wives, including the famous Princess Wencheng.

In those vassal states and tribes, the ruling mistresses had their own cattle, sheep, property, soldiers, and even land. A strong mistress might even hold the economic lifeline of the entire tribe.

The men on the grasslands only took charge of fighting, while the women managed the household—and this "household" included cattle, sheep, herdsmen, and the grasslands.

Nurhaci and Hong Taiji would frantically marry grassland widows in the inner palace precisely to acquire their power, property, and territory.

By the time of the Great Qing, Mongolia was not merely a vassal state paying tribute. Mongolian territory was truly incorporated into the Qing dynasty's maps, with Qing officials and troops stationed to administer it.

When Qing princesses married into Mongolia, it was an alliance through marriage, no different from princesses marrying other generals and ministers within the court; they were not gifts given to Mongolia.

The moment a princess arrived in Mongolia, she became the ruling mistress, possessing all the power and status due to a mistress on the grasslands. Backed by the Great Qing, as long as she was firm and shrewd enough, it was entirely possible for her to become the de facto master of the grasslands in terms of real power.

When the Great Qing originally formulated the policy of princesses marrying into Mongolia, it was aimed at having the princesses take over the financial power of the grasslands. It was just that after entering the Pass, the good aspects of the Great Qing were not fully Sinicized, while the bad aspects were influenced by the dross of Han culture, leading to a neglect of the princesses' education.

Even so, the Great Qing had exceptionally talented princesses who taught themselves and managed to sway the military, political, and financial power of their tribes.

Kangxi called his sons into the carriage, and the father and three sons began plotting how to make the princesses take over grassland power more smoothly.

Yinzhi said, "I'll help them drill troops! All the household servants sent over will be better than the people on the grasslands. Whoever has the bigger fist is the boss!"

Yinzhi said, "I'll help them compile books so the princesses can set up schools and teach the grassland people loyalty to the ruler and patriotism."

Yinying directly produced a large volume of a project plan.

Kangxi, the First Prince, and the Third Prince: "..."

Yinying rubbed his nose. "During this trip to the Mulan hunting grounds, we must carefully probe them for information. The intelligence gathered by the spies sent out by the Great Qing isn't as genuine and detailed as what they let slip themselves when they accidentally get drunk."

Yinying then pulled out a questionnaire: "Our preliminary goal this trip is to collect data and fill out this form. I'm making a new game for the princesses."

Kangxi said, "I want a copy."

Yinzhi shouted, "Don't forget me!"

Yinzhi said quietly, "Crown Prince Brother, I want one too."

"Everyone gets one," Yinying said. "The copy for Imperial Father will be specially made. Imperial Father can pull it out whenever he discusses grassland matters with the ministers in the future."

Yinying smiled mischievously. "When the Mongolian princes and ministers come to pay respects to Imperial Father, Imperial Father can also pull it out to give them a fright."

At the mere thought of that scene, Kangxi couldn't help but reveal a smile even more mischievous than Yinying's: "Very good."

Yinzhi flexed his muscles. "What's drinking got to do with anything? A man's friendship is forged by fighting!"

Kangxi pressed his brow and said, "First Prince, who taught you that weird phrasing?"

Yinzhi said, "It wasn't Crown Prince Younger Brother."

Yinzhi quickly said, "Definitely not Crown Prince Brother."

Yinying: "?"

Kangxi: "Baocheng!"

Yinzhi said, "Imperial Father, I already told you it wasn't Crown Prince Younger Brother, what are you roaring for?"

Yinzhi said, "It was me, it was me, it really was me!"

Kangxi: "All of you shut up! Baocheng! Stop randomly teaching your older brother how to talk! He already talks strangely enough!"

Yinzhi said, "Imperial Father, I don't like hearing you say that. How is my speaking strange?"

Yinzhi said, "Imperial Father, Big Brother's speaking isn't strange. And it really wasn't taught by Crown Prince Brother."

Yinying quickly stopped his older and younger brothers from adding fuel to the fire. "Alright, alright, it was me, it was me, it's all my fault. Imperial Father, this was just something Your Son casually chatted about with Big Brother normally, and besides, saying this isn't wrong either. Don't be angry; if you anger your body, no one can take your place."

The carriage was in complete chaos. The emperor's roaring voice, the First Prince's disdainful voice, the Third Prince's attempts to take the blame, and the Crown Prince's continuous efforts to put out the fire rose and fell in succession, making the surrounding eunuchs and guards laugh out loud.

Cao Yin was driving the carriage, and Nalan Xingde stood guard at the front. The two of them chatted with smiles.

Cao Yin said, "It's still just as lively."

Nalan Xingde smiled and nodded. "The First Prince is still just as lively."

Cao Yin sighed. "If Eledai were here too, he'd definitely say that with the First Prince around, the Emperor has become very lively as well."

Nalan Xingde was torn between laughter and tears. "You should shut your mouth. You don't have Eledai's thick skin; don't learn how Eledai talks, or you'll be asking for a beating."

Cao Yin said, "I wonder if the two of us will be back in the capital by the time he gets married."

Nalan Xingde said, "Definitely not. The Emperor keeping him from leaving the capital is precisely so he can stay peaceably at home and get married."

Cao Yin lowered his voice. "Wasn't he... implicated?"

The noise of hooves and carriages on the road was loud. Once Cao Yin lowered his voice, only he and Nalan Xingde could hear each other. It was very safe, with no need to worry about others eavesdropping.

Nalan Xingde shook his head. "The Emperor knows what kind of character Eledai has; if anyone could be implicated, he couldn't be."

Cao Yin thought about Eledai's character. "Indeed. But the Emperor seemed to tell him that he was implicated; perhaps the Emperor wants to knock him down a peg?"

Nalan Xingde said, "It's about time he was knocked down a peg. I heard that as soon as he came back, he wanted to smash the doors of Prince Kang's residence and Lord Tong Guogang's family estate. The Crown Prince said neither of those two families was on the list, and he was quite regretful."

Cao Yin was speechless. "...Truly him."

Nalan Xingde said, "As long as Eledai doesn't make any major mistakes himself, the more the Emperor detests that person, the brighter Eledai's future will be. There's nothing for us to worry about. You'd better worry about yourself."

Nalan Xingde felt genuine sympathy and regret for Cao Yin.

Cao Yin was well-versed in both literature and martial arts, good-looking, and had exceptional emotional intelligence, but unfortunately, he was a bondservant trusted by the Emperor.

If he were an ordinary bondservant with Cao Yin's talent and merits, it would be possible for him to serve as a major regional official or even enter the cabinet as a general or minister. But as the Emperor's most trusted bondservant, Cao Yin's future position was already fixed.

Cao Yin was bound to go to Jiangnan to serve as the Emperor's eyes and ears, spending his entire life as a textile commissioner.

Although called an official, a textile commissioner was also an imperial merchant, responsible for purchasing silk and other items needed by the emperor. This position could only be held by the emperor's closest confidant.

To others, being a textile commissioner meant plenty of grease, a not-so-low status, and the nurturing climate of Jiangnan—a very good post.

But Nalan Xingde believed that given Cao Yin's talent, serving merely as an imperial merchant purchasing goods for the emperor and as a spy monitoring Jiangnan was truly a great grievance.

Without these shackles, Cao Yin could easily win a hereditary peerage for himself and his descendants.

Cao Yin smiled. "What is there for me to worry about? I've already been as wild and unrestrained in my youth as I should have been, and I've got you lot as good brothers. After middle age, I can settle down in a secure place to spend my old age."

Nalan Xingde did not answer.

Faced with such an unsolvable matter, other than smiling and accepting it, Cao Yin was helpless as well—so it was better left unsaid.

They changed the subject, talking about the scenery along the way, pondering some poetry and phrases, and calling for water to be sent into the carriage to soothe the throats of the imperial father and sons who had roared themselves hoarse.

Soon, the roaring inside the carriage stopped, and the Emperor was once again coaxed into continuous laughter by the Crown Prince.

The smiles on the faces of the surrounding eunuchs and guards also deepened.

As long as Crown Prince accompanied him, the Emperor's mood was always easily turned bright. Life was easy for them as attendants, too.

When the imperial procession advanced to the Mulan hunting grounds, the Mongolian princes and nobles were already waiting.

Kangxi led the three imperial princes out of the carriage ahead of time, riding tall steeds to display the martial might of their imperial father and sons.

When they dismounted at the same time, the nobles knelt and kowtowed. After they finished kowtowing, Kangxi went forward to help the leader up while saying, "Why stand on such ceremony?"

Yinzhi's expression twisted slightly. He really wanted to complain that his Imperial Father was truly hypocritical.

Yinying kept a constant eye on Yinzhi's expression. The moment Yinzhi's brow twitched, Yinying shot him a side-glance like a knife, and Yinzhi immediately closed his mouth and behaved.

Yinzhi watched the eye interaction between his two older brothers and let out a deep sigh in his heart.

With an older brother like this, Crown Prince Brother has it so hard. Fortunately, Crown Prince Brother still has me as a younger brother to soothe his exhausted soul.

Kangxi also kept glancing sideways at Yinzhi, terrified that Yinzhi would blurt out wild words in front of the Mongolian princes and nobles.

When he saw Yinying use a look to stop Yinzhi, he didn't know whether to feel relieved or exhausted in his heart.

The First Prince's martial prowess was not bad; it was necessary to trot him out in the Mulan hunting grounds so the Mongolian princes and nobles could see just how formidable his imperial son was.

But the First Prince's personality... Hopefully the Crown Prince could keep a tight leash on him.

Kangxi laughed heartily and exchanged a few casual remarks with the Mongolian princes and nobles, then called the three princes over to formally introduce them to the Mongolian nobility.

Yinzhi: Rebellious and untamed.

Yinying: Reserved and noble.

Yinzhi: Crown Prince Brother said that when you don't know how to deal with strangers, you should shut your mouth, keep a straight face, and act cool.

Kangxi smiled and said, "What do you think of my three imperial sons?"

The Mongolian princes showered him with extravagant flattery while remaining dismissive in their hearts.

The eldest of these three princes hadn't even married yet; what on earth could they possibly see in them?

Still, the Emperor's face had to be given, especially since this Emperor was full of martial vigor and far more bellicose than Emperor Shunzhi. They were quite cowed.

The Mongolian princes called over their own children, having the grassland youths accompany the three princes to play.

They had already tipped off their children beforehand: they must let the three princes win, making them think they were very powerful, and not bruise their egos.

Looking at the group of dark-skinned little grassland heroes before him, Yinying exchanged a glance with Yinzhi.

Yinzhi flashed a mouthful of bright white teeth and smiled. "We aren't going to bother with all those formalities. This prince doesn't know how to do that flowery, scholarly self-introduction style of the Han people; men should make friends through martial arts. Want to wrestle?"

The little grassland heroes looked at each other in dismay.

In order to take good care of the Great Qing princes, this group tasked with reception not only knew the Han language fluently but had also memorized numerous Han poems, just waiting to have a refined and scholarly chat with the princes.

The First Prince playing completely outside the rulebook left them somewhat bewildered.

Yinying smiled with regal grace, the curve of his lips utterly perfect: "Wrestling, archery, horse racing—we can compare in any of them."

Yinzhi crossed his arms. "Not everyone is qualified to play with this lord. You also want to see whether I and my younger brothers are qualified to lead you, don't you?"

Yinzhi kept his straight face. He didn't know what to say, so he might as well just act as scenery for his older brothers.

Yinying and Yinzhi fed lines to each other—one wrapped needles in cotton, the other displayed a sharp edge—both radiating undisguised arrogance and bravado.

Young people had hot tempers and couldn't withstand provocation at all; their anger flared up instantly.

They were grassland men who grew up on horseback from childhood; could they possibly lose?

Someone muttered defensively, "If the Crown Prince and First Prince lose, don't blame us."

Yinying twisted his sleeve, put away his perfect smile, and said calmly, "My older brother, third younger brother, and I live deep within the palace. If you can't even win against us, it must mean you were deficient from birth and feeble afterward?"

The grassland noble youths: "...!!!"

Yinzhi sneered, "Since you have such confidence, let's set a stake. Imperial Father has prepared many rewards for you. Fine horses, strong bows, precious sabers, and gold and jewels are all here."

He swept his gaze around the grassland noble youths, his smile deepening. "Those who win against us can claim these rewards; the higher the ranking, the more you take. Let me see who won't even get a single reward these few days."

After finishing with his sleeves, Yinying straightened his lapels. "If your rankings turn out lower than mine and Big Brother's, then leave behind your weapons, horses, bows, and arrows as spoils of war for me and Big Brother—how about that? A competition has to have some stakes to be interesting."

The complexions of the grassland noble youths changed drastically.

They would rather offer up gold and jewels as stakes than lose the weapons they used and the horses they rode to the Crown Prince and First Prince.

Leaving behind their own weapons and horses—wasn't that just disarming and surrendering?!

"This prince and the Crown Prince are so young, yet you're actually afraid of us?" Yinzhi sneered. "Is it serious for grassland bear cubs to lose to young princes living deep in the palace and leave behind their weapons and horses as a lesson?"

Yinying gave Yinzhi a look.

Yinzhi spoke the words he had been brewing for a long time: "If you lords lack the confidence to win against Big Brother and Crown Prince Brother, you can also choose this prince to challenge."

After saying this, Yinzhi put his little face back into a straight expression.

The Third Prince, Yinzhi, was six years old this year.

The grassland noble youths cursed inwardly one after another—who on earth were they looking down on?!

"Interesting, let's play."

"That's right, those scholarly things don't suit us anyway. Just for fun, let's just play."

"A stake is a stake. Since the Crown Prince and First Prince aren't afraid of losing, of course we aren't either."

"Let's forget wrestling; we're older and have sturdier builds, it wouldn't be appropriate."

"Right, let's skip wrestling. It wouldn't do if anyone got hurt. Let's just compare archery and horse racing."

"Crown Prince, First Prince, how do you say we should compete?"

"I'll bring out my best bow and fastest horse."

"This first place, I'll claim it first." ...

Yinying and Yinzhi exchanged a "they've taken the bait" look.

Yinzhi pursed his lips. He knew that right now he only belonged to what Crown Prince Brother called the "atmosphere group." How annoying; if it were just archery, he could do it too.

But no one would compete against a six-year-old Third Prince. Even if they called over a child the same age as the Third Prince, it would just be toddlers playing around, which was boring.

The competition was thus settled.

Hearing that they would only compete in horse racing and archery, Yinying and Yinzhi set no age limits; any grassland noble youth could participate.

Though anyone could, only the sons of tribal leaders could receive the princes' rewards, and those who were too old would feel too embarrassed to come. Thus, each tribe only sent two or three youths, all around fifteen years old or younger.

"Horse racing is on me, archery is on you," Yinzhi said. "Let's show those fellows how formidable our brotherhood is."

Yinying and Yinzhi bumped fists. "Secure the top three, fight for first place."

Yinying had proposed wrestling precisely to leave some face for the Mongolian noble youths, so that no one would go home empty-handed. But since they were so confident, they couldn't blame him and Big Brother.

Kangxi held the Mulan hunting expedition precisely to display the might of the Eight Banners army and awe the Mongolian princes and nobles.

If Yinying and Yinzhi wanted to integrate into the circle of Mongolian noble youths, they also had to deflate their arrogance first; otherwise, their interactions would remain superficial.

Just as Yinying had told Yinzhi earlier, this friendship had to be fought out first before it could turn into true camaraderie.

Especially for this group of grassland men, martial prowess could sometimes win their approval much faster than power, status, or position.

"Actually, I can do it too," Yinzhi muttered.

"Leave them a bit of face," Yinying said, gently patting Yinzhi's shoulder. "If they lost to you, I'm afraid they'd die of shame and indignation."

Yinzhi was amused by Yinying and snuggled into Yinying's arms to act spoiled.

Yinzhi, who had previously looked utterly arrogant, now looked extremely nervous. "What if I come in last place? They grew up on horseback; maybe they really are better than us."

Yinying said, "Don't underestimate Imperial Father's harsh discipline toward us. How many fathers in this world do you think could harden their hearts to train their children like this?"

Not only did they have to read, recite, and copy things a hundred and twenty times when studying literature, but martial arts training was the same.

Martial arts novels said that practicing martial arts meant training through the three hottest days of summer and the three coldest days of winter, swinging sabers and swords and drawing bows to shoot arrows at least a hundred times every day.

After reading a martial arts novel, their Imperial Father slapped his thigh and thought: *Good! I'll have my sons do that too!* (×)

The playboy nobles of the grasslands were still playboy nobles; it was true that they treated horse racing, archery, and hunting as play, but play and formal training were two different things.

Otherwise, why was the Mongolian Eight Banners currently being beaten by the Manchu Eight Banners to the point where they didn't dare fight back?

The daily training volume of Kangxi's sons hadn't even been matched by veteran soldiers in the military camps.

They might lack experience when it came to battlefield killing, but in training ground competitions, they were very confident.

Even Zhao Liangdong, who had experienced numerous battles and returned to Beijing from Shanxi, had been shocked by the rigorous martial training volume of the imperial princes after being entrusted by Kangxi as their martial arts tutor.

Upon returning, Zhao Liangdong immediately increased the training volume for the noble scions at the Beijing Academy.

This time at the Mulan hunting grounds, Zhao Liangdong had also come.

Kangxi was somewhat nervous. "Qingzhi, do you think the First Prince and Crown Prince will end up in last place?"

Zhao Liangdong answered honestly, "Your Majesty might as well worry about whether the Mongolian princes will lose face if the First Prince and Crown Prince take first place every single time."

Kangxi said, "I'm not joking."

Zhao Liangdong answered honestly, "This subject isn't joking either."

Kangxi: "..."

He took a few deep breaths and asked in confusion, "My sons are that formidable? The First Prince aside, the Crown Prince has a very weak constitution."

Zhao Liangdong thought for a moment and said, "The Crown Prince's constitution can't be called weak; it can only be called strange. When the Crown Prince gets serious, as long as it's not a contest of pure strength, let alone the First Prince, even ordinary veteran soldiers are no match for him. Especially in archery—the Crown Prince is even better than this subject. But once the Crown Prince gets serious, he is bound to fall into a deep sleep for a long time afterward."

Zhao Liangdong paused and added, "It's either fainting or deep sleep. Your Majesty should also know about this."

Kangxi sighed. How could he not know about the Crown Prince's condition?

Whether studying books or practicing martial arts, whenever the Crown Prince exerted his full ability, he would always fall into a deep sleep for several days before recovering his vitality.

The imperial physicians said that was a manifestation of the Crown Prince over-consuming his vital energy, exhausting both his mental and physical strength.

Those two useless Daoist and Buddhist priests claimed that the Crown Prince's behavior was like inviting a deity to descend and possess his mortal frame—that an ordinary person's body simply couldn't bear too vast a soul's power.

The priests had even fished for information, asking him if the late Emperor had truly returned to the heavens, because these symptoms were quite similar to being possessed by the late Emperor.

After Kangxi told them that the late Emperor had indeed returned to the Eternal Sky, the priests said it was likely the late Emperor had left behind a bequest, but the Crown Prince's body simply couldn't withstand too powerful a force.

Kangxi had been so furious that he ran to the Ancestral Temple, standing with his hands behind his back glaring at his old man's spirit tablet for a long time. However, he didn't dare scold him—he just glared.

"The Crown Prince is competing with them—will something happen?" Hearing Zhao Liangdong say this, Kangxi trusted Yinying's ability, but he grew even more worried.

Zhao Liangdong said, "The Crown Prince knows his limits. Besides, to deal with that bunch, the Crown Prince doesn't need to use his true skills."

Zhao Liangdong added, "The Crown Prince would only use his true skills if he were competing in archery against ferocious generals like this subject."

Kangxi had already grown accustomed to Zhao Liangdong bragging and showing off at every turn. With Zhao Liangdong's skills, he had enough capital to boast and be proud.

Kangxi sighed. "I hope the Crown Prince doesn't tire himself out too much. If he loses, he loses—as long as he doesn't come in last place, that's fine."

Zhao Liangdong said, "Since he's already in the competition arena, for the Crown Prince to hold back and not use his full strength would be more tiring than using his full strength."

Kangxi immediately changed his tune. "The Crown Prince's health is important. If all else fails, just win first place then."

Having said that, Kangxi touched his chest, feeling exceptionally refreshed.

The Mongolian princes and nobles also learned that the Crown Prince and the First Prince were going to compete with their offspring in archery and horse racing.

Their moods and expressions were very relaxed.

Archery and horse racing? Wasn't that something you could win as long as you had hands and legs? Could princes living in the deep palace possibly surpass the eagles of the grasslands?

Despite the thinness of the blade, driven by the momentum of the galloping horse, it swept lightly past the targets, instantly slicing them in half without the horse's forward movement breaking its stride for even a second.

The Mongol princes dropped their jaws, struck completely speechless.

No way, could it be? Their grassland eaglets wouldn't actually lose, would they?

Just then, the grassland eaglets also arrived at the target-practice zone.

The leader among them took a vicious slash at a target, failed to check his momentum, and the blade slid off, glancing directly against the horse's body.

The poor steed let out a miserable whinny and bucked the grassland eaglet right off its back.

With a wave of Zhao Liangdong's hand, people immediately rushed in to carry the grassland eaglet away for medical treatment.

Kangxi's face grew dark with black lines. "Don't you people hunt frequently? How can you not even know how to use a sword on horseback?"

The Mongol princes awkwardly replied, "When we are on horseback, we mostly use bows and arrows."

Kangxi took a few deep breaths, his tone turning gentle as he inquired, "Could it be that when you ride horses, you only hunt with bows and arrows and never engage in any other training? When battle comes, do you use nothing besides bows and arrows?"

The Mongol princes: "..." What were they supposed to say? Their own offspring were so precious, how could they possibly let them go to the battlefield?

Kangxi gently advised, "Even if you can't bear to send your children to the battlefield, you still have to train their skills on horseback just in case. Overindulging a child is tantamount to destroying them. Your children... sigh..."

Yin祉 couldn't hold it in any longer. "Imperial Father, you might as well let your son go."

The Mongol princes: "..." This was getting a bit awkward.

Yin礽 thought for a moment and said with a smile, "You're still young; whether you win or lose, it would just make things awkward for them. After the older brothers finish competing, when we play privately, you can spar with them. There won't be any stakes then, just treat it as play."

Yin祉 pouted and said, "Alright, I'll listen to Crown Prince Brother."

Yin礽 asked Kangxi, "Does Imperial Father think this is acceptable?"

Kangxi nodded. "Acceptable. Bringing the Third Prince out was precisely to let him meet more people; you can arrange it as you see fit."

Yin礽 bowed from the saddle and said, "Your son obeys the decree."

Yin祉 looked at Yin礽, then looked at Kangxi, feeling a subtle sense of oddness in his heart.

Crown Prince Brother was like a completely different person; every word and action was excessively bound by rules, and his expressions and gestures toward Imperial Father were excessively humble and compliant.

Yin祉 gripped his reins tightly, feeling a faint, unexplainable wave of sadness.

He didn't know why he felt sad. Once Big Brother finished the race, he would ask him about it.

On the racecourse, the competition was nearing its end.

Yinzhi had pulled away from the others right from the start, and the gap only widened as the race went on. Looking at the rear end of Yinzhi's horse, the expressions of those trailing behind grew increasingly despairing.

They lashed their horses like madmen, desperate to run faster.

In horse racing, however, simply beating a horse harder with a whip wouldn't make it run faster.

Once frantic emotions took hold, their mistakes multiplied, and riders continuously tumbled from their saddles.

Kangxi's face turned completely black as he watched.

Everyone was a people of the horse-riding nations. After the Great Qing entered the Pass, the imperial princes all trained in the drill yards, only occasionally going to the Jingshan hunting grounds for practice.

You Mongols gallop across the grasslands every day; even if you lose, you shouldn't be losing by this much.

The Mongol Eight Banners were also troops of the Great Qing; Kangxi began to doubt the combat effectiveness of the Mongol Banners.

Yin礽, however, wasn't surprised at all.

Playing around on horseback since childhood was entirely different from a competitive sport like horse racing, just like a veteran driver who didn't know how to race cars.

From the moment they started riding, he and his brothers had run tracks just like this and experienced this exact training through blistering summers and freezing winters. How could a bunch of grassland eaglets who merely rode horses for fun ever compare to them?

Unsurprisingly, Yinzhi claimed first place.

After crossing the finish line, he reined in his horse just before the finish line, lifted his chin slightly, and looked coldly at those who had yet to reach the end—like a true eagle looking down from above on a flock of unfeathered, chirping weaklings.

When those grassland eaglets finally reached the finish line, they were greeted by Yinzhi's disdainful gaze; their dark, tanned faces lost almost all color, and they clenched their jaws tight.

Only after all the error-free grassland eaglets reached the finish line did Yinzhi turn his horse and ride away.

He didn't say a single word, leaving the group with nothing but his back. Yet, somehow, this group felt thoroughly mocked and insulted.

"A single horse race, and fully ten percent of the people got injured." Kangxi sighed. "Shall we continue tomorrow?"

Yin礽 said, "Imperial Father, let's race tomorrow instead. They look very tired, and your son doesn't want to win by taking unfair advantage."

The Mongol princes: "..." They never wanted to hear those four words—"taking unfair advantage"—ever again!

The grassland eaglets dragged themselves back in low spirits.

When one eaglet muttered that the princes merely had the advantage of being familiar with this type of racing format, his own father cracked a whip across the ground right in front of him, making him scramble and roll out of the way.

"If you lose, you lose! Don't make excuses!"

The faces of the Mongol princes and nobles turned even blacker with rage. They certainly didn't want to hear the Crown Prince ask "did you win by taking unfair advantage" a second time!!

Wasn't this humiliating enough already?!

This time, the Mongol princes had truly suffered a massive loss of face and were boiling with anger.

Watching the First Prince lead his two younger brothers to collect their horses and sabers, while the Third Prince squatted beside the injured horse letting out long sighs, they wished they could find a crack in the ground to crawl into.

The three imperial princes had brought out a massive array of rewards, yet not a single Mongol managed to win one—instead, they had ended up giving away their own horses and weapons!

Yin祉 squatted on the ground and sighed. "Sigh, what a good horse. Can it still be saved?"

Yinzhi patted Yin祉's head and said, "Leave it to Master Zhao. If it can be saved, we'll treat it; if it can't be saved, we'll turn it into horse-meat hotpot for you. Little brother, did you bring enough hotpot seasoning?"

Yinzhi directly called him "little brother," just as the other princes directly addressed each other as older or younger brother without numerical rankings attached—they all called Yin礽 by name or title appropriately.

Yin礽 said, "How could we possibly be short on hotpot seasoning? Rest assured, I definitely brought enough."

After inventing hotpot, he pulled Kangxi in as a stakeholder, using the dowry shops of Empress Xiaochengren to open a hotpot restaurant, which had now become a nest of Kangxi's intelligence agents.

When opening branch locations, Yin礽 had allowed Yinzhi and Yin祉 to buy shares, taking dividends without managing operations, as part of their admission gifts as older and younger brothers.

In the future, when the younger brothers enrolled in school, Yin礽 would also grant them shop dividends to prevent them from lacking money in the future and being led astray.

For now, Yin礽's dividends were just small change; once the Great Qing Corporation was fully up and running, the imperial princes truly wouldn't lack for money.

Changtai had already taken his navy down to the Nanyang (South Seas) to do business; Shi Lang, despite his advanced age, was experiencing a second spring in his career and had sailed off to the Dongyang (Eastern Seas).

Changtai kept Yin礽's words firmly in mind and kidnapped every skilled craftsman or physician he encountered locally, dragging them back. The divine doctor he brought back had even, by a fluke, saved Yao Qisheng's life.

Now Yao Qisheng was submitting memorials requesting retirement, saying that after retiring he wanted to go mess around with the fleet. Kangxi hadn't made up his mind yet whether to bring Yao Qisheng to Beijing to teach at the Imperial Academy or let him go play on the ships.

Zhao Liangdong patted the horse's rump, his stern face finally breaking into a rare, joyful smile. "It's a good horse; as long as its bones aren't broken, it can be saved. First Prince..."

Yinzhi waved a hand. "I know what Master Zhao wants to say. I don't need this many horses. Send all these horses to the Academy to be used as—what did little brother call it again? Oh, right, scholarships. Whoever does well on their final exams gets one. But little brother and I will go watch the matches. My horse can't be won by anyone cheating."

Yin祉 said softly, "I really want a new horse, too."

His horse was far too docile and didn't run very fast.

Yin礽 rubbed Yin祉's head and said, "We should ask Imperial Father for our horses. The horses at Imperial Father's stables are even better."

Yin祉 nodded. "Okay. Big Brother, help me pick one."

Yin礽 said, "No problem."

Kangxi strode over, laughing as he scolded, "The horses here aren't enough, and you're already eyeing Zhen's prized steeds?"

After paying his respects, Yin礽 replied, "Your son and younger brother will certainly pass Imperial Father's tests before we dare ask for Imperial Father's horses."

Yinzhi turned his head away, muttering internally that Kangxi was stingy.

Sensing that Yinzhi was grumbling about him in his heart, Kangxi was utterly gratified.

His eldest son actually knew enough to only mutter inwardly in front of outsiders instead of arguing with him face-to-face, giving him, his Imperial Father, plenty of face.

This was definitely thanks to the Crown Prince's good upbringing!

"Tomorrow is archery; they're going to have to bring out their true skills then," Kangxi said. "Baocheng, act within your abilities."

Yinzhi couldn't help himself. "Imperial Father, what do you mean by that? Wasn't my victory today achieved with their true skills?!"

Kangxi: "..." He had only just felt gratified!

Yin礽 advised, "Imperial Father is just giving the various Mongol tribes some face, pretending they didn't exert their full strength, rather than questioning Big Brother's victory. However, tomorrow they will likely dispatch genuine warriors to impersonate the princes' heirs; they won't dare to rely solely on actual noble youths anymore."

Yinzhi rolled his eyes. "Impersonate? Isn't that deceiving the Emperor?"

Yin礽 remarked, "We never specified who we were competing against to begin with."

Yinzhi sneered, "Good then, I hope they send their absolute best Mongol braves. It'll be even more fun when they lose. When it comes to archery accuracy, little brother cannot possibly lose."

Seeing how easily Yin礽 steered Yinzhi's train of thought off track with just a few words, Kangxi breathed a sigh of relief. He had truly been worried that Yinzhi's hot head and straightforward nature would cause a scene that left him with no way out.

Kangxi was starting to grow somewhat terrified of Yinzhi's simplemindedness and utter lack of tact.

"Indeed, tomorrow they will definitely dispatch true warriors," Kangxi said. "Baocheng, don't try too hard; it doesn't matter if you let them win."

Yin礽 nodded. "Your son understands."

The next day, catching sight of the few extra participants among the contestants whose builds were vastly different from the others, Yin礽 flashed a knowing smile.

Yin礽's facial features were delicate and fair, making him look like a carved figure of white jade.

The grassland eaglets sized up this Crown Prince of the Great Qing; no matter how they looked at it, this imperial crown prince did not look like someone with formidable archery skills.

The targets for the competition included stationary targets, moving targets, and targets that incorporated horse-racing elements—contestants would mount their horses and gallop toward the target zone, with a combined score calculated based on the time taken to traverse the zone and the targets hit. The rules were similar to the second half of Yinzhi's target-cutting horse race.

Yin礽 wrapped his hands in bandages, put on his thumb ring, and bent down to stretch his muscles.

At the sound of the whistle, the stationary target competition began, and Yin礽 was the first to take the field.

He drew his recurve bow, narrowing his eyes slightly.

Within his field of vision, the tiny targets seemed to enlarge bit by bit, and faint traces of arrows cutting through the air appeared to manifest in space.

These were merely illusions—hallucinations born from Yin礽 concentrating his mental focus to an extreme degree.

With a release of his fingers, a feathered arrow roared away from the bowstring, screaming through the void, and planted itself firmly right in the dead center of the bullseye.

Yin礽 drew another arrow, nocked it to the bow, and fired one after another in rapid succession.

His movements and expression were entirely effortless and relaxed, as if he weren't engaging in an activity requiring physical strength like archery, but rather reciting poetry, painting, tending to flowers and plants—dripping with absolute elegance.

Yet every single one of his arrows ruthlessly pierced the bullseye, embedding themselves deeply into the target with the shafts biting inches into the wood.

After emptying all ten arrows from his quiver, Yin礽 put away his recurve bow, unraveled the bandages wrapped around his palms at a leisurely pace, removed the thumb ring from his right thumb, and turned to leave the archery station.

The others stared in silence, involuntarily breaking out in a cold sweat without realizing it.

"Your turn."

The imperial guard reminded the next competitor.

That grassland eaglet snapped out of his daze, his lips parting and closing without being able to say a word for a long while.

He looked down at his own hands; they were actually trembling.

The grassland people excelled at riding and archery, and there were countless master archers among them. While that group of grassland noble youths wasn't particularly impressive, there were definitely absolute powerhouses on the grasslands, and they were well-accustomed to witnessing extraordinary talents.

When it came to archery accuracy, there were indeed people on the grasslands who could match Yin礽. But not a single person would ever inflict such suffocating, overwhelming pressure on them the way this Great Qing Crown Prince did.

Perhaps because the Crown Prince had gone first and hit the bullseye with all ten arrows, setting a "passing" standard that created immense psychological pressure, the second archer lost his composure entirely, missing the target completely with his very first shot.
