105. Two Chapters Combined [V]

Kangxi had the eunuchs bring three cushions for the three princes to kneel on.

The old father was very angry and had to make his sons kneel as punishment.

Consequently, Yinreng knelt obediently, Yinshi sat cross-legged obediently, and Yinzhi sat on his cushion looking around blankly, which made the old father’s liver ache with anger.

Kangxi slapped the table: "All of you, kneel properly!"

Yinreng maintained his kneeling posture and played dumb.

Yinshi asked in confusion: "Why? We didn't do anything wrong."

Only the honest child Yinzhi was startled and knelt properly.

Yinreng persuaded: "Huang-Ama, please take a look. It’s such a thick book. If you don't look at it now, it will be dark soon. Don't mind us."

Kangxi: "?"

He looked down at the quite thick "proposal plan" his son had handed over, rubbed his temples, and decided to ignore his sons, out of sight and out of mind.

Yinreng stared blankly into space; Yinshi started picking at his leg; Yinzhi, seeing that his two brothers didn't take Huang-Ama seriously, quietly moved his short legs and returned to a sitting posture on the cushion.

The group of serving eunuchs tried hard to suppress their laughter.

After a while, Yinreng felt his legs go numb from kneeling and shouted loudly: "Huang-Ama, your son needs to use the bathroom."

Yinshi immediately said: "Me too, me too."

Yinzhi, regardless of whether Kangxi could see him, nodded vigorously.

Kangxi, holding the proposal plan Yinreng had given him in one hand, waved the other hand like he was shooing away a fly: "Go."

The three princes immediately jumped up from their cushions and went to the bathroom with their arms around each other’s shoulders.

After returning, Yinreng directed his older and younger brothers to bring snacks and chairs, sat down beside Kangxi, and while eating, leaned over and asked: "Huang-Ama, aren't there any questions you want to ask your son?"

Kangxi looked at his three incredibly brazen sons and took a few deep breaths.

He kept telling himself, don't be angry, don't be angry, getting angry will ruin your health and no one will replace you, your sons were spoiled by you, they are your own flesh and blood!

"It’s well-written." Kangxi tried to calm himself down and think in imperial mode, "But although you listed many points to convince me that the risk of the mission is very low, as long as there is even a little bit of danger, you, as the Crown Prince, should not go."

Yinreng said: "Huang-Ama, it’s not that I can't go because I am the Crown Prince, but that I can't go because I am the sole heir to the throne."

The eunuchs began to tremble. Your Highness, what are you saying!

Kangxi rolled his eyes at Yinreng: "You know that, so why are you being willful?"

Yinreng said: "But Huang-Ama, although your son is the Crown Prince, I am not the only heir to the throne. To cultivate a more excellent heir to the throne with a very low level of risk—as an Emperor, you should set aside personal feelings and make a decision that is more in line with the interests of the Emperor."

Kangxi: "?"

Yinshi covered his forehead. The Crown Prince brother really dares to say anything.

Yinzhi was stunned. He felt it might be better to run to the Empress Dowager for help right now.

Kangxi slapped the table: "Yinreng!"

Yinreng rubbed Kangxi’s hand: "Huang-Ama, don't call your son by that name so loudly. Sigh, no one has called your son by that name for a long time; it sounds so unfamiliar. Big Brother, will you call me Yinreng from now on?"

Yinshi said: "No, I’ll call you Baocheng." Baocheng and Baoqing sound like brothers!

Yinreng said: "Oh, alright then. Huang-Ama, don't be angry, don't be angry. Your son is suggesting this as a Crown Prince."

Kangxi pressed hard on Yinreng’s head: "I think you want a beating!"

Yinreng shook his head vigorously against the pressure Kangxi applied: "I don't want a beating, I don't want a beating. Your son is thinking about this very seriously. While I have Huang-Ama’s protection, your son should travel more. For a ruler, reading ten thousand books is truly not as good as traveling ten thousand miles."

Yinreng tried hard to look up, trying hard to open his watery eyes wide, attempting to show his sincerity to Kangxi.

Being looked at by his son with watery eyes, Kangxi’s breathing stalled, and his tone softened involuntarily: "It’s too dangerous."

Yinreng looked up and said: "It’s not dangerous. Your son has the protection of the Great Qing Navy. How could it be dangerous to go as the Crown Prince of the Great Qing? Your son wants to travel the whole world while I still have Huang-Ama’s protection. The information collected from others lacks the reality and shock of seeing it with one's own eyes."

Yinshi looked at Yinreng’s expression, blinked thoughtfully, and also looked up, trying hard to widen his eyes: "Yes, yes, yes, Huang-Ama, little brother won't be able to go anywhere once he becomes Emperor. While Huang-Ama is still alive, hurry up and let little brother go out to play!"

Yinreng: "..." Big Brother, please shut up.

Kangxi: "..." The familiar heartache.

Yinzhi: "..." Even though I’m small, I know there’s something wrong with what Big Brother said.

Kangxi covered Yinshi’s face with his hand, not wanting to see Yinshi’s infuriatingly strange wide-eyed expression.

Although Yinshi wasn't old, Kangxi didn't think this eldest son could be associated with the word "cute." Yinshi forcing himself to look cute only made Kangxi feel nauseous.

Kangxi glared at Yinreng: "Is your real thought that as long as Ama protects you, you can do whatever you want?"

Yinreng said obediently: "It’s not exactly doing whatever I want. It’s important for a prince to broaden his horizons. The emperor of the neighboring Ross country even went to the West incognito. Your son is only going as an envoy."

After Kangxi began to value Tsarist Russia, he sent spies into the Russian capital.

The Russian nobles were very greedy, and the Russian emperor was still just an unimportant "puppet." A few porcelain vases were enough to make them easily reveal the movements of this young puppet Tsar.

Kangxi was immediately alerted when he heard that the Russian emperor had actually secretly run off to study.

To have such courage at such a young age—this young Russian emperor would surely become a major threat to the Great Qing after returning home.

The moment Kangxi learned this news, he had the thought of sending someone to assassinate the young Russian emperor. But after considering the practical situation, he regretfully found that he couldn't do it.

Once the young Russian emperor went incognito, he was like a drop of water merging into the ocean; the Great Qing could never find him.

It was precisely because of the precedent of the young Russian emperor that Kangxi did not immediately reject Yinreng’s request.

Kangxi was very conflicted in his heart. He also believed that it was important for the Crown Prince to broaden his horizons. When the Crown Prince grew up, he would certainly let him go to the south alone to help him inspect the territory.

Now that overseas matters were so important, it would be very beneficial for the Crown Prince to see the overseas world with his own eyes.

But Kangxi couldn't bear it.

When the Crown Prince inspected the Great Qing territory, no matter where he went, the post horses would gallop, and he and the Crown Prince could communicate every day or two.

If he went overseas, he wouldn't be able to wait for a letter from the Crown Prince for ten days or half a month.

Even if the Great Qing Navy was strong, other countries wouldn't attack a ship with the Great Qing Crown Prince on board as long as they didn't want to declare war on the Great Qing. But what if the Crown Prince couldn't adapt to the climate?

The Crown Prince was still so young; how could he rest assured letting him leave the country?

Kangxi said: "Baocheng, you are still young. If you really want to go, you should wait until after you come of age."

Yinreng thought. By the time he came of age, in history, that was when his relationship with Kangxi gradually deteriorated. He wasn't sure if Kangxi would still dote on him and let him go into the army alone.

It was better to finish unreasonable things before coming of age.

Yinreng said: "Huang-Ama, for the Crown Prince to go abroad, if we don't find a good opportunity, it might cause concern in other countries. Now that the French Emperor has written a letter in his own hand inviting us, it is only logical for your son to go to the West."

Kangxi sighed. The logic was sound, but he was truly worried.

"With me accompanying the Crown Prince brother, what is Huang-Ama afraid of?" Yinshi was getting impatient. Why was Huang-Ama so long-winded? Even his mother wasn't this long-winded.

Kangxi rolled his eyes at Yinshi: "With you there, I’m even more afraid."

Yinshi patted his chest and said: "Then from now on, don't be afraid!"

Kangxi: "?"

He discovered that he still couldn't understand his eldest son’s thought process.

Yinreng said: "Your son and Big Brother traveling together, looking after each other, Huang-Ama can really rest assured. The first cooperation with France signifies that the Great Qing is officially stepping onto the world stage. To be honest, your son doesn't feel at ease handing this matter over to others."

Kangxi frowned: "You don't feel at ease handing it over to Changtai either?"

Yinreng nodded: "Actually, Huang-Ama doesn't feel at ease either, right? If it weren't for the fact that an Emperor cannot leave the territory of the Great Qing, Huang-Ama would want to go personally."

Kangxi’s thoughts were guessed correctly by Yinreng.

He rubbed Yinreng’s hair: "Such a heavy responsibility, you are still young, Ama cannot bear it."

Yinreng said: "Your son still has Big Brother. Brothers are like tigers; with Big Brother there, your son is not afraid at all."

Yinshi patted his chest again: "Leave it to me!"

Kangxi hit Yinshi on the head: "Calling yourself 'Ye' (Master) in front of Ama?"

Yinshi: "...Leave it to your son. It was just a slip of the tongue. Huang-Ama, don't be so petty."

Kangxi took a deep breath. Forget it, forget it, this son is already like this, it can't be changed, you have to get used to it. Look at Concubine Hui, she is very calm now.

Last time when I talked to Concubine Hui about the eldest prince, the smile on her lips didn't move, and her eyes were calm and waveless; she was truly very calm.

Kangxi said: "If you are to go as an envoy, it should be after the Dutch War is successful. I will consider it again."

Yinreng stopped while he was ahead and, like a sycophant, massaged Kangxi’s arms: "Alright, your son won't bother Huang-Ama anymore. Huang-Ama, do you want to go pay respects to the Empress Dowager together?"

Yinshi drooled: "Horqin sent many little lambs, and the Empress Dowager said she would slaughter a few to make hot pot tonight!"

Kangxi was helpless: "The lingering heat of the autumn tiger hasn't passed yet, and you want to eat hot pot?"

Yinshi said: "Huang-Ama doesn't want to eat?"

Kangxi pinched Yinshi’s face: "Go, why wouldn't I go?"

Yinshi impatiently swatted away Kangxi’s hand: "Huang-Ama, go pinch little brother’s face."

Kangxi, who was disliked by Yinshi, actually went to pinch Yinreng’s face.

Yinreng gave a habitual, obedient smile.

Kangxi prepared to pinch Yinzhi’s face again, but Yinzhi immediately hid behind Yinreng, poked out half his little head, and stared at Kangxi vigilantly.

Kangxi: "...Except for Baocheng, everyone dislikes me."

Yinreng immediately said: "Huang-Ama is overthinking it; older and younger brothers just don't like having their faces pinched."

Yinshi: "Doesn't Huang-Ama want to reflect on himself?"

Yinzhi nodded, not knowing whose point of view to agree with.

Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng quickly said: "Big Brother, Third Brother, run!"

After saying that, Yinreng hugged Kangxi’s waist.

Yinshi scooped up Yinzhi and ran, shouting as he ran: "Huang-Ama! Your sons will wait for you at the Empress Dowager’s palace!"

Kangxi was amused: "You three... Baocheng! Let go! What kind of decorum is this!"

Yinreng only let go and played dumb with a smile after his brothers had run far away.

Kangxi looked at Yinreng’s silly smile and was extremely helpless: "You, the eldest and third princes are becoming less and less afraid of me; it’s all your fault."

Yinreng smiled and took the initiative to hold Kangxi’s hand and swing it: "Isn't it good that Big Brother and Third Brother aren't afraid of Huang-Ama? We are a family. No matter how others speculate about the royal family, we are just an ordinary big family, ordinary relatives."

Kangxi said: "Then why have you started calling me Huang-Ama now, instead of calling me Ama in private like before?"

Yinreng said: "I’ve grown up, it’s better to be more sociable, otherwise the people impeaching me will annoy me to death. But when writing letters, how about I call you 'Dad', Huang-Ama? Hehe."

Kangxi was helpless: "As you wish."

He knew that every word and action of the Crown Prince was being watched by the court officials, and the slightest disturbance would lead to countless impeachments; the matter of address was the same.

Kangxi threw all these impeachments directly into the wastepaper basket, "keeping them in the palace without issuing them," but his precious son, as always, would rather wrong himself than let his father worry.

Outside, the Crown Prince’s etiquette was always upright and perfect. Only when he was alone with him would Yinreng reveal the "overbearing" and "impolite" side of a spoiled precious son.

With no other sons around, Kangxi spoke his true feelings: "Do you really want to go abroad?"

Yinreng said: "Yes. While Huang-Ama is your son’s backing, your son wants to do more of what I like. The world is so big, your son wants to go see it."

Kangxi sighed: "Yes, you certainly want to; who wouldn't. If your Imperial Grandfather were still alive, I would want to too."

Yinreng said: "Imperial Grandfather always kept in mind the matter of letting the Great Qing step onto the world stage. Does Huang-Ama want to go pay respects to Imperial Grandfather and complain a bit? Hmm, Huang-Ama is so hardworking, it’s all Imperial Grandfather’s fault. If Imperial Grandfather hadn't caught smallpox, at Huang-Ama’s age, you would be exactly at the time to show your talents overseas."

Yinreng clenched his little fist with the hand not holding Kangxi’s and waved it twice: "With Huang-Ama’s martial prowess, you would definitely be better than Big Brother and me. Huang-Ama is so powerful, even if you went on a personal expedition, you couldn't go to the front lines to be a real great general; it’s such a pity."

Kangxi sighed again: "Yes, no place to use my skills."

Yinreng smiled: "I will realize your dreams for you, Huang-Ama! Whether it’s traveling everywhere to see things, or being a great general, hehe."

Kangxi said amusedly: "You."

Yinreng patted his chest: "Everything Huang-Ama wants to do but cannot do, leave it to me!"

Kangxi’s large hand gripped Yinreng’s small hand, his tone helpless and extremely doting: "I just dote on you too much. Alright, you exercise well, don't get seasick when the time comes. You must also learn to swim. And medical skills, you must understand some yourself. It is better to rely on yourself than others..."

Kangxi rambled on, just as Yinshi said, more long-winded than the concubines in the palace who had children.

Yinreng himself hadn't expected that Kangxi would agree to his request so easily.

Recalling his conversation with Kangxi, Yinreng guessed that it was the phrase "I will realize your dreams for you, Huang-Ama" that moved Kangxi.

Kangxi’s nature was restless, stubborn, and reckless, and he loved new things.

If the kind of Shunzhi that Yinreng fabricated existed and was alive, Kangxi would certainly have been like Peter the Great next door, packing his bags and running off to travel the world incognito.

But Kangxi was now the Emperor, and he couldn't do anything.

Just like how Kangxi used to give Yinreng the life of a Crown Prince he imagined, regardless of whether Yinreng needed it or not. Now Kangxi also handed over his dream of traveling the world to the little Crown Prince he raised.

Later generations say that raising a child is like raising an alt account, like playing a second life, where you want your child to realize the things you wanted to do but didn't.

Kangxi was currently the same.

Yinreng held his heart, feeling warm inside.

The current father and brothers were the treasures he dreamed of. So no matter how much he had to rack his brains, he had to protect the status quo and maintain their feelings.

It is not interaction without thought or based on temperament that is called sincere affection. Affection needs to be managed and carefully nurtured.

Kangxi, as an emperor who lost his parents early, didn't understand; his brothers were still young and didn't understand either.

Yinreng understood this principle. So he would take on this responsibility and enjoy it.

Changtai soon learned that if they could win this war, the Crown Prince and the Eldest Prince would visit France with the Great Qing Navy to sign an agreement with the French Emperor.

Changtai first thought it was too dangerous and wanted to ask Kangxi to think twice.

But when he started writing the memorial, he suddenly felt that this was quite good.

His nephew, the Crown Prince, had always lived with the Emperor, trembling with fear and walking on thin ice, not having a single moment to relax.

When visiting overseas, his nephew, the Crown Prince, would be free. He could dote on his nephew as much as he wanted, and whatever his nephew wanted to do, as long as it didn't affect his health, it was all fine.

Thinking of the days of relaxing with the Crown Prince, a gentle smile couldn't help but appear on Changtai’s face.

He ground the ink, picked up the brush, and rewrote the memorial.

In his memorial, Changtai first expressed his concerns about the Crown Prince traveling far away, then wrote that he trusted the Emperor’s judgment and supported the idea of tempering the Crown Prince, pledging his life and family’s honor that he would protect the Crown Prince and put the Emperor’s mind at ease.

After Kangxi revealed his intentions to his high-ranking officials, even those who stood in opposition to the Crown Prince strongly objected.

The opposing officials argued, firstly, that overseas lands were mere specks of dust and the Qing Dynasty should not lower its status by sending the Crown Prince on a diplomatic mission; secondly, they feared that if the mission succeeded, the Crown Prince’s position would become even more unassailable.

Once Kangxi had made up his mind, it mattered not who opposed him.

When it came to matters like suppressing the Three Feudatories, annexing Taiwan, or building the navy, there were very few in the court who agreed with Kangxi, yet he had gritted his teeth and seen them through.

It was the same now.

He merely felt, on occasion, the loneliness of being at the top.

It was only when Changtai’s memorial arrived that Kangxi finally smiled.

Compared to those who offered empty platitudes without understanding why Kangxi would do such a thing, Changtai’s memorial spoke directly to the Emperor’s heart.

Changtai had written down all the things Kangxi was worried about—disease, exhaustion, pirates—each one a very real possibility.

Kangxi could tell that Changtai was sincerely worried about the Crown Prince and had considered every eventuality.

Yet, Changtai supported him.

Once a beast of prey reaches a certain age, it must be driven out to hunt for itself.

The world stage is currently in turmoil; the Qing Crown Prince must feel the terror of the storm in advance and prepare himself mentally to lead this country through it.

Therefore, while the Emperor is still young, strong, and capable of controlling the domestic situation, the Crown Prince must go out and venture forth.

Just as when a young beast returns hungry and listless, the parents can toss it enough food to fill its belly, giving it the strength for the next hunt.

Kangxi closed the memorial and shut his eyes.

He imagined: if Shunzhi were still alive, could he have done as he pleased, just like the Crown Prince?

Perhaps it would have been more difficult, as Shunzhi had too few sons.

A cruel truth behind Yinreng’s request was that even if Kangxi were to lose two sons, he still had several others; the Aisin Gioro throne would remain unshaken.

Kangxi sighed softly.

He asked, "Where is the Crown Prince?"

Zhao Chang emerged from the shadows and said, "His Highness the Crown Prince is gathering the young princes together to watch them practice Boku."

Kangxi’s melancholy faded, and he looked up sharply, disbelievingly: "The young princes? Boku?"

Zhao Chang bowed his head and said, "His Highness has placed the Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Princes on the floor covered with thick blankets and is making them wrestle; whoever wins gets a pastry."

Kangxi took a deep breath, then another, and asked again, "Boku?"

Zhao Chang nodded: "Yes."

Kangxi rubbed his temples, stood up, and said, "Take me to see."

In Cining Palace, Consort Hui and Consort Rong were paying their respects to the Empress Dowager with the young princes they were raising when they ran into the other princes who had come to play with the Fifth Prince.

The Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Princes were already able to walk, but the Eighth was very young, and the Sixth and Seventh were physically frail, so they had never played with the other princes before.

Since they had bumped into each other today, Yinreng happily invited his younger brothers to play together.

As they played, somehow or other, it turned into a game of Boku.

Boku is the Manchu word for wrestling. Yinzhi wrestled Yinreng first; each won a round, and in the third, they both tumbled out of bounds. Yinzhi faced his younger brothers Yinzhen and Yinqi; although he was strong, his two younger brothers narrowly defeated him.

What remained was a chaotic brawl between the three younger brothers who had never learned Boku.

Yinreng cheered: "Go on! That's it! Little Eight, pull his pants!"

Yinzhi clapped: "Little Seven, bite them! Bite hard!"

Yinzhi jumped in anxiety: "Little Six! Don't be a coward! Pounce on him! If all else fails, go down together!"

Little Yinzhen said a mouthful of words, but he spoke too fast for anyone to understand.

Little Yinqi clenched his small fists, his face flushed red, too excited to say a word.

Kangxi stood outside the window, lowering his voice as he said to the Empress Dowager and the Empress Mother, "Imperial Grandmother, Imperial Mother, you two are just watching this?!"

The Empress Dowager laughed: "The little princes are having so much fun, isn't that good?"

Kangxi stood with his hands behind his back, rolling his eyes hard.

Who says he coddles his children?! Look at the Empress Dowager!!

106. Third and Fourth Update (Extra Update for Landmine) [V]

Kangxi watched from outside the window for as long as the young princes played.

He saw his three young sons acting like wolf cubs, refusing to admit defeat, their clothes in a miserable state by the end, and he couldn't help but close his eyes.

It was a good thing for children to have this kind of grit.

It was a good thing, right?

Yinreng smiled as he hugged his brothers one by one, kissed their little faces, straightened their clothes, and fed them pastries.

The brothers sat obediently around Yinreng, nibbling on their pastries while looking up with wide, blank eyes at this legendary Crown Prince brother.

Although they were still young, Consort Rong and Consort Hui constantly instilled in them that when they were healthier and older, their Crown Prince brother would take them out to play.

"The Crown Prince brother has so many delicious things and fun toys."

"The Crown Prince brother will play the zither for you and tell you stories."

"When you start your lessons, the Crown Prince brother will make toys that belong only to you."

"Eat well, take your medicine, grow up big and strong, and then the Crown Prince brother will come to take you out to play."

After Yinreng returned to the palace, he would visit them every day, smiling as he told them stories and gave them brightly colored picture books.

After Yinreng left the palace, the Fourth and Fifth Princes would come to see them, reading picture books with them while complaining about why the Crown Prince brother hadn't returned yet.

Thus, even though the three young princes hadn't spent much time with Yinreng, they already admired this supposedly omnipotent brother deeply.

This time, they finally had the chance to show off in front of him.

Crown Prince brother! I'm very strong! Take me to play!

Yinreng picked up his three brothers one by one to gauge their weight and said, "From now on, when I finish my lessons, I'll take you all to play."

Little Six, Little Seven, and Little Eight all raised their pastries and cheered.

Yinzhi frowned and said, "They're so small, how can they play with us? I don't want to babysit."

Why are there more and more kids snatching up my brothers? Father, can you stop having more? You just keep having them because you have brothers to help raise them? You just produce them and don't raise them, letting your brothers do the work, right?

This father only knows how to exploit his sons!

Little Six, Little Seven, and Little Eight stiffened, looking at the other brother in disbelief, tears welling up in their eyes.

"We can play together without necessarily doing the same thing," Yinreng quickly hugged his brothers to soothe them. "We can be together and break into groups to play different things, just like how we attend the same school but read different books. By the way, tomorrow I'll take you to meet your sisters. Be sweet, and let them take you horseback riding."

Little Six, Little Seven, and Little Eight nodded quickly, then glared fiercely at the eldest brother who didn't want to play with them.

Even if he was a child, Yinzhi wouldn't admit defeat. He glared back, making the three little princes shiver and dive into Yinreng's arms.

Yinreng laughed: "Eldest brother, don't be like that. What if the little ones get scared of you?"

Yinzhi crossed his arms and said, "I want them to be scared of me. You coddle them so much; if I'm not strict, they'll take advantage of your pampering and tear the roof down. Who else will keep them in line?"

Yinreng smiled: "Let Father handle it."

Kangxi pushed the door open with a dark face: "I can't handle it!"

Yinreng smiled and patted his brothers, who were frightened silly: "Quick, pay your respects to Father."

The three little dumplings rolled into a ball, calling out their respects to Kangxi while already prostrate on the floor.

Kangxi was amused by his three youngest sons, whom he had neglected for so long: "Is this the etiquette your mothers taught you?"

The three little dumplings trembled on the floor, on the verge of tears.

Apparently, when Consort Rong and Consort Hui taught them, whenever they were disobedient, besides saying "The Crown Prince brother won't take you to play," they also said, "Father will spank your bottoms and lock you in confinement."

Yinreng quickly shielded his three brothers: "They don't see Father often, so they're just too excited and nervous. Come, calm down. Little Six, Little Seven, Little Eight, let Father see what you've learned."

Under Yinreng's patient soothing, the three little dumplings climbed up and performed the salute again, trembling. This time, aside from the shaking, the movements were quite standard.

Yinreng praised: "My brothers are amazing! Right, Father?"

Kangxi kept a straight face: "It's just a salute, what's so amazing about that? When you were this age..."

Yinreng quickly interrupted: "When I was this age, I was still using Father's sleeve to wipe my mouth."

Kangxi: "..."

Yinzhi thought for a moment and said, "When I was this age, I don't think I knew anything either?"

Yinzhi said, "I don't remember. But Mother said I was very frail, probably couldn't even get up to salute Father."

Little Yinzhen: "I don't remember. Little Five, how about you?"

Little Yinqi said honestly: "I couldn't talk yet."

Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng patted his three brothers' heads: "Father, don't struggle. The Little Yinzuo, Little Yinyou, and Little Yinsi in front of you are already your three most worry-free sons."

The Empress Dowager laughed out loud in the back.

The Empress, who had learned some Chinese and understood what Yinreng said, also covered her mouth.

Yinzhi chimed in: "Be proud, Father!"

Kangxi: "...Baocheng, Baoqing, you two shut up."

Yinreng and Yinzhi exchanged a look and shrugged simultaneously.

Yinzhi, for some reason, blurted out without thinking: "Father, are you embarrassed into anger?"

Kangxi took a deep breath: "Third Prince, it seems I should separate you from the First Prince!"

Yinzhi quickly hid behind Yinreng, poking his little head out to watch Kangxi warily.

The Empress Dowager laughed: "Emperor, stop bullying your sons. Weren't you watching them happily just now?"

Yinzhi gave Kangxi a look that said, "So you are that kind of father," making Kangxi's chest ache again.

He wanted his eldest son to move out of the palace and establish his own household immediately. If he lived with his eldest son any longer, he felt he would lose years of his life.

Why are there such infuriating sons?!

Seeing that Kangxi was about to explode, Yinreng quietly kicked Yinzhi.

Yinzhi quickly said, "Father was just teasing us. I knew Father loves us the most! Father, please sit!"

Yinzhi pulled out a chair, Yinzhi placed a cushion, and the little Fourth and Fifth princes moved their short legs to serve tea and water.

Yinreng held Kangxi's hand and said obediently, "Father, please sit."

Kangxi, suddenly being fawned over by his sons, sighed deeply: "You, you just know how to protect them."

Yinreng smiled: "It's not that I'm protecting my brothers, it's that Father loves them and is just playing with them. Everyone knows Father loves his children and is the most benevolent father."

Yinzhi nodded vigorously: "That's right, that's right."

Kangxi glared at Yinzhi: "You know that too! If I didn't coddle you, you would have been locked in confinement long ago!"

Yinzhi rubbed his nose: "I know." He knew that if it weren't for the Crown Prince brother smoothing things over every time, he would have been beaten long ago.

Although he had been beaten a few times already.

After Kangxi drank the tea offered by his sons, he had them stand in a row and began to test their lessons, not even sparing the little ones who had only recently learned to talk.

In the feudal era, when fathers and sons interacted, it was mostly to test their studies.

Kangxi was very strict with his sons. He only smiled and nodded when satisfied, and emphasized heavily when he wasn't, and the three little princes were no exception.

Even someone as perfect as Yinreng only received a "passable" from Kangxi.

A look of impatience appeared in Yinzhi's eyes. It was always like this. Even when his brother did perfectly, Father wouldn't praise him properly, at most saying, "As expected of the Crown Prince."

Yinreng noticed that his brothers were a bit disappointed and said, "Father, we've performed so well, don't we get a reward?"

Kangxi said with a dark face: "What was so good about it!"

Yinreng said: "Everything was good. Look at me, I didn't make any mistakes in my lessons; Eldest brother barely made any either; Third brother has improved a lot; Fourth and Fifth are learning very fast; Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth are speaking fluently and know some allusions from the 'Three Character Classic.' It wouldn't be right not to give some rewards to such excellent sons."

Yinreng spread his hands: "Don't dampen our enthusiasm for learning. Only rewards provide motivation!"

Kangxi was helpless: "Learning is for your own good, and you're asking your father for rewards?"

Yinreng said: "We're still children, learning is so hard and boring; without Father's encouragement and rewards, we can't keep it up."

Kangxi stood up, walked to Yinreng, and patted his small outstretched palm: "Go, go, you only know how to covet the things in your father's storehouse. Take them and pick one item each."

Yinreng smiled: "Alright, Father is the best!"

He winked at Yinzhi. Yinzhi immediately said, "Father is the best! Thank you for the reward!"

The little princes also shouted in unison: "Father is the best, thank you for the reward!"

Hearing his sons all shouting "Father is the best," Kangxi smiled until wrinkles appeared at the corners of his eyes.

The Empress Dowager laughed: "Good, the princes have all done very well, I have rewards too. Baocheng, Baoqing, you two take your brothers to my storehouse and pick whatever you want."

The Empress also said: "Pick from my storehouse too."

Yinreng smiled and led his brothers to thank the Empress Dowager and the Empress, then continued to play with his brothers in a very relaxed manner.

The little princes were a bit reserved at first, but the toys Yinreng brought out were so interesting that they soon became immersed in them, forgetting they were being watched by Kangxi, the Empress Dowager, and the Empress.

Yinreng sidled up to Kangxi and smiled: "Aren't my brothers cute?"

Kangxi patted his precious son's head: "You, you like all your brothers and sisters, don't you?"

Yinreng said seriously: "No, I like my brothers too."

Yinzhi, who was playing cards with Yinzhi while eavesdropping, wore a triumphant smile.

Kangxi sighed: "Do you call that liking? That's you colluding with him!"

Yinreng held Kangxi's hands with both of his, his expression even more serious: "Father, don't say that. I won't allow you to scold yourself!"

Kangxi: "?"

The Empress Dowager and the Empress were stunned for a moment, then burst into laughter, nearly dropping their prayer beads.

Yinzhi and Yinzhi, who understood, also bit their lips to keep from laughing.

Kangxi gritted his teeth: "Baocheng, is your quick wit only used for bickering with your father?"

Yinreng hugged Kangxi's arm: "That's right, besides me, who else bickers with Father?"

Kangxi kept a straight face: "Your uncle."

Yinreng said: "Honestly, Uncle definitely has no intention of bickering with Father. He doesn't have that awareness."

Kangxi thought of Changtai's serious, innocent expression and rubbed his temples: "I sometimes wonder if he is your uncle or the First Prince's uncle."

Yinreng suppressed a laugh: "Some people are just born alike, nothing to be done."

Yinzhi turned around and chimed in: "Uncle Changtai really gets along with me, I love him so much."

Yinzhi nodded silently in his heart.

Compared to their own biological uncle who always smiled with such sycophancy and malice every time they met, Uncle Changtai was better.

Uncle Changtai never asked anything of them, only took them to play, taught them martial arts, and was especially patient in telling them stories about overseas lands.

Who could refuse an uncle who was handsome, patient, gentle, skilled in both literature and martial arts, and full of fresh stories?

Kangxi sighed: "Tell me, once Changtai takes you overseas for a few months, will the First Prince's personality get even worse?"

Yinzhi frowned. Talking bad about him to his face, Father is truly a big villain.

Yinreng shook his head: "Eldest brother has his own opinions; his personality is his own and won't be influenced by others. Father is overthinking it."

Yinzhi smiled triumphantly: "Father, that's right, I am who I am!"

Yinreng thought to himself, yes, the eldest brother is the eldest brother; in both lives, he is a unique firework.

Kangxi suddenly realized why Consort Hui had that dull, lifeless smile.

His own eyes were now lifeless too.

Yes, the First Prince is the First Prince; he is himself, no one can change him, not even I.

The First Prince's life is set. Better to have him move out of the palace early and have some peace.

I must find a wife for the First Prince and drive him out of the palace as soon as possible.

Choosing wives for the princes is a laborious task. Kangxi and the Empress Dowager first determine a list, then observe for several years before making a final choice.

Once determined, the future imperial princesses have no official status but stay obediently at home and do not participate in the draft; the royal family continues to observe them until the prince moves out of the palace.

During this time, they prepare for marriage at home, waiting for the prince to turn fifteen.

When the prince turns fifteen, the Imperial Clan Court petitions for a marriage. The Emperor designates the bride, the prince's father-in-law thanks the Emperor for his grace, and the Imperial Board of Astronomy sets the dates for the betrothal and wedding; only then is the marriage finalized.

If their virtue or conduct is found lacking before this, the royal family will immediately replace them. Unlike marrying others, where a betrothal ceremony provides security, here, the engagement is not easily broken.

In three years, Kangxi could "sweep" the First Prince Yinzhi out of the palace; it was time to look for a primary consort.

Kangxi worried that if he looked for a consort for Yinzhi first, Yinreng would be unhappy, so he asked Yinreng: "Do you want me to assign you two palace maids to accompany you to the Eastern Palace? Next year, you'll be moving into the Eastern Palace; you should have someone to warm your bed."

Yinreng said expressionlessly: "Father, are you dissatisfied with my health?"

Kangxi: "Huh?"

Yinreng said: "Have you forgotten that I have a deficiency in vital energy?"

Kangxi pondered: "Is, is that so?"

Yinreng sighed: "Father, you've hurt my feelings."

Kangxi quickly sought out the imperial physicians to ask.

The physician was speechless: "Your Majesty, although His Highness the Crown Prince no longer falls into comas often, it is still better not to indulge in women too early."

Kangxi argued: "...One or two palace maids is not called indulging in women."

Yinreng added: "Father, why not ask Daoist Zhang and Master Dehai?"

Kangxi remembered those two monks/priests who, while not very useful, had slightly better judgment than other religious figures, and called them into the palace.

Master Dehai sighed: "This... alas, Your Majesty, His Highness the Crown Prince has experienced ancestral possession and should cultivate his body by locking his essence. If it weren't for the fact that the Crown Prince is the heir to the country, actually..."

Daoist Zhang also said: "Actually... alas."

Yinreng knew the practitioners' rhetoric: "Actually, maintaining a virgin body is best, right? I think so too... ouch."

Kangxi gritted his teeth: "You are the Crown Prince! You cannot have no heirs!"

Yinreng said: "Father just wants me to have heirs. When I grow up, Father can choose a Crown Princess for me, and I can have children with her. Once I have children, it won't matter if I don't get close to other women, right?"

Yinreng couldn't handle having multiple wives and concubines; he was afraid his mother from the second life would chase him in his dreams.

Come to think of it, in his first life, he only had the Crown Prince's obsessive memory fragments, and these fragments contained absolutely no trace of women or children; he couldn't even remember the face of his previous life's Crown Princess.

He remembered even the court officials, yet he couldn't remember his bedfellows or heirs.

Perhaps it was because women and children were not the reason the Crown Prince was unwilling to let go even after two lifetimes.

Men of the feudal era, alas.

Yinreng felt a small sense of contempt for his first-life self.

But now! Yinreng puffed out his chest! I am a good youth born under the red flag and raised in New China! I firmly refuse to have multiple wives and concubines!

Kangxi frowned: "That would be treating you too unfairly."

Yinreng was extremely speechless: "Father, not everyone likes women. There are plenty of emperors and crown princes in history who didn't prioritize women. Isn't it good not to prioritize women? This is clearly a virtue worth praising."

Kangxi said: "Fine, I will choose a healthy Crown Princess for you. If the Crown Princess cannot bear children, then I will assign you concubines."

Yinreng couldn't control his own marriage or change Kangxi's thinking; being able to get Kangxi to agree to his willful idea of not having trial-marriage maids and giving the Crown Princess a few years was already good enough.

Yinreng said: "Father, I have two requirements for the Crown Princess."

Kangxi teased: "So you do have requirements for the Crown Princess; I thought you were completely uninterested in women."

Yinreng was speechless: "Father... forget it, think what you want. My first requirement is that the Crown Princess cannot be younger than me; at least she must be the same age. I don't have the patience to coax people."

Although Yinreng had no memory fragments of the women and children in his palace, he had the memories of his second life researching the history of the Qing Dynasty, so he knew he wouldn't marry until he was twenty.

只要太子妃和自己同龄或者比自己大，那么太子妃也是二十岁结婚，结婚年龄刚好。
康熙叹气：“你啊。你不耐烦哄女人？你的耐心都给哥哥弟弟了吗？”
胤礽做足了渣男的嘴脸：“是啊。”
康熙伸出手指，点了点胤礽的鼻子：“行。朕怎么会让你哄人？当然是太子妃照顾你。还有什么要求？”
胤礽道：“第二个要求，儿子要一个家中弟兄少、家族势力弱的太子妃。”
康熙皱眉：“为何？”
胤礽看了一眼面前已经满脸都是汗的僧道二人。
康熙也才意识到这还有两个外人，挥手让他们走。
胤礽在僧道二人离开前，给了两人赏赐，又给了他们寺庙赏赐。
德海大师和张道长回到香山之后，窃窃私语。还是太子好！你看那清朝的皇帝什么德性啊！居然要给这么小的孩子宫女！这什么家风！还好太子行为端正！
僧道二人离开后，胤礽道：“汗阿玛，儿子纵观史书，在王朝初期，皇后家世多强大；王朝稳固之后，皇后家世都会变弱。”
康熙想了想，的确是这么一回事。
胤礽道：“阿玛给儿子选一个自己家世不错、家中后院干净的太子妃，太子妃的教养肯定不错；太子妃没有太多兄弟、堂兄弟，族人也不强势，她就不会老念着娘家，只对儿子好。”
胤礽其实只是存了能不能在封建时代谈个恋爱的奢望。
他知道古代贵族女子的思想和现代人完全不同，嫁进皇家的女子更是如此。
贵族女子从小便被教导，出嫁是为了给娘家和娘家兄弟争夺利益。丈夫、孩子，都是清醒的贵族夫人为自己和娘家夺取利益的工具。
家丁不兴旺、甚至没有胞弟的太子妃，或许会沉下心和他谈恋爱吧。
胤礽只是这么奢望。奢望就是希望渺茫。
两人三观不同，他又藏着那么多秘密，和太子妃还是盲婚哑嫁，怎么可能和太子妃从夫妻变成爱人。
康熙沉默了许久，把胤礽揽怀里，揉了揉胤礽的头发：“你是……你是被佟家吓到了吧？”
胤礽愣了一下。
康熙当胤礽的沉默是承认，叹了许久的气。
父子俩依偎着彼此，就像是这天地间只有他们俩可以互相信任彼此。
“朕明白了。你是太子，太子继位不需要太子妃娘家的支持，太子妃娘家太强大反而让外戚尾大不掉。”康熙道，“朕给你选一个家族底蕴好、家庭和睦、家丁不兴旺的太子妃。”
胤礽笑道：“好！对了，还有好看！”
康熙板着脸道：“这是第三个要求了。”
胤礽道：“太子妃可是一国之母，怎么能不好看？不会吧不会吧，这还要儿子自己提要求吗？”
康熙板着脸道：“太子妃面貌端正就好，太好看被人说你重女色怎么办？”
胤礽道：“儿子就一个太子妃！怎么会叫重女色！而且我额娘可好看了！汗阿玛您说这话您自己不脸红吗！”
康熙回忆仁孝皇后。咳，没错，仁孝皇后很漂亮。
胤礽仰着头扯着嗓子：“老爹！！！儿子要漂亮媳妇！！！”
康熙哭笑不得：“闭嘴！害不害臊！”
胤礽道：“那您问问大哥，你给他指个不漂亮的媳妇！”
康熙还真叫来胤禔。
胤禔用看傻子的眼神看着康熙：“汗阿玛，您要不叫御医看看？”
康熙：“……”
他微笑：“朕决定了，朕一定要给你指一个丑陋的大福晋！”
胤礽和胤禔异口同声：“汗阿玛您三思啊！！！！”

惠妃端坐在椅子上，嘴角微笑就像是画上去的一样，双眼已经失去了光彩。
豆蔻年华的小姑娘们，素颜就是最好的打扮。

笑容贼甜……

翠色衣衫姑娘看上去年岁尚小，比起周围已经十三四岁已经略微长开的姑娘们，只能说可爱，算不上漂亮。

自家大哥现在笑得好傻，傻得让人不忍直视。
胤礽又看向康熙，康熙也在笑，笑得很慈祥：“这小孩长得很有福气。”
胤礽不懂康熙的福气评价是什么，但她也得到康熙认可了吧。
“那就她了？”胤礽道，“我看也觉得很适合大哥。”
盲婚哑嫁，若有一方稍稍动了一点感情，哪怕是见色起意，也会让婚姻生活好过一些。
康熙立刻遣人去问。
太监回报，那人姓伊尔根觉罗氏，父亲名为科尔坤。

康熙：“？”
他正要撸袖子揍儿子的时候，进来通报的太监拯救了即将挨打的胤礽。
太监报，汉军正白旗副都统石文炳已到，在乾清宫外候着等召见。
康熙赶紧整理衣衫，坐回椅子上，瞪了胤礽一眼：“老实点！”
胤礽乖乖站到康熙身边一侧：“老实，我可老实。”
石文炳……原本太子妃她爹？
石文炳，汉军正白旗人。
所有皇子的福晋，要么是满洲上三旗，要么是与蒙古联姻。独独太子妃的出身为汉军旗，即使她祖上为满人，这个身份也特别格格不入。
这也是胤礽在满洲勋贵中孤立无援的原因之一。
胤礽突然感到太阳穴针扎似的疼。
他眼前，跟走马灯似的闪过一些破碎的画面。
伴随着这些破碎画面的，还有强烈的愤怒、伤心、悲伤和失落。
“您做这些事之前不能和妾商量吗！”

“妾从来没有出卖过太子殿下！殿下不要污蔑妾！”
“我知道。你只是一个完美的儿媳妇，只是明哲保身，只是要保住你们石家，不可能与我同进退。”
“我已经不是太子殿下，但你还是太子妃。”
胤礽晕倒前，仿佛看到了一个面容臃肿的可怜男子，正在强忍着眼泪。
石文炳于康熙三十三年病逝。
大清皇太子胤礽与太子妃石氏于康熙三十四年成婚。
太子妃石氏守孝三年后，即使期间只育有一女，胤礽也独宠其八年。
直到康熙四十二年，索额图被宗人府拘禁，被康熙赐死。胤礽才于康熙四十三年十月，和侧福晋生了孩子。
那之后，胤礽再未与太子妃同房过。
从康熙三十四年到康熙四十七年，胤礽这个太子在康熙心中地位不断降低、不断被厌恶；
从康熙三十四年到康熙四十七年，石氏这个太子妃在康熙、皇太后心中地位不断上升，离完美的儿媳妇、太子妃的形象越来越近；
胤礽身边伺候的人不断被康熙处死流放；管理胤礽身边宫人的太子妃却仍旧是康熙口中最完美的太子妃，从未被康熙训斥过。
在康熙心中，胤礽身边的人都是带坏胤礽的人，唯独胤礽的枕边人石氏清白无暇。
在一片黑暗的空间中，十一岁的胤礽睁开眼睛。
在他面前，一个和他差不多大小、比他稍瘦一些，明明还是孩子，眉眼间已经有了细细因经常皱眉而形成的纹路的少年郎，正平静地看着他。
“从后世常理来看，一家儿子被家中长辈深深厌恶，他的妻子却被家中长辈不断赞扬，显而易见……”
从康熙三十四年到康熙四十七年，从康熙四十二年到康熙五十七年。
胤礽和石氏，为了各自的利益，渐行渐远。
“若有来世，妾必再不入帝王家。”
“若有来世，最好这世界上别再有什么劳什子帝王家，哈哈哈哈哈……”

太子平静的脸庞浮现微笑：“你叫我太子，我叫你保成？”
小胤礽尴尬笑。自己和自己面对面说话，感觉怪怪的。
太子席地而坐：“坐吧，我只是第一世的执念，马上快要消散，想和你聊聊。”
小胤礽乖巧跪坐。
太子无奈笑：“你和我……性格真不一样，就像是不同的人。”
小胤礽干笑：“每个人在人生不同阶段性格都完全不同，何况转世？”
太子沉默了一会儿，幽幽道：“的确。”
两人相对无言。
半晌，小胤礽主动开口问道：“那个，太子，您想和我聊什么？”
太子无语，他无语的模样特别像康熙：“你对自己用敬语，不尴尬吗？”
小胤礽再次干笑：“是、是有点。”
“别紧张。我不过是第一世残存的执念，有什么紧张？”太子单手托腮。
小胤礽小声问道：“你是因为见到了岳父才被激活吗？那个，我感受到了你对太子妃的愧疚和对那段婚姻的不甘。放心！有我在，什么悲剧都能扭转成喜剧！”
小胤礽掰着手指头，数着自己已经扭转了多少悲剧。
太子想要的父爱，太子想要的兄弟情，太子想要的既不揽权又完美的太子，还有索额图、常泰，所有太子第一世的不甘，小胤礽都会帮其抹平。
太子妃也一样。
太子静静地托腮看着小胤礽手舞足蹈。
待小胤礽炫耀完之后，太子才收起笑容，平静道：“那你岂不是很可怜？”
小胤礽呆滞：“啊？”
太子道：“转世之后，就是不同的人。你这一世只为重复我的过往，抹平我的不甘，你岂不是可怜？”
“说白了，我的不甘和你有什么关系？我错过的伤害的人，和你又有什么关系？凭什么你要用你的一辈子来抚平别人的伤口。”
“你的性格和我不同，喜欢的人和我不同。石氏是最完美的太子妃，所以你绝对不可能和她交心。”
“我相信你，你会用一辈子对她好，容忍她的一切，让她成为最幸福的女人。”
“可凭什么？”
太子淡淡道：“造成我和她悲剧的是皇家。只要我被废，我们就注定是悲剧。而我注定被废。和我没关系，和她也没关系。”
小胤礽攥紧膝盖上的布料。
他知道太子说得对。
这辈子他可能不会被废，是因为他的人格和记忆都是第二世，他虽然废物，但也算个心智成熟的成年人。
若一个真正的孩子处于这种境地，除了被废，没有其他未来。
太子走向毁灭；太子妃想活着，想保护家人，她只能和太子渐行渐远。
谁都没错，错的是这个世界。
如此中二病爆发的一句话，居然是太子和太子妃的写实。
“你……不是我。”太子道，“这个世界也不是我的世界。已经发生的事不能改变，你已经让我看到了另一种可能性。”
太子低头：“谢谢。”
小胤礽小声道：“但你也是我，你是第一世的我，你的遗憾也是我的遗憾。”
太子摇摇头：“可你也该为自己活。你的父亲、兄弟、舅舅……所有身边的人，都是第一世记忆中的人。你被这一切束缚，说是生活，却像是赎罪。”
赎罪……
小胤礽仰起头。
是吗？原来如此。是这样啊。
他心中萦绕着的淡淡灰暗情绪，原来是这样。
小胤礽苏醒第一世记忆之后，总会忍不住自问，千错万错，难道自己没错吗？被逼疯了也好，养成那样的性格并非自愿也好，他终归做错了许多事，害死了许多人。
所以，他就像是一个提线木偶，已经固定好的剧本中演出。说是在改变，也是在重复。
有时候，小胤礽会想，他真的活着吗？
太子站起来，抱住和他一样年纪的另一个世界的小太子：“所以，够了。至少你的枕边人，陪你走一生的人，选一个第一世不认识的吧。”
“何况，石氏那性格要强极了。你若娶她，她这辈子还是完美的太子妃。她累，你也累。”太子勾起嘴角，“她上辈子说过，不愿意再入皇室。你帮她选一个合适的适合她的、家世不那么复杂的男子，我知道你做得到。”
太子说起记忆碎片中没有的、第一世关于石氏的印象。
石氏是一个类似于《红楼梦》中王熙凤的能干女子。
当太子和康熙的关系生出裂痕的时候，她更是拼了命的当这个完美的太子妃，满足康熙对太子妃所有的要求，导致她累得没有时间和太子交心，也导致她累到生不出孩子。
石氏为了做完美的太子妃，完美的儿媳妇，没有余力再做胤礽的妻子。
可这不是她的错。
是她没用的丈夫的错，是康熙这个多疑的帝王的错，是封建时代对于太子妃的束缚的错。
以石氏的性格，入宫后会再次按照康熙的要求，事事以完美太子妃优先，压抑、劳累、痛苦，即使有丈夫宽慰也不得解脱。
“保成，为自己而活，也放过石氏吧。”太子拍了拍第三世、或者说第二世的自己的背，“我所有的知识和能力都会完全融入你的身体。你……保重。”
小胤礽看着怀中消散的光点，问道：“石文炳找借口带着女儿进京，将女儿托付给康亲王杰书教养，就是奔着太子妃之位来的吧。”
石文炳妻子为曾经的铁帽子礼亲王世系继承者，贝勒常阿岱之女。后常阿岱因罪削爵，铁帽子到了堂弟杰书头上，并从礼亲王改称康亲王。
常阿岱英年早逝。康亲王府代替了常阿岱，成为了石氏的外祖父家，照看接下几年需要相看亲事的石氏。
太子微笑：“嗯。”
小胤礽道：“现在的石氏肯定也想成为太子妃。你怕我满足她的愿望。”
太子微笑：“为了赎罪完全不顾自己，那太可怜了。何况她的愿意，不是她自己的意愿。人生在局中，自己无法跳出来。”
即便是后世，也有女子被家庭教育束缚，一辈子都不会为了自己而活。要改变她们，首先需要一个没有任何人逼迫她们的环境。皇宫显然那不适合。
小胤礽看着光点消失，在再次晕厥之前，才喃喃道：“我可怜吗？”
好像有一点啊。
原来他即使理智上知道自己变成那样情有可原，但也深深唾弃着堕落颓废和疯狂后的自己，并且想要重新来过，想要……赎罪。
冷漠猜忌的父亲，彼此仇视的兄弟，被他连累而死的太子党众人……他一直没有与自己和解。
“保成！保成！”
“弟弟！！！”
“呜呜呜哥哥！！！”

“是，汗阿玛。”
胤礽眼睛紧闭，双手死死捂住耳朵。
“醒了就睁开眼睛。”康熙磨牙，“保成！你差点吓死朕！”
胤礽睁开眼睛，讪讪道：“又不是儿子愿意这样。我怎么了？”
御医冷汗涟涟。他完全检查不出太子为什么晕倒。
康熙瞪了御医一眼，让中外名医再次会诊。

胤礽：“……”
康熙：“……”
康熙泄气：“先把……先把太子头上的肿包治好吧。”
胤礽默默拉起被子遮住脸。
康熙被胤礽逗笑了，笑出声的时候，心中郁气也一扫而空。
太子还是这么活泼，还知道害羞，身体应该没事了吧。
中外名医查不出原因，康熙大概已经知道太子晕倒的原因了。
他数了数日子，这段时间大清第一次参与世界战争，他忙得脚不沾地，胤礽也给他当帮手忙得脚不沾地，一直没有离宫。
胤礽在宫里待太久就会被诅咒侵蚀。以前胤礽每隔几日就会出宫玩耍，会去丰泽园种地，这段时间他们父子俩都忙得忽略了这件事。
“再过几日，就带你泡温泉去。咱们去温泉行宫过冬。”康熙点了点胤礽头上的小肿包，“免得你再次晕倒，满头肿包。”

康熙气得吹胡子瞪眼：“吓我一跳叫没事！”

胤礽赶紧哄弟弟。
胤禔白眼翻上了天。
这群弟弟一个个都脆弱得不像皇家的孩子，全是胤礽娇惯出来的。
不过胤禔也松了一口气。
太子弟弟最近性格很闷，时常板着脸，也不再每日念叨弟弟，胤禔很担心。现在看来，弟弟只是病久了窝床上犯懒。他早该把太子弟弟背出门散步。
康熙正带着大臣，一边散步一边问皇子们的功课，并安排正月后四阿哥胤禛入学的事，老远就看到一大群皇子蹦蹦跳跳。
康熙止住脚步，躲在了墙后。
一大群太监侍从也立刻非常熟练地找地方隐蔽。
大臣傻眼。
赵昌小声道：“陈大人，赶紧躲起来！”
陈梦雷赶紧蹲下，提着衣摆蹲着走到墙角康熙身后藏着。
大冬天的，他吓出了满头大汗。
皇上这是干什么？！
康熙伸手，赵昌从袖子里递过去一个短筒望远镜。
康熙拿起望远镜，失笑：“保成这个闲不住的人，自己病得走不动路，让保清背着都要起床和弟弟们玩耍。”
赵昌小声道：“皇上，奴才猜测，可能是大阿哥担心太子殿下躺着对身体不好，把太子殿下背了出来。”
康熙沉默了一会儿，面无表情道：“好吧，肯定是大阿哥。不过太子也是，唉，太纵着哥哥弟弟们。自己还病着，就由着别人胡来。这脾气，哪有一点太子的霸气？”
赵昌道：“太子殿下对外人还是很有气势，皇上不用担心。”
康熙叹气：“太子是君，其他皇子是臣。君臣有别，他究竟明不明白？你说呢，陈梦雷？”
陈梦雷：“？”
我说什么？皇上您满口抱怨，也没见您阻止啊。如果您不想让太子和其他皇子们相处，太子怎么会有机会和其他皇子相处？
陈梦雷疯狂擦汗，一个字都说不出来。
康熙有些失望。
陈梦雷的学问很好，但随机应变上有些差。康熙喜欢能说会道的人，比如李光地。
不过或许人太能说会道，就没心思潜心做学问。康熙决定再观望看看，如果陈梦雷还是这么闷，就打发陈梦雷去编书。
他的儿子们可不能被陈梦雷教得不会说话。
有一个不会说话的大儿子已经够了。康熙放下望远镜，胸口开始疼。
“不去阿哥所了，回乾清宫。”康熙远远看着皇子们蹦蹦跳跳走进阿哥所，放下望远镜，笑着摇摇头，“太子马上要和朕一起去温泉行宫，离开前，让他和兄弟们多相处一会儿。”
常泰传来了战报。大清第一次跟着法兰西喝肉汤的行动异常顺利，已经望见了胜利的曙光。
按照康熙和太子、大阿哥的约定，若此次战争胜利，太子和大阿哥就会代表大清出使法兰西，正式与法兰西签署同盟条约。
胤礽在病床上也看到了常泰的战报。
现在小阿哥们围在一起堆积木，胤礽靠坐在软塌上，正和胤禔说这件事。
看到常泰的战报之后，胤礽才发现常泰要参加的荷兰战争，不是他以为的法荷战争。
胤礽虽然第二世比较关心康熙朝同时代的海外大事，但还没关注到把年份倒背如流，只知道某个大致的时间段会发生什么事。
现在他才知道，常泰率领大清参战的时候，《奈梅亨条约》已经签订五年，法荷战争早就结束。
在《奈梅亨条约》中，法国虽然取得了“霸权”，但实际上的利益没有捞到多少。
法国占领的荷兰领土全还了回去，关税也恢复了最低。它只占领了部分西班牙的殖民地，并让欧洲大陆诸国承认了“太阳王”的称号。
chapters.translated_text:
As long as the Crown Princess is the same age as me or older, then she would also be getting married at twenty, which is just the right age.

Kangxi sighed: "You. You're impatient to coax women? Have you given all your patience to your brothers?"

Yinreng put on the face of a total scumbag: "Yes."

Kangxi reached out and tapped Yinreng on the nose: "Fine. Why would I make you coax anyone? Of course, the Crown Princess will take care of you. Any other requirements?"

Yinreng said: "The second requirement: I want a Crown Princess who has few brothers and a weak family influence."

Kangxi frowned: "Why?"

Yinreng glanced at the monk and the Taoist, who were already sweating profusely in front of him.

Kangxi realized there were two outsiders present and waved for them to leave.

Before they left, Yinreng gave the two of them rewards, and also gave rewards to their temple.

After Master Dehai and Daoist Zhang returned to Fragrant Hills, they whispered to each other. The Crown Prince is still the best! Look at that Qing Emperor's character! He actually wants to give such a young child palace maids! What kind of family style is this! It's fortunate the Crown Prince behaves properly!

After the two left, Yinreng said: "Father Emperor, I have observed history; in the early stages of a dynasty, the Empress's family is often powerful; after the dynasty stabilizes, the Empress's family influence tends to weaken."

Kangxi thought about it, and it was indeed the case.

Yinreng said: "If Father chooses a Crown Princess for me who has a decent family background but a clean household, her upbringing will certainly be good; if she doesn't have many brothers or cousins, and her clan isn't powerful, she won't keep thinking about her maiden family and will only be good to me."

In truth, Yinreng was just harboring a faint hope of being able to fall in love in the feudal era.

He knew that the mindset of ancient noblewomen was completely different from modern people, and this was even more true for women who married into the royal family.

Noblewomen were taught from childhood that marriage was for the sake of competing for benefits for their maiden families and brothers. Husbands and children were merely tools for a clear-headed noble lady to seize benefits for herself and her maiden family.

A Crown Princess with a less prosperous family, or perhaps even no brothers, might settle down and fall in love with him.

Yinreng was just hoping. And hope is a slim thing.

Their worldviews were different, he was hiding so many secrets, and it was an arranged marriage—how could they possibly turn from husband and wife into lovers?

Kangxi was silent for a long time, then pulled Yinreng into his arms and ruffled his hair: "Are you... are you scared by the Tong family?"

Yinreng was stunned for a moment.

Kangxi took Yinreng's silence as an admission and sighed for a long time.

Father and son snuggled together, as if they were the only two in this world who could trust each other.

"I understand. You are the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince does not need the support of his wife's family to ascend the throne. If the Crown Princess's family is too powerful, it will only lead to the tail wagging the dog," Kangxi said. "I will choose a Crown Princess for you with a good family foundation, a harmonious home, and no overbearing relatives."

Yinreng smiled: "Good! Oh, and she must be pretty!"

Kangxi said with a straight face: "That's the third requirement."

Yinreng said: "The Crown Princess is the mother of the nation, how can she not be pretty? No way, no way, do I have to ask for this myself?"

Kangxi said sternly: "As long as the Crown Princess has regular features, that's enough. If she's too pretty and people say you're obsessed with beauty, what then?"

Yinreng said: "I only have one Crown Princess! How could that be called being obsessed with beauty! Besides, my mother was very pretty! Father Emperor, don't you blush saying that!"

Kangxi recalled Empress Renxiao. Ahem, that's right, Empress Renxiao was very beautiful.

Yinreng tilted his head and shouted: "Dad!!! Your son wants a pretty wife!!!"

Kangxi didn't know whether to laugh or cry: "Shut up! Have you no shame!"

Yinreng said: "Then ask Big Brother if you assign him an ugly wife!"

Kangxi actually called Yinzhi over.

Yinzhi looked at Kangxi as if he were an idiot: "Father Emperor, should you call the imperial physician to take a look?"

Kangxi: "..."

He smiled: "I have decided, I must assign you an ugly First Princess Consort!"

Yinreng and Yinzhi said in unison: "Father Emperor, please think twice!!!!"

100,000

The matter of offspring is a feudal bad habit; it does not mean Yinreng thinks women must have children, nor does it mean the author thinks women must have children. Please be merciful.

107. Two Chapters Combined [V]

Even if Kangxi really wanted to "retaliate" against Yinzhi, he couldn't possibly assign him an ugly wife.

However, he still used marriage as a threat to make Yinzhi do many things.

Under Yinreng's persuasion, Yinzhi behaved for a while, acting as a truly filial son for a period.

Kangxi was so happy he couldn't help but sleep at Consort Hui's place for several days in a row, which scared Yinzhi pale.

Yinzhi pulled Yinreng aside and asked: "Baocheng, my mother is getting old, will there be any issues if she gives birth again?"

After growing a bit older, because the term "Crown Prince Brother" was too sticky and several silly brothers would look up whenever he said "Brother," Yinzhi became more accustomed to calling Yinreng by his milk name.

As for why he didn't call him "Second Brother," Yinzhi always felt that "Second Brother" got mixed up with the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth brothers, and wasn't special enough.

Yinreng said: "Consort Hui's age isn't considered old..."

Yinzhi said: "She's in her thirties!"

Yinreng originally wanted to say that being in one's thirties wasn't old, but he suddenly remembered this was ancient times. Given the birthing conditions, being over thirty really was considered a high-risk pregnancy.

Yinreng scratched his head: "Then what can be done? We can't stop Father Emperor from going to Consort Hui's palace, can we?"

In ancient times, effective contraceptive methods had to be used by men. Those "contraceptive soups" were basically abortion drugs; how could he let Consort Hui drink them?

Yinzhi was extremely worried.

This guy actually ran directly to Consort Hui, asking her to feign illness so she wouldn't have to sleep with Kangxi.

Consort Hui went dark before her eyes and almost fainted.

Fortunately, she understood her son; although he often angered her, he was truly filial to her, so she patiently asked why he was meddling in his parents' private affairs.

When Consort Hui heard Yinzhi say he was worried about the dangers of her giving birth, she was stunned for a long time.

"Mother?" Yinzhi had grown up and could no longer snuggle in her arms, so he just looked up at her.

Consort Hui took off her nail guards and gently stroked Yinzhi's hair, her still-beautiful face showing a complex expression: "Mother can no longer have children."

Yinzhi: "Ah?"

Consort Hui seemed to fall into memories and said softly: "Mother hurt her body giving birth when I was young, and now I can't have any more."

Yinzhi recalled Yinreng's popular science: "Giving birth too young is indeed very harmful to a woman's body. Mother has suffered."

Consort Hui's expression twisted slightly.

She truly never dreamed that her son would discuss the topic of childbirth with her.

Consort Hui wanted to scold her son, saying that as a man, he shouldn't ask about such things. But the words of reprimand wouldn't come out.

Childbirth is truly painful, and no woman expects a man to understand this. Even women themselves believe the process of nurturing life is "dirty" rather than "sacred." They are forced or volunteer to give birth, yet avoid mentioning the process itself.

Now, her son was saying that Mother had suffered; saying he felt bad for her body; saying that Mother should find a way not to give birth anymore, as health was the most important thing.

Consort Hui's lips trembled for a while, and she reached out quite improperly to pull her grown son into her arms: "Thank you, First Prince."

Yinzhi's body stiffened, and he wanted to break free, but he felt the grievance and trembling in Consort Hui's voice.

He hesitated for a moment, then, like he would with his younger brothers, reached out and gently wrapped his arms around Consort Hui's back: "Mother, from now on, I will protect you. You just need to focus on your health, don't worry about anything, and don't bother with trying to win favor. I will earn my own merits and become a Prince."

Consort Hui closed her eyes for a quiet moment, then pushed her son away. When she opened her eyes, they were as bright as if washed by tears.

"As long as you don't make the Emperor angry, I can breathe a sigh of relief; I don't expect you to achieve any great merits." Consort Hui gently straightened Yinzhi's clothes and tidied his hair. "My only wish is for you to be healthy and safe."

Yinzhi waved his arms: "I'm stronger than a tiger, Mother doesn't need to worry about me!"

Consort Hui smiled and nodded, changing the subject: "The Emperor is going to choose a consort for you. Do you have any requirements?"

Yinzhi said: "Good-looking, healthy, gentle temper, and no troublesome relatives."

Consort Hui laughed and scolded: "You really have a lot of requirements."

Yinzhi touched his nose: "Are these requirements a lot? Ordinary people have these requirements when marrying, don't they? Can't I, as a prince, have them?"

Consort Hui sighed: "For a prince's consort, family background is the priority."

Yinzhi rolled his eyes: "I said last time I wanted to marry into the grasslands and got beaten up by Father Emperor so badly. Isn't this just another marriage alliance?"

Consort Hui tapped her son's forehead lightly: "Don't say such things. If your Father Emperor hears you again, I won't be able to protect you."

Yinzhi sighed: "Alright, I won't say it. Mother, do your best. Anyway, just don't let the family be too complicated. I hate trouble."

Consort Hui nodded: "I will do my best."

Knowing that Consort Hui could no longer have children, Yinzhi felt a sense of relief.

He said to Yinreng: "Mother's body is fine now, but I'm a bit worried about my consort. Mother hurt her body because she gave birth too many times when she was young. Won't my consort be the same?"

Yinreng was shocked by Yinzhi's question.

He was a youth of the new era; caring for women was a matter of course. But his big brother was a feudal man!

Big Brother, the best man in the Qing Dynasty!

Yinreng said: "Don't worry, when the time comes, take some measures, and avoid sleeping together during the times when your consort is most likely to conceive to minimize the probability. Even if she accidentally gets pregnant, you can definitely ensure her body is well-rested before the next one."

Yinzhi nodded: "She's my wife, after all; I don't want to lose a woman's life because of childbirth."

Yinreng pounced on him: "Big Brother, you are the peerless best man of the Qing Dynasty!"

Yinzhi caught Yinreng, looking confused: "Caring about a wife's life makes me the peerless best man? The standards for this are too low."

Yinreng looked up and said: "No, no, no. In this era, caring about a wife's life is already being the peerless best man!"

Yinzhi was helpless: "What 'this era'? You talk as if you aren't from this era. What? Are you an ancient person?"

Yinreng said seriously: "I am a person from the future!"

Yinzhi rolled his eyes and said: "Oh. Then, future-man brother, do you know who your big brother's future consort is?"

Yinreng actually did know. But he wasn't sure about this lifetime.

Yinzhi's consort, the Irgen Gioro clan, subtly matched the family background Yinreng had hoped for when telling Kangxi about choosing a Crown Princess.

The Irgen Gioro clan was a great Manchu family, thriving with many descendants. But the branch Yinzhi's consort belonged to had few officials, and the most powerful person was Yinzhi's father-in-law, Kekun, who had reached the position of Minister of Personnel.

With a long-standing and prominent family background, few close relatives in government to drag the prince down, and a capable father-in-law with a harmonious family, the Irgen Gioro clan was indeed a good candidate for a consort.

Later, Yinzhi's father-in-law Kekun was dismissed from office, purely because he was implicated by Yinzhi—Kangxi wanted to deal with the First Prince's party led by Mingzhu, so the First Prince's father-in-law naturally couldn't remain a Minister.

However, in this lifetime, because the Shanxi Muerse corruption case broke out early, Kekun, who was still the Left Censor-in-Chief, was demoted three ranks by Kangxi for following his colleagues in saying Muerse was honest.

Now Kekun was climbing back up and hadn't become a Minister yet; it was unclear if he fit the range of families Kangxi had in mind for the First Princess Consort.

As for Kekun favoring Muerse, it wasn't that he truly supported Muerse or was part of his clique. If that were the case, when the Muerse corruption case broke out in Yinreng's first life, Kekun wouldn't have been demoted and then quickly reassigned as Minister of Personnel.

Kekun was just standing on the side of his Manchu colleagues, favoring a Manchu official during the impeachment by Han Chinese censors.

The struggle between Manchu and Han officials in the court, like factional strife, had nothing to do with right or wrong; it was only about stance. If Kekun dared to support Han officials in impeaching a Manchu official for corruption, he would be abandoned by his Manchu colleagues.

This was the wisdom of being an official; Yinreng had no ill feelings toward Kekun. Among the officials of this era, Kekun was considered relatively good.

Yinzhi said: "What? Future-man brother? Mute? What happened to you being a future man?"

Yinreng stood straight and said mysteriously: "If a prophecy is spoken, it won't come true."

Yinzhi didn't fall for it: "If you don't say it, how will others know you know the prophecy?"

Yinreng said: "I'll tell you when the prophecy comes true!"

Yinzhi spread his hands: "Fine, when you get married, I'll also say I predicted who your Crown Princess would be long ago. We'll both be amazing prophecy brothers."

Yinreng muttered to himself. You're still years away from marriage; who knows, by then Kekun might have climbed back to the position of Minister, and your wife will still be an Irgen Gioro!

Be careful, I might go find your future sister-in-law right now and badmouth you, sowing discord between you two, hmph!

"Speechless, aren't you?" Yinzhi patted Yinreng's shoulder. "Your little tricks work on Father Emperor, but how could they fool your big brother?"

Yinreng huffed twice, crossed his arms and said: "Father Emperor was on a whim, wanting me to help you look at wives. I was going to help you pick one who was especially pretty. Now, sigh, how can a younger brother help his older brother look? I won't go; let Father Emperor look himself."

Yinzhi immediately held Yinreng's hands: "Big Brother was wrong. Little Brother, hurry and go, you must go; I can't trust Father Emperor's taste!"

Yinreng snorted: "The concubines Father Emperor favors are all quite pretty."

Yinzhi gripped Yinreng's hands tightly and said sincerely: "Choosing one's own wife is different from choosing a son's wife! My mother nags every day, 'First Prince, although you said you wanted a pretty one, a consort's appearance should be dignified and blessed!' Dignified and blessed means a big face and thick lips, right? Would she want that if she were the one marrying?"

"Consort Hui can't marry a wife—ah, Big Brother, are you talking about a wife or a daughter-in-law? I'm confused." Yinreng pulled his hands back and shook his head. "I'll still convince Father Emperor to let you come along and peek."

Yinzhi gave Yinreng a bear hug, almost dislocating his bones: "It's all up to you, Little Brother!"

"Let go, let go! My bones are creaking!"

...

With Yinreng's prodding, Kangxi agreed to let Yinzhi hide behind a screen and peek at the young girls called into the palace by the Empress Dowager to play.

Looking for a wife naturally required a strategist, so Yinreng was also dragged along to peek.

Yinzhi had a ready excuse: "You can find a wife for yourself while you're at it!"

Yinreng rolled his eyes: "I'm still young, I don't need one."

Yinzhi said: "You're only two years younger than me. These people are about your age too. Don't talk! They're coming!"

Yinzhi squatted on the ground and pulled out a telescope.

Yinreng didn't know why Yinzhi had to squat, but he also took out his telescope.

Kangxi, who was also sitting behind the screen, showed a weary smile.

He whispered to Consort Hui: "Why does your son look so sleazy?"

Consort Hui smiled along, thinking to herself: No, that's your son.

Yinzhi excitedly tugged at Yinreng's hem: "They're here, they're here! Quick, squat down!"

"Why squat? Are you hiding in the bushes? We're behind a screen." Yinreng complained, but still obediently squatted with Yinzhi.

A group of young girls, the youngest eight or nine and the oldest thirteen or fourteen, walked gracefully into the Cining Palace to accompany the Empress Dowager in viewing chrysanthemums.

In the open space in front of the Cining Palace, chrysanthemum pots were arranged, and various shapes were built with wooden frames.

Besides the chrysanthemums, the palace servants had also set up colorful awnings in front of the Cining Palace to keep the girls from being exposed to the sun.

The girls walked on flower-pot shoes, holding handkerchiefs, with hairpins in their hair, stepping more steadily than Yinzhi and Yinreng had ever walked on plum blossom stakes.

Yinzhi was amazed: "The beads on their heads don't even shake! If I wore that, I would have already scratched my face with red marks."

Yinreng said: "When noblewomen are trained in etiquette, they walk wearing hairpins, and the hairpins shouldn't shake noticeably; that's the standard. Wait, why would you want to wear hairpins?"

Yinzhi said: "That's not the point! Don't you think they look like mannequins?"

Yinreng said: "That's quite a point; why would you want to wear hairpins, Big Brother!"

Yinzhi and Yinreng whispered to each other, leaving Kangxi confused.

He took a deep breath and said: "Your son..."

Consort Hui looked at Kangxi gently. What's wrong with my son? Emperor, please tell me.

Kangxi sighed: "This child must be like his Imperial Grandfather."

Consort Hui's smile stiffened slightly. How was she supposed to respond to that?

Kangxi added: "The First Prince is like his Imperial Grandfather, so who is the Crown Prince like?"

Consort Hui smiled: "Of course, he is like the Emperor."

Now it was Kangxi's turn for his smile to stiffen. He couldn't very well say he wasn't, could he?

Kangxi had no choice but to glare at the squatting little Crown Prince, thinking he must make Yinreng study etiquette properly tomorrow.

Yinzhi had been full of joy to choose a wife, but now his enthusiasm had cooled by more than half.

Most of the young girls were childish. They wore wide clothes, their hair was slicked with hair oil, their faces were covered in thick powder, their lips were painted into a tiny red dot, their steps and arm movements were almost identical, and the dignified expressions on their faces looked as stiff as wooden dolls.

Yinzhi put down his telescope, his expression gloomy: "I have to choose one from them?"

Yinreng was also speechless.

If these girls took off their makeup, they would surely be quite pretty. But they had to dress in a dignified way to see the Empress Dowager, and their words and actions had to be cautious; hadn't they all turned into dolls?

Yinreng said honestly: "When they are outside the palace, they must be quite lively and pretty."

Yinzhi was silent for a while and said: "Is it like the difference between flowers blooming on a branch and flowers picked and put in a vase?"

Yinreng was shocked. His big brother had actually started being poetic! My God! Are you still my big brother!

"Exactly." Yinreng said comfortingly, "Big Brother, don't worry, after she marries you, she definitely won't be like this."

Yinzhi had lost confidence: "Maybe even more wooden. The pressure on a prince's consort is huge; which of these people looks like they can handle pressure? I can beat ten of them with one hand!"

Yinreng sighed. Alright, his good big brother had returned to his true nature.

A prince's consort does have a lot of pressure, but it's not the kind of pressure you can beat ten people with!

Kangxi felt a headache listening to them: "Are they that ugly?"

Yinzhi said: "It's not a question of ugly or not, it's that you can't even tell what they look like."

Kangxi was curious.

So, instigated by his eldest son and his precious son, the supreme ruler of the Qing Dynasty actually took the telescope from his son and squatted behind the screen to peek at the young girls.

Consort Hui's eyes widened until the corners hurt, her body trembled slightly from excessive shock, and the lip balm on her lips faded.

Emperor! What are you doing, Emperor! How can you do such a thing!!

At this moment, Consort Hui missed Empress Renxiao very much.

When Empress Renxiao was still around, she would pinch the Emperor's hand with a smile that radiated dark energy and say, "Emperor, mind the rules."

After Empress Renxiao passed away, the Emperor had completely let go!

Consort Hui felt extremely aggrieved. Emperor, you still ask who the First Prince is like? Who do you say he is like? Look at yourself right now! You tell me who the First Prince is like!

Consort Hui clutched her heart, suffering from heartache.

After Kangxi saw the group of young girls, he was amused: "Indeed, you can't tell what they look like. Why is their makeup done like this?"

Yinreng said: "Old people like mature and dignified young girls, so naturally, they dress themselves to look mature."

Yinzhi said with a dark face: "It's dressing to look ugly, right? I have heard that some old people outside don't like to see young girls dressed up in fancy clothes, but this is too much."

Kangxi said: "Leave it to Father!"

He stood up and found Zhao Chang to whisper a few words.

Palace maids and nannies brought clear water, soap, soft towels, and essential oils for skincare.

Yinzhi said anxiously: "Never mind my accent! Hurry and help me see, is that girl super pretty!"

Super pretty...

Yinzhi said: "The one wearing the emerald-colored clothes, with small light yellow flowers on them, wearing red coral beads on her head, and smiling super sweetly! The one right in the middle under the big chrysanthemum rack!"

Smiling super sweetly...

Yinreng searched carefully: "Oh oh oh, she does have a sweet smile."

Actually, in terms of appearance, that girl in the emerald clothes couldn't be said to be the prettiest among the group.

The girl in emerald green looked quite young. Compared to the thirteen- or fourteen-year-old maidens around her who had already begun to blossom, she could only be called adorable, not quite beautiful.

But her smile was simply so sweet that even Yinreng was taken aback when he saw it.

Some people's smiles were extraordinarily lovely and incredibly infectious. This girl in green was precisely one such person.

That little girl in emerald green looked particularly endearing. The two dimples on her cheeks looked as if they were filled with honey, smiling so sweetly that an old father's(?) heart would almost melt.

Seeing her sweet smile, Yinreng felt a warm sweetness in his own heart, as if he had drunk honey.

If he were to date someone, the lady would have to be at least eighteen or older; otherwise, romantic notions would never cross his mind.

Yinreng lowered the telescope and glanced at his elder brother.

His elder brother was currently grinning like a fool, so silly that it was hard to look at.

Yinreng turned to Kangxi, who was also smiling, looking very benevolent: "This child looks full of fortune."

Yinreng did not understand Kangxi's criteria for "blessed," but evidently she had gained Kangxi's approval.

"Then is it her?" Yinreng asked. "I also think she suits Eldest Brother very well."

In an arranged blind marriage, if one party felt even a tiny spark of affection—even if it was merely love at first sight based on looks—it would still make married life much easier.

That tiny bit of happiness behind closed doors, compared to the devastation the environment inflicts upon women...

It is truly a blessing that Fucha-shi is not a transmigrator.
