chapters.translated_text:
This time, as a defeated nation, Switzerland also compensated the Qing Dynasty with a significant amount of money and grain. Yinshi didn't mind getting into a fight with the Swiss King in public, just to extort even more money and grain from him.

Yinreng was helpless. He had told Yinshi to be careful, which meant not to rush up with a blade and shout "What are you looking at?" at the Swiss King.

...

Leaving some envoys behind, Yinreng took most of the guards and, under the escort of the Qing Navy, headed to Vienna.

The Qing Navy was not weak in land battles either; they hadn't lost the archery and equestrian skills of the Eight Banners, and they had new weapons.

When Changtai was stationed in Europe, he had also brought Dai Zi along.

After arriving in Europe, besides changing his satirical poems about the Kangxi era into satirical poems about Europe, Dai Zi frantically studied mathematics, military science, and chemistry, drawing inspiration from European firearms.

The Qing Navy was very wealthy, and now the sailors had all upgraded their equipment, each holding the most advanced flintlock muskets.

Yinreng had a deep impression of Dai Zi. He knew that Kangxi detested Dai Zi for writing bitter poems, and after Dai Zi’s "mother-and-son" cannons lost their utility, Kangxi used Nan Huairen's false accusation to exile him. Therefore, he had long ago asked Changtai to bring him to Taiwan.

Kangxi had originally treated Dai Zi very well. Dai Zi entered service as a commoner, and Kangxi broke protocol to promote him to a reader in the Hanlin Academy, also letting him serve in the Southern Study alongside Gao Shiqi.

But Dai Zi was a scholar like Pu Songling. Compared to Pu Songling, who failed the exams repeatedly, given that Kangxi treated him very well, his writing of poems exposing the "man-eating" nature of the old society under Kangxi's prosperous age inevitably made Kangxi extremely disgusted.

Dai Zi had merits but no faults and was an honest official. The bitter poems he wrote didn't even reach the level of literary inquisition. It just so happened that Nan Huairen made a false accusation, so Kangxi took the opportunity to exile him.

This "blunder" of a not-yet-senile emperor easily believing a missionary and exiling a meritorious official was, behind the scenes, nothing more than the art of imperial manipulation.

Yinreng had "driven away" Dai Zi early on. Every time Kangxi saw a new weapon Dai Zi had created, he would still mutter about Dai Zi being ungrateful. It showed that although Kangxi could endure, his pettiness and grudge-holding were quite severe.

During this visit, Yinreng met with Dai Zi.

Yinreng didn't give Dai Zi any face; he scolded him right to his face and told him why Kangxi hated him.

"Imperial Father promoted you against protocol; you should at least give him some face. Even if you want to worry about the country and the people, can't you write more tactfully? Can't you write that the ministers are ungrateful for the Emperor's grace?" Yinreng scolded, "Uncle can save you once, but he can't save you forever. If you keep shooting your mouth off and causing trouble for Uncle, you can just go home and write your articles about worrying for the country and the people!"

Yinreng was just trying to scare Dai Zi. He couldn't bear to part with him.

Yinreng knew that Dai Zi was easily frightened but just had a stubborn brain; if he didn't explain it clearly, Dai Zi wouldn't be able to figure it out himself.

And others were embarrassed to tell Dai Zi that his bad luck was because that "magnanimous" emperor wasn't actually that magnanimous, and he hated that Dai Zi kept badmouthing him.

As the Crown Prince, Yinreng didn't have that concern.

Even if Kangxi heard these words, he would only nod and say his son was considerate of him, and that the scolding was well-deserved.

During the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, Dai Zi had recommended himself to serve in Prince Kang Jieshu’s army and performed meritorious service, and later worked hard to manufacture firearms. He was clearly a stubborn scholar who wanted to bring honor to his ancestors but just had a stiff mouth.

After Yinreng bluntly knocked him down a peg, he became honest.

He couldn't do flattery, but couldn't he write satirical poems and articles about Europe?

It just so happened that after following Changtai to Europe, he believed the Qing Dynasty was truly a prosperous age, at least not to the point of "man-eating."

In this world, you have to compare yourself to the worst to feel happy.

Thinking of Dai Zi, Yinreng poked his head out of the carriage and asked: "Where is Big Brother? Is he still hanging out with Dai Zi?"

Cao Yin said: "Yes. The Prince of the First Rank and Master Dai have been chatting all the way here."

Yinreng rubbed his forehead.

His own brother said he liked firearms very much and wanted to discuss firearm inspiration with Dai Zi.

They even rounded up a group of newly acquired foreign scientific talents to calculate some formulas he couldn't understand, saying they wanted to build a musket better than the flintlock.

Seeing Yinshi so rarely studious, Yinreng didn't stop them.

But as the days passed, Yinreng felt more and more panicked. He always felt that his brother, who liked to argue and make the Emperor angry, and Dai Zi, who liked to write bitter poems to satirize the Emperor, getting together would produce an incredible, strange reaction.

He hoped this was just an illusion.

To get to Vienna, one had to pass through French territory. Yinreng visited Paris on the way and saw the Palace of Versailles, which was under construction, before continuing his journey.

There were many European countries, but their land areas were not large.

A few days later, Yinreng arrived in Vienna.

Changtai and the young Duke of Hanover were riding on horses, waiting for the Qing delegation outside the gates of Vienna long ago.

When Changtai knelt to pay his respects, the young Duke of Hanover also bowed, being exceptionally polite.

Yinreng sized up the young Duke of Hanover.

This young Duke of Hanover had a more famous "name" in later generations—George I.

That's right, he was the George I who would later establish the Hanoverian dynasty during Britain's golden age.

Later generations had many bad reviews of this George I; he abused his wife, was on bad terms with his descendants, had very low popularity, and there were even unofficial histories saying he died of a cerebral hemorrhage caused by excessive straining while constipated.

Hmm, a smelly and painful way to die.

In screen portrayals, George I was also depicted as a strange-looking madman.

George I's parents were close relatives, so it would be normal if he looked strange.

However, the young Duke of Hanover appearing before him didn't look at all like the violent, mad king described by later generations.

He was a very handsome young man with a lovely smile. His figure wasn't particularly tall, but one could tell at a glance that he had a sturdy physique from being on the battlefield. No wonder he could become friends with Changtai.

People are all more or less attracted to good looks.

Seeing the handsome young man George, Yinreng's smile became much more sincere: "Uncle said he made a good-looking friend, so I specifically brought the best-looking people among my friends. It's a good thing I brought them, otherwise, I would have been overshadowed by you."

Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde smiled.

They were already used to it.

Europeans were particularly obsessed with looks and had a morbid pursuit of beauty. Their faces were sometimes more useful than their status.

After George sized up Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde, he said: "I still think Changtai is the best-looking."

Yinreng's smile stiffened.

Yinshi's expression was strange.

Changtai spread his hands to them: "I am his friend. If he said I looked ugly, I would probably break off relations with him."

Yinreng and Yinshi breathed a sigh of relief.

Thank goodness, it was a pure friendship between them.

It wasn't their fault for being suddenly nervous; the private lives of these Western European nobles were simply too chaotic, and bisexuality was everywhere.

George didn't know what these two little guys were thinking. He was very curious about these two young princes who had traveled so far to another country. When he was their age, he was just receiving education at home. The Qing princes were truly amazing.

George was only twenty-five this year, in the prime of his life. Everything he did revealed confidence, and he soon hit it off with Yinshi, ignoring their respective seniority and starting to call each other brothers.

Yinreng, on the other hand, gained the favor of the Duke of Hanover and Sophie.

Even though Sophie had lost someone she admired, seeing Yinreng, she thought it was worth it.

She had received a letter written by Leibniz, in which Leibniz highly praised Yinreng's wisdom and was very willing to follow Yinreng back to the Qing Dynasty to open up new scientific territories.

She was a wise and curious woman. After chatting with Yinreng about mathematics for a while, she fell deeply in love with Yinreng and really wanted to send women to him.

Yinreng once again refused Sophie's kindness on the grounds of his young age and the purity of the royal bloodline.

He was almost numb. Every time he chatted with these Western European nobles, they always wanted to stuff women to him. When they saw the two handsome men behind him, they even tried to stuff men to Yinreng?

Yinreng: ???

The guards behind him had already drawn their blades!

When his guards drew their blades, these people were not only not angry but very happy. Because no matter the denomination, those who believed in God thought homosexuals should be burned to death.

The Qing people were so resistant to being sent handsome men for the prince; everyone was of the same path!

Yinreng: ???

He couldn't help but want to curse in his heart.

You think homosexuals should go to hell, yet you present male noble beauties and openly keep male lovers? What kind of logic is this!

This time on the mission, Yinreng had truly accumulated a belly full of complaints, ready to vent them to his Imperial Father after returning to the capital.

Yinreng and Yinshi each played to their strengths. Yinreng was like a fish in water among the electors, and Yinshi was making friends and forming cliques among the heirs of the electors and high-ranking military officials. The Holy Roman Empire tour ended successfully.

Even the Swiss King, who hated France, held Yinreng's hand with teary eyes, asking Yinreng to come to Switzerland to play.

The guards behind Yinreng wanted to draw their blades again.

They thought these people were simply too dangerous; the way they looked at their Crown Prince was too intense, making the alarm bells in their hearts ring wildly.

"How exhausting." After finishing all the treaty signings, Yinshi collapsed on the bed, motionless.

Yinreng poked Yinshi's back in annoyance: "Aren't you going out to play every day? What's so exhausting?"

Yinshi said weakly: "Going out to play isn't exhausting; mediating their family and marital conflicts is really tiring."

Yinreng was full of question marks: "What? Mediating what conflicts?"

Yinshi sat up, crossed his legs, and hunched his back: "Just family and marital conflicts."

Yinreng waved his hand, telling Yinshi to be quiet. He took a few deep breaths and asked: "What did you mediate?"

Yinshi gave an example: "For example, Uncle's friend George, he failed to propose to the British Princess Anne and was forced by his father to marry an uncle's illegitimate daughter, so he felt very unbalanced."

Yinreng made a Psyduck-tilting-head gesture, searched his memory for a long time, and found this matter.

George I's original wife was his first cousin, a political marriage forced upon him by his father to strengthen the rule of the territory.

George I once had a chance to escape this political marriage. He traveled to England, hoping to gain Princess Anne's favor. Unfortunately, Princess Anne's father and brother did not agree.

"If it were a legitimate daughter, it would be fine, but an illegitimate daughter... he felt insulted." Yinshi shrugged, "His wife likes him very much and hopes he will dismiss his mistresses and live a life of just the two of them. They both take turns coming to me to vent their grievances. It's so hard for me."

Yinreng waved his hand again: "Wait, why do they come to you to vent their grievances?"

Something is wrong here, right?!

Yinshi spread his hands blankly: "I don't know either. Anyway, they just come to me to vent."

Seeing that Yinshi couldn't explain it clearly, Yinreng went to ask Changtai, who had been protecting Yinshi all along.

He followed a group of kings, so he didn't have to worry about safety. Yinshi had to accompany the young heirs to go hunting and playing, so Yinreng let Changtai follow Yinshi closely, firstly for protection, and secondly to keep an eye on Yinshi so he wouldn't mess around again.

Changtai didn't tell Yinreng about Yinshi acting as a psychological counselor for the young couples, probably thinking these things didn't count as messing around.

After hearing Yinreng's inquiry, Changtai said: "The First Prince actually didn't say much."

He repeated a few of Yinshi's psychological therapy lines.

"Ah? You're still enduring it like this? Are you even human?"

"Can't you get a divorce? We have 'he-li' (divorce) in the Qing Dynasty. Usually, at this time, we only advise divorce."

"Dump him!"

"What's the point of keeping such a man? Kick him out!"

"A steamed bun matches a dog, a match made in heaven."

"Don't talk to me if you're not getting a divorce."...

Yinreng was speechless: "That's it?"

Changtai nodded: "I don't understand either why those people love to chat with the First Prince about their emotional lives even more."

Yinreng felt a headache coming on.

He thought, this time you really can't blame Big Brother. Big Brother really didn't expect it at all, right?

"That young Duke of Hanover, George and his wife, they won't really want to divorce, right?" Yinreng rubbed his forehead, "This kind of political marriage, if Big Brother talks them into divorcing, I'm afraid the Duke of Hanover might be angered to death."

Changtai said: "Probably not. George needs his uncle's support to sit firmly in the position of the heir to the Hanoverian Elector. His uncle dotes on this illegitimate daughter very much."

Yinreng said: "Then why do they keep bothering my brother? Isn't it that they aren't divorcing?"

Changtai said: "I asked George. George said that everyone tells him he can't divorce, only the First Prince supports him in divorcing. Even if he can't divorce, he is very happy to see someone standing on his side."

Yinreng held his forehead: "...Then, what about George's wife?"

Changtai said: "She means the same thing. Everyone says she, an illegitimate daughter, is not worthy of the Elector's heir, only the First Prince supports her in kicking George out and finding happiness."

Yinreng: "...This works too? Don't they know Big Brother says the same thing to others? They believe such perfunctory words?"

Changtai said: "I don't know about that."

Yinreng rubbed his temples, leaned back in his chair, and said with dull eyes: "Uncle, I want to be quiet for a while."

Changtai said: "Don't worry too much, the First Prince didn't do anything."

Yinreng gave a bitter smile.

Yes, Big Brother didn't do anything subjectively, but do you know how terrifying this butterfly effect can be?

Do you know that George will become George I? Do you know how much the marriage and children of George and this wife will affect world history?

The future marriage and bloodline of their children are the fuse of the First World War!

Wait, what does this have to do with our Qing Dynasty?

Yinreng suddenly sat up straight.

He rubbed his face, took a deep breath, and said: "I'm just obsessed. That's right, Big Brother really didn't do anything. George is your friend, if he can escape this marriage..."

Yinreng thought of George's poor wife who was imprisoned until her death.

George himself had mistresses, but he didn't allow his wife to have lovers, unlike other nobles who played their own games and didn't interfere with each other.

He murdered his wife's lover, divorced his wife, and imprisoned his ex-wife. If they divorced, this poor woman might not have been so miserable in the future.

Changtai was silent.

Yinreng smiled: "Uncle, you didn't stop Big Brother, could it be that you wanted Big Brother to do psychological work for this couple so they would really divorce?"

Changtai nodded very honestly: "I had this thought. Given his personality, being overly disgusted with this marriage might lead him to do things that hurt his wife. At that time, he and his children would probably be at odds."

Yinreng asked: "Does Big Brother know Uncle's thoughts?"

Changtai nodded again: "The First Prince knows, but... sigh, the First Prince said, it's hopeless, just wait for death."

Changtai shrugged helplessly.

Yinreng laughed out loud.

...

When Yinshi and Yinreng left Vienna, George and his wife hadn't divorced either. However, there was no more resentment or longing in the eyes of George's wife when she looked at George.

Could Big Brother's psychological therapy really be useful? Yinreng wasn't sure anymore.

They left Vienna this time because they received a grand invitation from the newly succeeded British King, James II.

Just like the history Yinreng knew, in February of this year, British King Charles II passed away, and James II succeeded to the throne.

The British throne struggle came to a temporary end, society was stable, and they could finally enter Britain.

This was also the last stop of their mission to Europe.

James II never expected that he could ascend the throne so smoothly. After ascending the throne, his first act was to write a letter to his old friend Yinshi, inviting Yinshi to visit Britain.

For James II, although he hadn't known Yinshi for long, when he was frustrated, only Yinshi was the friend who supported and comforted him without regard for interests.

The depth of friendship lies not in time, but in heart-to-heart connection.

Yinshi was James II's confidant.

Now that he had turned the tables and become king, he naturally thought of this confidant friend first.

Yinreng was envious.

He moved among the Western European nobles with great social skills and gained good reviews, but unlike Big Brother, he hadn't become a confidant with anyone.

By the way, Big Brother also made a bunch of confidants in Vienna.

This is truly a talent!

James II's confidant Yinshi, however, didn't treat James II as a confidant. He shook Yinreng's shoulders happily, asking if he could use James II to gain some benefits.

Isn't friendship meant to be used!

Yinreng was shaken until he was dizzy.

To get to Britain as quickly as possible, they took the waterway into the Baltic Sea and then headed straight to Britain.

The ship was already rocking violently, and Yinshi was still shaking him; Yinreng almost got seasick.

After kicking Yinshi away, he said: "It's just signing a trade treaty and a non-interference treaty, at most go to the Royal Society to find some talents. You are on good terms with James II, ask him for some apprentices from the Royal Society, he will definitely let them go."

Yinshi patted his chest with a loud thud: "Leave it to me!"

After patting his chest, Yinshi said proudly: "How do you think my eye for people is so good? I just casually met an old man, and he actually became a king?"

Yinreng wanted to say that this was an accident. But he suddenly thought that George, who treated Yinshi as a psychological counselor, would also become the British King later.

He wasn't sure anymore.

Could it be that his brother really had an inextricable bond with the British kings?

This must not be true.

"It's just a coincidence." Yinreng said, "Don't think too much."

Yinshi smiled: "A coincidence is worth it. I'll go back and brag to my younger brothers; they will definitely envy me."

Yinreng couldn't help but smile too: "That's for sure. Just with the many things we encountered on our mission and the many merits we established, the younger brothers will definitely be extremely envious."

In this life, his Big Brother had established military merits early on and became friends with the heirs of Western European nobles during the mission. His prestige among the younger brothers would definitely be unique.

Yinshi said: "That's natural. Being older is still good; we two have finished the work, and they can't find a place to establish merits even if they want to."

Thinking of this, Yinshi couldn't help but laugh out loud many times.

Every time Kangxi praised his sons, he liked to compare them with him.

When those younger brothers of his had just held the bow and gotten on the horse, Kangxi would praise the younger brothers as "about the same as the eldest" or "better than the eldest."

Although Yinshi didn't hold a grudge against his brothers, he had always been dissatisfied with Kangxi.

Next, he had established such great merits, let's see if Kangxi would still be embarrassed to say, "You are about the same as the eldest."

Heh heh.

Hearing Yinshi's complaints, Yinreng nodded constantly.

Although his Imperial Father in this life was already much better, his education for his sons was as terrible as ever.

Making sons compare internally like this, isn't that hurting the feelings between brothers? Father really doesn't know how to teach children.

"What if Father still lies with his eyes open?" Yinreng asked.

Yinshi said: "Then I will ask him bluntly, Father, you are lying with your eyes open; this is not setting a good example for the younger brothers."

Yinreng: "...Forget it, be careful of getting beaten."

Yinshi shrugged.

The brothers laughed and played on the ship and finally landed on the island of Great Britain.

James II, who came to greet them in person, although his hair was already gray, was full of ambition and high spirits, and was now a very majestic king.

James II first exchanged salutes with Yinreng, then gave Yinshi a bear hug between soldiers, still looking like good brothers with Yinshi.

Other ministers saw this scene, their smiles were extremely intoxicated, as if they had seen something that made them very happy.

Yinreng noted this strange scene and quietly inquired during the banquet.

Before he could find out, Yinshi found out first.

Yinshi said: "I saved a lady in the garden who climbed a tree to save a kitten and couldn't get down. The lady complained that the people in Parliament betrayed the Anglican Church for the sake of profit."

Yinreng: "Ah? What lady?"

What kind of cheesy romance novel anime plot is this?!

Yinshi was helpless: "What kind of look is that? Don't make it seem like I'm seducing a girl on the road. That lady is definitely older than my mother. Seeing her full of melancholy, I thought of my mother."

Yinreng said: "Actually, Concubine Hui is not full of melancholy when facing people other than you... That's not the point, continue, what profit?"

Yinshi said: "James and the First Prince of the Qing Dynasty are close friends. With the First Prince of the Qing Dynasty as a go-between, they will definitely be able to gain great benefits in trade with the Qing Dynasty. They even dream of supporting me to replace you on the throne of the Qing Emperor, hehe, it's really interesting."

Yinreng widened his eyes: "She even said this to you? Who is she?"

Yinshi said: "She said she is the daughter of James II, named Anne. I am brothers with James, so I had to ignore the seniority and call her sister Anne. Sister Anne said, I must protect you well. Her family has already been torn apart by the throne; she saw that we have a good relationship and hopes we won't break up because of the throne."

Yinreng: "..."

Yinreng: "Who? What is her name? What do you call her?"

Yinshi said: "Sister Anne. What's wrong? Do you also think it's strange that we ignore seniority? Actually, I wanted to call her Aunt Anne, but it's a bit unfair to brother James."

Yinreng: "Ah this..."

Yinshi scratched his head: "Her desperate and painful look is really too much like my mother, I couldn't help but feel close to her. Is it not good like this?"

Yinreng: "Concubine Hui's eyes are really not desperate and painful when she sees people other than you... That's not the point, the point is..."

The point is this Anne, she is also a future British King!!!

Yinreng was truly convinced.

He believed that his Big Brother might really have some unspeakable fate with the kings of the British Empire!

Besides William III and Mary who didn't become friends with Big Brother, how many British King friends has Big Brother made?!

Could it be that Britain will become a friendly nation of the Qing Dynasty in the future?

What kind of satirical novel is this! The "friendly nation" of "rather give to friendly nations" has really become a friendly nation?

Then, when the American War of Independence comes, should the Qing Dynasty participate in the war to help Britain?

When the Glorious Revolution comes, who will the Qing Dynasty help?

Yinreng's hands were shaking now.

He discovered that because of Yinshi's unintentional actions, it would have a huge impact on the Qing Dynasty's future foreign policy.

Yinshi was puzzled: "Brother, why is your face shaking so hard? Why are your eyes as desperate as Mother and Sister Anne's?"

Yinreng took a deep breath, deep breath.

What could he say? What could he say? He couldn't say anything!

Yinreng held his head: "Don't bother me, let me be quiet for a while, let me think, let me think, there must be a way."

Yinshi was anxious: "Did I do something wrong? Brother, don't scare me."

Yinreng held his head: "No, no, Big Brother, you didn't do anything wrong, you did very well. It's okay, it's okay, don't worry."

He decided, sign new treaties with all European royal families now! A true non-interference treaty!

In the future, the Qing Dynasty will not participate in your European wars, we only do business!

No matter who is king or who is in power, it has nothing to do with our Qing Dynasty!

Yinreng spat out half his soul.

Later he remembered that he didn't even remember the name of Leibniz, who had a dispute and shared credit with Newton on an important law, so it was normal not to remember this person's name.

Although Yinreng didn't know Hooke's reputation in history, Hooke's reputation in current British society was huge.

Hooke's research and invention/modification of the microscope were said to have influenced many British people to enter the field of science, including the current President of the British Royal Society.

Yinreng excitedly discussed microscopes and the microscopic world with him, and Hooke regarded him as a soulmate.

Hooke loved invention and creation and was particularly skilled in architectural design, so he had a lot in common with an "all-rounder" like Yinreng who knew a little bit about everything.

Although Hooke was living well in Britain now and had no plans to travel far, he was willing to establish a private friendship with Yinreng and communicate with him through the Great Qing Navy to answer Yinreng's questions.

Who could refuse a noble Crown Prince of a great nation who could talk to them so well?

After learning that Yinreng wanted to take a group of scientific talents who couldn't get ahead in Britain back to the Great Qing, Hooke introduced many talented but unrecognized people to Yinreng and vouched for him with his own status, letting those people leave with Yinreng with peace of mind.

Hooke was just a pure scientist; he didn't have many political considerations when facing Yinreng.

After Yinreng hit a wall with Newton, Hooke, as a local insider, helped Yinreng get familiar with the Royal Society and easily obtained a large number of talents.

When Yinreng left Britain, Hooke gave his books, manuscripts, and drawings to Yinreng.

"I don't trust my descendants who don't understand science, nor those clumsy students," Hooke laughed. "The Crown Prince said he wants to build a museum? Then please find a place for my life's work as well."

Yinreng solemnly took Hooke's manuscripts and drawings: "I will definitely keep them safe. If you ever have any trouble, come to the Great Qing."

Hooke laughed: "What trouble could I have? My status in the British Royal Society is very high."

Yinreng said: "That's true. Write often."

He actually managed to become friends with a scientist—ahem, Yinreng meant that there was actually a scientist whose words he could understand instead of pretending to understand. Yinreng was determined to cling to this scientist friend and write more letters.

Because Hooke was of humble birth and helped many "mud-legged" low-class people like teaching assistants and apprentices, he was not well-liked by the members of the Royal Society. Because of Hooke's friendship with the Great Qing Crown Prince, his status within the Royal Society rose, and there were fewer people speaking ill of him.

However, Hooke didn't care about this anyway and didn't participate in the internal power struggles of the society, so he didn't mind the gap in his status. He could publish books and had his own laboratory, and he always thought he was particularly valued and popular in the society.

Hooke: I'm not being hated.jpg.

On the ship leaving Britain, Yinreng couldn't help but mentally create a meme for his friend, amusing himself.

"What are you giggling at?" Yinzhi's attire was becoming increasingly casual; he was now wandering around the ship wearing the kind of white tank top often worn by street-lounging old men in later generations, holding a large cattail fan in his hand.

Yinreng said: "I was thinking that Hooke is so amazing; it would be great if he could come to the Great Qing."

Yinzhi said: "He sent all his students and disciples to you; rounding it up, that's half of him."

Yinreng laughed: "He's a real friend. Once this ship of people returns to the Great Qing, we can establish the Great Qing Royal Academy of Sciences. Hooke's students and assistants have strong hands-on skills and will definitely be able to make many scientific instruments for the Great Qing. With microscopes, the Great Qing's medical research will definitely advance by leaps and bounds."

Yinzhi was not so optimistic: "Not necessarily. Is it certain that what is correct will be promoted? You don't know how stubborn those imperial physicians in the Imperial Hospital are. Just do it first; at worst, I'll arrange for these people to go to my fief."

Kangxi's letter said that he was already haggling with the ministers to secure an overseas fief for Yinzhi.

The Great Qing didn't have many overseas exclaves now, and Yinreng guessed that Kangxi might find a piece of land for Yinzhi near the Strait of Malacca or in Annam to serve as a fief, while also echoing the Great Qing Navy.

Yinzhi himself wanted the land in North America. But the Great Qing was relatively conservative now; land in South Asia was fine, as it had been China's sphere of influence since ancient times; but going to such a distant place to expand territory and actively starting a war with "friendly nations" made the ministers very uncomfortable.

Kangxi was also considering that the Great Qing needed to seize the opportunity brought by this mission to recuperate for a period of time, accumulate national strength, and did not plan to expand outward for the time being.

Yinzhi was full of anger and had to encourage his good friend James II to develop in the New World.

He really didn't understand what was worth lingering over in a small island nation like Britain. When James was the supreme commander of the navy, he had personally captured New York in the New World and had quite a reputation there; why not go to the New World?

With such vast land and such chaotic order, wasn't it perfect for James to develop?

If he were James, wouldn't it be better to move the capital to the New World and use the more vast land as the national territory?

"James seems to be almost persuaded by me," Yinzhi said, fanning himself with the large cattail fan. "Actually, I kind of regret it. What if he really goes? It would be quite awkward if I met him on the battlefield. But at his age, he might not live that long."

Yinzhi estimated that it would be another ten years before Kangxi let him out to roam again. In these ten years, he would have to marry, have children, and establish a firm footing in the imperial court.

Yinreng's mouth twitched.

If James II really went to North America and established a New Britain, the future American War of Independence might be a bit... ahem.

Interesting.

Yinreng had already figured it out. This would just make the West more chaotic. Chaos is good; even if it doesn't disturb the future historical process, it's good to give the Great Qing more time to develop.

"Ah, I really don't want to go back," Yinzhi said, his face full of depression. "Even if I get a fief, I probably won't be able to live there until I'm thirty or forty."

Yinreng asked: "Why?"

Yinzhi gently tapped Yinreng's head with the fan: "You grew up by the Imperial Father's side; don't you understand his desire for control? A fief is one thing, but whether you can go to the fief is another. I probably won't be able to stay in the fief permanently until you ascend the throne."

Yinreng had black lines on his forehead. So the "thirty or forty" you mentioned refers to me ascending the throne when you are thirty or forty?

"Not necessarily. Maybe when you have a son, Khan Father will let you go," Yinreng didn't refute the claim that Kangxi had a strong desire for control.

Kangxi might allow Yinzhi to fight in the south and north, but he would definitely have to live in the capital after returning. That piece of land was said to be for Yinzhi, but in reality, Yinzhi only enjoyed the tax revenue and offerings. Only after the new emperor ascended the throne would the vassal kings go to their fiefs.

Before Kangxi died, his sons couldn't pull off any tricks; after Kangxi passed away, sending his sons far away from the national territory to prevent them from killing each other was a very good method.

Originally, the Great Qing's control over land outside the Central Plains was weak. Even if the Great Qing's princes completely controlled the local power, it was at least better than those vassal states that submitted; the meat would still be in their own bowl.

However, there were exceptions. For example, if Kangxi really couldn't stand Yinzhi and drove him away early.

Yinzhi said: "Seeing the deaths of these dozen or so children in the Western royal family..."

Yinzhi frowned tightly: "I have to talk to Mother and have the Princess Consort take care of her health first, and wait until she's over twenty before we talk about having children."

Yinreng nodded. He thought the same.

With Big Brother having this kind of thinking, Sister-in-law probably won't die young in the future, right?

When Kangxi's letter stating that the Great Qing would remain neutral forever reached the various kings of the West, Yinreng and Yinzhi also received a urging letter from Kangxi.

Kangxi not only wrote to urge them but also issued an imperial decree directly to the other envoys of the Great Qing mission, requiring them not to delay halfway and to return at full speed.

If the urging letter and the imperial decree could still be excused by "the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank are abroad, and the imperial decree cannot be fully complied with," the letter from the Empress Dowager made Yinreng and Yinzhi have to return immediately.

The Empress Dowager said she was old and her health was getting worse by the day, and she hoped Yinreng and Yinzhi would return soon, fearing she wouldn't see them one last time.

Yinreng remembered that the Empress Dowager wouldn't pass away so soon, but there were always exceptions, so the Great Qing mission naturally rushed back with their lives on the line.

Kangxi was extremely humane to his ministers most of the time. When his imperial decree arrived, it brought along family letters for the ministers.

When Yinreng learned that Cao Yin's father had passed away, he was stunned for a moment.

He didn't have a good relationship with Cao Yin in his first life, didn't look highly upon the bondservants around Kangxi, and naturally didn't remember when Cao Yin's father passed away.

If he had known, he might not have brought Cao Yin on the mission.

Now that Cao Yin hadn't seen his father one last time, Yinreng felt very guilty.

Cao Yin was sad for a few days, but seeing that Yinreng was even sadder than him, he pulled himself together.

"My father's letter to me said that he was very happy that I was on the way to the mission when he passed away," Cao Yin privately shared the letter with Yinreng. "Father said that if I were in the country, I would already be shouldering family responsibilities. Now, at least before I shoulder those responsibilities, I can measure more land with my legs and see a wider world with my eyes."

The "Weaving Official" (Zhizao) was an official and also an imperial merchant, responsible for purchasing and managing all silk products used in the imperial palace in Jiangnan.

The Weaving Official would deal with all kinds of people and find it very easy to gather information, serving as the emperor's eyes and ears. Although the official rank was not high, even the local top official had to be respectful to them.

For such an important position, Kangxi would only trust the Cao family father and son.

It was just that Cao Yin had the talent to be ennobled, but could only stay in a small position like the Weaving Official, and Cao Yin's father was actually very sad about it.

Although Cao Yin only secretly showed the letter to Yinreng, since Yinreng saw it, it was equivalent to Yinzhi seeing it.

Yinzhi was very dissatisfied: "Did the Imperial Father not feel moved after seeing this letter? Letting Ziqing follow me is better than being some imperial merchant. Anyone can be an imperial merchant as long as they are honest. Ziqing is talented in both literature and martial arts, a material for a general or a prime minister; why?"

Yinreng patted Yinzhi's shoulder and just sighed softly.

In fact, they both understood "why." The Great Qing was not short of materials for generals and prime ministers, but the emperor was very short of people he could fully trust.

Kangxi would definitely compensate Cao Yin in other ways, but Cao Yin had to sit in this position of Weaving Official.

"Perhaps we can change the position of the Weaving Official; just buying and selling silk—this position is too idle," Yinreng said, lying through his teeth.

The Weaving Official was actually very busy, and the bulk of their work was not buying and selling silk.

Yinzhi said: "You mean... maritime trade?"

Yinreng nodded: "Fully opening the seas—we can't let Guangdong, Guangxi, and Fujian have all the fun; Nanjing can also set up a trade port. Moreover, Nanjing's location is special, and a naval base should also be set up. The navy needs to escort merchant ships, so it's normal to give Ziqing an official post."

Yinzhi nodded repeatedly and gave Yinreng a thumbs up: "Little brother is still the most thoughtful."

Yinreng said: "Don't tell Ziqing yet; I don't know if it will succeed. Once we succeed, we'll give Ziqing a surprise."

Yinzhi grinned: "I wonder if Ziqing will cry then. If he cries, I'll have Rongruo paint a picture of him crying."

Yinreng also followed with a mischievous laugh.

What a pity, what a pity, there's no camera, otherwise, hehehe.

I hope the talents of the Great Qing Royal Academy of Sciences can come up with a camera as soon as possible. I want to leave photos with my family at my most handsome, so as not to let those painters artistically process me into an ugly man.

If the camera is only invented when I'm old, I won't leave any photos.

"I wonder if the little brothers still remember us?" Feeling homesick, Yinreng looked at several boxes of gifts for his younger brothers and worried.

Yinzhi wasn't worried at all: "Don't remember? Then beat them a few more times; they'll remember after being beaten."

Yinreng: "...No need."

He felt even more anxious.

His eldest brother had become completely wild during the diplomatic mission. Once they returned to the Great Qing, he expected there would be quite a lot of chaos.

He hoped their father’s temper was as good as it had been when they left, and that he wouldn't hold it against his eldest brother.

While Yinreng and Yinzhi were on their return voyage, Kangxi checked the calendar and counted the days every single day.

There had been many troublesome matters in the Great Qing over the past two years, and Kangxi had even made a southern inspection tour to keep the southern gentry in check.

If not for Yinreng’s letters, Kangxi might not have been able to hold on.

Kangxi had never imagined that without Yinreng there to tease him, accompany him in reviewing memorials, and help him resolve his worries, his stress would be so immense.

Kangxi now had wrinkles between his brows, and his temper had grown increasingly volatile.

Furthermore, the Grand Empress Dowager was ill more often and lacked the energy to counsel him, Noble Consort Tong no longer received his special favor, and Changtai was far away overseas; there was actually no one in the entire imperial court who could privately console Kangxi.

The younger princes, who used to stand up against Kangxi alongside the Crown Prince and the First Prince, were now more obedient than ever, showing increasing awe and fear toward him, and they spent less and less time looking up at him to act spoiled.

Having been emperor for so many years, Kangxi should have long been accustomed to being a lonely man.

But after the Crown Prince was born, he had been entangled by that ignorant and fearless little life. Coupled with that knowledgeable and fearless fellow, the First Prince, Kangxi had lived nearly ten years of a lively life and was actually no longer used to being a lonely man.

Late at night, Kangxi would sometimes rest his head on his hand and fall asleep right there in the Qianqing Palace study. When he woke up, he would look around blankly, calling out "Baocheng," feeling a sense of desolation.

Later generations would call him an "empty-nester" during this time.

It was ironic. Clearly, only two people were missing from the palace, and clearly, Kangxi still had many people around him—even the number of princes and princesses had increased, though some had died young—yet Kangxi felt like an empty-nester.

When Yinreng and Yinzhi passed through the Strait of Malacca again and stopped to rest at the Great Qing city that had begun construction, Kangxi saw the estimated arrival time in Tianjin that they had mentioned in their letters.

He thought for a moment and decided to make another southern inspection tour, waiting for the Great Qing envoys directly in Nanjing.

He couldn't wait even a few more days.

The younger princes also received the news that their brothers were finally coming back.

Yinzhi, who had grown into a sturdy young lad, pouted and almost cried just like he did when he was little.

His brothers had been gone for nearly three years, and he had grown up. But these days felt no different from when he was a child.

Clearly, his brothers were already stirring up trouble in the imperial court at his age, yet he found it difficult just to keep up with his studies.

Clearly, when his brothers were around, he never had to worry about his studies. Back when he was still wobbly on his feet, he would follow them to cause mischief in the court.

"Who’s to say otherwise?" Yinzhen said listlessly, "Before I even started school, I followed Crown Prince brother and eldest brother to find trouble for corrupt officials. Now that I’ve been in school for two years, I can’t even find a chance to leave the palace."

Yinqi nodded vigorously.

He had also started school, but his progress was extremely slow; he was always being scolded by his tutors and punished by his father.

Back then, he was clearly held by Crown Prince brother and called a "little genius," a genius even more impressive than a talent!

Why did he become stupid the moment Crown Prince brother left?

This must be the fault of Crown Prince brother for abandoning me. QAQ.

"The little ones barely remember Crown Prince brother and eldest brother anymore," Yinzhen added, "Little Six, Little Seven, and Little Eight clearly cried when Crown Prince brother left the capital, but now they’ve completely put him out of their minds. Not to mention the rest of the younger brothers."

Yinzhen was very dissatisfied. Crown Prince brother used to be so good to Little Six, Seven, and Eight; how could they forget him?

Forgetting the eldest brother was one thing—the eldest brother wasn't a good person and loved to bully his younger brothers. But the games they played and the literacy cards they looked at were all left behind by Crown Prince brother; how could they be like this?

Little ungrateful wolves!

When Crown Prince brother returns, I’m going to complain to him and tell him not to play with them!

Yinzhen thought indignantly.

Yinzhi said with an air of maturity: "They are too young; it’s normal for them to forget. At least when they play with the toys Crown Prince brother made, they still remember his kindness."

Yinzhi felt very tired.

When the two brothers were around, he had never felt that playing with his younger brothers was any trouble.

Now that he was left alone, he realized how exhausting it was to visit his younger brothers every day.

Yinzhi’s daily studies were already tiring enough. He could have some common ground with the brothers who were already in school, but he really lacked the patience to play with those who weren't in school or were still drinking milk.

They were noisy, messy, and couldn't understand human speech—it was so annoying.

Yinzhi wondered, when Crown Prince brother was playing with him back then, was he actually quite annoying too?

But Crown Prince brother really, really liked him, always hugging and nuzzling him, saying he loved playing with him the most.

Crown Prince brother wouldn't lie, so it must be that he just lacked patience and his own love for his younger brothers wasn't enough.

Yinzhi felt a bit discouraged. Would Crown Prince brother be disappointed when he returned? Disappointed that he hadn't taken good care of the younger brothers.

"Third brother, what’s wrong?" Yinqi asked in a low voice, seeing Yinzhi’s expression.

Yinzhi twitched his lips: "I’m worried that when Crown Prince brother returns, he’ll say I didn't take good care of the younger brothers."

Yinqi said: "How could that be? Third brother has already done well enough."

Yinzhen also nodded: "We are so busy, yet we still go to see the younger brothers every day or two, and they still complain about us; we’ve done enough. We aren't Crown Prince brother, who has infinite patience for the younger brothers. Why does Crown Prince brother like them so much?"

Yinqi said honestly: "I don't know either. After taking care of them, I realized how troublesome they are. I couldn't even speak properly back then; I must have been even more troublesome."

The three younger brothers sighed in unison.

Yes, they had started to reflect.

Yinzhi remembered himself running around and stuttering;

Yinzhen remembered himself constantly causing trouble and being long-winded;

Yinqi remembered himself being slow to speak and walk, and being called a little fool by others...

They were all troublesome brothers to the Crown Prince.

"Shall we go beg Father to allow us to go to Nanjing together to welcome Crown Prince brother?" Yinzhen said, "I want to see Crown Prince brother sooner."

Yinzhi gritted his teeth: "Let’s go, together!"

Yinqi also nodded, gathering his courage.

Over the past two years, they had become increasingly afraid of Kangxi and never dared to make requests of him. But this time, they were going all out!

Seeing the three young princes come together for once, Kangxi put down his memorial and listened to what they had to say.

When he heard that Yinzhi, Yinzhen, and Yinqi wanted to go to Nanjing together to wait for the Crown Prince, he was stunned for a moment, then gave his sons a rare, gentle, and kind smile: "Alright. Ask the other princes; those who want to go can come along."

Yinzhi breathed a sigh of relief.

He went to ask the sixth, seventh, and eighth princes who were already in school. Although these three princes’ impressions of the Crown Prince and the eldest brother had faded, they still raised their hands and jumped with both feet, saying they wanted to go too.

They only vaguely remembered a brother who was very good to them, and a brother who always bullied them but would also protect them—a brother who was neither good nor bad.

But whether they were close or not didn't matter; they were going out to play!

The other princes were too young, so Yinzhi didn't bother them.

Thus, the ones going to Nanjing to welcome Yinreng and Yinzhi were still the same princes as before.

When Yinreng and Yinzhi finished resting in Taiwan, changed into new clothes, groomed themselves, organized their goods, and left some people behind, they boarded a steamship, left the main fleet with the other officials, and sailed toward Nanjing first.

The foreign talents and items that Yinreng had collected were on the larger ships behind, sailing slowly and directly to Tianjin Port.

They had spent the New Year on the return journey, and it was now the sixth month of the 25th year of Kangxi’s reign; the weather was extremely hot.

Yinzhi really wanted to tear off his prince’s long robe.

While sailing on the sea, they were in more southern regions, and Yinzhi had been wearing a white undershirt the whole time.

Now, having changed back into Great Qing attire and covering his body tightly, he felt incredibly uncomfortable, as if ants were crawling all over him, and he kept tugging at his clothes.

Yinreng was extremely helpless: "Eldest brother, stop tugging. What will it look like when Father sees you? Do you want to be beaten by Father in front of all the officials?"

Yinzhi pulled his collar askew and said weakly: "I’ll go change my clothes first and change back when we’re about to reach the shore."

After saying that, he ran off.

Yinreng hesitated for a moment, rubbed his nose, and followed Yinzhi into the cabin to change clothes.

The Great Qing envoys stood on the bow for a while to catch the breeze and also took off their official robes.

Ahem, it wasn't that they disregarded etiquette; they were just thinking that if they soaked their clothes in sweat now, they wouldn't look good later.

Only when they saw the coastline did they use the last of the fresh water on the ship, each cleaning their bodies with wet towels, grooming their hair, and putting on their official robes and formal attire.

When Yinzhi put on his prince’s hat, his complexion and expression were as if he were heading to the execution ground.

When Kangxi, with tears streaming down his face, went to welcome Yinreng and Yinzhi, he saw Yinzhi’s "dead-father" face and swallowed his tears back.

Kangxi asked: "What is this expression on the First Prince’s face?"

Are you very dissatisfied with me!

Yinzhi said weakly: "Father, Imperial Father, my good father, can you stop with all these ceremonies? Let’s hurry up and get in the carriage to return to the capital; your son is about to die of heat."

He tugged at his prince’s formal hat and then his formal robe.

"It’s all sweat," Yinzhi said, "I can’t take it anymore."

Kangxi: "..."

Kangxi raised his palm.

Yinreng reflexively hugged Kangxi’s arm: "Father, forget it, forget it. You know eldest brother’s temper, don't you? He’s just that kind of person, he has no bad intentions. The weather is really too hot; eldest brother is just awkwardly caring about you, worried you’ll get heatstroke! The emperor’s formal robes are so heavy; eldest brother feels bad for you!"

Yinzhi immediately came to his senses and nodded like a garlic-pounding machine: "That’s right, that’s right, your son is worried about you, Father. You must be very hot, right? Your face is covered in sweat. Father, let’s hurry and get in the carriage to return to the capital."

Kangxi: "..." I believe your nonsense!

The officials behind Kangxi watched this scene.

Hmm, this scene is so nostalgic.

The younger brothers, who were hesitating and not daring to come forward from a distance behind Kangxi: "..."

Little Eight said softly: "I... I remember now!"

Little Seven nodded: "That’s right, it’s eldest brother and Crown Prince brother."

Little Six also covered his mouth and cried: "Crown Prince brother and eldest brother are back!"

The other three princes: "..."

Don't know what to say, the mood is a bit complicated.
