151.三更（补周五欠更） [V]
查木杨得到曹寅拜帖之后，愣了许久。
他不是发愣曹寅来找他，而是发愣曹寅现在才来找他。
他还以为民变的事，曹寅会第一时间来拜访自己。
即使当时镇压民变的是地方衙役，但八旗地方驻军的主要职责就是镇压各地叛乱，曹寅理应先来问他。
至于文武差别，曹寅曾在军中效力，并以武官身份陪同太子出访国外，理应不会太在意文武差别。只有汉臣才比较在乎文武差别。
“快请。”查木杨道。
他让人整理了一下书房，并匆匆打理了一下仪容。
查木杨虽然现在是正一品的杭州将军，但曹寅是天子心腹，他可不敢狂妄。
曹寅进门之后，行了武将之间的礼，然后让人守在门外，并请查木杨把人都遣走，说有重要的事要和查木杨说。
查木杨忙让自己的心腹站在门窗处守着，关上门道：“难道曹侍卫有皇上的旨意？”
曹寅现在还未继任江宁织造，只身上还挂着御前侍卫的官职。
曹寅站起来，走到椅子后面挺胸站立，手放在了腰间的佩刀上。
垂首站在曹寅身后的小厮抬起头，走到椅子前坐下。
查木杨愕然。
胤礽道：“孤贸然来访，希望将军不要介意。孤身份需要保密，将军不必行礼。”
查木杨看着笑意盈盈，脸上被涂成蜡黄色的胤礽，脑袋空白了好几秒。
胤礽不催促，只继续笑着看着查木杨。
查木杨终于回过神，从胤礽的自称中猜出胤礽的身份。
他立刻站起啦，正准备下跪，又想起胤礽让他不要行礼，一时间站也不是跪也不是坐更不是，惶恐难安。
“将军请坐。”胤礽微笑道，“皇父曾与孤说，查木杨将军从蒙古正蓝旗护军统领擢升至杭州将军，诸事都办得井井有条，是个能臣。”
曹寅腹诽。太子又在胡说八道，皇上绝对什么都没说过。
查木杨却不认为太子会撒谎。
他虚着半个屁股坐在椅子上，感动道：“谢皇上谬赞！末将不敢当！”
胤礽道：“曹寅本该一来杭州就拜见你，不过皇父让他多查一些事，所以现在才来，将军不要怪罪。将军可有事要报知孤？”
查木杨苦笑：“末将得知的事，已经早早写了折子呈给皇上。末将刚来杭州不久，对杭州还不熟悉。”
胤礽手指轻轻敲了一下椅背，曹寅从怀里取出一个小账本，递给查木杨后，回到胤礽身后继续护卫。
胤礽道：“杭州富商王家急着出手这些桑田。据孤了解，这些桑田曾是旗营屯田。”
查木杨呼吸一滞，赶紧打开账本，和记忆细细比对。
他能从正二品的护军统领，被康熙直接越级提拔成正一品的杭州将军，能力相当不错。
来杭州的第一时间，他就埋头看旗营各项支出产出，知道后勤才是八旗军营整顿的基础。
虽他不记得旗营所有田地，但这片地正好在旗营屯田包围中，显然当初圈地的时候，不可能放过这一片地。
查木杨立刻严肃道：“能请太子殿下稍等一下吗？末将想查一查账本。”
胤礽轻轻抬起一只手：“请便。”
查木杨向胤礽告罪之后，打开一点窗户，对心腹说了几句话。
不一会儿，心腹就抱着一堆账本进屋。
胤礽没有起身。
心腹目不斜视地从胤礽身边走过，然后飞速离开屋内，没有询问，也没有好奇，可见查木杨治兵能力之强。
“曹寅，你去帮一下查木杨将军。”胤礽道。
曹寅犹豫了一下，把腰上刀解下递给胤礽后，才去帮查木杨。
查木杨看到这一幕，再次确认曹寅在皇帝和太子心中的地位。
听到太子命令之后没有立刻遵命，而是自主做出改变，这得太子非常信任曹寅、和曹寅非常亲近，曹寅才会习惯这样。
胤礽信任查木杨，但曹寅和胤礽学会了万事有最坏的打算。
胤礽的武艺不错，进兵营的时候因扮成小厮，没有带武器。若查木杨突然发难，这柄刀会派上用场。
不过若八旗军营哗变，就算太子有武器也很难逃出去吧？
曹寅心里很无奈。
太子有时候算无遗策，凡事都会思考最坏的情况；有时候又特别大胆，听说独身闯可能哗变的军营，都不是第一次了。
也不知道该说他家太子是谨慎好，还是胆大鲁莽好。
“这个！”查木杨率先翻到，“这是康熙初年的屯田名单！确实有这一片田！”
胤礽走上前，看了一眼账本时间：“觉罗柯魁？那家伙卖的啊，当初居然没有查出来。”
他讥笑道：“看来当初柯魁的案子并没有好好查。”
柯魁案发生的时候，胤礽还未出生。不过他听康熙说过这个案子。
爱新觉罗在记载姓氏的时候并不写完，而是称“觉罗氏”，就像是几个乌拉那拉氏都可以叫“纳兰氏”一样。
觉罗柯魁，便是一个宗室。
觉罗柯魁任杭州将军期间，侵占近一千五百间民房，圈地无数，纵容手下骑兵飞扬跋扈，放例子钱，导致杭州民不聊生，和当地地方官势同水火。
可惜大清刚入关没多久的时候根本不查贪污，觉罗柯魁身为宗室无人敢查，直到卷入庄氏《明史》文字狱案，才被革职拿办。
现在柯魁在京中当个闲散宗室，每日逛街遛鸟，快活得很。
“柯魁卖的地？是他能做出来的事。”胤礽叹气，“但柯魁被革职查办的时候，京中来人顺带查了查贪污受贿的事，该追回的应该都已追回，该上缴的据说都已经上缴国库。这些地怎么还在王家手中？”
查木杨没回答。
他不知道说什么。这些事他真的不知道。
胤礽也不是让查木杨回答，他只是自言自语，自己叹了口气。
“这肯定不是个例。当年柯魁贪腐，或许还有很多东西没查出来。二十多年了，现在才浮出水面吗？还是说，这其中有更多的东西？”胤礽看着桌面上的账本，“这些和浙江民变又有什么关系。”
见太子开始沉思，查木杨和曹寅都不敢说话，怕打断太子的思路。
半晌，胤礽又叹了一口气，道：“或许没什么关联，只是凑巧。有人来查，王家怕购买旗营屯田的事败露，以防万一先出手而已。”
曹寅道：“私自购买旗营屯田一事，就足以给王家定罪。太子殿下，我们可以先抓人，再慢慢审问。”
胤礽摇了摇头：“王家算什么？且让他们再挣扎一下。查木杨将军……”
胤礽的手伸进袖口中，摸出一枚兵符，轻轻放在桌面上：“孤只问你一句，杭州旗营会谋逆吗？”
查木杨看着兵符，瞳孔剧烈颤抖。
他顾不上可能会让外面的心腹知道太子的身份，立刻跪下：“末将誓死效忠皇上！”
胤礽摇了摇头：“不是你，是杭州旗营。”
查木杨双拳握紧，犹豫了一下，咬牙道：“杭州旗营末将能控制七成。”
胤礽道：“剩下三成的将领如何？”
查木杨道：“他们与当地士族有勾连。”
不是豪商王家，而是士族，是诗书传家的士族。
胤礽道：“孤命你把那些人的兵权缴了。他们若老老实实下狱，之后若发现清白，孤会补偿他们。”
查木杨仰起头：“那……不老实呢？”
胤礽垂眸：“见兵符不从，你问孤？”
查木杨垂首跪拜：“末将领命。”
胤礽道：“给你五日时间。五日之后，你来曹寅处回报孤。”
他把兵符丢给查木杨，查木杨惊恐地接住兵符。
“兵符放你这，五日后还给孤。”胤礽开玩笑道，“孤信任你，你不要辜负孤的信任。”
查木杨后背已经被冷汗打湿：“末将绝不辜负太子殿下信任！请太子殿下静候佳音！”
“回去了吧。”胤礽道，“五日时间，够奠定乾坤了。”
胤礽走出门的那一刻，又变成了小厮。
他低着头唯唯诺诺战战兢兢，似乎很害怕兵营中的气氛。
曹寅趾高气昂，目中无人，把文人的清高和皇帝近臣的傲慢表现得淋漓尽致。
心腹进门：“将军，那一位是……”
查木杨紧紧攥着兵符，声音微微颤抖：“别问。”
心腹赶紧道：”是！“
查木杨闭上眼，半晌，他睁开眼时，眼中血丝弥漫。
他点了几个人的名字，让心腹依次将人叫进门。
……
马车上，曹寅忐忑道：“有、有那么严重吗？”
直接清理军营？
胤礽无奈：“子清啊，我来这可不是为了那个小小的民变。”
曹寅呆滞。不是为了民变，那是为了……
他直觉太子这次搞事将搞得非常大。

152.二更合一 [V]
五日后，谣言传遍了整个杭州城。
繁华的街道变得萧条，民众们脸上都带着忧色。
杭州知府试图禁止谣言，但他下令之后，却迷茫发现，谣言比之前传得更加凶猛，原本不相信的人也相信了，连衙役都找借口跑了不少。
杭州知府找到杭州巡抚，想从巡抚大人那里探探口风。
杭州巡抚金鋐刚上任一年就遇到了浙江民变的事。他本就愁得头发大把大把掉，现在听到城中又有谣言，以为是哪个反清复明的家伙出来搞风搞雨，顿时紧张万分。
金鋐向曹寅抱怨此事，向曹寅询问圣上的意思。
曹寅脸上的微笑差点没挂住。
反清复明清太子？你知道你在说什么吗？
曹寅叹气：“我只说浙江如果有人谋逆，肯定大军会入境。这都传成什么了？你说大清这些年对南方百姓也不错吧，为何他们还是怕八旗军队？”
金鋐在心里吐槽，你这不是说废话吗？谁能不怕？
刀落在你祖辈头上的时候，你怕吗？
哦，你家是包衣，八旗的刀曾经落在你祖上过，你是不要脸的奴仆。
金鋐腹诽了一顿之后，恭敬道：“我们是不是该问问查木杨将军？若是平叛，肯定地方上这点兵不够用。”
曹寅疑惑道：“一些手无寸铁的平民百姓而已，你们地方上的兵还不够用？难道那群人刀枪不入？”
金鋐道：“这不是担心有反清复明的人浑水摸鱼吗？”
曹寅道：“若需要动用八旗，肯定得上面发令，我们去干什么？”
金鋐问道：“曹侍卫，你之前去八旗营地，查木杨将军怎么说？”
曹寅叹气：“他当然说了些尽忠职守的空话套话，还能说什么？他也是刚上任不久，对杭州的事了解不多。”
金鋐想问的不是这个。他想问的是，旗营会不会真的出手。
虽然调动八旗军队需要皇上兵符，但驻防将军有在管辖地范围内自主出兵平乱的权力。
但曹寅这一问三不知的模样，让金鋐闭了嘴。
他怀疑，这个嘴上无毛的年轻人估计知道得不多，脑子不怎么聪明，就是凭借着听话和一张好脸，才被圣上看重。
金鋐不说话了，曹寅还在继续说。
他长吁短叹，说什么要在离开之前再开一次文会，以后来杭州的时间就少了。
金鋐听得眼皮子直跳。
这种丝毫不关心自己要办的正事，只一心想着开文会的人，他耻于为伍。
金鋐便随意找了一个借口离开。
他离开之后，给他奉茶的小厮抬起头道：“他一定在心里骂了你无数次。”
曹寅站起来，给胤礽倒茶：“骂吧骂吧，我都习惯了。”
胤礽道：“等真相揭开，他就不敢骂你，而是怕你了。”
曹寅苦笑：“锅都臣来背？”
胤礽道：“这么大的锅怎么可能我们俩背？那自然让汗阿玛背。”
曹寅立刻道：“算了算了，我背就我背，别劳烦皇上老人家。”
胤礽差点把茶喷出来：“我爹那都能称老人家了？”
曹寅严肃道：“这是尊称。底下的人称呼你，也是太子他老人家。”
胤礽：“……很好，很有精神。”
谁敢当着他的面喊“太子老人家”，看我不放我哥哥弟弟揍死他们。
胤礽喝了一会儿茶，曹寅帮他按摩了一下肩膀和手臂，缓解伺候金鋐几个时辰的痛苦后，他伸了个懒腰，道：“等查木杨将军来，流言可以散播第二阶段了。”
曹寅刚应下，就听闻杭州将军来访。
查木杨进屋的时候，虽没有披甲，胤礽却能感受到他身上未散去的血腥气。
这血腥气不是鼻子嗅的，是直觉。
这五日，查木杨显然动了刀子，还能是亲自动刀子。
查木杨见屋内只有曹寅和太子两人，不再伪装，干净利落的跪下奉回兵符：“末将已经将军队全部控制妥当，随时等候太子殿下差遣。”
胤礽把兵符拿在手中把玩：“不听令的人，你写份折子给我，我亲手交给皇父。我相信将军，一定不会滥杀无辜。”
胤礽说着信任的话，查木杨却冒出了一头冷汗：“末将遵命。”
胤礽收起兵符，道：“请起吧，随便找个座位坐。曹寅，你也坐着，不用伺候。将军，你拔营在这几个地方切断要道，我会给杭州巡抚下令，让他不准百姓出城。遇到硬闯的，格杀勿论，罪责我来担。”
查木杨一头冷汗冒得更多了：“末将听令！”
胤礽笑道：“别紧张。这仗打不起来。你只需要摆出架势喊话，不会有人冲击关卡。”
查木杨擦了擦额头的冷汗，问道：“末将能冒昧询问太子殿下意欲如何吗？”
杭州将军好歹是正一品的武官，可以和太子以商量的语气说话。
胤礽微笑道：“我只是想让他们体面的自首。如果他们不想体面，就让杭州城里的老百姓，帮他们体面。”
查木杨没听懂。
别说查木杨，曹寅替胤礽做了这么多事，他自己都没听懂。
曹寅提前来杭州几个月，可不是真的如表现出的那样，除了开文会，什么都没做。
曹寅跟着胤礽出访几年，因为脸长得好看，在欧洲搜集情报的工作，基本都是交给他和纳兰性德负责。
比起在人生地不熟的欧洲搜集情报，根据胤礽所教的“万物皆有联系”思维，曹寅很快就把这次事件中可能出手的家族的名单和背后的原因整理好了。
这份名单也已经到了康熙手中。
现在曹寅为难的是，“没证据”。
这“没证据”的意思是，没有账本、物品、证人之类比较明显的证据。那些人有恃无恐，也明白如果没有证据，大清不会轻易抓人，得罪南方士族。
大清在南方本就很难收得起税。因为之前几次兵祸，平民百姓死得差不多，好地都被世族豪门捡了。世族豪门不交税，剩下那点百姓就算榨骨头，都榨不出几滴油。
南方富裕，却年年抗税年年哭穷，这当然不是因为老百姓刁蛮不服管，而是因为他们真的交不起。
如果得罪南方士族，大清这税就更收不上来。南方士族就是以此和大清朝廷抗衡。
胤礽认为这群人胆子很大。
因为几十年前，大清是不服管的都砍了，世族豪门死得少是因为跑得快，不是八旗不敢杀。
现在大清勉强算太平了，他们就认为大清的天子应该是以前的那种太平天子，该被他们钳制了。
胤礽不得不说……咳，他们说得很对。如果不造反，这件事很难解决。
那就局部地区造反吧。
五日后，谣言越演越烈。
胤礽把曹寅搜集到的消息，全部散播了出去。
哪家哪户见了哪些人，推举谁当出头鸟，为了自己能走私而雇佣地痞流氓伪造民变，给朝廷施加压力，这些都说得有鼻子有眼。
有些事是曹寅查到的，有些事是胤礽根据真实证据编的。
反正这个时代传谣不犯法。就算犯法，抓犯人也抓不到他大清皇太子头上。
除了大部分真实的消息之外，胤礽还传了许多假消息，半真半假混着玩。
比如某些耕读世家官宦世家在清军来的时候早早剃头，还帮忙镇压老百姓。现在大清说不剃头了，还澄清剃头令就是这帮人上书搞的，他们面子上挂不住，要反了大清。
他们这反也不是真的反，就是给大清一种南方人不服管教的印象，好继续推动剃头令。
谣言还称，他们甚至想再在南方搞几次屠杀，这样他们上能得到大清朝廷的信任，下能侵占更多的田地，那真是秦始皇吃花椒，赢麻了。
谣言一出，居然比这群人为了走私想禁海的真事流传得还广。
无论在哪个时代，都是最耸人听闻的谣言流传更广。
老百姓们不认为自己耸人听闻。
都要把八旗引来屠杀了，你说你就想走个私，谁信啊！
谣言蔓延之后，八旗军队拔营，在浙江各处要道驻扎。
浙江各地知府也接到了不准百姓擅自离开居住地的命令，以免误杀。
知府知县们挨家挨户通知，生怕哪些无知的老百姓去冲卡。
老百姓们也老实。他们一辈子被束缚在土地上，除非活不下去了，否则根本没有勇气乱跑。
现在兵祸可能又要来了，他们当然乖乖待在家里，免得出去乱跑被砍死。
村里的老百姓还好，城里人就痛苦了。
一旦商业中断，城池就像是被围住了一样，物资供应出现问题，许多老百姓都将面临断粮的危机。
其他城市还好，和村里还能继续交流，粮食能运进来。杭州城不准进也不准出，简直像一座死城。
还好新来的华家有良心，卖粮食居然按照封城前的金钱来卖，不囤积居奇，虽然每日有限额，那限额也能够老百姓吃饱肚子了，勉强保持了杭州城的稳定。
华家有良心，其他豪商大族可就脑子活络了。
他们当然要赚钱涨价。至于会不会死人，他们会开粥铺施舍免费粥给活不下去的人，这是大功德啊。
华家如此不上道，让他们嗤之以鼻。
你以为每日每人限量购买，就能维持库存吗？咱们豪族佃户奴仆无数，还会花钱雇佣人冒充百姓买粮。
看我们几日就把你们的粮买空，到时候那粮价，不是想怎么涨就怎么涨？
华家也有些本事，和杭州知府商量了，华家的船可以从海商入杭州湾，直接给杭州人供粮。
但华家再强，能供几日的粮？而且运粮不需要成本吗？
杭州老百姓人心惶惶，都恐惧临近的兵灾。那些处于谣言漩涡正中的人却一点都不担心，还有余力囤积居奇，真是看得棋盘外的人啧啧称奇。
闭城运粮这么大的事，虽然能瞒着杭州知府，杭州巡抚时瞒不住了。
于是，金鋐得知，他每次去找曹寅喝茶时，那个伺候特别周到麻利的机灵小厮，居然是太子殿下。
金鋐得知真相后，差点腿一蹬厥过去。
查木杨忍笑，心里舒坦极了。
还好还好，至少他没喝过太子奉的茶。
金鋐快哭了：“太子殿下，您太折煞微臣了，微臣、微臣……”
胤礽开玩笑道：“别怕，我还给曹寅跪过呢，他都没折寿，你肯定不会。”
回旋镖扎曹寅心口上了，穿着一身侍卫服的曹寅默默地看了自家太子爷一眼，用眼神控诉太子的冷酷无情。
金鋐看了一看脸色阴沉的曹寅，拍腿大笑道：“还有这事？那微臣不怕了。折寿的事，就拉着曹大人一起。”
他对曹寅服气了。

However, before that, Kunshan still had to be visited first.

Traveling south via the Grand Canal, then enduring the fatigue of carriage and horse, Yinreng arrived in the Kunshan region in just three days.

They first rested at an inn and then inquired about Gu Yanwu.

Gu Yanwu was highly skilled in managing finances and had a large garden estate in Kunshan nestled against the hills and water, named Tinglin Garden. He usually lived in Tinglin Garden, closing his doors to focus on his studies, only interacting with a few close friends and relatives.

After receiving a few copper coins as a tip, the waiter enthusiastically introduced them to Gu Yanwu's Tinglin Garden: "Our Mr. Tinglin doesn't like to see outsiders. Scholars come to seek an audience every day, but Mr. Tinglin almost never sees them. But even if they don't get to see him, those scholars are still happy to come to our Kunshan to soak up some of Mr. Tinglin's literary aura."

Yinreng asked, "Are there no scholars who have been able to see Mr. Tinglin?"

The waiter replied, "There are, but they are all introduced by the Xu family. Actually, if you want to pay a visit, you'd be better off visiting the Xu family."

Yinreng asked, "The 'Three Xus of Kunshan' who produced three Jinshi in one family?"

The waiter laughed, "Exactly. The Xu family doesn't turn anyone away. If you gain the Xu family's appreciation, you might be recommended to Mr. Tinglin."

After Yinreng had someone send the waiter away, his expression darkened.

Gali asked suspiciously, "Your... Young Master, is something wrong?"

Yinreng said, "The Xu family is using the teacher's reputation to gild their own names. Isn't the fame of the 'Three Xus of Kunshan' enough?"

Xu Yuanmeng didn't understand, "Is there something the Xu family is doing wrong?"

Yinreng was silent for a while and didn't answer, only telling the Shi brothers to investigate whether the Xu family had committed any illegal acts.

The Zhao brothers were very dissatisfied, "We could do that kind of thing too."

Yinreng said, "You lack the experience of following elders to govern a region. It's better to leave the intelligence gathering to them. But don't just fight with them all the time; you should learn what you can. They are all people capable of being local officials. If you were in their shoes, could you do it?"

The Zhao brothers said in unison, "Of course we could!"

Yinreng was speechless.

Like hell you could. You two are only fit to be great generals.

Never mind, prefects are easy to find, but great generals are rare; he should be happy about that.

After waiting for only half a day, the Shi brothers returned.

Shi Shiji said, "The Xu family descendants have committed many illegal acts, encroaching on civilian farmland and acting in an overbearing manner. They used to be more restrained, but later, using Gu Yanwu's name, they held grand literary banquets, accepted countless bribes, and even intervened in local official appointments."

Yinreng sneered, "Father only makes arrangements in secret, hoping the teacher can spend his later years in peace. After all, the teacher previously opposed the Qing to restore the Ming; even if his scholarship is great, traveling scholars only visit in secret, so how could it be such a grand affair known to everyone? And what's with this literary gathering screening? It's likely the Three Xus learned of the connection between me and the teacher and told their descendants to show him respect. The Xu descendants just saw an opportunity for profit and are using the teacher's name to amass wealth."

Yinreng flicked his sleeve, "Alright, we can send the calling card to the teacher now. With such unfilial relatives, the teacher will surely hold his nose and see me."

Relatives are, after all, the Achilles' heel for most people.

147. Two Chapters Combined [V]

The Gu family was almost entirely wiped out, and the Xu family were merely the nephews of Gu Yanwu.

In this era, the word "nephew" (waisheng) carries the "wai" (outside) character, making them almost outsiders. The Three Xus of Kunshan were still somewhat close to Gu Yanwu, but other descendants had no relationship with him at all.

If Tong Guogang couldn't even control his own brother Tong Guowei, how could Gu Yanwu control the Xu family?

But the Xu family was thick-skinned enough to sponge off Gu Yanwu's reputation without considering what trouble it might bring him. They completely ignored that when Gu Yanwu was wandering in destitution, not only did they not help, but the three nephews who had already become officials in Beijing lived off the money they borrowed from him.

The money still hasn't been repaid to this day.

But Gu Yanwu still didn't hold it against them.

After all, the Gu family was wiped out. He had to preserve some bloodline for his sister.

Moreover, the Xu family used to be decent. The people of Kunshan remembered the Xu family so fondly that even when the descendants did outrageous things, no one reported them—not only because the three Xu brothers were officials in the imperial court, but also because the Xu family had saved many people during the Kunshan massacre.

Gu Yanwu's sister and brother-in-law were good people; otherwise, they wouldn't have raised the Three Xus of Kunshan. It's a pity they died young, leaving their children and grandchildren without discipline.

So, when he saw Yinreng's calling card, he sighed and let this fellow, who claimed to be a Han scholar, roll in.

Gu Yanwu didn't look at Yinreng.

He looked at Xu Yuanmeng and asked, "Did you write those essays?"

Xu Yuanmeng bowed, "Yes."

Gu Yanwu said indifferently, "Not bad. Let me test you."

Xu Yuanmeng was incredibly excited, his arrogance from the imperial court completely vanished.

Gu Yanwu tested Xu Yuanmeng on some Confucian classics and gave him a few pointers.

Xu Yuanmeng looked like he had benefited immensely, which made the other scholar, Gali, feel a bit depressed.

Fine, he admitted this old man had some real skills.

Gu Yanwu looked at Gali and said indifferently, "Do you have anything you want to ask?"

Gali had indeed prepared a bellyful of questions, wanting to expose this fame-seeking person in front of the Crown Prince.

Then, Gali also respectfully performed a grand bow and obediently stepped aside.

Gu Yanwu said, "No one else?"

Yinreng: "Me, me, me!"

Gu Yanwu said, "If there's no one else, please leave."

Yinreng: "Teacher, look at this, look at this! Written by Mr. Tang! He says he's better at managing finances than you!"

Gu Yanwu scolded, "Who is your teacher! Let me see! Tang Zhen is just someone who talks on paper. If he's so good at managing finances, why haven't I seen him manage his own wealth well!"

Yinreng first gave the book to Gu Yanwu, then said, "But aren't Mr. Gu and Mr. Tang friends?"

He remembered that when Tang Zhen was sent by Kangxi to Taiwan to develop overseas affairs, he specifically visited Kunshan to see Gu Yanwu, and the two became soulmates.

Gu Yanwu flipped through the new book written by Tang Zhen: "Different paths, no common ground."

Yinreng: "?"

Tang Zhen and Gu Yanwu were both among the "Four Great Enlightenment Thinkers" of the late Ming and early Qing. He was the only one among the four who wanted to enter government service and become an imperial tutor.

Now he was indeed an imperial tutor and the Crown Prince's tutor.

Yinreng had three teachers. Du Lide had already retired and returned home; Gu Yanwu didn't even acknowledge him as a disciple; Tang Zhen kept finding excuses not to return to the Qing after a trip overseas and was now stationed in the New World.

Having these three teachers was the same as having none; he could only study by looking at the books or letters they wrote.

Being a Crown Prince to this extent was quite pitiful.

After Tang Zhen traveled overseas with the Qing navy, he absorbed overseas ideas and became increasingly radical.

However, his radicalism was only expressed in his scholarship. In his letters to the Crown Prince and Kangxi, Tang Zhen was very cautious, saying that reform was a century-long grand strategy and urging them to be extremely careful.

Gu Yanwu's thought was "benefit the country and enrich the people," doubting monarchical power, advocating for collective governance, and criticizing Neo-Confucianism; Tang Zhen also advocated for "policies to enrich the people," opposed monarchical autocracy, and rejected Neo-Confucianism.

This was the reason they could become soulmates.

But Gu Yanwu's thought was similar to "constitutional monarchy," while Tang Zhen was "moving towards a republic." Different branches within the same school of thought can fight more viciously than different schools of thought. It was no wonder they had a "falling out."

Moreover, Tang Zhen was now an imperial tutor and the Crown Prince's tutor, writing letters to Gu Yanwu every day about not needing a monarch, which made Gu Yanwu think this guy was failing the Crown Prince, spreading heretical ideas, and being disloyal.

It was clear that Tang Zhen was the one who entered government service, while Gu Yanwu was the one living in seclusion. When they argued, their positions seemed reversed.

They were both loyal to their own thoughts, regardless of their positions.

Tang Zhen was still physically strong and could run around with the Qing fleet; Gu Yanwu was already over seventy.

When Tang Zhen debated with Gu Yanwu using first-hand information, Gu Yanwu always felt frustrated.

So, to perfect his own thoughts, he had already learned multiple foreign languages, and his closest relative, Xu Yuanwen, had become his full-time book collector.

Yinreng sat cross-legged on a cushion, separated from Gu Yanwu by a low table: "When I went on my mission last time, I wanted to take the three Xu brothers with me, but none of them were willing to go."

Gu Yanwu said while reading, "They already regret it and are now cramming foreign languages."

Yinreng said, "Xu Yuanwen and Xu Bingyi are okay, but Xu Qianxue is a bit lacking."

Gu Yanwu flipped a page: "Xu Qianxue's scholarship is okay, but his character has indeed had some problems these years."

Yinreng said, "But Xu Yuanwen and Xu Bingyi are a bit bookish; they don't even know what's happening in their own home. It's a pity that Xu Yuanwen advocates for rectifying officialdom, controlling land annexation, and collecting taxes from officials and gentry. If he knew about his own family's affairs, he might be so angry he'd vomit blood and die."

Gu Yanwu scolded Tang Zhen first, then said, "Gongsu's temperament is indeed fierce; I'm afraid he really might die. Are you going to tell him?"

Yinreng said, "Telling him will have to wait until I return to the capital. I'm going to Hangzhou for an incognito inspection."

Gu Yanwu looked up: "You didn't come specifically to see me, but to go to Hangzhou for an incognito inspection."

Yinreng said seriously, "Of course I came specifically to see you! But I do have official business."

Gu Yanwu took a deep breath and rolled up the book.

Yinreng: "?"

Yinreng: "Ahhhhh, don't hit my head, don't hit, don't hit! What did I do wrong!"

Before visiting Gu Yanwu, Yinreng had warned the others that no one was allowed to step forward no matter what Gu Yanwu did.

Now that he was being beaten, the others just looked away with heartache.

Gu Yanwu cursed, "A gentleman does not stand under a dangerous wall—haven't you learned that? Didn't your teacher teach you? Tang Zhen is always running around outside and doesn't act like a proper Crown Prince's tutor at all! Even if you rely on your 'innate knowledge' to run around at a young age, you shouldn't do things that expose your identity while incognito!"

When Gu Yanwu learned that the Crown Prince had gone on a mission, he had already nearly had a myocardial infarction.

Gu Yanwu didn't like the Qing Emperor. He saw that this emperor was no better than other feudal monarchs, at most a so-called "enlightened ruler" who let the people barely survive.

But Gu Yanwu liked the Crown Prince very much.

He pinned all his hopes for saving the country and the people on the Crown Prince, Yinreng.

The Crown Prince did not disappoint his expectations. Whether it was the queue-cutting order, building shrines and erecting monuments for loyal Ming officials, or reaching out overseas to encourage trade, these policies were all in line with his heart.

Gu Yanwu didn't believe that without the Crown Prince, this mediocre emperor would do these things.

So when the Crown Prince, still a young boy, went on a long sea voyage, Gu Yanwu was nearly angered to death.

Wasn't that stupid emperor afraid something would happen to the Crown Prince!

Gu Yanwu hurriedly wrote to Tang Zhen, but that guy seemed to have gone to the New World and didn't reply at all.

Now this guy had actually bumped into him and was being scolded; he had caught him just in time.

Gu Yanwu had intended to scold him a few times and let it go, but who knew Yinreng actually had the heavy responsibility of an incognito inspection.

The old man's temper couldn't be quelled.

If you don't count the travel fatigue and lack of acclimatization, the danger of an incognito inspection is far higher than a mission abroad. It was bad enough that Yinreng stood under a dangerous wall, but he actually did things that would expose his identity.

The scholars he would receive would surely be checked by the Xu family. If those idiots in the Xu family knew, could their identities still be kept hidden!

Yinreng was chased and beaten by Gu Yanwu, scolded until he was bloody.

He felt wronged: "When Mr. Gu used to see me before, you would hold me on your lap, but now you're actually beating me!"

Gu Yanwu scolded, "Don't you deserve a beating!"

Yinreng said, "Deserve it... but I have no choice. There are too few people Father trusts and too much work to be done, so I have to do it. Not just me, my eight-year-old fourth brother was also sent to Tianjin to work."

Gu Yanwu: "..."

Gu Yanwu took a deep breath: "Does your father have some kind of serious illness?"

Xu Yuanmeng and the others: "..."

Never mind, Mr. Gu is a Ming loyalist; it's normal for him to scold the Qing Emperor.

(And they also thought the Emperor's approach was a bit too much like "pulling seedlings to help them grow," with a few small problems.)

Yinreng sighed: "I think so too. Don't worry, Teacher, us visiting you might actually be a better way to hide our identities."

Gu Yanwu snorted: "Are you here to ask me to devise a strategy for your incognito inspection?"

Yinreng shook his head: "Teacher can transcend hatred to teach me, so how could I make things difficult for you? I won't let you participate in Qing politics or devise strategies for Qing rule. I just have some academic questions I want to ask you. Our letters are all checked by Father, so some questions need to be asked in person."

Gu Yanwu looked at Xu Yuanmeng and the others and said, "He didn't send a eunuch to monitor you this time?"

Yinreng said, "I've grown up."

Gu Yanwu snorted: "Speak."

Xu Yuanmeng and the others broke out in cold sweat.

You're talking about things the Emperor shouldn't know right in front of us! Can you please send us away first!

Yinreng first asked about how to make current scholars accept natural science.

Most people who are literate now are Confucian scholars. Bound by Neo-Confucianism, they are relatively pedantic and find it difficult to accept new things.

Yinreng wanted to package natural science with Confucianism, preferably adding the Hundred Schools of Thought, to make the promotion of natural science smoother.

Gu Yanwu was a master of Confucianism, deeply loved by the Confucian community, and could offer suggestions to Yinreng.

This matter was important, but it could be told to Kangxi; it wasn't the focus of Yinreng's trip.

Yinreng's focus was whether he should spread his little notebook in the Qing.

After he gave the notebook to Gu Yanwu.

Gu Yanwu's face twitched violently, looking like he was about to have a stroke.

Gu Yanwu said, "Tang Zhen doesn't know where he got similar books, and his thoughts are becoming increasingly biased. Did you write these books?"

Yinreng: "Hehe."

Gu Yanwu rolled up the book and hit Yinreng's head hard: "Can you be patient, be more patient? You are still the Crown Prince! Do you not want to be the Crown Prince anymore and want the Emperor to cut off your head!"

Yinreng covered his head and said, "Father wouldn't cut off my head; at most, he'd put me under house arrest. Ouch, stop hitting! If it can't be promoted now, then forget it; I'll keep it for now. Teacher, take a look and see if there's anything that needs changing? I'm going to pass this down as a family heirloom."

Gu Yanwu was so angry he was nearly having a stroke.

It's bad enough that an imperial tutor is shouting about abolishing the monarchy every day, but you, as the Crown Prince and future emperor, are also messing around?! And you're asking me how to integrate these books into current social affairs?

Why is the "Holy Crown Prince" I favored so suicidal!

After Gu Yanwu finished beating Yinreng, he roughly finished reading the book, threw it into the brazier, and dictated his thoughts to Yinreng.

Gu Yanwu spoke very fast, without taking pen and paper, giving Yinreng no chance to record it.

Yinreng listened and memorized with all his might, mobilizing all his attention.

The others were bewildered. Is it useful to talk like this? Can you remember it?

Xu Yuanmeng was sweating profusely again. He really wanted to keep up with Gu Yanwu and the Crown Prince's train of thought, but found that the two were speaking like a heavenly book; he couldn't think fast enough.

Is this the gap?

It's one thing for Mr. Gu to have a huge gap with him, but why is the Crown Prince so young and yet the gap between them is so large?

He originally thought the Crown Prince was only outstanding in government affairs. If it came to scholarship, he could still be the Crown Prince's teacher. Now it seems the Crown Prince could be his teacher.

Xu Yuanmeng couldn't help but feel frustrated.

Gu Yanwu drove Yinreng out before dark and didn't let him stay the night.

They didn't talk much about the Xu family throughout the process. However, Yinreng already knew Gu Yanwu's handling of the Xu family.

Gu Yanwu was actually deliberately letting the Xu family grow arrogant, then writing to Xu Yuanwen to let the justice-seeking Xu Yuanwen deal with the lawless people in the clan in one go.

The Three Xus of Kunshan were all in the capital and neglected the discipline of the descendants in Kunshan; those clansmen were local bullies. And those illegal acts might even have the support of Xu Qianxue.

Xu Qianxue wanted to be the leader of the Han officials in the court, and there were too many places where he needed money; he urgently needed the family's support. He also enjoyed the power-showing act of accepting bribes.

Gu Yanwu deliberately indulged the Xu family and didn't write to expose them immediately, actually harboring the intention of knocking the Xu family down a peg and splitting the Three Xus.

With Xu Yuanwen's hatred of evil and Xu Bingyi's honesty and loyalty, once they discovered what Xu Qianxue had done in private, they would definitely draw a line with him.

In this way, the Xu family would at most lose one Xu Qianxue, and his sister and brother-in-law's family could be mostly preserved.

Yinreng felt a bit ashamed.

He had thought he was relying on threatening Gu Yanwu with the Xu family to get a meeting, but Gu Yanwu wouldn't be threatened by him at all; he just simply wanted to see him.

At night, Yinreng climbed onto the roof, imitating the knights in storybooks, drinking tea while watching the moon.

Gali also climbed up, lifting his robes: "Why is the Crown Prince sad?"

Yinreng looked at the moon and said, "Not sad."

He was just lamenting that he was becoming more and more suited to this era.

People who are suited to this era are the kind of people he hated in his second life.

Seeing that Yinreng didn't answer, Gali just sat beside him, keeping him company while drinking gloomy tea.

After a while, Gali said, "Is the Crown Prince regretting that the Three Xus of Kunshan appear upright, but in reality, their family also engages in corrupt practices?"

Yinreng said, "There is no official who isn't corrupt; it's a small matter. As long as it doesn't cost lives, it's just a matter of dismissal. Which official's clan doesn't have some land-grabbing incidents?"

Gali said, "But common things don't equal correct things. Is the Crown Prince worried about these things?"

Yinreng looked at Gali.

Do you know you are a super corrupt official in history? How can you talk to me about integrity? It's really strange.

Yinreng said, "If I am troubled, is there any way to stop it?"

Gali racked his brains: "Should we send more censors to various places to evaluate officials?"

Yinreng said, "You can submit a memorial to Father and suggest it."

Treating the symptoms but not the root cause is still better than doing nothing.

Yinreng shook the teapot: "Let's go, go downstairs, we have to travel tomorrow."

Gali nodded.

When he returned to his room, he was still pondering how to rectify officialdom.

The Crown Prince is noble and hopes for a clean officialdom; he should share the Crown Prince's worries.

The next day, Xu Yuanmeng took the initiative to visit the Xu family.

He took out a letter of introduction from a reclusive great scholar and accepted the stationery gifted by the Xu family.

The Xu family read the letter of introduction and understood why this person could see Gu Yanwu, so they were no longer on guard against their group.

When leaving Kunshan, Yinreng poked his head out of the carriage window and looked back.

Outside Kunshan city, fertile fields stretched to the sky. But the people busy in the fields had numb expressions; looking at the well-growing seedlings, there was no sign of excitement or satisfaction.

Yinreng understood that this was because the land was not theirs.

The rich have ten thousand acres of good land, while the poor have no place to stand an awl.

What could he do about this phenomenon?

Overthrow the local tyrants, make all land public, and then redistribute it?

If it were a time of war and chaos, when all order was shattered, it might be possible. Now, he was already doing his best to maintain the stability of the Qing carriage.

Gali asked, "Your Highness, what are you looking at?"

Yinreng became literary: "Looking at how powerless I am. Haha, just kidding."

Yinreng pulled his head back and closed his eyes to rest.

Although he couldn't move the land system now, he could do some things in areas that Chinese feudal society hadn't yet valued.

For example, commercial taxes.

The greatest suffering of farmers lies in taxes and labor services. If they could obtain a large amount of commercial tax and trade surplus, they could continuously reduce their taxes and abolish the poll tax.

After developing commerce, when the population is too large, farmers can be liberated from the land to work in the city and produce more goods.

These goods can be sold overseas and exchanged for food, minerals, and livestock, and the lives of the people will be further improved.

In this way, when the Qing is still strong and the emperor is not muddle-headed, a virtuous cycle can be formed.

High welfare is built on high resources. While overseas hasn't realized this, the Qing should complete the policy of enriching the people first. Even if the Qing carriage falls apart in the future, later generations picking up the wreckage can quickly create a sturdier, faster-running carriage.

Anyone who blocks the opening of the seas must be crushed.

Yinreng made up his mind and opened his eyes: "After arriving in Hangzhou, change the plan."

Xu Yuanmeng and Gali had traveled with Yinreng and already knew how capable the Crown Prince was. Yinreng didn't say what the plan was, but they immediately said "Yes," without any intention of refuting.

...

Above is heaven, below are Suzhou and Hangzhou.

Yinreng didn't go to Suzhou to play; he went straight to Hangzhou.

After arriving in Hangzhou, he started his "money-sprinkling" mode, taking out gold and silver to buy property in Hangzhou.

Because of Yinreng's extravagance, the Hangzhou gentry soon learned that a wealthy merchant from Southern Fujian had come to Hangzhou to develop, and he was extremely generous.

This Southern Fujian merchant's surname was Hua, and the five brothers of the clan had come.

The eldest Hua brother was a pure scholar; the second Hua brother was the chief steward, in charge of the family business; the third and fourth Hua brothers also understood poetry, but had an air of fierce bandits, likely people who often went to sea; the fifth Hua brother was still a child and had no presence.

The eldest Hua brother was naturally Xu Yuanmeng, the second was Gali, the third and fourth were the Shi brothers, and the fifth Hua brother with no presence was naturally Yinreng.

The Zhao brothers were very depressed: "What about us?"

Yinreng said, "Who told you not to speak the Southern Fujian dialect? Just be obedient guards."

The Zhao brothers were very angry, but had no choice.

Perhaps scholars of this era all had memory and language buffs. On the mission ship, there were many Southern Fujian soldiers, and Xu Yuanmeng and Gali had long since learned the Southern Fujian dialect.

The Zhao brothers also knew a little, but it was stumbling and didn't sound like a Southern Fujian person at all.

Moreover, Gali and the Shi brothers could all write poetry and understood the classics. The Zhao brothers... they could recite military books very fluently.

There was no way; they could only be excluded from the brothers and be the head guards.

However, there were benefits to being guards; they could always be by Yinreng's side. Thinking of this, Zhao Hongwei and Zhao Hongxi stopped complaining.

People rely on clothes.

Since the queue-cutting order was canceled, the clothing of the Qing had also undergone some changes. Especially since Kangxi issued an edict to restore the prosperous Han and Tang dynasties, their clothes had added some Han and Tang elements.

For example, some young scholars no longer wore long robes, but wore waist seals and carried swords, making themselves look fierce enough to immediately mount a horse with a knife; the traditional scholar standard of being both literary and martial was also brought up again.

Xu Yuanmeng was still a traditional weak scholar, while his "brothers" were all powdered and sword-bearing, having both a scholarly air and conforming to the trends of the era.

When Zhao Hongwei and Zhao Hongxi saw the Crown Prince personally applying powder and rouge for the Shi brothers, their laughter was so loud that the dust on the beams almost fell down.

The Shi brothers were extremely embarrassed.

Shi Shiji said, "Can we not wear powder?"

Yinreng said while drawing their eyebrows, "Don't move, no talking, no frowning. Hmm, that's it. You don't understand the scholar's obsession with appearance at all. A scholar with a face like jade and delicate features, even if he's a straw bag, will be treated with courtesy. You've been exposed to the sun and rain for a long time; you don't look like a proper scholar. Alright, see how my craftsmanship is."

Yinreng took out a glass mercury mirror, which was extremely clear.

The Shi brothers looked at the delicate, fair-skinned, and beautiful young men in the mirror and gasped.

Damn! Who is that in the mirror! Where did this monster come from!

The Zhao brothers poked their heads in, then retracted them, continuing to laugh uncontrollably.

Xu Yuanmeng, however, was full of admiration: "This is what a scholar should look like. The Crown Prince is truly amazing!"

Gali nodded: "Crown Prince, can you help me disguise myself too?"

I want the Crown Prince to help me draw my eyebrows! Gali said quietly in his heart.

Yinreng rolled up his sleeves: "Come, everyone come. Zhao Hongwei, Zhao Hongxi, don't think you can escape either."

The Zhao brothers were terrified: "We aren't scholars!"

Yinreng said, "You aren't guards now; you are generals. You look like people from the military; you must be made to look more rugged."

The Zhao brothers were helpless: "Okay." Anyway, as long as they aren't made into pretty scholars.

Xu Yuanmeng was full of struggle, but finally couldn't help but say: "Then this subject..."

Yinreng said, "Of course I won't forget the eldest brother. You all hurry up and get used to changing your titles; no 'subject' or 'minister' talk. If you delay my plan because of a slip of the tongue, I'll have the eldest brother beat you."

The expressions of several people were tense.

The Prince of the First Rank really would beat them.

Yinreng's university class was almost entirely female; left alone, he was forced to learn a great deal about makeup and assist the girls during various activities.

After his mother found out, she also taught him much about skincare and cosmetics, saying it could be used to coax a future wife.

While on a diplomatic mission to Europe, European nobles all wore makeup. Yinreng learned quite a few unnecessary skills there as well.

Now, he looked with satisfaction at the refined "brother" before him.

My makeup skills are actually quite good.

Gali looked at Yinreng's makeup supplies and said, "Fifth Brother, do you have any thoughts on selling these items?"

Gali was already fully immersed in his role, and Yinreng smiled, "If Elder Brother says they can be sold, then this younger brother shall give it a try."

Hearing Yinreng call him "Elder Brother," Gali felt as sweet as if he had drunk honey.

At this moment, he completely forgot that he was a friend of Yinreng's uncle. By becoming Yinreng's elder brother, he was now a generation apart from Changtai.

Xu Yuanmeng asked in confusion, "Your Hi... Fifth Brother, why must we do these troublesome things?"

Yinreng replied, "Secret investigations are only temporary; we need to leave more eyes and ears in Jiangnan. Doing business is the best way. If we establish a firm foothold now, these businesses can continue to be managed by our people in the future. Besides..."

Yinreng glanced at Xu Yuanmeng, Gali, and the others. "A gentleman loves wealth but acquires it through proper means; I am teaching you how to love wealth correctly. If you have enough money in the future, stop taking bribes. I hope you can have long and prosperous careers in the officialdom. These businesses will provide you with shares and dividends as a reward for accompanying me on this trip."

Xu Yuanmeng and the others immediately changed their expressions, saying they didn't need it.

Yinreng shook his head. "What I give you, you shall accept. I have already written to Father about this. He won't refuse such a small matter. In the future, you can also invest in overseas trade. That earns far more than exploitation or extortion. Gold and silver are fine, but you can't take them to the next life. Sleeping on a mountain of gold isn't comfortable, either. As for passing it down to descendants..."

Yinreng laughed at himself and continued, "Even dynasties aren't guaranteed to last forever, let alone powerful clans? For those families that have stood the test of time, the current heads may have no blood relation to the original founders at all, and it's even possible that the current heads and the original founders have a blood feud of extermination."

"Take the Kong family, for example... you have all read books, so you must be familiar with the lineage of the Kong family," Yinreng said indifferently.

The men present all turned pale.

As a typical representative of scholars, Xu Yuanmeng wanted to refute this, but his lips trembled, and he realized he couldn't.

Yinreng smiled, "Alright, let's not talk about things that haven't happened yet. Doing business is also beneficial for our current investigation. By putting on a show of wanting to settle down here, we won't attract too much attention while gathering information. Let's first align our backstories."

...

"The Hua family has been doing business in Annam and Old Port (Jiugang) for years, earning vast wealth at sea. After the Great Qing reclaimed Old Port and parts of Annam, they realized the strength of the Great Qing and, bringing a portion of their family wealth, wanted to return to the Great Qing to settle down and acquire property."

"This branch of the Hua family is merely a side branch. Currently, they have come to Hangzhou not to trade in foreign goods, but to engage in local business, and they intend to set up sacrificial fields for the Hua clan and plan to take the imperial examinations."

"The eldest of the Hua family is named Hua Boyu, a pure scholar with great learning; he seems to be a disciple of a reclusive great Confucian. According to the Xu family, he once visited Mr. Gu Tinglin, and Mr. Gu Tinglin allowed him to enter his tutelage for a day."

"The second of the Hua family is named Hua Zhongjue, capable in both literature and martial arts, quite shrewd, and seems to be the actual controller of this branch of the Hua family."

"The third of the Hua family is named Hua Shugui, skilled in poetry and prose, with the air of a wild scholar."

"The fourth of the Hua family is more like a martial man, and the fifth of the Hua family is still a child." ...

Wang Tan was turning two white jade beads in his hand, listening to his steward recount, point by point, the rise of the Hua family, the wealthy merchants from the South Seas who had recently become famous in Hangzhou.

Beside Wang Tan was a young man with handsome features but a sickly look of excessive indulgence and a greed in his eyes that made one feel very uncomfortable. He said sourly, "Sea merchants really make money. If it weren't for the opening of the seas, our family would be making even more."

Smuggling only required selling off old, worn-out goods to make a profit. After the seas were opened, they had to compete with other merchants, and the Wang family's business was becoming increasingly difficult.

Wang Tan sighed, "Since the opening of the seas, everyone has been eyeing Hangzhou."

It is said that there is heaven above, and Suzhou and Hangzhou below. Hangzhou's great river connects to Hangzhou Bay, allowing direct access to the sea. Since the opening of the seas, Suzhou has been far less prosperous than Hangzhou.

Hangzhou is also a place of outstanding people and flourishing imperial examinations, with many great Confucians. Those wealthy landowners from the south, having made money, all want to buy land in Hangzhou.

In the past, those wealthy landowners who came to Hangzhou were easily dismissed due to their accents and habits. Now, this family of wealthy landowners was actually a family of scholars who could speak the official language and had a letter from a great Confucian as a protective talisman; it was difficult for them to use their usual tactics.

That group of Confucian scholars accepted their offerings one by one, yet looked down on merchants' money as vulgar; compared to wealthy merchants, they were more willing to associate with scholars.

Thinking of this, Wang Tan glared at his son, Wang Zhuan.

If only his son were not so useless and would study properly. If the Wang family could produce a Jinshi, they wouldn't be in such a passive position.

Wang Zhuan was used to being glared at and ignored his father's gaze, still muttering, "They're just rootless outsiders anyway. Can't we join forces with the Hangzhou Prefect to find a crime and raid their home?"

Wang Tan said indifferently, "The Imperial Envoy is still in Hangzhou."

Wang Zhuan shut his mouth. He had forgotten about that.

Wang Tan sighed, "The Hua family really found a good opportunity. If the Imperial Envoy weren't in Hangzhou, how could they be so arrogant? Now, no family in Hangzhou dares to mess with them."

Behind Wang Tan, a middle-aged man with a goat-like beard said, "Master, perhaps they were eyeing the timing of the Imperial Envoy's arrival and came to Hangzhou specifically for that."

Wang Tan turned his head, "You mean they have a connection with the Imperial Envoy?"

The goat-bearded man said, "They might not necessarily have a connection with the Imperial Envoy, but they are certainly very well-informed. Perhaps they have patrons in the imperial court."

Wang Tan thought for a moment and said, "The Imperial Envoy's arrival in Hangzhou is no secret. They might not have patrons in the court, but we still have to be on guard. Forget it, since they have been so high-profile, as the host, I should at least entertain them."

The goat-bearded man asked, "Master, shall we invite them to a banquet?"

Wang Tan said, "Those twenty qing of land that have issues can be sold to them."

Wang Zhuan immediately said, "That is prime mulberry land!"

Wang Tan glanced at Wang Zhuan, "One must have a life to keep it. This Imperial Envoy currently looks impossible to bribe; even if we collude, we might not be able to deceive him."

Wang Zhuan wanted to say more, but he was just a playboy, and Wang Tan wouldn't listen to him at all.

Wang Zhuan stormed out in a huff.

Wang Tan looked at his son's back and sighed, "Zhuan'er has been spoiled by my mother and his mother. What can be done?"

The goat-bearded man bowed and smiled, "Although the Second Young Master is young, he is very intelligent and understands the classics and histories at a glance. He will surely become a Jinshi in the future."

Wang Tan thought of his second son, who was good at studying, and a smile couldn't help but appear on his lips.

He stroked his long beard and said, "Does that Hua Boyu really have the talent of a Jinshi?"

The goat-bearded man said, "A scholar whom Mr. Gu Tinglin is willing to see should at least be able to pass the Juren examination, right?"

Wang Tan thought of Gu Yanwu and nodded slightly, "That's true. The Hangzhou Confucian circle accepting him so quickly is truly thanks to Mr. Gu. Has the Xu family said anything?"

The goat-bearded man said, "They are just using Mr. Gu Tinglin's name to collect money; how would they know about Mr. Gu Tinglin's guests? They don't even know about the Three Xus of Kunshan."

Although those left behind in Kunshan were clansmen or even nephews of the Three Xus of Kunshan, they were all useless people.

If they were even slightly useful, they would certainly be living in Beijing with the Three Xus of Kunshan, being carefully taught.

Wang Tan sighed, "The people of the Xu family are so stupid. If it weren't for the name of the Three Xus of Kunshan, who would send them money? Wealth is not stable; nobility is the foundation of a family's survival. If Hua Boyu can really pass the Jinshi examination, what does it matter if I give him a small plot of land in Hangzhou?"

The goat-bearded man bowed, "Master, you mean..."

Wang Tan said, "Host a literary banquet in the name of Zheng'er's teacher. Although Zheng'er's teacher is only a Juren, he has quite a reputation for talent, and I trust his judgment."

The goat-bearded man bowed, "Yes."

...

Xu Yuanmeng said, "The invitation from the Wang family has arrived. Fifth Brother, shall we go?"

He was now used to calling Yinreng "Fifth Brother," and it felt quite pleasant.

To be brothers with the Crown Prince, after all.

Yinreng picked up the invitation and smiled, "Gold-dusted paper; worthy of the Zhejiang merchants, truly extravagant. Let's go, why not? I hear the Imperial Envoy will be attending this time as well."

The Imperial Envoy...

The expressions of everyone present were very strange.

I wonder what kind of expression that kid Cao Yin will have when he sees us.

Xu Yuanmeng frowned, "The Wang family are mere merchants, yet so many officials are fawning over them."

Yinreng threw the invitation on the table, "Although they are only merchants, they are also local tyrants and provide silk to the imperial palace, so they count as half-official merchants. By the way, they are also members of a certain prince's faction."

Yinreng paused and said, "Have they still not decided which prince's faction that 'certain' faction belongs to?"

Even Xu Yuanmeng couldn't help but suppress a smile that made his face look distorted.

Throughout the ages, the struggle for the throne has been bloody, but the struggle for the throne in this dynasty is quite comical.

The largest Crown Prince faction is the Emperor himself, which is common in other dynasties, but the First Prince's faction being beaten up by the First Prince and then dissolving in anger is just too ridiculous.

Even more ridiculous is that the anti-Crown Prince faction has assembled, but they still haven't decided which prince to choose.

Facing only foxes and wildcats, bristling their fur and crying angrily at me..."

The poem Cao Yin sang was Du Fu's *Parting of the Homeless*.

Some scholars present had lived through war, while others had heard of it from their elders.

Hearing Cao Yin's drunken, sorrowful singing, none could hold back their tears, weeping uncontrollably.

One scholar fell to his knees in tears and pleaded, "Lord Cao, you must tell His Majesty that the people of Zhejiang harbor no treasonous intentions—none at all!"

Cao Yin ignored him. He simply swayed his head and finished singing the entire poem, then, bleary-eyed and stumbling, made his way inside.

Looking at his sorrowful retreating figure, no one dared stop him.

Soon, word that the Eight Banners army might march to Zhejiang to suppress the rebellion spread through all the prominent clans in Hangzhou, leaving everyone terrified.

...

"Crown Prince, are you truly sure it's alright to make such a big scene?" Cao Yin was extremely apprehensive.

The Emperor had said not to escalate it, yet the Emperor had also said to follow the Crown Prince's judgment in everything. The Emperor...

*Your Majesty, aren't you going to dissuade the Crown Prince at all?!*

Yinreng flipped through the letter Zhao Shilin had sent and said, "I have already given them a chance. You explained the pros and cons clearly to them before, but seeing the court treat Han people with leniency, they assumed the Great Qing would share rule with the scholar-bureaucrats. That Wang Tan is merely a puppet pushed forward by the local gentry."

Yinreng looked up with a sneer. "In Jiangnan and Zhejiang, this holy land of Confucianism, what does a merchant count for? They are indulging and egging on the Wang family just to test the Qing court's bottom line."

Looking at the furious Yinreng, Cao Yin did not dare speak.

When his little Crown Prince was gentle, he was truly gentle, but when he grew angry, he was truly terrifying.

Cao Yin felt very fortunate that Prince Zhi hadn't accompanied the Crown Prince on this incognito trip. Otherwise, seeing the Crown Prince angry, Prince Zhi would probably have hopped the wall in the middle of the night behind the Crown Prince's back, slipped into the Wang residence, and personally lopped off Wang Tan's dog head.

Don't say it sounded absurd; Prince Zhi was capable of things even more absurd than that.

"Spread the word that someone is staging a fake civil unrest to reap profits, and let the common folk know," Yinreng said with a cold face. "Then have some elder scholars denounce the Qing army's cruelty, claiming that the Qing army won't care whether the unrest was faked or not—they will simply slaughter everyone in Hangzhou."

Cao Yin couldn't help but shudder. "Are we... are we really going that far?"

Yinreng said, "If we don't set rules for them while the south's terror of the Qing has yet to fade, they will truly believe the Qing is like the former dynasty where they can do as they please. If they dare even fake civil unrest, what won't they dare to do? Since they want to commit treason, let it be branded as treason. Xu Yuanmeng!"

Xu Yuanmeng was already pale as a sheet. His legs went weak, and he fell to his knees with a thud. "This official is here!"

Yinreng was taken aback and hurriedly helped Xu Yuanmeng up. "This isn't a formal court setting, why are you kneeling? You have a literary reputation now; host more literary gatherings and preach how good the commoners' lives are now, and how they mustn't be manipulated by ambitious schemers."

Xu Yuanmeng gave a bitter smile. "Understood."

It wasn't that he intended to perform such grand courtesy; his legs had genuinely given out. The sudden murderous aura radiating from the Crown Prince reminded him of how the young prince had casually annihilated the Kingdom of Quang Nam while talking and laughing—it had frightened him.

Yinreng looked at Gali, whose eyes were glittering with excitement.

Yinreng hesitated for a moment, then said, "Take advantage of the chaos in the city to buy up as much land and as many shops as you can."

Gali froze, repeating, "Buy land and shops?!"

Cao Yin asked, "Isn't competing with the people for profit improper?"

Yinreng retorted, "That depends on what 'people' you're talking about. Powerful clans and wealthy merchants count as the people, but do ordinary commoners not count as the people?"

Everyone in the room was stunned.

Yinreng said, "Acquiring shops and manors in Hangzhou is to stabilize prices and gather intelligence. Since Hangzhou must have a merchant family that owns half the city, that merchant might as well be the Emperor. At least future emperors, unless their minds are broken, won't easily seek to rebel against themselves."

After saying this, Yinreng felt as though he had insulted himself.

He added, "The shops and manors here will belong to the Great Qing Royal Corporation in the future. Cao Yin, you'd better learn some business and read more books. You've studied the classics and histories enough; if you want to become a high-ranking official, you must learn more worldly matters."

Xu Yuanmeng's lips twitched, wanting to object, but in the end, he lowered his head, lost in thought.

Cao Yin hastily cupped his hands with a wry smile. "Yes, yes, yes, this slave understands."

Yinreng teased, "Bondservant status has already been abolished, yet you still call yourself 'this slave.' Are you dissatisfied with Imperial Father's policies?"

Cao Yin quickly straightened his face. "No, not at all, it was a slip of the tongue! Your Highness must never mention this to His Majesty."

Yinreng said, "That depends on your performance. Shi Shiji, accompany Lord Xu to the literary gatherings and show off your talents. Playing the eccentric scholar should make it easier for you to get close to the literati than Lord Xu."

Shi Shiji replied, "As you command."

Yinreng said, "Shi Shibiao, accompany Gali to ensure his safety, and learn as much as you can along the way."

Shi Shibiao cupped his hands. "This humble officer obeys your command!"

Having finished the arrangements, Yinreng asked, "What's the matter with that Zhao Yuanbin? Why did you bring him to me?"

Cao Yin said, "Zhao Yuanbin is Lord Zhao Shilin's clan nephew, sent to Hangzhou to deliver a letter to Your Highness. Zhao Shilin told him to remain by my side for my use. I thought Your Highness might need a courier to maintain contact with Governor Zhao. I had him stay by Lord Xu's side in my name, so Your Highness can also openly use him to pass messages to me."

Yinreng joked, "So you won't have to disguise yourself and hop walls at night anymore?"

Cao Yin rubbed his nose and smiled. "Hopping walls too often makes this sla... this official worry about being caught."

Yinreng said, "Let him stay by Lord Xu's side, then. You don't need to explicitly tell him my identity, nor do you need to hide it deliberately."

Nowadays, scholars favored growing their hair. For Zhao Yuanbin, a scholar, to shave his head at Cao Yin's mere word showed he was a ruthless character who could be put to good use.

The court could not rely solely on men of high moral conscience. Some tasks could only be done by ruthless men.

"Cao Yin, make preparations to take me, your pageboy, to see the General of Hangzhou," Yinreng said. "Since Zhao Shilin trusts him, I'm willing to trust him once."

Yinreng recalled matters regarding the current General of Hangzhou.

Regional Banner garrisons were essentially cities within cities, where soldiers, dependents, and servants all lived together. The Garrison General not only oversaw drills, but had to handle matters great and small.

For such "hereditary" professional soldiers, the rapid decline in combat readiness was entirely predictable.

By the mid-Qing era, Garrison Generals were replaced in rapid succession, and few could manage regional Banners well. During Kangxi's reign, this General of Hangzhou named Zhamuyang was a rare competent commander.

General Zhamuyang died relatively early, passing away in the thirties of Kangxi's reign. As a provincial official, Yinreng didn't have a deep impression of him, but seeing Zhao Shilin's pleading letter, he finally recalled the man.

In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi, when the Emperor visited Hangzhou during his southern tour and saw that the Hangzhou Banner garrison drilled well, he had fondly remembered Zhamuyang, who had just died of illness at his post.

Right now, Zhamuyang had only taken office recently. Even if something had gone wrong with the Hangzhou Banner garrison in the past, it couldn't be blamed on him.

Cao Yin was flabbergasted. "A pageboy?"

Yinreng said, "Tonight, I'll scale the wall with you back to the grand Imperial Envoy Cao's residence. Why, are you dissatisfied with this pageboy?"

Cao Yin repeatedly bowed and cupped his hands. "I wouldn't dare, I wouldn't dare! Your Highness's words overwhelm me."

Yinreng said, "I've already knelt to you; what's wrong with acting as your pageboy?"

Cao Yin gave a bitter smile. "Your Highness, I beg you, please stop saying that. When we return, Prince Zhi will chase me down with a blade."

Yinreng said, "Isn't that for the best? It'll keep you from drinking every day, forgetting you're a military officer, and losing all your skills."

Yinreng patted Cao Yin's arm. "We haven't seen each other for how long, and the muscle on your arms is already this flabby? Have you not been practicing martial arts every day? When I need you in the future, you'll probably be wheezing just riding a horse."

Cao Yin said sheepishly, "I indeed slacked off a bit these days. I'll practice, I'll definitely practice every day."

Hadn't he thought that he would become a pure civil official from now on, with no chances to lead troops into battle, which was why he neglected martial arts and picked up books again?

Inside the room, except for Xu Yuanmeng who was still in a daze, everyone burst into hearty laughter at Cao Yin's expense.

In the dead of night, Yinreng scaled the wall and left with Cao Yin after all.

Before they left, Gali said sourly, "Ziqing, your martial arts have deteriorated so much; can you even protect the Crown Prince?"

Cao Yin retorted, "At least I'm better than you! Why don't we have a spar?"

Gali snorted coldly. Standing by the base of the wall, he looked up and watched the Crown Prince's retreating back as he scaled the wall, only returning to his room with a sigh after quite a while.

He somewhat regretted having gone to the Imperial Academy instead of becoming an imperial bodyguard.

Why had he gone to the Imperial Academy to become a civil official? If he were a bodyguard, what room would there be for Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde?

Gali, who was actually a complete lightweight in combat, thought to himself with unwarranted confidence.

...

Cao Yin brought Yinreng back to his temporary residence.

He hadn't brought many servants, but there were constantly servants traveling back and forth between Jiangning and Hangzhou, and the attendants around him changed frequently. Thus, the spies watching him couldn't accurately determine who was by his side.

Those pageboys all kept their heads bowed when going outside, and Yinreng was skilled at disguise. When Cao Yin took Yinreng out, nobody noticed an unfamiliar petty clerk in his retinue.

The Cao family had operated in Jiangnan for a long time; Cao Yin certainly possessed the skill to pull off such a deception.

Cao Yin was currently a civil official, and civil officials were not supposed to have close contact with military generals.

However, having previously declared that his deadline for the investigation was approaching, turning to any desperate remedy seemed perfectly natural.

While Cao Yin went to meet the General of Hangzhou, rumors were also being spread throughout the city.

He lifted the curtain and looked out the carriage window. Pedestrians on the streets of Hangzhou had thinned, and the hurried passersby wore expressions of deep worry.

That rumors could spread at such astonishing speed alarmed Cao Yin greatly.

This time, they were using rumors to investigate a case. But what if someone used rumors to disrupt governance? How would they counter it?

Cao Yin's expression turned grave.

Yinreng remarked, "Others using rumors to disrupt governance is hardly a novel occurrence. During disaster relief, most civil disturbances are sparked by rumors."

Cao Yin looked at Yinreng. "Crown Prince, does time flow differently for us? Why is it that after being parted for only a few months, Your Highness feels to me as though you've aged several years?"

Yinreng rolled his eyes at Cao Yin. "Are you trying to say that I seem old and world-weary, like I've aged years?"

Cao Yin smiled. "Mature, mature! Not old."

"Sigh," Yinreng sighed. "Do you think I want this? How carefree we were during the diplomatic mission! But after returning, there's an endless stream of problems and trouble to deal with. How could my heart not grow weary?"

Yinreng patted his chest. "This heart of mine has been worn old by Imperial Father's antics."

Recalling the relentless sequence of stunts Kangxi had pulled in the few months since their return, Cao Yin couldn't help but rub his forehead.

Their Emperor truly was...

In the nearly three years Yinreng had been away, Kangxi had made no drastic reforms. Yet the moment Yinreng returned, he let loose and went wild.

As Kangxi's confidant, Cao Yin could guess the Emperor's thoughts.

Their Emperor probably figured he could dump half the troublesome matters onto the Crown Prince, so he could act recklessly with complete peace of mind.

Thinking of how Prince Zhi had gone to Mongolia, the Third Prince was organizing the Academy of Sciences, and the Fourth Prince was supervising the construction of the Tianjin Naval Base, Cao Yin couldn't help but sigh.

Your Majesty, isn't exploiting the young princes like this going a bit too far?

After Cha Muyang received Cao Yin's visiting card, he was stunned for a long time.

He wasn't stunned that Cao Yin had come to find him, but that Cao Yin had only come to find him now.

He had assumed that Cao Yin would have visited him the moment the civil unrest occurred.

Even though it was local yamen runners who suppressed the unrest at the time, the primary duty of the local Eight Banners garrison was to suppress rebellions everywhere; Cao Yin should have come to ask him first.

As for the distinction between civil and military officials, Cao Yin had served in the military and accompanied the Crown Prince abroad as a military officer, so he shouldn't care too much about that distinction. Only Han officials cared about such things.

"Invite him in quickly," Cha Muyang said.

He had people tidy up the study and hurriedly groomed himself.

Although Cha Muyang was currently the Hangzhou General of the first rank, Cao Yin was the Emperor's confidant, and he dared not be arrogant.

After Cao Yin entered, he performed the salute between military officers, then had people stand guard outside the door, and asked Cha Muyang to dismiss everyone, saying he had important matters to discuss.

Cha Muyang hurriedly had his trusted aides stand guard at the doors and windows, closed the door, and asked, "Does Imperial Guard Cao have an edict from the Emperor?"

Cao Yin had not yet succeeded as the Jiangning Textile Commissioner and still held the rank of Imperial Guard.

Cao Yin stood up, walked behind the chair, stood with his chest puffed out, and placed his hand on the saber at his waist.

The servant standing behind Cao Yin with his head lowered looked up, walked to the chair, and sat down.

Cha Muyang was stunned.

Yinreng said, "I hope the General doesn't mind my abrupt visit. My identity must remain confidential, so there is no need for the General to salute."

Cha Muyang looked at Yinreng, whose face was painted a waxy yellow and who was smiling brightly, his mind blank for several seconds.

Yinreng did not urge him, just continued to look at Cha Muyang with a smile.

Cha Muyang finally came to his senses and guessed Yinreng's identity from the way he referred to himself.

He immediately stood up, ready to kneel, but then remembered Yinreng telling him not to salute; for a moment, he didn't know whether to stand, kneel, or sit, feeling anxious and uneasy.

"General, please sit," Yinreng smiled. "The Imperial Father once told me that General Cha Muyang was promoted from Commander of the Mongol Bordered Blue Banner to Hangzhou General, and that you handle everything in an orderly manner—you are a capable official."

Cao Yin grumbled inwardly. The Crown Prince is spouting nonsense again; the Emperor definitely never said any such thing.

Cha Muyang, however, did not think the Crown Prince would lie.

He sat on the edge of the chair, moved, and said, "Thank you, Your Majesty, for the undeserved praise! This subordinate is unworthy!"

Yinreng said, "Cao Yin should have visited you the moment he arrived in Hangzhou, but the Imperial Father had him investigate some other matters, which is why he has only come now. Please do not take offense, General. Do you have anything to report to me?"

He was able to be promoted directly by Kangxi from a second-rank Banner Commander to a first-rank Hangzhou General because his ability was quite exceptional.

The first thing he did upon arriving in Hangzhou was to bury himself in the Banner garrison's expenditures and output, knowing that logistics were the foundation of the Eight Banners' reorganization.

Although he didn't remember every piece of land belonging to the garrison, this plot was surrounded by garrison fields; clearly, when the land was enclosed, it would have been impossible to leave this piece out.

Cha Muyang said solemnly, "May I ask Your Highness the Crown Prince to wait a moment? This subordinate wishes to check the ledgers."

Yinreng raised a hand slightly. "Please do."

After apologizing to Yinreng, Cha Muyang opened the window slightly and said a few words to his trusted aide.

Before long, the aide returned to the room carrying a stack of ledgers.

Yinreng did not stand up.

The aide walked past Yinreng without looking sideways, then left the room quickly, neither asking nor showing curiosity, which showed the strength of Cha Muyang's ability to govern his troops.

"Cao Yin, go and assist General Cha Muyang," Yinreng said.

Cao Yin hesitated for a moment, then unbuckled the saber at his waist and handed it to Yinreng before going to help Cha Muyang.

Seeing this, Cha Muyang once again confirmed Cao Yin's status in the hearts of the Emperor and the Crown Prince.

Not immediately obeying the Crown Prince's order but making an autonomous change showed that the Crown Prince trusted Cao Yin deeply and was very close to him, which was why Cao Yin was accustomed to such things.

Yinreng trusted Cha Muyang, but Cao Yin had learned from Yinreng to always prepare for the worst.

Yinreng was skilled in martial arts, but because he was disguised as a servant when entering the camp, he was not carrying a weapon. If Cha Muyang were to suddenly turn hostile, this saber would come in handy.

However, if the Eight Banners camp were to mutiny, even with a weapon, would the Crown Prince be able to escape?

Cao Yin felt helpless inside.

Sometimes the Crown Prince calculated everything and considered the worst-case scenario; other times he was incredibly bold. He had heard that this wasn't the first time the Prince had entered a potentially mutinous camp alone.

He didn't know whether to call his Crown Prince cautious or recklessly bold.

Yinreng hadn't been born when the Keqi case occurred, but he had heard the Emperor talk about it.

The Aisin Gioro clan didn't write their full surname in records, instead using "Jueluo clan," just as several Ulanara clans could be called "Nara clan."

Jueluo Keqi was a member of the imperial clan.

During his tenure as Hangzhou General, Jueluo Keqi occupied nearly 1,500 civilian houses, enclosed countless lands, indulged his cavalry in tyranny, and practiced usury, causing the people of Hangzhou to live in misery and putting him at odds with local officials.

Unfortunately, when the Qing dynasty first entered the pass, they didn't investigate corruption at all. Being a member of the imperial clan, no one dared to investigate Jueluo Keqi until he was implicated in the Zhuang family's "History of Ming" literary inquisition case and was dismissed from office.

Now Keqi was an idle imperial clansman in the capital, spending his days strolling and walking his birds, living quite happily.

How is it that these lands are still in the hands of the Wang family?"

Cha Muyang did not answer.

He didn't know what to say. He really didn't know about these things.

Yinreng wasn't asking Cha Muyang to answer; he was just talking to himself and sighed.

"This is definitely not an isolated case. When Keqi was corrupt, perhaps many things weren't discovered. It's been over twenty years; has it only surfaced now? Or is there something more to it?" Yinreng looked at the ledger on the table. "And what does this have to do with the Zhejiang civil unrest?"

Seeing the Crown Prince begin to ponder, neither Cha Muyang nor Cao Yin dared to speak, fearing they would interrupt his train of thought.

After a while, Yinreng sighed again and said, "Perhaps there's no connection, just a coincidence. Someone came to investigate, and the Wang family, fearing their purchase of garrison fields would be exposed, sold them off just in case."

Yinreng shook his head. "What is the Wang family? Let them struggle a bit more. General Cha Muyang..."

Yinreng reached into his sleeve, pulled out a military tally, and placed it gently on the table. "I will only ask you one thing: will the Hangzhou Banner garrison mutiny?"

Cha Muyang looked at the tally, his pupils trembling violently.

He didn't care that his trusted aides outside might learn the Crown Prince's identity and immediately knelt down. "This subordinate swears to be loyal to the Emperor until death!"

Yinreng shook his head. "Not you, the Hangzhou Banner garrison."

Cha Muyang clenched his fists, hesitated for a moment, and gritted his teeth. "This subordinate can control seventy percent of the Hangzhou Banner garrison."

Yinreng asked, "What about the officers of the remaining thirty percent?"

Cha Muyang replied, "They have connections with the local gentry."

Not the wealthy merchant Wang family, but the gentry—the families of scholars.

Yinreng said, "I order you to strip them of their military power. If they go to prison obediently, and if they are found to be innocent later, I will compensate them."

Cha Muyang looked up. "And... if they are not obedient?"

Yinreng lowered his eyes. "If they don't obey the military tally, are you asking me?"

Cha Muyang bowed his head. "This subordinate obeys."

Yinreng said, "I give you five days. After five days, come to Cao Yin's place to report to me."

He tossed the tally to Cha Muyang, who caught it in terror.

"Keep the tally with you and return it to me in five days," Yinreng joked. "I trust you; do not let me down."

Cha Muyang's back was already soaked with cold sweat. "This subordinate will never let Your Highness down! Please wait for good news!"

"Let's go back," Yinreng said. "Five days is enough to settle the situation."

The moment Yinreng walked out the door, he became a servant again.

He walked with his head lowered, timid and trembling, as if he were very afraid of the atmosphere in the military camp.

Cao Yin was high and mighty, looking down on everyone, perfectly displaying the aloofness of a scholar and the arrogance of an emperor's close minister.

The aide entered the room. "General, that person was..."

Cha Muyang gripped the tally tightly, his voice trembling slightly. "Don't ask."

The aide hurriedly said, "Yes!"

Cha Muyang closed his eyes. After a long while, when he opened them, they were bloodshot.

He named several people and had his aide call them in one by one.

...

Cleaning out the military camp directly?

Yinreng sighed helplessly. "Ziqing, I didn't come here for that small civil unrest."

Cao Yin was stunned. If not for the civil unrest, then for...

He had a gut feeling that the Crown Prince was going to make a huge scene this time.

Five days later, rumors spread throughout the entire city of Hangzhou.

The bustling streets became desolate, and the people wore expressions of worry.

The Hangzhou Prefect tried to ban the rumors, but after he issued the order, he realized in confusion that the rumors were spreading even more fiercely than before. Even those who hadn't believed them now did, and many yamen runners had even run off using excuses.

Jin Hong complained to Cao Yin about this and asked for the Emperor's intentions.
