168. Two Chapters Combined into One [V]
The residences of the nobles in the capital were all clustered in one area.
In other words, although Mingju and Songgotu fought like cats and dogs whenever they met, they actually lived right next to each other.
When Kangxi originally bestowed residences upon the two meritorious officials who eliminated Oboi, he deliberately put them together, revealing the teenage Kangxi's mischievous sense of humor.
The young adult Kangxi's mischievous sense of humor was even stronger; later on, he bestowed new residences on Songgotu and Mingju—which turned out to be right next door to each other.

Now you can understand why Songgotu kept impeaching Mingju because someone outside the outer wall of Mingju's residence was burning incense and paper money to pray for good marriages? It was simply because the smoke was choking him.

The new residences bestowed by Kangxi were very close to the palace, and when it wasn't a rest day, Mingju and Songgotu basically lived there. Thus, when the Plain Blue Banner and Plain White Banner surrounded the mansions of Mingju and Songgotu, they also deployed their troops together.

Songgotu pushed open the door on their courtyard wall and grabbed the shoulders of Mingju, who was still unexpectedly drinking tea, shaking him fiercely: "You're still drinking your damn tea! Both of us are going to die right here!"
"We won't die; we're waiting for the Emperor's rescue." Mingju pushed Songgotu away and leisurely straightened his robes. "The Emperor will not abandon us."
Songgotu said gloomily: "Really? Will the Emperor's rescue arrive in time?"
Mingju glanced sideways at Songgotu and said, "The Emperor's rescue might not arrive in time, but Crown Prince will definitely protect us."
His own disciple—did he even need to ask? The Crown Prince definitely valued them deeply.

How did the Crown Prince become Mingju's disciple, you ask? Do you even need to ask? Back when the Crown Prince was still wobbling when he walked, who was the one who held him on his lap to give him his elementary education?
Did you think my title of Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince was fake? Hmph!

"That's true; Crown Prince places great value on me, his grand-uncle." Songgotu snatched Mingju's teacup and gulped down a mouthful. "It's a good thing the two of us got wind of it and sent our families out of the capital beforehand. Sigh, the Emperor is truly, truly... actually using the two of us as bait."
The more he spoke, the more aggrieved Songgotu felt: "What if they really burn us to death with a fire?"

Mingju gave Songgotu—who was chewing peonies like an ox—a sideways look, feeling heartbroken over his newly acquired, thousand-gold-worth new tea: "Hmph, the people of the Plain Blue Banner and Plain White Banner certainly won't burn us, but as for certain other people, it's hard to say."

Songgotu gulped down a mouthful of Mingju's super expensive tea and calmed down: "Could someone want to use our lives to pressure the Emperor? But given the Emperor's temperament, whether we live or die, he'll have backup plans."
A qualified monarch was extremely cold and ruthless when necessary.

Mingju said, "You and I are both bait placed on the chessboard by the Emperor. Whether we are captured by the other side won't affect the Emperor's victory. However, the two of us are not mere chess pieces, but living human beings. If something really happens to us, the Crown Prince might be very heartbroken, and it might even cause a rift in his relationship with the Emperor, so the Emperor will definitely guarantee our safety."
He gave Songgotu a blank look: "You know how to calculate political situations, but when it comes to calculating human hearts, you are still far behind."
Songgotu let out a cold snort and did not reply.
This time, he hoped Mingju's judgment was correct.

Songgotu hoped the Emperor would retain a backup plan to protect their lives out of consideration for the Crown Prince. This wasn't because he was greedy for life and feared death; he merely hoped that the Crown Prince revered the Emperor into his very bones, and that the Emperor could also treat him with familial affection.
The two sat facing each other and continued drinking tea.
This time Songgotu did not chew his tea like an ox, instead putting on an air of sufficient elegance and detachment.

Outside the courtyard wall, human voices were a boiling cauldron and the glow of torches soared into the sky; inside the courtyard wall, two old men sat facing each other, sipping light tea with serene expressions.
Liang Jiugong, who had slipped in to transmit the imperial decree, saw this scene and felt boundless admiration in his heart.
Grand Secretary Ming and Grand Secretary Song were truly the undisputed pillars of the court. This calm and composed attitude was truly astonishing.
"Liang Jiugong?" Songgotu was the first to clearly see the newcomer. "Why is it you?"
Liang Jiugong bowed and said, "Crown Prince has personally come."
Songgotu's hand trembled, and Mingju's thousand-gold white porcelain cup dropped onto the stone table, shattering into pieces: "The Crown Prince?!"
Mingju also dropped his teacup.

He cast a heartbroken look at the fragments of the teacup and frowned, saying, "A man of wealth and nobility does not sit under a crumbling eaves. How could the Crown Prince personally venture into a dangerous place?"

Liang Jiugong said, "Crown Prince is worried that someone might take this opportunity to stir up a mutiny and endanger Lord Song and Lord Ming. Crown Prince sent this slave in hoping that Lord Song and Lord Ming can lead people to disguise themselves and leave first, just in case."
Songgotu and Mingju exchanged glances and hurriedly had their household servants assemble to leave together, not daring to delay the Crown Prince's affairs.
But upon leaving, ignoring Liang Jiugong's obstruction, the two tacitly slipped away and blended into the crowd of onlookers, anxiously searching for the Crown Prince's traces.
Yinri led a hundred guards equipped with new-style flintlock guns and steel sabers, riding on horseback to personally rescue Songgotu and Mingju.
Not only did he come to the rescue personally, but he had also agreed with Kangxi that once he pacified the scene, Kangxi would appear at the appropriate moment.
If Kangxi missed such a great opportunity to reap fame in the military, Yinri would climb onto his emperor-father's back and wail just like he did when he was little.
Kangxi wiped his sweat: "No problem! I will definitely arrive on time!"
When Yinri rode his horse before the mutinous array of the Plain Blue Banner and Plain White Banner and hoisted the Crown Prince's insignia, the scene suddenly fell silent.
Yinri tightened his reins and slowly rode into the ranks of banner soldiers.
Without any orders from anyone, the banner soldiers automatically cleared a path wide enough for the Crown Prince's entourage to pass through.
Someone even passed torches forward, arranging two lines of flames on either side of the Crown Prince's entourage, as if creating a bright path out of thin air.

At Yinri's hint, the guards dismounted, holding their heads high and displaying the posture of having been rigorously trained, and solemnly followed the Crown Prince—who was mounted on a tall steed—into the encirclement of the mutinous banner soldiers.
Seeing the fearless Crown Prince and guards, the banner soldiers leaked a good deal of their inner confidence.
They immediately returned their sabers to their scabbards and quietly pushed them behind their waists to indicate that they had no intention whatsoever of harming the Crown Prince.

When Yinri reached the very center of the banner soldiers, the guards used whatever was at hand, actually enlisting the surrounding mutinous banner soldiers to help them temporarily build a high platform.

The banner soldiers foolishly went along with the work, a sight that caused some ambition-driven schemers who had slipped in to stir up trouble to beat their chests and stamp their feet in frustration.
These people couldn't accomplish anything!

Now the entire field had quieted down; those making a racket didn't dare utter a sound, and could only watch helplessly as Yinri moved a chair and sat upon the high platform, instantly controlling the situation.
Holding a large megaphone without a sound amplifier, Yinri roared through a speech to everyone present.
As for speeches, which liberal arts college student hadn't been forced onto the spot to participate in class, department, or school speech contests?
Even if he didn't know how, Yinri could use his golden finger to draw upon memories from his past life, adapting the classic speeches of famous leaders.
With cadenced tones, the most straightforward and unadorned vocabulary, and exaggerated body language, Yinri began his speech.

He started from history, popularizing the origin of the Eight Banners system for the clueless Eight Banners banner soldiers, going from history to the current situation, and from glory to predicament.
At times he spoke slowly and leisurely as if chatting about household matters, while at other times he clenched his fists and roared like a pre-battle oath.
The banner soldiers gazed up at Yinri's body, which was still youthful compared to their own, their facial expressions constantly shifting along with Yinri's tone.
"Gu understands why you are angry!"
"When you were born, the Great Qing was already the Great Qing. You are all people of the Great Qing, you are all merely people of the Great Qing, loyal only to the Emperor of the Great Qing."
"Yet you discovered that the Emperor cannot even dispose of his own army as he pleases."
"You don't understand, you are angry, and you believe this is treason!"
"Gu understands; Gu and the Imperial Father both understand!"
"Yet the old aristocracy has not yet grown old; how can we suddenly strip them of their special privileges? Wouldn't that chill the hearts of the nobles who fought to found the dynasty?"
"Lord Song and Lord Ming are not rebels; they merely hold different opinions. We all hope the Great Qing becomes better."
Yinri then used a small household for comparison.
As the head of a household, any decision regarding interests might reduce the interests of other branches in the family.
As the head of the great family, the Emperor wanting the entire family to be more prosperous is not wrong;
The dissatisfaction of those whose vested interests have been harmed is also not wrong;

We should seek common ground while reserving differences, discuss things properly, and strive for a method that both makes the family more prosperous and prevents the interests of those who have attained merits from being damaged.
"You have all eaten pastries. What do you do when there aren't enough pastries? Kill people? No, it is to find more pastry ingredients and make more pastries!"
"The reigning Emperor is the most brilliant sage emperor of the Great Qing; he will bring you more land and more wealth!"
"People of the Great Qing do not need to snatch pastries from people of the Great Qing to ensure everyone eats their fill!"

"The Manchus are like this, and the Han people are too. Everyone is a person of the Great Qing, and everyone is a subject of the most brilliant sage emperor! The Emperor is the sovereign of all of you!"……
While Yinri was roaring at the top of his lungs, Kangxi—who arrived right on schedule—appeared with the grand imperial entourage.
He walked step by step across the path illuminated by torches, ascended the high platform where Yinri was shouting, and took over from Yinri.
Kangxi said nothing; he merely had someone lift up a very, very large map—large enough for everyone present to see clearly.
Kangxi pointed at the map with a slender stick.
"The Great Qing is here."
The Great Qing was painted a bright yellow.
"The Direct Prince's fief is here."
"Here is the Ottoman Empire; here is the Russian state; here is France..."
The important and powerful countries were painted a bright red.
"These are their colonies."
The other colonies were white.
After introducing the world pattern, Kangxi put down the stick, spread his arms, and looked proudly at the subjects below the platform.
"Vast as the world is, if the Western barbarians can go there, so can we!"
After Kangxi finished these words, Yinri and the guards shouted together.
"If the Western barbarians can go there, so can we!"
The banner people felt their blood boiling and roared along.
"If the Western barbarians can go there, so can we!"
The onlookers, not knowing why, also felt their blood rush to their heads and raised their voices in shouts.
"If the Western barbarians can go there, so can we!"……
These words resounded through the inner city and lingered for a long time.
While Yinri was giving his speech, many officials and nobles harboring their own agendas had already slipped into the crowd.
They scrutinized this crown prince, who was young yet mature, shrewd, and cunningly intelligent, wanting to see how the Crown Prince would defuse this farce.
They had not expected that the Crown Prince had no intention of defusing the farce at all, but instead pushed it to an even crazier climax.

What they expected even less was that the Emperor not only ventured into danger himself, but didn't punish the rioting banner soldiers either, instead freezing this crazy farce at its most frenzied moment.
If they merely hadn't expected the previous events, then after following the Emperor to look at the world map, the violent pounding in their chests made them feel afraid.
They had been persuaded by the Crown Prince and the Emperor.
What was the point of food? There was only so much that could be eaten, and every year grain in the storehouses rotted away.
What was the point of gold and silver? There was only so much that could be used, and some rich people even used gold and silver to skim stones across water for fun.
They needed things that were fresher, more stimulating, and better able to display their status.
What could highlight their value better than rare items produced overseas?
While the Manchu officials were beaming with radiant faces, many Han civil officials despairingly closed their eyes.
The Manchus were indeed a bunch of barbarians.

Even after passing through the Shanhaiguan Pass, even after putting on court attire, and even after beginning to learn to speak classical phrases, the barbarism and blood-thirsty fierceness in their bones had not receded in the slightest.
They were a pack of jackals and tigers wearing human skin.
After despairing, most of the Han officials stubbornly opened their eyes again, forcing themselves to look at the world map behind the Emperor.
Some of them thought, "Heaven destroys those who do not look out for themselves."
Some of them thought, "If I do not enter hell, who will?"
Others among them were dazzled by the prosperity overseas.
In the end, they clenched their fists and roared along with reddened eyes.
"If the Western barbarians can go there, so can we!"
At this moment, these words entered the hearts of everyone present.
The next day, these words reached the ears of all the commoners in Beijing city.

Yinzhi worked overnight to step up the printing of newspapers, publishing the matter in full detail without embellishment. The article was personally drafted and penned by Yinri, with stylistic refinements by Kangxi.
In just a month, this newspaper spread to all corners of the Great Qing, and even missionaries saw it.
When the missionary Joachim Bouvet (Bai Jin) saw this newspaper, his hands trembled uncontrollably.
Bai Jin was a missionary sent to the Great Qing by King Louis XIV of France. He acted on Louis XIV's orders to deliver Louis XIV's letters and test the Great Qing's attitude toward Catholicism.

Previously, Kangxi had banned Catholicism from spreading in the Great Qing due to the Chinese rites controversy—actually, not just Catholicism. Kangxi didn't care about different denominational branches like Catholicism or Protestantism; he banned them all in one fell swoop.

The Crown Prince of the Great Qing had originally planned to visit the Vatican, but the Pope made the Crown Prince wait for two or three months on the grounds that he needed to fast and preside over some important ceremony.
The Crown Prince of the Great Qing simply loaded up the gifts intended for the Pope and returned to the Great Qing.
Feeling that he had lost face, the Pope wanted to find Catholic-believing kings to jointly denounce the Crown Prince.

As a result, whether it was Louis XIV of France or James II of England, both wrote letters rebuking the Pope for treating the Great Qing Crown Prince slowly, which caused the situation of the ban on religion in the Great Qing.
Clearly, for these two monarchs, they believed in Catholicism, but they didn't care much for the Pope's authority.
Europe nowadays was a place of powerful nation-states and kings to which religion was attached, rather than the Pope being the co-sovereign of multiple countries.
Bai Jin had entered the Great Qing last year.
Particularly unfortuitously, as soon as he arrived in the Great Qing, he happened to encounter the Grand Empress Dowager falling gravely ill and passing away.

The entire realm of the Great Qing was shrouded in grief. The Emperor argued with ministers every day over his grandmother's funeral, so how could Bai Jin, trembling with fear, dare to test the Great Qing Emperor who was like a roaring lion?
He could only subscribe to the Great Qing newspapers every day, translate useful news from the papers, and put it into letters written to Louis XIV.

Fortunately, the Great Qing Emperor also greatly admired their great Sun King; although he didn't allow him to preach, he treated him very well in terms of living standards and was even willing to dispatch special personnel to help him send letters to France.
However, worried that his letters might be leaked, Bai Jin only accumulated the letters he wanted to write, preparing to take them back to France personally.
When he saw the Great Qing Emperor's ambition, he could no longer sit still.
He believed that this matter must be transmitted back to France immediately.
The sleeping lion of the East had awakened! The Great Qing was by no means a peace-loving country as the Crown Prince claimed; they were also going to demand a share of the pie in world hegemony!
What was even more terrifying was that the Great Qing was full of heretics! They were heretics who believed in multiple deities and deserved to be tied to the stake and burned alive!
This trip had allowed Bai Jin to witness the prosperity of the Great Qing, and even more so, a culture vastly different from Europe and France.

The whole of Europe could still be said to share the same roots and origin. People of the Great Qing were like beings from another world; from their appearance to their culture, they were completely different from Europe.
"Those not of our race are bound to have different hearts." After learning this Great Qing proverb, Bai Jin deeply agreed with it.

Bai Jin believed that France should not become an ally of the Great Qing, but should join hands with other great children of the Heavenly Father who shared the same blood and roots to attack this terrifying country full of heretics!
Here there was vast land, massive wealth, and countless slaves.
The land of the Great Qing should naturally be the paradise bestowed by the great Heavenly Father upon His most loyal believers.
Greed and fanaticism flashed in Bai Jin's eyes.
Up in the roof beams, a figure in black shrunk into a ball, holding a charcoal pencil and scratching away to record his words.
Half an hour later, the candles in Bai Jin's room were blown out, and his words appeared on Kangxi's dragon desk.

Kangxi had just dealt with the ringleaders of this mutiny by the Plain Blue Banner and Plain White Banner, letting some off lightly while severely punishing them, purging certain individuals, and gathering the actual power of the two banners into his hands.
He hadn't even been happy for half a month when he was so angered by this letter that he wanted to draw his sword directly and hack Bai Jin to death himself.
"Ungrateful wretch, ungrateful wretch! Have I not treated him well enough?!" Kangxi slammed the table in anger.

"What's wrong with you, Aama? Are you sick? Has your brain been fried by a fever? Those Catholic fellows were ungrateful wretches to begin with, and those European fellows were bound to covet the Great Qing—wasn't that something you knew a few years ago? Why are you still shocked and angry now? Have you amnesia?"
Kangxi: "..."
Yinri quietly retreated a few steps to prevent any blood from patricide splashing onto himself.
Words so specifically designed to rub Kangxi the wrong way naturally came from the Great Qing's number one filial son, the Direct Prince.

Hearing that the Plain Blue Banner and Plain White Banner had mutinied, the Direct Prince marched into the capital without an imperial edict, traveling day and night with only a few dozen men, and arrived at the gates of Beijing on the morning of the second day of the mutiny.

If the courier hadn't run slightly faster than Yinzhen, and if Yinri hadn't rushed out to greet him in person upon receiving the news, Yinzhen would probably have been impeached by ministers for plotting rebellion.

When Galdan was on his eastern expedition against the Khalkha tribe, because of a political coup plotted by his poisoned brother's son, he had now hastily retreated. Yinzhen had nothing to do for the time being, and Kangxi also missed this eldest son he hadn't seen in a long time, so he allowed Yinzhen to stay in the capital to prepare for his wedding.

According to ritual institutions, an imperial prince should observe nine months of mourning for the Grand Empress Dowager, and Yinzhen had already completed the mourning period on June 25th. However, he had been out on the grasslands all along, so the matter of his wedding had been shelved.
Kangxi had recently been driven frantic by the ministers, and wanted Yinzhen to get married quickly and take a daughter-in-law to cheer himself up.
On the first day of Yinzhen's return to the capital, Kangxi and the Direct Prince shared deep father-son affection, and Consort Hui wept with joy, crying until a handkerchief was soaked through.
His son had grown up! His son had matured! His son finally knew not to make the Emperor angry!
On the sixth day after Yinzhi returned to the capital, Kangxi chased after the Prince Zhijun to beat him up.
Consort Hui was very calm. It's fine, my son behaved himself for a whole five days! Her son had grown up, her son had matured, her son would be fine once he took a wife.
In the eyes of a feudal traditional mother, taking a wife could cure all illnesses!
Right now, Kangxi just wanted Yinzhi to get lost immediately, preferably never to return.
Before his old father's anger could erupt, Yinzhi smoothed things over: "Even though Imperial Father knows, he still feels hurt because his good intentions were betrayed. That's only human nature."
Yinzhi thought about it and nodded: "That's true as well. Imperial Father, don't be angry; your son will go chop Joachim Bouvet right now."
Kangxi waved a hand, and Yinreng immediately hung onto Yinzhi, stopping him just as he had taken a step forward.
"Eldest Brother, that's not how you kill people. We are still in a friendly alliance with France," Yinreng said quickly. "If we want him dead, we should use a borrowed knife."
Yinzhi said impatiently: "So much trouble. Just tell me what to do, and tell me directly where you need me."
Although impatient, he honestly stopped in his tracks and didn't rush out to hack people behind his younger brother's back.
Kangxi felt a sense of relief. The eldest son had indeed matured. Once the eldest son took a wife, he would surely become even more mature.
In the eyes of a feudal traditional mother, taking a wife could cure all illnesses!

"Alright. There is indeed something for Eldest Brother to do right now," Yinreng said. "Imperial Father wants to reorganize the Plain Blue Banner and the Bordered White Banner. Drilling troops is Eldest Brother's specialty. Would Eldest Brother be willing to take charge of this for a while, until the new commander takes office?"

Yinzhi said: "Sure. I'm also sick of staying in the palace and listening to Consort Mother nag. Consort Mother really is getting more and more annoying. Is this what Younger Brother calls hitting menopause?"
Yinreng: "...... Consort Hui isn't even that old yet."
Kangxi asked curiously: "What is menopause?"

Yinzhi said: "It's when people get old and their temper changes, becoming suspicious, jealous, and paranoid. As people age, not only do their bones and skin shrink, but their brains and hearts shrink too, making them less and less like normal people. Throughout history, emperors in the historical records sob sob sob..."
Yinreng hurriedly covered Yinzhi's mouth.
Eldest Brother! My good Eldest Brother! Can't you censor yourself a bit?! Can you just say anything?!
Kangxi's mouth twitched: "What are you covering his mouth for? Isn't it just menopause?"
Yinreng gave an awkward laugh: "Eldest Brother definitely wasn't speaking ill of Consort Hui; Imperial Father must not spread rumors."
Kangxi put on a straight face: "Would I go spreading words to the consorts? Fine, fine, I know. You don't want words about the First Prince being unfilial to get out. I won't tell Consort Hui."
I won't say it publicly, I'll secretly tell Consort Hui that her son said she was losing her mind, Kangxi thought to himself.
Faced with Yinzhi's torment, Kangxi needed someone to share it with. Seeing Consort Hui suffering even more than him made him feel a lot more comfortable inside.
"Son is going to discuss with Eldest Brother how to handle the matter of the French missionaries. Imperial Father, please continue with your busy work." Yinreng grabbed Yinzhi and ran.
Yinzhi was dragged along by Yinreng, looking feeble and completely at the mercy of others, appearing utterly harmless.
Kangxi couldn't help laughing.
After laughing for a moment, his smile vanished, and he sighed: "Menopause, huh..."

Did emperors throughout history suspect the crown prince not only out of jealousy of the prince's youth and fear of their own aging, but also because of the natural shrinking of the heart and brain, turning them into senile fools?
In the prime of his life, Kangxi touched his chest, then touched his head, feeling a sense of melancholy.

169. Two Chapters Combined [V]
With Yinzhi back, the younger princes didn't dare to act mischievous anymore.
Yinzhi touched his head and said in disbelief: "Why is Imperial Father still spreading rumors that I eat children?"
Yinreng served tea to Yinzhi: "Congratulations, Eldest Brother, on achieving the fierce general status of stopping small children from crying."
After finishing his tea, Yinzhi said: "I've been drinking in the grasslands all this time, so I'm somewhat unaccustomed to drinking bland tea."
Yinreng produced a porcelain bottle from his chest as if by magic: "Want to try this?"
Yinzhi opened the wine bottle, sniffed it, and smiled: "What is this?"

Yinreng said: "Burning Knife. The alcohol content is very high, and it doesn't spoil easily. Remember to mix it with water when drinking. If you get injured, pour it on the wound; it can prevent the wound from worsening. Next time you set out, I'll pack more for you."
Yinzhi tucked the wine bottle into his chest: "Good, prepare more. Let's go, since they're afraid of me, I'll let them be afraid to their heart's content."
Yinzhi rubbed his palms together eagerly.
Although life on the grasslands was livelier than in the capital, losing the fun of teasing his younger brothers still left Yinzhi feeling rather regretful.
After returning, Yinzhi spoke with the instructors at the drill grounds, and the martial arts lessons were temporarily handed over to him to teach.
Yinzhi even brought along the few younger princes who hadn't started school yet to teach them together.

Yinreng stood off to the side with his arms crossed, watching. This wasn't Eldest Brother teaching his younger brothers; it was a total beating of his younger brothers to establish his prestige in front of them.
Poor younger brothers, even if they understood that Eldest Brother didn't eat children, they would probably still be left with psychological shadows in their hearts.
The smaller brothers were suppressed by Yinzhi, but Yinzhi and Yinzhen, as before, remained unconvinced.
The two of them grew bolder with every fight, and when working together, they really looked like they knew what they were doing.
This wasn't battlefield combat, so Yinzhi wouldn't deal fatal blows, and he actually got tangled up by them.
Yinzhi and Yinzhen were extremely proud and told the younger brothers to all charge together.
Fighting Eldest Brother meant no rules of martial honor.
Yinzhi was poked by the cloth-wrapped wooden swords of his younger brothers and howled in pain: "Baocheng! Come help me quickly!"
Yinreng smiled, picked up a cloth-wrapped wooden sword, and came over to guard Yinzhi's flank.
For many of the younger brothers, this was the first time they had seen their Crown Prince brother take action.
They suspected that Crown Prince brother could read minds; no matter from what tricky angle they threw a strike, it would be met with a whack on the back of the hand by Crown Prince brother.
After a few rounds, the backs of their hands were all swollen from being hit.
Yinzhi was immensely proud: "With the two of our brothers joining forces, we are invincible under heaven!"
"Oh? I'd like to see just how much you two are really worth."
A burst of laughter rang out, and Yinzhi's face instantly collapsed.

He gave a perfunctory arch of his hands in salute: "Imperial Father, if my younger brothers and I are serious, we could definitely beat you. But what if you resort to underhanded tricks and blame my younger brothers and me? I wouldn't mind—I'd just run off to the grasslands to hide. But Younger Brother still has to coax you... Ouch. Even if you rap your son's head, what your son said is the truth. Ouch, stop tapping, it hurts."
While tapping Yinzhi's head with a folding fan, Kangxi said angrily to Yinreng: "Baocheng, you judge this. Am I such a petty person?!"

Yinreng smiled to smooth things over: "Eldest Brother didn't mean Imperial Father is petty. It's just that Imperial Father, as both sovereign and father, always needs to maintain some face. If it's just one-on-one, we couldn't win against Imperial Father. But if it's two-on-one... Look, even the young brothers gathered together could suppress Eldest Brother; for you to win would be difficult."
Kangxi snorted coldly: "Then you're not allowed to make a move."
He looked at Yinzhi (Yinzhi) and Yinzhen: "Your martial skills are passable. Join forces with the eldest. I'll use a long staff, and you use wooden swords."
With that, Kangxi fetched a wooden stick smeared with ink and drew circles, insisting on having a sparring match with Yinzhi, Yinzhi, and Yinzhen.
Yinzhi sighed while rubbing his palms together eagerly.
Yinzhi and Yinzhen looked at each other in dismay. Fight against Imperial Father? They didn't quite dare.
"Go on, Imperial Father is teaching you martial arts, learn with all your heart," Yinreng encouraged the two of them. "Imperial Father is very strong, you don't need to worry."

An inch longer meant an inch stronger; Kangxi's long wooden staff already had the advantage over the three princes' small wooden swords. Moreover, although Yinzhi was strong, he was dragged down by his two younger brothers.
Yinreng could already foresee the outcome.
Imperial Father is truly insidious.
And the facts proved this true.

Earlier, the younger princes could suppress Yinzhi when they grouped together because there were no rules to the match. Those kids relied on the fact that Yinzhi wouldn't hit them hard, grabbing his legs and arms, hanging all over him.
Now there were rules. First, you couldn't step out of the circle; second, if an ink mark hit a vital spot, you were out.

Yinzhi had two half-grown kids running around chaotically beside him, making it impossible to unleash his skills; Kangxi leisurely poked away with his long staff, beating his sons like they were grandchildren.
Yinreng gave a dry cough.
Yinzhi's irritable mood calmed down, and he looked at Yinreng.
Yinreng blinked at Yinzhi, then made a horizontal swiping gesture.
Yinzhi cracked a wide grin and kicked Yinzhen right in the backside as Yinzhen rushed forward howling.
Yinzhen lost his balance, fell to the ground, and rolled head over heels toward Kangxi.
Kangxi was startled by the rolling Yinzhen and performed a frog leap, jumping right over him.
"Third Brother, go!" Yinzhi roared.
The tacit understanding cultivated with Yinzhi since childhood made Yinzhi instantly grasp Yinzhi's command; he immediately threw away his sword and grabbed Kangxi's legs just as he landed.
Kangxi: "?"
"Imperial Father, take this!" Yinzhi gripped his sword with both hands and slashed upward from below.
Kangxi's hand vibrated; though he didn't drop the long staff, it exposed an opening at his chest.
Yinzhi thrust the sword in his hand forward and pressed it against Kangxi's chest: "Imperial Father, your son has won."

Yinzhen scrambled up from the ground, patted the dirt off his clothes and head, threw away his wooden sword, and cheered while hopping on one foot: "We won, we won! We beat Imperial Father! Hahaha, Eldest Brother is invincible under heaven!"
Yinzhi rubbed his chest where he had been bumped by Kangxi's leg: "Ouch, that really hurts. But we won, hahaha!"
Yinzhi proudly cupped his hands in salute: "Imperial Father, we accept the win. Are there any rewards?"
Kangxi first rolled his eyes at Yinzhi, then glared at Yinreng.
Yinreng glanced to the side and started whistling.
Kangxi was amused to the point of anger. Bad son! So slick from childhood to adulthood!
"Fine, reward." Although Yinreng had been plotting behind the scenes, it was a fact that Yinzhi had won against him while dragging two dead weights, and Kangxi was rather pleased.
He rewarded Yinzhi with a set of fine brush, ink, paper, and inkstone, Yinzhen with a new sword, and Yinzhi with a bolt of silk.
Yinzhi was utterly baffled: "Imperial Father, I only get a bolt of silk?"
Kangxi teased: "This is a reward for you to woo your wife."
Yinzhi was speechless. Could he say that he didn't want a reward for an unfamiliar wife, but wanted a reward for himself instead?
Although Yinzhi had caught a glimpse of the Irgen Gioro clan when he was young and had liked that sweet-smiling little girl back then.
But how many years ago was that? Yinzhi had long since forgotten what the Irgen Gioro clan looked like, and naturally wouldn't hold any emotional attachment to her.

"Eldest Brother, take it. You always have to send something to Eldest Sister-in-law," Yinreng said. "Little Brother also has some jewelry collected here; Eldest Brother can take it to have jewelry made for Eldest Sister-in-law."
Yinzhi snapped back irritably: "Why give it to me? Didn't you also get betrothed? Keep it for yourself."
Yinreng said: "Her? Giving her these gold and silver jewels is far less useful than giving her a pile of scientific experimental equipment."
Besides, scientific experimental equipment was much more expensive than gold and silver jewelry, Yinreng complained internally.

Nothing burned money quite like doing science. Ever since Li Tong became the crown princess-to-be, she spent money even more lavishly. Although her output was also massive, Yinreng's heart would tremble every time he looked at her budget reports.

After listening to Yinreng's explanation, Yinzhi said: "Your woman is harder to deal with than mine. But the machines she makes are genuinely useful. When can steam engines be used on land vehicles so we won't need to raise horses anymore?"
Yinreng said: "Soon. We're currently lacking a material called rubber, which Eldest Brother can grow in your fief."
Yinzhi asked Kangxi: "Imperial Father, when can your son return to his fief?"
Kangxi had found it quite uninteresting listening to the two of them talk about their future wives with straight faces.
Hearing now that Yinzhi wanted to return to his fief, he said: "What's the rush? Can you bear to leave Baocheng?"
Yinzhi said: "I can't bear it, but once the domestic situation stabilizes, staying in the capital is boring anyway. It's better to help Imperial Father properly manage Nanyang."
Kangxi said: "We'll talk about that when the time comes. We haven't fought the Dzungars yet."
Yinreng couldn't help complaining: "Imperial Father, you finally remembered that we haven't fought the Dzungars yet?"
Kangxi gave Yinreng a light tap on the head: "You are not allowed to copy Baobao's—Baoging's way of speaking!"
The father and three sons chatted naturally, while the other princes—especially the younger ones who feared Kangxi—looked on with immense envy.
They also wanted to chat with Imperial Father like this.
Once they grew up, would they stop fearing Imperial Father? They really wanted to grow up.
Upon learning of the younger brothers' pipe dreams, Yinzhi and Yinzhen both shrugged helplessly.

Don't even think about it, it's impossible. Putting Crown Prince brother aside for a moment, why could Eldest Brother hang out with Imperial Father so casually? Because Eldest Brother was beaten by Imperial Father from childhood to adulthood and never mended his ways despite repeated admonitions.
They didn't have Eldest Brother's audacity to get beaten every day yet still seek out beatings every day, until finally even Imperial Father couldn't be bothered to hit them anymore.
However, Yinzhi and Yinzhen also felt a pang of envy in their hearts.

Perhaps Eldest Brother and Crown Prince brother really did hold different statuses in Imperial Father's heart. Aside from Yinzhi and Yinreng, they were the only ones who had birth names: Baoqing and Baocheng.

After stretching his muscles by sparring with his sons, Kangxi returned to handling state affairs. If an emperor in feudal times wanted to be a decent ruler, he had no choice but to toil over paperwork day in and day out.
Yinreng was given a brief holiday by Kangxi to accompany Yinzhi in dealing with the aftermath of the Eight Banners mutiny.
Yinzhi raised an eyebrow: "This counts as a holiday? This counts as a holiday? The holiday Imperial Father gave you is just changing places to work?"
Yinreng spread his hands: "What else?"

Yinzhi said: "Third and Fourth have both been put to work by Imperial Father, so I suppose there's really no help for it. Let's wander around the banner camps for a bit first, and then go play in the city for a while."
Yinreng smiled: "Alright."
As for slacking off, the two of them were old pros at it.

It was a pity that the three bodyguards who used to be by their side had now gone their separate ways: Cao Yin was in Nanjing, Nalan Rongruo was an ambassador to the Ottomans, and Orundai had been sent off by Kangxi goodness knows where.
But even without those three bodyguards, they could still find "substitutes."

And so, Yinzhi's former study companion Kuadai, Nalan Xingde's younger brother Nalan Kuixu, and another of Yinreng's maternal uncles, Changhai, were temporarily drafted as laborers to accompany the two imperial princes on a stroll.
Changhai was not as talented as Changtai; his own abilities were merely standard and mediocre, but he grew up with self-awareness and acted relatively low-key.
He rarely appeared in front of Yinreng, and even the court had forgotten that he was also Yinreng's uncle, acting as though Yinreng only had Changtai as an uncle.
Yet in his heart, he never harbored resentment or jealousy.

When Gabula passed away, he had already mapped out paths for his two sons. Changtai would pioneer glory for the Hesheri family and escort the Crown Prince; Changhai would hide behind Changtai's light, carefully preserving himself for the continuation of the Hesheri family.

Changtai looked glorious now, but Changtai was also in danger. Once the Hesheri family fell, the one who survived would be Changhai. And the glory brought by Changtai was something Changhai could share as well.
Sometimes, Changhai had indeed wondered if he should swap places with his eldest brother.

But recalling how, in their childhood, his eldest brother could stand in a horse stance for an entire day until he fainted, while he himself would roll all over the ground and throw tantrums after half an hour, he immediately dismissed the thought.
Being an idle noble suited him much better after all.
When Yinreng invited him to skip work today, Changhai was stunned for a moment. Remembering Changtai's instructions, he immediately went to snitch to the Emperor.
Kangxi was overjoyed; not only did he grant Changhai leave, but he also dispatched the Third and Fourth Princes along as well.
"The Emperor said the Third Prince and Fourth Prince have also worked hard today," Changhai said.
Yinzhi rubbed his forehead: "This prince just wanted to go out and roam carefree with the Crown Prince, yet I still have to bring kids along."
With the other younger brothers gone, Yinzhi acted much more arrogant in front of Yinzhi.
He put his hands on his hips and said unhappily: "What! Got something to complain about?!"
"I have plenty of complaints," Yinzhi pinched Yinzhi's arm. "You were pretty fierce when you were little, so how come you went off to mess with writing brushes now?"
Yinzhi said: "Eldest Brother has already claimed the martial side, so Younger Brother can only develop on the literary side."
Yinzhi nodded: "That's true as well. That publishing house of yours isn't bad."
Yinzhen immediately chimed in: "I'm different! I'm proficient in both pen and sword!"
Yinzhi retorted: "Fourth Brother, what you do cannot be called proficiency in both pen and sword. Never mind, if you say so, then so be it."
He always felt that his younger brothers were all eccentric oddities.
Even the quiet little clique of the Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Brothers gave him a chilling sensation.

The four princes visited the banner camp once, re-examined the new laws and decrees Kangxi had already promulgated, and personally sparred a few rounds with the low-ranking officers to win their cheers, before leaving the camp to have fun in the city.
Speaking of having fun, there wasn't actually anywhere particularly fun to go.
Yinzhi had actually wanted to visit certain pleasure quarters—he was just curious, thinking he had grown up and should go broaden his horizons—only to be cursed from head to toe by Yinreng.
For the Prince Zhijun to visit pleasure quarters, and to do so right when he was betrothed—just how fried did his eldest brother's brain have to be to think of such a thing?
Helplessly, Yinzhi had to return to his old profession and go listen to operas instead.
Through Yinreng's promotion, besides traditional operas, there were now many adapted foreign plays and dramas in the capital.
Actors dressed in foreigners' clothes stood on stage passionately enacting the grievances and romances of foreign royal families, which was quite popular among the ordinary citizens of the capital.

Ever since they learned that overseas was overflowing with wealth, the common people grew increasingly fond of inquiring about foreign lands. Foreign dramas happened to hit right on their preferences.

Yinzhi was better off; while running the publishing house, he hadn't touched few foreign plays. Yinzhen dealt with confiscations of property and beheadings every day and hadn't had the time to watch plays.
Yinreng shoved a handful of copper coins into Yinzhen's hand, telling Yinzhen to tip as he pleased.
Yinzhen pulled Yinzhi to the front of the stage, occupying the liveliest spot. Yinzhi and Yinreng sat upstairs, watching the show while chatting.
Yinzhi said: "Has Joachim Bouvet already left the capital?"
Yinreng said: "He has to go to Guangzhou first to rendezvous with the Paris Society."

The Paris Society was a branch of the Catholic order, with its main members being missionaries from France, and also one of the most stubborn and anti-Chinese factions in the clash of Sino-Western interests.
European Catholicism was in decline, and the most powerful Catholic nation was France. The Paris Society practically represented the secular attitude of the Catholic Church.

Yinzhi snorted coldly: "When we were on our embassy, Louis XIV said all those things about viewing us as nephews. Did he not lift a finger regarding the Pope's cold reception and the Catholic Church's current haughtiness toward the Great Qing?"

Yinreng said: "He didn't need to lift a finger; he only needed to offer interests, and the Pope would be foolish and short-sighted enough. It's just a minor squabble; it doesn't affect our alliance with France."
Yinreng smiled: "Nor does it affect our alliance with Protestant nations."
He pulled a letter from his sleeve and pushed it toward Yinzhi.
After unsealing it, Yinzhi frowned as he looked at the page full of cursive script. Having not read foreign languages for a long time, he found it a bit slow.
After a good while, he couldn't help laughing: "William and Mary are going to England? James is getting driven away after all?"
Yinreng said: "Isn't this the brilliant idea my good brother came up with for his pen pal, letting King James develop the New World?"
Yinzhi burst into hearty laughter, and Yinreng couldn't help laughing either.
The Glorious Revolution, which was originally supposed to start this year, had actually kicked off right on schedule. It was just that the story behind it had undergone many changes.
James II had never openly provoked the Church of England; he merely accumulated strength in secret, continuously sending his own people to the New World.
Having already established great meritorious service in the New World, he held immense prestige there, making it very easy to seize power in the New World.
When James II's Catholic wife gave birth to a male infant, the English Protestants made trouble once more, wanting James II to take a Protestant queen and forcing him to make concessions.
However, because James II had not openly opposed the Church of England and had never received the Pope's envoys throughout his life, this trouble was still limited to parliamentary bickering.

Even though Spain was defeated by France, these colonies hadn't been lost yet. Because France possessed vast colonies in Africa and lacked sufficient manpower and material resources to occupy the New World—and it was relatively far from them, making it hard to plunder.

Afterwards, Spain's American colonies would be gradually nibbled away by Britain and the newly established United States over a hundred years later. After World War II, Britain's colonies in the Americas were entirely acquired by the United States, forming the current partition.
It was still ninety years away from the founding of the United States. And the west coast of North America was so close to the Great Qing, heh...

While Yinzhen and Yinzhi were discussing matters concerning the Americas, Joachim Bouvet and the members of the Paris Society were already preparing to leave the Qing Empire together and return to France.
As they boarded the ship, they looked back one last time at the bountiful Qing Empire.
The Old Testament of the Bible coined a term called "The Promised Land."

According to legend, God bestowed Canaan upon Abraham. Since Canaan already had indigenous inhabitants, Abraham's descendants—the Hebrews—carried out a cruel slaughter and expulsion of the Canaanites, usurping the land of Canaan.
Expelling the indigenous people of Canaan was a right granted to the Hebrews by God.

Later, the "Promised Land" became a universal excuse for Western colonization. For instance, when the United States expanded westward from the narrow East Coast and massacred Native Americans, they also believed that the land where Native Americans had lived for generations was the "Promised Land" granted to them by God.
They coined another term: "Manifest Destiny."

That is, they were acting under God's command to slaughter and expel Native Americans, hunting them like animals. Whether it was scalping Native Americans or using their skulls as decorations, it was all "Manifest Destiny."
At this moment, these Catholic priests of the Paris Society had not yet uttered "Manifest Destiny," but they had long been murmuring about the "Promised Land" in their hearts.
Journeying east, there lay a land flowing with milk and honey—a land bestowed by God upon His believers.
This was not Canaan; this was the Qing Empire, the land of Huaxia spoken of by these heretics!
Could there be any place more worthy of being God's chosen people than the land of Huaxia?!
The missionaries of the Paris Society, their hearts stirred with surging emotions, gazed lingeringly at the Qing Empire until this fertile land vanished below the horizon.
They would recount their experiences in the Qing Empire to the great Sun King. Once the Sun King conquered Europe, this territory would surely become a new domain of the Sun King.
They hoped for it, and they believed in it.
But very soon, their surging passion was cooled.

A fleet of pirate ships flying Spanish flags plundered them of the gifts the Qing Empire had sent to the Sun King, tied the missionaries to the deck, and amused themselves by using them as bait to catch sharks.
Fortunately, the Qing navy arrived in a timely manner, drove off the Spanish pirate ships, rescued the surviving missionaries, and very cordially agreed to escort them back to France.

The matter should have ended right there. But at this point, a missionary who had been rescued by the Qing military felt a pang of conscience and handed over the letters that Joachim Bouvet had written to the Sun King to the Qing general.
The Qing general was furious, immediately led the missionaries on a return voyage, and reported the matter to the Emperor of the Qing.
The Qing Emperor dispatched a new diplomatic mission, escorting those ill-intentioned missionaries back to demand an explanation from the Sun King, Louis XIV.
This incident was written about in the new issue of the newspaper.
The subsequent newspapers, academic weeklies, and university seminar classes were all studying the Bible and Western history.
The literati in the capital began arguing once again.

One faction believed that they should continue the seclusion policy, establish diplomatic relations with no foreign nations, and not negotiate with tigers for their skins; the other faction believed that the country could not be locked away—they had to step outside and display their own strength to make those who harbored malicious intentions feel awe and dread.

The ministers in the imperial court also argued into a chaotic mess, and the matters regarding the Grand Empress Dowager's mausoleum and the handling of the Eight Banners mutiny were temporarily shelved by the ministers.
The Paris Society missionary incident served as a convenient stepping stone for them to back down and yield to the Kangxi Emperor.
After a chaotic entire year, the final two months finally grew peaceful.
In November, the Grand Empress Dowager was posthumously honored with the title Empress Xiaozhuangwen, and her tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

In December, while inspecting the "Zhaoxi Mausoleum" built for the Grand Empress Dowager, the Kangxi Emperor took the opportunity to visit his father's resting place and erected a Stele of Divine Merits and Saintly Virtues for him, fully affirming the lifelong achievements of Emperor Shizu, Fulin.
This time, the Kangxi Emperor fundamentally and openly overturned Fulin's "Edict of Self-Reproach," determining that Fulin's measures to promote Manchu-Han assimilation were entirely correct.

In history, the Kangxi Emperor also erected a Stele of Divine Merits and Saintly Virtues for Emperor Shunzhi, affirming his achievements, overturning Shunzhi's "Edict of Self-Reproach," and expressing his own determination to reform the Qing Empire.
Unfortunately, the three campaigns against Galdan and the War of the Nine Princes completely dragged down Kangxi's grand ambitions.

The Kangxi Emperor in this spacetime had practically accomplished every single thing he wanted to do, and he even had an executive vice-emperor cleaning up his messes. He was far more ambitious and filled with grand aspirations than the Kangxi Emperors of other spacetimes.

Bringing Yinzhen along, the Kangxi Emperor pointed at the Stele of Divine Merits and Saintly Virtues and said, "Baocheng, the Stele of Divine Merits and Saintly Virtues built for Us in the future must be twice as large as this one."
Yinzhen: "Alright, alright, alright. Yes, yes, yes. No problem at all."
Yinzhi rolled his eyes secretly behind Yinzhen's back.
This imperial father was truly too childish to bear watching. Without a younger brother to take care of him, could he really manage to be a proper emperor?

After building the Stele of Divine Merits and Saintly Virtues for Shunzhi to sing praises of his achievements, the Kangxi Emperor continued his Southern Inspection tour, accompanied by the Crown Prince, the Prince Zhi, the Third Prince, and the Fourth Prince.
First, he visited the Tianjin naval base, then inspected the river engineering works, and finally went to Nanjing to give Cao Yin a thorough beating.
After being beaten black and blue by the Kangxi Emperor, Cao Yin was patted on the shoulder and praised, and the Emperor bestowed upon him a concurrent third-rank military post.
"Don't worry, Us will definitely give you the opportunity to go out and fight in wars in the future," the Kangxi Emperor promised Cao Yin.
Cao Yin, his face battered and bruised, was moved to tears of gratitude.
Yinzhen whispered quietly among his older and younger brothers.
"Even when Imperial Father beats people, he shouldn't hit them in the face."
"Indeed, indeed. Why does Imperial Father specifically aim for Ziqing's face?"
"Perhaps because Ziqing is growing more and more handsome?"
"What! Imperial Father is jealous of Ziqing's beauty!" The youngest of them all, the Fourth Prince, Yinzhen, had a super loud voice. "Imperial Father is actually such a person."
Cao Yin: "..."
Kangxi: "..."
Kangxi: "The whip!"
He extended his hand, and Zhao Chang immediately handed the whip—specially designated for beating his sons—over to the Kangxi Emperor.
This whip, which was previously only used to beat Yinzhi and Yinzhen, finally landed on a new prince today.
Seeing his Eldest Brother and Crown Prince Brother scramble up a tree in an instant, Fourth Prince Yinzhen felt a profound sense of *f****.
After taking his beating, he looked around in all directions for his Third Brother.
Eldest Brother and Crown Prince Brother immediately climbed trees the moment Imperial Father pulled out the whip, but how come Third Brother was missing too?
Yinzhen looked left and right, only to find that Yinshi was busy helping the Kangxi Emperor wipe the whip clean and put it away properly.

Yinzhen: "..." Can this Third Brother still be kept? Your younger brother here just got beaten, and you're actually helping Imperial Father tidy up the murder weapon used to beat your younger brother? Why didn't you just help join in the beating directly?
Yinshi said innocently, "Fourth Brother, misfortune comes from the mouth. Eldest Brother has been beaten since he was small; do you also want to be beaten from youth until now?"
Yinzhen: "......We are breaking ties. I have no such brother as you."
Thus, the Fourth Prince and Third Prince underwent a brief severance of ties, which only healed the next day when Yinshi helped Yinzhen write his self-reflection essay.
Cao Yin stood to the side, grinning while baring his teeth.
Having not seen the Emperor's family for a long time, he had missed them terribly. Now, seeing that the Emperor and the princes still got along with such warmth, he breathed a sigh of relief.
At least for now, the Emperor's feelings toward the princes, especially toward the Crown Prince, had not changed.
*Hiss*, the bruising on his face really hurt.
During this trip to Nanjing, the Kangxi Emperor also went to pay respects at the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum.

The more the Kangxi Emperor read history books, the more he admired the Hongwu Emperor. Furthermore, he fancied himself and the Crown Prince as being just like the Hongwu Emperor and Crown Prince Zhu Biao, so he had deliberately come this time to show off.
Your son is impressive, but my son is even more impressive. Moreover, my son will definitely live a long and healthy life, living right up until he inherits my position.
The Kangxi Emperor exhorted Yinzhen, "After you ascend the throne, you must come and pay respects at the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum, and tell him that you have succeeded the throne."
Yinzhen wore a deadpan expression and perfunctorily replied, "Alright, alright, alright. Yes, yes, yes. No problem at all."
His imperial father was truly so childish.
However, taking advantage of this opportunity, Yinzhen brought up the matter of compiling the *History of Ming* with the Kangxi Emperor.
Official histories of every dynasty inevitably contained omissions and revisions, and the *History of Ming* smeared the Ming Dynasty rather terribly.

Although the Kangxi Emperor did issue certain directives regarding the Southern Ming period, he explicitly requested that they properly compile the history of the early and middle periods of the Ming Dynasty according to true history.
The reason was very simple.
Firstly, the Kangxi Emperor truly admired Zhu Yuanzhang and Zhu Biao [Note: likely a typo in original text for Zhu Di, but translating literally based on context of previous mentions];

Secondly, Nurhaci's rise occurred at the end of the Ming Dynasty, and the early and middle periods of the Ming Dynasty had nothing to do with Nurhaci or the Qing Empire, so there was no need for the Kangxi Emperor to delete or modify them.
The Kangxi Emperor also had a thought that he had only shared with Yinzhen: the more formidable the early Ming Dynasty was, the more incompetent the emperors of the late Ming Dynasty would appear.

Yet, the *History of Ming* still contained a great deal of black material on Zhu Yuanzhang and others. Many records—such as the claim that the Young Ming King was harmed by Zhu Yuanzhang—had no historical evidence to support them, yet they were jotted down simply under the label of "folk legends."
There was also the story of Shen Wansan helping Zhu Yuanzhang build city walls, and later being exiled by Zhu Yuanzhang during an argument because he flaunted his wealth too excessively.
In reality, Shen Wansan had always resided within the territory of Zhang Shicheng, Zhu Yuanzhang's rival for supremacy under heaven, and had repeatedly provided military supplies to Zhang Shicheng.

According to materials discovered through later generations of archaeological findings, Shen Wansan was already dead by the time Zhu Yuanzhang established the Great Ming, so the event of him helping Zhu Yuanzhang build city walls could never have happened.
As for the Shen family being liquidated by Zhu Yuanzhang—they had supported Zhang Shicheng, so it would have been strange if their family assets had *not* been confiscated by Zhu Yuanzhang.
Fallacies deliberately fabricated for the sake of smearing in the *History of Ming* were ubiquitous.
This was not the fault of the Kangxi Emperor; it was simply because the scholarly community hated Zhu Yuanzhang to the bone, and hated all the proactive emperors of the Ming Dynasty to the bone.
Perhaps this was because any emperor of the Ming Dynasty who accomplished even a tiny bit would inevitably clash head-on with the scholarly class.
The only emperor they praised as a wise and brilliant lord, the "Ren-zong" Emperor, only reigned for nine months, yet he received the highest evaluation among all Ming emperors.
The Kangxi Emperor sighed and said, "Seeing them willfully manipulate the history of the Ming Dynasty like this, Us is very worried about how the history after you and I die will be written."
He and Yinzhen had also stood on the opposite side of the scholarly community on multiple occasions.
Yinzhen said, "It doesn't matter if history books don't write good things about us; we have the *Veritable Records*, we have *Newspapers*, and we have tangible, visible actual achievements."
The Kangxi Emperor nodded. "Like the stele with no words erected by Empress Wu?"

Yinshi chimed in, "Imperial Father, what are you afraid of? At least the merits during your reign will definitely be wildly and extravagantly bragged about by Younger Brother. By the way, Younger Brother said you selected your temple name early on, called Shengzu [Holy Ancestor]?"
Yinzhen averted his gaze. *It wasn't me, I didn't do it, I definitely never said that.*
The Kangxi Emperor's brows twitched violently.

Yinshi was still chattering away: "Shengzu—that's a temple name that can only be used when posthumously honoring an ancestor. Imperial Father's standards are truly high. By the way, Younger Brother, what kind of temple name do you want?"
Yinzhen's mouth twitched. "How about Shizong [Listing Ancestor]?"
Yinshi said, "I think Renzong [Benevolent Ancestor] is not bad."
Yinzhen said, "The temple name Renzong sounds good on the surface, but those in history who received the temple name Renzong mostly seem to have been overhyped."

One was Emperor Zhezong [Note: Original says Song Renzong Zhao Zhen, but contextually referencing weak/swaying emperors] who vacillated and accomplished nothing, and the other was Ming Renzong Zhu Gaozhi who only reigned for nine months.
It was simply because both of their personalities were relatively weak and they both practiced "governance by inaction" that they earned the good reputation of "Renzong."
Yinshi said, "Then Gaozong [Exalted Ancestor]?"
Yinzhen said, "People in history with the temple name Gaozong are always the turning point where a dynasty transitions from prosperity to decline; it's inauspicious."

Yinshi clicked his tongue and said, "This won't do and that won't do, your standards are just as numerous as Imperial Father's. Then Imperial Father can be Shengzu, and you can be Shengzong [Holy Progenitor]? Imperial Father, what do you think?"
The Kangxi Emperor, who had just listened to his sons discuss a whole string of temple names, turned dark with rage.
He, this old father, thought it was terrible.
Did the two of you not think that discussing temple names while people are still alive is extremely inauspicious?!
The Kangxi Emperor gave Yinzhen and Yinshi two consecutive head-knocks with his knuckles: "Shut up! You are not allowed to talk about inauspicious things!"
Yinshi and Yinzhen clutched the bumps on their heads and exchanged a glance.
Yinshi: *Imperial Father's hand strength is truly formidable.*
Yinzhen: *What a pity there's nowhere to go file a complaint now.*
The two of them looked at each other with despondency.
When his two sons turned glum, the Kangxi Emperor thought of the exact same thing.

If the Grand Empress Dowager were still around, the two sons would already be bumping their swollen foreheads together and making an appointment to run off to file a complaint with the Grand Empress Dowager, right?
But now, the person who could shield them was no longer here.
"Let's head back." The Kangxi Emperor suddenly lost interest in showing off to the Hongwu Emperor.
Yinzhen and Yinshi flanked the Kangxi Emperor, supporting his slightly staggering figure.
As for the Third and Fourth Princes, they didn't understand why Imperial Father and their two older brothers had been joking around just a moment ago, yet suddenly seemed so saddened now.
Though they didn't understand, it didn't stop them from tightly gripping the corners of their older brothers' robes, trying to comfort them.
As he left the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum, the Kangxi Emperor instructed Cao Yin, "Properly repair and maintain the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum."
Cao Yin acknowledged the imperial decree.
The Kangxi Emperor sighed.

Those dazzling emperors in history would ultimately all lie down inside their mausoleums. No matter how incompetent or wasteful their descendants might be, they would never be able to jump out of their tombs to fiercely beat up their unfilial descendants and tidy up the old mountains and rivers.
He would be the same in the future.
The one way he was better than those emperors was that he had a perfect Crown Prince; he didn't need to worry too much about matters after his death.
"Baocheng, pay more attention to the compilation of the *History of Ming*."
"Understood, Imperial Father."
After leaving Nanjing, the Kangxi Emperor continued his Southern Inspection tour.
He traveled as far as Hangzhou, Zhejiang.

After Zhejiang had been purged by Yinzhen, it now appeared flourishing and vibrant, with all things bursting with vitality, and the expressions on the common people's faces looking as though they carried light.
Upon arriving in Zhejiang, the Kangxi Emperor went on an undercover micro-inspection among the populace.
Afterwards, he fell into deep thought.
"Baocheng, what if we did this in other places as well?"
"Imperial Father, let's wait until the Dzungar issue is pacified first; otherwise, we won't have enough troops to suppress rebellions."
"Sigh..."

While gazing at the ocean tides, the Kangxi Emperor said, "There are so many things that need to be done. I truly want to cut through the tangled hemp with a sharp knife and finish everything all at once."
Yinzhen said, "Imperial Father, please think thrice."

The Kangxi Emperor burst into loud laughter, patted Yinzhen's shoulder, and said, "It's a good thing your disposition is thorough and cautious, but a ruler must still do some things without hesitation or over-cautiousness, otherwise you'll miss prime military opportunities."
Yinzhen kept a straight face and said, "Son has already tried very hard to do relatively radical things."
The Kangxi Emperor also kept a straight face: "Far from enough!"
Yinshi couldn't hold it in anymore: "Imperial Father, are you sure Younger Brother is far from enough, or is it that you've overdone it?"
With a wave of the Kangxi Emperor's hand, a group of guards hoisted Yinshi up and tossed him straight into the calm sea where the tide had just receded.
"Baoqing, down you go! Shut your mouth!"
Yinshi and Yinzhen anxiously hugged each other and cried out, "Ahhhhh, Eldest Brother has fallen into the sea! Eldest Brother is going to be eaten by sea monsters!"
Swimming back up, Yinshi shook the water from his hair and asked, "What sea monsters? Where did sea monsters come from?"

Yinshi [Note: Likely Yinqi/Yinzhen in original, but translating literally] and Yinzhen said, "Crown Prince Brother said so! Crown Prince Brother said that when he and you went on a diplomatic mission overseas, you slew a giant sea monster!"

Yinshi fell silent for a moment before saying, "That's right, there are giant sea monsters in the sea. But that's in the deep ocean; there are none near the shore, so you must be extremely careful when you reach the deep sea."
The Kangxi Emperor suddenly felt a bit aggrieved.

If he had been the one tricking the Third and Fourth Princes about sea monsters, Yinshi would have already reacted with, *No way, no way, Imperial Father, you're such a grown-up yet you're still deceiving and terrifying little children, is that really okay with you?*
But when it came to Yinzhen, his own eldest son suddenly became exceptionally eloquent.
Younger brothers were meant to be doted on, but didn't fathers need that too?
The Kangxi Emperor once again wanted to toss Yinshi back into the sea, but fortunately, Yinzhen grabbed his arm tightly and held him back.

It was currently March; although it was already the season when spring flowers bloomed, the seawater was still quite cold. Even though Eldest Brother was an excellent swimmer, one still had to guard against catching a cold!
In this era, there were no miracle drugs for treating colds!

Finally, the Kangxi Emperor paid homage at the Mausoleum of Emperor Yu, personally composing a sacrificial essay for this prehistoric leader, erecting a stele of merits, and officially recognizing Emperor Yu as the ancestor of Huaxia and the Qing Empire.
Thus, the myth of the "integration of Yan and Huang," which had circulated in operas and storytelling scripts for a long time, was officially confirmed through the Kangxi Emperor's lips.
The Kangxi Emperor published an essay proclaiming it to the realm, establishing the Qing Empire's legitimacy as the successor of Yan and Huang.
From then on, the Qing Empire was simply the Qing Empire of Yan and Huang, ruling over the common folk of Yan and Huang, with ethnicities no longer being distinguished.

Although the Eight Banners still existed, the Kangxi Emperor formally announced the abolition of the regulations prohibiting "Manchu-Han intermarriage" and "intermarriage among various ethnic groups."
From then on, everyone would be referred to as people of the Qing, and there would be no more ethnic estrangement.
Of course, this was merely a verbal promise.

As long as the Eight Banners system was not abolished, the substantive gap in ethnic hierarchy would not be erased. After Manchu-Han intermarriage was restored, countless troubles awaited the Kangxi Emperor down the road.
At least half of those countless troubles would have to be handled by Yinzhen.

But at this moment, Yinzhen did not stop the Kangxi Emperor; instead, in his capacity as the Crown Prince of the Qing Empire and a subject of the Kangxi Emperor, he kowtowed to the Kangxi Emperor with utmost reverence and sang praises of the Kangxi Emperor's merits.
The Kangxi Emperor had sworn an oath before the Mausoleum of Emperor Yu—even if fulfilling this oath would entail countless hardships and obstacles, how could Yinzhen possibly stop him?
Yinzhen truly admired and adored the Kangxi Emperor of this era, even more so than the Kangxi Emperor of the other spacetime.
He was a time traveler, so everything he did was only natural.
Yet the Kangxi Emperor was merely a feudal monarch. He lived within this era, limited by his times and by his class, but his courage and audacity surpassed even Yinzhen, the time traveler.

Yinzhen suspected that without this iron-headed, reckless imperial father of his, he himself might right now only be making small-scale patches and repairs to the Qing Empire, and the transformation of the Qing Empire would absolutely not have been this massive or rapid.

Initially, he had been the one dragging the Kangxi Emperor along. But after returning from his overseas diplomatic mission, it turned out that the Kangxi Emperor was the one dragging him along, stumbling forward at a run.
Ahem, he couldn't put it that way—it sounded as if his own imperial father were some sort of wild... well, a spirited steed.
"It's time to head back," the Kangxi Emperor said. "Before we return, let us go take a look at the Confucian Temple. Hopefully, the turmoil there has already settled."
Yinzhen said, "It has surely settled already. The common people's capacity for acceptance is tremendous. The literati's adaptability and acceptance capacity are also extremely strong."
The Kangxi Emperor nodded. "Hopefully so."
However, what Yinzhen did not expect was that the biggest shock he encountered on his way back to the capital was not the Confucian Temple, but Gu Yanwu.
Gu Yanwu's wife had passed away this year.
When Yinzhen and the Kangxi Emperor passed through Kunshan, Gu Yanwu sent someone to deliver a letter, meeting with Yinzhen once again after their written "break" some time ago.
"You are sending civilian scholars on an overseas expedition, departing next month, is that correct?" Gu Yanwu, dressed in plain mourning attire, asked calmly. "I want to board the ship."
By this time, Gu Yanwu was already seventy-six years old. Although he was still in good health, he was already an old man approaching the age of seventy.
Yinzhen was extremely worried: "Teacher! Going out to sea is terribly exhausting, and suffering from an inability to adapt to the local climate and water is extremely dangerous!"
Gu Yanwu said, 'In your letters, you wrote, *"Teacher, I know one cannot govern a country with conspiracies; I know some things are wrong, but I must do them."*'
"Your transformation occurred only after your overseas mission. Therefore, I want to see why there are some things that, even knowing they are wrong, you must still do them."
Yinzhen remained silent for a long time before choking back his emotions and reluctantly agreeing.
"Teacher... please take good care of yourself."

After personally helping Gu Yanwu make arrangements, Yinzhen lingered in Nanjing for a period of time, wanting to see Gu Yanwu off onto the ship.
Upon learning of this, the Kangxi Emperor sighed and consented to Yinzhen remaining in Nanjing.
Yinshi also wanted to stay, but was hoisted away by several guards summoned by the Kangxi Emperor.

The Kangxi Emperor worried that if Yinshi stayed behind, he would haul out his fists the size of sandbags and brutally beat up a septuagenarian elder, bringing irreparable damage to the reputation of the Qing imperial family.
Concealing his identity and adopting a disguise, Yinzhen stayed behind in Nanjing, acting as a clansman of Cao Yin to handle matters concerning the "Civilian Visiting Delegation" alongside Cao Yin.
During the preparation phase for the fleet's diplomatic voyage, several more old fogies pulled strings through Gu Yanwu to jump the queue.
Upon looking at the roster, Yinzhen was dumbfounded.
Huang Zongxi, seventy-nine years old this year.
Wang Fuzhi, seventy years old this year.
Li Yong, sixty-two years old this year.
Li Bai, fifty-nine years old this year.
Li Yindu, fifty-seven years old this year...
Good heavens, aside from his teacher Tang Zhen, the four major early Qing Enlightenment thinkers had all shown up, along with famous remnants of the Ming loyalists.

If something were to happen to these individuals while on board the ship, these early Qing intellectual masters would practically be wiped out in one fell swoop. Who knew, later generations might even spin conspiracy theories claiming that the Qing imperial court deliberately caused these people's deaths.
Yinzhen was struck by a sudden headache.
He could still dispatch people to take extra care of Teacher Gu Yanwu, but should he simply accompany this whole train of important old men on their voyage himself?
With this queue of prestigious and respected old men blocking his doorway, Cao Yin was also suffering from a massive headache.
"Shall we leave it to His Majesty to make the final decision?" Cao Yin asked.
With a deadpan expression, Yinzhen handed a letter over to Cao Yin.
Cao Yin first glossed over the sugary, mushy opening lines of the letter, then looked toward the latter half of the missive.
The Kangxi Emperor said: Go ahead, quickly let them go, send them off with gongs and drums, and publicize their departure.
This was proof that the Ming loyalists were beginning to recognize his Great Qing!
Cao Yin gave a dry laugh. "What His Majesty considers differs from what people like us consider."
His Majesty only needed to issue commands. Difficulties? Weren't those things for ministers to resolve?
Yinzhen sighed. "They are willing to brave life and death to go out to sea; rejecting them would violate my conscience. So be it."
After consulting Gu Yanwu, Gu Yanwu agreed to let Yinzhen disclose his identity to this group of old men.

"Call Tang Zhen over here," Gu Yanwu said. "Since he is a teacher, if he doesn't come to protect you at a time like this, what is he running off to universities to argue with people for?! Does he even remember that he is the Crown Prince's Preceptor!"

Given that Gu Yanwu and Tang Zhen had completely devolved into "sworn enemies" who traded insults the moment either was mentioned, Yinzhen, caught in the middle as their disciple, could only offer a bitter smile and dare not speak.
Tang Zhen soon arrived in Nanjing, and his very first act was to get into a shouting match with this group of Ming loyalists.
They weren't arguing because of the former Ming or whether or not to take up official service.

By now, the Kangxi Emperor was showing the embryonic traits of an enlightened monarch, while Yinzhen even more so exhibited the signs of a sage Crown Prince. Huang Zongxi and Wang Fuzhi—who in later generations were hailed alongside Tang Zhen and Gu Yanwu as the four great enlightenment thinkers—both held the philosophy that the people were noble and the monarch was light, and both hoped the common people would fare well; naturally, they pinned high hopes on the Kangxi Emperor and Yinzhen.
Having many grievances and dissatisfactions, they directed their verbal artillery fire squarely at Tang Zhen, who fancied himself the preceptor to both the emperor and the crown prince.

他这次回京没见到胤祥。他陪着康熙南巡的时候，胤祥暂住在皇太后宫中。皇太后早早去温泉庄子享福，把胤祥也带去了，和他回京前后脚错过。
胤禔道：“好，好得不得了，就是听你没回来，立刻掉眼泪，像个小姑娘一样娇气，你怎么养的他？”
胤礽失笑：“该怎么养就怎么养呗。他想我不是理所当然？”
胤禔冷哼了一声，道：“放心，他是养在你东煌宫的皇子，谁敢对他不好？而且若不是他在花园里偷偷哭泣被你发现，或许咱们的弟弟妹妹们都快被刁奴们饿死了。谁都承着他那一泡眼泪的情。”
胤礽笑得前俯后仰。
兄弟俩在直亲王府悠闲度日的时候，没有忘记兄弟姐妹们。
当皇子和公主休沐时，他们就把人接到直亲王府一起玩耍。
康熙在京郊赐予了胤禔大量田庄。他们一行人在胤禔田庄上打猎摸鱼，好不快活。
几次玩耍之后，弟弟们终于不怕胤禔了，还会往胤禔背上攀爬，让大哥背着他们。
胤禔只会把他们往地上丢。
但往地上丢也好玩。小阿哥们一个接一个往胤禔身上爬，然后被胤禔一个又一个往下扯。
胤礽就只知道在一旁煽风点火，指挥弟弟们围攻胤禔。
胤禔十分无奈。
他怎么成为哄弟弟的玩具了？
康熙偶尔也会参加这个家庭活动，和子女们的关系亲近不少。
若康熙在的时候，胤禔总会和康熙比起来。
比狩猎骑马就罢了，比摸鱼爬树种田什么的，胤礽扶额，这对父子真是非常非常相似，真的是亲父子。
回京之后，胤礽的日子过得很悠闲很慢，但这悠闲的慢日子，又显得时间过得非常快。
本来今年，佟皇贵妃应该病重并升为皇后。
现在佟皇贵妃身体强壮着，每日和妃嫔们一起看戏游戏，与有女儿的妃嫔们一同不着边际的琢磨着怎么给女儿选个地多的额驸。
既然公主们去草原之后是去守国门的，那么额驸其实已经不重要了，额驸的势力很重要。
至于男人，天高皇帝远，公主们不能养面首吗（悄悄）。
到时候各玩各的，只要不弄出人命，想必皇上也不会说什么。
佟皇贵妃没出事，今年从南巡回来之后就没有什么大事，只有直亲王定亲这一件事了。
或许是往年都很忙碌，事情很多。今年从年中开始就没什么事了，康熙闲得心里发慌。
胤禔私下和胤礽吐槽，汗阿玛就是贱得慌，没事想找事。
于是康熙脑袋一拍，开始追缴国库欠银了。
胤礽：“……”他不知道该怎么形容，总之，汗阿玛威武吧。
胤礽问道：“汗阿玛，那么先追缴谁的欠银？派谁出面清缴？”
康熙道：“当然先从自家人入手，先追缴宗亲的欠银。宗亲都还欠银了，其他勋贵和汉臣肯定自己就会凑钱还上。至于人手，四阿哥之前不是做得不错吗？”
胤礽问道：“汗阿玛，您还记得，现在四弟才十一岁吗？”
十一岁是虚岁，胤禛才十岁啊！
康熙道：“都十一岁了！放在以前，都已经定亲成亲了！”
胤礽：“……”成吧，您是皇上，您说啥就是啥。
于是，才十周岁的胤禛再次挂印被拉童工，每日带人上门清缴欠银。
打虎亲兄弟。胤禛这次把胤祺、胤祚、胤祐和胤禩都带上了。
“我像你们这么大的时候，都去天津、南京为汗阿玛分忧了。你们不能一直待在宫里。”胤禛道，“虽然我们经验比不过哥哥们，但三个臭皮匠顶个诸葛亮，我们的智慧集合在一起，一定能想出让他们乖乖还钱的办法。”
胤祺很紧张。他为人宽厚，讨债这种事，他以前只躲在哥哥们身后吆喝，真不敢做。
胤祐和胤禩可能还没有回过神要干什么不提，胤祚非常兴奋。
胤祚其实出身可能是众位兄弟中最好的一位。
他的额娘安嫔虽只是个嫔，但其娘家是开国功臣，汉军旗的代表人物，总兵官刚阿泰之女，汉将抚西额驸李永芳的孙女。
刚阿泰因为和佟养量的政治斗争中失败，革职后病逝，李家已经几乎淡出了朝堂，但在军中势力并未完全消散。
所以安嫔是当初康熙朝第一批封嫔的人，并且位列众嫔之首。
可以说，安嫔“曾经阔过”。
对于“曾经阔过”的额娘，如今却连他的抚养权都拿不到，如今还在宫里当一个透明人，胤祚心里是极难受的。
他幼年时饱尽病痛之苦，性极能忍，且心思比同龄兄弟更深沉、更成熟。
胤祚敏锐的看到，四哥给他们的机会，可以让他早一些出现在汗阿玛眼中。
待他立下功劳，说不定就能带着生母在宫中也好过一些。
胤祐和胤禩的生母现在在宫中也是透明人，只是他们年纪小，还未想到这些事。
胤祚悄悄和他们说明其中利害之后，他们也支棱起来，拍着胸脯，一定要办好此事。
胤祺见弟弟们都非常积极，自己也颤颤悠悠地挺起胸膛。
不、不就是讨债吗！我、我很小的时候就跟着大哥去堵过大臣的门，我不怕！
我……
胤祺找到胤禔：“我还是很怕啊啊啊啊！大哥，快给我想个办法！我不能在弟弟面前丢脸！”
“嗯……要不你戴个面具？”胤禔给胤祺出馊主意，“戴狰狞一点的面具。”
胤祺：“可以吗？”
胤礽赶紧把胤祺拉走：“别听你大哥胡说。你到时候板着脸就好了。对了，如果你无法控制住表情，就在嘴里含一个苦的东西。”
胤祺：“有用吗？”
胤礽点头：“分散一下你的注意力。”
胤祺信了。
于是，在胤禛率领弟弟们去堵门的时候，胤祺在嘴里喊了一颗苦胆。
他把苦胆一咬破，整张脸都皱了起来，确实什么尴尬和害怕的心思都没了。
弟弟们都被胤祺这一张苦脸吓到了。
没想到和善的五哥还能做出这么可怕的表情！
当他们知道胤祺的“秘诀”之后，也含了苦胆在嘴里。
于是除了胤禛之外，其他皇子全拿出了一张皱成一团的苦脸，看上去十分震撼人心。
胤禛带着一群苦瓜脸弟弟们堵门，拿着胤礽贡献的大喇叭，对着宗亲大门大吼对方欠债情况。
弟弟们讨债，胤礽和胤禔自然不会闲着。
他早就派人了解了对方的经济情况，连对方什么时候出门喝小酒找歌女都知道得一清二楚。
于是胤禛就有很多话可以喊了。
XXX！你欠国库银子多少两，已经逾期多久没还！
你在XX日买马花了XX两白银！在XY日买假的古董花了多少两白银！在头牌面前争风吃醋一掷多少千金！
你有本事花钱买马买假古董并在头牌面前争风吃醋还争失败，你有本事还钱啊！
国库的钱要修河坝修路赈灾养保家卫国的士兵！国库里的钱是保障老百姓灾年能活得下去的救命银子！是八旗士兵的粮饷！
你赶紧还钱！必须还钱！不还钱我就每日在你门前念！
胤祉：“弟弟们放心，我已经刊登在报纸上了！”
给老赖一个专版，就问你怕不怕！
‎
