187. Two Chapters Merged into One [V]

Yinzhi originally wanted to recruit some people casually, both to replenish his troops and to take the opportunity to slight the generals of the Eight Banners.

He never expected that the Eight Banners army would almost all run off with him.

Yinzhi scratched his head, wanting to ask: I only promised not to deduct your rations, and it's one thing to recruit low-level soldiers with such conditions, but why would the low-level officers rather give up their official positions just to follow him? This made him feel exceptionally confused.

Yinreng, while looking at the account books, said: "What is there to be confused about? The imperial court seems to give the Banner soldiers many privileges, but how much of these privileges actually end up in the Banner soldiers' pockets? They just want to eat their fill and save a little money for their families."

The poverty of the Banner people began as early as the Kangxi reign.

Even though the Kangxi reign allowed the Banner people to farm, it only treated the symptoms, not the root cause. Because the income from the Banner people's farming was also exploited layer by layer by the large and small Banner lords.

They, the princes, were the exploiting class.

Yinreng pointed to a spot in the account book and said: "If we thoroughly investigate the corruption of rations, all the generals except for Eldest Brother would be arrested. But we cannot afford not to arrest them; record it first, and behead one or two of the worst offenders to serve as a warning to the others."

Yinzhi looked at those names, his anger flaring up, and he drew his sword to chop off a corner of the table.

Yinreng didn't even lift his eyelids and continued: "Disperse the New Army; those who can lead troops will lead troops. Once the troops are familiarized, these soldiers will be given to them."

The New Army was originally a place to cultivate mid-level officers. They all had the ability to lead troops.

Having lost so many people, Yinreng felt very heartbroken. But this batch of young men who had walked out of the baptism of blood and fire would be even more resilient and reliable, becoming the backbone of the army after the Eight Banners reform.

The ideology of loyalty to the monarch and patriotism could be cultivated starting from them.

These were matters for later; the urgent priority was to have these people quickly digest the soldiers Yinzhi had "swallowed" into the strength of the Central Route Army.

Although Galdan had hung up the "no-war" sign while waiting for logistics and supplies, he would definitely take action once he saw the Qing forces gathering.

"Baocheng, how do you think Galdan will attack?" Yinzhi asked after venting his anger, throwing his sword to the side.

Yinreng said: "He will run."

Yinzhi said angrily: "I haven't even had my revenge yet, and he's going to run?!"

Yinreng nodded: "He has reconciled with Tsewang Rabtan and has a way out, so naturally he won't fight the Qing to the death."

Yinzhi said: "Shall we pursue?"

Yinreng said: "This battle must certainly be fought all the way to Dzungaria. If we don't fight to the Dzungar royal tent, this battle will have no meaning. But given the current combat effectiveness of the Eight Banners army, I am very worried."

Yinreng opened the roster of soldiers just submitted by the various generals and introduced it to Yinzhi: "Although we nominally gathered an army of 100,000, that includes logistics personnel and auxiliary soldiers. Furthermore, the nobles and clansmen who went on the expedition all organized their strongest warriors into guard teams. These guard teams only care about protecting them and will not go into battle, so we only have 50,000 troops we can actually use, or even fewer."

Yinzhi sighed: "Father Emperor mobilized the army so long in advance, how is it still in such a ghostly state?"

Yinreng said: "At least the troops from Shengjing and Khorchin have arrived in the north and can block them."

Yinreng thought to himself that in original history, it was even more absurd than it is now.

The first expedition against Galdan was nominally a victory, but it was actually a crushing defeat. It was only because Galdan retreated and encountered a plague on the road, causing more deaths than in battle, that his imperial father declared victory.

At that time, the first clash between the Qing and Galdan, the Battle of Olon-Buir, was a defeat for the Qing.

Later, Kangxi sent 100,000 troops to encircle Galdan, and the troops under Changning fought Galdan and were defeated again.

Finally, there was the decisive Battle of Ulan Butung in the first expedition against Galdan. Galdan set up a camel-wall tactic, which Fuquan did not recognize, so he ordered the Qing army to charge forward carrying cannons, resulting in another crushing defeat.

But Galdan's reinforcements were cut off and he was short on ammunition. Relying on the Qing's powerful supplies, Fuquan exhausted Galdan's ammunition with several times the casualties; Tong Guogang died in this battle.

The Qing could have won if they had charged at that moment, but Galdan sent people to feign a request for peace, and Fuquan agreed, so Galdan ran away.

And by the time Galdan ran, the troops from Khorchin and Shengjing had not yet reached the designated meeting point due to the long distance and had not participated in the battle at all.

Both in terms of process and result, the Qing suffered heavy losses. But Kangxi could only hold his nose and call it a "great victory."

Fortunately, in this life, the troops from Shengjing and Khorchin set off early, and they chose an ambush spot closer to them. They had already arrived at the location and could participate in the battle.

Yinreng couldn't help but rub his forehead, remembering the frustration Kangxi felt at that time.

He once again suspected that the Father Emperor of the first life had held a grudge against him for twenty years, not because of his lack of worry, but because every time he thought of him, he remembered the humiliation of the first expedition against Galdan. He had been completely used as a target for displaced anger back then.

"The troops from Shengjing often fight against the Ross (Russian) Empire, so their combat effectiveness is still there. Can the Khorchin troops fight?" Yinzhi sat astride a chair, looking at the map with a worried face. "I don't trust that group of Mongol Eight Banners."

Yinzhi remembered how useless the Mongol warriors were under his command in the past.

Yinreng said: "Their task is to ambush the fleeing soldiers. Resting while the enemy tires, and pursuing the remnants, their morale and state are stronger than Galdan's troops. Even if they can't stop Galdan, they can eliminate as many of Galdan's soldiers as possible."

Yinreng's tone gradually turned cold: "If they are going to run, Eldest Brother, you should run ahead of them."

Yinzhi raised an eyebrow: "Where should I run to?"

Yinreng pointed to the Bortala River: "Here."

Yinzhi laughed: "That's running too far."

Yinreng said: "Prince Kang, Jieshu, is already waiting in Guihua City. Eldest Brother can rendezvous with Jieshu."

In history, Prince Kang Jieshu was also stationed in Guihua City, the later Hohhot.

At that time, Kangxi was full of confidence, thinking that the encirclement would surely succeed and force Galdan to flee west. The result...

Jieshu was severely sabotaged and became an isolated force. If it weren't for the fact that Galdan fled north instead of west, and encountered a plague on the retreat, this isolated force of Jieshu would definitely have been swallowed by Galdan.

However, based on the current situation in Dzungaria, Yinreng concluded that the Ross Empire would not openly support Galdan, and that Galdan would definitely flee west. Then, this army under Jieshu could truly play the role of interception.

"The light troops led by Arni, the Minister of the Lifan Yuan, have already scouted the movements of the troops led by Tsewang Rabtan. Eldest Brother does not need to annihilate them completely; as long as you can engage Tsewang Rabtan in battle, our strategic mission will be accomplished."

Arni was the Qing general who was defeated by Galdan in the Battle of Olon-Buir in original history.

He was also sabotaged by the sluggish Eight Banners army. The encirclement was agreed upon, but he was already engaging Galdan while the Eight Banners troops had only just set off.

In fact, among the light troops led by Arni, there were 2,000 elite scouts, the warriors best at long-distance trekking and intelligence gathering among the Mongol Eight Banners. Their combat effectiveness was stronger than the ordinary soldiers of the Manchu Eight Banners.

Now Yinreng was making the best use of everything, having Arni avoid direct combat and fully utilize the role of the scouts.

Yinzhi rubbed the stubble on his chin that he hadn't shaved for days: "As long as we engage in battle with Tse-whatshisname, it will prove that the leaders of both factions of the divided Dzungars are rebelling against the Qing. Then the Qing's march into Dzungaria will have a just cause."

Yinreng said: "Not only that. Although Tsewang Rabtan has tens of thousands of followers, those capable of fighting do not exceed 5,000. With Eldest Brother's strength, you will definitely be able to take at least a hundred heads. After he suffers heavy losses, he will know that the Qing is not to be trifled with and will not join forces with Galdan to attack the Qing again. Tsewang Rabtan is a person who can bend and stretch, and is extremely deep. He will definitely be an enemy of the Qing again, so this time, he might not necessarily be an enemy of the Qing."

Yinzhi sneered: "Because he hasn't unified the Dzungars yet. Once Galdan dies and he unifies the Dzungars, he will come back to harass the Qing. You want to feign a request for peace, actually to stabilize him, and then attack the Dzungars?"

Yinreng nodded: "Not only attack, I want to annihilate the entire Dzungar tribe."

Hearing Yinreng's cold words, Yinzhi patted Yinreng on the shoulder: "I will give the order to annihilate the Dzungar tribe; I will do it."

For the Mongol tribes, one must completely kill their noble bloodlines and disperse the women and children to various places to completely cut off their chance of making a comeback.

This was a very bloody and cruel thing. Yinzhi didn't want to make things difficult for Yinreng.

Yinreng patted the hand Yinzhi had placed on his shoulder and said: "How can I always let you, Eldest Brother, take the spotlight? Occasionally, I also want to have the merit of destroying a nation."

Seeing that Yinreng had made up his mind, Yinzhi sighed: "Fine. Whatever you do, Brother supports you. But don't force yourself."

Yinreng nodded.

As the Crown Prince of the Qing, there were some cruel things he had to do.

In modern times, countries at war do not harm civilians or kill prisoners. But in the feudal era, war made that impossible.

In order to fully incorporate Dzungaria into the territory, the tribes of the two Dzungar Khans would be broken up and sent to other tribes, and some would become consumables, just like Qin Shi Huang sending the people of the six states to build the Great Wall.

It was to exhaust the people; it was to make them work themselves to death.

Yinreng closed his eyes. After opening them, he tapped the table lightly: "Eldest Brother, have them come to the main tent for a meeting."

Yinzhi patted Yinreng's shoulder again: "Good."

Inside the main tent, Yinreng had already set up the sand table, hung up the map, and issued orders directly.

Some generals wanted to retort, saying the young Crown Prince was just talking on paper.

But with the Prince's hand on his sword, whoever showed dissatisfaction had the Prince's eyes tracing lines across their necks, so they had to shut up for the time being.

As the Crown Prince spoke in more and more detail, the look of horror on their faces grew increasingly intense.

The Crown Prince was already talking about arrangements thousands of miles away, and listening to what the Crown Prince said, these arrangements were already properly set up, just waiting for Galdan to flee west.

Changning said: "Crown Prince, are you sure?"

Yinreng waved his hand, and a Mongol Eight Banners soldier behind him stepped forward: "Arni's soldier. Tell the princes and generals the intelligence you obtained."

After the report was finished, Yinreng called for Jieshu's troops, the Khorchin troops, and the Shengjing troops.

"What is there to be surprised about? Among you, there are those who have followed the Crown Prince and this Prince on visits to Europe. Is this your first time seeing the Crown Prince's ability to plan strategies within the tent and decide victory thousands of miles away?" Yinzhi said displeasedly, "Do not use your shallow knowledge to gauge the Crown Prince's abilities. The Imperial Father has handed the command of the army to the Crown Prince; you only need to obey orders."

Changning took the lead: "Yes. This subject obeys. Your Highness, please issue your orders!"

Fuquan also said: "When it comes to fighting, I am not good at it. Crown Prince, you say how to fight, and this subject will fight accordingly."

With the Crown Prince's two uncles publicly expressing their support for the Crown Prince, others didn't have enough weight and could only obey.

Surprisingly, the generals of the Central Route Army, such as E'erke-Fiyanggū, known as the "Hundred-Victory General," also nodded like a pounding pestle, seemingly trusting the Crown Prince extremely.

Someone secretly asked Fiyanggū: "You haven't followed the Crown Prince to sea, how do you know the Crown Prince is powerful?"

Fiyanggū rolled his eyes at him and said: "The Crown Prince predicted the Ross Empire's surprise attack in the Northeast; the order to farm and nibble away at the Ross Empire's territory was given by the Crown Prince; the order to station the army at the Olon-Buir River to wait for Galdan was also given by the Crown Prince."

That person was extremely surprised: "Does the Crown Prince really have the ability to plan strategies?"

Fiyanggū said: "Hasn't the Crown Prince done more surprising things in the court? What is planning strategies compared to that?"

The man thought about it carefully, and it seemed to be the case.

Even the little princes raised by the Crown Prince were all crafty and cunning, like old oily hands in the officialdom.

Fiyanggū said: "Listen to the Crown Prince, and you'll never go wrong."

Even if he didn't listen to the Crown Prince, he had to listen to the Prince.

The few battles fought in cooperation with the Prince made Fiyanggū sigh that the waves behind were about to be slapped to death on the beach.

Not to mention the Prince's bravery, his combat intuition was truly formidable; he could instinctively choose the most suitable combat method without even needing to think.

Even the Prince spoke highly of the Crown Prince, so what else did Fiyanggū have to consider?

In short, even if he were a famous general fighting alone, he would rather lie flat as a salted fish and let the big boss lead him—it was truly fragrant.

Yinreng passed down orders one after another, only omitting the order for the Prince.

But everyone saw the suddenly missing Prince and knew that the Prince had a secret mission.

The Central Route Army was now under Fiyanggū's command. Fiyanggū, who had just wanted to be a salted fish, had to take the lead, feeling exceptionally helpless.

Other troops were also entering a state of combat in an orderly manner under Yinreng's command.

Yinreng didn't have much confidence in them to begin with; they only needed to use their artillery well, inflict as much damage as possible on Galdan's vital forces, and force Galdan to retreat.

Now that the Qing army's weapons were far superior to Galdan's, if they couldn't even force a retreat, Yinreng could only blame his own bad luck.

When Galdan put away the "no-war" sign, Yinreng saw the familiar camel city and breathed a sigh of relief.

Galdan, as expected, chose the camel city tactic just like in history.

The camel city tactic involved tying the legs of camels and surrounding them in a circle. Galdan's soldiers could defend or attack from within the camel city, turning the confrontation between the two armies into a positional battle, gaining a terrain advantage.

Even if these camels were killed, those mountains of meat could greatly mitigate the power of muskets and cannonballs.

But this was based on the old-fashioned firearms of the past.

Yinreng stood on a high ridge and, after seeing the camel city, said to Fuquan: "Prince Yu, is the fierce fire oil prepared?"

Fuquan's eyes showed admiration: "The fierce fire oil jars and the catapults are all prepared."

He had never heard of this strange tactic, yet the Crown Prince had actually guessed it in advance.

Yinreng said: "The Eight Banners soldiers' combat effectiveness is not as good as Galdan's; hand-to-hand combat will put us at a disadvantage. Pass my order: only exchange fire with Galdan; without my order, no one is allowed to charge."

Fuquan received the order and stepped down.

Yinreng said: "Prince Gong."

Changning's eyes lit up: "This subject is here! What does the Crown Prince want me to do?!"

Yinreng hesitated for a moment, then said: "You lead a team to Khalkha... wait, can you read a map? Can you use a compass? You won't get lost again, will you?"

Yinreng's series of questions made Changning feel extremely embarrassed: "This... the one that got lost wasn't the team I led! Your Highness, please trust me."

Yinreng hesitated for a moment and said: "Alright, I will trust you once. Go to this location on the map. Kill all the young and strong men; you can keep the women and children for yourself, or give them to others, I don't care. The same goes for the wealth."

Changning was stunned.

He took a careful look at the map: "This is... this is the tribe brought by the Dzungars? Your Highness, have you found the location of their tribe?"

Yinreng nodded.

It wasn't him who found the location of Galdan's tribe, but Princess Chunxi.

After Princess Chunxi arrived at the tribe where Tsereng was, she gathered cattle, sheep, and herdsmen to take refuge, while sending her guards and old herdsmen of the tribe to search for traces of Galdan's tribe.

The tribe brought by Galdan were outsiders, and relying on Galdan's military strength, they didn't hide much and were soon discovered.

As long as Galdan's tribe was not destroyed, even if Galdan were left with only a few riders, he could make a comeback in a few years.

When Yinreng let Changning leave with the people sent by Princess Chunxi, his hands hidden in his sleeves trembled slightly.

He had finally taken this step.

Yinreng looked up. Tonight the moon was bright and the stars were sparse; even if a fire was lit, there would be no rain.

However, the fierce fire oil could not be extinguished by water, and rain would not hinder his fire attack.

"Your Highness..." Cao Yin draped a cloak over Yinreng, "The wind is strong at night, please wait in the tent."

Yinreng shook his head: "I will wait here. Bring me the telescope."

Cao Yin handed the telescope to Yinreng.

Yinreng held the telescope, but for a long time, he couldn't summon the courage to look.

Only when the fire soared into the sky and the sounds of shouting and screaming shook even the leaves beside him did Yinreng lift the telescope.

The fire filled the sky, making the night as bright as day. Yinreng could clearly see the soldiers fighting and screaming, see the miserable corpses in the raging fire, and see blood and flesh flying and rivers of blood flowing.

Yinreng had thought he would feel nauseous, but he only felt slightly uncomfortable, and then he became numb.

Thinking of the order he gave to Changning, Yinreng thought that perhaps what his teacher Gu Yanwu said was correct: a person's bottom line is too easily broken. Once broken, one will use "great righteousness" as a name to break it a second time, a third time... many times.

And is what I am doing really in accordance with great righteousness?

"Your Highness, the wind is too strong, please go back?" Cao Yin persuaded again.

Yinreng put down the telescope and said: "How many soldiers are guarding me?"

Cao Yin said: "There are a total of one thousand elites."

Yinreng said: "Follow me on the expedition."

Cao Yin was shocked: "Your Highness! Where are you going! Leave any matters to this subject; you cannot put yourself in danger!"

Yinreng shook his head: "It doesn't count as putting myself in danger. I want to cut off Galdan's retreat. Sending others won't work; they will deliberately let Galdan go."

Cao Yin asked: "Hasn't the Prince already gone?"

Yinreng said: "The Prince went to the other side."

The Prince was going to intercept Galdan's other leader, Tsewang Rabtan.

Likewise, only the Prince could go to fight Galdan's leader. Others would deliberately hold back to prevent the Dzungars from being annihilated.

Galdan was an ambitious hero and was considered by Tibetan Buddhism to be the reincarnation of a living Buddha; he was both a secular and religious leader, and even a disciple of the Dalai Lama served by his side.

As long as Galdan was alive, he could use his status as a religious leader at any time to become an enemy of the Qing again.

Even if he escaped to a foreign country alone, he would definitely be used by foreigners and become a major threat to the Qing and China in pacifying the Northwest.

Yinreng said: "This is my order."

Cao Yin could only grit his teeth and kneel: "This subject obeys! This subject will definitely protect the Crown Prince's safety."

Yinreng turned around: "Rongruo, you stay behind. If Galdan sends someone to ask for peace, you immediately lead your men to pursue. After that, we can attack Galdan from the front and back."

Nalan Xingde asked: "Your Highness, you are pursuing Galdan yourself, so what is the use of the troops you sent to Shengjing and Khorchin?"

Yinreng smiled sarcastically: "If Galdan doesn't flee west but flees north, the troops from Shengjing and Khorchin will be useful. However, the troops from Shengjing and Khorchin are not meant to block Galdan, but to block those who would take advantage of the chaos. Khalkha Mongolia is empty, and Tsewang Rabtan will definitely divide his troops to plunder Khalkha Mongolia. The Ross Empire and foreign mercenaries might also come to get a share."

A person cannot calculate everything. Even if Yinreng thought it highly likely that Galdan would flee west, Galdan might have a brain spasm halfway and flee north. So, the manpower must be arranged properly.

Besides, Yinreng was waiting to catch that group of mercenaries disguised as missionaries.

Nalan Xingde said: "This subject will definitely not fail the mission!"

Yinreng nodded.

He donned his armor, mounted his horse, and quietly left with his guards.

All of this, except for the Central Route Army, was completely unnoticed by the other Eight Banners generals.

Fiyanggū felt his head was about to explode. He gritted his teeth and thought that the Crown Prince and the Prince were indeed brothers; this reckless personality was truly cut from the same cloth.

A soldier ran over: "General! The others from the Eight Banners have already charged up for hand-to-hand combat!"

Fiyanggū cursed: "Didn't the Crown Prince have an order! Only exchange fire with cannons and muskets, no hand-to-hand combat!"

Soldier: "They seem to have ignored the Crown Prince's order. Should we charge too?"

Fiyanggū sneered: "Charge what charge? Raise your flags and shout loudly. We've been fighting for so long, it's time to let them fight."

The soldier immediately went to pass the order.

The people of the Central Route Army immediately became idle. Although they shouted hard on the sidelines and occasionally snatched a kill or two, they did not participate in the hand-to-hand combat and lingered outside the battlefield.

Because the visibility at night was dim and the Eight Banners troops were each doing their own thing, the battlefield was very chaotic, and no one noticed the Central Route Army slacking off.

Fiyanggū found Fuquan: "Prince Yu, what is going on? Didn't the Crown Prince say only exchange fire, no attacking? Do you know how many people will die in hand-to-hand combat? Do you know that when the two armies are mixed together, our new-style muskets and cannons are useless! What exactly are you doing?!"

Facing Fiyanggū's anger, Fuquan sighed: "I gave the order."

Fiyanggū laughed in extreme anger: "You gave the order, so shouldn't those who violated the order be punished by military law?!"

Fuquan said: "More than half of the Eight Banners army took the initiative to attack, and the rest saw other troops attacking and followed suit. How can military law be punished?"

Fiyanggū said: "At least behead the few teams that attacked first!"

Fuquan shook his head: "Can't behead them; they agreed on it. Many teams took the initiative to attack together; at most, strip them of their titles. Sigh, this Prince will write a memorial to the Emperor to decide. Where is the Crown Prince?"

Fuquan thought the Crown Prince would come to blame them in person.

Fiyanggū mocked: "The Crown Prince knew long ago that you were useless and has already gone to intercept the fleeing Galdan himself."

Fuquan: "..."

"Prince Yu, Galdan sent someone to ask for peace..."

"Peace my ass! Pursue immediately!"

Fuquan was so scared he almost fell off his horse.

100,000

188. Two chapters combined [V]

It is not easy to set an ambush on the vast grassland.

One reason Kangxi decided on the encirclement tactic was the fear that Galdan would turn around and run back into the grasslands. The grasslands offer escape routes in every direction; if they ran their horses to death, they would never be able to catch up.

However, Yinzhi had been stationed here for over a year and had long since mastered the surrounding terrain.

After studying the detailed maps, Yinzhi set an ambush at the location where Galdan was most likely to retreat.

But this ambush was not a complete ambush.

He actually had the Crown Prince's ceremonial guards brought out and lit torches, practically shouting with a megaphone, "The Crown Prince of the Great Qing is here."

Yinzhi was gambling.

First, he was gambling that Galdan would believe the reckless and arrogant Crown Prince of the Great Qing was there; as an ambitious leader, Galdan might want to face the Crown Prince head-on.

Second, he was gambling that Galdan would think this was just a feint and that there were more ambush troops elsewhere, so he would only choose to charge through this spot.

The Crown Prince's ceremonial guards could not be used casually; their use must have been approved by the Crown Prince himself and held significant strategic importance.

Of course, it could also be that the Crown Prince was leading heavy troops in wait. Galdan must have also received intelligence long ago that the Crown Prince was still in the Great Qing military camp when the battle began.

The Great Qing army and Galdan's army were locked in a fierce battle; the Crown Prince could not suddenly conjure up many troops to block him.

So it was either a feint by the Crown Prince or sheer recklessness.

Of course, there could be accidents. Galdan might not follow Yinzhi's judgment and might detour directly.

At this point, it depended on Nalan Xingde's ability.

As long as Nalan Xingde could lead the central army to pursue in time and keep biting at Galdan's heels, Galdan would likely take the easiest escape route and collide head-on with the ambush set by the Crown Prince, rather than detouring.

In the era of cold weapons, when two sides engage in battle, one can only do their best and leave the rest to fate. Yinzhi could only do so much.

He once again cursed himself for not being an engineering student. If he could climb the tech tree and invent airplanes, Galdan could run wherever he wanted; if he could outrun an airplane's reconnaissance range, he would consider it his loss.

While Yinzhi was letting his imagination run wild, the scouting soldiers returned to report that Galdan was heading toward them.

The soldiers were energized, but Cao Yin was extremely worried: "Your Highness the Crown Prince..."

Yinzhi shook his head and took out his long musket.

Cao Yin sighed and had no choice but to arrange the troops according to Yinzhi's instructions.

Yinzhi jumped off his horse, stood on the prepared high platform, and rested his long musket on an iron frame.

Galdan's army was getting closer, close enough to see their banners.

Galdan wore an iron helmet and iron-plated armor, and even his horse was armored, looking like a tough, hard-shelled turtle.

Relying on his heavy armor, he took the lead and charged fearlessly toward the Crown Prince's ceremonial guards.

Yinzhi had been well-nourished since childhood, so he had no night blindness. Plus, the moon was bright and the stars were sparse tonight, and not a single cloud was in the sky; even the heavens were helping Yinzhi. Even at night, Yinzhi could see the person with the best equipment and the fastest horse in that group.

Although Galdan might have changed clothes while fleeing, just like a certain Cao thief in the Three Kingdoms period, Yinzhi didn't care about that anymore.

"Bang."

A gunshot rang out, grazing Galdan's shoulder armor.

Yinzhi let out a long sigh.

Even with "bullet time," it was still very difficult to hit Galdan due to the dim visibility, the high speed of the horses, and the inherent flaws of the musket.

However, Yinzhi's shot was both a sniper attempt and a signal.

When Yinzhi's gun fired, Cao Yin led the musket team to complete their formation, dismounting and crouching halfway, firing from the few-meter-high hill, looking down on the enemy.

When one squad of musketeers finished firing, they immediately retreated, and the second squad stepped forward; the two squads interleaved, and the second squad continued to fire.

This was the "Three-Layer Formation" created by Prince Mu Ying of the Ming Dynasty in Yunnan.

This formation had variations, such as the people in the back reloading and handing the muskets to the soldiers in front, allowing soldiers with better marksmanship to fire continuously.

Yinzhi still adopted the earliest Three-Layer Formation.

Musket recoil was heavy, and the mental pressure of shooting at night was high; rotating fire allowed each soldier to rest slightly, helping them better concentrate.

The thousand warriors Yinzhi brought were light troops and were not equipped with cannons.

However, they were each armed with the most advanced Great Qing musket and had been trained according to the standards of the new-style soldiers, having rotated through the border and served in the New Army. Therefore, it could be said that they were currently the most elite land force of the Great Qing.

Even when Galdan led his banner soldiers to turn and try to charge directly up this small hill, these warriors were completely fearless, continuing to fire in an orderly fashion.

Because of the fierce fire oil Yinzhi had prepared in advance, Camel City was turned into a sea of fire. The heavy armored soldiers were almost trapped in a branding iron within the flames.

Therefore, those who escaped this time were either lightly equipped to begin with or had discarded their iron armor at the first opportunity.

Iron armor was very expensive, and only a few nobles, like Galdan, had spare armor, which they changed into during the retreat.

When the musket team fired, many people fell off their horses, and many horses knelt on the ground, blocking the path of other horses.

Galdan's formation was in chaos for a moment, but soon the cavalry overwhelmed the fallen men and kneeling horses.

Yinzhi frowned slightly.

"There are too many people retreating!" Cao Yin looked at the dense crowd and said in horror, "How can there be so many?!"

Yinzhi said: "Perhaps the Eight Banners army did not follow my orders to use cannons and muskets for counter-fire, but instead charged into a melee."

Before one's own ammunition is exhausted, a melee might look lively, but it is difficult to eliminate the opponent's effective strength and instead consumes one's own.

Especially when the opponent is preparing to retreat and flee, if the Great Qing ranks are orderly, they can not only effectively inflict damage within the range of the cannons, but the musket infantry and cavalry can also, under the cover of the cannons, continuously approach Galdan's army, use muskets for long-range combat, and keep biting off the meat from the back of the opponent's formation while keeping a tight grip on them.

This was the tactic Yinzhi had formulated.

But if these people didn't listen to orders and charged into a chaotic mess with Galdan, let alone the Great Qing's cannons, even the muskets would have limited effect.

The Great Qing Eight Banners army lost their most advantageous weapon advantage and got into a chaotic melee with the Dzungars using sabers. How could the poorly trained Eight Banners army out-hack the Dzungar soldiers?

I'm afraid that when the Great Qing Eight Banners army stopped the cannon fire, the effective strength of Galdan's army had hardly been consumed at all.

Yinzhi took a deep breath.

Fortunately, he had prepared for the worst.

This wasn't because he had guessed that the Eight Banners army would deliberately disobey his orders.

To be honest, even if he had guessed the current situation, Yinzhi couldn't figure out for the life of him why the Eight Banners generals would ignore his orders.

Since the introduction of muskets, the Great Qing army's merit system was no longer based on head counts.

Even if it were, they could wait to cut off heads while cleaning up the battlefield; wouldn't that be more efficient than charging in to fight themselves?

To put it coldly, Yinzhi would rather they die in an internal conflict over grabbing corpses for heads than die in vain under the blades of the Dzungars while letting the Dzungars get away.

Perhaps the Eight Banners generals were deliberately adding trouble for him, not wanting him to achieve a perfect, flawless victory in a battle he commanded entirely?

Yinzhi sneered. Maybe that was really the case.

"Change formation." Yinzhi ordered.

He didn't specify what formation; the infantry immediately mounted their horses and scattered.

Yinzhi also mounted his horse but did not leave.

Now that he was getting closer and closer to Galdan, he no longer needed assistance to shoot at him.

One shot grazed Galdan's helmet.

Galdan's head shook, and his horse's sprinting speed slowed down.

Even if the iron helmet protected his head, the impact was still not pleasant.

Yinzhi narrowed his eyes and fired another shot.

It hit Galdan's helmet again.

Galdan's helmet had a face mask, making it very difficult to hit him.

But as long as he kept shooting at Galdan's helmet, the impact of the bullets would be enough to make him suffer.

Another shot.

Galdan's body swayed, and his horse's speed slowed further.

"Your Highness!" Cao Yin roared.

"Hmm." Yinzhi put away his gun and left with Cao Yin, mixing in with other banner soldiers and scattering.

"There are pits!"

As Galdan held his helmet and his horse's speed slowed, the cavalry in front of him who had rushed past him tripped, and a whole row fell.

Galdan opened his mask and spat out a mouthful of blood-tinged saliva: "How long have they been here! How could they have even dug pits!"

A Dzungar general next to him said: "Maybe they came when the battle started?"

Galdan sneered: "The battle just started, and he was already confident he could win?"

The people around him didn't dare to speak.

Their confident Camel City tactic had been easily crushed by fire, and their leader had been in a rage; if they dared to say one more word, they might be killed by him.

"Continue!" Galdan looked coldly at the cavalry who had fallen into the pits and couldn't get up.

These cavalrymen had already filled the pits, and they just needed to step over them.

For a time, the screams of the Dzungar cavalry were continuous.

But there were too many Dzungar cavalry retreating, and their screams were immediately swallowed by the sound of hooves and battle cries.

When Yinzhi saw Galdan, Galdan also saw the young man in the Great Qing army who was calmly shooting at him.

However, keeping a low profile on the battlefield was the best way to save one's life; Yinzhi didn't like to show his status with majestic armor like other generals. His armor was covered with a layer of black cloth, making him look like an ordinary soldier in the night.

Galdan chased Yinzhi relentlessly, just to avenge those few shots.

But he didn't bring many people, and most of them chased the Crown Prince's ceremonial guards and the areas where the Great Qing musket team was more concentrated; after all, he didn't know that the person shooting at him and finally retreating was the Crown Prince of the Great Qing.

This was also Yinzhi's strategy.

Yinzhi led Galdan on a jog, accurately winding around various traps, successfully causing many of Galdan's cavalry to fall.

Galdan knew there were traps and had the low-status slaves and civilian cavalry scout the path in front.

But this slowed his progress significantly, and the distance between him and Yinzhi grew larger.

Galdan tightened his horse's reins, staring at Yinzhi's direction with a gloomy expression.

Yinzhi also stopped.

He and Galdan were separated by a slope, and there were several trees in front that were rare on the grassland. Although Galdan also had muskets and bows, it was very difficult to hit Yinzhi.

"Retreat." Galdan was not someone who would be blinded by rage.

After calming down, he realized that this group of Great Qing soldiers might be stalling for time, waiting for the main force of the Great Qing pursuit to arrive.

Now, retreating was the most important thing; Galdan swallowed this humiliation and just firmly remembered the young man's appearance in his heart.

He believed that with that young man's courage and ability, as long as he didn't die, he would definitely meet him on the battlefield again in the future.

"What? Is Galdan not chasing me anymore?" Yinzhi said loudly with a smile, "As the former Dzungar Khan who had his home stolen and now has to rely on his nephew's breath, is my marksmanship accurate?"

Galdan's eyes widened in surprise.

Yinzhi laughed: "You've chased me for so long, was it just to avenge those few shots, and not because you recognized that I am the Crown Prince of the Great Qing, Aisin Gioro Yinzhi?"

Galdan gritted his teeth and then smiled: "So it was the Crown Prince of the Great Qing in danger; I admire your courage!"

Yinzhi said: "I have the warriors of the Great Qing by my side, just intercepting the fleeing Dzungar army; how is that being in danger? As for you, since you are already the former Dzungar Khan, don't call yourself 'Khan'; don't you feel embarrassed?"

Yinzhi paused and then smiled again: "So many of my shots didn't break your head; it seems your skin is indeed very thick, even muskets can't penetrate it. It's my fault for underestimating you."

Yinzhi bowed on his horse: "I admire you, I admire you."

Galdan's face turned dark red, but he did not continue the pursuit.

He stopped the Dzungar soldiers who wanted to step forward to capture the Great Qing Crown Prince, turned his horse, and said: "After we part this time, when we meet again, I will personally cut off your head!"

Yinzhi lowered his eyes.

Galdan was indeed an ambitious leader who could keep his cool. Even though he had released such a big bait, Galdan actually didn't take it.

Or was Galdan just trying to numb him?

Yinzhi raised his musket.

If you don't chase, then I will.

When Yinzhi shot a horse in the butt, the powerful impact caused the horse to leap high, almost throwing Galdan off.

Galdan was furious: "You are looking for death!"

He had intended to let Yinzhi go, but he didn't expect this young brat to dare to continue provoking him!

"Khan, shall we chase?" A general next to him said, "As long as we capture the Qing Crown Prince, the Qing army will definitely not dare to pursue us anymore!"

Galdan was also hesitant.

The bait of the "Great Qing Crown Prince" was too tempting, and Yinzhi was too infuriating, making it difficult for him to choose.

He didn't know when the Great Qing's pursuing army would arrive, or if he could catch that cunning brat before they did.

After struggling for a while, Galdan decided to make the safest decision: "Retreat! I will definitely pay back this humiliation a hundredfold!"

Galdan continued to retreat, and Yinzhi followed slowly behind him, occasionally firing cold shots with the people around him.

Galdan deliberately retreated very slowly, seemingly wanting to wait for Yinzhi to get close before turning around to catch him off guard.

But Yinzhi didn't fall for it. Galdan was slow, and he was even slower, as if he were out for a stroll, always keeping a distance that allowed Galdan to escape.

Cao Yin even let his horse walk: "Galdan is too good at holding back. How many times has Your Highness hit his horse's butt and the back of his head?"

The musket barrel was getting hot, so Yinzhi switched to another musket and continued to shoot at the back of Galdan's head, who was wearing heavy armor: "If he couldn't hold back, how could he have become the former Dzungar Khan?"

Cao Yin said: "Indeed. But he is still not as good as his nephew, Tsewang Rabtan. He is already the Dzungar Khan, yet he couldn't even beat the fleeing Tsewang Rabtan. I heard Tsewang Rabtan only has a few thousand troops?"

Yinzhi said: "Less than five thousand banner soldiers. He can fight the Great Qing's tens of thousands of banner soldiers, but he can't beat Tsewang Rabtan's few thousand, and he's been blocked from returning to Dzungar. I guess he might have deep uncle-nephew feelings for his nephew and is deliberately using himself as a whetstone for him."

Cao Yin was surprised: "Is it that touching?"

Yinzhi said: "Otherwise, how do you explain it? I suspect he is actually a loyal subject of his brother, always wanting to help his nephew ascend to the throne. But his nephew is too young, and there are too many treacherous officials in the country. So he pretended to usurp the throne, but actually, he was helping his nephew clear obstacles in domestic politics. When his nephew defeats him, he can die with a smile and go see his own brother."

Cao Yin said: "Didn't he kill another nephew?"

Yinzhi said: "Maybe he thought that other nephew was an obstacle for his nephew? Or maybe he wanted to stimulate his nephew's spirit."

Cao Yin said: "Wow, that's really touching."

Yinzhi nodded: "Yeah, it's so touching."

The two of them were talking loudly in the back; some of the warriors around Galdan were thoughtful, some suddenly realized, some had their mouths twitching, and some were secretly glancing at Galdan's expression.

Unfortunately, Galdan was wearing a mask, and it was too dark, so they couldn't see what expression he had now.

Yinzhi and Cao Yin continued to talk loudly.

Cao Yin said: "If that's the case, aren't the soldiers following Galdan very pitiful? They thought they were following Galdan to make achievements and become close ministers to the king, but in fact, they were all whetstones for Galdan's favorite nephew?"

Yinzhi sighed: "People have their own closeness and distance; there's nothing that can be done about it. Look, he fought Tsewang Rabtan to the death before, and now they have easily reconciled, and Tsewang Rabtan is providing him with logistical supplies without any grudges; doesn't that prove it? His nephew might have already discovered this."

The Dzungar warriors: "..."

A general couldn't help it: "Khan, aren't you going to refute a word?"

Galdan looked at the general gloomily: "Refute what?"

The general stammered and didn't dare to speak.

Galdan kept taking deep breaths, suppressing his anger: "Do you believe him?"

The general immediately said: "Don't believe, don't believe."

Galdan said: "If you don't believe, then what should I explain?"

The general didn't dare to speak again.

To put it plainly, they were indeed shaken.

Originally, they were living well in the Dzungar country, and the Khan said he wanted to take Khalkha Mongolia, but they were blocked on the grassland by Tsewang Rabtan leading a few thousand cavalry, and they had been whispering to each other.

The loyal soldiers around Galdan had already died once, leaving only loyal generals. Some of these people were captured serfs, and some were supply soldiers who came from Dzungar after Tsewang Rabtan opened the passage.

Most of them had not participated in Galdan's disastrous defeat against Tsewang Rabtan, and Galdan would not mention his own defeat, so they didn't know that Galdan was truly inferior in skill.

Of course, they also didn't know that the Khalkha Mongols and the Great Qing Eight Banners army were truly weak, so Galdan could defeat them, but he really couldn't beat his nephew.

Yinzhi's words were a clear attempt to sow discord, but they couldn't help but be shaken.

If this was just a "sharpening" that the Khan and the eldest prince were aware of, then what were all the people who died?

Especially this time attacking the Great Qing, there was basically no benefit at all, but the losses were heavy.

Why did the Khan want to attack the Great Qing? Wasn't Dzungar wide enough? Even Khalkha was ours now; shouldn't we be resting and building up our strength?

Attacking such a vast empire as the Great Qing should only be done after catching one's breath; that would be the rational thing to do, right?

Because of the disastrous defeat, the Dzungar soldiers were finally shaken in their hearts.

Even if Galdan had the dual status of Khan and Buddha, in the face of the terror of life and death, people would still be shaken.

Galdan clearly felt the wavering of those around him.

He took a deep breath, turned his horse's head, and faced the Crown Prince of the Great Qing again.

He drew his sword and said: "What exactly do you want to do?"

Yinzhi said: "Nothing. You must die here."

Galdan looked at Yinzhi carefully through his mask: "What do you have to rely on? Just those few baseless words?"

Yinzhi said: "When your attention was drawn by my words, you didn't notice the surrounding environment."

Galdan was shocked.

He took off his helmet and looked around. Unknown when, many torches had appeared all around.

"Rongruo, you finally came." Cao Yin laughed.

Nalan Xingde arrived in front of Yinzhi with a cavalry unit: "Please forgive me for being late."

Yinzhi said: "Not late, just in time."

Galdan looked at Yinzhi deeply: "The Great Qing army wouldn't come this fast."

Yinzhi said: "This is not the Great Qing's army; it is my Imperial Father's army, the central army of the Great Qing."

Galdan closed his eyes, then threw away his musket and drew the large sword from his horse's back: "Do you want to know why I still attacked the Great Qing when I could have already returned to Dzungar?"

Yinzhi shook his head: "I don't want to know. I only need to destroy all countries that dare to harbor designs on the Great Qing."

"You are the first."

"My eldest brother, the Prince Zhi, has already gone to intercept your nephew."

"Afterwards, I will personally lead the army into Dzungar to slaughter all your relatives."

"I want to make the Choros Esen line extinct."

Yinzhi said lightly: "Do it."

Galdan held his saber, not wearing his helmet, and roared as he charged toward Yinzhi, only to be shot into a sieve by muskets.

Even if he wore a helmet, the armor could no longer withstand the dense musket fire.

After everything was over, Yinzhi dismounted, walked to Galdan, and personally cut off Galdan's head, which was wide-eyed in death.

He held Galdan's hair and looked up at the horizon.

The sky was already turning white.

And the Great Qing Eight Banners soldiers who were supposed to be pursuing still hadn't arrived by the time their battle ended.

Perhaps they were fighting over credit and didn't have time to pursue;

Or perhaps they were misled by Galdan's feint and chased in the wrong direction.

But that didn't matter anymore.

Yinzhi looked down at the dripping head.

Galdan was already dead, leaving only Tsewang Rabtan.

But even if they were all dead, this was not the end.

"The whole army, prepare to move west with me." Yinzhi threw the head to a soldier.

The soldier hurriedly caught the head, getting blood all over himself.

"You take the head back to the capital at full speed and tell the Imperial Father in detail what happened here." Yinzhi turned his horse's head, "Head west and find a place with lush water and grass to set up camp and rest."

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin said: "We obey!"

Yinzhi led the Imperial Guards and half of the central army toward the west, and Donggo Feyanggū followed Yinzhi happily.

The other half of the central army was with Prince Zhi.

The greatest credit still belonged to our central army!

Strangely, the younger brothers all agreed that the First Prince was a bad person, but they didn't dislike him.

Only Yinzhen, whose mouth nagged every day, was both poisonous and long-winded, and he had high combat power.

Want to stop listening? Want to run? The Fourth Brother would grab you and force you to keep listening to his nagging.

"Fourth Brother, stop! My ears are calloused!"

Now, the youngest prince, the Fourteenth, blew a milk bubble and turned over to continue sleeping.

He had already learned the skill of sleeping soundly through the Fourth Brother's nagging.

"Fourth Brother, please nag as much as you want, I am as steady as a mountain."

Seeing these little ones disturbing Li Tong's recovery, Kangxi forbade them from going to the Empress Dowager's palace to bother her.

"Baocheng!" Yinzhi gave Yinreng a bear hug, almost suffocating him with his smell.

Yinreng pushed Yinzhi away, disgusted: "Big Brother, it's not like there's no water in Guihua City; you could still take a bath on time."

Yinreng touched his hair. On the march, long hair was indeed inconvenient; he would shave it into the traditional Manchu style and let it grow back slowly when he returned to the capital.

Although the "money-rat tail" braid was ugly enough to hurt one's eyes, there was a reason for the Manchu nomadic people to have such a hairstyle.

It was ugly, but it was convenient.

On the first day Yinreng arrived in Guihua City, Yinzhi helped him shave his head.

Yinzhi claimed his skills were excellent and he could definitely shave the best-looking braid for Yinreng.

After shaving, Yinreng touched his short hair stubble: "Where is my braid?"

Yinzhi pinched a tuft of hair and handed it over: "My hand slipped. Don't blame me, blame the traditional Manchu hairstyle, the braid is just too thin."

Yinreng was speechless.

He brought a basin of water and looked at his blue-shaved scalp in the reflection.

Alright, he hadn't become a Manchu yet, but he had become a monk first.

Yinreng stared menacingly at the small braid on the back of Yinzhi's head.

Yinzhi spread his hands, then took the razor and wiped the back of his head, handing his own small braid to Yinreng: "Here, if you want a small braid, you can find some paste and stick it on."

"Get lost!" Yinreng kicked him.

Yinzhi laughed out loud.

Yinreng said speechlessly: "If Father Emperor sees us two bald heads, I don't know how angry he'll be."

Yinzhi handed the hair to a servant to be burned. Nobles of this era were afraid of witchcraft, so shaved hair was always burned promptly.

"Why would he be angry? His own hairstyle changes every day. The Imperial Grandfather hasn't possessed you again to scold him, so what does it matter if we accidentally shaved our braids?" The surroundings were empty, and the guards were his own soldiers, so Yinzhi wasn't afraid of walls having ears. He asked, "Speaking of the Imperial Grandfather, does he still enter your dreams?"

Yinreng shook his head: "Ever since the great earthquake in the capital, after the Imperial Grandfather returned to the Eternal Heaven, he has not entered my dreams again."

Yinzhi said: "That's a great thing. Having Father Emperor nagging in front of you is annoying enough, let alone the Imperial Grandfather nagging in your dreams. You were truly miserable when you were young, never having peace awake or asleep."

Yinreng smiled: "If it weren't for the strange encounters back then, how could I be so capable?"

Yinzhi nodded: "That's true. Those naughty brothers are always wondering why you are omniscient. If they were like you back then, with someone urging them to study awake and asleep, they could do it too."

Yinreng laughed uncontrollably: "That won't do, don't persecute the younger brothers."

Once Yinreng arrived, Yinzhi finally agreed to take a bath.

The two changed into new clothes before going to see the commander of the Guihua City garrison—Prince Kang, Jieshu.

Prince Kang Jieshu's son-in-law, Elundai, was also here and had been promoted to Jieshu's deputy general.

This wasn't Jieshu abusing his power. Elundai had been transferred by Kangxi from the New Army and would eventually take over Jieshu's Banner soldiers.

Jieshu tacitly consented.

His older sons now had no ability, and the son he favored was only seven years old and would need many years to grow up. Even if he wanted to control the Plain Red Banner, it would be many years later.

With his loyalty to the Emperor, if the Eight Banners didn't change, the position of the Plain Red Banner master shouldn't be lost.

If the Emperor wanted to move the foundation of the Eight Banners system, his son wouldn't have the ability to stop it, so it was better to follow the Emperor. The Emperor would remember his family's loyalty, and if his son became more outstanding later, his future achievements wouldn't be bad.

The Emperor had his eyes on overseas territories and wanted to expand the borders, so he would definitely prefer to reuse Manchus and clansmen. The Emperor's current reuse of Han officials was just a helpless move. Who told the Manchu nobles and clansmen to insist on opposing the Emperor?

Look at those Manchus and clansmen who followed the Emperor and had talent; the Emperor trusted them deeply.

For example, Changtai, who led such a large navy and rarely returned to the capital, roaming outside all year round, hitting whoever he wanted, highlighting the "act first, report later" style. The Emperor was not only not wary of him but praised him every day, regretting that there wasn't a second Changtai among them.

Jieshu understood the Emperor.

The Emperor was a monarch who was truly broad-minded toward his subjects and almost never wary of external officials. The Emperor's great talent and bold vision made him extremely confident; he believed, and in fact, could indeed control all important officials.

When Jieshu heard the news that the Crown Prince was replacing the Emperor in the imperial expedition, he sighed softly and confirmed once again that his understanding of the Emperor was correct.

As long as the Emperor sat in the capital, even if he put his most beloved Crown Prince on the battlefield, the Emperor wouldn't be afraid at all.

It was just that the Emperor was a bit too bold. He had thought that the Crown Prince would return to the capital after killing Galdan, and that the march into Dzungaria would be led by Prince Zhi.

Unexpectedly, the Crown Prince actually led the Imperial Guards and the other half of the New Army to join Prince Zhi and march into Dzungaria together.

Elundai smiled and explained to his father-in-law: "Prince Zhi already has the merit of destroying a country. If he does it again, the momentum will be too great. Even if Prince Zhi has no intention of competing with the Crown Prince, the First Prince's party in the court might revive. If they revive this time, I'm afraid it won't be to push Prince Zhi to the position of Crown Prince, but to force the Emperor and the Crown Prince to deal with Prince Zhi, causing a rift between them."

Jieshu pondered for a while and sighed, nodding: "Indeed. They would force the label of 'merit overshadowing the master' onto Prince Zhi. Even if the Emperor and the Crown Prince were not suspicious of Prince Zhi, if the rumors were repeated too often, their close relationship might develop cracks."

Elundai said: "Actually, they think too much. Given the Crown Prince's character and conduct, no amount of rumors would affect his feelings for his brothers. The Crown Prince's ability also makes him unafraid of challenges from other brothers. It's just that the Crown Prince loves his brothers very much and would never let them fall into trouble. Based on my understanding of the Emperor and the Crown Prince, this time the Crown Prince's expedition to Dzungaria must have been fought for by the Crown Prince himself. The Emperor couldn't bear it."

Jieshu said: "I understand the Emperor, and you understand the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi. Our judgments shouldn't be wrong."

After saying this, Jieshu smiled: "The Emperor is confident in his own ability, so he doesn't fear external officials; the Crown Prince is also confident in his ability, so he doesn't fear his brothers. The Crown Prince is worthy of being the Crown Prince raised by the Emperor himself."

Elundai was a reckless person. He said bluntly: "That's not surprising. It's normal for the Emperor not to fear external officials, but the fact that the Emperor is not wary of a perfect Crown Prince is what surprises me the most. The Emperor's broad-mindedness is truly rare."

Jieshu nodded silently.

Even if this perfect Crown Prince was cultivated by the Emperor himself, as the Crown Prince grew and the Emperor aged, seeing the Crown Prince getting closer and closer to the throne, the Emperor actually wasn't panicked and generously shared half of his dragon chair with the Crown Prince early on. When the Emperor was in the capital, the Crown Prince was actually exercising the duties of supervising the country. This was truly surprising.

If it weren't for the fact that there was a Hongwu Emperor in the former Ming dynasty who had done this, and there were precedents in history books, the officials would have tried their best to stop it, fearing that the Crown Prince would disrupt the government and cause turmoil in the court.

"Chuntai's age is similar to the younger princes. I heard that the younger princes have begun to enter the court, so he can spend more time with them. If they get close and receive a bit of guidance from the Crown Prince, it will be infinitely useful in the future," Elundai said. "I don't want to sit in the position of Plain Red Banner Commander for too long."

Jieshu laughed: "The Eight Banners Commander is a high-ranking military and political official; even the prime ministers in the court don't dare to be disrespectful. You became a commander at a young age, and although it's temporary, you will definitely be confirmed after this battle. What else are you dissatisfied with?"

Elundai said honestly: "What's the point of staying in the country? The Qing Dynasty has already formed an alliance with Russia, Joseon is very obedient now, and Dzungaria is just a spent force. I want to take Shujin out to sea."

Jieshu said: "I can understand you wanting to go to sea to fight for a greater future. Why take Shujin? Isn't it dangerous overseas?"

Elundai sighed: "Father-in-law, Shujin's martial arts and talent are no less than a man's. But in the country..."

Elundai paused and spread his hands: "Listen to what you just said: I can fight for a future outside, but why take Shujin? Isn't it dangerous? If Shujin were a man, you would definitely say, 'Let Shujin go out with you to fight for a future'."

Jieshu was stunned.

Elundai said: "There are many female nobles in power overseas. The Crown Prince said that officials stationed overseas should bring their wives. The status of Qing noblewomen is equal to that of overseas nobles, so they can deal with female nobles. Shujin has such ability, so she shouldn't be confined to the backyard."

Elundai's expression when mentioning Shujin was always rarely gentle.

Jieshu was silent for a long time before asking: "Did Shujin suggest this to you?"

Elundai laughed: "With Shujin's character, how could she say anything to make things difficult for me? But Shujin and I have a tacit understanding; I understand what she yearns for even if she doesn't say it."

Looking at his son-in-law's sweet expression, a sense of sourness spread in Jieshu's heart.

In an era when most Manchu nobles gave their daughters Manchu transliterated names, or even "Big Girl, Second Girl," Jieshu gave his daughters beautiful Chinese names starting with the character "Shu," and every daughter received a good education in poetry and books, not following the fallacy that women shouldn't have talent. It was clear Jieshu loved his daughters.

Shujin was not only proficient in poetry and history but also inherited his essence in archery and equestrianism. If Shujin were a man, Jieshu would have already asked the Emperor for the position of heir.

Unfortunately, Shujin was a woman, a princess who would be married off.

Elundai understood Shujin, loved her, and was willing to take her to a broader, less restricted world when he fought for his own future. Jieshu should have been happy.

He should have been happy.

Jieshu clenched his fists until they creaked: "Let's go to the training ground and practice."

He really wanted to beat this son-in-law to death!

"Why are you showing off! Why are you showing off! Show off your head!"

Elundai said indifferently: "Father-in-law, you are old now. If I go easy on you, you won't be comfortable, and if I don't, I'm afraid of hurting you. I really don't dare to fight you."

Jieshu roared: "Go to the training ground with me!"

Yinreng, who had just lifted a foot to step into the room, stopped.

Was his timing bad?

Yinzhi pushed Yinreng into the room, then stepped in himself: "Why are you arguing again? Is the father-in-law and son-in-law relationship so hard to handle? I hope my future father-in-law won't be so difficult."

Seeing the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi enter, Jieshu glared fiercely at Elundai, embarrassed to continue arguing.

After he saluted the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi and was about to report the situation of the Guihua City garrison to the Crown Prince, Elundai stepped forward, passed him, and bumped fists with Yinreng.

"Your Highness the Crown Prince, I heard that the Eight Banners trash my father brought caused you a lot of trouble, forcing you to chase them yourself. Shouldn't my father be beheaded now for delaying military opportunities?" Elundai said with a smile.

Yinreng shot Elundai a glance and said testily, "Tong Guogang is already treating you well enough now, what more are you fussing about?"

Elundai shrugged: "It's just habit. If I don't curse him for a day, I don't feel right."

Yinreng said: "Then please get used to it. Tong Guogang doesn't have the authority to command soldiers, but he charged ahead of everyone and was hit by a stray bullet..."

Yinreng watched with satisfaction as a look of panic appeared on Elundai's face.

Elundai also realized he had lost his composure, coughed drily, and said: "He must be fine. If something were wrong, the Crown Prince wouldn't be speaking in such a relaxed tone."

Yinreng nodded: "It was just a graze. Your father's temperament is truly too volatile. I knew his character early on and had people keep a close eye on him, and even then, I barely managed to stop him. When they were dragging him back from the battlefield, he almost bit my men."

Yinreng felt utterly helpless.

He knew that Tong Guogang would have originally died on the battlefield while campaigning against Galdan, so he had long ago ordered people to keep a close watch on him, to prevent him from charging out at his advanced age.

But Tong Guogang was worthy of having raised Elundai, that incredibly stubborn blockhead; Tong Guogang was himself a stubborn old blockhead, who would howl and charge forward the moment he raised his saber.

Yinreng finally understood why Tong Guogang's father had forbidden him from going to the battlefield before he died, only for Tong Guogang to get his fill of it in his old age. He probably knew that Tong Guogang had a temperament that easily overheated on the battlefield and feared he would never return.

Those who do not fear death on the battlefield are indeed hard to kill, but the prerequisite is a cool head.

With Tong Guogang holding down the Tong family now, no matter how much Tong Guowei jumps around, he is only the head of the second branch and cannot stir up much trouble.

If Tong Guogang were to die, even if Elundai would certainly stand on their side, Tong Guowei is Elundai's elder and, to Kangxi, both an uncle and a father-in-law. Even with Kangxi's intervention, the power of the Tong family would inevitably fall into other hands, causing them trouble.

Small troubles are still troubles. Kangxi does not wish for his maternal clan to cause any more problems. Besides, Imperial Noble Consort Tong is already pitiful enough; there is no need to force her to her death.

Both for public and private reasons, Yinreng had finally spent great effort to pull Tong Guogang—who acted like a savage howling and charging forward the moment he hit the battlefield—back from the brink of death.

Now that he had run into Elundai, even with Jeshu nearby, Yinreng couldn't help but complain.

Jeshu listened to the scandalous affairs of his in-laws with great relish.

These two from the Tong family are truly interesting.

The more Elundai heard, the darker his face became, constantly cursing, "That old fool is looking for death," and "I'll scold him to death when I get back."

Yinshi nodded frequently while drinking his butter tea.

Even Imperial Father says I am unfilial; perhaps someone like Elundai is what counts as a truly filial son.

"Accompany me for a walk." After Yinreng finished complaining, he remembered something and patted Elundai on the shoulder.

Yinshi said to Jeshu: "Songgotu's logistics are arriving soon, and we will be breaking camp shortly. There are some things I need to discuss with you."

Jeshu said solemnly: "Please speak, Prince Zhi!"

Guihua City had long since been built into a city; although it was mostly occupied by garrison troops, there were also families of the garrison and logistics personnel. Gradually, other herdsmen began to gather toward Guihua City, and it already had the budding appearance of a prosperous city.

Outside the barracks, civilian houses had been built, and small vendors were calling out their wares.

Yinreng was already wearing casual clothes, so he went straight to the street with Elundai.

Elundai was puzzled: "What business needs to be handled on the street?"

Yinreng shook his head: "We are about to break camp and leave. I'm just here to stroll around and buy some things to send home. Father must be scolding me; I'll send some gifts back to bribe him, so that when I return, I won't get a beating before I've even been rewarded for my merits."

Elundai was left between laughter and tears: "Hey, hey, Young Master, you didn't come here without authorization, did you?"

Yinreng said: "When I left home, Father said all matters were under my full authority, so naturally I have the authority to come here; it cannot be considered unauthorized."

Elundai was speechless.

Yes, yes, yes. It was rumored that before the Crown Prince left the capital, the Emperor had specifically issued an edict handing the military power of the Eight Banners to the Crown Prince, and ordered the Eight Banners generals to treat the Crown Prince's orders as the Emperor's own, and that they were absolutely not to be disobeyed.

So the Crown Prince's actions at this moment indeed did not violate the Emperor's regulations.

But everyone knew that the Emperor was worried about the Crown Prince, that the Crown Prince's status was noble, and that after Galdan's death, the cleanup work should not be done by the Crown Prince on a long expedition.

Elundai lowered his voice and asked: "Are the Eight Banners troops really that useless, that the Crown Prince can't rest easy without coming himself?"

Yinreng said: "They aren't exactly useless. In this decisive battle against Galdan, they also played a significant role."

A flurry of random punches can kill an old master. Even with the new army being elite, they could only barely hold off Galdan's main force, and they lost twenty percent of their strength.

When the Eight Banners troops arrived with slightly more men than Galdan and very good equipment, they took the primary credit in the decisive battle.

The Eight Banners troops simply failed to fully execute his plan, making the victory imperfect and nearly allowing Galdan to escape with his remnants.

The fact that they almost let Galdan go confirmed Yinreng's suspicions.

The Eight Banners banner lords did not want Galdan to die.

They all understood that the reason the Emperor had been slow to take drastic action against the Eight Banners and had maintained their dignity was because of the threat from the Dzungars and Galdan.

If Galdan died, the threat from the Dzungars would be temporarily lifted, the situation within the Qing dynasty would stabilize, and the Emperor would certainly take action against the Eight Banners.

For the Eight Banners lords, this was probably a case of "the rabbit dies, the hunting dog is cooked; the birds are gone, the bow is put away"—quite tragic.

After Yinreng confirmed his suspicions, he initiated a high-risk plan.

He charged in front, and the Eight Banners troops, fearing he would die, had no choice but to chase hard behind him.

Yinreng and Yinshi only needed to gather the elites to scatter the Dzungar army, and the arriving Eight Banners troops would certainly have no choice but to help them swallow the scattered Dzungar forces—given their greed, they would absolutely not let the Dzungar remnants go.

These considerations were not what Yinreng wanted to tell Elundai; he wanted to talk about private matters.

"I'm telling you this, don't get excited, just keep it in mind," Yinreng said.

Elundai raised an eyebrow: "Am I such an impulsive person?"

Yinreng said: "Aren't you?"

Elundai sighed: "Fine, I am. Then why is the Young Master telling me? Wouldn't it be better to keep it from me?"

Yinreng said: "Some things, even if you will be impulsive, I must tell you."

Elundai scratched his shaved head. He had accidentally shaved off his little queue as well.

"Young Master, please speak, I will try my best not to be impulsive," Elundai said. "Or perhaps you could be a bit more tactful and give me some mental preparation."

Yinreng couldn't be bothered to give Elundai mental preparation: "The people I left by Tong Guogang's side said that after Tong Guogang was injured, poison was discovered in his medicine."

Elundai's expression immediately turned into that of a fierce demon: "Who?"

Yinreng said: "I told Tong Guogang and let him investigate it himself. But Tong Guogang has no intention of pursuing it."

Elundai stopped in his tracks, lowered his head, and gnashed his teeth until they creaked.

Yinreng and Elundai had walked to a relatively desolate area; the guards were far enough away to protect them, but unable to hear their whispers.

When Elundai stopped, Yinreng also stopped, looking up at the sky with his hands behind his back, and let out a long, deep sigh.

Knowing full well who wanted to harm him, yet still protecting them—Yinreng could guess even without Tong Guogang saying it.

Elundai could, of course, guess it too.

Although Elundai had offended many people and was one of the right-hand men of Yinreng, the "thousand-handed Guanyin," someone might use underhanded schemes to make Tong Guogang die, forcing Elundai into a period of mourning.

But the cost far outweighed the gain.

Not to mention that Elundai was a military official, and military officials do not lose their posts during mourning, only taking leave; even if they forced Elundai to observe filial piety and resign, with his status as Kangxi's cousin, he could easily be reinstated. Mourning would not trap Elundai at all.

Perhaps Tong Guogang's death could give Tong Guowei, who opposed the Crown Prince, more power. But why would an outsider do such a thankless task for Tong Guowei?

Therefore, this person could only be Tong Guowei.

Privately, Tong Guogang was shielding his younger brother; publicly, if the Emperor knew that the Tong brothers were killing each other, he would likely have an even worse impression of the Tong family, and even if they were his maternal clan, their future would likely be ruined.

Yinreng said: "Just keep it in your heart. That Tong Guogang can endure such a grievance shows that this grievance is not endured for his sake alone; for the sake of the family, you must endure it too."

Elundai laughed out of extreme anger: "He is certainly acting without fear, not afraid of tearing off the mask."

Yinreng said: "First, he didn't expect me to have planted people by Tong Guogang's side, so his intention wasn't to tear off the mask with you; second..."

Yinreng said helplessly: "Think about how many times you've stormed their doors in the capital; haven't you already torn off the mask with them long ago? Now you're blaming them for tearing off the mask with you?"

Elundai said: "I only beat them, I didn't want to kill them. I petition to have my father executed every few days, but I never said I wanted my uncle executed. I can still tell the difference."

The mutual destruction of Tong Guogang and Elundai, father and son, had already become a joke in the capital; no one bothered to care what they did.

Even though Elundai's "petitioning to execute my father" was unfilial and could have been impeached countless times, the censors were too lazy to impeach him anymore.

But although Elundai detested Tong Guowei, he had never dealt with him, only quietly watching Tong Guowei, who had been removed from his post and held only a sinecure, jumping around in silence.

Elundai knew in his heart that the Tong family's bones were connected even if broken; he couldn't stomp Tong Guowei to death in one go.

If Tong Guowei were stomped to death, their own family would also suffer severe damage.

So the best thing was to let Tong Guowei remain idle until death, jumping around in a dark corner until he rotted.

Who knew that he had let Tong Guowei go, but Tong Guowei would not let his family go.

"Fine, this subject will not be impulsive. This subject has to go to Dzungaria now, and then out to sea; I don't have time to be impulsive with him." Elundai snorted, having truly calmed down. "Since Tong Guogang knows his precious younger brother wants to kill him, he can solve it himself. As a junior, I won't overstep."

Yinreng said: "As long as you know. I was worried someone would add fuel to the fire and tell you this, making you impulsive at a critical moment."

Elundai calmed down and joked: "Would they say it was the Crown Prince or the Emperor who wanted to kill my father?"

Yinreng also joked: "To be honest, is your father worth it?"

Elundai spread his hands: "He's not worth a fart!"

It wasn't until the messenger soldier pulled out letter after letter, piling them up across his entire desk, that he came back to his senses.
