199. Two Chapters Combined [V]
From the 30th year of Kangxi onwards, the Great Qing had no more major internal troubles, and the people of the Great Qing entered a period of true recuperation.
The people of the Great Qing were at peace, but the officialdom of the Great Qing was a scene of blood and carnage.
Kangxi raised his butcher's knife, and some said that the moat of Beijing had turned red.
However, when Kangxi raised his butcher's knife this time, the common people clapped and cheered.

Yin Zhi had long since publicized this war in the newspapers. The Eight Banners army dragged their feet and refused to go to the battlefield, while the Prince of the First Rank led the New Army in a desperate resistance, with nearly 50% casualties; the Crown Prince led the Imperial Guard to supervise the battle, and seeing the decay of the Eight Banners, he personally led the Imperial Guard into the battle.

While the Eight Banners were still dragging their feet, the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank had already led the Imperial Guard, who had never seen blood, and the New Army, which had suffered over 50% losses, to the capital of the Dzungars, executing all the rebellious princes.
"The Imperial Guard is basically all sons of high officials."

"Don't just talk about the Imperial Guard, the New Army is the same. The New Army is all student soldiers from Beijing University. Only the children of the Eight Banners and high officials of the court can get in. It's called being a soldier, but it's actually training to be an officer."

"The grandson of the official my brother-in-law works for is studying there. They say it's called a reserve officer; you start as a small soldier, and after learning how to fight, you become a general."
"Isn't this just like the Yulin Army of Emperor Wu of Han in the operas?"
"Yes, that's the one, all young masters of official families."
"Oh my, the young masters of official families are at the front blocking the enemy, while the real army doesn't go to the battlefield? Why do I feel something is strange?"
"Hmph, there must be very deep water in this."
"Didn't the newspaper say it? Those who understand, understand; those who don't, I wouldn't be able to explain it to you anyway."...
The common people engaged in conspiracy theories, and the rumors became more and more exaggerated.

When these events in the capital spread to other places, they had turned into the Prince of the First Rank fighting bravely, the Eight Banners army watching coldly, and the Crown Prince, despite holding the emperor's ceremonial guard, being unable to command the army, so he led the Imperial Guard to fight directly and eventually won.

After the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank won, the Eight Banners army, fearing that they would report them to the Emperor, actually wanted to intercept and kill them. The Emperor was furious upon learning of this and had the rebellious generals of the Eight Banners beheaded, with heads rolling and blood flowing like a river.
Poor Crown Prince and Prince of the First Rank were still trapped in the ice and snow of the Northwest, their life or death unknown.
The Emperor was so angry he vomited blood.
Changtai had just come ashore when he received this terrible news and almost vomited blood himself.
He abandoned the main force, changed several poor horses, rushed back to the capital, didn't even change his clothes, and rushed into the palace with a stubbly beard.
Kangxi was eating mutton hot pot with the Empress Dowager and even invited him to eat together.
Changtai: "?"
Changtai: "Your Majesty, I heard you were ill..."
Kangxi: "Ah?"
Changtai: "Your Majesty, I heard the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank were intercepted and killed by the rebellious Eight Banners army, and you were angered into illness..."
Kangxi: "..."
The monarch and his subject looked at each other.
The Empress Dowager, who could already understand Chinese, was anxious: "What? What happened to the Crown Prince and the eldest prince?"

Kangxi was silent for a while, roughly understanding what had happened, and comforted the Empress Dowager: "It's nothing. They are currently enjoying themselves in Ili, perhaps eating lamb, roasting by the fire, and admiring the snow right now."
Changtai was bewildered: "Enjoying themselves and forgetting home?"
Kangxi said with disdain: "Look at your messy appearance... go to the side to change your clothes, take my clothes for him to change into, and then come over to drink with me."
Changtai was led to the side hall by a eunuch, his head full of confusion. After cleaning his body and face with hot water, he changed into Kangxi's casual clothes.
Kangxi gave this set of clothes to Changtai.

Receiving the Emperor's old clothes as a reward was an honor for an official. However, Changtai's house was already piled full of imperial gifts, and neither he nor Kangxi considered this a reward; there wasn't even an oral decree.
When Changtai came out after changing, the eunuch had already set the bowls and chopsticks for him.
The Empress Dowager smiled and invited Changtai to sit and eat meat, saying this was a sheep sent by Chunxi, and the meat was delicious.

Kangxi looked at Changtai's exhausted appearance and laughed: "Scared, right? If you think about it, you know it's impossible for the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank to be forced to that point. My control over the Eight Banners isn't that weak."
Changtai breathed a sigh of relief: "I heard this news as soon as I landed, and I was really scared, just thinking about rushing into the palace to protect the Emperor."

Changtai paused and smiled bitterly: "Now that I've calmed down, I realize that I rushed into the capital alone, and it seems I couldn't protect the Emperor anyway? How did I leave all my troops on the shore and not even bring a guard?"

Kangxi laughed loudly: "If you wanted to protect the Emperor, you should have at least brought a few guards; maybe you could have snuck into the palace to save me. Isn't coming alone just throwing your life away?"
Changtai mocked himself: "Perhaps I could have entered the palace to serve you, been trapped in one place with you, and waited for the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank to save us?"
Kangxi laughed loudly again and put a large chopstick of meat into Changtai's bowl: "Shut up and eat your meat; how could I have such a stupid brother-in-law."
The Empress Dowager was also amused.
She understood now; Songgotu was like this, and Changtai was too. The family of the Empress Renxiao was very interesting; no wonder they could produce such a good child as the Crown Prince.
Changtai was not reserved; since the Emperor told him to eat meat, he buried his head and ate.
The Empress Dowager was old and went back to rest after eating a few bites.
Kangxi continued to eat meat with Changtai and opened two bottles of wine; the two didn't use wine glasses but drank straight from the bottles.
Only then did Kangxi tell Changtai what had happened, bit by bit.
Changtai sighed: "Even if it wasn't a fifty percent loss, a twenty percent loss is enough to make one's heart ache."

The smile on Kangxi's face faded: "Yes. Those were all generals I cultivated; let alone twenty percent, even one percent or half a percent makes my heart ache unbearably. Look at this inner city; almost half of the households have hung up white cloth."
That was why Kangxi's great slaughter this time did not meet with much opposition in the court.

The Central Route Army, led by the Prince of the First Rank, Yin Ti, with the New Army as the main force, indeed consisted mostly of sons of nobles and officials. They were also the first batch of excellent students in the university and would all be people capable of leading troops in battle in the future.

"I originally let Zhao Liangdong follow the army, but he is old and ill and returned to the capital to offer me advice. After he learned that the delay of the Eight Banners led to a twenty percent loss in the Central Route Army, his illness became even more severe. You should go see him after you have rested for a day." Kangxi said gloomily.
Changtai also looked gloomy: "Yes."
The first batch of university students was small, and the excellent students were taught hand-in-hand by Zhao Liangdong and Jieshu.
To Zhao Liangdong, these people were not just students, but disciples.
Disciples are like sons; their feelings were not much different from those for his own children.

Hearing that many of his excellent disciples had died on the battlefield, and the reason was not a cruel battle but merely the fatigue of war caused by the Eight Banners' delay and the late arrival of reinforcements, Zhao Liangdong was writing memorials to impeach Fuquan and Changning even while ill.
At the time of the beheadings, Zhao Liangdong had his family carry him to the execution ground, constantly crying and shouting, "They deserve to die, they all deserve to die."
Kangxi personally came to the execution ground to supervise, watching head after head fall, his mood completely unmoved.
Only when he heard and saw Zhao Liangdong's sorrowful wailing did Kangxi feel a great pain in his heart and couldn't help but shed tears.

Not only Zhao Liangdong. Yuele, who was supposed to go to Guihua City to wait for orders with Jieshu but was persuaded by the Crown Prince to return home to retire due to his advanced age, also fell seriously ill.
As a prince, Yuele actually went to the most radical side of calling for the abolition of the Eight Banners and the establishment of a new system for the sake of these students.
There were also many officials who had taught at Beijing University who raised their arms and shouted that these people deserved to die, and should have died more miserably and in greater numbers.
Fuquan and Changning stayed behind closed doors, worried sick.
They were scolded whenever they went out now; where was the joy of winning a battle?

When Changtai learned that the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank were not only fine but also very happy, he evaluated objectively: "Prince Yu and Prince Gong didn't actually make big mistakes this time. If you have to say there was a mistake, it was just incompetence."
Kangxi snorted coldly: "Incompetence in a general is the greatest mistake."
Changtai thought to himself that he agreed. But on his lips, he still spoke well of Prince Yu and Prince Gong to soothe Kangxi's depression caused by his brothers' uselessness.

"The remaining New Army, after this baptism, can directly enter the Eight Banners army as generals upon their return," Changtai said. "Only generals who have gone through cruel wars can hone their talents. For the Emperor, this cannot be considered a bad thing."

Kangxi rolled his eyes at Changtai: "I know. I'm still heartbroken. Speaking of which, you have also cultivated many people in your navy, right? Let me use them first; I have beheaded too many people and can't find enough people to replace them for the time being. Let your people fill the positions first, and then change them when Baocheng and the eldest prince return."

Changtai said: "The navy is the Great Qing's navy, the Emperor's navy. If the Emperor wants people, I have a list here. They are all good talents honed through fighting and should be trained on land."

Kangxi nodded: "That's true; it's time for rotation and training. When the New Army people return, I will hand them over to you first, and you take them abroad for training. My generals cannot be ignorant of the situation abroad."
Speaking of this, Kangxi was a little depressed: "I want to go too. What do you think if I let the Crown Prince supervise the state and I go abroad for a stroll?"
Changtai's mouth twitched: "The Crown Prince will hug your thighs and howl."

Kangxi sighed: "When the Crown Prince visited foreign countries, he once said that the world is so big, he wants to go and see it. I want to too! How about I become the Retired Emperor and let the Crown Prince succeed to the throne early?"
Changtai was speechless.
How could he answer this? But since Kangxi was chatting with him privately, he had to answer.

"If the Emperor wants to be the Retired Emperor, I will also resign from the position of Navy General, become your guard, and go around together," Changtai said calmly. "With the position of Navy General, I am not at ease abroad. At that time, the Emperor and I can dress up as rich merchants or pirates; it will definitely be very interesting."
When Kangxi said he wanted to be the Retired Emperor, he knew he had made a slip of the tongue.
Although he had this thought in his heart, he shouldn't tell others, and especially shouldn't tell Changtai.
Although Changtai was his close friend, he was also the Crown Prince's uncle. The talk of early succession was too sensitive; if it spread, Changtai would be very embarrassed.
He was just thinking about how to divert the topic when he didn't expect Changtai to answer naturally.
Kangxi said happily: "You've been running outside for so long and you're still not at ease?"

Changtai said: "I have too many soldiers behind me, and the Great Qing; every step I take must be thought about for a long time, so of course I'm not at ease. I don't dare to leave the ship for a long time, and those foreigners don't dare to let me stay on land for a long time either."
Kangxi sighed: "That is indeed very bitter. But if you don't help the Crown Prince continue to manage the navy, the Crown Prince will be in a lot of trouble."

Changtai said: "Now there are many capable young generals in my navy, and many capable young people in the New Army. These people can all replace my position. I have been tired for so many years; if the Emperor rests, I also want to rest."
Kangxi couldn't laugh or cry: "Just be lazy. Okay, if I become the Retired Emperor, you will follow me on a micro-visit."
Changtai smiled: "It's a deal."

The two made this unreliable agreement after drinking. Changtai stayed in the palace for a day without returning to his mansion, but rode out of the city to find the army he had left behind. After organizing them, he returned to the capital with a team of people he could recommend to Kangxi.

These people were inserted by Kangxi into the Eight Banners to rectify the military discipline. Seeing the new officials take office, the Eight Banners army temporarily let go of their anxious hearts.
At least this showed that the Eight Banners would not be abolished immediately, and they still had food and pay.
After Changtai returned to the capital, the capital became even calmer.
Everyone knew that Changtai was the Emperor's Wei Qing, while the Crown Prince was not that stupid, tyrannical crown prince.
With the Emperor having Changtai lead the army stationed in the capital as guards, the restless hearts of the nobles could only be temporarily calmed.

Kangxi very arrogantly had Changtai change into guard clothes, and every day he brought Changtai, this guard, to show off in the streets, almost writing "If you have the ability, rebel against me" on the folding fan he was fanning in the dog days of summer, making the nobles who were dissatisfied with Kangxi grit their teeth.
The rumors spread too fast; not only did Changtai rush to the capital, but Dulide also dragged his sick body to the capital to protect the Emperor.
Kangxi was both moved and helpless.

He pointed at Changtai's nose and said: "First you came to the capital alone on horseback to protect the Emperor, and then Master Du came to the capital with a cane to protect the Emperor! Why are the people who want to protect me so useless! You are not protecting me, you are accompanying me to the grave!"
Changtai pretended not to hear and acted like a mute, not answering.
Seeing that Kangxi was in high spirits and could still joke and scold people, Dulide breathed a sigh of relief: "If that's the case, then I can only be buried with the Emperor."

"Alright, alright, don't say ominous words. Since you're in the capital, let the imperial physician take a good look at you." Kangxi looked at Dulide's physical condition and was extremely worried. "The Crown Prince is fine; he and the Prince of the First Rank pacified the Dzungars, turning it into the Ili Prefecture of the Great Qing. They are currently building Yining City in the Ili River Valley, and the Great Qing will station troops in Yining City in the future."
Dulide stroked his chest: "It's good that he's fine, it's good that he's fine."
Kangxi comforted: "Master Du, rest for now. If your health is better, you can also go to the university to take a look. The university is getting more and more lively now."
Dulide smiled: "Okay, I will definitely go and see."
After sending Dulide away, Chen Tingjing came to request an audience.
This time, he brought news of rumors to Kangxi again, and this time the news was not on the Crown Prince's side.

"The one who slaughtered the Dzungars was not foreign mercenaries, but the Crown Prince? The Crown Prince slaughtered Dzungar princes and civilians and pushed the blame onto foreign mercenaries?" Kangxi was so angry he laughed. "I won't even mention how kind and stupid the Crown Prince was when he cried after beheading a group of rebels in Hangzhou; even if he slaughtered them, so what? Shouldn't the Dzungar princes be slaughtered? This is a military merit; why would the Crown Prince need to push it onto others?"
Chen Tingjing breathed a sigh of relief when he heard Kangxi say this.
When he heard this rumor, he was also worried about whether the Qing army had slaughtered the city again.

Chen Tingjing didn't doubt the Crown Prince. He knew the Crown Prince couldn't do such a thing. But the Crown Prince might only be supervising the battle, and he believed that the Prince of the First Rank could definitely do such a thing.
The Crown Prince didn't want to slaughter the city, but the Prince of the First Rank slaughtered the city and pushed the blame onto foreign mercenaries, and the Crown Prince might have been deceived.

Now the Emperor's words calmed him down. With the Crown Prince's wisdom, it was impossible to let the Prince of the First Rank mess around, and it was impossible to be deceived by the Prince of the First Rank.
Thinking back to when the Crown Prince led them overseas, the Prince of the First Rank was causing trouble everywhere, and the Crown Prince was able to hold him back.

Chen Tingjing said: "The Dzungar princes deserve to die, and the rumors mostly start from the civilians to smear the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank. I request to lead a team of officials to support the Crown Prince. The newly built Yining City needs officials, and the Crown Prince also needs the pens of us scholars to clarify for him."
Kangxi was angry, but hearing Chen Tingjing's words, his anger was replaced by helplessness.

He first let Chen Tingjing sit down, and then said kindly: "Chen Ziduan, you just came back from Russia, and I was preparing to reuse you. Why are you running out again? Is there anyone chasing you in the capital? Other officials are racking their brains to come to the capital, but you always want to go out, and you are not even serving as a high-ranking official."
Kangxi really didn't want Chen Tingjing to run out again. The court also lacked capable officials who could do things and were to his liking.

Kangxi had already prepared the position of Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion for Chen Tingjing. After Chen Tingjing rotated through the Six Ministries, he could enter the Wenyuan Pavilion as a Grand Secretary, becoming what the people commonly called "Prime Minister," Kangxi's confidant.
But since Chen Tingjing went overseas with the Crown Prince once, he couldn't stay idle.
He didn't even want to be a local official, just running around with the temporary official hat of an envoy. Originally a high-ranking official of the court, he didn't even have a real position now.
Kangxi felt it was a waste of talent.

Chen Tingjing said seriously: "I serve as an official, first to repay the Emperor and benefit the people; second, to bring honor to my ancestors and leave a name in history. Many officials in the Hanlin Academy can do the things in the court. But overseas affairs and border affairs, forgive me for being conceited, are for me alone. Doing things that only I can do can better serve the Emperor and benefit the people, and can also better bring honor to my ancestors and leave a name in history."
Kangxi was speechless.
That's what he said, but everyone wants glory and wealth to be a high official, and you, Chen Tingjing, are...

"Alright, since you've put it this way, how can I stop you?" Kangxi said. "If you want to go to Ili, then go. Take more supplies for the Crown Prince. Given his temperament, he certainly won't return until he has smoothed out the affairs in Ili and established the city's foundation. You must urge him not to overwork himself. As for the Eight Banners and foreign affairs, I will handle them."
Chen Tingjing bowed excitedly: "Your subject obeys the decree!"

Watching Chen Tingjing leave in high spirits, Kangxi rubbed his forehead: "Changtai, among the Han people, there is no shortage of capable and righteous men like Chen Tingjing who do not covet power or wealth and only think of the country and the people. I truly envy the Han people."

Changtai said with a straight face: "Your Majesty, you are wrong there. Nowadays, there are no Han or Manchu people; everyone is a citizen of the Great Qing, and everyone is your subject. Besides, even if Your Majesty insists on distinguishing between Manchu and Han, am I not as good as Chen Tingjing?"

Kangxi laughed: "Fine, fine, fine, you are right. There are no Han or Manchu, only citizens of the Great Qing. Also, why are you acting so jealous? You are my brother-in-law; aren't you ashamed to say you don't covet glory and wealth?"
Changtai said: "I am the Emperor's brother-in-law, so why can't I be indifferent to glory and wealth? One's background does not affect one's character."
Kangxi fell silent.
Although Changtai's character was indeed good, hearing him brag about himself made Kangxi's hands itch.
Winter was monotonous, and the days of spring warmth and blooming flowers arrived very quickly in Yinreng's perception.
Before he had rested enough, the ice and snow in the Ili River Valley had melted.
The craftsmen captured from the Dzungars were all summoned by the Qing army, and the herdsmen and merchants within the Dzungar Khanate also spontaneously gathered at the foundation of Yining City.
Yinreng drew a circle on the ground, felt that the soil had thawed, and planted a flag of the Great Qing; the construction of Yining City continued in full swing.
The heavy snow had melted, and Yinreng sent another letter saying he needed to stay a little longer.
How long is this "little longer"... soon, right away, don't rush me, Khan Ama. Anyway, there won't be anything happening in the capital right now; just watch your son ship gold back to you.

With coal mines, gold mines, and a newly discovered iron mine, Yinreng led the Qing army to happily build workshops. With tools and money available, once the merchant caravans arrived, there was no shortage of supplies.
When Chen Tingjing arrived with a group of scholars, he found that the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank (Yinzhi) had gained weight, while they themselves were haggard.
Yinreng was surprised: "Why did Master Chen come?"

Chen Tingjing said: "The Emperor ordered me to bring supplies and craftsmen to the Crown Prince and the Prince of the First Rank. The newly built Yining City lacks officials, so I have come to assist the Crown Prince."
He glanced at the Prince of the First Rank.
Yinzhi: "Master Chen, why are you staring at me?"
Clearly, Yinzhi still respected Chen Tingjing quite a bit, otherwise, it would have been a direct "What are you looking at?"
Yinreng said: "Master Chen, if you have something to say, just say it."
He locked Yinzhi in a headlock: "I've already pinned down my older brother, don't worry."
Yinzhi: "?"
Chen Tingjing was between laughter and tears: "Very well. Please don't get agitated, Prince of the First Rank."
Yinzhi: "I can't even move, how could I be agitated?"

Chen Tingjing suppressed a laugh and said: "There are rumors in the capital that the Crown Prince massacred the city. I have brought many scholars who can write well to help the Crown Prince clarify the truth."
Yinzhi jumped up, nearly knocking Yinreng over: "Who?! Who is spreading rumors!! I want to have them sliced into a thousand pieces!!"

"Alright, alright, sliced into a thousand pieces, they aren't here anyway. We'll ask Khan Ama after we return to the capital." Yinreng hung onto Yinzhi to prevent him from going on a rampage. "It's no use getting angry at Master Chen now; isn't Master Chen here to help us clarify?"
Yinzhi calmed down: "Master Chen, I will take you to see something, and you will understand once you see it."
Chen Tingjing said: "Very well."
Yinzhi angrily led the scholars from the capital to the memorial monument.
The memorial monument here had already become a memorial wall. After the herdsmen learned what the Qing army was building, they came to help spontaneously during the winter.
Some Dzungar nobles ran out from their hiding places, wailed before the monument, and also actively joined the ranks of those carving names.
The people here followed Yinreng's example, not burning paper or offering sacrifices, but placing wreaths before the memorial wall, standing in silent mourning, and then continuing with their work.
Chen Tingjing and the officials and scholars from the capital all fell silent.

They carefully read the poems written by Cao Yin, the lyrics by Nalan Xingde, and the article personally written by the Crown Prince recording the cause and effect; their eyes turned red, and bloodshot veins spread across them.
After a long while, Chen Tingjing finally calmed down and said with a trembling voice: "I... understand. I will ensure that the truth of Yining City spreads throughout the world!"

200. Two chapters combined [V]
The scholars who dared to come to the Northwest to make contributions in this era had quite good ability and resilience.
After they arrived, city construction and population registration were carried out simultaneously, and even land reclamation was arranged.
Perhaps the herdsmen trusted the Qing army too much. Even though they only knew how to herd sheep, they actually listened obediently and learned the work of farmers.

The scholars wandered between the herdsmen and the Qing army with their brushes, their eyes filled with tears at the harmony between the military and the civilians, their literary inspiration flowing like a spring.
Chen Tingjing, whose body was becoming increasingly sturdy, wore short clothes and, instead of holding a brush, held a hoe to teach the herdsmen how to dig the land.
But his brilliant essays were all in his mind, and he could write them down as soon as he returned to rest.
Yinreng, pulling Yinzhi who wanted to go hunting, took a tour and was extremely shocked.
He shook Yinzhi's shoulders and said: "Older brother! How on earth did they learn the herdsmen's dialect so quickly?!"
Yinzhi swayed back and forth, yawning: "Didn't you learn it quickly too?"
Yinreng felt aggrieved. I learned it so quickly because I have a "memory cheat"! They didn't have a cheat, and their learning speed was about the same as mine; don't I have any face to lose!

Yinzhi rolled his eyes at Yinreng and spoke in Mongolian with Dzungar dialect characteristics: "Is it hard? Isn't Mongolian all about the same? Once you learn Mongolian, learning the local dialect here is very simple."
Yinreng held his head like a Psyduck.
Is that so? Was he the only one who thought it was difficult? Is dialect so easy to learn?
The generals in the Qing army heard Yinreng's confusion and shook their heads one after another.
No, no, no, no, we haven't learned it yet. Your Highness the Crown Prince, please don't compare the learning speed of those scholars with ours!
Also! Prince of the First Rank, don't you usually act as brainless as us! Why did you suddenly become smart!
The Prince of the First Rank picked his teeth: I was a genius to begin with.
Fiyanggu, while diligently studying the dialect, arranged for the entire army to do the same.
He called it "for the sake of the future," saying that since everyone would be stationed here, the dialect must be learned.
But seeing Fiyanggu's twisted expression, Yinreng always felt that Fiyanggu was just in pain himself and wanted the whole army to suffer with him.

However, it was a good thing for the soldiers to learn more. Yinreng not only didn't stop them but also had the soldiers learn classics, history, and philosophy from the scholars together with the selected herdsmen or the Dzungar minor nobles who had defected.
Administrative work was dumped on Chen Tingjing, and Yinreng, now idle, began to compile textbooks for the Dzungars.
Uniformity of writing. To completely assimilate Dzungar into the territory of the Great Qing, education was the top priority.
Yinreng first compiled Chinese and arithmetic textbooks, and then compiled local history books. This "since ancient times" was a good way to foster a sense of identity.
Yinzhi glanced at what Yinreng was busy with and ran away, not even entering Yinreng's tent to sleep.

Although Yinzhi, under Kangxi's cramming education, could be considered well-read, after he was freed from Kangxi's control, he got a headache whenever he saw anything with a lot of text, except for military books.
Rather than accompanying his younger brother to compile books, he was more willing to help Master Chen, even if it meant carrying sandbags at the construction site.

Master Chen Tingjing was speechless and very much wanted to find a ruler to rap the First Prince's head: "Compiling books can enhance your prestige, Prince of the First Rank. Please go help the Crown Prince!"
The Prince of the First Rank shrugged and spread his hands: "I don't need this prestige."
Chen Tingjing began to roll up his sleeves.
The Prince of the First Rank warned Chen Tingjing: "Master Chen, you can't beat me, don't make a move, you'll be the one to suffer if you do."
Chen Tingjing was so angry he leaned back.
Yinzhi laughed and acted like a sycophant, tapping Chen Tingjing's shoulders. With his full force, he almost knocked Chen Tingjing to the ground.
Suspecting the Prince of the First Rank was trying to murder him, Chen Tingjing angrily drove Yinzhi away, and Yinzhi went to the construction site laughing.
If he said he would carry sandbags, he would carry sandbags; the Prince of the First Rank never bluffed.
Anyway, as long as he didn't have to compile books.
Gusheng, who had become Fiyanggu's advisor, whispered to Fiyanggu: "What is this official's status?"
Although the Prince of the First Rank was quite close to other high-ranking Qing officials, this was the first time he had been so polite.
Fiyanggu whispered back: "Master Chen once taught the First Prince and the Crown Prince to read; he is a teacher to the princes."
Gusheng was astonished: "A teacher to the princes actually came to us?"
Fiyanggu said: "Most teachers to the princes stay in the capital living in luxury; only this Chen Tingjing is particularly strange, he likes to run around."

He introduced Chen Tingjing's deeds and said: "You say, he is a civil official, yet he has visited overseas several times and made so many military achievements. I haven't even had such an opportunity."
Gusheng suppressed a laugh.
His general seemed to be complaining about Chen Tingjing, but in reality, he was jealous.

Thinking about it, it made sense. The general had been stationed at the frontier for a long time to defend against the Russian Empire. But in terms of military achievements, it seemed that Chen Tingjing, this scholar, was actually more dazzling.

Whether it was entering Annam alone to lead reinforcements to destroy the Guangnan Kingdom, or acting as an envoy to the Russian Empire to orchestrate the Empress's coup and ascension, Chen Tingjing didn't look like a scholar at all.
Hmm...
Gusheng remembered the books he had read and sighed: "Master Chen is truly a very traditional scholar."
Fiyanggu was speechless: "How is he traditional?"

Gusheng said: "The commoner means that Master Chen is truly like the scholars of the Han and Tang dynasties. Didn't the scholars of the Han and Tang dynasties all have the ability to destroy a country single-handedly? The former Ming actually had them too; that Wang Yangming was one."
Fiyanggu's family was also a scholarly family among the Manchus, otherwise his sister wouldn't have become Shunzhi's confidante. So Fiyanggu had also read history books.
Hearing Gusheng's words, Fiyanggu also remembered those particularly outrageous "traditional" scholars recorded in history books.
He couldn't help but say: "He really is a traditional scholar."
Fiyanggu looked at the unrestrained scholars in front of him, wearing short clothes or with their long robes tucked into their belts.
"The Great Qing's traditional scholars might be increasing," Fiyanggu said. "We military generals are under a lot of pressure."

Gusheng flattered him: "The Crown Prince said that the General comes from a scholarly family. Although the General has now traded the pen for the sword, he is still considered a scholar, both civil and martial."
Fiyanggu rubbed his head, feeling a bit awkward.
That was true, but he had long since put his books aside.
Forget it, forget it. In order not to be outdone by this group of "traditional scholars," he had to pick up his books again.
Thus, Celing, who was studying hard while idle, welcomed the company of his good brother.

Yinzhi mocked Fiyanggu, saying that Empress Xiaoxianzhang was a famous talented woman, yet her younger brother had fallen to the point of studying with a Mongolian prince; Empress Xiaoxianzhang would definitely be angry enough to scold people in the heavens.
Fiyanggu muttered: "My sister wouldn't scold people."
Fiyanggu remembered his sister who managed his younger brother and all the family affairs at home, and said sheepishly: "It seems my sister really would scold people."
Empress Xiaoxianzhang was once a daughter pampered by her family. In this era, families that could cultivate their daughters into talented women were all doting on them.
Empress Xiaoxianzhang had both the talent of a Han noble lady and the boldness of a Manchu aunt; she was an expert at twisting the ears of disobedient younger brothers.
But when Fiyanggu last saw his sister alive, she had shed all her boldness and arrogance, and even her eyes were covered with a layer of gray.
She was humble, respectful, and cautious; all her emotions were hidden behind her lowered eyes, and even when she saw her family, there was no ripple in her gaze.

Fiyanggu didn't understand at that time. It was said that his sister was the most favored in the six palaces, but no matter how he looked at her, she didn't look like those favored concubines in the storybooks.
Yinzhi gave Fiyanggu a slap on the back, almost knocking him to the ground: "I'm talking to you, why are you distracted?"
Fiyanggu grimaced: "Prince of the First Rank, your strength is too great. This subordinate just remembered my sister."
Yinzhi asked curiously: "What kind of person was your sister? Like in the storybooks? Especially arrogant?"
Fiyanggu: "..." Prince of the First Rank, if you weren't a prince, with that mouth of yours, you would have been beaten up in a sack several times already.
Yinreng was finishing his book compilation work for the day and rubbed his wrists to ask Yinzhi for food.
Just like when they were young, whenever he was hungry, he would look for Yinzhi, and Yinzhi could always conjure up a pile of food for him like a magic trick.
"What's wrong? Older brother, are you bullying General Fiyanggu again?" Yinreng reached into Yinzhi's arms and, sure enough, found a cloth bag of smoked meat, asking happily while chewing.
Yinzhi said: "What are you saying? When have I ever bullied him? I just asked him if his sister was as arrogant as in the storybooks, and his face turned black. This person is really petty."
Yinreng almost choked: "Cough, cough, older brother, can you use your brain when you speak?"
Yinzhi said arrogantly: "I am a prince, and Fiyanggu is my subordinate, why should I use my brain when I speak?"
Yinreng and Fiyanggu looked at each other in silence.
Oh, so the older brother/Prince of the First Rank also knew that this question was very inappropriate, he was just being himself.

Yinreng answered for Fiyanggu: "Concubines in the palace, even if they are favored, can probably only be arrogant in front of servants and concubines of lower rank. In front of others, who isn't cautious? You grew up in the harem, don't you know?"
Yinzhi snatched a piece of smoked meat and put it in his mouth: "It's like that in Khan Ama's harem, I thought Imperial Grandfather's harem would be a little more relaxed."

Yinreng shook his head: "Look at the records of Empress Xiaoxianzhang in the real records of Imperial Grandfather's time, and you will know that Empress Xiaoxianzhang couldn't live happily. When Imperial Grandfather was sick from anger, she served him; when Ukumama was sick from anger, she served her; when Imperial Grandmother was scared sick, she still served her. The three of them were sick in turns, and she didn't have a single day of rest. She had to persuade this one and that one, and even remonstrated with her life..."

After Yinreng said a series of things, he realized that it was not good to speak ill of Shunzhi. He had also borrowed Shunzhi's reputation, so he shouldn't disparage this Imperial Grandfather too much.
Yinreng said: "Let's not talk about the harem. It's not good to bring up family affairs."

Yinzhi chewed the meat, speaking unclearly: "Fiyanggu isn't an outsider, what does it matter if we mention it to him? Empress Xiaoxianzhang is also our Imperial Grandmother, he is our... uncle-grandfather?"
Fiyanggu: "...I don't dare, Prince of the First Rank, please don't insult this subordinate."
Who would dare to be your uncle-grandfather, Prince of the First Rank! I'm afraid of losing my lifespan!
"Let's just count our seniority separately." Yinreng suppressed a laugh.

Seeing Fiyanggu's hidden expression of disgust, Yinreng didn't know who was more annoying, his older brother or his fourth younger brother, who was famous in the capital for being disliked by cats and dogs.
Yinreng missed his younger brothers.

His younger brothers were in a growth stage where they changed every day. This time when he returned to the capital, their appearance and height would have changed greatly. Missing his younger brothers' growth made him, as an older brother, feel sad.
Especially his little Thirteenth. Little Thirteenth was nominally under his care, yet he hadn't had time to properly teach him.
This time when he returned to the capital, he was determined to rest for a few years and raise his younger brothers.
There was nothing major in the country now. As for major events abroad, they would have to wait a few years.
"Why are you spacing out too?" Yinzhi snatched another piece of smoked meat.
Yinreng said the truth: "I miss my younger brothers. And the princesses in the palace, they are almost ready to be married, right? We must choose good families for them."
Yinzhi said decisively: "I don't miss them at all. A bunch of little devils, miss them my foot!"
Yinreng glanced at Yinzhi.
Although his older brother always said he didn't miss his younger brothers, every time he returned to the capital, he prepared gifts for his brothers and sisters.
Anyone who could make his older brother prepare gifts must have been kept in his heart.

"In another two or three months, after Master Chen smooths out the affairs in Ili, we will return to the capital." Yinreng said, "With Master Chen here, we don't need to worry about this place anymore."
Yinzhi, with the meat in his mouth, looked like a street loafer in the capital: "Master Chen is one step further away from the center."
Yinreng rolled his eyes at Yinzhi: "If Master Chen wanted to return to the capital, he would enter the center immediately."

Yinzhi said: "It's still Khan Ama who is unkind. Grand Secretary is just an empty title, wouldn't it be better to let Master Chen enter the Wenyuan Pavilion before letting him run around? By the way, younger brother, what posthumous title do you want to propose for Master Chen?"
Yinreng: "Huh?"
Yinzhi said: "If Master Chen doesn't have any issues later, a 'Wenzhen' is stable, right?"
Yinreng said: "Too low?"
He remembered that in history, Master Chen's posthumous title was "Wenzhen." Now Master Chen's contribution was much greater than in history, so "Wenzhen" would be very inappropriate.
However, in the posthumous title rules of the Ming and Qing dynasties, Wenzhen was already a second-tier title, and the one above it was "Wenzheng."

Because of the fame of Fan Zhongyan, Fan Wenzheng, and Sima Guang's evaluation that "Wenzheng is the most beautiful title, nothing can be added," Ming and Qing emperors would not easily give the title "Wenzheng."
Yinreng said: "Just based on Master Chen's current merits, I also want to strive for a 'Wenzheng' for him. But in my opinion, 'Wenzheng' is not as good as 'Zhongwu'."

"Zhongwu" was the highest tier among common posthumous titles. Compared to "Wenzheng," people with the title "Zhongwu" could almost be deified by the people, such as Zhuge Liang of the Three Kingdoms, Yuchi Gong of the Tang Dynasty, Yue Fei and Han Shizhong of the Southern Song Dynasty, Chang Yuchun of the Ming Dynasty, etc.

However, in the late Qing Dynasty, the title "Zhongwu" was abused, making it seem less prestigious—except for the "Zhongwu" given during the Daoguang period, which could barely be considered as having the merit of protecting the Great Qing, the remaining "Zhongwu" were all issued in batches to generals who suppressed the Taiping Rebellion, and by then "Zhongwu" was no longer valuable.

But at that time, the entire feudal dynasty was no longer valuable, so it was natural that the posthumous titles relying on the feudal dynasty were not valuable; it was not a problem with the title "Zhongwu" itself.
At present, "Zhongwu" was still the most desired posthumous title for all civil and military officials.

Fiyanggu was originally slandering how the First Prince and the Crown Prince could discuss Chen Tingjing's posthumous title while he was still alive; it was too unlucky, these two princes had no respect for their teacher.
But now, Fiyanggu just wanted to shout, discuss my posthumous title too! I also want "Zhongwu"! As a military man, I'm not afraid of what's lucky or unlucky!
"'Zhongwu,' Master Chen is not qualified enough to get the title 'Zhongwu' yet." Yinzhi wiped his mouth with his sleeve, "I am quite qualified, remember to give me the title 'Zhongwu' in the future."
Yinreng said: "Older brother, you are a clan prince, the posthumous title rules are different from those of ministers. How about 'Xian'?"
Yinzhi said: "Not good, I just want Zhongwu. It's not like clan princes can't have two-character posthumous titles."
Yinreng said: "It's really not according to the rules. How about I add an 'Yi' for you? How about Yi Xian Prince?"
I'll add the posthumous titles of the twelfth and thirteenth younger brothers for you, please, older brother, stop making trouble!
Yinzhi waved his hand: "No room for negotiation, nothing but 'Zhongwu' will do. Can't your older brother compare to a Zhuge Liang?"
Yinreng: "..." How is my younger brother supposed to answer this?
Fiyanggu: "..." Your Highness the Crown Prince, you must hold on! You must not let this shameless First Prince succeed!
After Yinzhi and Yinreng were full, they went out for a walk. While walking, they were still discussing the posthumous title.
Chen Tingjing saw the Crown Prince coming from afar and walked over to greet him.

Just as he got close, Chen Tingjing heard them discussing the posthumous title, and immediately the veins on his forehead burst, wanting to pick up a tree branch as a ruler and beat the palms of these two guys.
How could they discuss their own posthumous titles while they were still alive! You two are only this big! It's too unlucky!
And how could a clan prince have the title "Zhongwu"?! The posthumous titles of the Great Qing clan follow the emperor's posthumous titles!! "Zhongwu" is a minister's title!!
Seeing Chen Tingjing raise his hand, Yinzhi reflexively pulled Yinreng and ran: "Run! Master Chen is angry!"
Yinreng, with his mind blank, followed Yinzhi and ran: "Ow!"
Seeing the two big princes holding hands and running away, Chen Tingjing was stunned for a moment and couldn't help but laugh while holding his legs.
He turned to Cao Yin and Nalan Xingde, who had mixed in with the civil officials, and smiled: "How are they still the same as when they were young?"
Cao Yin smiled: "The Crown Prince said this is called a conditioned reflex. Did Master Chen beat the First Prince and the Crown Prince's palms when they were young?"
Master Chen recalled the situation when he was teaching the princes.

"The Emperor did give us the power to punish the princes. The teachers didn't dare to use it; if they did, the Emperor would actually be angry. Once, I was so angry that I hit the First Prince's palm. The Emperor wanted to hit me with a board."
Chen Tingjing remembered himself at that time, although it was only a few years ago, it felt like a lifetime ago.

"The Crown Prince and the First Prince threw themselves on me and argued with the Emperor. Later, the Emperor truly agreed that we could discipline the princes. However, we still rarely hit the princes' palms, wanting the study companions to do it instead. But the First Prince was upright and said if you want to hit, hit him, why hit innocent people."

After Master Chen finished recalling, he laughed: "It seems I was indeed the one who hit the First Prince's palms the most. But I never hit the Crown Prince's palms. The Crown Prince always took the initiative to share the burden for the First Prince."
It was when the Crown Prince and the First Prince were arguing with the Emperor at the Changchun Garden that the Emperor was so angry that he chased them with a leather whip.
It was estimated that the only one who would really hit the Crown Prince was the Emperor.
The two princes were chased by the Emperor, jumping up and down, and finally climbed a tree, making faces at the Emperor on the tree, making the Emperor so angry that he wanted to cut down the tree.
Chen Tingjing stood up from the stool where he had been beaten, smoothed the wrinkles of his clothes, and looked up at the two princes trying to anger the Emperor to death.
The Emperor threw the whip away and told him, beat them, beat them hard from now on, and he would never stop him again.
At that time, he really wanted to laugh out loud, and it took him a long time to hold it back.
Chapter 32 [V] (38)
He rubbed his face and said awkwardly, "I actually got scared by what the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi said."
Celing stammered, "I-Is- Is it even possible not to be scared?"
Cao Yin stretched lazily, "You'll get used to it. Our Crown Prince has already started thinking about what things will be like when society develops to a point where it no longer needs an emperor."

Nalan Xingde also had a look of calm familiarity, "The sages of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods had the social ideal of the Great Unity of the World. His Royal Highness the Crown Prince is also a sage; it is completely natural for him to see a more distant future and prepare for it."
Fiyanggu: "Normal?"
Celing stammered, "N-Normal?"
Yanxu sighed, "The more we get along with His Royal Highness the Crown Prince, the more unfathomable he feels."
Cao Yin said, "You should be happy. To be able to follow such a Crown Prince means that history books will surely have a prominent and vibrant chapter about us."
Nalan Xingde nodded.
The others looked at one another, and then smiled in unison.
"Ziqing's words are very true."
At this moment, there was a dazzling light in the eyes of all the young men.
Yinzhen (Yinreng) came once again to the side of the monument.
Perhaps influenced by Yinreng taking the lead, herdsmen and Qing soldiers continuously came over to bow before the monument.
Now, with the freezing cold and tight supplies, there were no offerings. But a simple bow perhaps could also comfort those who were innocently slaughtered in this massacre.
The stone tablets inscribed with the names of the victims had also been built a little less than half. The final glory of the Dzungar princes and nobles was all written upon them.
"Come, have a cup of wine to warm your body." Yinzhi poured a cup of wine for Yinreng. "This is wine brewed from highland barley; you can't drink this anywhere else."
Yinzeng said, "With our status, highland barley wine is something we can drink anytime we want. It's just that you stopped liking to drink it after returning to the capital."
Yinzhi laughed, "Don't expose me like that."
Not only did the two brothers drink, but they also set up a small coal stove and sat in front of the monument eating a small hot pot.
This memorial service could truly be called raving over a grave.

However, the two brothers set out an extra small plate, placed some dishes on it, and lit a stick of incense, as if they were eating hot pot together with the unjustly deceased souls who died tragically here—which could also be considered offerings.
Yinzhi said, "You come here every day; do you have some trouble on your mind?"
Yinreng bit on his chopsticks and said, "What trouble?"
Yinzhi said, "Knowing your personality, you're probably pondering those strange troubles of conscience and reality, the future and the present, all over again."
Yinreng wore a depressed expression. He really had been guessed correctly by his eldest brother.
Yinzhi said, "It's been so long, and you still haven't figured it out?"
Yinreng said dully, "Figured it out?"
Yinzhi filled Yinreng's cup with wine and said, "Figured out what? Tell your Eldest Brother about it? Let Eldest Brother mock you a bit."
Yinreng gave Yinzhi a sidelong glance and downed the wine in his cup in one gulp: "I've figured it out. In this era, events like this human purgatory right now are inevitable."
Yinzhi said, "And then?"
Yinreng stared at the empty wine cup in his hand and said, "What I want to protect are only the people of the Great Qing."
Yinzhi gave Yinreng a blank look: "What nonsense are you talking about?"
Yinreng said, "For this, turning other places into purgatory is also..."

Yinreng paused for a long time before softly continuing, "For this, even if I turn other places into purgatory and make the lives of ordinary commoners in other countries worse, I will stop at nothing."
If someone in this world is bound to suffer, if the beautiful wish of peaceful coexistence and common development is impossible to achieve in this era, then Yinreng can only abandon his conscience.

Yinzhi gave Yinreng a deep, evaluating look, reached out, and lightly flicked Yinreng's forehead: "What do you want to do next? It's fine, tell me. No matter how many wondrous and extraordinary traits you have, your brother won't be surprised."

The corners of Yinreng's mouth twitched as he said, "Three years from now, Europe will suffer a once-in-a-century great cold disaster. I want to weaken the European nations as much as possible during this cold disaster."
Yinzhi said, "You had the Great Qing purchase food from other countries early on—aside from foreseeing their continuous wars, did you also foresee the great cold disaster a few years later?"
Yinreng nodded.
Right here and right now, only the two of them were eating hot pot; no one else could hear them speak. Therefore, Yinreng confessed.

Yinzhi said, "As for foreseeing the climate, don't tell anyone about this besides me, including Khan Father. Although Khan Father is good to you right now, you are growing stronger while Khan Father is growing older. Coupled with too many people around him speaking ill of you, you must keep your guard up. Leave the matter of the great cold disaster to me; I will find an excuse to go to my fief and handle this well for you. You've been worried about this for so long just for this?"
Yinreng was silent for a long time, then nodded again.
Although utilizing the European great cold disaster was a strategy he had determined early on, he hadn't decided to what extent he would push it.

Encountering a once-in-a-century catastrophe, Europe would be just like the land of China in history: "Behind the vermilion gates of the rich, meat and wine go to waste; while out on the road lie the frozen bones of the poor."
Those who starved and froze to death would forever only be European commoners.
If he made a big fuss over grain supplies, the more severely the national strength of European countries was weakened, the more commoners would die.

Louis XIV turning from the Sun King into a figure universally reviled by the French people, leading to the subsequent French Revolution, had its roots in the severe humanitarian disaster that occurred during the great cold disaster.
Yinreng tossed and turned many times, asking himself: do I really have to go this far?
Perhaps the Great Qing only needed to do its own part well and govern its own country without doing anything extra.
But the tragedy of the Dzungars sounded the alarm for Yinreng.
As the connection between the Great Qing and the world grew increasingly close, the temptation that the Great Qing held for other countries also grew stronger.
Even if he didn't compete with other countries for supremacy, other countries would still use various methods to harass and weaken the Great Qing.
The Dzungars were just the beginning; afterwards, the Great Qing would face even more malicious hands from the shadows.

Therefore, the Great Qing cannot be wearied by constant reactions; it must take the initiative to strike and leave those countries with no time to reach out with malicious hands against the Great Qing.
For this, even if he is reviled for centuries, it is worth it.
