198. Two Chapters Combined [V]
The Ili River Valley was finally covered by heavy snow.
Far away in the capital, Kangxi looked at the frozen river surface of the capital and let out a deep sigh.

At this moment, the roads entering Dzungaria had already been sealed off by heavy snow. Baocheng was determined to stay in the Ili River Valley to finish building the city before leaving, making it impossible for him to return this year.
Clearly, pacifying the Dzungar rebellion was a great joyous event, yet Kangxi could not feel happy.
Looking at Fuquan and Changning, who had been summoned back by his imperial edict, he felt even less happy.
Kangxi asked his older and younger brothers very earnestly: "You led so many men of the Eight Banners to pacify the Dzungar rebellion—was the role you played just to eat My provisions for nothing?"
Fuquan and Changning: "..." They dared not answer.

Kangxi said: "Even if you didn't fight, just waving flags and shouting encouragement for the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi would have been considered putting in some effort. Now all your effort went into dawdling on the march? By the time the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi wiped out the Dzungar state, you hadn't even entered the borders of Dzungaria yet."
Fuquan: "..." Actually, the Eight Banners army still played a huge role in the decisive battle against Galdan; we were the main force!
Changning: "..." This subject entered the borders of Dzungaria—I had already stepped into Dzungaria's territory! I was only persuaded to turn back by His Royal Highness the Crown Prince!

Kangxi asked his older and younger brothers very earnestly: "We are all Khan Father's children, and we all received the teachings of the Grand Empress Dowager. Why are the two of you so different from Me? I just wanted a pair of siblings who could become my left and right arms—is it really that hard? I truly envy the Crown Prince. Look at Prince Zhi, look at the little Imperial Princes, look at My eldest daughter, Princess Chunxi. The Crown Prince's siblings can all assist the Crown Prince, but what about My brothers?"
Fuquan: "..." Emperor, the children you gave birth to are outrageously formidable. Since Changning and I won't do, please look for Khan Father.
Changning: "..." Chunxi is my daughter, but how dare I talk back right now?

Kangxi continued to sigh: "You look at the emperors of past dynasties—they all harbored suspicions toward their brothers. How good I was to you, every day hoping you would establish merits and achieve accomplishments, and giving you how many opportunities to do so? And how good the Crown Prince was to you. The Crown Prince helped you formulate strategies and drew detailed maps for you; all you had to do was follow the Crown Prince's orders to easily gain tremendous military achievements."

Kangxi took a deep breath and roared: "And the result?! You failed Me, and you failed the Crown Prince! Fuquan! Changning! As the commanders of the Eight Banners, you couldn't even control your own troops! The Crown Prince told you to strictly execute his orders, yet you worried about this and that, refusing to severely punish those who violated orders! The Crown Prince's orders are My imperial edicts—I said that long ago! Those who disobeyed the imperial edict—shouldn't you have beheaded them?!"

"If one head wasn't enough, you should have beheaded two, ten, a hundred! I wouldn't feel a shred of heartache even if all the heads of the Eight Banners generals were chopped off!" Kangxi angrily pointed to the west, "My Baocheng couldn't rely on you. He led the Imperial Guard and joined up with Prince Zhi's central route army, yet he was still able to fight all the way to Dzungaria and wipe out the entire clan of the Dzungar princes! My Baocheng took the Imperial Guard merely to supervise the battle; originally, he was only supposed to supervise from the safest rear! You forced My Baocheng, the Crown Prince of the Great Qing, onto the most dangerous battlefield! This matter—I will absolutely not let it go!"

Fuquan and Changning slid from their chairs to the ground, prostrating themselves to plead for mercy: "May the Emperor calm his wrath! This subject is guilty! This subject pleads guilty! Please, Emperor, do not fly into a great rage and harm your health!"

Kangxi paced back and forth: "I shouldn't fly into a great rage? Can I not fly into a great rage? My Crown Prince is still suffering in the ice and snow of the Northwest—how do you expect Me not to fly into a great rage!"
Fuquan gritted his teeth and said, "Emperor, this time the Eight Banners generals openly defied the Crown Prince's orders. Their Banner Masters can be replaced!"
Changning glanced at Fuquan, never expecting that his honest older brother would actually say such words.
After thinking about it, he also kowtowed and said, "The Eight Banners each serve their own masters, recognizing only their Banner Masters and not the Emperor. They must be reorganized!"
Kangxi glanced at them: "Before, when I wanted to abolish the Eight Banners, the two of you were strongly opposed."

Fuquan smiled bitterly: "Times have changed. Now the Great Qing has no internal troubles or external threats, so there's no need to worry about the Eight Banners stirring up trouble. Furthermore, this subject still believes that directly abolishing the Eight Banners is inadvisable; it should be done gradually."

Changning said, "Right, right, right, Emperor. Let's first strip away the titles of the Banner Masters and take all the Eight Banners into Your Majesty's hands, and then slowly reform them afterwards."
Kangxi said, "Take all the Eight Banners into My hands? Then how will the Banner Masters collect the tributes from the bannermen?"
Fuquan and Changning froze.
After thinking about it, they said, "Like the former Ming—let the imperial clan kings only collect taxes and not manage affairs?"
Kangxi said, "The two of you should go back and reflect behind closed doors first."
Fuquan and Changning were stripped of their Prince of the First Rank hats, both becoming Princes of the Second Rank (Commandery Princes), and were temporarily placed under house arrest.
Kangxi sat in his chair, pondering the matter of the Eight Banners.
Allowing the imperial relatives to continue enjoying the tributes of the banner people while staying out of political affairs was indeed one way.
This was equivalent to Kangxi and the imperial relatives each taking a step back—guaranteeing their glory and wealth while preventing them from threatening his power.
But Kangxi did not want to do this.
He didn't even want to take a single step back.

Doing this had major drawbacks. If the banner people still had to offer tributes to them, they could not completely become subjects belonging solely to the Emperor. The training of the banner soldiers would also be affected.
Moreover, the former Ming's practice of raising "Zhu" (the imperial clan) dragged down the national treasury of the former Ming.
With the former Ming as a cautionary tale, was he supposed to make the same mistake again and let an increasingly bloated imperial clan drag down the national treasury of the Great Qing as well?
What they seemed to want was the tribute of the banner people, but in reality, it was still the Great Qing treasury bleeding; the Great Qing was the one supporting them.

As early as the Han dynasty, there was the Edict of Grace (Tui'en Ling). Passing down grace generation after generation, distant imperial relatives would find their own livelihoods—the capable ones becoming officials and generals, the incapable ones farming or doing business. It wasn't as if the Han dynasty supported them forever.
Only the former Ming was so bizarre. Why should the Great Qing learn from the former Ming?
That Zhu Yuanzhang, because he started as a beggar, harbored delusions that once he became emperor, all his descendants would be able to enjoy blessings; as for us, Aisin Gioro...
Raising troops with thirteen suits of armor, our background was still a bit better than Zhu Yuanzhang's... right? Kangxi touched his chin and nodded.
That's right, our Aisin Gioro family has a better background than Zhu Yuanzhang; we cannot be as stingy and petty as Zhu Yuanzhang.
"We must let those red-girdles and yellow-girdles seek their own livelihoods." Kangxi muttered to himself, and then let out a deep sigh.
He really didn't want to talk to himself.
If the Crown Prince were here, how wonderful it would be for the father and son to discuss this together. When will the Crown Prince return?
Imagining how, if he abolished the Eight Banners before the Crown Prince returned, the Crown Prince would come back all huffy, tearful, and tugging at his sleeve, Kangxi couldn't help but smile.
Forget it; with the Crown Prince not by his side and no one to clean up the mess for him, he had better take it slowly.
He would start by abolishing the titles of a few Banner Masters and take it step by step.

"It's cold here, but once there's enough charcoal fire, it's actually better to live through than in the capital," Yinzhi leaned against a deer hunted from the snow and said cheerfully, "That wind in the capital—it blows so hard my face hurts."
Yinreng said, "Your face hurts? Rub sheep-fat snow cream on your face."
Yinzhi sneered: "I wouldn't smear those sissified things on myself."

Yinreng said, "It's just to protect your skin, how is that sissified? Are women the only ones allowed to protect their skin, while men aren't? There's no such logic. If your face gets injured, not only is it unsightly, but it also gets in the way. Getting injured on the battlefield is a meritorious honor, but getting injured because you refuse to apply skincare sheep-fat and wind-proof wax in dry, cold weather—Eldest Brother, watch out for becoming the laughingstock among your younger brothers."
Yinzhi gave Yinreng a blank look: "You've got a lot to say. Alright, alright, I'll apply it—I'll apply it as soon as I finish eating."

Yinzhi's grilling skills were top-notch, and Yinreng's seasoning skills were top-notch. With the two of them working together, even though the wild venison was stringy, it made Jieshu, Yanxu, Fiyanggu, Cao Yin, and the others crave it more and more.

After getting along for a long time, people unfamiliar with Yinreng and Yinzhi discovered that the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi were exceptionally unconcerned with formalities in private. Just like now, with the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi grilling the meat, their only job was to eat.

At first they hadn't dared, but later, after being led to act a bit uninhibitedly by Oelnde, Cao Yin, and Nalan Xingde, they grew bolder and bolder in freeloading meals, and even started chatting wildly with the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi.
Jieshu was the oldest and found it a bit hard to blend in with this group of young people. Holding a piece of venison, he ate it leisurely off to the side, listening to the young men chat.

While marveling that these young people were all proficient in both civil and martial arts and possessed extraordinary talent—in the future... no, they were already the pillars of the country—Jieshu also felt regretful that his own son wasn't among them.
Once he returned to the capital, he would definitely think of a way to have Cuntai accept the Crown Prince's teachings.
With his military exploits this time, asking the Emperor for the position of an Imperial Prince's study companion was something the Emperor would surely grant.
When His Royal Highness the Crown Prince was earnestly teaching his younger brothers, Cuntai would also be able to catch a bit of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince's teachings along the way.
After their bellies were full, Yinzhi and Yinreng went for a walk outside as usual.
Seeing Yinreng frown, Yinzhi said helplessly, "Baocheng, what are you worrying about this time?"
Yinreng said with worry, "I'm worried that Khan Father might, in a momentary fit of extreme rage, abolish the Eight Banners."
Yinzhi said indifferently, "Abolish them then."
Yinreng said, "What if the Eight Banners rebel?"

Yinzhi said, "Khan Father holds the Upper Three Banners in his hands; the Plain Red Banner belongs to Jieshu and won't rebel; the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner—their Banner Masters right now are the two of us..."

Yinzhi clapped his fist into his palm: "Oh, that's right. The Banner Masters of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner are nominally the two of us. Then why didn't the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner listen to us this time?"

Yinreng was speechless: "Did you only just realize this problem now? Although the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner nominally revere us as their masters, in order to weaken the Banner Masters, the ones who actually command the Eight Banners are the Commanders of each Banner. We don't have the authority to command and mobilize the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner; we can only collect tributes from the bannermen of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner."

Yinzhi said, "I remember Khan Father previously changed the Commanders of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner. The commanders of both banners should be people trusted by Khan Father. How could they possibly disobey?"

Yinreng said, "They weren't in the central route army; they had to listen to Prince Yu and Prince Gong. But once they return to the capital, they certainly won't rebel alongside the other Eight Banners."

Yinzhi said, "Then what are you worried about? Even if the Eight Banners rebel, now that Khan Father doesn't have to worry about Russia and Dzungaria, he has the capability to suppress the rebellion."

Yinreng sighed: "What I'm worried about is that Khan Father won't just dissolve the Eight Banners; he might also completely eliminate the generous treatment of the bannermen and imperial relatives, no longer supporting the bannermen and imperial relatives. The bannermen are one thing, but the imperial relatives..."

Yinzhi interrupted, "Cancel it if he wants to cancel it. You don't need to make me an Iron-cap Prince in the future either; at most, extend it by one generation to take care of your nephew. As for grandsons and great-grandsons after that, if they have ability, they can earn a princely title themselves; if they have no ability, they can honestly be wealthy commoners. If they can't even hold onto their wealth, they deserve to die."
Yinreng was amused by Yinzhi: "You're carefree, Eldest Brother, but the other imperial relatives aren't the same."

Yinzhi rolled his eyes: "That's a matter for Khan Father to consider. No matter what he wants to do, the two of us are trapped in Ili by heavy snow—can we grow a pair of wings and fly back to help him?"
Yinzhi cupped his hands in a salute toward the direction of the capital: "Khan Father, be careful. If you go too far, you must hold on until your sons return to save you!"
Yinzhi put down his hands: "Alright, I've already done what I could do. You hurry up too."

The corners of Yinreng's mouth twitched, but he also followed Yinzhi's example and cupped his hands in salute: "Khan Father, please don't mess things up. If you're going to mess things up, wait until your sons return and can help you clean up the mess before you do. Your son begs you."
Yinzhi patted Yinreng's shoulder: "Now the two of us have done everything within our power. You don't have to worry anymore, right?"
Yinreng: "……Mm."
Thanks to Eldest Brother, he also played the role of a filial son for once.
Perhaps the distant cupped-hand pleas of Yinzhi and Yinreng worked, for Kangxi did not mess things up this time by stripping the Eight Banners down to nothing all at once.
He merely stripped the Banner Masters of their banners, bringing them uniformly under his own name, eliminating the distinction between the Upper Three Banners and the Lower Five Banners.
The people of the Upper Three Banners were somewhat dissatisfied. But the people of the Lower Five Banners were numerous, suppressing the dissatisfied voices of the Upper Three Banners.

Kangxi executed a brilliant shift of contradictions, transferring the conflict between bannermen/imperial relatives and the Emperor into a conflict between the Upper Three Banners and the Lower Five Banners.
At Kangxi's command, Yinzhi (Yinzhi / Third Prince) fanned the flames in the newspapers.

One day he said that the Upper Three Banners looked down on the Lower Five Banners, thinking the Lower Five Banners were unworthy of belonging to the Emperor alongside them; the next day he said the Lower Five Banners were spouting nonsense, claiming the Upper Three Banners only had good luck and weren't their equals in terms of merit.
This war of words grew increasingly fierce, eventually evolving into: are the Han Banners unworthy of directly belonging to the Emperor as well?
The Han Banners: ?

The Eight Banners were originally a single entity, subdivided under banners into Manchu Captaincies, Han Captaincies, Mongol Captaincies, and Bondservant Captaincies. The Han Banners and Mongol Banners were originally also governed by imperial clan banner masters.
In order to weaken the power of the banner masters, the Emperor had the Han Banners and Mongol Banners separated out to be managed independently.
For instance, the Han Banners were originally managed by Tong Yangxing and Shi Tingzhu; they could be considered half-banner-masters of the Han Banners.

Afterwards, the Emperor further centralized military power, reclaiming the Han Banners from Tong Yangxing and Shi Tingzhu to be directly managed by the Emperor, and the Mongol Eight Banners were treated the same way.

In original history, Kangxi chose a woman of the Shi family as a consort for the Crown Prince precisely because the Shi family had once been considered half-banner-masters of the Han Banners. Even though their power had been curtailed, their influence within the Han Banners remained extremely strong, which could promote Manchu-Han harmony.
This "Manchu-Han harmony" did not refer to bannermen and ordinary commoners, but rather to the Han Banners and the Manchu court.
The demographic of the Han Banners was too special, situated in the cracks between bannermen and Han civilians, serving as a buffer zone between the Manchu court and the common people.

Therefore, if the Han Banners turned their hearts toward the Manchu court, it could actually alleviate some of the conflict between bannermen and Han commoners. Because ignorant commoners heard the word "Han" in "Han Banners" and assumed they were similar to themselves.
However, in this era, since Kangxi had abolished the Queue Order, there was no need to deliberately win over the Han Banners.

Therefore, the Han Banners and Mongol Banners originally belonged directly to the Emperor. The military power in the Emperor's hands was not limited to just the Upper Three Banners of the Manchu Banners. How could anyone say the Han Banners were just now coming under the Emperor's name?
However, the combat performance of the Han Banners and Mongol Banners this time was also nothing special.
They felt deeply aggrieved in their hearts.
If the Crown Prince had bypassed Prince Yu and Prince Gong to give orders directly to them, they certainly would have followed the Crown Prince.
But since the Crown Prince did not give them direct orders, they had no choice but to listen to Prince Yu and Prince Gong.

It wasn't that their combat effectiveness was inferior to the New Army in the central route army; that didn't mean their loyalty was inferior to the New Army either. Moreover, as for combat effectiveness, they weren't necessarily going to lose to the Imperial Guard, right? The Imperial Guard was just a bunch of showy facades; the reason they were able to achieve great merits this time was entirely thanks to the Crown Prince's cultivation.
The commanders of the Han Banners and Mongol Banners went to drink with the commanders of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner.
Gathering together, the commanders poured out their complaints.
It wasn't that they weren't loyal to the Crown Prince and the Emperor; it was that the Crown Prince didn't give them the chance!
As they complained, they began to mutually attack and blame one another.
"Why should the Crown Prince give you a chance? Because you got lost?"

"We in the Han Banners were in unfamiliar territory and didn't know the way—wasn't that normal?! Look at you instead—the Crown Prince said you could only use artillery to duel and weren't allowed to advance for hand-to-hand combat, yet how fast you ran!"
"Everyone else ran, so could we not run? Prince Yu didn't stop them either!"

"Sigh, we of the Mongol Eight Banners have it the worst. We didn't get lost, nor did we charge into hand-to-hand combat, and His Royal Highness the Crown Prince didn't take us with him either. Are those people of the Khalkha Mongols any closer to us than the Mongol Eight Banners?"

The Mongolian Eight Banners are Mongolian *zuoling* (captaincies) within the Eight Banners military system, not armies led by princes of the Mongolian grasslands. The armies led by Mongolian princes are known as "Mongolian Leagues and Banners."

Therefore, subsequently, the Mongols did not consider the Mongolian Eight Banners to be Mongolians, but rather viewed them as Manchus. Most of them also considered themselves Manchus, and only a small number returned to Mongolia. However, those Mongolian Eight Banners individuals who wanted to return to the Mongolian Leagues and Banners were discriminated against by them for a long time, being called "barbarians."

The Mongolian Eight Banners relied on the Qing court for their livelihood; the Mongolian Leagues and Banners did not want them, and the Crown Prince did not trust them. All these Mongolian Eight Banners men felt immensely aggrieved.

"Perhaps the Crown Prince doesn't distrust us; it's just that we belong to the left and right wings of the army. He has to give face to other imperial princes, especially Prince Yu and Prince Gong, and is unwilling to arbitrarily strip Prince Yu and Prince Gong of their military power, so he could only leave with the Imperial Guard," said a Manchu commander who had contact with the Crown Prince. "The Crown Prince is famously benevolent and righteous; he wouldn't cause internal conflict among the Banner armies at the critical moment of fighting Dzungaria."
The other commanders nodded one after another. This also made a lot of sense.
"What a pity! If only we could have followed the Crown Prince and left. The New Army aside, as for the Imperial Guard, what the hell are they!"
"And what the hell is the Mongolian Plain Red Banner led by Prince Kang!"
The commanders drank together again, feeling extremely depressed.
Such a good military merit had just vanished like that, and their positions as commanders might not even be secure anymore.
The commander of the Plain Blue Banner didn't even dare to return to the military camp.

The nominal banner master of the Plain Blue Banner right now was none other than the current Crown Prince. He had listened to Prince Gong Changning, taken the map given by the Crown Prince, and gone out on a huge tour following Changning, without reaping a single shred of merit.
They then gritted their teeth and followed Changning to chase after Dzungaria, only to be intercepted halfway—the Crown Prince had actually already wiped out the Dzungaria state.
The officers and soldiers of the Plain Blue Banner: "???"
The officers and soldiers of the Plain Blue Banner, who had a tradition of rebellion, were furious and wanted to revolt against that useless Prince Gong.
We of the Plain Blue Banner should naturally take orders from our banner master; by what right do you, Prince Gong, manage us? And you're so useless!
To hell with the Imperial Guard and the Central Route Army! To hell with the Plain Red Banner! We of the Plain Blue Banner are the Crown Prince's personal guard!

Fearing that the Plain Blue Banner would truly rebel, the commander hurriedly pacified the soldiers, telling them that if they rebelled, the Crown Prince's opponents might use their rebellion as an excuse; by then, the Crown Prince would be deposed, and they themselves would be finished. Only then did he barely manage to suppress the rebellion of the Plain Blue Banner.
The commander of the Bordered White Banner patted the shoulder of the commander of the Plain Blue Banner.

The grand banner master of the Bordered White Banner was the Prince Zhi. Yet Prince Zhi had always been with the New Army, only training them a few times in the capital. They were all adopted sons and stepsons, sharing the same hard lot as companions in misfortune.
"If only Prince Zhi were willing to come and be our commander, I would be willing to hold the banner for Prince Zhi."
"And then just casually follow Prince Zhi to pick up a few state-destroying merits?"
"Sigh."...
Listening to the reports from his spies, Kangxi laughed so hard he couldn't straighten his back.
Of course Kangxi would send people to spy on the commanders gathering to drink, having their words and actions recorded.

Hearing their resentful words, especially the complaints from the commanders of the Mongolian Eight Banners, the Plain Blue Banner, and the Bordered White Banner, Kangxi almost laughed tears out of his eyes.

"Baocheng and Baoqing are indeed unkind. They are the banner masters of the Plain Blue Banner and the Bordered White Banner; how could they just leave their banners aside and ignore them?" Kangxi wiped away his tears of laughter and said, "So what if they don't give face to Prince Yu and Prince Gong? They wouldn't mind. Baocheng is just too stubborn."
After he finished laughing, Kangxi sighed.
The more he gave to the Crown Prince, the more scrupulously the Crown Prince adhered to his duties, preferring to cause trouble for himself rather than overstep even slightly.

His Crown Prince had too high a sense of morality and was far too thorough in his thoughts. Even though everyone said how perfect the Crown Prince was, in Kangxi's eyes, he was still that child who needed his protection.
He would always remember those eight characters: "Extreme brilliance brings injury; deep affection is not long-lived."
Kangxi believed that the curse of the dragon vein had already been eliminated, but these eight characters had become his new heart-ache.
Kangxi regarded these eight characters as a new curse upon the Crown Prince.
Yet he did not know how to lift this curse for the Crown Prince.
"I must be more active and pluck out more thorns for the Crown Prince." Kangxi picked up the newly compiled draft of the *History of Ming* from his desk.
He and the Hongwu Emperor shared an increasing resonance.

Once upon a time, Kangxi sneered at the foolishness of the Hongwu Emperor in plucking out thorns. Jade cannot be made into a vessel without cutting and polishing; if one is to be an emperor and cannot even handle some small thorns, what kind of emperor are they?
Now, he just wanted to be a bit more "reckless" and do a bit more.
If in the future he departed for the Eternal Sky, leaving only the Crown Prince alone, even with brothers to assist, it would not be as easy as "two emperors" dealing with troubles together.

Furthermore, the Crown Prince was a good child who tended to overthink and would rather exhaust his own mind and energy than easily do anything to harm others. If only the Crown Prince were left behind, Kangxi truly wouldn't be at ease.
Perhaps the Hongwu Emperor was not worried about Zhu Biao's ability, but simply didn't want Zhu Biao's hands to be stained with the blood of founding officials and leave behind a bad reputation.
The tyrant role would be played by the father; the child only needed to be a wise monarch praised through the ages.
Kangxi stretched lazily, put down the *History of Ming*, and took out the letters previously sent by the Crown Prince from a wooden box.
He had already read them once. But no matter how many times he read them, it sounded as if a little Crown Prince was nagging right beside his ear, full of complaints.

What others saw was the Crown Prince plotting strategies with a master hand, possessing a wisdom bordering on the demonic, and commanding the Imperial Guard with composed ease to enter the war and destroy the state.
In the eyes of the old father, the Crown Prince was extremely irritable and kept cursing away.
Tucked inside the Crown Prince's letters were also letters from Prince Zhi.

Prince Zhi was much more blunt, directly cursing Prince Yu and Prince Gong as good-for-nothings. If he were the Crown Prince, he definitely would have stripped them of their military command right then and there. Whoever dared to object would be beheaded—chop down however many came, and hack them to pieces along with the Dzungar army.
Rebels deserved to be beheaded; their deaths were not a pity.
Kangxi's mouth twitched, and he couldn't help but support his forehead.
Fortunately, the Grand Prince was not the legitimate heir. If the Grand Prince succeeded to the throne, the next generation of the Great Qing would probably perish.
"However, rebels really do need to be beheaded somewhat," Kangxi muttered.

Before sealing the imperial seal in the first lunar month, Kangxi issued his final imperial edict: all those Eight Banners generals who disobeyed the Crown Prince's orders during the Battle of Hui River and were the first to order a halt to the shooting were to be executed.
The 30th year of Kangxi thus opened amidst bloodshed.

199. Two Chapters Merged into One [V]
Since the 30th year of Kangxi, the Great Qing no longer suffered from major internal troubles, and the people of the Great Qing truly entered a period of peace and rehabilitation.
While the commoners of the Great Qing were settled and secure, the officialdom of the Great Qing was a scene of bloodshed and terror.
Kangxi raised his butcher's knife, and some said the moat around Beijing City turned red.
However, when Kangxi raised his butcher's knife this time, the commoners all applauded in satisfaction.

Yinzhi had long since publicized this war in the newspapers. The Eight Banners troops dragged their feet and refused to go to the battlefield, while the Prince Direct made a desperate stand with the new army, suffering nearly fifty percent casualties; the Crown Prince led the imperial guards to supervise the battle, and seeing the corruption of the Eight Banners, he personally led the imperial guards to directly participate in the fighting.

While the Eight Banners were still dragging their feet, the Crown Prince and the Prince Direct had already led the bloodless imperial guards and the new army—which had suffered over fifty percent losses—all the way to the capital of Dzungaria, executing all the rebellious princes and nobles.
"Among the imperial guards, basically all of them are sons of high-ranking officials."

"Not to mention the imperial guards, the new army is the same. The new army consists entirely of student soldiers from Peking University. Only the children of the Eight Banners and high-ranking officials in the court can enter. Though called soldiers, they are actually being trained to become military officers."
"My brother-in-law's official master's grandson studies right there. They say they're called reserve officers; you serve as a private first, and after learning how to fight, you become a general."
"Isn't this just like Emperor Wu of Han's Yulin Guards in the operas?"
"Right, exactly that. All pampered young masters from official families."
"Oh my goodness, the little young masters from official families are blocking the enemy at the front, while the real army doesn't go to the battlefield? Why does this feel so strange to me?"
"Hmph, there's definitely deep water running here."
"Didn't the newspaper say it? Those who understand understand, and for those who don't, it's no use explaining..."
The commoners engaged in all sorts of conspiracy theories, and the rumors became increasingly exaggerated.

When these events from the capital spread to the provinces, they had morphed into: Prince Direct fighting a bloody battle while the Eight Banners army looked on coldly; the Crown Prince holding the Emperor's imperial insignia yet unable to command the army, so he led the imperial guards to directly enter the fray and ultimately won.

After the Crown Prince and Prince Direct achieved victory, the Eight Banners army, fearing the Crown Prince and Prince Direct would report them to the Emperor, actually attempted to intercept and assassinate the Crown Prince and Prince Direct. Upon learning of this, the Emperor flew into a rage, decapitating the rebellious Eight Banners generals until heads rolled like melons and blood flowed like rivers.
Pity the Crown Prince and Prince Direct, still trapped in the bitter ice and snow of the Northwest, their lives and deaths unknown.
The Emperor was so furious he vomited blood.
Changtai had just stepped ashore when he received this dreadful news, and he almost vomited blood as well.

He ditched the main force, switched through several poor, exhausted steeds, and rushed back to the capital in a panic. Without even changing his clothes and with stubble all over his face, he charged straight into the imperial palace.
Kangxi was currently keeping the Empress Dowager company eating mutton hotpot, and even invited him to join.
Changtai: "?"
Changtai: "Your Majesty, this minister heard that you fell ill..."
Kangxi: "Huh?"
Changtai: "Your Majesty, this minister heard that the Crown Prince and Prince Direct were intercepted and assassinated by the rebellious Eight Banners army, and you were angered into falling ill..."
Kangxi: "..."
The monarch and subject stared at each other in blank dismay.
The Empress Dowager, who could now understand spoken Chinese, panicked: "What? What happened to the Crown Prince and the Grand Elder Brother?"

Kangxi was silent for a moment, roughly figuring out what had happened, and comforted the Empress Dowager: "Nothing's wrong. Right now they're so happy in Yili they've forgotten to return home; they're probably eating roast lamb, warming themselves by the fire, and admiring the snow as we speak."
Changtai was bewildered: "So happy they forgot to return home?"
Kangxi said with disdain: "Look at that messy state you're in... Go change your clothes in the side room, have them give you a set of My clothes to wear, and then come back to drink with Me."
Changtai was led away by a eunuch with a head full of confusion. After using hot water to scrub and clean his body and face, he changed into Kangxi's casual imperial robe.
Kangxi simply gifted this set of clothes to Changtai.

Receiving the emperor's old clothes as a reward was an honor for a minister. However, Changtai's home was already piled with a room full of imperial bestowals, and neither he nor Kangxi regarded this as much of a reward—there wasn't even a verbal decree.
When Changtai emerged in his new clothes, the eunuch had already set out a bowl and chopsticks for him.
The Empress Dowager smiled cheerfully and invited Changtai to sit and eat meat, saying this was mutton sent by Chunxi, and the meat was exceptionally delicious.

Looking at Changtai's exhausted face, Kangxi burst out laughing: "Frightened out of your wits, weren't you? Just use your head—how could the Crown Prince and Prince Direct possibly be driven to such a state? My control over the Eight Banners isn't that weak either."
Changtai heaved a sigh of relief: "As soon as this minister stepped ashore and heard the news, I was truly terrified, and only thought of rushing into the palace to protect Your Majesty."

Changtai paused, giving a bitter smile: "Now that I've calmed down, this minister realizes that rushing alone into the capital in a panic wouldn't have helped me protect Your Majesty at all, right? How on earth did I abandon all my troops at the shore and come without even a single guard?"

Kangxi laughed heartily: "If you wanted to protect the Emperor, you should have at least brought a few more guards; then you might have sneaked into the palace to rescue Me. Coming all by yourself, isn't that just throwing your life away?"

Changtai mocked himself: "Perhaps this minister could have entered the palace to wait upon Your Majesty, getting trapped together in one place to wait for the Crown Prince and Prince Direct to rescue us?"

Kangxi laughed heartily once again, picking up a large chunk of meat with his chopsticks and placing it in Changtai's bowl: "Shut up and eat your meat. How did I end up with a foolish brother-in-law like you?"
The Empress Dowager was also amused.

She finally understood: Sertetu was like this, and so was Changtai. The entire family of the Empress Renxiao was extremely interesting, no wonder they could produce a child as fine as the Crown Prince.
Changtai wasn't reserved either; since the Emperor told him to hurry up and eat meat, he buried his head and stuffed himself.
The Empress Dowager was advanced in years; after eating a few bites of meat, she went back to rest.
Kangxi continued eating meat with Changtai and opened two bottles of grape wine. The two didn't even use cups, drinking straight from the bottle necks.
Only then did Kangxi tell Changtai what had happened, detail by detail.
Changtai sighed: "Even if the losses weren't half, losing twenty percent is still enough to break one's heart."

The smile on Kangxi's face faded: "Yeah. Those were all generals trained by Me. Never mind twenty percent, even if it were ten percent or five percent, My heart... hurts so much it's unbearable. Just look at the Inner City; nearly half of the households have hung up white mourning cloth."
That was why Kangxi had gone on such a killing spree this time without much opposition in the court.

In the central route army led by Prince Direct Yinzhi, which was primarily composed of the new army, the vast majority indeed consisted of nobles and officials' sons. They were also the first batch of outstanding students from the university, and would be the ones capable of leading troops into battle in the future.

"I originally had Zhao Liangdong join the army on the campaign, but he is old and fell ill, so he returned to the capital to offer Me strategies. When he learned that the central army suffered a twenty-percent loss due to the Eight Banners' advance being delayed, his illness worsened even further. After you've had a good day of rest, go pay him a visit," Kangxi said with a gloomy expression.
Changtai's expression also turned gloomy: "Yes."
The first batch of university students was very small, and the outstanding students were taught hand-in-hand by Zhao Liangdong and Jieshu.
To Zhao Liangdong, these people were not just students, but true disciples.
Master and disciple—their bond was practically no different from that of father and son.

Upon hearing that many of his outstanding disciples had died on the battlefield, and not from brutal combat, but merely from the exhausting warfare caused by Eight Banners delays and rescue forces arriving endlessly late, Zhao Liangdong wrote memorial after memorial even on his sickbed to impeach Fucquan and Changning.
When the executions took place, Zhao Liangdong had his family support him to the execution grounds, continuously crying and roaring "They deserve to die, they all deserve to die."
Kangxi personally came to the execution grounds to oversee it, watching head after head fall, batch after batch, his mood completely calm.
Only when he heard and saw Zhao Liangdong's grief-stricken, indignant wails did Kangxi's heart ache profoundly, and he couldn't help shedding tears.

Not just Zhao Liangdong. Because of his advanced age—he should have gone to Hohhot to stand by with Jieshu, but was persuaded by the Crown Prince to return home to enjoy his old age—Yala also fell gravely ill.
As a clan prince, Yala had actually walked to the most radical side of calling for the abolition of the Eight Banners and the establishment of a new system, all for the sake of these students.

There were also many officials who had once taught and lectured at Peking University, all raising their arms to shout that these people deserved their fate, that they should have died even more miserably and in even greater numbers.
Fucquan and Changning shut their doors and refused to step out, worried sick.
Everywhere they went outside now they were cursed; where was there any joy in winning a battle?

Knowing that the Crown Prince and Prince Direct were not only fine but also having a great time, Changtai offered an objective evaluation: "The Prince of Yu and the Prince of Gong actually didn't make major mistakes this time. If one insists on finding fault, it was merely incompetence."
Kangxi sneered: "Incompetence in a general is the greatest mistake of all."
In his heart, Changtai thought so too. But out loud, he still put in a good word for the Prince of Yu and the Prince of Gong, pacifying the depression Kangxi felt over having useless brothers.

"Having passed through this baptism of fire, the remaining new army can directly enter the Eight Banners troops to serve as generals upon their return," Changtai said. "Only generals who have been through cruel warfare can forge real talent. To Your Majesty, this can't really be considered a bad thing."

Kangxi gave Changtai an eye-roll: "I know. It's just that My heart still aches. Speaking of which, you've trained quite a few people in your navy, haven't you? Lend them to Me first; I've beheaded too many people and can't find enough qualified replacements for the time being. Have your men fill the positions first, and we can swap them back when Baocheng and the Grand Elder Brother return."

Changtai said: "The navy belongs to the Great Qing and to Your Majesty. Since Your Majesty wants men, this minister has a list here. They are all fine talents tempered through fierce combat, and it's time for them to gain some experience ashore."

Kangxi nodded: "Well said, it is indeed time for rotation and seasoning. When the men of the new army return, I'll hand them over to you first so you can take them abroad to gain some experience. A general of Mine cannot do without knowing the situation overseas."
At this, Kangxi felt a bit stifled: "I want to go too. What do you say if I make the Crown Prince act as regent while I go abroad for a stroll?"
Changtai's mouth twitched: "The Crown Prince will hug Your Majesty's thighs and howl in tears."

Kangxi sighed: "When the Crown Prince visited foreign countries, he once said that the world is so vast and he wants to see it. I want to see it too! How about I become the Retired Emperor and let the Crown Prince ascend the throne ahead of time?"
Changtai was speechless.
How on earth dared he respond to such words? Yet since Kangxi was chatting privately with him, he was forced to answer.

"If Your Majesty wishes to become the Retired Emperor, this minister will also resign from the post of Navy General and serve as Your Majesty's guard, traveling everywhere together," Changtai said calmly. "With the title of Navy General weighing on me, this minister wouldn't feel at ease abroad either. By then, Your Majesty and I could disguise ourselves as wealthy merchants or as pirates; it would surely be immensely interesting."
The moment Kangxi uttered the words about becoming the Retired Emperor, he knew he had made a slip of the tongue.
Although he harbored such thoughts in his heart, he shouldn't voice them to others, much less say them to Changtai.

Although Changtai was his close confidant, he was also the Crown Prince's uncle. The topic of early abdication was far too sensitive; if word leaked, it would put Changtai in a terribly awkward position.
Just as he was wondering what to say to steer the conversation away, he didn't expect Changtai to take it up so naturally.
Kangxi chuckled: "You've been running around outside for so long and you still don't feel at ease?"

Changtai said: "This minister has too many soldiers and officers behind me, as well as the Great Qing. Every step I take requires pondering for a long time, so of course I'm not at ease. This minister doesn't dare leave the ships for long, nor do those foreigners dare let this minister stay ashore for long."
Kangxi sighed: "That must indeed be quite hard. But by then, if you don't help the Crown Prince continue managing the navy, the Crown Prince will have no end of trouble."

Changtai said: "By now, there are already many formidable young generals in my navy, and many formidable young men in the new army as well. These people can all replace my position. Having toiled for so many years—since Your Majesty gets to rest, this minister should rest too."
Kangxi laughed despite himself: "You're just lazy. Fine, if I become the Retired Emperor, you'll tag along with Me to go on micro-visits among the populace."
Changtai smiled: "It's a deal."

Having struck this unreliable agreement after their drinking session, Changtai stayed in the palace for a day instead of returning to his estate. He rode out of the city to find the troops he had left behind, whipped them back into shape, and only then returned to the capital with a squad of men he could recommend to Kangxi.

These men were planted by Kangxi within the Eight Banners to straighten out the Eight Banners' military discipline. Upon seeing new officials arrive to take office, the hanging hearts of the Eight Banners troops finally settled down temporarily.
At least this showed that the Eight Banners wouldn't be abolished immediately; they still had rations and pay coming.
After Changtai returned to the capital, the city grew even more peaceful.
Everyone knew that Changtai was the Emperor's Wei Qing, while the Crown Prince was no foolish Crown Prince of Li.
With the Emperor having Changtai garrisoned in the capital to serve as his personal guard, the restless ambitions of the nobles could only be temporarily suppressed.

In an utterly swaggering manner, Kangxi had Changtai put on imperial guard attire and paraded him through the streets every single day. He practically wrote "If you've got the guts, rebel against Me" on the folding fan he was still waving in the dead of the dog days of summer, making the nobles dissatisfied with Kangxi itch with frustration.
Word traveled too fast; not only did Changtai rush to the capital at breakneck speed, but Dulidu also dragged his ailing body to the capital to protect the Emperor.
Kangxi was both touched and exasperated.

Pointing at Changtai's nose, he chided: "First you gallop solo into the capital to protect the Emperor, and right after that Master Du comes leaning on a crutch to protect the Emperor! Why is everyone coming to protect Me completely useless! You lot aren't protecting Me, you're trying to be buried alive with Me!"
Changtai simply acted like he didn't hear it, playing mute and refusing to answer.

Seeing that Kangxi was in high spirits and still capable of joking and cursing, Dulidu finally relaxed: "If it truly came to that, this minister would have no choice but to be buried as a sacrifice along with the Emperor."

"Alright, alright, don't say such inauspicious things. Since you've come to the capital, properly let the imperial physicians examine you," Kangxi said, looking at Dulidu's physical condition with extreme worry. "The Crown Prince is fine; he and the Prince Direct pacified Dzungaria, turning it into the Ili Prefecture of the Great Qing. Right now they are building Yining City in the Ili River Valley, and in the future the Great Qing will station troops in Yining City."
Dulidu stroked his chest: "As long as he's fine, as long as he's fine."
Kangxi appeased him: "Master Du can rest for the time being. Once your health improves, you can also go take a look at the university. The university is getting livelier by the day now."
Dulidu smiled: "Very well, this minister will certainly go take a look."
After seeing Dulidu off, Chen Tingjing came to request an audience.
The news he brought Kangxi this time was still about rumors, but this time the gossip wasn't standing on the Crown Prince's side.

"It wasn't foreign mercenaries who slaughtered Dzungaria, but the Crown Prince? The Crown Prince slaughtered Dzungarian princes and commoners, and then shifted the blame onto foreign mercenaries?" Kangxi was laughed to anger. "Never mind the fact that when the Crown Prince went to Hangzhou and beheaded a batch of rebels, he cried and vomited because he was too kind to the point of stupidity; let's just ask—even if they were slaughtered, so what? Didn't the Dzungarian princes deserve to be slaughtered? This is a military achievement, why would the Crown Prince ever need to push it onto others?"
Hearing Kangxi say this, Chen Tingjing let out a breath of relief.
When he first heard this rumor, he too had worried whether the Qing army had engaged in another city massacre.

It wasn't that Chen Tingjing doubted the Crown Prince. He knew the Crown Prince wouldn't do such a thing. But the Crown Prince might only have been supervising the battle, whereas he believed the Prince Direct was certainly capable of doing something like that.
The Crown Prince wouldn't want a massacre, but after the Prince Direct committed one and shifted the blame onto foreign mercenaries, the Crown Prince might have been deceived as well.
Now the Emperor's words calmed him down. Given the Crown Prince's intelligence, he would never let the Prince Direct run wild, nor would he be hoodwinked by the Prince Direct.
Back in the day when the Crown Prince led them overseas, the Prince Direct caused trouble everywhere, yet the Crown Prince was always able to rein him in.

Chen Tingjing said: "The Dzungarian princes deserved their deaths. These rumors mostly start from commoners trying to smear the Crown Prince and Prince Direct. This minister requests to lead a team of officials to assist the Crown Prince. The newly built Yining City needs officials, and the Crown Prince also needs the pens of scholars like us to clear his name."
Kangxi had been angry, but upon hearing Chen Tingjing's words, his anger melted into helplessness.

He first had Chen Tingjing sit down, and only then spoke in a coaxing tone: "Chen Ziduan, you've just returned from Russia, and I was just preparing to employ you heavily—why are you running off again? Is there someone chasing you out of this capital? Other officials rack their brains trying to come to the capital, yet you always want to go out, and it's not even to serve as a major regional governor."
Kangxi genuinely didn't want Chen Tingjing running outside anymore. The imperial court was short of capable officials who could both get things done and suit his preferences.

Kangxi had already reserved the position of Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion for Chen Tingjing. Once Chen Tingjing rotated through the Six Ministries, he could enter the Wenyuan Pavilion and become what folks colloquially called "Prime Minister," and one of Kangxi's closest confidants.
But ever since Chen Tingjing followed the Crown Prince on that overseas voyage, he simply couldn't sit still anymore.

Chen Tingjing didn't suspect the Crown Prince. He knew the Crown Prince couldn't do such a thing. But the Crown Prince might only have been overseeing the battle, while he believed Prince Zhi was definitely capable of doing something like that.

The Crown Prince wouldn't wish for a city massacre, but after massacring a city, Prince Zhi might have shifted the blame onto foreign mercenaries, and the Crown Prince might have been deceived as well.
Now the Emperor's words calmed him down. With the Crown Prince's wisdom, he could neither let Prince Zhi run amok nor be hoodwinked by him.
Thinking back to how the Crown Prince led them out to sea back then and Prince Zhi stirred up trouble everywhere, the Crown Prince was still able to keep Prince Zhi in check.

Chen Tingjing said, "The Dzungar nobles deserved their deaths; the rumors mostly start from commoners to smear the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi. I request to lead a team of officials to go and assist the Crown Prince. The newly built Yining city needs officials, and the Crown Prince also needs the writing brushes of us literati to clear the Crown Prince's name."

"Well, since you've put it this way, how can We stop you?" Kangxi said. "If you want to go to Ili, then go. Take more things for the Crown Prince. With his temperament, he certainly won't come back until he straightens out the affairs in Ili and establishes the city's foundation. You must advise him often not to exhaust himself. As for the affairs of the Eight Banners and foreign matters, We will worry about them."
Chen Tingjing bowed excitedly: "This subject obeys the imperial decree!"

Watching Chen Tingjing stride away full of enthusiasm, Kangxi massaged his brow: "Changtai, among the Han people, there is no shortage of talented and ambitious individuals like Chen Tingjing who care nothing for power and wealth and only think of the country and the people. I truly envy the Han people."

Changtai said with a straight face, "Your Majesty, you are mistaken there. Where are there any Han or Manchu people now? We are all people of the Great Qing, and all subjects of Your Majesty. Besides, even if Your Majesty insists on dividing Manchu and Han, am I, your subject, really inferior to Chen Tingjing?"

Kangxi laughed despite himself: "Fine, fine, fine, you are right, there are no Han or Manchu people, only Great Qing people. Also, what are you getting jealous for? You are my brother-in-law; aren't you ashamed to say you don't care about glory and wealth?"
Changtai said, "Your subject is Your Majesty's brother-in-law, so why can't I care nothing for glory and wealth? One's background doesn't affect one's character."
Kangxi fell silent.
Although Changtai's character was indeed quite good, listening to Changtai boast about himself like that, why did Kangxi's hands suddenly itch so much?
Winter is monotonous, and the days of warmth and blooming flowers arrived very quickly in Yinzhen's perception.
Before he had rested enough, the ice and snow in the Ili River Valley had already melted.
The artisans abducted from Dzungaria were all summoned by the Qing army, and the herdsmen and merchants within the Dzungar Khanate also spontaneously gathered at the foundation site of Yining City.
Yinzhen drew a circle on the ground, felt that the soil had thawed, and planted a flag of the Great Qing. The construction of Yining City resumed in full swing.
The heavy snow had melted, and Yinzhen sent another letter saying that he would be staying a little longer.

Just how long is "a little longer" ... Very soon, right away, Imperial Father, please don't urge me. Anyway, nothing much will happen in the capital right now; just watch your son ship gold back to you.

With coal mines, gold mines, and another iron mine discovered, Yinzhen led the Qing army in happily building workshops. With both tools and money, once the caravans arrived, supplies were in no short supply at all.
When Chen Tingjing led a group of literati to arrive, he found that the Crown Prince and the Direct Prince had each gained a full circle of fat, while they themselves looked terribly haggard.
Yinzhen was surprised: "Why has Master Chen come?"

Chen Tingjing said, "The Emperor sent this subject to deliver supplies and artisans to His Royal Highness the Crown Prince and His Royal Highness the Direct Prince. The newly built Yining City lacks officials, so this subject has come to help His Royal Highness the Crown Prince."
He glanced at the Direct Prince.
Yinzhi: "Master Chen, what are you looking at me for?"
Obviously, Yinzhi still held a fair amount of respect for Chen Tingjing; otherwise, this would have directly become a "What are you staring at?"
Yinzhen said, "Master Chen, if you have anything to say, just say it."
He put Yinzhi in a headlock: "I've already pinned Eldest Brother down, so you can rest easy."
Yinzhi: "?"
Chen Tingjing didn't know whether to laugh or cry: "Good. Will the Direct Prince please not get excited."
Yinzhi: "I can't even move, and you still expect me to get excited?"

Enduring a smile, Chen Tingjing said, "There are rumors in the capital that His Royal Highness the Crown Prince slaughtered a city. This subject has brought many scholars skilled in writing to help His Royal Highness clear his name."
Yinzhi bounded up, almost knocking Yinzhen over: "Who?! Who is spreading rumors?! This Prince will slice him a thousand times!!"

"Alright, alright, a thousand slices, anyway he's not here with us. We can ask Imperial Father when we return to the capital." Yinzhen hung onto Yinzhi, stopping him from running amok. "It's no use losing your temper at Master Chen now; hasn't Master Chen come to help clear our names?"
Yinzhi calmed down: "Master Chen, this Prince will take you to see something. Once you see it, you'll understand."
Chen Tingjing said, "Very well."
Seething with anger, Yinzhi led the scholars who had come from the capital to the monument.
The monument here had already been turned into a memorial wall. Once the herdsmen learned what the Qing army was building, they spontaneously came to help during the winter.
Some Dzungar nobles ran out from their hiding places, wailed tearfully before the monument, and also voluntarily joined the ranks of carving names.

Following Yinzhen's example, the people here did not burn paper money or offer sacrifices; instead, they placed some wreaths in front of the memorial wall, stood silently in mourning before it for a while, and then went back to their other tasks.
Chen Tingjing and the officials and literati who came from the capital all fell silent.

They carefully read the poems written by Cao Yin, the *ci* poetry written by Nalan Xingde, and the article personally written by His Royal Highness the Crown Prince detailing the cause and effect. Their eyes turned scarlet, with bloodshot veins spreading across them.

After a long while, Chen Tingjing finally calmed down, his voice trembling as he said, "This subject understands. This subject will definitely make the events of Yining City known throughout the realm!"
