Yinreng looked at himself in the mirror; his face was puffy, and there were dark circles under his eyes. Rather than being haggard, he looked more like a walking corpse.
He stroked his chest.
It felt like there was a sensation, but it wasn't real.
He didn't know if this was his dream, or if his five senses were dull because he didn't belong to this body.
After a few contacts, he shared the memories of his first life with the version of himself in this world.
He couldn't share the memories of his second and third lives, but he could recount them.
When he fell asleep in the real world, he would wake up in this world. In a vast spiritual world, he would chat with this deposed Crown Prince who looked exactly like his past self.
Come to think of it, his appearance in his third life was much more handsome than in his first life or the deposed Crown Prince before him.
After all, his Imperial Father in the third life was handsome.
The deposed Crown Prince had first been manic and restless, but now he had finally accepted reality and had simply shut himself off.
The deposed Crown Prince had locked himself deep within the spiritual world and let him out.
"Do whatever you want; it won't be any worse than the predetermined future anyway."
Hearing the deposed Crown Prince’s "broken jar" attitude, Yinreng felt like punching someone.
"Hey, hey! This is your own future! Don't just hand it over to a stranger like that!"
The deposed Crown Prince shut himself off and kicked Yinreng to the surface of the body’s consciousness.
The deposed Crown Prince, who was clearly more arrogant than the current Yinreng, indicated that he was sad, tired, and wanted to shut himself off for a while, so he could do as he pleased.
Yinreng was full of question marks.
Is this thing the former me, or the Eldest Brother during his bratty phase!
A disgusted sneer from the deposed Crown Prince came from deep within his consciousness.

Clearly, even though Yinreng told him that he and the Eldest Brother were both pathetic wretches, and that in the third life Yinreng and Yinzhi were super good brothers, the deposed Crown Prince’s hatred for the Eldest Prince was still deep in his marrow, and he wished he could drag him down to die together.
However, haven't I and the Eldest Brother already died together now? Deep in his consciousness, the deposed Crown Prince, who had somehow returned to his youth in soul form, hugged his knees tightly.
September, 47th year of Kangxi: Deposition of Crown Prince Yinreng;
October, 47th year of Kangxi: Stripping of Prince Yinsi’s title;
Time arrived at November, 47th year of Kangxi.

Yinreng knew that in this month, the Third Prince Yinzhi would accuse the Eldest Prince Yinzhi of using sorcery to curse the Crown Prince Yinreng, leading to Yinzhi being stripped of his title and placed under house arrest. Later, there would be a series of "you act, I act" dramas regarding the restoration of the Crown Prince.
Because Yinreng had suddenly taken over his body, the deposed Crown Prince had actually performed a convincing act of being mentally unstable.
Kangxi, in his great shock, actually felt a bit of sympathy for the deposed Crown Prince.

In the past few days, the imperial physicians said the deposed Crown Prince’s mental state had improved significantly. Kangxi, after all, still had some lingering feelings for the child he had raised, so he came to visit him personally.
Before Kangxi came to visit the deposed Crown Prince, Yinreng called for hot water and a young eunuch to help him groom himself and put on new, clean clothes.

Although he was under house arrest, Kangxi had specifically instructed that his life should not be neglected. Even though almost all the people serving him had been killed, the unfamiliar attendants would still serve him diligently.
When Kangxi saw Yinreng, Yinreng was reading, his eyes clear and his expression calm.
Seeing Kangxi arrive, Yinreng first scrutinized this Kangxi, who looked almost exactly like the Imperial Father from his first life.
He suspected that perhaps he hadn't traveled through time again, but had truly been reborn.
If he changed his current fate, would he be changing his true fate?
Ha, then would he still travel to the third life and meet the current Imperial Father, Eldest Brother, and younger brothers?
Yinreng was amused by his own imagination.
Finding joy in suffering was something he was very used to; even if it wasn't funny, he could still laugh.
But his smile gave Kangxi a fright.
Kangxi took a few steps back, hesitating: "Second Prince, are you alright?"
Hearing Kangxi call him "Second Prince," Yinreng was slightly stunned and sighed: "Imperial Father, how many years has it been since you called your son Baocheng?"
Kangxi was stunned, not expecting Yinreng to say this.

Yinreng stretched out his hands: "Your son has something to say to you in private, which others cannot hear. If you are worried, you can have someone tie my hands first. As for the cangue, a wooden cangue..."
Yinreng paused and smiled bitterly: "A wooden cangue is a torture device for serious criminals. Your son knows he is unfilial, but the wooden cangue is truly too torturous."
Kangxi was silent for a long time before saying: "I was just too angry."
Yinreng shook his head: "Imperial Father, your son knows you don't trust me right now, but I truly have very important words to say to you in private."
Kangxi was silent for another long moment before saying: "I am not yet so cowardly as that."
He waved his hand, and those around him retreated.
Kangxi said: "Speak."
Yinreng sighed, knowing there were still secret guards present.

He had to repeat: "My words can only be known by you, Imperial Father. If others know, they will surely be... by you, Imperial Father, in the future. I do not want to implicate the innocent. Please bind my hands."
Kangxi said unquestioningly: "Speak!"

Yinreng knew that this Kangxi would not listen to him, so he could only apologize by glancing at the location of the secret guards and said: "Imperial Father, although I am Yinreng, I am not the Yinreng you know. You should have read Buddhist scriptures; in the great thousand worlds and small thousand worlds, perhaps there is a world where history and the current situation are the same as they are now."
There were many legendary and supernatural novels in ancient times that described people accidentally entering another world and encountering their own selves.
Yinreng knew that Kangxi occasionally read such novels to pass the time and should know about these things.
Originally, Yinreng didn't want to tell Kangxi these things, but the deposed Crown Prince told him to explain it clearly to Kangxi.
Based on the deposed Crown Prince’s understanding of Kangxi, Kangxi would want to know about the future and wouldn't kill Yinreng immediately.
As for whether he believed it or not, that was another matter.

Everything the deposed crown prince possessed came from Kangxi. Once Kangxi stripped him of everything, the deposed prince could no longer influence Kangxi or the Qing Dynasty. If Yinreng wanted to make a change, he had to find another way, speak the truth, and see if Kangxi himself was willing to change these tragedies.
As for whether Kangxi would kill the deposed prince later out of fear.
Well, the deposed prince had already given up on himself; it didn't matter anymore.

After Kangxi reinstated the crown prince, he immediately purged the prince’s faction and rewarded the other princes and the officials who stood against the prince. Perhaps in his first life, Yinreng still held a glimmer of hope, but now he understood that after the first deposition, he had lost all hope of ascending the throne.
Better to die, better to die; it’s better than being ground down by a dull knife for over a decade.
Yinreng sensed the deposed prince's desire for death and agreed.
He himself felt that if it were him, having to go through another deposition and imprisonment, it would be better to die quickly.
When a person is not afraid of death, they are not afraid of much else. So, Yinreng painfully confessed his origins.
Regardless of whether Kangxi believed him or not.
Kangxi’s eyelids twitched; he knew why Yinreng had asked the others to leave.
Yinreng said, "My experience is very complex. First of all, I went through two reinstatements and two depositions..."
Kangxi said, "Stop. Someone, tie up the Second Prince's hands."
In the end, Kangxi believed Yinreng’s words. After binding Yinreng’s hands and feet, he let the secret guards leave and stand guard at the door.
"Continue," Kangxi said calmly. "I can see it now; you are not him. There is no malice in your eyes like his."
How could Kangxi not recognize the son he raised himself?
He had been suspicious earlier only because this person also carried a very familiar feeling, very much like his son.
Like his... former crown prince.
With his hands and feet tied, Yinreng felt somewhat uncomfortable.
He leaned back against the chair before he began to recount his story again.
He skipped over the two reinstatements and two depositions, starting first with the date of Kangxi’s death.
In the eleventh month of the sixty-first year of Kangxi, Kangxi passed away at the Changchun Garden, and his successor was the Fourth Prince, Yinzhen.
Hearing the date of his own death, Kangxi’s mouth twitched: "You really dare to say anything..."
Which brat did I raise?! Isn't this a bit too arrogant!!

Yinreng first hooked Kangxi’s interest with what he wanted to know most. Seeing Kangxi’s expression, which looked angry but was actually relieved, he said, "Father Emperor was the longest-reigning emperor, and your temple name was Shengzu..."
Kangxi interrupted: "What temple name?!"
Yinreng: "Shengzu..."

Kangxi interrupted again: "Shengzu is a posthumous title for ancestors; which idiot gave me the temple name Shengzu?! That fool, the Fourth? Is he not afraid that future generations will curse me for being unworthy?!"

Yinreng comforted Kangxi: "Father Emperor, it’s fine, it’s fine. The Fourth’s little fourth, the one named Hongli—wait, is Hongli not born yet? Never mind. Hongli succeeded the throne after the Fourth and gave his mother, the Niohuru clan, the posthumous title 'Sheng' as well—Empress Xiaosheng, just like Father Emperor. So, most people won't think Father Emperor’s temple name is undeserved."
Kangxi’s face turned blue and white, as if a volcano were about to erupt.
After a long while, he calmed down: "You lived that long?"
Yinreng said, "No, I followed shortly after Father Emperor passed away. I know about future events because I was reincarnated."
Yinreng then told Kangxi about his experiences in his second and third lives.

When he was reincarnated, he had no memories of his past lives, but perhaps because of the merit he earned from saving people, he regained his memories in his third reincarnation, which was also in a parallel world's Qing Dynasty.
Kangxi’s temples throbbed; he didn't know whether he should believe this strange person in front of him.
What made him even angrier was that Yinreng was bragging, saying that the Father Emperor in his third life was a very good person and very handsome.
Am I not handsome!
Kangxi’s anger almost brought him back to his explosive temper of his youth.
And Yinreng’s nagging and rambling made him dream back to the days of raising the little brat prince.
Back then, the little prince was also very noisy and chatty.
If this "Yinreng" was not lying, then Kangxi probably understood why he was fearless and so lively.
The so-called reincarnation memory was probably like reading a book. The content was remembered, but it was someone else's stuff, not something personally experienced.
The rambling guy in front of him, who seemed to have no guile, was the immature crown prince who hadn't yet reached adulthood and had been spoiled growing up.
And this guy was completely fearless!
"You... were injured and unconscious, and came to this world without knowing it?" Kangxi synthesized the information from Yinreng’s words and said, "You didn't die in the other world?"

Yinreng immediately said, "Don't curse me; I’m perfectly fine. Father Emperor rushed over from the capital, and I even complained to him that I was so badly hurt, yet he showed no worry. Father Emperor tapped my head and said that seeing I was out of danger, he was too happy to be worried, so how could there be any worry?"
Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng said gloomily: "I remembered the first life. At that time, I heard Father Emperor was seriously ill and was so scared that I brought the Third with me, riding fast to visit. When I arrived and heard Father Emperor was much better, I was overjoyed, and then I was scolded and sent back to the capital."
Kangxi: "..."
Yinreng sighed: "I remember explaining it to Father Emperor later, and Father Emperor acknowledged it too. But now Father Emperor says he has held a grudge against me for twenty years."
Kangxi: "..."

Yinreng said: "Father Emperor, I was only sixteen at the time, seventeen by lunar age, right? You raised me yourself; my only family was you. Even Songgotu, I rarely saw him back then... Never mind. I came to this world not to argue for myself. The person I want to argue with will never hear my defense. You and your son can resolve your misunderstandings yourselves. But if you’ve deposed him, just leave it at that. Don't reinstate him again."
Yinreng abruptly changed the subject to the Nine Dragons' Struggle for the Throne.

After the first deposition of the crown prince, Kangxi loathed the Eighth Prince’s faction, and there were only three people who could inherit the throne: the Third Prince Yinzhi, the Fourth Prince Yinzhen, and the Fourteenth Prince Yinzhen.

Based on his understanding of Kangxi, Yinreng analyzed: "Father Emperor’s future consideration was probably that the Fourth and the Fourteenth would act as backups for each other. Father Emperor didn't know how many more years he would live at the time, and there was a large age gap between the Fourth and the Fourteenth. If he left early, the Fourth would succeed; if the Fourth was old and lacked energy, the Fourteenth would be mature, so he would let the Fourteenth succeed."
Kangxi listened to Yinreng analyze his psychology and felt very strange: "What are you trying to say?"
Yinreng said: "No matter which of the Fourth or the Fourteenth succeeds, the other will definitely be imprisoned until death."
Kangxi said: "Are you blaming me?"

Yinreng said: "The person I want to blame can no longer hear my words. I am borrowing your son’s body to appear here, just to avoid some tragedies. I said these things just to gain your trust, so that you, the Emperor, know I am not lying to you."
Yinreng no longer addressed the Kangxi in front of him as "Father Emperor."
Kangxi sat up slightly.
Indeed, the guy in front of him, who claimed to be Yinreng from another world, was saying things that matched his deepest, most secret considerations.
He believed that perhaps this person really did come from another world.

Most emperors believed in ghosts and gods. When Yinreng confessed his identity, Kangxi didn't immediately call for someone to behead him, precisely because he had some curiosity about the supernatural.
And... who wouldn't want to know the future?
Emperors all have an adventurous spirit. Rather than rashly beheading someone, Kangxi preferred to hold such power in his own hands.
Yinreng closed his eyes to organize his thoughts before he began to say what he really wanted to say.
A hundred years after the Qing Dynasty, several hundred years after China, the things missed, the things encountered, and the things regretted.
Yinreng was actually a bit worried about whether he should let this Qing Dynasty rot; the ending was good anyway.
What if Kangxi woke up and China moved toward a constitutional monarchy?
Later, he thought of several constitutional monarchies, all of which had their own unique historical reasons, such as the emperor being a mascot. China did not have such reasons.
Even in feudal dynasties, imperial power and ministerial power were always in a tug-of-war. The monarch would never be willing to become a puppet.
Therefore, if there was to be reform, it must be a thorough reform, leaving no room for error.
Kangxi listened to the events of the Qing Dynasty two hundred years later, his face calm, even somewhat joyful.
Yinreng knew what Kangxi was happy about.

Throughout history, even if Kangxi wanted the Qing Dynasty to last forever, he knew it was impossible. What Kangxi worried about was that the Qing would not last a hundred years after the Manchus entered the pass.
Now that he knew it would far exceed a hundred years, wasn't he happy?

Yinreng was speechless: "This two-hundred-year national fortune is because foreigners helped us maintain it. Is it really good that future generations curse the Qing Dynasty whenever they mention it?"
Kangxi straightened his face and said seriously: "Of course it’s not good."
Yinreng: "...When you say it’s not good, can you please stop the corners of your mouth from curling up?"
Kangxi: "..."
Yinreng: "..."
The two looked at each other, as if playing some staring game.
Kangxi suddenly thought of the crown prince as a child. He had once played with the prince just as naively.
Kangxi put away his trance and said: "Don't worry about the affairs of this world; return the body to my son."
Yinreng felt a wave of disappointment.
He forced himself to cheer up and said: "Your son is currently self-isolating and needs to heal his heartache for a while."
Kangxi snorted: "What heartache is he healing? I didn't have heartache when I was forced to abdicate."

Yinreng said: "He only complained about it; could he really force you to abdicate? Being a crown prince for forty years is actually nothing; your pen pal Louis XIV’s crown prince didn't outlive Louis XIV either."
The soul of the deposed prince within Yinreng trembled, then silently calmed down.
Hearing Yinreng say this, Kangxi found that all his words were stuck in his throat.
"Enough," Kangxi sighed. "What do you want to fight for for him?"

Yinreng said: "Demote him to a commoner. Demote him to a commoner, give him enough money and people, and exile him overseas. Otherwise, even if he just becomes an idle clansman, he and his descendants will only end up dying miserably."
Kangxi: "Is he willing?"
Yinreng said: "He even wanted to shave his head and become a monk."
Kangxi was once again speechless.
The two sat in silence for a long time. They actually had nothing more to say.
Yinreng looked out the window, feeling that his time travel this time was completely useless.

The brotherhood couldn't be repaired, the future of the Qing Dynasty was confusing, and even his own fate couldn't necessarily be reversed—Kangxi reinstating the crown prince was just to temporarily stabilize the court situation, not because he truly wanted to reinstate him.
So even if Kangxi had made up his mind not to let the deposed prince succeed, he would use the deposed prince to the fullest before discarding him like a worn-out shoe.

After all, Kangxi was the kind of person who could use the First Prince and the deposed prince as whetstones for each other, and then let the Fourth and Fourteenth princes act as whetstones for each other.
It was just a pity for the Eighth Prince, Yinsi, who jumped in halfway and whom Kangxi hadn't anticipated. He was truly miserable.
First it was the eldest brother and himself, then the Fourth and the Fourteenth. Did he know his sons would be ground to ruin?
He knew, right?
And even if he knew, Kangxi believed that jade must be carved to become a useful object.
Yinreng was already numb to these things. What saddened him was that the now-aged Kangxi, with his waning spirit, no longer had the ambition for reform upon hearing what the Qing Dynasty would face.
The time point he arrived at was really bad. He could neither save himself nor the Qing Dynasty.
Kangxi saw the silent Yinreng and noticed his disappointment.
He felt embarrassed and angry, but didn't know how to vent it.
Vent it on this person from another world? What would be the use? Wouldn't that just be hitting his own son?

Yinreng didn't want to provoke the dissatisfaction of the Kangxi in this world. Because this Kangxi looked so much like the Father Emperor of his first life, it made him feel as if he had returned to his first life.
He forced a smile and said: "If the Emperor doesn't want to know about future events, should I tell you about my world?"
Kangxi said with a straight face: "Tell me."
He wanted to see how good the version of himself in the other world was, that he would make the crown prince of that world show such disappointment toward him.
Yinreng started from his childhood.
He omitted the dark history of pretending to be possessed by Fulin, only talking about the intimate past between him and his Father Emperor.
When Father Emperor was reviewing memorials, he would hold him in his arms while he was in swaddling clothes, coaxing him while feeling overwhelmed;
As he grew a little older, he would play with Father Emperor’s little braid, wiping his hands and grinding his teeth on Father Emperor’s dragon robe;
He and his eldest brother grew up together, making Father Emperor jump with anger, climbing trees to mock Father Emperor;

Every time Father Emperor wanted to beat him and his eldest brother, they would run to the Empress Dowager’s palace, and the Empress Dowager would rush out with her cane to beat Father Emperor back...
After finishing the childhood stories, it was time for him and his eldest brother to show their prowess.

Rushing into a mutinous barracks, leading the younger princes to attack the gates of the First Prince’s faction, going to sea together, destroying countries together, expanding the territory for the Qing Dynasty, reorganizing the Eight Banners, abolishing the queue order, and establishing universities...

The younger brothers were all very outstanding, being drafted by Father Emperor at a young age; the sisters were also very outstanding, and Princess Chunxi even made military contributions; among the officials, there were capable ones and those who wanted both father and son dead...
Abroad, there were Father Emperor and his eldest brother’s close friends, Yanxu was about to set off for Russia to marry the Empress, and the Qing navy was already famous overseas...

By the way, the Dzungars had just been destroyed by him and his eldest brother leading the Imperial Guard and the New Army; the Eight Banners army was huffing and puffing behind them, and before they even saw their shadows, the Dzungars were already destroyed, which was hilarious.
Kangxi looked at the brilliance in the eyes of the crown prince from another world and felt even more stifled in his chest.
Compared to the emperor of that world, he had to admit that his own courage was far from enough.
He had exhausted all his efforts just to keep the Qing Dynasty from collapsing; he simply didn't have the heart or ability to carry out these drastic reforms.
Perhaps he had thought about it, but the successive wars in the country and the suffering of the people had worn away his spirit.
He could only endure, hiding all his ambitions, waiting for the people of the Qing Dynasty, who had suffered so much from war, to recuperate.
Why could the emperor of the other world do it? Was it because that emperor shared power with the crown prince, letting the crown prince share his government affairs and pressure?

Kangxi remembered that he had once trusted the crown prince with power, letting him go to Jiangnan to make friends with scholars and gentry, putting all his effort into making a name for the crown prince.
He had never worried about the crown prince overstepping his bounds because the crown prince was his designated successor and would definitely become the emperor in the future.

Precisely because the crown prince would become the emperor, Kangxi had isolated the prince from a very young age, not letting him associate deeply with officials or brothers, worrying that these people would affect the crown prince’s judgment.
As a result, the crown prince became violent and even wanted to actively touch his power.
He understood the version of himself in the other world.
When he was young, he also had the courage to share power with the crown prince.
He didn't understand the version of himself in the other world.

How could he let the crown prince and his brothers get along so well, how could he let the young princes go out to work early, and how could he bear to let his most beloved crown prince have so many thrilling experiences at such a young age.
For the first time, Kangxi felt so lost.
After he was lost, he made a move that even he didn't understand.
He personally untied Yinreng’s hands and feet and asked him: "Do you want to see the brothers of this world?"
Yinreng was slightly startled, then shook his head gently.
No need.
After all, in this world, he didn't have a close brother.
"Baocheng? What's wrong? Why are you crying? Are you having a nightmare? Baocheng, wake up!"
"Ahhhhh Father Emperor, stop shaking me! My wounds haven't healed yet!!"
Yinreng, with tears streaming down his face, suddenly smiled: "My Father Emperor and eldest brother are calling me back. It seems the me in the other world had a nightmare."
The elderly Kangxi murmured: "Going back, huh."
Only now did he begin to seriously look at this crown prince from another world with eyes free of prejudice and vigilance.
Another Baocheng. A Baocheng raised by another version of himself, surrounded by brothers and sisters he could trust.
He didn't remember what his own seventeen or eighteen-year-old Baocheng looked like, but his Baocheng’s eyes would never be so gentle.
Yinreng’s consciousness pulled away from this body bit by bit.
For some reason, he knew that after his consciousness left this time, it would never return.
Perhaps in the dark, heaven saw that he had done well in that parallel world and gave him a chance to face his nightmare.

Whether this was a dream or not, whether Yinreng admitted it or not, this Kangxi who looked exactly like the Father Emperor of his first life, and that deposed prince who looked exactly like him in his first life, were nightmares he had told himself countless times "I don't care anymore," but were still deeply buried in his heart.
Seeing the nightmare again, Yinreng finally clearly distinguished the Kangxi of his first life from his current Father Emperor.
Different, completely different.
My Father Emperor is not him.

"Baocheng..." The elderly Kangxi hesitated for a long time before saying softly, "The crown prince... must be reinstated. I need some time to buffer, to paralyze the crown prince’s faction, before I can deal with them and pave the way for the next crown prince."
Yinreng said with tears: "Yes, son knows."
The elderly Kangxi said: "Wait, wait until this matter is over, I... sigh..."

He had originally planned to confer the title of Prince on the deposed crown prince, build a mansion outside the palace, and perhaps live with him in the future to repair their father-son relationship.
But...
Yinreng’s consciousness drifted away, and the deposed crown prince returned to his body.
At this moment, the elderly Kangxi said painfully: "I will demote him to a commoner and exile him overseas."
The deposed crown prince knelt and kowtowed: "Son, I obey the decree."
The elderly Kangxi looked down at the deposed crown prince.
His own son had returned.
The elderly Kangxi looked up; he seemed to see a translucent shadow.
A young crown prince in his prime.
Yinreng breathed a sigh of relief, tears on his face, and his smile finally became bright: "Thank you, Father Emperor."
His nightmare finally dissipated.
In the Qianlong era, a scholar could win over a group of Chinese people to build a country in Nanyang. His own brothers leading troops to sea couldn't lose to a scholar.
The deposed crown prince looked up, also looking at the other version of himself.
His expression gradually cleared, and the hope in his eyes rekindled.
Over the past few days, Yinreng had told him many stories about the scenery overseas.
He wanted to leave here, break free from everything, and see a wider world.
"Ahhhhh Father Emperor, the younger brother is crying and laughing, he’s really gone crazy."
"Hey! Baoqing! Wasn't it you who said not to shake him just now..."
Yinreng opened his eyes in pain: "Stop shaking, stop shaking, the wounds are splitting, it hurts, it hurts, it hurts..."
Kangxi and Yinzhi shouted anxiously: "Imperial Physician! Imperial Physician!"

Chapter 32 [V] (39)
During his serious illness, Kangxi suddenly felt that life was much more fragile than he had imagined; a casual bout of a cold had almost cost him his life.

The Crown Prince had not yet reached adulthood and had not yet married. Although he was older and more capable than Kangxi himself had been when he ascended the throne, the Crown Prince was still a tender youth.
If he were to pass away at this moment, what would happen to the Crown Prince?
In his delirious state of severe illness, Kangxi's mind recalled what the Crown Prince had said when he voluntarily requested to lead the imperial expedition in his stead.

The Crown Prince had said that if he himself were to die while the Crown Prince remained alive, it would probably be very difficult for the Crown Prince to stabilize the situation; at the very least, a bloody struggle would be necessary to secure the throne. If the court fell into such chaos, the foreign nations eyeing the Great Qing might strike. Even if they didn't, it would implicate the common people who were just now beginning to recuperate and rest.

On the other hand, if something unexpected happened to the Crown Prince while away, as long as he, the emperor, was sitting safely on the dragon throne, it would simply be a matter of choosing another successor, and the Great Qing would not fall into chaos.
The Crown Prince's words were cold and sober, leaving Kangxi with no choice but to agree.

Man's calculations, however, cannot surpass heaven's; who could have foreseen that the Crown Prince would be safe while campaigning abroad, while he himself would suddenly fall gravely ill in the palace?
Would the Crown Prince be able to rush back in time? What would be the consequences if he couldn't?
Even if the Crown Prince rushed back in time, would he be able to pacify the chaotic situation of his own sudden demise?

At that moment, Kangxi's greatest panic was not the approach of death, but what would become of the fine child he had raised with his own hands. Now that the court's situation was unstable and foreign powers were eyeing them covetously, he could not leave the Crown Prince alone to face all of this.
After Kangxi pulled through, he still felt lingering fear.
When he was gravely ill, the Crown Princess had actually had to resort to threatening the officials with a blade just to administer his medicine.
He wasn't dead yet!

It wasn't as if the officials didn't know the prescription and precautions left behind by the Crown Prince! To suddenly raise a fuss at this time under the pretext of "not being able to take medicine of unknown origin"—what were these people plotting?
There were even those who spoke with righteous indignation, claiming they wanted to take the medicine in his place to test for poison.
The divine medicine left by the Crown Prince was not in vast supply; if they finished testing for poison with the dosage they mentioned, would there be enough medicine left for the emperor?
What if they intentionally pretended to be poisoned?
Even if they did nothing, the emperor was already unconscious; if the poison-testing took too long and delayed his treatment, what then?
Fortunately, the Crown Princess was decisive and resolute enough.

Although this Crown Princess personally chosen by the Crown Prince was not the virtuous and wise mother everyone expected, she was entirely capable of shouldering the position of the Mother of the Nation.
Kangxi closed his eyes. He had managed to pull through here with great difficulty, so how could something happen to the Crown Prince at the exact same time?
Such a coincidence forced Kangxi to ponder whether there was some grand conspiracy behind it.
Why did he fall gravely ill at the very same time that the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi met with disaster?
Or could it be that they had already begun plotting and laying out their schemes back when he caught a cold?

To get the Russians to make a move—what a vicious scheme. It could eliminate the Crown Prince, prevent the alliance between Russia and the Great Qing, and even use the Crown Prince's prestige among the common people to force the Great Qing into declaring war on Russia, destroying the hard-won peace between Russia and the Great Qing.

The Great Qing had just concluded the rebellion-suppression war in Zhungaria. If they were to declare war on Russia once again, setting aside victory or defeat, just the mobilization of grain and provisions alone could drag down the flourishing national strength of the Great Qing and temporarily halt all of the empire's current reforms that were already yielding results.
Clever, they were all very clever.
Talents, they were absolute talents.
And these clever talents all stood on the opposite side of him, the Crown Prince, and the Great Qing. Truly wonderful! Simply wonderful!

"Khan Ama, if you are tired, please rest for a while," Princess Chunxi said only after Kangxi had calmed down. "Only when Khan Ama's health is restored can you exact this vengeance for the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi."

Kangxi sighed. "What Chunxi says is true. I will rest for a while. Mr. Tang, during this period you will reside in the side hall of the Hall of Mental Cultivation and assist me in processing memorials."
Entrusted with this heavy responsibility, Tang Zhen was neither servile nor overbearing, remaining calm and composed as he said, "Your subject obeys the imperial decree."
He had now temporarily become the emperor's private counselor, secretly devising strategies and ghostwriting for the emperor.

The Hanlin scholars who were originally on rotation to serve as the emperor's secretaries were temporarily given a holiday by the emperor, who used this pretense to make it seem as though he was still seriously ill.
Princess Chunxi guarded Kangxi until he fell into a sound sleep, then walked out to rest in the small partition room.
She was currently wearing palace maid attire; with her head lowered, those unfamiliar with her would not recognize who she was.
Even the Empress Dowager and Imperial Noble Consort Tong were unaware of her entering the palace. The day she entered, she was disguised as a guard by Tseleng's side.

Princess Chunxi had hurried into the palace precisely to tell Kangxi that although she had not traveled to the capital along the same route as the Crown Prince, she had once seen the military camps of the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi from a distance.
At that time, there was no rain.

Although the malaria struck fiercely, Yinreng had been prepared long in advance, having the imperial physicians prescribe medicinal tea and herbal bath packs for Kangxi early on to prevent malaria, so the malaria was not severe.
Kangxi had only been taken suddenly ill due to the dual affliction of a cold and malaria. After taking antibiotics—a substance Kangxi had never consumed before—his recovery rate was extremely fast.

Princess Chunxi personally prepared nutritious and easily digestible food for Kangxi every day, following the list written by Yinreng. Less than five days after regaining consciousness, Kangxi was able to get out of bed and walk.

Princess Chunxi could not help but sigh with emotion, "Although your daughter is also filial, when it comes to true filial piety, perhaps all of us combined cannot match the Crown Prince's thoughtfulness. The Crown Prince is truly meticulous, considering every single thing."

After the Crown Prince set out on the expedition, Kangxi had repeatedly looked over the medical prescriptions, medicinal diets, and dietary recipes for times when Kangxi fell ill that the Crown Prince had left behind.

Seeing these sheets of paper recording trivial matters one by one, Kangxi's mind conjured the image of that son of his—who seemed to have grown up, but in reality was still very tender—biting the end of his brush and racking his brains.
He had people properly preserve all the medicine and dietary recipes written by the Crown Prince.

There were so many tales of filial children through the ages that could be praised for eternity, yet Kangxi believed those overly exaggerated deeds could not compare to these few fluttering pieces of paper.
"Why have Changtai and Tseleng not sent any news back?" Kangxi asked in a deep voice. "It has already been five days. The Crown Princess as well."
When Changtai and Tseleng departed from the capital, he had allowed the Crown Princess to take along skilled practitioners of traditional Chinese medicine from the Academy of Sciences.

The Academy of Sciences was established single-handedly by the Crown Prince, and the foreign famous physicians within it were more trustworthy under the present circumstances than the people from the Imperial Hospital.
Moreover, everyone in the capital with ulterior motives was closely watching the Imperial Hospital, while the Academy of Sciences was a place they had overlooked.
Princess Chunxi did not dare to answer.
It was impossible for the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi to rebel.
Even taking ten thousand steps back, assuming the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi truly harbored rebellious intentions, it was impossible for them to jump out at this moment.

The Crown Prince's position was currently secure; what reason did he have to rebel? Changtai and Tseleng had even brought news that the Emperor had already recovered; even if the Crown Prince had lost his mind, he should have snapped out of it by now.
Therefore, all events pointed to a single possibility. A possibility that Princess Chunxi did not dare to think about, nor dared to speak aloud.
Princess Chunxi did not know how to comfort Kangxi. But Kangxi, having recovered his mobility, had no need for her comfort.

Princess Chunxi dazedly learned that Kangxi had already sneaked out of the palace, having someone disguise themselves as him to continue deceiving the officials, while Princess Chunxi helped cover for him.
How am I supposed to cover for this?! If the officials discover this, they'll probably accuse me of treason and storm the palace to behead me!
Princess Chunxi's head ached terribly.
It felt as though she was discovering for the first time that her Khan Ama was actually this kind of person.
Pressing her forehead, Princess Chunxi murmured, "Crown Prince Dianxia must have had a very hard time."
She was certain of it!
Time returns to the day Yinreng and Yinzhi were ambushed.
Assassins suddenly leaped out from the jewelry chest; Yinreng pushed Yinzhi away and took a blade to the shoulder.
Fortunately, the gunpowder of this era did not have remote detonation and required a fuse, so the jewelry chest did not explode.
It was also fortunate that the use of firelocks in this era was not particularly convenient and their accuracy was very low; during close-quarters assassination, they were not as effective as blades.
Therefore, the assassins first used blades to wound Yinreng, and only after Yinreng and Yinzhi dodged did they start firing their firelocks indiscriminately.
It was dusk, and the light was dim. The moment Yinreng pushed Yinzhi away, he pulled out a flash grenade.
"Close your eyes!"
Following the intense flash, Yinreng dragged Yinzhi away from the jewelry chest. Because they had previously been trained by Yinreng, the guards who closed their eyes in time swarmed forward.
The assassins' eyes were temporarily blinded, leaving them to fire their guns blindly.
Yinreng was very unfortunately hit by a stray bullet.
Truly unfortunate.
Before losing consciousness, he only had time to roar: "Hold onto Da Ge! Do not let him act recklessly! If you can't hold him, tie him up!"
When Yinreng woke up again, the military doctor was cleaning his wound.
The blade wound on his shoulder was very deep, though it missed vital organs, but there was poison on the blade, requiring bloodletting;
The stray bullet had struck his leg, missing the bone but hitting a major artery, resulting in severe blood loss as well.
This era lacked the conditions for blood transfusions, so heavy blood loss could only be endured on one's own, relying on bodily functions to recover.

The most common difficulties faced in warfare were, first, wound infection, and second, massive blood loss. Yinreng had trained the military doctors in advance for both, which was why his life was able to be saved.
The wound had already been stitched, life-saving medicine administered, and sugar water and milk prepared at all times to replenish blood sugar.
Unfortunately, Yinreng did not understand the preparation ratio for normal saline, so he could only use weak saline solution indiscriminately to clean the wound.
When Yinreng regained consciousness, he asked, "Where is Da Ge?"
The Commander of the Imperial Guards said with a hoarse voice, "Per Crown Prince Dianxia's orders, he has been tied up and is on his way now."
"Di Di!"
Before the Commander of the Imperial Guards could finish speaking, Yinzhi lunged forward, wailing loudly.
Yinreng said, "Don't be noisy. I won't stay awake long, listen to me quietly."
Yinzhi gritted his teeth and choked back his tears.
"Send word to Khan Ama, say we were suddenly struck by a torrential rain and are making camp in place..."
"Do not punish the Imperial Guards for now, pacify them as much as possible to prevent turmoil..."
"Seal off this matter, do not let people know it was Russia..."
After intermittently making his arrangements, Yinreng fell into a deep sleep once more.
Yinzhi cried for a while longer before wiping away his tears, forcing himself to be as calm as possible, and carrying out things according to Yinreng's instructions.
His mind was currently a blank; aside from following orders, he was completely incapable of thinking.
Yinzhi's arm was supported by wooden splints. During the melee, he had also sustained injuries.
Although he had injured a bone, once the bone was set and healed, it would be fine—far less severe compared to Yinreng's injuries.
Afterward, when Yinzhi received the news of Kangxi's grave illness, his mind finally cleared up. Enduring his panic, he prepared for the worst and awaited news from the capital.
If Kangxi recovered from his illness, he would only need to wait for Yinreng's injuries to heal completely.
If Kangxi...
Yinzhi stroked his unhealed arm, his face full of sinister ferocity.
By the time Changtai, Tseleng, and Li Tong arrived, Yinreng was still drifting in and out of consciousness, with fluctuating body temperatures and frequent low-grade fevers.
Once the first batch of life-saving medicine was successfully made, producing the second batch became slightly easier.
Li Tong had brought a bit more life-saving medicine this time, bringing Yinreng's fever under control.

Aside from the life-saving medicine, she brought many precious medicinal herbs and treatment instruments. The joint efforts of the military doctors and the renowned physicians from the Academy of Sciences finally managed to stabilize Yinreng's condition.
Although Yinreng's waking periods each day were not long, his low-grade fever had subsided, meaning he should have crossed out of the danger zone.
With Changtai's arrival, there was finally someone capable of taking charge in Yinzhi's place.
Yinzhi let out a breath of relief, collapsed, and fell into a deep sleep for two days.
Guarding his two nephews, Changtai harbored a furious hatred in his heart.
Although he knew these people's goal was to provoke a war between the Great Qing and Russia, he still couldn't help but want to walk right into the other party's plot and take the bait.
This was a covert scheme, yet also an overt stratagem.
The covert plot was injuring the Crown Prince; the overt strategy was the reactions of the common people, the court, and even the emperor after the Crown Prince was injured or even died.

If the Crown Prince died from his severe injuries, even if everyone knew this was plotted by certain parties, the Great Qing would never agree to a marriage alliance with Russia—even if they didn't go to war—and the fires of conflict would undoubtedly reignite along the borders.
Therefore, the Crown Prince used a clumsy pretext to seal off the news, gambling that the Emperor would recover swiftly.

People in the capital surely knew the Crown Prince had been ambushed, but whether the Crown Prince was dead, injured, or completely unharmed and merely playing a staged drama together with the Emperor, they did not know.

Hence, they could not burst out with the news of the Crown Prince's ambush either; if the news of the Crown Prince being ambushed spread in the capital at this time, following the vine to find the melon would easily expose their cloven hooves. They could only sit tight and watch the changes.

The key to this game of chess lay in whether the Emperor could recover early and regain control of the situation; in whether the Crown Prince could survive and prevent the opponent's scheme from succeeding; and in... whether the father-son affection between the Emperor and the Crown Prince was truly unbreakable.
Changtai felt a wave of fortunate relief.

The Crown Prince was still superior in skill, having planted two moves in advance and winning by half a step—the medical prescriptions and diet recipes he left behind not only caused the Emperor's condition to improve rapidly and seized the initiative, but also made the Emperor firmly believe in the Crown Prince's filial piety, preventing him from easily raising suspicions.
Next, the turning point of victory or defeat rested solely upon the Crown Prince alone.
Changtai clutched his head with both hands, hiding his collapsing emotions within the shadows of his arms.
Standing at the entrance of the camp and gazing at the heavily oppressive atmosphere of the Imperial Guard encampment, Tseleng could not help but tighten his fists.

He recalled the circumstances when he temporarily parted ways with the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi. How could a Crown Prince in whom they placed such trust suddenly fall victim to vile schemes and conspiracies?

Yanshu had followed General Fiyanggu back to the capital, and it was currently unknown where he had traveled. If Yanshu learned of this matter, as a prince about to go to Russia for a marriage alliance, what should he do?
Tseleng's mind was a tangled mess.
At that moment, rapid hoofbeats sounded.
Tseleng hurried forward to check the identity of the newcomer.
The newcomer pulled off their wind-proof hood, causing Tseleng's legs to go weak as he dropped straight to his knees. "Emp—"
Kangxi yanked Tseleng up by the collar. "Where are the Crown Prince and Prince Zhi!"
Tseleng scrambled up, stumbling as he led the way in front. "Prince Zhi has already endured several sleepless nights and is currently resting. The Crown Prince is in the main tent..."
"Your Majesty?" Changtai, sitting at the entrance of the main tent, raised his head, his voice carrying an unsuppressed exhaustion and choked sob.
Kangxi looked at Changtai's haggard face and the unsheathed blade resting across Changtai's lap, his heart turning cold. "The Crown Prince..."
Changtai forced out a sliver of a smile. "The Crown Prince's injuries have been brought under control; he merely needs quiet and proper recuperation."
Injuries...
Kangxi's vision went black. Even though he had mentally prepared himself, upon hearing those two words, he still felt the world spinning.
He strode past Changtai, hurrying inward.
Li Tong was just stepping out carrying a basin of hot water.
Seeing Kangxi arrive, she bowed slightly in greeting, then walked out of the main tent, leaving the space entirely to the father and son of the imperial family.
Kangxi looked toward the Crown Prince on the bed.
The Crown Prince had just woken up, leaning against the pillows and taking small bites of fruit to dilute the bitter taste of medicine in his mouth.
Seeing someone enter, Yinreng raised his head and watched Kangxi's expression transform from blankness to joy.
This scene involuntarily reminded him of his first lifetime.
Thus, Yinreng aggrievedly said, "Khan Ama, your son has been injured, and it's bad enough that you show no worry on your face—how can you even look happy?"
Kangxi's footsteps paused for a fraction of a second, then he strode forward quickly. Raising his hand high, he let it fall softly, tapping Yinreng on the head.
"Baocheng, you've scared me to death," Kangxi said, forcing down his emotions.

Yinreng finished off the fruit in two or three bites, wiped his sleeve across Kangxi's clothes, and complained, "Khan Ama scared your son to death, too. Half-conscious, when I heard Khan Ama was gravely ill, I was so frightened I nearly stopped breathing... Ow."
"You are not allowed to speak such inauspicious words!" Kangxi said severely.

Rubbing his head, Yinreng muttered, "Fine. Why did Khan Ama come here? Aren't you still recovering from illness? How strange, I clearly prepared medicine to prevent and treat malaria for Khan Ama, so how could Khan Ama still catch malaria..."
Whispering softly to himself, exhaustion washed over him. "Ama, your son is sleepy and needs to sleep a little longer. I'll wake up soon... Don't worry..."
Kangxi gathered Yinreng into his embrace, gently patting his back. "Sleep, sleep, Ama is here with you, protecting you. The moment you wake up, you'll see Ama."
"Mn..." Unable to hold on any longer, Yinreng fell asleep once more.

Although heavy blood loss tended to cause fatigue, it wouldn't make someone as lethargic as Yinreng. Yinreng guessed to himself that his current sleepiness, much like his over-exhaustion of the brain previously, was the self-regulatory and repair function of his body's "golden finger."
He believed that a benevolent person like himself was naturally blessed by heaven and would certainly come to no harm.
It was just... a little bit sleepy.
Moreover, in his dreams, he would return to his first lifetime, as if crossing over once more.
Yet this crossing didn't feel like a true transmigration; rather, it felt like being inside the body of another self, watching a tragedy unfold all over again as a bystander.
The 47th year of Kangxi: the first deposition of the Crown Prince.
At this node, the tragedy was extreme beyond measure.
If it were before the first deposition, he might still have been able to reverse the tragedy; if it were after the second deposition, he could have just laid flat and waited for death.
But between the first deposition and the second reinstatement... it was truly tormenting.
