Yinreng looked at himself in the mirror: his face was swollen, dark circles hung beneath his eyes, and rather than looking haggard, he looked more like a walking corpse.
He stroked his chest.
There seemed to be a sensation, but the sensation was not quite real.
He didn't know if this was a dream, or if it was because he didn't belong in this body, making his five senses somewhat dull.
After several contacts, he had shared his memories of his first lifetime with his self in this world.
The memories of his second and third lifetimes could not be shared, but he could recount them.

Whenever he fell asleep in the real world, he would wake up in this world—within an expansive spiritual world, chatting with this deposed crown prince whose appearance was identical to his own past self.
Come to think of it, the appearance of his third lifetime was much more handsome than his first lifetime and the deposed crown prince before him.
Who asked the Khan Ama of his third lifetime to be so handsome?
The deposed crown prince had initially been manic and frantic, but now he had finally accepted reality—he had simply shut himself in.
The deposed crown prince had locked himself away in the depths of his spiritual world and let him out.
"Do whatever you want; anyway, it won't turn out worse than the established future."
Hearing the deposed crown prince's self-abandoning, reckless words, Yinreng felt a sudden urge to hit someone.
"Hey, hey! This is your own future! Don't just hand it over to a stranger like that, okay!"
The deposed crown prince, having shut himself away, kicked Yinreng straight to the surface of the body's consciousness.

The deposed crown prince—who was clearly far more arrogant than the current Yinreng—expressed that Milord was heartbroken, Milord was tired, Milord wanted to shut himself away for a bit, do as you please.
Yinreng was filled with question marks.
Was this thing his former self, or was it Da Ge during his bear-child phase?!
From the depths of consciousness came the deposed crown prince's disgusted, derisive snort.

Clearly, even though Yinreng had told him that both he and Lao Da were pitiable creatures, and that in the third lifetime Yinreng and Yinzhi were super good brothers, the deposed crown prince's hatred for the First Prince was still deep-rooted to the marrow, making him wish he could drag the other guy down to perish together.

However, aren't Lao Da and I practically perishing together now, too? Deep within his consciousness, for some reason returned to his youthful soul form, the deposed crown prince tightly hugged his knees.
September of the 47th year of Kangxi: Yinreng is deposed as Crown Prince;
October of the 47th year of Kangxi: Yinsi is stripped of his title of Beile;
Time reached November of the 47th year of Kangxi.

Yinreng knew that in this month, the Third Prince, Yinzhi, would accuse the First Prince, Yinzhi, of using black magic and spells to curse the Crown Prince, Yinreng, resulting in Yinzhi being stripped of his peerage and placed under house arrest. And afterward came the series of theatrical performances where everyone played their roles of "you act for me and I act for you" to restore him to his position.
Because Yinreng had suddenly possessed his body, the deposed crown prince genuinely put on a performance resembling schizophrenia.
Terrified, Kangxi actually felt a bit more sympathy toward the deposed crown prince.

In recent days, the imperial physicians said the deposed crown prince's mental state had improved a lot. Kangxi ultimately still held some unextinguished affection for the child he had raised himself, so he came to visit him in person.
Before Kangxi came to visit the deposed crown prince, Yinreng had called for hot water and a young eunuch to tidy up his appearance and change into a new, clean set of clothes.

Although he was under house arrest, Kangxi had given special instructions not to mistreat his livelihood. Therefore, even though almost everyone serving him had been killed off, unfamiliar attendants would still serve him to the best of their ability.
When Kangxi saw Yinreng, Yinreng was reading a book, his gaze clear and his expression calm.
Seeing Kangxi arrive, Yinreng first looked over this Kangxi, whose appearance was nearly identical to the Khan Ama of his first lifetime.
He somewhat suspected that perhaps he hadn't transmigrated again, but had truly been reborn.
Then, if he changed his current self's destiny, would he be changing his own true destiny?
Ha, would he still transmigrate to the third lifetime and meet the current Khan Ama, Da Ge, and his younger brothers then?
Yinreng was amused by his own wild imagination.
Finding joy amidst suffering was something he was already very accustomed to; even when something wasn't funny, he could still laugh.
On the contrary, his smile gave Kangxi quite a start.
Kangxi stepped back a few paces and asked hesitantly, "Second Prince, are you well?"
Hearing Kangxi call him the Second Prince, Yinreng was stunned for a moment, then sighed, "Khan Ama, how many years has it been since you last called your son Baocheng?"
Kangxi froze, not expecting Yinreng to say such a thing.

Yinreng stretched out both hands. "Your son has things to say to Khan Ama alone; no one else can hear them. If Khan Ama is worried, you can have someone tie up your son's hands first. As for wearing the cangue, the wooden cangue..."
Yinreng paused, smiling bitterly, "The wooden cangue is an instrument of torture worn only by grave criminals. Your son knows he has been unfilial, but the wooden cangue is truly too tormenting."
Kangxi remained silent for a long moment before saying, "I let my anger overrule my senses."
Yinreng shook his head. "Khan Ama, your son knows you don't trust him right now, but your son truly has very important words to tell Khan Ama alone at this moment."
Kangxi remained silent for another long moment, then said, "I have not yet grown so cowardly."
He waved his hand, and those around him retreated.
Kangxi said, "Speak."
Yinreng sighed, knowing that hidden guards were still present.

He had no choice but to repeat, "What your son has to say can only be known by Khan Ama. If others find out, those others will certainly be... dealt with by Khan Ama in the future. Your son does not wish to implicate the innocent. Please bind your son's hands."
Kangxi said in an unquestionable tone, "Speak!"

Yinreng knew that this Kangxi would not listen to him, so he could only cast an apologetic glance in the direction where the hidden guard was located and said, "Khan Ama, although I am Yinreng, I am not the Yinreng you know. Khan Ama should have read Buddhist scriptures—the great thousand worlds, the small thousand worlds; perhaps there is a world where history and current circumstances are identical to the world today."
Ancient times had many legendary strange tales and anomaly stories depicting a person accidentally entering another world and encountering their identical self.
Yinreng knew that Kangxi occasionally read legendary strange tales to pass the time and should know of such things.
Originally, Yinreng hadn't wanted to tell Kangxi these things, but the deposed crown prince had insisted that he make it clear to Kangxi.
Based on the deposed crown prince's understanding of Kangxi, Kangxi would want to know the future and would not immediately kill Yinreng.
As for whether he believed it or not, that was another matter entirely.

Everything the deposed crown prince possessed came from Kangxi. Once Kangxi stripped him of everything, the deposed crown prince could no longer influence Kangxi or the Great Qing. If Yinzreng wanted to make a change, he had no choice but to take a different path—speak the truth plainly, and see if Kangxi himself was willing to change these tragedies.
As for whether Kangxi would kill the deposed crown prince out of fear afterward.
Well, the deposed crown prince had already given up caring and no longer gave a damn.

After Kangxi reinstated the crown prince, he immediately purged the crown prince's faction, rewarding the other princes and the officials who stood in opposition to the crown prince. Perhaps in his first life, Yinzreng still held onto a sliver of wishful thinking; now he understood that after the first deposition, he no longer had any hope of ascending the throne.
Death was better—death was better than being slowly sliced by a blunt knife for a dozen or so years.
Sensing the deposed crown prince's desire for death, Yinzreng agreed.
He himself felt that if he were in his shoes, having to endure another deposition and restoration, and experiencing being placed under house arrest, dying a swift death would be much better.
A person who is not afraid of death is afraid of nothing. Therefore, with much pain, Yinzreng confessed his origins.
Regardless of whether Kangxi believed it or not.
Kangxi's eyelids twitched, and he understood why Yinzreng had made the others leave.
Yinzreng said, "My experiences are very complicated. First of all, I went through being appointed and deposed twice..."
Kangxi said, "Stop. Guards, bind the Second Prince's hands."
In the end, Kangxi still believed Yinzreng's words. After binding Yinzreng's hands and feet, he had the secret guards leave and guard the doorway.
"Go on," Kangxi said calmly. "I can tell. You are not him. There is no trace of his hostility in your eyes."
How could Kangxi fail to recognize the son he had raised himself?
His previous doubts arose only because this person also carried a feeling he was extremely familiar with, very much like his son.
Like him... the crown prince of the past.
With his hands and feet bound, Yinzreng felt somewhat uncomfortable.
He leaned backward, resting against the back of the chair, before he began his narrative anew.
Skipping over the two depositions and restorations, the first thing he spoke of was Kangxi's date of death.
November of the sixty-first year of Kangxi, Kangxi passed away at Changchun Garden, succeeded by the Fourth Prince, Yinzhen.
Hearing the date of his own death, the corners of Kangxi's mouth twitched: "You really have some nerve..."
Which rebellious brat that I raised is this?! Isn't he being a bit too arrogant?!

Using the matter Kangxi wanted to know about most to hook his attention, and seeing Kangxi's expression that looked angry but was actually relieved, Yinzreng said, "Imperial Father was the longest-reigning emperor, with the temple name Shengzu..."
Kangxi interrupted: "What temple name?!"
Yinzreng: "Shengzu..."

Kangxi interrupted again: "Shengzu is posthumously conferred on founding ancestors! Which idiot gave Us the temple name Shengzu?! That blockhead Lao Si?! Isn't he afraid future generations will curse Us for being unworthy?!"

Yinzreng comforted Kangxi, saying, "Imperial Father, it's nothing, it's nothing. Lao Si's little fourth child, the one called Hongli—wait, hasn't Hongli been born yet? Never mind. Hongli ascended the throne after Lao Si, and his birth mother, the one from the Niohuru clan, also received the posthumous title Sheng—Empress Xiaosheng, just like Imperial Father. So ordinary people won't think Imperial Father's temple name is undeserved."
Kangxi's face turned a mixture of pale and ashen, as if a volcano was about to erupt.
After a long while, he calmed down: "You lived to be that old?"
Yinzreng replied, "No. I passed away shortly after Imperial Father died. I know about the affairs of later generations because I was reincarnated."
Yinzreng then proceeded to tell Kangxi about his experiences in his second and third lives.

During his reincarnation, he had no memories of his past life, but perhaps Heaven took pity on the merit of him saving people, so when he was reincarnated for the third time, his memories returned, and he still arrived at a parallel world's Qing Dynasty.
Kangxi's temples throbbed violently, not knowing whether he should believe this strange person before him.
What made him even angrier was that Yinzreng was still bragging endlessly about how good-natured and handsome his Imperial Father from the third life was.
Am I not handsome?!
This burst of anger from Kangxi almost brought him back to his hot-tempered youth.
Moreover, Yinzreng's rambling and nagging made him feel as if he had been thrust back into the days of parenting the little brat of a crown prince.
Back then, the little crown prince used to jabber away and was exceptionally noisy.
If this "Yinzreng" in front of him wasn't lying, then Kangxi probably understood why he showed no fear and was so lively.
The so-called memories of reincarnation were probably just like reading a book. The contents were remembered, but what was remembered were other people's things, not something personally experienced.
The rambling fellow before him who seemed utterly devoid of worldly cunning was just an un-capped, spoiled, and tender young crown prince.
And this fellow was completely unfazed and brazen!
"You... were injured and unconscious, and came to this world unconsciously?" Kangxi integrated the information from Yinzreng's words and said, "You didn't die in the other world?"

Yinzreng immediately said, "Don't curse me, I'm doing fine. Imperial Father hurried over from the capital, and I even complained to Imperial Father that I was so badly hurt yet Imperial Father didn't look worried at all. Imperial Father knocked me on the head and said that seeing I was in no danger, he was too busy smiling to have any look of worry."
Kangxi: "..."

Yinzreng said wistfully, "Then I thought of the events of my first life. Back then, when I heard Imperial Father was gravely ill, I was so frightened I hurried over with Lao San at a gallop to visit. When I arrived and heard Imperial Father had already recovered greatly, I was overjoyed, and then I got scolded and was sent back to the capital."
Kangxi: "..."

Yinzreng sighed, "I remember making things clear with Imperial Father afterwards, and Imperial Father acknowledged it too. Yet now Imperial Father says he has been holding a grudge against me for twenty years."
Kangxi: "..."

Yinzreng said, "Imperial Father, I was only sixteen at the time, seventeen by nominal age, right? You raised me with your own hands, and my only family was you. Even Songgotu—I rarely saw him back then... Never mind. I came to this world not to defend myself. The person I want to defend will never hear my defense again anyway. The misunderstandings between your son and you can be resolved by you and him yourselves. But since he was deposed, let him stay deposed; don't reinstate him again."
Abruptly changing the subject, Yinzreng steered the conversation toward the War of the Nine Princes for the Succession.

After the first deposition of the crown prince, Kangxi loathed the Eighth Prince's faction, leaving only three people capable of inheriting the throne: the Third Prince Yinzhi, the Fourth Prince Yinzhen, and the Fourteenth Prince Yinzhen (Yinzti).

Based on his understanding of Kangxi, Yinzreng analyzed: "Imperial Father's future consideration was probably that the Fourth Brother and the Fourteenth Brother would serve as backups for each other. Imperial Father didn't know how many more years he had to live at the time; the Fourth Brother and the Fourteenth Brother had a large age gap. If he passed away early, the Fourth Brother would ascend the throne; if the Fourth Brother grew old and lacked energy, the Fourteenth Brother would have matured, so the Fourteenth Brother would ascend the throne."
Hearing Yinzreng analyze his psychology, Kangxi felt a very strange sentiment: "What are you trying to say?"
Yinzreng said, "Regardless of whether the Fourth Brother or the Fourteenth Brother ascends the throne, the other will definitely be kept under house arrest until death."
Kangxi said, "Are you blaming Us?"

Yinzreng said, "The person I want to blame can no longer hear my words. I am temporarily borrowing your son's body to appear here simply to prevent some tragedies. Saying these words is merely to gain your trust, to let Your Majesty know that I am not lying."
Yinzreng no longer addressed the Kangxi before him as "Imperial Father."
Kangxi sat up slightly straight.
Indeed, the fellow before him who claimed to be Yinzreng from another world was now speaking words that matched the most hidden considerations deep within his own heart.
He believed that perhaps this person truly came from another world.

Most emperors believed in ghosts and deities. When Yinzreng confessed his identity, Kangxi did not immediately order someone to behead Yinzreng precisely because he harbored a shred of curiosity toward the supernatural.
And... who wouldn't want to know the future?
Emperors all possessed a spirit of adventure. Rather than rashly hacking someone to pieces, Kangxi preferred to grasp such powers in his own hands.
Closing his eyes to organize his thoughts, Yinzreng finally began to speak of the words he truly wanted to say.
A hundred years into the Great Qing, several hundred years into Huaxia—the things that were missed, the things that were encountered, the things regretted too late.
Yinzreng actually felt somewhat worried: should he let this Great Qing rot away, since the ending was good anyway?
What if Kangxi came to his senses? What if Huaxia reached a constitutional monarchy?
Later, he thought of several constitutional monarchies; they all had their own unique historical reasons, such as the emperor himself being merely a mascot. Huaxia did not possess such reasons.
Even within its feudal dynasties, the imperial power and the ministerial power in Huaxia had always been locked in a game of chess. A monarch would never willingly become a puppet.
Therefore, to reform, it must be a thorough reform, leaving not a single shred of leeway.
Hearing about the events of the Great Qing two hundred years later, Kangxi's face remained unperturbed, and he even felt a trace of joy.
Yinzreng knew what Kangxi was rejoicing over.

Looking across history, no matter how much Kangxi desired the Great Qing to endure for ten thousand years of everlasting youth, he knew this was utterly impossible. What Kangxi worried about was that after the Jurchens entered the pass, the nation would not even have a hundred years of fortune.
Now that he knew it would far exceed a hundred years, how could he not be happy?

Speechless, Yinzreng said, "These two hundred years of national fortune are only thanks to Westerners helping us sustain it. Later on, whenever future generations mention the Great Qing, all they do is curse. Is that really good?"
Adjusting his expression, Kangxi said solemnly, "Of course not."
Yinzreng: "...When saying it's not good, Your Majesty, could you please first lower the corners of your mouth a bit?"
Kangxi: "..."
Yinzreng: "..."
The two stared at each other, looking as if they were playing some kind of staring contest.
Suddenly, Kangxi thought of the crown prince in his childhood. He had once accompanied the crown prince in such a childish way to play.
Pulling himself out of his trance, Kangxi said, "Stay out of the affairs of this world, and return the body to my son."
A wave of disappointment washed over Yinzreng's heart.
Pulling himself together with difficulty, he said, "Right now your son is shutting himself off emotionally and needs to recuperate from his heartbreak for a while."
Kangxi snorted coldly: "What heartbreak is he recuperating from? I was forced to abdicate and didn't even have heartbreak."

Yinzreng said, "He was just grumbling a bit out of his mouth; could he really have forced you to abdicate? Being crown prince for forty years is actually nothing; the crown prince of your pen pal Louis XIV didn't outlive Louis XIV either."
The soul fluctuations of the deposed crown prince inside Yinzreng's heart trembled for a moment, then quietly subsided.
Hearing Yinzreng say this, Kangxi realized that all his retorts were blocked in his throat.
"Forget it," Kangxi sighed. "What do you want to secure for him?"

Yinzreng said, "Demote him to a commoner. Demote him to a commoner, give him ample money and people, and exile him overseas. Otherwise, even if he merely becomes an idle imperial clansman, in the end he and his descendants will meet nothing more than a miserable death."
Kangxi: "Is he willing?"
Yinzreng said, "He even wants to shave his head and become a monk."
Kangxi was once again left speechless.
The two sat in silence for a long while again, finding themselves with nothing more to say.
Looking out the window, Yinzreng felt that his time traveling here had truly been completely useless.

Brotherhood could not be mended, the future of the Great Qing was murky and uncertain, and even his own fate could not necessarily be reversed—Kangxi reinstating the crown prince a second time was originally just to temporarily stabilize the court situation, not out of a genuine desire to restore the crown prince.

Therefore, even after making up his mind not to let the deposed crown prince ascend the throne, Kangxi would still use the deposed crown prince to the absolute limit before discarding him like a worn-out shoe.

After all, Kangxi was someone capable of making the Eldest Prince and the deposed crown prince serve as whetstones for each other, and then doing the same with the Fourth Prince and the Fourteenth Prince.
It was simply a pity for the Eighth Prince, Yinsi, who had jumped into the mix midway and whom Kangxi hadn't anticipated. He truly had it exceptionally miserable.
First the eldest brother and himself, then the fourth brother and the fourteenth brother. Did he know his sons would be ground to ruin?
He knew.
And even knowing, Kangxi believed that jade cannot become an instrument without being carved.

Yinzreng had grown numb to all of this. What saddened him was only that Kangxi, now aged and with a weakening spirit, no longer possessed the ambition and drive for sweeping reforms upon hearing about the trials the Great Qing was about to face.
The timing of his arrival here was truly awful. He could neither save himself nor save the Great Qing.
Seeing the silent Yinzreng, Kangxi perceived his disappointment.
He felt somewhat embarrassed and somewhat angry, yet he didn't know how to vent it.
Venting it on this otherworldly person before him? What use would that be? In the end, it would still be striking his own son.

Yinzreng had no wish to provoke the dissatisfaction of the Kangxi in this world. Because the Kangxi of this world looked too much like the Imperial Father of his first life, it made him feel as though he had returned to his first life.
Managing a faint smile, he said, "Since Your Majesty doesn't want to know about the affairs of later generations, would you like me to tell you about the affairs of my world?"
With a straight face, Kangxi said, "Tell Me."
He wanted to see just how good the version of himself in another world was, that it could cause the crown prince of that world to look at him with disappointment.
Yinzreng started from his childhood.
Omitting the dark history of pretending to be possessed by Fulin, he only spoke of the intimate past between himself and his Imperial Father.
When Imperial Father was reviewing memorial tablets, he would hold infant him in his arms and coax him while flustered and exasperated;
As he grew slightly older, he would play with Imperial Father's little braid, wiping his hands and grinding his teeth on Imperial Father's dragon robe;
He and his eldest brother had grown up together since childhood, joining forces to drive Imperial Father up the wall, climbing trees to mock Imperial Father;

Every time Imperial Father wanted to beat him and his eldest brother, the two of them would run to the Grand Empress Dowager's palace, and the Grand Empress Dowager would rush out with her cane to beat Imperial Father right back...
After finishing the stories of childhood, it was time for him and his eldest brother to show off their grand prowess.

Rashly entering a mutinying military camp, leading the younger princes to storm the doorstep of the Eldest Brother's faction, setting sail together to conquer foreign nations, opening up territory for the Great Qing together, reorganizing the Eight Banners, abolishing the hair-shaving queue order, and establishing universities...

His younger brothers were all exceptionally brilliant, being drafted by Imperial Father at a tender age; his sisters were also exceptionally brilliant, with Princess Chunxi even earning military merits; the ministers included both formidable ones and those who wished for the death of their father-son pair...

Abroad were the lifelong close friends of Imperial Father and his eldest brother; Yansxu was about to set off for Russia to enter a political marriage with the Empress, and the Great Qing's navy had already shaken the overseas world...

Right, Dzungaria had just been wiped out by him and his eldest brother leading the imperial guards and the new army, while the main forces of the Eight Banners came panting heavily in pursuit behind them; before they even caught a glimpse of their shadows, Dzungaria had already been destroyed—it was hilarious enough to kill you.
Watching the brilliance that appeared in the eyes of the crown prince from another world before him, Kangxi felt an even tighter blockage in his chest.
Compared to the emperor of that world, he had to admit that his own魄力 (boldness/resolve) fell far short.
He had already exhausted his mental and physical efforts merely to keep the Great Qing from collapsing, and completely lacked the mental energy and capability to carry out such sweeping reforms.
Perhaps he had thought of it once, but domestic wars following one after another, leaving the common people destitute and plunged into misery, had already ground away his ambition.
He could only endure, hiding all his grand ambitions and waiting for the ordinary people of the Great Qing, who had suffered deeply from the fires of war, to recover and recuperate on their own.
Why could the emperor of another world do it? Was it because that emperor had shared power with the crown prince, letting the crown prince shoulder his government affairs and pressure?

Kangxi remembered once more that he, too, had once generously bestowed power upon the crown prince, letting him travel south to the Jiangnan region to mingle with scholars and literati, pulling out all the stops to build up fame for the crown prince.
Back then, he hadn't worried about the crown prince overstepping his bounds in the slightest, because the crown prince was the heir he had designated, destined to become the emperor in the future.

Precisely because the crown prince was to become emperor, Kangxi had isolated the crown prince from a very young age, preventing him from growing deeply close to ministers and brothers, worried that those people would influence the crown prince's judgment.
As a result, the crown prince grew tyrannical and even wanted to actively lay his hands on imperial power.
He understood the version of himself in another world.
In his youth, he too possessed the boldness to share power with the crown prince in this manner.
Yet he could not understand the version of himself in another world.

How could he let the crown prince and his brothers live together in harmony, how could he let young princes go out to work at such an early age, and how could he bear to let the crown prince he cherished most experience so many thrilling and harrowing trials at such a tender age?
For the first time, Kangxi felt such profound bewilderment.
Following this bewilderment, he made a move that even he himself could not understand.
With his own hands, he untied the bindings on Yinzreng's hands and feet, and asked him, "Do you want to go see the brothers of this world?"
Yinzreng paused slightly, then gently shook his head.
There was no need.
After all, in this world, he did not have a close brother.
"Baocheng? What is it? Why are you crying? Are you having a nightmare? Baocheng, wake up!"
"Ahahaha Imperial Father, stop shaking! Younger brother's wounds aren't healed yet!!"
Tear-streaked, Yinzreng suddenly smiled: "My Imperial Father and Eldest Brother are calling me back. It seems the me in the other world had a nightmare."
The aged Kangxi muttered, "Going back, are you."
Only now did he begin to seriously gaze upon the crown prince of this other world with eyes free of bias and vigilance.
Another Baocheng. A Baocheng spoiled to maturity by another version of himself, surrounded by trustworthy brothers and sisters.
He did not remember the appearance of the seventeen- or eighteen-year-old Baocheng in his own world, but his own Baocheng's brows and eyes would never be this gentle.
Yinzreng's consciousness was slowly being pulled away from this body.
For some reason, he just knew that after his consciousness left this time, he would never return.
Perhaps in the realm of destiny, Heaven saw that he had done well in that parallel world and gave him a chance to face his nightmare.

Whether this was a dream or not, and whether Yinzreng admitted it or not, this Kangxi who looked identical to the Imperial Father of his first life, and that deposed crown prince who looked identical to himself in his first life, were the nightmare he had countless times told himself "I no longer care about," yet still buried deep within his heart.
Seeing the nightmare once more, Yinzreng finally clearly separated the Kangxi of his first life from his current Imperial Father.
They were different—completely different.
My Imperial Father is not him.

"Baocheng..." The aged Kangxi hesitated for a long while before speaking softly, "The crown prince... must be reinstated a second time. I need some time to buffer, to lull the crown prince's faction into complacency before dealing with them, to pave the way for the next crown prince."
Tearfully, Yinzreng said, "Mn, your son knows."
The aged Kangxi said, "Wait—wait until this matter is over, I... sigh..."

He had originally intended to confer the title of Prince of the First Rank upon the deposed crown prince, build a prince's mansion outside the palace, and perhaps live together with the deposed crown prince in the future to mend their father-son relationship.
But...
Yinzreng's consciousness drifted far away, and the deposed crown prince returned to his body.
At this moment, the aged Kangxi spoke in pain: "I will depose him to a commoner and banish him overseas."
The deposed crown prince knelt and kowtowed: "Your son... obeys the imperial decree."
Looking down, the aged Kangxi gazed at the deposed crown prince.
His own son had returned.
Raising his head, the aged Kangxi seemed to perceive a translucent shadow.
A youthful crown prince in the prime of his life.
Yinzreng let out a breath of relief, tears hanging on his face as his smile finally blossomed into radiance: "Thank you, Imperial Father."
His nightmare had finally dissipated.
A mere scholar in the Qianlong dynasty could rally a crowd of Chinese to establish a nation in Nanyang. His own brothers leading troops out to sea certainly wouldn't lose to a mere scholar.
Raising his head, the deposed crown prince also looked toward the other version of himself.
His expression gradually cleared, and the hope in his eyes rose from the ashes.
Over these past few days, Yinzreng had told him much about the scenery overseas.
He wanted to leave this place, break free from everything, and witness a vastly broader world.
"Ahahaha Imperial Father, younger brother is crying and laughing at the same time, something's really wrong with him."
"Hey! Baochen! Weren't you the one who just said not to shake him..."
In agony, Yinzreng opened his eyes: "Stop shaking, stop shaking! The wound is splitting open, it hurts, hurts, hurts..."
Anxious, Kangxi and Yinzhi shouted: "Imperial physician! Imperial physician!"

204. Chapter One [V]
Changtai shot an angry glare.
Li Tong cast a resentful gaze.
The father and son duo of Kangxi and Yinzhi obediently went to inspect the training conditions of the imperial guards.
Having his bandages changed in front of Li Tong made Yinzreng feel somewhat embarrassed.

Sensing Yinzreng's awkwardness, Li Tong, with the detachment of someone handling official business, recounted everything that had happened in the palace and the capital since Yinzreng left Beijing, item by item.
As they chatted, Yinzreng entered the state of handling government affairs and was no longer awkward.
That was until he heard that Yinzhi and Yinzhen had been placed under confinement, causing Yinzreng to catch his breath short.
"Fourth Brother was beaten?" Yinzreng said. "How old is Fourth Brother anyway? What if ten board strikes cause permanent damage!"
Li Tong said, "The Emperor gave specific instructions: it must hurt, but without causing real harm. The boards were all hollowed out."
Yinzreng's heart ached terribly: "Even so... a few whip lashes would have been enough, why resort to board strikes? What did Fourth Brother do to make Imperial Father this angry?"
Li Tong told Yinzreng about Yinzhen "guaranteeing with his life" that day, leaving Yinzreng speechless for a long time.
He remained silent for a prolonged period before his eyes went blank, muttering words only he could understand.
Something about truly deserving to be biological brothers...
Something about how terrifying historical inertia is...
Something about walking Fourteenth's path so that Fourteenth has nowhere to walk...

Yinzreng rejoiced that Imperial Father didn't truly suspect him; otherwise, Yinzhen probably wouldn't have been beaten with boards, but rather chased down by Imperial Father with a saber, while Yinzhi clutched Imperial Father's legs shouting "Imperial Father, appease your wrath."
"By the way, Imperial Father came here, so who is guarding the capital? Were Third and Fourth Brothers released? Or are Prince Yu and Prince Gong in charge?" Yinzreng asked.
Li Tong shook her head: "I left the capital before the Emperor."
Yinzreng called over the imperial guards who had traveled alongside the Emperor.
The guard wore an awkward expression: "Crown Prince Highness, you'd better just ask the Emperor directly."
Yinzreng was filled with question marks. What was so difficult about this? Did this kind of matter even need to be kept from him?
Instinct told Yinzreng something was amiss. While sending someone to summon Kangxi, he had Li Tong temporarily withdraw.

If his guess turned out to be correct, he probably wouldn't spare Imperial Father's feelings later. Since Li Tong was Imperial Father's prospective daughter-in-law, it was best not to let her witness a father and son tearing into each other, so as to preserve a bit of face for Imperial Father as an elder.
As Li Tong was leaving, Yinzreng hesitated for a moment and called out to her: "About the matters in the palace, thank you."
Li Tong's heart skipped a beat, her smile bright: "It's what I ought to do."
With that, she hurried away, blushing.

Yinzreng touched his face. His thanks had been entirely free of any ambiguous intent, yet with Li Tong blushing, his own face couldn't help turning red too, as if he had spoken something extraordinary.
"Uncle, stop laughing," Yinzreng said, glaring at Changtai whose shoulders were shaking. "Would you like to step outside for a while too?"
Suppressing his laughter, Changtai said, "I actually quite want to watch you lecture the Emperor."
Yinzreng said, "Better not. If my guess is right, you'd better get me a comfortable carriage—we should be heading back to Beijing."
Yinzreng's expression turned gloomy.
Heavens, please don't let us have to fight our way back in when we return to the capital.
Emperor, Crown Prince, Eldest Prince—why are the three of you rebelling?
What an eternal "laughingstock" this was!
Bursting in with high spirits to see his son, Kangxi then revealed an awkward yet guilty expression and covered his ears.
Chuckling, Yinzhi said, "Younger brother, scold him! Scold Imperial Father!"
Furious, Kangxi said, "Which son dares to scold his own father!"
With a deadpan expression, Yinzreng said, "How could I possibly scold Imperial Father? At most I'll just nag a bit."

Kangxi offered a sheepish smile: "Stop nagging. As long as you and I are fine, let the capital be as chaotic as it likes. I left Chunxi in proper charge of guarding the capital; it won't get too out of hand."
Yinzreng asked, "Eldest Sister agreed to let Imperial Father leave the capital?"
He hadn't expected Eldest Sister to also be someone who enjoyed taking risks.
Kangxi said, "I left an imperial edict behind."
Taking a few deep breaths, Yinzreng repeated: "Imperial Father left Eldest Sister a scrap of paper and just ran away?"
Kangxi defended himself: "What scrap of paper! It was an imperial decree!"
Yinzreng: "...Imperial Father, get ready, we need to hurry back to Beijing. The capital itself won't be in chaos, but I'm worried something might happen to Eldest Sister."
What if someone mistook Eldest Sister for a rebel and hacked her to death!
Also worried about Chunxi, and seeing that the crown prince's injuries had stabilized and he was no longer lethargic every day, Kangxi gave the order to return to the capital.
Leaning close to Yinzreng's ear, Yinzhi whispered, "I thought you were going to scold Imperial Father."

Yinzreng said, "Scold him for what? If anyone's getting scolded, it's you and me. A Russian caravan suddenly popped up on the road, and instead of circumventing the Qing army, they actually closed in. Come to think of it, there must be something seriously wrong with this caravan. The two of us really got full of ourselves after wiping out Dzungaria, completely losing our caution..."
Yinzhi hurriedly clapped one hand over Yinzreng's mouth: "Alright, alright, stop chanting. Do you think you're Tang Monk, reciting the tight-fillet spell to your older brother? I know I was wrong."

Yinzhen shook his head, made Yinzhi let go of his hand, and continued, "Although Khan Ama's move was risky, it's also the fastest way to resolve this chaotic situation. As long as I'm fine and Khan Ama returns to the capital with me, all rumors will collapse on their own. Regarding the matter of the Ross country attacking me, as long as Khan Ama finds me before those officials do, the definition of the attack will be interpreted by Khan Ama."

The attack happened suddenly and occurred right in the middle of the Imperial Guards; everyone in the capital ought to be completely clueless about it. They would only find out what happened after the Crown Prince and the First Prince returned to the capital.

Therefore, all accusations against the Ross country would have to wait until the Crown Prince and the First Prince returned to the capital for them to spread rumors, and use those rumors to hijack public opinion to force Kangxi into making a decision.

However, if Kangxi bypassed all the officials to leave the capital, found the Crown Prince first, and learned about these matters first, Kangxi could unify the narrative upon entering the capital. They wouldn't be able to fabricate rumors based on "rumors among the Imperial Guards."
If anyone had doubts, then the person who had doubts would be giving themselves away and would be connected to this attack event.
Therefore, while Kangxi's move was indeed risky, the consequences were entirely controllable.

The worst-case scenario would be nothing more than the capital falling into chaos due to the Emperor's departure, followed by the Emperor leading the Imperial Guards in a sweeping siege of the capital.
Yinzhi said gloomily, "This isn't the worst-case scenario. The worst-case scenario is that after Khan Ama arrives here, he finds that you have already died from your severe injuries."
Yinzhen said, "If I die from severe injuries, then I die from severe injuries. Actually, the consequences..."

Yinzhi said, "Are very serious. Either Khan Ama and I will lead a large army to attack the Ross country together, or I will first kill the nobles in the capital by myself and then go fight the Ross country."

Yinzhen: "...I beg you to shut up, Big Brother. Even if it hasn't happened yet, you'll get beaten with the board for saying things like that. Fourth Younger Brother just got beaten with the board; do you want to follow in his footsteps?"
Yinzhi was curious: "How did Fourth Younger Brother get beaten with the board? Tell me quickly so Big Brother can have a laugh."
Yinzhen told Yinzhen (Yinzhen/胤禛) about the foolish thing he had done.

Yinzhi laughed out loud: "How could Fourth Younger Brother be so stupid? Even if he didn't believe Khan Ama, he shouldn't have said things that provoke Khan Ama. Just watch how I mock him when we get back."

Yinzhen smiled and stopped him: "Alright, don't bully Fourth Younger Brother. Fourth Younger Brother acted with pure sincerity; if you don't praise him, you're mocking him instead—watch out for Fourth Younger Brother hating you."
Yinzhi laughed: "Fine, let him hate me. Even if he hates me, there's nothing he can do about me; I can still kick his butt."

Kangxi was riding his horse ahead at a leisurely and dashing pace. Hearing the laughter coming from his two wounded sons inside the carriage, he turned his head to Changtai and asked, "Why are they laughing so loudly? Careful their wounds open up."
Changtai thought to himself silently: For so many days, the only time the Crown Prince's wounds opened up was when you and the First Prince went to shake him up.
"They seem to be laughing at the Fourth Prince," Changtai said.
Mentioning the Fourth Prince made Kangxi's face sink.
Kangxi scolded, "That Fourth Prince! He actually suspected that I would do something unfavorable to the Crown Prince! And what was that about pledging with his life? I don't have such a stupid son!"

Changtai said, "Although the Fourth Prince is indeed a bit foolish, his heart isn't bad. Confining him is one thing, but those ten board strikes will surely make the Crown Prince heartache for a long time."
Kangxi sneered, "I heard him laughing quite loudly; it doesn't look like he's feeling heartache."
Changtai said, "The one laughing quite loudly must be the First Prince."
Kangxi: "..."
Fine, the one laughing quite loudly definitely was his eldest son.
Kangxi said, "Give him a beating to help him remember the lesson, and stop letting a blockhead be used as a stepping stone by others."
Kangxi beating Yinzhen was not only because he was angry that Yinzhen didn't trust him, but even more so because he was angry that Yinzhen was stupid enough to become a tool for others to test him.
Actually, Kangxi also wanted to give Yinzhi a beating. The third and fourth sons were clearly the ones spent the most time being led by the Crown Prince, so how could they still fall for it?
Could it be that children born earlier are smarter? Even the eldest wouldn't fall for this kind of trick!

Changtai said, "The Third Prince and Fourth Prince simply have less experience. The First Prince and His Highness the Crown Prince have been out to sea and have deeper life experience, so they are naturally more mature than the Third and Fourth Princes."
Kangxi said, "That's true as well. It seems I still have to let them go out to sea too."

Kangxi was very worried about the safety of the Third and Fourth Princes' journeys, but then he thought that if the Crown Prince and the First Prince could go abroad when they were even younger, and now the Qing Dynasty had a better understanding of overseas regions and possessed life-saving medicine, why couldn't the Third and Fourth Princes go?
Could the Third and Fourth Princes possibly be more precious than the Crown Prince?
Kangxi sighed, "I want to go too."
Changtai said, "Then Your Majesty must exercise well, otherwise you won't be able to walk when you're old... Ouch, Your Majesty, why did you whip me?"
Kangxi brandished his whip: "You fellow who makes sarcastic remarks."
Changtai hurriedly spurred his horse away: "This subject wasn't making sarcastic remarks."
Celing foolishly watched from behind as the Emperor and General Changtai started fighting, and asked the Imperial Guard general beside him, "They—they're fighting!"
"Mm."
"Oh."
"I wonder who will win."
"General Changtai will definitely yield to the Emperor."
"Wasn't General Changtai always at sea? How is his horsemanship also so good?"...
The Imperial Guard generals whispered among themselves, each one completely calm.
Celing was even more baffled: "Aren't you guys worried at all?"
The Imperial Guard generals were puzzled: "Worried about what?"
Celing: "..." Worried about what? Uh, he was confused too.
Kangxi and Changtai rode their horses in a huge circle and came back. Changtai's horse's rump had been whipped a few times by Kangxi, but he himself was fine.
The two of them continued chatting about serious matters.
Changtai said, "We will pass by the Eight Banners military camp along the way; should Your Majesty stop by to pacify them?"
Kangxi said, "Alright, I'll just take a look to see if any problems arise in the Eight Banners military camp after I leave the capital."
Changtai said, "Princess Chunxi should have kept it hidden from the officials; the Eight Banners camp won't have problems so quickly."
Then, Changtai slapped himself heavily across the face.
The Eight Banners military camp had actually mutinied!

The news of the Emperor leaving the capital had still gotten out; the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner were clamoring to go greet the Emperor and the Crown Prince, actually tied up their respective commanders, had already left the main camp by fifty li, and collided head-on with the Imperial Guards.
Seeing Kangxi's dragon banner, the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner dropped to their knees in a flurry, clamoring to follow the Emperor and fight their way back to the capital.
Kangxi: "What's wrong with the capital?"
Changtai: "The scouts just came back to report, nothing's wrong with the capital."
The two looked at each other in dismay. Should the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner be considered in rebellion or not?

205. Second Chapter [V]
When Yinzhen learned about this matter, he was also stunned.
Yinzhi, on the other hand, laughed out loud: "These are all loyal subjects, how can you call it a rebellion? They came to pick us up."
Yinzhen: "...Shut up, Big Brother."
Yinzhi pulled the thin quilt over Yinzhen's body: "Khan Ama is still here; with Khan Ama backing you up, what are you worrying about?"
Just as Yinzhen wanted to say something, he remembered his dream and pulled the thin quilt up: "You're right."
So he lay down on the soft pillow and went to sleep.
He now completely trusted the Khan Ama of this lifetime and decided to relax a bit.

Kangxi was just having people look for the Crown Prince to discuss matters, when he heard that the Crown Prince and the First Prince said things like "with Khan Ama backing you up" and then both of them went straight to sleep.
Kangxi: "..."
Changtai patted Kangxi's shoulder with a buddy-buddy look and said, "They aren't married yet; they're both kids, it's normal to rely on Ama."
Kangxi: "...I'm going to have the First Prince get married as soon as I return to the capital! Immediately!"

Pressing his temples where blue veins were bulging, Kangxi pacified the generals and soldiers of the two banners, pardoned their crimes, and led the soldiers of the two banners toward the capital together.
Halfway there, Elundai hurried over with the Plain Red Banner.
Upon asking, Kangxi learned that Elundai had also received news of Kangxi's disappearance in the capital and had specially come to protect the emperor.
Kangxi sighed. Forget it, forget it. Since one was pardoned, the second would be pardoned too. What's more, Elundai was still his cousin.
Because the Crown Prince and the First Prince were injured, Kangxi traveled exceptionally slowly along this road.
When they were still two days away from the capital, Fiyanggugu, Cao Yin, and Nalan Xingde arrived in a flurry with a team of light cavalry.

Midway, they learned the news of Kangxi's disappearance and the uncertain conditions of the Crown Prince and the First Prince. They abandoned the main army and brought only a few hundred light cavalry, whipping their horses to gallop and protect the emperor.
Kangxi smiled, praised, and pacified them, then continued moving forward toward the capital.
"Your Majesty, the commanders of the Upper Three Banners request an audience without an imperial decree."
"Mm, pardon them, pardon them all."
"Your Majesty, the people of the Horqin Mongols have come to protect the emperor."
"Good."
"Your Majesty, the Shengjing Eight Banners have arrived."
"Tell them to get lost back home!!"

"Your Majesty, the commanders of the Bordered Blue Banner and Bordered Red Banner have arrived. They bound their own hands and carried thorn branches on their backs, declaring themselves that they harbor no rebellious intentions, but simply lacked Your Majesty's decree and dared not act without authorization, which is why they are late in protecting the emperor."
Kangxi pressed his forehead: "Oh."
Yinzhi was shelling melon seeds, tossing one into his own mouth and one into Yinzhen's mouth: "Khan Ama, the Eight Banners army has all mobilized, what about the provisions and forage?"
Kangxi said, "It's only a few days, it won't consume much provisions..."

Having said that, Kangxi issued an imperial decree telling those who should go back to go back, and not to stand here eating and drinking for free, as the capital couldn't hold that many people either.
The commanders of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner were finally rescued by people, and also came over tearfully to plead guilty.
After Kangxi gave each of them a few lashes with the whip, he temporarily relieved them of their posts.

Even if he didn't relieve them of their posts, the two of them could no longer command loyalty within the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner. Kangxi had a massive headache. Where was he going to find people next to manage these two miraculous Eight Banners armies of the Plain Blue Banner and Bordered White Banner? Should he just give them to the First Prince and Crown Prince for direct management?
Yinzhen said weakly, "I won't. Khan Ama, you give them all to Big Brother; Your son is recovering from injuries and has no time."
Yinzhi said, "Your son is going back to get married. Khan Ama won't even give your son time for his wedding, right?"

Giving Yinzhi a rap on the head, Kangxi ultimately couldn't bear to strike his heavily injured and weak precious son, so he had Changtai temporarily command the Plain Blue Banner and Nalan Xingde temporarily command the Bordered White Banner, barely managing to command public loyalty.
Kangxi sighed, "We'll just have to break them up and reorganize them."
Hopefully, breaking them up and reorganizing them could keep these two armies under control.
Most of the Eight Banners army had returned to their garrison posts, but the commanders didn't dare to leave, each leading a few hundred men to escort the emperor back to the capital.

When Kangxi arrived outside the walls of Beijing with a mighty army, a group of imperial clansmen and nobles surrounded Prince Yu Fuquan and Prince Gong Changning. With their mournful faces, they looked just as if they were about to be dragged off to the execution ground tomorrow morning.
The good-natured Fuquan was uncharacteristically expressionless and ice-cold, while Changning was picking his teeth.

"Open the city gates to welcome the Holy Majesty, what else can we do? Do you still want to hold the city and put up a stubborn resistance?" Changning propped up his leg like a street hoodlum. "What are those who didn't want to rebel afraid of? Could it be that you guys actually wanted to rebel?"
Fuquan said coldly, "Those of you who should leave the city to welcome him, leave; those who should stay behind closed doors, stay behind closed doors. What else can you do?"
The imperial clansmen and nobles looked at each other in dismay.
What else could they do?
They were worried the Emperor would take things to the extreme and execute all of them on charges of rebellion.

Just as the imperial clansmen and nobles were on tenterhooks, Princess Chunxi supported the Empress Dowager to open the palace gates, personally heading outside the walls of Beijing to welcome the Emperor, the Crown Prince, and the First Prince back to the palace.

Mingzhu and Songgotu each led a team of guards to flank and protect the Empress Dowager and Princess Chunxi, putting on the appearance of loyal subjects of the Qing Dynasty, which made many people's teeth ache.
Mingzhu and Songgotu glanced around at the crowd and sneered coldly.
Sorry, actually we were originally fiercely loyal subjects of the Emperor and the Crown Prince all along. Didn't expect that, did you?

Now that the Eight Banners army had defected to Kangxi without a decree to protect the emperor, it was enough to prove that the current Holy Majesty was not only the aspiration of the people's hearts, but also the destination of the military's heart. From now on, who would still dare rely on having a few soldiers in their hands to oppose the Emperor?
Did you think this was still the era when the Eight Princes ruled? The times have changed!
Yinzhen changed his clothes outside the capital, patted powder and rouge onto his face, and mounted a horse.
Yinzhi also removed the wooden board from his arm, pretending that he wasn't injured.
Guarding Kangxi on the left and right, they led thousands upon thousands of troops, casting a heavy shadow outside the walls of Beijing.

Seeing the Empress Dowager and Princess Chunxi coming out to welcome them, Kangxi dismounted with his two sons and stepped forward to greet them: "Your son is unfilial and has made the Imperial Mother worry."
The Empress Dowager choked up and said, "As long as you're safe, as long as you're safe."
Kangxi nodded toward Princess Chunxi: "Chunxi has had a hard time."
Chunxi cried, "Chunxi hasn't had a hard time."
I really have had a hard time, wuwuwu.
Kangxi said, "Help the Empress Dowager back to the palace, I have other matters. Songgotu, Mingzhu!"
The two veteran officials stepped forward: "This subject is here!"
Kangxi said, "I am right here, in front of the Eight Banners army, in front of the capital's common people, to announce the list of crimes!"
Songgotu and Mingzhu trembled all over, but without a moment's hesitation, they said, "This subject obeys the decree!"
The two of them exchanged a glance.
From today onwards, the two of them would no longer be able to serve as the bosses of the Anti-Crown Prince Party.
Songgotu and Mingzhu each held a copy of the imperial decree, taking turns to read them aloud.
From imperial clansmen to nobles, from Manchu officials to Han officials, as soon as a name was read, someone would be dragged away by the Qing soldiers to be beheaded directly.
These two imperial decrees turned out to be entirely lists of executions.
After reading the two imperial decrees, Songgotu and Mingzhu switched to another imperial decree.
In this imperial decree, some were exiled, some were demoted to commoners... all trials implicated their families.
One of the families turned out to be Tong Guowei's.
Elundai grinned with joy, personally leading men to drag Tong Guowei away, and marched toward Tong Guowei's estate.

Tong Guogang took half a step forward, but ultimately didn't plead for mercy. He only let out a soft sigh, withdrew the half step he had stepped out, his straight back becoming immensely hunched, as if he had aged many years.
The third imperial decree was simply dismissal from office for investigation.
The officials who had their official hats stripped away actually breathed a sigh of relief, their faces filled with fortune.
Once the three imperial decrees were read, everyone looked eagerly toward the final imperial decree.
The final imperial decree was indeed as expected, an imperial decree of rewards.
The first to be granted titles and rewards was Princess Chunxi.
Princess Chunxi was already a First-Rank Princess (Gurun Princess), bestowed with the title of a Prince of the First Rank, and would henceforth draw the stipend of a Prince of the First Rank.
Although a Gurun Princess ranked on par with a Prince of the First Rank, she actually fell far short of a Prince of the First Rank.

For instance, speaking solely of the silver stipend, a Prince of the First Rank received ten thousand taels of silver a year. A Gurun Princess received only four hundred taels, and even with subsidies when marrying outside the borders into the Mongol alliances, it only reached one thousand taels.
Although there were manorial lands and the like, it could still be seen that a princess's treatment fell far short of an imperial prince's.

If a princess stayed in the capital, the expenses of maintaining a princess's residence were about the same as a prince's mansion. Therefore, even favored princesses of the Qing Dynasty had to rely on selling jewelry to maintain their daily outward dignity.
This decree by Kangxi set a precedent where a princess's treatment was equal to an imperial prince's.
Princess Chunxi knelt on the ground to receive the decree, sobbing uncontrollably and unable to speak.
Afterward, when other princesses learned of this decree, the last trace of confusion about their future was swept away. Even the most cowardly princesses were filled with ambition for the future.
The second person Kangxi rewarded turned out to be Yinzhi and Yinzhen.

Both Yinzhi and Yinzhen were granted the title of Beile, with the conferred titles of "Cheng" and "Yong." Although the two of them were still young and it was still far from the time to leave the palace and establish their own mansions, they were already Beile Cheng and Beile Yong. Although not as high as the First Prince, it still showed the Emperor's fondness for the two imperial princes.

Everyone knew that Kangxi was acknowledging Yinzhi and Yinzhen for standing firmly on the side of the Crown Prince and the First Prince this time, upholding the family affection between Kangxi, the Crown Prince, and the First Prince.
Yinzhen touched his butt and curved the corners of his mouth smugly: "Taking a beating in exchange for a Beile title, it's worth it."
Yinzhi said slowly, "I didn't get beaten, and I'm a Beile too."
Yinzhen was so angry he wanted to fight Yinzhi.
Yinzhen no longer had the energy to listen to the remaining rewards.
His vision went black, and he couldn't hold on much longer.
Thus, Yinzhen tugged on Kangxi's sleeve as a signal.

Kangxi, who was still maintaining his imperial dignity, immediately said, "This time, some people in the imperial court colluded with the forces of the deposed emperor of the Ross country to rebel. I have already discussed with the Empress of the Ross country to jointly suppress the rebellious forces on both sides. My Crown Prince and First Prince were both injured in the attack! My serious illness was also because someone poisoned me!"
The attack was real, but the poisoning was fake; let them carry the blame together anyway!
The officials were terrified, and the common people were filled with indignation.

Kangxi said, "But Heaven stands on my side and the Crown Prince's side! The Eight Banners army and the people all stand on my side and the Crown Prince's side! Both the Crown Prince and I are safe and sound! Heaven blesses the Qing Dynasty! Heaven blesses me! Heaven blesses the Crown Prince! Return to the palace!"
The eunuch shouted in a shrill voice: "Set off! Return to the palace!"
Kangxi took Yinzhen and Yinzhi onto the imperial carriage, and the procession set off to return to the capital.
The imperial carriage was fully enclosed. Kangxi and Yinzhi squeezed together on one side, while Yinzhen sat alone on the other side, propping his feet up on the seat and lying flat.
Yinzhi re-splinted his arm with wooden boards and hung it up. Kangxi fed Yinzhen sugared water.
"Endure for a bit, endure for a bit, we'll be back in the palace soon," Kangxi said anxiously.
"Mm..." After finishing the sugared water, Yinzhen crossed his hands over his abdomen and continued lying flat.
Yinzhi hung up his arm and said self-deprecatingly, "If anyone saw what we look like inside the carriage, Khan Ama's hard-acting performance just now would completely collapse."
Kangxi kicked Yinzhi: "Shut up! Talk more and you won't even think about getting married this year! I'll keep you waiting another year."
Yinzhi was dumbfounded: "Khan Ama! Your son has already reached adulthood!"
Kangxi put on the face of a tyrannical father: "Talk more and you won't even think about taking a wife after coming of age! Believe it or not, I'll keep you until you're thirty?"
Yinzhi obediently shut up.
Although he knew keeping him until thirty was impossible, not getting married this year was extremely likely!
Yinzhen said weakly, "Big Brother, there's only one month left this year, how could you possibly get married this year? Khan Ama is teasing you."
Yinzhi was dumbfounded: "Oh right."
Kangxi laughed so hard at his foolish eldest son that tears came out.
206. First Chapter [V]
As soon as Yinzhen returned to the palace, he lay flat.
A crowd of imperial physicians surrounded Yinzhen, feeling so distressed that they plucked out a few strands of their beards in anguish.
Yinzhen had often fainted since childhood due to frequent overexertion of his energy (falling asleep the moment his head hit the pillow), and now even his physical body was weakened.

Thus, the oldest imperial physician mustered the courage to tell Kangxi that His Highness the Crown Prince might never be able to get too close to women in this lifetime, asking Kangxi to arrange fewer women for the Crown Prince.
Kangxi's face turned as dark as the bottom of a pot.
He suddenly remembered—let alone the Crown Prince, his eldest son, who was already approaching adulthood, didn't even have women in his quarters yet.
Imperial princes were usually arranged trial-marriage palace maids around the age of eleven or twelve, yet he had actually forgotten about this matter.

However, since Yinzhi was getting married soon and his arm was still broken, it was obviously inappropriate to arrange trial-marriage palace maids for him at this time, so Kangxi turned his gaze to Yinzhi (Yinzhi/胤祉) and Yinzhen (Yinzhen/胤禛).
Yinzhen hurriedly stopped him: "Sexual relations too early damage the body; my younger brothers should grow up a bit more."
Kangxi thought of his children who had died young and sighed, saying, "Let's talk about it after they turn fifteen."
Yinzhen breathed a sigh of relief.

He certainly didn't want to experience his younger brothers and sisters constantly dying prematurely, only to be grabbed by his younger brothers who would cry and complain about their nephews and nieces constantly dying prematurely.
Because the Eight Banners had spontaneously come to protect the emperor this time, Kangxi's heart was completely settled, and he had set off a bloody storm right at the city gates.
In truth, Kangxi's evidence in hand wasn't entirely conclusive, and Yinzhen even suspected that Kangxi was deliberately weeding out dissidents.
However, feudal society was just like that; the standard for judging a case wasn't based on evidence, but on whether the Emperor believed it or not.

Kangxi couldn't be bothered to play any guessing games of political intrigue with them; he brought his massive army crashing back to the capital, beheaded all who refused to submit, and simultaneously filled the positions with newly cultivated talents, leaving only Kangxi's sole voice in the court immediately.

Mingzhu and Songgotu underwent a complete transformation, becoming fiercely loyal subjects of Kangxi and the Crown Prince. Their private reputations among the officials could be described as stinking to high heaven.
The Anti-Crown Prince Party discovered that their two leaders were actually hardcore Crown Prince partisans, and several of them went crazy.
After this, no one ever mentioned the Anti-Crown Prince Party again.
It seemed they had all developed post-traumatic stress disorder regarding opposing the Crown Prince.
As the New Year approached, the capital flowed with blood. Kangxi scheduled Yinzhi's marriage for the first month of the new year to bring some festive joy to the Qing Dynasty.
The First Prince's wedding had been delayed many times over; everything was already prepared, leaving only the final wedding procedures.
If not for the newly appointed Ministry of Rites officials needing to familiarize themselves with the procedures, Yinzhi might really have been able to take a wife within this year.
However, since Kangxi had given his imperial word that Yinzhi wouldn't be allowed to marry this year, he wouldn't be allowed to marry. Yinzhi could only roll his eyes at his Khan Ama.
Yinzhi complained: "Khan Ama, why are you so childish?"
Kangxi said, "Everything you're saying right now, I'm writing down in a little notebook. After your new marriage, I'll slowly settle accounts with you."
Yinzhi hurriedly shut his mouth. He was worried that after finally managing to marry a wife, he would be dispatched by Kangxi to work in some remote place, leaving no time even for newlyweds' bliss.
Yinzhi changed the subject: "After I get married, when will Younger Brother get married?"
Kangxi's face was full of reluctance: "His health isn't good, I'll keep him for another two years and talk about it after he comes of age."

Yinzhi speechlessly said, "Khan Ama keeps the princesses, saying he can't bear for them to marry out, and saying he'll only let them marry after they turn twenty. Younger Brother is taking a wife, not marrying out; do you have to be like this, Khan Ama?"
Kangxi defended himself: "How can this be the same? You also only took a wife after coming of age."

Yinzhi couldn't be bothered to argue with Kangxi. Anyway, even if Kangxi were in the wrong, he would only punish him by making him write large characters, and the one who suffered bad luck would always be him.

chapters.source_text:
“你之前不还嫌弃直亲王吗？”有人酸溜溜道。
“唰！”
一群耳尖的小阿哥们立刻齐刷刷转头看向大阿哥的岳父科尔坤。
科尔坤的后背立刻被冷汗浸湿。
他急中生智，擦了擦眼泪：“我怎么可能嫌弃直亲王？只是我最疼爱的女儿，就算嫁的人再好，我也难受啊。你难道就能把你女儿欢天喜地的嫁出去？”
对方很想说“是”。但看到小阿哥们纷纷点头，对科尔坤投来赞赏的目光，他只能干巴巴回答道：“那哪可能。”
胤礽忍笑。
不愧是能做到尚书的人，科尔坤还是厉害。第一世若科尔坤没卷入明珠和索额图的争夺，或许在事业上还能更进一大步。
这一世，就看看大哥的岳父能有多大能耐。
胤礽正笑着的时候，察觉有人一直在看着他。
他视线转过去之后，那个人对胤礽尴尬一笑，不自在地移开视线。
胤礽正疑惑时，胤禩凑胤礽耳边小声道：“那是二嫂的阿玛，富察倪满。”
胤礽愣了一下，对着倪满轻轻点了点头。
和准岳父点头示意后，胤礽揉了揉胤禩的脑袋：“八弟好厉害。”
胤禩明明很得意，但还是装得云淡风轻：“我就是在记人的时候记忆力好。”
胤礽夸奖道：“这可是一项大能耐。”
胤禩的脑袋在胤礽的掌心转悠了一圈，就像是一只小奶猫。
他已经十岁，但在胤礽面前，还和小时候一样。
不过不止他，其他阿哥都一样，所以大家都习以为常，谁也不会笑话谁在太子哥哥面前幼稚。
倒是不经常见到宫中阿哥们聚在一起的大臣们惊讶得不得了。
他们虽早知道太子在一众兄弟中威望极高。但这已经不是威望的问题了吧？
看着阿哥们对太子的亲昵，仿佛他们是太子一手带大的似的。
知情人默默闷了一口酒。
呵，你们怎么知道，他们不是太子一手带大的呢？
惠妃毕竟是后宫妃嫔，不能长时间待在宫外。
在胤禔和大福晋重新拜完父母后，她就和康熙回宫了。
康熙离开之后，现场又吵闹起来。
胤禔的一群臭弟弟还试图把胤禔灌醉，让他进不了洞房。
胤祉还在那和胤禛唱双簧，说胤禔手断了，就算没喝醉也不能进洞房。
胤禔立刻怒道：“老子一只手都能揍你俩！”
胤祉和胤禛摆开架势：“来啊来啊！”
胤礽挨个给了两个不老实的弟弟一脚：“你们俩别嚣张，现在惹怒了大哥，等你们成亲的时候，掂量掂量大哥会怎么报复你们。”
胤祉和胤禛这才老实下来。
胤礽道：“七弟、八弟，你们俩跟在大哥身边，不准大哥喝酒。就说大哥伤没好，谁让大哥喝酒，就让他来找我，我帮大哥喝。”
胤禩和胤祐拍着胸脯道：“交给我们！”
他们俩养在惠妃宫中，与胤禔关系比其他兄弟更亲近，更适合帮胤禔挡酒。
虽然胤禔自己没觉得。
“四弟，帮忙招呼宗亲那群人。五弟，你招呼番邦来的人。三弟、六弟，你们二人去其他大臣的地方。”胤礽道，“我带着小九他们去闹洞房。”
年长一点的弟弟道：“我们也想去！”
“你们等会儿来。”胤礽道，“帮大哥把场面先撑住。我带弟弟们去滚床。喜床先要小孩子滚一圈，寓意多子多福。”
九阿哥胤禟举起手来，就像是后世的小学生：“太子哥哥，我可以在大哥的床上撒尿吗？”
胤礽给了小胤禟头顶一个爆栗：“不可以！你敢调皮，大哥在教你们武艺的时候绝对重点盯着你。”
小胤禟捂着脑袋：“大哥已经重点盯着我了。”
小胤俄告状：“对对对！大哥就喜欢针对我俩！”
小胤禌老实道：“难道不是因为你们俩偷偷去剪大哥刚留的大辫子的缘故吗？”
胤礽：“……你们给我说清楚。”
明明他在宫里啊！虽然他为了养伤大部分时候都在休息！他就一个错眼，就有两个不自量力的弟弟去撩大哥的老虎须了？！
小胤禟和小胤俄手牵手往后院跑：“哎呀哎呀，压喜床，别错过吉时！”
胤礽单手背在身后，微笑：“小十一，慢慢和哥哥说。”
小胤禌丝毫没有卖哥哥的愧疚，他睁着天真烂漫蠢呼呼的大眼睛道：“好！”
小胤祹和小胤祥对视一眼，然后耸肩。
胤礽随手抱起年纪最小、也最沉默的小胤禵：“一边走一边说。”
小胤禵环抱住胤礽的脖子，小脑袋搁在胤礽肩膀上，看得其他小阿哥很是羡慕。
他们已经过了可以被太子哥哥随时抱在怀里的年龄了。
据说当年兄弟少，三哥和四哥小时候是被太子哥哥抱着长大，太子哥哥还为五哥写歌弹钢琴启蒙。
好羡慕啊。
小胤禵觉察到哥哥们羡慕的视线，把脑袋埋在胤礽怀里，小手收紧了一些，嘴角上弯。
哼，平时都欺负我年龄最小。
年龄最小也有好处！
小胤禵终于找到了“报复”老喜欢欺负自己的臭哥哥们的办法。
胤礽带着几个小阿哥们在喜床上乱滚一气。
当胤禔喝了一肚子水，好不容易结束应酬，和其他年纪稍大的弟弟们来洞房的时候。
胤礽正在嗑瓜子，脚不能下地的大福晋头戴喜帕端庄安静地坐在床沿上，其他臭弟弟们则脱了鞋，在大福晋身后跳来跳去。
他听着大木床发出嘎吱嘎吱的响声，就像是要散架了似的，脸立刻黑了。
“啊！大哥来啦！”
“快跑快跑！”
“呃，我们帮大哥滚床，为什么要跑？”……
小阿哥们跳到地上穿鞋子，但还是被胤禔敲了脑袋。
胤礽忍笑：“洞房我们就不闹了，大哥你和大嫂好好歇息。咱们明日再见。走，回宫了。”
“啊？不能闹洞房？”
“我想闹洞房。”
“我就等着闹洞房！”……
“好了，今天大哥已经很累了。”胤礽守在这里，就是不想让其他勋贵子弟来闹洞房。
闹洞房真是个恶习，他不想让其他人折腾大哥大嫂。
“你住在这啊，明日和我一起回去。”胤禔道。
胤礽瞥了胤禔一眼：“得了，你好意思，我还不好意思。明日见。”
胤礽笑着对大福晋拱手：“大嫂，今后我的大哥就拜托你照顾了。”
弟弟们有样学样，对着大福晋拱手：“大嫂！今后大哥就拜托你照顾了！”
大福晋双手绞着衣角，虽戴着喜帕看不到众人的模样，但太子和其他皇子们的笑声，仍旧让她面红耳赤，心中熨帖不已。
她感受到了皇家这一众兄弟的感情，也感受到了这些皇子都在努力向她表达善意。
在嫁进皇家之前，她听过许多皇家可怕的传闻，也听过许多关于直亲王的可怕传闻。
但现在，她听着小阿哥们的笑闹，感受着直亲王和其他阿哥深厚的兄弟情，她突然不怕了。
在皇家的那种环境，也能被弟弟们喜欢信赖的大哥，肯定不会是坏人吧。
胤礽带着弟弟们离开。
胤禔拿着喜称挑开了伊尔根觉罗氏的喜帕。
伊尔根觉罗氏眼前一亮，面前出现了一张丰神俊朗英气十足的脸庞。
“你叫什么名字？在家我总不能还叫你福晋？”胤禔没有丝毫不自在，大大咧咧地问道。
伊尔根觉罗氏悬起的心脏在看到胤禔的脸、听到胤禔的提问后，彻底落了地。
她害羞道：“妾身、妾身闺名为……”

“哈哈哈哈弟弟，她的闺名居然叫大花！大花啊！笑死我了！”第二日，回宫履行完拜见皇上、太后、惠妃流程的胤禔，把大福晋丢在宁寿宫陪太后聊天，自己来东煌宫找胤礽分享笑话。“好歹也是尚书的女儿，怎么名字这么糙！”
胤礽嘴角抽搐：“大嫂的闺名为满语中很大的花朵的意思，并不能简单直译为大花。”
因为在婚礼上逞能，而又把手吊起来的胤禔单手拍着大腿笑道：“她汉文闺名也是大花！我问了她的贴身老嬷嬷，她家都叫她大花和花花，哈哈哈哈哈，花花！”
胤礽很认真地问：“大哥，你在我这里疯狂嘲笑大嫂，大嫂知道吗？”
胤禔道：“知道啊。她说完她的闺名，我就笑了。”
胤礽瞪大眼：“哈？”
胤禔道：“她狡辩的话和你刚说的一样，非说那是满语闺名。我当即把她奶嬷嬷叫来一问，嘿嘿，大花、花花，全家都这么叫她哈哈哈哈。”
胤礽深呼吸：“大哥，大嫂的反应是？”
胤禔笑得更大声了：“她当即就哭了，笑死我了！”
胤礽的表情很是绝望。
在洞房花烛夜把新娘子气哭，大哥你好棒棒啊，弟弟给你竖起中指点个赞。
胤礽已经不想继续询问胤禔昨天的洞房花烛夜究竟洞房了没有。
如果没洞房，原因肯定是胤禔因逞能再次断手和把新娘子气哭，怎么想都让人心梗。
如果这都还能洞房……胤礽更心梗。
胤禔还在狂笑。显然大福晋的闺名深深娱乐了他，让他立刻跑来分享给弟弟。
胤礽真的怀疑，也就是现在是封建社会，他大哥是皇帝亲儿子直亲王，否则这样的人怎么可能讨得到老婆？
别说讨老婆，大哥肯定很小的时候就被人套麻袋揍死了吧？
怎么会有这样的人啊！
当胤禔笑够之后，擦着笑出来的眼泪道：“她的闺名也太蠢了，我给她取了一个新名字叫玉英。同样是花的意思，科尔坤在书中找个花的雅称很难吗？”
正心梗的胤礽愣住，他反问：“你给嫂子取了‘玉英’的名字？什么时候取的？”
胤禔道：“她一哭我就给他取了。我取了新名字她就笑了，真好哄。”
胤礽再次无语。
他这个大哥，是太讨人厌还是太会撩？或者两者都有？
他有点可怜未来的大嫂了。大嫂估计会对大哥又爱又恨，就和汗阿玛一样，见不到的时候想得慌，一见面就想抽出鞭子暴揍大哥。
胤礽叹了口气，让人收拾了许多东西给胤禔，又给了胤禔一个小本本，上面写着什么节日可以送给大嫂什么东西。
胤禔翻了几页：“你真细致。你就这么送弟媳东西？”
胤礽摇头：“没有。”
胤禔问道：“你自己都不送太子妃东西，怎么让我送？”
胤礽沉默。
这要他怎么说？说他察觉到李彤对他的爱意，有点胆怯？
胤禔已经止住了笑，表情有些严肃：“哥知道你见了汗阿玛后宫这样子，对女人有点发憷，但弟媳是个好女人，你可以接纳她。有她照顾你，你哥我也放心些。”
胤礽道：“我不是不接纳她，我只是怕辜负她。”
胤禔轻轻捏了一下胤礽的脸。
胤礽不满：“大哥，我都多大的人呢？不准捏脸。”
胤禔道：“多大的人也是我弟弟。有时候我觉得你很奇怪，太在乎别人。兄弟和长辈，朋友和亲戚，自己的女人，甚至平民走卒和外国的平民走卒，你都要放在心中。你累不累？”
胤礽嘴唇翕动，最终低下头，没有说话。
他能说，他这并不叫在乎，只是新社会中最朴素的人道善恶观吗？
那个时代最基本的良知，放到这个时代，居然被人当做大圣人了。
“好，我知道了。”胤礽道，“我在改。”
胤禔道：“哥不是让你改，你现在这样很好。哥只是怕你太累。放松点，有什么哥帮你背着。你还有那么多弟弟。他们受了你那么多照顾，你也该让他们分担你的责任。还有弟媳妇，如果不是你一直在帮助她，她早就被逼死了。她现在的成就别说女人，许多男人一辈子都难达到。将来青史中，肯定有她浓墨重彩的一笔。你还要怎么对得起她？”
胤礽叹气：“嗯嗯嗯，大哥你说得对。我立刻给她准备礼物。”
胤禔道：“这就对了。”
在送胤禔出宫的时候，胤礽才发现，本来应该是他教训在新婚洞房夜把新娘子气哭的大哥，怎么最后变成他被大哥教训了。
胤礽挠挠头，回去让人把早就准备好的红宝石金簪给李彤送去。
李彤穿得很素净，几乎不佩戴首饰。但胤礽看李彤送给他的五音盒，以及李彤随手制作的钟表，用色都非常艳丽。
胤礽猜测，李彤其实是很喜欢艳丽的色彩。
李彤的五官比平常女子稍显英气，本身也应该很适合艳丽的色彩和华丽的装束。
送簪子的太监回宫时，送来了李彤的回礼。
那是一只带轮子的发条小老虎，转动发条就会满地乱跑。
胤礽忍不住笑出了声：“她是把我当孩子吗？”
但笑归笑，胤礽还是一边看书，一边玩小老虎，爱不释手。
现代社会无论男人女人，至死都是会玩玩具的孩子。胤礽来到这个世界之后，还第一次玩到发条玩具。
康熙来看望宝贝儿子的时候，发现儿子正在玩玩具。
他刚想说玩物丧志，就被跑来跑去的发条老虎吸引了。
当知道这发条老虎是太子妃送给儿子的礼物时，康熙微微点头。
第二日，康熙拿来了一只更大的老虎，和儿子的小老虎摆在一起，父子俩一边批改奏折，一边让老虎父子满桌子乱跑。
“如果乌库妈妈知道汗阿玛找儿媳妇帮你制作大老虎玩具，肯定会用拐杖抽你。”
“朕等着皇玛嬷入梦来揍朕。”
父子俩一边案牍劳形，一边互相打趣。
几日后，大福晋回门。
胤礽听说，他大哥把大福晋的兄弟、堂兄弟们都揍了一顿。
胤礽赶紧找胤禔询问原因。
胤禔道：“玉英跟我抱怨，说她才刚成亲，就有人托她办事。唉，早就听说外戚会很麻烦，就像是佟国维一样。为了预防他们将来打着我的名号给我找事，我先揍他们一顿。”
胤礽：“……”他已经不知道该如何说了，只希望大哥这毛病别传染给弟弟们。
延禧宫中，惠妃和大福晋相对呆坐，半晌无语。
惠妃：“我儿子……大阿哥他……”
大福晋哭丧着脸道：“额娘，儿媳没用，儿媳劝不住，拉不住呜呜呜……”
大福晋说着说着，眼泪就涌了出来。
大阿哥一回门，立刻叫来她的兄弟和堂兄弟们，问他们是不是打着自己的旗号做坏事，给自己抹黑，还用亲戚的身份压自己做事。
她的兄弟和堂兄弟们还没回答，大阿哥就动了手，以一敌多，单手把这些人全打趴下，还骂这些人废物，让一只手都打不过，全是被酒色掏空了身体的酒囊饭袋。
“以后你们谁敢让本王福晋难过，本王就让你们全家难过！”
伊尔根觉罗氏全家都懵了。
直亲王啊，我们全家不就等于你福晋全家？
这件事传出去，伊尔根觉罗氏全族都被同情了。
他们是造了什么孽，才会和直亲王结为亲家啊！
惠妃握着大福晋的手，频频叹气：“他、他就是这种做事不过脑子的人。你、你要多劝劝他，劝不动，就、就来……”
就来告诉我？但我也管不住他啊。
惠妃急中生智，道：“劝不住，你就告诉太子！”
大福晋被惠妃这句话吓得眼泪都停止了：“我哪能去和太子告状啊。”
惠妃仔细想想。对啊，大福晋哪可能单独去找太子告状？
她道：“你去和太子妃交好，让太子妃写信告诉太子！”
大福晋点头：“儿媳知道了！”
曲线救国，明白！
惠妃又拿出许多珠宝，道：“这些你拿回你娘家，安抚你的家人。”
大福晋瘪嘴：“我已经赏赐过一次了。”
惠妃道：“那这些就由本宫赏赐下去。你若缺什么，伸手问大阿哥要。大阿哥钱多得是，太子可宠大阿哥。你不用替大阿哥省钱。”
大福晋虽然嘴里说是，但并没有准备问大阿哥要钱要东西。
她才刚新婚，不好意思问大阿哥要钱要东西，这显得不够贤惠。
何况……何况大阿哥替她揍人的时候，她虽然吓到了，其实也蛮高兴。
她被指为大福晋之后，在家待嫁多年。
因直亲王的名声，和频频延后的婚事，她没少遭家族一些人白眼，连阿玛和额娘都经常叹气。
曾经亲近她的小姐妹们也不理睬她了，还私下嘲笑她说不准会被暴虐的直亲王打死。
只有李彤经常给她送一些新奇好玩的东西逗她开心，并安慰她，说直亲王和太子绝非外界所传那样。她曾经见过太子与其他皇子来科学院，他们感情都非常好，对人也非常好，特别是对自己的亲人，好得令人羡慕。
“你将来成了直亲王的福晋，就是他的亲人，他定也会对你非常好。”
大福晋在宫中可以乘坐小轿子。她往脸上补了些粉和胭脂，去东煌宫门口与胤禔汇合。
下轿子时，胤禔一边和胤礽继续说话，一边虽然看都没看下轿子的大福晋，却单手稳稳扶住了大福晋。
“弟弟，你不是说你家太子妃喜欢艳色的东西？玉石珍珠多给我点，反正你也没用。”
“你想要什么自己去库房拿，难道还要我帮你搬？你搬完留张纸条通知我就成。”
“提前和你说一声再拿呗，免得汗阿玛又说我是贼。”
大福晋努力抑制住上翘的嘴角。

210.二更 [V]
直亲王成亲不到一个月，伊尔根觉罗氏就成了京城笑柄。
康熙得知后，默默赏赐了伊尔根觉罗氏许多东西。
嗯，辛苦了。和大阿哥做亲戚就是这样，连他这个当汗阿玛的都不例外。
幸亏纯禧公主很快接着成亲，把京中人的注意力转移了过去，伊尔根觉罗氏才没被笑多久。
策棱来迎亲的时候，几乎全族出动。
这架势，让许多老宗亲很恍惚。
连之前两个先帝迎娶蒙古皇后蒙古妃子时，阵仗也没有这么大。
更让他们惊讶的是，纯禧公主居然不是蒙着盖头坐轿子离开。
她一身红色戎装，骑着高头大马，领着一队卫兵奏着军乐厉害，看上去不像是新娘子，倒像是出征的将军。
礼部的官员愁得差点把胡子全拔了。
还好历史书上有记载，商朝的皇后妇好曾经领军出征，唐朝的平阳公主也曾经军乐下葬，那么大清立下了赫赫军功的固伦公主以这样的方式出嫁，也、也算符合礼仪？
还好，还好史书中有相关的记载，让他们可以帮大清皇室圆过去，不至于让大清皇室显得太蛮夷。
纯禧公主出嫁后，京中其他公主们的婚事也该提上日程了。
虽说康熙准备把公主们都留到二十才出嫁——他听名医说，女子二十岁之后生孩子会更安全。虽他不管自己嫔妃几岁生孩子，但对女儿，毕竟是不同的。
但二十出嫁，不代表二十才选人。
现在国内无事，康熙频频邀请蒙古王公子弟来京城围猎，让适龄的女儿们同行。
蒙古贵族子弟中许多有野心的人眼馋策棱的遭遇，都很想走策棱的老路。
可惜，大清的公主在后宫之中能见到的男人不多，所以找额驸的标准，都是比对着自己的兄弟来。
可哪怕把太子、大阿哥等人的能力砍半，蒙古王公子弟中都很难有人达到。
胤礽看出了姐妹们的失望，劝说她们换个标准。
“若选不出喜欢的，就选能控制的。没了爱情，就要权力。总不能一头都没拿到。”胤礽冷酷的话，得到了姐妹们的认同。
看了大姐的经历，比起男人，她们也更向往大姐的辉煌。
其他不说，大姐的俸禄从一千两变成了一万两，那可是白花花的看得见的银子！
于是公主们不再执著于额驸们的能力。
对自己能力有自信的公主专盯着地盘大、位置好的王公贵族瞅，对自己能力没自信的公主就选家庭简单、性情好说话的人。
康熙现在已经不在乎这些蒙古王公。若不是女儿们都想学纯禧建功立业，他其实更乐意让女儿们嫁给国内重臣，轻松一些。
所以女儿们选中了人，他再查探一番，若这个人之前没有劣迹，就统统同意了。
他也告诉女儿们，若不想去蒙古，也和他说，他在京中给她们选额驸。
但公主们都再次重申要为大清守土戍边的志向。
见到这一幕，胤礽的心情其实有些不好。
当初，他以为这一代的公主仍旧需要执行抚蒙古的任务，所以把公主们往守土戍边上培养。公主们专注事业，有成就感，就会冲淡远离家乡的寂寞。
她们有政治任务，大清也会对她们更多资源倾斜，让她们更好过。
胤礽没想到，陈廷敬神来一笔，居然帮索菲亚夺位成功，索菲亚还要和大清和亲。
大清和罗斯国联姻后，夹在两国之间的蒙古的战略地位就不是很重要了。
再加上大清的军事实力增长迅速，蒙古却止步不前。当胤礽和胤禔飞速灭掉准噶尔的时候，蒙古就注定会在康熙和胤礽在位期间老实。至少他这一代的公主们就没必要抚蒙古了。
但因为之前胤礽给她们喊的口号太响亮，纯禧公主又做出了这样的成就，不想去蒙古的公主或许无法说出不想去蒙古的话。
除非哪个公主真的身体非常差，或者性格有缺陷，否则她们肯定是前仆后继往蒙古和其他边疆去的。
不是搞事业不好。但胤礽希望，公主们的选择更自由一些。想搞事业的公主能放手搞事业，想要安稳生活的公主也可以安心享受后院。
就算在现代，无论男女，都有想卷的和想躺平的。胤礽之前的好心，现在却把公主们都架在了火上，让公主们丧失了选择。
政治斗争从来都是尔虞我诈，你死我活。虽然有大清支持，但公主们仍旧很危险。
更何况大清总会衰落，那时候公主们的处境将更加危险。
胤礽不安，向姐妹们道歉，并希望她们能想清楚再做决定。
公主们都很惊讶。
已经选好额驸，将会第二个出嫁的荣宪公主笑得直不起腰：“太子啊，你这人……怎么说呢，真是从小到大都没变啊。”
胤礽茫然。
荣宪公主笑道：“我们都不是蠢人。若能力不够，我们不会乱来。去了蒙古，我们有广阔的公主府，有庄园，有卫兵，想要悠闲生活还不容易吗？反倒是比在京中容易多了吧？”
胤礽：“好、好像是哦。”
很娴淑文静的端静公主也微笑道：“我知晓太子的好意。我们会量力而为。但在关键时刻，就算我再懦弱，也会举起刀来。历朝历代改朝换代时，公主都非常凄苦，大多沦为玩物。若真到了那时候，我宁愿战死，总能留下些名声，留下些尊严。”
其他公主们纷纷点头。
她们读过书后，对公主们的命运都非常了解。
改朝换代之后，皇子或许还能隐姓埋名逃走。但公主是高贵的玩物，达官贵人最爱收集，基本是逃不掉的。所以许多末代公主为了避免受辱，一根白绫一杯毒酒，与国同休。
那她们为何不拿着武器，死在更有价值的地方？
“你的担心是多余的。”荣宪公主很逾越地揉了揉胤礽的头发，“我们都很感谢你，感谢你给了我们更有尊严的选择。谢谢你，保成，不用担心我们。我们是公主，原本就该比寻常女子多承担一些责任。”
胤礽低着头，红着眼眶笑道：“我现在真该好好道歉了。对不起，我低估了你们，是我的错。”
荣宪公主恶作剧地狠狠揉乱了胤礽的发髻：“没错，你的确得好好道歉。作为赔礼，快来帮我们选一选额驸的人选。最好你再帮我们设计一套我们去了就能用的建设方案。”
胤礽点头：“好。”
他顺便把弟弟们全部找来，把这个作为他们的作业。
弟弟们连连叫苦。
刚入学启蒙的小胤祹和小胤祥茫然：“我、我们也要完成这个功课？”
胤礽点头：“哥哥相信你们。”
小胤祹和小胤祥嘴一瘪。其实太子哥哥你可以不用这么相信我。
小胤禵抱着胤礽的腿，咧嘴得意笑。
这时候身为最小弟弟的优势又出来了！
“不懂的地方问其他哥哥、问我。”胤礽挨个抱了抱自己才启蒙的小弟弟，“完成这个功课，可比写大字有趣多了。”
小胤祹和小胤祥点头。好吧，哥哥说得对。
于是胤礽丢掉了康熙给他的工作，又开始了全心全意帮助姐妹和带弟弟的生活。
因胤祹入学了，他还把胤祹也接到了东煌宫中，与胤祥一起抚养。
入学后的阿哥们都住阿哥所，小胤祥和小胤祹年纪太小，东煌宫和阿哥所是邻居，胤礽一个人住也太寂寞，就带着两个弟弟一起住了。
其他阿哥们还好，小胤禟、小胤俄和小胤禌都羡慕得想哭了。
前面的哥哥被太子哥哥悉心教导过，后面的弟弟可以住在东煌宫，就他们中不溜秋的，两头都没沾到。
胤礽见三人吃醋了，哭笑不得。
他和小九、小十和小十一接触不多啊，这三个弟弟怎么也如此黏人？
于是平日里，他就多照顾了这三个弟弟一些，送给了他们许多自己新做的玩具。
他和李彤现在通信较多，虽只是说些身边的事，但也算熟悉起来，可以主动伸手要东西了。
胤礽说了许多玩具构想，让李彤也给弟弟们做了许多有趣的益智玩具。
小孩子的对感情都十分敏锐。胤礽全心全意对他们好，小九、小十和小十一很快就感受到了。
于是他们更加吃两个小弟弟的醋了。胤礽的安抚，安抚了个寂寞。
看着胤礽焦头烂额带孩子，本来不满胤礽丢掉政务，让他一个人忙碌的康熙大笑三声，扬长而去。
胤礽无语地看着大笑三声扬长而去的康熙。
爱新觉罗·玄烨，又名大胤禔。

纯禧出嫁后，下一个（划掉）出嫁（划掉）成亲的是延叙。
和亲王延叙立下了赫赫战功，威名远播，在罗斯国上层已经传得有些妖魔化了。
据传延叙身高三米，青面獠牙，喜欢砍人头颅当装饰品，简直就像是《圣经》里的恶魔。
延叙去罗斯国前，胤礽搜集到罗斯国对延叙的评价，在送别酒宴上好好笑话了一番延叙。
胤禔笑得直不起腰：“你赶紧把你这张脸重新弄白，先抑后扬，让罗斯国的贵族们被你的美貌吓一跳。”
延叙嘴角微抽：“对不起，直亲王，我没有美貌这东西。”
“你太谦逊了。”
“相信你的脸。”
“对你的礼仪培训没忘吧？”
“罗斯语和法语诗歌背熟了吗？”
“太子弟弟说过，反差萌才是真的萌，哈哈哈哈。”
一众进化成损友的战友们笑得前俯后仰，还有人笑话延叙的“和亲王”，该读成“和亲、王”。
胤礽这时候可不笑了：“不准这么说。和亲王的和，是和平。而和平，则建立在绝对的实力上。他不是和亲，而是给罗斯国和大清带来长久的和平。”
众人立刻不敢拿延叙的称号开玩笑了。
延叙也严肃道：“臣必不辜负太子殿下期待！”
胤礽道：“好了好了，别这么严肃。我相信你。你是我们大清第一个驻外大使，我给你的纲要只是初步方案，还未验证过。你摩挲出一套经验，今后汗阿玛才好派其他大使。你责任重大，千万要保重身体。”
延叙道：“臣知道。”
延叙自请联姻的时候，本以为自己是去做探子，准备牺牲自己造福家族。

延叙若做不好这个大使，他会羞愧得自杀。
延叙带着一队士兵出发了。
这些士兵将围绕大清大使馆驻扎，保护延叙的安全，并在必要的时候执行保护大清国民的任务。
士兵每隔三年就会轮换回国，延叙可随轮换士兵回国，也可不回来。康熙给了延叙充分的自由和信任。
其实驻外大使最好还是轮换，但现在情况不允许，由联姻的宗亲担任大使，无□□换。
走一步算一步吧。
康熙和胤礽亲送延叙到京郊，久久伫立。
延叙离开后，曹寅紧接着离京。
他又立了战功，康熙给他升了官，他现在要去江宁接管旗营，按照新军培养方式进行培养。
同时，曹寅也要作为文人和江南文人联络，成为康熙的眼线。
若之后大清再无需要他的战事，他可能就会一直留在江宁，很少再进京了。
离开之前，曹寅求胤礽向李彤要了一个五音盒和一个发条动物当礼物，送给自己的儿子。
曹寅还和纳兰性德笑，说纳兰性德没有女儿，否则可以结一门娃娃亲。
纳兰性德道，让曹寅赶紧生女儿，好结娃娃亲。
胤礽记得曹寅上辈子的大女儿嫁给了宗室，过得也不错。
不过曹寅这辈子因在草原上征战，还没有女儿。不知道他还有没有女儿出生。
曹寅现在身强力壮，又立下汗马功劳，将来曹家地位肯定更加稳固，不用愁女儿的婆家。
“记得节俭，别为了排场去借钱……”曹寅离开前，胤礽絮絮叨叨。
曹寅捂住耳朵：“知道了知道了，太子殿下您相信我，我不是奢侈的人。”
胤礽：“我不信。你悠着点。”
纳兰性德点头：“我也不信，你还是得好好学学怎么经营家中庶务。”
曹寅一腔感伤都被这两人念叨没了，离开的时候马跑得飞快。
胤礽没想到，曹寅前脚刚走，纳兰性德后脚也要离开。
康熙终于认可了纳兰性德的能力，重用纳兰性德，让纳兰性德出任山西总督。
山西出了很多贪官，康熙整顿了多次吏治都不见成效。
他看着纳兰性德光风霁月，家里又很有钱，不像是能被金钱腐蚀的样子，就把纳兰性德丢进了山西官场的大染缸中。
纳兰性德很高兴，明珠却颇为无语。
他只好不断叮嘱纳兰性德，千万别收别人的钱，家里有钱，不需要纳兰性德受贿。
和胤禔一起来为纳兰性德送行的胤礽哭笑不得。
胤禔还笑话明珠，谁都知道明珠是个大贪官，他怎么好意思说这个。
明珠涨红着脸道，那是以前的事，该罚的皇上都罚过了，现在他的家产是自己攒的。
胤禔给了明珠一个大大的白眼。
是是是，你不是受贿，你自己攒，自己攒，呵呵。
胤礽倒是安抚明珠，说明白明珠现在很清廉。
老实说，清廉肯定谈不上，但明珠确实没有再让依附他的官员送钱了。因为他和索额图去当了奸细，坐到了反太子党头目的位置。为了康熙清算的时候别把他们清算上，他们俩都不敢收官员的东西。
他们俩现在跟着康熙在海外搂钱，搂钱效率比收受敬奉高多了。
这次来纳兰府，胤礽还被纳兰揆叙缠上了。
纳兰揆叙让胤礽检查他的功课，他想现在就去海外。
明珠虎着脸道：“你和你媳妇生个儿子再说！”
纳兰揆叙道：“我和妻子一起去！”
胤礽打圆场：“多去外面走走，身体更健康，说不准更容易生孩子。你若有信心，我和汗阿玛说说，给你一个机会。”
纳兰揆叙得意地对着明珠笑。
明珠吹胡子瞪眼，最终自己也忍不住得意笑了。
两个儿子都很厉害，他当然得意。
索额图他那么多儿子，被揍了很多次之后也只是变老实，完全没有变厉害。索额图已经放弃儿子，开始培养孙子。
他儿子可比索额图厉害多了！这说明索额图那家伙肯定比他差！
我还有一个儿子……
明珠的视线投向自己的小儿子。
才十三岁的纳兰揆方正背贴着墙根慢慢往外溜走。
明珠气沉丹田，大吼道：“混账！你又逃课！”
纳兰揆方像兔子一样跳了起来，拔腿就跑。
明珠和胤礽、胤禔告罪后，挽起袖子一边跟着追，一边指挥仆人对纳兰揆方围追堵截。
胤礽、胤禔和纳兰性德、纳兰揆叙一起抄着手围观。
胤礽：“揆方性子很皮？”
性德：“三弟只是不爱读书。”
胤禔：“你们家居然还有不爱读书的人？！”
揆叙：“他只是不爱仕途学问，只愿学一些风花雪月的诗词，立志要超过大哥。”
胤礽无语。
他想起揆方第一世的妻子也是康亲王的女儿，他将来会成为鄂伦岱的连襟。
杰书那位小女儿也是个才女，夫妻二人游山玩水，吟诗作画，在纳兰家和康亲王家的庇佑下成为了一对富贵闲人，好不快活，可惜双双未到而立之年便英年早逝。
胤礽道：“读书就罢了，他不爱读就不读吧。纳兰家有你们俩人，也养得起一个富贵闲人。但我看他身体有些虚，你们该让他好好锻炼身体。”
胤禔道：“说来容若和容德的身体以前也很虚弱。你们一个爱酒，一个不爱动弹，身体居然比明珠还差。”
纳兰性德：“我现在身体非常好。”
纳兰揆叙：“我现在身体也非常好！我也可以上场杀敌！”
胤礽道：“好了好了，我知道你们身体已经很好，把你们弟弟也操练一番。”
太子都发话了，他们俩再舍不得让幼弟劳累，也答应下来。
纳兰性德虽很快就会离京，但他可以以不指导揆方诗词为由，逼迫揆方不逃武艺课。
送行的宴会，无奈在揆方被明珠罚跪祠堂中草草结束。
这也能看出明珠和太子、直亲王很熟悉了，都不在意他们还在府中。
在明珠揍人的时候，索额图从小门中进来，把太子和直亲王邀请进他家中做客。纳兰性德和纳兰揆叙则去与明珠一同拦着想护着小儿子的觉罗氏，一同教训揆方。
胤禔好奇地看着索额图和明珠围墙上的小门。
索额图解释道：“老臣与纳兰老贼当内应时，得皇上提醒，修了这扇暗门，以随时传递消息。”
胤禔和胤礽对视一眼。
胤禔：我总觉得汗阿玛没安好心。
胤礽：显然是汗阿玛恶趣味的体现。
不久后，鄂伦岱也离开了京城。
他说佟家因佟国维的事声望大减，他得再去立一些更大的功劳。
于是鄂伦岱要去南方，接任两广总督，与开始频频犯边的安南国交涉。
当初安南国与大清合力灭掉广南国之后，一直吞并广南国。
但康熙将广南国设为胤禔封地，安南国便心生不满，不过因为惧怕大清海军，国内局势也不稳固，暂时忍耐下来。
现在郑氏再次废掉一个安南国想要亲政的傀儡皇帝后，安南国□□势稳定下来，他们又开始打广南国那片领土的主意。
两广总督年老请辞，康熙就派有作战经验，且更加锐气十足的鄂伦岱接替两广总督。
这不但是康熙信任鄂伦岱，更是表示自己对佟家的支持。
佟家倒台的只是佟国维，和整个佟家没关系。
鄂伦岱匆匆赴任，走时还请求康熙，把妻子也一同带走。
本来他想带着妻子去海外，却因为佟家的事，不得不留在国内当大官。但即使在国内，鄂伦岱这混不吝的性子也不打算遵循什么传统，准备带着武艺高强的妻子一同建功立业。
康亲王失眠了一宿，第二日黑着眼圈给鄂伦岱和女儿送行。
胤礽与一个个各奔前途的友人分别，他没想到的是，康熙三十二年他最后分别的人，居然是胤禔。
直亲王胤禔请求出海就番，康熙准了。
