chapters.translated_text:
After the princes, there are the Empress Dowager and the princesses, followed by the clansmen with the three titles of Iron-Cap Prince, Prince, and Prince of the Second Rank, and then the officials of the first, secondary first, and second ranks.

Each of these individuals has a subscription quota of one thousand.

Only after these people have finished their subscriptions will the exchange be opened to the common people.

This exchange is purely on a first-come, first-served basis, but each person can only exchange ten gold and silver coins per day, using their household registration.

In other words, those without household registration and "long-term laborers" cannot exchange for gold and silver coins.

Such an exchange system cannot prevent the speculation of gold and silver coins.

Clansmen and officials with subscription quotas can sell their quotas to others at high prices, and merchants who want to speculate on coins can also hire ordinary people to exchange for gold and silver coins.

The reason Kangxi issued this imperial decree was not to stop coin speculation.

No matter how high the price of these first few batches of gold and silver coins is speculated, it will not affect the Qing Dynasty's policy of promoting the new currency.

By doing this, Kangxi is actually adding fuel to the fire—compared to gold and silver coins with low serial numbers that can be snatched up by anyone with money, these gold and silver coins with "subscription qualifications" based on status and rank are clearly more valuable.

As long as they are genuine gold and silver coins, looking at the serial number on the coin tells you what status the person who should have held it had, which invisibly increases the value of the gold and silver coins.

Clansmen and officials who were originally on the sidelines, once they saw that there was such a thing as subscription qualifications, would immediately scramble to subscribe even if they didn't want to support Kangxi's new currency reform before.

When the clansmen and officials have snatched up the first batch of coins, the common people, seeing the lively scene of the upper-class nobles scrambling for the new currency, will be full of confidence in the value of the new currency and will surely exchange for it quickly.

The new currency is worth the same amount no matter when it is exchanged. Stimulated by the subscription system in the front and the purchase limits in the back, the common people all believe that the earlier they exchange for the gold and silver coins, the more valuable they are, and they will definitely take out their family savings to exchange for them at the first opportunity.

The facts were exactly as Kangxi had expected; the common people in the capital, who were originally on the sidelines, were like crazy, lining up every day to exchange for the new currency.

The mint was operating at full capacity, and the coins minted each day were sold out by midday.

In less than two months, there was no trace of traditional gold and silver fragments in the capital; even shops stopped accepting them.

"I know your gold and silver are real, but look at this..." The shopkeeper took out a silver coin of the smallest denomination and flicked it, "This gold and silver is hard to preserve. If it gets nicked or bumped, and the weight decreases, the value shrinks. We all use this now, understand?"

The out-of-town merchant caravans were dumbfounded.

Fortunately, all that is needed for currency exchange is household registration, so they could also go and line up to exchange.

But the daily inventory of gold and silver coins available for exchange was limited, and sometimes they couldn't make it in time.

At this time, bank staff would take out a stack of paper banknotes.

Not enough gold and silver coins? It doesn't matter, you can use paper banknotes. Our banknotes can be exchanged for gold and silver coins at any time, and they have anti-counterfeiting marks and the Emperor's jade seal on them; counterfeiting is a crime punishable by the execution of the entire clan.

"This is just like the silver notes from your money shops; you only get as many banknotes as the gold and silver you deposit. Later, when you pay taxes or something, you can also use banknotes. If you are worried about the value of the banknotes, use them to buy things first, and when you leave the capital, line up early to exchange the banknotes for gold and silver coins."

The leader of the out-of-town merchant caravan thought it made a lot of sense.

He would use banknotes for emergencies for the time being, and exchange them for gold and silver coins when leaving the capital; wouldn't that avoid losses?

When one merchant caravan tried using banknotes for an emergency, it became a routine for subsequent caravans arriving in the capital to exchange for gold and silver coins and banknotes as the first thing they did upon entering the city.

The bank printed many booklets and distributed them to every customer, teaching them how to distinguish between genuine and fake gold and silver coins and banknotes.

Storytellers also added a new service: taking banknotes and gold and silver coins to teach the audience how to distinguish between true and false.

Seeing this trend, the theaters even wrote many plays about true and false currency, teaching the audience how to distinguish between true and false while constantly performing stories of counterfeiters being beheaded.

Under Yinreng's request, the students of Peking University also took the booklets and walked through the streets and alleys, setting up stalls in every dark and poor corner of the capital to explain the new currency so that the poor would not be deceived.

After a period of time, the "university students" of Peking University saw their prestige among the people rise sharply.

Some people in the folk said that these "university students" were knowledgeable and were the true pillars of the country. Unlike those pedantic scholars who took the imperial examinations, who couldn't even fart beyond "zhi hu zhe ye." Letting pedantic scholars govern the country would certainly not be as good as the "university students."

"University students are also good at reading. Besides reading the classics, they also know about natural science, mountains and rivers, and how to help the common people make money. Of course, university students are better than scholars who only read the classics."

"I heard that university students also learn how to fight; they are all both civil and martial."

"The scholar who came to my stall to buy a pancake last time counted on his fingers for a long time and couldn't figure out how many copper coins to give. A university student who was eating a pancake wiped his mouth and immediately stated the correct amount."

"The word 'university' has one more character than 'student,' which must mean they are more powerful."...

It is now the 33rd year of Kangxi, and the imperial examination and the palace examination are being held, with the best scholars from all over the country gathered in the capital.

The students participating in the imperial examination all considered themselves the most powerful scholars, aside from those already serving as officials in the imperial court.

Many students were not participating in the imperial examination for the first time. When they came to the capital in the past, ordinary people would always run over to soak up their "literary star" aura and respect them very much.

But this year, the situation was different. The common people always looked down on them, saying they couldn't count, couldn't tell north from south, and some even complained that they were too weak.

They had heard the words "not as good as university students" countless times.

Of course, they knew there was a "Peking University" in the capital, a place where the Emperor specifically trained the children of nobles and officials, and it had now merged with the Qing Dynasty's Imperial Academy.

This government school was different from the government schools of previous dynasties where noble children just wasted time. It is said that the new trends in the country all started from the university. The Emperor and the Crown Prince also valued university students more; achieving good grades in the university was much easier than getting an official position through the imperial examination.

In this era, information was blocked, and even if they heard rumors about the university, the students didn't necessarily believe them.

They were indignant, and it just so happened that the university had an "Open Day" where any candidate for the examination could make an appointment to visit. Naturally, they immediately took their household registration and examination credentials to enter the university and observe the university students' studies.

Gao Qizhuo was one of them.

Gao Qizhuo was only eighteen this year and could participate in the imperial examination, which could be called a true young talent.

He was also a child of an official family, but his father died early, and the family fell into decline. His elder brother had already given up the imperial examination to provide for his studies and had taken a hereditary position. He had come to the capital with the hopes of his whole family and had always been cautious to prevent any accidents during the imperial examination process.

But he never expected that despite all his precautions, he would run into such a bizarre thing just by visiting the university.

The story goes like this.

According to those who had visited before, there were too many eye-opening things in the university, and it basically took a whole day to visit.

But the food in the university was too expensive, so it was best to bring your own water and dry rations to save money. There were also places selling dry rations and water at the university gate, which were very cost-effective, so you could bring money to buy things at the gate and take them in.

Gao Qizhuo's father died early, and he was raised by his uncles, so he lived very frugally. Naturally, he brought copper coins to the university gate to find food to take in.

Gao Qizhuo was from Tieling, Liaoning. People from his area were generally taller and could eat a lot, and Gao Qizhuo was no exception.

He wandered around with his copper coins for a long time, trying to find a shop where he could buy enough food for the day with the coins in his pocket.

He wandered around, going further and further away, when he suddenly heard a scream.

Rationally speaking, under the feet of the Son of Heaven, Gao Qizhuo certainly shouldn't get involved in bullying incidents. Because if you threw a pole here, you could hit several high-ranking officials.

But Gao Qizhuo hadn't regained his senses yet, thinking he was still in Tieling, so he picked up half a blue brick from the side of the wall and rushed into the small alley where the scream came from.

In the small alley, several tall and sturdy men with yellow belts tied around their waists were being chased and beaten by two thin and weak people.

Seeing someone coming, the tall and sturdy men yelled, "Call someone to save us... Ah! Manbao! You are just a red belt! I am a yellow belt! How dare you beat... Ouch, ouch, Master, Manbao, you are the master, you are my Jue Luo master! Don't hit the face!"

The other thin young man said, "Manbao, stop hitting, someone is coming, let's go!"

Manbao glared at Gao Qizhuo with a gloomy face.

Only after hearing the terms "yellow belt" and "red belt" did Gao Qizhuo realize he shouldn't have acted rashly.

He quickly threw the blue brick in his hand to the side and said, "I didn't see anything."

After saying that, he prepared to turn and run.

At this moment, a team of people carrying sticks rushed out from the other end of the alley.

"Run!"

The two thin young men immediately let go of the people on the ground and ran towards Gao Qizhuo.

The young man named Manbao stumbled and almost fell to the ground, and Gao Qizhuo reflexively helped him up.

"Beat those three people in front to death for me!"

Three? Gao Qizhuo was stunned, then turned and ran.

How did they count him in!

All three had long legs and ran very fast. The servants behind waved their sticks and chased hard.

On both sides, street vendors opened large umbrellas to cover their stoves; customers eating at roadside stalls who were far from the main road covered their bowls, and those close to the main road held their bowls and walked to the side while eating.

Apparently, the noble and official children in the university were young and vigorous, and fighting was very common, so the people nearby were already very used to it.

Gao Qizhuo, who had suffered an undeserved disaster, didn't know the way and could only follow the two thin young men in front.

But I don't know if he had been too unlucky lately, just as he was about to distance himself from the people behind, he was blocked by a carriage.

When the carriage saw a team of people carrying sticks rushing over, it didn't drive away, but stopped and blocked the road tightly.

A thin hand wearing a gold-inlaid jade ring stretched out of the carriage window, lifted the curtain a little, and then retracted it.

"Yo hey!"

A young man jumped off the carriage.

Then a line of young men and little boys jumped off the carriage, a full eight of them.

Gao Qizhuo, who almost crashed into the carriage, was shocked.

How did so many people fit in this small carriage?

After he stopped, he realized that the plain-looking carriage with inconspicuous decorations was not small at all; it was actually pulled by four horses.

The two thin young men running in front of him were slightly stunned and wanted to run to the side.

The two tallest people among this group of young men kicked the knees of those two, grabbed their arms, and pressed them to the ground.

"Running away?"

"You crashed into my brother's carriage and still want to run? Ouch, isn't this Fahai?"

Fahai looked desperate.

The thin young man next to him looked at Fahai, then at the group of young men who were smiling and rushing towards the servants with sticks, and the expression on his face gradually became desperate.

Only Gao Qizhuo stood there foolishly, out of place with the entire noisy atmosphere.

The young men had already rushed behind him. Some pulled whips from their waists, and some used scabbards directly to beat the group of servants, who were fierce in appearance but weak in reality, until they were howling and screaming, constantly shouting "We are from the mansion of Prince XX, Beile, Beizi," trying to scare away this group of highly skilled young men.

But this group of young men laughed even more happily.

"Prince's mansion? The master is beating the people from the Prince's mansion!"

"Except for the people from the Zhi Prince's mansion, which Prince's mansion do I dare not beat?"

"Isn't it even more daring to beat people from the Zhi Prince's mansion? If they are from the Zhi Prince's mansion, we are saving them by beating them."

"Interesting, someone actually dares to fight at the gate of the university, all of you go to jail for me!"

Upon hearing "jail," Gao Qizhuo was desperate.

He was here to take the imperial examination! If he was thrown into jail, what would happen to the examination?!

Gao Qizhuo wanted to run away, but a team of well-dressed guards rushed over and surrounded the place, and he couldn't run at all.

Just when Gao Qizhuo was desperate, a handsome and gentle voice came from the carriage: "No need to arrest the three people in front of the carriage. Third brother, fourth brother, take them to the carriage behind, and you two ask what happened."

"Alright, second brother." The two released the people they were pressing on the ground, "Walk yourselves, do you want me to invite you?"

Fahai said with a bitter face, "Can you not tell my big brother?"

Yin Zhi smiled and said, "You guess?"

Yinzhen said with a straight face, "The imperial examination is coming up soon, and you don't stay at home to study properly, but run out to fight? Are you going to make E'lundai so angry that he writes a letter home from the Annan battlefield to scold you? Are you embarrassed? And you..."

Yinzhen's gaze shifted to the thin young man's red belt: "Are you a Jue Luo?"

The man nodded, his lips moving, not knowing how to salute.

"Forget it, get in the carriage first." Yinzhen looked at Gao Qizhuo again, "How did you get mixed up with them? Judging by your clothes, you are a student who came to the capital for the examination, right?"

Gao Qizhuo quickly said, "This humble person heard someone calling for help, so I rushed to save them, and then I was chased by a group of servants. This humble person doesn't know what happened either."

Seeing the carriage of this group of young men, their attitude towards the servants of the Prince's mansion and the red-belted Jue Luo, and the respectful appearance of the guard leader nearby, he knew that this group of people were definitely high-ranking officials he couldn't afford to offend, so he immediately used the most humble self-address.

"Really?" Yinzhen looked at Fahai.

Fahai said muffledly, "It's true. He was implicated by me and Manbao."

Manbao also nodded.

Gao Qizhuo breathed a sigh of relief. It seems that the thin young men named Fahai and Manbao are not bad, at least they know how to clear him, an innocent person.

He was about to say goodbye, but Yin Zhi said, "Alright, alright, we'll talk slowly when we get on the carriage. You come too."

Gao Qizhuo: "..." Can I not come! Isn't the misunderstanding already cleared up!

Fahai and Manbao lowered their heads and followed Yin Zhi and Yinzhen into the carriage. Gao Qizhuo glanced at the surrounding guards and followed them into the carriage in terror.

He regretted it, he really regretted it very much. Why did he reflexively rush out when he heard a cry for help?

His brother said that this habit of his would kill him sooner or later.

Look, even if he isn't killed, this imperial examination might be ruined.

I hope it only delays this imperial examination, and I can still participate in the next one. Don't strip me of my status as a scholar!

Gao Qizhuo was full of despair.

Fahai and Manbao were also very desperate.

Manbao was also worried that his imperial examination would be ruined, and he wouldn't even be able to pursue an official career in the future.

Thinking of his mother, who worked hard at home, supported their three brothers with needlework and the meager subsidy of the Jue Luo, and whose eyes were already a bit blurry, he couldn't help but clench his fists.

But the other party insulted his mother, and even if it happened again, he couldn't swallow this breath no matter what.

Fahai's despair had nothing to do with the imperial examination or his official career.

He was just desperate that he had finally fought once, and was caught red-handed by the Crown Prince and a group of princes.

Was his usual serious and upright scholar image going to be ruined like this?

Ruined is one thing, but what if His Highness the Crown Prince tells his big brother about this? Fahai had very complex feelings about E'lundai—he was unconvinced and admired him, and had a lot of dissatisfaction. So he would rather not take the Jinshi examination this time than have E'lundai write a letter to reprimand him.

But if he couldn't take the Jinshi examination this time, E'lundai would find out, right?

Fahai held his head: "Your Highness Prince Cheng, Your Highness Prince Yong, please give me a trick, what should I do so that you won't tell my big brother about this?"

Prince Cheng, Prince Yong?

Manbao took a deep breath, showing a desperate expression of "as expected."

He had only seen the princes in the palace from afar when he was studying at the university, and he didn't remember their appearances clearly; he only inferred their identities from the arrogant attitude of this group of people.

How unlucky was he to be blocked and beaten before the imperial examination, and also run into the princes?

The most terrible thing is, could His Highness the Crown Prince, whom he admires the most, be there too?!

Even though Manbao had already heard the Prince Cheng and Prince Yong in front of him say the term "second brother," he was still holding onto luck (self-deception).

Only Gao Qizhuo was still standing there foolishly.

Prince Cheng? Prince Yong? Who are they?

Kangxi's conferring of princes was not like later generations, where it would be broadcast on television news countless times. Gao Qizhuo, who was in Tieling, had never heard the titles of Prince Cheng and Prince Yong.

In fact, if someone had connections in the capital, the first thing they would do upon arriving in the capital was to inquire about who they shouldn't offend, so as to avoid trouble.

But unfortunately, Gao Qizhuo was a poor scholar whose father died early; he had no connections and no money to inquire.

100,000

223. Two updates combined [V]

Yinreng led the university open day, letting students understand the benefits of the university, in preparation for the opening of the next university.

He brought his younger brothers to observe the effect of the university open day, and as soon as he arrived, he encountered a fight, which made his face black with anger.

Yinreng brought a group of younger brothers and the three people involved in the fight to the Zhi Prince's mansion—the Zhi Prince's mansion had completely become a "den" for the Crown Prince to bring his cubs, and Kangxi also allocated many palace servants to the Zhi Prince's mansion to serve the Crown Prince and a group of princes.

Yinreng sat in the head seat, and the group of princes sat in two rows according to odd and even numbers, just like a mountain stronghold leader holding a meeting. In the middle of the hall, there were three stools, and the three poor scholars shrank their shoulders, just like small minions being interrogated by the mountain stronghold leader.

Yinreng brushed the tea leaves with the cup lid, took a sip of tea, and then said slowly, "Do you three know you were wrong?"

This was the first time he had spoken to someone he admired, and it was in this situation. Manbao said with a gray face, "I should have run away, I shouldn't have fought back."

Knowing that his ugly behavior today would definitely be told to E'lundai by the princes, Fahai said with dull eyes, "I should have pulled Manbao to run away first, and settled the account later, instead of rushing up to fight with people."

Even though Gao Qizhuo was dizzy and entered the Zhi Prince's mansion, he still didn't know who the person in front of him was. Because when he entered the Zhi Prince's mansion, he had no chance to stick his head out of the carriage window to see the plaque.

He didn't know why he encountered such a bizarre thing, and he was crying without tears: "I, I... I shouldn't have forgotten that this is the capital, and I can't just rush out."

Yinreng put the teacup on the table and said, "Sixth brother, tell them where they went wrong."

Yinzuo smiled and said, "That group of people blocked Manbao because they wanted to grab Manbao's family land and insulted Manbao's mother. It was impossible not to fight back. Fahai is loyal and righteous, and it is also a matter of temperament to advance and retreat with Manbao. As for this student surnamed Gao, he boldly went to save people when he heard someone calling for help, which is even less of a mistake."

The three looked up at the Sixth Prince, with a glimmer of hope shining in their eyes.

Yinzuo continued: "But their timing was indeed wrong, and their methods were also wrong. Even if they couldn't swallow this breath, they could have smarter ways. For example, Fahai, have you forgotten that you are the cousin of Khan Ama? Have you forgotten how protective your big brother is? Have you forgotten that your teacher is Nalan Xingde? If you reveal your identity, who would dare to beat you? Do you understand how to borrow power? You learn from the playboy's fighting, why don't you learn from the playboy's way of suppressing people with power?"

Fahai's lips moved. He just didn't like to suppress people with power and wanted to succeed on his own.

Yinzuo said again: "Manbao, the university is right next to you. Whether you climb over the wall into the university to ask for help, or go to the busy street and describe your humiliation passionately, and then say that you would rather be punished than beat this group of people who insulted your mother. Even if you fight in front of everyone, you won't be punished, and you might even be rewarded. You also have power you can borrow, understand?"

Manbao nodded vigorously, his face even grayer. I am really stupid, really, I have lived for so many years in vain.

"As for Student Gao, your only mistake was indeed forgetting that in the capital, you have no ability or skill to save people, and you will only implicate yourself. But I admire this character of yours." Yinzuo said to Yinreng, "Crown Prince brother, this kind of fool is really rare."

Yinreng subtly felt that he had been scolded.

Because his third life was sacrificed for righteous deeds.

He looked at the student who almost lost his qualification for the imperial examination because of his righteous deeds, and always felt that this person's name was familiar.

Yinreng asked, "What is your ancestral home?"

Crown Prince brother... Crown Prince brother... Crown Prince brother... These four words kept echoing in Gao Qizhuo's ears.

Gao Qizhuo, who was already completely stupid, reflexively replied: "This humble person... This humble person's ancestral home is Tieling."

Yinreng nodded, the ancestral home matched: "What relatives do you have at home? How are your parents and brothers?"

Gao Qizhuo said sadly: "My father died early, and my mother has also passed away. I only have one elder brother."

Yinreng said: "Are you in the Han Army Banner?"

Although Gao Qizhuo didn't know why the Crown Prince knew, he nodded and replied: "Yes, this humble person is in the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner."

Yinreng was puzzled.

The Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner and the second son in the family matched, but this father didn't match.

In the 33rd year of Kangxi, Yinreng, who was not yet married, had a good relationship with Kangxi. During the palace examination, Kangxi taught Yinreng how to choose Jinshi, and Yinreng also participated in the ranking of the palace examination, so Yinreng had a memory of this list of Jinshi.

In his second life, Yinreng unconsciously paid attention to the officials with political achievements in the Kangxi, Yongzheng, and Qianlong dynasties, and remembered many capable ministers.

So he felt very familiar as soon as he heard the name Gao Qizhuo.

Yinreng, who had turned on the memory cheat, soon dug out a person with the same name from the depths of his memory.

Especially when his mother happily asked him, now that he had achieved the rank of Jinshi, whether he could be buried in the Tong family ancestral grave, Fahai felt miserable.

Mingzhu pondered for a moment and said, "Given Elundai's temperament, not only will he not reprimand you, but he will also praise you. Why? He is good to you, yet you are unhappy?"

Fahai hung his head and remained silent.

Jue-luo-shi, who was bringing snacks to supplement Mingzhu and Fahai's meal, saw this and sighed, "It's for your mother, isn't it?"

Mingzhu was puzzled: "What's wrong with his mother? Elundai is so far from the capital, and he even took the Heshuo Gege with him; isn't the Tong household still managed by his mother? Could anyone possibly give her a hard time?"

"You don't understand the affairs of the inner courtyard," Jue-luo-shi said. "It is precisely because she now has the power of the mistress of the house that she has developed even greater ambitions. If she only wanted a title of honor, with Fahai's abilities, that wouldn't be impossible in the future. What is most feared is if she wants to enter the Tong family ancestral grave and be buried with Tong Guogang..."

Mingzhu frowned: "Even with a title, one is buried separately. How could a concubine enter the ancestral grave? Where would the face of Tong Guogang's primary wife be placed!"

Fahai's head hung even lower.

Seeing this, Mingzhu scolded: "Is your mother really forcing you with this matter? You must not be muddled about this. If you open your mouth to ask for this, Elundai will certainly not agree. The Tong family only has you three brothers left; if a rift arises because of this, wouldn't the Tong family be in an even more difficult position? Listen to me, properly persuade your mother. There is more to posthumous honors than just being buried in the ancestral grave. You just need to be a good high-ranking official, earn a title, and when the time comes, you can request a title of honor for your mother, build a grand tomb, or even build a separate temple to worship her—wouldn't that still be very glorious?"

Jue-luo-shi also persuaded: "In the future, you can have your mother buried with you, so she can accompany you in the afterlife and enjoy family happiness. Isn't that better than trying to follow Tong Guogang and continuing to serve others?"

Fahai wiped away his tears and said, "I don't want to have a rift with my eldest brother and third brother either. It's just that my mother said her only wish in this life is to be buried in the ancestral grave and hold her head high, I..."

Mingzhu and Jue-luo-shi exchanged glances, their expressions helpless.

This was very troublesome.

"Drag it out, take it one step at a time," Mingzhu said. "Or you can promise her that you will work hard, and when the time comes, donate a temple for your mother and erect a merit stele; that counts as doing your best. One must learn to be flexible."

Fahai was dumbfounded. Did this mean... to deceive her first?

The naive lad Fahai left the Nalan mansion in a daze.

Mingzhu said to Jue-luo-shi, "Do you think this kid can be flexible?"

Jue-luo-shi shook her head: "The people of the Tong family are all very stubborn; I'm afraid it's difficult. But you don't need to worry. Even if he falls out with Elundai over this and they never see each other again, if they encounter any issues in the imperial court in the future, they will certainly still help each other out of tacit understanding. After all, they are biological brothers; blood is thicker than water."

Mingzhu said: "I'd believe that for other families, but for the Tong family..."

Mingzhu shook his head. Tong Guowei's cautionary tale was right there.

Fahai was his son's only indoor disciple. If Fahai and Elundai fell out, his son would certainly be in a difficult position. Mingzhu thought about it and went to discuss with Songgotu if there was any way to resolve this matter.

Songgotu rolled his eyes: "This is simple. Leave it to me."

Mingzhu looked at him with disdain: "Simple? Fine, I'd like to see what method you have."

Songgotu snorted: "Wait and see!"

A few days later, while Kangxi was reviewing memorials with Yinreng, he saw a pile of memorials impeaching Elundai and Fahai for fighting among themselves.

The father and son were dumbfounded. Elundai was so far away, how could he be fighting with Fahai?

Kangxi: "Shall we go and watch the show?"

Yinreng threw down the memorial: "Sure!"

Thus, the father and son set aside state affairs, quietly disguised themselves, and left the palace to gather information.

Although they could have directly summoned guards to inquire, where was the fun in that compared to going out to find out for themselves?

After some investigation, it turned out that Fahai wanted his mother to enter the ancestral grave, Elundai firmly disagreed, the two brothers had broken off relations, and Fahai wanted to leave the Tong family and establish a separate lineage.

Fahai even said, "What's a primary wife? What's Jue-luo-shi? Can't my mother, the mother of a Jinshi, overturn all of this?"

Kangxi and Yinreng were full of question marks.

Kangxi asked: "Baocheng, do you think this is something Fahai would do?"

Yinreng hesitated. He really wasn't sure, because in original history, Fahai did indeed fall out with Elundai over this matter.

But back then, Fahai had already become the teacher of the Fourteenth Prince and considered himself a teacher of an imperial prince, which gave him the confidence. Now, Fahai shouldn't be this reckless, right?

Yinreng said: "Shall we go and ask?"

Kangxi thought of the Tong mansion, frowned for a while, and then said: "Fine."

He hadn't been to the Tong mansion in a long time.

When the father and son arrived at the Tong mansion, both Fahai and Kuadai were terrified.

This rumor actually alarmed the Emperor and the Crown Prince? Would Fahai's Jinshi position be gone?

Fahai was almost in tears: "Your Majesty, I didn't, I haven't done this, I haven't said these things!"

Kuadai also spoke up for his second brother: "My second brother's mother indeed had this thought, but my second brother did not agree and has been suffering over this, not daring to let my eldest brother know."

Kangxi was amused: "But now it's spread all over the capital that you, kid, are going to split the clan out of filial piety. So, are you splitting or not? If you want to split, I will make the decision for you."

Yinreng was speechless. He thought Kangxi would offer some advice, but he didn't expect Kangxi to add fuel to the fire.

Yinreng said: "Since your mother wants to be buried in the ancestral grave, she certainly wouldn't want you to split the clan. Kuadai nodded: "The concubine has indeed been holding my second brother and crying, saying she doesn't want to leave the Tong family and won't let my second brother split the clan."

Kuadai was actually quite disgusted by this matter and had at one point not wanted to deal with his second brother.

But seeing his second brother in such pain, and knowing this was indeed a frame-up by someone else, Kuadai, who was soft-hearted toward his brothers, couldn't stay angry and had been thinking about how to help Fahai clear his name.

As a companion to the Prince Zhijun, Kuadai was now a second-rank imperial guard and had extensive connections. Yet, he couldn't find out who was slandering his second brother.

In the end, he could only attribute it to political enemies who wanted the Tong family to suffer.

After learning the cause and effect, Kangxi left with satisfaction.

On the way back to the palace, Kangxi asked: "Baocheng, who do you think is behind this?"

Yinreng said: "This matter appears to be an impeachment of Elundai and Fahai, but in reality, it acted like pulling the firewood from under the cauldron, removing the worries of Elundai and Fahai and crudely smoothing over the rift between them. Kangxi nodded: "This method is very familiar. Who did you think of?"

Yinreng said: "What about you, Khan Ama?"

Kangxi laughed: "You write the person you suspect on a piece of paper, and we'll exchange."

After Yinreng and Kangxi finished writing, they exchanged and looked. Yinreng had written "Mingzhu," while Kangxi had written "Mingzhu, Songgotu."

Yinreng was puzzled: "It's normal for Mingzhu to care about Fahai, but why did the Uncle Grand-Uncle get involved?"

Kangxi said: "There were people of Songgotu among those who impeached them. Ever since those two old fellows stopped fighting, they like to do everything together when looking for fun. Perhaps Mingzhu found Songgotu, and they acted together."

Yinreng was even more stunned: "Since when did they get along so well?"

Kangxi laughed heartily: "Since they started acting as undercover agents against the anti-Crown Prince party, perhaps?"

After laughing, Kangxi sighed again: "Actually, they were always this close. When we were getting rid of Oboi, I discussed everything with them. They were my playmates and my right-hand men. It's just that later..."

After sighing, Kangxi smiled and shook his head: "They fought their whole lives, and now that they are old, they've become friends again. That's good."

As the older generation of officials passed away one by one, Kangxi felt lonely while becoming increasingly soft-hearted toward the old ministers.

After a series of twists and turns, Songgotu and Mingzhu had become his right-hand men once again, fully supporting all his reforms, and Kangxi's feelings for them became increasingly close.

Yinreng held his forehead: "Friends? You must never let Mingzhu and Songgotu hear you describe their relationship like that, they would probably vomit, right?"

Kangxi laughed so hard he almost choked.

On the already concluded Annam battlefield, Elundai learned about the events in the capital and frowned: "Split the clan? Fahai wants to split the clan with me?!"

Yinzhi leaned over to look: "It's fake. It's probably Mingzhu's doing. He wanted to pull the firewood from under the cauldron, scare Fahai's mother, and make her stop bothering Fahai with this matter."

Elundai said: "Mingzhu? Why would he do that?"

Yinzhi said: "Are you stupid? Fahai is Rongruo's disciple, and you are Rongruo's friend. If Fahai fights with you, how difficult would it be for Rongruo? Mingzhu dotes on Rongruo so much; whoever makes Rongruo feel troubled, he solves them."

Yinzhi paused for a moment and added: "Except for himself."

Elundai chuckled.

What a "except for Mingzhu himself." Indeed, before, that guy Rongruo was so worried he almost died, and it wasn't because of any romance, but because of Mingzhu's ambition.

Rongruo was so smart that he saw through Mingzhu's ambition and the potential downfall of the Nalan family at a glance. As a subject, he didn't want to be disloyal to Kangxi, who had always valued him; as a son, he couldn't be unfilial and didn't want to go against Mingzhu.

Wasn't that why he was so depressed he almost died?

"So this matter is settled? That woman won't make a scene anymore?" Elundai said.

Yinzhi said: "What else is there to make a scene about? Didn't Fahai already make a scene for her, wanting to break off the brotherly relationship with you and split the clan with her? With such a filial son, what else could she be dissatisfied with?"

Elundai laughed heartily: "Yes, yes, yes, Fahai was even going to split the clan for her, truly filial. In consideration of Fahai's filial piety, I won't hold it against her. Except for the ancestral grave matter, which I will absolutely not compromise on, as for the rest, after she dies, I will petition the Emperor to posthumously grant her a title, which will be doing right by Fahai."

Yinzhi said: "His mother's title, let him earn it himself; why bother you? You aren't the one who gave birth to or raised him, though you are currently supporting his whole family."

Elundai touched his nose and said nothing.

With Tong Guogang dead and Tong Guowei's family scattered, he only had these two relatives left, so it was impossible to say he wouldn't care. Now that he was the head of the household, Elundai's mindset was very different from before.

"Alright, let's not talk about this. You can handle the cleanup of the battlefield here in Annam. I don't think that Later Le Dynasty is of much use; just like in the Yongle Emperor's time, let's abolish the vassal state and establish a province. I'll go tell Khan Ama," Yinzhi said. "Help me take care of the Princess; I'm going to Europe."

Elundai was puzzled: "Europe? Prince Zhijun, what are you going to Europe for?"

Yinzhi said: "Don't worry about my affairs; just do your own job well."

Elundai said: "But if you leave the vassal state without authorization, how will you answer to the Emperor?"

Yinzhi rolled his eyes at Elundai: "What answer do I need? I've already told Khan Ama; I won't just stay obediently in the vassal state. Khan Ama has already given me an imperial decree to act as I see fit."

Elundai laughed: "If there's a decree, I won't try to persuade you. The Princess will stay with my Gege, so there will definitely be no trouble. When Prince Zhijun returns, there might already be a big fat boy."

Yinzhi said: "I won't be gone that long; I'm just going for a spin and will be back soon."

According to Baocheng's prophecy, the Great Cold Disaster in Europe should have begun to show its consequences.

For such an important matter, Yinzhi wanted to see it for himself. Once it was confirmed that Europe had a food crisis, he could descend upon Europe as a savior and boost the reputation of the Great Qing.

Yinzhi had a sufficient reason for the diplomatic mission. Now that he was a vassal king in charge of the Baoqing Strait trade route, how could he not greet his old friends in Europe and offer everyone some discounts?

Thinking of the name "Baoqing Strait," Yinzhi's face darkened slightly.

His Khan Ama must have had something seriously wrong with his head to change the strait to this name.

Hearing Yinzhī speak with such gravity, the first to jump up and agree with both hands was not Yinzi or Yinzhen, who were already quite arrogant and unrestrained in the court, but the honest man, Yinqi.

Yinqi said indignantly, "Exactly! Those people are simply not normal human beings!"

Seeing Yinqi so angry, Yinzi and Yinzhen exchanged glances, their vigilance toward the overseas nations doubling.

Yinqi was in charge of the Lifan Yuan (Court of Colonial Affairs). If those overseas people could make an honest man like Yinqi turn into a fire-breathing monster, they must truly be formidable.

The three of them tried hard to adjust their mindset and think about how to be arrogant.

But when they followed Yinzhī to the West and saw him cordially bumping fists and hugging the European kings and heads of state who came to welcome them, draping his arms over their shoulders with such intimacy as if they were long-lost best friends, they were all dumbfounded.

Yinzi: "Big Brother, what happened to being vigilant toward all Westerners?"

Yinzhen: "Big Brother said we shouldn't be nice to foreigners, that we should be arrogant, and that we shouldn't talk about feelings, only interests. Does hooking arms, calling each other brothers, and going hunting and drinking together mean we have a bad relationship in Western customs?"

Yinqi: "I miss Crown Prince Brother."

Big Brother! When you teach us, can you not say one thing and do another! How are we supposed to learn from you!

The three younger brothers were extremely confused.

Yinzhī rolled his eyes at his three younger brothers.

Watch closely and learn. I call them brothers, but behind it all, it is for the benefit of the Great Qing and Baocheng.

And are you all blind? Can't you see I'm just putting on a show?

The three "visually impaired" brothers really couldn't tell. Because Big Brother was laughing and having fun with those kings and leaders from the bottom of his heart, and he received many gifts from them!

Even when Big Brother wanted to return the gifts, they refused to accept them, only asking for some of Big Brother's calligraphy or some random paintings.

According to Big Brother's logic: Westerners don't understand etiquette; if you are good to them, they accept it while bad-mouthing you behind your back.

According to Big Brother's actions: Westerners give gifts, Big Brother accepts, Big Brother doesn't return the favor, and Big Brother still bad-mouths them behind their backs.

Who is the rude beast in human skin here?!!!

……

"Ugh... the younger brothers seem a bit confused," Yinreng sighed. "Big Brother... Big Brother needs to take it easy. With his talent, how are the younger brothers supposed to learn?"

Yinzhī's talent was too strong; he could inexplicably become best friends with many kings and future kings.

He had the title of the "Perfect Crown Prince" in the West, but in terms of personal relationships, his bond with those Western kings and future kings was definitely not as deep as Yinzhī's.

Yinzhī was a "King's Best Friend" who could sway someone's governing policy in just a few words.

Everyone thought the Great Qing's Prince Zhi had no schemes, was straightforward, and was a hearty person completely unrelated to politics and etiquette.

How are you supposed to let the younger brothers learn from that? Big Brother, can you teach them something they can actually learn!

Yinreng sighed: "Father Emperor, I still think I should go overseas now to help the younger brothers solve their problems."

Kangxi ruffled Yinreng's hair and said earnestly, "Younger brothers have their own fortunes. Besides, Prince Zhi has always been a very reliable and steady person; how can you not trust your big brother?"

Yinreng was speechless.

First of all, there is no such saying as "younger brothers have their own fortunes," only "children and grandchildren have their own fortunes."

Secondly, Big Brother is reliable and steady? I do think Big Brother is reliable and steady, but Father Emperor, do you even believe what you're saying?

But Kangxi wouldn't budge, and Yinreng was helpless.

He could only sigh and turn the letters of distress from his overseas brothers into new exercises, assigning them as homework to his other brothers.

"You will all go overseas to broaden your horizons in the future. If you look at your brothers' confusion now, it will be much easier when you go out later."

The younger brothers, who were busy as can be in the court, had to deal with the excessive homework assigned by the imperial tutors, and even had to participate in university exams: "..."

Crown Prince Brother, do you know the idiom "pulling up seedlings to help them grow"?

Even if your brothers are capable, you can't exploit them like this!

Yinreng sighed: "If you can't finish your homework, don't you know how to knock on the ministers' doors? Here, this is an imperial decree I requested from Father Emperor for you. With these decrees, you can knock on any minister's door and have them help you with your homework. Father Emperor and I both have think tanks; you should have them too. How can you be princes without support? And there are students in the university; you can assign the homework I gave you to them as well."

The princes looked at each other, holding the imperial decrees.

What does this mean? Forming cliques by imperial order?

Well, since it's the expectation of Father Emperor and Crown Prince Brother.

The group of princes had no choice but to take the decrees and go knock on the ministers' doors separately.

"Open up! Open up! Minister XX, help me with my homework!"

The ministers opened their doors, completely bewildered.

Your Majesty! Crown Prince! What new way have you thought of to torment us!

The ministers were on the verge of tears.

They had to work, take remedial classes, pass exams, and now help the princes with their homework.

Your Majesty! Crown Prince! People will die if they are exploited like this!

"Baocheng, the ministers have been much quieter lately, and the complaint memorials have disappeared."

"Yes, Father Emperor, the ministers have finally understood your painstaking efforts."

The father and son high-fived, feeling very gratified.

100,000

226. Third and Fourth Update [V]

Just as the Great Qing ministers finally understood the painstaking efforts of Kangxi and Yinreng (they didn't), and were working together to build a prosperous Great Qing, life in the West became very difficult.

The Tsardom of Russia and the Ottoman Empire were locked in an inextricable war; England and France, having each propped up puppets to vie for the Spanish throne, ignited the Anglo-French War once again, dragging the entire European continent into it.

Land wars are always meat grinders and money pits.

The two great powers, England and France, slaughtered each other on the battlefield, their national strength being consumed crazily.

By this time, the ruler of England was already William III.

Under the persuasion of his best friend, the Great Qing's Prince Zhi, James II led his Catholic supporters to renounce the English throne and head to the New World to open up "New England."

James II's daughter, Princess Mary, and her husband, the Dutch Stadtholder William III, were welcomed to England by the Church of England, ruling as joint monarchs.

This great, bloodless regime change was later known as the "Glorious Revolution."

The English finally got rid of the evil Catholic king and welcomed a new, enlightened king who only believed in Protestantism, and the power of Parliament soared, basically establishing a new political system of constitutional monarchy.

The English Catholics also had a wise leader to take them to open up new territories, no longer fearing persecution by the Church of England.

The English viewed the Great Qing Crown Prince, who supported Queen Mary and William III, as a friend; the new English viewed Prince Zhi, James II's best friend, as an Eastern sage who guided the saint.

In short, England's national strength (in their own view) reached a result that both sides were satisfied with without any consumption; England got rid of the chaotic political situation, and its strength soared.

William III also introduced a large amount of Dutch investment into England and brought the advanced Dutch economic operating model to England. The British military was refreshed, and the economic landscape was completely different.

Under such premises, it was only natural for William III to dare to go to war with the Sun King, Louis XIV.

It should have been like this.

But who would have thought that a huge cold disaster would sweep across the European continent, breaking the delicate balance between war consumption and gains, and the European commoners seemed to be unable to survive overnight.

But this war, which had spread across the entire European continent, could not be stopped just because one wanted it to.

Consequently, the reputations of William III and Louis XIV in their respective countries plummeted, and their public opinion turned sharply downward.

The French no longer called Louis XIV the Sun King, the British tried to block William III's orders, and even the Dutch cursed William III for sucking the blood of the Dutch to support the British.

The Dutch originally invested in England because it was profitable. When they were making money, they called William III the wisest and greatest king. Now that they were losing money, William III became a traitor to the Netherlands.

Yinreng received this news from afar in the Great Qing and sighed with a smile.

History is a circle. Many situations in modern society can find shadows in history. For example, the current Dutch, don't they look like the stock investors of later generations?

By the time Yinzhī dragged his feet to the European continent to wait for his three younger brothers, it was already September in the solar calendar.

At this time, Europe was about to enter its darkest moment.

At this time, Yinreng's letter also arrived.

Yinzhī squeezed Yinreng's letter and smiled, telling his younger brothers to buck up, and to mobilize all the officials and folk scholars who remained in Europe for visits and work, and have them lobby the European countries to mediate the war.

"The great cold disaster and the war have made life miserable for the people of Europe. Europeans are also human, born of parents. My Great Qing is a land of etiquette and righteousness, and cannot bear to see people suffer. You take my recommendation letters and go lobby the various countries, hoping they can stop the war and work together to save the people," Yinzhī's grand principles came one after another. "The best strategy is to stop the war, the middle strategy is to cease fire, and the worst strategy is for us to sell them grain at a low price to help them with disaster relief. Although the Great Qing's national strength is limited, we cannot bear to see the people suffer, and we are willing to squeeze grain from our own teeth to help our friendly neighbors."

Yinzhī's three younger brothers: "..."

The officials and folk scholars: "..."

If this were said by the Crown Prince, they would believe it. But coming from Prince Zhi, why did they always feel that Prince Zhi was like a weasel paying a New Year's call to a chicken, with no good intentions?

However, the power to mobilize grain was in the hands of the Emperor, and Prince Zhi was only acting on orders.

The Emperor and the Crown Prince were benevolent, so doing such things was normal. They only had prejudices against Prince Zhi, which was why they were suspicious.

Even if the Great Qing's officials and folk scholars didn't have a heart of benevolence, they hoped to leave their names in history by mediating the European war.

The officials and the literati of the folk visiting delegation were all well-read, and they knew the allusions in historical books by heart.

Anyone who has read history knows that the most brilliant time was the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods.

Isn't Europe now exactly like the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods?

If the brilliant stories they had read in history books could be realized in the European Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, maybe they could also earn the title of a sage in the future.

And this was mediating an overseas war, which sounded even more impressive than fighting among themselves at home.

Of course, among these people, there were also truly benevolent people who truly believed that Europeans were also human.

For example, Gu Yanwu and others who were already very old but whose health was getting better and better.

They had some trouble acclimatizing after coming to Europe, but after seeing the unique customs and traditions, the fire of their ideals burned fiercely in their hearts, and it seemed that their bodies had even become younger.

They had been overseas for several years.

In these years, the ships of the Great Qing folk scholar visiting delegation had been coming and going, and people had changed several batches, but none of the old men who had met Yinreng before the visit had returned.

Yinreng specifically instructed the Qing army to take care of them. They lived in the same manor in the Netherlands, went out together, made foreign friends together, and came back together to organize their experiences and write books.

When Europe became chaotic, they couldn't bear to see the people suffer, and coupled with their poor health, they originally planned to return to the country to organize their drafts, print the new books into volumes, and fulfill their last wish.

But after Yinzhī's words, they changed their minds.

These old men, with one foot in the grave, remembered the various tragic events of the Central Plains people after the Qing army entered the pass, and couldn't help but empathize.

They had struggled, they had escaped, and in the end, they had lost all their dreams.

Now that history seemed to be repeating itself, even if they couldn't settle their regrets, at least doing what they should do at the last moment of their lives, saving a few lives, could be considered not in vain for their twilight years.

In the letter Yinreng sent to Yinzhī, there were words asking Yinzhī to take good care of Gu Yanwu and the other old men and have them return to the capital quickly.

Yinzhī had already prepared a ship for them, but they were unwilling to leave.

Yinzhī couldn't be bothered to care about other people he didn't know, so he just found Gu Yanwu and said, "You are Baocheng's teacher. If you die here, how can I explain it to Baocheng? You also know how soft-hearted Baocheng is to those close to him. I will never let Baocheng be sad for you. If you don't leave, I'll tie you up and take you away."

Gu Yanwu sighed: "Prince Zhi, give this letter of mine to the Crown Prince. If the Crown Prince still insists on me leaving after reading it, I will leave."

Yinzhī was speechless: "I think you're just stalling for time. Forget it, isn't it just letting a steamship make a trip? I can afford this bit of money."

Yinzhī knew Gu Yanwu was stubborn, and if he forced Gu Yanwu away, there might be an accident on the way. Since Gu Yanwu had relented, he would do as Gu Yanwu said.

Yinzhī originally thought that no matter what Gu Yanwu wrote, Yinreng would not agree to the elderly Gu Yanwu staying in the troubled times of Europe.

But after Yinreng saw the letter, he let out a long sigh and couldn't say a word of refusal.

Confucius spoke of benevolence, Mencius spoke of righteousness. A person's death may be heavier than Mount Tai or lighter than a goose feather.

It is a principle that every scholar knows, but very few can practice it.

Just as great generals would rather die on horseback during a campaign than die in pain and memories.

Gu Yanwu would rather die on the road to realizing his dreams than die on a warm bed.

"The rise and fall of the world is the responsibility of every individual." Perhaps in the eyes of later generations, including the world outside of China as part of the "world" is simply foolish.

But there must always be some foolish people in the world, some people with an international spirit, some people who treat foreigners as human beings, to keep this world from looking so terrible.

Those who selflessly helped the Chinese people during China's century of humiliation, those Chinese peacekeepers who sacrifice overseas every year, those doctors, teachers, and engineers who aid poor countries... Facing them, can the ordinary people who type the words "foolish" on the keyboard really say the word "foolish" to their faces?

Perhaps there are really people who can say it.

But Yinreng couldn't say it.

As the Crown Prince of the Great Qing, he couldn't help but scheme against foreigners, and he couldn't treat foreigners as human beings. But he would never insult these true "sages," nor would he stop these true "sages."

There was just one thing Yinreng didn't understand.

"Father Emperor, with Teacher's wisdom, can't he see that it is only the common people who want to end the war, while the European nobles all crave war, and everything he does is a futile effort?" Yinreng asked in confusion.

Even though his son had grown up, Kangxi still ruffled Yinreng's hair and said, "Baocheng, look at the history books, those sages who wandered around during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, didn't they know they couldn't stop the war? But they still wandered around."

Sometimes, the fog in the heart only needs a gentle touch to dissipate immediately.

Yinreng understood quickly.

Some things, even if you know they are useless, you still have to do them.

Many sages in history books were going against the heavens. Going against the heavens was almost becoming one of China's traditions.

So what else was he confused about? He could only smile helplessly, then write a letter to his teacher, asking him to take care of his health.

Kangxi asked: "Do you want to see this scene with your own eyes?"

Yinreng nodded: "I want to."

Kangxi sighed: "I want to, too. The Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, who wouldn't want to see them with their own eyes?"

Yinreng nodded again.

Kangxi said: "It's a pity, there are too many things in the country."

Yinreng also sighed along.

Kangxi patted Yinreng on the shoulder and said: "Baoqing is overseas, you don't have to worry. The south is unstable again, I'm going on a southern tour to knock some sense into them. Will you be afraid to supervise the country alone?"

Yinreng laughed: "Father Emperor, what are you saying? How could your son be afraid of supervising the country? Father Emperor, please go on your southern tour with peace of mind."

Kangxi said: "On this southern tour, you will have full authority over state affairs, no need to report to me."

Yinreng: "...Father Emperor, your southern tour isn't just to be lazy, is it?"

Kangxi knocked Yinreng on the head hard: "What nonsense are you talking about? There are many things for me to do on my southern tour, definitely busier than you. I'm letting you handle state affairs with full authority to test you. You're getting married next year, I want to test if you can really stand on your own."

Yinreng was helpless: "A test for getting married? If your son fails the test, won't you let your son get married? Ouch, stop knocking, stop knocking, your son knows."

Yinreng covered his head: "If you knock again, your son will become stupid!"

Kangxi said with a straight face: "I think you're pretty stupid right now. You have to work hard. When Zhu Di was fighting in the grasslands, his fat son handled state affairs with full authority and did a good job; you can't be worse than the former Ming Zhu Di's fat son! Otherwise, I will punish you severely when I come back!"

Yinreng nodded vigorously: "Okay, okay, okay." Zhu Di's fat son was indeed a true fat son, the kind that would collapse a kang.

Kangxi said seriously: "Be serious!"

Yinreng also said seriously: "Your subject obeys the decree!"

After Kangxi decided on the southern tour, he was still not very at ease about leaving the Crown Prince alone in the capital.

He first gathered the Eight Banners commanders and warned them to listen to the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince's orders were his orders. He had already given the half of the military tally belonging to the Emperor to the Crown Prince. Even if the Crown Prince told them to go fight the Tsardom of Russia, they must go immediately.

He also wrote to the frontier generals, saying that he was about to go on a southern tour and that the Crown Prince would have full authority to supervise the country, so they should also be obedient and not violate the Crown Prince's orders.

Kangxi also knocked on the ministers in the capital one by one, telling them not to have any ulterior motives; if they made things difficult for the Crown Prince, he would return it a hundredfold when he came back.

The generals and ministers were sweating profusely.

Your Majesty, you have learned from Jiang Taigong fishing so many times that the fish in the pond are almost extinct; can you please let us go?

Even when you were here, didn't the Crown Prince's orders already equal your decrees? How would your subjects dare to violate the Crown Prince? Are you worrying too much?

Some people complained privately that Kangxi didn't look like a kind father, but a doting mother who spoiled her son.

After Kangxi finished knocking on people, he chose a temporary auxiliary team for the Crown Prince.

Mingzhu and Suo'ertu were of course both there, Chen Tingjing was urgently recalled to the capital, and Tang Zhen was also rushing back.

Kangxi also recalled Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin to hold important positions in the Imperial Guard in the capital, but did not lift their local positions, only letting them stay in the capital to assist the Crown Prince temporarily, and continue to be sent out after he returned to the capital.

Nalan Xingde and Cao Yin, who received Kangxi's decree, smiled bitterly.

Your Majesty, it's just a trip to the south of the Yangtze River, is it necessary?

Although it was indeed the first time the Crown Prince had supervised the country alone in the capital, the Crown Prince had gone overseas alone and had also gone on an expedition alone.

Well, maybe Prince Zhi was by the Crown Prince's side at that time, maybe it couldn't be called "alone."

And the second time the Crown Prince went on an expedition, he was almost assassinated; it was understandable that the Emperor was overly worried now.

After Kangxi pointed out a circle of ministers, he was still not at ease.

He looked at the young ministers and put the Crown Prince's recommended Gali and Aling'a to important use.

Kangxi said seriously: "The Crown Prince has been kind to you both; you must remember this!"

Gali's expression was fanatical.

Aling'a's expression was serious, sighing constantly in his heart.

Why did he get on the Crown Prince's boat? He really didn't understand.

But now that the Emperor had said so, and even asked the historian to record this sentence in the Veritable Records. If he betrayed the Crown Prince in the future... oh well, he would be infamous for ten thousand years.

Yinreng saw Kangxi so busy and wanted to persuade him, but in the end, he sighed and let his old father continue to be busy.

He knew that the last assassination had left too much of a psychological shadow on Kangxi. So no matter how excessive Kangxi's reaction was now, he could only obediently appease him to reduce the worry in Kangxi's heart.

Yinreng remembered that in his first life, he had supervised the country in the capital many times. Although he had to report major events to Kangxi before making decisions, he was just an executor, but the Kangxi of the first life was not worried at all and trusted him very much.

As for the current Father Emperor, he didn't know if it was trust or distrust; he really couldn't understand, so he could only appease his overly worried old father, indulging Kangxi in finding fault with ministers every day, like a paranoid, handing over all power to him, for fear that he would suffer.

Kangxi finally finished his work and went on a southern tour with a light load.

In the first life, although Kangxi's southern tour did not disturb the people, it could not be completely undisturbed; the Emperor's pomp was also necessary, otherwise how would the Cao family, who received the imperial carriage, go bankrupt.

In this life, Kangxi had long since stopped caring about the Emperor's pomp and airs. He took a team of Imperial Guards with him, didn't even bring any concubines, and swaggered out of the capital.

Kangxi first went to Nanjing, then to Hangzhou, then took a boat to Taiwan, and finally went to Annam to take a look, and then took a boat back to the capital.

Yinreng was speechless looking at the long southern tour route Kangxi had arranged.

Fine, going to Annam is also called a southern tour.

Yinreng was already prepared that Kangxi might go on a southern tour to his big brother's vassal state and then return slowly.

Before leaving, Kangxi promised Yinreng: "Baocheng, don't worry, when you get married, I will definitely come back. And I'll call your big brother back too."

Yinreng calculated the time and said speechlessly: "Father Emperor, are you planning to spend the winter in the south and then return slowly? Fine, you spend the winter in the south slowly, and when the weather is warm, come back, just treat it as going to a hot spring manor to spend the winter."

Kangxi smiled and nodded, waved his sleeves and left, not like an Emperor, but like a free and easy swordsman in a book.

Yinreng's mouth twitched.

……

"Your Majesty, are you sure? Are you sure and certain?" Changtai asked repeatedly.

Kangxi kicked Changtai on the butt: "Why do you have so much nonsense? Hurry up and change your address."

Changtai: "...Prince Gong, overseas is dangerous, would you like to think about it again?"

Kangxi said with a smile: "The Emperor has issued an imperial decree, asking me to assist Prince Zhi in handling overseas affairs and to spread the name of the Great Qing's benevolence. Even if it is a mountain of knives and a sea of fire ahead, I must go. Minister Chang, don't worry."

Changtai rolled his eyes.

Your Majesty! You've really gotten into character, haven't you?!

Changtai regretted it.

He shouldn't have perfunctorily agreed with Kangxi when Kangxi sighed "I'll be old if I don't go overseas," saying that he would also resign from his post to accompany Kangxi to wander when Kangxi became the Retired Emperor.

He originally thought, how could an Emperor in his prime abdicate to become a Retired Emperor just to wander overseas? That promise was just empty words.

But Changtai never expected that the Emperor could go on a southern tour without abdicating to become a Retired Emperor.

Ahem, going on a southern tour first and then a western tour can also be called a southern tour, no problem.

"Alright, don't you trust Baocheng? Baocheng will definitely be able to handle domestic affairs in an orderly manner," Kangxi rubbed his hands, "Tell me, if I go overseas, can I achieve the merit of destroying a country?"

Changtai was lifeless: "Your... ouch."

Kangxi kicked Changtai hard.

chapters.source_text:
常泰拍了拍腿上被康熙踹出的灰印子，深呼吸后，缓缓道：“王爷，我们是去拯救欧洲老百姓，不是去打仗。您可能没有灭国之功，但救国之功或许能指望指望。”
康熙笑道：“那还不快走。”
常泰抹了一把脸，看了一眼表情兼顾茫然和风中凌乱的将士们，特别是禁军将士们，沉声道：“拔锚！启航！”
……
京城中。
胤礽每日都能接到康熙的书信。
第一世中胤礽觉得每日和康熙通信很烦。现在心境却大不相同。若接不到康熙的书信，他才会心情不好。
“汗阿玛到南京了，速度真快。哈，曹寅干得不错，汗阿玛说你管的海军训练得好。”
“汗阿玛到昆山了。汗阿玛还是舍不得徐家人啊。徐家估计快起复了。”
“汗阿玛这么快就到苏州了？马上去杭州？汗阿玛不在苏杭多玩玩？难道是天气太冷的缘故？或许确实应该早日去南方。冬季在安南，应该会舒适许多。”
“汗阿玛启航去台湾了？不知道施家剩下的兄弟能不能抓住机会。”
“汗阿玛很快就继续南下？果然，汗阿玛是想在安南过冬。或许汗阿玛记着去看怀孕的大儿媳？”……
胤礽笑得十分无奈：“汗阿玛怎么走得这么快？只不到一旬，就到大哥的封国了。看来汗阿玛此行主要目的是考察南洋。说什么下江南，南洋也是长江以南对吧？”
胤礽的弟弟们疯狂嫉妒自家汗阿玛。
这次南巡，康熙不仅一个妃嫔都没带，甚至一个阿哥都没带。
他们本来还以为能捞上和汗阿玛一起南巡的机会，逃掉些许政务呢。
汗阿玛真是，吃独食丢不丢人！
胤礽道：“好了，你们也别嫉妒汗阿玛。等你们四个哥哥回来，就轮到你们出海了。现在多学一点，对你们……”
弟弟们捂耳朵：“别念了别念了。”
太子哥哥什么都好，就是爱念叨。
“太子殿下太子殿下！皇上新的信来啦！”曹寅亲自跑进宫送信。
胤礽道：“这次信怎么这么快？一天两封信，我看看……艹？！”

顾炎武看着海外他们自称盛世、自称世界霸主的国家中，那些根本不能称之为人的百姓，顾炎武看着他们互相攻讦连年征战的原因，明白了太子为何要违背本性。
刚入关的残暴满清是野人，是未开化的蛮夷。

无论哪个国家，只要其他人肯学他们的生活，就能成为他们的族人。

当初宋朝许多人疑惑，燕云十六州的汉儿为何鼎力支持金人？
因为他们已经在金国统治下几百年，已经是金人而已。

他们是严格按照血缘种族区分。华夏的“非我族类其心必异”，这“族类”是文化概念。但他们是生物概念。

传教士在大清做官的时候，都能被其他清朝官员尊重尊敬，当普通同僚看待。欧洲完全不可能。
观察之后，顾炎武明白了。就算现在大清和这些国家再怎么交好，但大清、华夏一旦露出疲态，这群野兽立刻就会撕掉伪装的人皮，露出嗜血的獠牙。
顾炎武参观完海外的科学院，看到了海外军队的武器，看到了他们的工厂。
他发现，现在正处于一个剧烈变革的时代。大清只能跟着一同往前奔跑，否则很快就会被甩开。那这群野兽就要扑过来了。
所以太子就算违背善良的本性，也要迅速压制国内的混乱，让大清的力量都用在奔跑上。
无论是用诡计逼迫江南豪族退让，还是激着书生们去孔府门口绝望自杀，或者是任用宗室女子戍守边疆……所有令人费解的行为，都是基于太子想让大清快点跑起来。
太子现在能信任的只有自己的亲人。
帝国就是这样。皇室之间互相猜忌，但遇到大事，他们能信任的也只是血缘。
所以无论公主，还是才几岁的小皇子，都被太子送上了官场前台，一同拉着推着大清往前跑。
顾炎武明白了，终于明白了。
他明白的时候，很想给太子写信，向太子道歉。
但他知道，若他向太子道歉，太子反而会难受。以他对太子的了解，反而他要继续对太子抱有更高的道德要求，才会让太子心里轻松一些。
太子需要在所有人都认为他做得正确的时候，有一个他尊敬的人以更高的道德要求他，告诉他就算为了利益应该如此做，但错了就是错了，这样太子才不会迷失。
就如这一封书信，太子知道不应该同情大清之外的百姓，但若有人帮他同情大清之外的百姓，太子心中会好受许多。
这不是虚伪，只是身处黑暗的人，也会趋向光明。
顾炎武和康熙相对沉默许久。
两人一个吃烤兔，一个慢吞吞喝羊肉汤。
当他们吃饱之后，胤禔亲自送上水果，然后坐在他们中间，道：“你们俩演什么哑剧？”
顾炎武吹胡子瞪眼：“没家教！”
康熙骂道：“你的礼貌呢！”
胤禔道：“我本蛮夷，你们俩习惯就好。所以你们俩演什么哑剧？有什么话就说啊，憋着不难受吗？对了，顾先生，你好好骂我老爹一顿。他说他南巡，结果南巡到欧洲来了，我弟弟在京城焦头烂额，简直不当人父！”
顾炎武沉默了半晌，道：“太子不像你，直亲王很像你。”
康熙道：“太子最像我。直亲王大概像……”
康熙脑海里闪过到处道歉的惠妃的模样，怎么也说不出直亲王像惠妃的话。
他道：“直亲王像他的皇玛法。”
顾炎武道：“你敢去你父皇陵墓前说这句话吗？”
康熙道：“怎么不敢？我实话实说。”
顾炎武：“呵呵。”
胤禔道：“你们俩干嘛啊？你们说你们想说的话啊，损我干什么？好了，皇父你也别抱怨了，我像你，像极了你，行了吧？”
康熙：“……不，你一点都不像我，滚一边去。”
胤禔：“呵呵。”
康熙把大儿子骂走，然后无奈道：“我这大儿子啊，性情太野了。”
顾炎武却道：“其实大皇子是个很好的孩子。你运气非常好，大儿子和二儿子都非常优秀善良。其他儿子虽然蠢了一些，但品行也不错。”
康熙看到顾炎武眼中的落寞，得意极了。
怎么，前明遗民，发现朕天命所归了？
能生养出这么多优秀的儿子，可不代表朕天命所归？
“顾先生，欧洲乱局何解？”康熙道，“朕其实是想让他们继续打，打烂最好。但太子却劝朕，最好调停诸国。朕知道太子在海外之事上绝不会犯妇人之仁。顾先生可知道太子为何会这么说？”
顾炎武无语：“你不能自己问太子？跑这么远来问我。”
康熙理所当然道：“我这个当父亲的怎么能问儿子？”
顾炎武：“……”你都能把儿子丢下跑路了，还怕丢这个脸？
顾炎武没好气道：“太子的意思恐怕是，若欧洲太乱，他们恐怕就会疯狂将国内危机转移到海外。只要加大对海外的掠夺，只要掀起更多的战争，他们能在战争中死很多平民，又能在战争中掠夺很多粮食财富，还能将国内的惨状原因撒谎成外国人不肯被他们抢夺。”
康熙脸色越来越阴沉：“真无耻。大清是目前最富饶的国家。或许他们会为了转移国内危机，不管不顾地联合起来朝大清开战？”
顾炎武道：“满清再蛮夷也是人，不理解他们很正常。你既然出来了，那就好好看看这里，好好了解这里的一切。”
他站起来，道：“这里才是华夏永远的敌人。一个永远不可能消灭的敌人。这是文明之争。”
说完，他转身离开，并不想和满清皇帝多待。
他已经获得了太子同意的书信，可以启程去欧洲诸国调停战争了。

229.二更合一 [V]
胤礽再次得到康熙书信的时候，他正在筹备过年。
康熙走了，正月还是得过。
祭祖、祈福、宫宴、赏赐……康熙拍拍屁股一走了之，什么都没和胤礽说，只能胤礽自己拿主意。
虽然这些事都可以依照以前的惯例，但祭祖祭天一事，向来是皇帝独有的权力。哪怕胤礽曾经代替康熙去了无数次，但那也是康熙下旨。
现在康熙屁的旨意都不给一个，胤礽只能自己给自己下命令，代替康熙去。
胤礽想太皇太后了。
若是太皇太后在，他皇帝老爹不在京城也没关系，太皇太后会把一切办得妥妥当当。皇帝不下旨，太皇太后下令也是一样。
皇太后不是太皇太后，她能帮佟皇贵妃稳定后宫就已经算很了不起，不能指望她太多。
胤礽又想胤祉、胤禛和胤祺了。
特别是胤祉和胤禛，已经封爵的弟弟可以帮他做很多事。
当然，他最想的是大哥。
如果大哥在，大哥大概会直接说，“既然汗阿玛不在，那祭祖祭天什么的全部等汗阿玛回来再说。汗阿玛怪罪，我帮你担着”。
嗯，大哥会直接让他撂挑子不干。汗阿玛摆烂，他和大哥也一起摆烂。
虽然他不会真的摆烂，大概率还是会把事情都扛起来。但有个人和他一起骂汗阿玛，心里也舒坦啊。
胤礽拆开信，以为康熙会叮嘱一些年节的事。
结果康熙全写自己在海外怎么（划掉）玩耍（划掉）忙碌，没有一句话询问国内，更没有半句话指点胤礽做事。
倒是胤禔写的信一半是对“叔叔”的吐槽，一半是绞尽脑汁帮胤礽分忧。
胤礽感动极了。
连他不爱动脑子的大哥都为了他绞尽脑汁思索国内该怎么办，汗阿玛您不羞愧吗？
胤礽深深叹了一口气，恶狠狠地瞪了康熙的书信一眼。
本着独郁闷不如众郁闷的心情，胤礽再次把知情人全部召集起来，当众读了康熙的信。
胤礽希望，以此让康熙回来时尴尬。
他也只能这样报复康熙了。
阿哥们一个个白眼都翻上了天，仿佛一个个都大哥附体；大臣们都在扶额，表情疲惫极了。
常宁干巴巴道：“皇上还真的以我的名义出访啊？不会有问题吧？”
胤礽道：“有问题，汗阿玛自己担着。”
常宁撇嘴。他就怕皇上甩锅，让他背锅。
但他无法反抗，只能受着，太悲哀了。
福全道：“皇上的判断很有道理。若欧洲太乱，他们可能对我们发起掠夺的战争。到时候无论他们战胜还是战败，能不能缓解他们自己的矛盾，都会给我们大清带来灾难。皇上此举也是有不得不去的道理。”
胤礽道：“这和汗阿玛自己去欧洲有关系吗？汗阿玛可以让大哥去调停，甚至可以派我去。”
福全：“……”他难道不知道是这个道理吗？他只是帮皇上狡辩一下。
吐槽完康熙之后，胤礽就开始分配工作。
胤礽自己要代替康熙在京城主持祭祖祭天工作，比如去天坛祷告、去太皇太后和顺治坟前祷告。
其他祖先的陵墓，康熙以前自己可以找借口不去，胤礽却是不行的。
他便把胤祚、胤祐和胤禩全派了出去，替康熙祭祖。
太子下令让其他皇子代替康熙祭祖，这在大清历史上头一遭。但介于顺治死得早，康熙严格来说才能算是大清入关后第一个长期统治的皇帝，所以什么规矩都可以从康熙朝来，大臣们睁一只眼闭一只眼，懒得说了。
京城中宫宴的准备工作，自然交给福全和常宁这两个宗室老人。
剩下的小阿哥们就是一块砖，哪里需要哪里搬，连刚入学没多久的小胤禵也逃不过。
小胤禵难过极了。
他只是一个刚启蒙的孩子，为什么就要承担这么重的政务了？他的小脑袋瓜子根本没办法运转这么快！
小胤禵抱住脑袋：“我会早衰，一定会早衰。”
胤祹和胤祥拍着弟弟的肩膀：“习惯就好。太子哥哥和大哥都是这么过来的。”
小胤禵含着一泡眼泪：“都是汗阿玛的错。”
胤祹和胤祥心道，谁不是呢。
还好康熙也大概认为大过年的，自己在欧洲逍遥不太好。
胤礽终于接到了康熙的圣旨——提后宫妃嫔的份位的圣旨。
康熙信中道，他在欧洲手写圣旨封胤祺为贝子，其他阿哥们年纪尚小，不好封爵，便赏赐他们各自的额娘。
已经封妃的妃嫔加三个月俸禄；有皇子存活的妃嫔们若还未到贵人，一并诏封为贵人；若生有已经出嫁的公主的妃嫔未到贵人，也诏封为贵人；安嫔虽未晋升，但待遇上升到妃嫔。
胤礽猜测，待六弟封爵时，安嫔就能终于升上妃位了。
在原本历史中，有许多妃嫔这时候应该已经晋升了。
但这一世的康熙太过忙碌，在后宫又无特别想要晋升之人，所以便一直忽视了后宫的份位——原本历史中几次低位妃嫔晋升，都是跟着佟皇贵妃、温僖贵妃、小佟贵妃等来的。
几个生母份位很低的阿哥们听到自家额娘晋升的消息，各个眉开眼笑，干活的劲头都足了不少。
特别是胤祐。因为他天生残疾，带累出身较好、当时也颇为受宠的戴佳氏几乎被打入了冷宫，虽有贵人待遇，但一直是庶妃。
现在这戴贵人，终于坐实了。
胤礽见阿哥们很开心，反正康熙也不在宫中，就放阿哥们在过年这几天休憩时陪着自己的生母。
为了让妃嫔们别因为康熙不在而寂寞，他又以太后的名义，请了戏班子和模仿外国的话剧社轮流在京中唱戏演戏。
妃嫔们每日聚在一起笑呵呵，半点没有因为康熙不在而忧愁。
康熙的策略的确非常厉害。只是后宫晋升了一批低位嫔妃，热闹就掩盖了康熙“南巡”还不带重臣的不自在。
现在朝中一些大臣又开始想要依附其他阿哥了。
投靠太子是锦上添花，甚至太子这锦上已经不需要花了。
他们倒不是真想谋逆，只是看皇上和太子的态度，对诸位皇子非常好，皇子们将来势力肯定很大。他们跟着皇子，就和在朝中找更厉害的重臣依附一样。
而且，后宫低位妃嫔逐渐晋升，年幼的阿哥们逐渐长大，或许……或许太子将来位置仍旧有变呢？
就算皇上真的很放心太子，不可能猜忌太子。但太子曾经重伤过……对吧？
活不过皇帝的太子比比皆是，小阿哥们也不一定完全没有机会。
总之，他们先投靠。最低是投靠一个有实权的宗室，最高说不定能撞上一个从龙之功。
因现在留在京城中的小阿哥们都还没有出宫建府，他们无法直接接触到小阿哥们，小阿哥们的母族就各个收到了许多礼物。
母族的概念更大。
不是只有父母姐妹兄弟这个小家庭是母族，同一个宗族都能算母族。这么多人，总会有一两个打着皇子旗号为非作歹的人。
一时间，胤礽收到许多对外戚的弹劾。
他看着折子上的诛心之语，不由疲惫。
这些弹劾又多少是真正正义的愤慨，又有多少是试探他对皇子的态度？
或许还有挑拨离间的成分吧。
无论杀多少人，无论灭多少族，只要坐在这个位置上，这些尔虞我诈都不会消失。
前段时间大臣们忙了起来，他耳根清净了不少。临近年节，再多的活都得停下来休息。
康熙不在，胤礽原本准备的一些改革，也只能暂时搁置一旁，等康熙回来商量。
胤礽仍旧很忙，大臣们却是闲了起来。一闲起来，他们就要内斗，还要挑拨他和皇子们内斗。
“汗阿玛，您什么时候回来。”胤礽看着桌案上的折子，自言自语。
以前康熙在的时候，虽然也无时无刻有算计，但胤礽处理这些算计的时候，并不是很疲惫。
现在想来，或许是因为做决定的是康熙的缘故。
胤礽虽给出了意见，但拍板的是康熙，承担最大责任的也是康熙，胤礽心理压力小了许多。而且有康熙为他把关，他就知道自己做的是错是对。如果两人意见不统一，还能一起商量。
出谋划策和做决定是两回事，他多谋，康熙擅断。其实擅断的人远远比多谋的人厉害，更能当一个领导者。
胤礽试图把弟弟们和大臣们都叫在一起商量。
商量完之后，他心中的压力也丝毫没有缓解。
因为最终，还是得由他来做决定。现在没有康熙对他说“好”还是“不好”。
第一世胤礽监国多次，但从未自己在重大事件上做过决定。
第三世胤礽早早参与政务，但哪怕是和大哥出海的时候，所做之事也是提前或者事后禀报康熙，由康熙拍板做决定。
哪怕几次“突发事件”，其实也无伤大雅，打完之后是留是放弃，也是康熙做决定。
胤礽现在才初次体会到做皇帝和做太子的不同。
皇帝的权力，在于“做决定”、在于“承担责任”。
金口玉言，一言九鼎。皇帝做了决定，整个朝廷就会动起来。之后每件事是对是错，皇帝就要承担责任。
对权力欲重的人而言，这样纲常独断大权在握的感觉非常令人沉迷。
而像胤礽这样对责任看得太重的人，就压力非常大了。
胤礽很想问康熙，在康熙决定擒拿鳌拜的时候，决定削藩的时候，决定废除剃发令的时候，决定让他出海的时候，决定建立大学崇尚新学的时候……在做出无数个很冒险的决定的时候，康熙心中是如何想的。
康熙在承担巨大压力的时候，是如何自我缓解的？总不能是靠着挼他和与大哥斗嘴吧？
胤礽胡思乱想，想着想着回忆起童年，忍不住笑出了声。
笑完之后，胤礽把弟弟们放出去，让他们各自领着弹劾自家外戚的折子，去严查其中是否有非法之事。
他又发现卫贵人的娘家再次蠢蠢欲动，便让胤禩管理内务府的库房，好好敲打觉禅家。
胤禩的生母觉禅氏，汉姓卫氏，所以称卫贵人。
卫贵人是后世难得从文物中发现真实姓名的后宫嫔妃，她本名叫“双姐”。
想想后世清穿文中，良妃总会有非常雅致的名字，什么琳琅、婉妮、淑倩、子曦……其实良妃历史中查的出真实姓名，大可不必随便编一个（滑稽）。
康熙在胤礽面前提起后宫嫔妃的时候，偶尔会说她们的闺名。
每当胤礽听到宫里妃嫔们的姓名时，就不由叹气。这些名字，清穿文绝对不肯用。
比如后世女穿成卫双姐什么的，名字一出，逼格都没了。
现在这位清穿文常客卫贵人卫双姐得知家里给胤禩拖后腿，气得大病一场，甚至想过要不要一死了之，不拖累胤禩。
当惠妃风风火火把这件事告诉胤礽，求太子拿主意的时候，胤礽整个人懵了。
至、至于吗！
这辈子，汗阿玛又没有因为胤禩夺嫡而骂你，你怎么心态还是崩了！
胤礽赶紧亲自去劝卫双姐女士，希望她能振作起来。
“卫贵人，胤禩心思细腻，最容易被感情左右。若没有你这个生母时时刻刻护着他，和他说心里话，帮他挡住来自觉禅家一些小人的利用，他若是被骗了怎么办？”胤礽苦口婆心，“即使惠妃母是胤禩的养母，养母和生母毕竟隔着一层，胤禩还是得让你来保护。”
惠妃也劝说道：“对对对，我即使想保护八阿哥，他面子薄、性子倔，也不肯被我保护。咱们怀胎十月好不容易生下了这些孽障，不好好护着还能怎么办？至少在他们得罪皇上得罪其他人的时候，咱们得备足东西去道歉啊。你若病了，难道让我去？我养大了胤禩，难道还要替他磕头道歉？你可别气我了。”
卫双姐女士被惠妃逗乐了。
她这时候其实不应该笑。
太子和惠妃双双来劝解她，这么大的阵仗，她本该忐忑极了。
但惠妃这话实在是太好笑，卫贵人实在是没忍住。
“姐姐，妾只是受了风寒，很快就好，很快就好。”卫贵人的精神立刻振作起来，“太子殿下，让您担忧了。妾绝对会立刻好起来，不让八阿哥难过。家里的事，您也让八阿哥放心。妾永远站在八阿哥这边，八阿哥可千万别留手。”
胤礽见被家里亲人连番打压，让她为家里做事，替家里和八阿哥牵线，一时间气得钻了牛角尖的卫贵人终于振作起来，松了一口气：“这些话，卫贵人还是和八弟亲自说吧。”
胤禩攥紧的拳头缩在袖子里，红着眼眶，道：“额娘。”
卫贵人：“八阿哥……”
她慌慌张张坐起来：“八阿哥怎么来了？八阿哥您不是正在拜谒昭陵吗？”
惠妃给胤礽使了一个眼色，他们俩悄悄离开。
离开之后，惠妃听着屋里的哭声，叹气道：“还好老大虽然是个孽障，但我不用担心我娘家给老大拖后腿。”
因胤禔和胤礽关系极好，惠妃与胤礽关系也非常亲近，所以说话就比较随意。
胤礽笑道：“惠妃母性格坚强，您娘家可不敢来找您麻烦。再说了他们要是来烦您，大哥那鞭子，就算我都拦不住。”
惠妃抱怨：“他现在心野得很。小时候还说在京中分府后邀请我去住。现在他去了海外，连封国都不想待。直亲王妃还大着肚子，他一不知道陪着，二不知道让直亲王妃回京城，让我照顾。我这颗心啊，愁得不行。我生他的时候是不是太用劲，把他脑子摔坏了？”
听到惠妃这口无遮拦的话，胤礽不由扶额：“应该、应该还好。欧洲的事很重要，大哥也是不放心。至于直亲王妃不回京……车马劳顿，京中也寒冷，不如封国温暖，或许不回来更好一些。”
惠妃叹气：“好了好了，不用替他说话，我已经习惯了。”
胤礽苦笑。
惠妃这一声“习惯”，真是委屈极了。
其实惠妃哪里不知道直亲王这么做自有他的道理？她不过是想儿子、想儿媳、想还未出生的孙子孙女了。
惠妃回宫之后，胤礽去探望了荣妃、德妃和宜妃。
德妃和宜妃还好，还有其他子女在身边，虽担心四阿哥和五阿哥，心里倒也不是很焦急。
荣妃就有些六神无主。
海外路途遥远，海上风浪危险，遥远的欧洲也有可能水土不服。荣妃死了太多孩子了，胤祉就是她的命。随着时间一天一天的增加，荣妃晚上甚至做起了噩梦。
胤礽见状，就让已经出嫁的荣宪公主回京，暂时陪着荣妃。
荣妃不断对着荣宪公主抹眼泪：“太子是个体贴人。三阿哥离开后，太子对我如同亲母，我何德何能。”
荣宪公主抱着额娘，轻轻拍打额娘的背。就像是小时候她难过的时候，额娘抱着她，轻轻拍打着她的背一样。
她知道，太子是个非常体贴的人。
能遇见这样的太子，是他们一家人的幸运。
“三阿哥在欧洲，说不定半点都没有思念我们。”荣宪公主道，“你看大阿哥天天都想往外跑，那些勋贵大臣们也总想出海。三阿哥上次去了东瀛，被汗阿玛和太子催了许久才回来。我们急成这样，他可快活了。你又不是不知道，他的真实性子，可能比大阿哥好不到哪去，从小就爱乱跑。”
荣妃擦了擦眼泪，笑出了声：“是啊，他就爱乱跑。小时候在天坛避地震的时候，他差点连累宜妃受罚。我和宜妃因此还互不说话了好长一段时间。”
荣宪公主也回忆道：“是啊。但无论他怎么乱跑，太子都能把他找到。他就算躲在柜子里，我们都找不到他，太子也能立刻寻到他。”
荣妃点头。
她眼中出现怀念的神色，也出现了自豪的神色。
即使比不过大阿哥与太子生死与共的兄弟之情，但胤祉在太子心中的地位绝对能在众阿哥中排第二。
因为当太子和大阿哥还长时间在宫中生活时，胤祉就是他们的小尾巴，被太子和大阿哥轮流抱着长大。
胤祉每一次跑丢，每一次躲起来，每一次被皇上欺负，都是太子护着他。
“等三阿哥回来，咱们听听他在外面玩了什么。”荣宪公主向往道，“太子说，他会找机会让我也能出海。我也想去外面看看。我想会会外面的女国王女王公，我大清公主绝不会输给她们。”
荣妃酸涩道：“好，好，能出去都出去。额娘就在京中等你们回来。”
荣宪公主点头。
她没说，其实荣妃也有机会出去。
因为汗阿玛曾经说过，待太子登基之后，有子有女的妃嫔可以出宫和儿女住，不必在宫中苦熬。
无论荣妃去她的公主府，还是去胤祉未来的封国，想出外走走难道难吗？
只是这话太犯忌讳，她不敢说。
不过胤祉那性格，真的能管好一个封国吗？荣宪公主有些忧愁。
……
“阿嚏。”胤祉抱着暖炉缩成一团，“欧洲也冷得过分了！”
胤祺道：“这个冬天肯定会死很多人。他们能不能别打了？”
胤禛烤着火：“说不准他们还想打得更厉害一些，这样吃饭的人就更少了。你看这天寒地冻，死的先是老弱病残和穷人，说不准他们还开心呢。”
胤祉皱眉：“四弟慎言！”
“就我们几个人在这，慎言什么？”胤禛冷哼，“连汗阿玛亲自出马，都不能说动路易十四停战。这群人没救了。”
胤祉和胤祺沉默。
汗阿玛和大清其他大臣、文人的游说成果原本不错。
英国等国都同意停战，和法国商量一同救灾。
但没想到受到大寒灾影响最严重的法国，居然坚决反对停战。
他们完全不能理解。
胤祺道：“路易十四不是一个蠢人。他难道不知道再这样下去，他可能控制不住国内民众叛乱了？”
胤祉把暖炉抱得更紧了一些，道：“他可能做到，只是停不下来啊。”
胤祺问道：“为什么？”
胤祉道：“我困了，问你四哥。你四哥喜欢说话。”
说完，他就开始打瞌睡。
胤禛和胤祺都有点生气。
这三哥气人的本事，有时候比大哥还厉害。
胤禛瞪了挑起话题，但又不接着说下去，非要他解答的胤祉，道：“可能是国内的贵族们在战争中获得了太多利益，他们不肯停下来，路易十四就不敢停下来。朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨，平民的死伤和他们有什么关系？路易十四则认为，那些平民就算再暴动也不会影响他的皇位，倒是贵族们支持率降低，会影响他。”
胤祺：“……这样啊。但不对吧，每个王朝的衰败，都是从百姓起义开始。”
胤禛白了胤祺一眼：“这里是欧洲！”
